title: ‘The Pitt’ to Be Honored by Cedars-Sinai (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: “The Pitt” will be honored by Cedars-Sinai with the Hollywood Leadership Award at its upcoming Sunset Soirée gala. The award recognizes the medical drama’s authentic portrayal of life in the emergency room and commitment to portraying the realities of emergency medicine with accuracy and heart. Star and executive producer Noah Wyle, executive producer and director John Wells and creator and showrunner R. […]
content:
“The Pitt” will be honored by Cedars-Sinai with the Hollywood Leadership Award at its upcoming Sunset Soirée gala.

The award recognizes the medical drama’s authentic portrayal of life in the emergency room and commitment to portraying the realities of emergency medicine with accuracy and heart.

Star and executive producer Noah Wyle, executive producer and director John Wells and creator and showrunner R. Scott Gemmill receive the honor at the Cedars-Sinai Board of Governors’ Sunset Soirée on Oct. 11 on the Warner Bros. Studio Lot in Burbank.

The evening will also honor philanthropists and community leaders Jaime and Andrew Schwartzberg with the Philanthropic Leadership Award, commemorating their decades of meaningful service, mentorship and transformative support of Cedars-Sinai’s mission.

Popular on Variety

“We’re excited to honor the incredible team behind ‘The Pitt,’ celebrating the power of storytelling and philanthropy to inspire meaningful change,” said Peter L. Slavin, MD, president and CEO of Cedars-Sinai. “Through their commitment to raising awareness about healthcare and emergency medicine both on and off screen, the team behind ‘The Pitt’ is helping shine a light on the importance of lifesaving care and the breakthroughs that make it possible.”

Slavin continued, “We’re also deeply grateful to Jaime and Andrew Schwartzberg for their generosity and longstanding commitment to Cedars-Sinai, alongside their extraordinary leadership and wide-reaching impact across the Los Angeles community beyond our hospital walls. Their dedication to our mission helps advance groundbreaking research and brings new possibilities in healthcare within reach.”

More than 750 guests are expected to attend the gala, which is raising funds for Cedars-Sinai’s Innovation to Impact campaign. The campaign, a $60 million initiative launched by the Board of Governors, is focused on accelerating early-stage research across five critical areas: children’s health, cancer, neurosciences, autoimmune diseases, metabolic diseases and aging. Central to this effort is the advancement of single-cell technology, empowering investigators to study diseased cells at the individual level and uncover the root causes of complex human conditions.

Musician Andy Grammer is set to perform during the festivities. Event sponsor and acclaimed Beverly Hills steakhouse Steak 48 will host a signature pop-up experience.

title: Xilam Animation Unveils Raft of Legacy, Returning IP Series Presales at Unifrance Rendez-vous (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Academy Award-nominated French animation studio Xilam Animation has inked a wave of presales for the latest content from its line-up of iconic comedy franchises during the Unifrance Rendez-Vous, contradicting the sales slowdown announced by France’s National Film Board and Unifrance earlier this week. Among these titles, the landmark ninth season of “Oggy and the Cockroaches” […]
content:
Academy Award-nominated French animation studio Xilam Animation has inked a wave of presales for the latest content from its line-up of iconic comedy franchises during the Unifrance Rendez-Vous, contradicting the sales slowdown announced by France’s National Film Board and Unifrance earlier this week.

Among these titles, the landmark ninth season of “Oggy and the Cockroaches” has been presold to Warner Bros. Discovery EMEA and APAC, while “Zig & Sharko”’s upcoming fifth and sixth seasons have licnensed to JioStar India Private Limited and Warner Bros. Discovery Italy. “Chickies,” the new spin-off to hit series “Where’s Chicky?,” is heading to Radio Canada and SVT Sweden, as Xilam announced it will bring the first two completed episodes to MIPCOM, with a full delivery planned for 2027.

“Our legacy brands remain a cornerstone of our business, continuing to resonate with generations of fans, while maintaining highly engaged online communities,” underlines Safaa Benazzouz, EVP Distribution at Xilam Animation, who’s currently attending the Rendez-vous. “The fresh content we’re creating across ‘Oggy and the Cockroaches,’ ‘Zig & Sharko’ and our ‘Chickies’ spin-off will ensure that these iconic IP continue engaging both new and existing audiences. Having such a strong roster of broadcasters already on board is testament to how evergreen these titles are and the ongoing demand for comedic, character-driven animations worldwide.”

Popular on Variety

One of the longest-running of French animated series, “Oggy” returns in its ninth season to the core elements that made the series a global success.

Led by the inventive and explosive rivalry between Oggy and the cockroaches, the new season, made up of 78 seven minute episodes, is directed by Julien Daubas (“Oggy,” “Asterix & Obelix: The Big Fight”) and Lucas Pinatel (“Zig & Sharko,” “Submarine Jim”) with returning broadcaster France Télévisions on board. It is slated for delivery between Q3 2027 and Q2 2028, in celebration of the franchise’s 30th anniversary in 2028.

“Oggy and the Cockroaches” is available in over 190 territories, with a digital fan base spanning 32M YouTube subscribers and 18B views, along with 22M subscribers across social media.

Courtesy of Xilam Animation

Two new seasons of “Zig & Sharko,” another legacy IP at Xilam which celebrated its 15th anniversary last year, are also spearheading the Studio’s slate at the Unifrance Rendez-vous.

With French longstanding partner Gulli returning to commission these fifth and sixth installments and deals announced across India (JioStar India Private Limited) and Italy (Warner Bros. Discovery), these two 52 x 7-minute slapstick comedy seasons is beginning to delight viewers across the world once again. “Zig & Sharko” is Xilam’s most established IP on YouTube, with over 39M subscribers and 23 billion views across eight dedicated channels worldwide.

Seasons 5 and 6, directed by Andrès Fernandez, will follow a summer vacation theme, with each season exploring the main characters’ idea of a perfect getaway – Zig in Season 5 and Marina in Season 6.

‘Zig & Sharko’ Credits Xilam Animation

“Chickies,” the latest upcoming spin-off to Xilam’s hit short-form series “Where’s Chicky?,” wraps this wave of sales with a cheerful tone.

A global YouTube hit generating over 2.5 billion views a year and available on leading international broadcasters, SVOD, FVOD and AVOD platforms worldwide, “Where’s Chicky” is now coming to TV series format with a 78-part season of seven-minute episodes. The CG animated series expected to be delivered by June 2027.

Already pre-sold to France Télévisions, the series is set to deliver by June 2027. It is directed by “Zig & Sharko” alums Cédric Diestsh and Anh Tu Cao, following Chicky, Bekky and Poyo, three curious and cheerful chicks who have had enough of being cooped up and expand the coop with new characters known as the “Chicklets.”

At Unifrance Rendez-vous, Xilam Animation presents its brand new IP “Submarine Jim”, a 52×11-minute whacky, 2D-animated series already pre-sold to France Télévisions, Super RTL and both European and international broadcasters including BBC (U.K. and Ireland), RTS (French, Switzerland), RTBF and VRT (Belgium), NPO (Netherlands), YLE (Finland), NRK (Norway) and Noga (Israel), as well as Warner Bros. Discovery in EMEA, Latin America, Southeast Asia and South Korea.

title: Jenny Slate Joins Dylan O’Brien In Hulu Comedy Pilot ‘Lex’
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Jenny Slate (Dying for Sex) has been tapped as the female lead opposite Dylan O’Brien in the Hulu comedy pilot Lex. Written by Sean Clements, the comedy centers on Lex (O’Brien), a disgraced former reality star who accidentally films a murder in the background of a $20 Cameo video, and finds himself at the […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Jenny Slate (Dying for Sex) has been tapped as the female lead opposite Dylan O’Brien in the Hulu comedy pilot Lex.

Written by Sean Clements, the comedy centers on Lex (O’Brien), a disgraced former reality star who accidentally films a murder in the background of a $20 Cameo video, and finds himself at the center of a global conspiracy — and on the run from powerful forces who want him dead. Using the skills he acquired navigating reality TV’s toxic social dynamics, Lex must fight to not get killed, to expose the truth, and most importantly… to get back on TV.

Slate will play the only other series regular role in the pilot, Holly, the recently fired personal assistant of a murdered tech CEO, who gets sucked into a global conspiracy along with former reality star Lex (O’Brien). Using her organizational skills—and a knowledge of firearms she picked up somewhere along the way—she’ll help Lex try to clear his name. If it eliminates her as a suspect, too, great!

Watch on Deadline

Clements and O’Brien executive produce along with Paul Simms. 20th Television is the studio.

Emmy-nominated for her role in FX’s Dying For Sex, which streams on Hulu, Slate can currently be seen starring alongside Chris Pine in the indie feature Carousel, which premiered at Sundance earlier this year. She’ll next lend her voice to DreamWorks Animation’s Forgotten Island. Slate, also known for her starring role in A24’s Obvious Child and for co-creating, co-writing and voicing Marcel The Shell With Shoes On, is repped by Linden Entertainment, Mosaic, CAA, and Yorn Levine Barnes.

title: ‘Gail’ First Look: Superfan Of Canadian Band Our Lady Peace Speaks Her Piece – Toronto Film Festival
summary: EXCLUSIVE: The Toronto Film Festival is stacked with music-themed documentaries this year – films on the Pretenders and Chrissie Hynde, Thai pop star/actress Lisa, singer Darlene Love, and the alt-country band Chaparelle among them. The documentary Gail, which holds its world premiere at TIFF on Saturday, focuses not so much on the Canadian band Our […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: The Toronto Film Festival is stacked with music-themed documentaries this year – films on the Pretenders and Chrissie Hynde, Thai pop star/actress Lisa, singer Darlene Love, and the alt-country band Chaparelle among them.

The documentary Gail, which holds its world premiere at TIFF on Saturday, focuses not so much on the Canadian band Our Lady Peace itself, but on its undisputed no. 1 fan, Gail Lichtman, a subway station agent from the Bronx. She’s been following the group for decades.

Michael Maxxis directed the film, which is programmed in the TIFF Docs section. Jason Reitman executive produces alongside Jason Blumenfeld and Our Lady Peace. We have your exclusive first look at the film in the teaser-trailer below.

Courtesy of Gail

“For more than thirty years, Bronx subway worker Gail E Lichtman has devoted nearly every spare dollar and vacation day to following the Canadian rock band Our Lady Peace, attending more than 150 concerts around the world,” notes a synopsis. “When the band embarks on an anniversary tour across Canada in the dead of winter, Gail sets out after them by bus, train, and ferry. Through the comedy, exhaustion, and unexpected tensions of the road, her eccentric devotion gradually reveals an intimate portrait of loneliness, joy, and the universal search for purpose, belonging, and hope. Funny, tender, and deeply human, Gail celebrates the extraordinary meaning that can be found in an ordinary life.”

Watch on Deadline

“This film has a kind of whimsical quality about it that when you see it, it makes sense the connection to Jason Reitman,” TIFF documentary programmer Thom Powers told Deadline when the festival lineup was announced.

Our Lady Peace in concert. Somewhere in the crowd: the band’s superfan, Gail Lichtman. Courtesy of Gail

Gail is produced by Morgan Gold, Michael Maxxis, Shane Reid, Natalie Allan, Our Lady Peace’s Raine Maida, Jason Murray, and Duncan Coutt.

Maida, singer and principal songwriter of Our Lady Peace, comments, “For 27 years I’ve watched Gail show up. 130 Our Lady Peace shows, 25 of my solo shows, VIP after VIP. Always the last person to wait in the cold by the tour bus after the show. A humble but complicated NYC transit worker who has somehow found her way into the front row again and again.

“As we prepared to launch the OLP 30 Tour, our manager Jason Murray, bassist Duncan Coutts, and myself found ourselves together at a Toronto Maple Leafs game discussing how to document this milestone. The obvious choice was another rock documentary. Unable to stomach that cliche, an idea hit me – What if we turned the camera around? Instead of asking what it’s like to spend thirty years in a band, we ask what it’s like to spend thirty years believing in one. To have Gail tell our story.”

Maida continues, “Through her eyes, I could finally ask the questions I’d been carrying for decades. Who was this fiercely loyal, deeply opinionated, endlessly resilient woman from Yonkers who had quietly become part of the fabric of our lives?”

Maida sought out Michael Maxxis to helm the project.

“I have always been fascinated by people, especially those whose lives unfold in the margins,” Maxxis observes. “At a concert, the artist is illuminated while the audience disappears into a mass of silhouettes. This was an opportunity to turn the lights around and explore the life of someone who had spent decades looking toward the stage. What was happening inside one of those silhouettes? Where did she come from? What did she return to when the concert ended? How deep could we go? Those questions were far more interesting to me than making a conventional film about a successful band.”

Gail is a production of Marching Orb and Charlie Boy Films. Music is by Our Lady Peace and Eric Rosse; the score is composed by Lesley Barber. Cole Grom edited the film; the director of photography is Morgan Gold.

Watch the teaser for Gail here:

title: Keanu Reeves Sets Thriller ‘Kill Current’ As First Pic Under New Label Two Dragonflies, Teaming With The Arena & Zando
summary: EXCLUSIVE: When Erik Feig launched The Arena, an independent studio focused on the creation of global franchises in event action and more, a Keanu Reeves collaboration seemed inevitable. And now, it’s coming to pass. Deadline has learned that The Arena has preemptively acquired and will finance and produce a Keanu Reeves-led adaptation of Oliver Lowe’s upcoming […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: When Erik Feig launched The Arena, an independent studio focused on the creation of global franchises in event action and more, a Keanu Reeves collaboration seemed inevitable. And now, it’s coming to pass.

Deadline has learned that The Arena has preemptively acquired and will finance and produce a Keanu Reeves-led adaptation of Oliver Lowe‘s upcoming novel Kill Current: A Jon Hendricks Thriller.

Reeves will also produce with Alexandra Grant via Two Dragonflies, with the project marking the first to emerge from his new, previously unannounced production banner. Molly Stern and her publisher Zando will exec produce.

Kill Current is the first novel in a forthcoming thriller series centering Jon Hendricks, a burned-out CIA officer who is pulled back in to avenge the protégé he trained and lost. Offering a globe-spanning, edge-of-your-seat action thriller about shifting alliances and the race for the world’s most precious and valuable assets, the first novel from Lowe is slated for publication by Zando in May 2027.

Watch on Deadline

“This project further underlines our focus on launching high-concept IP for global audiences across different media,” said Feig, who leads The Arena as CEO. “Keanu Reeves is a singular talent and synonymous with the kind of intelligent action franchises we are aiming to make. We are thrilled to work with him and Alexandra Grant and equally thrilled that Matt Reilly and Melissa Goodall were able to swoop in and get this!”

Explaining the draw of the source material, Zando’s founder and CEO, Stern, said: “Oliver Lowe’s masterful story, the first in his upcoming Jon Hendricks series, is poised to reinvent the geopolitical thriller for the modern era. Kill Current is rooted in the issues shaping today’s world — semi-conductors, global supply chains, technological and information warfare. It delivers the fast-paced, globe-trotting read and complex, intriguing characters that thriller fans of any era crave.”

As an action star and producer, Reeves is coming off the fourth installment of his John Wick franchise, which grossed nearly $450M worldwide, with the Donnie Yen spin-off Caine in post and a fifth entry with Wick in development.

The actor told Deadline: “I’m excited and grateful for the opportunity to develop the character Jon Hendricks with these wonderful collaborators and that this is the project that launches Two Dragonflies which I share with my partner, Alexandra Grant.”

Grant added, “Taking Kill Current from publishing into film form, and aligning with The Arena, Oliver Lowe and Zando is the kind of creative work Keanu and I have set up Two Dragonflies to do.”

Reeves and Grant founded Two Dragonflies to tell stories across art, film, TV, animation, comic books, games and literature. As an actor, Reeves’ upcoming projects include the Warner Bros. sci-fi flic Shiver and The Entertainment System Is Down from multiple Palme d’Or winner Ruben Östlund. He is represented by WME and Ziffren Brittenham.

Lowe is the pen name for writer Casey Stegman, whose fiction has been published by Tough, Shotgun Honey, Dark Yonder, Cowboy Jamboree, Bristol Noir and Punk Noir Magazine. Most recently, a story of his was included in The Best Mystery Stories of the Year, guest edited by John Grisham.

Zando comes to Kill Current following work alongside numerous authors whose work has gone on to film and television success, including Andy Weir (The Martian; Project Hail Mary), Gillian Flynn (Gone Girl; Sharp Objects), Sally Rooney (Normal People; Conversations with Friends) and Blake Crouch (Dark Matter).

Former Lionsgate film head Feig launched the Saudi-backed The Arena, a company looking to tap the modern fandom ecosystem, in October 2025. Other projects announced so far fall under their South Town banner, based on SNK video games set in the shared world of South Town. This includes the film Fatal Fury, written by The Dark Knight‘s David S. Goyer; their animated series Fatal Fury: The Vow with Skybound; the Godfather-inspired film Geese, written and directed by Grant Singer; plus adaptations of webtoon Art of Fighting, Metal Slug and Samurai Shodown.

In June, the company expanded its exec team with the addition of Melissa Goodall, Zach Hamby, Megan Fleming and Sajan Alagiri, as we were first to report.

Chili Finger marks the co-directorial debut of Edd Benda and Stephen Helstad under their Beyond the Porch banner. Written by Helstad, the film follows Jessica Lipki (Greer), a small-town lawyer who discovers a severed human finger in her […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Sumerian Pictures has acquired U.S. and Canadian distribution rights to dark comedy Chili Finger, which premiered at SXSW and stars Judy Greer, Sean Astin, Bryan Cranston and John Goodman.

Chili Finger marks the co-directorial debut of Edd Benda and Stephen Helstad under their Beyond the Porch banner. Written by Helstad, the film follows Jessica Lipki (Greer), a small-town lawyer who discovers a severed human finger in her bowl of chili at a regionally beloved fast-food chain.

Pic is produced by Sam Sandweiss and Jo Henriquez. Rob Williams, President of Sumerian Pictures, negotiated the acquisition on behalf of Sumerian Pictures with Jessica Lacy of Gersh on behalf of the filmmakers.

Additional cast include Dann Florek, Madeline Wise, Sarah Herrman, Sara Sevigny, and Paul Stanko.

Watch on Deadline

“Audiences are in for a treat. Chili Finger is a comedic feast, and we plan to make a meal of it,” said Sumerian founder Ash Avildsen and Williams.

“Hundreds of dedicated craftspeople and talent breathed life into our Chili Finger story, and it is a dream realized to celebrate everyone’s work on the big screen,” shared Benda and Helstad. “Sumerian understands our movie’s resonance with audiences, and we are grateful for their commitment to bring our American folktale to theaters and homes nationwide.”

Sumerian’s slate includes Sundance Grand Jury Prize and Audience Award winner Josephine, starring Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan, the romantic comedy Mile End Kicks, and Horsegirls, directed by Lauren Meyering.

title: Paul Feig Plotting ‘The Italian Job’ – The Dish
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Director Paul Feig in the early stages of planning a heist. Paramount Pictures is in early talks with The Housemaid director to mount a follow-up to the 2003 film The Italian Job. The studio is out to writers right now, but no elements are yet attached. Inspired by the 1969 Michael Caine-starring British film, […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Director Paul Feig in the early stages of planning a heist.

Paramount Pictures is in early talks with The Housemaid director to mount a follow-up to the 2003 film The Italian Job. The studio is out to writers right now, but no elements are yet attached.

Inspired by the 1969 Michael Caine-starring British film, the F. Gary Gray-directed The Italian Job starred Mark Wahlberg, Charlize Theron and Edward Norton. The film, notable for seeing the robbers escape in Mini Coopers before the inevitable double-crossing took place between the co-conspirators, did well at the box office, grossing $176 million worldwide.

Feig is coming off the hit The Housemaid, the Sydney Sweeney-starrer that grossed $400 million worldwide for Lionsgate, with a sequel in the works. The CAA-repped Feig’s other big films are Bridesmaids, The Heat and Ghostbusters.

Watch on Deadline

Stay tuned.

title: Channing Dungey on Warner Bros. TV Group’s Big Year of Pickups, Renewals and New Deals — Despite Industry Distractions and Ownership Uncertainty
summary: Warner Bros. TV Group isn’t acting like a studio with an uncertain future. Even as the fate of Warner Bros. Discovery remains up in the air — given the uncertain timeline of a Paramount Skydance acquisition — the studio has been on a development and production spree in recent months. This summer the division, under […]
content:
Warner Bros. TV Group isn’t acting like a studio with an uncertain future. Even as the fate of Warner Bros. Discovery remains up in the air — given the uncertain timeline of a Paramount Skydance acquisition — the studio has been on a development and production spree in recent months.

This summer the division, under chairman Channing Dungey, reupped its megadeal with John Wells — whose hit juggernaut for HBO Max, “The Pitt,” already won four Emmys last weekend and is expected to dominate the drama category at Monday night’s main ceremony.

Also, Variety can exclusively reveal that Matt Reeves and his 6th & Idaho production shingle (“The Penguin”) have reupped their overall deal with Warner Bros. TV. Reeves and company first signed on in 2020 to produce all TV projects with the studio. (“Matt has a true knack for getting into the psyche of his characters and he and his team have delivered some of the most compelling, thought-provoking stories over the years,” Dungey says.)

Popular on Variety

Other overall deals housed at the company include prolific creators like Greg Berlanti, Bill Lawrence, Chuck Lorre, Mindy Kaling, Lucia Aniello/Paul W. Downs and Jen Statsky.

Meanwhile, since January, the studio has landed 12 new series orders — most recently, the long-awaited revival of the “Manifest” franchise at Netflix, “Arrivals: A New Manifest Mystery.” Warner Bros. also lined up pickups for scripted series such as the DC-themed true-crime mockumentary “The People v. Gorilla Grodd” at HBO Max; the Brett Goldstein romantic comedy “Escorted” and horror drama “Stillwater” at Prime Video; the reimagined comic “Afterlife With Archie” at Disney+; and sitcom “I Suck at Girls” at Netflix.

Then there are the dozen series that have been renewed in recent months: “The Pitt,” “It: Welcome to Derry,” “Stuart Fails to Save the Universe” and “Rooster” at HBO Max, “Leanne,” “Untamed” and “Running Point” at Netflix, “Shrinking” and “Bad Monkey” at Apple TV, and broadcast hits “Memories of a Killer” (Fox) and “Georgie & Mandy’s First Marriage” (CBS). At ABC, “Abbott Elementary,” the No. 1 broadcast comedy in multiplatform among adults 18-49, returns for Season 6 next month.

And if that’s not enough, the studio is also spending big on the upcoming “Harry Potter” series it’s producing for sibling HBO Max; and it’s behind one of the most anticipated new series on Netflix in the coming year, “Scooby-Doo: Origins.”

Dungey’s studio domain also includes unscripted fare (including new seasons of “The Real Housewives: New York City,” “The Real Housewives: Salt Lake City” and Season 30 of “The Voice”), syndication (“Extra” and “The Jennifer Hudson Show”) and animation (including recent orders for Genndy Tartakovsky’s “Heist Brothers” and Tubi’s “Yokoso Scooby-Doo”).

As head of WBD U.S. networks, her oversight includes top 10 networks TBS, TNT, TLC and Food Network, and launched the No. 1 new unscripted series with TLC’s “Suddenly Amish.” Also this year, Discovery’s “Shark Week” had its best ratings since 2019, while “Puppy Bowl” scored its best audience in eight years across multiple platforms.

“Certainly when I when I look up toward my boss and everything that’s happening on the corporate level, it’s a complicated time,” says Dungey. “But it is not impacting our day-to-day business in any real way… My focus is continuing to work with the best creatives, develop the best shows, find the best homes for them, and that’s all been happening.”

Variety spoke with Dungey about the state of the studio and cable portfolio, and what’s next.

Two seasons in, what have you learned from the success of “The Pitt?”

What we’ve discovered with “The Pitt” is two things: audiences really love the weekly drop. “The Pitt” isn’t alone in this. We drop “Ted Lasso” weekly, for example. I think that there is something about the event. I think you appreciate them more when you watch them one at a time as opposed to binge. But the other really significant thing is the idea that you have it on an annual cadence. People right now are losing their mind that we’re already putting out teaser trailers for “The Pitt” Season 3 when it feels like “The Pitt” Season 2 just ended. And that feels good to the audience. It keeps them engaged and it keeps them connected to these characters. When you’ve got 18, 20, 22 months between seasons, sometimes even longer, life goes on and you kind of forget. Like, “why did I like that show so much?” I am hopeful that more streamers will put effort into trying to bring shows back on an annual cadence.

How did the “Manifest” spinoff finally happen?

“Manifest” original recipe did very well on Netflix, and there was a desire to continue to explore stories and ideas within that universe. It took a little bit for [creator] Jeff [Rake] and team to nail the right way to approach the concept. Even though it’s taken a little bit of time, I think we’ve now built something else that has a really great long-running engine at its core.

How much does the new show play off the old one? Is it a continuation of the story?

It was very important to Netflix that people who never watched the original could dive in and appreciate it on its own. But if you were a hardcore fan of the original, there’s enough connective tissue and mythology and Easter eggs that reward you for having been a part of this universe for such a long time. That’s part of why it was a little tricky to figure out exactly how we wanted to build it.

Will there be any cameos from the original cast?

Possibly. There’s definitely room for some of that if we choose to. But at this point there aren’t any big plans to do that.

There’s been a lot of conversation lately about the difficulty with Season 2 drop-offs on some of the streamers.

It’s always been hard. Back in the day, I always would say, getting through Season 2 is always the toughest. Because things launch, they’re new, they’re exciting, you’ve got a plethora of stories to tell. Then you have to do that all over again in Season 2 … And then it’s a one-two punch if you take forever to bring it back and then you drop all the episodes and you watch it all in a matter of days. It’s hard to remain part of the conversation.

You were looking to replicate that regular “Pitt”-like cadence with the police drama “American Blue,” which was passed on by HBO Max. How’s the search going to find it a new home?

We still have a couple of bites. We have the finished pilot, and we have another five scripts done to follow it. So if one of these places picks it up, we’ll be ready to rock ‘n’ roll. And we also still have “How to Survive Without Me,” which is the other pilot that we did in contention at Max. That is also the “Pitt” model, but the relationship drama version. It’s Greg Berlanti doing what he did so well with shows like “Brothers and Sisters,” with Ray Romano and Josh Jackson and Kaley Cuoco.

What’s the word on that one?

We should be getting some word imminently. We’re waiting on another script to go into Max, and hopefully that’s the thing that says “greenlight, go.”

Most recently, Hulu canceled Mindy Kaling’s “Not Suitable for Work” after just a season. I know you’re looking to shop it around. How difficult is that? A few years ago a show like that would have been given a second season or would have quickly found a second home on another streamer.

Every platform has their needs and they know what’s going on internally. “Not Suitable for Work” is a tremendous show. I love that cast so much. I’m very hopeful that we land a second season somewhere else. But it’s tough, especially with comedy, you really have to develop that relationship with the characters, and it takes time.

As for “Ted Lasso,” does Jason Sudeikis have another three-season arc? How much of it is mapped out?

We haven’t heard any creative beyond the season that we are finishing editorial on right now. When you get to the end of this season, I think you can see that it could go either way. There’s definitely branching narrative that could continue forward, and if Season 4 becomes the end, then I think it’s satisfying in its own way too.

Is that a Jason call? An Apple call? Who are we waiting on to see if there will be a Season 5?

With this, it’s always a complicated conversation. I think you can say it’s a little bit of everybody.

With the success of “Stuart Fails to Save the Universe,” how far can you take “The Big Bang Theory” franchise? More series?

This is such a rare gift, right? To have a multi-camera comedy give birth to a single-camera comedy, then to a multi-camera comedy, and back to a single. I don’t think it’s ever been done before that hat trick in exactly that way, I’m really excited that we’re going to be doing a second season. I don’t know if Chuck has another idea in his back pocket for how to extend this universe further, but I’ll certainly be the first in line to hear it if he does.

Let’s talk about your expectations for “Harry Potter” as we get closer to Christmas. This is going to be unlike most launches that you’ve experienced.

Oh, 100%. I’ve never been a part of a of a show this big, in terms of the way this world has been realized. The opportunity that we’ve had to really bring the books to life in the fullest of ways because we’re not limited by a running time in that way has been really exciting and I think will be really rewarding for audiences.

What’s it like to be working on a project where you know it’s going to be going on for years? You can spread out costs and plot things out.

Casey and I joke about this. You feel sort of like you’re the people at the beginning of the marathon carrying the baton, and you’re going to run as far as you go, and then you’re going to hand it to somebody else. Because I mean, this is probably another decade from here. But it’s really been fun to be here at the beginning and to help bring this all to life.

Has any of the corporate uncertainty changed the way you can greenlight a show?

We have not run up against any of those problems or challenges in terms of programming. Certainly as a largely independent studio, we are still buying projects and selling them to all different platforms at all different times. I have not seen any impact in terms of the decisions that Casey [Bloys] and the team are making on the HBO Max side either. And in terms of what we’re doing with the U.S. Nets, most of that programming is done on an annual cadence. We’re well into our buying for ‘27 and ‘28 and all of that is moving forward.

What’s the biggest thing you’ve had to actually put on hold or adjust?

We haven’t really put anything on hold. I think that if this deal continues to go on, we may soon. With some of these longer-term overall deals, it’s not that you’re putting anything on pause, but if you’re going to be making a big long-term commitment, certainly we’re going to want to discuss that with our partners across the aisle.

Have you found that the threshold for green lights has changed at all in the business?

In terms of green lights and acquisitions around town, I think that most of the platforms that we work with, everyone is being a little bit more scrutinous about what they want to buy, what they want to invest in. There was a there was a period a few years ago where it felt like people were ordering everything straight to series off a pitch. And now it’s a little bit more like, “We’d like to see a couple of scripts, maybe three scripts. We want to hear the series pitch for the season before we commit.” And I think it just reflects the fact that everyone’s slates are a little more compressed than they were. People are being much more deliberate about the decisions that they make,

How would you describe the state of development in the industry right now?

It’s been pretty consistent. 2022, 2023 was the beginning of a little bit of a contraction in the business as a whole. And certainly around that time, broadcast got extra skinny. That impacts the number of projects that you’re developing. But I feel like since that time we’ve remained pretty level year over year.

How are budgets looking now? You’re producing what I imagine is one of the most expensive shows on television with ‘Harry Potter.’

I think everybody is being a bit more fiscally responsible than they were in that really boom, bonanza time. In the pre-COVID time it did feel like there was almost a freewheeling attitude toward it, especially from some of the streamers. I don’t think you feel that anymore. We’re spending what we need to spend to make the best possible shows at all different price points.

Sam Register is leaving as head of Warner Bros. Animation, Cartoon Network Studios and Hanna-Barbera Studios Europe. Are you able to fill that position, or do you have to wait for the ownership issue to be resolved?

That’s absolutely a role that we’ll be looking to fill. Sam built such an incredible team, and the creatives who have been working with Sam for so many years are all still in place. I do want to tap a new leader of the division. We shared the news with Paramount that Sam was going to be departing, but there is no impediment to filling that role.

Now that you’ve been in charge of the U.S. network for a while, how have your thoughts about the future of linear evolved? Can they continue to be programmed as cable networks or at some point do they become more seen as content engines for HBO Max and streaming platforms?

It’s an interesting question and I think it’s both — meaning, there is still a very loyal dedicated audience watching these cable networks on linear. We’re having ratings growth on Food. We launched two new shows, “24 in 24” and “100 Cooks,” that both broke through without having some of our big-name talent attached to them. So there is still a lot of real meaningful growth in linear. But we’ve spent a lot of time talking internally about the fact that in this current day and age, we can’t just think about these networks as linear networks. We do have to think about them as brands, and how can we extend and enhance these brands. So many of them have great consumer connection. Especially when you think about HGTV and Food. People are more likely to buy a can of paint if it has the HGTV logo on it. They’re more likely to download a recipe if it has the Food Network logo on it.

Do you ever think about where they might fit in and be integrated with the Paramount cable networks?

There are definitely some networks that they have that I think could work very nicely with some of ours. The opportunity for growth as you pull things together is potentially very exciting. I am hopeful that there will be a point where we can actually engage in some of these conversations. But for now, it’s all theoretical.

Have you had any conversations with David Ellison about the company, Warner Bros. TV and the cable networks?

I’ve had a couple of meetings with David, but more of a “getting to know you” on both sides and less of “Here’s the vision for the structure in the future.” It’s too early in the process for those conversations.

Would you like to remain a part of this company post-merger?

I love my team at Warner Bros. Television Group. I love our shows, our talent. And I’ve become very happy in my U.S. networks role, which was something that I didn’t see coming almost two years ago. The best-case scenario for me is something that allows me to continue to play around in both of these spaces.

title: Taylor Swift Has Never Won a Grammy for Record or Song of the Year. With Three No. 1 Hits Eligible for 2027, Which Will She Choose for Victory?
summary: There are two points of view you could take on Taylor Swift and her Grammys history: (a) Swift has been a Grammys hoarder. (b) Swift has gotten robbed by the Recording Academy… regularly. Which of these contradictory statements is true? How about both of them? They’re not actually as oxymoronic as they appear; it just […]
content:
There are two points of view you could take on Taylor Swift and her Grammys history: (a) Swift has been a Grammys hoarder. (b) Swift has gotten robbed by the Recording Academy… regularly. Which of these contradictory statements is true?

How about both of them? They’re not actually as oxymoronic as they appear; it just depends which categories you’re considering. On the one hand, Swift is the all-time top honoree when it comes to Album of the Year, having picked it up four times (for “Fearless,” “1989,” “Folklore” and “Midnights,” spread out over a period of 14 years). She got so much attention for that record-shattering four-peat that there may be a popular perception that she’s already won enough Grammys for one person’s lifetime. In all, she’s picked up 14.

But here’s what very few people realize, or remember: She has never won Record of the Year or Song of the Year. That’s not a misprint. The biggest pop music star of the 21st century, and the one with the most No. 1 Hot 100 hits this century — 15 — has never been rewarded in either of the two all-genre Grammy categories that honor singles. Whether you love her, can’t stand her or fall somewhere in-between, that oversight for someone who is quantifiably the modern era’s most reliable crafter of indelible songs is kind of flabbergasting to consider.

Popular on Variety

Now, if things had to be that lopsided, and Swift had to pick just one of the Grammys’ top three categories in which to be such a dominative force, she’d probably say she was happy where she landed. She’s long talked about how happy she is to have helped keep the album format alive, as an artform and a commercial force, in the age of quick-hit streaming. But we can also guess that she’s competitive enough that the shutouts for record and song have to nag at her. They’re certainly seen as sins of omission in the world of Swifties who pay lasting and unforgiving attention to perceived snubs.

Is this the year for Swift to finally make up for lost time in either Record or Song, or both? It’s fair to say she is coming into the nominating process well-armed. Of those aforementioned 15 No. 1 hits, three of them came within the eligibility period for the 2027 Grammys, which just ended — and no other artist can similarly lay a claim to three recent charttoppers. It seems like quite an advantage, having taken “The Life of Ophelia,” “Opalite” and “I Knew It, I Knew You” to the summit, all in short order,

Except, of course, for the part where she has to pick just one.

That’s not literally accurate; Swift or her team would be free to submit multiple entries in the same category, to put on the general ballot that will go out to Recording Academy voters on Oct. 12. But obviously she won’t, as fortune favors jockeys who don’t attempt to race astride two (or more) horses at once. So there’s a slight bit of suspense as to which of the three smashes Swift and team will place their bets on.

Here at Variety, we are fairly certain we’ve figured out what the plan of attack will be. So jump ahead to the end if you can’t stand waiting. But if you want to know what the arguments are, here are some of the pluses and minuses Camp Swift will definitely have considered in deciding what to formally submit for election.

“Opalite.” This is the one we can fairly safely rule out as something Swift might pick for a single submission in a top Grammy category. We render that judgment with a bit of sorrow, because Variety’s critic is on record as having chosen “Opalite” as the most ineluctably catchy and fun song of all the material on her “The Life of a Showgirl” album. If that opinion was widely shared — and we do have company in that! — this would seemingly make it a natural pick for a Record of the Year slot (if less so Song, which is more about the writing than the vibe). Yet even though it made it No. 1, an honor afforded very few songs in a calendar year, it wasn’t a multi-week No. 1. It’s just starting the race too far behind the other two tunes in terms of perceived impact.

Why wasn’t “Opalite” a longer-lasting No. 1, when it was such a fan favorite from the moment “Showgirl” came out last October? Partly because it was a victim of the success of “Ophelia” and that song’s massive tail. Before it ever officially became a single, the streaming for “Opalite” was spread out over months and months. As an album track, it debuted at No. 2 on the Hot 100 the week “Showgirl” came out, and it remained in the top 10, on and off for 14 weeks prior to ever getting a music video or getting a radio push. But “Ophelia” was so huge, it soon became apparent that it had a shot at breaking Swift’s personal record for the most weeks one of her singles spent at No. 1, which surely was one reason why it kept getting pushed and “Opalite” kept getting pushed back. Eventually “Ophelia” hit the 10-week mark, a rare feat. When it was finally time to move on after that, “Opalite” had already been consumed in such mass quantities that it couldn’t stay on top for long. But in an alternate universe, the two “O” songs might have switched places and “Opalite” would have benefited from the more advantageous slot.

“The Fate of Ophelia.” The song’s 10 weeks at No. 1 set a personal high mark for Swift, as noted above. Would anyone have picked a song named after a drowned Shakespeare character to be Swift’s longest running topper and, by some commercial standards, the biggest song of her career? She would have, and that’s the only pre-release forecasting that counts. It broke both the single-day and single-week streaming records on Spotify. But its fate was really tied to viewing as much as pure listening, thanks to a Swift-directed music video that had the star and backup dancers romping through a variety of soundstage settings, imagining her as everything from a silent-movie damsel in distress to a ’60s go-go girl.

The real fate of “The Fate of Ophelia” wasn’t really measured in numbers, though. It was in TikTok clips and Instagram Stories and Facebook reels, etc., as the dance moves seen in the music video got memorized and charmingly copied by millions of users. Mostly by kids, yes, but some of the more novel adoptees really went viral. Moms and grandmas doing the “Ophelia” steps? Dog trainers making up modified choreography to get their German shepherds into the action? The craze had a sweetness to it. All these reenactors clearly weren’t being force-fed a hit. They were taking it to their hearts because it made them want to step lively. And anybody in the Recording Academy who either watched all those homemade clips or had a kid who did may feel that affection bubbling up again when they see “Ophelia” on their ballot.

If they see “Ophelia” on their ballot, that is. Because we haven’t forgotten the third contender from her recent catalog, one that would seem to have equally as good a case as this to be put in front of Academy voters next month…

“I Knew It, I Knew You.” It’s easy to tick off the reasons why Swift might choose her theme song for “Toy Story 5” over either of the songs from “The Life of a Showgirl”:

Recency bias. Of course it’s fresher in people’s minds than “The Fate of Ophelia,” which came out early in the eligibility period last October, and will be just over a year old when voters receive their ballots in six weeks. The Disney/Pixar tune only came out in June, a full eight months later, which has to count as an advantage, even if all release dates ought to be equal. (To quote “The Fantasticks”: Try to remember / The kind of October / When that ancient autumn smash came out…)

The blockbuster movie factor. A star as big as Swift can’t exactly be seen as riding another franchise’s coattails; when this single was released, the blowout unveiling created such a stir, you almost could have thought “TS5” was looking to ride hers, as much as anything. But we do have to consider that there will be Grammy voters, mostly older, who managed never to hear “Ophelia,” through Swift indifference or a general seclusion from contemporary hits, who will have been exposed to “I Knew It…” because they do not wall themselves off from the biggest or most critically appreciated movies of the year. And unless they fled for the exits at the first sign of a credit, they got a swift dose of the star at her winsomest.

The gentle factor and the country factor. Again, older voters who find a lot of contemporary pop assaultive may have a sweet spot for a Swift song that is this easy on the ears. And her return to a country-pop sound, after so many years in a different lane, may sit well with the Nashville contingent, since she made such a concerted effort to court country radio and make it sound as if, in her heart, she’d never left. Of course, she’ll have to deal with country-inclined voters being tempted to peel off for Ella Langley’s “Choosin’ Texas,” so there’s that. But after years and years of country being ignored by the Grammys in the top three categories (which Variety published a commentary about last year), it will be interesting if Swift and Langley together should offer the Academy an irresistible chance to put two country tunes among the finalists for top honors.

Surprising longevity. “I Knew It…” hasn’t quite rivaled “Ophelia” on every numbers scale — but for just about anyone else, this might be the song of their career. The fact that “Toy Story 5” has slipped down the box-office charts a little after making a gazillion dollars has not resulted in much slippage for Swift’s song. It currently stands at No. 3 on the Hot 100, and seems pretty locked into that slot, after 12 weeks of release. Songs attached to animated films usually have a limited shelf life, but this one is showing the very rare longevity of a “We Don’t Care About Bruno” or “A Whole New World,” with a twangy twist. When home video hits, the renewal it could enjoy is anyone’s guess.

She wants a damn Oscar. Well, we’re presuming… but doesn’t everybody? Perhaps the biggest factor for “I Knew It…” possibly being Swift’s pick for a Grammy campaign is that she can double it up with an Academy Awards campaign.

The idea that “I Knew It…” might be her preference to put in front of Grammy voters certainly got a big boost when she recently appeared in front of members of the Academy’s songwriters’ wing for an exclusive, invite-only Grammy Museum appearance. In the Q&A she did with Academy CEO Harvey Mason Jr., she didn’t really play any cards as far as discussing any of the eligible songs. But when she took to the piano for a climactic performance that was later released to the public on video, Swift did an Eras Tour-style mashup of three songs she felt were related, in terms of dealing with memory. “I Knew It, I Knew You” was one of those three songs. It felt like a choice.

So which will it be?

The verdict: A split decision. Of course, artists have the option of submitting different songs for Record and Song of the Year, although in most cases they’ll go with the same tune for both. But everything we sense about which direction Swift will go leads us to believe that she will lay different bets on both numbers, when both have so much going for them (and in the case of “I Knew It…,” still so much at stake with other awards shows).

For Record of the Year, we prophecize that she will go with “The Fate of Ophelia.” It’s a category where bops often stand a better chance than ballads. And for Song of the Year, she can favor “I Knew It, I Knew You,” where it’s a little easier to pick out her songwriting chops from the production choices, and which has some very notable nostalgic lyricism sprinkled in among the kind of lyrics that a tyke can still reasonably grasp. There’s no real reason to think that her chances in either category would be diminished by not favoring the same song in both.

Have we pegged this correctly? Check back Oct. 12, when the not-entirely-secret preliminary ballot goes out to voting Academy members, and we’ll know for sure whether she employed a split strategy and we really are knew-it-alls.

[This is the first in a series of columns looking at the prospects for the 2027 Grammy Awards.]

.

title: The Best Tech at IFA 2026: From 4K Projectors and Wearables to Headphones and TV Smart Lighting
summary: While CES is the biggest tech industry showcase in the United States, IFA is the largest consumer electronics trade show in Europe. For more than 100 years, some of the best and biggest communication and tech companies from around the world have gathered in the heart of Berlin, Germany at the Messe Berlin exhibition grounds, […]
content:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

While CES is the biggest tech industry showcase in the United States, IFA is the largest consumer electronics trade show in Europe. For more than 100 years, some of the best and biggest communication and tech companies from around the world have gathered in the heart of Berlin, Germany at the Messe Berlin exhibition grounds, for a chance to debut new innovations to the public for the first time.

In 2026, IFA (rebranded as Innovation For All) took place from Sept. 4 to Sept. 8 with companies like XGIMI, ASUS and TCL showing off their latest products. Additionally, the tech showcase featured a concert series at night with some of the hottest recording artists and DJs in Germany, including BUNT., Ikkimel & Friends Open Air and others.

“From radio to TV, personal computers, and now AI and robotics. For more than 100 years. IFA has been the place where society first encounters new technology,” says Leif Lindner, CEO of IFA Management, in a press conference. “Technology alone has not created progress. Understanding does. The future is not something on the horizon. The future is now.”

The Variety team visited the conference floor, attended keynote addresses, and had hands-on time in various tech demos to find the very best new tech products of the year.

From advanced 4K digital projectors and gaming controllers to motorized TV mounts and stylish noise-canceling headphones, we’re highlighting the top brands and releases. We reviewed products in home entertainment, networking, home décor and other categories, based on our first impressions.

TCL Best 4K TV TCL Designer 4K TV (A400U) Learn More at Best Buy

Instead of an ugly black slab, the TCL 4K QD-Mini LED Designer Series (A400U) offers a sophisticated and ultra-thin design that’s made to be mounted flush against a wall. It’s a real work of art, and doubles as a 4K TV that seamlessly blends into your home décor with up to 85 inches in size. It sports a sleek and stylish QD-Mini LED display with bright and vibrant color contrast with deep black levels with silky motion at 144Hz refresh rate and Dolby Vision, HDR10+ and DTS:X video support.

XGIMI Best Home 4K Projector XGIMI AURA 3 Pro Learn More AT XGIMI

Delivering a movie theater experience at home, the XGIMI AURA 3 Pro changes the way we watch movies at home with a home digital ultra short-throw projector. It feels like a real movie theater in your living room. title: Paul Mescal, Emma Corrin, Emilia Clarke Lead London National Theatre’s Starry 2027 Slate
summary: London’s National Theatre has unveiled its 2027 program, with Paul Mescal, Emma Corrin and Emilia Clarke topping a star-heavy slate of 18 productions, eight of them world premieres, spanning the venue’s three stages and beyond. Mescal returns to the Lyttelton theater for a repertory season, playing Biff Loman in Rebecca Frecknall’s staging of Arthur Miller’s […]
content:
London’s National Theatre has unveiled its 2027 program, with Paul Mescal, Emma Corrin and Emilia Clarke topping a star-heavy slate of 18 productions, eight of them world premieres, spanning the venue’s three stages and beyond.

Mescal returns to the Lyttelton theater for a repertory season, playing Biff Loman in Rebecca Frecknall’s staging of Arthur Miller’s “Death of a Salesman” before switching to the role of Michael Carney in Caitríona McLaughlin’s production of Tom Murphy’s “A Whistle in the Dark,” a co-production with Ireland’s Abbey Theatre. Tracy Letts makes his U.K. stage acting debut as Willy Loman opposite Monica Dolan’s Linda Loman, with Ciarán Hinds also joining the cast.

Emma Corrin will star as Catharine Holly in Michael Grandage’s revival of Tennessee Williams’ “Suddenly Last Summer,” marking Grandage’s first National Theatre production since 2010, with Arty Froushan and Harriet Walter rounding out the cast. Emilia Clarke will make her National Theatre debut in David Hare’s “Plenty,” directed by former National Theatre director Richard Eyre, staged ahead of Hare’s 80th birthday and the play’s 50th anniversary.

Popular on Variety

Uzo Aduba, a three-time Emmy winner, also debuts at the venue in “The Adeyemis – A Family Saga,” Oladipo Agboluaje’s family drama in the Dorfman theater, directed by Lucian Msamati in his own National Theatre directing debut. Rosamund Pike will make her Broadway debut reprising her role in Suzie Miller’s “Inter Alia” when the hit transfers to the Music Box Theater from Nov. 10, directed by Justin Martin, with co-stars Jamie Glover and Cormac McAlinden also debuting on Broadway.

Indhu Rubasingham, director and co-chief executive of the National Theatre, said next year’s program “brings together a remarkable range of work that looks across the last century to explore the perspectives, cultures and conflicts that continue to shape our world.” Kate Varah, executive director and co-chief executive, said the 2027 slate “reflects a scale, ambition and reach that places us at the heart of the U.K.’s thriving cultural ecosystem,” pointing to a National Theatre audience that now spans 184 countries.

The remaining world premieres include James Graham’s “Major,” reuniting the writer with director Jeremy Herrin after their acclaimed “This House” to dramatize John Major’s rise to prime minister, and Rubasingham’s staging of Moira Buffini’s “The Great Indaba,” a co-production with MGC dramatizing the 1998 Good Friday Agreement. Carmen Nasr’s “Samira,” set during the Arab Spring and directed by Emily Burns, stars May Calamawy, Joshua McGuire and Sirine Saba.

Also opening are Natasha Gordon’s stage adaptation of Bernardine Evaristo’s “Mr Loverman,” directed by Paulette Randall with a cast including Gary Beadle, Jo Martin and Danny Sapani; Phyllida Lloyd’s new musical “Glorious Madness,” built around songs written by Joan Armatrading, with Iman Qureshi penning the book and KPPL Productions co-producing; Punchdrunk’s immersive “Ghostlight,” conceived and directed by Felix Barrett and curated by Lucy Kirkwood to mark 50 years since the National Theatre’s South Bank home opened; and “The Last Wild,” a co-production with the Unicorn Theatre adapted by Jude Christian and directed by Unicorn Artistic Director Rachel Bagshaw for primary school and family audiences.

Beyond the rep season, the classics slate includes a revival of “West Side Story” co-directed by Marianne Elliott and Miranda Cromwell, using Jerome Robbins’ original choreography as reproduced by Julio Monge, and Robert Hastie’s staging of Tom Stoppard’s “Rosencrantz and Guildenstern Are Dead,” marking 60 years since its original London and Broadway productions and starring Mawaan Rizwan and George Fouracres.

On tour and in transfer, Jim Cartwright’s “The Rise and Fall of Little Voice” moves from its Dorfman run to seven regional theaters, directed by Hastie with a cast including Francesca Mills, Jill Halfpenny and Paul Chuckle. The stage adaptation of “Ballet Shoes” embarks on a U.K. tour with Chris Harper Productions as co-producer, with casting including Anton Du Beke; Frozen Light will provide multisensory performances for audiences with profound and multiple learning disabilities at select venues, with separate access performances offered across the wider tour. The musical “Pride” transfers to London’s Bridge Theatre from Nov. 12 following sold-out runs at the Dorfman and Cardiff’s Sherman Theatre.

The National Theatre’s digital reach will also expand in 2027, with more than 25 new titles added to the National Theatre at Home streaming service, a free YouTube stream of Rubasingham’s staging of “The Jungle Book” through the Take Your Seats initiative, and six new titles joining the National Theatre Collection for schools.

title: Playoff State of Mind: Yankees Tap Billy Joel for Merch Collection, Just In Time for the Postseason
summary: The New York Yankees are heading towards another (likely) postseason run and the team has tapped one of New York’s most famous faces (and voices) to help root them on. Athleticwear brand Sportiqe has released a Billy Joel x New York Yankees collection, that pairs the brand’s T-shirts, sweatshirts and hoodies with Joel’s lyrics and […]
content:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

The New York Yankees are heading towards another (likely) postseason run and the team has tapped one of New York’s most famous faces (and voices) to help root them on.

Athleticwear brand Sportiqe has released a Billy Joel x New York Yankees collection, that pairs the brand’s T-shirts, sweatshirts and hoodies with Joel’s lyrics and the baseball team’s most famous motifs. A press release says the official collaboration “pairs the music of hometown legend Billy Joel with the energy, pride and unmistakable passion of New York fandom.”

The Billy Joel x Yankees collection reworks one of the singer’s most famous lyrics as a rallying cry for the MLB team, with “New York State of Mind” printed on T-shirts, crewneck sweatshirts and on the back of a unisex hoodie. The navy blue Yankees logo is also featured prominently on each piece.

Joel was born in the Bronx and the singer has had plenty of connections to the Yankees throughout his career, including a bestselling live album recorded during his two sold-out concerts at Yankee Stadium in 1990. That concert run is commemorated in a vintage-inspired T-shirt that is also part of the Sportiqe collection.

Pricing for the official collaboration ranges from $52 to $109 with women’s sizes running small to XL and sizing for the unisex pieces running from XS to 3XL. You can shop the full collection here and see some of our favorites below.

Sportiqe VINTAGE-STYLE PICK Billy Joel x Yankees Concert Tee Buy Now AT SPORTIQE $60

CLASSIC CREWNECK Billy Joel x Yankees Ashlyn Crewneck Buy Now AT SPORTIQE $98

OFFICIAL UNISEX HOODIE Billy Joel x Yankees Dove Drake Hoodie Buy Now AT SPORTIQE $109

Depending on who you ask, Joel is generally considered more of a Mets fan. The singer’s 2008 Shea Stadium run was commemorated into a live album and DVD, titled “Live at Shea Stadium: The Concert.” The singer also famously played the final concert ever at Shea Stadium, a.k.a. “The Last Play at Shea.”

In addition to the Yankees collab, Sportiqe also has a Mets collection inspired by Joel, including a vintage-inspired T-shirt that commemorates Joel’s 2008 performance of “Piano Man.”

Sportiqe Billy Joel x Mets Asphalt Duke Tee Buy Now AT SPORTIQE $60

Joel has also performed the national anthem for Mets fans on a couple of occasions, including Game 3 of the 2015 World Series between the Mets and the Royals, and before Game 2 of the 1986 World Series between the Mets and Red Sox.

The Mets have been mathematically eliminated from the playoffs this season. The Yankees, meantime, hold the first wild-card spot in the American League.

content:
EXCLUSIVE: Cassady McClincy Zhang has been promoted to series regular for Season 4 of CBS‘ Tracker.

Zhang has recurred since last season as Reenie’s sharp new hire Mel, who is eager to prove herself on Colter’s cases.

She now joins Justin Hartley (Colter Shaw), Fiona Rene (Reenie), and Chris Lee (Randy) among the show’s series regulars.

Zhang was previously a series regular on The Walking Dead. She also recurred on Castle Rock and Chicago Med. Her feature film credits include Do Revenge and Love, Simon. She can soon be seen starring in the upcoming features And Out Comes the Wolf, The Snare and May and the Woodsman.

She is repped by CESD, Untitled Entertainment, and Sloane, Offer, Weber & Dern.

Watch on Deadline

Tracker returns for Season 4 on Sunday, October 4 at 9 p.m. ET/PT on CBS. The premiere episode will also stream on Paramount+.

Tracker, based on the bestselling novel The Never Game by Jeffery Deaver, stars Hartley as Colter Shaw, a lone-wolf survivalist who driven by the troubles of his past, uses his instincts to find the missing and collect rewards. Following last season’s explosive finale, Colter is wrestling with hard truths about his family’s history. In the wake of these shocking revelations, and aided by his trusted team, Colter must put the past in the rearview to focus on what he does best: using his instincts and survival skills to find the missing and collect rewards.

The series is produced by 20th Television. Hartley, Ken Olin, Elwood Reid, Sharon Lee Watson, Alex Katsnelson, Travis Donnelly, and Ryan O’Nan executive produce. Fiona Rene also stars as Reenie.

title: ‘RuPaul’s Drag Race UK All Stars’ Sets Fall 2027 Global Premiere On WOW Presents Plus

content:
For the first time in herstory, RuPaul’s Drag Race UK is headed to WOW Presents Plus from the BBC, with the streaming platform ordering the first-ever All Stars edition.

RuPaul’s Drag Race All Stars is set to premiere in Fall 2027 to celebrate “the artistry of the Queens who have worked the UK runway.”

The competition series will stream on the platform alongside all eight seasons of RuPaul’s Drag Race UK and the three seasons of RuPaul’s Drag Race UK vs. The World.

“It has been a pleasure working with everyone at The BBC, and we wish them well,” Fenton Bailey and Randy Barbato said in a statement. “While we don’t get to choose when opportunity knocks, we could not be more excited for this new chapter.”

The Drag Race franchise is a global phenomenon with local editions around the world, including Canada, México, Belgium, France, Brazil, Australia, the Philippines, and more. MTV recently renewed the original RuPaul’s Drag Race for Season 19 and ordered Season 12 of RuPaul’s Drag Race All Stars.

Watch on Deadline

Baile and Barbato added, “Historically, during times of anxiety and regression, the queer, trans, and drag communities are often targeted. Today is no exception. We at World of Wonder are so grateful to our members for their support, and we remain steadfast in the values that make RuPaul’s Drag Race more than just a fiercely entertaining show. For millions, it’s a lifeline, a safe space, and a celebration, and WOW Presents Plus is incredibly proud to keep providing that platform.”

News of RuPaul’s Drag Race UK All Stars came after The Sun reported the BBC had axed the main series amid major cuts at the British broadcaster.

Gunning is one of the four leads of the streamer’s Feral, a darkly comedic thriller series based on the 1987 novel by Shirley Conran, sources tell Deadline. Reps for Netflix […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: For the first time since her big breakout moment with Baby Reindeer, the darkly comedic stalker thriller turned water cooler phenomenon, Jessica Gunning is returning to Netflix.

Gunning is one of the four leads of the streamer’s Feral, a darkly comedic thriller series based on the 1987 novel by Shirley Conran, sources tell Deadline.

Reps for Netflix declined to comment. In the series, four very different women learn to survive on a lethal tropical island after their mining exec husbands are kidnapped. The question is, can they put aside their differences, their self-doubts and their vanities to stay alive?

Sources said Gunning plays Annie, a quietly dutiful wife who has sacrificed her ambitions to raise four sons under her domineering husband, Duncan.

Watch on Deadline

Jude Mack is the show’s creator. Emma Freeman (Interview with the Vampire, Stateless) is directing, with Oscar nominee Liza Marshall (Hamnet, Mary & George) producing alongside Laurie Borg (Foundation, Industry).

Gunning earned essentially every top honor one can — including an Emmy, Golden Globe, BAFTA TV Award, Actor Award, Critics’ Choice Award and Independent Spirit Award — for her work in Baby Reindeer, which premiered on Netflix in April 2024, emerging organically through word of mouth as one of their most memorable buzz titles in recent memory. In the show from Richard Gadd, she plays Martha, a vulnerable and deeply troubled woman who becomes fixated on Gadd’s struggling bartender/comedian, Donny Dunn.

With heat on her following her turn in the miniseries, Gunning took on films including Steven Soderbergh’s The Christophers, Sunny Dancer opposite Bella Ramsey and The Magic Faraway Tree. Upcoming, she’ll be seen in both the Marc Forster film Anxious People and the Apple TV series Berlin Noir. She is repped by Markham, Froggatt and Irwin, UTA, and Untitled.

Best known as an actor, Mack can currently be seen in Ted Lasso Season 4. Previously, she’s put in turns in everything from Apple’s Prime Target to Mickey 17, Mission: Impossible – The Final Reckoning and the Netflix action comedy Back in Action. Behind the scenes, Mack previously co-created and starred in Amicable, an Avalon comedy pilot for BBC Three, adapted from plays developed at the Edinburgh Fringe. She is repped by Independent Talent Group, Casarotto Ramsay & Associates and Granderson Des Rochers.

Director Freeman is repped by Cameron’s Management, Mgmt Entertainment and CAA.

title: September Showdown! SCOTUS Orders Blue State AGs To Respond To ParaBros Merger Antitrust Suit Objection From Iowa & Montana
summary: When all is said and done, the antitrust clash between Paramount Skydance and a dozen blue states may be best articulated by a certain Earth, Wind & Fire tune and remembering a day or two in September. In a move that could be read as a lifeline or a death knell depending on your POV, […]
content:
When all is said and done, the antitrust clash between Paramount Skydance and a dozen blue states may be best articulated by a certain Earth, Wind & Fire tune and remembering a day or two in September.

In a move that could be read as a lifeline or a death knell depending on your POV, the Supreme Court just told California Attorney General Rob Bonta and 11 of his colleagues that they have two weeks to respond to a challenge by Iowa and Montana to their efforts to kneecap the $111 billion ParaBros merger.

“Upon consideration of plaintiffs’ motion for expedited consideration, it is hereby ordered that defendants are allowed until September 25, 2026, to file responses to the motion for leave to file a bill of complaint,” the SCOTUS said in an order Wednesday.

While the edict doesn’t mean the conservative High Court is taking up the red states’ request for Motion to Leave to File a Bill of Complaint, it doesn’t mean they’re not either. Today’s order could suggest the Supreme Court is considering Iowa and Montana’s request for “expedited consideration” in the partisan matter. Still, even if the red states get their way if might be months before any hearing in DC — time that will surely deepen and harden already Mariana Trench deep animosity between the Melrose lot based Paramount and the various state capitols.

Watch on Deadline

Also, the September 25 deadline puts the coalition of Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Nevada, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, Oregon, and Washington in a bit of a bottleneck. The SCOTUS deadline is one day after the dozen blue states are set to argue against the David Ellison-owned Para’s desire for a $1.88 billion bond in front of a federal judge in Oakland. it also comes just a few days before a $7 million a day ticking fee to Warner Bros Discovery shareholders kicks in forTeam Ellison. That ticking fee, which is the basis of Paramount’s protest of “extraordinary losses” out of the court case and its March 2, 2027 trial start date, adds up to over $635 million a quarter — so do the math.

Waving off lMAGA chummy Para’s leaked threats of leaving California for a kinder red state and more as “blackmail,” Golden State AG Bonta, in an August 10 guest column for Deadline, called the long anticipated July 13 filing against Paramount and WBD “a straight up antitrust enforcement case. One that is very cut and dry.” David Ellison and crew disagree, pointing to midterms real politick and CNN ownership as the true cause of the move to stymie a deal that has been approved by “good friend” Donald Trump‘s DOJ, the UK, the EU, Canada, and many more.

In her promise to take the matter to the Supreme Court, Iowa AG Brenna Bird, while seeing no sin in the DOJ white glove sign off on the merger earlier this year, condemned Bonta and the other 11 AGs on August 25 as “more hostile to this pro-competition merger than Europe and China.”

Neither officials at the Hawkeye State’s AG, nor Bonta’s staff at the California Department of Justice responded today to Deadline’s request for comment on the order by the John Roberts-led SCOTUS. Paramount reps also were as quiet as church mice on what could be a defining moment in this big stakes, big egos battle.

Or, to put it in a dance move mode, with a bit of tweak: “Do you remember/the twenty-fifth night of September? ..how the stars stole the night away?”

title: ‘Entourage’ Creator Slams ‘God-Awful’ Ad Reuniting Jeremy Piven and Adrian Grenier: A ‘S—ty Imitation’ That ‘Makes Me Puke’
summary: “Entourage” creator Doug Ellin has spoken out against an ad reuniting Jeremy Piven and Adrian Grenier, calling it a “cheap, shitty imitation” of his beloved HBO comedy. While Piven and Grenier are technically playing themselves in the ad — not super agent Ari Gold and movie star Vincent Chase — their performances, dialogue and dynamic […]
content:
“Entourage” creator Doug Ellin has spoken out against an ad reuniting Jeremy Piven and Adrian Grenier, calling it a “cheap, shitty imitation” of his beloved HBO comedy.

While Piven and Grenier are technically playing themselves in the ad — not super agent Ari Gold and movie star Vincent Chase — their performances, dialogue and dynamic are certainly reminiscent of “Entourage.” (Piven snakes his way through a mansion party to find Grenier on a yacht, where he pitches him a new movie role.)

“Many people worked really hard to make our show as good as it was,” Ellin wrote on Instagram. “When I see cheap, shitty imitations that try to pass for what we did it makes me puke.”

Popular on Variety

On Wednesday, Variety broke the news of Piven and Grenier’s on-screen reunion, which took place in a three-minute spot for Jake Paul’s gambling app Betr. Ellin said in a video message that he received “400 messages” about the “god-awful commercial,” clarifying that he was not involved in its creation.

Ellin said he’s not bitter over not being paid for the ad. He simply wishes the writers of “Entourage” would get more credit for the hard work they put into the scripts and character development, only for their work to be distilled into an “embarrassing” emulation of the HBO hit.

“I watch it and I want to throw up, because I would suffer, along with many other people, over every syllable, every fucking word,” Ellin said. “So I watch this trash, this shit, and go, ‘Ugh, ugh.’ There’s no bitterness. I want everyone to get paid, get rich. Just fucking do your own shit. That’s all.”

Ellin then seemed to take a shot at Piven — who won three Emmys for playing Ari on the series — claiming that the actor distanced himself from “Entourage” in the years following the 2011 series finale and 2015 movie.

“I not only wrote, we found these people. We cast these people,” Ellin said of forming the “Entourage” ensemble. “I actually had to beg Piven to do the show because he didn’t wanna do it. And he didn’t wanna talk about it afterwards. Like, he wanted to get away from it, because he had so much better shit going on. But now he’s back on it, because he’s getting paid.”

A representative for Piven did not immediately respond to Variety‘s request for comment.

Responding to Ellin’s comments, a spokesperson for Betr said in a statement, “We were excited to bring Jeremy and Adrian back together, appearing as themselves. Creating that kind of unexpected cultural moment with two amazing actors was exactly what we wanted for Betr 2.0.”

The statement continues, “We’re really proud of how the spot came together, and the response has been overwhelmingly positive, generating nearly 10 million organic social views in less than 24 hours. We had a lot of fun making it, they had a lot of fun making it, and people seem to be having a lot of fun watching it. We appreciate Doug watching the ad and helping promote it. Betr 2.0 is available now.”

On another social media app, X, Ellin continued to lash out against the ad. “I have zero positivity in watching things I busted my ass [off] on for years [be] turned into garbage,” he wrote. “Go create your own shit. And if you need money … Flip burgers. This is trash and theft. Period.”

Responding to a fan who said he hoped Ellin was behind the ad, the “Entourage” creator fired back: “I think it’s pretty damn obvious I didn’t write it. My god.” And, with apparent sarcasm, Ellin replied to a fan asking for an “Entourage” reboot: “Piven should write and direct. I can’t wait [to] watch.”

Ellin has often been asked about doing an “Entourage” reboot since the series ended 15 years ago. A proper revival has never been in development, but the cast and (for a while) Ellin have expressed an interest in returning to the world of Vinny Chase. Earlier this month, however, Ellin threw cold water on the possibility, saying on the “Joe Vulpis Podcast” that a reboot or spinoff is unlikely, and “I don’t spend one second thinking about ideas unless somebody’s paying me.”

The closest he got to a revival was a 2022 pilot titled “Ramble On,” a dramedy about established stars looking to reinvent their careers that starred “Entourage” favorites including Kevin Connolly and Kevin Dillon alongside Charlie Sheen. Ellin released the trailer for the project, but it ultimately failed to sell to a distributor.

Ellin currently hosts the “Victory” podcast with “Entourage” star Kevin Dillon.
