title: Prime Video’s ‘The House of the Spirits’ Showrunners Francisca Alegria and Fernanda Urrejola Lead Alma Media Lab Slate (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Chile’s Francisca Alegría and Fernanda Urrejola, co-showrunners of Prime Video’s epic saga “The House of the Spirits” lead the slate of Alma Media Lab, a fledgling publishing-to-screen company based in Miami. Inspired by such companies as Hello Sunshine or Alloy Entertainment, Alma Media Lab will focus on books and series conceived simultaneously in close collaboration […]
content:
Chile’s Francisca Alegría and Fernanda Urrejola, co-showrunners of Prime Video’s epic saga “The House of the Spirits” lead the slate of Alma Media Lab, a fledgling publishing-to-screen company based in Miami.

Inspired by such companies as Hello Sunshine or Alloy Entertainment, Alma Media Lab will focus on books and series conceived simultaneously in close collaboration with their authors on projects mainly aimed at the U.S. Hispanic and Latin American market.

“What makes Alma different is its method: a discipline of strategic storytelling, built on 25 years of television and a foundation in philosophy, that adds value to creators’ work at every stage. The story is refined on the page, published as a book and adapted for the screen with its own author — creators keep their voice and their rights protected, and buyers receive material that arrives developed, proven and ready,” said Coca Gómez, co-founder & chief content officer, Alma Media Lab, who will serve as head writer on the drama series that Alegría and Urrejola are developing.

Popular on Variety

Coca Gómez and Alma Media Lab Partner Andres Arango Garay Credit: Melissa Berrios

“We’re extremely happy to be developing a show that celebrates one of the juiciest pillars of our modern Latin American identity alongside prolific writer/creator Coca Gómez, whose long career in television has shaped some of our country’s most memorable stories,” said Alegria, adding: “Fernanda and Coca have known each other for over 15 years and now we’ve found the story that finally brings them together as creative partners. After ‘The House of the Spirits,’ we’re chasing that same instinct: stories rooted in Latin America that don’t just travel, but redefine what audiences worldwide expect from our countries’ storytelling.”

“The publishing-to-screen model has already built some of television’s biggest franchises in English. In the U.S. Hispanic and Latin American market, its equivalent has yet to be built,” noted Gómez, a London-born Chilean, whose multiple credits include Chilean series “Cerro Alegre” and “Machos,” both of which she co-created.

Since its launch in January 2026, Alma Media Lab has signed a number of development deals with some of the most influential Hispanic creators working today.

Among them is Latin American bestselling author Carla Guelfenbein, with whom Alma Media Lab holds the exclusive rights to adapt two of her novels with her: the Alfaguara Prize-winning “In the Distance With You” (“Contigo en la distancia”) and “The Nature of Desire” (“La naturaleza del deseo”).

Carla Guelfenbein Credit: Micaela Altamirano 666

“Novelists spend so much of our lives writing alone. To step out of that solitude and encounter Coca’s agile, brilliant and extraordinarily generous mind has been an exhilarating creative experience,” said Guelfenbein.

“’The Nature of Desire’ is an emotionally charged portrait of passionate love, delving into its most intoxicating heights and devastating depths – a story of longing, risk and transformation. The novel captivated readers with extraordinary enthusiasm and the series promises to ignite that same fervor, drawing viewers into a world they will be eager to experience, discuss and share,” she added.

Alma Media Lab also holds the exclusive rights to Federico Arellano’s memoir, a prominent Colombian jurist, law professor, human rights expert and defense lawyer, who spent 37 years pursuing the truth about the bombing of Avianca Flight 203, long attributed to the infamous Colombian drug lord Pablo Escobar.

His book arrives at the end of this year as the first title from Alma Publishing, Alma Media Lab’s own imprint, with a premium series in parallel development, according to Gómez.



“I present my opera prima, the account of a legitimate fight, of the abrupt change of course in my life and of the sharps and flats that the score of my existence has set before me. It stands as an instrument of historical memory — of the violent course of our grieving nation. It is the complete story of a boy who dreamed of being an artist and became a warrior; a survivor more than a victim, and today a distinguished jurist, inspired by the love of God and by the legacy of his beloved father, still claimed to this day, living between the case files and the songs of his superhero,” Arellano said.



Another Alma Media project in the works is an audiobook trilogy reimagining “Machos,” the telenovela that marked a generation across Latin America and was sold to more than 40 countries.

The trilogy is a work-for-hire commission for Storytel and RDF Media — Canal 13’s audio arm, whose Emisor Podcasting studio produced ‘Caso 63,’ the leading scripted original podcast in Latin America, adapted in English by Spotify as ‘Case 63,’ starring Julianne Moore and Oscar Isaac. Storytel and RDF Media hold the rights to the property.

Gómez noted: “The potential reach of these projects goes beyond the U.S. Hispanic and Latin American markets given the fact that 600 million people speak Spanish worldwide.”

title: Nepal’s Oscar Contender ‘Elephants in the Fog’ Rallies Flood Relief Efforts at Toronto and Beyond (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Nepal’s Academy Awards entry “Elephants in the Fog” is the sole Nepali film at the Toronto Film Festival, where director Abinash Bikram Shah has turned the film’s international visibility toward the floods devastating communities back home – among them people directly connected to the production. Lead actress Puspa Thing Lama is from Nuwakot district, one […]
content:
Nepal‘s Academy Awards entry “Elephants in the Fog” is the sole Nepali film at the Toronto Film Festival, where director Abinash Bikram Shah has turned the film’s international visibility toward the floods devastating communities back home – among them people directly connected to the production.

Lead actress Puspa Thing Lama is from Nuwakot district, one of the worst-affected areas. Co-producer Prachanda Man Singh Shrestha, also from Nuwakot, has lost his home. “There is something difficult about watching a film travel internationally while people close to it are dealing with the loss of homes and livelihoods,” Shah tells Variety.

The production has already held a fundraising screening in Kathmandu, channeling the proceeds to the Prime Minister Disaster Relief Fund, and has worked with the Zonta Club and Rotary Clubs on support for children caught in the Bhotekoshi flooding. On Sept. 17, the film’s French production and distribution partners are staging a Paris screening, with Nepal’s Ambassador to France among those expected to attend; the evening’s distributor revenue will go to Nepal’s flood-relief fund. “We know that a film cannot solve a disaster,” Shah says. “But cinema can gather people in a room, create attention and sometimes turn that attention into action.”

Popular on Variety

The floods have also complicated the local release in Nepal. “It is hard to ask people to go to a cinema when many are dealing with displacement, loss and uncertainty,” he says. Despite that, “Elephants in the Fog” has carried into its second week since opening Sept. 4, taking in some NPR69 lakh ($45,000) in its first seven days. “But the conversations after screenings have meant just as much to us as the box office,” Shah says.

At the center of the film is Pirati, matriarch of a Kinnar community in a forested Nepalese village, played by first-time screen actress Puspa Thing Lama, who has spent decades as an LGBTIQA+ rights advocate. “She is not simply a representative of a ‘third gender’ community. She is a mother and a leader, with authority, affection, fears and contradictions,” Shah says.

Lama traveled to Cannes when the film took the Un Certain Regard Jury Prize and is now in Toronto. “There is something powerful about seeing someone who has spent decades working to make her community visible now occupying these spaces in her own right, not as a subject being discussed, but as an artist whose performance is being recognized,” Shah says. The Asia Pacific Screen Awards have nominated her for best performance; the film also picked up nods for best film and best director.

“I was drawn to the Kinnar community because of the richness and complexity of the community beyond the marginalization,” he says. The relationships between the women gradually became the film’s core – a story about mothers and daughters, and about people creating family when the structures around them have rejected them.

Sales company Best Friend Forever has closed deals across 14 territories. New agreements place the film with MetFilm Distribution in the U.K., Filmin in Spain, Vedette in Benelux, Trigon in Switzerland, Lev Cinema in Israel, Jayantii in Australia, EFAR Films in India, PT Falcon in Indonesia, the Film Development Council of the Philippines and Silk Route for inflight. Those join previously announced deals with Arizona Distribution and Les Valseurs Distribution in France, missingFILMs in Germany and Austria, Imovision in Brazil and The Tea Folks Films for domestic Nepal distribution. A pan-Latin America deal is expected shortly; North American rights are in advanced negotiations.

“The film has traveled much further than we ever expected, but its meaning remains rooted in the place where it began,” Shah says.

title: Mikel Gurrea’s Awaited ‘Saints,’ Toplined by ‘The Beloved’ Star Victoria Luengo, Swooped on by M-Appeal (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Mikel Gurrea’s “Saints,” starring Victoria Luengo, who played opposite Javier Bardem in “The Beloved,” will be brought to market at San Sebastián by Berlin-based M-Appeal which has acquired its international sales rights. M-Appeal will launch its campaign as “Saints” (“Sants”) weighs into San Sebastián Festival, running Sept. 18-26, as one of its highest-profile titles, one […]
content:
Mikel Gurrea’s “Saints,” starring Victoria Luengo, who played opposite Javier Bardem in “The Beloved,” will be brought to market at San Sebastián by Berlin-based M-Appeal which has acquired its international sales rights.

M-Appeal will launch its campaign as “Saints” (“Sants”) weighs into San Sebastián Festival, running Sept. 18-26, as one of its highest-profile titles, one of its main competition world premieres from a fast emerging Spanish director.

A stylish family drama plus a building – and singular – heist thriller, “Saints” marks the second feature from “Gurrea” who studied at the London Film School, the same alma mater as “Alcarràs” director Carla Simón. He already bowed his feature debut, “Suro,” in San Sebastián competition in 2022, marking him out as a talent to track.

Popular on Variety

A step-up in ambition – in its visuals, production values, locations, ever more challenging heists and emotional odyssey of the protagonist – Catalan-language “Saints” (“Sants”) stars Luengo as Lali, a drifter and thief, is summoned back to Barcelona by a sudden phone-call informing her that estranged mother Gloria (Ariadna Gil) is gravely ill.

There, Lali falls in with an an elite professional band of church religious artefact thieves, led by the charismatic ex-nun Rosario (Eulàlia Ramon), who gives part proceeds from the robberies to the needy.

That means Lali has to establish her priorities – between a new chosen family and her biological family, her dying mother. Once carefree, Lali learns to care.

“‘Saints’ pulled us in and never let go. Mikel Gurrea directs with real warmth and wit, balancing heartfelt moments with a welcome lightness,” said Maren Kroymann, of M-Appeal.

“At its center is Victoria Luengo, one of the most exciting faces in European cinema right now, delivering a performance that is both grounded and thrilling to watch,” she added.

Luengo already starred in “Suro.” “Since ‘Suro,’ Victoria has become a dear friend. She happens to be one of the best actress that I have ever seen. So, I always want to work with her,” Gurrea told Variety.

“The story takes us somewhere we did not expect, built around a series of heists that never lose sight of their characters, and culminates in an uplifting ending, exactly the kind audiences crave We are proud to be backing a director of such promise and trajectory,” Kroyman noted.

Co-written with Francisco Kosterlitz (“The Hunter’s Silence,” “Suro”), “Saints” is produced by Nocturna Pictures, Lastor Media, Deliris Films with Italy’s Kino Produzioni.

Laura Rubirola Sala, Tono Folguera and Ariadna Dot produced;

Giovanni Pompili, Lara Costa Calzado served as co-producers.

Lastor Media co-produced Carla Simón’s Berlin Golden Bear winner “Alcarràs” with Kino Produzioni.

“The relationship between Lastor Media and Kino Produzioni has been key to expanding our financing capacity. At the same time, the growing competitiveness of Catalan-language films has made us look increasingly outward,” Rubirola Sala told Variety. “Today, if we want to make films with the ability to travel internationally, completing their financing with international funds is essential.”

title: ‘Gomorrah’ Writer Maddalena Ravagli to Make Directorial Debut With Sicily-Set ‘The Place of Eternal Summer’ (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Maddalena Ravagli, who is known for penning some of the most successful Italian scripted series including “Gomorrah” and “ZeroZeroZero,” is making her directorial debut with Sicily-set story “The Place of Eternal Summer” (“La terra dell’estate”). Shooting is now underway in Sicilian locations on Ravagli’s first feature, which will mix coming-of-age and action movie tropes under […]
content:
Maddalena Ravagli, who is known for penning some of the most successful Italian scripted series including “Gomorrah” and “ZeroZeroZero,” is making her directorial debut with Sicily-set story “The Place of Eternal Summer” (“La terra dell’estate”).

Shooting is now underway in Sicilian locations on Ravagli’s first feature, which will mix coming-of-age and action movie tropes under the blazing Sicilian sun. Ravagli co-wrote the screenplay with her “Gomorrah” and “ZeroZeroZero” co-writer Leonardo Fasoli.

“The Place of Eternal Summer” is a tale of friendship between Leo and Turi, who are two very different kids, across three summers, each five years apart.

Popular on Variety

“They meet at 10, find each other again as teenagers, and reunite once more on the threshold of adulthood,” says the synopsis. “Summer after summer, as everything around them changes, so does their friendship, allowing them to find a space of freedom in a world that seems to have already decided who they should become.”

“As a screenwriter, I have always tried to give voice to the different worlds that inhabit our country, especially the ones that are too often unseen and unheard, and simply pushed to the margins,” Ravagli said in her directors’ statement.

“As a parent, I have mostly observed and listened, and this reminded me of how difficult it can be to truly know ourselves and come to terms with who we are. This is what made me feel the need to tell this tragic, poignant, but also funny and life-filled adventure. And adventure that, in a way, belongs to all of us as we search for the courage to find ourselves and be who we truly are,” the debuting director went on to note.

“The Place of Eternal Summer,” which features a slew of emerging Italian talents, is being produced by Moontrip, a banner set up by Rome-based Cattleya, which is owned by ITV Studios, with Fasoli and Ravagli, and Tramp Limited. Beside Productions, Vision Distribution and Sky are also on board.

The film will be theatrically released in Italy by Vision Distribution with international sales being handled by Vision Distribution International Sales.

title: Alma Pöysti, William Spetz, Pekka Strang Join Jon Blahed’s Romantic Comedy ‘The Bottom Line’ (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Actors Alma Pöysti, William Spetz and Pekka Strang are attached to Jon Blåhed’s romantic comedy “The Bottom Line,” with Pöysti set to play the lead role of Iris. The project will be pitched at the Finnish Film Affair (Sept. 23-25), which is the industry program of the Helsinki Intl. Film Festival. Pöysti is best known […]
content:
Actors Alma Pöysti, William Spetz and Pekka Strang are attached to Jon Blåhed‘s romantic comedy “The Bottom Line,” with Pöysti set to play the lead role of Iris. The project will be pitched at the Finnish Film Affair (Sept. 23-25), which is the industry program of the Helsinki Intl. Film Festival.

Pöysti is best known for Aki Kaurismäki’s Cannes Jury Prize winner “Fallen Leaves,” for which she was nominated for a Golden Globe and a European Film Award.

The film centers on 45-year-old Iris, a musician performing aboard the ferry between Vaasa and Umeå, stuck in a life that never quite turned out the way she imagined. When a younger music producer suddenly sees her in a new light, a longing for something different awakens – but pursuing it draws her into a web of lies that threatens everything she already has.

Popular on Variety

At its heart, the film is a romantic comedy about self-deception, longing and the courage to accept who you are – before losing what matters most.

The film takes place in Vaasa, Umeå and aboard the four-hour ferry crossing the Kvarken between Finland and Sweden. The ferry connects two countries and three languages – Swedish, Finland-Swedish and Finnish – and becomes an emotional space in the film, with Iris caught between different versions of the life she could be living.

Blåhed describes the film as “a modern romcom with a tragicomic edge, combining warmth, humor and sexuality.”

For Blåhed, who grew up in northern Sweden close to the Finnish border and has roots in both countries, the Kvarken region is a very personal setting. His ambition is to create something distinctly rooted in this rarely depicted part of the Nordic region while telling a universal story about love, relationships, ageing and our obsession with self-fulfilment.

Music will play an important part in the film, with Iris’ performances reflecting her emotional journey. Markus Krunegård is attached to write the original songs performed by Iris in the film. Pöysti will perform the songs in the film.

The film is written by Blåhed and Helmi Tolonen, and is produced by Mia Welin for Anagram Sweden (part of Studio TF1), in co-production with Just Republic in Finland. Scanbox is attached as Nordic distributor. The project is in development and financing.

The film has been developed with support from the Swedish Film Institute and the Amos Anderson Fund.

title: Zurich To Honor ‘The Artist’, ‘Moonlight’ & ‘I’m Still Here’ Distributor DCM
summary: The Zurich Film Festival will honor Berlin and Zurich-based distributor DCM with a Career Achievement Award at its upcoming edition kicking off on September 24. The award is being given to the company’s co-founders Marc Schmidheiny, Christoph Daniel, Dario Suter and Joel Brandeis as well as its Swiss managing director Stephanie Candinas for their long-standing […]
content:
The Zurich Film Festival will honor Berlin and Zurich-based distributor DCM with a Career Achievement Award at its upcoming edition kicking off on September 24.

The award is being given to the company’s co-founders Marc Schmidheiny, Christoph Daniel, Dario Suter and Joel Brandeis as well as its Swiss managing director Stephanie Candinas for their long-standing commitment to culture

They will be presented with the honor ahead of the screening of Wim Wenders’s documentary From Inside Out: The Architecture of Peter Zumthor, which DCM is distributing in Germany and Switzerland having also acted as a producer on the film.

Founded in 2008, film distributor and production studio DCM is known for distributing Oscar-winning films such as The Artist, Moonlight, and most recently I’m Still Here, as well as the family-entertainment blockbusters Bibi & Tina and The School of Magic Animals (Schule der Magischen Tiere).

Watch on Deadline

The history of DCM and its founders have been closely tied to the Zurich Film Festival since the company was launched in 2008.

Their first feature production Waffenstillstand, celebrated its European premiere at ZFF in 2009 and was honored with the Audience Award.

DCM expanded its business into Switzerland in 2013 with the distribution of Kon-Tiki. It has also played a significant role in supporting Swiss cinema releasing local hits such as The Awakening of Motti Wolkenbruch (Wolkenbruch) and Bonjour Switzerland (Bon Schuur Ticino).

This summer, the DCM-produced series Heidi wrapped filming in the Bergell valley and will air on Swiss broadcaster SRF next year.

It consolidated its position in Switzerland in 2025 with the acquisition of the country’s biggest independent distributor Ascot Elite Entertainment, in a friendly takeover instigated by the latter company’s founding owners Karin G. Dietrich, Ralph S. Dietrich and Stephan Giger.

“DCM is a company run by film and cinema lovers, and it has brought a breath of fresh air to the German-language film scene,” said Christian Jungen, CEO of the ZFF.

“The founders always act entrepreneurially and in the interest of the films. Much like us at the ZFF, they have a great passion for good American independent film, for German cinema and for Swiss film. With the acquisition of Ascot Elite, they made a spectacular move and are now ensuring that exciting auteur films continue to reach a large audience in cinemas as the largest indie player in the German-speaking market. With our Career Achievement Award, we want to thank the DCM team for what they have accomplished so far and encourage them in their continued commitment with the new company.”

Marc Schmidheiny, co-founder and partner of DCM, said the company had been in love with the Zurich ever since showing Waffenstillstand at the festival during its fifth edition.

“Since then, we’ve watched as industry giants, role models and cherished colleagues were honored for their work on the ZFF stage, and we have celebrated alongside them,” he said.

“To now stand on this stage ourselves and receive a price is both an honor and motivating for us. Because after the initial shock – caused by the misunderstanding that this was a Lifetime Achievement Award, which we feel far too young for – this is instead an incentive for the next chapters and films that will hopefully keep bringing us back to ZFF.”

Alongside Wenders’ latest work, the 22nd Zurich Film Festival will present further films from the DCM Film AG catalog, including the world premiere of Frauke Finsterwalder’s Eurostrash.

The festival runs from September 24 to October 4.

title: Channel 4 & Paramount’s 5 Make History With Advertising Deal
summary: Channel 4 and Paramount UK network 5 (previously Channel 5) have struck a historic pact over advertising. For the first time, two UK public service broadcasters will join together on ads, with Channel 4 Sales becoming the exclusive partner for a broad portfolio of Paramount brands in the UK including All Creaturs Great and Small […]
content:
Channel 4 and Paramount UK network 5 (previously Channel 5) have struck a historic pact over advertising.

For the first time, two UK public service broadcasters will join together on ads, with Channel 4 Sales becoming the exclusive partner for a broad portfolio of Paramount brands in the UK including All Creaturs Great and Small network 5.

Paramount and Sky previously had an ads deal in place, which is now over.

Under the terms of the agreement, Channel 4 Sales will assume responsibility for airtime sales across 5’s portfolio of TV and streaming channels including Milkshake!, 5USA, 5Star, 5Select and 5Action, along with Paramount UK networks like MTV, Comedy Central and Nickelodeon. Paramount Advertising International will exclusively handle advertising sales for Paramount’s direct to consumer brands in-house, including Paramount+ and Pluto TV, while continuing to handle social alongside sponsorship and creative partnerships.

Having been in the role for several months now, the move represents another big step from new Channel 4 CEO Priya Dogra, who has been carrying out a root-and-branch review of Channel 4 and is actioning a plan that will see nearly 350 employees laid off. She previously ran ads at pay-TV giant Sky.

Watch on Deadline

Dogra said the 5 partnership is a “tremendous proposition for advertisers, rooted in the power of public service broadcasting.” “This groundbreaking collaboration will give advertisers seamless access to a unique portfolio of trusted, premium brands and even larger audiences. It will also generate new commercial opportunities for two distinctive commercial PSBs, helping support further investment in British programming,” she added.

5 boss Reemah Sakaan added: “5 is on an incredible run, delivering must-watch hits that draw large, loyal audiences across every platform. Combine that momentum with Channel 4’s commercial strength, and advertisers get a scale and targeting proposition they won’t find anywhere else.”

title: PBS Buys Dutch Dementia Doc ‘Human Forever’, Which Follows ‘The Greta Thunberg Of Healthcare’
summary: EXCLUSIVE: PBS has picked up a Dutch documentary that follows Teun Toebes, a humanitarian activist known as ‘the Greta Thunberg of healthcare.’ Human Forever comes from indie Dutch producer Super7even Productions, which struck the deal directly with PBS. Other buyers unveiled today are SBS in Australia and RUV in Iceland, who joins the likes of […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: PBS has picked up a Dutch documentary that follows Teun Toebes, a humanitarian activist known as ‘the Greta Thunberg of healthcare.’

Human Forever comes from indie Dutch producer Super7even Productions, which struck the deal directly with PBS. Other buyers unveiled today are SBS in Australia and RUV in Iceland, who joins the likes of France’s Arte, Belgium’s VRT and Netherlands streamer Videoland.

The doc has been released theatrically in more than 30 territories to date, and its producers claim it is the most-watched human interest doc in Dutch cinema history with nearly 80,000 watching theatrically.

In Human Forever, Toebes embarks on a three-year journey across four continents and 11 countries to improve the quality of life of people living with dementia. Travelling alongside director Jonathan de Jong, he explores how dementia is approached in different countries and what care pathways can be made to include as many people as possible.

Watch on Deadline

The doc has led to policy discussions and informed educational programs at universities such as Tale, Cornell and Oxford, according to its makers.

On Thursday, de Jong and Toebes are releasing a related book, Human Forever: Searching the World for a Better Life with Dementia, via September Publishing. It looks at dementia care in four continents and countries such as South Africa, New Zealand Norway.

For PBS, the acquisition is a latest from the international docs market, and comes after the likes of The American Revolution last year, Skin of Glass in 2023 and Bombshell in 2019.

The news comes after Super7even founder de Jong announced a new venture, SuperIndie, with MN Media’s Jeffrey de Graaf, which is billed as an integrated studio for human interest, nature and social impact-driven docs and features for international audiences.

SuperIndie’s inaugural slate includes Human Forever sequel There is No Society, which we revealed in December last year, along with A Girl Like Rose, which looks at the life and career of Belgian supermodel Rose Bertram, and other doc titles including Patterns of Life, WOW! and Ecolopolis.

“It is so encouraging to see our film being appreciated, discussed and sought after by three major international broadcasting companies in different continents,” said de Jong. “We are thrilled that PBS, SBS and RÚV have recognised the potential in this story and its vital messages will be able to reach more people in the States, the Nordics and Australia.

“The film is rooted in our journey across different countries, and the questions it asks about ageing, dementia and the role of community are universal. These new acquisitions reinforce that broadcasters are looking for stories that don’t simply highlight the challenges, but also explore practical, hopeful approaches to improving quality of life. It is a testament to the power of independent documentary production and the backbone of our work at Super7even and SuperIndie.”

title: Snäxx Launches As Europe’s Latest Microdrama App Player
summary: Europe has its latest microdrama platform, Snäxx. The service, which has been in the works for some time, has the backing of Germany vertical video business Black Forest Studios and a board of “top-level” media, entertainment, technology and investment industry execs. Earlier this year, we reported Station 19 actor Boris Kodjoe was among the app’s […]
content:
Europe has its latest microdrama platform, Snäxx.

The service, which has been in the works for some time, has the backing of Germany vertical video business Black Forest Studios and a board of “top-level” media, entertainment, technology and investment industry execs. Earlier this year, we reported Station 19 actor Boris Kodjoe was among the app’s advisors.

The service will launch on November 1 on iOS and Android and claims to be “Europe’s first premium microdrama platform.” Others may dispute that title having launched services in the likes of the UK and France, but Black Forest is attempting to position it differently.

What its founders claim sets it apart is Snäxx is not being positioned purely as a short-form app, but as building part of “a new European content ecosystem.” As we outlined earlier this year, the plan is to eschew low-cost mobile-first productions from outside Europe and replace them with higher-end stories that have “European creativity” and “global ambition.”

Watch on Deadline

We also reported back in January that the app would launch with 16 completed series such as Black Forest Royale, about the life of an aristocratic German-American patchwork family in a castle in the Black Forest, high-speed thriller Guts and Mountain Medical, a drama similar to German series Schwarzwald Klinik.

At launch, Snäxx will have original productions and “selected content from independent producers, studios and rights holders.”

Black Forest, which operates a huge production studio out of Freiburg, claims Snäxx will have a ‘dual format’ strategy meaning content can play vertically on mobile and in 16:9 for television, streaming and other horizontal services. The app’s makers add this means it “represents more than any other outlet.”

Snäxx is now “actively” inviting European and international producers, distributors and rights holders to pitch in their microdrama content.

“Europe has extraordinary writers, producers, actors, studios and IP,” said Sebastian Weiland, co-founder of Snäxx and Black Forest Studios. “What has been missing is a platform built specifically to turn that creative strength into premium mobile entertainment.”

Black Forest Studios was built as one of Europe’s first production houses specifically for microdrama. The operation allows producers to develop, produce and post-produce, and deliver projects in-house, with “AI-supported workflows and a highly-efficient production pipeline designed specifically for serialized short-form storytelling.”

The final element to the Snäxx model is being billed a ‘Re:Format’, where broadcasters, distributors, studios and produces sitting on film or TV content can have them repurposed for the vertical platform.

Hernan Lopez’s Owl & Co. recently valued the vertical video space at $150M, excluding China, where the medium originated.

title: Goodfellas Boards World Sales On Kamila Andini’s ‘Four Seasons In Java’ Ahead Of Toronto Premiere
summary: Goodfellas has picked up international sales rights to Indonesian filmmaker Kamila Andini’s Four Seasons In Java ahead of its world premiere in the Centrepiece programme at Toronto International Film Festival. Produced by Ifa Isfansyah through Indonesian production company Forka Films, the film stars Putri Marino as Pertiwi, a woman who returns to her village after […]
content:
Goodfellas has picked up international sales rights to Indonesian filmmaker Kamila Andini’s Four Seasons In Java ahead of its world premiere in the Centrepiece programme at Toronto International Film Festival.

Produced by Ifa Isfansyah through Indonesian production company Forka Films, the film stars Putri Marino as Pertiwi, a woman who returns to her village after years in prison and is forced to confront the people, memories and violence that shaped her past.

Pertiwi’s return is met with rejection from much of the community and even her own family. As she begins to confront the circumstances surrounding her past, she embarks on a deeply personal journey to redefine her understanding of home, family, justice and peace.

The film combines psychological drama, mystery and elements of magical realism, exploring the aftermath of violence against women while examining memory, trauma, social judgement and the possibility of healing.

Watch on Deadline

Andini’s previous films have all played widely and won awards on the international festival circuit. Before, Now & Then, also handled internationally by Goodfellas, premiered in Competition at the Berlinale in 2022, where it won the Silver Bear for Best Supporting Performance for Laura Basuki.

Yuni premiered at Toronto in 2021, where it won the Platform Prize and subsequently became Indonesia’s submission for the Best International Feature Film category at the Oscars.

“Four Seasons In Java is a story about a woman who has to face the different seasons of her life and the consequences of what happened to her,” said Andini.

“Pertiwi’s journey is very personal and intimate. It is about finding peace and discovering herself, but also about questioning how society defines what is right and wrong, who is believed and who is not.”

In addition to Putri Marino, the cast is headed by Arya Saloka, Christine Hakim and Hana Malasan, with supporting roles played by Iswadi Pratama, Hargi Sundari, Nagra Kautsar Pakusadewo, Totos Rasiti, Shofia Shireen, Dwika Pradnyana and Hanna Aretha.

Four Seasons In Java is an international co-production involving Indonesia, France, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Saudi Arabia and Singapore. The project previously participated in international industry platforms including CineMart, at the International Film Festival Rotterdam (IFFR), the Berlinale Co-Production Market and the Venice Gap-Financing Market. It has also received support from international film funds including the Hubert Bals Fund, Netherlands Film Fund, Sørfond and CNC France.

Forka Films also produced Andini’s The Seen And Unseen, Yuni and Before, Now & Then, along with Eddie Cahyono’s Siti and Garin Nugroho’s Memories Of My Body, with several of its productions playing at major festivals including Toronto, Berlin and Venice.

title: Ed Sheeran Says Dropping Macklemore From Tour Was ‘Promoter’s Decision, Not Mine,’ Explains Why He’s Not Speaking Out on Israel and Palestine
summary: Ed Sheeran has commented on the decision to drop Macklemore from his U.S. Loop tour after the rapper made forceful “free Palestine” comments on stage during a political speech during the rapper’s performances opening for the singer at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey on Sept. 4 and 5. am appalled by the conflict between Israel […]
content:
Ed Sheeran has commented on the decision to drop Macklemore from his U.S. Loop tour after the rapper made forceful “free Palestine” comments on stage during a political speech during the rapper’s performances opening for the singer at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey on Sept. 4 and 5.

am appalled by the conflict between Israel and Palestine. The suffering and pain caused on both sides is a human tragedy. There are too many wars across the world causing immeasurable pain, none of which should be tolerated.

Macklemore asked to join my tour last year and I agreed, because I respect him as an artist.

Popular on Variety

As with all my support acts, I agree that they play a setlist of their choosing.

After Macklemore’s performances at my New Jersey shows, venues on my upcoming tour dates communicated that they would pull the shows if he was still supporting. I was informed that this stance was based on how Macklemore conveyed part of his message during his performance, rather than on everything that was said. I spoke with the venues at length all week to try and build a bridge. One of those people was Robert Kraft. I was also involved in direct talks with promoters along with activists on both sides to try and find a mutual resolution for all, but the venue’s and promoter’s decision was final.

Macklemore coming off tour was the promoter’s decision, it was not mine. Macklemore’s contract for the tour was with the promoter, not me.

I would never let down the fans who had made plans, nor would I abandon the touring crew and the other support acts and musicians who rely on me for work and to make a living.

I have always used my platform and music to bring people from all backgrounds and cultures together and this won’t ever change. Those who have been to one of my shows will know that they are about unity, joy, escapism, love, and a place for everyone to feel welcome.

I am not complicit. I have my personal views on this devastating conflict. Just because I choose not to speak publicly, it doesn’t mean I don’t have them, and it doesn’t mean I don’t care. Nor does it mean I don’t support causes in my own, personal way.

There is a reason I do not use my professional platform for politics – my audience includes young people, often children, of all backgrounds. Those who come to my shows do not expect a political forum. I respect Macklemore’s strength of purpose to stand up and shout for what he believes. However, there is room for multiple approaches to the same end: peace. I choose to use my fame and platform to be a place of safety and sanctuary, to maintain diplomacy and keep conversations open, not closed. If we only focus on shouting the loudest, nothing will ever change. There are different approaches to being an advocate for change.

I have spent this week trying to build bridges, to find a solution and unfortunately, was unable to do so. I know who I am, both as a person and as an artist, and those who know my heart know my values too.

Sheeran had not previously commented on the incidents, in which Macklemore unexpectedly told audiences that he wanted people in Gaza and the occupied West Bank to know they had not been forgotten. “A big part of the reason why I wanted to do this tour in the first place is so I could stand up in stadiums like this and say two words that are very near and dear to my heart: ‘Free Palestine,’” Macklemore said, to a decidedly mixed response from the crowd. “I said, ‘Free Palestine!’ I want those words to be loud and clear, so that people all the way in Gaza to the occupied West Bank know that we have not forgotten about them.”

The rapper then sang his song “Hind’s Hall” as images from the destruction in Gaza were shown on the screens inside the stadium. The song is about the pro-Palestine demonstrators who occupied a building at Columbia University after the murder of Hind Raja. Macklemore made similar comments on the second night; it seems likely he was aware that the New York metropolitan area is home to nearly 2 million Jewish residents, the largest population in the world outside Israel.

Messina Touring Group, promoter of the U.S. leg of Sheeran’s Loop Tour, said in a statement Monday: “As the concert promoter for Ed Sheeran’s U.S. Loop Tour, we have been notified by venues on the upcoming U.S. tour dates that they will not allow a concert to take place with Macklemore on the lineup, which would result in the cancellation of the tour and impact hundreds of thousands of fans. After discussions with stakeholders, Macklemore will not be performing on the remaining support dates.”

Macklemore was on the bill to perform at eight of the 10 shows Sheeran has left on his stadium tour, which will resume on Sept. 19 in Philadelphia. The rapper was scheduled to perform at venues such as Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, Georgia, Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis and more.

Macklemore’s politically-themed set at the Sept. 4 concert sparked a petition from the Israeli American Council, which demanded the rapper be removed from the remaining dates on the Loop tour. The petition read: “This was an Ed Sheeran concert – not a political rally, not a protest, and not an activist event. The issue is not whether Macklemore has the right to hold political views. The question is where the line should be drawn when an opening act uses a global concert platform to advance a one-sided political agenda.”

Macklemore’s speech went viral across social media and generated a second wave of headlines after the singer Pink reposted a call for the rapper to be dropped from Sheeran’s tour.

title: Magic: The Gathering’s ‘Reality Fracture’ Designers Unveil New ‘What If’ Set Details as Four Cards Debut (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: The world of Magic: The Gathering will break with the upcoming release of new mainline set “Reality Fracture,” something Magic maker Wizards of the Coast says fans have been asking for for a long time. “Doing another ‘what if’ set is a frequent player request, so it was something I’ve been on the lookout to […]
content:
The world of Magic: The Gathering will break with the upcoming release of new mainline set “Reality Fracture,” something Magic maker Wizards of the Coast says fans have been asking for for a long time.

“Doing another ‘what if’ set is a frequent player request, so it was something I’ve been on the lookout to do for years,” Magic: The Gathering head designer Mark Rosewater tells Variety. “What finally made it happen was the story. Once I heard about the Echoverse, I was like, ‘Okay, we have our “what if” set.'”

Releasing Oct. 2, “Reality Fracture” takes on “The Echoverse,” which Wizards describes as “Jace Beleren’s magnum opus, an artificial Multiverse of his own design” that will bring a host of warped cards and characters to Magic. Per Wizards, “Your favorite legends will take on new colors, your favorite cards will be twisted into new versions, and the story of Jace Beleren will reshape the Multiverse as you know it. It’s an exciting time to be a fan of Magic‘s Multiverse, and we’re bringing this mind-bending celebration to Commander!”

Popular on Variety

“Research was a huge part of ‘Reality Fracture,'” Wizards of the Coast worldbuilding design manager Meris Mullaley says. “The Echoed Pairs represent a kaleidoscope of divergent paths, some inspired by top-down character or plane ideas, other driven by mechanical hooks. We talked at length at how legendary characters would think, behave, or appear if they embodied a different mana color.”

Variety has an exclusive first look at four new cards (one with two art variants) from the upcoming set:

Wizards of the Coast

Wizards of the Coast

Wizards of the Coast

Wizards of the Coast

Wizards of the Coast

See more from Variety‘s interview with Rosewater and Mullaley below.

What new mechanics were you trying to introduce with Reality Fracture and how much was purposefully done in contrast to previous sets or even specific cards?

Mark Rosewater: The only brand new mechanic is empower Jace. The set has a “what if” theme and Jace was the antagonist of the story, so we were looking for an existing mechanic that we could stretch into something completely new that would allow us to expand the feel of Jace in the cards. Empower Jace was inspired by the amass mechanic (first seen in War of the Spark), but instead of creating a creature token, you’re creating a planeswalker token. We’ve never made common planeswalkers, so having common cards create a planeswalker token was dipping into space we’d never previously explored. Empower Jace was popular from the very first playtest, and never left the set. We think players are going to really enjoy it.

At what point did Wizards decide that a reverse Strixhaven was going to be the main setting of this storyline?

Rosewater: Very early in the set’s design, we were planning to have the expansion set on a while number of planes in the Echoverse, but after getting feedback on March of the Machine that the story spread around too much, we decided to center it on just one plane. This also allowed us to tell a much more personal story. The first plane we considered was Mirrodin Pure, an alternate take on the planet Mirrodin that we had hinted at many years ago, but never made. We ended up changing to Hexhaven, a what if version of Strixhaven, as that was a setting we’d just been to and there was a clean way to create a new version of it, doing something players had been asking for (ally-colored colleges rather than the normal enemy-colored ones of Strixhaven).

Meris Mullaley: Hexhaven offered newer Magic players a recent setting they would be familiar with, with Secrets of Strixhaven being the preceding Magic multiverse set. Mirrodin has a deep history and is loved by fans and that inspired our creative choices for legend pairs like Karn.

Were there always plans for Hexhaven going back to when they made the first Strixhaven set — or did you consider other planes that have longer history in the game and stronger connections to Jace like Ravnica?

Rosewater: We didn’t create Hexhaven until we were making Reality Fracture. When building the colleges in original Strixhaven, we had no plans for an ally-colored version of the schools.

Mullaley: I joined the project midway through creative development after Hexhaven was firmly part of the plan.

The flavor text of Entrust the Spark heavily suggests Jace dies, or at least gives up his Planeswalker spark. Can you confirm that plot point?

Mullaley: In the conclusion of the Reality Fracture web fiction, Jace dies by Vraska’s hand. His mind and body served as a physical tether for the Echoverse reality and the only way to stop the Echoverse from overwriting the original Multiverse was to break that connection. His spark leaves his body after he dies and seeks Tam out, which was something Jace had planned.

What was the process for deciding to make a ‘what if’ set?

Rosewater: Doing another “what if” set is a frequent player request, so it was something I’ve been on the lookout to do for years. What finally made it happen was the story. Once I heard about the Echoverse, I was like, “Okay, we have our ‘what if’ set.”

Magic’s last attempt at a “what if” set in Planar Chaos led to some notable color pie breaks. How was that avoided this time around? How were creature types and their usual color affiliations treated?

Rosewater: The big lesson of Planar Chaos was that we shouldn’t mess around with the color pie. It’s hard to communicate that a color doesn’t do something when someone can just point to a printed card and go, “yes you do”. So when I was first asked about Reality Fracture, I said I’m excited to do a what if set, but messing with the color pie is off the table. If a character shows up in a new color, we have to represent them with the mechanical tools of that color.

Mullaley: Research was a huge part of Reality Fracture. The Echoed Pairs represent a kaleidoscope of divergent paths, some inspired by top-down character or plane ideas, other driven by mechanical hooks. We talked at length at how legendary characters would think, behave, or appear if they embodied a different mana color.

Will we see more of the Echoverse and Hexhaven in the future? If the Hexhaven schools become popular, is there a way to bring them back like the clans were brought back after disappearing in Dragons of Tarkir?

Rosewater: We can’t speak to the future. R&D does have a saying though, “Success breeds repetition.”

Mullaley: Emrakul was trapped in the moon of Innistrad during the events of Eldritch Moon. Sometimes creative work is throwing a pass that your future self or your future peers may catch and run with years down the road.

title: Emmy Producers on Recruiting Taylor Swift, the Ideas She Brought to the Show and How This Year’s Telecast Wound Up Short
summary: When you hire Mariska Hargitay to host the Emmys, the fact that she has a few friends in high places pays off. And that starts with Taylor Swift. “They’re genuine friends,” executive producer Dionne Harmon said. “She’s like, ‘lemme hit Tay Tay!’” Emmy executive producers Jesse Collins, Harmon and Janae Rouzon-Clay from Jesse Collins Entertainment […]
content:
When you hire Mariska Hargitay to host the Emmys, the fact that she has a few friends in high places pays off. And that starts with Taylor Swift.

“They’re genuine friends,” executive producer Dionne Harmon said. “She’s like, ‘lemme hit Tay Tay!’”

Emmy executive producers Jesse Collins, Harmon and Janae Rouzon-Clay from Jesse Collins Entertainment and NBCUniversal live events and specials exec VP Jen Neal met with reporters immediately after Monday night’s Emmy telecast wrapped to share some behind-the-scenes details about this year’s show — and of course, the top questions revolved around Swift’s surprise appearance in a pre-tape parody of Hargitay’s “Law & Order: SVU.”

The idea was among the first to come up when Hargitay met with her writers (led by Ariel Dumas from “The Late Show With Stephen Colbert”) — and they immediately started brainstorming things for Swift to do.

Popular on Variety

“That was an idea that Taylor responded to,” Collins said of the sketch, which centered on the “SVU” team trying to figure out how or if Swift would show up at the Emmys. Swift played a fellow detective attempting to decipher some of the codes that would signal the superstar’s plans on the night.

“Their whole conversation was about how she was going to make it great and comfortable and all the things for her,” Collins said of Hargitay’s pitch to Swift. “Taylor loved the script and she had some thoughts and we worked that in.”

What were Swift’s notes? “The Easter eggs,” Collins said of some of the notations and hints that the singer gave throughout the bit. Added Rouzan-Clay: “She wanted them to be really official. And correct.”

The parody was filmed under tight security and secrecy on the “SVU” set in late August.

“The ‘SVU’ set is like walking into Mariska’s home,” Collins said. “And she made everybody comfortable, especially Taylor.”

As for keeping the cameo a secret, it was a small group that participated in the shoot. “And this was Mariska’s friend, so we made a promise to Taylor that we would keep it under wraps,” Collins said. “When you make a promise to Captain Benson, you keep it. We don’t want to go to awards show jail.”

Swift was so game that she was willing to take the time to participate in a large portion of the pre-taped bit. “Taylor’s been such a fan of Mariska’s for a long time, and when she was on set, she talked a lot about it,” Neal said. “She’s actually watched almost every single episode. She named her cat ‘Olivia Benson’!”

And yes, that was the real Olivia Benson the cat in Swift’s arms at the end of the sketch, alongside the TV Olivia Benson as played by Hargitay.

“That was, last minute, Taylor’s idea,” Collins said. “The night before, she was like, ‘What if I put the cat in the scene?’ And we were like, that would be awesome. So we did it. And the cat delivered!”

Rouzan-Clay said there was no doubt there would be an “SVU” presence (and some “dun-duns”): “We were going to do ‘SVU’ because I think everyone, the fans, everyone who tuned in, thought, ‘what will be the SVU thing?’ And if you’re going to do it, I think everyone we all felt like you have to one up what everyone’s thinking. And I can’t think of anything better than to throw Taylor in an ‘SVU’ sketch. Like, no one saw that coming. And if you’re going to have a nod to ‘SVU,’ that seemed like the coolest way to do it.”

Hargitay was game to utilize her contacts, which is why, besides Swift, viewers also got to see New York Knicks player Jalen Brunson in the show’s cold open.

“That was the beauty of Mariska hosting,” Collins said. “Everybody wanted to come play with her, and she was able to work with the team to come up with ideas that would make people comfortable after they said yes. You saw it in the open and the SVU sketch.”

Added Rouzan-Clay: “Mariska’s had such a great year and has so many connections with Jalen and Taylor and all the people in Hollywood that were happening in pop culture this year. So it was really just a dream for us to work with her to appeal to this broad audience. She really has something for everyone, and is broadly beloved.”

Here are a few more behind-the-scenes nuggets we gleaned from the producers about this year’s show:

Trae Patton/NBC

Hargitay spent time with a vocal coach and in off-site rehearsals to prepare for all the singing she had on this year’s Emmy telecast, including the opening “I Love Rock ‘n’ Roll” parody “I Love TV Screens.”

“She really worked hard on that song,” Collins said.” A lot of vocal sessions recorded it in New York. And she did some more work on it in L.A., really perfecting it. I mean, this is one of the hardest-working hosts I’ve ever seen on any award show. When we shot that opening piece, we shot one scene in New York and two full days in L.A. On Thursday after the media press conference, we came here. She started shooting at around 2 in the afternoon, and we left the plaza at midnight, 12:30 a.m. The work that she put in was unparalleled.”

Even while preparing to host the Emmys, Hargitay did not take a break from shooting “SVU.”

“The writers were in an office out of ‘SVU’ for the last couple months, so it was basically like, bust a perp, run up, do a joke, go back,” Collins said.

Added Neal: “When Mariska signed on, she said, ‘If I do this, I want it to be the best Emmys ever.’ So she was so committed, and she gave her all in terms of all of this. Like truly a dream, and totally committed and prepared.”

Dumas and the “Late Show” writers were hired after Jesse Collins Entertainment and NBC did a large search to find the proper head writer for Hargitay.

“She put together a great team, all New York writers who were willing to work at ‘SVU,’ which we’re all fans of,” Collins said. “Like you walk on that set and you’re like, ‘oh man, it’s the interrogation room. That’s Ice-T over there!’”

Trae Patton/NBC

Noah Kahan was tapped for the “In Memoriam” after NBC and Jesse Collins Entertainment worked with him on the Macy’s 4th of July Fireworks special earlier this summer.

“We only got to have him on a pre tape for that show, and so we thought he was the perfect voice for this, and he really delivered,” Rouzan-Clay said. “He’s had a big year.”

Added Collins: “He’s selling out stadiums, so we knew people would love him.”

Trae Patton/NBC

Reba McEntire chose the Dolly Parton song “Appalachian Memories” to perform as tribute to her late friend. And on stage, she was wearing Parton’s butterfly ring.

“We were fortunate enough for Reba to agree,” Collins said. “She’s shooting her show right now, but she made time for this. She was like, ‘It’s a beautiful story behind that record.’ It’s Reba McEntire, so you’re gonna say yes.”

Said Neal: “Reba and Dolly have a long history, obviously, and connection. She went to the family, and the family lent her one of the rings of Dolly. So it was very special, purposeful for that specific song.”

The producers had an entire document lined up to chart Hargitay’s multiple wardrobe changes throughout the evening.

“It had the corresponding hair looks for each one,” Harmon said. “It was very specific, very intentional. She and her glam team were super on top of it.” Said Rouzan-Clay: “They knew going in how much time she had between each look, and they worked it out.”

Added Collins “And there was a lot of effort to construct the show so that she could go from the long hair to the short. If you go back and watch, it was exactly 19 minutes to get from one to the other, and the show was constructed.”

Trae Patton/NBC

The decision to place the more emotional elements of this year’s Emmys — including the honor for Michael J. Fox, the Parton tribute and the In Memoriam — was purposeful, the producers said.

“I think the science behind opening with guys with TVs on their heads — you’ve got to wait a little bit before you get to the emotion,” Collins said.

“There was so much levity about the show, but we did want to pay respects to those moments,” Harmon said.

Added Rouzan-Clay: “I think even in delivering the emotional pieces, it was nice that there was some levity. Even in Macaulay and in Dan’s speeches for Catherine, it was emotion-filled, but there were moments that really spoke to the people that they knew. I think we got lucky with Reba, with the In Memoriam. … all of these moments, really genuinely connected, and they came together organically.”

The producers continue to offer nominees a chance to share their thank-yous to run at the bottom of the screen as they give their acceptance speech. Some take advantage of the offer, others don’t.

“We’ve done it multiple years,” Harmon said. “Not everybody turns in their list, but if they do, we put it up. It’s just a personal choice. Some people don’t want to forget. It’s not about time. It’s about not forgetting.”

Trae Patton/NBC

The one bleep of the night came from John Mulaney’s joke about DJ Khaled — and his famous proclamation that ‘real men don’t go down on their wives.’

“John’s gonna do John!” Rouzan-Clay said.

Neal noted that it was a standards and practices issue: “When you’re broadcasting to the audience at home and you want a family-friendly environment … there are just different S & P rules. Rules are the rules!”

Mulaney rehearsed his segment and the producers knew most of what he would say — but clearly not the DJ Khaled gag.

The show was actually running four to five minutes ahead of time for much of the evening — allowing the producers not to rush things.

“It gave Mariska some time to have some fun too, and breathe with some of those moments,” said Rouzan-Clay. “And we didn’t have to rush people off the stage.”

Trae Patton/NBC

At the end of the night, they also knew they could ask presenters Woody Harrelson and Matthew McConaughey to stretch things out. (Although an originally planned idea to have the duo take a DNA test seems to have been nixed, as it was listed in early rundowns but didn’t actually happen.)

“You book Woody and Matthew,” Collins said of the backup plan if the show went short. “And you just don’t know what they’re going to do.”

The producers were braced for the variety series category potentially having multiple winners — which they didn’t have to ultimately worry about, as only “The Late Show With Stephen Colbert” ultimately won.

“We were ready for a lot of different options,” Harmon said. “We were going to be good either way.”

Trae Patton/NBC

The producers and Neal gave high marks to Hargitay’s performance.

“She was a dream for a host,” Neal said. “She is a triple threat. She has so much range of all the things she can do. And I was glad that she had the opportunity to showcase that to audiences and see her in a different way that’s very different from playing Olivia Benson. I look at her year. Her documentary being an Emmy Award winner, her play on Broadway. I think that Mariska was able to show audiences at home just how talented she is. She loves comedy. She wants to be able to sing and dance. These were some of the things that she wanted to do.”

title: ‘Harry Potter’ HBO Series Casts Its Arthur Weasley, Moaning Myrtle, Colin Creevey
summary: Season 2 of HBO’s “Harry Potter” series has cast three key roles. Rafe Spall (“Trying,” “Life of Pi”) has joined the show as Arthur Weasley, with Molly Hewitt-Richards (“Code of Silence,” “Casualty”) as Moaning Myrtle, and Jasper Ambrose (“Bridget Jones: Mad About the Boy,” “The Sheep Detectives”) as Colin Creevey. content:
Season 2 of HBO‘s “Harry Potter” series has cast three key roles.

Rafe Spall (“Trying,” “Life of Pi”) has joined the show as Arthur Weasley, with Molly Hewitt-Richards (“Code of Silence,” “Casualty”) as Moaning Myrtle, and Jasper Ambrose (“Bridget Jones: Mad About the Boy,” “The Sheep Detectives”) as Colin Creevey. As previously announced, Season 2 will be based on the book “Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets.”

Spall is repped by B-Side and UTA. Hewitt-Richards is repped by Curtis Brown Group. Ambrose is repped by Sylvia Young Agency.

Popular on Variety

Fans of the franchise will recall that Arthur is the patriarch of the Weasley family, which includes Harry’s best friend Ron. Moaning Myrtle is a ghost and former Hogwarts student who haunts one of the girls’ bathrooms at the school. Creevey is a first-year Hogwarts student who is a big fan of photography and of Harry.

Arthur was played by Mark Williams in the film franchise, while Myrtle was played by Shirley Henderson. Creevey was played by Hugh Mitchell.

These are the latest new additions to Season 2 of “Harry Potter.” Others include Kit Harington as Gilderoy Lockhart as well as Bonnie Hill as Ginny Weasley, Lenny Rush as Dobby, and Billy Barratt as Tom Riddle.

“Harry Potter” will debut on HBO and HBO Max on Dec. 25. The series stars:

Dominic McLaughlin as Harry Potter, Arabella Stanton as Hermione Granger, Alastair Stout as Ron Weasley, John Lithgow as Albus Dumbledore, Janet McTeer as Minerva McGonagall, Paapa Essiedu as Severus Snape, Nick Frost as Rubeus Hagrid, Rory Wilmot as Neville Longbottom, Lox Pratt as Draco Malfoy, Leo Earley as Seamus Finnigan, Elijah Oshin as Dean Thomas, Tristan Harland as Fred Weasley, Gabriel Harland as George Weasley, Ruari Spooner as Percy Weasley, Alessia Leoni as Parvati Patil, Sienna Moosah as Lavender Brown, Finn Stephens as Vincent Crabbe, William Nash as Gregory Goyle, Warwick Davis as Filius Flitwick, Sirine Saba as Pomona Sprout, Daniel Rigby as Vernon Dursley, Bel Powley as Petunia Dursley, Paul Whitehouse as Argus Filch, Johnny Flynn as Lucius Malfoy, Bertie Carvel as Cornelius Fudge, Luke Thallon as Quirinus Quirrell, Katherine Parkinson as Molly Weasley, Amos Kitson as Dudley Dursley, Gracie Cochrane as Ginny Weasley, Richard Durden as Cuthbert Binns, Louise Brealey as Rolanda Hooch, Bríd Brennan as Poppy Pomfrey, Leigh Gill as Griphook, and Anton Lesser as Garrick Ollivander.

Season 1 is written and executive produced by Francesca Gardiner. Mark Mylod will executive produce and direct multiple episodes of the series for HBO in association with Brontë Film and TV and Warner Bros. Television. The series is executive produced by author J.K. Rowling, Neil Blair, and Ruth Kenley-Letts of Brontë Film and TV, and David Heyman of Heyday Films.

title: Israeli Filmmakers Among 1,500 Names to Sign Petition Defending ‘NAZA’ Directors After Their Citizenship Is Threatened Over Gaza Doc
summary: Prominent Israeli filmmakers are among 1,500 industry names that signed a petition launched on Monday expressing solidarity with “NAZA” directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, who have faced backlash from authorities at home after the hot-button documentary premiered at Venice Film Festival last week. “In recent days, we have witnessed an unprecedented campaign of incitement […]
content:
Prominent Israeli filmmakers are among 1,500 industry names that signed a petition launched on Monday expressing solidarity with “NAZA” directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, who have faced backlash from authorities at home after the hot-button documentary premiered at Venice Film Festival last week.

“In recent days, we have witnessed an unprecedented campaign of incitement and instigation against the film’s creators,” the petition says, which is signed by Israeli filmmakers including Ari Folman, Nadav Lapid, Orna Ben-Dor Niv, Hagai Levi and Shlomi Elkabetz. “And the distance between it and the incitement to violence and physical threat to their lives is shrinking.”

It adds: “We, filmmakers, call on all who are still fighting for freedom of expression and creation to join in expressing support and solidarity with Rachel Szor and Yuval Abraham. The central role of art and journalism is to hold a mirror up to the society in which they exist, to create discourse and discussion without assumptions, even when the reality is difficult.”

Popular on Variety

Details of the petition, which first surfaced in Israeli media reports, were confirmed to Variety by the international publicist for “NAZA.”

“NAZA” shows “in detail the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza,” according to its official synopsis. The doc, which was shot in secrecy at night on the rooftops of Tel Aviv, features revelatory interviews with 24 Israeli military intelligence officers and soldiers.

The allegations in the film, which include the use of artificial intelligence to identify potential Hamas targets and bomb their homes in Gaza knowing that entire families are inside, have been denied by an Israeli military official, who recently spoke to the Associated Press on condition of anonymity pending a formal statement from the army.

After “NAZA’s” Venice premiere, where it won the special jury prize and earned a record-breaking 24.5-minute ovation, Israel’s culture minister Miki Zohar threatened to revoke the citizenships of its co-directors, who are both Israeli. On Monday, Israeli Defense Forces Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir reportedly instructed the military’s top legal official to examine legal action against the film claiming it “defamed the military.”

Though Variety was not immediately able to confirm that the “NAZA” directors have returned to Israel, they said in an interview at Venice that they intended to do so, regardless of the difficulties they may face.

“We live there. Our lives are there, our families are there, our friends are there,” Abraham said, adding: “There is a political solution and good life for Palestinians and Israelis. That’s what motivates us to make this film and what we hope to be able to continue to do.”

When a series of brutal deaths expose a hidden bloodline curse tied to the full moon, two estranged brothers are forced to confront their past—and their father—before the violence consumes them all.” Below is a first look image from the movie.

Pic was written by The Michaels (Michael Mitton & Micheal Bafaro) and co-written by Jay Stamatis and Edmond Giovanni Coisson. Micheal Bafaro directed.



Executive producers include Evan Tylor, Caterina Scrivano, and James C. Clayton of IndustryWorks Studios, along with Keli Price of Price Productions. EP Price negotiated the deals for Nolte and Gibson with CAA and IAG on behalf of the production.
