title: HBO’s ‘Harry Potter’ Series Casts Arthur Weasley, Moaning Myrtle & Colin Creevey
summary: Hogwarts has three new additions. HBO’s Harry Potter TV series has cast Rafe Spall as Arthur Weasley, Molly Hewitt-Richards as Moaning Myrtle, and Jasper Ambrose as Colin Creevey. The trio of actors will join the cast for Season 2, with filming currently underway at Warner Bros. Studios Leavesden in the UK. Spall will take up […]
content:
Hogwarts has three new additions.

HBO‘s Harry Potter TV series has cast Rafe Spall as Arthur Weasley, Molly Hewitt-Richards as Moaning Myrtle, and Jasper Ambrose as Colin Creevey.

The trio of actors will join the cast for Season 2, with filming currently underway at Warner Bros. Studios Leavesden in the UK.

Spall will take up the recurring role played by Mark Williams in the Harry Potter films. A pure-blood wizard in the employ of the Ministry of Magic, Weasley is a father of seven children, including Harry Potter’s best friend Ron.

Spall’s credits include Sky’s hit series Under Salt Marsh and Apple TV comedy Trying. Repped by B-Side and UTA, he follows in the footsteps of his father, Timothy Spall, in joining J.K. Rowling’s wizarding universe. Timothy played Peter Pettigrew (Wormtail).

Watch on Deadline

Hewitt-Richards, who has appeared in BritBox series Code of Silence and BBC drama Casualty, will play the ghost who haunts the second-floor girls’ bathroom at Hogwarts. Shirley Henderson portrayed Myrtle in the movies. Hewitt-Richards is repped by Curtis Brown Group.

Finally, Ambrose (The Sheep Detectives) will play Creevey after Deadline reported that HBO was casting for the role. Creevey first appears in Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets and is frequently seen around the grounds of Hogwarts with a camera, fanboying over Potter himself.

Hugh Mitchell played Muggle-born Gryffindor wizard Creevey in the 2002 film Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, but the character did not return for the rest of the movie series. Ambrose is represented by Sylvia Young Agency.

They join other new additions for Season 2: Kit Harington as Gilderoy Lockhart, Bonnie Hill as Ginny Weasley, Lenny Rush as Dobby, and Billy Barratt as Tom Riddle.

Recurring cast members include Dominic McLaughlin as Harry Potter, Arabella Stanton as Hermione Granger, Alastair Stout as Ron Weasley, John Lithgow as Albus Dumbledore, Janet McTeer as Minerva McGonagall, Paapa Essiedu as Severus Snape, and Nick Frost as Rubeus Hagrid.

The Harry Potter series is written and executive produced by Francesca Gardiner. Mark Mylod will executive produce and direct multiple episodes of the series for HBO in association with Brontë Film and TV and Warner Bros. Television. The series is executive produced by Rowling, Neil Blair, and Ruth Kenley-Letts of Brontë Film and TV, and David Heyman of Heyday Films.

title: Emmys Producers Dish On Taylor Swift ‘SVU’ Sketch (Including The Easter Eggs), Mariska Hargitay’s Hosting Chops, Dolly Parton Tribute & More
summary: That Taylor Swift cameo at the Emmys was actually filmed on the Law & Order: SVU set, by the way. After Monday night’s telecast of the 78th annual Emmy awards, producers Jesse Collins, Dionne Harmon and Jeannae Rouzan-Clay joined NBCUniversal’s EVP of Live Events & Specials Jen Neal to break down the biggest moments from […]
content:
That Taylor Swift cameo at the Emmys was actually filmed on the Law & Order: SVU set, by the way.

After Monday night’s telecast of the 78th annual Emmy awards, producers Jesse Collins, Dionne Harmon and Jeannae Rouzan-Clay joined NBCUniversal’s EVP of Live Events & Specials Jen Neal to break down the biggest moments from the show, including Swift’s surprise, if pre-recorded, appearance.

The network went into the night making a splash by hiring Hargitay as the first woman to host the ceremony in 15 years. Naturally, she called upon several of her very equally famous friends for the occasion, spoofed her own show, and even sang.

Here, the producers explain what worked in their favor during a show that saw several broken records, including for Widow’s Bay (which won a historic number of trophies for a comedy series in a single year) and welcomed many of Hargitay’s personal friends to the Emmys TV stage.

Watch on Deadline

The SVU sketch. Obviously, Hargitay hosting TV’s biggest night on her home network meant the broadcast was bound to include a Law & Order: SVU nod. Audiences were treated to much more than that when the eventual sketch included one of the most famous people on the planet. That’s right, the SVU sketch largely centered around why Taylor Swift would not attend the Emmys.

“Everyone who tuned in thought, ‘What will be the SVU thing? If you’re gonna do it, I think everyone in this room, we all felt like you have to one up what everyone’s thinking, and I can’t think of anything better than to throw Taylor in an SVU sketch,” Rouzan-Clay said. “No one saw that coming, and if you’re going to have a nod to SVU, that seemed like the coolest way to do it. And they solved the crime, just like they always do.”

While the pop singer was nominated in several categories last weekend for her Eras Tour: The Final Show, it’s quite clear that Hargitay called in a favor by having Swift appear in a pre-recorded sketch with her during the primetime broadcast. Swift was actually supporting husband Travis Kelce at the Kansas City Chiefs season opener against the Denver Broncos on Monday night.

“I think it was always in the first meeting, we wanted to come up with something for Taylor to do, and Mariska’s writing team was just brilliant, and they came up with a couple of ideas, and that was an idea that Taylor responded to,” Collins said.

He says the scene was actually shot on the SVU set in New York City in late August, and it was Swift’s idea to bring her cat (named after Hargitay’s character Olivia Benson): “Last minute, Taylor’s idea, like the night before, she’s like, ‘What if I put the cat in the scene? That would be awesome, right?’ And so we did it. And the cat delivered, and so it was just great.”

As for how they kept it a secret for nearly a month? They kept the circle of trust small, Collins said.

“We made a promise to Taylor that we would keep it under wraps,” he said, adding: “You make a promise to Captain Benson [or her friends], you gotta keep it.”

Swift’s one request. In return for appearing in the Emmys SVU sketch, Swift apparently had one single request. Those Easter Eggs? They’re real.

“She had some thoughts, and we worked that in,” Collins revealed. When pressed for more, Rouzan-Clay cryptically said: “The Easter Eggs, she wanted them to be really official.”

They are surely referring to when Swift turned to the camera and said: “Saccharide, Ares, from the vineyard, north or south.”

“The Swifties will solve the Easter Eggs,” laughed Harmon.

Mariska Hargitay gets an A+. Despite some mixed reviews on the show overall, it’s hard to deny Hargitay’s ability to draw star power to the Emmys stage. It’s a stage you might think needs little help attracting stars, and yet there’s nearly no other circumstance where someone like Swift or Knicks point guard Jalen Brunson might’ve participated in the spectacle.

“That was the beauty of Mariska hosting was just everybody wanted to come play with her,” Collins said. “She was able to work with the team to come up with ideas that would make people comfortable after they said yes.”

Neal added that she not only attracts a broad TV audience, but she also has an expansive celebrity network to draw upon.

“Mariska’s had such a great year and has so many connections with Jalen and Taylor and all the people in Hollywood, with that happening in pop culture this year. So it was really just a dream for us to work with her to appeal to this broad audience,” she said. “She really has something for everyone and is broadly, broadly beloved. So we’re really thrilled to work with her.”

She kind of did steal her writer’s room from Stephen Colbert. The late-night host joked during the show that he was loaning his writers to the actress and host for the night, and he honestly wasn’t far off. Ariel Dumas was hired as the head writer for this year’s Emmy writers room, and she also served as the head writer for Late Night with Stephen Colbert. And, to be fair, they won an Emmy, too.

“We did a fairly large search looking for the perfect head writer for Mariska, and Ariel just was it,” Collins said. “She put together a great team, all New York writers who were willing to just work at SVU, which we’re all fans.

You didn’t hallucinate the hair transformation. “There was a lot of effort to construct the show so that she could go from the long to the short [hair],” Collins said. “Yes, you can go back and watch. It was exactly like 19 minutes to get from one to the other.”

Of the host’s glam for the night, Harmon continued: “Listen, there was an entire document. Yes, there was a document that had the outfits, that had the corresponding hair looks for each one. It was very specific, very intentional. Her and her glam team were super on top of it.”

They thought about SVU: The Musical. While the prevailing SVU sketch during Monday night’s Emmy awards was not a musical number, the producers did think about it. And, regardless, Hargitay still showed off her vocal chops.

“I mean, she really, really worked hard on that song,” Collins said. “A lot of vocal sessions recorded in New York. She [also] some more work on it in LA, like really perfecting it. I mean, this is one of the hardest working hosts I’ve ever seen on any of the show.”

To illustrate that point, he continued: “We shot that opening piece… we shot one scene in New York and two full days in L.A. One on Thursday after the press conference. We came here. She started shooting at around two in the afternoon, and we left the plaza at 12:30 [in the morning]…the work that she put in was unparalleled.”

Is she rehired? TBD on whether Hargitay gets the gig again. Unlike the Oscars, the Emmys change TV networks on an annual basis. No host network has been announced for 2027, but NBCU is clearly happy to have Hargitay sign on again next time the network is up to host.

“She can do what she wants to do,” Neal said. “She’s so wildly talented, and we were just thrilled with how she was tonight, and through the process leading up to, and who she is for the NBC family.”

Honoring Dolly Parton. The late, great cultural icon received her own tribute at Monday night’s ceremony, with Sally Field and Reba McEntire remembering their old friend. Collins says McEntire chose the song she would perform, and she was gifted with one of Parton’s rings to wear for the occasion.

“We were fortunate enough for Reba to agree,” he said. “She’s shooting her show right now, but she made time to shoot it, and she’s like, ‘This is a song that she would like to sing.’ It’s a beautiful story behind that record.”

The in memoriam. The producers said that Noah Kahan was an early choice for the in memoriam tribute, which saw him perform Paul Simon’s “Bridge Over Troubled Water.”

“We worked with him in July on another show,” Neal said, referring to NBC and Macy’s Fourth of July special. “He was incredible, and he was really, really great. We only got to have him on a pre-tape for that show, and so we thought he was the perfect voice for this, and he really delivered.”

Before they booked Kahan, they’d already settled on Simon’s record for the moment. Collins added: “When we were thinking that record, and we went and listened to his album, we’re like, ‘Oh, he’s gonna make this his own.’ He already was a big fan of that song, and it doesn’t hurt that he’s selling out stadiums. He’s had a big year.”

On ending a minute early. This year’s ceremony caught some early slack for cutting a few categories from the primetime broadcast and instead relegating them to the non-televised ceremonies over Labor Day weekend. But, it looks like it largely worked out in NBC’s favor. If you can believe, the Emmys ended a minute early this year — and at one point, they actually had to fill time, because the show was running nearly six minutes ahead. So what do you do when you have the rare luxury (and maybe pain??) of trying to fill time during an awards show?

“You book Woody [Harrelson] and Matthew [McConaughey], right?” says Collins of the last presenters of the night, who did seemingly get to riff more than they might’ve under other circumstances. “And you just know that they’re gonna do what they do.”

Added Harmon: “It gave Mariska some time to have some fun too and breathe with some of those moments, and we didn’t have to rush people off the stage. It was really nice.”

And yeah, they did also beg honorees to keep their speeches to a minimum. From Collins: “Well, we went out to every nominee saying that we have 45 seconds, and there’ll be a clock right away. People respected it. It still drifted a little bit, but we knew we were doing good on time, and I think the room just had a great energy. At least that’s what it felt like from where we were, and so I think it just all came together.”

Things to change for next time? “I think we should have given Mariska more dancers,” Collins laughed.

title: The Coven Boards French Legalized Cannibalism Horror ‘Sunnyside’ As Filming Begins
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Terrifier 3 sales outfit The Coven has boarded French- language horror picture Sunnyside as principal photograph begins in the Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes region of France. The debut feature of Yoann Luis, Sunnyside is set in a dystopian world where humans are raised for food. “Sunnyside is part of the tradition of socially conscious genre cinema, where […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Terrifier 3 sales outfit The Coven has boarded French- language horror picture Sunnyside as principal photograph begins in the Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes region of France.

The debut feature of Yoann Luis, Sunnyside is set in a dystopian world where humans are raised for food.

“Sunnyside is part of the tradition of socially conscious genre cinema, where we examine power dynamics in society as humans become a resource,” said Luis.

“The legalization of cannibalism becomes a provocative metaphor for our relationships of domination, the commodification of bodies, and social and territorial divides.”

The feature film builds on Luis’ previous short film 100% Organic in which animals and human beings swap places.

Watch on Deadline

Sunnyside costars Lucille Guillaume (Mads) and Rod Paradot, César winner for Most Promising Male Actor in Standing Tall and Molière winner for Best New Actor in the original stage production in Paris of Florian Zeller’s The Son

Alongside the Coven, French genre maestro Xavier Gens has also boarded the feature as an associate producer.

Gens recently directed the Netflix megahit Under Paris and series Lupin, with his filmography also including Hitman for 20th Century Fox in 2007, which grossed over $100M worldwide.

Paris-based ESC Films is on board to distribute theatrically in France, having previously released Red Rooms, When Evil Lurks, Terrifier 2 & 3, The Ugly Stepsister and The Sadness.

Sunnyside is produced by Luis and Axel Zeiliger of Block 8 Production, and Florent Steiner and Guillaume Natas on behalf of EV.L Prod, as well as Executive Producers Priscilla Ross Smith and Kendall Anlian of The Coven.

The Coven will also handle worldwide sales, after making a splash in the horror world as sales and EP on cult hit Terrifier 3, which grossed over $100M worldwide and spawned viral IP expansion.

The Coven recently launched their first video game for the franchise last November titled Terrifier: The ArtCade Game on Xbox, Nintendo Switch, PS5 and Steam, from Selecta Play.

“The Coven is originally a French company, and we have been looking for the perfect opportunity to invest and partner here,” said Smith, who has lived in Lyon for more than seven years. “Sunnyside is the perfect mix of artistic and commercial themes, and the connection with the team was immediate for us.”

Shooting officially began on September 14, 2026.

title: Screamfest To Open With ‘The Night Driver’ Starring Josh Lucas, David Arquette & Alyssa Milano
summary: EXCLUSIVE: The 2026 Screamfest Horror Film Festival will open with Jeremy Weiss’s latest feature, The Night Driver, starring Josh Lucas, David Arquette, and Alyssa Milano. The festival, which runs October 6-15 at the TCL Chinese Theatre, announced its first wave of titles today. The lineup features 8 world premieres, 6 North American premieres, 1 US […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: The 2026 Screamfest Horror Film Festival will open with Jeremy Weiss’s latest feature, The Night Driver, starring Josh Lucas, David Arquette, and Alyssa Milano.

The festival, which runs October 6-15 at the TCL Chinese Theatre, announced its first wave of titles today. The lineup features 8 world premieres, 6 North American premieres, 1 US premiere, and 3 West Coast premieres.

Highlight titles alongside The Night Driver include The Caged by Jeffrey Scott Collins and starring Edmund Kingsley (Capsule), Callen Carter, and Raffi Chapman (Vesper); Grow, by Brian Gottlieb and starring Annet Mehandru (The Americans) and Philip Tabor (Heights); Wounds, by Ron Krauss and starring Jack Kilmer (Palo Alto) and Paris Jackson (Swarm).

Screamfest will also honor veteran cinematographer Peter Deming with a Career Achievement Award. Deming’s acclaimed credits include David Lynch’s Mulholland Drive and Twin Peaks, for which he received an Emmy nomination for the 2018 episode “Part 8”, as well as Evil Dead II, Scream 2, 3, and 4, and Drag Me to Hell.

Watch on Deadline

The Night Driver is Weiss’ directorial debut. The film follows Hurdis Jones (Josh Lucas), a traveling pharmaceutical salesman who is desperate to return home to his wife Cheryl (Alyssa Milano) and family after surviving a run-in with a psychotic killer, only to be stalked relentlessly by him across the country and framed for several murders along the way. The police are on a nationwide manhunt for Hurdis, and it is up to Detective Granger (David Arquette) to prove Hurdis’ innocence.

Scroll down to see the full list of Screamfest titles.

FEATURES:

213 Bones (USA, 2025) – North American Premiere

Directed by Jeffrey Primm

Written by Jeffrey Primm, Dominic Arcelin

Produced by Joyce Schweickert, John Michaels, Tyler Jon Olson

Cast: Colin Egglesfield, Dean Cameron, Scott Peat, Francesca Barker McCormick, Liam Woodrum, Sarah Brooks, Joyce Schweickert

As a series of brutal murders terrorizes a college town in 1993, a masked killer’s identity becomes the center of a high-stakes whodunit where every clue leads deeper into danger.

Abandoned (UK, 2026) – North American Premiere

Directed by Joby Stephens

Written by Joby Stephens, Joe Bird and Andrew Daniel

Produced by Joby Stephens, Joe Bird, Annie James, Michela Testa, Debora Bruno and David Weaver

Cast: Grace Gallagher, Cameron Wight

Chasing a viral video to save their channel and friendship, two urban explorers break into a derelict facility scarred by sinister experiments. Trapped among its secrets, they enter a nightmare where history manifests as evil.

Apocalypse Z: A New World – (Spain, 2026) – US Premiere

Directed by Carles Torrens

Written by Ángel Agudo (based on the novels by Manel Loureiro)

Produced by Núria Valls and Adrián Guerra

Cast: Carlos Alcaide, Julia Martínez, Jose María Yazpik Mónica López, Tamara Casellas, Santiago Vaca and Berta Vázquez

The story takes us to the Canary Islands, which have become Europe’s last refuge following the outbreak of the TSJ virus. When a special mission sets out for the mainland in search of vital supplies, Roberto joins the team with questionable intentions. The dangerous operation turns into a desperate race for survival, and Roberto and his companions find themselves caught between hordes of infected and divided loyalties. Then the timeless question arises: save yourself, or risk everything to preserve what little humanity remains?

The Caged (UK, 2026) – World Premiere

Directed by Jeffrey Scott Collins

Written by Jeffrey Scott Collins

Produced by Joseph C. Grano, Jeffrey Scott Collins, Gaby Whyte Hart, Llewelynn Greef

Cast: Tamzin Merchant, Edmund Kingsley, Raffiella Chapman, Callen Carter, Virge Gilchrist, Barbara Mariposa, Whoopie Van Raam, Oliver Henry Arnold, Mark Moraghan, Ahmad Sakhi, King Kerim

Distributor: Saban Films

Starring Tamzin Merchant and Ed Kingsley, The Caged (inspired by true events) follows a British family that moves into an old cottage in Essex, England in 1988 and is terrorized by a dark presence; after researching the history of their new home, they quickly learn why – the site was once referred to as THE CAGE, a medieval prison where many women were held as witches and put to death – including England’s most notorious witch, Ursula Kemp, who was hanged for witchcraft in 1582.

The Exit State – (US, 2026) World Premiere

Directed by Gabriela Ledesma

Written by Josh George, Gabriela Ledesma, Callie Schuttera

Produced by Callie Schuttera, Gabriela Ledesma

Cast: Callie Schuttera (Weapons), Josh George, Sharon Lawrence, Clayton Farris (Weapons), Johnny Bazaldua, Nikki Dixon, Jeremy D. Howard, Cindy Nguyen, Stakiah Lynn Washington

A group fleeing America’s authoritarian collapse takes refuge in a safe house — and discovers it’s anything but safe

Distributor: Chroma

Grow – (US, 2026) World Premiere

Directed by Brian Gottlieb

Written by Brian Gottlieb and Aimee Scher

Produced by Aimee Scher, Brian Gottlieb & Michael Tipps

Cast: Peter Vack, Annet Mahendru, Janis Dardaris, Phillip Tabor

Blending horror, dark comedy, and surrealism, GROW is a psychosexual nightmare about bodily autonomy and what to expect when he’s expecting.

Insecta (Uruguay, 2026) – World Premiere

Directed by Martin Florio

Written by Martin Florio, Leonel D’Agostino, Andrea Gobera Fajer

Produced by Fernando Gaston / Telemundo Studios

Cast: Mayra Hermosillo, Rocío de la Mañana, Luis Felipe Tovar

A famous horror novelist returns to an isolated farm to say goodbye to her dying father. There, she discovers that the enigmatic young woman taking care of him knows more than she lets on; the monstrous imaginary insect that tormented her in childhood may be more real than she ever thought.

Nervous (South Korea / UK, 2026) – North American Premiere

Directed by Abner Pastoll

Written by Richard Hobley

Produced by Junyoung Jang, Abner Pastoll

Cast: Sarah Bolger, Asung Ko, Sungsoo Yune

After discovering a silent vinyl record in her new home, a woman begins losing the ability to hear her husband’s voice, spiraling into a seductive nightmare beyond her control.

The Night Driver (USA 2026) – World Premiere

Directed by Jeremy Weiss

Written by John Cork

Produced by Andre Relis, Jib Polhemus, Jessica Russo

Cast: Josh Lucas, Alyssa Milano, David Arquette

One night in the middle of the country, traveling salesman Hurdis Matheson drives down a dark stretch of highway when he accidentally hits a long-haired stranger. The stranger survives, but is badly wounded. Hurdis agrees to drive him to the hospital. As they drive, he realizes something is wrong with his passenger. Before he knows it, The Stranger becomes violent and attacks him. A couple of days later in California, Hurdis’ wife, Cheryl Jones, begs her old friend Detective Hank Granger to help find her husband. She hasn’t heard from him in two days, and suspects something happened to him. Granger agrees to help but becomes entangled in a bigger case with the FBI regarding Hurdis Jones. They suspect he is a serial killer on a rampage, leaving a trail of homicide scenes across the country. Meanwhile, Hurdis is running, driving, and speeding to get home. But everywhere he turns, The Stranger stalks him. He can’t seem to lose him. What happens next will lead to a climax that leaves audiences speechless. Reminiscent of films such as High Tension or The Sixth Sense, The Night Driver swerves with twists and turns that deliver shocking surprises that no one can anticipate.

NINE (France, 2026) – West Coast Premiere

Directed by Luis Bujeau, Sabine Crossen, Jeremy Guetta

Written by Puissance 9

Produced by Puissance 9

Cast: Aurelia Poirier, Pierre Azema, Eloise Le Baud, Sabine Crossen

Melanie and her friends return to the family home for one final weekend.

A place steeped in memories and unspoken truths, it soon becomes the reflection of a fractured mind. What begins as a simple reunion turns into a psychological descent, where each of them is forced to confront their own shadows. Within these walls, Melanie’s psyche slowly reveals itself — her fears, her defenses, her shifting identities. Nine is a psychological thriller that plunges into the heart of a mind at war — an intimate and universal experience about the courage to fully exist.

Once Upon A Time In A Horror Movie (USA, 2026) – North American Premiere

Directed by Ashley Cahill

Written by Ashley Cahill

Produced by Pantea Ghaderi

Cast: Neeley Dayan, Mabel Thomas, Shane Graham, Allison Gold, Julia Clarke, Alex Joseph, James DeBello, Casey Anderson, Jonathan Walker Harville.

Hoping for an unforgettable birthday, a group of friends sign up for an immersive horror-movie experience that promises to place them inside their own 1980s slasher film. But as the night unfolds, the lines between fiction and reality disappear, and what begins as a game of make-believe soon becomes a desperate fight for survival, where the only way to stay alive is to make it to the final reel.

Postmortem – (Columbia, 2026) – World Premiere

Directed by Andres Beltran

Written by Andres Beltran

Produced by Jason Cherubini

Cast: Allegra Leguizamo, Julio Cedillo, Tony Revolori, Andres Londono

Stricken with grief, a medical forensic investigator works on a case that makes her believe she can bring her deceased husband back to life, only to unravel a series of events that lead to unforeseen and perilous consequences

Processing Charlie (USA, 2026) – World Premiere

Directed by David Harari

Written by David Harari

Produced by David Harari, Alexis Brown

Cast: Asis Fris, Michael Ursu, Kelly Pantaleoni, Sophie Guillen

An act of kindness quickly becomes a nightmarish fight for survival when a young man, dealing with his fractured marriage, takes in a needy, long-lost cousin. Part pervert, part psychopath, Cousin Cole’s dark secrets slowly bubble to the surface as Charlie realizes too late that no good deed goes unpunished.

Serena (USA, 2026) – West Coast Premiere

Directed by Rob Alicea

Written by Jonathan Benecke and P.T. Hylton

Produced by Jerry Careccio, Rob Alicea, Brodrick Haygood, Jonathan Benecke and P.T. Hylton

Cast: Andi Matichak (Halloween, Halloween Kills, Halloween Ends), Steven Strait (The Expanse), Ashleigh Murray (Riverdale, The Other Black Girl)

Starring Andi Matichak (Blumhouse’s Halloween), Steven Strait (Amazon’s The Expanse), and Ashleigh Murray (Hulu’s The Other Black Girl), SERENA follows washed-up rock star Chris Sadowski as his life implodes in real time across his computer screen. With a baby on the way and eviction closing in, he signs on to beta-test an experimental AI assistant calling itself ‘Serena’. What begins as a quick payday mutates into a psychological chokehold, as every window, alert, and keystroke pushes Chris toward the final question: is Serena saving him… or dismantling him piece by piece?

Slay (USA, 2026) – North American Premiere

Directed by Kyra Gardner

Written by Jimmi Simpson, Kyra Gardner

Produced by Mary Kate Van Den Berg, Jimmi Simpson, Kyra Gardner

Cast: Zoey Luna, Aya Cash, Shawnee Smith, Malina Pauli-Weissman, Sean Giambrone, Beck Nolan, Talia Jackson, Reise Alexander, Ruby McCollister, River Alexander, Isidora Goreshter, Andrew Bowser, Jimmi Simpson

Teen influencer Chloe Cruz has built a life that looks perfect online – a devoted boyfriend, a loyal friend group, and an audience watching her every move since she was little. But beneath the curated image, Chloe struggles to understand who she is, and who everyone else expects her to be. When a friend is murdered, her seemingly perfect world comes into question. Seeking refuge from the press, Chloe and her friends retreat to a secluded, disco-themed cabin, where old tensions and new fears collide. As a masked killer closes in and paranoia takes hold, Chloe must confront the fragile identity she’s built – and the possibility that someone knows exactly how to tear it, and her friends, apart.

Still Ohio (USA, 2026) – West Coast Premiere

Directed by Kaylin Allshouse

Written by Kaylin Allshouse

Produced by Kaylin Allshouse, Elizabeth MacLeod, Devon Tayman

Cast: Fernanda Lopez, Michael Zapesotsky, Sofia Angelopoulos, Jake Melamed

In her feature film debut shot entirely in Ohio, writer/director Kaylin Allshouse explores the troubles of long-distance relationships and the transition into adulthood, all set alongside the vicious nature of an endless time loop. This indie horror follows Ana (Fernanda Lopez), a college student transferring to Tulane to be with her boyfriend, Doug, after the distance proved to be too much. Doug arranges for Ana to carpool down to Louisiana with three of his friends– Henry (Michael Zapesotsky– Off The Grid; Unspoken), Julia (Sofia Angelopoulos), and Johnny (Jake Melamed). En route, Ana discovers that Doug does not know his “friends” nearly as well as he led her to believe. As they make their way through the backroads of Ohio, the four find themselves returning to the same gas station over and over again, despite all efforts to escape. When their journey takes a deadly turn, Ana must finally reckon with what has led her to these circumstances and stand up for herself before she gets trapped in the time loop forever. Through these elements of horror and adolescence, Allshouse crafts a poignant story about self-resilience that will have you returning to it again, and again, and again, and again.

Valley View Motel (USA, 2026) – North American Premiere

Directed by Nick Psinakis

Written by Nick Psinakis & Kevin Ignatius

Produced by Nick Psinakis, Kevin Ignatius & Mick Thyer

Cast: Laura Im, Soulo Smith, Kevin Ignatius, Nick Psinakis, Judy Lee, McKenzie Such, Tom Mesmer, Melissa Collins, Corin Clay.

It’s 1977 in this neon-noir thriller, and after a diamond heist goes seriously awry with multiple slaughters, two small-time crooks attempt to flee the wrath of the hitman put on their tail. Seeking refuge at a motel in the remote foothills of Pennsylvania run by a very peculiar owner and his sister, they have no idea what even grimmer hot mess they have stumbled into and soon must figure out a way to survive the night.

Wounds (USA, 2026) – World Premiere

Directed by Ron Krauss

Written by Ron Krauss

Produced by Ron Krauss, Ira Houston

Cast: Jack Kilmer (Palo Alto, The Nice Guys) Paris Jackson (Swarm)

Caleb, a young SFX makeup artist struggles to create realistic effects until he witnesses a brutal murder. Intrigued by what he saw, he descends into a psychological abyss as he takes on extreme measures to create his masterful effects.

title: Quentin Tarantino to Publish ‘Cliff Booth’ Novel Before Brad Pitt and David Fincher’s Movie Streams on Netflix
summary: Quentin Tarantino is writing a novel version of his “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood” spinoff “Cliff Booth.” It will debut later this year, timed to the release of the forthcoming film starring Brad Pitt, who reprises his Oscar-winning role as a longtime stuntman. Tarantino’s book is titled “The Adventures of Cliff Booth,” which differs […]
content:
Quentin Tarantino is writing a novel version of his “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood” spinoff “Cliff Booth.” It will debut later this year, timed to the release of the forthcoming film starring Brad Pitt, who reprises his Oscar-winning role as a longtime stuntman.

Tarantino’s book is titled “The Adventures of Cliff Booth,” which differs slightly from the sequel movie’s moniker, “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth.” David Fincher is directing the follow-up film for Netflix. Tarantino, who wrote the screenplay, also published a novelization of his 2019 feature “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood.”

Tarantino’s latest novel will be published on Dec. 8 by HarperCollins. That’s after “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” lands in Imax theaters on Nov. 25 and ahead of the movie’s Netflix bow on Dec. 23.

Popular on Variety

“Cliff Booth,” both the novel and movie, take place in Hollywood, 1977 — eight years after the original story. In “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood,” Leonardo DiCaprio and Pitt portray an aging actor and his longtime stunt double who are struggling to find their place in show biz. Paying tribute to the golden age of Hollywood, “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood” was set in the late 1960s against the backdrop of the Manson family murders, with Margot Robbie playing Sharon Tate, the up-and-coming actress married to director Roman Polanski.

Although plot details for the sequel have been kept under wraps, the novel’s logline teases that “the Swinging Sixties are long gone — but Clifford Booth keeps on keeping on…War hero, stuntman, bartender, cinema projectionist…with the occasional “clandestine services” for his friends…”

Sony released “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood,” which was a critical and commercial hit. The movie earned more than $400 million at worldwide box office against a $90 million budget, in addition to 10 Oscar nominations and two wins. Netflix is producing the sequel, which carries a $200 million production budget.

Tarantino decided against directing “Cliff Booth” because he’s long expressed a desire to retire after making 10 movies. He’s made nine already — “Pulp Fiction,” “Inglourious Basterds” and “Reservoir Dogs” among them — and he didn’t want a sequel to be his last.

“I love this script, but I’m still walking down the same ground I’ve already walked,” Tarantino said last year on the “The Church of Tarantino” podcast. “It just kind of unenthused me. This last movie, I’ve got to not know what I’m doing again. I’ve got to be in uncharted territory.”

title: Thailand Film and Tourist Officials on the Rise of Thai Cinema, Global Productions and the Impact of ‘The White Lotus’
summary: Following a spike in popularity for Thailand’s film and TV industry, the country’s filmmakers and tourism officials want to make sure it lasts. Nithee Seeprae, Cod Satrusayang, Raymond Phathanavirangoon and Banjong Pisanthanakun joined Variety at the Toronto International Film Festival to discuss Thailand’s growing presence in the global film industry, both in the original work […]
content:
Following a spike in popularity for Thailand’s film and TV industry, the country’s filmmakers and tourism officials want to make sure it lasts.

Nithee Seeprae, Cod Satrusayang, Raymond Phathanavirangoon and Banjong Pisanthanakun joined Variety at the Toronto International Film Festival to discuss Thailand’s growing presence in the global film industry, both in the original work of Thai filmmakers and the influx of international productions shooting across the country.

Pisanthanakun, whose latest film “Inherit” debuted at TIFF, is one of the filmmakers helping to introduce Thai cinema to audiences around the globe. “It’s one of the best film festivals in the world, and I’m so excited that my film got the chance to premiere [at TIFF],” Pisanthanakun said during the Variety Global Conversation. “It’s a big opportunity for Thai horror.”

Pisanthanakun is considered one of the defining voices of contemporary Thai cinema, with his film “Pee Mak” as the country’s highest-grossing title of all time. Pisanthanakun’s movies, plus films like “How to Make Millions Before Grandma Dies,” have further established the country’s presence in the international film industry. The latter became the first Thai film shortlisted at the Oscars for Best International Film.

Phathanavirangoon, the producer and founder of the SEAFIC Script Lab, says he’s noticed a new energy among Thai filmmakers, pointing to the rise of international productions coming to Thailand, such as “The Creator” and “Jurassic World: Rebirth,” as well as the country’s homegrown films.

“Both sides go hand-in-hand to show people what Thailand actually has to offer, especially in terms of cinema,” Phathanavirangoon said.

The panelists also discussed the impact of “The White Lotus,” which filmed its third season in Thailand. Satrusayang, the head of studio at TSixtySix, worked on the hit HBO series and says creator Mike White was deeply immersed in Thai culture and intended for it to serve as a love letter to the country. The season featured Thai actors and traditional dances, food and locations, all of which helped introduce viewers to different aspects of the country’s culture.

After the island Koh Samui appeared in “The White Lotus,” online interest in the location spiked 88%, and the island’s hotel reservations increased by 44%. This increased visibility has also contributed to the rise of “set-jetting,” with audiences seeking out destinations they’ve seen on screen. The Tourism Authority of Thailand (TAT) launched a new campaign, “Amazing Locations: From Scene to Scenic,” to capitalize on that interest and connect the country’s growing prominence as a filming destination with tourism.

“We try to promote both sides,” Seeprae, the deputy governor of TAT explained. “I hope when audiences see a Thai movie or a movie shooting in Thailand, they will follow the movie to Thailand. And of course, also, the ‘Scene to Scenic’ [campaign] tries to encourage all the producers to shoot in Thailand too.”

International productions continue to travel to Thailand for filming, with more than 383 productions coming to Thailand this year alone, says Seeprae, the deputy governor of TAT. Revenue income has increased by about 5% to 10%, nearing about 6 million Baht last year. The country has also seen a 5% to 10% increase in productions shooting in Thailand over the past year.

Revenue has continued to grow, and the influx of projects has created additional employment opportunities for Thai crews. The booming business and government support are key to the industry’s success, but Phathanavirangoon notes that Thai crews can movie magic no matter how much can afford to spend.

“At every single price point, there’s something there for you to shoot and there’s something there for you,” he said. “There’s a team there that’s ready to support you.”

Thailand has notably been used to portray locations across Asia and has served as a backdrop for projects including “The Creator,” “Jurassic World” and “Star Wars.” With the growing success of Thai films and the country’s increased visibility on screen, filmmakers hope international audiences will continue engaging with Thai stories and culture rather than simply seeing Thailand as a stand-in for other locations.

“The next step in the evolution of that is to make sure that the Thai side of the deal — the creators and the artists in Thailand — carry that forward by making Thai culture and Thai content appealing to an international audience so that the momentum doesn’t stop,” Satrusayang said.

Satrusayang’s company works on international productions filming in Thailand. With the growth of the country’s local film industry, he recently launched a separate company focused on local-language content and empowering young Thai filmmakers. As Pisanthanakun sees it, “continuity” is the key to Thai cinema’s evolution.

“Right now, it’s more and more genres that can travel, but in one year, only a few films can do that,” said Pisanthanakun, who also produces projects from up-and-coming talents. “I need more than that so people can see Thai films and Thai locations more than this.”

Phathanavirangoon concurred: “If we do our job right, the future will be very bright because there are a lot of talents in Thailand, and we want to promote them and help them to show the country in the future.”

title: Netflix’s ‘The Murder of JonBenét Ramsey’ Sets Release Date, First Look at Melissa McCarthy and Clive Owen
summary: The Netflix limited series “The Murder of JonBenét Ramsey” will premiere on Dec. 10, with the streaming platform also releasing a first look photo of Melissa McCarthy and Clive Owen as Patsy and John Bennett Ramsey. The series explores the unsolved murder of JonBenét, who died Christmas night in 1996. Her body was found in […]
content:
The Netflix limited series “The Murder of JonBenét Ramsey” will premiere on Dec. 10, with the streaming platform also releasing a first look photo of Melissa McCarthy and Clive Owen as Patsy and John Bennett Ramsey.

The series explores the unsolved murder of JonBenét, who died Christmas night in 1996. Her body was found in the basement of her family’s house just hours after she was reported missing, sparking public outrage and speculation.

Emily Mitchell stars as the titular role alongside Garrett Hedlund, Alison Pill, Shea Whigham, Owen Teague, Clifton Collins Jr., Angus Caldwell, Jaime Ray Newman, Rory Cochrane and Chris Bauer. The cast also includes Will Patton, Jeremy Bobb, John Billingsley, Josh Stamberg, Margo Martindale and Tzi Ma.

Popular on Variety

Richard LaGravenese serves as showrunner, writer and executive producer, with Anne Sewitsky directing and executive producing. The series was co-written by Harrison Query and Tommy Wallach, who also executive produce alongside McCarthy and Sewitsky. David C. Glasser, Ron Burkle, Bob Yari and David Hutkin executive produce for for 101 Studios.

“The Murder of JonBenét Ramsey” was first reported to be in the works in March 2024 and completed production in January 2025. It was formally greenlit at Paramount+ that same year before moving to Netflix in July.

Netflix previously released “Cold Case: Who Killed JonBenét Ramsey” in 2024, timed near the 28th anniversary of Ramsey’s murder. It ultimately became the most-watched series on the streaming platform during the week of Nov. 25, totaling 13.4 million views in those seven days.

See the first look photo of McCarthy and Owen below.

title: Israel’s Oscar Entry ‘Tell Me Everything’ Finds International Distribution as Paradise City Sales Unveils Trailer (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Moshe Rosenthal’s “Tell Me Everything” continues to build momentum after winning 10 Ophir Awards, including best picture, best director and best screenplay, from a record-breaking 16 nominations. Israel’s submission for the international feature Oscar, the father-son drama has secured a string of international sales, including France (Maverick), as well as Australia and New Zealand (Moving […]
content:
Moshe Rosenthal’s “Tell Me Everything” continues to build momentum after winning 10 Ophir Awards, including best picture, best director and best screenplay, from a record-breaking 16 nominations.

Israel’s submission for the international feature Oscar, the father-son drama has secured a string of international sales, including France (Maverick), as well as Australia and New Zealand (Moving Story) and Indonesia (PT Falcon). HBO CEE has also picked up digital rights across Central and Eastern Europe.

The film premiered in Sundance’s World Cinema Dramatic Competition and has since screened at nearly 30 international festivals.

Popular on Variety

Set against the pop culture boom of the late 1980s and the growing HIV epidemic, “Tell Me Everything” follows 12-year-old Boaz, who discovers a devastating secret about the father he idolizes. The revelation threatens to tear his family apart and leaves a wound that follows him into adulthood as he tries to rebuild the bond with his father.

The film stars newcomer Yair Mazor and Ido Tako (The Vanishing Soldier”). Assi Cohen, one of Israel’s biggest comedy stars, takes on a rare dramatic role as Boaz’s father, while Keren Tzur (“Karaoke”) plays his mother. Mor Dimri and Neta Orbach also star.



“Tell Me Everything” marks Rosenthal’s second feature following “Karaoke,” which premiered at the 2022 Tribeca Film Festival and went on to earn 14 Ophir nominations, including best film and best director. The film has since screened at more than 90 festivals, won a dozen awards and is being developed for remakes in several territories, including North America and Germany.

“Tell Me Everything” is produced by Alona Refua, Maya Fischer, Roi Kurland and Gal Greenspan at Green Productions (“A Letter to David”); Ben Giladi at Liminal Content (“Karaoke”); and Moshe Edery and Leon Edery at United King Films (“Footnote”).

Émilie Georges and Naima Abed of Paradise City, whose credits include “Call Me by Your Name,” “Drift” and “Atropia,” are co-producers. Executive producers are Jonathan Margolis, Isaac Zablocki, Fred Toczek, Sharon Chazin Lieblein and Limor Gott Ronen.

title: Kennedy Center Board Votes To Close Immediately Amid Financial Woes And Renovation Plans
summary: The board of the Kennedy Center voted to immediately close the main part of the arts complex on Tuesday, with officials citing repair needs and financial woes. The vote was for a resolution presented to the board on Tuesday, according to a source familiar with the board’s actions. The resolution outlined the structural needs of […]
content:
The board of the Kennedy Center voted to immediately close the main part of the arts complex on Tuesday, with officials citing repair needs and financial woes.

The vote was for a resolution presented to the board on Tuesday, according to a source familiar with the board’s actions. The resolution outlined the structural needs of the center and a recent incident in which a piece of the ceiling collapsed amid heavy rains.

Donald Trump, who serves as the board’s chairman, initially announced the closure plan in February. The board is dominated by members appointed by the president.

He posted on Truth Social on Tuesday, “The Board of The Kennedy Center today agreed, almost unanimously, to close the Building for Safety reasons, and so that it can begin the process of Reconstruction.”

Watch on Deadline

He wrote that he had raised $17 million for the Kennedy Center account to “keep it afloat.”

Major programming at the center largely ended in July, as the board had previously set that as the timeline to shutter the facility for two years for renovations, funding by a congressional appropriation of more than $250 million.

But Rep. Joyce Beatty (D-OH), an ex officio member of the board, challenged the closure plan, and a federal judge last spring ruled that the center’s board had to more fulling consider the impact of such an action before shuttering. In August, the board voted in favor of a plan to shut down the main complex but keep open The Reach, an extension that opened in 2019, for limited performances.

Earlier on Tuesday, the judge, Christopher Cooper, nixed a plan to return Trump’s name to the front facade of the complex, after earlier ordering it to be taken down. Cooper ruled that only Congress could approve the installation of a recognition for Trump in the front of the building or of a Donald J. Trump Plaza. He cited laws designating the center as a memorial to John F. Kennedy.

The center’s attorneys have argued that giving Trump such recognition is essential to raising money to bring the institution out of financial straits. They are appealing the judge’s initial decision.

In his Truth Social post on Tuesday, Trump wrote that the renovation and resconstruction “cannot begin until such time as the D.C. Circuit rules on the Board’s approved name. If the ruling is a negative one, which it should not be, and is not overturned by the U.S. Supreme Court, the Reconstruction and the Renovation of The Kennedy Center will not take place. The attorneys from the DOJ will ask for an expedited appeal.”

title: Robert De Niro In Talks To Play Dodgers Hall Of Famer Tommy Lasorda In Skydance Sports Pic ‘Tommy & Me’; Reid Carolin Directing
summary: EXCLUSIVE: With Mr. Irrelevant already gaining buzz prior to its holiday opening, Skydance Sports is looking to hit another home run with its next big pic on one of the more iconic baseball figures in the last 50 years. Sources tell Deadline, Oscar winner Robert De Niro is in talks to play Tommy Lasorda, the […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: With Mr. Irrelevant already gaining buzz prior to its holiday opening, Skydance Sports is looking to hit another home run with its next big pic on one of the more iconic baseball figures in the last 50 years. Sources tell Deadline, Oscar winner Robert De Niro is in talks to play Tommy Lasorda, the legendary Dodgers manager, in a new sports pic going by the working title Tommy & Me with Reid Carolin directing for Skydance Sports.

There are no details yet as to the approach the film will take in chronicling Lasorda’s story.

Script is by George Gallo, Cambron Clark and Carolin. Skydance Sports is serving as lead studio, with Jesse Sisgold, Jason T. Reed, Sandino Moya-Smith producing for the company, alongside Mandalay Pictures’ Peter Gube, Intuition Productions’ Keri Selig and Diane Galardi, and Reid and Garret Livetz for Free Association.

An iconic ambassador for the Dodgers organization, Lasorda began his career as a player for the Philadelphia Phillies, embarking on a brief stint in the U.S. Army and going back to the minor league before making his way to the Brooklyn Dodgers in 1949. He spent most of his brief playing career in the minor leagues — though he pitched for a time for both the Dodgers and the Kansas City Athletics.

Watch on Deadline

Lasorda’s greater impact on his sport came behind the scenes in the Dodgers organization, where he elevated over time from scout to minor-league manager to the major-league coaching staff. He joined as third-base coach in 1973 — under Hall of Fame manager Walter Alston — became the Dodgers’ manager in 1976, and led the club until 1996, compiling a 1,599-1,439-2 record. During his time as manager, he guided Los Angeles to four National League pennants and two World Series championships.

Lasorda was named National League Manager of the Year in 1983 and 1988, managed four All-Star Games, and was named to the National Baseball Hall of Fame in 1997, with his No. 2 jersey being retired by the Dodgers. After retiring from the Dodgers dugout, he managed the U.S. baseball team at the 2000 Summer Olympics in Sydney, leading the squad to defeat the heavily favored Cuba and win gold. His reputation as one of baseball’s most beloved and recognizable figures only grew with age. A passionate ambassador for both the Dodgers and the city of Los Angeles he died in 2021 at 93.

RELATED: Tommy Lasorda Dies: Los Angeles Dodgers Legend & Baseball Hall Of Famer Was 93

Coming off the Netflix serial killer thriller The Whisper Man, which amassed around 55 million views during its first two weeks on the platform, De Niro will next be seen in Focker-in-Law, the fourth entry in the Fockers film series, out November 25. He is repped by CAA and Grubman Shire Meiselas & Sacks.

The director of the 2022 Channing Tatum starrer Dog and the upcoming Amazon MGM motorcycle racing drama Isle of Man, Carolin is Tatum’s producing partner at Free Association. As a producer, his credits include the Magic Mike films, Logan Lucky and Adam Sandler’s Spaceman, to name a few. He’s also exec produced titles like this year’s Sundance prize-winner Josephine and is repped by CAA, Range Media Partners, and Hansen, Jacobson, Teller.

Gallo is repped by Gang, Tyre, Ramer; Clark by CAA and Untitled.

title: Amazon Prime Video Debuts $30-A-Month Bundle With AMC+, BritBox, MGM+, PBS Masterpiece & Starz
summary: In the latest addition to the bulging category of streaming bundles, Amazon Prime Video is launching a package including AMC+, BritBox, MGM+, PBS Masterpiece and Starz. The $29.99-a-month U.S. offering is priced 39% below the cost of each of the five individual services. In recent years, dozens of combinations of streaming have hit the market, […]
content:
In the latest addition to the bulging category of streaming bundles, Amazon Prime Video is launching a package including AMC+, BritBox, MGM+, PBS Masterpiece and Starz.

The $29.99-a-month U.S. offering is priced 39% below the cost of each of the five individual services.

In recent years, dozens of combinations of streaming have hit the market, creating a crowded marketplace. As streaming pay-TV provider YouTube TV has evolved into the No. 1 distributor, it has sliced and diced its offerings into a range of packages and price points. Rival operators Charter, Comcast and DirecTV have followed suit.

While it continues to support its own original titles, Prime Video is also increasingly looking to serve as a one-stop streaming shop for consumers disoriented by choice. Similar to rival Roku, the Amazon platform offers dozens of streaming services as add-ons for Prime subscribers, including a number of bundled offerings. The consumer proposition, along with creating a centralized hub where they can access streaming, is also to simplify payments. With individual services, a pain point for subscribers comes in with turning services on and off, changing tiers or updating credit cards across multiple providers.

Watch on Deadline

The new bundle is the first Prime Video has offered encompassing five services. That number is not unprecedented in the market overall, however, as Comcast recently expanded its StreamSaver package to encompass six different streamers.

“Our subscriptions and bundles business continues to see incredible growth because we stay focused on delivering unmatched selection, value and convenience,” said Ryan Pirozzi, Head of Prime Video Channels, U.S.

title: Comedians Steve Furey & Willie Simon Set Courtroom Comedy Podcast ‘Petty Cases’ With Almost Friday Media
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Almost Friday Media is bringing the absurdity of classic ’90s courtroom television into the modern digital age with Petty Cases, a new video podcast hosted by stand-ups Willie Simon and Steve Furey that premieres on YouTube and wherever you get your podcasts on Tuesday, September 22. Set to air weekly, Petty Cases‘ premise is […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Almost Friday Media is bringing the absurdity of classic ’90s courtroom television into the modern digital age with Petty Cases, a new video podcast hosted by stand-ups Willie Simon and Steve Furey that premieres on YouTube and wherever you get your podcasts on Tuesday, September 22.

Set to air weekly, Petty Cases‘ premise is simple: put ridiculous arguments on trial and let comedians decide who’s right. In each episode, Willie and Steve preside over absurd, low-stakes disputes that would never make it anywhere near a real courtroom, but are somehow important enough to ruin a friendship, relationship, roommate situation or group chat. And they aren’t doing it alone.

Comics stepping into the courtroom alongside the duo include Bert Kreischer, Ron Funches, Morgan Jay, Frankie Quiñones, Craig Conant, Steph Tolev, Caitlin Peluffo, Shapel Lacey, Asif Ali and Fiona Cauley, with additional guests to be announced. Check out a teaser above.

Watch on Deadline

Because Willie and Steve are stand-ups first, every case becomes a comedy set in disguise. They deliver opening statements that function as mini stand-up sets, before getting into the case and arguing their positions through a barrage of jokes, interruptions, accusations and increasingly ridiculous evidence. A guest judge decides the verdict in the end.

Petty Cases is executive produced by Paige Hymson, EVP of Talk Content & Podcasts at Almost Friday Media, and produced by Katie Felber, who also plays the show’s courtroom clerk.

At the center of the series are two comics who are quickly making names for themselves in the Los Angeles comedy scene.

“Willie and Steve are exactly the kind of hosts we wanted for this,” Hymson said. “They’re genuinely funny stand-up comedians, so we’re not trying to manufacture comedy around a format. The format gives them a playground. You get the opening statements, the arguments, the guests, the verdict and basically nonstop punchlines the entire time.”

Furey told us of the inspiration, “Willie and I were huge fans of Judge Judy and always thought it was a hilarious show. We started thinking about what it would look like to take that courtroom format and turn the comedy way up. After a few beers and a lot of deliberation, Petty Cases was born.”

Petty Cases, Simon said, “has a little bit of everything. Part courtroom show, part advice column, part comedy podcast with some stand-up mixed in. The production value is insane, and I’ve never seen anything like it. That’s what makes it so exciting in a saturated field where so many shows are just two people talking.”

Almost Friday Media is a media company producing sketch comedy, branded content, podcasts and social video across a growing portfolio of brands, including Almost Friday TV and Friday Beers. Recently, the company has been expanding into film and television with On Campus: Game of the Week, an unscripted format at Netflix, the film Boys for Life, slated for theatrical release via Paramount Primal, and Last Night Was a Movie, a half-hour comedy series in development at FX.

Simon and Furey are represented by Brillstein Entertainment Partners.

content:

The true-crime limited series will debut globally December 10th, 2026. Along with the date, the streamer released an official first-look photo featuring Melissa McCarthy and Clive Owen as Patsy and John Bennett Ramsey.

The announcement comes two and a half months after Netflix closed a deal to acquire the completed series from David C. Glasser’s 101 Studios, which had been in turnaround since its original platform, Paramount+, opted not to proceed with it late last year.

The Murder Of JonBenét Ramsey is co-written by Harrison Query and Tommy Wallach, directed by Anne Sewitsky and showrun by Richard LaGravenese. It centers on the infamous unsolved Boulder, CO murder case and the devastating personal and public reckoning that followed the death of JonBenét Ramsey, with the story told through multiple perspectives, including the Ramsey family, investigators, and the media.



LaGravenese, Query, Wallach, McCarthy and Sewitsky executive produce with Glasser, Ron Burkle, Bob Yari, David Hutkin for 101 Studios.

title: Taylor Frankie Paul Sets Return to ‘The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives’ Following Chaotic Season 5 and Ongoing Legal Battle
summary: Taylor Frankie Paul is returning to production on “The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives.” Though Hulu declined to comment on Paul’s involvement in Season 6, Variety confirmed the news with multiple sources after it was implied in social media posts from cast member Mikayla Matthews, who announced she was quitting the show on Sept. 14. […]
content:
Taylor Frankie Paul is returning to production on “The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives.”

Though Hulu declined to comment on Paul’s involvement in Season 6, Variety confirmed the news with multiple sources after it was implied in social media posts from cast member Mikayla Matthews, who announced she was quitting the show on Sept. 14.

Outside of her Season 5 confessionals, Paul hasn’t shot new material for the reality show since March, when production was put on pause due to a police investigation into domestic violence allegations she and her ex-boyfriend Dakota Mortensen made against each other. Shortly thereafter, TMZ released video from a separate domestic incident between them, which led ABC to cancel her season of “The Bachelorette.” Paul and Mortensen have made additional allegations against each other in the months since, leading to mutual restraining orders and a battle for custody over their shared son, Ever. (No charges have been filed in the matter.)

Popular on Variety

Season 6 recently entered production without Paul. But on Monday, Matthews shared in an Instagram post saying that she was leaving the show after receiving news that upset her, which she implied was related to Paul. On Tuesday, she made another post all but confirming that her exit was a moral objection to Paul’s return.

Though Matthews didn’t mention Paul by name, she wrote, “The ONLY reason I’m leaving the show is because I was told a certain person was coming back. I told them before agreeing to do 6 that I wasn’t going to film if that certain someone came back. Because it’s UNETHICAL and kids are involved. And I’m being put in an unfair position because of the things I’ve seen and heard that I don’t agree with.”

“Mormon Wives” cast members Mayci Neeley and Layla Taylor may be next to jump ship. Both left comments of support on Matthews’ initial post, and told fans their futures with the show were unclear. “I am finishing this current season that we are filming and then not sure for after that,” Neeley wrote in a TikTok comment after being asked about her status. She then posted a video about material that was cut from the recently released Season 5 with a caption that read, “At the end of the day I don’t care about having ‘aura’ I care about providing for my family and being a good wife/ mother. Period. Going into SLOMW my intention has never been the fame, it has always been $$$ to provide for my fam and to positively impact people by sharing my story. So I’ll take the cut and stay happy & healed.” Responding to a similar fan question about Matthews’ exit, Taylor wrote, “I just love her so much. It’s such an impossible situation for everyone involved, but I am finishing season 6 and then tbd.”

title: How Competitive ‘Pokémon’ Inspired Author Ava Reid’s New Dystopian YA Series ‘Winterveil’
summary: It’s the start of another dark academia season and fantasy author Ava Reid (“A Study in Drowning,” “Innamorata”) is celebrating with the release of her new YA dystopian novel, “Winterveil.” The first book in a planned duology, “Winterveil” is set at Valeran Academy, which boasts the brightest – and precociously criminal – students in the […]
content:
It’s the start of another dark academia season and fantasy author Ava Reid (“A Study in Drowning,” “Innamorata”) is celebrating with the release of her new YA dystopian novel, “Winterveil.”

The first book in a planned duology, “Winterveil” is set at Valeran Academy, which boasts the brightest – and precociously criminal – students in the nation, who are trained to be elite assets in a Cold War that has dragged on for nearly a century. Amid eerie war simulations, cutthroat competitions and foreboding new technology, four students are drawn together for a mysterious mission.

Without getting into spoilers, we can reveal this political tale has one particular inspiration that might come as a surprise: competitive “Pokémon.”

Popular on Variety

“I, like so many of us, grew up playing ‘Pokémon’ as a kid,” Reid tells Variety. “Playing ‘FireRed,’ ‘LeafGreen.’ I have all my Pokemon plushies right behind me on my couch right now. But it was during the pandemic that I think so many of us got very involved in kind of esoteric hobbies, and my hobby that I got really into during COVID was competitive ‘Pokémon,’ specifically.”

And that’s what it sounds like, according to Reid, “’Pokémon’ where you play against you know other players and you have battles.” “And I’m talking specifically about the official competitive format of Pokemon, the one that’s run by the Pokémon Company itself,” Reid says. “There are different fan formats where you can play online, but the official competitive format is called VGC. So I got very, very into VGC, watching a bunch of kind of VGC content creators, playing on the in-game ladder myself.”

Reid’s time spent playing some hard core Pokemon inspired aspects of the competitive nature of the academy within “Winterveil,” a book that publisher HarperCollins has described as “The Secret History” meets “The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes.”

“The thing about ‘Pokémon’ is that it works on so many different levels,” Reid says. “There’s a very low skill floor if you just want to engage in the main games and you beat the Elite Four and you catch all the Pokémon. It’s super fun. Pretty much anyone can do it. That’s the aspect of the game that’s marketed toward literal children, but then there’s also competitive Pokemon. It’s a turn-based strategy game, so like chess, but actually many orders of magnitude more complicated than chess. Wolfe Glick, who’s the most famous competitive ‘Pokémon’ player, he’s kind of like the [chess grandmaster] Magnus Carlsen of competitive ‘Pokémon,’ he said that competitive ‘Pokémon’ is like chess, but sometimes the pieces explode, which I think is a great way to explain it. It’s very chesslike. It’s strategic, it’s tactical, but it’s so much more complicated than that. There’s so many ways to customize your ‘Pokémon.’ There’s a lot of math and mathematical equations and probabilities and percentages. So that is the particular element that inspired aspects of ‘Winterveil,’ is competitive ‘Pokémon,’ specifically.”

When she’s not playing competitive Pokemon, Reid has been hard at work on “Necromantica,” the sequel to her gothic fantasy epic “Innamorata.” After that massive cliffhanger in the first book, which released in March, there’s not much Reid can say yet about the sequel, which debuts next April, except that fan-favorite character Waltrude will certainly return.

“Waltrude will be back,” Reid says. “She’s a POV character in the sequel, and Marozia is now a POV character in the sequel, which I think is obvious because she’s on the cover. But a large part of the story actually revolves around Gamelyn, who is the Master of Blood, who we’ve not seen very much in the first book. I don’t even think he’s had a line of dialogue, but he is a very, very significant character in the sequel and I’m very excited for that. I think his plot line and his chapters are some of the best things that I’ve ever written. Personally, I believe that, so I’m really excited.”

Elsewhere, Reid is collaborating with “Room” writer Emma Donoghue on a film adaptation of Reid’s 2024 novel, “Lady Macbeth,” told from the point of view of the titular character herself.

“We’re still pretty early. We’re still working on the script, but things are definitely moving along,” Reid says. “They’re moving along behind the scenes, as so many of these things do, which is kind of a hurry up and wait situation, similar to publishing.”

Reid isn’t sure what the distribution plans for the film will be, but is not opposed to a streaming launch on the heels of the success of her filmmaker aunt Olivia Newman’s “Remarkably Bright Creatures” on Netflix. The TV movie was nominated for an Emmy at Monday’s awards show and star Sally Field took home the lead actress award in the category.

“I don’t know if we’re even in the stage to be thinking about that,” Reid says. “I would prefer to have a theatrical release, I think, but my aunt’s movie just came out, ‘Remarkably Bright Creatures,’ and that was on Netflix and that has just done extraordinarily well in that format. So it’s definitely something I’m open to.”

title: ‘Salvation’ Review: A Pin-Sharp Portrait of an Aspiring Life Coach in Personal Freefall
summary: Our first impression of Danny Carlton, the callow protagonist of “Salvation,” is that he doesn’t look like a man you’d trust with your life. He’s young, but that’s not the issue. It’s more the palpable air of uncertainty around him, evident in his shallow, darting gaze, his chummy but hesitant speech, his slightly gormless affect; […]
content:
Our first impression of Danny Carlton, the callow protagonist of “Salvation,” is that he doesn’t look like a man you’d trust with your life. He’s young, but that’s not the issue. It’s more the palpable air of uncertainty around him, evident in his shallow, darting gaze, his chummy but hesitant speech, his slightly gormless affect; he seems a nice enough lad, eager and solidly gym-built, but you wouldn’t readily hand him any greater responsibility than mowing your lawn. Appearances, of course, can be deceiving, but the great, growing sadness of Tom Nicoll‘s remarkable character study is that, in this case, they’re not. Danny is going nowhere, and just about everyone but him seems to know it, including his mentor and peers on the cockamamie life-coaching course that he thinks will finally make something of him.

A quietly assured and impressive debut for Scottish writer-director Nicoll, “Salvation” is a timely work, in conversation with much recent discourse about the toxic pressures — social, physical and psychological — placed on GenZ men living heavily online. But the film doesn’t feel opportunistically ripped from the headlines. Danny, played with spiraling panic and desperately contrived machismo by a superb Liam Harkins, is a perceptively drawn, tragically human character rather than a representative construct of his time and age. And while his story says much about modern manosphere dynamics, it’s also heavily informed by more constant concerns of British class, gender and geographical difference.

Popular on Variety

There’s much thematic weight here, but balanced throughout with tension and humor — beginning with the all-too-real absurdism of the training retreat where we first meet Danny, and where self-styled life coach Marshall Allison (Kevin O’Loughlin) is fleecing young men for thousands of pounds with the promise that they’ll follow in his footsteps. There’s much jargon-y talk of unlocking freedom and earning potential, repeated with dead-eyed belief by Marshall’s protégés, some with more persuasive swagger than others. Danny is one of the unpersuasive ones, in part because he seems too honest for all this. “It’s not all about the money,” he argues, when Marshall critiques his salesmanship, only to be swiftly corrected by his teacher: “It kind of is.”

Still, at the end of the weekend, Danny gets his certificate, because everyone does — and he returns home to Greenock, a post-industrial coastal town in the Scottish lowlands, an allegedly qualified life coach. Hey, it beats working in a pub, which is what he’s been doing up until now; all he needs is a bit of capital to set up his home office, build his website and secure some advertising, and once the clients come rolling in, he’ll pay back the loans in no time.

But apart from Scott (Stephen McMillan), an anxious, socially awkward 22-year-old with even less of a handle on the real world than Danny, no one’s really buying what he’s selling. A handful of other male applicants lose interest fast; he quickly drops his lone female client when she reveals more knowledge of e-commerce than he has. It turns out that even in this dubious professional field, some fakers are faker than others: Danny has mantras and breathing exercises, but no smell of success to him. And when the loan sharks come calling, his barely-a-business plan starts crumbling in wince-inducing fashion.

In Harkins’ brilliantly twitchy, discomfiting performance, the terror of failure is written across Danny’s smooth, blokey face; so is the woebegone recognition of said failure in just about everything he does. We can hardly miss anything that Danny feels, fears or notices: Nicoll and DP Alex Grigoras shoot much of “Salvation” in tight, peering closeup, made all the more confrontational by the use of cramped Academy ratio throughout. It’s a formal choice that chimes with the character’s routine reliance on his phone’s front-facing camera to put his best face forward, whether in consultation with clients or attempting to hawk his skills on Instagram and TikTok.

Life offline could yet save Danny — Kathleen McDermott gives a wonderful, hard-bitten performance as his supportive but unsentimental mom Jackie, who wearily recognizes the limits of her influence — but there’s no promise in Nicoll’s relentlessly screw-tightening script that he’ll ever find his way there. There’s always another internet grift for someone looking to save himself fast, and without any gimmicky visual intrusions, the film feels authentically tuned into the aspirational mentality and oppressive reality of contemporary social media. There’s no need for of-the-moment hectoring or scare-mongering in “Salvation,” however; Danny’s arc on its own feels enough of a cautionary tale.

title: DOJ Takes Paramount’s Side Against States in Fight Over $1.9 Billion Bond
summary: The Department of Justice sided with Paramount on Tuesday, arguing that a coalition of 12 states should be forced to post a bond as the price of continuing to block the Warner Bros. merger. Paramount has argued that it stands to lose at least $1.88 billion due to the delay resulting from the states’ antitrust […]
content:
The Department of Justice sided with Paramount on Tuesday, arguing that a coalition of 12 states should be forced to post a bond as the price of continuing to block the Warner Bros. merger.

Paramount has argued that it stands to lose at least $1.88 billion due to the delay resulting from the states’ antitrust lawsuit. The company has asked Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin to require the states to post a bond in that amount, which would compensate the company in the event that it prevails at trial.

The DOJ is not a party to the state litigation, but filed a “statement of interest” in the case on Tuesday. The document argues that the states must post a “proper bond” because they are acting in the role of “private persons” in enforcing federal antitrust law.

Popular on Variety

The DOJ approved the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger in June and issued an unusual and lengthy statement explaining its support for the transaction. The 12-state coalition, led by California, reached the opposite conclusion in July, filing suit to prevent the merger from reducing competition in the theatrical and basic cable markets. A trial is scheduled to begin on March 2.

Paramount voluntarily agreed not to close the deal until after a trial is held back in July. At the time, Martinez-Olguin had issued a 28-day temporary restraining order, but had not imposed an injunction that would block the deal indefinitely.

Rather than fight an injunction motion — and potentially be forced to appeal an adverse ruling — Paramount chose instead to concede the issue and concentrate its trial defense. But the company had a change of heart in August, arguing that the states should be forced to post the bond or, in the alternative, allow the merger to proceed.

In opposing Paramount’s request, the states noted that courts routinely waive the bond requirement when states are suing to enforce public interests. Martinez-Olguin waived the requirement to post a bond when she granted the temporary restraining order.

The states also argued that requiring states to post a bond would gut their enforcement power. They also argued that Paramount had given no reason why the court should rewrite a stipulation that Paramount had voluntarily acceded to less than a month earlier.

“Permitting Paramount to enter the stipulation and then rewrite it almost immediately would allow it to unfairly renege on its commitments,” the states argued. “Paramount has failed to show any change in circumstances that would justify its attempt now to rewrite the terms of the stipulation it submitted to the Court.”

A hearing on the bond request is set for Sept. 24.

Paramount has separately challenged whether the states have authority to enforce federal antitrust law at all. In a filing last week, the company suggested that one of its defenses will be that such authority “is vested in the U.S. Department of Justice.”

title: Viola Davis to Receive San Diego International Film Fest’s Gregory Peck Award for Cinematic Excellence – Film News in Brief

content:
Viola Davis will be this year’s recipient of the Gregory Peck Award for Cinematic Excellence at the San Diego International Film Festival. Davis, an EGOT winner, is being honored for her work as an artist, activist, producer, philanthropist and New York Times bestselling author.

“Viola Davis is one of the most extraordinary artists of our time,” Tonya Mantooth, CEO and artistic director of San Diego International Film Festival, said. “Her performances bring power, vulnerability and truth to every role, while her work beyond the screen has helped create opportunities for others. The Gregory Peck Award celebrates an enduring contribution to cinema, and Viola Davis embodies that legacy. We are honored to celebrate her remarkable artistry and impact.”

The award, presented by Cecilia Peck, kicks off the 25th year of the festival and will be presented at the Night of the Stars Tribute on Oct. 13. The festival has also announced Jesse Eisenberg’s “The Debut” as the opening night film. The San Diego International Film Festival will take place from Oct. 13-18 in San Diego, California. The epic fantasy hits the big screen as part of GKIDS and Fathom Entertainment’s Studio Ghibli Fest 2026. A 4K restoration of the film will be in theaters from Sept. 26-30 in both the original Japanese and English-dubbed versions.
