title: Naomi Watts, Demi Moore, Rachel Zegler and More Were Buzzing at Thom Browne’s Bug-Filled NYFW Show
summary: The Shed was abuzz Wednesday night for Thom Browne’s Spring/Summer 2027 fashion show, which transformed the Hudson Yards arts venue into a lush garden for the finale of New York Fashion Week. Luckily for Browne, his A-list front row — Rachel Zegler, Demi Moore, Adam Scott, Britt Lower, Penn Badgley, Anna Wintour, Naomi Watts and […]
content:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

The Shed was abuzz Wednesday night for Thom Browne‘s Spring/Summer 2027 fashion show, which transformed the Hudson Yards arts venue into a lush garden for the finale of New York Fashion Week.

Luckily for Browne, his A-list front row — Rachel Zegler, Demi Moore, Adam Scott, Britt Lower, Penn Badgley, Anna Wintour, Naomi Watts and Liev Schreiber (the latter two reunited to watch their daughter Kai walk the runway) — are, apparently, big fans of bugs. For his latest offering, the New York designer continued his fascination with creepy-crawlies, sending sequin fly and moth appliqués, butterfly-wing embroidery, jacquard grasshoppers, grass-like tweeds and countless beetles down a circular path surrounding a looming chrysalis.

At the center of the set sat a giant white cocoon, surrounded by dancers dressed as butterflies, from which a black widow eventually emerged in a black silk duchess gown. The show opened to music from “A Bug’s Life,” while the ambient hum of buzzing bees drifted through much of the presentation.

Popular on Variety

Zegler, whose favorite insect is the bee, says the collection was practically made for her. “They’re so smart!” she mused to Variety after the show. “I actually kept bees with my friend Andrew in Ireland. I got stung on the shoulder and it was the best moment ever.”

The “Evita” star even has matching insect tattoos with her best friends: Zegler has a bumblebee inked on her ribcage, while her two friends have a dragonfly and ladybug, respectively.

Rachel Zegler at the Thom Browne fashion show WWD via Getty Images

Janelle Monae at the Thom Browne fashion show WWD via Getty Images

Janelle Monáe, meanwhile, gravitated toward the show’s many butterflies. Among the dancers — outfitted in low-slung skirts and high-neck one-piece swimsuits — were, according to the show notes, the “leopard lacewing, the emerald swallowtail, the Arizona hairstreak, the purple emperor, the scarlet Mormon, the Rajah Brooke’s birdwing, the Rothschild’s birdwing, the Apollo, the Sapho longwing, the painted lady.”

“I’m going through my own metamorphosis,” Monáe says of her affinity for the winged creatures.

Metamorphosis was a fitting theme for Browne himself, whose work has evolved considerably from the appointment-only gray suits he sold out of the West Village at the beginning of his career. He ushered in this brighter, more whimsical chapter in Milan earlier this year, where seersucker flowers, ants, dragonflies, grasshoppers and bee motifs similarly crawled across the collection.

Adam Scott, Britt Lower and Victoria Pedretti at the Thom Browne fashion show WWD via Getty Images

Model on the runway at the Thom Browne fashion show WWD via Getty Images

Browne, of course, hasn’t strayed far from his signature tailoring. Amid beekeeper-style hats and beetle-shaped attachés, structured wool coats, tiered pleated skirts and waist-cinching corsets made their way across the Astroturf runway. And at the Emmys the previous night, Browne dressed one of the ceremony’s biggest winners, Matthew Rhys, in a custom three-piece gray tuxedo — quintessential TB.

But is this especially playful era — even by Browne standards — a final form for the designer? Those who have found the past few years’ red carpets a snooze, should sure hope so. I, for one, would happily welcome a bulbous ladybug or cricket-like exoskeleton at my next premiere.

I look forward to Zegler getting her hands on one of the collection’s bright yellow apian looks. As she tells Variety: “Thom, if you’re out there: All the bumble bee stuff, you know where to find me!”

title: Oscars: France Selects Cannes Prizewinner ‘Minotaur’ for International Feature Race
summary: France has selected Andrey Zvyagintsev’s Cannes Grand Prize winner “Minotaur” to represent the country in the international feature film race at the Oscars. The choice was made Wednesday by France’s Oscar committee following auditions with the producers, international sales agents and U.S. distributors behind the five-shortlisted films, including Mubi, Neon and Sony Pictures Classics. “Minotaur” […]
content:
France has selected Andrey Zvyagintsev’s Cannes Grand Prize winner “Minotaur” to represent the country in the international feature film race at the Oscars.

The choice was made Wednesday by France’s Oscar committee following auditions with the producers, international sales agents and U.S. distributors behind the five-shortlisted films, including Mubi, Neon and Sony Pictures Classics.

“Minotaur” prevailed in a particularly eclectic and wide-open field that also included Antonin Baudry’s two-part historical epic “De Gaulle,” Arthur Harari’s “The Unknown,” Marine Atlan’s “La Gradiva” and Louis Clichy’s animated feature “Iron Boy.”

The selection of “Minotaur” reflects France’s growing role as a production and financing hub for filmmakers from outside the country. Last year, France submitted Iranian filmmaker Jafar Panahi’s “It Was Just an Accident,” which had won the Palme d’Or at Cannes and went on to secure an Oscar nomination. The choice had sparked pushback in parts of the French industry over whether a country should be represented by a foreign-born filmmaker working largely outside the French language.

Popular on Variety

A dissident Russian filmmaker who lives in exile in France, Zvyagintsev made his Russian-language drama with France’s Charles Gillibert‘s CG Cinéma and MK Productions. A portrait of corruption in contemporary Russia, “Minotaur” is represented internationally by MK2 Films, while Mubi has acquired North America and several other territories.

“In what promises to be a highly competitive field, this selection underscores both France’s unique role in major global co-productions and our country’s commitment to supporting the great filmmakers of our time, while maximizing our chances of winning the Oscar for Best International Feature Film,” said Gaetan Bruel, the president of the National Film Board (CNC).

“It all starts now. The CNC and Unifrance, determined to ensure that France shines once again this year at this major international film event, will strongly support not only the French nominee but also all French films nominated in any Oscar category, as part of a renewed strategy. The goal is to win,” he continued.

The country has not won the international feature prize since Régis Wargnier’s “Indochine” took the honor in 1993, despite remaining one of the category’s most consistently represented nations.

This year’s French Oscar committee was presided over by Charles Tesson and included Coralie Fargeat, Emilie Lesclaux, Sophie Mas, Grégory Chambet, Nadim Cheikhrouha, Thierry de Clermont-Tonnerre, Ron Dyens, Nicolas Eschbach, Adeline Monzier and Sylvie Pialat.

The 2027 race also marks the first year under new Academy rules allowing non-English-language films that win the top prize at one of six designated international festivals — Berlin, Busan, Cannes, Sundance, Toronto and Venice — to enter the international feature race without being their country’s official submission.

The Academy is set to unveil its 15-film international feature shortlist on Dec. 15, with nominations announced Jan. 21. The 99th Academy Awards will take place March 14, 2027.

title: Wesley Wang Launches Digital Media Studio Wesley Wang Media, Sets Caellum Allan As Head Of Film & Television & Unveils Initial Slate
summary: EXCLUSIVE: In the spring of 2024, we reported on a buzzy young filmmaker named Wesley Wang — a Harvard student who got a feature take on his short nothing, except everything. set up at TriStar in a competitive situation, with Darren Aronofsky producing. The project isn’t moving forward at Sony, but we can now tell […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: In the spring of 2024, we reported on a buzzy young filmmaker named Wesley Wang — a Harvard student who got a feature take on his short nothing, except everything. set up at TriStar in a competitive situation, with Darren Aronofsky producing. The project isn’t moving forward at Sony, but we can now tell you that Wang is making more big moves.

Wang today announces the launch of Wesley Wang Media, a creator-led entertainment company working in film & TV that will fund original, serializable IP outright and release it across social platforms including YouTube.

Projects on WWM’s slate include Extract 14, an interactive true-crime series that will invite audiences to decode bodycam footage and surveillance logs and digital interfaces, with a $100,000 bounty for the first resolution. Principal photography is slated for December.

Watch on Deadline

Secondly, there’s The Algorithm, a high-concept scripted thriller to be produced by podcaster-creators Colin & Samir, using a digital-first format with 15- to 18-minute episodes.

Other projects in development include a prequel series and feature film based on the Tribeca-winning Violet and Marlowe, Industry Plant, Last to Leave, and Response, a greenlighted horror short to be directed by Jason Rodelo, with a feature version being developed in parallel.

Wang’s right hand at Wesley Wang Media is Caellum Allan, who joins as Head of Film & Television from Sony’s TriStar Pictures. In his new role, he’ll oversee the company’s scripted slate, creative development strategy, and filmmaker partnerships across scripted programming, immersive narrative experiences, and feature-length productions.

At the heart of Wang’s vision for WWM is a model where the public dictates which stories are worth further exploration. As the creator economy booms, the model is designed to run the traditional studio system in reverse: test work publicly first, then invest more deeply in the concepts that resonate. Projects that demonstrate demand online will be scaled into features, series, franchises, brand partnerships, and live experiences, with WWM owning a piece of every breakout it backs.

Wang’s concept for his company stems from personal experiences he speaks to with refreshing candor. The emerging filmmaker wrote and directed nothing, except everything. in his senior year of high school and paid for it by teaching chess lessons and cold-emailing 200 producers off IMDbPro until one of them said yes. A full year of festival submissions went nowhere, and in September 2023, he decided to see what might happen in posting the short to YouTube. It popped online, with over a million views in 10 days and 9.5M+ lifetime, and quickly captured studio interest, with four studios bidding on feature rights. Sony’s TriStar won, Aronofsky’s Protozoa came on to produce, and Wang, then 19 and studying economics at Harvard, was attached to write and direct, making him one of the youngest filmmakers ever to set up a feature at a major studio, alongside Backrooms‘ Kane Parsons.

The year and a half that followed taught Wang much more than the deal itself: He had signed rights to the short away, and with them, the ability to make the film the way he had made all his past work. Notes arrived asking for changes he did not believe in, every revision climbed a chain of approvals, and weeks passed before he heard anything back. He had reached millions of people directly, without anyone’s permission, and then handed over the right to reach them again. In August 2025, he and Sony agreed to part ways, and early this year, with a fire in the belly, Wang left Harvard to build the studio he wished had existed when he was 17.

Seemingly, Aronofsky saw the writing on the wall early on when it came to Wang — the potential he had to break out as one of the hottest young directors of a new digital-native generation. And Wang now hopes to deliver in the vein of Curry Barker with Obsession, who got to his $750,000-budgeted debut off of YouTube shorts, sold it to Focus for around $15M, and captured the biggest worldwide gross in the history of Focus Features. Wang cites Backrooms‘ Parsons, Talk to Me‘s Danny and Michael Philippou, and The Amazing Digital Circus as other big inspirations — creatives and projects that were validated in public before an executive was involved, only for creators to be paid a premium by studios for something they had no hand in creating, or to come in house.

Another project, reflecting Wang’s mission, is a competition series — a new take on Project Greenlight — that will award $100,000 to a digital-native filmmaker to make their dream movie. Anyone can apply: There’s no requirement of a film degree, agent, reel, prior credits, or anything else. WWM will co-own the ultimate project alongside the filmmaker. Applications are now open at this link.

Caellum Allan’s appointment at WWM marks a reunion with Wang, with whom he intersected at TriStar as the champion of his breakout short film nothing, except everything.

“Caellum and I have had a great creative relationship from the beginning,” Wang told Deadline. “He understood what I was trying to do before there was an obvious roadmap for it, and I’ve always trusted his taste, instincts and ability to see the bigger opportunity in a filmmaker’s work. We share an ambition to make projects that are creatively bold, commercially exciting and capable of reaching a real audience. I couldn’t imagine a better partner to help build this slate.”

Allan brings more than a decade of experience developing commercially driven films across the studio and streaming landscape. At TriStar, he worked on a slate that included Labyrinth, with Robert Eggers attached to direct; an adaptation of Paulo Coelho’s The Alchemist; and the studio’s adaptation of Guys and Dolls. Previously, he was a creative executive within Netflix’s Original Film division. His credits also include Thanksgiving, Roald Dahl’s Matilda the Musical, I Wanna Dance with Somebody and The Boys in the Band.

Allan has built a reputation for identifying distinctive international filmmakers and helping introduce them to the American studio system following his involvement with acquiring the first U.S. projects from directors including Michiel Blanchart, Kirill Sokolov and Yeon Sang-ho, who’ve subsequently gone on to direct major English-language productions.

“Everyone wants to find the next great filmmaker; far fewer are prepared to take the first meaningful risk on one,” Allan said. “What drew me to Wesley Wang Media is the belief that the next generation of filmmakers shouldn’t have to wait for permission. They should have the opportunity to make ambitious work, build an audience and let the work create its own momentum.”

Wang is represented by WME and 3 Arts Entertainment.

title: ‘Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo’ Review: Takashi Miike Brings Trouble To Tokyo In A Funny Riff On Abel Ferrara’s Corrupt Cop Drama – Toronto Film Festival
summary: Takashi Miike took to the stage at the world premiere of his new film Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo like a rock star. “I’m Miike” he roared. “I’m back!” Which is immediately funny, because he’s never, ever really been away; arguably the hardest working man in showbusiness, Miike is never very far from a movie camera. Produced […]
content:
Takashi Miike took to the stage at the world premiere of his new film Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo like a rock star. “I’m Miike” he roared. “I’m back!” Which is immediately funny, because he’s never, ever really been away; arguably the hardest working man in showbusiness, Miike is never very far from a movie camera. Produced by the late British producer Jeremy Thomas — who formed a very fruitful alliance with the Japanese auteur, starting with 13 Assassins in 2020 — the latest in the Bad Lieutenant franchise is arguably the lightest of the three. It’s violent for sure, but Miike goes easy on the gore, giving free rein to his expressive, hangdog star to mine the story’s rich, deep seam of jet-black humor.

The first Bad Lieutenant (1992) was definitely an Abel Ferrara joint, the last in a long run of sleazy, gritty New York-centric dramas that he began with 1979’s Driller Killer. Ferrara’s bad cop, played by Harvey Keitel, was anything but fun, an oversight corrected by Werner Herzog in the outrageous Bad Lieutenant: Port of Call New Orleans (2009), featuring Nicolas Cage at his OTT best. Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo sits somewhere in the middle, being somehow the least extreme of the three, which is a turn-up for the books when you consider that Miike made the ultra-violent yakuza movie Ichi the Killer (2001).

Watch on Deadline

Miike has pretty much factored in your awareness of the Bad Lieutenant series and doesn’t spend too much time exploring how this particular lieutenant got to be so bad; he just is. About to be divorced, by a wife who has taken his two kids with her, Lieutenant Yabuki (Shun Oguri) has a dozen rackets running all at once, taking kickbacks from the mob and spending most of the proceeds on drugs, hookers and gambling (the rest he wastes). There’s clearly a slim shred of a conscience, since, in the film’s opening scenes, he shows up, bleary-eyed, to take his kids to school, but Yabuki’s colleagues are wary of him, not least because his last partner came to a very sticky end some 15 years prior.

Yabuki, then, is on the way out, but what keeps him there is his knowledge of the Seiryu-kai, a real-life yakuza gang that dominated the Japanese crime scene until relatively recently. But when a series of tattooed gangsters start turning up dead, tied up BDSM-style with their necks broken, Yabuki is the man to call (“We could use his expertise”). At the same time, Ishizuka (Shotaro Mamiya), a recently freed member of the Seiryu-kai, is out looking for revenge on the people who wronged him, starting with his estranged wife. In classic Miike style, the poor woman is chopped into tiny little bits (off-screen) and her flesh moulded into meatballs, which Ishizuka leaves outside for the crows (a “sky burial”, Yabuki calls it).

Roughly half an hour in, Yabuki meets Gwen (Lily James), an FBI agent on a classified assignment to look for the missing daughter of a high-ranking politician and potential Vice-President of the United States. Gwen has a dark secret, a mission that went badly wrong, and the job is more of a gun to the head than a chance to make good. If she finds the girl, she can wipe the slate clean and “get my life back”; if not, then her career is over. Seeing a kindred spirit beneath the all-American veneer, Yabuki joins forces with her. The pair even have sex (“How does it feel to be f*cked by a scumbag?” asks Yabuki).

The search for the missing girl brings a surprise Basic Instinct-style erotic-thriller element to the usual formula, which seems extraneous at first but later turns out to integral to Yabuki’s downfall (the pre-ordained fate of the bad lieutenant is always baked in and non-negotiable). For all his badness, however, Yabuki is really quite charming, and part of his appeal is not so much that he’s completely amoral with his hedonism, it’s that he no longer cares any more.

Shun Oguri fits the part perfectly, like Columbo on meth, but sadly, the same can’t really be said of Lily James, who doesn’t quite have the girl-boss sass the role requires, even though she does, literally, kick ass in a terrific bar-room brawl. Some of this is down to the sequences in English; Oguri’s accent is sometimes hard to make out, which isn’t helped by the low sound mix and Miike’s tendency in dialogue scenes to show a reverse shot of the person not talking.

The film’s limited resources become a little more obvious towards the end, but Miike wears his low-budget bona fides with pride, and the lo-fi production values only add to the grittiness of its urban setting. In short, this is classic Miike, not at his most shocking but certainly as slick as he’s ever going to get. It’s also a reminder that Miike makes good movies with the same speed that he makes bad ones; in fact, he probably finished the next one while you were reading this and is likely starting on another one right now. Whatever it is, he’ll be back soon enough.

Title: Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo

Festival: Toronto (Special Presentations)

Director: Takashi Miike

Screenwriter: Daisuke Tengan

Cast: Shun Oguri, Lily James, Shotaro Mamiya, Liv Morgan, Jun Kunimura, Hiroshi Tachi

Distributor: Neon

Running time: 1 hr 48 mins

title: Oscars: France Selects ‘Minotaur’ For Best International Feature Film Race
summary: France has selected exiled Russia director Andrey Zvyagintsev’s French-produced political thriller Minotaur as its entry for the Best International Feature Film category of the 99th Academy Awards. The submission was chosen from a shortlist also featuring Antonin Baudry’s historical biopic De Gaulle: Tilting Iron, Louis Clichy’s animated feature Iron Boy, Marine Atlan’s La Gradiva and […]
content:
France has selected exiled Russia director Andrey Zvyagintsev’s French-produced political thriller Minotaur as its entry for the Best International Feature Film category of the 99th Academy Awards.

The submission was chosen from a shortlist also featuring Antonin Baudry’s historical biopic De Gaulle: Tilting Iron, Louis Clichy’s animated feature Iron Boy, Marine Atlan’s La Gradiva and Arthur Harari’s’ The Unknown.

Minotaur world premiered in Cannes where it won the Grand Prix, and has also been selected for It is also Telluride, Toronto, New York and BFI London Film Festival among many other festivals.

The film taps into the mood in Zvyagintsev’s native Russia in 2022 as businessmen in a provincial city get to grips with the implications of their country’s invasion of Ukraine as workers are drafted into the army and they are asked to contribute financially to the war effort.

Watch on Deadline

Dmitriy Mazurov plays successful company director Gleb, whose seemingly perfect life starts to unravel, not due to the conflict but rather his suspicions that his wife (Iris Lebedeva) is having an affair.

It is Zvyagintsev’s first film since Loveless in 2017 which won the Jury Prize in Cannes and went on to be nominated for an Oscar.

It marks the second year running that France has selected a non-French language picture to represent it in the Best International Feature Film category, following the selection of Jafar Panahi’s It Was Just An Accident last year.

French-German-Latvian co-production Minotaur is lead produced by Paris-based CG Cinéma, Mk2 Productions and Latvia’s Forma Pro Films.

Mubi will release the film in U.S. theaters on November 20, 2026.

The selection committee, which was kept under wraps until the announcement of their choice, was presided over by critic and former Cannes Critics’ Week artistic director Charles Tesson.

He was joined by sales agents Grégory Chambet (WTFilms) and Nicolas Eschbach (Indie Sales) as well as producers Nadim Cheikhrouha (The Voice Of Hind Rajab), Thierry de Clermont-Tonnerre (I’m Still Here), Ron Dyens (Flow), Emilie Lesclaux (The Secret Agent), Sophie Mas (Arco), Sylvie Pialat (Timbuktu); The Substance director Coralie Fargeat and New York-based French cinema promotion expert and programmer Adeline Monzier.

title: AMC NASCAR Drama Series ‘Thunder Road’ Rounds Out Cast
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Josh Macqueen (Motorheads), Aspen Kennedy (Queen Sugar), Haley Dillon (Blue Ridge) and Mackenzie Porter (9-1-1: Nashville) round out the cast of AMC’s NASCAR drama series Thunder Road. The series will debut on AMC and AMC+ in 2027. From John Fusco, Thunder Road is the multi-generational saga of the fictional Whitlock family, whose legacy in […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Josh Macqueen (Motorheads), Aspen Kennedy (Queen Sugar), Haley Dillon (Blue Ridge) and Mackenzie Porter (9-1-1: Nashville) round out the cast of AMC‘s NASCAR drama series Thunder Road. The series will debut on AMC and AMC+ in 2027.

From John Fusco, Thunder Road is the multi-generational saga of the fictional Whitlock family, whose legacy in stock car racing is as deep as the family’s ties to the Southern hill country roots that shaped them.

In Thunder Road, Dennis Quaid stars as racing legend Duane Whitlock, aka The Wrecking Ball, a towering figure who built a racing empire from a legacy of moonshine runs and dirt tracks and refuses to let it die. With ruthless competitors who will stop at nothing to dethrone and destroy them, the Whitlocks are a blue-collar dynasty at the edge of extinction – and the old king is fighting to hold onto the crown.

The previously announced series regulars also include Chase Stokes, Michael Rooker, Matt Barr, Maggie Grace and West Duchovny. Michael Rooker and Devon Allman will appear in recurring roles.

Watch on Deadline

Macqueen will guest star as Trey Whitlock, the youngest son of NASCAR legend Duane Whitlock. Trey has prodigious racing skills and a media-ready smile that have made him the most touted up-and-comer in motorsport. With his long-awaited debut in the Cup Series, Trey must shoulder not only the world’s expectations but the full weight of keeping his family’s storied race team afloat.

Kennedy will heavily recur as Bobby “Breeze” Roberts, who is every sponsor’s dream: easygoing, personable, and as dependable off the track as he is on it. His consistent performance has made him an asset to Whitlock Racing Team, but beneath his cool exterior burns an ambition to escape the middle of the pack and start chasing checkered flags.

Dillon will guest star as Dakota Voss, who has a preternatural gift for turning data into wins, and the confidence to match. The youngest Lead Race Engineer in NASCAR, she’s leveraged her aerospace expertise to take Farley Performance from the history books to the technological cutting edge.

Porter will heavily recur as Bonnie Taylor-Whitlock, an aspiring country singer convinced that she belongs onstage, even if it’s just the stage in her husband Calvin’s taproom. She may be a little drunk on her own spotlight, but she’s also savvier than she lets on, helping Calvin scheme his way to entrepreneurial success.

Fusco is set to executive produce alongside showrunner Taylor Elmore, Cliff Roberts with Syndicate Entertainment, Mark L. Smith, and NASCAR Studio’s Tim Clark and John Dahl. Gladys Cheng serves as producer. The show is produced in association with NASCAR.

Macqueen recently appeared in the Amazon/MGM series Motorheads, from showrunner John Norris. He can also be seen playing one of the leads in Netflix’s series Surviving Summer. Macqueen recently wrapped work on the upcoming Netflix series The Sticks and the indie feature U.A.P. He is repped by Anonymous Content, Innovative Artists and GGSSC.

Kennedy landed his first network television role on OWN’s Queen Sugar, which he followed up with a leading film role in Sony Pictures’ The Forge. Kennedy recently recurred on CBS’ hit series Fire Country. Up next, he is set to star in the upcoming western, Florida Wild. Kennedy is represented by CGEM Talent, J. Pervis Talent Agency, Stewart Talent, and Meyer & Downs.

Dillon is an actress known for her role as Dixie in the television series Blue Ridge, starring Johnathon Schaech. Her other credits include the feature film Bad Counselors and an appearance in Luke Combs’ music video for “The Kind of Love We Make.” She is repped by The Anthem Collective.

Porter recurs on Ryan Murphy’s show 9-1-1: Nashville, and prior to that, on Prime Video’s The Runarounds. She also starred as the lead in the hit Netflix series Travelers and had a series regular role in AMC’s Hell on Wheels. She is repped by Link Entertainment and Red Management.

title: ‘The Traitors’ Renewed For Three More Seasons At Peacock After Winning Third Consecutive Emmy
summary: Alan Cumming is set to banish more celebrities after Peacock handed The Traitors a supersized three-season renewal. The mystery entertainment series has been picked up through Season 8 at the NBCUniversal streamer. It comes after the Studio Lambert-produced show won its third consecutive Emmy for Outstanding Reality Competition Program and Cumming won his third consecutive […]
content:
Alan Cumming is set to banish more celebrities after Peacock handed The Traitors a supersized three-season renewal.

The mystery entertainment series has been picked up through Season 8 at the NBCUniversal streamer.

It comes after the Studio Lambert-produced show won its third consecutive Emmy for Outstanding Reality Competition Program and Cumming won his third consecutive Emmy for Outstanding Host for a Reality Or Reality Competition Program. The show itself came home with seven Emmy nominations and wins.

After winning the Emmy on Sunday, Cumming said: “The audience is so amazing. It is so diverse, and it’s just incredible the way you all get together and watch the show together. That is so beautiful, that a show about treachery and betrayal brings people together.”

The move is not a surprise given that the show is Peacock’s second-biggest title after Love Island USA, and its fourth season, which premiered in January, was up 72% over Season 3.

The three-season renewal comes after The Traitors was already renewed for Season 5, which will premiere next year. Before that, NBC will air a civilian version of the show, premiering on September 17.

RELATED: ‘The Traitors: New Blood’ Season 1 Cast Photos: Meet The Civilian Contestants Of NBC Competition

The Traitors is based on Dutch format De Verraders, a game that splits its contestants into two groups: The Faithful and the Traitors. At the beginning of the season, Cumming picks the Traitors that will pit the Faithful against each other by murdering them one by one while trying to remain undercover. The Faithful attempt to uncover the Traitors in a roundtable where they vote each other out and banish them from the game. At the end of the game, if there are Traitors left in the game, they will split the money between them. If there are no Traitors left, the money is divided among the Faithful.

RELATED: 2026 Premiere Dates For New & Returning Series On Broadcast, Streaming & Cable

Season 4, which was shot, as ever, in Scotland, featured Rob Rausch, Maura Higgins, Eric Nam, Tara Lipinski, Johnny Weir, Mark Ballas, Natalie Anderson, Kristen Kish, Stephen Colletti, Dorinda Medley (again), Candiace Dillard Bassett, Colton Underwood, Lisa Rinna, Yamil ‘Yam Yam’ Arocho, Ron Funches, Michael Rapaport, Monet X Change, Tiffany Mitchell, Caroline Stanbury, Donna Kelce, Rob Cesternino, Porsha Williams and Ian Terry. It included a dynamite finale with [SPOILER ALERT] snake-wrangler Rausch, who made his name as a contestant on Love Island USA, fooling Love Island UK star Higgins to win the finale prize.

The Traitors is exec produced by Cumming, Stephen Lambert, Mike Cotton, Sam Rees-Jones, Rosie Franks, Tim Harcourt, Jack Burgess and Darrell Olsen.

title: Matthew Lillard Says ‘I Feel Ashamed’ for Acting in ‘Scream 7’ After Melissa Barrera Got Fired: ‘I Blew That. I’m on the Wrong Side of History’
summary: Matthew Lillard feels “ashamed” for starring in this year’s “Scream 7” after Melissa Barrera was fired from the franchise due to social media posts criticizing Israel amid the war in Gaza. Lillard starred in Wes Craven’s original “Scream” in 1996 as Stu Macher. He reprised the role in “Scream 7,” which opened in theaters in […]
content:
Matthew Lillard feels “ashamed” for starring in this year’s “Scream 7” after Melissa Barrera was fired from the franchise due to social media posts criticizing Israel amid the war in Gaza. Lillard starred in Wes Craven’s original “Scream” in 1996 as Stu Macher. He reprised the role in “Scream 7,” which opened in theaters in February and became the highest-grossing entry in the series with $214 million.

Attending a recent 30th anniversary screening of the original “Scream,” Lillard was asked by a fan about the difficulty of speaking out on politics as an actor. Lillard made headlines last year for saying “fuck ICE” at a “Scream” screening.

“I don’t know how else to do it,” Lillard told the fan (via Entertainment Weekly). “For me, I have queer kids. If I’m not standing up for queer kids or kids in the trans community, then what the fuck am I doing? If I’m not standing up against ICE, then what the fuck am I doing?”

Popular on Variety

Lillard noted that “I don’t think it’s easy all the time” to speak out, noting what happened to Barrera as an example. “Scream” franchise producer Spyglass fired her after she starred in two franchise installments and was gearing up to return for “Scream 7.” The company said it had “zero tolerance for antisemitism or the incitement of hate in any form, including false references to genocide, ethnic cleansing, Holocaust distortion or anything that flagrantly crosses the line into hate speech.”

“Melissa Barrera, who’s a beautiful actor, was fired for what she said after the whole Palestinian — what started happening in Israel,” Lillard said. “It’s really fucking bullshit and really hard, and she’s on the right side of history. When they start coming after your job, sometimes things are worth it… When that happened to Melissa, the whole world didn’t pipe up. But she was a year early on what the fuck’s going on. But the whole world should have popped up and said, ‘She’s right.’ And they didn’t. And that’s brutal.”

“I went back to do ‘Scream,’ and I got called out. And I’m like, ‘Oh, fuck. That’s brutal,’” he continued. “I feel bad about that. I feel ashamed about that. Because in that moment I was so excited to go back, I didn’t really think about Melissa and that journey. I didn’t say no. I’m embarrassed; that’s the truth… I blew that. I’m on the wrong side of history for that. I still like being in the movie [but] it may not have been the best idea.”

After war broke out in Gaza in 2023, Barrera took to Instagram to share her views on the conflict. She was critical of Israel and accused the nation of “genocide and ethnic cleansing.” The post led to her firing, which in turn sparked backlash from her supporters against the release of “Scream 7”. Protesters gathered outside of the “Scream 7” premiere in Los Angeles, for instance, and called for a boycott of the horror film in a show of support for Palestine.

title: How to Stream ESPN on Sling: Watch ‘Monday Night Football,’ College Football and More for $19.99 a Month
summary: Just as the fall sports calendar starts heating up, watching ESPN directly is about to get a little more expensive. content:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

Just as the fall sports calendar starts heating up, watching ESPN directly is about to get a little more expensive.

Beginning Sept. 17, ESPN is raising the price of its standalone ESPN Unlimited plan from $29.99 to $31.99 per month, while its annual subscription jumps from $299.99 to $319.99. The lower-cost ESPN Select tier is also increasing from $12.99 to $13.99 per month and from $129.99 to $139.99 annually.

For sports fans primarily interested in ESPN’s flagship channels, however, Sling TV offers a cheaper route. The streamer’s recently launched Sling Essentials package costs $19.99 per month and includes both ESPN and ESPN2 alongside more than 10 other channels, including Disney Channel, Freeform and Hallmark Mystery. Subscribers also get 50 hours of DVR storage.

Popular on Variety

For fans who want even more college sports, Sling also offers Sling Select with Sports Extra and a Season Pass option, which bundle in channels such as ESPNU, SEC Network, ACC Network and more for broader access throughout the college football season.

Sling Essentials particularly timely with football season underway. ESPN remains the home of “Monday Night Football,” with the New York Giants taking on the Los Angeles Rams on Sept. 21 at 8:15 p.m. ET, followed by the Philadelphia Eagles and Chicago Bears on Sept. 28. ESPN2 also carries the alternate “ManningCast” for select “Monday Night Football” games.

College football is another major draw. ESPN’s networks will carry more than 1,000 games throughout the 2026-27 season across ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, SEC Network, ACC Network and other platforms, in addition to the network’s weekly “College GameDay” coverage.

The basic $19.99 Sling Essentials subscription gets you ESPN and ESPN2, but diehard college fans can tack on Sports Extra for an additional $11 per month, bringing the total to $30.99. The add-on brings SEC Network, ACC Network, ESPNU and ESPNEWS into the mix, giving viewers substantially more access to SEC and ACC games throughout the season.

Baseball fans also have plenty to watch as the MLB postseason race enters its final stretch. ESPN will exclusively televise a Sept. 23 doubleheader featuring the Cleveland Guardians against the Boston Red Sox at 7 p.m. ET, followed by the Houston Astros against the Seattle Mariners at 10 p.m. ET. “Baseball Tonight” programming will surround marquee matchups with analysis and highlights.

On the basketball front, ESPN remains one of the WNBA’s national television partners. The league returns from its FIBA World Cup break this week before concluding the regular season Sept. 24, with the playoffs tipping off Sept. 27. Disney’s ESPN and ABC networks will carry two first-round playoff series and one semifinal series.

And ESPN’s appeal goes well beyond the games themselves. Its year-round studio slate includes “SportsCenter,” “Get Up,” “First Take,” “NFL Live,” “The Pat McAfee Show,” “Pardon the Interruption,” “College GameDay” and more, offering pregame coverage, postgame reaction, highlights, interviews and analysis throughout the week.

Stream ESPN on Sling TV here.

title: Macklemore Donating $1 Million Salary from Ed Sheeran Tour to Support Palestine: ‘I Invite Robert Kraft to Match My Donation’
summary: Macklemore has announced that he’ll be donating the $1 million in net earnings he received from supporting Ed Sheeran on his Loop Tour to organizations working to support the Palestinian people, and invited billionaire Robert Kraft to match his donation. The rapper was dropped from Sheeran’s current tour earlier this week after saying “free Palestine” […]
content:
Macklemore has announced that he’ll be donating the $1 million in net earnings he received from supporting Ed Sheeran on his Loop Tour to organizations working to support the Palestinian people, and invited billionaire Robert Kraft to match his donation.

The rapper was dropped from Sheeran’s current tour earlier this week after saying “free Palestine” on stage and delivering a political speech at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey at the beginning of September. He appeared to place the blame on New England Patriots owner Kraft, saying that the mogul had rallied other stadium owners to refuse to allow him to perform at their venues.

A rep for Kraft declined to comment on Macklemore‘s request to match the donation.

Popular on Variety

On Wednesday, Macklemore posted another lengthy note on social media sharing that he would be donating his net earnings to organizations including Palestine Children’s Relief Fund, Heal Palestine, Gaza Soup Kitchen, Medical Aid for Palestinians, UNRWA USA National Committee and Anera.

“With everything that has happened over the last 48 hours, I want to bring the conversation back to where it belongs: to the Palestinian people who are still being killed, still living under military occupation, and still fighting for their freedom,” he wrote. “I will be donating the entire $1 million of my net earnings from Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour to six organizations working directly to support the Palestinian people. And I invite Robert Kraft to match my donation. Whatever we disagree about, perhaps we can agree on this: Palestinian lives are worth protecting. A Palestinian life is no less valuable than any other life on this earth.”

Macklemore explained that he wants to “center the parents carrying their children into hospitals without the basic resources to treat them, and the physicians, paramedics, journalists and aid workers who keep going back in. I want to center the organizers and activists who have paid real costs for standing with Palestine. Their risk is of a far different order than mine.

“Palestinians have lived for decades without basic rights and should not have to wait another day to be free,” he continued. “That is where my focus will remain. I will continue to stand with the Palestinian people and their fight for liberation. When the news cycle moves on, which it will, don’t move with it. Free Palestine.”

Macklemore’s latest efforts come after a tumultuous day for Sheeran, who released a statement on Tuesday morning sharing that he had nothing to do with Macklemore’s dismissal from his tour and that he preferred to remain neutral when it came to political causes. Not long after, all of the supporting acts on the Loop tour — Finneas, Aaron Rowe, Lukas Graham and Beoga — announced that they were dropping out in solidarity with Macklemore and the Palestinian people.

title: Box Office: ‘Resident Evil’ Reboot Targets Franchise-Best $45 Million Debut
summary: Movie theater operators are counting on “Resident Evil” to scare some life into the early fall box office. Sony’s horror-comedy reboot of the zombie-infested property is targeting a strong $40 million to $50 million in its domestic debut. With strong reviews and glowing word-of-mouth, rivals and independent tracking services believe that initial ticket sales will […]
content:
Movie theater operators are counting on “Resident Evil” to scare some life into the early fall box office.

Sony’s horror-comedy reboot of the zombie-infested property is targeting a strong $40 million to $50 million in its domestic debut. With strong reviews and glowing word-of-mouth, rivals and independent tracking services believe that initial ticket sales will surpass $50 million and could near $60 million.

Sony spent $75 million to produce the movie, the second remake and eighth installment in the horror series. Exhibitors are particularly excited because this take on “Resident Evil” was directed by Zach Cregger, who electrified the box office with last August’s breakout hit “Weapons.” That R-rated movie, an original thriller about students who went missing in the middle of the night, opened to $43 million en route to sleeper hit status. “Weapons” ended its box office run with a mighty $270 million globally against a $38 million budget and won an Oscar for Amy Madigan.

Popular on Variety

“Resident Evil” began as a 1996 video game and expanded into a multimedia franchise that spans sequel games and film and television adaptations. The property was first adapted for the big screen in 2002’s “Resident Evil,” starring Milla Jovovich. She reprised her role as Alice, a former security specialist and covert operative, in five follow-up films in the 2000s and 2010s. Those movies collectively generated $1 billion globally and were once the highest-grossing series based on video games. Sony attempted to reboot the property with 2021’s “Resident Evil: Welcome to Raccoon City,” a critical and commercial failure with $42 million worldwide against a $25 million budget. All of the original “Resident Evil” films opened in the $20 million range (not adjusted for inflation), while “Welcome to Raccoon City” faltered with $5.3 million in its debut, so this reboot will easily rank as the largest opening weekend in the long-running franchise. The highest grossing installment is 2010’s “Resident Evil: Afterlife,” which launched to $26 million domestically and ended its theatrical run with $300 million globally.

In the new “Resident Evil,” Cregger reunites with “Weapons” actor Austin Abrams, who stars as a medical courier who fights through a viral outbreak of infested monsters in Raccoon City. Critics have praised the cinematic gorefest, with Variety’s Owen Gleiberman calling it “different, and much better, than the other ‘Resident Evil’ movies.”

As this weekend’s only major release, “Resident Evil” won’t have any trouble securing the No. 1 spot on domestic box office charts. Elsewhere, “Practical Magic 2” will attempt to rebound after a rough start while mid-summer holdovers like “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” and “The Odyssey” will remain atop box office charts.

Although this weekend is light on newcomers, the fall box office is expected to heat up before September ends. Next weekend brings a trio of new movies, including Paramount’s Brad Pitt-led survival thriller “Heart of the Beast,” Universal and DreamWorks Animation’s “Forgotten Island” and A24’s “To Catch a Predator”-inspired “Primetime,” starring Robert Pattinson. There’s also Disney’s re-release of “Avengers: Endgame,” which is returning to theaters before “Avengers: Doomsday” opens in December. In the meantime, it’s Cregger and his band of zombie slayers to the rescue.

title: ‘Jawbreaker The Musical’ Extends LA Run, Lori Alan Stepping Into Principal Sherwood Role
summary: The Flawless Four will walk the halls of Reagan High for another weekend as Jawbreaker The Musical announces an extension for its Los Angeles workshop. Following overwhelming demand for the stage musical adaptation of Darren Stein’s 1999 teen cult classic, the production will continue with three more performances the weekend of Sept. 25-27 at the […]
content:
The Flawless Four will walk the halls of Reagan High for another weekend as Jawbreaker The Musical announces an extension for its Los Angeles workshop.

Following overwhelming demand for the stage musical adaptation of Darren Stein’s 1999 teen cult classic, the production will continue with three more performances the weekend of Sept. 25-27 at the Hudson Theatre.

After Jawbreaker (1999) star Rebecca Gayheart graduated to the role of Principal Sherwood in the workshop production, Lori Alan (The Pee-Wee Herman Show, Spongebob Squarepants) will take over the character for the weekend.

Alan’s return to the Hudson comes after she originated the role of Mae in the cult musical Reefer Madness, which premiered at the venue in 1998.

Watch on Deadline

Written and directed by Stein, Jawbreaker stars Gayheart, Rose McGowan and Julie Benz as a group of high school girls who accidentally kill their best friend in a birthday prank gone wrong and have to cover up the crime, while transforming a geek (Judy Greer) into one of their clique to keep their secret.

Directed by Matt DiCarlo (The Comedy About Spies) with choreography by Jay Jackson (RuPaul’s Drag Race alum Laganja Estranja), the musical features a book written by Stein, with original music by Jeff Thomson (Pump Up the Volume) and lyrics by Jordan Mann (Trails). It’s produced at Hudson Theatre by Knot Free Productions.

title: House Lawmaker Requests Emergency Court Hearing After Kennedy Center Closure
summary: After fencing went up around the Kennedy Center and the main building was closed to the public, a House lawmaker on Thursday an emergency hearing, warning that the shutdown violates a judge’s order. The board, dominated by allies of President Donald Trump, voted for a resolution on Tuesday to immediately close the main building of […]
content:
After fencing went up around the Kennedy Center and the main building was closed to the public, a House lawmaker on Thursday an emergency hearing, warning that the shutdown violates a judge’s order.

The board, dominated by allies of President Donald Trump, voted for a resolution on Tuesday to immediately close the main building of the complex, citing safety issues while the center has been working on plans for a large scale renovation. The resolution also pointed to a recent incident in which a portion of the ceiling collapsed to the floor following a recent rainstorm.

But attorneys for Rep. Joyce Beatty (D-OH), an ex officio member of the center board who has been challenging the closure plan, noted that U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper’s order prohibits a shutdown until he lifted a preliminary injunction, something that he has yet to do. The judge has ruled that renovations could proceed, but a closure could come only after the board made a fuller analysis of its impact.

Per a court filing, a staffer at a law firm representing Beatty sought to enter the main building on Wednesday but was advised by security that it was closed to the public.

Watch on Deadline

Cooper has given the center until Thursday morning to respond to Beatty’s motion for an emergency hearing.

The judge on Tuesday prohibited the board’s latest plan to return Donald Trump’s name to the facade of the complex or to designate its grounds for him. Trump, who serves as the center’s chair, posted on Truth Social that they would seek an expedited appeal, but that the renovation would not proceed if courts rule against the naming plan.

Beatty has said that she is not opposed to a renovation, but previous plans were to keep the center open as the rehab was carried out in phases.

title: ‘Dancing With The Stars’ Season 35 Premieres To 24% Audience Boost With Ladies’ First Routines Still To Come
summary: Dancing with the Stars is off to a dazzling start with last night’s Season 35 premiere on ABC and Disney+. The episode, which saw only the male celebrities and their pro partners compete, attracted 6.67 million total live + same-day viewers, according to preliminary data from Nielsen. When the company’s Big Data + Panel numbers […]
content:
Dancing with the Stars is off to a dazzling start with last night’s Season 35 premiere on ABC and Disney+.

The episode, which saw only the male celebrities and their pro partners compete, attracted 6.67 million total live + same-day viewers, according to preliminary data from Nielsen. When the company’s Big Data + Panel numbers are available later in the week, that number is likely to rise.

That’s a 24% increase over the Season 34 premiere to deliver the show’s biggest premiere audience in six years. Among adults 18-49 specifically, the season opener jumped 40% to a 1.48 rating — the show’s best performance in the demo in nearly a decade.

In fact, funny enough, the premiere was the top entertainment telecast among adults 18-49 across all of television since ABC’s presentation of The Oscars. Dancing with the Stars is surging among young women, unsurprisingly, given the shows and influencer circles that it has been mining from for celebrity contestants. Disney says that the premiere delivered a 2.53 rating among women 18-34, making it the best premiere delivery in 13 years.

Watch on Deadline

This all bodes very well for the new season, especially the big boost in total viewers over the Season 34 premiere. Last season became a juggernaut for Disney, ending with the best finale audience in nearly a decade.

The kickoff continues Wednesday night with premiere night two, when the ladies will take the stage with their professional partners. This year’s cast is one of the biggest ever, so the premiere was split into two nights with an elimination after each. Disney hasn’t explicitly confirmed the premiere vote tally yet, since the women have yet to compete, but online voting crashed on night one and host Alfonso Ribeiro said toward the end of the episode that they’d experienced record-breaking text votes.

Last season’s premiere was only one episode on a Tuesday night, so these would be the comparable numbers, though it’s worth noting that some of the season’s biggest “gets” won’t hit the ballroom floor until Wednesday night, including Maura Higgins, Ciara Miller, Julia Stiles, and more. So, it’s entirely possible that Wednesday does even better.

More data will be available later this week. Dancing with the Stars is produced by BBC Studios.

title: ‘Resident Evil’ To Scorch The Earth With $80M Global Debut – Box Office Preview

content:
After a record $4.67B summer, last weekend’s Warner Bros/Alcon’s Practical Magic 2 didn’t exactly light the fall on fire. But this weekend’s Sony/Constantin‘s revival of Resident Evil from Zach Cregger could very well do the trick with a $40M-$50M domestic start and another $31M overseas for a global around $80M on the high end.

While many were bullish on Practical Magic 2 over the total awareness, reviews at 38% kept the older female audience from expanding. Also, the sequel’s addition of Joey King and Maisie Williams didn’t bring the underi25s running. So don’t immediately assume that the marketplace is in a funk.

RELATED: ‘Resident Evil’ Red Carpet Premiere Photos: Austin Abrams, Zach Cherry, Kali Reis & More

Watch on Deadline

Resident Evil is a completely different movie: Aside from the potential draw of franchise fans, there’s the additional appeal of cinephiles, particularly those who love Cregger, as well as de facto horror fans. Not to mention, mic drop, it’s the best-reviewed Resident Evil in the franchise’s 24-year history at 96% certified fresh. Previous Evil pics have been rotten on Rotten Tomatoes with critics.

RELATED: Zach Cregger Talks ‘Resident Evil,’ Intense Drive To Work With Spielberg That Led Him To ‘The Flood’ & ‘Obsession’/‘Backrooms’ Fervor – The Deadline Q&A

At $80M worldwide, Resident Evil would rank ahead of the global start of Weapons at $70M WW (in reported, not like-for-likes). The previous seven Resident Evil titles have racked up more than $1.2 billion worldwide, with 2010’s Resident Evil: Afterlife owning the franchise opening record stateside of $26.6M.

Sony International has markets split, with Constantin taking German-speaking and Metropolitan taking French-speaking. Total offshore market count is 62, with Sony owning 58 of ’em. Thailand, CIS and South Africa are opening next weekend, with Japan going on October 9. Resident Evil will raid China at a later date, the feature IP having fared well there. 2016’s The Final Chapter in reported did close to $160M in the Middle Kingdom. Eastern Europe has been a prime market for Resident Evil as well.

RELATED: The 65 Movies That Have Made More Than $1 Billion At The Global Box Office

Of the international start, Sony’s bunch should do around $23M-$24M, which would be on par with Weapons in like-for-like comps, on par with 28 Years Later, 27% above Evil Dead Rise, 34% over Smile 2, 45% over Saw X, 49% over Black Phone 2 and 84% above Sinners.

Historically, top markets for the Resident Evil franchise have been Japan (home market), Germany (Constantin’s market), Mexico, France, Taiwan, Spain, South Korea, UK, Italy, Thailand, Brazil, and Australia. However, given the new take on the franchise, all eyes are on an expanded moviegoers in SPRI such as the UK, Mexico, Japan, Australia, Spain, Saudi Arabia, Brazil, Argentina, Colombia, Italy, and Malaysia.

RELATED: 48 Of The Most Anticipated Movies Of 2026

Stateside, even if Resident Evil falls back on a $40M opening, it’s still a record start for the franchise. The $75M production is booked at 3,000 locations with previews starting tomorrow at 2PM. The asterisk here is whether or not the video game fans will fully embrace Cregger’s take. Note that he’s an avid fan of the game, and made it with every ounce and intention of a fan. He said publicly that he hasn’t seen any of the previous Resident Evil films. For a minute, Warner Bros was in the running to scoop up his version of the reboot when the Constantin rights came up, but Sony made damn well sure they’d have them. Anything north of $43.5M would rep a record start for Cregger at the domestic office, ahead of Weapons.

Also opening this weekend is Vertical’s Sundance acquisition, The Weight, starring Ethan Hawke and Russell Crowe at 1,504 theaters in North America with an eye on single digits. Previews start at 7PM with an Alamo Drafthouse simulcast across the country followed by a Q&A with Hawke, Julia Jones and director Padraic McKinley. Rolled into previews will be AMC Dolby Cinema Wednesday night early access screening at 200 theaters. Critics are 93% fresh. Blurb for action crime thriller: Desperate to save what is left of his family, during the height of the Great Depression a battle-scarred veteran is hired to help smuggle a fortune in gold across 100 miles of impenetrable wilderness.

GKIDs has StudioCanal and Aardman’s production Shaun the Sheep: The Beast of Mossy Bottom booked in 2,173 domestic theaters. Thirty reviews on RT stand at 100%.Hopeful second weekend hold for Practical Magic 2 based on audience scores is between -50% and -60%, so between $12M-$15M.

title: Flamingo Estate’s Richard Christiansen on Pamela Anderson’s Pickles, Julianne Moore’s Honey and the Dolly Parton Coffee That ‘Got Away’
summary: Richard Christiansen was working in the offices at Flamingo Estate, his farm and lifestyle brand in the Highland Park neighborhood of Los Angeles, when Pamela Anderson’s son, Brandon Lee, called him to ask if he’d be interested in collaborating with his mother. “He said, ‘Would you like to do something with my mom? She’s a […]
content:
Richard Christiansen was working in the offices at Flamingo Estate, his farm and lifestyle brand in the Highland Park neighborhood of Los Angeles, when Pamela Anderson’s son, Brandon Lee, called him to ask if he’d be interested in collaborating with his mother.

“He said, ‘Would you like to do something with my mom? She’s a big gardener,’” Christiansen recalls. “They don’t have the same surname, so I didn’t know who he was talking about so I was like, ‘OK, who’s your mom?’ He said, ‘Pamela Anderson.’ I was like, ‘Holy shit!”

At that point, Flamingo Estate was making a name for itself, among other things, for its celeb honey collaborations. Christiansen had already partnered with Julianne Moore and LeBron James to create their limited-edition lines of honey. All Flamingo Estate celebrity partnerships benefit not-for-profits. The celebs do not get paid for their work.

Popular on Variety

When Anderson arrived for their first meeting, Christiansen gave her his customary honey pitch. “I wanted her to do a honey, like many of the ones we’ve done,” says Christiansen, who grew up on a bee farm in Australia. “Honey’s easy for us. I take my hives to someone’s house to do. Like we tied them to LeBron’s roof or for Ed Ruscha recently, we put the hives in his studio. Julianne Moore’s honey was from her garden in Montauk. It’s some of the best. It’s dark and it’s almost molasses, like whisky.”

But Anderson had another idea. “She said matter-of-factly, ‘I want to do pickles with you. It’s my aunt’s recipe,’” Christiansen says. Anderson’s $38 jars of pickles raised $500,000 for the California Wildlife Center.

I am talking to Christiansen on Zoom shortly before the release of his new book, “Pleasure Principles.” The gorgeously illustrated and designed 408-page tome, subtitled “An Almanac from the Garden,” features recipes, DIY projects and musings on a range of topics from the cinematic history of the moon to celebrity restaurants in L.A.

If anything, “Pleasure Principles” serves as a look inside Christiansen’s very creative and colorful mind. “I don’t have a car,” he explains. “I ride my bicycle everywhere, and when I’m on my bike, I dictate into my phone. That’s maybe why everything’s short, these short little stories.”

Christiansen’s latest Hollywood collaboration is a first for him, a movie tie-in with “Practical Magic 2.” Not only do several Flamingo Estate products, including bottles of olive oil and Green Goddess candles, appear in the movie, but Christiansen has also curated a gift box inspired by the Nicole Kidman and Sandra Bullock film.

It’s a few days after Dolly Parton passed away in August. I ask Christiansen to name a celebrity he’d love to work with. “We were going to do a coffee with Dolly called ‘8 to 6’ instead of ‘9 to 5,’” he says. “We had some lovely conversations about it, and then it didn’t end up happening because we were too young at that point and our distribution probably couldn’t handle the weight of her reach. That was the one that got away.”

title: Ed Sheeran Backlash Explodes as Ms. Rachel, Hannah Einbinder and More Slam Singer After Macklemore Dropped From Tour: ‘Silence During a Genocide Is Not Neutral’
summary: Voices across Hollywood and Washington are speaking out after Macklemore was dropped from Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour for making pro-Palestine comments on stage. “Hacks” star Hannah Einbinder, one of TV’s most politically outspoken stars, wrote on her Instagram stories on Tuesday, “Ed Sheeran i say this as a ginger. i hope you get a REALLY […]
content:
Voices across Hollywood and Washington are speaking out after Macklemore was dropped from Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour for making pro-Palestine comments on stage.

“Hacks” star Hannah Einbinder, one of TV’s most politically outspoken stars, wrote on her Instagram stories on Tuesday, “Ed Sheeran i say this as a ginger. i hope you get a REALLY bad sun burn. the kind on the back of your entire body where it hurts to lie down or walk or sit.”

YouTuber and children’s entertainer Ms. Rachel also took to Instagram to call out Sheeran. She wrote on Monday, “Ed Sheeran had an opportunity [to] show that we won’t be bullied into punishing people for supporting Palestine. Instead he caved to people who refuse to accept what the world knows. A genocide is happening in Gaza. We all need to speak out against it.”

Popular on Variety

She added, “If more than 20,000 white children were killed in another part of the world, everyone would be shouting about it at their concerts. Treating some children’s lives as less worthy of outrage is racist. Silence during a genocide is not neutral.”

“Wicked” star Marissa Bode, who is in a wheelchair, said in a TikTok video, “Ed Sheeran, my legs may not work like they used to before, but at least I have a fucking spine. Free Palestine, bitch!”

Sen. Bernie Sanders posted a statement on X, slamming New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft, whom Macklemore partially blamed for his removal from the Loop Tour in a statement about his exit. “In the United States of America, billionaire stadium owners should not be able to silence artists because they speak out on political issues. Today it is the genocide in Gaza. What’s next? If they can silence one artist, they can silence anyone,” Sanders wrote.

On Sept. 4, Macklemore sang out “Free Palestine” during his set at New Jersey’s MetLife Stadium. The comments made headlines, and the rapper was removed from Sheeran’s Loop Tour on Sept. 14. The same day, Macklemore released a lengthy statement on Instagram explaining his side of the story. He wrote, “Last Monday, in the middle of all the media attention surrounding Pink and what I said at MetLife, Ed told me that Robert Kraft called him. We were scheduled to play Gillette Stadium later this month, which is owned by the Kraft Group. Ed told me that Kraft said I would not be allowed to perform in his stadium. Ed also told me that Kraft had rallied some of the other stadium owners and collectively they gave him an ultimatum: if Macklemore stays on the tour, you will not be allowed to play in our venues.”

He added, “Ed was in a fucked up position. He knew it. His typical apolitical stance was being challenged in a way it never had been before. He told me that the words ‘Free Palestine’ and the image of the Palestinian flag were hurtful to a lot of people he spoke with. I told him that if those words were more offensive than tens of thousands of Palestinian children being killed by Israel, then there was a fundamental disconnect between where those people stood and where I stood. But he couldn’t get past his public facing, ‘I don’t take sides.’”

On Sept. 15, Sheeran released his own statement. He claimed that he spoke with venue owners “at length all week to try and build a bridge” after Macklemore’s comments. Sheeran also asserted that dropping Macklemore was “the promoter’s decision, it was not mine.”

“I would never let down the fans who had made plans, nor would I abandon the touring crew and the other support acts and musicians who rely on me for work and to make a living,” he added.

Despite Sheeran’s comments, openers Finneas, Aaron Rowe, Lukas Graham and Irish band Beoga all left the tour after Macklemore was dropped.

On Wednesday, Macklemore announced that he will donate the $1 million net earnings he received from the Loop Tour to organizations that support the Palestinian people.

“With everything that has happened over the last 48 hours, I want to bring the conversation back to where it belongs: to the Palestinian people who are still being killed, still living under military occupation, and still fighting for their freedom,” he wrote on Instagram. “I will be donating the entire $1 million of my net earnings from Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour to six organizations working directly to support the Palestinian people. And I invite Robert Kraft to match my donation. Whatever we disagree about, perhaps we can agree on this: Palestinian lives are worth protecting. A Palestinian life is no less valuable than any other life on this earth.”

Shortly after Macklemore’s announcement, Kraft put out a statement saying that he and Sheeran are donating $2 million each to the Palestinian cause. The statement, released on the Gillette Stadium X account, read, “I have dedicated much of my life to building bridges between all people. I believe deeply that all lives are worth protecting. Earlier today, before Macklemore challenged me to match his donation, Ed called me and asked me to commit $2 million to match his donation to aid in the region to fight this humanitarian crisis. Ed now plans to reach out to other venue owners and our goal is to continue to work together to build bridges”

title: Jessica Chastain to Star in New Netflix Drama Series ‘The Retrievals’
summary: Jessica Chastain has joined Netflix’s “The Retrievals,” a new drama series from the streamer. The Oscar-winning actor will star as Kaitlyn Langford, a former art historian who has “spent the last decade stuck in an endless cycle of failed fertility treatments,” per Netflix. “When she learns she’s also a victim of criminal drug diversion at […]
content:
Jessica Chastain has joined Netflix’s “The Retrievals,” a new drama series from the streamer.

The Oscar-winning actor will star as Kaitlyn Langford, a former art historian who has “spent the last decade stuck in an endless cycle of failed fertility treatments,” per Netflix. “When she learns she’s also a victim of criminal drug diversion at the Yale Fertility Center, she faces a devastating personal reckoning and becomes a key plaintiff in this historic lawsuit against Yale.”

Chastain “was the writing team’s ‘exemplar’ while crafting the role of Kaitlyn,” said showrunner, writer and executive producer Molly Smith Metzler. “As a performer, she has the rare ability to convey extreme restraint and unbridled freefall, often at the same time. It gives me goosebumps just thinking about what Jessica’s going to do with this role.”

Popular on Variety

Chastain joins previously announced cast members Emilia Jones and Amy Ryan.

As previously reported by Variety, the show will follow “an unlikely community of IVF patients who come together to crusade against Yale University after they are operated on without anesthesia — because a nurse stole their fentanyl.”

“The Retrievals” is based on the New York Times and Serial Productions podcast of the same name by Susan Burton.

In addition to Metzler, the series is executive produced by Dani Gorin, Tom Ackerley, and Margot Robbie for LuckyChap; Colin McKenna (“Maid,” “Sirens”), Caitlin Roper for The New York Times, and podcast writer Susan Burton. The project is produced by LuckyChap and Quiet Coyote. Lila Neugebauer (“Maid,” “Sirens,” “The Beast in Me”) serves as the pilot director and executive producer.

title: Paramount May Be Bluffing About Leaving California, But L.A. Mayor Taking It Seriously
summary: Paramount has been threatening to leave California since July, when the state sued to block it from merging with Warner Bros. Discovery. Attorney General Rob Bonta has called it “blackmail” meant to stop him from enforcing antitrust law. But Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass, for one, is taking the threat seriously and is trying to […]
content:
Paramount has been threatening to leave California since July, when the state sued to block it from merging with Warner Bros. Discovery.

Attorney General Rob Bonta has called it “blackmail” meant to stop him from enforcing antitrust law. But Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass, for one, is taking the threat seriously and is trying to do whatever she can to persuade the company to stay.

“We’ve heard the same information that everybody has,” said Steve Kang, the mayor’s film czar, on Wednesday. “We need to be prepared for every option to be available — whether it’s true or not.”

Paramount faces an Oct. 1 deadline to close its transaction or begin accruing a $7-million-a-day “ticking fee” owed to WBD shareholders. In recent days, the noise about a potential relocation has started to pick up with reports in Politico and TMZ that the company is taking affirmative steps toward a move.

Popular on Variety

Bass has already done most of what she can do, urging Bonta last month to come to the table and reach a deal.

Bonta’s office has repeatedly said that it is open to good faith talks, but has said it will only agree to a resolution that includes “robust structural remedies.” A court-supervised settlement conference has been set for Oct. 14-15.

In a statement on Wednesday, Bonta’s office said the threat to move out of California is nothing new.

“We cannot comment on a company’s plans,” the A.G.’s office said. “It’s no secret that Paramount has been making this threat, despite its alleged commitment to California and Hollywood. What Paramount decides to do is Paramount’s choice alone. We’ll continue to apply the law without fear or favor and continue to be open to coming to the table for good faith discussions.”

Paramount declined to comment.

Kang was appointed in 2025 to serve as Bass’ liaison to the film community. Asked what steps Bass could take, aside from pressuring Bonta, to get Paramount to stay, Kang cited her support for increased subsidies for production in California and in Washington, D.C.

“Creating a film-friendly environment is our first and foremost priority,” he said. “We’re hoping they don’t leave. We’re hoping all sides are speaking to one another. This is an issue between the attorney general and Paramount. All we can do is encourage discussions among all parties.”
