He’ll play a stranger, named Jude, who will arrive in Port Charles in October, we’ve learned. No other details have been revealed, so stay tuned. Traval joins another […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Another new face will soon be arriving in Port Charles.

Wil Traval (Messiah, Jessica Jones) has joined the cast of ABC’s venerable daytime drama General Hospital. He’ll play a stranger, named Jude, who will arrive in Port Charles in October, we’ve learned. No other details have been revealed, so stay tuned.

Traval joins another new cast member who is heading to Port Charles, Blythe Howard. She portrays Monet, a new lawyer who recently joined Miller & Davis, the firm run by Diane Miller (Carolyn Hennesy) and Alexis Davis (Nancy Lee Grahn), and meets with a Port Charles resident in need of legal counsel, Deadline has confirmed. She’ll appear September 23, according to TV Insider, which first reported her casting.

Traval was a series regular on Michael Petroni’s Netflix series Messiah, opposite Michelle Monaghan, John Ortiz, and Jane Adams. His other series regular credits include Netflix’s Jessica Jones, opposite Krysten Ritter, and ABC’s Red Widow opposite. Rahda Mitchell, Goran Visnjic. and Clifton Collis Jr. He also recurred on Dynasty and had notable arcs on Arrow, Chicago P.D., Grimm, and Once Upon a Time.

Watch on Deadline

Australian actor Traval is best known in his native homeland for his role as Dr. Jack Quade on the long-running medical drama All Saints and Detective Peter Church in police drama White Collar Blue. Traval is repped by Clear Talent Group and managed by The Van Johnson Company.

Frank Valentini serves as General Hospital‘s executive producer. Elizabeth Korte and Chris Van Etten are the show’s co-head writers.

General Hospital airs weekdays on ABC and streams on Hulu.

title: Griffin Dunne, Zack Fox & Johnno Wilson Added To Cast Of Netflix’s ‘A Hundred Percent’ As Production Wraps
summary: EXCLUSIVE: As Netflix has completed production on the upcoming comedy series A Hundred Percent in Los Angeles, three new cast members have been revealed: Griffin Dunne (After Hours), Zack Fox (Abbott Elementary) and Johnno Wilson (Resident Evil). They join the previously announced Nick Kroll, Sam Richardson, Jason Mantzoukas, Vanessa Bayer, Diane Lane, Tiffany Boone, and […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: As Netflix has completed production on the upcoming comedy series A Hundred Percent in Los Angeles, three new cast members have been revealed: Griffin Dunne (After Hours), Zack Fox (Abbott Elementary) and Johnno Wilson (Resident Evil). They join the previously announced Nick Kroll, Sam Richardson, Jason Mantzoukas, Vanessa Bayer, Diane Lane, Tiffany Boone, and Lisa Gilroy.

A Hundred Percent is a half-hour comedy about a group of friends who are stars in the world of wellness and self-optimization. Their books, podcasts, and morning routines might help us live our lives more perfectly, but away from the screens and mics, they are most definitely far from perfect.

Dunne plays Chris, the estranged father of Konstantine (Mantzoukas), who resurfaces in his life just as his star is on the rise.

Fox plays Strick Lennon, a popular live-streamer in the manosphere. Strick is Konstantine’s stiffest competition, and promises to be a strong ally just when he needs one.

Wilson plays Alex, a pioneer in the world of Longevity; he is the Chief Immortality Officer of a male-centered wellness empire and media conglomerate. Very wealthy, very healthy, and very lonely.

Watch on Deadline

Netflix picked up the series in January, joining the streamer’s live-action comedy slate, which also includes Nobody Wants This, Running Point, A Man on the Inside, Emily in Paris, Tires, Survival of the Thickest, Big Mistakes, and The Hawk.

Gabe Liedman serves as showrunner, executive producer, and writer. In addition to starring, Kroll also writes and executive produces. Additional EPs include Max Joseph and Alex Plapinger.

title: Alan Ritchson In Talks To Star In Sony’s Adaptation Of ‘Helldivers’ From Director Justin Lin
summary: Following the exit of Jason Momoa, Sony Pictures and Justin Lin have moved fast to find his replacement for their feature adaptation of Helldivers. Sources tell Deadline that Alan Ritchson is in talks to star in the film based on Arrowhead Game Studios’ video game franchise, with Lin still on board to direct. Sony had […]
content:
Following the exit of Jason Momoa, Sony Pictures and Justin Lin have moved fast to find his replacement for their feature adaptation of Helldivers. Sources tell Deadline that Alan Ritchson is in talks to star in the film based on Arrowhead Game Studios’ video game franchise, with Lin still on board to direct.

Sony had no comment. If a deal closes, Ritchson would play one of the helldivers, with more roles to be announced.

Details regarding the plot of the film are under wraps. Helldivers is expected to hit theaters on November 10, 2027.

Helldivers is a cooperative, twin-stick shooter game that debuted in 2015. As part of the elite unit called the Helldivers, players must work together to protect Super Earth and defeat the enemies of mankind in an intense intergalactic war.

Watch on Deadline

In Helldivers 2, gamers step into the boots of the Helldivers, whose mission is to spread peace, liberty and Managed Democracy using the biggest, baddest and most explosive tools in the galaxy. The sequel sold more than 12 million units across PlayStation 5 and PC in the first four months after its 2024 launch. The game recently expanded to Xbox and continues to perform.

Hutch Parker is producing the film with PlayStation Productions’ Asad Qizilbash and Lin through his Perfect Storm Entertainment.

Sony Pictures and PlayStation Productions previously worked together on Uncharted, starring Tom Holland and Mark Wahlberg, which earned $407 million globally and is one of the 10 highest-grossing video game adaptations of all time; Peacock’s series Twisted Metal; and the Emmy-winning The Last of Us for HBO.

Ritchson, who can currently be seen in the fourth season of his Prime Video series Reacher, is repped by WME and Range.

title: Donald Trump Says He’s Banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico From the White House ‘Effective Immediately’ Because of ‘Their Constant Fake News’
summary: President Donald Trump said he is immediately banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House, slamming the news outlets for their “fake news” reporting. On Friday afternoon, Trump wrote on social media, “I am proud to announce that, effective immediately, I am banning Fake News CNN, MSNOW (who recently changed their name from […]
content:
President Donald Trump said he is immediately banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House, slamming the news outlets for their “fake news” reporting.

On Friday afternoon, Trump wrote on social media, “I am proud to announce that, effective immediately, I am banning Fake News CNN, MSNOW (who recently changed their name from MSNBC due to lack of viewership and credibility!), and Politico (The recipients of an illegal and ridiculous $8 Million Dollar subscription, an All Time Record, directly from the United States Government, under Crooked Joe Biden, in order to keep them ‘alive.’ Seems like corruption to me!), from the White House as a result of their constant ‘reporting’ FAKE NEWS! Media Outlets shouldn’t be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they’re covering the President of the United States, the Trump Administration, or the United States of America.”

Trump added: “Other Fake News Media Outlets to follow.”

Popular on Variety

Variety has reached out to CNN, MS NOW and Politico for comment.

In his social media post, Trump did not indicate what triggered his decision to declare that the three news outlets would no longer be welcome at the White House. Variety has asked the White House for comment.

Trump’s reference to U.S. government subscriptions to Politico is based on data from USAspending.gov, a government website that tracks federal spending, which showed government agencies collectively spent more than $8 million combined in payments for Politico subscriptions and products in 2024, as reported by CBS News.

Last year, the White House blocked AP staffers from the Oval Office, Air Force One and other areas after the news service continued referring to the body of water on the southeastern periphery of the North America as the Gulf of Mexico, after Trump decreed on his first day back in office in 2025 that henceforth it should be known as the “Gulf of America.” The AP sued over the shoutout, but an appeals court found that the White House’s ban of the news outlet was not a First Amendment violation.

title: Amazon Moves to Toss ‘Criminal’ Production Assistant’s Harassment Suit
summary: Amazon MGM has filed a motion to throw out a suit brought by a production assistant on the upcoming series “Criminal,” saying that his claim that the showrunner pointed a gun at him is “pure invention.” The plaintiff, Ijaaz Noohu, filed the suit two weeks ago, alleging he was subject to racial and sexual harassment. […]
content:
Amazon MGM has filed a motion to throw out a suit brought by a production assistant on the upcoming series “Criminal,” saying that his claim that the showrunner pointed a gun at him is “pure invention.”

The plaintiff, Ijaaz Noohu, filed the suit two weeks ago, alleging he was subject to racial and sexual harassment. Among other things, Noohu accused showrunner Ed Brubaker of rubbing his back and of making comments about running his hands through Noohu’s hair.

The complaint also alleged that Noohu was asked whether he supports Hamas, and was subjected to racial stereotypes about curry, mathematical ability and “Tiger Moms.” The most sensational allegation, offered with scant detail, was that Brubaker once pointed a functional firearm at him and pulled the trigger.

Popular on Variety

In its demurrer filed on Thursday, Amazon MGM says it has no record of any report of the firearm incident, and accuses Noohu of making it up.

The demurrer describes Noohu as “an opportunist, not a victim,” and quotes from an email Noohu sent in 2024, pitching himself for a promotion to be the show’s executive producer, saying it would “make the show better.”

Amazon’s lawyers also state that Noohu never raised a complaint of harassment or discrimination during his work on the show.

“His contemporaneous emails and texts — including the one begging to keep working closely with Brubaker, his supposed harasser — breathe not a word of harassment, discrimination, or distress,” the demurrer states. “Nor did Noohu ever hold himself out as religious or as sensitive to sexual content on a production he knew was based on mature, adult subject matter as a matter of course.”

The demurrer also states that it is implausible that anyone would have pointed a gun at Noohu and pulled the trigger without it being reported.

“Had that happened, every person in the room, Noohu included, had a duty to report it, and in a post-‘Rust’ industry on high alert to firearms, someone would have. No one did. Defendants first learned of the supposed incident when Noohu reemerged peddling the story and demanding a payday.”

Amazon also alleges that Noohu sat on his allegations for nearly two years, until the beginning of the press tour for “Criminal,” in order to achieve maximum leverage.

title: Navigating AI, Super-Serving Audiences, Engaging the Creator Economy and More at Variety’s 2026 Entertainment and Technology Summit
summary: Executives, marketing professionals, entrepreneurs and creators across the field of film, television and gaming came together for a day of keynote speakers, panels and networking on Thursday for the Variety Entertainment & Technology Summit presented by EY. Industry professionals from Blumhouse Atomic Monster, Sony, Warner Bros., Mattel, Reddit and more spoke about navigating AI, engaging […]
content:
Executives, marketing professionals, entrepreneurs and creators across the field of film, television and gaming came together for a day of keynote speakers, panels and networking on Thursday for the Variety Entertainment & Technology Summit presented by EY.

Industry professionals from Blumhouse Atomic Monster, Sony, Warner Bros., Mattel, Reddit and more spoke about navigating AI, engaging fandom, the creator economy and the future of the entertainment industry during the event at the Beverly Hills Four Seasons Hotel.

A keynote conversation with Nick Kroll touched on his desire for productions to shoot in Los Angeles and his upcoming Netflix comedy series “A Hundred Percent.”

Bill Hader spoke in a keynote conversation about voicing Cat in the Hat and why young people are resistant to AI.

Director, writer and producer James Wan, of Blumhouse Atomic Monster, addressed the accessibility to technology that allows the breakout success of YouTube creators on films like “Obsession” and “Backrooms,” both of which Atomic Monster Blumhouse had a hand in.

Keith Le Goy, Sony’s TV chief, talked about how the company has activated its incredibly engaged audience. Nintendo of America president and COO Devon Pritchard discussed the Switch 2 and “Legend of Zelda” projects, including a film collaboration with Sony Pictures.

Other sessions included top media executives from NBCUniversal Entertainment, Crunchyroll, Hulu and more, who spoke about super-serving audiences and the dangers of AI slop. Panelists in another session discussed the possibilities for AI as a catalyst for communal engagement. Marketing professionals discussed how creators and platforms fuel fandom, and entertainment leaders talked about AI’s place in the industry.

Read below for a few key takeaways from the 2026 Entertainment and Technology Summit:

When Stories Speak: Reaching Audiences in the Next Era of Entertainment

Nancy Hall, U.S. CEO at WPP Media, talked about how to know when something resonates with audiences between short-form, long-form and live experiences. “The red thread of these formats and of telling stories in this way is making them participatory, giving people the opportunity to respond to them, to talk about them, to shape them, to share them, and that’s what makes stories culture and not just content,” she said.

The conversation, moderated by Variety editor-in-chief Cynthia Littleton, discussed how to turn buzz into business.

LISTEN to Turning Buzz into Business With WPP Media’s Nancy Hall and Audible’s Tom McKenna on Variety’s “Strictly Business” podcast Tom McKenna, Audible global head of media, operations and business development, highlighted the company’s launch of its new brand, which focuses on stories that speak to its audience.

“We’re taking things that are everyday moments and making them more valuable,” he said. “It’s about how Audible enriches a listener’s life.”

McKenna and Hall talked about the unique advertising Audible has engaged this year, like an ad that took TikTok out of a phone and onto a building in Times Square. Hall said the brands that think of media as a “creative canvas” are the ones that break through the “sea of sameness.”

Looking to the future, McKenna said those who are willing to take risks will be the ones who succeed. Hall said modern marketing is rooted in science and art. “We have to market today to two different entities,” she said. “We have to ensure that humans desire us, but that machines recommend us.”

The Future of IRL: Trends in Event and Experiential Entertainment

Senior vice president of global experiences for Paramount Marie Marks highlighted hospitality’s ability to offer something no other format can offer. A hotel where families stay with IP for days is a “full flywheel of experiences” that is powerful when done right.

The growing Nickelodeon hotel business has 1,000 rooms in the market and another 2,000 in development globally. “A big learning for us was actually that the IP alone is not enough,” Marks said. “The underlying product has to be exceptional. One’s not enough without the other.”

A brand like Hallmark is largely associated with one season, and in recent years has launched cruises and in-person experiences.

President of Hallmark Media and chief brand officer Darren Abbott said the company has found success in expanding because as consumers want to spend more time at the holidays, they do so by spending more time with Hallmark.

Natalia Premovic, chief consumer products and experiences officer at Mattel, attended an in-person Uno event in Los Angeles in August. She said attendees connected over the game strategy with people they might not have met otherwise.

Premovic and Marks have seen these experiences expand the fanbase across generations.

“No longer does the screen have to be the end of the interaction with the IP,” Marks said. “Increasingly so, it’s really just becoming the beginning.”

Titans of Innovation Roundtable

Billy Parks, head of FOX creator studios, had a light bulb moment 15 years ago while working with AT&T. He realized allowing creators to use their voice and authentic audience relationship drove more engagement than prescribed talking points.

Sean Atkins, CEO of Dhar Mann Studios, believes the marketing system is broken. “When you have creators who now have the same skill as the Super Bowl, the fact that they get a phone call that says, ‘Hey, would you stand up for 15 seconds and hold a Coca-Cola for $25,000?’ is ridiculous.”

Christina Kothari, global head of consumer marketing at Reddit, recently tapped into the creator economy for a brand partnership for “Resident Evil.” Three Reddit creators were invited to a preview of the film and live Ask Me Anything with the director.

“Creators often get invited to these premieres, and that’s important because they’re a media channel and they give you the reach that you need,” she said. “But to pair those creators with the really in-depth fans that have been building these communities on Reddit for years, created a really special environment, and the content that was captured there was so authentic and so fun.”

“I’m really excited to find new ways to kind of partner with the fandoms on Reddit and bring them in real life together with creators with IPs that they love,” she added.

Kothari is excited to find new ways to partner with young creators. Parks said he is inspired by young people and creators, two audiences he said are tapped in and challenging traditional approaches from media companies.

The Creator Boardroom: Building Culture and Scaling Partnerships

Jarret Myer, CEO at UPROXX Studios, said the creator economy is bigger than people think it is.

“It’s studios, it’s artists, it’s creators that are all happening outside of the traditional Hollywood formation,” he said. “More and more these people are creating the monoculture moments that everyone is talking about. To me, missing out on that is missing out on the point of entertainment and culture.”

Culture Genesis partners with “culture-shifting content creators” like YouTube streamer IShowSpeed. These creators are able to create moments of mass consciousness that Culture Genesis CEO Shaun Newsum called “mini Super Bowls.”

Zach Miller, JesserCo president, challenged the traditional channels for advertisers: “Do you just want to spend the money on the traditional media channel that has always been the place to spend it, and cross your fingers and hope to find younger audiences there, or do you need to broaden your strategy and think about either swapping some of that spend on TV for digital channels that allow you to reach that audience, or at least expand the spend so that you reach your sort of core audience that you’ve been historically reaching on TV?”

For Newsum, the next frontier continues to engage fandoms through creators on YouTube and leverage their audiences.

The New Era of the TV Business

Jeremy Helfand, global vice president and head of Amazon Prime Video advertising, said the television business is changing around personalization and accountability within advertising.

For Josh Mattison, executive vice president of digital revenue pricing, planning and operations for Disney Advertising, it has never been more relevant that audiences are coming together around things that bring connection.

“From a consumer perspective, or from a brand perspective, you want to follow fandom wherever people are watching, and they’re watching in more ways than ever,” he said.

Puja Vohra, CMO and executive vice president of advertising sales at Fox Corporation, said people align around great content. She has seen advertisers consider how to capture the power of broadcast, precision of digital and flexibility of streaming.

Vohra said the power of big television events is in the people: “That power of communal viewing, of being able to engage masses of people around a virtual couch, if you will, that is what leads to engagement and lean in, and you’re more receptive to messages.”

Live entertainment remains important, and Mattison said the goal is to meet viewers where they’re at and build a daily habit with television.

Behind the Business: Netflix Comedy and the Return of “A Different World”

Laughs have always been important at Netflix, said Tracey Pakosta, vice president of comedy original series for the platform.

“A Different World,” a sequel to the original sitcom hits Netflix on Sept. 24. Showrunner Felicia Pride brought the concept to the streaming service with a goal to modernize the look and feel of the show while staying true to much of the feeling from the original.

Pride said that multihyphenate legend Debbie Allen, who spearheaded the original series, was “very clear that now is the time to hear from young Black America, and that felt like a charge I could get behind.”

Along with Netflix and Allen, Pride worked to discover the tone of the sequel series. The project shot at HBCUs in Atlanta to achieve an authentic texture to the setting at the fictional Hillman College.

“We wanted to be honest and truthful about life, but also be hopeful,” Pride said of the potential fan reactions to the season’s content.

While the original series had 22 episodes per season, the sequel season debuts with 10, which Pakosta was excited about.

“I think more is more always, but I also understand this cycle of streaming and the wanting to make the best version of that show,” she said. “A lot of times the story in the first season eight makes the most sense, and then there are other stories where 10 makes more sense.”

Storytelling Vanguards

Writer and comedian Joel Kim Booster has not felt a shift in the wake of box office hits like “Obsession,” and he is hesitant about the possibility.

“It does always feel like in the wake of the success of things like ‘Obsession,’ a lot of the people at the top learn the wrong lessons and make decisions that may seem like they try to replicate the same thing without realizing that at the core of what made ‘Obsession’ a success was its originality, its purity in idea and story,” he said.

Creator and showrunner Nick Antosca said the “Obsession” effect is real, but “it doesn’t get rid of the gatekeepers or the gates.” The success was made possible because Universal put marketing money behind it, he said.

Kim Booster said it is important to recognize that the “Obsession” effect is localized to mid-budget horror movies. When asked what the antidote is, he said movies like “The Invite” and films made outside of the awards conversation.

“Someone told me that the only way this movie that I’m talking about would be in theaters is if people felt like they needed to see it to be a part of the discourse around award season,” he said. “I hope that small little indie movies, little indie dramas can get made without needing to be nominated for an Oscar or at least an indie spirit.”

When asked if he listens to feedback, actor and “In Your Dreams” host Owen Thiele said his podcast is a personal venture that has built parasocial relationships from fans and some notes are hard to tune out because those fans feel they have a reason to give a note.

The panel also discussed where the speakers go for real inspiration. Antosca said he turns everything off and reads novels to feel less like “a sponge that’s squeezed into a rock” after months in production.

Looking forward, the panel called for more representation in the industry. Antosca said he hopes more original and unexpected things will pop through. Musician, composer and music supervisor Este Haim said she wants to see more women hired to compose for shows, and Thiele wants to see more shows and movies that give queer Black leads fulfilling emotional arcs.

(Pictured top: actor and “In Your Dreams” podcast host Owen Thiele, comedian and actress Lisa Gilroy, musician, composer and music supervisor Este Haim)

title: Javier Bardem to Star in Drama Series ‘The Spread’ at HBO From Bill Dubuque, Sean Sansiveri
summary: In a highly-competitive situation, HBO has given out a straight-to-series order for the drama “The Spread” with Javier Bardem attached to star and executive produce, Variety has confirmed. The project hails from writers Bill Dubuque And Sean Sansiveri, who also executive produce alongside Bardem. This will be Sansiveri’s first credited TV writing role. Matthew Vaughn […]
content:
In a highly-competitive situation, HBO has given out a straight-to-series order for the drama “The Spread” with Javier Bardem attached to star and executive produce, Variety has confirmed.

The project hails from writers Bill Dubuque And Sean Sansiveri, who also executive produce alongside Bardem. This will be Sansiveri’s first credited TV writing role. Matthew Vaughn will direct and executive produce. Brad Weston executive produces for Makeready, with Ian Stratford and Michael Bloom of Topic Studios also executive producing. The series is a co-production between HBO and Fifth Season TV Studio.

The logline states, “Miami is turning paradise into power — Wall Street South — a subtropical collision of industry titans, elite hedge funds, staggering wealth, ruthless competition, sex, nightlife and fun on an industrial scale. Into this sun-soaked arena comes a visionary billionaire (Bardem) who collects the brilliant, the hungry and the dangerous, then turns their ambitions loose on the markets that power America. He chases something bigger: the power to shift the center of economic gravity to Miami — and decide how long the party lasts.”

Popular on Variety

“Having long wanted to set a scripted series in Florida, HBO couldn’t be more excited to explore the gilded chaos of Miami and bring it to life with this kaleidoscope of extraordinary, visionary talent who is as fearless as the story itself,” said Francesca Orsi, executive vice president of HBO Programming and head of HBO Drama Series and Films.

This marks the latest major series role for Bardem in recent years. He is fresh off the Apple TV adaptation of “Cape Fear,” in which he played the villainous Max Cady. He also recently starred in “Monsters: The Lyle and Erik Menendez Story” at Netflix as Jose Menendez. He is primarily known for his film roles, which include his Oscar-winning turn in “No Country for Old Men,” as well as celebrated performances in films like the “Dune” franchise, “Being the Ricardos,” “Biutiful,” and “Before Night Falls.”

He is repped by WME and Goodman Genow.

Dubuque is best known as the co-creator of the hit Netflix series “Ozark,” for which he shared in the show’s three Emmy nominations for outstanding drama series. He most recently created the crime drama “M.I.A” at Peacock, which is also set in South Florida, and executive produced the Netflix limited series “His & Hers,” which was also Fifth Season production. He is also known for writing films like “The Accountant” starring Ben Affleck and its sequel as well as “The Judge” starring Robert Downey Jr. and Robert Duvall.

He is repped by WME. Sansiveri is repped by CAA.

“‘The Spread’ is a gripping story of power and ambition, set against the vivid, glamorous backdrop of Miami,” said Noah Greenshner, executive vice president and head of TV Creative for Fifth Season. “We’ve brought together an exceptional creative team to capture the energy of this world and city, and we’re thrilled to be working alongside them and our partners at HBO, Makeready, and Topic to bring it to life.”

title: Don Palathara’s Indian Drama ‘Monkey Play’ Selected for Vancouver’s Inaugural Works-in-Progress Lab (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: “Monkey Play” (“Kurangukali”), the latest project by Indian filmmaker Don Palathara (“1956, Central Travancore,” “Family”), has been selected for the Vancouver Film Festival’s new Business Hub Works-in-Progress program, which showcases up to eight feature-length projects in the final stages of production. The film, which Variety unveiled last year, follows Sethu and Nikita, who, in the […]
content:
“Monkey Play” (“Kurangukali”), the latest project by Indian filmmaker Don Palathara (“1956, Central Travancore,” “Family”), has been selected for the Vancouver Film Festival’s new Business Hub Works-in-Progress program, which showcases up to eight feature-length projects in the final stages of production.

The film, which Variety unveiled last year, follows Sethu and Nikita, who, in the wake of their young daughter’s death, retreat to an isolated house in the hills of Idukki in the southern Indian state of Kerala. Their fragile relationship is disrupted when Sethu encounters a feral child in the forest and brings him home. As the couple’s lives begin to revolve around the child, their grief takes different forms, quietly altering the way they see each other and the world around them.

What begins as an attempt to live with their loss gradually takes them into an uncertain space where memory, perception and reality begin to overlap.

Popular on Variety

Palathara’s cinema is known for its subtle emotional layers and exploration of human relationships. His previous work includes “Family,” which had its world premiere at the International Film Festival Rotterdam in 2023, as well as “Everything Is Cinema” (2021), “Joyful Mystery” (2021), “1956, Central Travancore” (2019), “Vith” (2017) and debut feature “Shavam” (2015). His films often tackle complex social realities with a meditative approach that eschews judgment.

“This is a film about the biggest fear of any parent,” Palathara said about “Monkey Play.” “Here, we have decided to face it and look at the aftermath. The film explores that psychological territory through grief, asking what happens when the mind tries to replace someone who is irretrievably gone,” he told Variety.

“Blending psychological thriller, drama and elements of the uncanny, the film uses the landscape of Idukki and the ambiguity between reality and perception to create a deeply intimate yet genre-driven experience.”

“Monkey Play” stars Dileesh Pothan, Parvathy Thiruvothu, Rajesh Madhavan and Arjun Radhakrishnan.

The film is produced by Kerala-based Artisan Films, whose debut feature, “Ekadesham,” is currently in post, Mankind Cinemas and Guardian Angel Films. Producing are Dixon Podudas, Jomon Jacob (“The Great Indian Kitchen”), Amshunath Radhakrishnan, Jose Mathew and Palathara.

Taking place Oct. 1-11, the Vancouver Film Festival’s curated WIP program, which runs Oct. 5-6, will showcase up to eight projects, four Canadian and four international, providing filmmakers with an opportunity to present their films to leading international industry professionals.

title: Banned: CNN & MS Now Shut Out Of White House By Trump; POTUS Says “Other Fake News Media Outlets To Follow”
summary: The President of the United States has banned CNN, MS Now and others from the White House. Floundering in the polls and in the war with Iran, the notoriously thinned skinned and authoritarian former Apprentice host just posted on his Truth Social: “I am proud to announce that, effective immediately, I am banning Fake News […]
content:
The President of the United States has banned CNN, MS Now and others from the White House.

Floundering in the polls and in the war with Iran, the notoriously thinned skinned and authoritarian former Apprentice host just posted on his Truth Social: “I am proud to announce that, effective immediately, I am banning Fake News CNN, MSNOW (who recently changed their name from MSNBC due to lack of viewership and credibility!), and Politico (The recipients of an illegal and ridiculous $8 Million Dollar subscription, an All Time Record, directly from the United States Government, under Crooked Joe Biden, in order to keep them “alive.” Seems like corruption to me!), from the White House as a result of their constant “reporting” FAKE NEWS!”

Trump promses there are more bans to come with “other Fake News outlets to follow.” Though, with the likely exception of friendly Fox News and some other conservative publications, no one seems to know who those other outlets could be. The New York Times? The Washington Post? The Atlantic?

Watch on Deadline

BTW – Typos are Trump’s

CNN’s Kaitlan Collins, a frequent subject of sexist Trump attacks, doesn’t seem to have asked POTUS a question today, so no real indication why this ban is in place. Also, according to media sources I’ve spoken too, CNN and MS Now journalists remain in the Executive Mansion right now as an Oval Office announcement on drug prices is coming today, so perhaps “ban” means something different to Trump than everyone else.

As for CNN and MS Now. The former briefly covered the ban missive on-air this afternoon, whole the latter seemed to turn the other cheek — for now.

A full-on ban is something that Trump has not engaged in before in this term or his first time in the White House. That can’t be said for the Pentagon, where ex-Fox host Pete Hegseth took away credentials from a number of journalists and banned all media from the halls of the Defense Department.

Back at the White House, Trump did try to revoke the press credentials of then CNN reporter Jim Acosta in his first term, but lost that first amendment dust-up in court. Since returning to office in 2025, POTUS has taken over the White House Correspondents Association for all practical purposes. He has also repeatedly attempted to keep the Associated Press out of formal events and administration announcements.

Stay tuned.

title: Lea Michele Remembers Duncan Sheik: Death Of ‘Spring Awakening’ Composer “Does Not Seem Real”
summary: Lea Michele, who gained her first major fame as a cast member of Broadway’s Spring Awakening, paid tribute to the musical’s late composer Duncan Sheik today, remembering their first meeting and her thoughts upon his passing yesterday. “I met Duncan when I was 14 years old,” Michele wrote in an Instagram Story post this afternoon. […]
content:
Lea Michele, who gained her first major fame as a cast member of Broadway’s Spring Awakening, paid tribute to the musical’s late composer Duncan Sheik today, remembering their first meeting and her thoughts upon his passing yesterday.

“I met Duncan when I was 14 years old,” Michele wrote in an Instagram Story post this afternoon. “I listened to a demo on tape of him singing songs from Spring Awakening outside of my middle school before my first audition.

“I’m at a loss for words,” she continued. “This one hurts and does not seem real. Thank you for everything you gave us. And for the time we had together. Sending all my love and prayers now to Nora, Ines, and Duncan’s family.”

In addition to the message, Michele posted two brief videos on Instagram Story of what appear to be from a Spring Awakening rehearsal in which she’s singing the number “Mama Who Bore Me” with Sheik accompanying her on acoustic guitar and Groff looking on.

Watch on Deadline

Michele was cast in early workshops of the musical – written by Sheik and Steven Sater – and appeared as the lead female character Wendla Bergmann. She, along with Jonathan Groff and John Gallagher Jr., all three largely unknown at the time, followed Spring Awakening to its Off Broadway premiere in 2006 at the Atlantic Theater Company and, later that year, to Broadway’s Eugene O’Neill Theatre.

The musical is set in late 19th-century Germany and tells an often dark story of teenagers dealing with their awakening sexuality and feelings of love. Groff played Melchior, a radical thinker who has a tragic and doomed affair with Michele’s Wendla.

All three of the musical’s young stars would go on to major Broadway careers. Michele, after her TV success on Glee, returned to Broadway in Funny Girl and Chess. Groff starred in the hits Company and Just In Time, while Gallagher would star in American Idiot, Jerusalem, Long Day’s Journey Into Night and, most recently, Swept Away.

The Broadway production of Spring Awakening earned 11 Tony Award nominations, winning Best Musical, Best Book (for Sater), Best Original Score (Sheik and Sater), Best Director (Michael Mayer) and, for Gallagher, Best Performance by a Featured Actor in a Musical. The original Broadway cast album, featuring Michele, Groff and Gallagher, won the 2008 Grammy Award for Best Musical Show Album.

Singer-songwriter Sheik died Thursday, September 17, at a hospital in Manhattan of cardiac arrest. He was 56.

A major new revival of Spring Awakening directed by Danya Taymor (The Outsiders) was announced recently by producers Seaview for an engagement at the Off Broadway venue Studio Seaview set to begin previews on November 27 ahead of an official December 17 opening. Deadline recently revealed the cast consisting largely of young newcomers, with Amalia Yoo — who gained considerable attention and critical acclaim when she made her Broadway debut last year in the Tony-nominated play John Proctor Is the Villain — set to play the role of Ilse.

title: ‘Wonder Man’ Had 52% Audience Retention Yet Was Canceled As Broadcast TV Sees Higher Renewal Rates Than Streaming — Report
summary: In an interesting turn of events, broadcast series are more likely to be renewed than those on streaming, according to a new report from data intelligence company Luminate. The report, released Friday, found that the broadcast networks renewed 65% of their output in 2025 versus just 44% across the major SVOD services, bucking a conventional […]
content:
In an interesting turn of events, broadcast series are more likely to be renewed than those on streaming, according to a new report from data intelligence company Luminate.

The report, released Friday, found that the broadcast networks renewed 65% of their output in 2025 versus just 44% across the major SVOD services, bucking a conventional wisdom in the streaming era that the online medium would be TV’s best chance of longterm survival.

Now, as Luminate points out, the broadcasters have more limited budget ranges and programming slots, as well as more straightforward viewership data. All three of these factors make renewal decisions for broadcast series less complicated, and the annual return of the broadcast season forces the decisions to be made much quicker.

Streaming has already developed somewhat of a reputation for being unforgiving. These platforms churn out so much content that cancellations come at a higher rate as well, though the streamers don’t have to be nearly as swift in the decision making process, which puts many shows in limbo indefinitely. Luminate uses Netflix’s The Politician as an example, given the show hasn’t returned since 2020 and yet there’s been no formal status announcement.

Watch on Deadline

Netflix often bears the brunt of the criticism in this regard, but Luminate’s study actually found that it had the highest renewal rate among all the major SVODs over the last several years, renewing about 50% of its U.S. slate, on average, from 2022 to 2025.

However, Luminate also finds that new hits with long-running potential are harder to come by. Freshman series represented only about 42% of U.S. scripted output across the major streamers in 2025, suggesting perhaps a course correction from an oversaturated market.

Audience retention is a better metric for understanding success in streaming. Luminate suggests the key benchmark is 50% retention rate, meaning at least half of the audience that started the first episode made it to the end.

That’s not always the case, though. Per Luminate’s data, Marvel’s Wonder Man (on Disney+), Prime Video’s On Call, and Netflix’s The Waterfront all exceeded that 50% benchmark and were still dropped. The Waterfront had the highest of them all with 62% of the audience sticking with the series in the first 12 weeks of release.

Wonder Man, particularly, was a perplexing case. The series, which Luminate says retained 52% of its audience over 12 weeks, was initially renewed for a second season. It was then axed a few months later.

This is not an exact science, and it depends largely on the service. For example, Apple TV appears to accept the lowest retention, particularly for prestige series like The Studio, which captured a 28% retention rate over 120 days. That’s even lower than The Last Frontier, which was the most-watched canceled series on the streamer in the last year or so, per Luminate.

Peacock is another streamer with a much lower retention threshold. The most-watched canceled series on the platform over the last year or so was The Copenhagen Test with 33%.

Overall, scripted is faring much better than unscripted despite some outlying hits like The Traitors, Dancing with the Stars, and Love Island. On streaming, only about 38% of unscripted series were renewed from 2022 to 2025.

Read the full report here.

title: Costume Designers Guild Dresses Up Its 2027 Awards Date & Timeline
summary: Start dressing that set: The Costume Designers Guild said Friday that its 29th annual CDG Awards is set for Thursday, February 25, in Los Angeles. It also revealed other key dates for the 2027 CDGA; see them below. Nominations for IATSE Local 892’s awards, which celebrate excellence in film, TV and shortform costume design and costume […]
content:
Start dressing that set: The Costume Designers Guild said Friday that its 29th annual CDG Awards is set for Thursday, February 25, in Los Angeles. It also revealed other key dates for the 2027 CDGA; see them below.

Nominations for IATSE Local 892’s awards, which celebrate excellence in film, TV and shortform costume design and costume illustration, will be revealed on Friday, December 18. Other details including the venue, host, presenters, career honorees and more will be revealed in the coming months, the guild said.

Frankenstein, Wicked: For Good and One Battle After Another took the top film prizes at the 28th CDG Awards in February, with The Studio and Palm Royale among the TV winners. Since the guild launched its awards show in 1999, the Academy Award for Costume Design has gone to a period film every year but four: Mad Max: Fury Road (2016), Black Panther (2019), Black Panther: Wakanda Forever (2023) and Wicked: For Good (2025). Kate Hawley won hte Academy Award for Frankenstein back in March.

Watch on Deadline

The Costume Designers Guild includes more than 1,000 costume designers, assistant costume designers and illustrators working in motion pictures, TV, commercials, music videos and new media programs throughout the world.

Here is the full timeline for the 2026 CDG Awards (all times Pacific):

Friday, October 2

Online submissions open at 9 a.m. PT

Friday, November 6

Online submissions close at 5 p.m. PT

Wednesday, December 9

Nomination ballot CDG voting opens at 9 a.m. PT

Wednesday, December 16

Nomination ballot CDG voting closes at 5 p.m. PT

Friday, December 18

Nominations announced

Monday, January 25

Final ballot CDG voting opens at 9 a.m. PT

Monday, February 1

Final ballot CDG voting closes at 5 p.m. PT

Thursday, February 25

29th Costume Designers Guild Awards

title: ‘MobLand’ Season 2 Proves the Show Just Wouldn’t Work Without Tom Hardy
summary: A mere 10 minutes into the Season 2 premiere of “MobLand,” aptly titled “I Wanna Be Your Dog,” there is a massacre at the racetrack. Increasingly on edge and triggered by his son Kevin’s (Paddy Considine) disloyalty, Conrad Harrigan (Pierce Brosnan), patriarch of the Harrigan crime family, lets his temper get the best of him. […]
content:
A mere 10 minutes into the Season 2 premiere of “MobLand,” aptly titled “I Wanna Be Your Dog,” there is a massacre at the racetrack. Increasingly on edge and triggered by his son Kevin’s (Paddy Considine) disloyalty, Conrad Harrigan (Pierce Brosnan), patriarch of the Harrigan crime family, lets his temper get the best of him. In a spray of bullets, he ends an already tense partnership with the Turkish mob. Unmoved by the consequences of his own chaos, Conrad does what he’s done for years: call his longtime fixer, Harry Da Souza (Tom Hardy), to clean up his mess.

​

Erasing crime scenes, tying up loose ends and identifying threats is something Harry can do in his sleep. With a menacing calm that pulsates off of him, Harry is neither alarmed nor surprised when he receives a call from Conrad. But Harry’s position in the Harrigan dynasty has cost him a great deal. His 18-year marriage to his long-suffering wife Jan (Joanne Froggatt) is in trouble. (In fact, Harry is just now on the mend after accidentally being stabbed by Jan a couple of months prior.) Moreover, the couple’s teenage daughter, Gina (Teddie Allen), infuriated with her parents’ dysfunction, has run off with Kevin’s wannabe gangster son, Eddie (Anson Boon). Unfortunately, Harry doesn’t have the bandwidth to deal with his wife and daughter, and as usual he turns his attention to the Harrigans, whose family unit is coming apart at the seams. Even matriarch Maeve (Helen Mirren) seems intent on sabotaging her husband for her own gain or perhaps revenge for some festering resentment.

​

As the anchor in the “MobLand” universe, when reports began stirring earlier this spring that Hardy had been axed from the series, audiences were puzzled. The show centers around the work Harry executes to keep the Harrigans thriving in London’s criminal underworld while staying off law enforcement’s radar. Back then, Variety confirmed that after Season 2 wrapped this past March, Hardy fell out with executive producer Jez Butterworth, 101 Studios and others. At the time, reports said the clash was so severe that Hardy would not return for a third season.

​

The news of Hardy’s ousting ricocheted across the entertainment world, baffling fans and even some of Hardy’s “MobLand” co-stars. “Tom is a very special person,” Mirren told Variety at the Taormina Film Festival. “I think he’s absolutely remarkable. My support of him is genuine and heartfelt.” As the news spread, “MobLand” producers set a meeting with Hardy in London to hash things out. Now, he is officially returning for Season 3 of the Paramount+ series.

​

Though critics received just four episodes of the 10-episode second season of “MobLand” for review, what’s clear to any viewer is that Harry’s position within the Harrigan crime family is undergoing a major transformation. Growing increasingly weary of Conrad’s lack of impulse control, frustrated by Kevin’s cowardice and with his own personal life in shambles, Harry is undoubtedly coming closer to his boiling point.

​

After all, not only does he know where all the bodies are buried, but Harry moves with such a calculated callousness that he could very likely dismantle all Conrad and Maeve have built from the inside out. Since Hardy is returning for the third season of the show, Harry will be forced to choose a side, either standing firmly with the Harrigans or going his own way. For the Harrigans’ sake, let’s hope he remains an ally. If the Harrigans’ choose to make an enemy of Harry, what he could unleash would be more brutally murderous than anything Maeve or Conrad could begin to conjure.

title: ‘Sweet Magnolias’ Canceled at Netflix as Sheryl J. Anderson and JoAnna Garcia Swisher Set New Series ‘Ladies of the House’
summary: It’s bittersweet news for “Sweet Magnolias.” The romantic drama starring JoAnna Garcia Swisher, Brooke Elliott and Heather Headley has been canceled at Netflix after five seasons. But Swisher, alongside “Sweet Magnolias” creator Sheryl J. Anderson, are pairing up for a new drama series ordered by the streamer titled “Ladies of the House.” Anderson will serve […]
content:
It’s bittersweet news for “Sweet Magnolias.”

The romantic drama starring JoAnna Garcia Swisher, Brooke Elliott and Heather Headley has been canceled at Netflix after five seasons. But Swisher, alongside “Sweet Magnolias” creator Sheryl J. Anderson, are pairing up for a new drama series ordered by the streamer titled “Ladies of the House.”

Anderson will serve as showrunner of “Ladies of the House,” with Swisher potentially starring and executive producing with Kate Gordon under their Rolling Clover banner, alongside executive producers at Black Label Media. The show is loosely based on the novel by Lauren Edmonson.

The logline reads, “When the charismatic owner of a winery dies unexpectedly, his wife and two adult daughters must battle through their issues with each other in order to confront challenges with the business, their extended family, and the men in their lives. Good friends and good wine will aid in the journey to hang on to the winery, but what matters most is that they find a way to hang on to each other.”

Popular on Variety

“I’m thrilled to be embarking on this new adventure with JoAnna and Netflix,” said Anderson. “When Jo shared the novel with me, I immediately saw the foundation for a series centered on three women grappling with the complexities of family, friendship, and romance — the kind of stories Jo and I most enjoy telling. I cannot wait to share the Richardson women and their world with Netflix’s global audience.”

Swisher added, “From the moment I read Lauren Edmondson’s Ladies of the House, I fell completely in love with Daisy, Cricket and Wallis: their relationships, their messiness, their strength, and most of all, their heart. I am beyond excited to continue to tell meaningful, female-driven stories alongside the incredible Sheryl J. Anderson, and to bring this to life through our production company Rolling Clover and with our wonderful partners at Black Label. Netflix has been my creative home for the past seven years, and I couldn’t imagine a better place, or a better team, to tell this story.”

Deadline broke the news.

title: Dana Walden Envisions Partnerships Between Creators and Disney at Created in L.A. Kickoff Event: ‘Maybe We Can Tell Some Stories Together’
summary: Disney kicked off its first creator event Created in L.A on Thursday night at El Capitan Theatre in Hollywood. Over 350 creators, innovators and industry leaders came together for the first day of a two-day event with the idea to exchange ideas, build relationships, and explore the future of creator-led storytelling and the business behind […]
content:
Disney kicked off its first creator event Created in L.A on Thursday night at El Capitan Theatre in Hollywood.

Over 350 creators, innovators and industry leaders came together for the first day of a two-day event with the idea to exchange ideas, build relationships, and explore the future of creator-led storytelling and the business behind it.

Opening the evening was creator, entrepreneur and media personality Jon Youshaei. The event was conceived and hosted by Youshaei, whose career involves leadership roles at YouTube and Instagram, as well as his own success as a creator. He is known for in-depth interviews and behind-the-scenes conversations with creators and entertainers including MrBeast, Mark Rober and Kevin Hart.

Youshaei highlighted the power of the creators in the room, many of whom had traveled from Argentina, Australia, England, Netherlands, Canada, Georgia and Morocco to attend. He also highlighted their social media followings: “The creators at this event have over 800 million subscribers on YouTube, 80 million followers on Instagram and over 350 million followers on TikTok, which altogether makes over 1.6 billion followers combined.”

Popular on Variety

After sharing a brief history of the theater, Youshaei recounted his pitch to Disney about showcasing the work of creators. He told the audience, “I said, ‘Hey, I have this crazy idea. What if we premiere videos from creators on the big screen? I’m talking about the same videos we usually watch on our phones and our laptops, but have recently gotten so damn good that they deserve to be played in a theater, that deserve to be premiered on a red carpet, that deserve to be celebrated with 350 of the most creative people in the world?’”

The executives at Disney said yes, resulting in the creation of this two-day event, which also includes keynote speakers and conversations.

Dana Walden, president and chief creative officer of the Walt Disney Company, noted how special the theater i s for Disney, having hosted the premieres of iconic films such as “The Lion King,” “The Avengers,” “Frozen,” “Coco” and “Lilo & Stitch.”

She also acknowledged the vital role creators play in Disney’s ecosystem.

“What strikes me about this room is the instinct so many of you have for your audience. You know them intimately. You hear from them constantly, and you adjust in real time based on what they want. And that is very different from the kind of content that we produce.” She elaborated, “It can take years for our films and series to reach their audiences and for you it could be seconds. And there’s something that we can learn from that immediacy, from treating the audience as a true collaborator. My hope for these two days is that we’ll exchange ideas and learn from each other — that some of what makes your storytelling so special rubs off on us, and that some of what we’ve learned about telling stories over many decades will be useful to you.”

Walden concluded by expressing her hope that Created in L.A. would herald the beginning of incredible relationships. “Maybe we can tell some stories together.”

The evening concluded with Youshaei introducing the Golden State Award. The award recognizes strong filmmakers or subscriber count.

The first award went to Lucas and Curtis Nicotra, who go by the name Sticks. Their film “The Technoblade Movie,” premiered alongside Zach King’s parody of “Star Wars,” “Cardboard Strikes Back.” King received the second Golden State Award.

title: Sesame Street Transforms Chappell Roan’s ‘Hot to Go!’ Into the Potty-Training Anthem ‘Got to Go,’ With Lead Vocals From Cookie Monster
summary: Sesame Street has a half-century-long tradition of legendary musical guests and innovative adaptations: from Stevie Wonder’s iconic performance in the early ‘70s to Tony Bennett retrofitting his timeless classic “Fly Me to the Moon” to be a story about the show’s worm character Slimy on an expedition to the moon (“Slimy to the Moon,” of […]
content:
Sesame Street has a half-century-long tradition of legendary musical guests and innovative adaptations: from Stevie Wonder’s iconic performance in the early ‘70s to Tony Bennett retrofitting his timeless classic “Fly Me to the Moon” to be a story about the show’s worm character Slimy on an expedition to the moon (“Slimy to the Moon,” of course); from the Fugees’ inclusion anthem “Just Happy to Be Me” to blues legend B.B. King singing an ode to the letter that has meant so much to his career; from Smokey Robinson getting groped by the letter “U” for “U Really Got a Hold on Me” to — this writer’s personal favorite — opera legend Marilyn Horne trilling an orchestral version of “C Is for Cookie” on an elaborate mock-Egyptian set while wearing a tiara adorned with a bouncing cookie.

And some 57 years after the show premiered, its brilliant combination of education, musicality and humor continues: In a newly released video, they transform Chappell Roan’s “Hot to Go” into a potty-training anthem called “Got to Go” with inimitable lead vocals from the Cookie Monster.

Popular on Variety

It’s a note-for-note rendition too, complete with the song’s chanted middle section from guest vocalists Elmo and Abby Cadabby. And although we don’t get to see Muppets doing the world-famous hand-gestures spelling out the song’s title, instead we get singing letters spelling out POTTY.

Cookie Monster intones in his trademark broken English:

“Stop and listen to me body/ It’s saying that it’s time for potty,

There’s a growing feeling in my tummy, that me gotta go pee, me gotta go pee…

There they go again, now me legs are grooving/ There might be a mess if me don’t get movin’…

“P-O-T-T-Y, woah-oh, your body knows when you’ve got to go…”

It even starts with a talking number one and two.

Contacted by Variety, a rep for Chappell Roan said the singer had no comment. Indeed, none was necessary: Granting permission for her and cowriter/producer Dan Nigro’s song to be used in such an amusing and imaginatively instructive way — for young children, no less — is a statement in itself.

title: ‘Knife: The Attempted Murder of Salman Rushdie’ Review: Alex Gibney Profiles the Controversial Author During His Harrowing Hospitalization
summary: There’s nothing more distressing in “Knife: The Attempted Murder of Salman Rushdie’ than the unflinching closeups of the author’s wounded body in the days and weeks after August 12, 2022, when he was repeatedly stabbed while on stage at a literary festival in upstate New York. The camera lingers over his mangled hand and the […]
content:
There’s nothing more distressing in “Knife: The Attempted Murder of Salman Rushdie’ than the unflinching closeups of the author’s wounded body in the days and weeks after August 12, 2022, when he was repeatedly stabbed while on stage at a literary festival in upstate New York. The camera lingers over his mangled hand and the train-track of stitches running up his belly. His right eye is a bloodied bulge. The power of Alex Gibney’s documentary, which premiered at Sundance, lies in Rushdie’s decision to showcase his scars — quite literally, by sharing footage that his wife Rachel Eliza Griffiths shot throughout his time in the hospital. It’s a visceral complement to what is otherwise a solid, if standard, profile of the author from Gibney, the Oscar- and Emmy-winner known for churning out reliably comprehensive, reporter-style investigations of power and politics.

In Gibney’s upcoming “Musk,” an HBO-produced Elon Musk mega-doc that showed at Venice, the SpaceX and Tesla overlord is an AI-generated talking head. Thankfully no such uncanny simulations are in play here. The Indian-born writer has control of the mic from the get-go with running voiceover narration that starts the film alongside a feverish recreation of the attack visualized from Rushdie’s point of view: Blinding stage lights turn his assailant, a New Jersey man by the name of Hadi Matar, into a shadowy mass, and each jab of the knife is heard as a fleshy thud. Matar is only mentioned by name once. In Rushdie’s retelling, he becomes a symbol for the punishing incursions upon his life and liberties since the publication of his 1988 novel “The Satanic Verses” scandalized the masses and put a target on his head, courtesy of a fatwa issued by Ayatollah Khomeini, then the Supreme ruler of Iran.

Popular on Variety

Wondering why he didn’t fight back or run away, Rushdie moves into an extended reflection on his relationship to death and fatalism. In the present thread, we follow his recovery through Griffiths’ tenderly diaristic documentation, which includes, at one point, a call from family friend Wes Anderson. Meanwhile Gibney employs archival news footage and old on-camera interviews with Rushdie to take us back to his identity-crisis-riddled early years between India and his adopted home of London, and the emotional abuse he suffered while living with his alcoholic father. But for the most part, Gibney keeps to the events after 1988, when Rushdie’s Islam-inspired magical realist tome became the flashpoint for a fiery debate over free speech and creative freedom.

Excerpts from the novel are accompanied by scratchy animated renderings of the story — about two Indian-Muslim men living in London who undergo spiritual upheavals after surviving a plane crash — that echo Rushdie’s existential musings and emphasize the work as a product of his imagination. It’s a way of highlighting the absurdity of the violent response from orthodox Muslim communities — all this rage for a story? — and more generally, the dangers that religious extremism poses to civil society. When Ayatollah Khomeini called for Rushdie’s righteous assassination in 1989, protests and book burnings broke out in the U.K., Pakistan and India; elsewhere, bookstores were destroyed, editorial offices torched, and Rushdie’s Japanese translator, Hitoshi Agarashi, was murdered. These aren’t breaking revelations for what is — for a certain generation, at least — one of the late 20th century’s most shocking and widely-discussed controversies.

But lest we dismiss these events as contained to the past, the 2022 assault stands as a reminder that artistic expression remains as frighteningly vulnerable as Rushdie’s brutalized body. That message might feel obvious for anyone even remotely tapped into the American news cycle, but it’s given a weighty (if obligatorily sentimental) personal touch by the resilient Rushdie and his support system, led by the tenacious Griffiths — his rock against a seemingly neverending saga.

title: Cody Fern Recalls Filming ‘House of Cards’ When The Kevin Spacey “Nuclear Bomb Hit”
summary: Nearly eight years later, Cody Fern is looking back on his time on Netflix’s final season of House of Cards, amid the firing of Kevin Spacey. While discussing his feature directorial debut Closing Night at TIFF, the actor recalled playing “the main villain” on the sixth and final season, before “the nuclear bomb hit” the […]
content:
Nearly eight years later, Cody Fern is looking back on his time on Netflix’s final season of House of Cards, amid the firing of Kevin Spacey.

While discussing his feature directorial debut Closing Night at TIFF, the actor recalled playing “the main villain” on the sixth and final season, before “the nuclear bomb hit” the show with sexual misconduct allegations coming out against Spacey.

“I was in House of Cards,” he told Entertainment Weekly. “I was cast as the main villain of Season 6, playing a Jared Kushner type.”

Fern continued, “Oh yeah, we filmed for a couple of months, and then the nuclear bomb hit. Then I got to come back and work on Robin Wright’s season, and I was a wonderful wallflower. So I got to have the pre- and post-[Spacey] experience, and I’ve got some wild stories.”

Watch on Deadline

After House of Cards was renewed for Season 6 in 2017, actor Anthony Rapp accused Spacey of making a sexual advance on him at a party in 1986 when Rapp was 14. Spacey became the subject of allegations from 15 others, including eight people who worked on the Netflix political drama.

The streamer subsequently dropped Spacey from the starring role of Frank Underwood, announcing that Robin Wright would lead the final season as Frank’s widow Claire Underwood.

Spacey was found not liable in Rapp’s case, and he has never been found guilty on any charges relating to sexual misconduct, all of which he has denied.

title: As The CW Turns 20, President Brad Schwartz Says Network “Continues To Evolve” For New Viewers
summary: As The CW celebrated its 20th anniversary Friday, President Brad Schwartz said the network “continues to evolve for a new generation of viewers.” The exec reflected on the milestone in a short LinkedIn post, illustrated by photos of an official commemoration held at the Nasdaq Marketsite in New York’s Times Square. The network, initially created […]
content:
As The CW celebrated its 20th anniversary Friday, President Brad Schwartz said the network “continues to evolve for a new generation of viewers.”

The exec reflected on the milestone in a short LinkedIn post, illustrated by photos of an official commemoration held at the Nasdaq Marketsite in New York’s Times Square.

The network, initially created as a 50-50 venture by Warner Bros. and CBS, went on to serve principally as a home for shows the companies produced. Many of them were hour-long, young-skewing dramas. In 2022, Nexstar acquired 75% of The CW, with CBS parent Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery each retaining 12.5% stakes.

That programming mix has changed significantly under Nexstar, a local TV giant that already owned the largest collection of CW affiliates before taking over the network. Today, there are seven days of programming, with a lot more live sports and unscripted fare.

Watch on Deadline

At the Television Critics Association summer press tour in 2006, the network announced an inaugural lineup, which drew upon several series that had been on The WB and UPN. The first year of The CW included America’s Next Top Model, Gilmore Girls, 7th Heaven, One Tree Hill, Smallville, Supernatural, Veronica Mars and Everybody Hates Chris.

When streaming gained momentum in the 2010s, The CW licensed many of its shows to Netflix, with that arrangement coming to an end when HBO Max launched in 2020. All along, with a focus on viewers between 18 and 34, the network had a digital focus. Its free, ad-supported streaming app was one of the first major destinations for video, long before connected-TV became a major outlet for broadcasters.

When Nexstar initially took control of The CW, its execs highlighted how much money it had lost compared with its broadcast peers. Initially, they projected it would turn profitable within three years due to their overhaul, but the process has taken more time due in part to cash-intensive investments in sports. Execs now expect the network to enter the black in the fourth quarter.

The CW “has entertained audiences, launched unforgettable series and talent,” Schwartz wrote. Under Nexstar’s ownership, he added, it “has entered an exciting new chapter – expanding its programming, building a major presence in live sports, and reaching audiences across broadcast, streaming, and digital platforms.”

One intriguing corporate aspect to The CW’s future is how the minority 25% held by Paramount and WBD will be managed if the companies manage to complete their planned $110 billion merger. Antitrust lawsuits by 12 state attorneys general and the Writers Guild of America have stymied the deal.

Nexstar, in a parallel situation, has faced an antitrust challenge to its $6.2 billion takeover of rival Tegna. Last April, a federal judge froze the deal after it had officially closed, siding with DirecTV and several state attorneys general arguing it was monopolistic. Nexstar has appealed, with the Ninth Circuit expected to take up the appeal later this year.

title: Netflix Cancels ‘Sweet Magnolias’ After 5 Seasons, Orders New Sheryl J. Anderson & JoAnna Garcia Swisher Series ‘Ladies Of The House’
summary: EXCLUSIVE: It is bad news-good news for Sweet Magnolia fans. Netflix has canceled the romantic drama starring JoAnna Garcia Swisher, Brooke Elliott and Heather Headley after five seasons. At the same time, the streamer has greenlighted a new drama series from Sweet Magnolias‘ executive producer/showrunner Sheryl J. Anderson, with Swisher set to executive produce and […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: It is bad news-good news for Sweet Magnolia fans. Netflix has canceled the romantic drama starring JoAnna Garcia Swisher, Brooke Elliott and Heather Headley after five seasons.

At the same time, the streamer has greenlighted a new drama series from Sweet Magnolias‘ executive producer/showrunner Sheryl J. Anderson, with Swisher set to executive produce and eyed to star.

Like Sweet Magnolias, which Anderson adapted from the novels by Sherryl Woods, Ladies of the House is loosely based on Lauren Edmonson’s novel and has three women at the center.

In it, when the charismatic owner of a winery dies unexpectedly, his wife and two adult daughters must battle through their issues with each other in order to confront challenges with the business, their extended family, and the men in their lives. Good friends and good wine will aid in the journey to hang on to the winery, but what matters most is that they find a way to hang on to each other.

Watch on Deadline

Anderson, who will again serve as showrunner, executive produces alongside Swisher and Kate Gordon under their Rolling Clover banner as well as Black Label Media.

L-R: JoAnna Garcia Swisher, Sheryl J. Anderson and Kate Gordon Danette Anderson/Courtesy

Netflix took a wait-and-see approach with Sweet Magnolias whose fifth season debuted on June 11. It drew 2.8 million views in its opening week, down 30% vs. the premiere week viewership for Season 4, which was on the more modest decline side for Netflix series this year. (The season rose to 3.5M views in its first full week before dropping from the Top 10 after 3 weeks.)

The streamer also did not commission a Season 6 writers room ahead of time the way it typically does for established shows.

Netflix makes its renewal decisions based on cost vs. performance. Sweet Magnolias is done on a modest budget, which would explain its five-season, 50-episode run with solid but not blockbuster viewership (and devoted fan following).

But this time, Netflix had another factor to consider, Anderson and Swisher’s new series in development which was heating up internally and ready to go. I hear the decision came down to whether to renew Sweet Magnolias for a sixth (and final) season or greenlight Ladies of the House, with Anderson and Swisher shifting their attention to the new series. Netflix ultimately went for the second option.

The call was made at the last minute — I hear Netflix ran out the clock, with the options on the Sweet Magnolias cast allowed to expire Thursday night which was also when Ladies of the House was picked up. Sweet Magnolias’ cancellation followed Friday.

This is a sad development for Sweet Magnolias fans who would’ve liked a proper conclusion with a final season for the South Carolina drama (with an Annie and Ty reconciliation probably at the top of their wishlist). They are not left completely in the lurch — while there were several cliffhangers, there weren’t major jaw-dropping twists in the Season 5 finale, which once again ended with the eponymous Sweet Magnolias (Swisher, Elliott & Headley) doing a margarita toast. Deadline asked Anderson in June whether the closer was crafted to also work as a potential series finale in case there is no Season 6.



“I actually think some of our cliffhangers are pretty big but, beyond the ritual of ending with a toast, we always strive to give our audience a balance between the tension of the open questions: Who’s leaving, Who’s coming back, Who’s staying together, all of those, with emotional satisfaction,” she said. “I think maybe in some cases, the emotional satisfaction and the joy is greater than the open questions, but the open questions are certainly there, and we certainly have big thoughts about, if we are lucky enough to get another season, the stories that we will tell.”

(L to R) Brook Elliott as Dana Sue Sullivan, Heather Headley as Helen Decatur and JoAnna Garcia Swisher as Maddie Townsend in Episode 502 of ‘Sweet Magnolias’ Netflix

Following the news of Sweet Magnolia’s cancellation, the writers posted a message to fans on the show’s IG page, accompanied by the Magnolias’ signature “pour it out” line.

“All grand adventures must eventually end. And here, dear friends, is where ours goes. Sweet Magnolias is now complete with five seasons streaming on Netflix,” they wrote before thanking the cast crew, producers, Netflix and fans. (You can see the post below.)

Sweet Magnolias was part of Netflix’s slate of comfort food, feel-good series. Since its 2020 debut, it has earned 100M views and appeared in the Global Weekly Top 10 fourteen times across more than 60 countries.

As Anderson and Swisher bid farewell to Sweet Magnolias, they are focusing on Ladies of the House.

“I’m thrilled to be embarking on this new adventure with JoAnna and Netflix,” Anderson said. “When Jo shared the novel with me, I immediately saw the foundation for a series centered on three women grappling with the complexities of family, friendship, and romance — the kind of stories Jo and I most enjoy telling. I cannot wait to share the Richardson women and their world with Netflix’s global audience.”

Swisher spoke about the reasons why she wanted to adapt Ladies of the House, considered a modern retelling of Sense and Sensibility.

“From the moment I read Lauren Edmondson’s Ladies of the House, I fell completely in love with Daisy, Cricket and Wallis: their relationships, their messiness, their strength, and most of all, their heart,” she said. “I am beyond excited to continue to tell meaningful, female-driven stories alongside the incredible Sheryl J. Anderson, and to bring this to life through our production company Rolling Clover and with our wonderful partners at Black Label. Netflix has been my creative home for the past seven years, and I couldn’t imagine a better place, or a better team, to tell this story.”

title: Maisie Williams Played ‘Practical Magic 2’ Character As “Sapphic Icon” Despite Sequel Omitting Book’s LGBTQ Plot
summary: As the Owens sisters returned to the big screen, Practical Magic 2 left a lot a material behind in the Alice Hoffman book. Maisie Williams, who plays Antonia Owens in the sequel now in theaters, explained that she played the character as a lesbian, despite that part of her life not being made clear in […]
content:
As the Owens sisters returned to the big screen, Practical Magic 2 left a lot a material behind in the Alice Hoffman book.

Maisie Williams, who plays Antonia Owens in the sequel now in theaters, explained that she played the character as a lesbian, despite that part of her life not being made clear in the Susanne Bier-helmed adaptation of Hoffman’s The Book of Magic.

“There’s been a lot of different edits to the movie, and there was a lot of different versions of the script, but I always played Antonia as a sapphic icon,” Williams told Gay Times. “And I love that. I think it brought a real joy to the scenes when we would be talking about Gideon, because Antonia just has a completely different perspective on men altogether.”

From a script by Akiva Goldsman, Georgia Pritchett and Kelly Marcel, Practical Magic 2 sees Sally (Sandra Bullock) and Gillian (Nicole Kidman) chasing Sally’s daughter Kylie (Joey King) to England, where they try to unravel an ancient family curse and save Kylie’s comatose boyfriend Gideon (Xolo Maridueña).

Watch on Deadline

Whereas Practical Magic 2 explores Kylie’s love story, it sacrifices much of Antonia’s rich backstory from the 2021 novel, which reveals that she is a lesbian and gives her a love interest of her own, a lawyer named Ariel who also helps them get to the bottom of the family curse. The book also finds her pregnant with her best friend’s baby.

@gaytimes Is Antonia a lesbian in Practical Magic 2? Does the Owens curse only affect straight people? We caught up with Maisie Williams and Joey King to find out! The highly anticipated sequel to the 1998 classic, Practical Magic, sees the return of Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman as Sally and Gillian Owens, as they reunite with Sally’s daughters, Kylie and Antonia, to break their family’s centuries-old curse 🔮 #practicalmagic #lesbiansoftiktok #sapphic #interview #queertiktok ♬ original sound – GAY TIMES

Although the sequel didn’t give Antonia the romance she deserved, perhaps the third time’s a charm, if Sandra Bullock’s ideas for a trilogy come to fruition. “We’ll do a number three if this takes off. And we’ll pass the torch to the girls,” she told Vanity Fair.
