Popular on Variety

Sony Pictures’ superhero blockbuster “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” placed sixth in its eighth week of release, collecting $772,975. The Marvel tentpole crossed another historic milestone to reach a running local total of $133.9 million, to occupy third position on the all-time U.K. and Ireland box office chart, sitting just behind “Skyfall.”

Disney’s documentary “Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger” took seventh place in its second frame with $659,899, lifting its cume to $5.1 million. Paramount’s “Bad Apples” bowed in eighth position with an opening weekend of $658,468. Trafalgar Releasing captured ninth place with the rollout of “Transformers: 40th Anniversary Event,” taking $585,683. “Insidious: Out of the Further,” distributed by Sony, rounded out the top 10 in its fifth week, taking $263,374 for a running total of $10.5 million.

In specialized release, Mubi’s “Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma” lifted its running cumulative total to $1.3 million. Mubi also launched Garth Jennings’ documentary “Pulp: What Do You Do for an Encore?” with a special one-night-only live broadcast Q&A featuring frontman Jarvis Cocker and Jennings hosted from Picturehouse Central. The Friday event generated $98,392 from 51 locations, with weekend encore screenings lifting the title’s overall haul to $150,455.

Looking ahead to the upcoming theatrical frame, mid-week programming begins with National Theatre Live presenting “The Misanthrope,” followed by Paramount launching David Ayer’s action thriller “Heart of the Beast,” starring Brad Pitt and J.K. Simmons, across 300+ locations.

A heavy slate of new titles and restorations arrives on Friday. Wide and saturation rollouts across 300+ locations include Universal’s “Sense and Sensibility.” Neon is opening Na Hong-Jin’s thriller “Hope,” starring Hwang Jung-min, Zo In-sung, Hoyeon, Taylor Russell, Alicia Vikander, and Michael Fassbender, across 100+ locations.

Specialized and limited debuts opening across 25+ screens include Mubi’s release of Nicolas Winding Refn’s “Her Private Hell,” starring Sophie Thatcher and Charles Melton; BUFF Studios’ “Shadows of Beirut”; and Dartmouth Films’ nature documentary “North Sea, Nature Untamed,” directed by Mark Verkerk. Additional specialized and platform offerings include Sony’s “Rehearsals for a Revolution”, MetFilm Distribution’s release of Ross McElwee’s “Remake,’ Blue Finch Film Releasing’s “Boorman and the Devil”, and Metis Films’ “Babystar”.

Family and international releases opening Friday include Vue Lumière’s double bill “We’re Going on a Bear Hunt + The Tiger Who Came to Tea”, Dreamz Entertainment’s Indian title “Meesaya Murukku 2,” Bakrania Media’s “The Vvaan” and “Mitrata”. Disney is opening “Avengers: Endgame Encore” and Studiocanal is bowing the 40th anniversary release of Michael Mann’s “Manhunter.”

title: Business Culture Podcaster Sammi Cohen Is Launching Social Commerce Network (SCN), a Livestreamed News Show Inspired by TBPN and Aimed at Being a Next-Gen CNBC
summary: Sammi Cohen has hundreds of thousands of followers who tune in to her podcast focused on the intersection of business, tech and culture — and she thinks they’re hungry for a live dose of her brand of news and analysis. Next month, Cohen is launching Social Commerce Network (SCN), a digital-first business news network livestreamed […]
content:
Sammi Cohen has hundreds of thousands of followers who tune in to her podcast focused on the intersection of business, tech and culture — and she thinks they’re hungry for a live dose of her brand of news and analysis.

Next month, Cohen is launching Social Commerce Network (SCN), a digital-first business news network livestreamed across YouTube, X, TikTok and Instagram. SCN will broadcast three times per week (on Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays) from 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. Pacific. The show will feature a mix of news and interviews with CEOs and other business folks spanning consumer businesses, tech and fintech, retail, CPG, beauty and the creator economy.

Cohen will be joined as a co-host on SCN by Alaina Hartley, who is an ex-principal at VC firm Greycroft and a former Bain & Co. consultant who now heads her own consumer-brands consultancy, Santa Monica-based Dream Hunter.

Popular on Variety

SCN will officially launch on Oct. 6. The show will be shot in a new studio in Los Angeles’ Sawtelle neighborhood.

“Think CNBC for the generation that gets their news on their phone,” Cohen told Variety. “It’s a news show for the generation that is getting their news on social media.”

Cohen has built an audience of over 500,000 followers across digital platforms, including 250,000 on Instagram and 107,000 on YouTube. She produces short-form video and hosts the weekly podcast “Social Currency,” in which she conducts interviews with CEOs. Cohen said she’s going to continue producing the weekly podcast as well along with the thrice-weekly SCN shows. “It’s gonna be a lot!” she said.

For each of SCN’s broadcasts, the plan is for the first half of the show to cover the latest breaking news, with the second half comprising short-form interviews with CEOs and decisionmakers, “the people in the conversations we’re talking about,” Cohen said.

Another touchstone for Cohen is TBPN, the Technology Business Programming Network, which streams a daily talk show focused on Silicon Valley and Wall Street. TBPN was acquired this spring by OpenAI, whose execs see the show as promoting a “constructive” dialog with leaders about the future of AI.

“I think what TBPN has done was brilliant,” Cohen said. “They knew exactly what their target audience was and created a media platform to serve this audience.”

But Cohen expects the viewers of SCN to be more female skewing, according to Cohen: She said her followers are roughly 70% women.

“We are going to be talking about the companies driving massive shifts across the landscape of consumer businesses, and interviewing the leaders of those companies,” said Cohen, with an eye on women-led enterprises.

To fund the launch of SCN, Cohen has lined up several sponsors — across tech, fintech, hospitality, creator media and marketing — but she declined to name them. “We are looking to build this show alongside our sponsors who have come on board for the first year,” said Cohen. “They are truly partners in building the show with us.”

In the first two months, Cohen is going to be “hyper-focused on what our audience looks like,” and what kind of coverage they want to see going forward.

Why is she launching SCN now? “It is such an exciting time in the media landscape right now. My take on the industry is, as all forms of communication become automated, people are yearning for a human touch in media, and there’s nothing more human than live,” she said, adding that SCN producers will incorporate live feedback and questions from viewers for the show’s hosts. In addition, said Cohen, “we are seeing this incredible opportunity for creators like me to make their own media businesses.”

title: Channing Tatum Calls Rumors He Has a Burner Instagram Account ‘F—ing Hilarious’: ‘Can’t Believe Y’all Think This Is What I’m Doing With My Free Time’
summary: No, Channing Tatum is not running an Instagram burner account to troll his ex Zoë Kravitz — but he does find the idea pretty funny. “Yo I truly can’t believe y’all think this is what I’m doing with my free time,” Tatum wrote on his Instagram Story on Monday night after days of fan speculation. […]
content:
No, Channing Tatum is not running an Instagram burner account to troll his ex Zoë Kravitz — but he does find the idea pretty funny.

“Yo I truly can’t believe y’all think this is what I’m doing with my free time,” Tatum wrote on his Instagram Story on Monday night after days of fan speculation. “Fuckin hilarious.”

Tatum’s response comes after rumors circulated that he may be behind the Instagram account @bidness_nonya, which fans noticed had been leaving snarky comments on posts about Kravitz and her fiancé Harry Styles. Things escalated when a screenshot allegedly showed Tatum as the account’s only follower, leading to the “Magic Mike” actor’s statement.

“Also, why would I follow a burner account if I didn’t want people to connect me to it?” Tatum continued in his Story post. “Wtf come on. But if I really need to say it, I only have one IG account @channingtatum.”

Popular on Variety

Some fans have floated the theory that @bidness_nonya could be a former Tatum fan account that changed its name, hence explaining Tatum’s follow.

Tatum and Kravitz started dating in 2021 and got engaged in 2023 before ending their relationship the next year. Kravitz was first linked to pop star Styles in August 2025, and in April of this year it was reported that the two were engaged.

As it turns out, Tatum doesn’t seem to have much free time, with several high-profile projects on his docket. He’s been busy promoting his critically acclaimed indie film “Josephine” — which is set to hit theaters on Nov. 20 — and also has blockbuster “Avengers: Doomsday” coming up in December, in which he reprises his “Deadpool & Wolverine” character Gambit. Plus, he’s in production on “Isle of Man,” a drama about the annual motorcycling race event that he’s also producing alongside Brad Pitt.

title: Goodfellas’ CEO Vincent Maraval Says Michel Hazanavicius Cut Eight Days of Production on WWI Film ‘The Third Hand’ by Using AI
summary: Vincent Maraval, the veteran CEO of major French sales-production company Goodfellas, spoke about the effects of AI in the industry while taking part in San Sebastián’s fifth edition of ots Creative Investors’ Conference, co-organized with CAA Media Finance. Asked by CAA’s Roeg Sutherland how the new technology is changing his processes, Maraval cited how AI […]
content:
Vincent Maraval, the veteran CEO of major French sales-production company Goodfellas, spoke about the effects of AI in the industry while taking part in San Sebastián’s fifth edition of ots Creative Investors’ Conference, co-organized with CAA Media Finance. Asked by CAA’s Roeg Sutherland how the new technology is changing his processes, Maraval cited how AI cut eight days of production on a major scene of “The Third Hand,” the latest film by Oscar-winning “The Artist” director Michel Hazanavicius.

Goodfellas recently launched sales at TIFF on the latest by Hazanavicius, which just wrapped production. The film follows a young French soldier wounded in battle in WWI, who then wakes up in the laboratory of a mad scientist who grafted a German hand onto his abdomen. The cast features Bérénice Bejo, Rebecca Marder and François Civil.

Popular on Variety

“[The film] starts on the battlefield in the First World War,” said Maraval. “Without AI, it’s ten days of shooting. With it, it’s two days.” When confronted by Sutherland about the loss of jobs this shrinkage might have caused, the exec affirmed “it’s the director’s choice,” and said new technology is making it possible for filmmakers to tell stories they wouldn’t otherwise have access to telling. The Frenchman brought up Oscar-winning animated film “Flow” as an example, saying director Gints Zilbalodis animated the film on his computer, and “without the software, that would have been impossible for him to tell that story.”

“If we use AI to open our creativity and imagination, it will help,” added Maraval, saying the technology might also make films “more profitable.”

On the subject of profitability, the French exec said the industry is currently more reliant on private equity than the older model of securing pre-sales. “More and more films are financed by private equity,” he said. “So we try to do a mix of pre-sales and some equity for countries which are difficult to sell.” Maraval also said they used to fully fund films from pre-sales at Goodfellas, but they don’t do that anymore, as it’s not only very “complicated” to do so in the current landscape, but there is also “more money from outside people who want to invest in cinema.”

Commenting on the healthy U.S. box office for 2026, Maraval said: “There is money in cinema, there is an economy, there is a dynamic, and our job is trying to combine these dynamics to find the solutions.”

Another major market change is the focus on localized markets. Maraval spoke about the fact that local market share has increased exponentially in the last year, with audiences eager to consume films made by local filmmakers, in their local language, and that reflect burning issues in their countries. The exec emphasized how Goodfellas is currently doubling down on international talent, recently having worked with several Spanish filmmakers, including “La Bola Negra” mavericks Los Javis.

Vincent Maraval at San Sebastián

Maraval decided to invest in the film after hearing from long-time collaborators at both San Sebastián and Movistar Plus about the Spanish duo. This, he said, speaks to a personal shift for him: delegating more, listening to his team more, and letting the younger generation at Goodfellas inform him about up-and-coming talent and trends. “I was totally auteur-driven, but I learned different things from my film. Being auteur-driven was easy. When you do Kore-eda, Mungiu, Dardennes, it’s very easy to do estimates,” he noted, before adding that Goodfellas became involved in Genki Kawamura’s “Exit 8” after a member of his team alerted him of the potential of the video game adaptation. “Without this new generation in the office, I’d have missed that film.”

Speaking about the current state of the industry and what might loom in the near future, Maraval said: “Every news we have is depressing.” “In France, we are on the verge of having an extreme right-wing [government]. We already have city halls cutting all the cultural subsidies. If we look at that, we can freak out, but we go somewhere else.”

“The beauty of cinema is that it takes place in the whole world,” he added. “This year, we haven’t done one French film. We’ve done many Spanish films. We go somewhere else, and that will push us to discover new talent. The rest of the world is depressing, and it’s scary to see. But local cinema in each country is becoming more powerful; people don’t want to see foreign films anymore, and that’s part of this political climate. We know we are in the business of exception, and the rest is depressing.”

title: MIPCOM Bets On Creators, Brands & AI As International TV Business Readies For Cannes Get-Together
summary: MIPCOM boss Lucy Smith wants the world to know that October in Cannes is now about more than buying and selling TV programs. “Our biggest challenge is changing the perception,” she says, with this year’s event just weeks away. “You don’t come to MIPCOM just for your distribution deals anymore. You’re coming because you’ve got […]
content:
MIPCOM boss Lucy Smith wants the world to know that October in Cannes is now about more than buying and selling TV programs.

“Our biggest challenge is changing the perception,” she says, with this year’s event just weeks away. “You don’t come to MIPCOM just for your distribution deals anymore. You’re coming because you’ve got to find valuable IP, or you want to find out more about what’s going on in branded entertainment, or you’re looking at what’s happening in vertical drama or AI.”

Distribution remains the spine of MIPCOM, but as the international TV industry has changed, so has its biggest annual get-together. “We are a marketplace, but it’s not just a buy-and-sell market anymore,” Smith says.

That wider remit for MIPCOM means embracing the creator economy, brand partnerships and tech.

Watch on Deadline

Put simply, it had to change to stay relevant. Consolidation and industry shifts are impacting its core distribution business. For example, Warner Bros. and Paramount may have separate stands and spaces in Cannes this year, but that is unlikely to be the case when MIPCOM 2027 kicks off. The same is true of Banijay and All3Media.

The medium-sized and small distributors, meanwhile, are feeling the pinch. Acquisition execs still attend MIPCOM in healthy numbers, but often with reduced buying power as their budgets come under pressure.

Smith’s first MIPCOM was in 2006 and she now runs the market, which is organized by RX France. She says: “We evolve with the changes in the industry. We came out of probably ‘24 thinking, ‘This whole industry is just changing so much, and there’s less funding from traditional sources, so what does all that mean?’”

The change under her leadership is visible. First, there was a heavy push into co-production and FAST channels, and then into brands and the creator economy.

“We really wanted to make sure we were bringing more of the creative conversations around funding and IP. That was the first step, and then we brought the MIP Innovation Lab, so we could address streaming in a broader way.

“And then, the big push had to be the creator economy.”

YouTube had its biggest-ever presence at MIPCOM in 2025. It will be even more visible this time. Smith says partnering with the Google-owned company was “the right way to really make a mark and to say MIPCOM would be focusing and pivoting to the creator economy.”



This year, Dhar Mann Studios kicks off MIPCOM, with a pre-market headline session on Sunday, before proceedings start in earnest on Monday. Powerhouse digital producer Mann and DMS CEO Sean Atkins will jointly keynote.

“We all know that you know creator-led businesses are reshaping the global media landscape and we knew that that was that was something we needed to address,” Smith says. “We were getting calls from studios saying, ‘Hey, we want to meet all these creator-led businesses.’ And these businesses are really at that intersection of creators, brands and branded entertainment.”

Having partnered with BrandStorytelling last year, RX France launches MIP BrandWorks this time to cover off its branded entertainment activity, with denstsu the headline partner.

“We want to become the home of branded entertainment because we see ourselves as the gateway to the global entertainment content and media business. If you want to be working in content, and obviously brands need to be embedded in content to be culturally relevant, this is where you come and do that.”

Artificial intelligence is also on the menu. A new conference and market will run under the MIP AI Entertainment Forum banner, with Versos AI and Protégé the partners.

“Companies involved in AI and entertainment have a specific need to be part of the content industry conversations,” Smith says about the reason for launching the new forum.

“You’ve got the studios and producers, the production side of things, you’ve got the workflow piece, and you’ve got the licensing part; those will be the pillars.”

While the focus is shifting, MIPCOM’s USP remains bringing a critical mass of people together. In a world of Zoom meetings and with pressure on travel budgets, the numbers are not as big as in yesteryear, but no other international TV event gathers 10,000 people.

“We know that bringing people together at one time in one place gives them the opportunity to work together on what these new businesses are,” Smith says. “We wanted to bridge the gap in the conversations between traditional media companies, who remain hugely important, and these newer creator-led studios.”

Glitz and glamor are in the DNA of Cannes. The film festival and Cannes Lions lean into that with starry photocalls and A-lister parties. MIPCOM has the same setting and its own share of photo moments, but as it expands its focus, the event is still really all about dealmaking.

“If you really want to do business and understand these new ways of doing business, this is where it’s going to be happening, and this is where things will start moving forward,” Smith says.

title: ‘Gangs Of London’ Producers Suing Vice, Claiming They Are Owed $20M From Sale Of Pulse Films
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Thomas Benski and Marisa Clifford, founders of Gangs of London producer Pulse Films, are suing Vice Media, claiming they are owed more than $20 million. Vice took a majority stake in Pulse Films in 2016 before acquiring Benski and Clifford’s remaining 22% shareholding in December 2021 for $10M in cash and $43.24M in loan […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Thomas Benski and Marisa Clifford, founders of Gangs of London producer Pulse Films, are suing Vice Media, claiming they are owed more than $20 million.

Vice took a majority stake in Pulse Films in 2016 before acquiring Benski and Clifford’s remaining 22% shareholding in December 2021 for $10M in cash and $43.24M in loan notes. Soon after, Vice ran into serious financial difficulty, with Benski and Clifford alleging that the company failed to pay loan notes totalling $20.4M, breaking the terms of their sale agreement.

The producers — who exited Pulse in 2022 — claimed that they were persuaded not to exercise their contractual rights by former Vice executives, who they accuse of making fraudulent misrepresentations about the company’s financial health and failed sale to Antenna Group.

Vice Group entered Chapter 11 bankruptcy in May 2023. Three months later, a consortium of former lenders — led by Fortress Investment Group, Soros Fund Management and Monroe Capital — acquired the company after a bankruptcy auction.

Watch on Deadline

Vice Media’s position is that Benski and Clifford’s allegations are baseless and lacking in evidence. The company intends to vigorously defend its position.

Details of the dispute emerged for the first time in a UK High Court ruling earlier this month, during which Benski and Clifford failed in their efforts to get Vice to disclose thousands of documents relating to their grievance.

Judge Peter MacDonald Eggers dismissed Benski and Clifford’s pre-action disclosure application, but did not reach any conclusions on the merits of their case. Deadline understands that the producers will continue to pursue action against Vice and are currently assessing their legal options. The duo, who now run Magna Studios, declined to comment.

A Vice Media spokesperson said: “Vice Media is pleased to note that the London High Court has dismissed an application for pre-action disclosure by Thomas Benski and Marissa Clifford in relation to allegations concerning events prior to Vice Media’s Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2023.

“Those allegations are groundless. In dismissing the application, the court relied on the vague, inconsistent and unsatisfactory way in which the allegations have been advanced. We will continue robustly to defend any claim, to the extent it is pursued.”

Benski and Clifford’s pre-action disclosure application named four defendants, including Pulse Films and Nancy Dubuc, the former CEO of Vice Media. Pulse Films’ intellectual property, including Sky series Gangs of London, now sits under Vice Studios.

Summarizing Benski and Clifford’s claims, Judge Peter MacDonald Eggers wrote that they have “advanced serious allegations of fraudulent misrepresentation and unlawful means conspiracy against the respondents [at Vice]. In particular, the applicants’ case is that they were induced not to exercise valuable contractual enforcement rights by alleged repeated and false assurances by the respondents as to the valuation, solvency and an imminent sale of the Vice Group.”

He continued: “Whether the allegations of fraud and conspiracy can be established will be an issue in any substantive proceedings which may be issued by the applicants in respect of their claim and will turn on the respondents’ knowledge about the Vice Group’s financial position and the failure of the sale process at the time they were allegedly giving assurances to the applicants.”

The judgment added: “The respondents deny the allegations of fraud and conspiracy, which they state are couched in ‘unacceptably nebulous terms, based on unwarranted inferences, and without any sufficient evidential foundation.'”

Vice’s position is that its executives were not obliged to keep Benski and Clifford abreast of the company’s financial position and that they dealt with duo with “honesty and integrity” at “all times.”

title: ‘Prima Facie’ Trailer: ‘Wicked’ Actress Cynthia Erivo Stars As Hotshot Lawyer In Adaptation Of Hit Stage Play
summary: Sony Pictures has dropped the official trailer for Prima Facie starring Wicked Oscar-nominated actress Cynthia Erivo as hotshot young barrister Tessa whose personal life and career unravel after she is brutally sexually assaulted by a person in her law world circle. The process of seeking justice is given extra weight by the fact that she […]
content:
Sony Pictures has dropped the official trailer for Prima Facie starring Wicked Oscar-nominated actress Cynthia Erivo as hotshot young barrister Tessa whose personal life and career unravel after she is brutally sexually assaulted by a person in her law world circle.

The process of seeking justice is given extra weight by the fact that she has a track record in defending men charged with sexual assault. What she lives through as the accuser shakes her belief in the judicial system that was once the core of her identity.

The feature, directed by Susanna White (The Buccaneer, Andor), has just world premiered at TIFF and is set for a theatrical in the UK and Ireland on November 13. U.S. Distribution has yet to be announced, with UTA Independent Film Group and CAA Media Finance co-repping sales.

The feature is adapted from Suzie Miller‘s one-woman play Prima Facie which took the theater world by storm with Jodie Comer in the lead role. The production won Olivier Awards for the West End production including Best Actress for Comer, who then won a Tony Award for her performance on Broadway.

“I read the script, and then fell in love with the script because I loved the grey area that it dealt with,” Erivo told the Deadline Studio at TIFF.

“That Tessa wasn’t a straightforward human being. That she was complex in many, many different ways, and that she had a hand in the law. That she was having to deal with, and that that law then was dealt upon her. The navigation of all that for me was a really interesting thing to have to play and to have to deal with, and I saw it as a challenge and thought, well, I think this might be a good challenge to face.”

title: ‘The Gentlemen’ Star Chanel Cresswell Boards Netflix’s ‘The Lords’ Day’

Cresswell plays Freddy’s wife Tammy in fellow Netflix UK series The Gentlemen and has a wealth […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Chanel Cresswell, star of This is England and The Gentlemen, has boarded Netflix‘s upcoming series The Lords’ Day.

The BAFTA-winning star will play an as-yet-unrevealed role in the high-stakes political thriller starring Damson Idris in the lead role.

Cresswell plays Freddy’s wife Tammy in fellow Netflix UK series The Gentlemen and has a wealth of other big credits to her name.

She won a BAFTA for he performance in Shane Meadows and Jack Thorne’s This is England ’90 and appeared in all three of those hit Channel 4 mini-series’. Other shows include Vardy v Rooney: A Courtroom Drama, in which she played Coleen Rooney, Sherwood, and Power: The Downfall of Huw Edwards.

Starring Harry Lawtey, Arsema Thomas, Sophie Willan, Gemma Whelan and Timothy Spall alongside Idris (Snowfall), the adaptation of the Michael Dobbs book from Doctor Who make Bad Wolf follows Harry Jones, a British secret service agent at the center of a crisis at the heart of British politics. As with Cresswell’s, the other roles are being kept hush hush for now.

Watch on Deadline

The Lords’ Day logline reads: “On the State Opening of Parliament, British spy Harry Jones (Idris) finds himself inside the iconic building amidst a lockdown. As the siege escalates, loyalties are tested and selfless sacrifices are made, leading to a desperate fight for survival where not everyone will emerge alive. Can Harry use his skills and training to be the country’s saviour?”

title: Piers Morgan To Sue Princess Diana’s Brother Over “Bulls***” Claims In His Bombshell Memoir: “Why Should We Believe Anything In This Book?”
summary: Piers Morgan is on the warpath over Swan Song, the bombshell memoir from Charles Spencer, brother of the late Princess Diana. Spencer’s book has dominated the headlines in the UK for days following his explosive allegation that King Charles III said Diana would soon be forgotten in the aftermath of her death. Morgan drew attention […]
content:
Piers Morgan is on the warpath over Swan Song, the bombshell memoir from Charles Spencer, brother of the late Princess Diana.

Spencer’s book has dominated the headlines in the UK for days following his explosive allegation that King Charles III said Diana would soon be forgotten in the aftermath of her death.

Morgan drew attention to another section of Spencer’s book, in which the Earl claimed that Morgan published “intrusive” images of Diana in a gym while he was editor of The Daily Mirror. “I come across in the despicable manner imaginable,” Morgan said of Spencer’s book. “There’s just one problem — it’s all bulls***. And very easy bulls*** for me to prove it.”

Deadline has contacted Swan Song‘s publisher, Penguin Michael Joseph, for comment.

Watch on Deadline

Speaking on his YouTube show Piers Morgan Uncensored, the former CNN anchor continued: “The photographs, which he says that I published, were printed by The Sunday Mirror on November 7, 1993. I joined The Daily Mirror in October 1995. In fact, at the time of the gym pictures, I was doing a showbiz column on The Mirror’s arch rival, The Sun.”

'It's all bullsh*t… you'll be hearing from my lawyers.'



BREAKING: Piers Morgan plans to take legal action against Earl Spencer over “fabricated inaccuracies” made about him in his bombshell book on Diana.



Watch more 👇



📺 https://t.co/ZWOoVI5C3O@piersmorgan pic.twitter.com/3w66CTrwZc — Piers Morgan Uncensored (@PiersUncensored) September 21, 2026

Morgan added that Spencer had printed “fabricated inaccuracies” that strike “at the heart of his credibility.” He said: “If Earl Spencer can be so incredibly defamatorily wrong about such basic facts involving me, well why should we believe anything else that he puts in this book?”

Morgan then addressed Spencer directly. “You will be hearing, and your publishers, from my lawyers because I would like the complete lie you have published about me and those photographs to be removed from your book. And I would like a donation to be made to the King’s Trust for the damage that you have caused with your lie.”

In his book, Spencer recalled a conversation he had with King Charles in 1997 over whether Princes William and Harry should walk behind the coffin of Diana ahead of her funeral. Spencer said his reservations were met with a “stream of anger” from Charles.

He writes that the then Prince “unleashed down the phone what I have always taken to be his pent-up contempt for Diana, and his horror that the world was so bowled over by her death. ‘Rest assured,’ he hissed, ‘we’ll forget her soon enough.’”

In response, Buckingham Palace said last week: “While we do not comment on books as a matter of principle, His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and colour memory in ways others do not recognise, even many years after such a loss.”

title: Queer Horror Explored in ECAM Incubator Title ‘The Unmoving Hands’
summary: Among the five Madrid Film School (ECAM) Incubator titles this year comes “The Unmoving Hands” (“Las manos quietas”) from Barcelona-based Victor Diago, who describes his project as a “queer horror story about desire, love and the unstoppable urge to let oneself be swallowed by that abyss.” The horror thriller follows Hector, who roams the streets […]
content:
Among the five Madrid Film School (ECAM) Incubator titles this year comes “The Unmoving Hands” (“Las manos quietas”) from Barcelona-based Victor Diago, who describes his project as a “queer horror story about desire, love and the unstoppable urge to let oneself be swallowed by that abyss.”

The horror thriller follows Hector, who roams the streets of Barcelona seeking young men for his father, known as the Doctor, who is 140 years old and finally feeling the weight of his years. The Doctor feeds off these youth who come willingly to bask in his power and enjoy the illusion of being loved. Anxious to save his father, Hector is a ready accomplice until Bilal appears, who he falls in love with and tries to save from the fate of the others.

“The victims don’t see themselves as victims. They willingly, so to speak, go into the wolf’s den. They know what they are and what they will become – and they want to become that.”

Popular on Variety

“At the heart of the script lies an extraction system: powerful men who consume the vital energy of the young men who lack it,” he said, describing it as a “direct allegory of late capitalism.”

The setting, Barcelona’s sketchy El Raval neighborhood, is pivotal to the story. “El Raval is a space with a specific political history. A neighborhood of immigration, marginalization and coexistence between cultures. The characters who inhabit it are the populations that the city expels to its margins while consuming them as fuel for itself,” Diago explained.

Given its setting, the film will feature an international cast with dialogue in Catalan, Spanish, French and Arabic. “We’ve always talked about the film having a kind of Tower of Babel feel, with different cultures and languages mixed together. That gives us flexibility when looking for international partners and we’re now focused on finding co-producers who can join us in both the development and production stages,” said its producer-executive producer Andrés Mellinas.

“The film has a sense of happiness and lightness, so you understand why these people are together and why they’re having such a good time. But gradually, something starts to nag at you: there’s clearly something wrong, and something horrible is going to happen. We wanted to play with that tension rather than immediately presenting a world of predators and victims, or good guys and bad guys, and instead explore the gray areas. And all of this unfolds in a completely surreal world inhabited by vampires,” Diago noted.

According to Mellinas, the project is in an advanced development stage, having passed through various programs, including the Crossroads Co-Production Forum in Thessaloniki, Greece and the Mediterranean Film Institute script lab last year. It already has a berth on Spanish streaming platform Filmin, which it got during the ECAM forum.

After securing federal and regional funds, they hope to lock in regional and national television support.

According to Mellinas, they’re also working on a short film based in the universe of the movie. “We are using that as a proof of concept, but also as a way of financing the movie itself.”

title: El Sol Ermitaño Launches at San Sebastián Festival With WIP Title ‘Lovers Go Home’ (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Colombia’s Federico Durán, long associated with Rhayuela Films (“Alias María”) where he remains a shareholder, has officially launched his new company El Sol Ermitaño at the San Sebastian Film Festival where the first of its slate, “Lovers Go Home!” participates at the festival’s pix-in-post program, WIP LatAm. Directed by Juan Sebastián Mesa (“The Nobodies”), the […]
content:
Colombia’s Federico Durán, long associated with Rhayuela Films (“Alias María”) where he remains a shareholder, has officially launched his new company El Sol Ermitaño at the San Sebastian Film Festival where the first of its slate, “Lovers Go Home!” participates at the festival’s pix-in-post program, WIP LatAm.

Directed by Juan Sebastián Mesa (“The Nobodies”), the drama follows the virtual relationship between a webcam model living in Medellín who develops an unlikely relationship with a U.S. war veteran. It stars Ángela Cano (“One Hundred Years of Solitude”) and Dave Dewar, and is a co-production involving El Sol Ermitaño and Rhayuela Films (Colombia), Potenza Producciones (Spain), Dublin Films (France) and Camera Oscura (Canada).

“That El Sol Ermitaño’s first major international showcase is none other than San Sebastián is both a confirmation and a consolidation of the experience. ‘Lovers Go Home!’ began as a simple, almost intimate idea that has grown by bringing together talent and territories, resulting in a four-country co-production between Colombia, Canada, Spain and France. Seeing it receive increasingly significant recognition fills me with enormous pride,” said Durán, who joins Sebastián Mesa and producers Carlo D’Ursi and David Hurst at the drama’s WIP presentation.

Popular on Variety

“El Sol Ermitaño means looking outward without losing sight of our own territory. Our team has deep roots in Medellín, where I made my first feature film 27 years ago, and where we are shooting several productions this year. This is fundamental to our philosophy, as we define ourselves as an associative company, working from the local toward the global. That is why we currently have co-production projects with France, Spain, Canada, Chile, Brazil, Argentina and Mexico, with sales potential and recognition projected worldwide,” he told Variety.

“Co-production is the best way to ensure that Ibero-American cinema can be seen in our own countries,” Durán said in previous interviews.

The project has received support from Colombia’s FDC, Ibermedia, Spain’s ICAA, Nouvelle-Aquitaine in France, Telefilm Canada and SODEC in Canada. Its development trajectory has also included Carolina Foundation Screenwriting Workshop, the Chalet Mauriac residency and Cinéma en Développement at the Toulouse Film Festival.

“Lovers Go Home!” screens on Tuesday, Sept. 22 at the Tabakalera and is among several other feature films in the new company’s pipeline.

On October 29, “The Awakening” (“El Despertar”), the posthumous film by Jaime Osorio Márquez, will be released theatrically in Colombia by Cinecolor following its screenings at the Guadalajara, Sitges and BIFF film festivals.

Produced in association with RCN Estudios and co-produced by Rhayuela Films, the supernatural thriller stars Claudio Cataño (“One Hundred Years of Solitude”), Andrea Olaya, Alejandro Buitrago, Héctor Sánchez and Carlos Mariño. Its sales agent Latido Films has already reported multiple sales worldwide.

Also in post is “La Unión,” the debut feature of Catalan director Cordelia Alegre, which has recently wrapped. The project is a co-production with Rara Colectivo Audiovisual (Colombia), Dos Soles Media and WKND (Spain).

El Sol Ermitaño’s slate includes fiction series and feature films in development with Ibero-American creators that include Matías Rojas-Valencia, Carlos Mariño, Rodrigo Triana, Jorg Hiller, Andrés Borda and OpenVizor, among others.

The 74th San Sebastian Film Festival runs Sept. 18-26.

title: ‘Paper Tiger’ and ‘Musk’ Documentary Among 2026 Santa Fe International Film Festival Lineup (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: The Santa Fe International Film Festival (SFIFF) has announced this year’s lineup, which will open with Robert Burnett’s “In Memoriam,” starring Marc Maron, and close with James Gray’s “Paper Tiger,” starring Adam Driver and Miles Teller. Taking Place Oct. 14-19 in Santa Fe, N.M., the festival’s Centerpiece program will feature Peter Farrelly’s “I Play Rocky” […]
content:
The Santa Fe International Film Festival (SFIFF) has announced this year’s lineup, which will open with Robert Burnett’s “In Memoriam,” starring Marc Maron, and close with James Gray’s “Paper Tiger,” starring Adam Driver and Miles Teller.

Taking Place Oct. 14-19 in Santa Fe, N.M., the festival’s Centerpiece program will feature Peter Farrelly’s “I Play Rocky” and Martin McDonagh’s “Wild Horse Nine,” which stars John Malkovich, Sam Rockwell, Steve Buscemi, Mariana di Girolamo, Ailín Salas, Tom Waits and Parker Posey.

“This year’s program embodies the mandate of our festival — to ensure both established and emerging filmmakers are given the opportunity to tell stories that inspire, challenge and connect with audiences,” said Jacques Paisner, the artistic director of SFIFF.

Popular on Variety

Alex Gibney’s Elon Musk documentary, “Musk,” will also be featured at the festival, alongside Nanette Burstein’s “Carl Sagan: We Are Made of Star Stuff,” Danny Boyle’s “Ink” and Ava DuVernay’s “14th.” Simon Stone’s “Elsinore” with Andrew Scott and Olivia Colman will be featured at The Spotlight presentation.

SFIFF will also include the Out of Competition program, which highlights international narrative features and documentaries, including Cristian Mungiu’s “Fjord” and Noah Segan’s “The Only Living Pickpocket in New York.” The Competition program showcases the new generation of international filmmakers across narrative and documentary films, such as Ali Asgari’s “A Bit of Light” and Jérémy Comte’s “Paradise.”

The Special Screenings program will feature “Major Barbara” and “Our Effed Up World,” while the New Mexico program spotlights four films showcasing the state and its communities. Actress and singer Pam Grier will be awarded the Lifetime Achievement Award, and actor Zahn McClarnon will receive the Visionary Award.

title: BookTok Sensation Quan Millz Signs With Verve (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Verve has signed Quan Millz, the publishing phenom behind one of BookTok’s biggest literary empires, for representation. The agency will work with Millz to expand his catalog and audience across publishing, film, television and beyond. The self-published author has released more than 70 books, built a multimillion-dollar business outside the traditional system and grown a […]
content:
Verve has signed Quan Millz, the publishing phenom behind one of BookTok’s biggest literary empires, for representation.

The agency will work with Millz to expand his catalog and audience across publishing, film, television and beyond.

The self-published author has released more than 70 books, built a multimillion-dollar business outside the traditional system and grown a loyal following on TikTok. The author and online personality currently boasts more than 1.2 million followers and 37.3 million likes on the platform and has reached more than 300 million users over the past 12 months alone.

Among his work are the books “My Psycho Baby Daddy,” “The Coldest Thug Ever,” “Pregnant By My Mother’s Gay Husband,” “My Pastor Got A Stripper Pregnant,” “This Hoe Got Roaches In Her Crib” and “Knocked Up By An AI Love Doll From Hell.” His book “Old Thot Next Door” is described as a “ratchet psychological thriller/ urban erotic psychological thriller” by the author. His unapologetically outrageous titles are just one of the reasons Millz has become a viral sensation — though popstar Lizzo did recreate a number of his book covers for Halloween last year.

Popular on Variety

In addition to the hilarious names, the novels have received thousands of positive reviews from readers, proving he has captured a devoted Gen Z audience traditional publishing struggles to reach.

“Millz’s novels are salacious, controversial, hilarious, suspenseful and completely unapologetic,” said the company. “Blending crime, thriller, horror, satire, romance and relationship drama, he has created a literary universe where outrageous premises collide with authentic street perspective, unforgettable characters and relentless page-turning momentum.”

Millz will continue to be represented by attorney Nancy C. Prager.

title: ‘Iron Boy,’ ‘Tangles’ and ‘The Violinist’ Among Animation Is Film’s 2026 Festival Line-Up
summary: Leah Nelson’s “Tangles,” Louis Clichy’s “Iron Boy” and Ervin Han and Raúl García’s “The Violinist” are among the titles set to screen during Animation Is Film’s ninth edition. The festival will take place October 16 through 19, with the main programming taking place at TCL Chinese 6 Theaters in Hollywood, Calif. For the first time […]
content:
Leah Nelson’s “Tangles,” Louis Clichy’s “Iron Boy” and Ervin Han and Raúl García’s “The Violinist” are among the titles set to screen during Animation Is Film’s ninth edition. The festival will take place October 16 through 19, with the main programming taking place at TCL Chinese 6 Theaters in Hollywood, Calif.

For the first time in AIF history, the festival will commence with the world-first theatrical premiere of the first two episodes of Dana Terrace’s “Knights of Guinevere.”

“We’re thrilled to kick off another lively, animated weekend of the year’s very best with a special theatrical presentation of Dana Terrace’s Knights of Guinevere,” said Animation Is Film’s Director Matt Kaszanek. “Dana is the artist behind one of the most beloved animated series of this decade. So naturally, it is with otherworldly excitement that we embrace her return to showrunning with a big-screen presentation of this visionary series.”

Popular on Variety

In addition to the aforementioned titles, AIF’s lineup will include Masanao Kawajiri’s “Cherry and Virgin,” Shingo Natsume’s “Ghost – End of Night,” Nicolas Athané and Marco Nguyen’s “Jim Queen,” Sébastien Laudenbach’s “Viva Carmen!” and Louise Bagnall’s “Julián.” Also in competition is “O filho da Puta (Son of a Bitch)” from Otto Guerra, Érica Maradona, Tânia Anaya and Sávio Leite.

“Continuing our commitment alongside Animation Is Film is a wonderful opportunity to extend, in Los Angeles, the international journey of the films and talents revealed and celebrated in Annecy,” added Mickael Marin, CEO of CITIA. “We are delighted to contribute to their encounter with new audiences and to see AIF pursue, with this new edition, its essential mission in support of animation that is ever more bold, creative and free.”

In addition to a number of screenings, the festival’s lineup also includes studio presentations, retrospective screenings,filmmaker talks and works-in-progress. Audiences can expect a behind-the-scenes look at Walt Disney Animation’s upcoming “Hexed” as well as a theatrical presentation of Paramount’s “Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender, Yoshiaki “Vampire Hunter D: Bloodlust” and a look at Matt Braly’s “Clara and the Below.”

Tickets are available now at AnimationIsFilm.com.

title: “Choosin’ Texas” Sets Record For Longest-Running No. 1 Pop Single
summary: UPDATED, 10:02 AM: All Mariah Carey’s wants for Christmas this year is her record back. Ella Langley’s “Choosin’ Texas” has become the all-time Hot 100 champion with a 23rd week atop the Billboard singles chart, breaking the tie with Carey’s holiday ditty. The latter’s 22 weeks at the summit took multiple chart-year runs, making the […]
content:
UPDATED, 10:02 AM: All Mariah Carey‘s wants for Christmas this year is her record back.

Ella Langley‘s “Choosin’ Texas” has become the all-time Hot 100 champion with a 23rd week atop the Billboard singles chart, breaking the tie with Carey’s holiday ditty. The latter’s 22 weeks at the summit took multiple chart-year runs, making the Alabama native’s achievement that much more remarkable.

Here are the longest-running No. 1 hits in the Hot 100’s 68-year history:

1. “Choosin’ Texas,” Ella Langley, 2026 (23 weeks, to date)

2. “All I Want for Christmas Is You,” Mariah Carey (22 weeks, 2019-26)

Watch on Deadline

3. (tie) “A Bar Song (Tipsy),” Shaboozey (19 weeks, 2024)

3. “Old Town Road,” Lil Nas X feat. Billy Ray Cyrus(19 weeks, 2024)

5. (tie) “Last Night,” Morgan Wallen (16 weeks, 2023)

5. “Despacito,” Luis Fonsi & Daddy Yankee feat. Justin Bieber (16 weeks, 2017)

5. “One Sweet Day,” Mariah Carey & Boyz II Men (16 weeks, 1995-96)

PREVIOUSLY August 31: There’s a new queen of the Billboard Hot 100, with a small asterisk.

Ella Langley’s stone smash “Choosin’ Texas” has racked up a phenomenal 20th week at No. 1 on the U.S. pop singles chart, becoming the first non-holiday single to hit the milestone. Mariah Carey’s “All I Want for Christmas Is You” holds the overall record with 22 weeks at the summit, but that includes chart-topping runs during the past seven years.

In many if not most ways, Langley’s feat is more remarkable. “Choosin’ Texas” first reached No. 1 way back in mid-February before it was dethroned by a pair of songs the next two weeks. It then hit the top again for a week and fell back three times before losing out for three more weeks and ascending to the throne again in early July. And the single Langley sings and co-wrote with Miranda Lambert and Joybeth Taylor has been No. 1 since.

During that stretch of chart-position leapfrog, the song made runners-up of such chart behemoths as Drake, Bad Bunny, Bruno Mars, BTS, Olivia Rodrigo, Ariana Grande and Taylor Swift — twice. Here’s the seven-minute official video for “Choosin’ Texas”:

Certified at six times platinum, the track has spent 28 weeks atop Billboard’s Hot Country Songs chart since late November — one of only 32 songs ever to lead the pop and country tallies. “Choosin’ Texas” also reached No. 3 in the UK. It hails from Langley’s million-selling sophomore album Dandelion, which Columbia Records’ Sawgod imprint released on April 10.

“Choosin’ Texas” this week broke the tie with Shaboozey’s “A Bar Song (Tipsy)” and Lil Nas X’s “Old Town Road” featuring Billy Ray Cyrus, which now sit at No. 3 among all-time longest-running Hot 100 chart-toppers with 19 weeks each.

title: Janeane Garofalo Reteaming With Ben Stiller On Apple TV Comedy ‘Protective Custody’
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Janeane Garofalo, the two-time Emmy nominated actress and comedian known for her work in the likes of Wet Hot American Summer and The Larry Sanders Show, is set for a recurring role in Protective Custody, the Apple TV comedy starring and exec produced by Ben Stiller and Benicio Del Toro. Character details are being […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Janeane Garofalo, the two-time Emmy nominated actress and comedian known for her work in the likes of Wet Hot American Summer and The Larry Sanders Show, is set for a recurring role in Protective Custody, the Apple TV comedy starring and exec produced by Ben Stiller and Benicio Del Toro.

Character details are being kept under wraps. Garofalo comes to the project as a frequent collaborator of Stiller’s: She’s appeared opposite him in everything from The Ben Stiller Show to the films Reality Bites, Mystery Men, The Cable Guy and Permanent Midnight. She and Stiller even previously co-authored a New York Times bestseller, 1999’s Feel This Book: An A–Z Guide to Self-Improvement, Spiritual Supremacy, and Sexual Satisfaction.

Hailing from Mike Judge, as well as Steve Hely and Dave King, his collaborators on the Adult Swim series Common Side Effects, Protective Custody follows a disgraced financier accused of massive fraud who is thrown into protective custody, where he must navigate prison politics, salvage his reputation and confront the consequences of his actions while awaiting trial.

Watch on Deadline

The series is co-written, co-showrun and exec produced by Judge, Hely and King, with Judge also directing. As previously announced, the cast also includes Amy Sedaris, Samson Kayo and Sonny Valicenti.

Ben Silverman, Howard Owens and Rodney Ferrell are exec producing for Propagate Content, alongside Stiller and John Lesher for Red Hour, Michael Rotenberg and Oly Obst for 3 Arts Entertainment, Del Toro, Nanette Burstein and Blair Breard.

For Garofalo, the latest chapter of her career has included roles in Showtime’s Billions, TV Land’s Younger, Netflix’s Wet Hot American Summer: Ten Years Later and Comedy Central’s Broad City. Upcoming, she’ll be seen starring opposite Jack Haven in the indie thriller Grind and reprising as Heather Mooney in the Romy and Michele sequel from 20th Century Studios. She is represented by Gersh and Independent Artist Media.

title: J.K. Simmons Joins Will Poulter In Apple TV’s ‘Beat The Reaper’; Tim Van Patten To Direct & EP
summary: EXCLUSIVE: J.K. Simmons (Heart of the Beast, The Westies) is joining Will Poulter as a series regular in Apple TV’s Beat The Reaper, based on the novel of the same name by Josh Bazell. Additionally, Tim Van Patten (Masters of the Air, Boardwalk Empire) will direct the pilot and serve as executive producer on the […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: J.K. Simmons (Heart of the Beast, The Westies) is joining Will Poulter as a series regular in Apple TV‘s Beat The Reaper, based on the novel of the same name by Josh Bazell. Additionally, Tim Van Patten (Masters of the Air, Boardwalk Empire) will direct the pilot and serve as executive producer on the new series hailing from Apple Studios and New Regency.

From showrunner and executive producer Sam Catlin, Beat the Reaper follows Dr. Peter Brown (Poulter), an intern at Boston’s worst hospital, with a talent for medicine, a shift from hell, and a past he’d prefer to keep hidden. But when a patient recognizes him from his dangerous past, Brown has eight hours to elude the government, mob hitmen, quack surgeons, and a trail of dead gangsters to somehow beat the reaper.

Simmons will play Dr. Friendly, an incompetent surgeon in the book who works at the same hospital as Peter.

Watch on Deadline

Beat the Reaper is executive produced by Catlin under his overall deal with Apple TV. Arnon Milchan, Yariv Milchan, Natalie Lehmann, and Laura Delahaye will executive produce, and Rachel Toffler will co-executive produce, for New Regency.

Simmons is an Academy Award winner following his big win in 2015 for Best Supporting Actor. He received the honor for his portrayal of jazz instructor Fletcher in Whiplash. He received an Oscar nomination for bringing to life William Frawley in Aaron Sorkin’s Being the Ricardos. On the small screen, Simmons leads the series The Westies from MGM+. He will next be seen in the films Purgatory, The Prince, Heart of the Beast, and The Thing That Hurts. Simmons is represented by Gersh.

Van Patten became an Emmy Award Winner in 2012 in the category of Outstanding Director in a Drama series for his work in the Season 2 episode titled “To The Lost.” As a supervising producer, he won a group Emmy in 2010 for HBO’s The Pacific, which received the honor for Outstanding Miniseries. Additional directing credits include HBO’s The Sopranos, Apple TV’s miniseries Franklin, Netflix’s Black Mirror and Perry Mason. Van Patten is repped by CAA and Range Media Partners.

title: Original ‘Rent’ Cast To Reunite For Livestream Benefit Concert Next Month
summary: Idina Menzel, Adam Pascal, Anthony Rapp, Daphne Rubin-Vega and other cast members of Jonathan Larson’s Rent will take part in a one-night-only 30th anniversary benefit concert to be livestreamed from Broadway’s Richard Rodgers Theatre next month. The October 26 Rent, the 30th Anniversary Concert in which the musical will be performed in full with benefits […]
content:
Idina Menzel, Adam Pascal, Anthony Rapp, Daphne Rubin-Vega and other cast members of Jonathan Larson’s Rent will take part in a one-night-only 30th anniversary benefit concert to be livestreamed from Broadway‘s Richard Rodgers Theatre next month.

The October 26 Rent, the 30th Anniversary Concert in which the musical will be performed in full with benefits going to Broadway Cares/Equity Fights AIDS, will feature original cast members Menzel, Pascal, Rapp, Rubin-Vega, Wilson Jermaine Heredia and Fredi Walker as well as other performers who appeared in Rent over the years such as Nicholas Christopher, Jordan Fisher, Renée Elise Goldsberry, Jai Rodriguez, Ephraim Sykes and Aaron Tveit.

While in-person tickets are sold out, $30 livestream tickets are available. In all, more than 50 past Rent cast members and special guests will take part in the concert to benefit

Watch on Deadline

Joining the original principal cast will be original understudies and ensemble players Yassmin Alers, Gilles Chiasson, Shelley Dickinson, David Driver, Darius de Haas and Rodney Hicks. Other “alumni” performers will include Natalie Venetia Belcon, Adam Chanler-Berat, Merle Dandridge, Trey Ellett, Jose Llana, John Eric Parker and Antonique Smith.

Rent’s original director Michael Greif returns to helm the evening. More of the cast will be announced in the coming weeks. Performers are subject to change.

The show’s original music supervisor, Tim Weil, also will return, leading original Rent band members Kenny Brescia, Jeff Potter and Daniel A. Weiss, who will be joined by Steve Gelfand.

The presentation is produced by Broadway Cares/Equity Fights AIDS and Andy Jones, founder of Baseline Theatrical. Rent features a book, music and lyrics by Larson, with music arrangements by Steve Skinner.

Rent reimagines La Bohème in the AIDS-era East Village of New York City, following a tight-knit group of artists navigating love, loss and survival at the turn of a generation. The musical debuted at the New York Theatre Workshop before transferring to Broadway’s Nederlander Theatre in 1996 where it played 5,123 performances before closing September 7, 2008. The original Broadway producers were Jeffrey Seller, Kevin McCollum and Allan S. Gordon.

The livestream of Rent, the 30th Anniversary Concert is produced in collaboration with The League of Live Stream Theater.

title: Angus Sampson Signs With Buchwald & Sweeney Entertainment
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Australian actor and filmmaker Angus Sampson has signed with Buchwald and Sweeney Entertainment for representation.
