Then there is the matter of audiences, which has become an even more key aspect of financing at a time when distribution has become ever-harder to master. The producers on stage believe that the best way of tackling distribution issues is to understand what audience a project is for from its very inception, and keep that in mind through development and production.

“There is an audience that loves movies, a younger audience, too, and that is open to different authentic voices in a way five or ten years ago we wouldn’t be that confiden about,” noted StudioCanal’s Ron Halpern. “That’s a great thing for all of our local or mixed-language productions.”

“‘Obsession’ and ‘Backrooms’ are two movies that completely changed the way Hollywood is talking about films,” added De Maio. “Distributors need to bring the movie to the audience, and what’s happened with Curry [Barker] and Kane [Parsons] is that they brought their own audiences. They had a loyal following, so they were able to convert that audience, which doesn’t always convert from YouTube to cinema.”

“I think 75% of the audience for ‘Obsession’ was 18 to 34,” speculated De Maio. “That’s insane. It’s a horror movie based on YouTube IP. When we think about movies now, it’s really healthy to have a discussion about who’s the audience, how do we reach that audience, and then financially and creatively be aware of that when you’re building the project.”

Halpern said they have a “sense” of who the audience is from very early on in the building of their projects. When putting together the Andrew Garfield-Florence Pugh two-hander “We Live in Time,” Halpern’s team knew Pugh would “deliver the TikTok audience,” and she did. “If you can’t figure out your audience, then your film better be extraordinarily good.”

title: London Film Festival Industry Forum Lineup: Danny Boyle, PC Williams, Akinola Davies Jr. and More
summary: The BFI London Film Festival has revealed the full lineup for its Industry Forum. Joining the previously announced Spotlight conversations with producers James Wilson and Pippa Harris, “Ink” director Danny Boyle will be interviewed live by Matt Belloni for his “The Town” podcast and costume designer PC Williams will be in conversation with her collaborator […]
content:
The BFI London Film Festival has revealed the full lineup for its Industry Forum.

Joining the previously announced Spotlight conversations with producers James Wilson and Pippa Harris, “Ink” director Danny Boyle will be interviewed live by Matt Belloni for his “The Town” podcast and costume designer PC Williams will be in conversation with her collaborator on “My Father’s Shadow,” director Akinola Davies Jr.

The Industry Forum kicks off on Oct. 8 with a panel of cinema programmers — including Curzon’s Ben Lyndon, Picturehouse’s Carol McKay and BFI Imax’s Madeleine Mullett — reflecting on the state of U.K. movie theaters after a record-breaking spring-summer season. On Oct. 12, international producers lan Maher (“Everybody Digs Bill Evans”), Adrià Monés (“The End of It”), Dyveke Bjørkly Graver (“Fjord”) and Rodrigo Teixeira (“Paper Tiger,” “I’m Still Here”) will discuss their experiences with co-productions, funding opportunities and creative challenges with collaboration across different countries.

Popular on Variety

Other panels include one on working within archives to shape a storyline with Theo Rollason (“Queer Edward II”), Nanette Burstein (“Carl Sagan: We Are Made of Star Stuff”), Rafael Guendelman (“Az Zeeb”) and the BFI National Archive’s Simon McCallum; as well as a discussion showcasing exciting new voices in screenwriting hosted by Take Three program director Holly Daniel.

“This year’s Industry Forum brings together an exceptional group of filmmakers and industry voices, including both U.K. and international talent whose work is having a real impact on cinema around the world,” said Kristy Matheson, director of the BFI London Film Festival. “From world class producers, directors and craftspeople to programmers, writers and archivists, we’re proud to showcase the remarkable range of people shaping cinema today, while creating opportunities for the wider industry to come together, exchange ideas and build new connections.”

View the full London Film Festival Industry Forum program here.

title: Brad Pitt on the ‘Moving Experience’ of Co-Starring With a Dog in ‘Heart of the Beast’ and the State of Indie Cinema: It ’Feels as Strong as the ‘90s’
summary: Brad Pitt underlined his credentials as a dog guy in San Sebastian on Wednesday, hailing the experience of working with his “Heart of the Beast” co-star, a German Shepherd called Uber. “I did have a really moving experience with Uber,” he said at a press conference ahead of the film’s premiere. “We tried to make every […]
content:
Brad Pitt underlined his credentials as a dog guy in San Sebastian on Wednesday, hailing the experience of working with his “Heart of the Beast” co-star, a German Shepherd called Uber.

“I did have a really moving experience with Uber,” he said at a press conference ahead of the film’s premiere. “We tried to make every day a play day for him. There were times he would do things that were just amazing that were not in the script that you see in the film, and his expressions still really move me.”

Shooting in New Zealand, Pitt said “being out there with this beautiful beast was pretty special… it was really kind of beautiful. We’re out in this beautiful location. We’re wet, we’re cold, 12 hours a day. We don’t have trailers. We’re sitting out on logs, but everyone’s kind of up for the task.”

Popular on Variety

Pitt added that “when the dog would show up on set, the energy would change — like people just got a little happier, a little bit excited.”

But it wasn’t just his four-legged acting companions that Pitt praised, with the star — who also produces “Heart of the Beast” through his Plan B production company — celebrating the current state of bold independent cinema.

“I think the current setup has actually been really conducive to independent cinema in a really cool way, because more eyes are getting on these projects,” he said, adding that “it feels even as strong as in the ’90s.”

“Heart of the Beast” director David Ayer added: “There’s new pipelines of discovery out there. We have people coming in off YouTube or the internet, which has always sort of been held to the side, but now we’re seeing what I believe may be the ascent of it as we find filmmakers in that space”

Also starring J.K. Simmons and Anna Lambe, “Heart of the Beast” follows Pitt as a Special Forces veteran stranded deep in the Alaskan wilderness with his traumatized military combat dog. The film has been met with warm praise from critics, with Variety‘s review saying it was in spirit “not far removed from an old Disney movie” adding that “Pitt gives a true performance, and so does the canine actor playing his trusty companion.”

Despite “Heart of the Beast” premiering on Wednesday night in San Sebastian, Pitt has already been in town a few days to soak up the Spanish sunshine. On Tuesday a large crowd gathered outside the Maria Cristina hotel, where he reportedly spent 20 minutes signing autographs and taking selfies.

title: ‘You Crazy Thing’ Director Miia Tervo Proves That Everyone Deserves to Be Seen – and That Perfection Is Boring (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Finnish director Miia Tervo didn’t have to look far for the inspiration for her third feature “You Crazy Thing,” about Aino, a mental health nurse who’s preparing a performance with her patients for a talent competition. “My mother worked in a mental hospital for 37 years. We lived in a small village in Lapland, and […]
content:
Finnish director Miia Tervo didn’t have to look far for the inspiration for her third feature “You Crazy Thing,” about Aino, a mental health nurse who’s preparing a performance with her patients for a talent competition.

“My mother worked in a mental hospital for 37 years. We lived in a small village in Lapland, and there was only this hospital – and the forest. There was a joke that the only thing separating the nurses from the patients were the keys,” she told Variety.

“We live in a class-based society, and I could see that my mum wasn’t appreciated for her work. It felt like nobody could see her. But when people were in need, when they felt broken, she was there for them. That’s one of the main themes of the film. Do we actually see each other?”

Popular on Variety

Tervo added: “I wanted to give her this film because it’s crazy that they’re out there saving people while we walk red carpets. That’s why I give her all my awards, too.”

Arsen Sarkisiants

The upcoming film, which debuts its first-look stills, was produced by Marko Talli for Yellow Film & TV and co-produced by Paloma Production (Denmark) and Garagefilm International (Sweden).

Pihla Viitala, Adam Pålsson and Clara Dessau lead the cast that combines professional and amateur actors.

“I wanted to create a safe place where they could be themselves. The best thing about my work is that I can give them the space to shine,” she noted.

“[In the past] I didn’t have any dreams. I always thought I would die of alcoholism before turning 30 because that’s what happened to people in our village. But we weren’t victims, and my mother really enjoyed her work. She preferred being with the ‘crazy’ people because they didn’t play social games. They were free.”

While Tervo might be following her mother’s perspective – “She never believed in social hierarchies or norms” – hers is a fictional story. One that also sees Aino fall for one of her patients.

“I started thinking about how having or not having money, or having mental health problems in the family, affects identity. If identity is what we think about ourselves, then how does it affect love and loving? How does class affect how and who we love? Can you can suffer from feelings of worthlessness even if you are rich, and can you feel valuable even if you are poor?”

“At one point, I thought that just because I come from a poor family, I couldn’t love a rich person. That there’s a gap. It’s really about this triangle of class, identity and love,” said Tervo. And, again, about being seen.

“In this society, everyone wants to be seen. We think we need a special gift or talent, but with Aino, you can be seen in all your glory – whoever you are. You don’t need to be a magician or perform crazy stunts.”

Still, that doesn’t make Aino a saint.

“People who do this job have seen so much sorrow and life in all its forms. I thought: Aino actually wants to be crazy. It would liberate her, you know? When you help others, you can forget about yourself. You can escape your own issues and forget your own sadness.”

Arsen Sarkisiants

Tervo, also behind award-winning “Aurora” and “The Missile,” has always celebrated messiness in her work. Her characters misbehave and make mistakes, but she never punishes them for it.

“It’s always more interesting to see not the façade we put on but how we are in our secret lives,” she said.

“It’s not easy to talk about depression or mental health challenges, especially your own. But often, it’s precisely those vulnerable places that make people fall in love. It was always that part, the part where I’d forgotten to lock the door, that drew people in. For love to be real, you have to dare to be the mess that you actually are. Nobody wants to live with a perfect person. It’s boring.”

With “You Crazy Thing,” Tervo is no longer hiding – also when it comes to her personal struggles.

“I’m a recovering alcoholic who has been sober for many years now. I used to self-medicate my sadness and depression with alcohol. I drank because, for a while, it did what nothing else could. It put a wall between me and the reality I wanted to escape. That worked until it didn’t,” she recalled.

“Maybe this film is inviting me to dare to be seen, too. I don’t use social media, but I write about the themes of my life. One of biggest themes is wanting to live again. How do you find the will to live once you’ve lost it?”

Now, “with enough distance and therapy,” she can face all these things. Also in her films.

“Creating a dark yet warm dramedy out of painful incidents, emotions and experiences makes us wonder about the shame surrounding mental health challenges and the stigmas that come with them. Once you’ve come through something like that, you also want to feel this joie de vivre, as clichéd as it is,” she said.

“Depression can be a black sun. But, in a strange way, that black sun can also be an opportunity for change. Now, in the mornings, I sit and don’t ask for anything particular; I just give thanks.”

“For a girl who never learned how to dream, I’m now learning to appreciate this miraculous life that we have.”

title: White House Says Trump’s Ban of CNN, MS NOW and Politico Does Not Violate First Amendment: Access ‘Is a Privilege — Not a Right’
summary: White House officials are defending U.S. President Donald Trump’s ban of CNN, MS NOW and Politico, claiming that it does not violate the First Amendment. A Tuesday court filing obtained by The New York Times alleges that the news outlets had breached standards of conduct, accusing them of “trafficking in verifiable falsehoods about national security […]
content:
White House officials are defending U.S. President Donald Trump‘s ban of CNN, MS NOW and Politico, claiming that it does not violate the First Amendment.

A Tuesday court filing obtained by The New York Times alleges that the news outlets had breached standards of conduct, accusing them of “trafficking in verifiable falsehoods about national security and other issues, and publishing sensitive or classified information.”

“Access to the White House is a privilege — not a right,” the filing states, according to The New York Times. The documents also claim that the denial of access is a “preliminary matter” and the news organizations can contest the decision until Friday.

Popular on Variety

Trump announced the ban on Truth Social on Friday, writing that he was expelling the outlets from the White House “as a result of their constant ‘reporting’ FAKE NEWS.” On Monday, CNN, MS Now and Politico released a joint statement saying that they planned to sue, alleging that the ban violated the First Amendment.

“This morning, we notified the government that we are filing a lawsuit today to protect our First Amendment rights and defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports or publishes,” their statement said. “Without notice or process, the White House revoked our journalists’ credentials because it objected to our reporting. Left unchallenged, this threatens press freedom and the public’s right to independent journalism free from government interference.”

An emergency hearing will be held on Wednesday regarding the outlets’ request for a temporary court order reversing the ban. U.S. District Judge Timothy J. Kelly, who was appointed by Trump in 2017, will preside. Kelly previously ruled against Trump in 2018 when he similarly expelled CNN reporter Jim Acosta, whose credentials were restored when Kelly determined that Trump had not given him sufficient notice.

Trump’s ban of CNN, MS NOW and Politico has sent shock waves through the media industry. In an unprecedented move, ABC News, CBS News, NBC News and Fox News have all suspended pool coverage of the president in solidarity with CNN.

“The public has a vital interest in receiving accurate, independent information about its government,” the five networks said in a joint statement Monday. “No administration should restrict a news organization because it objects to its reporting.”

title: ‘Where’s Wanda’ Season 2: Watch Trailer For Apple TV’s Darkly Comic German Series From UFA Fiction
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Here’s the trailer for Season 2 of Apple TV’s German dark comedy Where’s Wanda?. The sophomore season starring Heike Makatsch (Love Actually), Axel Stein (The Vault), Lea Drinda (The Gryphon), Leo Simon and and Nikeata Thompson (Späti) debuts globally on October 21, and this is the exclusive trailer ahead of the launch. Episodes will […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Here’s the trailer for Season 2 of Apple TV‘s German dark comedy Where’s Wanda?.

The sophomore season starring Heike Makatsch (Love Actually), Axel Stein (The Vault), Lea Drinda (The Gryphon), Leo Simon and and Nikeata Thompson (Späti) debuts globally on October 21, and this is the exclusive trailer ahead of the launch. Episodes will drop weekly through December 9, as previous announced.

The UFA Fiction German-language comedy-drama picks up after the events of the first season, which saw Carlotta and Dedo Klatt (Makatsch and Stein) searching for their lost daughter Wanda (Drinda). As the season opens, Wanda is seemingly caught red-handed standing over a dead body and is hauled off to jail.

Carlotta and Dedo have to do everything in their power to prove her innocence and avoid losing her again, with their investigation taking them to the heart of their sleepy suburban town, Sundersheim.

Watch on Deadline

In the trailer we see a shaken Wanda in jail. The scene morphs back to the murder scene, as Wanda finds a body dead backstage at a funfair. As the curtains pull back, she is revealed standing over the corpse with a bloodied trophy in her hands as the audience gasps. From there, her parents hatch their crazy plan to set her free and reveal the killer.

“We end Season 1 with Wanda returning to her family, which is a great relief for them,” said Where’s Wanda? exec producer Nataly Kudiabor in an exclusive interview. “We had already announced that Wanda will be in prison in Season 2, and that has a huge impact on the family,” she said. “They have just got their daughter back, and now they have to deal with what this will do to them.

“It also affects the family’s position in Sundersheim. What are the neighbours thinking? What do the people in Sundersheim think? Is it right that their daughter is in prison? There are a lot of questions being asked.”

Sam Riley, Alexandra Maria Lara, Harriet Herbig-Matten, Gisa Flake, David Schütter, Palina Rojinski Suzanne von Borsody, Kostja Ullmann, Devid Striesow, Frederic Balonier, Sascha Geršak, Torben Liebrecht , Aaron Maldonado-Morales and Anton Dreger are also cast in Season 2.

Oliver Lansley created, written and executive produced season 2, alongside UFA Fiction co-Managing Director and executive producer Nataly Kudiabor and Oliver Ossege. The series was co-created and based on a story by Zoltan Spirandelli, though he was not involved in Season 2, we understand. Tobi Baumann and Christian Ditter.

We sat down for an exclusive interview with Kudiabor this week, who said Drinda’s titular character would be far more present in Season 2.

“We always felt that Wanda was the heart of the show, so we wanted her to return and to give her more screen time,” she said. “Lea Drinda is a fantastic actress, and this time she isn’t hidden away for several episodes – she is there from the beginning.”

Kudiabor revealed there would be “surprises” for the audience. “We love our surprises. For example, new neighbours move in: the Kimballs, played by Sam Riley and Alexandra Maria Lara, who are internationally known. They are a couple in real life, and we cast them as a couple in the show, which I think was a great idea. They bring a new layer to the series.”

She added there would be “more twists and turns,” saying: “Oliver is very good at leading the audience in one direction and then revealing something unexpected from another side. There are also lots of interesting new characters in Sundersheim whom audiences haven’t seen before.”

Kudiabor said that if Season 1 was about “the search, the neighbours and everything people were hiding in Sundersheim,” Season 2 was about “what the crisis is doing to the family and how they rebuild afterwards.”

Working with Apple TV

Where’s Wanda? was the first German-language original to come from Apple TV, with the likes of Constellation and Berlin ER following later. Prior to the show’s launch, there was a feeling within the German television production community that the global streamer’s future in Germany hinged on its success, with several privately voicing the opinion to Deadline at the time.

The Season 2 renewal was validation the dark comedy had cut through, and Kudiabor praised the collaborative nature of Apple’s execs, with UFA Fiction in regular communication with Jay Hunt’s London office throughout the process. She noted that having an English writer in Lansley was “really helpful” to the flow of the development.

“We were very excited to make Apple TV+’s first German original,” she said. “It’s great to work for a streamer with so many excellent shows. I’m a big fan of Apple’s productions, and quality is very important to them.

“They always challenge us to do our best in terms of storytelling and production value, and it’s a great experience to be challenged and to keep getting better. Sometimes you think you know best, but ultimately it’s teamwork.”

She compared the first mover experience to that of Wiedemann & Berg when it made Dark as Netflix’s debut German original.

“If you’re the first show in a market for a streamer, you have to learn how to work together,” said Kudiabor. “I imagine it was a similar experience for Netflix when it made Dark. In the second season, the process was extremely nice and easy because we already knew each other and understood how things worked. There was a lot of trust in us, which was really nice.”

German market in flux

UFA Fiction, known for the likes of the Deutschland and Ku’damm franchises, has been on a roll over recent years, with Wanda? and Prime Video YA smash Maxton Hall – The World Between Us driving its streamer slate, with the likes of Disney+ miniseries Sam – A Saxon and Netflix movie Rising High also cutting through.

However, the Fremantle-owned company could be seen as an outlier in the German production market. Last week at Seriesly Berlin, much of the chatter was about a general lack of funding outside of the global streamers, and whether international co-production could fill the gaps. With the likes of Sky Deutschland exiting the originals market in the past half-decade, things remain tough.

“Streamers and commissioners are flooded with good ideas,” said Kudiabor. “What do you need to stand out? We’re really trying to work on that. I’m not saying we achieve it all the time, but we’re giving it our best, and perhaps our work shows that this approach is working for us.”

She attributed UFA’s hot streak on “a mixture of luck, timing, having the right talent and finding the right story,” and hinted at several upcoming projects.

“At the moment, we’re working for Amazon, with two shows launching there,” she said. “We’re working with Disney and have some developments with them, and we’ve just worked with Apple. We’re also working with HBO, so there are a lot of opportunities.

“But it’s also about excellence. We’re challenging ourselves to ask, before we go out: Is this really the best story we have? Is this the best talent? Is there something else we can do before we go shopping?”

Kudiabor admitted the success of Maxton Hall, which became Prime Video’s most-watched international original series.

“The first season was amazing, but I don’t think we expected such sensational success,” she said. “I loved the second season, but wait for the third – it’s even more mind-blowing. The fans are so engaged and give their feedback through social media, which is crazy. Our main actors are now big stars, and it’s really a ride.

“It’s a once-in-a-lifetime moment. When you go to the premieres, it feels like a real event: The fans are going crazy and they really want to be part of it.”

As for the future, Kudiabor said UFA Fiction will look to work with more production companies across the Fremantle group, as TV consolidated giants look to use their assets to create co-productions.

“I’ve been speaking with colleagues in the Netherlands, for example, because our markets are quite similar and they have great shows coming out there,” said Kudiabor. “We recently had a meeting here to look for a project we could make together, so we want to develop something jointly. We’re also speaking with some UK companies.”

Meanwhile, UFA Fiction is hoping Apple sees a long-term future for Where’s Wanda?. “Creatively, we have lots of ideas, but of course I can’t speak for Apple,” said Kudiabor. “Right now, we’re just happy to be returning for a second season. We hope to excite the viewers, and then we’ll take it from there.”

title: ‘Ali G: Who Iz I?’ Writer Defends Amazon Movie Amid Outcry Over Sacha Baron Cohen’s Character Reinforcing “Harmful” Racial Stereotypes
summary: EXCLUSIVE: As the self-anointed “voice of youth” in the late 1990s, Ali G was a British cultural sensation, parroted in school playgrounds and quoted in Parliament. But nearly 30 years on, Sacha Baron Cohen has been criticized for “microwaving a relic from a generation ago” with his unexpected decision to reboot the suburban rude boy. […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: As the self-anointed “voice of youth” in the late 1990s, Ali G was a British cultural sensation, parroted in school playgrounds and quoted in Parliament. But nearly 30 years on, Sacha Baron Cohen has been criticized for “microwaving a relic from a generation ago” with his unexpected decision to reboot the suburban rude boy.

In interviews with Deadline, Black British comedians voiced dismay at Amazon MGM Studios’ upcoming film Ali G: Who Iz I?, arguing that the character is no longer associated with its roots of satirizing white men trying to adopt Black street culture. Instead, they said Ali G perpetuates racial stereotypes, diminishes the Black experience, and appropriates culture in a way that is damaging to the Black community.

Baron Cohen and Amazon MGM Studios declined to comment, but Deadline spoke with Colton Dunn, one of three Black writers who worked on Ali G: Who Iz I?, who said he did not recognize the criticisms. He argued that Baron Cohen remains faithful to Ali G’s origins, adding that the jokes target the movie’s subjects rather than Black people. “From my point of view, Ali G is not a racist character. Ali G is a tool to expose racists,” he said.

Watch on Deadline

Dunn explained: “He puts himself in the most ridiculous situations, and he doesn’t do that because he’s racist. He goes into these crazy-ass places, places where people would kill him if they knew what was going down. I don’t think he’s doing that from a racist point of view. That’s why I signed on. I wouldn’t sign on to work with somebody that I thought was racist, that’s against everything that I’ve done.”

The debate erupted after the trailer for Ali G: Who Iz I? went viral last month. Jack Black, Tom Brady and Diplo all endorsed the character’s return, but it also sparked an online campaign to get the movie shut out of British cinemas because Ali G perpetuates “harmful stereotypes.” The campaign looks set to fail (Vue is among the theater chains planning to screen Who Iz I? when Sony releases it in the UK on October 23), but its message resonated with some in the Black British comedy community.

Gina Yashere, a standup who co-created and starred in CBS comedy Bob Hearts Abishola, accused Baron Cohen of ostensibly adopting Blackface and “cosplaying” as another race. “He’s not targeting white people,” she told Deadline. “People watching that character are going to laugh because it’s a caricature of Black people.” Curtis Walker, another standup who starred in BBC series Paramount City, said he found Ali G “degrading” and “disgusting,” adding that it was “sad” that Amazon MGM Studios was backing the character, rather than Black creators.

Yashire and Walker first voiced their concerns 26 years ago, when they were interviewed by New Nation, a newspaper for Britain’s Black community. The criticisms then grew louder at the Ali G in Da House premiere in 2002, when protesters demonstrated in Leicester Square, waving placards comparing the comic creation to Al Jolson, the American entertainer who was famous for performing in Blackface.

Baron Cohen was aware of the concerns at the time, not least because Walker confronted him at an industry event. Baron Cohen told WTF with Marc Maron in 2016 that he decided not to engage publicly with the critics, even though he considered himself “vehemently against any form of racism.” He has long asserted that Ali G wants to be Black, but his true ethnicity is intentionally ambiguous. “He’s not Black. He is delusional,” he told NPR’s Fresh Air in 2009.

Yashire and Walker’s views are shared by younger Black comics in the UK. Dane Baptiste, creator of BBC shows Sunny D and Bamous, said Ali G created a “skewed idea of Blackness” in Britain, and his revival is akin to “microwaving a relic from a generation ago.” He told Deadline: “After Black Lives Matter and the brief humanization of Black people and Black creatives, it seems very dubious that we are now regressing back, not just five years, but 25 years, to bring back a character that was able to flourish because there were no accurate portrayals of Black Britishness on screen.”

Mo Gilligan, one of the UK’s most successful comedians, picked up on this theme during a recent appearance on The Louis Theroux Podcast. The BAFTA-winner said the depiction of Ali G became very “normalized” in the UK and there was a sense among some in the Black community that “you were being laughed at, not laughed with.”

Sacha Baron Cohen as Ali G

Athena Kugblenu, a BBC New Comedy Awards finalist, argued that the latest incarnation of Ali G has had to embrace more “acute” racial stereotypes, including dreadlocks and a rastacap, because his costume is no longer unusual amid the assimilation of Black culture over the past 30 years. “He’s an analogue character in a digital age,” she wrote in an Instagram post liked by fellow comics, including Living With Yourself star Aisling Bea. A source close to Baron Cohen denied that Ali G has dreadlocks in the film.

Michael Eboda, the former New Nation editor and CEO of Powerful Media, added: “There are far more serious things in the world than Ali G. It’s just something that has had its time. It was there for a minute, and now it’s just a bit sad that he’s having to rehash it.”

Colton Dunn, whose credits include Widow’s Bay and Key and Peele, found Ali G “hilarious” when he first encountered the character during high school. “We all felt we knew a guy just like Ali G. I don’t remember it being controversial at all,” he said. “I don’t know what the experience is like for the Black performers in Britain. I’m not going to speak on their experience and I respect their experience, but I also respect my experience.”

Dunn declined to comment on specific scenes or storylines, but said Baron Cohen has been working on the movie for years and Ali G’s contemporary relevance has been honed alongside many collaborators. The film is expected to touch on issues including cancel culture and immigration, while also having “ridiculous, silly-ass fun,” according to Dunn.

Peter Fincham, the British television producer who first gave Ali G a platform in topical comedy series The 11 O’Clock Show, told Deadline that he was fascinated to see how the character has moved with the times. He admitted, however, that if a young white comedian was creating Ali G today, “questions would be asked” by studios and broadcasters. “The culture has changed. Sacha’s a very smart guy and will be sensitive to that, and I’m sure it will be reflected in the film,” said Fincham, who co-hosts Insiders: The TV Podcast.

title: John Cleese Accuses BBC Of “Social Engineering” After Cutting Blackface Sketches From ‘That Mitchell And Webb Look’
summary: John Cleese is unhappy with the BBC for removing sketches from comedy series That Mitchell and Webb Look. The BBC confirmed earlier this week that jokes featured in David Mitchell and Robert Webb’s show had been cut ahead of it being restored to iPlayer for its 20th anniversary. As many as 11 sketches were removed, […]
content:
John Cleese is unhappy with the BBC for removing sketches from comedy series That Mitchell and Webb Look.

The BBC confirmed earlier this week that jokes featured in David Mitchell and Robert Webb’s show had been cut ahead of it being restored to iPlayer for its 20th anniversary.

As many as 11 sketches were removed, including a self-referential skit in which Mitchell and Webb joked about the appropriateness of Blackface while in Blackface.

Cleese, who is no fan of historical revisionism, attacked the BBC in X/Twitter posts, describing the edits as “social engineering.”

Watch on Deadline

“If the BBC could prioritise making great programmes ahead of social engineering they might be worth the licence fee,” he wrote.

If the BBC could prioritise making great programmes ahead of social engineering they might be worth the licence fee https://t.co/hyP6iYHg4M — John Cleese (@JohnCleese) September 23, 2026

In another, Cleese shared a post from James Dreyfus, star of BBC comedies including Gimme Gimme Gimme and The Thin Blue Line.

“So, the BBC have decided that 11 of Mitchell & Webb’s sketches are no longer deemed ‘appropriate for modern day audiences,’ despite the fact that ALL their material comes from an intelligent source base, that pokes fun at & ridicules the foolish & ignorant,” Dreyfus wrote.

“And people have the nerve to suggest that ‘we’d miss the BBC if it suddenly disappeared’…? Not in its current incarnation, believe me…”

Cleese responded: “The BBC knows what’s best for us. And some of us know what’s best for the BBC.”

The BBC declined to comment beyond a statement issued earlier this week. “That Mitchell and Webb Look has been made available on BBC iPlayer. This is a 20-year-old sketch show; in consultation with the programme makers, we have included the ones that still work today and not the ones that don’t,” a spokesperson said.

Cut sketches include one in which Mitchell and Webb play English Civil War re-enactors who have grown bored of their roles and recreate a conflict between government forces in the Democratic Republic of Congo and a rebel militia.

Mitchell asks: “Are you absolutely sure that this isn’t racist?” They agree to stop the reenactment at the first sign of racism. When one threatens the other with a machete, they halt the reenactment, concluding: “It’s racist. Very, very racist. Shame.”

In another sketch, Webb and Olivia Colman parody a makeover show and are confronted by a woman in a burqa. It then cuts to Webb discussing whether the sketch is offensive, with the woman in the burqa removing her garment to reveal Mitchell in Blackface.

In 2020, Cleese voiced his disapproval of a decision by BBC Studios-owned broadcaster UKTV to scrub an episode of classic British comedy Fawlty Towers from its back catalog.

UKTV removed “The Germans” from its Gold Box Set of downloadable programs, citing the fact that it contained “racial slurs.” UKTV was not specific about the slur, but it is believed to have been uttered by character The Major (Ballard Berkeley), who uses the n-word when referring to Caribbean sportsmen.

“The Major was an old fossil leftover from decades before. We were not supporting his views, we were making fun of them,” said Cleese. “If they can’t see that, if people are too stupid to see that, what can one say?”

title: Brad Pitt Praises Streamers For Creating Opportunities & Says He Believes The Indie Film Space Is Currently Just As Strong As In The ’90s — San Sebastián
summary: Brad Pitt was optimistic about the current indie film landscape during a packed-out press conference this morning at the San Sebastián Film Festival, where he is set to screen his latest feature, Heart of the Beast. “The current setup is really conducive to independent cinema in a really cool way because more eyes are getting […]
content:
Brad Pitt was optimistic about the current indie film landscape during a packed-out press conference this morning at the San Sebastián Film Festival, where he is set to screen his latest feature, Heart of the Beast.

“The current setup is really conducive to independent cinema in a really cool way because more eyes are getting on these projects. It even feels as strong as in the ’90s,” Pitt told the audience in San Sebastian when asked about the current film landscape.

The veteran actor also spoke positively about what he described as the creative opportunities streaming platforms have added to the movie business.

“Streaming has brought us so many more opportunities for actors, writers, directors. And because of that, we have a greater plethora of really interesting stories and really interesting talents, and that’s been amazing,” he said.

Watch on Deadline

But Pitt added a caution to his comments and highlighted what he described as the tightening space in the marketplace for mid-budget films, which he said were his bread and butter.

“Movies got so expensive. We always talk about how the very big tentpole movies are able to recoup. And the more independent, lower-budget, or anything in the middle ground—anything from 30, maybe 40, 60—has a really difficult time getting made, even movies like ours, because it’s very difficult for the studio to recoup that middle budget,” he said.

Pitt added: “I’m hoping those movies still have space, because that’s usually where I end up most, in the middle ground.”

Heart of the Beast was one of the late additions to this year’s San Sebastián lineup. Pitt is here at the festival with director David Ayer. The film follows a former Army Special Forces soldier (Pitt) and his retired combat dog who battle for survival after a plane crash deep in the unforgiving Alaskan wilderness.

The film’s official synopsis reads: After a harrowing plane crash, Special Forces officer James Belmont (Pitt) and his combat dog, Odin, find themselves stranded deep in the Alaskan wilderness. Together, they are forced into a brutal fight for survival against the elements.

Cameron Alexander wrote the film. Olivia Hamilton, Marty Bowen, Ayer, and Pitt are producers. Exec producers include Damien Chazelle, Scott Lumpkin, Cameron Alexander, Chris Long, Pete Chiappetta, Anthony Tittanegro, Andrew Lary, Sophie Cassidy, and Zack Conroy.

The project reunites Pitt and Ayer for the first time since Fury, their 2014 WWII drama for Sony, and comes following Pitt’s starring role in the Oscar-nominated Apple flick F1.

Paramount debuted footage of the pic at this year’s CinemaCon. The studio will release the film on September 25.

title: Studiocanal Announces Wrap Of Final Film In Ambitious German-Language ‘Woodwalkers’ Trilogy
summary: Studiocanal has announced the official wrap of the final instalment in hit German-language trilogy Woodwalkers alongside unveiling a January 28, 2027 theatrical launch date in Germany and a first image. A production between Blue Eyes Fiction and Studiocanal Germany, the trilogy was launched in 2024 as the partners’ most ambitious German-language production to date. The […]
content:
Studiocanal has announced the official wrap of the final instalment in hit German-language trilogy Woodwalkers alongside unveiling a January 28, 2027 theatrical launch date in Germany and a first image.

A production between Blue Eyes Fiction and Studiocanal Germany, the trilogy was launched in 2024 as the partners’ most ambitious German-language production to date.

The first two instalments of the trilogy, which were distributed by Studiocanal, drew more than two million admissions in Germany, with Woodwalkers 2 described by the partners as the most successful German family film of 2026 to date.

Watch on Deadline

Adapted from the best-selling novels by German writer Katja Brandis, the trilogy follows the adventures of a group of teenagers with secret shapeshifting abilities, known as ‘Woodwalkers’.

The final chapter sees protagonist Carag and his friends face their greatest challenge yet, when relentless adversary Andrew Milling declares the “Day of Vengeance”. The declaration sees Carag’s battle against his former mentor enter a decisive phase.

Production on the final chapter began this summer on location in Romania and in the German region of Bavaria and was completed this week.

Florian Sigl returned to direct with Emile Chérif also back in the role of Carag, alongside Lilli Falk as Holly, Johan von Ehrlich as Brandon, Sophie Lelenta as Lou, Olivia Sinclair as Tikaani and Emil Bloch as Jeffrey.

The adult cast was led once again by Oliver Masucci (Andrew Milling), Martina Gedeck (Lissa Clearwater), Hannah Herzsprung (Anna Ralston) and David Schütter (Carag’s father Xamber).

Behind the camera, Armin Golisano (Manitou’s Canoe) served as director of photography, Christoph Kanter (The White Ribbon, Chantal im Maerchenland) as production designer, and Mara Laibacher (Babo – The Haftbefehl Story) is costume designer.

Woodwalkers 3 is a production of Blue Eyes Fiction (Help, I Shrunk My Teacher, The Four Enchanted Sisters) with Lothar Hellinger as producer and Bianca Krippendorf as executive producer, in co-production with Studiocanal (The Robber Hotzenplotz, Paddington) and Dor Film Vienna.

title: CNN’s Interactive ‘Office Hours’ Has John Berman Testing New Skills
summary: John Berman has done almost everything an anchor can do at CNN. He guides viewers through breaking news during hours of “CNN News Central.” He’s filled in for Anderson Cooper, co-hosted a morning show and is trained to handle CNN’s “Magic Wall” on primary and election nights. Now he has a new assignment – but […]
content:
John Berman has done almost everything an anchor can do at CNN. He guides viewers through breaking news during hours of “CNN News Central.” He’s filled in for Anderson Cooper, co-hosted a morning show and is trained to handle CNN’s “Magic Wall” on primary and election nights.

Now he has a new assignment – but you won’t find it on the traditional CNN schedule

Popular on Variety

Berman has been hosting a new CNN program called “Office Hours” that runs periodically on the news giant’s nascent subscription product “CNN All Access.” During “Office Hours,” Berman interacts with subscribers and helps to answer their questions about elections, politics and more. On Wednesday evening, Berman will host a new edition of the program alongside Kate Bolduan and Sara Sidner, his “News Central” co-hosts.

“This doesn’t feel like television,” Berman says during a recent interview. “Even though there are cameras rolling.”

Berman is one of a growing number of traditional news anchors being assigned to new interactive formats that give viewers and subscribers more say over what gets discussed. Across the TV-news sector, there is an emerging focus on letting the people who are tuning in have more say or on hiring people with deep expertise in a certain topic who can help guide news aficionados in a more personal, unvarnished way.

“You have this great tribe of people” coming to CNN’s digital venues, says Ryan Kadro, senior vice president of content strategy at the Warner Bros. Discovery-backed news unit. “People are watching video, reading all of the articles and want to keep going further.” He adds: “The baseline premise we’ve had for a long time is that we need to engage more directly with people that are coming to us and make talent available.”

CNN also faces competitive pressures. MS NOW has put significant emphasis on giving more access to its anchors and correspondents via interactive video sessions on its new “Membership” subscription product. Even Rachel Maddow and members of “Morning Joe” have committed to weekly hangouts with subscribers. And of course, there are many other digital corners where headline-seekers can talk to one another.

“So many of these conversations were done on platforms in other places — in comments, on X,” says Kadro. CNN’s goal was “to take the conversations happening around us and bring it to our ecosystem and make our subscriptions stickier.” CNN has introduced new on-screen elements to some of its TV programs — like a “rail” for text chats from correspondents — in a bid to keep conversations from moving elsewhere.

Even so, executives have been methodical, not rushed, about crafting CNN’s new interactive format. CNN did three or four early sessions via Zoom, Kadro says, then sought feedback from attendees. Participation on the first “Office Hours” with Berman was three times what had been expected, Kadro says. From there, the company set about crafting something that would work on its new app.

The new show puts Berman into situations he might not typically encounter on TV. During one recent “Office Hours” ostensibly focused on the coming midterm elections, the anchor found he kept getting questions and comments about President Trump’s proposal to hand out $5,000 checks to Americans if Republicans emerged victorious. “On TV, we talked about it and it went away,” he says, but “not for the people we were talking to.” With that in mind, Berman knew he could turn the interactions into a conversation the next time he was anchoring on TV. “I was getting direct feedback at night and turning it around in the morning.”

Now that Paramount Skydance has prevailed in its bid to take over CNN’s parent, there is certain to be new scrutiny on what elements of CNN’s current business plan new managers wish to keep. For a TV veteran like Berman, there is, for now, a chance to pivot when it comes to facilitating new kinds of interactions with news viewers. “I’m trying to respond to the people who are viewing it,” Berman notes. “I don’t have control, and I don’t mind that.”

title: Diane Lane Joins Li Jun Li in Hulu Limited Series ‘Victoria’
summary: Diane Lane has joined the upcoming Hulu-Onyx Collective limited series “Victoria,” Variety has learned. The erotic thriller, which was announced last week with a series order, will star Li Jun Li as Maxine Tao, who is described as “a brilliant con artist who finds herself in a dark web of power, luxury and the crosshairs […]
content:
Diane Lane has joined the upcoming Hulu-Onyx Collective limited series “Victoria,” Variety has learned.

The erotic thriller, which was announced last week with a series order, will star Li Jun Li as Maxine Tao, who is described as “a brilliant con artist who finds herself in a dark web of power, luxury and the crosshairs of a seductive killer who knows her secrets.”

Lane joins as Lee Calloway, said to be “a savvy venture capitalist accustomed to getting what she wants and has worked too hard to let anyone stand between her and the win.”

This is the latest in a string of high-profile TV roles Lane has taken on in recent years. She previously appeared in shows like “A Man in Full” and “House of Cards” at Netflix, as well as Season 2 of “Feud” for FX/Hulu and “The Romanoffs” at Amazon. She is primarily known for her roles in films like “Under the Tuscan Sun,” “Unfaithful,” and “Hollywoodland.” Her work in “Unfaithful” earned her both an Academy Award and Golden Globe nominations, while she was also nominated for Golden Globes for “Under the Tuscan Sun” and the TV movie “Cinema Verite.” “Cinema Verite” also earned her an Emmy nomination, as did “Feud,” while Lane was nominated for an Emmy early in her career for the CBS miniseries “Lonesome Dove.”

Popular on Variety

She is repped by CAA, Range, and Weintraub.

Christy Hall is the creator, writer, executive producer, and showrunner on “Victoria.” Geeta Vasant Patel will direct the pilot and executive produce. Lilly Burns, Elise Henderson, and Tony Hernandez of Counterpart Studios executive produce, with Li co-producing in addition to starring.

title: David Ellison Mulls Tapping Elon Musk for Paramount Investment While Closing in on Warner Bros. Takeover: Report
summary: David Ellison, seeking fresh capital for a merged Paramount-Warner Bros., is considering reaching out to Elon Musk — the controversial tech mogul who is the world’s richest person — to “become part of a syndicate of equity investors into Paramount,” according to a report by Semafor. According to the report, citing anonymous sources, “Musk’s name […]
content:
David Ellison, seeking fresh capital for a merged Paramount-Warner Bros., is considering reaching out to Elon Musk — the controversial tech mogul who is the world’s richest person — to “become part of a syndicate of equity investors into Paramount,” according to a report by Semafor.

According to the report, citing anonymous sources, “Musk’s name is one of a number of wealthy individuals that Paramount CEO David Ellison has considered tapping for the syndicate,” but it did not identify others Ellison is supposedly mulling as investment partners. The Semafor report said the amount of Musk’s potential investment in Paramount could not be learned.

Paramount declined to comment. A rep for Musk did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Popular on Variety

Musk, the one-time Trump administration official who leads SpaceX, Tesla and X, among other businesses, had a net worth estimated at about $950 billion as of Wednesday, per Forbes.

Paramount’s deal to merge with Warner Bros. Discovery is close to the finish line, after the company reached a settlement with 12 state attorneys general to settle their antitrust lawsuit over the pact. The judge in the case has scheduled a hearing Thursday to go over the points of the proposed consent decree; pending the judge’s approval, the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger is expected to close in about two weeks.

Oracle founder Larry Ellison (David’s father), who is also one of the world’s richest men, has business ties to Musk: Larry Ellison invested $1 billion in Musk’s 2022 deal taking Twitter (since renamed X) private. Larry Ellison also invested in Tesla in 2018, and served on its board for several years.

For Paramount’s WBD deal, valued at $111 billion, Larry Ellison has personally guaranteed $46.7 billion in equity financing. In addition, Paramount has lined up $24 billion in commitments from the sovereign wealth funds of Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates. According to Paramount, the three Middle Eastern funds would own 38.5% of the combined Paramount-Warner Bros. Last week, the FCC approved Paramount’s petition to allow 49.5% of its equity to be held by foreign entities if the Warner Bros. Discovery merger is consummated.

Among the top-line terms in Paramount’s settlement with the states: Paramount is prohibited from selling the Paramount Studios or Warner Bros. lots in the state for at least five years, and is obligated to invest at least an additional $300 million on film production in the U.S. annually (for a total of $1.5 billion over five years). The newly merged company also must release at least 30 movies for theatrical distribution in the first two years (something Ellison has repeatedly promised he would do) and at least 32 in years 3-5, with a 45-day window for wide-release films.

In addition, under the proposed settlement, the merged Paramount-Warner Bros. also will be subject to monitoring by a “news editorial independence board,” which will establish “guiding editorial and journalism principles for” for CNN and CBS News.

title: ‘Conclave’ Director Edward Berger, Matthew Libatique to Be Feted at Evolution Mallorca International Film Festival
summary: Oscar-winning Swiss-Austrian director Edward Berger (“Conclave,” “All Quiet on the Western Front”) and American cinematographer Matthew Libatique (“Requiem for a Dream,” “Black Swan”), a triple Oscar nominee, will receive the top honors at the upcoming Evolution Mallorca International Film Festival. The event, which takes place in the largest of Spain’s Balearic Islands between Oct. 28 […]
content:
Oscar-winning Swiss-Austrian director Edward Berger (“Conclave,” “All Quiet on the Western Front”) and American cinematographer Matthew Libatique (“Requiem for a Dream,” “Black Swan”), a triple Oscar nominee, will receive the top honors at the upcoming Evolution Mallorca International Film Festival. The event, which takes place in the largest of Spain’s Balearic Islands between Oct. 28 and Nov. 4, will also honor veteran German actress Iris Berben (“Triangle of Sadness”).

Berger will receive the Evolution Vision Award, which recognizes narrative excellence reflecting the mission of building bridges between cultures and people. Libatique will receive the Cinematography Icon Award, recognizing artistic and technical excellence in the art of cinematography, while Berben will be honored with the Evolution Icon Award in homage to a performer whose extensive and brilliant career has achieved international acclaim.

Popular on Variety

In celebration of Berger, the festival will host a special screening of Cannes Best Director winner “Fatherland,” directed by Paweł Pawlikowski and produced by the “Conclave” director. The screening will be followed by a conversation between Berger and producer Jeanne Tremsal. Earlier this week, it was announced Berger would be reteaming with “The Riders” star Brad Pitt for a long-anticipated “World War Z” sequel.

Berben will receive the inaugural Evolution Icon Award during the festival’s opening gala on Oct. 28. The festival has praised Berben’s work beyond the screen, especially her tenure as the President of the German Film Academy between 2010 and 2019, where she “helped strengthen the public profile and cultural significance of German cinema.”

As for Libatique, Darren Aronofsky’s frequent collaborator will give an Icon Talk followed by a roundtable discussion on cinematography. Libatique is the fifth recipient of the award dedicated to the craft, with the festival also hosting a Cinematography Focus forum between Oct. 28-30. The forum “reinforces one of Evolution’s key professional platforms, dedicated specifically to the craft, technique, and creation of the cinematic image.”

Spanish actor and producer Marc Clotet will preside over this year’s jury. The actor’s return to Mallorca has a special significance, given that he was featured in Benito Zambrano’s “The Sleeping Voice,” the opening film of the festival’s inaugural edition in 2012. “I am delighted to serve as jury president for a festival as special to me as the Evolution Film Festival,” Clotet said. “15 years after attending the first edition, being able to contribute my perspective after all these years of experience is a challenge I approach with great respect and excitement.”

Goya-nominated Clotet has built a career spanning both national and international projects. In 2021, Clotet founded the production company Funicular Films alongside Aina Clotet, Marta Baldó, and Jan Andreu. Through this company, he has spearheaded projects such as the successful series “This Is Not Sweden” and the Cannes Critics’ Week-winning film “Viva,” which played at the major French festival earlier this year.

The festival also revealed more details of its Made in Baleares section, dedicated to bridging together films from the Balearic Islands. This year, the section will feature 32 projects, including 17 short films, seven feature films, five documentary short films and three student short films. The selection reflects the diversity, professional growth, and rising ambition of the Balearic audiovisual sector. It also reinforces Evolution’s commitment to a program that blends local talent with new voices and established figures from international cinema.

The festival’s 15th edition will also see the event expand into the municipality of Calvià, which is celebrating its Year of Cinema in 2026. The festival notes the expansion reinforces “its commitment to the audiovisual sector as a cultural, creative, and economic driver, as well as a tool to showcase the region and attract new productions.”

“Celebrating our fifteenth edition is a momentous occasion for Evolution,” said Sandra Lipski, founder and director of the Evolution Mallorca International Film Festival. “We are proud to continue building a platform where international voices and local talent converge. Our new collaboration with Calvià reflects a shared ambition: to create meaningful opportunities for filmmakers, promote Mallorca as an exceptional filming location, and contribute to the growth of the island’s audiovisual community.”

The Mayor of Calvià has highlighted the significance of the municipality hosting the festival this year, stating that the “arrival of the Evolution festival represents a renewed commitment to cinema as an audiovisual sector that helps reduce seasonality, while also attracting high-quality tourism.”

The Evolution Mallorca International Film Festival was founded in 2012 to promote Mallorca as a key destination for international film culture. The full program, screening schedules, and upcoming guest announcements will be revealed on Oct. 15.

title: Power at Any Age: Gloria Reuben Urges Menopausal Women to Advocate for Their Health
summary: Throughout her illustrious life and career, Gloria Reuben has shared her story through music and acting. She started learning classical piano when she was a young girl and was the lead singer of a rock band as a teenager. Then in her early 20s, Reuben moved from Toronto to Los Angeles, where she waited tables […]
content:
Throughout her illustrious life and career, Gloria Reuben has shared her story through music and acting. She started learning classical piano when she was a young girl and was the lead singer of a rock band as a teenager. Then in her early 20s, Reuben moved from Toronto to Los Angeles, where she waited tables at a restaurant and took acting classes before booking her first big break, a TV commercial. Soon after, she made the jump from full-time waitress to working actress in order to pursue her creative passions. “You made the right decision. Keep the faith,” she told herself at the time.

These days, the veteran entertainer is starring in multiple TV series, shooting films and regularly performing jazz. Creative expression — specifically music, what she calls the “enduring factor” in her life — has carried her through everything she’s achieved and conquered, and how she’s navigated the world of show business for decades.

Now, the actress and musician is sharing the latest chapter of her story.

For several years, Reuben was navigating a force shaping nearly every part of her daily life – menopause, specifically, hot flashes due to menopause.

Vacation plans and long flights required strategizing and prepping to manage sudden waves of heat. At work, wardrobe fittings suddenly meant second-guessing fabrics and layers in case of hot flashes on and off camera. Then, on set, she felt disconnected from her scene partners, which forced her to be in her head instead of in the present moment. “I felt like I didn’t know my body anymore,” she shares. “Like my body was a stranger. It was very unsettling.” For years, Reuben was navigating moderate to severe hot flashes due to menopause, both day and night, with constant uncertainty of when the next one might strike.

For much of women’s lives, change is something they learn to navigate. From puberty and first heartbreak to career pivots and, for some, motherhood, women are thrown into an endless evolution of identity that comes with simply being alive.

Then comes menopause.

OK McCausland for Variety

It’s a transition that remains one of the most misunderstood and underdiscussed health topics, yet all women who reach midlife will experience menopause. Menopause is a natural occurrence in a woman’s life and is defined by 12 consecutive months without a menstrual period. Too often, menopause — including hot flashes — has been framed as something women are expected to endure and struggle with, as though aging itself is something to apologize for. In fact, hot flashes are one of the most commonly reported symptoms of menopause.

Nearly half of women going through menopause may experience moderate to severe hot flashes, and these symptoms may last 10 or more years for some. Menopausal hot flashes and night sweats disproportionately impact women of color, with Black and Hispanic women experiencing more frequent and bothersome hot flashes due to menopause.

The increasing frequency and unpredictability of Reuben’s hot flashes, including sleep disruptions from nighttime hot flashes, took a toll. “When the natural phase of a woman’s body changes into the phase of menopause, for me, personally, it definitely brought a lot of things into question,” she shares, alluding to the mental toll and fears of a hot flash “erupting” during a day on set or an evening out. “It’s very challenging on all fronts, especially if a woman is being silent about it or struggling with it on her own… I carried, unknowingly I think, a great deal of shame around it and embarrassment,” she says. “That was very difficult.”

OK McCausland for Variety

There’s no one-size-fits-all approach to managing moderate to severe hot flashes due to menopause. But there are treatment options available. One option is VEOZAH, the #1 prescribed hormone-free treatment FDA-approved for moderate to severe hot flashes due to menopause.* VEOZAH blocks the binding of NKB, a brain chemical known to trigger hot flashes during menopause, in the brain’s temperature control center. VEOZAH is not a hormone. It’s proven to reduce the number and severity of hot flashes, day and night, based on clinical studies measuring efficacy over 24 hours at four and 12 weeks. For some women, it can start working as early as one week, but results may vary from person to person and women should speak with their doctor about what this may mean for them.

It’s important for people to know that VEOZAH can cause serious side effects, including liver problems. Expect blood tests before and during treatment. Stop VEOZAH and call your doctor if you have signs or symptoms of liver problems, like feeling more tired, decreased appetite, nausea, vomiting, itching, yellowing of eyes or skin, pale stool, dark urine or stomach pain. Keep reading for additional Important Safety Information, including BOXED WARNING.

Reuben first heard about VEOZAH when she saw a television commercial for the treatment and later consulted with her doctor about her menopausal hot flashes. “I was looking for a hormone-free and FDA-approved option,” she says. For Reuben, conversations with her doctor and advocating for her own health led to her choosing VEOZAH as the treatment option for her moderate to severe hot flashes due to menopause. “We talked about treatment options, including the possible benefits and possible side effects. Before starting VEOZAH, my doctor did a blood test to check my liver, and since I’ve been taking VEOZAH, my doctor has done follow-up liver blood testing,” she recalls. “I got my prescription a few days later, and in about a week there was a decrease in my menopausal hot flashes, both day and night.” Individual results may vary and women should speak with their doctor about what this may mean for them.

The menopause advocate adds, “VEOZAH has worked well for me as a treatment for my moderate to severe hot flashes due to menopause. I’m not constantly wondering when the next hot flash will happen.”

OK McCausland for Variety

For Reuben, as her hot flashes became less frequent, so did the worry that came with anticipating when the next one might strike. “Instead of planning my day, and night, around my hot flashes, I can focus more on the things that matter most to me,” she shares.

Don’t use VEOZAH if you have cirrhosis, severe kidney problems, kidney failure or take CYP1A2 inhibitors. Keep reading for additional Important Safety Information, including BOXED WARNING.

“I’m always collaborating and always keeping in touch with my health care provider,” Reuben shares.

OK McCausland for Variety

Beyond the physical symptoms, Reuben says menopause prompted an unexpected reckoning. She started to confront bigger questions about what this next stage of life could look like. Rather than viewing menopause as an ending, she began reframing it as an invitation to advocate for herself physically and emotionally — a perspective that would ultimately shape the way she approached her overall health. “It feels good to be reconnected,” she says of her mind and body.

Reflecting on her menopausal experiences, Reuben says advocating for herself and her health “in every single way” allowed her to “participate in my own healing process. I found a way to reframe every area of my life. It’s not just a new chapter, it’s a new volume.”

One of the biggest lessons menopause taught Reuben is that strength doesn’t always mean handling everything alone. She hopes more women feel comfortable asking questions and leaning on trusted health care providers.

“I experienced that ‘you have to do it all. You have to be a superwoman. You have to just handle it.’ Yes, sometimes, and sometimes you have to ask for help,” Reuben says. “Oftentimes in my life it’s been, ‘Oh no, I got this. Oh, I can handle this.’ The asking for help, asking questions and being open to communicate about what’s really going on is key for all of us. In particular, when a woman’s body is changing and there are a lot of questions to ask. It’s a very unknown territory because each body is different. Each woman’s experience is going to be different. However, you don’t have to do it alone. The first step is communicating with your health care provider. Learning about the science of what’s going on, listening to your body and communication.”

OK McCausland for Variety

Power does not expire with age. Knowledge and shared stories empower women at any age to transform uncertainty into actionable clarity.

“Unexpectedly for me, this time of my life has been a really joyful time of freedom that I didn’t anticipate and there’s an openness that I definitely didn’t anticipate,” she says.

Joyful freedom has led Reuben to pursue her creative passions with renewed exuberance and fewer struggles. Reuben wrote her first book, “My Brothers’ Keeper: Two Brothers. Loved. and Lost.,” and recently wrote her first play. She’s regularly journaling, working on TV and film sets, creating playlists for each character she portrays, performing on stages and pulling inspiration from her own life for artistic endeavors.

Music is still her longstanding throughline, healing force and inspiration. She’s also inspiring others.

“I’d like women who are going through menopause and experiencing moderate to severe hot flashes, day and night, to know about the treatment option that worked for me,” she says. “I’d encourage them to speak to their health care provider, discuss what they’re feeling and the possible treatment options for them. They don’t have to suffer in silence. They don’t have to grin and bear it. They don’t have to do it alone.”

To learn more, visit VEOZAH.com

*IQVIA TRx data from May 2023 to June 2026

What is VEOZAH™ (fezolinetant)?

VEOZAH is a prescription medicine used to reduce moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms due to menopause. VEOZAH is not a hormone. Vasomotor symptoms are the feelings of warmth in the face, neck, and chest, or sudden intense feelings of heat and sweating (“hot flashes” or “hot flushes”).

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION

What is the most important information I should know about VEOZAH? VEOZAH can cause serious side effects, including:

Liver Problems. Your healthcare provider will do a blood test to check your liver before you start taking VEOZAH. Your healthcare provider will also do this blood test monthly for the first 3 months, at month 6, and month 9 after you start taking VEOZAH or if you have signs or symptoms that suggest liver problems. If your liver blood test values are elevated, your healthcare provider may advise you to stop treatment or request additional liver blood tests.

Stop VEOZAH right away and call your healthcare provider if you have the following signs or symptoms of liver problems:

feeling more tired than you do usually

decreased appetite

nausea

vomiting

itching

yellowing of the eyes or skin (jaundice)

pale feces

dark urine

pain in the stomach (abdomen)

Do not use VEOZAH if you:

have cirrhosis.

have severe kidney problems or kidney failure.

are taking certain medicines called CYP1A2 inhibitors. Ask your healthcare provider if you are not sure.

Before you use VEOZAH, tell your healthcare provider about all of your medical conditions, including if you:

have liver disease or problems.

have kidney problems.

have any medical conditions that may become worse while you are using VEOZAH.

Tell your healthcare provider about all the medicines you take, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements. VEOZAH may affect the way other medicines work, and other medicines may affect how VEOZAH works.

The most common side effects of VEOZAH include:

stomach (abdominal) pain

diarrhea

difficulty sleeping (insomnia)

back pain

hot flashes or hot flushes

These are not all the possible side effects of VEOZAH. Tell your healthcare provider if you have any side effect that bothers you or does not go away.

Call your healthcare provider for medical advice about side effects. You are encouraged to report negative side effects of prescription drugs to the FDA. Visit www.fda.gov/medwatch or call 1-800- FDA-1088.

Please see full Prescribing Information and Patient Information, including BOXED WARNING at VEOZAH.com.

title: ABC Developing Series About Police Divers In New Orleans From Steven Kane, 20th Television & Dwayne Johnson’s Seven Bucks
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Jack Ryan and Halo showrunner Steven Kane has landed on his next project. Kane is developing ABC’s Dive with 20th Television and Dwayne Johnson’s Seven Bucks, which is set in New Orleans, a city defined by its relationship to water. Dive will follow an elite team of police divers and investigators who solve crimes […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Jack Ryan and Halo showrunner Steven Kane has landed on his next project.

Kane is developing ABC’s Dive with 20th Television and Dwayne Johnson’s Seven Bucks, which is set in New Orleans, a city defined by its relationship to water.

Dive will follow an elite team of police divers and investigators who solve crimes that begin where the surface ends. Kane quietly referenced the show at a recent TV event in Europe, at which point he said he had told ABC commissioners: “If this is successful it could be franchised.” Casting is not yet set and we are told the show is in early development.

Kane is a former The Closer, NCIS and Without a Trace writer who went on to co-create and exec produce TNT’s The Last Ship. He subsequently show-ran Paramount+’s adaptation of Halo and then the fourth and final season of Prime Video’s Jack Ryan. We understand Kane is also developing an international thriller currently being packaged in Europe and a series based on his forthcoming graphic novel.

Watch on Deadline

For Dive, he has joined with EP Kristina Sorenson and the team at Seven Bucks, the company run by champion wrestler-turned movie star Johnson and Dany Garcia. Seven Bucks’ TV credits include Ballers, Young Rock and The Titan Games.

At ABC’s recent upfronts, the Disney-owned network left its number one show High Potential off the fall schedule, keeping the hit crime drama starring Kaitlin Olson on the bench for midseason.

Kane is repped by WME, Morris/ Yorn, and Rain. Sorenson is repped by The Nord Group.

title: ‘Bling Empire’ Breakout Kim Lee To Host ‘Rice To Riches’ Reality Show For KC Global Media Asia
summary: KC Global Media Asia is in pre-production on Rice to Riches, a reality show to be co-produced and hosted by DJ and producer Kim Lee, who won a new legion of fans following her appearances on Netflix’s Bling Empire. Rice to Riches is described as “an uplifting masterclass on how content creators make an income […]
content:
KC Global Media Asia is in pre-production on Rice to Riches, a reality show to be co-produced and hosted by DJ and producer Kim Lee, who won a new legion of fans following her appearances on Netflix’s Bling Empire.

Rice to Riches is described as “an uplifting masterclass on how content creators make an income and monetize their social media into brand deals and original products.”

The show will have Lee exploring the Asian content creator world, visiting the homes, production spaces and offices of leading creators to get the inside scoop on their early professional lives and how each of them have become influencers and financial powerhouses.

The eight-episode first season will feature nine content creators including Michael Le from the U.S., Jestinna & Christinna Kuan from Malaysia, and Kevin Ninh from the U.S., with more creators to be announced. Production is taking place in the U.S. and Asia beginning in October.

Watch on Deadline

A Los Angeles native, Lee is also known for appearances on Yo! MTV Raps Asia and Prime Video’s CryptoKnights. As a DJ, she has toured and done shows with Steve Aoki, Martin Garrix, Diplo and Skrillex.

“We are so excited to be in business with a creative powerhouse like Kim Lee and Rice to Riches is a true collaboration between us,” said George Chien, KC Global Media Asia Co-Founder, President & CEO.

“Most people don’t understand the world of Asian creative economy and we can’t wait to highlight these individuals and this growing and profitable enterprise in a way that is both informative and entertaining.”

Said Lee: “I’m thrilled to be co-producing this project with KC Global Media. Their vision and experience make them the perfect partner. I can’t wait for audiences to watch what we’re creating together.”

Headquartered in the U.S., KC Global Media Entertainment has offices in Singapore, Taiwan, Malaysia, China, Philippines and Korea. Founded by former Sony execs Andy Kaplan and Chien, the company’s Asian arm, KC Global Media Asia is involved in production, distribution and programming and operates a bouquet of channels including AXM, Animax and Korean GE network ONE.

title: Deborah Ann Woll & Luke Kirby Join Hulu’s ‘The Testaments’ For Season 2
summary: EXCLUSIVE: The Testaments, the series following up Hulu’s hit Margaret Atwood adaptation The Handmaid’s Tale, has added two more to Season 2: Deborah Ann Woll (Daredevil: Born Again) as a recurring guest star and Luke Kirby (The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel) as guest star. Woll plays Sylvia, whose work as a seamstress keeps her in close […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: The Testaments, the series following up Hulu‘s hit Margaret Atwood adaptation The Handmaid’s Tale, has added two more to Season 2: Deborah Ann Woll (Daredevil: Born Again) as a recurring guest star and Luke Kirby (The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel) as guest star.

Woll plays Sylvia, whose work as a seamstress keeps her in close proximity to the Wives and daughters of Gilead’s Commanders.

Kirby plays the literal-minded Commander Fletcher, who lives as a recluse on a farm in one of Gilead’s Colonies, where his eccentricities have made it difficult to find a wife.

This follows our scoop that Charlie Carrick, who plays Gilead’s Commander Judd, has been upped to series regular for Season 2, with Haley Wong coming aboard for the series regular role of the dutiful and pregnant wife, Prudence.

Watch on Deadline

Based on Atwood’s 2019 novel, The Testaments is a dramatic coming-of-age story set in the totalitarian theocracy of Gilead that follows young teens Agnes, dutiful and pious, and Daisy, a new arrival and convert from beyond Gilead’s borders. As they navigate the gilded halls of Aunt Lydia’s elite preparatory school for future wives, a place where obedience is instilled brutally and always with divine justification, their bond becomes the catalyst that will upend their past, their present, and their future.

Chase Infiniti plays Agnes, with Lucy Halliday as Daisy, and Ann Dowd reprising her Handmaid’s Tale role of Aunt Lydia.

The Testaments is created by showrunner Bruce Miller (The Handmaid’s Tale), who exec produces alongside Warren Littlefield, Handmaid’s star Elisabeth Moss, Steve Stark, Shana Stein, Maya Goldsmith, John Weber, Sheila Hockin, Daniel Wilson, Fran Sears, Gianna Sobol and Mike Barker, who directed the first three episodes and finale of Season 1. The series is produced by MGM Television and 20th Television.

Season 1 premiered in April, with production on Season 2 commencing in August.

The show’s cast also includes Mabel Li, Amy Seimetz, Brad Alexander, Rowan Blanchard, Mattea Conforti, Zarrin Darnell-Martin, Eva Foote, Isolde Ardies and Kira Guloien.

Recently seen reprising her role of Karen Page, friend and ally to Matt Murdock (aka Daredevil), in Marvel Television’s Daredevil: Born Again — a role she first played in the 2015 series Daredevil — Woll is otherwise best known for starring in HBO’s True Blood. She is repped by Matt Luber & Michael Adler from Luber Roklin Entertainment.

Kirby is best known for starring roles in Prime Video’s The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel and has more recently seen opposite Jennifer Garner in the second season of Apple TV’s The Last Thing He Told Me. Next up, he’ll be seen in Law & Order Toronto: Criminal Intent Season 4, premiering October 1. His upcoming film projects include the MRC erotic thriller Mother’s Helper (with Shailene Woodley), indie comedy Close to Nowhere (with SNL‘s Veronika Slowikowska) and Netflix’s Better Than the Movies. He is repped by Gersh.
