title: Jodie Turner-Smith Sued for Allegedly Enabling Brother’s Sexual Misconduct and Drug Dealing
summary: Richard Smith, the brother of actor Jodie Turner-Smith, was sued by three women for alleged sexual misconduct and drug dealing; Turner-Smith was named in the suit as allegedly enabling his behavior. Three Jane Does filed a lawsuit with the Los Angeles Superior Court against Smith and Turner-Smith on Thursday. They each accused Smith of engaging […]
content:
Richard Smith, the brother of actor Jodie Turner-Smith, was sued by three women for alleged sexual misconduct and drug dealing; Turner-Smith was named in the suit as allegedly enabling his behavior.

Three Jane Does filed a lawsuit with the Los Angeles Superior Court against Smith and Turner-Smith on Thursday. They each accused Smith of engaging them in unwanted sexual activity. The lawsuit claims that Turner-Smith enabled Smith’s behavior by paying his bills, providing housing and giving resources that supported his lifestyle, including allegedly gifting him an Audi that he used to transport drugs.

“Turner-Smith’s role is distinct from Smith’s alleged direct conduct,” the lawsuit claimed. “Turner-Smith knew of significant dangers associated with Smith and, despite that knowledge, continued to provide or make available resources that enabled Smith to maintain housing, transportation, and a lifestyle in which the alleged conduct continued.”

Popular on Variety

“This is a fictional lawsuit filed by someone who has been harassing Jodie while hiding behind the name Jane Doe. The claims are not true. This is an abuse of the legal system, allowing someone to make up facts and file meritless legal document,” a representative for Turner-Smith said in a statement to People.

The first Jane Doe alleged that Smith isolated her in a bedroom in June 2024, wouldn’t let her leave, pressured her to do drugs and involve her in non-consensual sexual activity with him and another man. The second woman alleged that a year earlier, her relationship with Smith became “increasingly coercive, unhealthy, and controlling.” She also claimed to be pressured to use drugs, engage in non-consensual sex with other men and witnessed “drug use, drug sales or distribution activity, sexual parties, firearms, and conduct by Smith that caused her to fear for her safety.” The third Jane Doe claimed that Smith offered her housing in exchange for sex and that Smith allegedly forced drug use and sexual activity upon her.

title: White House Has Spent More Than $440,000 on Pro-Trump TV Ads Paid for by U.S. Government; Administration Defends ‘Unapologetically American’ Spots and Denies They’re Campaign Ads
summary: TV ads featuring President Donald Trump that began airing this week — including one in which he declares that “America will never be a communist country” and touting his administration’s policy goals — were paid for by U.S. taxpayers. The spots have drawn criticism from Democrats and Republicans alike, with lawmakers saying they look like […]
content:
TV ads featuring President Donald Trump that began airing this week — including one in which he declares that “America will never be a communist country” and touting his administration’s policy goals — were paid for by U.S. taxpayers. The spots have drawn criticism from Democrats and Republicans alike, with lawmakers saying they look like campaign ads, coming just weeks before November’s midterm elections.

As of Friday, the Trump administration has spent at least $443,000 on the first ad, the AP reported, which started airing Wednesday on Fox News and Newsmax. The ads feature sound bites of Trump claiming he will defeat “communism, socialism and Marxism.” On-screen text in the spot claims the administration enacted the “largest tax cuts in history,” is “reigniting American manufacturing” and will “defend law and order and police.”

The White House on Friday issued a statement defending the ads, noting that multiple other presidential administrations have run PSAs promoting policies and to “make the case for the nation’s direction.”

Popular on Variety

‘The attacks on President Donald J. Trump’s public service announcements are highly dishonest. The announcements are very clearly not campaign ads; President Trump is not on the ballot and there is no call to action,” the White House said in a statement. “Instead, the announcements are a reminder for Americans to love their country and know why it’s worth defending — at home, at the border, and abroad. That’s not partisanship — that’s a government that still believes in the country it serves.”

Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-Md.), in posts on social media, said the ad violates the Hatch Act, which prohibits certain political activities of federal employees to ensure that federal programs are administered in a nonpartisan fashion. The pro-Trump ad from the White House “may be felony criminal theft and conversion of government property for political campaign purposes,” Raskin wrote. “It is a Hatch Act violation for any government employees who worked on it or used government resources to make it.”

Sen. Thom Tillis (R-N.C.) said the ad is “inappropriate” and that the White House’s use of taxpayer dollars to fund the campaign “feels like Viktor Orbán,” referring to the right-wing former prime minister of Hungary, The Hill reported.

On Friday, the White House began running a new 60-second ad in a similar vein. The ad features shots of Mount Rushmore at night with excepts from Trump’s July 4th weekend. “We know that this is not an ending,” Trump says in the ad. “This is only the beginning of the Golden Age of America.”

The Trump White House insisted the ads are entirely in-bounds. “When prior Administrations utilized the airwaves, it was called ‘public education.’ When this Administration promotes pride in our country, many of those same voices call it ‘propaganda,'” it said in a statement. “Patriotism isn’t partisan. These public service announcements are unapologetically American, clearly disclosed, and aimed at the country — not a line on the ballot.”

The Trump White House said administrations of both parties have used public service announcements to explain policy and make the case for the nation’s direction. For example, it cited the Biden administration’s “We Can Do This” public-health campaign and the Obama administration’s use of national ads to promote Obamacare subsidies and open enrollment.

Meanwhile, Trump’s “America will never be a communist country” ad is soundtracked with the song “Love Me” by JMSN, whose real name is Christian Berishaj.

In a post on X Thursday, JMSN said, “To anybody who has followed my career and knows what I stand for and built my career on, it should go without saying that I would never authorize my music to be used for ANY political agenda or campaign.” He said Trump “illegally” used the song “without asking but still the public goes full ret*rd and immediately assumes that a license was granted.”

“I’ve built my career independently outside of any major system and have made it a point to not sacrifice my artistic integrity,” JMSN said. “I don’t have a publicist or anything so being forced in a situation like this and having to comment is ridiculous.” He added, “I am looking at lawyers and handling this internally.” Variety has reached out to the White House for comment.

title: Margaret Qualley and Sabrina Carpenter Join Tom Holland in Fred Astaire Biopic as Adele Astaire, Ginger Rogers
summary: Tom Holland has found his dance partners for Sony Pictures’ yet-to-be-titled Fred Astaire biopic: Margaret Qualley and Sabrina Carpenter. As previously announced, Holland will play the debonair dancer in the upcoming Sony film, directed by Paul King, with Amy Pascal producing. Golden Globe nominee Qualley (“Maid,” “The Substance,” “Love of Your Life”) will star as […]
content:
Tom Holland has found his dance partners for Sony Pictures’ yet-to-be-titled Fred Astaire biopic: Margaret Qualley and Sabrina Carpenter.

As previously announced, Holland will play the debonair dancer in the upcoming Sony film, directed by Paul King, with Amy Pascal producing. Golden Globe nominee Qualley (“Maid,” “The Substance,” “Love of Your Life”) will star as Adele Astaire, while Grammy winner Carpenter will portray Ginger Rogers. Fred and Adele were major stars on Broadway and London’s West End before Fred went on to be one of cinema’s greatest stars, with co-star and dance partner Ginger Rogers.

“I am thrilled and honored to have been entrusted with telling the story of Fred Astaire and his original dance partner — his big sister Adele — to the big screen,” King said in a statement about the casting news. “Fred left a timeless legacy of dance on film — most famously in his collaborations with Ginger Rogers — while Adele’s work has been lost to history; indeed, no footage of her dancing survives. The cinematic challenge of bringing to life these icons of the twentieth century is one that I could not imagine without Tom Holland, Margaret Qualley and Sabrina Carpenter by my side.”

Popular on Variety

King directs from a script he co-wrote with Steven Levenson, based on the book “The Astaires: Fred & Adele” by Kathleen Riley. Riley also serves as a script and story consultant.

Ava Astaire McKenzie, Fred Astaire’s daughter, and her son, Tyler McKenzie, who serves as a consultant and co-producer on the project, also shared their support.

“I’m delighted to support this endeavor to celebrate the extraordinary careers and enduring legacy of my father and aunt, who were among the biggest musical stars of their era,” said Astaire McKenzie. “With Kathleen Riley’s seminal biography as its foundation, and the creative team in place, the story of their partnership both on and off the stage is in the best care.”

McKenzie added: “Guided by the incredible filmmaking team led by director Paul King, writer Steven Levenson, producer Amy Pascal and Tom Holland, I know their legacy will be beautifully brought to life for a whole new generation.”

Fred Astaire starred in more than 30 film musicals, in addition to his stage career on Broadway and the West End over the course of a seven-decade career. Astaire is usually remembered for his pairings with Rogers, who starred in several films with him, including the classics “Swing Time” (1936), “The Gay Divorcee” (1934) and “Top Hat” (1935).

Holland has been attached to star as Astaire for five years, and after spending the summer with dominating the box office with “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” and “The Odyssey,” he’s been rehearsing for the part. (The movies are the two highest-grossing films of 2026.)

“I’m diving back into the dance studio,” Holland teased during a recent appearance on “Good Morning America.”

One might remember that before he was a Marvel superhero, Holland began his acting career on the London stage, playing the title role in “Billy Elliot the Musical” on the West End from 2008 to 2010. With that background, Holland also said that he intended to do all of the dancing himself. “I have a desire to use no doubles, to do all of the dancing, to shoot those dances in one shot — how he would have done it.”

Holland is among the producers of the Fred Astaire film (via his Billy 17 banner), alongside Pascal and Rachel O’Connor; and Ben Holden and Josh Hyams on behalf of Lightbulb Pictures. Executive producers are Harry Holland and Will South (on behalf of Billy17), Will Clarke and Andy Mayson (Altitude Films) and Levenson.

Holland is repped by WME and Sloane Offer; Qualley is repped by CAA, Anonymous Content and Sloane Offer; Carpenter is repped by Paradigm Talent Agency, Foundation Media Partners, Volara Management, Perlman Management Group and Goodman Genow; and King is repped by Independent Talent Group, WME and Davis Law Group.

Deadline first reported news of Qualley and Carpenter’s involvement.

title: Bryce Dallas Howard on the Declining Statistics for Female Directors in Hollywood: ‘Whatever Is Currently Being Done is Not Enough’
summary: Bryce Dallas Howard is calling on Hollywood to make a change. While at Variety’s L.A. Power of Women event on Wednesday in Beverly Hills, the actress and filmmaker reflected on the declining statistics for women directors in Hollywood. A 2025 study described the year as a “Great Recession” for female filmmakers, with just nine women […]
content:
Bryce Dallas Howard is calling on Hollywood to make a change.

While at Variety’s L.A. Power of Women event on Wednesday in Beverly Hills, the actress and filmmaker reflected on the declining statistics for women directors in Hollywood. A 2025 study described the year as a “Great Recession” for female filmmakers, with just nine women directing the 100 top-grossing films at the U.S. box office. That figure corresponds to just 8.1% of female directors (or a ratio of 11.3 men for every woman). In 2024, women accounted for 13.4% of directors of the 100 top-grossing films.

“The facts are that the numbers are an indication of something real,” Howard told Variety senior entertainment writer Angelique Jackson. “Whatever is currently being done is not enough.”

Howard speaks from experience: she has directed several episodes of the Star Wars shows “Ahsoka,” “The Mandalorian,” “The Book of Boba Fett” and “The Skeleton Crew,” as well as the feature-length documentaries 2019’s “Dads” and 2025’s “Pets.” In 2021, Howard was announced to direct a reboot of Disney’s “Flight of the Navigator,” but the project is still billed as being in pre-production.

Throughout the industry, Howard has seen a focus on mentorship for female filmmakers, but what Hollywood must prioritize more of, she explained, is sponsorship.

“It’s really difficult to get paid to do the thing that you want to do in this business,” Howard said. “And the amount of time between jobs is so significant that, unless you come from privilege or you have another job that somehow allows you to be flexible, you’re not getting a shot. You’re not even getting a chance, and that has to change.”

Sponsorship is greater than just funding a movie, Howard noted. Companies need to step up to finance the research and development throughout the project — ranging from early workshops to cultivating a team of artists to bring the film to life.

“There are so many brilliant artists and so little support, and it is incumbent upon people like me to make that a reality,” she said. “And I constantly fall short. And I will not quit.”

Next up, Howard directed two episodes of “Ahsoka” Season 2, and said that working on the Star Wars show, starring Rosario Dawson, was one of the “best summers of [her] life.”

“The first season was so fantastic, and to build on that, [creator and Lucasfilm president Dave Filoni] is getting to do a lot of stuff that he’s been waiting decades to do,” Howard said about the action-packed episodes. “Rosario and him are just partners. He trusts himself, but he trusts Rosario just as much.”

title: Ari Emanuel Details Hollywood Rise in New Memoir:  Harvey Weinstein Feuds, Signing Martin Scorsese and a Tense Evening With Larry David and Elon Musk
summary: Ari Emanuel has spent more than three decades making deals, building companies and occasionally screaming his way through Hollywood. Now, the superagent-turned-media mogul is telling his own story. In a new memoir “Roll the Calls,” released Sept. 22, Emanuel chronicles his rise from the CAA mailroom to one of the most powerful positions in entertainment […]
content:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

Ari Emanuel has spent more than three decades making deals, building companies and occasionally screaming his way through Hollywood. Now, the superagent-turned-media mogul is telling his own story.

In a new memoir “Roll the Calls,” released Sept. 22, Emanuel chronicles his rise from the CAA mailroom to one of the most powerful positions in entertainment and sports. The 432-page book was written alongside J.R. Moehringer, the Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist who collaborated with Prince Harry on “Spare” and Andre Agassi on “Open.

As its title suggests, “Roll the Calls” takes its name from the old-school agency practice of having an assistant line up one phone conversation after another — a routine that defined Emanuel’s famously relentless work style. The book moves through his early days at CAA and ICM, the 1995 founding of Endeavor and its eventual merger with the William Morris Agency, as well as the acquisitions of IMG and UFC and the creation of TKO Group Holdings, which brought UFC and WWE under the same corporate umbrella. Emanuel now serves as executive chair and CEO of TKO and executive chairman of WME Group.

But the memoir is as much an account of Emanuel’s temperament as his dealmaking. Emanuel writes candidly about his lifelong struggles with dyslexia, growing up in Chicago alongside his high-achieving brothers Rahm and Zeke Emanuel and developing the combative personality he would become notorious for in Hollywood. That reputation famously provided some of the inspiration for Jeremy Piven’s foul-mouthed agent Ari Gold on HBO’s “Entourage.”

Rage, competition and an almost compulsive need to keep moving recur throughout the book. Emanuel recounts fights, grudges and professional feuds alongside major career victories, while also reflecting on anxiety, therapy, family and the fleeting satisfaction of success. Despite his ascent from mailroom employee to billionaire entertainment executive, Emanuel writes that the rush of achievement rarely lasts.

The book is also packed with Hollywood names. Emanuel recalls signing Oprah Winfrey, clashing with Jeffrey Katzenberg and Harvey Weinstein, dealing with Michael Ovitz and navigating the careers and projects of longtime clients including Martin Scorsese and Mark Wahlberg. He also discusses dropping Donald Trump as a client after Trump entered the White House and recounts interactions with figures ranging from Barack Obama to Elon Musk.

Some of the more colorful anecdotes extend beyond the boardroom. Emanuel writes about nearly being hit by a truck in Los Angeles in the 1990s — an episode he frames as a turning point in his determination to stop letting fear dictate his decisions — as well as a near-confrontation between Larry David and Musk at Emanuel’s 2022 wedding to fashion designer Sarah Staudinger. He also revisits behind-the-scenes battles on films including Martin Scorsese’s “The Departed.”

Emanuel co-founded Endeavor in 1995 after leaving ICM and spent the following decades turning the upstart talent agency into a sprawling entertainment company. Endeavor merged with William Morris in 2009, acquired sports and fashion giant IMG in 2014 and bought UFC in 2016 in a deal valued at roughly $4 billion. UFC later combined with WWE to form publicly traded TKO Group Holdings in 2023. Endeavor itself was taken private by Silver Lake in 2025.

title: ‘Adults’ Star Rachel Marsh On Creating “Hiccup” Pop Anthem With Director: “We Tried All Different Versions”
summary: After unexpectedly dropping the summer anthem with Season 2 of Adults, Rachel Marsh is looking back on her journey to onscreen pop icon. The actress, who plays dental assistant Carly in the FX comedy series, explained that she and director Paul Briganti “tried all different versions” of her hit pop single “Hiccup”, which appeared in […]
content:
After unexpectedly dropping the summer anthem with Season 2 of Adults, Rachel Marsh is looking back on her journey to onscreen pop icon.

The actress, who plays dental assistant Carly in the FX comedy series, explained that she and director Paul Briganti “tried all different versions” of her hit pop single “Hiccup”, which appeared in the episode “Pop Girlie”, now available to stream on Hulu.

“It’s interesting because this is [Carly’s] livestream, but I was supposed to take it super seriously. But also, the joke is that I’m bad at it,” she explained to A*Pop. “So, holding all three of those things in my hands was very confusing.”

Marsh continued, “So, in that sense, Paul our director, we just tried a bunch of shit and saw what was coming across as someone earnestly trying to do a good job, but also not doing a good job. So, it was a really fun, almost like an acting exercise to be like, ‘lemme just try to be stupid and see if that is coming across in a way that someone is trying really hard,’ or ‘lemme try to take this very seriously and see if that comes across in a way that’s very earnest.’ We tried all different versions of it.”

Watch on Deadline

In the episode, while awaiting the results of her dental school exams, Carly decides to explore her inner dream to become a pop star, releasing her rusty—albeit catchy—single “Hiccup” with reluctant support from her boyfriend Samir (Malik Elassal).

Malik Elassal as Samir and Rachel Marsh as Carly in ‘Adults’ (FX)

Marsh can currently be seen in the romantic-comedy The Love Hypothesis, which is now available to stream on Prime Video.

title: Adam Brody Declares Support For “Free Palestine” Ahead Of ‘Nobody Wants This’ Season 3
summary: As Netflix prepares to release another season of its mixed-faith Jewish rom-com Nobody Wants This, leading man Adam Brody is using his platform to speak up for Palestinians. The 2x Golden Globe-nominated actor emphasized his support for “Free Palestine” as the topic of Israel’s attacks on Gaza came up in a recent interview ahead of […]
content:
As Netflix prepares to release another season of its mixed-faith Jewish rom-com Nobody Wants This, leading man Adam Brody is using his platform to speak up for Palestinians.

The 2x Golden Globe-nominated actor emphasized his support for “Free Palestine” as the topic of Israel’s attacks on Gaza came up in a recent interview ahead of Season 3 of Nobody Wants This, arriving Oct. 22 on Netflix.

“Between COVID, a second Trump term, Israel-Gaza, it’s really brought out some different beliefs that I was ignorant to, and then disheartened by,” he told GQ about Hollywood’s conservative pivot.

Brody admitted that “truthfully,” the Israel-Hamas conflict has not come up for him in recent interviews, despite his role as Rabbi Noah Roklov in the Erin Foster-created series. “I have spoken a lot about it privately. I haven’t spoken much about it publicly,” he noted.

Watch on Deadline

“Put me down as thinking it’s a genocide. Put me down as wanting a free Palestine,” said Brody. “It’s awful that it’s taken so much death and misery, but it does feel like it’s reaching a breaking point that it should have a while ago. I’m hopeful that another administration can really do some good and correct some of these policies that are helping that situation be as awful as it is.”

Adam Brody and Kristen Bell in ‘Nobody Wants This’ Netflix

In Nobody Wants This, agnostic podcaster Joanne Williams (Kristen Bell) begins an unexpected romance with Rabbi Noah Roklov (Brody), which shakes both their families as Joanne immerses herself in Noah’s culture and decides to convert to Judaism.

Brody’s comments come after several of his Hollywood peers were among around 100 arrested outside the United Nations General Assembly in New York City, where they were protesting the arrival of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Thursday.
