title: Chuck Varga Dies: Singer With Shock Metal Band GWAR Was 68
summary: Chuck Varga, a founding member and vocalist of the shock-rock heavy metal band GWAR, has died following a battle with cancer. A resident of Brooklyn, New York, Varga was 68. His death was announced GWAR bass player Casey Orr, who said Varga, who during his time with the band sometimes played the character Sexicutioner, died […]
content:
Chuck Varga, a founding member and vocalist of the shock-rock heavy metal band GWAR, has died following a battle with cancer. A resident of Brooklyn, New York, Varga was 68.

His death was announced GWAR bass player Casey Orr, who said Varga, who during his time with the band sometimes played the character Sexicutioner, died peacefully with wife Bambi at his side.

“He was one of a kind,” Orr said in the statement. “As an artist, as a performer; as a scholar and a gentleman. I’m better for having known him and the world is lesser for his leaving. He is most likely being welcomed into Valhalla right now by Brockie and Smooty and all who went before. Raise your glass and tell his tales. Legends never die. Hail Varga! Hail Sexicutioner!”

Varga disclosed his cancer diagnosis last April, with his GWAR bandmates launching a nationwide blood donation campaign in his honor. Donors received a shirt designed by Varga.

Watch on Deadline

Varga performed vocals with the band during its 1986-1996 breakthrough, returning for stints from 2000-2002 and 2014-2017 and 2022.

Born in 1958, Varga later attended Virginia Commonwealth University where he met and befriend fellow student Hunter Jackson, and the two would set up a production space called The Slave Pit with the intention of making student movies. The creative community of musicians, artists, and filmmakers associated with The Slave Pit soon gave rise to the rock band GWAR, which combined heavy metal music, sci-fi and medieval Nordic mythology and Kiss-style costumes taken to violent and grotesque extremes.

The band became a favorite in the Richmond area before expanding their fanbase nationwide. In 1993 GWAR was Grammy-nominated for its long form music video Phallus in Wonderland (they lost to Annie Lennox) and three years later received another Grammy nominations in the Best Metal Performance category for the single “S.F.W.” (losing to Nine Inch Nails).

Heavy metal band GWAR in 2004 at a Times Square video shoot Brad Barket/Getty Images

Varga left the Richmond-based band in 1997, relocating to New York City to pursue opportunities in the film, TV and Broadway realms. He would occasionally and intermittently perform with GWAR until 2017. Following his departure from a full-time and permanent position with the band, Varga founded Hyperreal Productions, a costume and set design company.

Complete information on survivors was not immediately available.

title: Israeli Americans Protest ‘NAZA’ by Screening October 7 Footage Outside New York Premiere: ‘Compassion For Palestinian Civilians Doesn’t Require Us to Erase October 7’
summary: The Israeli-American Council organized a protest Saturday afternoon outside the New York Film Festival premiere of “NAZA,” which the organization has described as an “anti-Israel” film that “makes serious allegations about the IDF’s conduct in the Gaza Strip while ignoring findings and information that contradict its claims” and fails to present the full “context of […]
content:
The Israeli-American Council organized a protest Saturday afternoon outside the New York Film Festival premiere of “NAZA,” which the organization has described as an “anti-Israel” film that “makes serious allegations about the IDF’s conduct in the Gaza Strip while ignoring findings and information that contradict its claims” and fails to present the full “context of the October 7 attack that led to the war.”

“We mourn every innocent life lost in this war, Israeli or Palestinian. But compassion for Palestinian civilians does not require us to erase October 7, ignore Hamas or accept one narrative without questioning it,” said Noa Peri-Jensch, chief communities officer of the Israeli-American Council (IAC). “This is why we are here today: not to prevent anyone from speaking, but to make sure that our voices, our experiences and the truth are being heard as well.”

“NAZA,” which was shot at night on the rooftops of Tel Aviv and shows “in detail the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza,” recently won a special jury prize at the Venice Film Festival. The documentary is now set to release in more than 50 territories before becoming available to stream for free on The Guardian’s website.

Popular on Variety

As “NAZA” screened inside Lincoln Center’s Alice Tully Hall, more than 50 protesters gathered outside the venue, where mobile LED trucks projected graphic footage from October 7 and portraits of those who were killed that day. Demonstrators carried various versions of signs that read, “LEARN THE FACTS. KNOW THE TRUTH.” There was also an additional security presence outside the venue, with over a dozen police officers on watch.

Peri-Jensch introduced Rom El-Hai, a survivor of the Oct. 7 attack on the Nova music festival. He said “it doesn’t surprise [him]” that the New York Film Festival would screen a film made by “traitors” to the Israeli cause.



“If there is someone here who wants to make a film about genocide, about hatred, brutality and killing innocent people, all the material is here,” El-Hai said, flashing his phone to the crowd. “I took pictures of everything. I saw the hatred with my own eyes.”

Karen Toledano, a protestor who stood in solidarity with the IAC, expressed that she feels like Israeli voices “have been stifled” within the creative community



“I feel like our voices have been stifled in spaces that have called themselves inclusive for many years,” Toledano said. “Sometimes when I do try to have a calm conversation and I’m encountered with anger, I know in my head that there just isn’t an argument on the other side. But it doesn’t make it any easier to swallow when really all you want to do is talk about the facts and set the record straight.”

On Thursday, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu delivered a defiant address to the U.N. General Assembly, which prompted a mass walkout of delegates who left the room when his speech began, “Where were you when the Iranian tyrants butchered and maimed tens of thousands of unarmed Iranian civilians?”

Hundreds of pro-Palestine protestors gathered outside the United Nations building, resulting in roughly 100 arrests, including Hannah Einbinder and Susan Sarandon.

“The U.S. government has the power to bring an end to all of this killing, pillaging, and land theft, yet instead it chooses to welcome the butcher of Gaza with open arms,” Einbinder wrote online after being released from detention. “The fact that the orchestrator of all this bloodshed is roaming freely in our cities is an indictment of BOTH REPUBLICANS AND DEMOCRATS who enable and protect architects of genocide like Netanyahu. Let us not mistake the spectacle for the story: genocide is the headline, and it is time for it to end.”

title: Marine Atlan’s French Oscar Hopeful ‘La Gradiva’ Takes Top Prizes at 30th Queer Lisboa – the Biggest Edition to Date
summary: French filmmaker Marine Atlan’s lauded debut film “La Gradiva” proved the big winner at the 30th Queer Lisboa – International Queer Film Festival, taking the best feature film and Audience Awards. A sweeping portrait of the vicissitudes of youth, the film, which also won the top prize at the Cannes Critics’ Week, follows a group […]
content:
French filmmaker Marine Atlan’s lauded debut film “La Gradiva” proved the big winner at the 30th Queer Lisboa – International Queer Film Festival, taking the best feature film and Audience Awards.

A sweeping portrait of the vicissitudes of youth, the film, which also won the top prize at the Cannes Critics’ Week, follows a group of French students on a final-year school trip to Pompeii, led by a passionate teacher eager to instill in them cultural and historical appreciation.

Lorena Ros’ Spanish documentary “Up and Running” (“Corren las Liebres”) likewise scored best documentary and Audience Awards. The film offers a candid look at the growing marginalization and homelessness amongst the trans ex-prisoner population in Barcelona.

Popular on Variety

This year’s festival, which closed Saturday with a screening of Leah Nelson’s animated feature film “Tangles,” was the most popular ever, attracting the highest number of attendees in its history, with more than 11,500 admissions at the festival’s 67 screenings over nine days — a 53% increase over 2025.

“This edition of the festival was particularly rewarding for us,” Queer Lisboa artistic director João Ferreira told Variety. “We surpassed the historic milestone of 11,500 spectators, the highest attendance ever recorded in our festival. And it was equally rewarding because we saw the audience respond to a particularly ambitious film program, which we put together to mark our 30th anniversary, from the retrospective — which was also one of the most extensive in our history in terms of number of screenings — to the many films from the major European festivals that we managed to premiere in Portugal.

“Having started the festival in 1997 as the first film festival in Lisbon, and still going strong, despite the many adversities we faced in these three decades, this really shows the artistic and political pertinence of queer cinema,” Ferreira added.

Indeed, with a program strongly characterized by themes of family, romantic and sexual relationships and a hopeful future, the festival team highlighted throughout the event the excellent shape of contemporary queer cinema and in particular the impressive range of the 2026 harvest of new films, which led to nine sold-out screenings, notably of “The Man I Love,” “Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma,” “Bitter Christmas,” “The Faggots & Their Friends Between Revolutions,” “Orlando,” “La conscience politique,” “The Passion According to GHB” and “Jim Queen.”

In awarding “La Gradiva” the festival’s top prize, the jury, comprised of cultural manager Kathleen Gomes, film programmer Maria João Madeira and actor Miguel Nunes, said the film was “a journey to a contemporary Italy that follows a group of teenagers at a decisive moment in their transition to adulthood. Amidst ruins, tectonic shifts and the vibrancy of nature, the characters question themselves, fall in love and hurt one another, navigating a landscape as ancient as it is unstable. The archaeology of history, the formation of identities and the search for a sense of belonging converge as the vital force behind this dazzling debut work, which touches on the fragility of human nature.”

Variety’s Jessica Kiang wrote in her review: “Seismically sensitive and deeply moving, Atlan’s film is simply one of the most piercingly accurate and immersive portrayals ever, of that fleeting moment when — not really a kid but still, really, a kid — you are simultaneously the most forcibly socialized and possibly the loneliest you will ever be.”

“La Gradiva” is one the five finalists in the race to be France’s entry for this best international feature Oscar. The film will be released Stateside via 1-2 Special and is being handled in Portugal by NOS Audiovisuais.

Up and Running (Corren las Liebres) Courtesy of Queer Lisboa

Commenting on its selection of “Up and Running” as best doc, the jury — comprising film programmer Diana Cipriano, journalist Filipe Santa-Bárbara and Luis Rosado from the RTP2 editorial team — said the film won “for the generosity and respect shown through the camera’s lens, for the magnetism of the women it portrays, particularly Noa, and the way it allows their character to rise above all their vulnerabilities.”

In the same section, the jury also awarded a special mention to Nông Nhật Quang’s Vietnamese doc “Baby Jackfruit Baby Guava.” The film, which premiered at Visions du Réel, journeys into the past through the director’s diaries and family photographs.

Nuestro Cuerpo Es una Estrella que Se Expande Courtesy of Queer Lisboa

Mexican documentary “Nuestro Cuerpo Es una Estrella que Se Expande,” by siblings Semillites Hernández Velasco and Tania Hernández Velasco, a reflection on trans sensibilities intertwined with the landscape and family ties, won the top prize in the Queer Art Competition, a section dedicated to works that explore the boundaries of cinematic languages and genres.

The jury, comprising Brazilian director Leonardo Mouramateus, curator Marta Mestre and German filmmaker Matthias Müller, also awarded a special mention to “Life Is About Losing Everything,” by brothers Benjamin Ramírez Pérez and Stefan Ramírez Pérez, “a fascinating and colorful hybrid that serves as an adaptation of the highly distinctive universe of Canadian poet and feminist writer Lynn Crosbie,” presented as a world premiere at the festival.

Je veux qu’on se souvienne de nous Courtesy of Hutong Productions, Le Bal

In the Short Film Competition, “Je veux qu’on se souvienne de nous,” by French writer Hélène Giannecchini, won the best short award, while “Fronteriza,” a Brazilian-Paraguayan production by Nay Mendl and Rosa Caldeira, won the AltContent Award.

Taking the top prize in the In My Shorts Competition, dedicated to short films from European film schools, was “Ãsheghetam,” a French-Swiss-Iranian production by Iranian filmmaker Filmsaaz.

Across both sections, the festival screened 32 short films, judged by Brazilian cinematographer Aline Belfort, filmmaker Caio Amado Soares and programmer Lou Loução.

title: Chris Hansen Reacts to ‘Primetime’ and Robert Pattinson’s Portrayal of Him: ‘So Bizarre’ and ‘Detached From Reality’
summary: Chris Hansen finally took a seat for “Primetime,” and he was not happy about the portrayal of himself. The former “To Catch a Predator” host said on Fox News’ “Jesse Watters Primetime” in August that he left the offices of distributor A24 without seeing the film due to the legal agreement they wanted him to […]
content:
Chris Hansen finally took a seat for “Primetime,” and he was not happy about the portrayal of himself.

The former “To Catch a Predator” host said on Fox News’ “Jesse Watters Primetime” in August that he left the offices of distributor A24 without seeing the film due to the legal agreement they wanted him to sign. “I’ve never seen anything quite like it,” he said of the agreement. He also said he found Robert Pattinson’s impression “overly dramatic,” but that his family thought it was a “pretty good imitation.”

Following a screening of Lance Oppenheim’s drama, Hansen has now shared his reactions to the full film in a 20-minute-long YouTube video posted to his channel, “Have A Seat With Chris Hansen,” on Friday.

Popular on Variety

“It was so bizarre and so in-and-out of reality,” Hansen said. “Obviously, I’m not objective because the character is, you know, me, but it was so detached from reality or anything I’ve experienced then or now doing the investigations. I’m not sure what the point of it was.”

The former host went on to criticize Pattinson’s performance, saying that “this version of Chris Hansen” was “so detached, so unhinged, so dark, so unlikeable… I mean, it’s upset my colleagues, current and former.” Hansen explained that he had about 13 members of his former crew see the film, and while some felt that the “film work was good” in terms of the story, they “got bored after the first 30 minutes.”

Hansen also called out Oppenheim for having a “dark image of what he wanted to do,” regardless of whether it had really happened in that way, in the host’s opinion. “He wanted to create a horror-like film with interesting photography and didn’t want to hear anything else,” he said. “[He] didn’t want to have his mind polluted by anything positive that this actually achieved over the last 22 years.”

He continued: “Hollywood wants to demonize the guy doing what I think is very good work that has created a dialogue that didn’t exist before and an awareness that didn’t exist before. And yet they turn him into the bad guy. And so you have to question the motives of not coming forward and talking to me or anybody who I worked closely with over the years. And they didn’t want to hear that Chris Hansen is a good guy. They didn’t want to hear that this work is important.”

He went on to say there was not one thing he liked about the film. When asked if there were any scenes that he saw that he knew didn’t happen, he responded, “almost every one of them.” “In a way, it’s a hit piece on me and the series, which is weird,” he said.

The film stars Pattinson as Hansen in 2006 as “To Catch a Predator” transitioned from “Dateline NBC” to its own primetime block. A24 labeled the film as “inspired by true events,” rather than a biopic.

Pattinson himself hoped Hansen would come around on the portrayal. “I would hope the amount of inspiration his character has given a lot of people for years is some kind of compliment,” the actor said following Hansen’s comments on his imitation.

“Primetime” opened in theaters on Friday after making its world premiere at the Venice Film Festival, where it garnered buzz and a seven-minute ovation. It took second place at the box office with $8.49 million domestically.

content:

title: Chuck Varga, Founding Member of Heavy Metal Band Gwar, Dies at 68
summary: Chuck Varga, a founding member and vocalist of the heavy metal band Gwar, died on Friday following a battle with cancer. He was 68. Gwar bassist Casey Orr announced his death in a statement shared to Facebook, writing, “Chuck Varga has left this earthly realm. He passed peacefully, his beloved wife Bambi holding his hand. […]
content:
Chuck Varga, a founding member and vocalist of the heavy metal band Gwar, died on Friday following a battle with cancer. He was 68.

Gwar bassist Casey Orr announced his death in a statement shared to Facebook, writing, “Chuck Varga has left this earthly realm. He passed peacefully, his beloved wife Bambi holding his hand. He was one of a kind. As an artist, as a performer; as a scholar and gentleman. I’m better for having known him and the world is lesser for his leaving.”

Orr also shared that Varga would likely be welcomed into Valhalla, a hall where soldiers go after they die in Norse mythology, by late band members Dave Brockie and Cory Smoot.

Popular on Variety

“Raise your glass and tell his tales,” Orr concluded. “Legends never die. Hail Varga! Hail Sexicutioner!”

While on stage, Varga would often play a character named Sexicutioner. The rock band, known for its unconventional costumes and intentionally offensive lyrics, was nominated for two Grammys, one in 1993 for Best Long Form Music Video and another in 1996 for Best Metal Performance. Gwar is currently preparing to tour this October.

Varga’s battle with cancer became public in April, and the band organized a blood drive and fundraiser in his honor. Donors would receive a shirt designed by Varga, with Gwar’s Bob Gorman noting that Varga’s “illustrations, character designs, performances and artistic vision” continue to influence the band and his aesthetic “helped define an entire universe.”

Varga attended Virginia Commonwealth University, where he met fellow student Hunter Jackson. The two co-founded The Slave Pit, a production space aimed toward creating student films, and its creative community ultimately led to the creation of Gwar.

In 1997, Varga left the band and moved to New York City to focus his career on film, TV and Broadway. He would return to perform with Gwar intermittently until 2017, when he founded the costume and set design company Hyperreal Productions.

title: San Sebastián: Mike Leigh’s ‘Tender Loving Care’ Wins Golden Shell & Best Screenplay
summary: Mike Leigh’s latest and potential last feature, Tender Loving Care, has won the San Sebastián Film Festival’s top prize, the Golden Shell, alongside the award for Best Screenplay. Scroll down for the full list of winners. Leigh’s Tender Loving Care also won the Silver Shell for Best Leading Performance for actress Kate O’Flynn, who shared […]
content:
Mike Leigh’s latest and potential last feature, Tender Loving Care, has won the San Sebastián Film Festival’s top prize, the Golden Shell, alongside the award for Best Screenplay. Scroll down for the full list of winners.

Leigh’s Tender Loving Care also won the Silver Shell for Best Leading Performance for actress Kate O’Flynn, who shared the prize with Asta Kamma August for her role in Growth of the Soil. That film, directed by Hans Petter Moland, also won the Jury Prize for Best Cinematography.

The Special Jury Prize was awarded to Border, directed by Ah Biao; the Silver Shell for Best Director went to Amanda Kernell for Brace Your Heart, while Javier Cámara won the Silver Shell for Best Supporting Performance for his work in 5 More Minutes. The City of Donostia/San Sebastián Audience Award went to La bola negra.

Ira Sachs presided over this year’s jury in San Sebastián. His fellow jurors were director and screenwriter Genki Kawamura, screenwriter Catherine Paillé, actress and producer Alice Braga, actress Patricia López Arnaiz, actor Bill Skarsgård, and producer Mike Goodridge.

Watch on Deadline

Leigh was not present in Spain to accept his awards. The veteran filmmaker is currently in New York for the U.S. premiere of Tender Loving Care, so he sent a video message to Spain.

“What a great honour it is. Thank you for awarding Tender Loving Care, our film, but not least and especially for The Golden Shell. Thank you, thank you, and love to everybody,” Leigh said.

title: ‘Evil Dead Burn’ Gets HBO Max Exclusive Streaming Premiere Date
summary: Evil Dead Burn, Sébastien Vaniček latest contribution to the long-running Evil Dead franchise, will make its global streaming debut exclusively on HBO Max on Friday, October 2. The New Line Cinema/Warner Bros. Pictures chiller will debut on HBO linear on Saturday, October 3, at 8 p.m. ET, following special showings of Fede Álvarez’s Evil Dead […]
content:
Evil Dead Burn, Sébastien Vaniček latest contribution to the long-running Evil Dead franchise, will make its global streaming debut exclusively on HBO Max on Friday, October 2.

The New Line Cinema/Warner Bros. Pictures chiller will debut on HBO linear on Saturday, October 3, at 8 p.m. ET, following special showings of Fede Álvarez’s Evil Dead (2013) and Lee Cronin’s Evil Dead Rise (2023).

Released to theaters last July, Evil Dead Burn, directed by Vaniček and written by Vaniček and Florent Bernard, stars Souheila Yacoub, Tandi Wright, Hunter Doohan, Luciane Buchanan, Erroll Shand and Maude Davey.

The synopsis: “After the loss of her husband, a woman seeks solace with her in-laws in their secluded family home. As one by one they are transformed into Deadites – turning the gathering into a family reunion from hell – she comes to discover that the vows she took in life live on… even in death.”

Watch on Deadline

The film is directed by Sébastien Vaniček and written by Sébastien Vaniček and. It is produced by Rob Tapert and Sam Raimi. The executive producers are Bruce Campbell, Romel Adam, Sarah Spurway, Jose Cañas and Lee Cronin.

Following Sam Raimi’s original trilogy, which included The Evil Dead (1981), Evil Dead II (1987) and Army of Darkness (1993), the franchise was rebooted with Álvarez’s Evil Dead in 2013. Cronin’s Evil Dead Rise steered the movies in a new darker direction, scoring $147M globally. Evil Dead Burn hit U.S. theaters July 10, and next-in-line Evil Dead Wrath from Francis Galluppi is set for 2028.

title: ‘Family Guy’ Releases Devilish Trailer For Halloween Special With Kieran Culkin
summary: Family Guy is expecting a treat for Halloween: Kieran Culkin will voice none other than the Devil himself in Hulu’s October 5 special Family Guy: Happy Hell-o-ween. Check out the new trailer for a little glimpse. The animated series has been celebrating Halloween with special episodes since 2006, and this year is no different. The […]
content:
Family Guy is expecting a treat for Halloween: Kieran Culkin will voice none other than the Devil himself in Hulu’s October 5 special Family Guy: Happy Hell-o-ween. Check out the new trailer for a little glimpse.

The animated series has been celebrating Halloween with special episodes since 2006, and this year is no different.

The synopsis: “Brian and Stewie find themselves in Hell — not an annoying day, the actual underworld — paying for 24 seasons’ worth of bad behavior. When they manage to annoy even the Devil himself, they end up in charge.”

In the trailer – watch it above – the demise of Brian and Stewie after they get hit by a car is followed by a quick trip to Hell where they’re soon filling in for a fed-up Satan. Flashes of the underworld, Family Guy-style, ensue, with flames, skeletons, demons, a mariachi band and various forms of torture setting the mood.

Watch on Deadline

Best of all: Peter makes a visit, explaining, “In real life, I’m choking on a Now and Later that I refuse to chew.” Watch the trailer to see if he sticks around.

Family Guy, a 20th Television Animation production, stars Seth MacFarlane, Alex Borstein, Seth Green, Mila Kunis, Mike Henry, Patrick Warburton and Arif Zahir. MacFarlane is the creator and executive producer. Rich Appel and Alec Sulkin serve as executive producers and showrunners, while Steve Callaghan, Danny Smith, Kara Vallow, Mark Hentemann, Patrick Meighan, and Alex Carter are executive producers.

title: ‘The Simpsons’ Boss on Season Premiere Guests Emma Thompson and Colin Jost; ‘Treehouse of Horror’ Spoilers; Jack in the Box Meal Easter Eggs and Movie Update
summary: “The Simpsons” returns on Sunday, Sept. 27, on Fox with a Season 38 opener (“The Children’s Book Job”) that parodies children’s books, featuring guest voice Emma Thompson as a beloved children’s book author who comes to town for a benefit to save Springfield Elementary from closing. But when her character — saucy British writer Constance […]
content:
“The Simpsons” returns on Sunday, Sept. 27, on Fox with a Season 38 opener (“The Children’s Book Job”) that parodies children’s books, featuring guest voice Emma Thompson as a beloved children’s book author who comes to town for a benefit to save Springfield Elementary from closing.

But when her character — saucy British writer Constance Clavinger — turns out to be a handful (getting drunk at the airport bar, for starters), Homer struggles to get her to the school on time. They go on an adventure across town as he tries to get her, “Get Him to the Greek” style, to a school book fair organized by new PTA president Marge.

Colin Jost also appears as himself, reading his own children’s book to the Springfield Elementary audience, much to their indifference.

Popular on Variety

In one sequence, Homer daydreams that Springfield and its citizens have turned into settings and characters from kids’ books like “The Very Hungry Caterpillar,” Richard Scarry’s universe, “Don’t Let the Pigeon Drive the Bus,” “Captain Underpants,” “Diary of a Wimpy Kid” and more.

“The genesis of this was, when you’re lucky enough to work on ‘The Simpsons,’ you can ask yourself, ‘What kind of cool thing can we portray in the Matt Groening/‘Simpsons’ style that we’ve never done?’” says executive producer Matt Selman. “And one of those are classic children’s books, like ‘Make Way for Ducklings.’”

Selman calls the episode a “love letter” to that world of children’s books. “I love my love letters,” he says. “Richard Scarry, Eric Carle from ‘The Hungry Caterpillar,’ all these generational children’s artists. We got really excited about that.”

Dan Vebber is the credited writer on the episode, while Matthew Nastuk is the director; Selman says Vebber and co-executive producer Mike Price cooked up the story idea, “a take on the ‘mild-mannered person has to get crazy person from ‘Point A’ to Point B’ kind of story … Two people thrown together in crazy situations become friends, become enemies and then become friends again. I love a good ’80s movie structure. So, for all the people who still love ‘Get Him to the Greek,’ this is the episode for you!”

Thompson’s character plays a large role in the episode. “If you’re going to write a giant guest part, you want an icon, a bucket list person like Emma Thompson,” Selman says. “And she threw herself into it with full gusto. It’s sort of an interesting season premiere in that you’re meeting a new character and it’s kind of Homer’s side adventure.”

Homer is enlisted to pick up Constance — and, realizing that he has been spending too much time ignoring his family and playing a free game on his phone, ultimately decides to make up for it by saving the day.

“It makes a lot of great points about parenting and trying not to be a checked-out parent,” Selman says. “And this line I like in it, Homer says, ‘children’s books are a better parent than I’ll ever be.’ It’s a good little bit of truthfulness there from Homer.”

Among more upcoming episodes, “Diary of a Chimpy Kid” (Oct. 4) follows Bart and Lisa as they adopt a baby chimp. “Homer watches a YouTube video about what adult chimps do to their human owners, which is bite off their fingers, faces and genitals,” Selman says. “And Homer becomes terrified of a baby chimp as Bart and Lisa learn how to co-parent. There’s some genital mutilation comedy in that one, but I am very pleased with it!”

In another upcoming episode, “The Kosmic Kruiser,” Bart and Lisa are trapped in an abandoned immersive theme park experience. And “Testing 1-2-3” will look at the world of neurodiversity. “I think it’s terrific,” Selman says of threading the needle on that one between being funny and being empathetic. “We’re very proud of it.”

As for “Treehouse of Horror XXXVII” (Oct. 25), the original opening is a “Simpsons”/“Nightmare Before Christmas” mashup, produced by Stoopid Buddy Stoodios — featuring “Simpsons” versions of the “Nightmare Before Christmas” characters.

Then, one segment is inspired by the British novel “The Husbands,” by Holly Gramazio, in which Homer goes to the shed and comes out as a different husband for Marge. Suddenly, she’s married to Lenny. Or Kang and Kodos. Tiffany Haddish guests as Marge’s best friend in one of her new husband realities, “kind of like how in rom-coms characters always have a sassy best friend,” Selman notes. “She lectures Marge about dating, and it’s like a stand-up set.”

Another segment is described as “Freaky Friday” meets “Pet Sematary,” where “Homer accidentally kills Bart and the dog and buries them, and they come back just having their bodies switched. And in the third one, “Homer mysteriously vanished years ago, and the teenage versions of Bart and Lisa find out that evil witch versions of Patty and Selma have trapped him in endless murderous Driver’s Ed films.”

This year’s “Treehouse of Horror” is timed to the show’s current tie-in with Jack in the Box. The fast-food chain is currently promoting a “Munchie Meal of Horror,” featuring six collectable glow-in the dark cups (which have already sold out at many locations).

“One of the great joys of this job is to do these little collabs with industries you’re not part of, like fast food or video games or toys or theme parks or whatever,” Selman says. “These collectible cups are just gorgeous and pretty high quality. Like everything we do, they sold out in one second. Yeah. Now they’re on eBay for $200. I said, ‘make sure you make enough cups!’ And they said, ‘we know about how many cups to make.’ And guess what? They didn’t!”

The “Simpsons” meals are full of references from the show — like Bart’s twin brother Hugo, from Season 8, who appears on a cup. “In that episode, Hugo would eat fish heads, and in our version of the cup, Hugo is eating the Jack in the Box fish sandwich. It’s just very fun to do a 30-year fish callback.”

Selman admits that “I procrastinated from working on the stuff that I should be working on by working really hard on this box. And there are so many ‘Simpsons’ Easter eggs on this box that you would think it was Easter, not Halloween. You can quote me on that. Definitely quote me on that.”

And here’s perhaps the ultimate obscure Easter egg: On the “Munchie Meal of Horror” box, several “Simpsons” characters are dressed like the now-obscure 1970s era “Jack in the Box Bunch” like the “Hamburgermeister,” “Onion Ring Thing” and “Secret Sauce Agent.” (Those characters were eliminated in 1980, but a grown-up version of “Jack” returned in 1994 — this time in a suit and round clown head. He’s still the chain’s spokesperson today.

“When I was a kid, I would go to Jack in the Box, and there was the Jack in the Box version of the McDonaldland gang that no one remembers but me. It was a very goofy bunch of fast food mascots. And so I made the bullies wear those costumes. That’s what the bullies are dressed up as, and people are like, ‘Who are they dressed as?’ They’re dressed as the 1970s Jack in the Box Gang: Secret Sauce Agent, Onion Ring Thing and Hamburgermeister. I haven’t gone on the internet to see if anyone has figured this out! But that is a big mashup.”

The meal box also includes comical gravestones with dead “Simpsons” favorites like Frank Grimes. “I bet he didn’t think he’d ever be on a Munchie Meal box, right?” Selman says.

He adds: “This is how hard the movie is that I’m just throwing myself into these boxes.”

Oh yes, the movie. How’s that going? The new “Simpsons” movie is currently slated to premiere on Sept. 3, 2027 (shifted from its original July 23 date). It’s already written, and yes, it may have a title. But Selman won’t share just yet.

“The working title is ‘New Simpsons Movie,’ but we might have an actual title,” he says. “It hasn’t been approved yet. But [the movie] is going to be great! It’s already ’S’ tier.”

S tier? “People love to rank things on the internet as part of our reductive society that we live in, right? People will rank things between F-D-C-B-A, and then S is the best. And people will do it for everything. What’s the best protein drink? What’s the best Alan Moore graphic novel? So, the movie’s going to be S tier. That’s my promise to you.”

Here’s the logline to “The Simpsons” Season 38 premiere, “The Children’s Book Job”: “Marge hopes to save Springfield Elementary by inviting a reclusive British children’s author (guest star Emma Thompson) to appear at the school’s book fair. But Homer botches his assignment of picking the author up at the airport, and the drunken pepper pot leads him on a desperate wild chase to get her to the school on time.” The episode airs Sunday, Sept. 27, at 8 p.m. on Fox, and streams the next day on Hulu.
