summary: At this weekend’s Zurich Summit a group of film financiers were asked by Deadline for their thoughts on the prospects of a U.S. federal film incentive. Last week, a bipartisan group of lawmakers unveiled the bill for a 20% incentive, which with bonuses could bring the total rebate to 30%. The move has long been […]
content:
At this weekend’s Zurich Summit a group of film financiers were asked by Deadline for their thoughts on the prospects of a U.S. federal film incentive.

Last week, a bipartisan group of lawmakers unveiled the bill for a 20% incentive, which with bonuses could bring the total rebate to 30%. The move has long been called-for by the U.S. industry concerned by the exodus of production overseas.

Alex Walton, former Co-Lead & Partner at WME Independent, told the Summit the move was “hugely positive”: “It’s wild to think there hasn’t been an efficient tax credit in America. It has helped many other countries. Spain is booming because of it now; and all over Europe. It’s going to take some time to be realized and for financial institutions to be able to cash flow it. But you’ve got to believe it will happen within the next three-four years, and then that will see all the foreign tax credits compete harder to maintain their positions.”

A start date is not yet set. The proposed text from last week stated that the credit would apply to qualifying film and TV productions beginning in taxable years after December 31, 2026 (effectively targeting projects starting in 2027). But bills can take years to pass.

Watch on Deadline

Andrea Scarso, Managing Partner at prolific financier IPR.VC, whose credits include Marty Supreme and Materialists, agreed that a U.S. incentive would be “positive” but also cautioned against rising production costs: “It remains to be seen whether the prices and budgets are also going up by the same amount, which is something that happens in some foreign territories when they increase the amount of tax credit or soft money. It’s always a balance. But overall, I think it’s good news.”

Sarah Schweitzman, Co-Head CAA Media Finance, noted: “What’s important is that when you look at some of the international markets, you realize that we’re making movies there because of a tax incentive situation and I think if we’re able to federalize a tax incentive program in the U.S. it’s going to create many more jobs and invigorate crews, which is something we absolutely need in the U.S.”

A recent Motion Picture Association study claimed that a federal film tax credit could increase U.S. production spending by $125BN and add more than 143,000 jobs by 2035.

You can read more about the bill here.

title: Chris Rock Says Infidelity and Struggling to ‘Make It’ Aren’t Just Hollywood Problems: ‘If You Got No Love, You’re Broke as F—k’
summary: Chris Rock’s new movie “Misty Green” centers on a fictional actress (Rosalind Eleazar) mounting a Hollywood comeback after years in the throes of a fading career. Misty’s journey pokes fun at some of the trappings of trying to “make it” in the entertainment industry, a pursuit that Rock himself is rejecting after his decades-spanning career […]
content:
Chris Rock’s new movie “Misty Green” centers on a fictional actress (Rosalind Eleazar) mounting a Hollywood comeback after years in the throes of a fading career. Misty’s journey pokes fun at some of the trappings of trying to “make it” in the entertainment industry, a pursuit that Rock himself is rejecting after his decades-spanning career in the biz.

“Most people don’t make it, quote unquote, in Hollywood,” he told Variety at the “Misty Green” New York Film Festival premiere Saturday night. “Making it is, to me, where I’m at right now: my daughter having great kids. Having love in your life. If you got no love, you’re broke as f—k. That’s making it. All this other stuff, it’s just a job at the end of the day.”

Rock plays a director who reunites with Misty after previously getting her booted from a “Cinderella” remake. (Earlier this month, he revealed to Variety that he originally imagined Donald Glover for the role.) Rock and Eleazar’s characters bond over their shared inability to remain faithful in relationships, playing into a familiar stereotype about Hollywood life.

Popular on Variety

“I don’t think it’s a Hollywood thing, it’s just life,” Rock told Variety. “Our two characters bond over our infidelities. And, yeah, it’s a lot. But it’s show business, man. Rock ’n’ roll!”

“Misty Green” also marks a real-life underdog moment for Eleazar, who tops the call sheet on a feature film for the first time. Following its premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival, Variety chief awards editor Clayton Davis declared that Eleazar “is a best actress contender that dares anyone in the room to argue otherwise.”

“I’ve had bouts of not working,” Eleazar explained. “ I know many actors that have had huge bouts of not working and are constantly knocked down. And I have a lot of respect for actors that get up and do it all over again. But it’s also a universal story about any industry. It’s not just about actors.”

Rounding out the ensemble are Adam Driver, Daniel Kaluuya, Anna Kendrick and Topher Grace. On just a $5 million price tag, Rock says he was able to assemble a star-studded cast for “Misty Green” by keeping the production local to Los Angeles.

“That was one of the reasons I got this great cast, because I just happened to be filming in L.A., so that definitely helped,” he said. “I would love to film more movies in L.A. It’s a money thing at this point. Tax incentives would help.”

title: Adam Brody Calls for a ‘Free Palestine,’ Says He’s Never ‘Ducked’ Politics: ‘I Just Answer the Questions I’m Asked’
summary: Adam Brody is calling for a “free Palestine” and explaining why his political activism doesn’t come up more often during his red-carpet and press appearances. “I just answer the questions I’m asked,” the actor told GQ. “And it’s true. I’m not wearing a pin, so I’m not inviting a certain question, and perhaps I should. […]
content:
Adam Brody is calling for a “free Palestine” and explaining why his political activism doesn’t come up more often during his red-carpet and press appearances.

“I just answer the questions I’m asked,” the actor told GQ. “And it’s true. I’m not wearing a pin, so I’m not inviting a certain question, and perhaps I should. I really admire people who do. But 99% of what I’m asked about is about the show. I’m not trying to plead ignorance—here we are doing a political interview, so it makes sense that we wade into this territory—but I’ve never ducked a question, really, not a political question anyway.”

The “O.C.” actor explained that while he hadn’t spoken publicly about the Israel-Gaza issue before, it comes up “a lot” for him in private. He then made his stance on the conflict clear: “Put me down as thinking it’s a genocide,” he said. “Put me down as wanting a free Palestine. It’s awful that it’s taken so much death and misery, but it does feel like it’s reaching a breaking point that it should have a while ago.”

Popular on Variety

Brody, who isn’t on social media, also defended his decision to remain offline. “I think being off social media has been the healthiest thing. I’m forced to use a lot of tools and products where I don’t believe in the heads of those companies, but I’m sure as shit not going to be on anything that Elon Musk is a part of,” he said. “I know people are doing really good work on [X], and I’m really glad about that. But it’s not for me, and I don’t have any guilt about not being on it. Sorry, I feel great about it.”

Brody has starred in Netflix’s romantic comedy series “Nobody Wants This” as rabbi Noah Roklov since Season 1 premiered in 2024. Season 3 is due on the streamer on Oct. 22.

“That ‘first time’ feeling, all over again. After recommitting to each other at the end of last season, Joanne (Kristen Bell) and Noah (Adam Brody) are moving into a home — and a relationship — that finally feels solid, embracing every exciting ‘first’ that comes with building their life together,” reads the official description for the new season. “Sasha (Timothy Simons) and Esther (Jackie Tohn) are thrust back into the dating world, whether they like it or not, stumbling through all the awkwardness (and unexpected thrill) of getting to know someone new, right as Morgan (Justine Lupe) takes her career to the next level, on her way to becoming an (almost) media sensation. Meanwhile, Sasha and Morgan have been circling something neither of them has been able to admit to.”

Erin Foster created the series and executive produces along with Jenni Konner and Bruce Eric Kaplan, who both serve as showrunners.

title: ‘Avengers: Endgame Encore’ Scores Massive $86 Million Globally, Brad Pitt’s ‘Heart of the Beast’ Launches to $50 Million Worldwide
summary: “Avengers: Endgame” returned to theaters and assembled a massive $86 million globally, including $26 million in North America and $60 million overseas. Disney and Marvel’s 2019 blockbuster was already the second-highest-grossing movie in box office history with $2.79 billion; this weekend’s haul brings the movie’s staggering tally to $2.88 billion. It’s only $39 million behind […]
content:
“Avengers: Endgame” returned to theaters and assembled a massive $86 million globally, including $26 million in North America and $60 million overseas.

Disney and Marvel’s 2019 blockbuster was already the second-highest-grossing movie in box office history with $2.79 billion; this weekend’s haul brings the movie’s staggering tally to $2.88 billion. It’s only $39 million behind 2009’s “Avatar,” which is the biggest worldwide release of all time with $2.9 billion.

Disney and Marvel reissued “Avengers: Endgame” to stoke excitement for “Avengers: Doomsday,” which opens in December. The upcoming comic book tentpole, which reunites just about every superhero on this planet (and others) and reintroduces Robert Downey Jr. not as Iron Man but as the villain Doctor Doom, is expected to be one of the biggest movies of the year. This re-release offered new footage as well as a chance to introduce viewers to the studio’s new take on premium large formats called “Infinity Vision.” It’s not a new technology but rather a “certification” that guarantees movie theaters will “meet rigorous technical standards,” per Disney. (As a note, “Avengers: Doomsday” won’t have access to Imax, the most ubiquitous of the PLFs, because “Dune: Part III” debuts on the same day and has the entire Imax footprint exclusively for three weeks.)

Popular on Variety

“Bringing ‘Avengers: Endgame’ back to theaters with an exclusive look at ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ is a smart way to give audiences a reason to revisit the film on the big screen and build excitement for what comes next,” says Rentrack’s head of marketplace trends Paul Dergarabedian. “‘Avengers: Doomsday’ is poised for one of the biggest opening weekend performances of all time.”

Directed by Anthony and Joe Russo, “Avengers: Doomsday” will be the 39th installment in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. It’s the most successful film franchise in history with $35.07 billion across all movies, a benchmark that was recently lifted by this summer’s juggernaut “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” with $2.2 billion.

“Avengers: Endgame Encore,” which the re-release has been dubbed, beat out several new releases to top domestic and global box office charts. Including this weekend’s grosses, “Endgame” strengthened its position as the third-largest North American release of all time with $884 million. Meanwhile, in a new milestone, “Avengers: Endgame” became the second movie ever to clear $2 billion at the international box office.

In terms of new releases, Paramount’s wilderness thriller “The Heart of the Beast” opened to $30.1 million from 63 markets. Along with a softer $20 million start in North America, the film has collected $50.1 million globally. Since it carries a hefty $82 million budget, “Heart of the Beast” will rely on staying power and interest at the international box office to recoup in its theatrical run. Reviews and word-of-mouth should help; “The Heart of the Beast” landed a strong 87% on Rotten Tomatoes and “A-” grade on CinemaScore exit polls. David Ayer (“The Beekeeper”) directed “Heart of Beast,” which stars Pitt as a retired veteran who navigates a brutal 58-mile trek to safety after he and his trusted combat dog survive a harrowing plane crash in the Alaskan wilderness.

Another newcomer, Universal and DreamWorks Animation’s “Forgotten Island,” struggled with $7.8 million from 34 markets. The movie has yet to land in several key international territories. Globally, “Forgotten Island” has earned just $20.6 million, including a softer-than-expected $12.8 million domestically. Universal shelled out $80 million to produce the family film, so the studio needs the positive reviews and audience reception to help “Forgotten Island” stick around beyond its debut. Directed by Joel Crawford and Januel Mercado, the story follows around two best friends who get stranded in a mystical world. H.E.R., Dave Franco and Jenny Slate lead the voice cast.

Earlier this week, Universal became the first to cross $5 billion worldwide in 2026, fueled by Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey” with $1.75 billion and “The Super Mario Galaxy Movie” with $1 billion.

title: How to Stream the VMAs Live Online
summary: The MTV Video Music Awards return Sunday night with one of the show’s biggest lineups in years, including Madonna’s first VMA performance in more than two decades, a Dolly Parton tribute from Kacey Musgraves and the world premiere of a new Taylor Swift music video. The 2026 MTV VMAs air live Sunday, Sept. 27 at […]
content:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

The MTV Video Music Awards return Sunday night with one of the show’s biggest lineups in years, including Madonna’s first VMA performance in more than two decades, a Dolly Parton tribute from Kacey Musgraves and the world premiere of a new Taylor Swift music video.

The 2026 MTV VMAs air live Sunday, Sept. 27 at 7:30 p.m. ET/4:30 p.m. PT from the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles. The ceremony will broadcast on CBS and simulcast on MTV, while cord-cutters can stream the entire show live on Paramount+. However, cable-cutters can stream the VMAs live online on DirecTV, currently offering a 5-day trial.

Snoop Dogg will host this year’s VMAs, which return to Los Angeles for the first time since 2017. Madonna, the night’s most-nominated artist with 11 nods, is set to open the show with her first VMA performance in 23 years, marking her first live appearance on the awards stage since her memorable 2003 performance alongside Britney Spears and Christina Aguilera.

The performance lineup also includes LISA, RAYE, Shaboozey, Gunna, Sienna Spiro, GENER8ION and Yung Lean. LISA will give the television debut of her new single “SaWaDiKa,” while GENER8ION and Yung Lean will premiere “STORM II” onstage. Shaboozey, meanwhile, will perform “Cowgirl” before being joined by Gunna for the first broadcast performance of their collaboration “High Noon.” RAYE and Sienna Spiro will both make their VMAs performance debuts.

One of the night’s most anticipated moments will be a special tribute to Dolly Parton, with Musgraves returning to the VMAs stage for her first performance at the ceremony in five years. Musgraves, who is nominated this year for best country for “Dry Spell,” will perform in honor of the country music icon.

There will also be a tribute to George Michael featuring RAYE, sombr and Teddy Swims, while Nirvana will receive this year’s Video Vanguard Award, 34 years after the band first performed at the VMAs in 1992.

Swift will have an especially busy night. In addition to receiving the inaugural MTV VMA Artist Director Honors — a new award recognizing musicians whose directing work has advanced music video storytelling — she will debut the music video for her new single “Patient Zero” during the telecast. Swift directed the video, which stars Colin Farrell and Dakota Johnson.

The honor recognizes Swift’s increasingly expansive body of work behind the camera, including videos for “The Man,” “cardigan,” “willow,” “Anti-Hero,” “Bejeweled,” “Fortnight” and “The Fate of Ophelia,” as well as “All Too Well: The Short Film.” Swift enters this year’s ceremony with nine nominations.

The 2026 MTV Video Music Awards air live Sunday, Sept. 27 at 7:30 p.m. ET/4:30 p.m. PT on CBS and MTV. Stream the VMAs live online on DirecTV.

title: Box Office: ‘Avengers: Endgame Encore’ Returns to No. 1 With $26 Million, ‘Primetime’ Scores Impressive $19 Million Debut
summary: “Avengers: Endgame Encore,” a re-release of Disney and Marvel’s 2019 blockbuster (with extra footage!), emerged victorious at the domestic box office over several new releases. “Avengers: Endgame Encore” generated $26 million from 3,060 North American theaters over the weekend, a sizable haul for a movie that’s been available to watch online for years. It was […]
content:
“Avengers: Endgame Encore,” a re-release of Disney and Marvel’s 2019 blockbuster (with extra footage!), emerged victorious at the domestic box office over several new releases.

“Avengers: Endgame Encore” generated $26 million from 3,060 North American theaters over the weekend, a sizable haul for a movie that’s been available to watch online for years. It was even bigger overseas with $60 million for a massive global tally of $86 million. Excitement for the re-release certainly bodes well for the studio’s upcoming “Avengers: Doomsday,” which opens in December and brings back nearly all of Earth’s Mightiest Heroes on another save-the-universe mission.

“Re-releases rarely earn more than $10 million,” says David A. Gross, who publishes the box office newsletter FranchiseRe. “As a marketing exercise, [this] is an effective way to build early word-of-mouth.”

Popular on Variety

Among new releases, A24’s “Primetime” enjoyed a sizable $19.2 million debut from 2,863 venues. This marks the third-best opening ever for A24, ranking behind this summer’s juggernaut “Backrooms” ($81.4 million) and Alex Garland’s 2024 dystopian “Civil War” ($25.5 million) and ahead of Josh Safdie and Timothée Chalamet’s 2025 frenetic sports drama “Marty Supreme” ($15.7 million). “Primetime,” directed by Lance Oppenheim and starring Robert Pattinson as “To Catch a Predator” host Chris Hansen, was produced for just $15 million, so it’s already well-positioned to turn a theatrical profit.

“This is an outstanding opening for an original crime drama,” Gross says. “Robert Pattinson has built an impressive filmography. The actor is a bona fide star, and he’s carrying this movie.”

Indeed, “Primetime” underscores the bankability of Pattinson, whose mighty year at the box office includes the indie hit “The Drama,” Christopher Nolan’s summer blockbuster “The Odyssey” and Denis Villeneuve’s upcoming “Dune: Part III.” Gen Z fueled the turnout for “Primetime,” with 69% of audiences under the age of 30. Moviegoers gave “Primetime” a mixed “B” grade on CinemaScore, which isn’t surprising given the unsettling nature of the film; it revolves around Hansen’s efforts to confront child sexual predators in complex sting operations. Meanwhile, the real-life Hansen was less enthused. After he finally saw the movie, he called it “so bizarre” and “detached from reality.”

This weekend’s other newcomers, Paramount’s Brad Pitt-led survival adventure “The Heart of the Beast,” Universal and DreamWorks Animation’s family-friendly “Forgotten Island,” struggled in their opening weekends despite great reviews and will need to stick around to justify their budgets.

“The Heart of the Beast” landed at No. 3 ahead of “Primetime” with $20 million from 3,435 theaters. It’s a decent start for an original movie that’s catering to adults. However, it’s disappointing for a movie carries a hefty $82 million price tag. Theater owners keep about 50% of ticket sales, so “Heart of the Beast” will rely on staying power and interest at the international box office to recoup in its theatrical run. It’s already faring better overseas, with $30.1 million from 63 markets for a global start of $50.1 million. Reviews and word-of-mouth should help; the film scored an 87% on Rotten Tomatoes and a strong “A-” grade on CinemaScore exit polls. David Ayer (“The Beekeeper”) directed “Heart of Beast,” which stars Pitt as a retired veteran who navigates a brutal 58-mile trek to safety after he and his trusted combat dog survive a harrowing plane crash in the Alaskan wilderness.

“Forgotten Island” stumbled in fifth place with $12.8 million from 4,548 venues. It’s also struggling overseas, where it has earned $7.8 million from 34 markets. Globally, “Forgotten Island” has earned a soft $20.6 million. The PG movie cost $80 million to produce, so Universal needs the family film to enjoy the box office longevity that benefited recent original animated efforts, such as DreamWorks Animation’s “The Wild Robot” and Sony’s sports-centric “GOAT,” both of which parlayed positive sentiments into ticket sales in the months after their debuts. “Forgotten Island” was embraced by critics and audiences, scoring an 94% on Rotten Tomatoes and “A” on CinemaScore. Directed by Joel Crawford and Januel Mercado, the story revolves around two best friends who get stranded in a mystical world. H.E.R., Dave Franco and Jenny Slate lead the voice cast.

“Hopefully these audiences’ reactions portend a long domestic run,” says Universal’s domestic distribution chief Jim Orr.

In any case, Universal has enjoyed a strong run at the box office and can afford a miss, should “Forgotten Island” struggle to break out. The studio recently became the first to cross $5 billion worldwide in 2026, fueled by Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey” with $1.75 billion and “The Super Mario Galaxy Movie” with $1 billion.

None of the new releases were able to outpace “Resident Evil,” which secured second place with $23 million from 3,684 locations in its second outing. Although that’s a steep 60% drop from last weekend’s leading $60 million debut, Sony’s reboot of the ’90s video game is already set up nicely in its theatrical run. The movie, directed by Zach Cregger of “Weapons” fame, has outperformed the entire domestic hauls of its franchise predecessors, having earned $103.4 million domestically and a mighty $196.5 million globally so far against a $75 million budget.

After an unexpectedly strong summer and a decent start to fall, the domestic box office stands at $7.8 billion and is on the verge of crossing $8 billion — a milestone the market didn’t reach last year until December. With several big blockbusters on the horizon, including “Avengers: Doomsday” and “Dune 3,” this will easily be the biggest year for movie theaters since the pandemic upended the box office.

“This weekend is another reminder that moviegoers in 2026 are showing up for everything from classic blockbuster reissues to original horror, thrillers, action and specialty titles,” says Rentrak’s head of marketplace trends Paul Dergarabedian.

title: How To Watch & Stream The 2026 MTV Video Music Awards
summary: The MTV Video Music Awards are back tonight for the 42nd awards show, celebrating the best music videos of the year. Hosted by 3x VMA winner Snoop Dogg, the ceremony broadcasts live on Sunday night from the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, with performances from Madonna, Kacey Musgraves, Lisa, Sombr and more. Madonna leads this […]
content:
The MTV Video Music Awards are back tonight for the 42nd awards show, celebrating the best music videos of the year.

Hosted by 3x VMA winner Snoop Dogg, the ceremony broadcasts live on Sunday night from the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, with performances from Madonna, Kacey Musgraves, Lisa, Sombr and more.

Madonna leads this year’s nominations with 13 categories, tying Lady Gaga’s 2010 record for most nominations in a year. She’s followed by Taylor Swift (11), Sabrina Carpenter (nine) and Ariana Grande (eight) in earning the most nominations.

Tonight’s awards show will honor Nirvana with the Video Vanguard Award, and Taylor Swift will receive the inaugural MTV VMA Artist Director Honors, with her “Patient Zero” music video from The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore making its world premiere during the simulcast.

Watch on Deadline

This years MTV VMA performances will include tributes to Dolly Parton and George Michael, marking 40 years since his solo debut album Faith.

With all this and more expected for the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards, read on for how to watch or stream the awards show.

How Can I Watch The 2026 VMAs?

The 2026 VMAs will air live from on Sunday, Sept. 27 from 7:30-9:30pm ET/4:30-6:30pm PT on CBS, simulcast on MTV and streaming on Paramount+ (Premium) in the US. The show will be available globally the next day on Paramount+ and MTV.

Who Is Presenting At The 2026 VMAs?

The VMA presenters include some of this years nominees and winners of VMAs past, as well as a survivor, a superhero, a scream queen and a Saturday Night Live alum.

The lineup features Alex Warren, Belmont Cameli, Brandon Sklenar, Charli xcx, Ciara Miller, David Corenswet, Ella Bright, Isabel May, Jeff Probst, Rachel Dratch, Teyana Taylor, Troye Sivan and Tyla.

Who Is Performing At The 2026 VMAs?

Returning to the VMAs stage for her first performance there in 23 years, Madonna will open the awards show with some songs from Confessions II, presented by Spotify.

Following Dolly Parton’s death at age 80 last month, Kacey Musgraves will perform a tribute to the Queen of Country. Meanwhile, Raye, Sombr and Teddy Swims will team up for a tribute performance directed by Adam Blackstone, celebrating 40 years since the late George Michaels’ career-defining album Faith (1987).

Also performing at the 2026 MTV VMAs are Gener8ion & Yung Lean, Lisa, Shaboozey & Gunna and Sienna Spiro.

For more info, visit MTV.com.

title: Kevin Mayer Shares Thoughts On Paramount-Warner Bros Merger – Zurich Summit
summary: Former Disney exec Kevin Mayer, who oversaw his former employer’s 2019 acquisition of 20th Century Fox, has shared his thoughts on the Paramount-Warner Bros merger. The pragmatic exec, who has been co-CEO of Blackstone-backed media company Candle Media since 2021, told a panel at the Zurich Summit this weekend that consolidation in the media and […]
content:
Former Disney exec Kevin Mayer, who oversaw his former employer’s 2019 acquisition of 20th Century Fox, has shared his thoughts on the Paramount-Warner Bros merger.

The pragmatic exec, who has been co-CEO of Blackstone-backed media company Candle Media since 2021, told a panel at the Zurich Summit this weekend that consolidation in the media and entertainment sector was inevitable in a period of declining revenues.

“If we’re going to be intellectually honest about answering this question, you have to also ask yourself, what would happen if the merger didn’t happen,” he said in a response to a question on the merger.

Mayer said the film industry was in a phase of decline with “fewer and fewer” great financial outcomes, and that the status quo of a number of independent studios working with declining revenues no longer made financial sense.

Watch on Deadline

“Their ability to finance, to distribute and to market product is going to start to deteriorate very substantially. It already has, frankly. If we keep the standalone, the status quo, you’re going to have a larger number of very weak companies unable to do much in the future. That’s the future you’ve got to measure this consolidation against, in my opinion, not against some fanciful future where everything is as good as it was five, 10 years ago”.

Mayer said he expected Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison to keep his promises around producing 30 movies a year for at least five years after sealing of the deal.

“I did this once. I negotiated Disney’s purchase of 21st Century Fox, and I was responsible for integrating those two companies,” he said.

“David Ellison made some promises. I expect he’ll keep them. We have public promises that are that explicit… are very hard to reverse yourselves. I think for a period of time… for five years, he’ll do what he says. He’ll make the movies and he’ll release them theatrically, he’ll do it all.”

Mayer said he felt it was likely that Warner Bros. would continue to operate as a separate entity, based on his own experiences at Disney.

The biggest rub in the deal, he suggested, would be job losses in the industry, even if believed consolidation has “necessary”.

“When you hear these promises of $6 billion in synergies, that’s a euphemism for a lot of layoffs… That’s an extremely difficult thing, obviously, and that’s what I think this merger portends.”

title: ‘Avengers Endgame: Encore’ Powers $86M WW Re-Release Opening Ahead Of ‘Doomsday’ Global Domination
summary: What was old at the global box office this weekend was new as Disney/Marvel Studio’s Avengers Endgame: Encore led in an exceptional take for a re-release of $86M WW. Beamed Andrew Cripps, Disney’s Global Boss of Distribution, “The success of the re-release reiterates that there’s a massive fanbase for this franchise, and the fact that […]
content:
What was old at the global box office this weekend was new as Disney/Marvel Studio’s Avengers Endgame: Encore led in an exceptional take for a re-release of $86M WW.

Beamed Andrew Cripps, Disney’s Global Boss of Distribution, “The success of the re-release reiterates that there’s a massive fanbase for this franchise, and the fact that it’s a 7-year-old movie on Disney+, it’s an incredible opening.”

Close to 14% of Encore‘s cash came from Imax, which made $13.7M off the superhero pic for $4M domestic and $9.7M abroad.

Yes, with a handful of minutes of extra footage of the Russo Brothers’ upcoming Avengers: Doomsday, Encore was an advertisement for that movie, but one which yielded more bucks to the overall Marvel Cinematic Universe with $35 billion global across 38 titles. After this weekend, the lifetime worldwide take for Avengers: Endgame moves to $2.885B, behind Avatar‘s $2.92B and ahead of Spider-Man: Brand New Day‘s updated global tally of $2.495B.

Watch on Deadline

With $26M stateside, that repped the third best start for a re-release behind 1997’s re-issue of Star Wars ($35.9M) and 2011’s The Lion King 3D ($30.2M).

Overseas with $60M, Encore was the second-highest foreign debut for a re-release behind Titanic 3D in 2012 at current rates. That James Cameron movie at the height of the 3D craze did $67M boosted by China.

Avengers: Endgame bowed to No. 1 in China ($13.5M), UK ($5.4M), Mexico ($4.2M), Italy ($2.6M), Brazil ($2.2M), Germany ($2M), Australia, and was the best non-local in Japan ($2.6M) and Spain ($1.7M). Disney estimates that Encore was the highest ever opening weekend for a MPA re-release in UK, Mexico and Brazil as well as Netherlands, Greece, S. Africa, Poland, Albania, Bosnia, Bulgaria, Croatia, Hungary, Israel, Kazakhstan, Macedonia, Romania, Saudi Arabia, Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Turkey, Ukraine, UAE, India, Indonesia, Philippines, Hong Kong, Vietnam, Taiwan and all smaller Latin American territories.

Pic was second-highest opening ever for a MPA title in Italy, Australia, Malaysia, New Zealand, Singapore and Argentina.

Other No. 1 openings were Austria, Belgium, Norway, Poland, Sweden, Switzerland, Bosnia, Croatia, Czechia, Jordan, Kyrgyzstan (non-local), Lebanon, Qatar, Romania, Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Tajikistan, Turkey, Uzbekistan, Hong Kong, Malaysia, Singapore, India (non-local with $2.8M), Indonesia (non-local), Vietnam (non-local), Argentina and all smaller Latin American territories.

The Anthony and Joe Russo-directed movie ranked second in Korea in the holiday period of Chuseok holidays (Sept. 24-27) that’s described as the country’s Thanksgiving by sources. The No. 1 pic in Korea was The Assassin in a box office weekend where three local films dominated the top 5.

France did $2.1M, but Paramount’s Heart of the Beast led there with a Brad Pitt wow factor, that David Ayer-directed military vet and dog feature seeing $3.8M.

Austin Abrams in ‘ Resident Evil Sony

Second place worldwide is a fight between zombies and Pitt. Sony/Constantin’s Resident Evil posted a second frame of $50.3M, $27M of that coming from 65 overseas markets on 12,500+ screens. Cume abroad in both Sony and Constantin territories is $93M with an overall $196.5M WW.

UK, Mexico, and Australia each set franchise records in just the second weekend with market totals of $11.5M ($2.9M weekend), $9.0M ($2.2M weekend), and $5.4M ($1.7M weekend), respectively. France (Metropolitan) earned $1.8M (-39%) for a market take of $5.0M, and Germany (Constantin) grossed $1.5M (-40%) for a local cume of $4.5M. Next stops are China on Oct. 5 and Japan on Oct. 9 for the flesh-eating beings.

Odin and Brad Pitt in ‘Heart of the Beast’ Paramount Pictures

Heart of the Beast barked up $50.1M WW with $30.1M abroad from 63 markets. As we told you, France was tops, but also New Zealand and this is the ultimate outdoors film for them ($454K including previews from 128 sites). Also big was United Arab Emirates where a lot of yank moviegoers are with $1M, No. 1 at 58 sites. Middle East grossed $2.6M on the pic.

Rest including previews (except Argentina) were UK (No. 3, $2.7M at 559 locations), Mexico (No. 2, $2.4M), Australia (No. 3 with $1.6M at 307), Spain (No. 3, $1.5M at 326), Italy (No. 3 $1.2M at 370), Japan (No. 4, $1.2M at 344), Germany ($1M, No. 3 at 428 sites), Brazil (No. 4 $925K at 585 locations), Colombia (No. 2 $872K at 210), Netherlands (No. 3 $574K at 116 locations), Taiwan (No. 3 $419K at 90 sites), Poland (No. 3 grossing $407K at 178 locations), India (opened at #5 grossing $392K at 345 locations, Peru (No. 3 $304K at 108 locations), Ukraine (No. 1 $306K at 171 locations), Argentina (No. 3 $292K at 180 locations), Portugal (No. 1 $290K at 48 locations), Hong Kong (No. 4 $285K at 57), and Belgium (No. 3 grossing $276K at 80 locations).

A24’s Primetime with $19.1M stateside, had a limited launch abroad with $1.2M in France, Germany, Austria, India, Taiwan, Baltic’s and Iceland for an overall $20.3M WW. Of that, France did $530K and Germany/Austria was $325K. What’s interesting is some distribution sources believe, at least stateside, that Heart of the Beast is going to have a fantastic multiple off that A- CinemaScore, while Primetime is front loaded with a B. I beg to differ as Primetime sells itself when you sit in theater, however, the truth will be in the numbers.

Raissa (Liza Soberano), Prince Mermahn (Kevin McCann), Raww (Dave Franco) and Jo (H.E.R.) in ‘ Forgotten Island

Universal’s second weekend foreign, first weekend in North America of DreamWorks Animation’s Forgotten Island did $18.4M WW ($5.6M foreign from 34 territories and $12.8M domestic).

Philippines led with No. 1, $1.5M this weekend at 280 locations, well above major tentpoles Super Mario Bros, Despicable Me 4, Zootopia 2 and Minions: The Rise of Gru. It’s the biggest opening of the year for a Universal title there ahead of Odyssey. Spain did $500K at 390 sites for a No. 5 rank. The film has received a strong 7.3 FilmAffinity Score, just below The Wild Robot (7.5) and above Inside Out 2 (7.1) and Puss In Boots: The Last Wish (7.0). Italy was also No. 5 bow with $500K at 372. Brazil did $400K, No. 6 at 682. That includes $190K in previews. Israel posted No. 1 with $300K at 70 sites in line with Trolls and above Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse, Puss In Boots: The Last Wish, Wish, Hoppers and The Wild Robot. Forgotten Island opens into Sukkot Holidays, which run from Sept. 25 to Oct. 3. Korea, bowed to $219K at No. 10 at 550 sites, which includes $117K in previews. The film has received a strong CGV Egg score (96%). Sweden saw $150K at 132 in No. 5, an opening at this level is in line with Elio, Goat and Puss In Boots: The Last Wish. Australia held over with $737K in weekend 2 for a $1.8M cume. School holidays are taking place in 50% of the market, with the remaining 50% starting next Monday. Forgotten Island ranks No.4, as the top family film in the market, above Coyote vs. Acme (No.8), PAW Patrol (No.7) and Shaun the Sheep (No.10). Mexico added $300k in weekend dos to reach $1.4M cume. Forgotten Island ranks No.7 in the market.

title: Zoe Saldaña “Can’t Imagine” Taking On Another Taylor Sheridan Show: “‘Lioness’ Is All I Can Handle”
summary: Although Zoe Saldaña speaks highly of collaborating with Taylor Sheridan, don’t expect her to make a trip to Dutton Ranch anytime soon. The Lioness star recently explained why starring as Joe McNamara “is all that I can handle at this time,” noting she doesn’t have any plans to pop up elsewhere in the Sheridan TV […]
content:
Although Zoe Saldaña speaks highly of collaborating with Taylor Sheridan, don’t expect her to make a trip to Dutton Ranch anytime soon.

The Lioness star recently explained why starring as Joe McNamara “is all that I can handle at this time,” noting she doesn’t have any plans to pop up elsewhere in the Sheridan TV universe after three seasons on the Paramount+ series.

“I’m number one on the call sheet. I am first one in, last one out. I am prepping months before anybody ever is able to prep,” she told People. “So it’s already a lot of work for me.”

Saldaña said she “can’t imagine me taking on more of a Taylor Sheridan world,” adding, “The good takeaway that I’m grateful for is that he knows that I’m reliable, just like Joe is.”

Watch on Deadline

“I have my views, and I come with all heart, all brains, all muscle at all times,” said Saldaña. “So, no, I think I’m good here at Lioness.”

Starring and executive produced by Saldaña and Nicole Kidman, Season 3 of Lioness sees hidden networks, foreign operatives and personal betrayals collide. Joe (Saldaña) walks the line between duty and home as unseen forces circle her world. Patterns appear where they shouldn’t, names vanish and paths rearrange. Guided by Kaitlyn (Kidman) and Westfield (Michael Kelly), Joe confronts enemies operating in the shadows, leaving her to reckon with a war that now reaches into every part of her life.

title: ‘Musk’ Producer, Atwater-Magnific Exec & ‘Gods Don’t Give Gifts’ Director Talk AI: “It’s Important To Get In The Driver’s Seat” – Zurich Summit
summary: Musk producer Nick Shumaker, Hollywood film financier Vania Schlogel, directors Zack London (Gods Don’t Give Gifts) and Nick Holt (AI: Probably Nothing to Worry About) took to the stage at the Zurich Summit this weekend to dig into the implications of AI for film. Schlogel, who is founder and managing partner of L.A.-based Atwater Capital, […]
content:
Musk producer Nick Shumaker, Hollywood film financier Vania Schlogel, directors Zack London (Gods Don’t Give Gifts) and Nick Holt (AI: Probably Nothing to Worry About) took to the stage at the Zurich Summit this weekend to dig into the implications of AI for film.

Schlogel, who is founder and managing partner of L.A.-based Atwater Capital, also took up the baton of Chief Strategy Officer at AI creative platform Magnific, formerly known as Freepik, this summer.

The exec said that while her roots were in Hollywood film finance, she had understood it was an imperative for her to get to grips with AI during a board meeting at Magnific.

“In an interview about a year ago with the Financial Times, I’d actually said very publicly, that when all this AI stuff gets really big, I’m just going to go back to Idaho and disappear into the mountains, and that’s always actually been the genuine kind of feeling I espouse, as I’m not a technologist. I’ve always been a traditional Hollywood financier,” she told the panel.

Watch on Deadline

“Our founder showed us videos and images from our largest competitor and how they had become viral, and it was sexualized children’s IP, it was horrible depictions of women, some of them famous, some of them not… some very racist things,” she explained. “I had this light bulb moment that this might not be something that I have necessarily been inured to historically, but I actually do need to be involved in.”

Since embracing the technology, Schlogel said she had seen multiple cases where the use of AI made sense, commercially and ethically, even if there were aspects of the technology she has qualms about such as the way in which the confident tone of AI assistants can encourage “cognitive surrender” in human beings even when their level of expertise on a subject is higher that the LLM they are consulting.

“It really is on all of us to get in front of it so that we can shape the ethical direction it goes. Because this will shape society, is shaping society, is even shaping human empathy and how we view each other. So it’s so important to get in the driver’s seat of it, whether you love it or hate,” she said.

Shumaker, head of AC Independent at Anonymous Content, acknowledged the power of AI as a tool across the cinema chain but said he felt compelled to raise questions around the use of original content by generative AI programs.

“The whole fair use in AI thing needs to be addressed. The lawsuits from New York Times, from every major media outlet, disregarding just stealing things from my perspective and ingesting is totally inappropriate. And I just want to put that on record,” he said.

“That we can say that this is the way things are going, at the same time as there’s theft with regards to intellectual property, it’s not a good thing. The notion that we get clogged up in lawsuits for five or six years to address that is not good for humans, for creators, or frankly, for the future of writers or cinema.”

He clarified that while Alex Gibney’s Musk, on which he is a producer, touches on the way Elon Musk is using AI to shape the future, and not necessarily for the best, the documentary used very little of the technology in its production.

He noted the Elon Musk avatar had been created in CGI by humans at a company, which has collaborated with Gibney in the past, with AI only used at the post-production stage to help lip-synching.

London, who is also known under the YouTube pseudonym of Gossip Goblin, is currently gearing up for the theatrical release of his fully AI-generated sci-fi anthology Gods Don’t Give Gifts.

He echoed Schlogel comments on needing to get ahead of the technology, suggested that the polarisation of views in the creative communities around AI was not necessarily helpful or going to change anything in the outcome..

“The the tricky thing is that people see AI as this monolithic thing. Obviously you have full end-to-end automation on one end of the spectrum, and super light AI augmentation on the other, like tweaking the voice of Adrien Brody in The Brutalist. That’s a pretty vast spectrum,” he said.

“It’s become such a polarized topic, you have kind of radical zealots on both sides of the equation. You have the burn Hollywood to the ground side and you have the fuck AI side that you know basically refuses to even accept that it’s part of the equation,” he said.

“The reality is that it’s happening. It’s coming. There’s no point in human history where we’ve seen incredibly advanced technology and said, ‘No, we’re not going to do it.’ The luddites didn’t succeed, and probably the anti-AI movement won’t either.”

Talking about the use of AI on his upcoming film Gods Don’t Give Gifts, London said it would never have been made without the technology.

“This film would never get greenlit otherwise. It’s way too esoteric and niche and cerebral, and so it’s not that we’re replacing a story that would otherwise get told and hire more people. This story wouldn’t exist otherwise; it wouldn’t get made. “

The trio were joined on stage by director Nick Holt, whose documentary AI: Probably Nothing to Worry About was playing at the summit’s parent event the Zurich Film Festival this weekend

Revolving around interviews with computer scientist Geoffrey Hinton, known as “the godfather of AI,” for his work building artificial neural networks, DeepMind founder Demis Hassabis, as well as Anthropic and OpenAI engineers among others, it explores the question of whether AI will save or destroy humanity. ,

Tapping into questions around how AI will impact creativity, Holt said that, for now, he thought AI tools could make filmmaking more accessible.

“We’ve all got access to a pen and pencil, but not all of us can writer a Booker or Pulitzer award-winning novel. I think there are people with who could use AI to roll out concepts and films that otherwise might not get made. I just hope there’ll be a sense that the best work will always rise to the top,” he said.

“Hollywood studios aren’t shy of making 100 million dollar duds, and then the 14 year old in his bedroom or her bedroom using AI tools could make the next big hit. I think it’s a phenomenal tool for that, but I think the interesting thing that we have to deal with is are these systems grown rather than built, and then where does it go as far as our limitations?

title: ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Co-Director Explains It’s ‘Very Difficult’ to Evolve Marvel Characters, But ‘We Need To Surprise Ourselves’ and ‘Audiences’
summary: “Avengers: Doomsday” co-director Anthony Russo has opened up about the pressure that comes with evolving the franchise’s iconic superhero characters, explaining that finding the balance between moving the story forward and honoring those already-beloved characters can be “very difficult.” “It’s a very difficult part of the process because, I mean, we basically just have to […]
content:
“Avengers: Doomsday” co-director Anthony Russo has opened up about the pressure that comes with evolving the franchise’s iconic superhero characters, explaining that finding the balance between moving the story forward and honoring those already-beloved characters can be “very difficult.”

“It’s a very difficult part of the process because, I mean, we basically just have to use our own meters because we love the characters, we love the history, we love them in the same way that many fans do,” Russo said during a Q&A after a screening of “Avengers: Endgame Encore” (via GamesRadar+).

He continued: “But the one thing we always like to remind people of, you know, fandom does not speak with a single voice. There’s a wide variety of opinion in terms of who responds to which characters and which versions of which characters people respond to, it’s a very complex relationship that people have with the characters.”

Popular on Variety

Russo also said that he and his brother and co-director Joe have “a lot of respect for the storytelling journey that these characters have had up to this point.” “That’s part of their magic, a big part of their magic. But at the same time, we need to surprise ourselves in terms of who those characters are, where they can go, what they can do, what can happen, and in doing that, we hopefully surprise audiences as well.”

The director’s comments come nearly a year after an “Avengers: Doomsday” trailer spotlighted a much more serious Thor (Chris Hemsworth) than Marvel fans had seen in 2022’s “Thor: Love and Thunder.” The Taika Waititi-directed film performed well at the box office upon its release, but it divided fans who felt the character had become, in Hemsworth’s own words, “too silly.”

Russo also revealed that the film’s full cast has yet to be announced. “The cast is so large, and we’ve announced some of the cast, and we haven’t announced some of the cast,” said Russo. “I get confused myself over who we’ve announced and not announced, so I have to just slow down.” So far, the confirmed cast includes Hemsworth, Robert Downey Jr., Chris Evans, Paul Rudd, Simu Liu, Tom Hiddleston and more.

“Avengers: Doomsday” will hit theaters on Dec. 18.

title: Neil Patrick Harris to Star in ‘Damn Yankees’ Broadway Revival
summary: A revival of “Damn Yankees,” starring Neil Patrick Harris and Julianne Hough, will open next spring on Broadway. It’s the first Broadway revival of “Damn Yankees” in more than 30 years. Following last fall’s run at D.C.’s Arena Stage, this revised production features a book by Will Power and Dough Wright, with additional lyrics by […]
content:
A revival of “Damn Yankees,” starring Neil Patrick Harris and Julianne Hough, will open next spring on Broadway.

It’s the first Broadway revival of “Damn Yankees” in more than 30 years. Following last fall’s run at D.C.’s Arena Stage, this revised production features a book by Will Power and Dough Wright, with additional lyrics by Lynn Ahrens and direction and choreography by Sergio Trujillo.

“Damn Yankees,” which revolves around a middle-aged man who makes a Faustian bargain for his losing baseball team to somehow beat the unstoppable New York Yankees, debuted on Broadway in 1955 with Robert Shafer, Gwen Verdon, Ray Walston and Stephen Douglass. It won seven Tony Awards, including best musical. Richard Adler and Jerry Ross wrote the music and lyrics, with a book by George Abbott and Douglass Wallop. The show was last revived on Broadway in 1993 with Jarrod Emick, Bebe Neuwirth and Victor Garber.

“’Damn Yankees’ has always been one of our great American musicals, but I wasn’t interested in simply reviving it,” says Trujillo. “This ‘revisal’ preserves the heart, wit and soaring score that audiences love and is a real opportunity to bring joy back into the theater. ‘Damn Yankees’ is a celebration of America, and I hope audiences see themselves in it and remind them of the magic that only a great American musical can deliver. Let’s play ball!”

Popular on Variety

This revival moves the original 1950s-set story into the 21st century. Here’s the official logline: “It’s the early 2000s, and diehard baseball fan Joe Boyd dreams of seeing his beloved Baltimore Orioles return to glory. So when a charming stranger and his captivating accomplice arrive with an offer too good to refuse, Joe makes a deal that could give both him and his team a second chance. There’s just one catch…”

Harris will play the devil in disguise known as Applegate, Hough is making her Broadway debut as Joe’s wife Lola and Austin Scott is playing Young Joe. The rest of the cast has yet to be announced.

Harris won a Tony for the 2014 revival of “Hedwig and the Angry Inch” and has hosted the Tony Awards several times. He was recently on Broadway in “Art,” a play revival in which he starred alongside James Corden and Bobby Cannavale.

“I’ve never done the big Broadway musical, with a big ensemble and dance numbers. It’s been a bucket list for me,” Harris said during a press conference on Sunday at Yankees Stadium. Of his character, he added, “Playing someone who is devilish is always good. It’s fun to be naughty. I want Applegate to be as alluring and puppet-mastery as possible.”

“Damn Yankees” will play at the Marquis Theatre, with previews beginning on March 24 ahead of opening night on April 20.

In a first for Broadway, Major League Baseball and its production label MLB Studios will serve as a partner on the production.

“Baseball is mythology. Broadway is mythology. They both deliver thrilling, unrepeatable live entertainment to millions of fans each year,” said Haley Swindal, who serves as lead producer with Lia Vollack (“MJ”). “Bringing them together — with MLB at the table and this extraordinary creative team — isn’t just a revival. It’s a collision of American icons.”

Swindal is the granddaughter of legendary New York Yankees owner George Steinbrenner. Nicknamed “The Boss,” Steinbrenner was also a Broadway producer who invested in six productions, including the 1970 Tony Award-winner “Applause” and the 1974 musical “Seesaw.”

Noah Garden, MLB’s deputy commissioner of business and media, added, “We’re thrilled to partner with the entire team on the return of ‘Damn Yankees’ to Broadway, led by such great talents in Neil, Julianne and Austin. It’s incredibly important that our game continues to resonate outside the diamond and into different areas of culture. Baseball and Broadway fans both love high drama, high stakes and high hopes that they’re about to watch something unforgettable happen. ‘Damn Yankees’ celebrates that shared spirit, and we’re proud to help bring that energy to the stage.”

title: Nat Geo Kicks Off New Multi-Year Doc Franchise With ‘Africa Earth’s Wild Home’
summary: Unlike most conglomerate-owned media companies, National Geographic is still pouring money into documentaries. Their latest docuseries “Africa Earth’s Wild Home” is a seven-parter that took four years to make and employed over 50 people. It’s the first series in a multi-year franchise that will document the planet, one continent at a time. Nat Geo partnered […]
content:
Unlike most conglomerate-owned media companies, National Geographic is still pouring money into documentaries. Their latest docuseries “Africa Earth’s Wild Home” is a seven-parter that took four years to make and employed over 50 people. It’s the first series in a multi-year franchise that will document the planet, one continent at a time.



Nat Geo partnered with National Geographic Society’s global community of Explorers and scientists and Rolex’s Perpetual Planet Initiative to make the seven-series franchise.



Nat Geo president Courteney Monroe says that the partnership demonstrates a “shared commitment to protecting our natural world.”



“It’s proof of what’s possible when storytelling, science and a shared sense of purpose come together,” says Monroe. “Through this collaboration, we are expanding what natural history storytelling can reveal, whose voices it can elevate and how deeply it can connect audiences to the wonders of our planet.”



“Africa Earth’s Wild Home” is narrated and executive produced by Academy Award nominee Wunmi Mosaku. It was filmed in nearly 30 African countries and used new technology and cutting-edge CGI to reveal the continent’s history and the forces that shaped its natural environments. To capture how Africa’s varied ecosystems shape the animals that live within them, film crews were sent to deserts, forests, jungles, mountains and islands.



Showrunner and series editor Gavin Boyland says Africa became the first continent in the multi-year franchise because people often associate wildlife with Africa.



“Africa got the best wildlife,” says Boyland. “It’s got the most spectacle. It’s got the charismatic animals. So, what we wanted to do from the outset is show people a different side of Africa. So, while we absolutely filmed lions and elephants and all the kind of familiar wildlife, but we also wanted to show different environments, different landscapes and different species that live in those landscapes as well.”



Instead of reaching out to typical Western researchers and scientists, Boyland and his team went to Africa and approached wildlife guides, drivers, photographers, and locals who saw wildlife daily.



“Those people were able to point us towards new behaviors,” says Boyland.



“Africa Earth’s Wild Home” features sequences that have never been filmed before, including the smallest crocodile hunting bats in pitch-black caves, a grumpy black rain frog, a flying saucer beetle that digs trenches to harvest water from coastal fog, giant “vegetarian” land tortoises hunting birds, golden wolves hunting pelicans three times their size and a male fossa fighting to gain access to a female’s mating tree.



“The series inspires us to look closer, learn more and care more deeply,” says Jill Tiefenthaler, CEO of National Geographic Society. “That’s the same passion that drives our National Geographic Explorers, who are working every day to understand and protect the natural world. With partners like Rolex and Disney, we magnify the impact of their work, inspiring millions to care about our planet and its future.”



The final episode in “Africa Earth’s Wild Home” focuses on conservationists, photographers and scientists whose work safeguarding the continent underpins the series. Both the episode and the series build on a 70-year partnership between National Geographic and Rolex.



“Across seven episodes, the extraordinary filmmaking reveals that protecting Africa’s wild heart starts with understanding its fragile ecosystems,” says Rolex director of communication and image Arnaud Boetsch. “By shining a spotlight on the Explorers and scientists working on the frontlines of conservation, the series promises to spark not just wonder but hope for the future.”



“Africa Earth’s Wild Home” premieres Oct. 2 on National Geographic and streams on Disney+ and Hulu on Oct. 3. The series was produced by BBC Studios Natural History Unit for National Geographic.

title: Anthony Mackie Says Chris Evans Gave Him the ‘Avengers: Endgame’ Script Early, Revealing How He’d Become Captain America: ‘It Was Really Great and Really Emotional’
summary: Chris Evans and Anthony Mackie’s bond goes beyond their shared roles as Captain America. They’re also close friends, so much so that Evans gave Mackie early access to the “Avengers: Endgame” script, which is when the actor learned how he’d become the superhero. “Chris Evans is somebody who I hold near and dear,” Mackie said […]
content:
Chris Evans and Anthony Mackie’s bond goes beyond their shared roles as Captain America. They’re also close friends, so much so that Evans gave Mackie early access to the “Avengers: Endgame” script, which is when the actor learned how he’d become the superhero.

“Chris Evans is somebody who I hold near and dear,” Mackie said in a recent interview with Cigar Aficionado. “We’re at Chris’ house, and because he’s Captain America, he gets the [script] pages first. So he’s like, ‘Yo, did you read the new scene?’ I’m like, ‘Nah, what’s up?’ So, he takes me down…and he gave me the script and let me read it. And it was really great and really emotional to learn it from a friend…I don’t know a lot of actors who would have appreciated or celebrated that moment with a fellow actor in that way because I was taking his job for all intents and purposes.”

Evans first suited up as Captain America in 2011 in “Captain America: The First Avenger.” Mackie took over as the titular hero after receiving the iconic shield from Evans’ Captain America at the end of “Avengers: Endgame” in 2019. He led his first feature film as the superhero in 2025’s “Captain America: Brave New World.”

Popular on Variety

The Disney and Marvel 2019 blockbuster returned to theaters on Friday with extra footage as a special theatrical re-release leading up to “Avengers: Doomsday,” which comes out on Dec. 18. The re-release, titled “Avengers: Endgame Encore,” generated $26 million domestically over the weekend and $60 million overseas for a global tally of $86 million.

The film was already the second-highest-grossing movie in box office history with $2.79 billion. After this weekend, the movie has grossed $2.88 billion.

content:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

Some of the best athletes in the world are in Japan this week for the 2026 Asian Games, a multi-sport competition held every four years for countries in Asia.

This year’s Asian Games take place in Nagoya, located in the Aichi Prefecture in Japan, and Aichi–Nagoya 2026 makes the 20th edition of the event. Almost 20,000 athletes will compete for medals across 43 disciplines in Nagoya, including Filipino tennis star Alexandra Eala, Chinese Olympic swimming champion Pan Zhanle, Filipino Olympic gymnastics champ Carlos Yulo and the Indian men’s cricket team, who are the current title holders of the Twenty20 World Cup, Champions Trophy and Asia Cup.

How to Watch Asian Games 2026

A number of Asian broadcasters are airing the Asian Games live on TV and online through their respective streaming channels, including CCTV5 in China, RTM in Malaysia, MeWatch in Singapore and KBS and SBS in South Korea.

You can access all of those livestreams for free via a virtual private network like ExpressVPN. Download ExpressVPN (starting at just $2.99) and set your location to any of the countries above to watch an Asian Games live feed online for free.

Here in the U.S., viewers can also watch the Asian Games online and on television through Willow TV (available on Sling or Amazon Prime Video for just $10). Willow TV is best known for its international cricket coverage, but the streamer will also have hours of live coverage of the other sports as well. You can also access replays of past events.

Willow is available on its own through Prime Video, or as part of the Sling Desi Binge Plus package, which also includes access to Desi-themed series and movies on SonyLIV, Jio Cinema, Simply South and more. Sling has the package marked down to $10 for a limited time.

Both Sling and Prime Video let you watch the Asian Games online through Willow on your phone, tablet, computer or smart TV.

The 2026 Asian Games kicked off on Sept. 19 and run through Oct 4. For those wanting to watch Eala play, the women’s tennis tournament runs from Sept. 27 to Oct 3. Cricket, diving and athletics (track and field) are also among the sports still being contested this week.

The Asian Games come on the heels of the 2026 Commonwealth Games, which were held in July for athletes from nations across the British Commonwealth — I.e. countries that are currently or were formerly part of the British Empire.

title: Bill Gates Warns Unregulated AI Development Could “Cause A Billion Deaths”
summary: As Trump brushes off the need for additional guardrails around artificial intelligence, Bill Gates is sounding the alarm. In a recent interview, the Microsoft co-founder urged the U.S. government to implement regulations around the development of AI, following a meeting with CEOs of several of biggest AI companies, who agreed it’s necessary to slow down […]
content:
As Trump brushes off the need for additional guardrails around artificial intelligence, Bill Gates is sounding the alarm.

In a recent interview, the Microsoft co-founder urged the U.S. government to implement regulations around the development of AI, following a meeting with CEOs of several of biggest AI companies, who agreed it’s necessary to slow down the pace of the growing tech.

“No one thinks self-regulation is enough,” he said on NBC News’ Meet the Press. “You need law enforcement and the politicians to get into the discussion about what safeguards and monitoring look like. And that has to be a required thing. And it will be a little bit of overhead for the industry, but not a dramatic slowing of what they’re doing.”

Watch on Deadline

Gates added, “AI is certainly powerful enough to drive events that, you know, cause a billion deaths. You know, so even though it’s pretty hard to get to 100%, there’s never been a weapon as powerful as the combination of people with ill intent using the latest AI tools.”

Following recent warnings from those working in AI, California Gov. Gavin Newsom signed an executive order this month to fast-track stringent oversight and control of AI. Convening “a group of world-leading experts” within the next 60 days, the order lays out a discussion of “safety plans” and “an emergency shutoff, or ‘kill switch,’ for frontier models.”

On a federal level, Trump has brushed off concerns about AI as “a hoax,” insisting the U.S. government “already have tremendous CRIMINAL and REGULATORY power” over AI companies.

title: Jeff Probst Says “Nothing Has Changed” On ‘Survivor’ After Paramount Scrapped DEI: “We Need Diversity”
summary: Although Paramount was one of several companies to roll back their DEI initiative when Trump was re-elected, Survivor continues to operate by it. Host Jeff Probst recently noted that “nothing has changed” with how the reality competition series approaches diversity, equity and inclusion, noting that it was “one of the biggest positive changes ever” for […]
content:
Although Paramount was one of several companies to roll back their DEI initiative when Trump was re-elected, Survivor continues to operate by it.

Host Jeff Probst recently noted that “nothing has changed” with how the reality competition series approaches diversity, equity and inclusion, noting that it was “one of the biggest positive changes ever” for the CBS show that launched in 2000.

“And if you watch our show, you know that we’re so diverse — and it’s not just skin color or ethnicity. It goes much deeper than that. It’s one of the biggest positive changes ever,” he told The New York Times. “Our stories are so much more interesting now because we have people from completely different walks of life.”

Probst continued, “I feel no pressure. No one ever says, can you count the numbers again? But Jesse Tannenbaum, who runs our casting team, knows: There’s no stopping, not because we’re told to do it. This is what we need. We need diversity. It’s for narrative. All those differences matter in the story when you throw people together and force them to rely on each other while conspiring against each other. The more diverse, the more interesting.”

Watch on Deadline

In 2020, Paramount implemented a DEI initiative to make CBS and its other brands more inclusive, which the company rolled back last year amid the Trump administration’s attacks on such programs. Months later, Skydance pledged there would be no DEI policies under the Ellison’s reign as they sought the FCC’s approval of the merger.

Following its milestone 50th season, Probst returns to host Survivor for Season 51, airing Wednesdays at 8pm ET/PT on CBS and streaming live on Paramount+.

title: Jeff Probst Says ‘Survivor’ Needs Diversity Despite Paramount’s DEI Rollbacks: ‘All Those Differences Matter in the Story’
summary: Fifty seasons later, one key factor of “Survivor” remains the same: the show’s approach to diversity. Longtime host Jeff Probst told The New York Times that “nothing has changed” in the reality competition series’ approach, despite Paramount’s rollback of DEI initiatives to align with Trump’s mandates in 2025. Diversity, he explained, is integral to the […]
content:
Fifty seasons later, one key factor of “Survivor” remains the same: the show’s approach to diversity.

Longtime host Jeff Probst told The New York Times that “nothing has changed” in the reality competition series’ approach, despite Paramount’s rollback of DEI initiatives to align with Trump’s mandates in 2025.

Diversity, he explained, is integral to the show’s functionality. “And if you watch our show, you know that we’re so diverse — and it’s not just skin color or ethnicity. It goes much deeper than that. It’s one of the biggest positive changes ever,” Probst said. “Our stories are so much more interesting now because we have people from completely different walks of life.”

Popular on Variety

He continued: “I feel no pressure. No one ever says, ‘Can you count the numbers again?’ But Jesse Tannenbaum, who runs our casting team, knows: There’s no stopping, not because we’re told to do it. This is what we need. We need diversity. It’s for narrative. All those differences matter in the story when you throw people together and force them to rely on each other while conspiring against each other. The more diverse, the more interesting.”

While the show’s DEI initiatives have stayed the same, Probst explained how casting has changed since the show began in 2000.

“In the early seasons, the approach to casting and storytelling was different from the kind of storytelling we’re doing now,” Probst said. “You would cast for type. And friction was part of where we were at — we wanted friction in our storytelling, arguments and finger-pointing.”

Probst became more than just the host when he signed on as showrunner of the 51-season show in 2010, with the goal of making the series more cinematic.

“I always saw the game as a device. So when I was given the reins, the three things I really wanted to do were make it more cinematic; I wanted it to dive deep into Joseph Campbell’s “Hero’s Journey”; and I wanted it to be a family show. I knew that would change who we put on the show and the types of stories that we told.”

title: 2026 MTV VMAs Red Carpet: Taylor Swift, Lisa, Raye and More
summary: The 2026 MTV VMAs are in full swing, and music’s biggest stars are showing up and out on the red carpet.  Hosted by Snoop Dogg, this year’s Video Music Awards promises audiences a jam-packed program, including a performance from Madonna (her first at the show in more than two decades), a Dolly Parton tribute and, […]
content:
The 2026 MTV VMAs are in full swing, and music’s biggest stars are showing up and out on the red carpet.

Hosted by Snoop Dogg, this year’s Video Music Awards promises audiences a jam-packed program, including a performance from Madonna (her first at the show in more than two decades), a Dolly Parton tribute and, of course, the world premiere of Taylor Swift’s “Patient Zero” music video. 2026 also marks the first time the show has returned to Los Angeles since 2017.

In addition to Madonna and Musgraves, the night’s lineup is set to include performances from LISA, RAYE, Shaboozey, Gunna, Sienna Spiro, GENER8ION and Yung Lean. For RAYE and Sienna Spiro, the performance will be their VMAs debut. Shaboozey will perform “Cowgirl” and then join Gunna for the first broadcast performance of their collaboration “High Noon,” while LISA will debut her new single “SaWaDiKa” on television. GENER8ION and Yung Lean will premiere “STORM II” onstage.

Kacey Musgraves will perform the tribute to Parton, making her first appearance on the VMAs stage in five years. She is nominated for best country for “Dry Spell” this year. RAYE, Sombr and Teddy Swims will perform a tribute to George Michael. 34 years since Nirvana first performed at the VMAs in 1992, the band is set to receive this year’s Video Vanguard Award.

In addition to her video premiere, Swift will also be honored with the inaugural Artist-Director Award.

The 2026 MTV VMAs air live Sunday, Sept. 27 at 7:30 p.m. ET/4:30 p.m. PT from the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles. Learn how to stream the show here.

title: ‘Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother’ Starts Strong, Eyes ‘American Fiction’-Style Rollout — Specialty Box Office
summary: Bassam Tariq’s Mahershala Ali-starring TIFF favorite Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother had a strong limited opening as distributor Amazon MGM launched the awards contender into a platform release hewing to the path of American Fiction.. Also this weekend, A History of Concrete had a terrific expansion, as did If I Go Will They Miss […]
content:
Bassam Tariq’s Mahershala Ali-starring TIFF favorite Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother had a strong limited opening as distributor Amazon MGM launched the awards contender into a platform release hewing to the path of American Fiction..

Also this weekend, A History of Concrete had a terrific expansion, as did If I Go Will They Miss Me. Late summer phenomenon Buddy is still scaring up box office.

Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother launched in six theaters in New York and Los Angeles to $199k ($33.1k per screen average). The awards contender by Tariq (Mogul Mowgli) is Certified Fresh at 97% on Rotten Tomatoes with strong exit polling that showed a 60% ‘excellent’ with an 89% in the top two boxes and an overall 80% ‘definite recommend.’ Ali stars as Latif, a devoutly religious hitman who struggles to balance work, faith and fatherhood. When his wife dies, he embarks on a desperate journey across Houston to protect his children.

A hefty 47% of the audience for the action drama was 25–34. Some 72% is non-white with at 41% African American, 18% Hispanic, and 19% Asian.

Watch on Deadline

Tariq (Mogul Mowgli) “has a unique voice” with a young cinephile audience,” says Amazon MGM Studios head of domestic theatrical distribution Kevin Wilson. “And having [Ali] as an actor is making a lot of people pay attention.”

Comps aren’t obvious but he says the best one may be 2023 multi-Oscar-winner American Fiction by Cord Jefferson, starring Jeffrey Wright. The comedy-drama had a strong limited opening ($224k) followed by a slow rollout. Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother is eyeing 15 locations next week including Atlanta, Chicago, Washington, D.C. and Austin, playing in particular to non-white audiences who championed the movie’s debut. It will hit the top 10 to 12 markets, 30 to 40 screens, the following week, and move into moderate release Oct. 16 with 500 to 800 locations.

Platform rollouts are heavily reliant on word of mouth. “The best thing is other moviegoers telling their friends how good the film is,” Wilson says. Both Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother and American Fiction are from Amazon MGM’s Orion Pictures banner, which has had a great run under President Alana Mayo with titles from Nickel Boys and Till to Bottoms and Women Talking.

New indie releases: Ha Chan,Shake Your Booty! from Sony Pictures Classics directed by Josef Kubota Wladyka opened to $236.6k on 540 screens.

The Stunt Driver from IFC Films, by Michael Dowse starring Jay Baruchel, debuted with $102k at 670 locations.

Deep In The Heart 2: A Texas Rivers Story, directed by Ben Masters and narrated by Ethan Hawke, grossed an estimated $60k from 80 theaters across the state, as per mtuckman Media. This is a follow-up to 2022 doc Deep in the Heart: A Texas Wildlife Story, narrated by Matthew McConaughey, that grossed $480k.

Janus Films presented the 4K re-release of Douglas Keeve’s UNZIPPED exclusively at the Film Forum in NYC to $24k including sold out Q&As. The doc chronicles the launch of Isaac Mizrahi’s legendary Fall 1994 collection. Expands nationwide in October.

Sumerian Pictures opened Sundance comedy The Incomer on two screens (NYC and LA), grossing an estimated $18.2k.

Greenwich Entertainment’s The Scout is eyeing a $14.5k, also at Film Forum exclusively. The debut feature from Paula González-Nasser adds LA next week.

Holdovers: John Wilson’s comedic documentary The History Of Concrete from Magnolia Pictures had a strong expansion to 50 screens (from 1), grossing an estimated $350k for a cume of $511k. Expand to over 50 markets next week.

If I Go Will They Miss Me from Rich Spirit, starring Danielle Brooks and J Alphonse Nicholson and directed by Walter Thompson-Hernandez, is reporting $158k in week 3 on 101 screens for a $758k cume. Many engagements saw higher box office this weekend over last despite fewer shows due to a rush of new releases, indicating strong word of mouth.

American Doctor from Watermelon Pictures passed the half million mark with $23k at 30 theaters. The cume to date is $556.7k for the Gaza-set documentary that opened August 14.

R-rated kids show horror satire Buddy from Roadside Attractions is looking at another $717k from 709 runs for a cume pushing $26.4 million since its August 28 opening.

Daniel And The Fiery Furnace from faith-based distributor EKKL Entertainment is reporting a $1.5 million second weekend on 1,301 screens for a $6.2 million cume.
