title: Taylor Swift Premieres ‘Patient Zero’ Music Video at VMAs, Turning Her New ‘Showgirl: Encore’ Single Into a Dramatic Ghost Story
summary: It’s a love story? Hardly — it’s a ghost story. Taylor Swift brought her “Patient Zero” music video to the MTV Video Music Awards Sunday night for its official world premiere, following up the release of the single at the beginning of the weekend with visuals that take the triangle in the song into more […]
content:
It’s a love story? Hardly — it’s a ghost story. Taylor Swift brought her “Patient Zero” music video to the MTV Video Music Awards Sunday night for its official world premiere, following up the release of the single at the beginning of the weekend with visuals that take the triangle in the song into more dramatic and even spookier realms than might have been anticipated. Dakota Johnson and Colin Ferrell amping up the tension, which ultimately has reverberations that go beyond just a bad breakup.

Fans had only seen a 13-second teaser for the video prior to its premiere on the CBS/MTV/Paramount+ telecast, and they now know which character the headstone was for in the cemetery Swift and Johnson visit.

Popular on Variety

The video is, of course, Swift’s latest directorial effort, and the occasion of her attendance at the VMAs was receiving the inaugural Artist-Director Honor. It was not her only trip to the podium; after the initial speech and video premiere, Swift came back later in the show to accept a video of the year award for “The Fate of Ophelia,” at which point she thanked Dolly Parton for her inspiration.

The singer’s initial remarks prior to sharing the video were brief, after an introduction by Johnson. “First of all, I want to say thank you to MTV for giving this platform to music videos so long ago,” Swift began. “I got to start making music videos and being a part of music videos 20 years ago, and since then, I’ve gotten to be a part of making 60 music videos — roughly 60. Eighteen of those, I wrote and directed, and I really love writing and directing music videos. I’ve gotta tell you, though, that the main reason why I love writing and directing music videos so much is because you, the fans, make it so much fun. It’s so rewarding because you actually care about what we’re making. So, you know, I wanna say thank you to everyone who ever worked on a music video that I got to be a part of. I learned something from every single person that ever worked alongside me on these projects. Mainly I want to say thank you to the fans…

“And rather than say anything else, I think rather than than keep talking, I would love to, if it’s OK with you, show you my latest music video, stsarring my friend Dakota Johnson and Colin Ferrell. Cinematography by Chivo.”

“Chivo” is a nickname for Oscar-winning cinematographer Emmanuel Lubezki, who often works with Steven Spielberg, and who was shooting a Swift video for the first time. She seems especially enamored of that collaboration; Lubezki’s name came up as the first and only onscreen credit at the end of the premiere.

The video has Johnson and Farrell portraying a couple whose relationship appears on the rocks, with Swift acting as a counselor to the woman, singing lyrics about how she is the man’s ex and can tell her exactly how things will go. Things are just a little less sinister in the song’s lyrics than in the way things play out on screen. Johnson is seen getting angry with Johnson after a banquet at which he speaks, as the music drops out for a driving scene in which he seems to be gaslighting her with accusations about her drinking, after she has become upset at the sight of him flirting with female guests.

‘Patient Zero’ music video

The video cuts to flashback of similar experiences in which Swift, his then-companion, reacted more angrily to his infractions. There’s a headline that reads “Heiress dies of mystery illness — husband inherits billions” (with the additional explanation, “Spouse inherits estate amid unanswered questions”). Then we see the two women standing at a gravestone with a photo that suggests it was Swift’s character who was born in 1986 and died in 2022. Johnson places black roses on the headstone of Swift’s dead heiress character, with it left unclear whether she’s taken any lessons from Swift’s purely spectral counsel or not.

The Patient Zero video is finally out in the world! Getting to work with Emmanuel Lubezki was something out of a dream sequence, and I learned so much from getting to watch his genius in action. I want to thank Dakota and Colin for trusting me with their time, taste, and talent… pic.twitter.com/vkLCO167Ea — Taylor Swift (@taylorswift13) September 28, 2026

Swift was more expansive in her remarks about the new video in a message she posted on social media immediately after the premiere. “The ‘Patient Zero’ video is finally out in the world!” she wrote. “Getting to work with Emmanuel Lubezki was something out of a dream sequence, and I learned so much from getting to watch his genius in action. I want to thank Dakota and Colin for trusting me with their time, taste, and talent (giggling with your friend because you’re twinning for an entire shoot was a new and truly delightful experience). And Colin’s turn as a villain is even more impressive when you get to be around him. He’s an absolute light and as kind as they come. Cara, thank you for agreeing to play the lusty other woman. That’s what friends are for? With the ‘Patient Zero’ video, I got to explore the cinematic and literary genres I love so much. I wanted to incorporate elements of gothic ghost stories, true crime, psychological thrillers all in a setting I hadn’t really shot in much. The house was a metaphor for the coldness of a relationship that’s faded and atrophied. Thank you to Ethan Tobman for your insightful production design, and bringing that feeling to life. My editor Chancler Haynes has outdone himself. And lastly, thank you to the VMAs for giving us a World Premiere at the place where celebrating music videos became a thing. And so much love for you guys, always.”

Taylor Swift at the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards held at Peacock Theater on September 27, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. JC Olivera

Following the VMAs premiere, an alert told fans they could view “Patient Zero” on Spotify Premium, Apple Music or Amazon Music. Notably, Swift has withheld her recent videos from YouTube’s free tier for a couple of days upon release before putting them up there as well, presumably because views on non-paid services do not count toward the consumption totals that fuel the Billboard charts. It will be available on YouTube as of Tuesday, the alert noted.

In advance of the music video’s release, Swift took to her Instagram Stories on Sunday to post a short clip of herself talking to the camera, with a dateline revealing for the first time that the “Patient Zero” video was shot all the way back in March. (Needless to say, no NDA gets respected like a Taylor Swift NDA.) It gives confirmation that she hatched the idea for a VMAs premiere half a year ago, and held onto it as a secret till this date.

Says Swift in the IG clip: “Walking through here and seeing the way that Chivo has lit this and the way the sets are and how brilliantly Ethan has done this set design, I’m kind of rethinking the release of the video. Like, I need to figure a way to get this on TV or something. I’m sort of like: ‘Google, when are the VMAs?'” A caption under the video states the obvious: “Turns out the VMAs are Sept. 27, aka today.”

In that quote, “Chivo” is a nickname for Oscar-winning cinematographer Emmanuel Lubezki, and “Ethan” refers to Ethan Tobman, her longtime production designer.

Beyond her nominations at the VMAs for “The Life of a Showgirl” and “The Fate of Ophelia,” Swift was given a guaranteed trip to the podium for whatever speech or unveiling she might have in mind when CBS announced that she would be receiving the inaugural Artist Director Honor. The award is given to an artist who is accomplished behind the camera as well as in front of it. Producers have described it as analogous in stature to the VMAs’ traditional Video Vanguard award, while noting that it is an unknown whether any other artists will receive this new honor in the future.

When she came back to accept her award for video of the year for “Ophelia,” she said, “Thank you so much for giving this award to this video… I just I loved making this video because I wanted it to seem like one continuous shot, so I learned a lot about hiding cuts in places. And I want to thank everybody who helped me on this video shoot because, just the choreography… I love so much Mandy Moore as my choreographer… production designed by Ethan Tobin, my editor Chancellor Haynes, and my cinematographer on this video I’ve gotten to work with before, he’s one of the people who gave me the confidence to actually direct videos on my own. His name is Rodrigo Prieto.

“And lastly, but most importantly, I want to thank and dedicate this award to one person, without whom this wouldn’t be happening, and that person is the ultimate showgirl, Dolly Parton. Every single song that she wrote, her storytelling was so vivid and so rich… Listening to her songs, it’s like watching the best music video you have ever seen in your life every single time you hear what she has written. And man, she handled this thing with such grace and joy and love and gratitude for the fact that she got to do this, and everything that happened in her life or her career, she channeled back into love and gratitude and appreciation for her fans. I’m lucky I got to be one of them and I will always be one of them. I love you all so very much and I think that we were all very lucky to share this planet with Dolly Parton for a time, and thank you for this amazing moment.”

LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA – SEPTEMBER 27: Taylor Swift attends the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards at Peacock Theater on September 27, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by John Shearer/WireImage) WireImage

The VMAs now have CBS as their primary home, allowing Swift a much higher profile for her music video than it would have gotten prior to last year, when MTV was still seen as the show’s go-to network (although the ceremony is still simulcast on the former music network).

The song “Patient Zero” came out Friday morning, as a single and also as part of a quartet of previously unreleased tracks newly tagged on to her 2025 “The Life of a Showgirl” album for an expanded edition titled “The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore.” The other three new songs are “Cleveland!” (about Travis Kelce and his hometown), “Pink Clouding” and “Babylon.”

In her announcement for the expanded edition of the album, Swift wrote that about a year ago she “took a trip to Sweden to celebrate with Max (Martin) and Shellback, my two collaborators on this album. Really we just wanted to reflect and take in how grateful we were for the moment we were in, but there was a studio there and we did what we do when we feel anything at all: We wrote more songs.”

Of the single itself, she said in an audio clip released to radio stations, “I was hanging out with a bunch of friends, and one of my friends told us that she had been reached out to by the new girlfriend of an ex of hers, asking for guidance on if she had had the same experiences with this guy that this new girlfriend was having. And everyone in our group just immediately started saying like, ‘Oh, I’ve been through that too’, and telling the stories of when this kind of reach out had happened for them. And I thought to myself, if this has happened to all of us, it’s such an interesting kind of angle on humanity and on relationships, and I wonder if I could write something from the perspective of getting this phone call, and really only from the perspective and the side of the phone call of the ex who’s been through it before.”

The theme of the song is summed up in the concluding lines: “So if you wanna kick it, then I’m with it, I’ve been there / Felt the reeling, done the healing, said the curses and the prayers / When the fever turns a dreamer into a pathetic ghost / If he’s killing you, I see you, I was patient zero.”

title: Korea Box Office: ‘The Assassin(s)’ and ‘Tazza 4’ Dominate Chuseok Holiday Weekend Surge
summary: Director Hur Jin-ho’s political crime thriller “The Assassin(s)” powered to the top of the South Korean box office over the weekend of Sep. 25–27, leading a major holiday box office surge across the peak Chuseok festival frame. According to data from KOBIS, the tracking service operated by the Korean Film Council, the newly opened local […]
content:
Director Hur Jin-ho‘s political crime thriller “The Assassin(s)” powered to the top of the South Korean box office over the weekend of Sep. 25–27, leading a major holiday box office surge across the peak Chuseok festival frame.

According to data from KOBIS, the tracking service operated by the Korean Film Council, the newly opened local title generated $8 million from 1,119,156 admissions over the three-day frame across 1,532 screens, claiming 40.9% of the weekend market. the period investigation drama reconstructs the August 15, 1974 assassination attempt on President Park Chung-hee during a National Liberation Day ceremony that resulted in the death of First Lady Yuk Young-soo. The plot follows a detective, played by Yu Hae-jin, alongside a veteran newspaper society desk chief, portrayed by Park Hae-il, and a rookie reporter, played by Lee Min-ho, as they investigate missing ballistic evidence that contradicts the state’s lone-gunman verdict. Since launching on Sep. 23, the release has accumulated $11.2 million from 1,566,222 admissions.

Crime saga “Tazza: The Song of Beelzebub” opened in second place, taking in $4.1 million from 566,526 admissions across 1,045 screens, accounting for 21.3% of the market. Directed by Choi Kook-hee and starring Byun Yo-han, Noh Jae-won, and Ayaka Miyoshi, the fourth installment in the comic-adapted gambling franchise follows a betrayed former online casino operator who enters the international poker circuit for a high-stakes duel of vengeance. Counting previews and holiday crowds since its Sep. 23 release, the title has earned $6.1 million from 833,030 admissions.

Popular on Variety

“The Odyssey” took third place in its eighth weekend, adding $3.2 million from 364,763 admissions across 843 screens. The film took 16.6% of the weekend market. Its haul has reached $96.3 million from 11,783,301 total admissions since its Aug. 5 launch.

Last week’s chart-topper in admissions, “The Intern,” moved to fourth place in its sophomore frame. Directed by Kim Do-young and starring Choi Min-sik and Han So-hee, the Warner Bros. Korea comedy remake generated $1.5 million from 206,347 admissions across 722 screens, capturing 7.6% of receipts. That lifted its cumulative total to $5.3 million from 756,057 viewers.

Auteur Lee Chang-dong’s social drama “Possible Love” debuted in fifth place, earning $557,981 from 72,022 admissions across 195 screens. The Venice Grand Jury Prize winner stars Jeon Do-yeon, Sul Kyung-gu, Cho Yeo-jeong, and Zo In-sung, centering on the psychological tension between a working-class couple in the aftermath of a strike and a wealthy couple filming a documentary about them. Since its Sep. 23 bow, South Korea’s Oscar submission has amassed $890,241 from 115,938 admissions.

“Obsession” was in sixth place in its fourth frame, grossing $542,493 from 67,619 admissions across 471 screens. The film now has $6.6 million from 849,155 ticket buyers.

“Avengers: Endgame Encore” opened in seventh place, taking $550,939 from 63,273 admissions over the frame across 178 screens and has $941,892 from 107,950 viewers.

“Resident Evil” was in eighth place, collecting $291,213 from 36,459 admissions. The survival horror reboot has reached $1.4 million from 186,950 total admissions.

“Spider-Man: Brand New Day” placed ninth, pulling in $154,701 from 22,278 admissions, lifting its haul to $67.4 million from 9,032,429 admissions.

Rounding out the top 10 was the British animated adventure “Octonauts: Above and Beyond – Season 2”, which opened with $89,565 from 12,636 admissions across 239 screens, reaching $125,089 from 17,779 viewers since its Sep. 23 debut.

The overall market collective gross for the weekend was $19.6 million, a healthy uptick from last week’s $7.6 million, thanks to the holiday.

title: Kacey Musgraves Pays Heartfelt Tribute to Dolly Parton With ‘I Will Always Love You’ Performance at MTV Video Music Awards
summary: Kacey Musgraves led a touching tribute to Dolly Parton at the MTV Video Music Awards 2026, honoring the late country icon just a month after her death with a rendition of “I Will Always Love You.” The pre-taped performance began with footage of Parton introducing the classic 1974 tune. “I’d like to leave you fellas […]
content:
Kacey Musgraves led a touching tribute to Dolly Parton at the MTV Video Music Awards 2026, honoring the late country icon just a month after her death with a rendition of “I Will Always Love You.”

The pre-taped performance began with footage of Parton introducing the classic 1974 tune. “I’d like to leave you fellas with a little bit of advice,” she said. “Don’t criticize your wife’s judgment. You just remember who she married. Just kidding you. There’s a lot of truth in that and I would also like to say about life, I hope it treats you real kind and I hope that you have all that you ever dreamed of.”

Kacey Musgraves pays tribute to Dolly Parton at the #VMAs with a cover of "I Will Always Love You."



(via CBS/MTV/VMAs) pic.twitter.com/mORHb9t9lh — Variety (@Variety) September 28, 2026

She then began singing the chorus of “I Will Always Love You” as Musgraves joined in, accompanied by a piano. Musgraves stood perched at the mic with her eyes closed for most of the performance, which was met by thunderous applause from the audience.

Popular on Variety

Following Parton’s death in August, Musgraves dedicated her song “Rainbow” to Parton at her concert at Boston’s TD Garden, followed by a rendition of her 1977 classic “Here You Come Again.” Then, at her “Middle of Nowhere” tour stop at New York City’s Madison Square Garden just a few days later, she covered “9 to 5,” a song that she’d included in her shows over the years.

“I’m not over it, and I’m never gonna be over it,” she told the MSG crowd regarding Parton’s death. “The world definitely lost a light, and it’s hard for me to talk about. And I know how much Dolly meant to everybody also in this room. I think why it feels so dark is it’s already hard to navigate these times right now, and then we lose a matriarch like that. It’s the closest thing we’ve ever had to royalty.”

Musgraves had also shared the stage with Parton at the 2019 MusiCares Person of the Year event, where she kicked off a tribute to the country icon alongside Katy Perry for a duet on “Here You Come Again.” The Queen of Nashville herself then joined them in a white dress with flowing sleeves.

Musgraves has been vocal about her appreciation for Parton in the past, telling Rolling Stone in 2021 that she appreciated her as a “style icon” and a “businesswoman.” “First and foremost she’s a songwriter,” she said. “But she wasn’t afraid to be a beautiful, sexy woman, proud of her femininity, proud of her body. It just seems like she didn’t ever need to shrink her flamboyant nature to fit among the men that she worked with.”

title: Madonna Opens MTV Video Music Awards With Sabrina Carpenter and Charli xcx, Plus Sombr, Debi Mazar and More
summary: Madonna performed for the first time in 23 years at the MTV VMAs on Sunday, opening the show by bringing out special guests Sabrina Carpenter and Charli xcx to perform their respective duets. After a 20-minute telecast delay due to the NFL game, the pop icon began her performance perched on the top of a […]
content:
Madonna performed for the first time in 23 years at the MTV VMAs on Sunday, opening the show by bringing out special guests Sabrina Carpenter and Charli xcx to perform their respective duets.

After a 20-minute telecast delay due to the NFL game, the pop icon began her performance perched on the top of a piano as Carpenter played the keys. Dressed in a black waistcoat and knee-high boots, Madonna traded verses with Carpenter, who wore a glittery ensemble along with a beret. Madonna then descended the stairs and removed her coat to reveal a red-and-black corset as dancers lifted her onto a table that rolled around a choir in the audience wearing white veils.

Madonna circled back to the stage, which had been transformed into the bathroom set from the “Danceteria” music video. Charli xcx emerged from one of the stalls to the tune of the freshly released “Danceteria Afterhours” remix, as did Madonna along with actresses Debi Mazar and Julia Garner. Throughout the performance, Seth Rogen, Andrew Watt and Sombr made cameos before the two-song spectacular came to an end. “Make some noise for Madonna!” said Charli.

Popular on Variety

Madonna has been a perennial fixture at the VMAs since its inception, dating back to her iconic performance of “Like a Virgin” at the show’s 1984 debut. In the decades that followed, she performed “Express Yourself” in 1989, “Vogue” in 1990, “Ray of Light” with Lenny Kravitz in 1998 and, of course, alongside Britney Spears and Christina Aguilera during her last VMAs performance in 2003.

She also led all other artists in nominations for the 2026 VMAs, earning 13 nods. Taylor Swift followed with 11 nominations, Sabrina Carpenter with nine and Ariana Grande with eight.

Madonna brings out Charli xcx during her #VMAs performance pic.twitter.com/fBzA6A7zt9 — Variety (@Variety) September 27, 2026

Days before her appearance, VMAs producer Van Toffler spoke with Variety about bringing Madonna back to the stage. “Well, look, we can deny it as much as we want, but Madonna is the M in MTV,” he said. “I knew it the day I started there. She is the queen of MTV. She makes great videos. She’s provocative. She always pushed us, and this year’s performance will be no exception.”

The pop titan is coming off of a momentous year on the back of her 15th album “Confessions II,” which was released in July. The record, her first in seven years, was a sequel of sorts to her seismic 2005 album “Confessions on a Dance Floor,” reuniting her with producer Stuart Price for 16 tracks that embraced contemporary dance music while nodding to her roots and backstory.

Madonna kicked off the era with the debut of the lead single, “Bring Your Love,” during a surprise appearance during the second weekend of Carpenter’s headlining set at Coachella in April. In the months that followed, Madonna staged key activations including a rave at West Hollywood’s Abbey and a performance in partnership with Grindr at New York City’s Times Square. Following the release of “Confessions II,” she dropped new versions of several songs including “Love Sensation” featuring Kylie Minogue and “Danceteria Afterhours” with Charli xcx, which arrived just days before the VMAs performance.

title: ‘Roseanne’ Star Michael Fishman Apologizes to Fans for the ‘Chaos’ of Roseanne Barr Feud: ‘I’m Gonna Keep Pushing Out Love’
summary: Michael Fishman, who played D.J. Conner on the ABC sitcom “Roseanne,” has taken to social media after making headlines for feuding with his former co-star Roseanne Barr earlier this month. In August, Fishman said that the show’s 2018 reboot “was rightfully canceled” after Barr posted a racist tweet, to which Barr responded that Fishman was […]
content:
Michael Fishman, who played D.J. Conner on the ABC sitcom “Roseanne,” has taken to social media after making headlines for feuding with his former co-star Roseanne Barr earlier this month. In August, Fishman said that the show’s 2018 reboot “was rightfully canceled” after Barr posted a racist tweet, to which Barr responded that Fishman was a “brainwashed bigot” and “a fucking little worm” in an episode of the “Can’t Be Censored” podcast.

He began by apologizing to fans of the show for the“chaos over the course of the past week.” “I’ve heard from a lot of you [that you] feel like your TV family is fighting,” Fishman said in the video posted on his Instagram page. “I had the privilege of growing up with so many of you or around so many of you. And the truth is, I’m gonna keep pushing out love and light because it’s the path that I’ve chosen over the years.”

Popular on Variety

He continued: “Our show has been a comfort show for you. So I want you to know we’re not going to ruin it. I’m going to do whatever I can to uphold that legacy and make sure it stays with you.” He added that “the show meant something to me as a kid,” and “it became even more real afterward.”

“Gentle reminder to shine,” he wrote under the video. “We find our way home and back together.”

Fishman appeared on all nine seasons of “Roseanne,” which ran from 1988 to 1997, and the nine-episode revival season that aired in 2018. At the time, Variety reported that the show finished its first season as the number one scripted primetime television show in the 18-49 age range. Fishman also reprised his role for four seasons on the follow-up “The Conners,” which ran for seven seasons from 2018 to 2025.

See Fishman’s full video here.

content:
Benjamin Satterley, the high-flying champion wrestler known variously to AEW and WWE fans as Pac, Bastard, Adrian Neville and Neville, has died. That, according to an announcement from All Elite Wrestling. He was 40.

Details surrounding his passing are unclear. Pac was featured at AEW’s All Out pay-per-view from Chicago on Saturday night. He challenged Andrade El Idolo for the AEW National Championship, but lost.

The statement from AEW reads in part, “A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England, Satterley began his wrestling career in 2004 and went on to perform for wrestling organizations all over the world, captivating fans with innovative high-flying moves and incredible in-ring ability. Pac signed with All Elite Wrestling in 2019 and held multiple AEW Championships and competed in some of the most memorable matches in AEW history. Our condolences go out to Satterley’s family, friends and fans.”

All Elite Wrestling is saddened to announce the passing of Benjamin Satterley, aka Pac. A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England, Satterley began his wrestling career in 2004 and went on to perform for wrestling organizations all over the world, captivating fans with innovative… pic.twitter.com/uqzO371t2V — All Elite Wrestling (@AEW) September 28, 2026

In the AEW, Satterley was the outfit’s All-Atlantic Champion and a two-time World Trios Champion.

Watch on Deadline

He won the NXT Championship in the WWE’s developmental adjunct and later became a two-time WWE Cruiserweight Champion.

Satterley was known as “The Man that Gravity Forgot” for his signature finishing move, a spectacular corkscrew shooting star press off the top rope. You can see it in the video below.

title: MTV VMAs: Taylor Swift Dedicates Video Of The Year Award To Dolly Parton “The Ultimate Showgirl”
summary: Taylor Swift won the night’s top award at the MTV Video Music Awards, taking home a Moonperson trophy for Video of the Year for “The Fate of Ophelia.” Swift took the stage to accept the award and said she was “proud” of the work she did on the video, as it was “one continuous shot” […]
content:
Taylor Swift won the night’s top award at the MTV Video Music Awards, taking home a Moonperson trophy for Video of the Year for “The Fate of Ophelia.”

Swift took the stage to accept the award and said she was “proud” of the work she did on the video, as it was “one continuous shot” and she had to learn “a lot about hiding cuts” in strategic places.

The singer also made a special mention to Dolly Parton, whom she called “the ultimate showgirl.”

“I want to thank and dedicate this award to one person, without whom just this wouldn’t be happening, and that person is the ultimate showgirl, Dolly Parton,” Swift said in her speech. “Every single song that she wrote, her storytelling was so vivid and so rich. It was like listening to her songs. It’s like watching the best music video you have ever seen in your life every single time you hear what she has written, and she handled this thing with such grace and joy and love and gratitude for the fact that she got to do this, and everything that happened in her life or her career, she channeled back into love, and gratitude and appreciation for her fans.”

She continued, “I am lucky I got to be one of them, and I will always be one of them. I love you all so very much, and I think that we were all very, very… I think we were all very lucky to share this planet with Dolly Parton for a time, and thank you for this amazing moment. I love you all.”

title: ‘Lanterns’ Stars Kyle Chandler & Aaron Pierre On Going Deeper Into Hal’s Psyche And The Jordan Boys Legacy
summary: SPOILER ALERT! This post contains details from the penultimate episode of HBO’s Lanterns. HBO’s Lanterns gave audiences, and John Stewart (Aaron Pierre), a much deeper understanding of Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler) in the penultimate episode of the DC series on Sunday night. The episode opens with a flashback to 1975, when Hal gets in trouble […]
content:
SPOILER ALERT! This post contains details from the penultimate episode of HBO‘s Lanterns.

HBO’s Lanterns gave audiences, and John Stewart (Aaron Pierre), a much deeper understanding of Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler) in the penultimate episode of the DC series on Sunday night.

The episode opens with a flashback to 1975, when Hal gets in trouble with his baseball coach for refusing to hand over the ball to his teammates. Sound familiar? Back in present day, John has managed to exhume Hal’s body and retrieve the decommissioned power ring, awakening the Halogram to get his help opening the lockbox in the storage unit. It works, and they soon discover that the lockbox contains a dark matter manhole to another planet.

For all the strife that Hal has caused John up to this point, even in his death the partners in intergalactic crime find their way back to one another again.

Watch on Deadline

“We used to describe each other as these characters, like two dogs who lived in the same household, who, at home, they would maybe fight and tear each other apart, but when they were going for maybe a walk, and another dog entered the equation, bam, they were a unit, and there was nothing you could do to to to disrupt or destroy that unit,” Pierre said. “They become dangerous when they’re together. The dynamic is unbreakable, and as soon as they’re on their own, they’re tearing each other down and apart.”

On the other side of the dark matter manhole, the pair find themselves on a deserted planet which seems to have already been utterly destroyed. John soon deduces that this is Anton’s (Paul Ben-Victor) planet, the one that had been systematically that wiped out by the Manhunter.

The Halogram’s decade of missing memories and context create even more frustration for John, who’d gone back to Rushville in the first place because his mother had told him that Hal was ready to apologize for everything he’d done. He was dead by the time John arrived, and this version of him wouldn’t even know what to apologize for. Not to mention, they’ve got more pressing issues. When John becomes affected by the same gas that made Anton’s people kill themselves, the Halogram is the only thing that saves him.

“I think his understanding of who Hal is certainly evolves over the course of the series,” Pierre tells Deadline. “It’s almost like throughout these episodes, John is putting together a puzzle, but the puzzle is 1000 pieces, and sometimes elements of that puzzle form before others, and he thinks he has an understanding of exactly who Hal is, and then he formulates another part of the puzzle, and that conflicts with what he thought he understood, and it’s an ongoing thing.”

The piece of the puzzle that clicks into place this episode harkens back to Hal’s childhood. Not only does that 1975 flashback illustrate Hal’s complicated relationship with his father, it also reveals a history of mental health struggles when Hal reveals that his father killed himself. Since he was a test pilot, no one batted an eye. Among the things he left behind was a note that told Hal he’d be better off without him — and a lifetime of trauma for his son. It was a cycle that had repeated itself for generations in Hal’s family: The Jordan boys’ legacy.

“I’m not fearless because I’m brave. I’m fearless because I’m broken,” the Halogram tells John.

The “heartfelt moment” as Chandler calls it, reframes Hal almost entirely. It follows another moment earlier in the episode, when Kerry (Kelly Macdonald) tells John that Hal once described his trainee like someone’s favorite football team: Impossible to root against but exceedingly maddening to remain loyal to.

“That’s not information that someone just throws in there. That’s a detailed storyline that is also meant to manipulate an audience’s emotions and bring them that much closer into the whole story,” Chandler said. “That’s another great thing about this whole show is that there are those fence posts along the way, and they’re pretty detailed. You don’t miss them in scripts, and you can build around those things as an actor too.”

The end of the episode finds Hal and John facing yet another foe: Sinestro. Turns out, this planet is where he’s been hiding all along.

As for how John’s revelations about Hal might impact the finale, Pierre remains coy about exactly what’s in store, telling us: “I won’t reveal the end, but once we get very near to the end, at least, he has this immense respect and appreciation for Hal, and if if nothing else, I think even Hal knows that he could trust John with his life, and John knows that he could trust Hal with his.”

“You don’t always need to love each other for that to be a truth, and I think that’s something that this series explores. But interestingly enough, speaking on that love element, I think that there is a very there’s a very sincere respect and and a mutual brotherly love there between the two of them,” Pierre continued. “I think a truth that John understood at a certain point in the series [is that] he’s never gonna fully know Hal, but what he can do is understand who Hal is fundamentally at his core, at least. He may never understand all of the nuances of who this individual is, but he can discover who this man is at his core. And once that curiosity was satisfied, I think he was very at peace with everything that the two of them had been through — the highs, the lows, the inbetweens, the moments that felt like purgatory. I think he just he just finds peace with it, because he knows who this individual is at his core, no matter what decoration or nuances surround it.”

Lanterns ends next Sunday at 9 p.m. ET/PT on HBO.

title: Taylor Swift’s “Patient Zero” Music Video Drops: Watch It On Apple Music, Amazon Music Or Spotify
summary: UPDATED with video: The music video for Taylor Swift’s new song “Patient Zero” made its world premiere during the MTV Video Music Awards tonight on CBS and MTV. A teaser clip of the video dropped Thursday, when news of Sunday’s full video fleshed out the storyline hinted at in the teaser released Thursday: Swift and […]
content:
UPDATED with video: The music video for Taylor Swift’s new song “Patient Zero” made its world premiere during the MTV Video Music Awards tonight on CBS and MTV.

A teaser clip of the video dropped Thursday, when news of Sunday’s full video fleshed out the storyline hinted at in the teaser released Thursday: Swift and Dakota Johnson playing doppelgangers of a sort, both of whom fall in love with a billionaire (played by Colin Farrell), and both of whom meet tragic ends.

In a post about the video, which she directed, Swift wrote, “Giggling with your friend because you’re twinning for an entire shoot was a new and truly delightful experience.”

Watch on Deadline

Swift continued, “With the Patient Zero video, I got to explore the cinematic and literary genres I love so much. I wanted to incorporate elements of gothic ghost stories, true crime, psychological thrillers all in a setting I hadn’t really shot in much. The house was a metaphor for the coldness of a relationship that’s faded and atrophied.”

You can watch the video on Spotify, Apple Music or Amazon Music.

The Patient Zero video is finally out in the world! Getting to work with Emmanuel Lubezki was something out of a dream sequence, and I learned so much from getting to watch his genius in action. I want to thank Dakota and Colin for trusting me with their time, taste, and talent… pic.twitter.com/vkLCO167Ea — Taylor Swift (@taylorswift13) September 28, 2026

The debut was announced by CBS and MTV in a statement earlier this week. “The exclusive premiere builds on the longstanding VMAs tradition of bringing artists and audiences together for major live music moments while giving artists a global stage to introduce new work and shape the cultural conversation in real time.”

The premiere, they continued, “also reflects the unpredictability that has long defined the show – where unexpected pairings, performances and premieres can become the moments everyone is talking about.”

This time around, the “unexpected pairings” include the appearance of guest stars Farrell and Johnson in the video directed by Swift with cinematography by Oscar winner Emmanuel Lubezki (The Revenant, Birdman, Gravity).

“Patient Zero” is Swift’s new song from The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore, the expanded Showgirl album that includes four previously unreleased song and will be available to stream beginning Friday.

CBS Mornings unveiled a brief (13 second) sneak peek at the video today just before Swift posted the teaser on her social accounts. In the clip, Farrell and Johnson appear in blink-and-miss-it fashion, and we see a cemetery, lots of water, Swift crying, and some other cryptic images.

Watch the teaser below.

On Wednesday, Swift announced that the expanded version of last year’s The Life of a Showgirl album will be released Friday with four previously unreleased songs including the first single “Patient Zero.” (The other new songs are “Cleveland!,” “Pink Clouding” and “Babylon.”)

Hosted by Snoop Dogg, the VMAs air Sunday (7:30-9:30 p.m. ET/4:30-6:30 p.m. PT) on CBS, simulcast on MTV and streaming on Paramount+ (Premium) in the U.S. The show will also be available globally the next day on Paramount+ and MTV.

title: African Finance Rising, Distribution Doldrums and Other Hot-Button Topics on the Agenda at This Year’s Durban FilmMart
summary: As the fall festival season winds down, the temperature will be heating up next month in Durban, South Africa, where the 17th Durban FilmMart takes place from Oct. 9 – 12. This year’s event arrives amid surging hopes but lingering anxieties for an African industry at a crossroads. For the continent’s filmmakers, there’s plenty of […]
content:
As the fall festival season winds down, the temperature will be heating up next month in Durban, South Africa, where the 17th Durban FilmMart takes place from Oct. 9 – 12. This year’s event arrives amid surging hopes but lingering anxieties for an African industry at a crossroads.

For the continent’s filmmakers, there’s plenty of cause for optimism. Long marginalized or pigeonholed by festival programmers, African cinema has achieved an undeniable foothold in the main programming strands of A-class fests. Established auteurs are regularly joined on the red carpet by a rambunctious cohort of newcomers who are pushing African filmmaking in new and exhilarating directions, such as South African directors Jason Jacobs and Devon Delmar, the duo behind last year’s Rotterdam-winning docudrama “Variations on a Theme.”

The talent pipeline has never been so rich and varied. Witness Rwandan debutante Marie-Clémentine Dusabejambo taking home the Caméra d’Or in Cannes with her searing post-genocide drama “Ben’Imana” (pictured), or Nigerian directors Arie and Chuko Esiri hitting the Croisette with “Clarissa,” a Lagos-set adaptation of Virginia Woolf’s “Mrs. Dalloway,” starring Sophie Okonedo, David Oyelowo and Ayo Edebiri, that was swooped on by Neon. Venice gave its prize for best first feature to Cameroon’s Auguste Bernard Kouemo Yanghu (“House of the Wind”). Based on talent alone, the future looks undeniably bright.

Popular on Variety

More encouraging than the northbound flow of films from the Global South is the fact that financing isn’t only flowing in the opposite direction. Whereas African film production was long underwritten by European funding bodies and cultural institutions, a rash of homegrown financing tools has begun to emerge, from institutional heavyweights like the Next Narrative Africa Fund and CANEX Creations Inc. — the IP investment arm of the African Export-Import Bank — to equity investors like MBO Capital, Volition Capital and Capital Film Productions.

“For the first time in the history of African film, there are a number of equity players who are investing in film,” says Big World Cinema CEO Steven Markovitz, who alongside the African creative sector-focused HEVA Fund recently spearheaded the inaugural African Film Investor Roundtable, gathering top investors and financiers of the continent’s creative industries.

To bolster that point, Markovitz says he’s witnessed a “critical mass of equity investors” entering the market, splashing out anywhere from $100,000 to $3 million per project. “There is this moment where film is seen as a credible investment asset class,” he says. “It’s now up to us as producers to get ready for investors and start being able to understand the needs of equity investors in this environment.”

Therein, however, lies the rub. Just as the financing possibilities for African producers are flourishing, distribution channels are dwindling. After successive waves of corporate consolidation and belt-tightening that have seen global players like Prime Video, Netflix and Canal+ either exit from or scale back their investment in the African market, “the number of buyers has shrunk instead of expanding,” says Marie Lora-Mungai, founder of advisory firm Restless Global and a leading expert on Africa’s creative industries.

“There is more funding and capital than ever before…. However, the reason we are not seeing more deals, despite the sudden availability of capital, is that financiers can only invest or lend if they are reasonably convinced that the film will make its money back,” she says. “So capital is arriving into a market where demand contracted first, which is the opposite sequence to the one everybody planned for.”

If there’s a bright side, it’s that “[African] producers and film entrepreneurs aren’t sitting idle [and] are thinking outside the box to find various ways around the issue,” Lora-Mungai says. Local and regional streaming platforms are again looking for innovative ways to monetize the demand for African content, while policymakers in a number of countries are putting the creative industries front and center.

Meanwhile, financiers like CANEX Creations Inc. and initiatives like the African Producers Accelerator — launched last year by Markovitz’s Big World Cinema and the Bertha Foundation — are increasingly gearing their efforts toward curating market-ready commercial projects and pairing them with potential investors.

Taken together, such issues suggest a rich range of talking points for African industry professionals to dissect when the Durban FilmMart kicks off in its sun-splashed coastal home. Across four days, this year’s DFM should reaffirm its influential role as a rare space where representatives of the continent’s scattered screen industries can gather to discuss the challenges they face.

“We are still so separated,” says Tshepiso Chikapa Phiri, CEO of the Known Associates Group and chairperson of the Durban FilmMart Institute. “Let’s start coming together and talking about what collaboration looks like — collaboration from an infrastructure point of view, collaboration from a policy point of view, collaboration from an incentives strategy point of view.

“We need to have much more structured conversation and much more intentional conversations,” she adds. “To talk for the four days of DFM and then walk away and then meet again the following year and have the same conversations, that’s self-defeating. Talk is one thing. But the action is going to be what sets us apart.”

title: Florence Pugh Speaks Out Over Cornell University Sexual Assault Case: ‘We Need Our Men to Be as Horrified and Sickened as Us’
summary: Florence Pugh has posted a lengthy statement on social media in response to a controversy that has erupted at Cornell University over an alleged sexual assault incident that took place two years ago. Last week, news broke that a former Cornell student had accused seven men of raping and drugging her at a frat house […]
content:
Florence Pugh has posted a lengthy statement on social media in response to a controversy that has erupted at Cornell University over an alleged sexual assault incident that took place two years ago.

Last week, news broke that a former Cornell student had accused seven men of raping and drugging her at a frat house party in October 2024, allegations that were only made public after she filed a lawsuit against the college. According to her attorney, after an investigation at the university, two of the accused were expelled with the remaining students received lesser sanctions, such as temporary suspensions, workshops or essay-writing assignments. Nobody was arrested.

The former student — identified as Jane Doe and 20 at the time — is now suing the school and the fraternity members, claiming they failed to protect her and prevent the alleged assault.

Popular on Variety

In a post on Instagram on Sunday, Pugh described described the incident as an “horrific act,” adding that she knew “this has happened before, and I hate the idea of it happening again.” She also urged men to speak out and to be “leading conversations about how we change the allowance and complicity of this behaviour as much as we are.” She concluded: “Be angry for us. Please.”

The statement from Pugh comes just days after she outlined her long-standing support for Palestine, telling Vanity Fair that she didn’t know “why it took so long for people to start talking and for people to actually feel sympathy.”

Read the full Instagram post from Pugh below:

After reading about the young woman who was gang raped at her college by her friend and school peers, I’m feeling uneasy and sick and anxious. I’m processing quietly and watching everything and everyone and every man. I have a few thoughts on this horrific act that happened at Cornell College in 2024. I know this has happened before, and I hate the idea of it happening again.

This is really the moment where we need our men to be as horrified and as sickened as us. You need to be leading conversations about how we change the allowance and complicity of this behaviour as much as we are. How can you expect us to trust that it’s “not all men” when in moments like this, many of you stay quiet?

A drugged gang rape takes action and conversations. It immediately makes me wonder- had it been in the works for a while? Was the damage of this poor woman’s body thought about over and over before? Every single person who knew or heard about this happening, should be looked at with serious concern. They are as evil as those planning it. To know that a torture as violent as rape is about to happen ‘upstairs’ and not do ANYTHING ABOUT IT, is sick, cowardly and cold.

The thing that makes me most heartbroken, is it’s a want to kill a soul. This is a killing of a soul. Destroying of a body and killing of a soul. And they’ve been let off? All it takes is write a quick ‘I’m so sorry I raped a girl while she was drugged with my friends, we thought it would be fine?’ essay and you’re good to go! This is unacceptable.

We are not hard enough on those that want to damage human lives. I salute all those at the college that are fighting for that girl, exposing those boys and making life unbearably impossible to find joy during their terms. They should not be allowed to walk freely like the rest of us who treasure and care for souls.

Colleges/schools/universities repeatedly fail women around the world. You build men that get taught through time and time again that they can do extreme harm and that they won’t be harmed in return.

I’m no longer tired – I’m enraged by schools protecting boys, in fear of their futures being wrecked. What about the life that those girls then have to endure, with the knowledge that his reputation is more precious than her truth? Or to feel that no one with the power to do something cares that you were abused. It’s further soul-destroying.

Those that protect and lightly sentence men that rape and destroy, should be punished and watched closely. Why are you protecting someone that fiercely?

There is no equality until you respect our bodies. There is no equality until you stop damaging our souls. There is no equality until you let us live. There is no equality until we can say we feel safe. We are the life force of this earth, start ****ing protecting us. Be angry for us. Please.

title: Banijay Entertainment, Combining All3 Media, Unveils Milestone Mipcom 2026 Lineup, Bowing ’Reputation,’ ‘Date Knight’ and a Formidable Format Franchise Offer (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Harnessing its might with a merged All3 Media for the first time at a market, Banijay Entertainment hits Mipcom 2026 with the biggest presence of any company in the world, with its stand in front of the steps of the Palais des Festivals now rebaptized Banijay House, and a formidable combined lineup. One example of […]
content:
Harnessing its might with a merged All3 Media for the first time at a market, Banijay Entertainment hits Mipcom 2026 with the biggest presence of any company in the world, with its stand in front of the steps of the Palais des Festivals now rebaptized Banijay House, and a formidable combined lineup.

One example of that: Banijay’s format franchises now offer “The Traitors,” “Survivor,” “Fear Factor” and “The Circle” under one roof. Former All3Media titles impact every sales category from “Maya” in premium scripted to a bevy of Studio Lambert titles, “Midsomer Murders” and “The Assassin” in returning favorites, two Lion TV docs in factual and its “Legends” in Netflix shows.

In other developments, Banijay will present what it describes as “highly anticipated premium scripted staples and versatile next-gen formats,” the first led by BBC One legal thriller “Reputation,” starring Naomie Harris and Christina Hendricks, and U.K. high-stakes thriller” “Maya” also headed by Tobias Menzies (“Outlander”) and marking one of the latest incursions by Starz into U.K. drama.

Popular on Variety

According to Plum Research, a stunning 90% of views and 75% of titles viewed on streaming services takes place on the long tail. Potential evergreens from Banijay to be shopped at Mipcom include “Rogue Heroes,” “A Remarkable Place to Die,” “A Woman of Substance,” “Bergerac,” “Midsomer Murders,” “The Assassin” and more.

Underscoring Banijay Entertainment’s position as the world’s leading provider for streamers, the company argues, upcoming Netflix releases include “Beat Luke Littler” from Workerbee, Netflix, “Will You Marry Me?” co-produced by Workerbee and Initial, “Simon Says” from Bunim/Murray Productions and Studio Lambert’s “Monopoly.”

Further Netflix launches take in returning scripted hits House of Guinness from Kudos and Legends co-produced by Tannadice Pictures and Lion Television.

“Mipcom 2026 marks a major milestone for Banijay Entertainment – our first distribution showcase as a combined group, and the first opportunity to unite the full force of our creative talent, standout catalogue and exceptional pipeline of new IP,” said Cathy Payne, CEO Banijay Rights.

“Bold, distinctive and built to travel, our offering reflects our expanded strength across English-language and premium content, and position as a go-to for buyers for every genre, every screen and every platform,” she noted.

“As an expert franchise-builder with a world-leading catalogue of culture-defining brands, we are harnessing the collective strength of our global creative community to develop and roll out the next wave of standout IP and cross-platform originals,” added Banijay Entertainment’s James Townley, Chief Content Officer, Development and Lucas Green, Chief Content Officer, Operations.

“We’re talking fresh ideas with cut-through potential, iconic brands reimagined for new audiences and entertainment designed to travel across screens, platforms and generations. This is Banijay Entertainment: greater in scale, bolder in ambition, and built to create the hits of tomorrow,” they went on.

A drill-down on some of Banijay’s biggest drama plays at Mipcom and a selection of factual shows and formats:

Premium Scripted

“Reputation”

A pedigree package bound for BBC One and BBC iPlayer and sourced from Banijay U.K. scripted powerhouse The Forge Entertainment (“A Woman of Substance,” “Falling”). Billed as a gripping legal drama, it stars Naomie Harris (“Skyfall”) as a hot-shot lawyer hired to represent international pop star Davina Knight (“Mad Men” leading light Christina Hendricks) in the celebrity case of the decade. Anya Reiss (“Becoming Elizabeth”) writes and exec produces.

“Maya”

From “Fleabag” producer Two Brothers Pictures for Channel 4 and Starz and sparking good word of mouth when teased at February’s London TV Screenings, “Maya” led by Ramsey and Daisy Haggard, weighs in as a witness protection thriller billed as “darkly comedic” and “atmospheric” written and created by BAFTA and International Emmy nominee Haggard (“Back To Life,” “Breeders”). She also co-directs the series from Two Brothers Pictures (“The Tourist,” “Fleabag,” “Boat Story”) alongside Jamie Donoughue (“Doctor Who,” “The Last Kingdom”).

‘Maya’ Bella Ramsay and Daisy Haggard Courtesy of All3Media Intl.

“Open Water”

Commissioned by the BBC, an adaptation of Caleb Azumah Nelson’s multi award-winning debut novel of the same title from Mam Tor Productions, behind “Half Man,” and B-Side Productions. An ode to early love adapted by Azumah, tracking the increasingly deep relationship between budding photographer Marcus and dance student Effie. “Deeply romantic,” Banijay promises.

“Wallander”

A modern-day Swedish-language reboot, here Gustaf Skarsgård (“Oppenheimer,” “Vikings”) plays the iconic sleuth across three 90-minute films as he life seems to unravel: 42, divorced and estranged from his daughter, his father is also slipping away, Adding further key cast earlier this year, produced by Jarowskij/Yellow Bird, Swedish network TV4 and Banijay Rights and written by Antonia Pyk (“Beartown”), Josefin Johansson (“Top Dog”) and Jörgen Bergmark (“Huss”) Molly Hartleb (“Top Dog”) directs.

“Counsels”

Co-created by Bryan Elsley, creator of the landmark “Skins,” a BBC One multi-strand young legal hotshots drama tracking five fellow trainee lawyers in Glasgow. now hitting their disparate first jobs. Made in association with All3Media International, a play for a younger crowd co-produced by Germany’s ZDFneo, its Millennial/Gen Z targeting channel. A standout at Series Mania’s Buyers Upfront in March and part of the BBC’s recent investment in drama in Scotland.

Further Banijay Hulu titles take in “The Mob” from Studio Lambert and Primal Media and for Prime Video is “The Grand Tour· from Studio Lambert, “The Crouches” from Workerbee, Pokeepsie Film’s “Drawn Together,” a hit staring Ester Expósito (“Elite”) and LOL: Last One Laughing, produced by Banijay Entertainment labels in 11 territories.

Third party shows include reality series “Werewolves,” from Studiocanal, a hit on Canal+, and obstacle-course-set physical process competition “Ninja Warrior” from Tokyo Broadcasting System (TBS), whch joins Banijay’s superbrands.

The title underscores Banijay’s push into sportainment, with, for example, licensed non-live sports programming on the six global streamers growing from around 5,000 hours second quarter, 2022 to 12,000 hours Q4 2025, according to Ampere Analysis.

Banijay Rights brings to the table titles such as “Counsels,” “Careless” from Synchronicity Films and Easy Tiger for Stan and Channel 4; “The Northumbria Mysteries” from Lonesome Pine for the BBC; “Monarch of the Glen” from Ecosse Films for Channel 5 and PBS Masterpiece, alongside hits “All Creatures Great and Small,” “Black Snow,” “Maigret” and “Trigger Point” among others.

Formats

“Date Knight”

A new flagship dating reality addition to Banijay’s Mipcom slate, “Date Knight” invites singles via roleplay to become knights, elves, witches and warriors, “forging connections and taking chances on love in ways they might never dare to in real life.” But can love survive when participants return to their real-life personas? From Denmark’s Nordisk Film TV, a Banijay company, “visually ambitious, emotionally engaging,” says Townley. A distinctive show touching on universal relationship issues.

‘Date Knight’

“100 Knives”

Billed as the “largest cooking show in history,” “100 Knives” is backed by two Banijay companies, Mastiff Sweden (“Love is Blind”) and Bunim/Murray Productions (“Keeping Up With The Kardashians”), as well as Smart Dog Media (“The Masked Singer”). Made for Sweden’s TV4 it weighs in as a high-pressure culinary smackdown where 100 chefs, from food truck owners to fine dining apprentices, split into brigades as they face escalating challenges. Following TV4’s Swedish commission, a Danish adaptation has been confirmed with Metronome, part of Banijay Nordic, for TV 2.

“Last One Standing”

Co-developed by RTL Creative Unit, a co-producer on “The Traitors,” Banijay’s SimpelZodiak for Videoland, and part of Banijay’s drive into “sportainment” formats such as soccer survival series “Football Island,”Townley has noted. That title, moreover, is cruelly literal. Set against a desert-like backdrop, celebrities live take on elite-level trials thought up by top athletes until they drop or beg out.

“The Million Dollar Idea”

A brand new format announced this July, created by Endemol Shine Germany, behind “Staying Alive,” for SAT.1 everyday inventors transform brilliant idea into market-ready products. Or attempt to. “Everyone can relate to the excitement of having a great idea and imagining what it could become. ‘The Million Dollar Idea’ taps into that universal ambition and turns it into uplifting entertainment,” Townley has said.

Factual

“One Born Every Minute”

Capturing the drama of birth in a hospital labor ward, the revival of the observational doc series which ran for 11 seasons on Channel 4 over 2010-18, scoring a BAFTA for Best Factual Series, and hitting a its height five million viewers. Dragonfly once more produces the 12-episode return for the U.K.’s Channel 4 and E4, a series renewal which will highlight evolving family dynamics, advances in maternity care, and the real-life challenges faced by NHS staff in 2026, say E4 and Dragonfly, a Banijay company.

“A Beautiful Obsession”

Oscar-winning director Kevin Macdonald (“One Day in September”) charts the human drama of Pep Guardiola’s tumultuous two final seasons at soccer club Manchester City made for Prime Video, Brad Pitt’s Plan B, Workerbee,a Banijay company, and City Studios, part of the soccer club, but with a development deal with Sony Pictures Television. “Pep playing himself is a bit like having Robert De Niro play a football coach,” McDonald told Deadline.

Pep Guardiola in ‘A Beautiful Obsession’

“Meet the Owens”

One of England’s best young soccer player in history before injury, Michael Owen is now battling to turn his owning horses – 140 – into a business. “Meet the Owens” catches up with Owen, a self-described “boring prick,” wife Louise, and four children, including “Love Island” star Gemma, mostly at Manor House, a Cheshire stables owned by the family. Produced by Whisper “Sven,” “Built in Birmingham: Brady & The Blues”) for Prime Video UK.

“Riddled With Plastic” (w/t)

Presented by biologist Liz Bonnin, behind 2018’s “Drowning in Plastic,” this doc feature for BBC Two and BBC iPlayer which follows a world first experiment at the University of Lincoln and Brighton and Sussex Medical School, where scientists dissect a human body to better understand how much microplastic is in it, and where it is.

“The Epstein Files” (w/t)

Another title from Lion TV, now a Banijay company, for Channel 4, presented by Emily Mathis who famously interviewed Prince Andrew about his links to Epstein in 2019. The docuseries includes firsthand testimony from survivors and what is described as forensic analysis of the documents, networks and powerful individuals connected to Epstein.

title: China Box Office: ‘Avengers: Endgame Encore’ Tops Pre-Holiday Weekend
summary: Marvel Studios’ “Avengers: Endgame Encore” claimed the top spot at the mainland China box office during the Sept. 25–27 frame, grossing RMB83.8 million ($12.5 million) over the weekend, according to Artisan Gateway. The Marvel epic’s cumulative lifetime haul in China is now $647.8 million. Dirty Monkeys’ war comedy-drama “Once Upon a Time in the Middle […]
content:
Marvel Studios’ “Avengers: Endgame Encore” claimed the top spot at the mainland China box office during the Sept. 25–27 frame, grossing RMB83.8 million ($12.5 million) over the weekend, according to Artisan Gateway.

The Marvel epic’s cumulative lifetime haul in China is now $647.8 million.

Dirty Monkeys’ war comedy-drama “Once Upon a Time in the Middle East” moved to second place after a long run at the top, collecting $7.6 million in its seventh weekend. Directed by Wen Muye (“Dying to Survive”) and starring Shen Teng, Jiang Qiming, Aarif Rahman, and Omar Sherif, the late-summer hit has lifted its cume to $341.2 million since rolling out on August 11. The story follows a Chinese chef in a fictional Middle Eastern city who transforms his restaurant into a sanctuary for local orphans and civilians amid regional armed conflict.

Pearl Studio’s animated fantasy comedy “All Wishes Come True!” held third position in its eleventh weekend, generating $4.6 million. Directed by Mu Zhengyang, the long-running animated feature has reached a cumulative total of $296 million since launching on July 18.

Popular on Variety

Riverrun Grace Film’s crime comedy “The Old Fox” debuted in fourth place, pulling in $3.6 million. Directed by Li Taige, the film stars Yu Qian as a retiring veteran police officer who discovers suspicious anomalies during an apparently routine theft investigation. When his inquiry leads directly to a ruthless corporate chairman played by Tony Leung Ka-fai, the two seasoned operators become locked in a battle of wits.

Rounding out the top five, Pearl River Film Group’s crime thriller “V” took $2.8 million in its sixth frame to lift its cumulative gross to $96 million. Directed by Han Yan (“Love Never Ends”) and featuring an ensemble cast led by Tony Leung Ka-fai, Zhu Yilong, Tan Jianci, and Kara Wai, the film chronicles an ambitious man’s rapid ascent to power and the lingering consequences that threaten his success.

Mainland China’s overall weekend grosses reached $39.9 million amid a customary quiet corridor ahead of the impending Golden Week holiday. The 2026 year-to-date box office stands at $4.34 billion, down 29.4% compared to the same period in 2025.

title: ‘Ludwig’ Becomes Most-Watched UK Scripted Show Of The Year
summary: BBC and BritBox comedy-drama Ludwig has gone from strength to strength as it becomes the UK’s most-watched scripted launch of the year so far. The first ep of Season 2, which wrapped last week, has now been watched by an audience of 9.1 million, according to Barb data from overnights.tv. The BBC was celebrating the […]
content:
BBC and BritBox comedy-drama Ludwig has gone from strength to strength as it becomes the UK’s most-watched scripted launch of the year so far.

The first ep of Season 2, which wrapped last week, has now been watched by an audience of 9.1 million, according to Barb data from overnights.tv.

The BBC was celebrating the milestone this morning and said this places Ludwig ahead of all rival scripted shows across both broadcasters and streamers, placing it ahead of the likes of the BBC and Prime Video’s The Night Manager Season 2 with 8.7 million and fellow BBC comedy-drama Small Prophets (7.6 million). On the unscripted side, Ludwig cannot match The Traitors from earlier this year, also for the BBC, which was watched by a consolidated audience of a whopping 13.3 million.

Ludwig stars David Mitchell as John Taylor, a reclusive puzzle maker who pretends to be his brother when he goes missing and infiltrates the local police station to investigate, before becoming embroiled in other cases. Mark Brotherhood is creator, Big Talk produces and the show, which has already been recommissioned for a third season plus Christmas special starring David Suchet, also stars Anna Maxwell Martin and Izuka Hoyle.

Watch on Deadline

Big Talk boss Kenton Allen said: “Ludwig is a gloriously eccentric detective at the heart of a show that has never played by the usual rules, so to see more than nine million people embrace him is genuinely thrilling. Mark Brotherhood has created that rare thing: a clever, funny, warm-hearted show that audiences seem to have made part of their lives.”

Ludwig Season 2 ended last Thursday to 1.6 million overnight viewers but catch-up on BBC iPlayer has been where it has amassed serious numbers. The first season broke out at a time when audiences were looking for cozy viewing and was the BBC’s top-rated scripted launch of 2024.

title: VMI Worldwide Partners With Empire Studios, Rascal Entertainment & Green 13 On Survival Thriller ‘Snow Predator’
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Empire Studios, Rascal Entertainment, Green 13 Films and VMI Worldwide have partnered on Snow Predator, a survival thriller directed by Coz Greenop. The film has been written by Charley McDougall and is currently shooting at Shinfield Studios in the UK. The film stars Daniel Stisen, Eloise Lovell Anderson, Jason Flemyng, Genevieve Chenneour, Jack McEvoy, […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Empire Studios, Rascal Entertainment, Green 13 Films and VMI Worldwide have partnered on Snow Predator, a survival thriller directed by Coz Greenop.

The film has been written by Charley McDougall and is currently shooting at Shinfield Studios in the UK.

The film stars Daniel Stisen, Eloise Lovell Anderson, Jason Flemyng, Genevieve Chenneour, Jack McEvoy, Daniel O’Reilly, Jack Parr, Cole Anderson James, Crystal Wright, Melina Farahani, Neve O’Reilly, Mya Greenop and Tim Cullingworth-Hudson.

The synopsis reads: After Betty (Anderson) inherits a remote cabin from her estranged father, Andy (Flemyng) the young thrill-seeker ventures deep into the frozen Canadian wilderness with her friends, only to become trapped by a brutal storm and hunted by a relentless polar bear — forcing a Search and Rescue team, headed up by Scott (Stisen) into a deadly race to reach them before it does.

Watch on Deadline

The film is produced by Charley McDougall, Jamie McLeod-Ross, Luke Adams, Andre Relis and Jessica Russo.

Daniel O’Reilly, Jade Jelly, Julie Paquit, Mickey Guerin, Bradley Stryker and Rustin Matthew serve as Executive Producers. Becca Hirani of EMRJ Entertainment serves as production manager.

McDougall said in a statement: “The ambition is to make something that feels and delivers the kind of visceral, edge-of-your-seat experience audiences want from this genre.”

VMI Worldwide is handling worldwide sales.

title: HLD Talent Signs Content Creator Heather Bowling
summary: EXCLUSIVE: GK Barry agency HLD Talent has signed content creator and By Babes co-founder Heather Bowling. The social media star, business owner and neurodiversity advocate is joining up with the likes of Barry, Mariam Musa and Shakira Khan at the London-based HLD, which is lead by creators agent Hannah Holland. She is known as a […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: GK Barry agency HLD Talent has signed content creator and By Babes co-founder Heather Bowling.

The social media star, business owner and neurodiversity advocate is joining up with the likes of Barry, Mariam Musa and Shakira Khan at the London-based HLD, which is lead by creators agent Hannah Holland.

She is known as a the co-founder of By Babes, a UK-based and community-driven beauty and cosmetics brand, and creates much of her content around the company’s focus and products.

HLD called her “bold, ambitious and completely herself” and noted that she has a “built an incredibly loyal and highly engaged audience who have grown with her and who are invested in far more than just the content she creates.”

Bowling appeared on Season 5 of Footasylum’s YouTube series Locked In and made an appearance on Barry’s podcast Saving Grace.

Watch on Deadline

“As she enter this next chapter, we’ll be working together to build on everything she’s already created, while opening up new opportunities across premium fashion and beauty, entrepreneurship, media, presenting and beyond,” said HLD in a statement.

Bowling was previously with Insanity.

title: ‘Harry Potter’ Producer David Barron Backs AI Adaptation Of ‘The Call Of The Wild’
summary: EXCLUSIVE: David Barron, the British film producer with credits on six Harry Potter films, is entering the generative artificial intelligence space. Barron has agreed to produce an AI adaptation of Jack London’s 1903 novel The Call of the Wild, which is written and directed by Simon Rumley (Crushed, Red White & Blue). The film will be generated […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: David Barron, the British film producer with credits on six Harry Potter films, is entering the generative artificial intelligence space.

Barron has agreed to produce an AI adaptation of Jack London’s 1903 novel The Call of the Wild, which is written and directed by Simon Rumley (Crushed, Red White & Blue).

The film will be generated at nmatic, with CGI and traditional VFX helping deliver more complex scenes. Filmmakers are billing it as the first faithful adaptation of London’s novel because it will be made from Buck’s subjective experience.

“London’s canvass is so epic, the Alaskan geography so gruelling, the dog and wolf fights so visceral that a faithful cinematic adaptation has hitherto been logistically and financially impossible,” said Barron. ”But technology has finally caught up with London’s vision, and we believe now is the time to do justice.”

Watch on Deadline

The Call of the Wild tells the story of a pampered St. Bernard dog, who is torn from his life of privilege in California’s Santa Clara Valley and is sold into the brutal world of the 1890s Klondike Gold Rush, where he discovers the wild instinct that has always lurked within.

The film has been adapted for the screen several times, including a 2020 Michael Green film starring Harrison Ford.

David Barron, Mark Sandell (A Liar’s Autobiography) and Nick Price produce. Chris Catchpole, Carl Lyttle, and Toby White head up prompting and technical at nmatic.

title: Lightdox Acquires Rights To ‘My Home Of Wind And Sand’ Before Zurich Film Festival World Premiere
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Lightdox has acquired world sales rights to the documentary My Home of Wind and Sand ahead of its world premiere Tuesday at the Zurich Film Festival. Filmmaker Patrick Wally spent over a decade on his film, a portrait of women’s rights, human rights and climate activist Najla Mohamed Lamin, who was born in a […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Lightdox has acquired world sales rights to the documentary My Home of Wind and Sand ahead of its world premiere Tuesday at the Zurich Film Festival.

Filmmaker Patrick Wally spent over a decade on his film, a portrait of women’s rights, human rights and climate activist Najla Mohamed Lamin, who was born in a Sahrawi refugee camp in Algeria. Lamin has led a peaceful campaign supporting the right of Western Sahara to self-determination, a dream of Sahrawi refugees that has been frustrated for more than half a century.

Nobel Peace Prize nominee Greta Thunberg is expected to attend Tuesday’s world premiere and will participate in a conversation afterwards with Lamin. Thunberg visited the Sahrawi refugee camps last year, where she and Lamin conducted a workshop on climate change.

Director Patrick Wally Courtesy of WyFilm

“Told through conversations with the filmmaker – who gradually becomes visible inside the story – the documentary refuses to reduce Najla to a symbol of a geopolitical conflict,” notes a synopsis. “Western Sahara is experienced through one person living its consequences in real time. Najla addresses international institutions, builds practical spaces for women and children, raises her family and continues to argue for peaceful resistance even as a generation born in exile grows older without a political resolution.”

Watch on Deadline

The synopsis continues, “When armed conflict resumes after decades of ceasefire, the convictions that have shaped Najla’s public life are tested. The film follows her as she asks what pacifism, patience and agency can mean when history seems immovable – and whether one person can still create change inside circumstances that appear impossible.”

Najla Mohamed Lamin at the dunes near the Sahrawi refugee camp of Smara. Courtesy of WyFIlm

Anna Berthollet, CEO of Lightdox, commented, “Najla has lived her entire life with an unresolved conflict. Yet Patrick’s film is not a geopolitical story; it is an intimate portrait of how she chooses to live, raise her children and build a future for her community. He spent eleven years following her journey and bringing her story and mission to the screen. At a time when Western Sahara is once again receiving international attention, we believe it is important that Najla’s perspective is part of that conversation. We feel very humbled to have been entrusted with bringing Patrick and Najla’s deeply personal story to audiences around the world.”

The border wall berm and Moroccan military base separating the Moroccan occupied territory from the

Polisario controlled territory of Western Sahara. Courtesy of WyFilm

The unresolved status of Western Sahara has been largely ignored in the U.S. and much of the West, but it has kept the Sahrawi people in terrible limbo. Spain ruled the territory as its colonial possession for the better part of a hundred years, but after it ceded claims in the mid-1970s, hopes for the territory to determine its own future were dashed when Morocco took control of much of Western Sahara. The Polisario Front, representing the Indigenous Sahrawi people, seeks self-determination and is supported by Algeria (where the refugee camps are located). The United Nations officially designates Western Sahara as a “Non-Self-Governing Territory.”

In a director’s statement, Wally said, “When I met Najla ten years ago, I knew this film needed to be made. At the time I had never heard of the issue of Western Sahara. I thought of myself as reasonably informed about the struggles shaping the world, yet I knew nothing about more than 200,000 Sahrawis living for generations in refugee camps in the Algerian desert, established after the war and displacement of 1975. That absence in my own awareness shocked me.

“What struck me first, however, was not the conflict in the abstract but Najla herself. I was surprised by my own assumptions. Here was a woman raised in a refugee camp who was exceptionally articulate, politically precise and full of a vision for the future. She spoke about peaceful resistance, about a generation born in the camps, and about the endurance required to believe in a bright future when nobody outside seems able to see it.”

An aerial view of the Sahrawi refugee camp Smara, in the Algerian desert, near Tindouf. Courtesy of WyFilm

Along with directing, Wally serves as the film’s cinematographer. The film is produced by Shirin Hooshmandi, Najla Mohamed Lamin, and Patrick Wally. Anna Kirst edited the film, with additional editing by Daniel Rutz. The music is by Ahmed Zain.

In addition to Tuesday’s world premiere at the Zurich Film Festival, My Home of Wind and Sand will hold public screenings on Wednesday, Thursday and Sunday.

title: Victor Glover, First Black Astronaut to Fly to the Moon, Signs With CAA (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: CAA has signed astronaut Victor Glover for representation in all areas. Glover is a retired U.S. Navy captain and an emeritus NASA astronaut, making history several times throughout his career as a space explorer. In 2020, Glover piloted the first operational flight of SpaceX’s Crew Dragon spacecraft, Resilience, to the International Space Station. On this […]
content:
CAA has signed astronaut Victor Glover for representation in all areas.

Glover is a retired U.S. Navy captain and an emeritus NASA astronaut, making history several times throughout his career as a space explorer.

In 2020, Glover piloted the first operational flight of SpaceX’s Crew Dragon spacecraft, Resilience, to the International Space Station. On this mission, Glover served as a Flight Engineer for Expeditions 64 and 65, becoming the first Black American astronaut to live aboard the ISS.

Then, this April, Glover piloted NASA’s Artemis II mission, becoming the first Black astronaut to fly to the moon. Glover and the Artemis II crew completed a nearly 10-day mission, traveling as far as 252,756 miles from Earth, farther than any humans have ever traveled. Glover spent a total of 178 days in space, completing 4 spacewalks

Popular on Variety

Before Glover was selected to be an astronaut in 2013, during a term as a legislative fellow in the U.S. Senate, he’d built a successful career as a Naval aviator. Glover was a test pilot in the F/A‐18 Hornet, Super Hornet and EA‐18G Growler and has flown over 45 aircraft, accumulating over 4000 hours in the skies. He has been awarded the Defense Superior Service Medal, Navy Commendation Medal, two Navy and Marine Corps Achievement Medals, NASA Distinguished Service Medal and NASA Space Exploration Medal.

The California native is a alum of California Polytechnic State University, where he now serves as an executive advisor. He also hold Masters degrees from the Naval Postgraduate School and has been awarded honorary Doctorates from California Polytechnic State University and Howard University.

title: Kristen Stewart, Riley Keough and Wagner Moura to Star in Olivier Assayas’ Next Film ‘Spiritual World’
summary: French director Olivier Assayas (“The Wizard of the Kremlin”) has set his next movie, “Spiritual World,” with a starry cast including Kristen Stewart, Vicky Krieps, Riley Keough and Wagner Moura. The movie reunites Assayas with Stewart who won a Cesar Award for best supporting actress for her role opposite Juliette Binoche in his 2015 film […]
content:
French director Olivier Assayas (“The Wizard of the Kremlin”) has set his next movie, “Spiritual World,” with a starry cast including Kristen Stewart, Vicky Krieps, Riley Keough and Wagner Moura.

The movie reunites Assayas with Stewart who won a Cesar Award for best supporting actress for her role opposite Juliette Binoche in his 2015 film “Clouds of Sils Maria.” A year later, she had the leading role in “Personal Shopper,” a supernatural drama for which Assayas won best director at Cannes.
