Described as being in a similar vein as “Personal Shopper” but steamier, “Spiritual World” will star Stewart as a haunted, clairvoyant young woman plagued by mysterious premonitions.

Popular on Variety

The film will start shooting in February in France and Germany with an international cast that also includes Barbara Sukowa (“Deux”) and Niels Schneider (“The Unknown”).

Assayas is also reteaming with Paris-based producer Olivier Delbosc for “Spirtual World.” The pair worked together on Assayas’ latest film “The Wizard of the Kremlin,” an ambitious political thriller with Jude Law portraying Russian President Vladimir Putin and Paul Dano a spin doctor named Vadim Baranov. The movie, which also starred Alicia Vikander, world premiered at the Venice Film Festival.

Arte France, the Franco-German network, is co-financing the film which is currently being developed by Delbosc without a French studio attached.

One of Europe’s most celebrated auteurs, Assayas has been navigating between French and international projects spanning different genres for decades. He notably directed Cuban Five (“WASP Network”), an espionage thriller starring Edgar Ramírez, Penélope Cruz and Gael García Bernal; and the HBO mini-series “Irma Vep” with Vikander.

Moura, who won an Oscar for his role in “The Secret Agent,” is currently shooting Bradley Cooper’s Ocean prequel alongside Krieps, while Keough recently filmed Albert Serra’s “Out of This World.”

Stewart, who made her directorial debut last year with “The Chronology of Water” which competed at Cannes, was back on the Croisette this year with Quentin Dupieux’s “Full Phil,” a Paris-set burlesque comedy in which she starred opposite Woody Harrelson.

title: Matt Groening on the Future of ‘Futurama’ as the Series Gets Another Finale: ‘We Will Rise Again’ (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: “Futurama” is over. Long live “Futurama!” As the long-running animated series wraps its Season 14 Monday on Hulu, there are no further plans at the moment for it to return as a regular series. (However, three supersized Hulu specials are still to come). But given how often the Matt Groening animated comedy has wrapped — […]
content:
“Futurama” is over. Long live “Futurama!”

As the long-running animated series wraps its Season 14 Monday on Hulu, there are no further plans at the moment for it to return as a regular series. (However, three supersized Hulu specials are still to come).

But given how often the Matt Groening animated comedy has wrapped — only to be rebooted again a few years later — it’s hard for anyone involved, including Groening, to assume that this time it’s really done.

“They can put us in a coffin. They can nail the lid shut, but they can’t bury us. We will rise again,” Groening told Variety. “I guess I’m not too worried.”

Popular on Variety

“Futurama” first premiered on Fox in 1999 but ended its run there in 2003. Comedy Central revived it in 2008 and wrapped the show up in 2013. It returned again in 2023 via Hulu.

Each time the show went away, or it looked like the series was ending, the producers prepared an episode that could double as a series finale — only for the show to later come back. That’s why the producers had some fun with the episodic name for the year’s latest “finale.” Monday’s episode — the “Futurama” Season 14 ender — was given the title “Final Ending: The Last Conclusion.” The episode is a bit of an origins/flashback story; here’s the logline: “Fry and his brother sneak into a PG-13 movie as kids … with shocking consequences for the future.”

And yes, this could always double as a regular series finale. But don’t bet on it.

“The thing about ‘Is Futurama coming to an end?’ Well, we’ve come to an end many times before. We make a joke about it with the season finale. It’s redundantly, fatalistically titled,” Groening said. “I think we have a whistling-past-the-graveyard attitude these days because we’ve been in this situation many times before. We have lots more stories to tell. The animators and the actors and the writers all would love to do more stories and we’ll see. You never know.”

In the meantime, “Futurama” marches on with those three specials (dubbed “XXXL-Sized”) first announced at this summer’s San Diego Comic-Con. Those extended episodes, which are currently in production, will kick off in 2027 with a Christmas-related installment.

“The people at Hulu/Disney were saying, ‘Hey, give us some big stories that we can promote,’ and we said, ‘Gotcha,’” Groening said. “So these three that are coming up are kind of epic stories, and they’re promotable.”

“The nature of these stories, in general for ‘Futurama’ and also ‘The Simpsons,’ is that each episode could be a movie,” he added. “I mean, we pack enough melodrama and shenanigans in every episode to stretch it out. It’s just fun to tell a bigger story, but also take the time to breathe a little bit. Because one of the things that animated shows are bedeviled by is a short running time.”

Beyond the extended Christmas installment, Groening won’t share what the other two specials are about just yet, only to note that “we’ve been on the air forever, since 1999, so there’s more to the overall arc of the story of the characters. Stuff that we have hinted at from the very beginning is finally paid off, and some unanswered questions for true fans will finally be answered. But I can’t really be more specific. If you ask me again in a year, then I can talk about it.”

But he did share more on the Christmas (or in “Futurama” parlance, “Xmas”) edition: Robot Santa, the violent version of St. Nick who has made occasional visits on “Futurama” since Season 2, will play a role.

“Our version of Christmas, of course, is with Robot Santa,” Groening said. “Which back in the day was very controversial, because our robot Santa thought he was Santa — but he thought everyone was naughty, so he would go around trying to kill everyone. That was not considered in the Christmas spirit. At first there was some talk about not running the shows. It was controversial. But now everybody has figured out, hey, it’s all it’s all in good fun!”

On a recent episode of “The Making Of” podcast, exec producer David X. Cohen, who developed “Futurama” with Groening, noted that “Final Ending: The Last Conclusion” is the sixth time the show has been written as a potential series finale and now the upcoming “XXXL” trilogy also means they’ve been given a seventh stab at a “series finale.”

“When we were writing this season finale, from our point of view, it could have been the series finale and that is a situation that we have been in probably more than any other show in history,” Cohen told the podcast. “The one that’s going to be on shortly is our sixth series finale, in the sense again that at the time we wrote it might be, and we are now currently working on the seventh series finale. I feel like we’ve gotten pretty good at it.

“In my mind, if we go off the air, the characters are still having their adventures and interesting things are still happening,” Cohen added. “And I like to leave the audience thinking that there’s beautiful things ahead for these characters, whether or not we get to see them. That’s sort of the guiding philosophy for these series finales we’ve written.”

What happens if, after the three upcoming specials, “Futurama” really doesn’t come back? “If it doesn’t happen, we’ll do something else,” Groening said. “I love the group of people that work on this. It’s just a blast to work together. In fact, the cast of ‘Futurama’ and the animation studio and many of the writers also worked on ‘Disenchantment,’ which I did with Netflix for five seasons.”

That’s why Season 14’s penultimate episode, “A New New York Yankee in King Elfo’s Court,” featured a “Futurama”/”Disenchantment” crossover episode. Bringing together a Netflix and Hulu series wasn’t easy. “That was a very nimble negotiation to have Disney and Netflix working together,” he said.

“Futurama” stars John DiMaggio, Billy West, Katey Sagal, Tress MacNeille, Maurice LaMarche, Lauren Tom, Phil LaMarr and David Herman. Groening created the series, which he developed with David X. Cohen. Groening, Cohen, Ken Keeler and Claudia Katz are EPs; the series is produced by 20th Television Animation, a part of Disney Television Studios. Animation comes from Rough Draft Studios.

title: ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ Season 23 Casts Sarah Levy, Martin Martinez and Trevor Tordjman (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: “Grey’s Anatomy” is filling out its Season 23 cast: Sarah Levy, Martin Martinez and Trevor Tordjman have joined in guest starring roles. Levy will play Corrie. The official character description reads, “Witty and a bit of an oddball, Corrie is very pregnant. She has a lot of anxiety about giving birth to her second child […]
content:
“Grey’s Anatomy” is filling out its Season 23 cast: Sarah Levy, Martin Martinez and Trevor Tordjman have joined in guest starring roles.

Levy will play Corrie. The official character description reads, “Witty and a bit of an oddball, Corrie is very pregnant. She has a lot of anxiety about giving birth to her second child after the traumatic experience she had with her first child.” Levy is best known for playing Twyla Sands in “Schitt’s Creek,” created by and starring her father and brother, Eugene and Dan Levy. Her other credits include Hulu and Syfy’s “SurrealEstate” and the Osgood Perkins film “The Monkey.” Up next, she’ll appear in the films “Run” and “Sidelined 3.”

Martinez plays Charlie, who “has had a rough upbringing and as a result of the trauma he’s experienced, he has a tough exterior and struggles to trust other people.” He has had roles in Netflix’s “Never Have I Ever,” “Magnum P.I.” and Amazon’s “Primo.”

Popular on Variety

Tordjman plays Thomas, “the fun loving and charming boy next door who doesn’t realize he is as cute as he is. Thomas is at the hospital to help ensure his brother’s girlfriend is okay.” He has been seen in the Disney Kids and Family titles “Zombies” and “Bunk’d” as well the Canadian series “The Next Step,” Apple TV’s “The Studio” and HBO Max’s “The Sex Lives of College Girls.”

“Grey’s Anatomy” saw a major cast shakeup in the Season 22 finale with the exits of Owen Hunt and Teddy Altman, played by Kevin McKidd and Kim Raver, respectively. Read Variety‘s interview with showrunner Meg Marinis about their departures, the Season 22 finale and where the show is headed here.

title: Anne Hathaway Blocked from ‘Hot Ones’ on ‘Verity’ Press Tour After Doctor Warns It Could Disrupt Pregnancy: ‘I Might Go Into Early Labor’
summary: Anne Hathaway’s “Verity” press tour has included solo podcast appearances and joint on-camera interviews with her co-stars Dakota Johnson and Josh Hartnett, but don’t expect the Oscar winner to stop at “Hot Ones.” The Sean Evans-hosted interview series, where celebrities are asked questions while eating increasingly-spicy chicken wings, has become one of the most popular […]
content:
Anne Hathaway‘s “Verity” press tour has included solo podcast appearances and joint on-camera interviews with her co-stars Dakota Johnson and Josh Hartnett, but don’t expect the Oscar winner to stop at “Hot Ones.” The Sean Evans-hosted interview series, where celebrities are asked questions while eating increasingly-spicy chicken wings, has become one of the most popular press tour stops in recent years. However, Hathaway’s doctor ordered her not to eat spicy wings amid her pregnancy.

Speaking on the “Talk of the Townsends” podcast, Hathaway said that she was interested in doing an interview on “Hot Ones” since the online interview series appears in her new movie “Verity.” Hathaway filmed an episode of the show in character as Verity Crawford for a scene in the Colleen Hoover film adpatation.

Popular on Variety

“We did the first three wings for real, and then I switched to dummy wings. And then I thought that I was gonna be able to do the ‘Hot Ones’ challenge to do press for this film because it just made sense,” Hathaway explained. “But then I got pregnant, and my doctor said I couldn’t do it because I might go into early labor. So I still haven’t done the gauntlet yet. I’m not sure when that’s gonna happen. Maybe next year.”

“Verity” marks the fifth and final press tour for Hathaway this year following “Mother Mary,” “The Devil Wears Prada 2,” “The Odyssey” and “The End of Oak Street.” She’s traveled the globe and appeared on dozens of red carpets while pregnant with her third child with husband Adam Shulman. The actor is due later this year and plans to take a few months off from working after her whirlwind 2026.

“The movie [Verity] releases on October 2nd. And on October 3rd, I’m going to vanish in a plume of smoke and you’re not going to see me until you have to,” Hathaway quipped to Entertainment Tonight, noting that she will be back in front of the camera in March 2027 to film “Days of Thunder 2” with Tom Cruise.

“Verity” opens in theaters Oct. 5 from Amazon MGM.

title: ASIFA-Showcase Set For November, New FYC Event From Annie Awards Group
summary: As we draw closer to another awards season, ASIFA-Hollywood has penciled in a new FYC campaign. The group behind the Annie Awards has revealed ASIFA-Showcase, a two-day event of screenings, panels and presentations set for next month in Los Angeles. Billed as bringing together some of the biggest names in animation, ASIFA-Showcase runs November 14-15 […]
content:
As we draw closer to another awards season, ASIFA-Hollywood has penciled in a new FYC campaign. The group behind the Annie Awards has revealed ASIFA-Showcase, a two-day event of screenings, panels and presentations set for next month in Los Angeles.

Billed as bringing together some of the biggest names in animation, ASIFA-Showcase runs November 14-15 at the Audrey Irmas Pavilion as part of the four-day Infinity Festival Hollywood. The goal is to give ASIFA-Hollywood members an inside look at the films, TV shows and creative talent shaping the year in animation.

ASIFA-Showcase attendees can see the latest toon features and TV programs amd hear directly from the filmmakers and creative teams behind them as they delve into the artistry, storytelling and shaping animation this awards season. From major studio productions to independent animation, the event is designed to create a place where the animation community can discover new work, exchange ideas and celebrate the artists who bring these stories to life.

Studios in the mix include Apple TV, Crunchyroll, Disney/Pixar, Disney Television, IFC, LAIKA, Marvel Animation, Netflix Animation, Paramount+, Sony Pictures Animation, Tierney Corp, Universal Pictures/DreamWorks Animation and Warner Bros. Animation

Watch on Deadline

“We wanted to create an event that belongs to the animation community and gives the incredible work being produced across our industry a place to be seen, discussed and celebrated as awards season begins,” said Aubry Mintz, Executive Director of ASIFA-Hollywood. “The Showcase has drawn an extraordinary lineup in its very first year, and we’re excited to bring so many parts of our animation community together in one place.”

ASIFA-Hollywood produces the Annie Awards, the annual celebration of animation whose 2026 ceremony saw eventual Best Animated Feature Oscar winner Kpop Demon Hunters sweep all 10 of the categories for which is was nominated.

ASIFA-Showcase also will serve as a fundraising event. The broader Infinity Festival Hollywood runs November 12-15 and features programming across entertainment, animation, gaming, sports and emerging media.

title: Netflix’s ‘Women Like Us’ Adds Nine To Cast
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Women Like Us, the Netflix film from the Obamas’ Higher Ground and Charles D. King’s Macro Film Studios, has rounded out its cast with nine additions: Greg Tarzan Davis (Top Gun), Melanie Liburd (Bad Boys: Ride or Die), Harry Lennix (The Blacklist), Joy Bryant (Parenthood), Danielle Pinnock (Ghosts), Dewayne Perkins (The Studio), six-time Grammy […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Women Like Us, the Netflix film from the Obamas’ Higher Ground and Charles D. King’s Macro Film Studios, has rounded out its cast with nine additions: Greg Tarzan Davis (Top Gun), Melanie Liburd (Bad Boys: Ride or Die), Harry Lennix (The Blacklist), Joy Bryant (Parenthood), Danielle Pinnock (Ghosts), Dewayne Perkins (The Studio), six-time Grammy winner Samara Joy, Tiffany Boone (Mufasa: The Lion King) and Gail Bean (The Drop: A Snowfall Saga).

Character details haven’t been disclosed. Announced in July, the film is led by Vivica A. Fox, Vanessa Williams, Jenifer Lewis and Whoopi Goldberg.

Women Like Us is the story of a recently widowed woman is dragged to the Hamptons by her lifelong best friends and sister on what should have been her 30th anniversary. The weekend becomes a reckoning with grief, with marriage, with the sisterhood that’s carried them throughout the years, and with the realization that dreams don’t have an expiration date.

Watch on Deadline

Tasha Smith is directing from a script by Ali Kinney, with writing from Tracy Oliver. James Lopez and Poppy Hanks are producing for Macro, whose founder King is exec producing. Anikah McLaren and Mark R. Wright are producing for Higher Ground, whose Michelle Obama is exec producing.

Women Like Us is the latest of many projects stemming from a partnership between Netflix and Higher Ground, which won an Oscar for its work on their doc American Factory. Others upcoming include the series The Altruists and All the Sinners Bleed, as well as an untitled mother-daughter comedy starring Julianne Moore.

Davis is repped by CAA, Untitled, and Hansen, Jacobson, Teller; Liburd by Accelerate, Independent Artist Group, Untitled, and Christopher D. Abramson, P.C.; Lennix by Innovative Artists and Untitled; Bryant by Gersh, Principal Entertainment LA, and Schreck Rose Dapello; Pinnock by IAG, Mainstay Entertainment, and Hansen, Jacobson; Perkins by CAA, Artists First, and Schreck Rose Dapello; Boone by CAA, Vault Entertainment, and Toczek Suddleson; and Bean by Innovative, Echo Lake Entertainment, and The Hay Law Group.

title: Dan Trachtenberg Developing Original Pic Inspired By ‘Sleeping Beauty’ At Disney
summary: EXCLUSIVE: After breathing new life into the Predator franchise at 20th Century, Dan Trachtenberg and Disney have found another property on which to give a fresh spin. Sources tell Deadline the Prey director is coming on to direct an original idea inspired by the classic Disney tale Sleeping Beauty. The untitled project is in early […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: After breathing new life into the Predator franchise at 20th Century, Dan Trachtenberg and Disney have found another property on which to give a fresh spin. Sources tell Deadline the Prey director is coming on to direct an original idea inspired by the classic Disney tale Sleeping Beauty. The untitled project is in early development and is said to take the story in an entirely new direction with Trachtenberg’s distinct sensibility.

While plot details are being kept under wraps, insiders say this take has no connection to the Maleficent films starring Angelina Jolie. Trachtenberg and Rayna McClendon came up with the new story, with Alex Anfanger and Dan Schimpf penning the script.

Trachtenberg and his longtime producing partner Ben Rosenblatt will produce, as will Star Wars producer Michelle Rejwan. EVP Production Jessica Virtue is overseeing the project with Creative Executive Alina Mota, reporting to Disney Live Action president Daria Cercek.

Watch on Deadline

Trachtenberg and Disney have strong ties after he helped to successfully relaunch the Predator franchise with 2022’s Prey, which was a success on Hulu, earned critical praise and landed an Emmy nomination for Outstanding TV Movie. He followed that with last year’s Predator: Badlands and the animated pic Predator: Killer of Killers for Hulu, which has a 94% score on Rotten Tomatoes. The three Predator pics from Trachtenberg are the highest-rated on Rotten Tomatoes in the franchise.

He is currently in pre-production on a top-secret pic at Paramount.

Anfanger and Schimpf are the co-creators of the Comedy Central series Big Time In Hollywood, FL.

Trachtenberg is repped by CAA, Untitled Entertainment and Johnson Shapiro Slewett and Kole. Anfanger and Schimpf are repped by Mosaic, CAA, and Ginsburg Daniels Kallis.

title: ‘Resident Evil’ Producer Carter Swan Developing Keenspot Comic Book ‘The Crying Boy’ For Film
summary: EXCLUSIVE: As Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil prepares to cross $200M at the worldwide box office, the film’s producer Carter Swan has a new project to announce — a film adaptation of the Keenspot comic book series The Crying Boy by Niall O’Rourke & Rob Moran. Published in 2024, The Crying Boy follows a grieving widow […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: As Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil prepares to cross $200M at the worldwide box office, the film’s producer Carter Swan has a new project to announce — a film adaptation of the Keenspot comic book series The Crying Boy by Niall O’Rourke & Rob Moran.

Published in 2024, The Crying Boy follows a grieving widow trying to rebuild her life in Queens after the violent death of her husband. Things take a turn for the worse when she must save her young son from an even more terrifying fate, when the haunting painting of a crying child that he eerily befriends proves to be the vessel for an ancient demon that has preyed on children for millennia.

Following a Ringo Award nomination for Best Single Issue or Short Story, The Crying Boy‘s first issue is currently in its third printing, with a deluxe collection of the series planned for 2027 via Keenspot’s book distribution deal with Simon & Schuster. Rona Mark is scripting the big-screen adaptation.

Watch on Deadline

The comic’s co-creator O’Rourke said, “Super excited to work with Carter Swan and develop the project. He brings an incredible amount of experience and knowledge to this. We hit it off straight away after he read the script and he was a big fan of the Keenspot comic book series.”

A senior producer at PlayStation Productions for nearly eight years — through end of 2025 — Swan worked on Cregger’s Resident Evil during his time there, as well as HBO’s The Last of Us, Uncharted, Gran Turismo, Twisted Metal and Until Dawn. As an executive producer on The Last of Us, he earned Emmy nominations in 2023 and ’25.

For a time the world’s largest publisher of webcomics, Keenspot was founded in 2000. The company first broke into film with the Universal rom-com Marry Me — a 2022 adaptation of one of its webcomics starring Jennifer Lopez and Owen Wilson. The company’s first animated adaptation was Grubbs, based on the comics by Max Weaver, whose voice cast included Wil Wheaton, Jerry O’Connell, Jodie Sweetin and more.

Presently, Keenspot is also developing the animated adaptations Toy starring Kate Micucci and Kung Fu Legume starring Sherry Cola and Kheng Hua Tan, among other projects.

Chris Crosby, comic book publisher Keenspot’s CEO, said: “The Crying Boy has been one of Keenspot’s best-received titles and we’re ecstatic that a producer like Swan will be helping to bring it to the big screen. It’s a testament to the awesome creativity of writer Niall O’Rourke and artist Rob Moran that this adaptation is attracting talent of the highest caliber.”

title: Comedian Chris Hardwick Going Back To ‘The Middle Ages’ In Third Stand-Up Special
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Comedian Chris Hardwick has announced that The Middle Ages — his third stand-up special and first in a decade — will premiere on Gorilla Comedy+ on October 5. It’ll then be unveiled on 800 Pound Gorilla’s YouTube channel at 7 p.m. CT. on October 20. In The Middle Ages, Hardwick takes on middle age, […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Comedian Chris Hardwick has announced that The Middle Ages — his third stand-up special and first in a decade — will premiere on Gorilla Comedy+ on October 5. It’ll then be unveiled on 800 Pound Gorilla’s YouTube channel at 7 p.m. CT. on October 20.

In The Middle Ages, Hardwick takes on middle age, marriage, fatherhood and a rapidly changing world. Now in his 50s, he finds comedy in the indignities of aging, from growing pill collections and questionable digestive choices to prostate exams and realizing Gen Z are “time millionaires.”

Check out a trailer above.

Watch on Deadline

“The foundation of this set came from my 2019/2020 tour with the intent to shoot the special in 2021, but the pandemic had other plans!” Hardwick told Deadline. “In January of 2022 we had a baby and I paused work stuff for what ultimately became a three-year hiatus. BUT in that time, I learned piano, became a parent and got even MORE middle-aged than I was before, so in a weird way the delay actually kind of helped the set, and I’m super excited it’s finally happening! HUGE thanks to 800 Pound Gorilla, who not only have built a fantastic comedy community but who’ve also been an absolute dream to work with.”

Hardwick has worked in every sect of comedy, from the stand-up stage, to acting and writing in television and film, to voiceover work and hosting various podcasts and talk shows such as @midnight and Talking Dead. His previous hour specials, 2012’s Mandroid and 2016’s Funcomfortable, aired on Comedy Central. This summer, he returned to podcasting with I Think You’re Overthinking It, a weekly chat show with AMC+ that marks the latest incarnation of his former longtime pod The Nerdist Podcast. He also exec produces and hosts NBC’s The Wall, which this year was nominated for a Critics Choice Real TV Award for Best Game Show. He is repped by UTA, Brillstein Entertainment Partners, and Goodman, Genow, Schenkman.

This story originated as part of Deadline’s Comedy Means Business newsletter. Sign up here.

title: Former ‘South Park’ Writer Launches Site to Expose Information About Cornell University Sexual Assault Case: ‘There Will Be Accountability’
summary: Following the news that a former Cornell student had accused seven men of raping and drugging her at a frat house party in October 2024 — and none faced legal consequences — former “South Park” writer Toby Morton has launched a website dedicated to documenting the account of the woman (identified as Jane Doe), her […]
content:
Following the news that a former Cornell student had accused seven men of raping and drugging her at a frat house party in October 2024 — and none faced legal consequences — former “South Park” writer Toby Morton has launched a website dedicated to documenting the account of the woman (identified as Jane Doe), her lawsuit and the school’s response to the case.

“I’m building this carefully, and it will take time,” wrote Morton on the site’s homepage. “I’ve already received names, photographs, documents, messages, and other information related to the case. Before publishing those materials, I want to make certain that every identity is correct, every photograph is of the right person. TheCornell7.org will bring together her account, the lawsuit, public records, documented reporting, institutional responses, and additional verified information as it becomes available.”

He continued: “The goal is not to be first. The goal is to build a record that can withstand scrutiny. This will take time. It will be careful. It will be documented. And there will be accountability.”

Popular on Variety

While much of the site remains under construction, Morton shared a separate statement to Instagram about his work, explaining that while he is “not a journalist,” that fact makes him “more dangerous.” “I have no limits, no boundaries, nobody to tell me I’ve gone too far,” he wrote.

Information around the event has begun to surface following a lawsuit filed by the student against the college two weeks ago, which claimed that the school failed to protect her and prevent the alleged assault. At the time, following an investigation by the university, two of the men were expelled, while the other five received lesser punishment. The lawsuit claims that some of them were able to write essays to the school to reduce their disciplinary action, according to her attorney.

On Sunday, Florence Pugh posted a statement on social media in response to the case, describing the incident as a “horrific act.” “I’m feeling uneasy and sick and anxious,” she wrote. “I’m processing quietly and watching everything and everyone and every man.”

In addition to writing credits on “South Park,” Morton voiced Scott Tenorman on the show. He also wrote on “Mad TV.”

title: John Le Carré’s Cold War Spymaster George Smiley Returns in First Look at Matthew Macfadyen in ‘Legacy of Spies’
summary: John Le Carré’s legendary British Cold War spy George Smiley, last seen on screens in the acclaimed film “Tinker Tailer Soldier Spy’ (played by Gary Oldman, coincidentally now starring as another fictitious agent in “Slow Horses”), has finally returned. In the first image from BBC and MGM+ upcoming espionage thriller series “Legacy of Spies,” two-time […]
content:
John Le Carré’s legendary British Cold War spy George Smiley, last seen on screens in the acclaimed film “Tinker Tailer Soldier Spy’ (played by Gary Oldman, coincidentally now starring as another fictitious agent in “Slow Horses”), has finally returned.

In the first image from BBC and MGM+ upcoming espionage thriller series “Legacy of Spies,” two-time Emmy and BAFTA winner Matthew Macfadyen appears in the iconic role. In another image, Charlie Hunnam is seen as the embattled, world-weary agent-runner and field operative Alec Leamas.

Filming has now wrapped on the eight-part series, which is adapted from le Carré’s bestseller “The Spy Who Came in From the Cold,” and drawing on material his 2017 novel “A Legacy of Spies.” Alongside Macfadyen and Hunnam, the show stars Daniel Brühl, Devrim Lingnau Islamoğlu, Agnes O’Casey, Felix Kammerer, Dan Stevens, Jake Dunn, Anjana Vasan, Charlotte Ritchie, Joe Alwyn and Hugh Laurie. Showrunners and writers are Stephen Cornwell (“Message from the King,” “A Most Wanted Man”) and Clarissa Ingram. Michael Lennox (“Say Nothing,” “Crystal Lake”) serves as an executive producer and had lead directorial duties.

Popular on Variety

Charlie Hunnam as Alec Leamas in ‘Legacy of Spies’

© The Ink Factory | Photographer Csaba Aknay

In “Legacy of Spies,” when Leamas recruits Doris Quinz (Islamoğlu), a young and dynamic East German woman, to smuggle high-value Stasi documents into the West, it sets in motion a series of events that threaten to explode in the crucible of Cold War Berlin. Pursuing Leamas and Doris are Josef Fiedler (Brühl) and Hans-Dieter Mundt (Kammerer), two Stasi operatives whose ferocious desire to shut down the intelligence leak is matched only by their internal rivalry and an iron will to outmatch each other.

Pulled into the action is Liz Gold (O’Casey), an idealistic young woman whose courage and conviction force Leamas to navigate a world where loyalties fracture and betrayal is inevitable. Behind the scenes, the brilliant and taciturn spymaster Smiley orchestrates operations while the elusive Soviet mastermind Karla looms in the shadows, setting the stage for a conflict that will define a generation. As per the description: “Personal lives become collateral in a ruthless intelligence war, and as the lines between duty and love begin to blur, every emotion becomes a weapon.”

“Legacy of Spies” is set to launch exclusively on BBC iPlayer and BBC One in the U.K., and on MGM+ in the U.S., Germany, Spain, Italy, Austria, Belgium, the Netherlands, Brazil and Spanish-speaking Latin America. The series will also air on SBS in Australia, Sky New Zealand and Sky Switzerland, and CANAL+ across France & French-speaking territories, Central & Eastern Europe and Sub-Saharan Africa.

The series was filmed principally in the Czech Republic, with location filming also in the U.K. and Germany.

title: Mohammad Rasoulof, O Mipo to Receive Tokyo Film Festival’s Kurosawa Akira Award
summary: Mohammad Rasoulof, the Iranian filmmaker who secretly left his country in 2024 after being sentenced to eight years in prison, will receive the Kurosawa Akira Award at the 39th Tokyo International Film Festival. He will share the honor with director O Mipo. The two were chosen by a committee of filmmakers Yamada Yoji and Lee […]
content:
Mohammad Rasoulof, the Iranian filmmaker who secretly left his country in 2024 after being sentenced to eight years in prison, will receive the Kurosawa Akira Award at the 39th Tokyo International Film Festival. He will share the honor with director O Mipo.

The two were chosen by a committee of filmmakers Yamada Yoji and Lee Sang-il, cinematographer Ashizawa Akiko and TIFF programming director Ichiyama Shozo. Capcom Co., Ltd. backed the award’s return in 2022, after it had gone 14 years without being presented. Last year it went to Lee and Chloé Zhao.

Rasoulof won the Golden Bear at Berlin in 2020 for “There Is No Evil,” which later played at the 33rd TIFF. His “The Seed of the Sacred Fig” took the Special Jury Prize at Cannes in 2024, and as Germany’s entry it was later nominated for the Oscar for best international feature. He was still finishing that film when he had to flee Iran in secret, shortly before Cannes. He was jailed in 2010 while shooting a film and arrested again in 2022, then provisionally released after eight months. He has shot many of his films in secret and smuggled them abroad to screen.

Popular on Variety

The committee praised the “humanist perspective” of his recent work, “which portrays even those who perpetrate oppression as ordinary citizens.”

“Receiving the Kurosawa Award is a great honor for me,” Rasoulof said. “His films are profound explorations of the human condition and the moral choices we make in moments of crisis.”

O started out as a script supervisor after working at Obayashi Nobuhiko’s production company. She made her feature debut in 2006 with “The Sakais’ Happiness.” “The Light Shines Only There” (2014) won her best director at the Montreal World Film Festival and was Japan’s Oscar submission. “Being Good” (2015) was named best Asian film at the Moscow International Film Festival. After a nine-year gap in which she had two children, she came back with “Living in Two Worlds” (2024), which competed at Shanghai. Her latest, “How Dare You?” (2025), played in competition at Zlín.

O said getting the award on the 20th anniversary of her debut left her grateful and humbled. “Winning the Shindo Kaneto Award in 2010 provided me with the vital support to keep making films. Though my progress has been slow, reaching the Kurosawa Akira Award is a stroke of fortune that makes me truly savor what a happy cinematic journey I have had,” she said.

The festival will also show a selection of Kurosawa’s favorite films, along with two of his own. The lineup is Charles Chaplin’s “The Circus” (1928), 4K restorations of Kurosawa’s “Sanshiro Sugata” (1943) and “Ikiru” (1952), and Abbas Kiarostami’s “Where Is the Friend’s House?” (1987).

Isomura, who won the Japan Academy Film Prize for best supporting actor for “The Moon,” will serve as jury president of the Ethical Film Award. Three members of TIFF’s student PR team will sit on the jury with him. The prize was set up with Sumitomo Corporation in 2023 and highlights films dealing with the environment, poverty, discrimination and diversity. This year’s nominees are Brenda Lígia’s “Amadeo and the Hypothetical New World” (Brazil), Isabelle Stever’s “I Rarely Wake Up Dreaming” (Germany/Ukraine) and Vee Shi’s “Time and Tide” (Australia).

Isomura said watching things on a small screen can fool people into thinking they understand something right away, when real understanding of social issues comes from working toward the answers. “Cinema possesses the unique power to pause our hurried pace, allowing us to experience that very process through the lives and emotions of others,” he said.

Isomura also hosts the Shizuoka Film Festival in his hometown. His Netflix credits include “Alice in Borderland,” and Netflix will release his next project, “Did Someone Happen to Mention Me?” worldwide on Oct. 22. The Ethical Film Award will be presented on Nov. 2, along with a talk session with Isomura.

The festival runs Oct. 26–Nov. 4. Its TIFFCOM market takes place Oct. 28–30.

title: How to Watch Tonight’s ‘All American’ Series Finale Online Free
summary: After eight seasons and more than 100 episodes, The CW’s “All American” bids farewell tonight. The high school football drama airs its final episode tonight at 8 p.m. on The CW, closing a chapter that first premiered in October of 2018. Viewers can tune into the hour-long “All American” finale on TV through their local […]
content:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

After eight seasons and more than 100 episodes, The CW‘s “All American” bids farewell tonight.

The high school football drama airs its final episode tonight at 8 p.m. on The CW, closing a chapter that first premiered in October of 2018.

Viewers can tune into the hour-long “All American” finale on TV through their local CW affiliate, or stream the show as it airs with a live streaming service like DIRECTV (currently offering a free trial here). DIRECTV carries a live CW feed that you can use to watch “All American” online free without cable.

You can also watch the “All American” finale online through Fubo and Hulu + Live TV, both of which also offer free trials that let you watch the show on your computer, phone, tablet or smart TV. The final episode will be available to stream the next day on cwtv.com.

Tonight’s series finale is titled “To Live and Die in L.A,” and welcomes back original cast members, Daniel Ezra (Spencer) and Samantha Logan (Olivia), as friends and family rally around Olivia as she goes into labor. Ezra also returned to direct the final episode.

As Spencer James, Ezra played the main protagonist in the series, whose life in Crenshaw is turned on its head after he is recruited by coach Billy Baker (played by Taye Diggs) to play for a high school football team in Beverly Hills. The series followed the friendships and relationships made on and off the football field, while addressing themes of classism, adolescence and race.

Diggs departed the show in a shocking season five episode, while original cast members Ezra, Logan, Cody Christian, Karimah Westbrook and Monet Mazur left at the end of season six. After a time jump, “All American” picked up in season seven with Greta Onieogou (Layla), Bre-Z (Coop) and Michael Evans Behling (Jordan) leading the cast along with a new group of regulars.

Per an episode description, tonight’s series finale focuses on Spencer as he “navigates one of the toughest and most important days of his life. Meanwhile, Olivia leans on her mom to help her make the right decision. Friends and family, old and new, gather as one chapter ends and new chapters begin for our favorite Crenshaw and Beverly natives.”

The series finale episode is written by executive producer Nkechi Okoro Carroll along with co-showrunner Jamie Turner.

Watch the “All American” series finale tonight at 8 p.m. ET/PT on The CW or stream it online free through DIRECTV. You can also watch all previous episodes of the show on Netflix or by purchasing it through Prime Video.

“All American” is the last remaining scripted series on the CW that launched before the network’s sale to Nexstar. Okoro Carroll and Turner produce alongside Greg Berlanti, Sarah Schechter and David Strauss. The series — inspired by former NFL playe Spencer Paysinger — is produced by Warner Bros. Television and CBS Studios in association with Berlanti Productions.

title: CBS and MTV VMAs Attract a Combined 8.4 Million Viewers, Making it the Most-Watched Since 2015 and Up 51% From Last Year
summary: The Moon Man still has some life. CBS’ and MTV’s coverage of the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards averaged a combined 8.43 million viewers on Sunday night, according to Nielsen Live+same day fast nationals. Those numbers are subject to change once finals are in, but for now that makes it the most-watched VMAs in 11 […]
content:
The Moon Man still has some life. CBS’ and MTV‘s coverage of the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards averaged a combined 8.43 million viewers on Sunday night, according to Nielsen Live+same day fast nationals. Those numbers are subject to change once finals are in, but for now that makes it the most-watched VMAs in 11 years (since 2015, when it only ran on MTV) and puts it up 51% vs. last year’s show.

The VMAs were likely assisted by an NFL football overrun (which went late until the Baltimore Ravens defeated the Dallas Cowboys), pushing the start time of the VMAs by several minutes (to 7:51 p.m. ET). The show still started at 4:30 p.m. PT inside L.A. Live’s Peacock Theater, but wound up being tape-delayed as a result on CBS.

That 8.43 million number includes the simulcast on CBS and MTV, as well as an encore on MTV. But in an apples-to-apples comparison, the show last year (on Sept. 7, 2025) also aired on CBS, MTV and encored on MTV — and that telecast brought in 5.60 million viewers.

Popular on Variety

In individual network numbers, the CBS telecast averaged 7.61 million viewers, up 52% from last year (5.00 million). MTV’s simulcast averaged 686,000 viewers (up 40% from last year’s 481,000). And the MTV encore brought in 142,000 viewers (up 31% from 108,000 last year).

According to CBS, this year repped the best same-day audience for the VMAs since 2015, when the awards show hit a big 12.73 million viewers.

In demos, this was the most-watched VMAs in adults 25-54 (3.11 million) since 2019 (3.55 million) and was up +34% from last year (2.32 million). In adults 18-49, the show took in 2.66 million — the best since 2018 (3.02 million) and up 32% from 2025 (2.02 million). And in adults 18-34, the show averaged 1/09 million, the best since 2020 (1.14 million) and up 46% from last year (751,000).

CBS also reported social highlights: 31.1M interactions and 159M video views (up 8% from last year).

The 2026 VMAs opened with Madonna — in her first VMAs performance in 23 years — with Sabrina Carpenter and Charli XCX. The show also featured Taylor Swift winning the video of the year award, taking the MTV VMA artist director award and premiering her new music video to “Patient Zero.”

Also, Nirvana received the video vanguard award, and tributes were held for Dolly Parton and George Michael. Other performers included GENER8ION, Gunna, Kacey Musgraves, Lisa, Madonna, Raye, Shaboozey, Sienna Spiro, Sombr, Teddy Swims and Yung Lean.

Snoop Dogg hosted the 2026 VMAs. Gunpowder & Sky produced the special, while. Van Toffler served as producer. Jesse Ignjatovic of Den of Thieves, Barb Bialkowski and Bruce Gillmer were executive producers alongside Barry Barclay and Floris Bauer. Melanie Block was co-executive producer and Gary Lanvy as co-producer. Snoop Dogg was executive producer alongside producers Sara Ramaker and Jasmin Ratansi. Jen Proctor was executive talent producer.

title: Broadcast To Hit A Double, Peacock Going Deep In NBC Sports Coverage Of MLB Wild Card Playoffs
summary: Sports fans of a certain age can readily recall NBC’s coverage of the Major League Baseball playoffs regularly pre-empting the network’s “Must-See TV” primetime lineup in the 1990s. While today’s ratings and programming landscape has changed dramatically in the intervening decades, this year’s playoffs (starting Tuesday) are shaping up as a back-to-the-future milestone for NBC […]
content:
Sports fans of a certain age can readily recall NBC‘s coverage of the Major League Baseball playoffs regularly pre-empting the network’s “Must-See TV” primetime lineup in the 1990s.

While today’s ratings and programming landscape has changed dramatically in the intervening decades, this year’s playoffs (starting Tuesday) are shaping up as a back-to-the-future milestone for NBC Sports. Its exclusive coverage of the wild card round (which aired on ESPN and ABC from 2022 to ’25) will deliver boosts to the broadcast network and streaming flagship Peacock.

Four games a day, starting at 2 p.m., 5 p.m., 8 p.m. and 10 p.m. ET, will be carried on Tuesday and Wednesday. Depending on the status of each best-of-three series, Thursday will see between one and four games before later playoff rounds shift to Turner and Fox. Viewership of MLB has been on the rise, with all rights holders seeing improvement over 2025 levels through the second half of the season. Last year’s World Series comeback by the L.A. Dodgers against the Toronto Blue Jays benefited from going the maximum seven games, but its average of 15.71 million viewers a game was the best for any Series since 2017, demonstrating the sport’s recent momentum.

Two of the Tuesday and Wednesday games (at 2 and 8) will air on NBC, with the other two airing on cable TV’s NBC Sports Network. If series move to a deciding third game on Thursday, NBC will air between one and three games, depending on where things stand. It’s a step up for broadcast TV compared with recent years, when only one game per day aired on ABC and extends a pendulum swing back to broadcast for the sport, whose entire pre-World series playoffs in 2019 aired on cable TV except for one game.

Watch on Deadline

Peacock will stream every inning of the wild card round, between eight and 12 games. It will be the latest injection of live sports in a year that has already seen the Winter Olympics, the Super Bowl, NBA and NHL playoff games, and Spanish-language World Cup coverage. The streaming service ended June with 48 million subscribers after adding 2 million in the second quarter, which included Love Island USA and the start of the World Cup. It also increased prices in August during the runup to college football and NFL season, with MLB playoffs and the NBA not much farther down the line.

Six years after launch, Peacock finally turned a profit in the second quarter. NBCU Media Chairman Matt Strauss said live sports has been a key part of the company “playing to our strengths” in streaming.

NBCU reached a 3-year rights deal with MLB worth a reported $600 million in November 2025. “We are excited to reignite NBC Sports’ storied Major League Baseball history through this comprehensive and innovative partnership that will honor the past and create new traditions,” NBC Sports President Rick Cordella said at the time.

All wild card series have used the best-of-three format since 2022, replacing the prior set-up that pitted select lower-seeded teams against each other in a single-elimination game.

NBCU not only has more wild card games to work with; it also got lucky this year with the markets and teams represented in the kickoff to the postseason. Two longtime rivalries will be renewed, with the Boston Red Sox taking on the New York Yankees and the Philadelphia Phillies playing the Atlanta Braves. The other series also feature major markets and marquee teams, as the Chicago White Sox face the Houston Astros and the Chicago Cubs battle the San Diego Padres.

The presence of both the Cubs and the White Sox is just the fourth time that both Chicago teams have made the playoffs in the same year. The last time was in the Covid-altered 2020 season. Before that, the teams both made it in 2008 and when they dueled in the 1906 World Series (which was won by the White Sox).

The Astros are also the first team in MLB history to finish a full 162-game regular season without a winning record and still make the playoffs. Houston had 81 wins and 81 losses.

During a media conference call on Monday, play-by-play announcer Jason Benetti, analysts Anthony Rizzo and Joey Votto, and senior producer Matt Borzello talked about their approach to the wild card games. One feature similar to those incorporated into NBA and NHL telecasts is “Inside the Pitch,” in which players and former players positioned next to the field break down the action.

The combination of physical proximity and playing experience allows the broadcasters to “pick up on things like the conversations players are having that don’t reach the broadcast booth,” Rizzo said. Vatto said he and Rizzo pick up on the “little nuances” and the “tendencies and mannerisms” in a way they hope can benefit the viewer.

title: Matthew Macfadyen Is Iconic Le Carré Spy George Smiley In First Glimpse At The BBC & MGM+’s ‘Legacy Of Spies’

content:
We’ve got first glimpse at Matthew Macfadyen descending into the John le Carré universe to play iconic spymaster George Smiley.

The BBC and MGM+‘s Legacy of Spies has dropped first-look images including the Succession star donning those trademark glasses and Charlie Hunnam as Alec Leamas, which can be seen below.

The eight-part drama marks Smiley’s long-anticipated return to television, a first in four decades, when he was played by Alec Guinness, although he was portrayed in the 2011 movie version of Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy by Gary Oldman.

Legacy of Spies is adapted from The Spy Who Came in from the Cold and draws on additional material from 2017’s A Legacy of Spies.

Watch on Deadline

When Leamas, a highly experienced Circus field operative, recruits Doris Quinz, a young and dynamic East German woman, to smuggle high-value Stasi documents into the West, it sets in motion a series of events that threaten to explode in the crucible of Cold War Berlin. Pursuing Leamas and Doris are Josef Fiedler and Hans-Dieter Mundt, two Stasi operatives whose ferocious desire to shut down the intelligence leak is matched only by their internal rivalry and an iron will to outmatch each other. Pulled into the action is Liz Gold, an idealistic young woman whose courage and conviction force Leamas to navigate a world where loyalties fracture and betrayal is inevitable.

Charlie Hunnam as Alec Leamas in ‘Legacy of Spies’

The images have been released to coincide with the end of production in the Czech Republic.

The show is one of the most highly-anticipated UK-U.S. co-pros of the upcoming year and also stars Daniel Brühl as Josef Fiedler, Devrim Lingnau Islamoğlu as Doris Quinz, Agnes O’Casey as Liz Gold, Felix Kammerer as Hans-Dieter Mundt, Dan Stevens as Bill Haydon, Jake Dunn as Peter Guillam, Anjana Vasan as Connie Sachs, Charlotte Ritchie as Ann Smiley, Joe Alwyn as Jim Prideaux.

Back in June, we revealed that Hugh Laurie would also star in Legacy of Spies. He is playing Control, the fiendish and commanding head of The Circus and Smiley’s morally fickle superior.

Legacy of Spies is set to launch on BBC iPlayer and BBC One in the UK, and on MGM+ in the U.S., Germany, Spain, Italy, Austria, Belgium, the Netherlands, Brazil and Spanish-speaking Latin America. The series will also air on SBS in Australia, Sky New Zealand and Sky Switzerland, and CANAL+ across France & French-speaking territories, Central & Eastern Europe and Sub-Saharan Africa.

Legacy of Spies was commissioned by Lindsay Salt, Director of BBC Drama. The series is produced by The Ink Factory (The Pigeon Tunnel, The Night Manager), in co-production with Amusement Park Film (All Quiet on the Western Front) and in association with 127 Wall Productions and Paramount Television Studios, for the BBC and MGM+. The series is written by Stephen Cornwell (Message from the King, A Most Wanted Man) and Clarissa Ingram, Michael Lennox (Say Nothing, Crystal Lake) will serve as an executive producer and is lead director, with Claudia Llosa (The Vampire Lestat, The Milk of Sorrow) serving as second director and co-executive producer. The executive producers are Stephen Cornwell, who is also showrunner, Graham Yost (Justified, Silo), Simon Cornwell (The Pigeon Tunnel, The Night Manager), Michele Wolkoff, Malte Grunert (All Quiet on the Western Front), Chris Rice, Macfadyen, Hunnam, Clarissa Ingram, and Joe Tsai. Susanne Bier and Mike Lesslie are also executive producers. The executive producers for the BBC are Gaynor Holmes and Nick Lambon. Nick Cornwell is executive producer for the John le Carré estate. Sam Costin and Llosa, are co-executive producers and Nancy Bray is producer for The Ink Factory. Fifth Season is handling global sales.

title: Iran’s Mohammad Rasoulof & Japanese-Korean Filmmaker Mipo O To Receive Kurosawa Akira Award At Tokyo Film Festival
summary: Tokyo International Film Festival has announced that Japanese-Korean filmmaker Mipo O and Iranian filmmaker Mohammad Rasoulof will be presented with the Kurosawa Akira Award at this year’s edition of the festival. The award is designed to recognize the legacy and ongoing influence of renowned auteurs and is presented to filmmakers who have “made waves in […]
content:
Tokyo International Film Festival has announced that Japanese-Korean filmmaker Mipo O and Iranian filmmaker Mohammad Rasoulof will be presented with the Kurosawa Akira Award at this year’s edition of the festival.

The award is designed to recognize the legacy and ongoing influence of renowned auteurs and is presented to filmmakers who have “made waves in cinema and are expected to help guide the industry’s future”. Last year’s recipients were Kokuho director Lee Sang-il and Chloé Zhao.

This year’s recipients were selected by a committee comprising Lee, veteran filmmaker Yoji Yamada, cinematographer Akiko Ashizawa and TIFF Programming Director Shozo Ichiyama.

After making her feature directorial debut in 2006 with The Sakai’s Happiness, Mipo O won Best Director at the Montreal World Film Festival with her 2014 film, The Light Shines Only There, which went on to win 60 awards in Japan and internationally. Following a hiatus for childbirth and childcare, she returned to feature filmmaking in 2024 with box-office hit Living In Two Worlds followed by How Dare You? last year.

Watch on Deadline

“Since making her directorial debut in 2006 with The Sakai’s Happiness, director O Mipo has consistently created works that offer a multifaceted perspective on individuals living on the margins of society, refraining from viewing them through a simple lens of good vs. evil,” said the selection committee.

The TIFF selection committee also noted that Rasoulof has faced censorship, prison sentences and filmmaking bans from the Iranian government, yet has relentlessly pursued his unique method of filmmaking often relying on guerilla-style shooting. He won the Golden Bear at the Berlinale in 2020 for There Is No Evil, and the Special Jury Prize at Cannes for The Seed Of The Sacred Fig in 2024.

The committee said: “Director Mohammad Rasoulof has consistently produced profound works centered on the theme of human rights oppression under state regimes. Notably, his recent films There Is No Evil and The Seed Of The Sacred Fig have gained international acclaim for their humanist perspective, which portrays even those who perpetrate oppression as ordinary citizens.”

TIFF is also presenting a selection of Akira Kurosawa’s favorite films including Charlie Chaplin’s The Circus (1928) and Abbas Kiarostami’s Where Is the Friend’s House? (1987), along with 4K restorations of two of Kurosawa’s own titles – Sanshiro Sugata (1943) and Ikiru (1952).

TIFF also announced that actor Hayato Isomura (Alice In Borderland, What Did You Eat Yesterday?) will head the Ethical Film Award Jury. Three titles from this year’s TIFF selection met the criteria for the Ethical Film Award: Brenda Lígia’s Amadeo And The Hypothetical New World (Brazil), Isabelle Stever’s I Rarely Wake Up Dreaming (Germany, Ukraine) and Vee Shi’s Time And Tide (Australia).

title: ‘Toy Story 5’ Giddy Ups To 20 Million Views In First Five Days On Disney+
summary: Disney/Pixar’s Toy Story 5 cleared 20 million views in its first five days of streaming around the world on Disney+, enough to feasibly make it the No. 1 film on the OTT service. The Andrew Stanton-directed movie began streaming on Disney+ on Sept. 23. The launch builds on the strength of Toy Story, which is […]
content:
Disney/Pixar’s Toy Story 5 cleared 20 million views in its first five days of streaming around the world on Disney+, enough to feasibly make it the No. 1 film on the OTT service. The Andrew Stanton-directed movie began streaming on Disney+ on Sept. 23.



The launch builds on the strength of Toy Story, which is the most-watched film franchise on Disney+ with over 2B hours streamed globally per the studio.



In addition, Disney’s highest grossing movie of 2026 YTD at $1.1 billion global has driven 168M hours of lift to the franchise since the teaser trailer was released.



The fifthquel also ranks among the top ten theatrical film premieres on Disney+ worldwide to date, joining the other four Toy Story movies, all of which consistently rank among the top 20 movies on Disney+ each year. Again, all according to Disney.

The highest grossing animated movie in MPA history, Zootopia 2 ($1.866B), clocked 32M views globally in its first seven days on Disney+. The movie began streaming on March 11. Back in September 2024, Disney’s Inside Out 2 ($1.698B), drew 30.5 million views worldwide on Disney+ in its first five days on the streamer.



The Toy Story franchise has grossed more than $4B at the worldwide box office. Across all retailers, Toy Story generates more than $1B in annual global retail sales and reaches fans across every Disney park and cruise ship, including four fully immersive lands, 23 attractions, and two hotels. The franchise has generated more than $50B in total economic impact worldwide over the past 30 years.

title: Federal Film & TV Tax Credit Bill Adds Eight New Senate Co-Sponsors
summary: A bill to establish a 20% federal film and TV tax credit has added eight new co-sponsors in the Senate, a boost to the legislation as backers pin their hopes on passage during Congress’ lame duck session. Sen. John Cornyn (R-TX), Sen. Steve Daines (R-MT), Sen. Andy Kim (D-NJ), Sen. Bernie Moreno (R-OH), Sen. Alex […]
content:
A bill to establish a 20% federal film and TV tax credit has added eight new co-sponsors in the Senate, a boost to the legislation as backers pin their hopes on passage during Congress’ lame duck session.

Sen. John Cornyn (R-TX), Sen. Steve Daines (R-MT), Sen. Andy Kim (D-NJ), Sen. Bernie Moreno (R-OH), Sen. Alex Padilla (D-CA), Sen. Tim Sheehy (R-MT), Sen. Mark Warner (D-VA) and Sen. Raphael Warnock (D-GA) have signed on to the bill, called the Motion Picture, Television and Entertainment Revitalization Act. Sen. Adam Schiff (D-CA) and Sen. Tim Scott (R-SC) introduced the bill in the Senate last week, concurrently with a House version that also has a slate of bipartisan supporters.

The bill has the support of President Donald Trump, who urged lawmakers to establish such a credit in a Truth Social post late last month.

Watch on Deadline

The credit would be available to projects with a minimum spend of $1 million and with at least 75% of the principal photography days occurring in the U.S. There also are additional 5% bonus credits for productions in rural opportunity zones and disaster recovery areas, as well as to independent productions and multi-state producers. Bonuses also are available to producers who bring production back to the U.S. in a measurable way. The incentive also will be a supplement to state credits.

With the House out until the midterms and the Senate leaving this week, the bill won’t advance before the November election. But backers are aiming for later in the year, perhaps as an attachment to year-end spending legislation.

title: Todd Rundgren Slams Taylor Swift, Says She ‘Ruined Music’ and Is ‘the Apotheosis of Mediocrity’
summary: Todd Rundgren, the singer-songwriter and producer behind hits like “Hello It’s Me” and “I Saw the Light,” recently slammed Taylor Swift, calling the pop star “the apotheosis of mediocrity” and claiming that she “ruined music.” “To me, Taylor Swift is the apotheosis of mediocrity,” Rundgren said in an interview with Vulture. “It’s the era of […]
content:
Todd Rundgren, the singer-songwriter and producer behind hits like “Hello It’s Me” and “I Saw the Light,” recently slammed Taylor Swift, calling the pop star “the apotheosis of mediocrity” and claiming that she “ruined music.”

“To me, Taylor Swift is the apotheosis of mediocrity,” Rundgren said in an interview with Vulture. “It’s the era of the female artists.”

Rundgren got on the topic of Swift when asked who his target would be if he were to produce an album to make fun of an artist today. (He produced “Bat Out of Hell” by Meat Loaf in 1977 and famously said he didn’t care if it succeeded or not because he wanted to make fun of Bruce Springsteen.) “Taylor Swift, of course,” he responded. “There’s an argument to be made that she ruined music. It’s an understandable phenomenon.”

Popular on Variety

He continued to explain that the biggest artists in the world are now female “because of video games.”

“Back in the ’90s, boys stopped spending money on music and started spending it on video games, and that left the music market with, ‘Well, where do we go here?’ And they said, ‘Well, there’s all these young girls and they’ve got their allowances, too,” he said. “Why don’t we start making music for young girls instead of Pearl Jam or something like that?”

Rundgren’s comments come on the heels of Swift’s most recent musical release, “The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore.” She broke two Spotify records thanks to the deluxe version of her 2025 album: the new release “Patient Zero” broke the record for the most-streamed song by a female artist in a day so far this year, while Swift had the most streams out of any female artist in a day in 2026.

At the 2026 MTV VMAs, Swift was honored with the inaugural Artist-Director Award.

title: ‘School Girls; or, the African Mean Girls Play’ Broadway Review: An Exceptional Portrait of Black Girlhood
summary: Late girlhood has a sacredness that can’t be replicated. It’s a particular time in life between innocence and adulting, allowing young women to swing between the two. Jocelyn Bioh’s sensational play, “School Girls; or, the African Mean Girls Play,” captures this magic and anguish, set against the specificity of mid-1980s Ghana. Directed by Whitney White, […]
content:
Late girlhood has a sacredness that can’t be replicated. It’s a particular time in life between innocence and adulting, allowing young women to swing between the two. Jocelyn Bioh’s sensational play, “School Girls; or, the African Mean Girls Play,” captures this magic and anguish, set against the specificity of mid-1980s Ghana. Directed by Whitney White, who also helmed Bioh’s Tony-nominated “Jaja’s African Hair Braiding” three years ago, “School Girls” is an uproariously funny and heartbreaking portrait of sisterhood framed by the consequences of colonialism, anti-Blackness, and colorism. In just 75 minutes, “School Girls” captures what it means to be Black and female across time, space and place.

“School Girls; or, the African Mean Girls Play” opens in the Aburi Mountains of central Ghana in 1986, at the Aburi Girls Boarding School. With Bobby Brown’s “Every Little Step” floating through the boom box, the audience meets the kind-hearted Ama (Lucia Aremu), who is eager to finish her studies and wed her longtime beau. Mercy (Jordan Rice) and her cousin Gifty (Nia Otchere-Sarfo) are witty and carefree, focused on convincing Mercy’s physician father to buy them the latest Nikes. Then there is Nana (Erin Morton), sweet as pie and a newcomer to the group. Nana is focused on getting into university, but her larger body makes her a target for bullies. The queen bee of the group is Paulina (a sensational Denée Benton), who rambles on about her American cousins and her pro-football player boyfriend Kofi, whom no one has actually met. Self-absorbed and vicious, Paulina wields her cruelty toward all the girls (particularly Nana) as if it were a weapon. Her barbs are sharp enough to bring even Regina George to tears.

Popular on Variety

Though Paulina typically spends her days belittling her friends and humiliating Nana, presently, her focus is on something grander. With the blessing of the shrewd but motherly Headmistress Francis (Heather Alicia Simms), Paulina has decided to compete in the Miss Ghana 1986 pageant, hoping to reach the Miss Universe competition. Paulina even allows the other girls (except Nana) to throw their hats in the ring. However, when a new American Ghanaian student, Ericka Boafo (Jasmine Amy Rogers), enrolls in the second week of school, Paulina quickly realizes her dreams may be much further out of reach than she expected. Possessing a Midwestern accent, Calvin Klein dresses, Black American skin and hair care products, and a butter-pecan skin tone, Ericka quickly wins over the crew Paulina has ruled for years. Desperate to regain her dominance while dazzling pageant recruiter Eloise Amponsah (Tony Award winner Patina Miller), who was Miss Ghana 1966, Paulina launches a campaign to crush Ericka’s spirit and dash her chances in the spotlight.

In the boarding school’s clean but modest cafeteria with scenic design by Teresa L. Williams and lighting by Stacey Derosier, the girls laugh, weep and fuss over everything from their understanding of the fine-dining experience at White Castle to a deep-seated New Edition obsession. But beyond the humor and laugh-out-loud moments, the play conveys a deeper truth. Paulina, who appears poised and confident, is trapped in a swirl of self-loathing, clinging to damaging bleaching creams and lying about who she really is. Nana, in a bigger body, often tries to shrink herself in tone and timbre. Gifty, whimsical and fun, has dyslexia and is only willing to read in front of Mercy. Finally, Ericka has a shameful secret of her own, one that Paulina is determined to use against her.

Throughout most of the play, Tony-winning costume designer Qween Jean drapes the girls in the school’s green, orange and gold-toned uniforms. However, for their audition with Eloise, who comes elegantly dressed in Western fabrics, as if she were Dominique Deveraux, and a practiced accent to match, the girls are transformed in bold, glittering dresses of the era, encapsulating their transition into womanhood. Moreover, the contrast between Paulina and Eloise shows who Paulina might become and the cost of getting there.

“School Girls; or, the African Mean Girls Play” is a joyous and gutting play centering the treasure of Black sisterhood, exceptionalism and the pain and anguish of putting your best foot forward and still falling short of someone much less qualified. It is an ever-timely examination of what it is to be a Black woman or girl in a world that constantly labels you as unworthy. With exceptional performances from the entire cast and homages to musical legends like Whitney Houston and Janet Jackson, Bioh and White present a reflection of the Black female experience in all of its dazzling idiosyncrasies, triumphs and pains.

title: ‘Hirayasumi’ Anime Unveils Footage, Key Visual and Lead Voice Cast Ahead of NHK Debut
summary: New footage from the anime adaptation of Shinzo Keigo’s manga “Hirayasumi” has been unveiled, along with a key visual and the principal voice cast, ahead of the series’ January 2027 premiere on Japan’s NHK General TV. Viz Media and Shogakukan-Shueisha Productions (ShoPro) released the material. International streaming plans have yet to be revealed. Production +h., […]
content:
New footage from the anime adaptation of Shinzo Keigo’s manga “Hirayasumi” has been unveiled, along with a key visual and the principal voice cast, ahead of the series’ January 2027 premiere on Japan’s NHK General TV.

Viz Media and Shogakukan-Shueisha Productions (ShoPro) released the material. International streaming plans have yet to be revealed. Production +h., which made “The Orbital Children” and “Dead Dead Demons Dededede Destruction,” is animating the series.

The teaser trails follows Hiroto, a relaxed 29-year-old part-timer, through his daily routine in the Asagaya neighborhood. It also sketches his close bond with the elderly neighbor he calls Granny and the arrival of his cousin Natsumi, who has come to the capital to study at art school.

Popular on Variety

The key visual places Hiroto and Natsumi in front of the one-story Asagaya house he inherited from Granny. Joining them are Hideki, Hiroto’s closest friend; Akari, who studies alongside Natsumi at university; and Yomogi, a real estate agent from the neighborhood.

Uchida Yuma voices Hiroto. His previous roles include Fushiguro Megumi in “Jujutsu Kaisen,” Ash Lynx in “Banana Fish” and Mikage Reo in “Blue Lock.”

“‘Hirayasumi’ is a wonderful work where human drama unfolds amidst the ordinary moments of everyday life. I hope to have fun portraying Hiroto while staying true to his unpretentious personality and easygoing vibe,” Uchida said.

Takahashi Mayu plays 18-year-old Kobayashi Natsumi, a reserved newcomer from Yamagata who privately hopes to become a manga artist and often clashes with her laid-back cousin. Takahashi finished second in the Kimi Koe Project, a scheme set up to find and train new voice actors, and her earlier credits include “The Legendary Hero Is Dead!” She said that on reading the original manga, she felt she had never identified with a character so strongly, adding: “I’m truly delighted to be involved in this wonderful work that I love so much.”

Veteran performer Aikawa Rikako voices Wada Hanae, the 83-year-old Granny, a pensioner who once served school lunches and starts eating dinner with Hiroto twice a week after a chance meeting. Aikawa’s voice roles span Squirtle in the “Pokémon” franchise, Oxnard in “Hamtaro” and Ishishi from the “Kaiketsu Zorori” series.

“All of the characters are very kind. And yet, deep inside, they carry pain and worries of their own. ‘Hirayasumi’ brings not so much a flutter in the heart, but a catch in the chest, followed by a slow, tender swell of emotion,” Aikawa said.

Suezawa Kei (“Fate/Grand Order: Camelot – Wandering; Agateram,” “FLCL Progressive”) directs and handles series composition and scripts. Asano Naoyuki (“Urusei Yatsura,” “Keep Your Hands Off Eizouken!”) is character designer, Nishimura Mika (“Typhoon Noruda”) is art director and Sawada Kaori (“What Did You Eat Yesterday?,” “When Spring Comes”) composes the music.

Shinzo’s manga began its run in Shogakukan’s “Weekly Big Comic Spirits” in 2021 and now spans 10 volumes, with more than 1.7 million copies in print worldwide. Its honors include best serial comic at Lucca Comics & Games 2024 as well as the 71st Shogakukan Manga Award.

Shinzo made his debut in 2008 with “Nankin.” His 2016 series “Moriyamachu Driving School” became a feature film, and “Tokyo Alien Bros.” received a live-action adaptation in 2018. An autobiographical one-shot about his recovery from lymphoma, which Shinzo created during the COVID-19 pandemic, also inspired “Hirayasumi.”

title: Rob Lowe Says ‘St. Elmo’s Fire’ Sequel Is Still ‘In the Works,’ Confirms There’s a Script: ‘All of Us Actors Want to Do It’
summary: Rob Lowe finally has an update on the long-discussed “St. Elmo’s Fire” sequel. “It is definitely in the works, for sure,” the actor said when asked about the project’s current status during a “Watch What Happens Live” appearance on Sunday. “All of us actors want to do it, and we’re supposed to get a draft […]
content:
Rob Lowe finally has an update on the long-discussed “St. Elmo’s Fire” sequel.

“It is definitely in the works, for sure,” the actor said when asked about the project’s current status during a “Watch What Happens Live” appearance on Sunday. “All of us actors want to do it, and we’re supposed to get a draft of the script the first week of October.”

While Lowe didn’t give much away, the news that the sequel is making progress is the latest update fans of the 1985 classic have been waiting on since the film was first announced in 2024. The “Parks and Recreation” actor told Entertainment Tonight that he’d “met with the studio” and had “been talking about doing it for about four months.” “But it’s very, very, very, very, very early stages,” he added. “So we will see.”

That same year, Lowe’s “St. Elmo’s Fire” co-star Demi Moore said that “conversations are happening” around the sequel and revealed that discussions were underway with Sony, the same studio behind the original film. She also said the studio was “really behind [and] driving this,” though they were still “looking for the right partner” to write it.

Popular on Variety

Variety previously reported that NBC was developing a series adaptation of the film back in 2019, though it never materialized. Josh Berman had been attached to write and executive produce along with Chris King. At the time, the series was described as a modern adaptation of the film that showcases a group of close friends struggling with career, commitment and the responsibilities of adulthood.

Released in 1985, “St. Elmo’s Fire” starred Lowe, Moore, Emilio Estevez, Andrew McCarthy, Ally Sheedy, Judd Nelson and others. Joel Schumacher directed and co-wrote the script with Carl Kurlander.

title: Russo Brothers On The Hulk Appearing On ‘Avengers: Doomsday’: “Certainly Involved In The Story That Revolves Around Doom”
summary: Many questions surround Avengers: Doomsday, and one major one is whether Mark Ruffalo will reprise his role as Bruce Banner. The actor recently appeared in Spider-Man: Brand New Day as Banner, and the Russo Brothers teased that the Hulk is “certainly involved” in the story around Doctor Doom. “I think [what] we could say is, [Banner] is […]
content:
Many questions surround Avengers: Doomsday, and one major one is whether Mark Ruffalo will reprise his role as Bruce Banner.

The actor recently appeared in Spider-Man: Brand New Day as Banner, and the Russo Brothers teased that the Hulk is “certainly involved” in the story around Doctor Doom.

“I think [what] we could say is, [Banner] is certainly involved in the story that revolves around Doom,” Joe Russo told Empire Online. “We will not confirm nor deny his appearance in Doomsday.”

Anthony Russo added, “The farthest we can go is to say, there are characters and actors who have not been announced, who are a part of Doomsday.”

Watch on Deadline

Avengers: Doomsday is set to be released on December 18 as part of Phase 6 of the MCU. The film follows 2019’s Avengers: Endgame, which the Russos also directed.

Avengers: Doomsday will feature different groups of heroes from different universes, including the Avengers, the Wakandans from Black Panther, the Thunderbolts (known as the New Avengers) from Earth-616, the Fantastic Four from Earth-828, and the original X-Men.

RELATED: 15 Movies & Shows To Watch Before ‘Avengers: Doomsday’

In a recent interview, the Russo Brothers said they started filming Avengers: Doomsday without a finished script.

“We’re improvisation-based, rehearsal-based directors,” Joe Russo told AP. “We like to see what the actors bring to the characters, and sometimes you don’t get the actors until a few days or few weeks before you shoot them. And a lot of the time, that’s when the magic happens.”
