title: Netflix Scores Ratings Hit With ‘Wonka’s The Golden Ticket’
summary: Willy Wonka has delivered for Netflix. The streamer has landed a bona fide reality ratings hit with Wonka’s The Golden Ticket after the Charlie and the Chocolate Factory-themed competition series debuted at number two on its English-language TV chart. The series scored 4.6M views in its opening week, becoming one of Netflix’s biggest unscripted launches […]
content:
Willy Wonka has delivered for Netflix.

The streamer has landed a bona fide reality ratings hit with Wonka’s The Golden Ticket after the Charlie and the Chocolate Factory-themed competition series debuted at number two on its English-language TV chart.

The series scored 4.6M views in its opening week, becoming one of Netflix’s biggest unscripted launches in recent years

This is in line with the latest season of Love Is Blind – season ten set in Ohio – which also scored 4.6M in its opening week. The Kinetic Content show is considered one of Netflix’s biggest unscripted hits (its premiere came before Netflix changed the way it calculates viewers).

The numbers bode well for a renewal of the Eureka-produced show. Age of Attraction, Velvet Hammer’s dating reality series that launched earlier this year, premiered with 3.8M viewers in its first week and was handed a quick renewal, although admittedly The Golden Ticket is a more expensive show to produce.

Watch on Deadline

Shot in Australia, the series sees 12 lucky golden ticket winners entering the Chocolate Factory to compete for a sweet prize: a lifetime supply of money. As the winners and their partners step through the factory gates, they face a series of series of challenges. There are games, tests and temptations designed to test the competitors physically, mentally, and morally before one walks away with the prize.

A two-part finale for The Golden Ticket will premiere on September 30.

Wonka’s The Golden Ticket was only bested on the list by Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story, which was number one with 14.5M views in its second week. This comes after it received 12.5M views in its first four days on the service. Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story also ranked in the Top 10 list in 92 countries, up from 89 in its first week.

Crew Girl was at number three with 4.5M views.

Elsewhere, A Different World, the sequel series to the classic sitcom from 1987, debuted at number four with 4.2M views. This was followed by the second season of The Gentlemen, Gabby’s Dollhouse, WWE’s Raw, the first season of The Gentlemen, The Great British Baking Show and Danny Go!.

title: Curry Barker’s Next Movie ‘Anything But Ghosts’ Sets May 2027 Release From Focus Features
summary: Curry Barker fever will continue into next summer as Focus Features and Blumhouse Atomic Monster are releasing the Obsession filmmaker’s next movie, Anything but Ghosts on May 7. That’s similar to the launch date of Obsession, which bowed during the third weekend of May this year (May 15). It opened to $17.1M domestic, but held […]
content:
Curry Barker fever will continue into next summer as Focus Features and Blumhouse Atomic Monster are releasing the Obsession filmmaker’s next movie, Anything but Ghosts on May 7.

That’s similar to the launch date of Obsession, which bowed during the third weekend of May this year (May 15). It opened to $17.1M domestic, but held like a rock, spiking an unprecedented 39% in its second weekend ($23.9M) and another 14% in its third weekend with $27.3M for a final domestic tally of$263.4M and nearly $520M worldwide.

As we first told you, Focus has worldwide rights on Anything but Ghosts, with Universal Pictures International handling international distribution for the studio. Barker co-wrote the movie with his

longtime creative collaborator and Obsession star Cooper Tomlinson. Anything but Ghosts stars Tomlinson and Barker as wannabe “ghosthunters” who find themselves in over their heads as things spiral wildly and terrifyingly out of control. Violet McGraw and Chris Reinacher also star with Bryce Dallas Howard and Aaron Paul. Barker has saidin interviews that the feature takes place in the same universe as Obsession.

RELATED: ‘Game Of Thrones: Aegon’s Conquest’ Movie Gets 2029 Release Date

Already opening on May 7 next year is Lionsgate’s Mel Gibson-directed The Resurrection of the Christ (Part One) — technically that’s going on May 6 — as well as 20th Century Studios’ Patrick Schwarzenegger-Phoebe Dynevor movie Beach Read. Sony kicks off summer 2027 on April 30 with the feature take on Nintendo video game The Legend of Zelda.

The other production companies on Anything but Ghosts are Spooky Pictures, Divide/Conquer, in association with Image Nation and Barker and Tomlinson’s That’s a Bad Idea. EPs are Daniel Bekerman, Barker, Tomlinson and Ben Ross. Producers are Roy Lee, Steven Schneider, Jason Blum, Adam Hendricks and Greg Gilreath.

Focus Features acquired Obsession out of TIFF Midnight Madness 2025 for $15M. The CAA Media-financed movie went onto become Focus’ highest-grossing movie ever in addition to being the highest-grossing movie ever acquired out of a film festival (unseating The Blair Witch Project‘s $248.6M WW gross). Barker’s debut feature, Milk & Serial, first streamed on YouTube to close to 3M views off a production budget of $800. Obsession was made for $750K by Capstone Studios before Focus picked up the title.



Barker mentioned to Deadline at our DGA TIFF panel that on Anything But Ghosts, “The hardest day on Obsession was the easiest day on Anything but Ghosts.”

He added, “We had a 130-page script and we had 26 days to shoot it. I’m also starring in it and directing and I’m the lead character. I have more lines than anyone in the movie.”

“Zach Kregger just told me, ‘You have to cut 30 pages’ and I probably should have listened to him. So, did my manager; he told me that, too.”

“But I didn’t cut a single page because I wanted to shoot all of it,” says Barker who was at TIFF for the one-year anniversary of the Obsession premiere, “It was the hardest thing I’ve ever done and we were compromising shots left and right off the shot list. Gone. Just like coverage was going out the windows. It was crazy.”

title: Former Paramount Exec Dan Cohen Joins Black Bear

content:
Black Bear, the company behind movies such as Train Dreams and Sing Sing, has a new head of television distribution.

The company, founded by Teddy Schwarzman, has hired former Paramount exec Dan Cohen in the role. It comes just over a year after Cohen left the studio ahead of its takeover by David Ellison’s Skydance.

Cohen, who was Chief Content Licensing Officer at Paramount and President of Republic Pictures, will oversee post-theatrical distribution of its movies, which including upcoming titles such as Wicker, Wife & Dog, Jason Statham Stole My Bike and A Woman in the Sun.

Recent deals for the company include Tuner, starring Leo Woodall and Dustin Hoffman, on Paramount+, and Ric Roman Waugh’s Shelter and Guy Ritchie’s In The Grey with Starz.

Watch on Deadline

The company is also launching Black Bear Digital Networks, which will help independent content owners monetize across FAST and AVOD networks. It is working with companies such as Sinclair Networks, Tubi, CJ Enm and The National Wrestling Alliance.

“Dan brings an exceptional combination of licensing expertise, industry relationships, and strategic vision,” said Black Bear CEO Teddy Schwarzman. “His experience will be invaluable on multiple fronts, as we continue to invest in our U.S. distribution business, expanding our reach across the post-theatrical marketplace, and as we open doors for other media entities to connect with audiences across the digital landscape.”

“Black Bear has built an excellent brand over the past 15 years, with a strong track record of championing original stories that connect with both critics and audiences,” added Cohen. “I have immense confidence in what they’re building for the future. There’s a great opportunity to expand the ways Black Bear films reach audiences while also creating new avenues for third-party content owners through Black Bear Digital Networks. I look forward to helping grow both businesses and finding new ways to bring great content to audiences.”

title: Lady A’s Charles Kelley Shares Blood Cancer Diagnosis: ‘I’m Confident That We’re Going to Get Through It’
summary: Charles Kelley, the co-lead vocalist and founding member of the country band Lady A, has been diagnosed with the rare blood cancer multiple myeloma. The singer shared the news on his Instagram on Tuesday, with the caption “A little health update” under the video. “Hey everybody. Just wanted to give a quick update on some […]
content:
Charles Kelley, the co-lead vocalist and founding member of the country band Lady A, has been diagnosed with the rare blood cancer multiple myeloma.

The singer shared the news on his Instagram on Tuesday, with the caption “A little health update” under the video.

“Hey everybody. Just wanted to give a quick update on some health issues I’m dealing with,” Kelley said. “I had [a] couple random rib fractures that happened, which sparked my doctor into having me do several different blood tests. And one of the last blood tests we did, they found a blood cancer in there called multiple myeloma, and it’s rare.”

“I’m young, I feel healthy, and the treatments I will say have just come so far, even in the past five years,” he continued. “Even life expectancy just far exceeds what it used to be and, I don’t know, I feel really hopeful. I really do.”

Popular on Variety

Kelley likened sharing the news of his health with his sobriety journey: “Just getting this stuff off your chest is so freeing, and it takes the power away from it a little bit that we want to let y’all know what was going on. But we’re going to get through it. You know, I think in sobriety it’s all about one day at a time and that we’re not in control, and so that’s the way we’re looking at it.”

Kelley has been outspoken about his struggles with alcohol, and in 2022, the band — formerly known as Lady Antebellum — shared that they would be postponing the remainder of their “Request Line Tour” in support of Charles Kelley’s “journey to sobriety.”

The singer concluded the video by sharing that he is “hopeful” and will “try” to let fans in throughout the journey. “It’s just another hurdle, and you know, I’m confident that we’re going to get through it.”

From Dec. 10 through 21, the group will perform a run of Christmas shows as part of the “This Winter’s Night” tour.

title: Casey Bloys Poised to Run HBO and Paramount+ as Cindy Holland Confirms Her Exit From Studio on Eve of Merger Closing
summary: HBO chief Casey Bloys is poised to take the reins of all of Paramount and Warner Bros. streaming operations once the two companies merge. On Tuesday, Cindy Holland announced she was stepping down from her role running Paramount+ and other direct to consumer streamers under the Paramount umbrella. The shuffle comes as Paramount Skydance is […]
content:
HBO chief Casey Bloys is poised to take the reins of all of Paramount and Warner Bros. streaming operations once the two companies merge. On Tuesday, Cindy Holland announced she was stepping down from her role running Paramount+ and other direct to consumer streamers under the Paramount umbrella.

The shuffle comes as Paramount Skydance is days away from closing its hard-won $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery.

Holland confirmed her departure in a memo to staff sent Tuesday afternoon, acknowledging that Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison has made the decision regarding streaming leadership, although she did not reference Bloys by name.

Popular on Variety

“As David readies for the next phase of his vision, we’ve discussed my role and the future of the combined businesses. David is optimizing for HBO stability as we move into this next chapter, and I fully support that. I know this team has the leadership and expertise to manage through the transition and the next phase of the company, and to this end today will mark my last day here,” Holland wrote.

Over the past few weeks, speculation emerged that Bloys was likely to come over post merger in the top role overseeing all streaming operations. Bloys is a near 25-year veteran of HBO who has steered TV’s most prestigious brand through choppy waters and three massive corporate takeovers in eight years. There’s also speculation that JB Perrette, who now heads streaming business operations and gaming for WBD, will join Bloys in steering HBO, HBO Max and Paramount+.

Holland was part of the pioneering team that built Netflix into the world’s biggest subscription streaming platform. Her 18-year run at that streamer included nine years as Vice President of Original Content. Holland established the network’s original programming strategy and oversaw the teams behind flagship hits like “House of Cards,” “Stranger Things,” “The Crown,” “Icarus,” “When They See Us” and “The Queen’s Gambit.” Between Netflix and Paramount, Holland served as CEO of Sister — the production company formed by Elizabeth Murdoch. Her exit comes as the industry speculates wildly about the fate of other division leaders across both companies.

Here is Holland’s full memo:

When I joined David’s team in January 2025, we proceeded to set three goals: i) advise on the Warner Bros. Discovery acquisition, ii) integrate and transform Paramount+ & revive Pluto TV, and iii) build an unparalleled team in this industry. In just over 12 months, I’m proud to say we accomplished all three and it’s been a joy to work closely with all of you.

Together with the Product team, we drove significant strategic and organizational change across DTC — building a new foundation for growth on both services, while investing in greater depth and breadth of programming and delivering strong revenue, profit, and subscriber growth for the division.

As David readies for the next phase of his vision, we’ve discussed my role and the future of the combined businesses. David is optimizing for HBO stability as we move into this next chapter, and I fully support that. I know this team has the leadership and expertise to manage through the transition and the next phase of the company, and to this end today will mark my last day here.

As I reflect on my time here and all that we’ve built together in this short time, what stands out most to me is this team. I have never been more proud of a group of people. What we’ve accomplished together is remarkable — landing quarter after quarter while navigating extraordinary uncertainty and change with resilience, focus and ambition. We grew Paramount+ to an all-time subscriber high, delivered the best retention in the service’s history, and drove double-digit growth in both engagement and revenue. We built an extraordinary content pipeline, greenlighting more than 40 new and returning series and setting all-time records with Landman, the most-watched series in Paramount+ history, and Dutton Ranch, the service’s biggest original series debut ever. We transformed live sports into a powerful streaming growth engine, securing landmark agreements with UFC and Zuffa Boxing and expanding our WNBA and UEFA Champions League rights – with UFC Freedom 250 becoming the largest-ever audience for an exclusive live event on Paramount+ and UFC 329 setting a new platform record for peak concurrent streams for an exclusive live event. And we undertook Pluto TV’s biggest product transformation in a decade, dramatically increasing registered viewing and VOD consumption while delivering strong financial performance across the business. These are extraordinary accomplishments – but what makes me proudest is how we achieved them: together, with an unwavering commitment to our audiences, our creative partners and one another.

I joined Paramount because I believe in these businesses, and because I believe wholeheartedly that the combination of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery serves the best interests of artists and audiences worldwide. I’m looking forward to seeing what you all accomplish together in this next, momentous chapter.

title: Penn Badgley Swore Off Sex Scenes. His Wife Says It Was Not Her Idea: ‘He Decided to Do This for Mental Health Reasons’
summary: Penn Badgley infamously swore off sex scenes before the production of “You” Season 4, revealing on a viral episode of his “Podcrushed” podcast in Feb. 2013 that he told showrunner Sera Gamble he was no longer interested in filming intimate scenes on camera. The actor then told Variety later that same month that “it’s important […]
content:
Penn Badgley infamously swore off sex scenes before the production of “You” Season 4, revealing on a viral episode of his “Podcrushed” podcast in Feb. 2013 that he told showrunner Sera Gamble he was no longer interested in filming intimate scenes on camera. The actor then told Variety later that same month that “it’s important to me in my real life to not have” sex scenes, clarifying: “My fidelity in my relationship. It’s important to me.”

Cut to more than three years later and Badgley’s wife, Domino Kirke-Badgley, is speaking out after spending all this time being accused online of blocking her husband from doing sex scenes. When Badgley cited his marriage as a reason he did not want to act in sex scenes anymore, social media was quick to come for Kirke-Badgley, even though Penn had cited her as the reason he even accepted the lusty lead role in “You” in the first place.

Popular on Variety

“A few years ago, the internet decided I’d asked my husband to stop doing sex scenes. The truth is, my husband decided to do this for mental health reasons,” Kirke-Badgley wrote on Instagram. “After working in the industry since he was just 12 years old, believe me, it was time. In the entertainment world, they call actors ‘puppets’ behind their backs, and it’s even more disturbing when they start out as child actors… after years of trying, Penn decided to take a stand and let the world see him. And guess what, he hasn’t lost fans and he’s still getting hired!”

“The characters that my husband has played over the years, people have come to expect that he will continue to play that guy,” she added in the video post. “I was super happy for him and very proud of him because I understood how major it was, and yeah … it’s just relational hygiene.”

Badgley has been married since 2017 to Kirke-Badgley, who “encouraged” him to play Joe on “You” even though the part required him to film various sex scenes.

“There’s almost nothing I could say with more consecration. That aspect of Hollywood has always been very disturbing to me — and that aspect of the job, that mercurial boundary — has always been something that I actually don’t want to play with at all,” Badgely told Variety in 2023. “I told [Sara Gamble before Season 4] kind of my desire, and she immediately was accepting and responsive. I’m always very practical. I said I know it can’t be none, because there’s something coded into the DNA of the show, and I signed the contract, and so it is what it is but as little as possible would be my preference.”

There were fewer sex scenes in “You” Season 4, and all of them were performed fully clothed as a result of Badgley speaking up. The actor’s initial comments earned a polarizing response online, with his detractors criticizing him for equating sex scenes with real sex. Many of Badgley’s critics pointed out that intimacy coordinators are now a staple in Hollywood so that sex scenes remain safe during filming. He later told GQ magazine that his comments got “blown out of proportion.”

“What I was speaking about wasn’t actually the final product,” Badgley said. “It was sort of like the culture inherent to the production of all movies, but particularly those scenes. It’s like, look, we know that Hollywood has had a history of flagrant exploitation and abuse.”

Badgley said he was “nervous to even have that conversation” with “You” showrunner Sera Gamble, adding, “It was not easy. It was easy because of Sera’s response, and I felt relieved. But technically speaking, if I thought I’d had the ability to set that boundary earlier, I would have. We shall see if setting that boundary, of course, has any ramifications. Just simply, it does limit the number of projects you can be a part of.”

Next up for Badgley is the romantic comedy “You Deserve Each Other,” co-starring Meghann Fahy.

title: Everything We Know About Netflix’s ‘Icebreaker’ Adaptation So Far
summary: Another hockey book adaptation has entered the chat. Netflix is currently building out its cast for the series adaptation of Hannah Grace’s Icebreaker book that kicks off the Maple Hill series. This in addition to their show The Sticks that is also currently in the works. For everything we know about Netflix’s Icebreaker book adaptation […]
content:
Another hockey book adaptation has entered the chat.

Netflix is currently building out its cast for the series adaptation of Hannah Grace’s Icebreaker book that kicks off the Maple Hill series. This in addition to their show The Sticks that is also currently in the works.

For everything we know about Netflix’s Icebreaker book adaptation so far, read on.

When will Netflix’s Icebreaker series adaptation come out?

A release date has not yet been set. The show has begun to assemble its cast.

Watch on Deadline

Who will lead the Icebreaker show at Netflix?

Daisy Jelley (Poser, How To Have Sex) will portray Anastasia “Stassie” Allen, and Connor Simos (Subversion) will portray Nate Hawkins in the college hockey drama series.

Who else is in the cast of Netflix’s Icebreaker adaptation?

Gabriel Tierney (Rivals, Enola Holmes 2), Auliʻi Cravalho (Moana), newcomer and professional athlete Peter Berry, Chaneil Kular (Best of the Best, Sex Education), Devin Craig (Sex Lives of College Girls, Maize) and Aidan Shaw (We Were Liars, Heated Rivalry, Finding Her Edge) have joined the ensemble cast.

Tierney will play Aaron; Cravalho will portray Lola; Berry is Robbie; Kular will play JJ; Craig will portray Henry and Shaw is Russ.

What is Hannah Grace’s Icebreaker book about?

Stassie is a transfer athlete gunning for Olympic gold. Nate is the campus star chasing the NHL. When an accident forces their teams to share one rink, Anastasia Allen and Nate Hawkins collide—and discipline gives way to obsession, because the only thing more dangerous than wanting to win is wanting each other.

Who else is behind Netflix’s Icebreaker series?

Jade Halley Bartlett (Road House, Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness, Miller’s Girl) created and executive produced the series. Amanda Lasher (Gossip Girl, The Bold Type, Togetherness) serves as showrunner, writer and excutive producer. Grace also executive produces along with Alex Cooper, Matt Kaplan and Mina Lefevre for Cooper’s Unwell Productions.

title: Cindy Holland Leaving Paramount Ahead Of WBD Merger
summary: One of the biggest executive suite questions about Paramount following its pending acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery — who will lead streaming — may have been answered. Cindy Holland is leaving Paramount Skydance where she was Chair of Direct-To-Consumer having previously served as an advisor to Skydance CEO David Ellison. Her last day is today. […]
content:
One of the biggest executive suite questions about Paramount following its pending acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery — who will lead streaming — may have been answered.

Cindy Holland is leaving Paramount Skydance where she was Chair of Direct-To-Consumer having previously served as an advisor to Skydance CEO David Ellison. Her last day is today. Holland announced her departure in a company memo, which you can read below.

The move leaves Casey Bloys, Chairman and CEO of HBO and HBO Max Content, as the likely streaming head of the combined Paramount-WBD. Holland hinted at that in her email to staff, indicating that she and Ellison had discussed his plan for the leadership of the combined HBO Max and Paramount+ streamer and he would be going for “optimizing for HBO stability” [aka Bloys], something Holland supported.

Since Ellison announced earlier this year that HBO Max and Paramount+ will merge into one streaming platform after Paramount’s acquisition of WBD, it has become clear that the move would come down to a choice between Holland and Bloys for who would lead the combined streaming operation as both are accomplished top-level streaming executives, neither of whom would report to the other.

Watch on Deadline

“As David readies for the next phase of his vision, we’ve discussed my role and the future of the combined businesses. David is optimizing for HBO stability as we move into this next chapter, and I fully support that,” Holland wrote. “I know this team has the leadership and expertise to manage through the transition and the next phase of the company, and to this end today will mark my last day here.”

Holland, who was behind Netflix’s foray into original programming, was initially recruited by Ellison as an advisor in January 2025 to help draft the post-Paramount merger streaming strategy before she took the rains of the operation as Chair of Direct-to-Consumer of Paramount Skydance in August 2025, overseeing Paramount+ and Pluto.

“Cindy is one of the most exceptional executives in our industry — a force of nature whose impact on Paramount over the past year has been significant,” Paramount CEO Ellison said. “Under her leadership, P+ reached new heights, Pluto TV underwent its most significant transformation in a decade, and we strengthened our content and sports portfolio – all while the business exceeded the ambitious goals we set. Just as importantly, she built an exceptional team and a strong foundation for the future. Cindy has been a trusted partner to me and so many others, and I couldn’t be more grateful for her leadership, her relentless drive and everything she’s done for our company.”

Holland’s departure raises questions about the future of her top executives post-merger, some of whom have been longtime close collaborators of hers, led by Paramount+ Head of Originals Jane Wiseman, who worked for Holland at Netflix and Sister before joining her at Paramount.

The two put together Paramount+’s programming strategy, which includes expanding the slate, dominated by Taylor Sheridan dramas into “female forward dramas” with a string of series orders, starting with Discretion, starring Nicole Kidman, which recently began production.

Bloys had indicated that he would like to keep his senior HBO team intact after parent WBD is acquired by Paramount.

In her note, Holland reflected on some of her accomplishments over the past 13 months.

“We grew Paramount+ to an all-time subscriber high, delivered the best retention in the service’s history, and drove double-digit growth in both engagement and revenue,” she said. “We built an extraordinary content pipeline, greenlighting more than 40 new and returning series and setting all-time records with Landman, the most-watched series in Paramount+ history, and Dutton Ranch, the service’s biggest original series debut ever.”

During her tenure, Sheridan, who is behind Paramount+’s biggest hits, including Landman, Dutton Ranch, Lioness and Tulsa King, announced that he would be moving to NBCUniversal in January 2029. Meanwhile, Holland played a key role in attracting Stranger Things creators the Duffer Brothers, whose show she had championed at Netflix, for a big film and TV overall deal at Paramount.

Holland’s memo indicates that WBD may have been a target for Ellison months before he made the first unsolicited offer for the company in September 2025 while his Skydance Media was still going through regulatory approval on its Paramount acquisition.

“When I joined David’s team in January 2025, we proceeded to set three goals: i) advise on the Warner Bros. Discovery acquisition, ii) integrate and transform Paramount+ & revive Pluto TV, and iii) build an unparalleled team in this industry,” Holland said. “In just over 12 months, I’m proud to say we accomplished all three and it’s been a joy to work closely with all of you.”

He also gave the WBD merger her full endorcement.

“I joined Paramount because I believe in these businesses, and because I believe wholeheartedly that the combination of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery serves the best interests of artists and audiences worldwide,” Holland said. “I’m looking forward to seeing what you all accomplish together in this next, momentous chapter.”

During her nearly two decades at Netflix, including nine years as VP Original Content, Holland established the streamer’s original programing strategy and spearheaded the crop of scripted series that put the streamer on the map, including House of Cards, Orange Is the New Black, BoJack Horseman, The Crown and The Queen’s Gambit.

Since her departure from the streamer in September 2020, Holland had taken on board and advisory roles before returning to the executive ranks as Global CEO of Elisabeth Murdoch and Jane Featherstone‘s Sister in 2023. She spent 15 months in the role before taking the Senior Advisor position at Skydance.

title: New ‘South Park’ Takes On Data Centers And The Billionaires Who Build Them
summary: While President Trump was holding a press conference at the White House this morning and extolling the AI-related work of Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, Anthropic’s Dario Amodei and SpaceX’s Elon Musk, a promo for tomorrow night’s South Park episode dropped. It was less salutary. Here’s the logline for Episode 6 of Season […]
content:
While President Trump was holding a press conference at the White House this morning and extolling the AI-related work of Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, Anthropic’s Dario Amodei and SpaceX’s Elon Musk, a promo for tomorrow night’s South Park episode dropped. It was less salutary.

Here’s the logline for Episode 6 of Season 29: “Butters is unhappy with the data centers that the billionaires are building in our backyards.”

The clip opens with an X-Pest exterminator guy ringing the doorbell at Butters’ home.

Watch on Deadline

“I understand you’ve got some billionaires in your back yard,” he says.

“Yeah, there’s more of these stupid billionaires every day!” replies Butters.

The first image from the episode (see it above) shows Butters in what appears to be his back yard with the X-Pest exterminator guy, who has strapped on his tank of poison and has his sprayer wand at the ready.

The topic of data centers is a hot one across the country and especially in Hollywood, where unions and workers worry about job displacement and writers and directors express concern over what it might do to their art.

Among the biggest players in the data center land rush is, of course, Oracle CEO and Paramount-WBD deal financier Larry Ellison. South Park airs on Comedy Central, which is owned by Paramount. As in the past, the show’s creators are seemingly not afraid to bite the hand that feeds them.

Mark Ruffalo and others have decried the introduction of “really profoundly scary technology” into Hollywood and how AI might impact media outlets soon to be owned by Ellison and his son David.

“Larry is a classic Oligarch,” wrote Ruffalo. “They are crushing workers and consolidating the wealth of the world for their own power and concentrated dominance.”

Paramount, for its part, responded by accusing Ruffalo of using “antisemitic tropes” in his argument, especially when linking the Ellisons’ studio acquisition to Oracle’s work with the Israeli military.

title: ‘Vanderpump Rules: Lisa Las Vegas’ Trailer & Episode Release Guide Schedule Set At Bravo
summary: Lisa Vanderpump is taking Bravo viewers behind the scenes of the opening of her hotel in Sin City with Vanderpump Rules: Lisa Las Vegas, set to premiere at 9 p.m. Tuesday, October 20. Set to air over two nights, the three-part event will feature fan favorites joining the celebration, with cameos from Lala Kent, Tom Schwart and […]
content:
Lisa Vanderpump is taking Bravo viewers behind the scenes of the opening of her hotel in Sin City with Vanderpump Rules: Lisa Las Vegas, set to premiere at 9 p.m. Tuesday, October 20.

Set to air over two nights, the three-part event will feature fan favorites joining the celebration, with cameos from Lala Kent, Tom Schwart and Real Housewives of Beverly Hills alum Garcelle Beauvais.

Vanderpump teamed up with Caesars Entertainment and is betting big on her most ambitious Vegas venture yet: a namesake hotel. This isn’t just another grand opening; it’s Lisa’s biggest gamble to date and a chance to cement her legacy. With a to-do list longer than the Strip itself, LVP and her A-team pull back the curtain on what it really takes to get a boutique resort ready for its lavish opening – and VIP check-in – Vanderpump style.

Lisa is joined by her husband Ken Todd, daughter Pandora Vanderpump Sabo, longtime business partner Nick Alain and a trusted team of collaborators. Longtime friend Kevin Lee also is back in Lisa’s orbit after a stint working with one of her rivals.

Watch on Deadline

The down-to-the-wire drama wouldn’t be complete without some SURvers lending a helping hand. Natalie Maguire, Venus Binkley, Chris Hahn, Angelica Jensen, Marcus Johnson and Audrey Lingle take a road trip in support of Lisa.

Vanderpump Rules: Lisa Las Vegas is produced by 32 Flavors, a part of Sony Pictures Television and Evolution Media, an MGM Company. Alex Baskin, Michael Beck, Natalie Neurauter, Brian McCarthy, Brittany Nabors, Barry Poznick, Lisa Vanderpump and Ken Todd executive produce.

Here is the episode release schedule and loglines:

“Part 1: Vegas? That’s Epic, Baby!”

Tuesday, Oct. 20 at 9 p.m. ET/PT

Lisa Vanderpump gets the chance to open up her very own hotel on the Las Vegas Strip, but she and her team feel the pressure as they attempt to check everything off their never-ending to-do list. Walking into the space, everything feels like a construction site and Lisa fears those around her have a lack of urgency. Also on the agenda? Making up with a former friend and reminding her SURvers that photoshoots are work, not play.

“Part 2: If It Was Easy, Everyone Would Do It”

Tuesday, Oct. 20 at 10 p.m. ET/PT

With time running out, Lisa and her team rush to put the finishing touches on the hotel. Guests begin to check in before all the rooms are ready and late deliveries, holes in the ceiling, and complaining guests threaten to derail the opening. At home, Lisa opens up about how her childhood affected her drive to succeed.

“Part 3: Misbehave Accordingly”

Wednesday, Oct. 21 at 9 p.m. ET/PT

Lisa Vanderpump has opened 39 restaurants and now finally, her very own hotel. With celebrity guests arriving in droves to celebrate the grand opening party, excitement is at an all-time high, but so are the expectations. Lisa only gets one chance to make a lasting first impression and the pressure is on for The Vanderpump Hotel to keep the momentum going long after the party ends.

title: Doc Talk Podcast Hits Road With Makers Of ‘Union Town’, ‘Black Sunflowers‘, ‘Edward Said: Between Worlds’ & Camden Film Festival Leaders
summary: September brought a rash of film festivals (well, maybe “rash” is the wrong word; that sounds like a skin condition. How about a “slew” instead?). In any case, it was one film festival after another this month, beginning with Venice, continuing with Telluride, then Toronto, and for documentary lovers, the Camden International Film Festival in […]
content:
September brought a rash of film festivals (well, maybe “rash” is the wrong word; that sounds like a skin condition. How about a “slew” instead?). In any case, it was one film festival after another this month, beginning with Venice, continuing with Telluride, then Toronto, and for documentary lovers, the Camden International Film Festival in Maine.

Deadline’s Doc Talk podcast team packed up the recording equipment and headed into the field to report from the North American fests. On the latest edition of the show, we bring you a selection of our interviews, including with two-time Oscar-winning filmmaker Barbara Kopple, director of Union Town. She premiered that film in Venice, then hopped the pond for Toronto before heading to Camden for her U.S. premiere. Kopple tells us why stories about working-class Americans have fascinated her going back to the landmark Harlan County U.S.A. 50 years ago.

Director James Marcus Haney tells us about his film Black Sunflowers, executive produced by Sean Penn, which premiered at TIFF. We also speak with two of his protagonists, young Ukrainian women whose lives have been dramatically impacted by Russia’s war of aggression on their country. The documentary explores how many young Ukrainians feel compelled, in the absence of a secure future, to seek out adrenaline-fueled experiences like street racing and wild ragers.

Watch on Deadline

Another documentary hosting its world premiere in Toronto is Edward Said: Between Worlds, an examination of the titular Palestinian scholar and activist who became a leading advocate for the Palestinian cause from his base in academia in the U.S. Director Maiken Baird, producer Sarah Mowaswes and consulting producer Najla Said (Said’s daughter) join us to reflect on a man who advocated late in his life for a one-state solution, that is, a model for Israelis and Palestinians to live in peace in a secular democracy.

RELATED: ‘Edward Said: Between Worlds’ Documents Man Who Advocated For Palestinian Cause, Foresaw Way To Resolve Israeli Palestinian Conflict – Toronto Studio

In Camden, we also got to speak with the leaders of that festival: Points North Institute executive director Elise McCave and PNI’s artistic director Sean Flynn (PNI is the nonprofit that puts on CIFF). They address the challenges facing the documentary field, which have intensified with the loss of funding for public media under the second Trump administration. They also share their reaction to the success of To Hold a Mountain, the Sundance-winning documentary that gained critical support through the Points North Institute’s Dianne Weyermann Fellowship, named for the late Participant Media executive and champion of independent documentaries.

RELATED: ‘Always,’ ‘Evidence’ Among Big Winners At 21st Camden International Film Festival

That’s on the new episode of Doc Talk hosted by Oscar winner John Ridley (12 Years a Slave, Shirley) and Matt Carey, Deadline’s senior documentary editor. The pod is a production of Deadline and Ridley’s Nō Studios.

title: Florence Pugh Credits Tom Holland for ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Role: ‘This All Happened Because of Tom’
summary: Florence Pugh appeared on The Tonight Show with Jimmy Fallon Monday night and revealed that fans of her Marvel character, Yelena Belova, really have Tom Holland to thank for her appearance in “Spider-Man: Brand New Day.” “This all happened because of Tom,” said Pugh. “Years ago, when I just started my relationship with Marvel and […]
content:
Florence Pugh appeared on The Tonight Show with Jimmy Fallon Monday night and revealed that fans of her Marvel character, Yelena Belova, really have Tom Holland to thank for her appearance in “Spider-Man: Brand New Day.”

“This all happened because of Tom,” said Pugh. “Years ago, when I just started my relationship with Marvel and ‘Black Widow’ came out, my Yelena wasn’t as obviously big as all of the other big superheroes. He, on the red carpet of his previous movie, when someone said, ‘Who do you want to be in the next movie with?… And he said, ‘No, actually, I want to do it with Florence Pugh, who plays Yelena.’ So because of that, fans were then so excited about the idea of it.”

Pugh has played the character of Yelena since 2021 when she appeared in “Black Widow,” and has since reprised the role for 2025’s “Thunderbolts*” and 2026’s “Spider-Man: Brand New Day.” Within the MCU, Yelena is known as an assassin and the successor to the Black Widow title.

Popular on Variety

“Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” which premiered on July 31, has grossed $2.49 billion at the domestic box office, making it the third highest-grossing movie of all time. It ranks behind 2009’s “Avatar” ($2.92 billion) and 2019’s “Avengers: Endgame” ($2.88 billion). “Well done, Spidey!” said Pugh of the accomplishment.

Scheduled to release in theaters on Dec. 18, Pugh is also set to start as Princess Irulan Corrino once again in “Dune: Part Three” from director Denis Villeneuve. That same day, theatergoers will once again get to see her reprise her role as Yelena in the highly anticipated “Avengers: Doomsday,” the Anthony and Joe Russo-directed follow-up to 2019’s “Avengers: Endgame.”

Watch the full segment here.

title: Aaron Sorkin Says ‘Social Reckoning’ Reshoots Had Nothing to Do With Trailer Backlash, Explains Why Trump Isn’t Named: It’s ‘Not a Red-Blue Thing’
summary: Ahead of the release of “The Social Reckoning” on Oct. 9, director Aaron Sorkin is telling all on the film’s much-discussed reshoots, limited test screenings and why Trump is never named explicitly, despite the January 6 riot playing a part in the plot. In a recent interview with Vanity Fair, Sorkin explained that the reshoots, […]
content:
Ahead of the release of “The Social Reckoning” on Oct. 9, director Aaron Sorkin is telling all on the film’s much-discussed reshoots, limited test screenings and why Trump is never named explicitly, despite the January 6 riot playing a part in the plot.

In a recent interview with Vanity Fair, Sorkin explained that the reshoots, which took place after the trailer was released, had nothing to do with the initial mixed reactions and were simply to “make it better.” “We weren’t correcting anything,” he said. “There are two kinds of reshoots: one is the ‘Oh, we’re in trouble. We need to reshoot this.’ And that usually happens on $150 million superhero movies. The other kinds of reshoots are ‘Oh, we really like this movie. It’s good. Let’s make it better.’”

He explained that Sony Pictures chairman and CEO Tom Rothman asked if there was anything he’d want to reshoot, if given the option. “Yeah, I would go back and rewrite and reshoot the whole thing,” said Sorkin, before clarifying that there were only two scenes he felt he could add something to. “And so he opened the checkbook and gave us three days of shooting.”

Popular on Variety

A follow-up to 2010’s “The Social Network,” “The Social Reckoning” follows former Facebook engineer and whistleblower Frances Haugen (Mikey Madison) and Wall Street Journal reporter Jeff Horwitz ( Jeremy Allen White) as they expose the inner workings of Facebook. Their work culminated in “The Facebook Files,” a 2021 investigative series revealing Facebook’s harmful effects on teens and its role in spreading misinformation, including content linked to political violence.

However, despite the relevance of politics to the real-life events the film is based on and its recreation of Jan. 6, Trump is not mentioned by name in “The Social Reckoning,” a decision Sorkin stands by.

“I want to be clear: I was never asked to do that, to not mention Trump by name,” he said. “I turned in the script and a day or two later met with Tom Rothman, who was full speed ahead on it. And I promised him, unprovoked, that we would not see any Trump signage, no ‘Make America Great Again.’ The movie is about Facebook’s role and the rise of divisiveness, extremism, and hyper-partisanship in the country. It is not a red-blue thing, even though, obviously, it will be felt that way.”

Sorkin also revealed that a scene in which one of Facebook’s senior officials says, “I don’t know what that bitch thinks she’s doing,” had to be rewritten to remove the expletive, per the outside legal firm hired by Sony’s. “The lawyer said, ‘Unless you can show me that at one point a senior Facebook executive referred to an ex-employee as a bitch, you can’t do that.’ So it was that.”

On the subject of test screenings, Sorkin said that the studio “had a real concern for secrecy,” which meant the test screenings were each “70 people on the studio lot, all of them Sony employees.” “It is not a great polling sample,” he added.

title: Fiona Lowe, Daughter of Chad Lowe and Kim Painter, Dies at 13
summary: Fiona Hepler Lowe, the daughter of actor Chad Lowe and Kim Painter, has died. She was 13. Fiona’s death was confirmed to People on Tuesday by the Lowe family, who wrote “We are deeply heartbroken by the loss of our beloved Fiona” in a statement. Fiona was described by her family as “a loving young […]
content:
Fiona Hepler Lowe, the daughter of actor Chad Lowe and Kim Painter, has died. She was 13.

Fiona’s death was confirmed to People on Tuesday by the Lowe family, who wrote “We are deeply heartbroken by the loss of our beloved Fiona” in a statement. Fiona was described by her family as “a loving young girl who was smart, creative, and loved to dance.” “She was adored by her sisters and she was deeply loved by her parents,” they wrote. “In fact, she was the light of our lives.”

“Her passing is devastating for our entire family, and we ask for prayers and privacy at this time. If you or someone you know is struggling with mental health, please reach out to the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline by calling or texting 988,” the statement concluded.

Popular on Variety

Fiona was born on Nov. 16, 2012, to Chad and Kim, and was the second daughter in the family. Mabel Painter, 17, was born in 2009, and Nixie Barbara, 10, was born in 2016. Her middle name, Hepler, was Lowe’s late mother’s maiden name and is his brother Rob Lowe’s middle name, per People. Lowe and Painter got married in 2019.

Chad has appeared on shows including “Pretty Little Liars” and “Supergirl,” among others. He won an Emmy for playing Jesse McKenna on “Life Goes On.” Rob is best known for roles across film and television, including “The Outsiders,” “St. Elmo’s Fire,” “Parks and Recreation” and more.

Fiona is survived by her father, Chad, her mother, Kim and her sisters, Mabel and Nixie.

If you or anyone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please call the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline by dialing 988 or go to SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources.

title: ‘Final Payment,’ ‘Zoom In, Zoom Out’ Win Big at Pingyao; ‘Congo Boy’ Takes Rossellini Prize
summary: Niu Niu’s “Final Payment” and Dong Jie’s “Zoom In, Zoom Out” each won two prizes at the 10th Pingyao Crouching Tiger Hidden Dragon International Film Festival in China. “Final Payment,” from Shanxi-born Niu, won the Fei Mu Award for best film, along with best actor for Niu’s father, Niu Jianrong. “Zoom In, Zoom Out” took […]
content:
Niu Niu’s “Final Payment” and Dong Jie’s “Zoom In, Zoom Out” each won two prizes at the 10th Pingyao Crouching Tiger Hidden Dragon International Film Festival in China.

“Final Payment,” from Shanxi-born Niu, won the Fei Mu Award for best film, along with best actor for Niu’s father, Niu Jianrong. “Zoom In, Zoom Out” took the Fei Mu jury award and the Cinephilia Critics’ Award.

The best film prize carries RMB1 million ($149,000), split equally between the director, for the development of their next film, and the film’s China distributor.

“Tearing through a very small rip, the film leads us into a reality and emotional landscape so expansive, where we sigh, lament, and reflect. The director’s approach is concise, unpretentious, and masterful, earning the wholehearted recognition of the entire jury,” the jury said.

Popular on Variety

The film follows a homeowner locked in a standoff with his contractor over the last payment for a renovation, a dispute drawn from Niu Jianrong’s own experience.

Niu Jianrong, an experienced TV and film director, made his debut as a lead actor in the film. Along with best actress winner Sun Yi, he received a Louis Vuitton accessories box engraved with the festival logo.

“You jury’s bold for giving me this award,” Niu Jianrong said on stage. “It was such torture, my director-son trained me really hard. In real life, I’m my son’s father; but in front of the camera, he’s my father.”

Accepting the jury award, Dong said the team approached the film “with absolute purity of intent, which allows me to fully and unreservedly embrace the joy of making it. It’s the joy of conquering something immensely difficult alongside dear friends, the joy of connecting with audiences after the premiere, and, above all, the joy of simply being here, in this very moment.”

Xu Zao won the Unitree best director award for his debut animated feature “Light Pillar,” which carries RMB200,000 ($29,800) toward his next film. The jury cited his “strong aesthetic awareness” and “astute yet warm approach,” which “encourages everyone to hold up the beacon and keep moving forward even on a cold night.”

Sun won best actress for Wang Xiaozhen’s “A Joke.” The jury said she “delivers a delicate performance with restraint, portraying the regret and growth within an intimate relationship.”

The Fei Mu jury also gave a special mention to Cai Chengjie’s “Suzhou Quartet,” produced by Huang Bo, “for its bravery, for its belief that the movie screen is still vast and open to new adventures and new forms of storytelling.”

In the Crouching Tigers international competition, Rafiki Fariala’s “Congo Boy” won the Roberto Rossellini Award for best film and $20,000, split between the director’s next film and the film’s China distributor. The jury cited its “simple style that echoes the great tradition of neorealism.” Fariala, who was not in Pingyao, sent a video thanking the festival and closed it by singing a folk song.

Rafael Manuel won best director and $10,000 for “Filipiñana,” which Jia Zhangke executive produced and Unknown Pleasures acquired for Greater China.

Lenti Liang’s “Our Secrets” won the Fei Mu best short film award and RMB50,000 ($7,450), sponsored by Nowness of Meta Media. On stage, Liang said the film drew on her own childhood trauma, and that after her mother saw it in Pingyao, the two talked it through and she had made peace with it.

Wang Wenting’s “Black Goat” won the Unitree best student short film award in the Pingyao Corner section, with RMB30,000 ($4,470) and a Unitree robot dog.

Earlier in the festival, Ann Hui received the Crouching Tiger Hidden Dragon East-West Award. Pingyao also honored Marco Müller and Han Sanping with the International Contribution to Chinese Cinema Award, and producer Tang Yan, founder of Hello Group, which owns social app Momo, with the 10th Anniversary Award.

The full list of winners:

Fei Mu Awards – Hidden Dragons

Best Film: “Final Payment,” dir. Niu Niu

Unitree Best Director: Xu Zao, “Light Pillar”

Best Actress: Sun Yi, “A Joke,” dir. Wang Xiaozhen

Best Actor: Niu Jianrong, “Final Payment,” dir. Niu Niu

Jury Award: “Zoom In, Zoom Out,” dir. Dong Jie

Special Mention: “Suzhou Quartet,” dir. Cai Chengjie

Best Short Film: “Our Secrets,” dir. Lenti Liang

Best Short Film Special Mention: “If a Walnut Falls,” dir. Liu Bohao

Roberto Rossellini Awards – Crouching Tigers

Best Film: “Congo Boy,” dir. Rafiki Fariala

Best Director: Rafael Manuel, “Filipiñana”

Jury Award: “Ben’imana,” dir. Marie-Clémentine Dusabejambo

Special Mention: “Yesterday the Eye Didn’t Sleep,” dir. Rakan Mayasi

Pingyao Corner

Unitree Best Student Short Film: “Black Goat,” dir. Wang Wenting

Special Mentions: “Rainforest,” dir. Justine Moo; “Whose Home,” dir. Huang Duojia

Youth Jury Award: “Whispers in May,” dir. Chen Dongnan

Netpac Award – Best First Film: “Yesterday the Eye Didn’t Sleep,” dir. Rakan Mayasi

Cinephilia Critics’ Award: “Zoom In, Zoom Out,” dir. Dong Jie

PYIFF–NAAC Distribution Award: “A Girl Unknown,” dir. Zou Jing

Honorary Awards

Crouching Tiger Hidden Dragon East-West Award: Ann Hui

International Contribution to Chinese Cinema Award: Han Sanping, Marco Müller

10th Anniversary Award: Tang Yan

title: Christy Carlson Romano Says She and ‘Even Stevens’ Co-Star Shia LaBeouf Were ‘Like Oil and Water’ While Filming the Disney Channel Show
summary: Christy Carlson Romano, who first broke out on the Disney Channel sitcom “Even Stevens,” is opening up about her experience working alongside co-star Shia LaBeouf. Speaking with Amanda Hirsch of the Not Skinny But Not Fat podcast on Tuesday, Romano said that she and LaBeouf were “like oil and water,” despite being just 14 and […]
content:
Christy Carlson Romano, who first broke out on the Disney Channel sitcom “Even Stevens,” is opening up about her experience working alongside co-star Shia LaBeouf. Speaking with Amanda Hirsch of the Not Skinny But Not Fat podcast on Tuesday, Romano said that she and LaBeouf were “like oil and water,” despite being just 14 and 12 years old, respectively, at the time.

Romano explained that their incompatibility on set stemmed from how they were raised.

“I was being raised and brought up to be this type A, I mean exactly like Ren Stevens. Like, you know your lines, you hit your marks, you don’t mess up,” she said. “You’re a New York kid, like that comes with a certain echelon… I was trying to go to pre-college Juilliard… everything we were doing, my mom called it cross-training, came with a certain dollar amount of training.”

Popular on Variety

In comparison, LaBeouf has long been open about his tumultuous childhood and has said that his father was a recovering addict, and at times abusive. “He was a Venice Beach kind of bum kid,” said Romano. “It’s like that kind of vagrant fun, but also very chaotic and very scary lifestyle, and he was very young to be having that.” She likened his upbringing to the lifestyle depicted in the 1995 Larry Clark film “Kids.”

Romano did give LaBeouf credit for finding his manager at just eight years old; the “Transformers” and “Holes” star “had a dream and made it happen for himself,” she added.

“Even Stevens” ran from 2000 to 2003 and followed Ren (Romano) and Louis (LaBeouf), the two younger siblings of the Stevens family who were described as having opposing personalities and often clashing.

This isn’t the first time Romano has weighed in on her relationship with LaBeouf. Earlier this year, the actress posted — and then deleted — a statement reading “Shia doesn’t deserve to be on the Rushmore. I’ll be writing a Substack on this so you can understand why,” to X. The comment came after “That’s So Raven” star Raven-Symoné was asked who she’d put on her Disney Mount Rushmore, to which she responded that LaBeouf would be one of them.

On Tuesday, the actress also posted a photo of herself with LaBeouf and his father on the set of “Even Stevens” to Instagram. “Recently found this picture. Shia and I spent 3 years of our lives right next to each other in adjoining trailers, both of us enduring painful childhoods,” she wrote. “If only we could have been there for each other, but we were each going through our own battles and could barely take care of ourselves.” She concluded by writing that she’d “finally” be sharing everything in her forthcoming memoir, “Once Upon a Trainwreck: The Fall and Rise of a Child Star,” which will be available on Oct. 6.

title: ‘Final Payment’, ‘Congo Boy’ Win Top Awards At Pingyao International Film Festival
summary: Chinese director Niu Niu’s Final Payment scooped the Best Film Award in the Fei Mu Awards of this year’s Pingyao International Film Festival (PYIFF), while Rafiki Fariala’s Congo Boy won Best Film in the festival’s Roberto Rossellini Awards. Final Payment, which also won Best Actor for Niu Jianrong’s performance, revolves around a homeowner clashing with […]
content:
Chinese director Niu Niu’s Final Payment scooped the Best Film Award in the Fei Mu Awards of this year’s Pingyao International Film Festival (PYIFF), while Rafiki Fariala’s Congo Boy won Best Film in the festival’s Roberto Rossellini Awards.

Final Payment, which also won Best Actor for Niu Jianrong’s performance, revolves around a homeowner clashing with a contractor over the final payment following a set of renovations on his home. PYIFF’s competition jury stated: “Tearing through a very small rip, the film leads us into a reality and emotional landscape so expansive, where we sigh, lament, and reflect. The director’s approach is concise, unpretentious, and masterful, earning the wholehearted recognition of the entire jury.”

The Best Film award came with a cash prize of $150,000 (RMB1m) with half given to the director for the development of their next film, and half given to the distributor in China. Niu Niu previously directed Mr Junjun, which was awarded with the Jury Award and Youth Jury Award at PYIFF in 2023.

Watch on Deadline

Also in the Fei Mu Awards, Xu Zao won Best Director for Light Pillar, while Best Actress went to Sun Yi for Wang Xiaozhen’s A Joke. The Jury Award was presented to Dong Jie’s Zoom In, Zoom Out, which had its world premiere in Venice Critics Week, while a special mention went to Cai Chengjie’s Suzhou Quartet.

The Fei Mu awards are focused on the festival’s Hidden Dragons section, which selects first, second and third films from emerging directors making Chinese-language films, while the Roberto Rossellini Awards focus on the Crouching Tigers section for emerging international directors.

Congo Boy, which took Best Film in the Roberto Rossellini Awards, also won Best Actor when it premiered in Un Certain Regard at this year’s Cannes film festival. The PYIFF award came with a cash prize of $20,000, with half given to the director for the development of their next film, and half given to the distributor in China.

The PYIFF jury stated: “The Jury unanimously has been moved by this autobiographical story, told in a simple style that echoes the great tradition of neorealism. For a film focusing on a character that confronts his world with optimism despite dark times and takes on his shoulders the destiny of his entire family.”

Also in this section, the Philippines’ Rafael Manuel won Best Director for Filipiñana, while the Jury Award went to Ben’imana, directed by Marie-Clémentine Dusabejambo, which won the Camera d’Or at this year’s Cannes. The PYIFF jury also awarded Rakan Mayasi’s Yesterday The Eye Didn’t Sleep a Special Mention.

Hong Kong filmmaker Ann Hui received the Crouching Tiger Hidden Dragon East-West Award, shortly before she receives the Camellia Award at Busan International Film Festival next week.

Pingyao’s International Contribution To Chinese Cinema Award went to Marco Müller, who founded the festival with Chinese auteur Jia Zhangke and currently serves as Artistic Director of the Film Art Research Centre at Shanghai University, and veteran producer, director and former chairman of China Film Group Han Sanping. Hello Group chairman Tang Yan was presented with a 10th Anniversary Award.

This year’s PYIFF opened on September 24 with a screening of the 4K restoration of Fei Mu’s Spring In A Small Town; closed with Good Trip, co-directed by Hong Kong filmmakers Norris Wong and Hoi Wong, and also screened Jia’s short film Torino Shadow, which premiered at this year’s Cannes.

PINGYAO INTERNATIONAL FILM FESTIVAL 2026 AWARDS:

FEI MU AWARDS:

Best Film: Final Payment, dir: Niu Niu

Best Director: Xu Zao, Light Pillar

Best Actress: Sun Yi, A Joke, dir: Wang Xiaozhen

Best Actor: Niu Jianrong, Final Payment, dir: Niu Niu

Jury Award: Zoom In, Zoom Out, dir: Dong Jie
