content:
SPOILER ALERT! This post contains details from Tuesday night’s episode of Dancing with the Stars.

It’s another exciting night in the ballroom as 13 contestants are still eyeing the Len Goodman Mirrorball Trophy during Week 3 of Dancing with the Stars.

Last week, the judges reinforced just how tough they are going to be this season, once again declining to score anyone above a 7. Still, three couples — Jenna and Val, Ezra and Daniella, and Amber and Pasha — walked away tied for the top of the leaderboard with 21 points. We also said goodbye to Alan Bersten and chef Giada De Laurentiis.

Week 3 is Yacht Rock night, so the remaining couples are performing to hits from artists including Fleetwood Mac, The Doobie Brothers, and Luther Vandross.

Watch on Deadline

Here is how the night went.

Olympian Amber Glenn with Pasha Pashkov danced a Foxtrot to “Hold the Line” by Toto. SCORE: 24

Actress Julia Stiles with Ezra Sosa danced a salsa to “I Can’t Go for That (No Can Do)” by Daryl Hall & John Oates. SCORE: 19

Late-night sidekick Guillermo Rodriguez with Whitney Carson danced a Foxtrot to “Escape (The Piña Colada Song)” by Rupert Holmes. SCORE: 15

Actress Tatyana Ali with Jan Ravnik performed a Quickstep to “Maneater” by Daryl Hall & John Oates. SCORE: 21

Actor Harry Shum Jr. with Jenna Johnson performed a jive to “You Make My Dreams Come True” by Daryl Hall & John Oates. SCORE: 24

Musician Taylor Hanson with Britt Stewart danced a Foxtrot to “What a Fool Believes” by The Doobie Brothers. SCORE: 18

Reality star Maura Higgins with Mark Ballas danced a Quickstep to “Turn Your Love Around” by George Benson. SCORE: 22

Reality star Ciara Miller with Brandon Armstrong performed a Cha Cha to “Never Too Much” by Luther Vandross. SCORE: 18

Savannah Bananas midfielder Jackson Olson with Emma Slater performed a paso doble to “Easy Lover” by Philip Bailey and Phil Collins. SCORE: 18

Comedian and podcaster Connor Wood with Rylee Arnold danced a Foxtrot to “Everywhere” by Fleetwood Mac. SCORE: 20

Actress Jenna Dewan with Val Chmerkovskiy danced a samba to “Africa” by Toto. SCORE: 21

Reality star Tyler Cameron with Sharna Burgess danced a jive to “Still the One” by Orleans. SCORE: 17

Paralympian Ezra Frech with Daniella Karagach danced a Foxtrot to “Just the Two of Us” by Grover Washington Jr. featuring Bill Withers. SCORE: 21

Who goes home?

The competition is now down to 12 as Taylor Hanson and Britt Stewart were sent home. Next week is all about Mariah Carey, so the couples will perform a variety of the pop superstar’s biggest hits.

title: Danny Boyle Says ‘28 Years Later Part 3’ Will ‘Have a Lot of Cillian Murphy in It’ and Backs Jack O’Connell as the Next James Bond
summary: Danny Boyle is adamant: “28 Years Later” part 3 will happen. “‘28 Years 3,’ or whatever it ends up being called, will get made because people keep asking about it. Quite when I’m not sure, but there’s a script – a very good script by Alex Garland,” he said. And it will feature Cillian Murphy. […]
content:
Danny Boyle is adamant: “28 Years Later” part 3 will happen.

“‘28 Years 3,’ or whatever it ends up being called, will get made because people keep asking about it. Quite when I’m not sure, but there’s a script – a very good script by Alex Garland,” he said. And it will feature Cillian Murphy.

“[It will have] a lot of Cillian Murphy in it. Whether he’ll take his kit off anymore, that I don’t know. He’s got the Oscar now.”

Boyle spoke at Zurich Film Festival, where he presented “Ink” – and found some time to weigh in on these Bond rumors.

Popular on Variety

“They should cast Jack O’Connell as Bond,” he said.

Danny Boyle left “No Time to Die,” allegedly due to creative differences with producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson, as well as star Daniel Craig.

“When they asked me to do Bond, we came up with the story [with John Hodge] and they lost confidence in it. It’s a shame, because it could have been really good.”

He thinks that Denis Villeneuve will look after the franchise very well.

“Villeneuve is amazing. Did you see that beginning of [‘Dune: Part Three’], which they showed before ‘The Odyssey’? God, if I was directing ‘The Odyssey,’ I would have thought everybody would be disappointed in my film following it. But obviously, Chris Nolan has more confidence than I have.”

During a masterclass at the fest, Boyle also gushed about his “Ink” lead Jack O’Connell. In a biographical drama, adapted by James Graham from his stage play, he plays Larry Lamb who accepts the offer posed by Rupert Murdoch (played by Guy Pearce) to be the editor of The Sun newspaper.

“Have you seen ‘Back to Black’? It’s a wonderful film. He plays the boyfriend and that’s an impossible part. It was an incredible performance,” he said.

“I thought he should play Larry Lamb, because he’s weird. Despite the fact that he’s playing a monster, you’re still interested in him. You’re still intrigued by him and he doesn’t repel you. It was true of the guy in ‘Ink,’ because by the end of the film, his moral conscience – if there ever was one – has dissolved entirely as he pursues success. And you still have to root for him.”

“I used to say it’s the same as Al Pacino at the end of ‘The Godfather Part II,’ when he has ordered the murder of his brother, and yet you’re still intrigued by Pacino just sitting there all alone.”

He wanted to show a different side of Murdoch in the film.

“People are fascinated by him, and repelled by him, but this comes from a time when he first arrived in the U.K. and was a very different figure. I thought it’s really interesting not to play into the caricature of him, because back at the beginning, he wasn’t like that at all. He’s quite a prudish man, weirdly.”

Then, despite knowing that his actions go against his morality, he accepts it: “Because the numbers are good.”

“You would describe him as a bit of a soft liberal, which is interesting, because Trump was a Democrat and now he’s a Republican president. These guys move where the power is.”

He added: “I really do believe that what they did in 1969, and the beginning of this newspaper, has actually more impact on our lives today. There’s a clear thread that runs from this ignition point to where we are today. We have lost our relationship with the truth, and by that I mean our dependable relationship with the truth.”

“We’ve replaced it with – and the most powerful man in the world is the best example of it – with brazen assertions and loud stories, and completely counter-intuitive declarations. Somebody tells the truth, he says it’s a lie and ‘fake news.’ It’s the kind of attention economy, or clickbait, that didn’t exist in 1969, but you can see its origins.”

He noted: “You have to acknowledge that their success is something that we’re all complicit in. I think you have to accept that you can’t just blame Trump, which I’ve just done, but you have to accept your own responsibility in it. The idea of the film was to try and make that an engaging journey that people went on, and you discover something about where we are now, how we got there, and whether we want to do anything about it.”

Still, change is possible, he said.

“There’s a politician who emerged in Britain, who will probably disappoint us, but he’s just become Prime Minister: Andy Burnham.”

“He’s concentrating on a much more long-term problem rather than the divisiveness which everybody likes to encourage. He’s concentrating on something that connects us all, which is how are we going to look after our older population. We’re going to need a solution. So yes, change is possible.”

“You have to look for those sprouts of hope.”

title: Ajay Devgn Says ‘Drishyam 3: The Conclusion’ Surpasses Predecessors, Ends Franchise for Good (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Top Bollywood star Ajay Devgn tells Variety he is confident “Drishyam 3: The Conclusion” clears the bar set by its predecessors, calling the psychological thriller’s twists unpredictable even for genre-savvy audiences accustomed to guessing outcomes. Speaking ahead of the film’s Oct. 2 release, Devgn says the Hindi-language franchise ends definitively, unlike its open-ended Malayalam-language counterpart. […]
content:
Top Bollywood star Ajay Devgn tells Variety he is confident “Drishyam 3: The Conclusion” clears the bar set by its predecessors, calling the psychological thriller’s twists unpredictable even for genre-savvy audiences accustomed to guessing outcomes.

Speaking ahead of the film’s Oct. 2 release, Devgn says the Hindi-language franchise ends definitively, unlike its open-ended Malayalam-language counterpart.

Devgn, who plays the protagonist Vijay Salgaonkar, watched the completed film on Tuesday and emerged reassured, despite what he describes as the pressure of following two successful predecessors, particularly the second installment, which he calls a difficult film to follow. He watched it alongside people whose judgment he trusts, and came away without the fear that audiences might feel it could have been better. He credits writer/director Abhishek Pathak and the writing team, saying the film is shot well and grips audiences throughout.

Popular on Variety

“You will not be able to guess,” Devgn says. “So, the twists and turns are a lot, and they are unexpected.”

The “Drishyam” franchise centers on a family man who covers up an accidental killing to protect his wife and daughters, then finds himself locked in a battle of wits with the police officer investigating the case.

The “Drishyam” story has traveled widely since Jeethu Joseph’s original Malayalam film starring Mohanlal opened in 2013. It was remade in Kannada as “Drishya” and in Telugu as “Drushyam,” both in 2014, and in Tamil as “Papanasam” in 2015, with Kamal Haasan in the lead and Joseph again directing. The Hindi version, starring Devgn and Tabu, also arrived in 2015, followed by a Sinhala remake and the Chinese adaptation “Sheep Without a Shepherd” in 2019. Joseph’s Malayalam sequel arrived in 2021, with Pathak’s Hindi “Drishyam 2” following in 2022. The Malayalam “Drishyam 3” opened earlier this year and has grossed INR239 crore ($25 million). Panorama Studios, which holds the Hindi and international remake rights, is now developing Korean, Spanish and English versions of the franchise, while limiting its own Indian-language output to Hindi.

On playing the character across all three films, Devgn says Salgaonkar has “become more calmer, I would say. He’s more prepared,” he says, noting the story picks up directly where “Drishyam 2” left off rather than showing a further gap in the character’s development, so there is limited room to trace additional emotional evolution beyond what the film itself depicts.

Devgn spoke to Variety on the sidelines of the FICCI-Frames Indian media industry conference in Mumbai where he was in conversation with Alok Jain, head – Hindi and English entertainment business (streaming, TV and studios), JioStar.

Despite the Malayalam “Drishyam 3” leaving its ending open, Devgn says the Hindi version takes a different approach entirely. “This is a completely different script altogether,” he says. “There is no comparison. There is nothing. And in our film, we’re not leaving any loophole or anything. We are finishing it. This is the conclusion.”

Devgn says his next release, the comedy “Golmaal 5,” is complete and will arrive in January. He has also wrapped an as-yet-untitled film carrying the working title “Ranger,” a Luv Ranjan production, and is preparing to start work on “Chauhan.”

Asked about further installments of the “Raid” franchise, Devgn says he would continue only with the right material. “Hopefully, yes, if we get a great script, because you don’t plan it,” he says, adding that a strong script is what would determine whether the franchise moves forward. The “Rudra” franchise remains on pause, a decision he says was intentional.

Devgn also addressed the Hindi-language film industry’s turnaround after a pandemic-era slump he attributes to audiences outpacing the industry’s output as international viewing habits reshaped expectations. He says the industry has since worked to catch up with a more evolved audience, with some films succeeding as a result. He adds that theatrical viewing endures in India in part because it remains one of the few affordable, communal entertainment options families can enjoy together, contrasting it with the shorter, costlier outings offered by restaurants. Once audiences have a good experience at the theater, he says, they tend to return.

Devgn says he is also developing a few scripts with an eye toward returning to directing, tentatively within the next two years.

On the broader evolution of Indian audiences amid a global shift toward AI-generated content, Devgn says viewers have become highly discerning, often able to judge from a trailer alone whether a film is worth watching, and says that instinct is right the vast majority of the time. He says a weak film struggles regardless of how strong its marketing is, since audiences can sense when they are being misled.

Asked about AI’s role in storytelling, Devgn, who owns generative AI company Prismix, says, “I think it is here to stay. I myself have an AI company,” he says, adding that the venture is performing well. He says full audience connection may take time, since viewers know AI-generated content isn’t real, but reiterates his belief that the format will endure.

title: Beta Film Takes ‘Rex – Vienna Calling’ Worldwide as Season 2 Goes Into Production (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Beta Film has unveiled a broad international sales footprint for “Rex – Vienna Calling,” the latest incarnation of the three-decade-old “Rex – A Cop’s Best Friend” franchise, as production gets underway on a second season. The series has been sold to SBS in Australia, Rai in Italy and TV 2 in Denmark. Elsewhere in Europe, […]
content:
Beta Film has unveiled a broad international sales footprint for “Rex – Vienna Calling,” the latest incarnation of the three-decade-old “Rex – A Cop’s Best Friend” franchise, as production gets underway on a second season.

The series has been sold to SBS in Australia, Rai in Italy and TV 2 in Denmark. Elsewhere in Europe, buyers include Alpha TV in Greece, HRT in Croatia, Planet TV in Slovenia, STVR in Slovakia, Nova in Bulgaria and TVR in Romania, while Baltic deals take in Duo Media Networks in Estonia, SIA Tet in Latvia and LNK in Lithuania.

Action Channel in Japan and SHANT TV in Armenia are also on board, with further sales under negotiation.

Popular on Variety

The deals come as the evergreen IP continues to find traction in an increasingly on-demand television market. Audience analytics firm PlumResearch describes mature streaming markets as shifting “from hits to habits,” with much viewing taking place across the long tail rather than being concentrated solely around new releases.

The longevity of “Rex” offers a case in point. Over its 30-year history, the police-dog franchise has spawned multiple local adaptations. Canadian remake “Hudson & Rex,” another long-running Beta title, was recently renewed for a tenth season.

“Rex – Vienna Calling” stars Maximilian Brückner (“War Horse,” “Cherry Blossoms”) as detective Max Steiner, who teams with German Shepherd Rex to tackle cases across Vienna. Six new feature-length episodes are currently shooting at some of the Austrian capital’s most recognizable locations.

The first season opened to almost 1.6 million viewers on Germany’s SAT.1, posting a 7% overall share and 9.9% among 14-49s. In Austria, the six feature-length episodes averaged 701,000 viewers and a 27% share on ORF, while the Italian premiere on Rai 2 drew more than 750,000 viewers and a 5.6% share, rising above one million once on-demand and catch-up viewing was included.

Produced by MR Film in co-production with SAT.1 and ORF, “Rex – Vienna Calling” is distributed worldwide by Beta Film. The series is backed by FISAplus, the Austrian Television Fund and the state of Lower Austria.

title: Mubi Takes Global on Los Javis ‘La Mesías’ and Rodrigo Sorogoyen’s ‘Riot Police’ as Movistar Plus Rolls Out Iconic Hits Around the World (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Mubi has taken worldwide rights to two iconic series from Movistar Plus International, the overseas distributor of the biggest Spanish pay TV and SVOD operator: “La Mesias,” from “La Bola Negra” directors Los Javis, and “Riot Police,” the first premium TV series from “The Beloved” director Rodrigo Sorogoyen. Further headlines: Nominated on Sept. 23 for […]
content:
Mubi has taken worldwide rights to two iconic series from Movistar Plus International, the overseas distributor of the biggest Spanish pay TV and SVOD operator: “La Mesias,” from “La Bola Negra” directors Los Javis, and “Riot Police,” the first premium TV series from “The Beloved” director Rodrigo Sorogoyen.

Further headlines: Nominated on Sept. 23 for an International Emmy, four-part “The Anatomy of a Moment,” from Alberto Rodriguez (“The Tigers”), has rolled out in further territories in Europe.

The in-all 33 new deals were unveiled during the first day of trading at Madrid’s mega-market and forum Iberseries & Platino Industria, where Movistar Plus has a large market presence led by screenings or presentations of top titles bound for October’s Mipcom.

Popular on Variety

On Tuesday, Movistar Plus International hosted a showcase, screening and cocktail of Spain’s sex trade chronicle “El Castillo,” a standout at San Sebastián; a screening of withering LOL Millennial comedy “Many People Have to Die,” marking out creator Victoria Martín as a major Spanish comedic talent; and a presentation of “Killing a Bear,” based crime drama turning on the deep social conflict surrounding the death of brown bear Cachou, found dead in a ravine in the Pyrenees in 2020. The “small, local story vividly illustrated the polarized world we live in,” creators Jorge and Alberto Sánchez Cabezudo have told Variety.

‘La Mesías’

A Movistar Plus Original, large scale “La Mesías” delivered a first instance of Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi’s full-on creativity, working with the budget they required, shooting each episode with different genre influences – psychodrama, sci-fi, procedural and musical – and a pop sensibility and varying formats across multiple timelines, all of which they have now repeated in “La Bola Negra.”

“La Mesías,” like La Bola Negra,” also explores legacy and repression, here the psychological trauma left by a messianic mother, who turns her family into a cult.

“The series talks about religion, but as a form of education and this is what makes it interesting,” told Variety on set in 2023.

Key territories for the Mubi deal were announced in exclusivity by Variety in July.

‘Riot Police’

World premiering at San Sebastián in 2020 and starring “The Beloved’s” Victoria Luengo, Riot Police confirmed Sorogoyen’s ability to bring a big screen punch to his first premium series.

A six part series “Riot Police” also underscored his ability to mix genre and social point, exploring the failures and fragility of the masculine psyche as a riot police squad become the subject of an internal police enquiry led by Luengo’s character after bungling an eviction. The series closed early deals with HBO Latin America and Canal+ in France.

“The series I’ve seen rarely evolve in style,”Soroyogen told Variety in 2020. But Riot Police does in the use of hand-held, anamorphic fisheye lense camerawork for the eviction moving to a 15 minutes sequence shot in final episode.

‘The Anatomy of a Moment’

Co-produced with Arte France, starring “Money Heist’s” Alvaro Morte, “The Anatomy of a Moment” delivers Rodríguez’s fictionalized vision of how three key figures of “Shakespearian stature,” Rodríguez has said– Spanish Prime Minister Adolfo Suárez, Spanish Communist Party head Santiago Carrillo and armed forces chief Manuel Gutiérrez Mellado – wrestled democracy for Spain over 1976-77and almost lost it in a 1981 botched coup d’état. New international distribution takes in pubcasters RTP (Portugal), RTS (Switzerland), RTV (Slovenia) and Cinob0 (Greece).

More Top Sellers: ‘Querer,’ ‘The New Years,’ ‘The Nameless’

A top best series Grand Prix winner at Series Mania last year, Alauda Ruiz de Azua’s’s marital rape series Querer,” part family drama, part courtroom thriller, she has observed, continues to roll out around the world. Already acquired by Arte, Querer has now been licensed to Cinobo Poland, Italy’s MyMoviesOne, Latvia’s Latvia’s Mobilais and South Korea’s LG Plus.

Movistar Plus International has closed Greece and Poland, both with Cinobo, and Latvia (Latvijas Mobilais) on Sorogoyen’s “The New Years,” on-off couple romantic saga that played Venice in 2024 alongside Alfonso Cuarón’s Cate Blanchett starrer “Disclaimer” for Apple TV+, and Thomas Vinterberg’s big StudioCanal play “Families Like Ours.

France’s Filmo, Media4Fun and South Korea’s LG Plus have bought “The Nameless,” a portrait of evil family horror series from Filmax (“[REC]”), Pau Freixas (“The Red Band Society,” “You Shall Not Lie”) and Pol Cortecans (“You Shall Not Lie”),

A Drill-Down on More Deals:

*Cinobo Greece has picked up two seasons of “Bellas Artes” plus “A 100-Million Reward.”

*Filmo has also licensed “La vida breve.”

*Flow, the big Argentine streaming service covering Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay, has become one of the first operators to buy “Many People Have to Die,” as well as “The Center,” “La Caza. Irati” and doc “Bisbal.”

*”Riot Police” also sold to Media4Fun.

*Italy’s MyMovieOne has acquired global electricity power outage anthology “OffWorld,” including episodes by Sorogoyen, Rodríguez, Isaki la Cuesta, Isa Campo and Rail Arévalo.

*Poland’s TVP has taken “La Canción,” from “Hierro” and “Rapa” creators Pepe Coira and Fran Araujo, placing Spain’s stunning 1968 Eurovision win in Spain’s dawn-of-democracy later liberty. Further acquisitions take in Costa del Sol mob lawyer comedy “Marbella,” crime investigation thriller “La Caza.Irati,” from Banijay’s DLO Producciones and two seasons of Canary Islands-set murder mystery “Hierro.”

*South Korea’s LG, a streaming service, has licensed “El centro,” “La Caza. Irati,” two ‘Hierro’ seasons, “El dentista’,” and “La vida breve.”

title: Zygi Kamasa’s U.K. Film Distributor True Brit Entertainment Files for Administration Due to ‘Extremely Challenging Market Conditions’
summary: True Brit Entertainment, the U.K. theatrical distributor that launched less than three years ago, has filed for administration, a British legal process similar to Chapter 11 bankruptcy. The company, which was founded by former Lionsgate U.K. & Europe CEO and Marv Studios Group CEO Zygi Kamasa, becomes the latest casualty of the U.K.’s extremely tough […]
content:
True Brit Entertainment, the U.K. theatrical distributor that launched less than three years ago, has filed for administration, a British legal process similar to Chapter 11 bankruptcy.

The company, which was founded by former Lionsgate U.K. & Europe CEO and Marv Studios Group CEO Zygi Kamasa, becomes the latest casualty of the U.K.’s extremely tough distribution market, having failed to ignite the local box office despite critically-acclaimed releases including “The Death of Robin Hood” starring Hugh Jackman.

“In extremely challenging market conditions, the company has taken the difficult decision to enter administration.” Kamasa said in a statement sent to Variety. “An independent specialist has now been appointed to oversee the company and assess the options available, with the aim of achieving the best possible outcome for the company and its creditors.”

Popular on Variety

True Brit was announced in Nov 2023 with a focus exclusively on U.K. films for theatrical release, launching with a stated aim to invest in and release 4-8 titles a year and co-finance over $50million worth of productions annually. The new venture came with funding led by talent management and entertainment company Three Six Zero, which reps names including Calvin Harris, Frank Ocean, FKA Twigs, plus a minority investment from Matthew Vaughn’s Marv.

The first True Brit release was “The Critic” starring Ian McKellen and Gemma Arterton, which it acquired out of Toronto in 2023 and put in U.K. cinemas the following year. This was followed by the Danny Dyer comedy “Marching Powder,” which hit a high note, grossing more than $4 million in the U.K. and Ireland. But subsequent releases, including Gurinder Chadha’s musical comedy-drama “Christmas Karma” and the boxing drama “Giant,” both of which True Brit co-produced, struggled, as did “The Death of Robin Hood,” which earned under $800,000.

The latest release, the Bella Ramsey-starring coming-of-age comedy-drama “Sunny Dancer,” despite an impressive promotional campaign and buzz from its world premiere in Berlin, also failed to land, underlining the ongoing struggles in the U.K. for independent film.

Upcoming titles for True Brit include Anthony Wonke’s boxing biopic “In the Shadows,” which is due to world premiere later this month at the BFI London Film Festival, and the Maika Monroe-led psychological horror comedy “Victorian Psycho,” which premiered in Cannes. It’s unknown what will now happen to these releases.

Variety‘s sister publication Deadline was first to report the news of True Brit going into administration.

title: Hearst Networks UK Buys ‘American Chopper’ Revival Series ‘Orange County Choppers Original’
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Orange County Choppers Originals is headed out of the garage and travelling to Europe. Hearst Networks has bought UK rights to the ‘reborn’ ob doc series from Off The Fence, which has boarded the show after striking an agreement to represent it worldwide (excluding the U.S.). The new series – which aired in the […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Orange County Choppers Originals is headed out of the garage and travelling to Europe.

Hearst Networks has bought UK rights to the ‘reborn’ ob doc series from Off The Fence, which has boarded the show after striking an agreement to represent it worldwide (excluding the U.S.).

The new series – which aired in the U.S. on Discovery Channel, Discovery Turbo TV, Discovery+, and Discovery GO after launching in February – is the latest chapter in the motorbikes franchise that began in 2002 with American Chopper and is bases around the Orange County Choppers custom bikes business. A second season has been ordered, with the number of eps doubling to 12.

Prior to Orange County Choppers Originals‘ launch, there had been no new American Chopper episodes since 2020’s finale, American Chopper: The Last Ride. At one point, there had been a six-year gap due to legal problems between Paul Teutul Sr. and his son, Paul Teutul Jr., the father and son at the center of the series, but they were ultimately settled and the pair reunited on-screen.

Watch on Deadline

The Hearst agreement, brokered by OTF’s SVP North America and Global Networks, Sam Thompson and Hearst Networks’ Acquisitions Manager, Hannah Gray, marks a first international deal for the revival.

Orange County Choppers Originals is based around Teutul Sr., founder and CEO of Orange County Choppers, who has spent over 30 years crafting custom motorcycles for major corporations and sports teams. The series shifts the focus to his workshop in Florida, where he reunites with some of the original team while introducing fresh talent. It also delves into his personal life, highlighting his charity work and passion for animal welfare and rescue on his hobby farm.

Hearst’s Gray said: “Orange County Choppers has everything we look for in great factual entertainment: big builds, strong characters and plenty of heart. With Paul Sr. back at the centre of the story, we’re excited to bring this new chapter to UK audiences.”

Orange County Choppers Original sees Teutul Sr.’s team design and build one-of-a-kind motorcycles for charitable causes, with each episode following them through engineering challenges, tight deadlines, and unexpected setbacks, culminating in auctions or raffles to raise funds and awareness.

Joan Kay, co-CEO of OCC said: “Everyone loves a comeback story and this one comes with the rebirth of an iconic brand and frankly, Paul Sr. is kicking ass. We’re very excited to partner with OTF on the global revival of the show as the company shares our values of working with entertainment with purpose and has an enviable reach and network of partners around the world across all platforms.

“This show isn’t just television, it has proved itself as a cultural phenomenon with the power to ignite fans and enthusiasts and turbocharge bike culture – we can’t wait for you all to see it.”

OTF’s Thompson said: “We’ve seized this opportunity wholeheartedly because the facts speak for themselves. There’s an existing fanbase hungry for more, with proven ratings, engagement, sponsorship and merchandising potential. We’re especially excited to have Hearst Networks on board as a quality broadcast partner and look forward to sharing the rollout of this rare gem.”

The American Chopper franchise has previously broadcasted in 160 territories in 35 languages worldwide, and OTF’s acquisition offers a new opportunity for buyers at MIPCOM in just under two weeks’ time in Cannes, France.

title: European Film Academy To Honor Beki Probst, Marin Karmitz & Sandra den Hamer With New Community Award
summary: The European Film Academy has named Beki Probst, Marin Karmitz and Sandra den Hamer as the first recipients of its new Community Award for an Outstanding Contribution to European Film Culture. The award, paying tribute to “a decisive and continuous contribution over many years to the development and expansion of European film culture”, will be […]
content:
The European Film Academy has named Beki Probst, Marin Karmitz and Sandra den Hamer as the first recipients of its new Community Award for an Outstanding Contribution to European Film Culture.

The award, paying tribute to “a decisive and continuous contribution over many years to the development and expansion of European film culture”, will be presented during the European Film Awards weekend in Athens in January 2027.

The trio will be presented with the award on January 15, on the eve of the main ceremony at the traditional Welcome Night gala dinner, taking place this edition at the Acropolis Museum housing some 4,000 artefacts dating as far back as 1,200 BCE.

Probst is best known internationally as the founder of the Berlinale’s European Film Market, having entered the cinema world as the founder with her Swiss husband of the Queenie Cinemas in Berne in the 1960s, which grew into a successful chain of arthouse cinemas still existing today.

Watch on Deadline

Born into a Sephardic Jewish family in Istanbul, Probst studied Law and Journalism and worked briefly as a film journalist.

From 1981 to 1988, she was the Berlinale delegate for Turkey and Greece and after initiating Locarno’s industry program, she was asked by Berlinale Director Moritz de Hadeln to start the European Film Market in 1988 in its current form.

Under her management, which continued into 2014, the EFM became one of the largest and most important international film market in Europe.

She has previously been feted with the Berlinale Camera, the Prix du cinéma Suisse, the French Chevalier des Arts et des Lettres and the Order of Merit of the Federal Republic of Germany.

Karmitz is known as the founder of France’s independent exhibitor, producer, film financier and sales agent mk2 film. Born in Romania in 1938, Karmitz arrived in France as a refugee with his family in 1947.

After studies at the IDHEC film school in Paris, he worked as assistant director to the filmmakers Jean-Luc Godard, Agnès Varda, Jacques Rozier, Yannick Bellon and Pierre Kast. before directing his first short film, Nuit Noir, Calcutta, based on a screenplay by Marguerite Duras, in 1964.

In 1965, he worked with Samuel Beckett on the adaptation of Comédie. In the same year, the feature was selected to open the Venice International Film Festival and shocked audiences with its avant-garde material.

He launched mk2 Productions in 1967 and made his feature-length directorial debut with Seven Days Somewhere Else (1968), followed by Comrades (1970) and Blow for Blow (1972), which were screened at international festivals.

He opened his first cinema in Paris in 1974 in response to Blow for Blow, about a group of textiles workers who take their factory boss hostage in protest at the work conditions, being shut out of mainstream circuits.

In 40 years, he would produce 108 films and distribute over 350 in theatres, among them Krzysztof Kieslowski’s Three Colours trilogy, for which he received a nomination for the European Film Awards 1994, twelve films by Claude Chabrol, Alain Resnais, Louis Malle, the Taviani brothers, Theo Angelopoulos, Lucian Pintilié, Gus Van Sant, Ken Loach, Abbas Kiarostami, Hong Sang-Soo, Michael Haneke, Walter Salles and Xavier Dolan.

Den Hamer has an extensive track record in the Dutch film industry.

From 2007 to 2023, she was the director of the Netherlands Filmmuseum in Amsterdam. Under her leadership, the re-named Eye Filmmuseum opened a brand-new museum building and a new collection centre in Amsterdam.

Its eclectic programming includes large retrospectives, international conferences and as well as exhibitions, exploring the work and careers of filmmakers such as Bela Tarr, Apichatpong Weerasethakul and Alex van Warmerdam among many others.

Before that, Sandra den Hamer worked for 23 years at the International Film Festival Rotterdam, including roles as co-ordinator of CineMart and the Hubert Bals Fund. From 1996 to 2007, she directed the festival.

She also served as President of the Board of the Association of European Cinematheques (A.C.E.). From 2023 to 2026. she was appointed interim executive director at the Netherlands Film Fund. Today she chairs the Board of the IDFA Institute and the Gerrit Rietveld Academy in Amsterdam.

Gathering 5,700 members from more than 50 countries across Europe, the European Film Academy oversees the annual European Film Awards, which alternates taking place in its home city of Berlin and another European city, which is Athens this year.

The 39th ceremony marks the second time it is unfolding in its new January slot, after the academy decided to shift it from a long-running December slot to integrate the awards more fully into the wider awards season.

title: Netflix Renews Indian Reality Breakout ‘Lock Upp’ For Second Season
summary: Netflix is returning the inmates to the Lock Upp jail. A second season of the ‘captive reality’ series, whose full title is Lock Upp: Sach Yaa Sazaa has been ordered following Season 1’s breakout summer, where it placed number one of Netflix’s TV shows list within two days of the premiere and remained in the […]
content:
Netflix is returning the inmates to the Lock Upp jail.

A second season of the ‘captive reality’ series, whose full title is Lock Upp: Sach Yaa Sazaa has been ordered following Season 1’s breakout summer, where it placed number one of Netflix’s TV shows list within two days of the premiere and remained in the top ten for seven straight weeks.

The response to the show was so strong that five weekly episodes were expanded to six to satisfy demand, Netflix has said. It eventually amassed 50 million hours viewed in a month.

The show sees Indian celebrities thrown together in a jail cell, where they compete in challenges. What broke through with audiences was some of the more divisive characters discussing their public perception and confronting narratives that have surrounded them.

Watch on Deadline

Netflix said Season 2 “build on that world, bringing audiences back inside the jail for another chapter where personalities collide, dynamics shift, and every secret has the potential to change the game.”

Riteish Deshmukh and Farah Khan return as hosts, with Balaji Telefilms producing. Show creator Ekta Kapoor is producing alongside Shobha Kapoor and Manisha Sharma, with Malaya Pradhan the showrunner.

“Lock Upp: Sach Yaa Sazaa became appointment viewing overnight,” said Monika Shergill, VP of Content at Netflix India. “Viewers invested, debated, and kept coming back. It captured the zeitgeist — not just as entertainment, but also as a space where celebrities talked about topics they rarely do, owned their choices and confronted past trauma.

“Ekta’s bold homegrown idea and the scaled adaptation on Netflix led to entertainment maxxing. Season 2 will be about recreating the same Netflix effect with many new surprises for our audiences.”

Ekta Kapoor, Jjoint Managing Director at Balaji, added: “Lock Upp: Sach Ya Sazaa on Netflix went far beyond what we imagined. The conversations, the inmates, and their most memorable moments continued to live with audiences even after the finale. That’s what makes the return of Lock Upp so exciting.

“The next season will take audiences back into a world they know, but with an entirely new set of stories, personalities, and surprises. And Farah and Riteish will continue to helm the Lock Upp as the formidable jailer duo, bringing their own energy, unpredictability, and dynamic to the next chapter.”

Lock Upp originally launched on ALTBalaji and MX Player in 2022, but was rebooted for Netflix.

title: ‘Doctor Who’: Multiple BBC Studios Labels Likely To Apply For Tender
summary: EXCLUSIVE: At least one BBC Studios indie will be throwing its hat in the ring to become the next producer of Doctor Who, with scripted boss Jamie Hall telling Deadline he “firmly believes” the entire BBC group should “reap the rewards” of the iconic sci-fi series. Hall said “we’ve probably got one, potentially two companies” […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: At least one BBC Studios indie will be throwing its hat in the ring to become the next producer of Doctor Who, with scripted boss Jamie Hall telling Deadline he “firmly believes” the entire BBC group should “reap the rewards” of the iconic sci-fi series.

Hall said “we’ve probably got one, potentially two companies” going for the multi-million pound tender, which if successful would bring the show back in house following two seasons made by Sony-owned Bad Wolf, starring Ncuti Gatwa. His comments followed BBC Studios CEO Tom Fussell recently saying BBC Studios would be applying “with gusto.”

Hall wouldn’t reveal the names of the indies but said he would “100%” be happy for more than one to enter the race.

Watch on Deadline

BBC Studios runs an in-house drama label, which made Doctor Who before Bad Wolf, while it also owns several scripted indies outright including Baby Reindeer maker Clerkenwell Films, Happy Valley producer Lookout Point and Sherwood indie House Productions.

While he hasn’t seen his labels’ proposals, Hall said he has been “very open” and honest with those keen to go for the tender because the process is “quite an onerous undertaking and costs quite a bit of money.” “I have to make sure that it doesn’t become a distraction from the day job,” he added.

If two BBC Studios labels enter, they will likely join Line of Duty producer World Productions, whose boss Simon Heath has previously indicated his ITV Studios-owned outfit is interested. More thoughts from producers can be found in our future Doctor Who analysis from over the summer.

Published a fortnight ago, the tender calls for a “relevant, surprising, brave and inspiring” new vision for the show that should premiere in 2028-29. Notably, it said it is happy for indies to pitch a series using “episodic writers” rather than a “showrunner model,” which would do away with how Doctor Who has been made in recent years.

After several years with Bad Wolf and after the termination of the just-ended Disney+ co-pro deal, Hall was adamant that Doctor Who “should sit within the BBC and the whole group should reap the rewards of it.”

Questioned on what he would want to see from a revamped Doctor Who, Hall harked back to the days when Matt Smith and David Tennant were playing the Doctor.

“It feels to me that there is an opportunity to get back to what the core offering was in that time,” he added. “It will be off screen for two or three years and that gives the audience a great chance to have a break then rediscover, while also bringing a new audience.”

title: Callum Scott Howells & Gabrielle Creevy Leading Adaptation Of Vanessa Savage Thriller ‘The Night They Vanished’ For BBC Studios & Channel 4
summary: EXCLUSIVE: It’s a Sin star Callum Scott Howells and Gabrielle Creevy (Black Doves) are leading an adaptation of Vanessa Savage’s romantic thriller The Night They Vanished for BBC Studios and Channel 4. Cameras have rolled in Wales on the six-part series that tells the story of Anna (Creevy), whose world is blown apart when she […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: It’s a Sin star Callum Scott Howells and Gabrielle Creevy (Black Doves) are leading an adaptation of Vanessa Savage’s romantic thriller The Night They Vanished for BBC Studios and Channel 4.

Cameras have rolled in Wales on the six-part series that tells the story of Anna (Creevy), whose world is blown apart when she discovers her childhood house listed on a true-crime website as the scene of her family’s future deaths. Intriguing blind date Cai (Scott Howells) runs the true-crime site but swears he didn’t post it. The police say it’s a hoax, but Anna’s family have vanished.

Angharad Elen (The Light In The Hall) and Hannah Daniel (Mudtown) are adapting Savage’s novel, her third thriller. BBC Studios’ new label CliffEdge Entertainment, which has just been unveiled to Deadline by scripted boss Jamie Hall, is producing and selling worldwide. Channel 4 has pre-bought the drama while we understand a deal with a U.S. buyer is close.

Watch on Deadline

Additional cast includes Tamzin Outhwaite (The Wives, Ridley Road, The Tower) as Anna’s stepmum Jo and Steffan Rhodri (Gavin & Stacey) as Idris, Anna’s father, along with Matthew Gravelle (Mudtown), Lisa Victoria (Pobol y Cwm), Jack Quick (Pobol y Cwm), Andrew Lennon (Death Valley), Callum Hymers (The Pact), and Bella Shewan.

Scott Howells is best known for Russell T. Davies’ It’s a Sin and is starring in Deadpoint, another BBC Studios thriller for Channel 4. Creevy plays Eleanor in Netflix hit Black Doves, which will soon launch Season 2.

Creevy said: “Anna is a firecracker – sharp, loyal and carrying more hurt than she lets on. The moment her past comes roaring back, she’s forced into a nightmare she thought she’d escaped. It’s a gift of a role and I can’t wait for audiences to unravel the truth with her.”

Scott Howells added: “Cai is charming, complicated and never quite what he seems. He could be the love of Anna’s life… or the centre of a terrifying conspiracy. Playing someone who keeps you guessing is exactly the kind of challenge I love.”

The Night They Vanished has been pre-bought by Polly Scates, Channel 4 Head of Acquisitions and Felix Jones, Acquisitions Manager. EPs are Sarah Creasey, Sathe, Elen, and Branwen Williams for BBC Studios. Series producer is Sian Elen John and the Director is Geraint Todd.

title: How HBO’s Casey Bloys Wound Up With the Keys to Paramount-Warner Bros.’ Streaming Empire, and What’s to Come
summary: In the end, Casey Bloys knew he was holding all the cards. As the industry continued to speculate about whether the HBO boss or Paramount’s Cindy Holland would wind up with control of the two companies’ soon-to-be-merged streaming behemoth, in recent weeks the momentum seemed to be on Bloys’ side. So when Paramount direct-to-consumer chair […]
content:
In the end, Casey Bloys knew he was holding all the cards.

As the industry continued to speculate about whether the HBO boss or Paramount’s Cindy Holland would wind up with control of the two companies’ soon-to-be-merged streaming behemoth, in recent weeks the momentum seemed to be on Bloys’ side.

So when Paramount direct-to-consumer chair Holland told colleagues Tuesday that she would be leaving, her staff at the company was disappointed — having seen firsthand the exec’s tremendous impact inside the company over the past year — but not surprised.

Bloys had recently become a bit bullish on the merger. As he made the rounds last month during Emmys weekend, the chairman of HBO and HBO Max content wasn’t shy in sharing his hope that Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery would soon come together. That’s because the alternative, he told industry folk, might be more dire.

Popular on Variety

The uncertainty of a deal, which at that point was still facing a lawsuit from California Attorney General Rob Bonta and 11 other state AGs, was having a negative impact on business, and it needed to be resolved, Bloys said. But his pro-deal sentiment was a bit of a break from the hope inside other Warner Bros. segments that the merger might not happen.

Industry insiders who spent time with Bloys over cocktails and canapés that weekend read his eagerness for the deal to be consummated as a sign that the exec was feeling good about his future — or, at least, HBO’s stature inside a merged Paramount-Warner Bros.

It was no secret that Bloys wouldn’t accept anything less than reporting to the combined company’s boss, David Ellison, and his domain would have to (at the very least) include everything that he oversees right now at Warner Bros. Discovery. “I think you probably know the answer to that,” he told Variety when asked in July whether he would report to anyone other than Ellison. The idea that Bloys would accept just running the HBO fiefdom — in the vein of John Landgraf’s FX purview at Disney — was a nonstarter, as Bloys’ role had long since expanded to all of the direct-to-consumer world, and such a move would have been seen by Bloys as a step back.

But that meant Ellison faced a Sophie’s choice. Ellison had made it clear that he eventually wanted to merge HBO Max and Paramount+ into a single entity, but the CEO quickly learned neither Bloys nor Holland could be expected to report to the other in a new corporate structure.

Ellison could have kicked the can down the road, as HBO Max and Paramount+ will continue to operate as separate services for consumers in the near future — given that there are different revenue streams attached to distribution deals. Both are also profitable, which means it doesn’t make sense to immediately shut one of them down and subsume it into the other one. Most immediately, HBO Max and Paramount+ can probably start being sold as a bundle, but combining the two organizations will take time (observers point to how long Disney has taken to combine Disney+ and Hulu).

Even so, it seemed very unlikely that the new company could launch with both Bloys and Holland still in charge of their respective domains. Not only would that pit the two streamers against each other internally, but a bake-off would cause huge internal distractions at a time when the company needs to focus on integrating operations. “If you’re going to do this, you should have one person guiding the strategy, and that means you’re not having any confusion with who’s being pitched and where shows are going,” said one insider.

Plus, keeping both execs would have left two hefty salaries on the books, and the new company — saddled with around $80 billion of debt — is going to have to enact massive cost cuts, and fast.

Ellison is said to be a boss who is loyal to his underlings, particularly with his own hires. And that’s why there might have been a world where Holland remained in some capacity. But others noted that Holland — who spent 16 years at Netflix as the architect of its original content strategy before a brief stint at Sister and then being wooed by Ellison — didn’t need a job she didn’t want. Said one agent: Ellison “wanted to try to make it work with everyone, and he couldn’t.”

Holland had spent the last few years in Ellison’s orbit, first as an adviser for Skydance Media on streaming as the company bought Paramount Global. After that acquisition closed in August 2025, she was his choice to come in and overall direct-to-consumer while helping him pursue Warner Bros. Discovery.

Holland was seen as one of the key leaders inside the new Paramount Skydance structure and highly respected. When she arrived, Paramount+ was a skeleton operation and needed an immediate reinvention. She brought in Jane Wiseman as executive vice president and head of originals for Paramount+, and they started to broaden out the streamer’s programming mix — greenlighting more than 25 new series in a short amount of time. “Cindy was really instrumental in a lot of the success we’ve had in the past year,” said one insider. “She really does it all.”

But HBO is HBO. If Bloys did give Ellison the ultimatum that the combined streamer needed a clear-cut, singular leader, Ellison likely knew he had to choose the 22-year HBO vet who had taken the brand to new heights. (Bloys, who first joined HBO in 2004, has run the flagship brand since 2016 and HBO Max since 2020.)

Rumors that Bloys had met with Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos — and might be plucked for a role at that company if things didn’t turn his way at ParaWarSkyBros — might have also sweetened the pot for the Bloys to stay on for Paramount-WBD. “There were all these rumors that that he was going to take this Netflix job,” one source said. It’s still unclear how real or likely such a move actually was, but Ellison may have realized he need the industry to have some clarity on who would run the Paramount-Warner Bros. streaming business before the deal closes.

“It’s hard to get inside his head,” said one source. “But if I’m David Ellison, I’m thinking I need Casey Bloys. I need HBO, and I can’t afford to lose him almost more than Cindy.”

After Bonta last week struck the controversial settlement between 12 states and Paramount Skydance that paved a path for the merger, the general consensus around town was that JB Perrette, Warner Bros. Discovery CEO/president of global streaming and games, was destined for a big job at the new company, and that Bloys wouldn’t be going anywhere. (The judge overseeing the state AGs’ case has yet to rule on the settlement.)

“He’s played his hand brilliantly,” one insider said of Bloys, even before Holland’s exit was announced. “It seems like he’s very happy, and JB too. It’s like they both have some feeling of confidence. I could see it in JB, his whole demeanor has changed, more relaxed and confident.”

For Holland, no matter how much she had accomplished over the past year in righting the Paramount+ ship, HBO will be the flagship property of this new entity, and you can’t mess with the crown jewel. In her farewell memo to colleagues, Holland admitted as much: “David is optimizing for HBO stability as we move into this next chapter, and I fully support that,” she wrote.

Meanwhile, Holland’s immediate exit has caused a scramble inside Paramount+, which remains a lean operation to begin with. A crew obviously needs to remain in place to keep the streamer operational, but it’s now unclear what this means to the staff once Bloys takes over. Because the deal hasn’t yet closed, Bloys’ oversight might not be announced until next week, which keeps things in a bit of a limbo until then.

This will greatly increase Bloys’ programming domain, starting with the Taylor Sheridan universe: “Dutton Ranch,” “Landman,” “Tulsa King,” “Lioness” and more. There’s also an upcoming fifth and final season of “Star Trek: Strange New Worlds,” Season 2 of “Dexter: Resurrection” (which returns Oct. 30) and crime drama “MobLand,” which was recently renewed for a Season 3.

Now, the new questions emerge: How will Bloys program Paramount+ vs. HBO Max, and is there crossover in what is developed and ordered while the two streamers remain separate?

“I think ‘Landman’ is something that could easily be on the periphery of HBO,” said one insider. And indeed, under Bloys, soon those Paramount+ shows and HBO series will be a part of one big family.

title: ‘Sense and Sensibility’ Inspires Handcrafted Apparel Collection From Designer Sarah Flint, Featuring Embroidered Heels and Painted Scarves
summary: Jane Austen is getting a style upgrade just in time for the latest trip to the Dashwood family estate. Designer Sarah Flint has teamed with Focus Features on a new capsule collection inspired by the upcoming “Sense and Sensibility” adaptation, translating the contrasting personalities of sisters Elinor and Marianne Dashwood into shoes, scarves and Georgian-era […]
content:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

Jane Austen is getting a style upgrade just in time for the latest trip to the Dashwood family estate.

Designer Sarah Flint has teamed with Focus Features on a new capsule collection inspired by the upcoming “Sense and Sensibility” adaptation, translating the contrasting personalities of sisters Elinor and Marianne Dashwood into shoes, scarves and Georgian-era floral details.

The limited collection, available beginning Sept. 30 exclusively on Sarah Flint’s website, centers on two of the designer’s signature shoe silhouettes. The more understated “Emma” is fashioned after the sensible, reserved Elinor, while the “Natalie” takes its cues from Marianne’s more romantic and free-spirited personality. Both styles are made from linen and hand-embroidered with Japanese anemones, nodding to the needlework and textile traditions of the period.

Sarah Flint Capsule Collection SHOP ONLINE

The capsule also includes two hand-painted scarves: an Anemones Scarf painted by Flint herself and the Dashwood Scarf, created by longtime collaborator Katarzyna Strozynska-Goraj. Colors and motifs throughout the collection were pulled from the visual world of the film.

“Anemones are one of the classic English garden flowers, and in the old language of flowers, they mean anticipation,” Flint said. “We hand-embroidered it onto linen, the same slow, careful way women of that era would have worked, one stitch at a time, because printing it would have missed the point.”

For Flint, the collaboration was also something of an Austen fan project. “I’ve wanted to do something with this book for years, so when this collaboration came together, it felt like the equivalent of a superfan getting asked to plan a reunion tour,” she said. “I didn’t want a shoe with a movie logo slapped on it. I spent real time on where Elinor ends and Marianne begins, down to which thread color went on which shoe.”

The collection arrives just weeks before Focus Features and Working Title’s new “Sense and Sensibility” hits U.S. theaters on Oct. 16. Daisy Edgar-Jones stars as Elinor opposite Esmé Creed-Miles as Marianne, with Caitríona Balfe as Mrs. Dashwood, Frank Dillane as John Willoughby, George MacKay as Edward Ferrars and Fiona Shaw as Mrs. Jennings.

Directed by Georgia Oakley (“Blue Jean”) from a screenplay by bestselling author Diana Reid, the film follows the Dashwood sisters after the death of their father forces the family to leave its estate and adjust to more modest circumstances, all while navigating romance, heartbreak and the rigid expectations of Georgian society. Oakley’s debut feature, “Blue Jean,” earned her a BAFTA nomination, while Reid is best known for novels including “Love & Virtue.”

The film also marks another Austen adaptation from Focus and Working Title, whose previous literary outings include Joe Wright’s 2005 “Pride & Prejudice,” starring Keira Knightley, and Autumn de Wilde’s 2020 “Emma,” starring Anya Taylor-Joy.

Of course, “Sense and Sensibility” has particularly formidable cinematic shoes to fill. Ang Lee’s acclaimed 1995 adaptation starred Emma Thompson as Elinor and Kate Winslet as Marianne, with Thompson winning the Academy Award for best adapted screenplay.

The Sarah Flint x “Sense and Sensibility” capsule is available beginning Sept. 30 at SarahFlint.com, ahead of the film’s theatrical release on Oct. 16.

title: Paramount Deal and U.S. Film Incentive Reflect Hollywood’s Deepening Ties to Government
summary: Last week, politicians decided they could not let Hollywood slip away. First, California Gov. Gavin Newsom pushed for a resolution of the Paramount antitrust case out of fear that the studio would leave the state. And in Congress, Republicans and Democrats joined to introduce a U.S. film incentive, recognizing they are at risk of losing […]
content:
Last week, politicians decided they could not let Hollywood slip away.

First, California Gov. Gavin Newsom pushed for a resolution of the Paramount antitrust case out of fear that the studio would leave the state. And in Congress, Republicans and Democrats joined to introduce a U.S. film incentive, recognizing they are at risk of losing a critical industry to foreign competition.

In short, it was the week that Hollywood became too big to fail.

“The American government has never done this,” says Stephen Galloway, dean of the Chapman University film school. “You have the government stepping in and not saying, ‘How can we prevent you from causing damage?’ Instead, they’re saying, ‘How can we prevent you from being damaged?’ That’s a fascinating turn.”

Popular on Variety

In both cases, the result is a deepening integration with the state. The Paramount antitrust settlement entails five years of government monitoring and commitments to keep ownership of studio lots, to produce a certain number of films and to install an oversight board as a watchdog for news networks CBS and CNN.

Neither side in the merger battle wanted this outcome. Paramount CEO David Ellison wanted to buy Warner Bros. Discovery without conditions but was willing to accept some state intrusion as the price of scale. California Attorney General Rob Bonta, meanwhile, wanted to block the deal outright or at minimum force divestitures.

“Structural remedies are always preferable to behavioral,” said Paula Blizzard, Bonta’s antitrust chief, at a seminar on Sept. 14, “because the government gets in, it says, ‘Change the structure; get more competitors,’ and then the government gets out.” A behavioral solution, she added, would require the state to become a “de facto participant” in the market.

Just a week later, Bonta flipped and announced a package of behavioral remedies. The consent decree requires Paramount to release at least 30 films a year and to negotiate WBD and Paramount cable carriage contracts as separate entities. The deal even requires Paramount to quadruple its U.S. production volume if a federal subsidy is adopted.

Bonta’s critics called the deal a “cave.” Compared with blocking the merger, it is. But it also commits the attorney general’s office to enforcing Paramount’s production levels in an unprecedented way.

“If we think that there is a problem, then we are going to initiate the court process,” Blizzard told Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín at a hearing on Sept. 24. “This is an area where it may come back to you.”

Hollywood has historically been wary of government involvement, whether in the form of censorship or via anti-monopolization efforts. But unions and studio chiefs celebrated last week’s developments.

“In almost every instance, Hollywood by and large resisted and was scared of interference,” Galloway says. “The contrast is that these two moves are by and large welcomed by Hollywood.”

Democrats often decry “corporate welfare,” but have long made an exception for Hollywood studios, which provide union jobs. Now Republicans are coming around too. Last year, Texas increased its state incentive and offered bonuses for “faith-based” projects and films that promote Texas heritage.

“The cultural aspects were used to get more traditional fiscal conservatives on board with something that could be seen as a Hollywood handout,” says Pete Johnson, a media industry researcher and visiting assistant professor at New York University, who sees Texas as a precursor to President Trump’s backing of a federal film incentive.

Across party lines, the fear of losing Hollywood has proved a powerful motivator. Paramount’s threat to leave California spurred action from Newsom and L.A. Mayor Karen Bass. And the end of Peak TV and the decline in production jobs have galvanized support for incentives.

Sen. Tim Scott is a Republican from South Carolina — not exactly a film hub — but even he is a fan. “We cannot stand by as more and more American film production moves overseas,” he said last week, “taking jobs, investment and an important source of American cultural influence with it.”

Pictured: Paramount CEO David Ellison attended President Trump’s state dinner on Sept. 24, capping a historic week

title: Funko Unveils Ultra-Limited Marvel NYCC Figures, Including $100 Light-Up Sorcerer Supreme Doom
summary: Funko is bringing some heavy Marvel firepower to New York Comic Con this year, including an ultra-limited light-up Doctor Doom figure that will be one of just 500 produced. The collectibles company has unveiled a new batch of Marvel Pop! figures timed to NYCC 2026, led by the $100 Pop Super Grail SFX Sorcerer Supreme […]
content:
Funko is bringing some heavy Marvel firepower to New York Comic Con this year, including an ultra-limited light-up Doctor Doom figure that will be one of just 500 produced.

The collectibles company has unveiled a new batch of Marvel Pop! figures timed to NYCC 2026, led by the $100 Pop Super Grail SFX Sorcerer Supreme Doom. The four-inch vinyl bobblehead depicts Victor von Doom in his Sorcerer Supreme era and features a light-up effect. Only 500 will be made, with each arriving pre-packaged in a UV-resistant Premium Plastic Pop! Protector.

The $100 Doom is an in-person exclusive that will be sold in limited quantities at Funko’s NYCC booth. For collectors who don’t manage to snag the grail version, Funko is also releasing a standard Sorcerer Supreme Doom Pop! for $15, which will be available both at the convention and on Funko.com.

Also joining the lineup is a particularly bloodthirsty take on Spider-Man: a Vampire Miles Morales figure. Priced at $40, the 4.1-inch Pop! turns the fan-favorite wall-crawler into a fanged Marvel variant. Funko is producing 1,000 of the limited-edition figures, which will also come housed in a UV-protective case and be available in limited quantities at the company’s booth.

Wolverine collectors, meanwhile, will have an even tougher hunt on their hands. Funko’s $50 Ultimate Wolverine Pop! is limited to just 500 pieces and features the X-Men hero unmasked and claws out. Like the other high-end limited editions, it comes pre-packaged inside a Premium Plastic Pop! Protector.

All of the convention exclusives will sport a 2026 Fall Convention sticker and feature Funko’s new authentication packaging, which uses micro-optic technology and individual item codes that can be verified through Octane5.

The releases arrive as Funko prepares for New York Comic Con, taking place Oct. 8-11 at Manhattan’s Javits Center, where the company will set up shop at Booth 4515.

Fans hoping to buy select NYCC exclusives online won’t necessarily have to race to checkout the second they drop, either. Funko is introducing a credit card pre-authorization drawing system for its convention releases. Entries open Monday, Oct. 5, and close Wednesday, Oct. 7. After the window closes, randomly selected buyers will be notified and automatically charged for the items they pre-authorized.

Any inventory left over after the drawings will be released on Funko.com and Loungefly.com on the morning of Oct. 8, though considering some of these Marvel figures number in the hundreds, collectors may not want to count on leftovers.

title: Drew Carey to Host ‘Undercover Boss’ Return at CBS, Which Also Orders New Reality Series ‘Stacks of Cash’ and ’24 Hour Millionaire’
summary: CBS is tripling down on its unscripted lineup, bringing back a new version of “Undercover Boss” — this time hosted by Drew Carey — and greenlighting two new series: “Stacks of Cash,” hosted by Mike O’Malley, and “24 Hour Millionaire,” from the executive producers behind “Big Brother.” In the case of “Undercover Boss,” CBS said […]
content:
CBS is tripling down on its unscripted lineup, bringing back a new version of “Undercover Boss” — this time hosted by Drew Carey — and greenlighting two new series: “Stacks of Cash,” hosted by Mike O’Malley, and “24 Hour Millionaire,” from the executive producers behind “Big Brother.”

In the case of “Undercover Boss,” CBS said it is bringing the show back for a 12th season with “a refreshed take,” which includes bringing in Carey as host. The series has been off the air since 2022. Meanwhile, “Stacks of Cash” is a game show where six contestants answer questions to earn uniquely shaped blocks, which they then stack their way “toward a gold line.” And “24 Hour Millionaire” follows contestants as they must continually engage in social strategy and physical competitions over the course of 24 hours, with one player winning $1 million at the end of the day.

CBS announced the orders on Wednesday; “Undercover Boss” is in pre-production, while “Stacks of Cash” has already filmed its episodes. “24 Hour Millionaire,” which has been in development for the past year at CBS, is also in pre-production.

Popular on Variety

Carey recently marked his 20th season hosting “The Price Is Right” for CBS, while O’Malley starred in the Eye sitcom “Yes, Dear”; more recently, he’s been known as a TV showrunner for series like “Heels” and “Survivor’s Remorse.”

“These orders reflect our commitment to building a deep year-round unscripted slate with formats that are ambitious, entertaining and distinctly CBS,” said Mitch Graham, executive vice president of alternative series at CBS, in a statement. “We couldn’t think of a better time to bring back a reimagined version of ‘Boss,’ with Drew Carey serving as our host through undercover journeys that tap into the heart and authenticity of hard-working employees that audiences have always loved seeing. Our new series ‘Stacks of Cash’ delivers another fun, appealing family game show and ’24 Hour Millionaire’ gives us an exciting new format that feels incredibly groundbreaking in the competition space.”

“Undercover Boss” first launched in 2010 on CBS; it won Emmys for outstanding reality program in 2012 and 2013. The logline: “Corporate leaders go undercover within their own organizations to gain firsthand insight into their workforce and operations.” Studio Lambert produces the show; Stephen Lambert, Jack Burgess, Abigail McCarthy, Niall O’Driscoll and Tim Harcourt are executive producers.

As for “Stacks of Cash,” the series is based on a format developed by Eureka Studios Group Pty Ltd and Seven Network Limited. Chris Culvenor, Paul Franklin, Rikkie Proost, Sonya Wilkes, David Tibballs, Ves D’Elia and Ed Egan serve as executive producers.

And here’s the logline for “24 Hour Millionaire”: “An epic series that assembles the most skilled game players and puts them to the ultimate test: 24 nonstop hours of social strategy and physical competitions where one player is guaranteed to walk away with a $1 million prize. Only the best of the best will be invited, and they will be challenged to play an entirely new game where literally every second counts. In this ticking time bomb of strategy and gameplay, they will face off in a groundbreaking series where thinking fast is essential; assessing threats is critical and performing under pressure is crucial. With no breaks and no rest, the pressure builds as the clock ticks down over an intense 24 hours, pushing even the most accomplished competitors to their limits.”

“Big Brother” executive producer Fly on the Wall Entertainment is behind the show; Allison Grodner and Rich Meehan are EPs.

title: Jeff Hiller Joins CBS’ ‘Eternally Yours’ In Guest Role
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Jeff Hiller is adding another supernatural series to his resume. Hiller, fresh from the success of Apple’s Widow’s Bay, is joining CBS comedy series Eternally Yours, as a guest star. He will appear in multiple episodes starting with the third episode. The series premieres on Thursday October 8. Hiller plays Aldrict, an old-world vampire […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Jeff Hiller is adding another supernatural series to his resume.

Hiller, fresh from the success of Apple’s Widow’s Bay, is joining CBS comedy series Eternally Yours, as a guest star.

He will appear in multiple episodes starting with the third episode. The series premieres on Thursday October 8.

Hiller plays Aldrict, an old-world vampire who has crossed paths with LIZ several times over the centuries and is a bit of a troublemaker.

Eternally Yours is an eternal love story about two vampires, Liz (Allegra Edwards) and Charles (Ed Weeks), who have been married for five hundred years, and their struggles to accept the human, Max (Jaren Lewison), who is dating their daughter, Emma (Helen J Shen).

Watch on Deadline

The role reunited Hiller with Joe Port and Joe Wiseman, who created Eternally Yours and serve as showrunners and executive producers. Last season, Hiller starred on two episodes of their other CBS show Ghosts as a server named Jeff. He also appeared in CBS comedy Elsbeth.

Eric Tannenbaum, Kim Tannenbaum and Jason Wang exec produce alongside Port and Wiseman. CBS Studios is the studio.

Hiller’s had a busy year; in September 2025, he won the Emmy for Outstanding Supporting Actor in a Comedy Series for his work on HBO’s Somebody Somewhere. He was also nominated for an Emmy in the Outstanding Guest Star in a Drama series category this year for his work on Apple’s Pluribus.

Then came Widow’s Bay, where he plays Dale, who works in the town hall for Mayor Tom Loftis, played by Matthew Rhys. He was just upped from guest star to series regular for season two.
