content:
It’s a wrap. Production on the third season of Wednesday has officially concluded, Netflix announced today. The streamer also released a new Season 3 photo (see above) of Jenna Ortega (Wednesday) sitting at a typewriter.

Season 2 ended with some major cliffhangers, with Enid transforming into a full Alpha werewolf to save Wednesday after she captured and buried alive by The Slurp (Isaac Night). Enid then fled with the uncertainty that she can ever return to her human form, and the search for her continues. The season ended with Wednesday, Uncle Fester, and Thing hitting the road in a motorcycle sidecar in a desperate rescue mission to track Enid down.

We also saw Ophelia, played by Eva Green in Season 3, who turns out is alive in Grandmama Hester’s basement. We see her writing “Wednesday Must Die” on the basement wall at the end of Season 2.

Watch on Deadline

The returning cast includes Jenna Ortega (Wednesday Addams), Catherine Zeta-Jones (Morticia Addams), Luis Guzmán (Gomez Addams), Isaac Ordonez (Pugsley Addams), Emma Myers (Enid Sinclair), Hunter Doohan (Tyler Galpin), Joy Sunday (Bianca Barclay), Moosa Mostafa (Eugene Ottinger), Georgie Farmer (Ajax Petropolus), Billie Piper (Isadora Capri), Luyanda Unati Lewis-Nyawo (Sheriff Ritchie Santiago), Victor Dorobantu (Thing), Evie Templeton (Agnes DeMille) and Fred Armisen (Uncle Fester).

Previously announced new Season 3 cast includes Eva Green as Aunt Ophelia, Winona Ryder as Tabitha, Chris Sarandon, Noah Tayler, Oscar Morgan, Kennedy Moyer, Lena Headey, Andrew McCarthy and James Lance. Joanna Lumley has been upped to series regular.

Wednesday is created by Alfred Gough and Miles Millar and directed by Tim Burton. Season 3 is slated to premiere in 2027.

title: ‘Ink’ Helmer Danny Boyle To Receive Gotham Film Awards’ Director Tribute
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Danny Boyle, whose latest film Ink opened last month’s Venice Film Festival, has been tapped to receive the Gotham Director Tribute at the 36th annual Gotham Film Awards in November. The honor recognizes recognizes filmmakers whose bodies of work have made significant contributions to contemporary cinema. It will celebrate Boyle’s four-decade career that includes […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Danny Boyle, whose latest film Ink opened last month’s Venice Film Festival, has been tapped to receive the Gotham Director Tribute at the 36th annual Gotham Film Awards in November.

The honor recognizes recognizes filmmakers whose bodies of work have made significant contributions to contemporary cinema. It will celebrate Boyle’s four-decade career that includes winning the Best Director Oscar in 2009 for Slumdog Millionaire as well as Ink, his pic about the beginnings of tabloid journalism in the UK in 1969 when Rupert Murdoch launched The Sun.

Jack O’Connell, Guy Pearce as Murdoch and Claire Foy star in Ink, from Netflix, which hits theaters December 11 ahead of a January 8, 2027 bow on the streamer.

Watch on Deadline

RELATED: Baz Bamigboye Looks Back On True Tabloid Life With ‘Ink’ Director Danny Boyle & Writer James Graham

Boyle’s other credits include Shallow Grave, Trainspotting, 28 Days Later, The Beach, Slumdog Millionaire (which won a total of eight Oscars including Best Picture), 127 Hours, Steve Jobs, T2 Trainspotting, Yesterday and most recently 28 Years Later. In 2012, he directed the London Olympics Opening Ceremony.

“Across four decades, Danny Boyle has established himself as one of the true auteurs of his generation,” said Gotham Film & Media Institute executive director Jeffrey Sharp. “From the energy and urgency of Shallow Grave and Trainspotting to the achievements of Slumdog Millionaire, 127 Hours and Steve Jobs, he has consistently brought a singular voice and perspective to the screen. With Ink, Danny once again proves his ability to take a compelling story and make it feel wholly cinematic. We’re delighted to honor his remarkable career with the Gotham Director Tribute and to celebrate this exciting new chapter in his work.”

The Gothams, among the first of the major awards shows during film kudos season, has set its 2026 ceremony for November 30 at Cipriani Wall Street. Nominees will be announced October 27.

Earlier this week it began revealing its honorary tribute awards, with Laika tapped to receive the fest’s Anniversary Tribute.

title: CBS Orders ‘Undercover Boss’ Reboot With Drew Carey, ‘Stacks Of Cash’ & ‘24 Hour Millionaire’ Unscripted Series
summary: CBS is expanding its unscripted slate with series orders to three shows: a reboot of Undercover Boss hosted by Drew Carey and new series Stacks of Cash, hosted by Mike O’Malley, and 24 Hour Millionaire (working title) from Big Brother executive producers. Targeted seasons, premiere dates and additional details will be announced at a later […]
content:
CBS is expanding its unscripted slate with series orders to three shows: a reboot of Undercover Boss hosted by Drew Carey and new series Stacks of Cash, hosted by Mike O’Malley, and 24 Hour Millionaire (working title) from Big Brother executive producers.

Targeted seasons, premiere dates and additional details will be announced at a later date, CBS said Wednesday.

Based on the British series, Undercover Boss originally premiered on CBS in 2010 and aired for 11 seasons, the most recent in 2022. The reboot is in pre-production with Carey, who has hosted CBS’ The Price Is Right since 2007, as the host.

Stacks of Cash is in post-production. The game show filmed in Portugal, the latest U.S. unscripted series to be shot abroad in order to save costs.

Watch on Deadline

24 Hour Millionaire, which has been in development at CBS for more than a year, also is in pre-production.

RELATED: 2026 TV Series Renewals Photo Gallery

“These orders reflect our commitment to building a deep year-round unscripted slate with formats that are ambitious, entertaining and distinctly CBS,” said Mitch Graham, EVP Alternative Series at CBS. “We couldn’t think of a better time to bring back a re-imagined version of Boss, with Drew Carey serving as our host through undercover journeys that tap into the heart and authenticity of hard-working employees that audiences have always loved seeing. Our new series Stacks of Cash delivers another fun, appealing family game show, and 24 Hour Millionaire gives us an exciting new format that feels incredibly groundbreaking in the competition space.”

Series descriptions provided by CBS follow below:

UNDERCOVER BOSS

The Emmy Award-winning series returns for its 12th season with fan-favorite television personality Drew Carey joining as host and a refreshed take on a beloved format for today’s audience. Corporate leaders go undercover within their own organizations to gain firsthand insight into their workforce and operations. Undercover Boss is produced by Studio Lambert. Stephen Lambert, Jack Burgess, Abigail McCarthy, Niall O’Driscoll and Tim Harcourt are executive producers.

STACKS OF CASH

An edge-of-your-seat game show hosted by Emmy-nominated actor Mike O’Malley (Heels, Survivor’s Remorse), where six contestants face off in a quiz-driven battle with towering stakes. Players answer questions to earn uniquely shaped blocks, then stack their way toward a gold line. One wrong move can send everything crashing down. Stacks of Cash is based on a format developed by Eureka Studios Group Pty and Seven Network Limited. Chris Culvenor, Paul Franklin, Rikkie Proost, Sonya Wilkes, David Tibballs, Ves D’Elia and Ed Egan are executive producers.

24 HOUR MILLIONAIRE (working title)

From the executive producers of Big Brother, 24 Hour Millionaire is an epic series that assembles the most skilled game players and puts them to the ultimate test: 24 nonstop hours of social strategy and physical competitions where one player is guaranteed to walk away with a $1 million prize. Only the best of the best will be invited, and they will be challenged to play an entirely new game where literally every second counts. In this ticking time bomb of strategy and gameplay, they will face off in groundbreaking series where thinking fast is essential, assessing threats is critical and performing under pressure is crucial. With no breaks and no rest, the pressure builds as the clock ticks down over an intense 24 hours, pushing even the most accomplished competitors to their limits. 24 Hour Millionaire is produced by Fly on the Wall Entertainment with Allison Grodner and Rich Meehan serving as executive produce

title: Mike Flanagan’s ‘Carrie’ Envisioned As Three Seasons In “Dream Scenario”
summary: Mike Flanagan adapted Stephen King’s Carrie into a series, and in a “dream scenario,” he would like it to run as a trilogy. Already counting on King’s approval of the adaptation, Flanagan has a specific vision for Carrie that could potentially go beyond the original story. “In my dream scenario,” Flanagan said in an interview with Collider. […]
content:
Mike Flanagan adapted Stephen King‘s Carrie into a series, and in a “dream scenario,” he would like it to run as a trilogy.

Already counting on King’s approval of the adaptation, Flanagan has a specific vision for Carrie that could potentially go beyond the original story.

“In my dream scenario,” Flanagan said in an interview with Collider. “I think it’s three seasons. In my dream scenario, I think Carrie has a wonderful three-step arc. It’s a trilogy, really.”

Carrie follows misfit high‑schooler Carrie White (Howell) after having spent her life hidden away inside the walls of her home with her fiercely protective mother, Margaret (Samantha Sloyan). Following her father’s unexpected death, Carrie enters the public high school ecosystem and is forced to navigate a viral bullying scandal that tears through her community.

Watch on Deadline

Carrie also faces the relentless pressure and casual cruelty of the social‑media age, and the awakening of mysterious telekinetic powers that rise alongside her adolescence.

The supernatural horror miniseries premieres on October 7 on Prime Video with Summer H. Howell in the title role.

Carrie was first adapted into a film in 1976, with Brian De Palma directing a screenplay written by Lawrence D. Cohen and Sissy Spacek as Carrie. A direct sequel, directed by Katt Shea, The Rage: Carrie 2 was released in 1999, with Emily Bergl playing Rachel Lang, Carrie’s younger half-sister.

In 2002, a television film directed by David Carson and based on a screenplay by Bryan Fuller debuted on NBC, with Angela Bettis as Carrie.

Before the new miniseries on Prime Video, Kimberly Peirce directed a 2013 remake starring Chloë Grace Moretz.

title: Florence Pugh Says ‘Instagram Censored Me’ Over Cornell 7 Posts Addressing Sexual Assault Case: ‘Another Shock That Women Are Censored’
summary: Florence Pugh’s press tour for Netflix’s “East of Eden” brought her to “The View,” where co-host Sara Haines brought up the Oscar nominee’s recent social media posts speaking out on the sexual assault case at Cornell University. “Even in modern times, women have to bear the consequences of sexual violence, like the allegations currently playing […]
content:
Florence Pugh‘s press tour for Netflix’s “East of Eden” brought her to “The View,” where co-host Sara Haines brought up the Oscar nominee’s recent social media posts speaking out on the sexual assault case at Cornell University.

“Even in modern times, women have to bear the consequences of sexual violence, like the allegations currently playing out with the so-called Cornell 7,” Haines said. “The case is still pending, and some of the accused have denied any wrongdoing, but I saw what you wrote about this. This was really important for you. Can you explain why you felt the need to speak up?”

“Rape is something that lives. The fear of it lives in our bodies, and when stories like this come out and it’s really not picked up in the way that you hope it’s picked up, it makes me feel scared, it makes me feel anxious, it made me feel so much rage,” Pugh answered. “I’m lucky enough to do what I do and I have a platform and I wanted to talk about it.”

Popular on Variety

Pugh is one of the most prominent celebrities condemning the Cornell 7, the name given online to the seven male students accused of drugging and gang raping their female classmate at Cornell University in October 2024. The woman is now suing her alleged assaulters as well as their fraternity, Cornell University, her former sorority and more. According to the woman’s attorney, Cornell’s original investigation into the alleged crime resulted in only two of the accused men being expelled. The other students received lesser sanctions, such as temporary suspensions, workshops or essay-writing assignments.

“East of Eden” star Pugh, who will next be seen on the big screen in “Avengers: Doomsday” and “Dune: Part Three,” originally posted about the Cornell University sexual assault case in an Instagram post that the social media platform covered with a content warning that read: “This post contains content that some people may find upsetting.” Pugh put up a second post calling out Instagram for “blocking” her statement. As of the publication of this story, Instagram is only blocking Pugh’s second post with a content warning. The actor’s first post is available to see on the platform (see photo below).

“I’m able to come here and talk about it in real life, even though, sadly, Instagram censored me when I said it, which is also just another shock that women are censored, even when they go through these things, they can’t talk about it,” Pugh said about Instagram. “I feel very lucky and honored that we get to talk about this today. Thank you for bringing it up. It’s an ongoing conversation and it will always be an ongoing conversation until we’re harder on those that do that to women.”

In her original post on Instagram, Pugh described the alleged sexual assault incident as an “horrific act,” adding that she knew “this has happened before, and I hate the idea of it happening again.” She also urged men to speak out and to be “leading conversations about how we change the allowance and complicity of this behavior as much as we are. Be angry for us. Please.”

“This is really the moment where we need our men to be as horrified and as sickened as us,” the actor added.

Pugh added her in second post: “Instagram decided to block my post from getting in front of the right people. Tut tut tut. Oh dear. That doesn’t look great does it? Here’s another go at it in case you were one of those people that can no longer see my post.”

After Pugh’s post, several other celebrities such as Mariska Hargitay, Josh Gad, Hudson Williams and more used social media to also condemn the Cornell 7. “Arrest them,” wrote “Heated Rivalry” star Williams on his Instagram story while sharing a photo of the seven accused men. “Fuck them and fuck Cornell, too!”

“We refuse for this victim to be reduced to just another story. Cornell has failed to protect its students,” Hargitay posted on her Instagram in a shared statement with the Joyful Heart Foundation, the organization she founded to support victims of sexual assault, domestic violence, and child abuse.

title: ’24 Jump Street,’ Hugh Jackman’s ‘Treasure Island’ Remake Get Holiday 2027 Release Dates
summary: Sony has slated the highly anticipated comedy sequel “24 Jump Street” and Ridley Scott’s “Treasure Island” remake starring Hugh Jackman for release around the 2027 holiday season. “Treasure Island” hits theaters first on Nov. 11, 2027, while “24 Jump Street” releases on Dec. 10, 2027. Variety exclusively revealed in June that “24 Jump Street” was […]
content:
Sony has slated the highly anticipated comedy sequel “24 Jump Street” and Ridley Scott’s “Treasure Island” remake starring Hugh Jackman for release around the 2027 holiday season. “Treasure Island” hits theaters first on Nov. 11, 2027, while “24 Jump Street” releases on Dec. 10, 2027.

Variety exclusively revealed in June that “24 Jump Street” was in the works, with stars Jonah Hill, Channing Tatum and Ice Cube in talks to return for the franchise’s third installment. Rodney Rothman (“Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse”) will serve as director and co-wrote the script with Hill and Meghan Malloy. Phil Lord and Chris Miller — who helmed 2012’s “21 Jump Street” and 2014’s “22 Jump Street” — are returning as producers. Neal H. Moritz. Tatum and Reid Carolin are also producing for Free Association, along with Hill and Matt Dines under their Strong Baby banner.

Also in June, it was revealed that Jackman and Scott were teaming up to adapt Robert Louis Stevenson’s classic swashbuckling tale for the big screen. Scott will direct “Treasure Island” with a screenplay by Emmy-winning “Adolescence” writer Jack Thorne. Scott also serves as producer with Michael Pruss for his Scott Free banner. Thorne will executive produce “Treasure Island.”

Popular on Variety

Sony also dated Roshan Sethi’s thriller “The Surgeon” for April 2, 2027, and the coming-of-age comedy “Narcs” for Aug. 20, 2027. Michelle Yeoh stars in “The Surgeon” as a skilled doctor who is kidnapped and forced to operate on a mysterious patient. “Narcs” stars Mason Thames, and plot details remain under wraps. John Phillips, who wrote “No Hard Feelings” and “Dirty Grandpa,” makes his directorial debut with the project.

Two films also got their release dates shifted. “Grandgear,” from “Godzilla Minus One” director Takashi Yamazaki, was set to debut on Feb. 18, 2028, but will now drop on Jan. 14, 2028. “Helldivers,” based on the popular video game series, was set for release on Nov. 10, 2027. Sony pushed the title to June 9, 2028.

title: SCP Foundation Anthology Movie in the Works at Neon, Based on Online Horror Forum
summary: Neon is developing an anthology movie based on the community-driven horror forum The SCP Foundation. The project, which will focus on platforming emerging filmmakers, is slated for release in 2027. The SCP Wiki, created in 2008, is a collaborative speculative fiction website where users submit written works that expand the lore of the SCP Foundation, […]
content:
Neon is developing an anthology movie based on the community-driven horror forum The SCP Foundation. The project, which will focus on platforming emerging filmmakers, is slated for release in 2027.

The SCP Wiki, created in 2008, is a collaborative speculative fiction website where users submit written works that expand the lore of the SCP Foundation, a secret organization that collects and studies supernatural and often highly dangerous objects and entities for the good of humanity. Some of the most popular entries include SCP-173, a concrete statue that attacks anyone who breaks eye contact, and SCP-682, a supremely intelligent reptile that can adapt to any environment and rapidly heal any injury.

In Neon’s release, the studio made a point to emphasize that it is releasing the film under the Creative Commons license CC BY-SA and has been in communication with the SCP Wiki team about adapting its works. Neon’s announcement comes after the SCP Wiki team denounced a film from A24, Spooky Pictures and Image Nation shortly after it was unveiled. After the A24 film was announced, the SCP team wrote in a statement, “We have not had any communication with the filmmakers, producers, or distributors for this project, despite our best efforts, and to the best of our knowledge they have not made any efforts to contact us. Furthermore, A24 does not and cannot have any exclusive rights to anything related to the SCP Foundation, including any films that Spooky Pictures or anyone else may choose to create.”

Popular on Variety

Internet IP went from pariah to pay dirt in Hollywood after the success of A24’s “Backrooms,” based on the web series by 21-year-old Kane Parsons, who wrote and directed the film. After the horror-thriller grossed $400 million against a $10 million budget, Warner Bros. scooped up film rights for Trevor Henderson’s viral horror creation Siren Head and attached Brian Duffield as director and Zach Cregger as the writer. TriStar Pictures acquired another one of Henderson’s creatures, Cartoon Cat, for a movie adaptation in the weeks after.

title: David Ellison Taps Mattel’s Ynon Kreiz to Be Co-CEO of Merged Paramount-Warner Bros.
summary: Ynon Kreiz, who is stepping down as CEO of Mattel after eight years, will join David Ellison’s Paramount — which is expected to close its mega-merger with Warner Bros. Discovery on Oct. 6 — as co-CEO of the new company, Paramount announced. As chairman and CEO, Ellison will lead all strategy, creative and technology functions. […]
content:
Ynon Kreiz, who is stepping down as CEO of Mattel after eight years, will join David Ellison’s Paramount — which is expected to close its mega-merger with Warner Bros. Discovery on Oct. 6 — as co-CEO of the new company, Paramount announced.

As chairman and CEO, Ellison will lead all strategy, creative and technology functions. Kreiz, as co-CEO, will oversee the company’s day-to-day operations and integration of the combined businesses. It’s a “pairing that joins complementary skillsets to amplify results,” Paramount said in announcing the appointment Wednesday. The businesses of the combined company (whose name has not yet been announced) will report jointly to both Ellison and Kreiz.

Kreiz will start at Paramount on Oct. 5, 2026, as co-CEO. He also will join the company’s board of directors.

Popular on Variety

News of Kreiz’s hiring came shortly after Paramount cleared the final step before it could close the $111 billion Warner Bros. Discovery merger when a judge approved the company’s settlement of the antitrust lawsuit brought by 12 state attorneys general. The merger is expected to close Oct. 6, according to Paramount regulatory filings.

Ellison’s appointment of Kreiz “caps a long-term plan: pursue both Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery, then partner with a leading executive of his caliber to integrate, operationalize and manage the businesses as they build one of the most ambitious next-generation media companies in the industry’s history,” according to Paramount’s announcement.

One source close to the situation told Variety said that Ellison’s courting of Kreiz has been in the works for months and was “another ace up Ellison’s sleeve.”

Ellison, in a companywide memo Wednesday about Kreiz’s appointment, wrote, “We still have work to do before the [Warner Bros.] deal closes, and nothing changes until it does. But I wanted you to hear this from me first. I hope you’re as excited as I am to welcome Ynon to our leadership team.”

Ellison said in a statement: “Bringing together Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery to create a next-generation global media company is a transformational moment for our industry. Leading it takes a rare combination of strategic vision, operational depth and experience running a public company at the highest levels of media. Ynon brings all three. In Ynon, I’m adding a partner with strong leadership and the operating firepower this integration demands. It’s a division of labor built on our complementary strengths, with clear reporting lines and it lets me focus where I can contribute most: long-term strategy, the company’s overall creative direction, talent relationships, strategic partnerships, technology and capital allocation. We’re like-minded, we see this business the same way and there’s no one I’d rather partner with. Together we’ll build one integrated company that is creator-first, tech-forward and built to scale globally.”

Kreiz said in a statement provided by Paramount: “I’m excited to partner with David to build the next-generation media and entertainment company — bringing together premium content and iconic brands at the highest quality and scale, serving global audiences across every entertainment vertical and distribution platform. David is a unique talent and executive: a rare blend of business acumen, creative instinct, and clear vision. I very much share that vision, and I’m inspired by what we can accomplish together. The industry is at an inflection point, demanding evolution, investment, and a willingness to rethink business models. I look forward to working with the leadership team to build a cohesive global entertainment platform — one that stands out with best-in-class operations and execution powered by technology, with unparalleled creative relationships, production capabilities, and global reach. We will continue empowering creators, make this company a greenfield for innovation and storytelling, and collaborate with key partners to reach and engage fans worldwide.”

Gerry Cardinale, founder and managing partner of RedBird Capital Partners — Paramount’s co-controlling shareholder and a member of its board of directors — praised Ellison’s ability to lead the company through two “historic acquisitions.” In August 2025, Skydance Media closed the deal to acquire Paramount Global. Cardinale added that Ellison has at the same time been “running the business and building a team that’s already exceeding our synergy targets, beating our financial metrics, and never wavering on our commitment to the creative community.”

Mattel earlier Wednesday announced that Kreiz will step down as chairman and CEO effective Oct. 2, “to take a senior leadership position at another public company.” Roger Lynch, Condé Nast’s CEO, has been named Mattel’s next CEO.

Kreiz, a veteran media exec, is the former chairman and CEO of Maker Studios, a YouTube-oriented digital content network acquired by Disney in 2014. Kreiz exited Disney in 2016 and joined Mattel in 2018. From 2008-11, he served as chairman and CEO of Endemol Group, and before that was a general partner at venture-capital firm Balderton Capital (formerly Benchmark Capital Europe) from 2005-07. Earlier in his career, Kreiz co-founded and was chairman and CEO of Fox Kids Europe.

Mattel has credited Kreiz with boosting its market share across key toy categories, ranking No. 1 globally in dolls, vehicles, and infant, toddler and preschool segments. Mattel also noted that Kreiz oversaw Mattel Studios’ first theatrical release, “Barbie” starring Margot Robbie, which was the top global box office film of 2023 and has stood as Warner Bros. Pictures’ highest-grossing movie of all time.

Said Cardinale, “Ynon has spent his career at the intersection of media, technology and franchise-building — pairing extraordinary storytelling with the technology to deliver it to fans everywhere. He understands not just how fans connect with the IP they love, but the economics that make entertainment endure. Great leaders accomplish great things. Historic ones know when to bring in the right partner to make it last — and that’s what David has done. It’s exactly why the company will have the operational firepower and the cutting-edge leadership to win.”

Along with Kreiz, the leadership of the combined Paramount-WBD is already taking shape. Casey Bloys, head of WBD’s HBO, is poised to assume oversight of the combined Paramount-Warner Bros. streaming business after Cindy Holland announced Tuesday she was stepping down from her role running Paramount+ and other direct-to-consumer.

title: Macklemore Announces Free Palestine Tour “Sold Out Immediately,” Lineup Coming Soon
summary: As Ed Sheeran was forced to cancel shows over severe weather, Macklemore quickly sold out his Free Palestine Tour. On Wednesday, the 4x Grammy winner revealed that all three shows on his tour in support of Palestinians “sold out immediately” after he announced the tour last week. “I’m honestly blown away. We put these shows […]
content:
As Ed Sheeran was forced to cancel shows over severe weather, Macklemore quickly sold out his Free Palestine Tour.

On Wednesday, the 4x Grammy winner revealed that all three shows on his tour in support of Palestinians “sold out immediately” after he announced the tour last week.

“I’m honestly blown away. We put these shows together fast and in community, believing that musicians can stand in solidarity with Palestine, use the stage to raise funds and show what collective action can look like,” he wrote on Instagram. “When those in power try to silence our calls for liberation, art will always be a form of resistance.”

Macklemore continued, “Dublin, Paris and London, thank you for showing up the way you did. The response to these shows is another reminder of how many people across the world are standing together for a free Palestine. Lineups coming soon. Can’t wait to be together.”

Watch on Deadline

Last week, Macklemore announced the Free Palestine Tour, which is “supporting the Palestinian people and movement,” running 10/26-10/30 in Dublin, Paris and London.

Sheeran dropped Macklemore from his tour earlier this month amid an outcry around the opener’s “Free Palestine” onstage remarks. Opting to remain publicly neutral on the issue, Sheeran subsequently released a statement saying it was the “promoter’s decision” after Gillette Stadium owner Robert Kraft assembled several of the tour venues to give him an ultimatum.

Following the statement, fellow tour openers Finneas, Aaron Rowe and Lukas Graham dropped out of the tour, along with Sheeran’s backing band Beoga.

Meanwhile, protesters gathered outside the Philly stop of Sheeran’s Loop Tour to call him out for dropping Macklemore, as he apologized onstage.

title: Joachim Rønning Sets Horror Film ‘System’ With Spooky Pictures & Image Nation Studios
summary: Joachim Rønning, the Norwegian filmmaker most recently at the helm of Tron: Ares, has set up his next film, the horror flick System, with Spooky Pictures and Image Nation Studios. Currently in production in London, System‘s plot isn’t being disclosed. Unusually, its cast will remain under wraps, as well. Rønning is directing from his own […]
content:
Joachim Rønning, the Norwegian filmmaker most recently at the helm of Tron: Ares, has set up his next film, the horror flick System, with Spooky Pictures and Image Nation Studios.

Currently in production in London, System‘s plot isn’t being disclosed. Unusually, its cast will remain under wraps, as well.

Rønning is directing from his own script co-written with brother Andreas Rønning. He’s also producing the film via his banner The Saga Company. Under a multi-title partnership with Image Nation, Spooky Pictures’ Roy Lee (Weapons, It) and Steven Schneider (Paranormal Activity, Insidious) are also producing. Image Nation Studios CEO Ben Ross (Watcher, Company) and Spooky Pictures’ Rami Yasin (Hokum) are exec producing.

UTA Independent Film Group arranged the financing and is repping sales.

Watch on Deadline

Rønning broke out with the Academy Award-nominated Kon-Tiki, directed with Espen Sandberg, before going on to Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Men Tell No Tales, Maleficent: Mistress of Evil and Young Woman and the Sea — all for Disney, as was Tron: Ares. He is represented by UTA and Sloane, Offer, Weber & Dern.

Previously, Spooky Pictures and Image Nation Studios have partnered on genre projects including Late Night with the Devil, Charlie Polinger’s The Plague, Hokum starring Adam Scott, Casey Affleck’s Company and Guy Nattiv’s The Liberation. Most recently, they announced the SCP Foundation flick V/H/S: SCP with A24.

title: Neon Counters A24’s SCP Foundation Movie With “Open-Source” Project To Release Under Creative Commons License
summary: Earlier this month, we scooped A24’s acquisition of an SCP Foundation movie from Spooky Pictures and Image Nation Studios, intended to bring one of the internet’s largest fan-built horror and sci-fi universes to the big screen for the first time. The announcement ruffled feathers, precipitating a unique form of drama. Within hours, we heard from […]
content:
Earlier this month, we scooped A24’s acquisition of an SCP Foundation movie from Spooky Pictures and Image Nation Studios, intended to bring one of the internet’s largest fan-built horror and sci-fi universes to the big screen for the first time.

The announcement ruffled feathers, precipitating a unique form of drama. Within hours, we heard from a group known as the SCP Foundation Wiki Licensing Team, which expressed concerns about the possibility of the studio claiming exclusive rights to a project based on community-generated IP with very specific licensing requirements.

Now, Neon has countered A24 with an SCP Foundation project that is expressly taking the group’s concerns into account. Development on this project was in motion before the A24 announcement, we’re told.

Watch on Deadline

Created in 2008, the SCP Wiki is a collaborative speculative fiction website revolving around the SCP Foundation, a secretive organization that secures and contains anomalous or supernatural items and entities to protect humanity as well as the anomalies themselves. Over its nearly two decades of existence and with thousands of contributors, the site has built an engaged, global fanbase and has inspired short films, web series and games.

Acknowledging the communal roots of the project, Neon is approaching its SCP Foundation movie as an “open-source horror project” slated for release in theaters against A24’s next year. Who specifically will contribute to Neon’s version, and which will make it to theaters first, is not yet clear.

Neon expressed its commitment to releasing its film and related materials under the Creative Commons license CC BY-SA, meaning that they will not permanently control the film. Other creators will be able to copy, share, screen, build on or adapt the film — even commercially — under the Creative Commons license, provided that they credit the SCP creators and filmmakers, release their own adaptations under the same license, and avoid claims to an exclusive distribution arrangement.

Neon has been in communication the SCP Wiki team to ensure the film’s distribution does not deviate from their mission and licensing guidelines.

News of the rival SCP Foundation movie comes following production wrap on 4 X 4: The Event, rising genre filmmaker Alex Ullom’s second horror film for Neon on the heels of this summer’s It Ends. Other recent and upcoming in-house productions include Osgood Perkins’ The Young People; David Robert Mitchell’s They Follow; Matt Johnson’s The Vice Guide; and Arie and Chuko Esiri’s Clarissa.

Coming off the release of Na Hong-jin’s Cannes monster flick Hope, Neon’s slate for the rest of the year includes fellow awards candidates like Fjord, Paper Tiger, Artificial and A Place in Hell, among other titles.

title: ‘Nobody Wants This’ Rabbi Consultant Slams Adam Brody As An “Ignorant Jew” Over “Free Palestine” Support
summary: Following his public support of “Free Palestine,” Adam Brody is facing backlash not only from viewers, but a recent colleague. Ahead of Season 3 of Nobody Wants This, premiering Oct. 22 on Netflix, the show’s former technical consultant, Rabbi Steve Leder, slammed the 2x Golden Globe-nominated actor as an “ignorant Jew” for referring to Israel’s […]
content:
Following his public support of “Free Palestine,” Adam Brody is facing backlash not only from viewers, but a recent colleague.

Ahead of Season 3 of Nobody Wants This, premiering Oct. 22 on Netflix, the show’s former technical consultant, Rabbi Steve Leder, slammed the 2x Golden Globe-nominated actor as an “ignorant Jew” for referring to Israel’s attack on Gaza as a genocide.

“Hi Adam, you might not remember me. My name is Rabbi Steve Leder, and I was the technical advisor for Season 1 of Nobody Wants This,” he prefaced in the video. “My job was to make sure that your character was authentic and that everything in Season 1 about Judaism was authentic.”

In Nobody Wants This, agnostic podcaster Joanne Williams (Kristen Bell) begins an unexpected romance with Rabbi Noah Roklov (Brody), which shakes both their families as Joanne immerses herself in Noah’s culture and decides to convert to Judaism.

Watch on Deadline

Leder continued, “Your pronouncement the other day about a genocide in Gaza was truly shocking, not only because of your misuse and mischaracterization of the word ‘genocide’—there is no genocide in Gaza, there are genocides happening in other countries happening but you failed to mention any of them. You, by your own admission are a relatively ignorant Jew, and your ignorance really showed the other day.

“If you’re gonna use a word like ‘genocide,’ you oughta know what it means. And by the way, being so flippant about a word like ‘genocide’—’hey put me down for [thinking it’s a] genocide’ like you’re asking for a table for two at Craig’s is disgusting,” he added. “Here’s some more technical advice; if you nothing about something, you should say nothing about it.”

Since Israel’s ongoing strikes on Gaza in the wake of Hamas’ Oct. 7, 2023 attack, multiple organizations have classified Israel’s actions as a genocide against Palestinians, including the United Nations, Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch.

Last week, Brody told GQ, “Put me down as thinking it’s a genocide. Put me down as wanting a free Palestine. It’s awful that it’s taken so much death and misery, but it does feel like it’s reaching a breaking point that it should have a while ago. I’m hopeful that another administration can really do some good and correct some of these policies that are helping that situation be as awful as it is.”

Brody’s comments came after several of his Hollywood peers were among around 100 arrested outside the United Nations General Assembly in New York City, where they were protesting the arrival of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu last Thursday.

title: ‘His & Hers’ Team Developing Alice Feeney’s Next Book ‘Twist’ As Series With Fifth Season
summary: EXCLUSIVE: His & Hers became one of Netflix’s most-watched series ever after launching earlier this year. The team behind the Jon Bernthal and Tessa Thompson-led thriller have once again teamed with Fifth Season to adapt the next book from His & Hers author Alice Feeney. William Oldroyd will return to write and direct a series […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: His & Hers became one of Netflix’s most-watched series ever after launching earlier this year.

The team behind the Jon Bernthal and Tessa Thompson-led thriller have once again teamed with Fifth Season to adapt the next book from His & Hers author Alice Feeney.

William Oldroyd will return to write and direct a series based on Feeney’s upcoming book Twist, which is being published at the start of next year. He has teamed up with Fifth Season, which will serve as the studio, Kristen Campo’s Campout Productions, Jessica Chastain and Kelly Carmichael’s Freckle Films, Bill Dubuque and Thompson’s Viva Maude, to develop it as a series.

Twist is a thriller about love, marriage, murder, and revenge. It centers around a flight attendant living a double life with two different husbands and a murder that shatters their lives. Told across dual POVs, the story twists and unravels as secrets surface, in a marriage thriller that asks if we can ever really know the person we marry.

Watch on Deadline

The book will be published in the U.S. in February 2027 from Macmillian Publishers.

His & Hers, which premiered on Netflix in January, was the streamer’s most-watched show of the first half this year, receiving 104M views globally from its launch through to the end of June.

The series starred Thompson, who also executive produced, as a former news anchor, who returns to her small town in Georgia to report on a murder and ends up clashing with her ex-husband, played by Bernthal.

Feeney has been busy optioning her work for TV and film; Deadline revealed earlier this year that Downton Abbey and All Her Fault producer Carnival Films was adapting her book My Husband’s Wife and Beautiful Ugly in in the works as a film from the producers of The Housemaid. Her debut novel Sometimes I Lie was set up at Warner Bros. TV in 2019 with Sarah Michelle Gellar set to star.

Twist exec producers include Oldroyd, Campo, Chastain, Dubuque, Thompson, Kelly Carmichael and Kishori Rajan.

“Twist gives us the opportunity to reunite an extraordinary creative team around yet another brilliant, gripping thriller from Alice Feeney,” said Noah Greenshner, EVP, Head of TV Creative for Fifth Season. “The incredible success of His & Hers demonstrated what this group can accomplish together, and we’re thrilled to continue that relationship with Alice, William, and Bill, as well as our partners at Campout Productions, Freckle Films, and Viva Maude.”

Feeney added, “Having had such a wonderful experience with His & Hers, it was a very easy decision to get the band back together for Twist. It feels like a dream come true. I love this book, I love this team, and I can’t wait to see these characters come to life on screen.”

Oldroyd is represented by WME and Johnson Shapiro Slewett & Kole. Feeney is represented by WME and Curtis Brown.

title: Mark Ruffalo Says Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger Will ‘Stifle Creativity’ and ‘Weaken Free Speech’: It ‘Should Never Have Been Approved’
summary: Mark Ruffalo is speaking out against the Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger once again, this time following the news on Wednesday that the deal has been approved and is tentatively set to close next week. “This merger will stifle creativity, weaken free speech, and cost people their jobs — it is a bad deal for this country […]
content:
Mark Ruffalo is speaking out against the Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger once again, this time following the news on Wednesday that the deal has been approved and is tentatively set to close next week.

“This merger will stifle creativity, weaken free speech, and cost people their jobs — it is a bad deal for this country and should never have been approved,” wrote Ruffalo in a statement posted to Threads on Wednesday. “This is an incredibly disappointing outcome for the hundreds of thousands of us who stood up to block it, but it’s also not the end. This grassroots movement isn’t going to fade away and neither is our resolve.”

He continued: “This was never about just one merger: this was about fighting back against corrupt oligarch billionaires trampling the interests of everyday people to line their own pockets. We’re still in that fight. Join us.”

Popular on Variety

Ruffalo has long been outspoken about his opposition to the merger. Earlier this month, Ruffalo encouraged California Attorney General Rob Bonta and his coalition of 11 other state AGs not to settle their lawsuit against Paramount Skydance, which would effectively keep David Ellison from acquiring Warner Bros. Discovery.

“Don’t you dare, [Rob Bonta], do not cave,” Ruffalo wrote on X. “5,670 filmmakers put their necks on the line for you to fight this merger. Another 75,000+ and counting have signed to tell you not to concede in just 3 weeks. You work for the people — the very people who will be hurt if you let this lousy deal filled with empty promises go forward. Please sign to send a message to the AGs and Paramount. Reject the deal. The people don’t want it!”

title: Satyajit Ray Film by Srijit Mukherji, New Feluda and Eken Mysteries Lead Bengali Streamer Hoichoi’s 10th Anniversary Slate
summary: A Satyajit Ray film from Srijit Mukherji heads a lineup of more than 25 series, films and TV titles that Bengali streamer Hoichoi has set for its 10th year. The slate also brings new cases for detectives Feluda and Eken Babu and the platform’s first animated series. In “Maharaja Tomare Selam,” Ray agrees to his […]
content:
A Satyajit Ray film from Srijit Mukherji heads a lineup of more than 25 series, films and TV titles that Bengali streamer Hoichoi has set for its 10th year. The slate also brings new cases for detectives Feluda and Eken Babu and the platform’s first animated series.

In “Maharaja Tomare Selam,” Ray agrees to his son’s request to make a children’s film. He then battles money trouble, resistance from the industry and the pressure of his own reputation on the road to what would become a classic of Indian cinema, “Goopy Gyne Bagha Byne.” Jeetu Kamal, Ritwik Bhowmik, Rudranil Ghosh, Sairity Banerjee, Shatakshy Nandy and Arijit Dutta star.

The Hoichoi Studio film lineup also includes “The Eken: Kerala-e Kurukshetra,” directed by Joydeep Mukherjee. In it, a botched secret mission drags Eken Babu into a mystery in Kerala. Anirban Chakrabarti, Ritwick Chakraborty, Raima Sen, Somak Ghosh, Suhotra Mukhopadhyay, Ambarish Bhattacharya, Arna Mukhopadhyay, Subrat Dutta and Kamaleswar Mukherjee make up the cast.

Popular on Variety

Parambrata Chatterjee directs and appears in “Jononi,” about a college professor who goes looking for her housekeeper’s missing teenage daughter and finds secrets closer to home. Koel Mallick, Koneenica Banerjee and Joy Sengupta also star. Debaloy Bhattacharya’s “Bhugun,” starring Abhishek Banerjee and Parno Mittra, follows a wealthy Bengali family whose deal with a tantric to restore its fortune brings down a deadly curse.

On the series side, Kamaleswar Mukherjee directs “Feludar Goyendagiri: Baksho Rawhoshyo,” in which Feluda chases the secret of a box swapped during a train journey. Tota Roy Choudhury, Kalpan Mitra and Subhadip Chakrabarti star. Other returning franchises include “Birangana 2,” “Kuheli 2,” “Thakumar Jhuli 2,” “Tansener Tanpura: Mohonbashi” with Vikram Chatterjee, and “Choddobeshi 2,” created by and starring Parambrata Chatterjee. He also directs “Agambagish: Drolmar Khorgo,” starring Saswata Chatterjee. In it, the tantric saint Krishnananda Agambagish takes on a band of ghostly dacoits in 17th-century Bengal.

New series include Pratim D. Gupta’s “Chaalchitro: The Ekchala Murders,” about a serial killer who leaves female victims posed as goddesses in the run-up to Durga Puja. It stars Tota Roy Choudhury, Anirban Chakrabarti, Chanchal Chowdhury and Sweta Mishra. Raima Sen leads “Kumari,” created by Sahana Dutta. Ayan Chakraborti’s “Shrimoti Not Out,” starring Ananya Chatterjee and Joy Sengupta, follows a 48-year-old woman who learns she is pregnant just as her son is about to marry. Mimi Chakraborty headlines Aditi Roy’s “Uttoron: Charulata,” and Sabyasachi Chowdhury stars in “Detective Tarinicharan,” a murder mystery set in colonial Darjeeling.

Rounding out the series slate are “Debipokkho,” “Kauriburir Mandir,” “Mangolik,” “Konya,” “Shoti,” “Jujuma” and “Kanamachhi.” Sanglap Bhowmick directs the animated “Shri Ramkrishna,” which traces the life of spiritual master Ramakrishna Paramahansa. On TV, Madhumita Sarcar and Arjun Chakrabarty star in “Katha-Amrito,” and Trina Saha stars in “Sholaka Rawhoshyo.” The streamer is also continuing to back Bangladeshi creators and productions.

“For me, 10 years of Hoichoi is not just about the number of shows we have made or the milestones we have crossed. It is about the stories, characters and creators that have stayed with people and, in many ways, become part of Bengali popular culture,” said Soumya Mukherjee, COO of Hoichoi. “When we started, the ambition was simply to create a home for Bengali stories. Ten years later, that belief remains the same, but the possibilities around those stories have become much bigger. We have seen Bengali IP grow beyond the screen it was created for, through adaptations, licensing, theatrical, partnerships, new formats and, increasingly, our stories are traveling beyond Bengal and beyond language.”

Hoichoi’s library now holds more than 600 Bengali films and over 200 original series, watched in India, Bangladesh and overseas. Beyond subscriptions, it makes money from licensing, branded content, theatrical releases and distribution deals. It has also moved onto technology it built itself.

Newer bets include Hoichoi FM, which carries original audio fiction inside the app, and Sooper, a microdrama venture working across languages and markets. The company is also testing AI tools for development and production through LoglineAI.

Vishnu Mohta, co-founder of Hoichoi and LoglineAI, said the first decade had been about proving a language-first platform could build a meaningful global business. “The next decade is about expanding what that platform can become,” Mohta said. “Technology, AI and new formats are opening up possibilities that simply didn’t exist when we started. Our ambition is to use those possibilities without losing the cultural instinct and storytelling sensibility that made Hoichoi what it is.”

title: Bradley Whitford on Bringing Back ‘The West Wing’ as a ‘Limited Series’
summary: Bradley Whitford is ready to return to the White House. The actor tells me that it may be time to bring back “The West Wing” as a “limited series of some kind.” Series creator Aaron Sorkin has had fans chomping at the bit ever since he told Variety’s Michael Schneider he was inspired to write […]
content:
Bradley Whitford is ready to return to the White House.

The actor tells me that it may be time to bring back “The West Wing” as a “limited series of some kind.”

Series creator Aaron Sorkin has had fans chomping at the bit ever since he told Variety’s Michael Schneider he was inspired to write more episodes while attending a 25th anniversary of the show at the White House in 2024. “I just got a couple of ideas for episodes just walking around the White House,” Sorkin said at the time. “Like, ‘why didn’t we ever do this? Why didn’t we ever do that?’”

Whitford inspired a “West Wing” reunion earlier today when his fellow castmates Martin Sheen, Dulé Hill, Mary McCormack and Josh Malina joined him at the unveiling of his star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame.

Popular on Variety

“I’ll work him, I’ll work him,” Whitford said of trying to get Sorkin to commit.

Bradley Whitford says he’ll “work” Aaron Sorkin on bringing back “The West Wing” and thinks the time may be right for a “limited series of some kind.” pic.twitter.com/eqFkT5T66k — Variety (@Variety) September 30, 2026

Hill said the cast wouldn’t hesitate if Sorkin decides to write a new season. “I always say that’s a question for Aaron Sorkin,” he said when asked about a revival. “If he writes it, then I will come. I think if he writes it, then we all will be there.”

However, Hill continued, “Sometimes I wonder though where things are in the world. Things are so outlandish, I don’t know how you dramatize any of that. With him writing, it would be a lovely thing to hopefully steer the collective consciousness of our society back toward humanity and connectivity and understanding.”

Dulé Hill says the “West Wing” cast is ready to return if Aaron Sorkin decides to write a new season: “We all will be there.”



via Bradley Whitford’s Hollywood Walk of Fame ceremony pic.twitter.com/xde3oQceuY — Variety (@Variety) September 30, 2026

“The West Wing” premiered on NBC in 1999 and ran for seven seasons before ending in 2006. The ensemble also included Rob Lowe, Allison Janney, Richard Schiff, John Spencer, Janel Moloney and Stockard Channing.

The series won 27 Emmy Awards from 95 nominations.

If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

The 2026 Formula 1 season takes a bit of a detour this weekend as the drivers head to the F1 Bahrain Grand Prix — but not in actual Bahrain.

The annual race in the Kingdom of Bahrain has been moved to Malaysia for this weekend, following uncertainties in the Middle East triggered by President Trump’s war in Iran. Now officially known as the “2026 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia,” the race takes place this Sunday, Oct. 4 live from the Sepang International Circuit in the Southeast Asian country.

The official starting time for the Bahrain Grand Prix is at 3 p.m. Malaysia time (3 a.m. ET/12 a.m. PT). Apple TV is the official U.S. streaming home for Formula 1 and viewers can tune into the race through the Apple TV website or app (Amazon Prime members can also add Apple TV to their streaming channels here).

While Apple TV now costs $14.99/month after a recent price hike, this weekend’s F1 race is free to watch online on the streamer. Fans can watch the practice rounds, qualifying and Sunday’s race online for free, with no subscription required. Apple says the race weekend is part of Apple TV’s previously announced plan to make select races and practice sessions available free to fans throughout the season.

Apple TV is streaming the F1 Bahrain Grand Prix in 4K with Dolby Vision and immersive 5.1 surround sound. Note: you’ll need a streaming device that supports 4K content in order to get the 4K feed.

title: Golden Globes Predictions: Let the Genre Games Begin for ‘Obsession,’ ‘Michael,’ ‘Wildwood’ and More
summary: Variety Awards Circuit section is the home for all awards news and related content throughout the year, featuring the following: the official predictions for the upcoming Oscars, Emmys, Grammys and Tony Awards ceremonies, curated by Variety chief awards editor Clayton Davis. The prediction pages reflect the current standings in the race and do not reflect […]
content:
Variety Awards Circuit section is the home for all awards news and related content throughout the year, featuring the following: the official predictions for the upcoming Oscars, Emmys, Grammys and Tony Awards ceremonies, curated by Variety chief awards editor Clayton Davis. The prediction pages reflect the current standings in the race and do not reflect personal preferences for any individual contender. As other formal (and informal) polls suggest, competitions are fluid and subject to change in response to buzz and events. Predictions are updated every Thursday.

Explore Awards Circuit Predictions Pages

Oscars | Emmys | Grammys | Tonys

Zendaya in “Dune Part Three” Warner Bros.

Golden Globes Predictions Commentary (Updated: Sept. 30, 2026): The Golden Globes submission deadline is coming up on Oct. 30, the night before Halloween. Fitting, since for the next 30 days, studios get to decide what costume their movies should wear for the early phase of awards season.

The Globes split their top film prize into two genres, drama and comedy/musical and the line between them has always been drawn by strategy as much as tone. Remember, this is the same awards show that “The Martian” once won best comedy.

For the third year in a row, the comedy/musical side looks more competitive than its drama counterpart. We’re used to seeing it the other way around, and several major players still haven’t declared.

On the drama side, Christopher Nolan’s summer blockbuster “The Odyssey” and “La Bola Negra,” the acclaimed epic from Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi (better known as Los Javis), lead the early pack. The Netflix title picked up the People’s Choice Award at the Toronto International Film Festival this month, four months after the duo won best director at Cannes. That bodes well for its run.

The race is still waiting on first reviews for a couple of contenders in the wings. Sources tell Variety that Denis Villeneuve’s “Dune: Part Three” held its first intimate, small-group screenings this past week. Early word is very positive.

And on Friday, the New York Film Festival unveils Tony Gilroy’s “Behemoth!” as its centerpiece selection, with Pedro Pascal as a former child prodigy cellist. Searchlight releases it Dec. 4, and it could make for an interesting addition to the race.

No studio has a trickier sorting job than Amazon MGM Studios this year. It holds three contenders that could all plausibly claim the drama side: Phil Lord and Chris Miller’s “Project Hail Mary” with Ryan Gosling, Peter Farrelly’s “I Play Rocky,” which finished first runner-up for TIFF’s People’s Choice Award and Bassam Tariq’s critically acclaimed “Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother,” the Orion Pictures release starring Mahershala Ali as a devout hitman.

“Your Mother” is all but certain to run in drama. So expect at least one of the other two to go the comedy route, if only to keep the studio from splitting its own vote. Our bet is “Hail Mary” goes comedy, and “Rocky” goes drama.

Focus Features has a choice to make with “Obsession,” Curry Barker’s micro-budget possession thriller that has grossed more than $400 million worldwide. If the studio follows the “Get Out” (2017) and “The Substance” (2024) playbooks, many expect a comedy push. But assess the landscape, especially for breakout star Inde Navarrette, who looks primed for a best actress Oscar nom as a possessed young woman and this pundit starts to wonder — wouldn’t a drama run make more sense?

“Obsession” will likely find recognition in cinematic and box office achievement, and Navarrette should be nominated on either side of the house. Its best picture prospects face far steeper hurdles. I think the real question is where can she win?

Sandra Hüller in “Fatherland” and “Rose” Mubi

Drama actress is less stacked than usual. The only presumed threat to win is Sandra Hüller, who arrives with a double dose of Paweł Pawlikowski’s “Fatherland” and Markus Schleinzer’s “Rose,” which earned her the best leading performance prize in Berlin. On the comedy side, most pundits and analysts see the trophy as preordained for Julianne Moore’s towering work in Jesse Eisenberg’s beloved “The Debut.” Navarrette would also have to contend with Olivia Wilde in “The Invite,” a film poised to be a big player across the board.

A drama win would position the 25-year-old Latina breakout as the alternative to Moore, and recent history shows what that moment can do. In each of the past two years, a Globes lead drama winner was someone the Actor Awards (formerly SAG) had passed over: Fernanda Torres for “I’m Still Here” and Wagner Moura for “The Secret Agent.” Both used the win as a springboard into nomination voting and landed Oscar noms. SAG voters have long been resistant to non-English-language performances. Let Hüller, whose two contenders are both in German, walk away with drama actress and she inherits that narrative.

UPDATE: Variety has confirmed that “Obsession” will be submitted as a comedy at the Globes.

Antoine Fuqua’s “Michael,” starring Jaafar Jackson and the first biopic ever to cross $1 billion worldwide, is also awaiting an official decision and it can go either way based on Globes history. “Bohemian Rhapsody” (2018) and Baz Luhrmann’s “Elvis” (2022) were embraced as dramas, and both won lead actor there. “Ray” (2004) and “Walk the Line” (2005) went comedy/musical and did the same. Among other music-driven films, “A Star Is Born” (2018) found love as a drama, while “Inside Llewyn Davis” (2013) went comedy. There’s no rhyme or reason, so anything can happen. We think a comedy/musical run is ultimately in the cards for “Michael,” alongside a run in cinematic and box office achievement. But again, anything can still happen.

Speaking of box office, what many may not realize is that films must officially submit for the category. Nothing lands on the ballot automatically, and at the 2025 Globes, Villeneuve’s team opted to keep “Dune: Part Two” out of the box office race and vie only for best picture (drama), where it landed a nomination.

We’re keeping that in mind for the final chapter. “Dune: Part Three” opens Dec. 18, the same day as Marvel’s “Avengers: Doomsday” and both will have enough presales to qualify, should their studios choose to enter. The hurdle is the calendar. Motion picture nomination ballots go out to voters Nov. 24 and are due back Dec. 4, and Dec. 2 is the final date for film press conferences and uploads to the Globes’ screening platform. In practical terms, either movie would have to show itself to the several hundred voting journalists more than two weeks before opening day. Based on how Marvel has handled prerelease screenings in the past, I wouldn’t expect “Doomsday” to open its doors that early. “Dune 3” is far more likely to play in those stakes. So in other words, don’t assume anything.

Another development worth watching for is several studios are taking their animated feature contenders seriously enough to push well beyond that single category.

Laika is gearing up for a huge push behind Travis Knight’s “Wildwood,” and the stop-motion studio isn’t settling for an animated feature nom. It’s trying to change the conversation around animated movies, which too often get dismissed as “kids’ fare.” At 132 minutes, “Wildwood” is billed as the longest stop-motion feature ever made and it’s Laika’s first PG-13 release. After a Telluride conversation earlier this month with Knight and six-time Oscar-nominated cinematographer Caleb Deschanel, the studio previewed selected scenes at SCAD AnimationFest last week. The film world premieres at the BFI London Film Festival on Oct. 11, then opens AFI Fest as its U.S. premiere on Oct. 21, two days before Fathom Entertainment releases it in theaters. Sources tell Variety that in addition to animated feature, Laika plans to submit “Wildwood” for best picture (drama). The Globes reopened their top categories to animation in 2021, but the three animated films to win a top Globe (“Beauty and the Beast,” “The Lion King” and “Toy Story 2” ) all did it in comedy/musical, long before that. A drama bid is new terrain, but it also sends the message: take animation seriously.

And Laika does have some Globes history on its side with “Missing Link” pulling off an upset win for animated feature in 2020, coincidentally over “Toy Story 4,” which ultimately won the Oscar.

“Wildwood” won’t be alone. Independent Film Company’s “Tangles,” Leah Nelson’s hand-drawn adaptation of Sarah Leavitt’s graphic memoir about her mother’s Alzheimer’s, is also expected to vie in drama. The biographical Cannes sensation boasts a powerhouse producing team that includes Julia Louis-Dreyfus and Seth Rogen (destined to be an acting nominee for “The Invite”).

Every placement will ripple into the lead acting races, which the Globes also split by genre. If “Hail Mary” goes comedy, Gosling heads to the side of the house where he won his only Globe, for “La La Land.” A comedy/musical run for “Michael” gives Jackson’s screen debut a friendlier lane than drama, which is filling up fast.

Robert Pattinson in “Primetime,” “The Odyssey,” “Dune: Part Three” and “The Drama” A24 / Universal Pictures / Warner Bros.

Start with Robert Pattinson, who has four movies in theaters this year — “The Drama,” “The Odyssey,” “Primetime” and “Dune: Part Three.” How many noms can he collect? For now, his turn as “To Catch a Predator” host Chris Hansen in Lance Oppenheim’s “Primetime” looks like his easiest path, in actor (drama), with “The Odyssey” offering another option in supporting actor alongside his co-star John Leguizamo. The front-runners in the actor (drama) category are Andrew Scott, playing the late Ian Charleson in Simon Stone’s “Elsinore” and Pattinson’s “Odyssey” co-star Matt Damon. Behind them, John Turturro (“The Only Living Pickpocket in New York”), Pedro Pascal (“Behemoth!”), Sebastian Stan (“Fjord”) and Anthony Ippolito (“I Play Rocky”) will fight for spots.

Pattinson isn’t the only big name with more than one ticket to the Hollywood party. Penélope Cruz is also in the hunt with two possible supporting actress bids, for “The Invite” and “La Bola Negra,” plus an actress (drama) play for Florian Zeller’s “Bunker,” opposite her real-life husband, Javier Bardem, who could join her with a drama actor nom of his own.

Wilde should find enough room for her performance in “The Invite,” in addition to a directing nom for it as well. Perhaps even a third, in supporting actress for “Behemoth!” if it catches on. What a year for her.

Hüller, meanwhile, can double up in drama actress with “Fatherland” and “Rose,” and she has a path in supporting actress for “Project Hail Mary” (and I guess “Digger?”). Nothing in the Globes rules stops a performer from landing two, three or four noms in the same year.

We’re also always looking for the Globes picks that come out of nowhere and breathe life into a campaign many had underestimated. Could Gemma Chan or Channing Tatum start supporting runs for Beth de Araújo’s “Josephine?” Could Globes favorite Scarlett Johansson get one going for James Gray’s “Paper Tiger?” And I keep circling Merritt Wever in “Primetime” as a possible nom-morning shocker. It would be well deserved.

Variety’s predictions in every film category follow below. Not all category placements are confirmed, and all are subject to change.

The 84th Golden Globe nominations will be announced Monday, Dec. 7, with the ceremony, hosted by Nikki Glaser, set for Sunday, Jan. 10, 2027.

Projected nomination leaders (films): “The Odyssey” (10); “The Debut” (7); “The Invite” and “La Bola Negra” (6); “Wild Horse Nine” (5); “Dune: Part Three,” “Fjord” and “Michael” (4)

The list of Oscar predictions in all categories can be found here.

Variety parent company Penske Media Corporation owns Golden Globes producer Dick Clark Prods. in a joint venture with Eldridge.

title: Mark Ruffalo Slams Approved ParaBros Merger: “Bad Deal For This Country”
summary: Mark Ruffalo has been one of the fiercest critics of the $111 billion Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery merger and after the deal became a reality today, the man who plays the Incredible Hulk in the MCU came out swinging. “This merger will stifle creativity, weaken free speech, and cost people their jobs — it […]
content:
Mark Ruffalo has been one of the fiercest critics of the $111 billion Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery merger and after the deal became a reality today, the man who plays the Incredible Hulk in the MCU came out swinging.

“This merger will stifle creativity, weaken free speech, and cost people their jobs — it is a bad deal for this country and should never have been approved,” the two-time Emmy winner and HBO regular said today after U.S. District Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín signed off on the antitrust settlement between te David Ellison run company and a dozen state Attorneys General.

“This is an incredibly disappointing outcome for the hundreds of thousands of us who stood up to block it, but it’s also not the end.”

Watch on Deadline

In a post, retweeting Deadline’s story on the approval,” Ruffalo added: “This grassroots movement isn’t going to fade away and neither is our resolve. This was never about just one merger: this was about fighting back against corrupt oligarch billionaires trampling the interests of everyday people to line their own pockets. We’re still in that fight. Join us.”

This merger will stifle creativity, weaken free speech, and cost people their jobs — it is a bad deal for this country and should never have been approved. This is an incredibly disappointing outcome for the hundreds of thousands of us who stood up to block it, but it's also not… — Mark Ruffalo (@MarkRuffalo) September 30, 2026

A close ally of Sen. Cory Booker (D-NJ) in rallying against the melding of the two historic Hollywood companies, and a very public advocate that California AG Rob Bonta “not cave” on the antitrust front, Ruffalo has also faced accusations of antisemitism for his critical remarks about weapons the Larry Ellison-founded Oracle provided to the Israeli military. A Paramount spokesperson late last month said of the Task star they are “troubled when antisemitic tropes are invoked in purported service of a business dispute.”

Ruffalo and outgoing California Gov, Gavin Newsom are known to have had words about the merger at the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards, where the actor was a nominee, on September 14. A week later, after several days of behind closed door talks between Bonta’s team and Para and WBD execs, a settlement was announced. Bemoaned by many as lacking all conviction, while being full of passionate intensity, to paraphrase William Butler Yeats, the agreement secured few concessions from the Ellisons that they had clearly been offering even before the much anticipated antitrust suit was filed on July 13.
