content:
EXCLUSIVE: Protagonists’s label Protagonist Picks is handling world sales on crime feature American Muscle, the directorial debut of Joel Veach.

David W. Thompson, Brendan Sexton III, Liana Wright-Mark, Gbenga Akinnagbe, Jorge Garcia, and Lauren Glazier star in the character-driven thriller which was shot entirely in Santa Clarita, California.

The film follows a debt-ridden mechanic (Thompson) desperate to escape his violent past. When his estranged sister returns and two ruthless debt collectors come looking for payment, long-buried family secrets resurface, setting the stage for an explosive reckoning.

The film has played at Cinequest, Big Apple Film Fest, and Burbank, and was nominated for Best Debut at Raindance. RSL Films and Ghost Gang Productions produce.

Watch on Deadline

Veach previously wrote the psychological thriller Old Man, starring Stephen Lang, and directed the short film Guys With Guns, which premiered at the Raindance Film Festival.

title: CNN Again Removed As TV Pooler Set To Travel With Donald Trump
summary: CNN will not be the TV pooler covering President Donald Trump’s trip to Texas and Oklahoma on Thursday, despite being listed on the schedule earlier in the week. The change signaled once again that the White House was restricting the network from certain access, namely travel on Air Force One. The network was scheduled to […]
content:
CNN will not be the TV pooler covering President Donald Trump‘s trip to Texas and Oklahoma on Thursday, despite being listed on the schedule earlier in the week.

The change signaled once again that the White House was restricting the network from certain access, namely travel on Air Force One. The network was scheduled to serve as the TV pool traveling with Trump to Tennessee last Saturday, but was removed from that assignment as well.

Trump banned CNN, MS NOW and Politico from access to the White House grounds last month. But less than a week later, a federal judge granted a temporary restraining order requiring access to be restored.

Although the networks are back in, the White House has continued to restrict CNN from certain gatherings with the president. The judge’s order had to do with access to the White House grounds and did not directly address whether Trump could bar outlets from areas like Air Force One and the Oval Office, where press availability is typically restricted to members of a smaller group of pool reporters.

Watch on Deadline

That said, attorneys for the three networks have cited the White House’s continued prohibitions on CNN as further examples of First Amendment retaliation. The networks are seeking a preliminary injunction that will prohibit the White House from denying access to three outlets on a longer term, typically until a trial is held or if a higher court issues a ruling on appeal.

Asked for comment, a White House official said, “President Trump is the most accessible President in history — holding open press events, regular gaggles and interviews, taking questions nearly every day, and speaking directly to the American people through social media. But if a reporter walks into an interview with their headline and narrative already decided, why do they need to be in the room? They can write their garbage from anywhere. Even after outlets were given access to the White House, they declined to cover various events proving this isn’t about access. It’s performative and dishonest.”

title: ‘Ebenezer’ Trailer: Johnny Depp Leads Ti West’s Dickens Remake
summary: UPDATE: Paramount has dropped the first full trailer for Ebenezer, starring Johnny Depp as Scrooge. Check it out above. PREVIOUS, July 23: Comic-Con got a double dose of three-time Oscar nominee Johnny Depp, who after showing up as Scrooge character on the streets of the Gaslamp district Thursday crashed Collider’s Directors on Directing panel in […]
content:
UPDATE: Paramount has dropped the first full trailer for Ebenezer, starring Johnny Depp as Scrooge. Check it out above.

PREVIOUS, July 23: Comic-Con got a double dose of three-time Oscar nominee Johnny Depp, who after showing up as Scrooge character on the streets of the Gaslamp district Thursday crashed Collider’s Directors on Directing panel in Hall H with the trailer for Ebenezer, the Ti West-directed holiday movie coming out November 13.

Hysterical is all we have to say: Depp is so method, you can’t even make out what he is saying, in complete mumble. That was apparent earlier today during his Gaslamp appearance — and Deadline was standing less than 12 feet in front of him.

Watch on Deadline

In Hall H, after hobbling on stage with a candle (“I’m speaking into the candle”), he handed it off to director John Francis Daley, who was sitting at the end of the dais. Depp’s Scrooge turned to the crowd and said, “Have you no lives? No responsibilities?”

Watch the trailer above. In looks it’s Tim Burton’s Sweeney Todd — very period, very dark gothic as you’d expect a Ti West title to be, and it’s the Scrooge you’ve never seen before (sorry, Bill Murray). We have Depp’s Ebenezer sinking in a bed, throwing snow balls at a couple. It’s very comical. The beginning credits drum up all the alter egos he’s played — i.e., Jack Sparrow, Edward Scissorhands — which have led to this.

Early on in the trailer, Depp’s Ebenezer turns to the camera and beams, “It’s good to be back.”

Johnny Depp takes the stage at Comic-Con as Ebenezer Scrooge, which he portrays in the upcoming film ‘Ebenezer’



‘Ebenezer’ releases in theaters November 13, 2026



More on his #SDCC appearance here: https://t.co/2EuAloBjla pic.twitter.com/kClfWx0QDQ — Deadline (@DEADLINE) July 23, 2026

Nathaniel Halpern adapted the Charles Dickens classic. The pic also stars Ian McKellen, Rupert Grint, Sam Claflin and Daisy Ridley.

Collider pulled off a surprise trailer in its first post-Covid Comic-Con panel in 2022 when Keanu Reeves crashed its panel with the first teaser for Lionsgate’s John Wick: Chapter 4.

title: ‘Lanterns’ Episode 7 Hits 7 Million U.S. Viewers in Three Days as Season Reaches Average of Nearly 19 Million Globally
summary: The seventh episode of “Lanterns” reached 7 million viewers in the U.S. in its first three days of availability. That total comes from a combination of Nielsen’s measurement of linear viewers on HBO’s cable channel plus streams on HBO Max. The DC Universe series has shown strong viewership thus far, averaging above 12 million viewers […]
content:
The seventh episode of “Lanterns” reached 7 million viewers in the U.S. in its first three days of availability.

That total comes from a combination of Nielsen’s measurement of linear viewers on HBO‘s cable channel plus streams on HBO Max. The DC Universe series has shown strong viewership thus far, averaging above 12 million viewers per episode to date in the U.S. and nearly 19 million when factoring in international viewing.

It can be expected that these averages will continue to climb: HBO’s most similar recent series is “It: Welcome to Derry,” which saw 6.5 million U.S. viewers in three days with its most-watched episode — slightly fewer than the latest “Lanterns” tally — and later went on to hit a global average of 19.7 million.

Popular on Variety

Other recent HBO and HBO Max dramas to compare to include “Euphoria,” which hit 8.7 million viewers globally in three days with its Season 3 finale, at which point the series was averaging 25 million per episode, and “The Pitt,” which ended its second season with 9.7 million finale viewers in the U.S. and a season average of 15.4 million. (HBO did not provide a global tally for “Lanterns” Episode 7.) HBO’s last DC series, “The Penguin,” concluded with an average of more than 27 million viewers per episode in 2024.

“Lanterns” is also continuing to bring in new viewers as the season progresses, with 1.5 million new viewers watching the series premiere within the last week. The series finale will be released this Sunday.

title: Kelly Clarkson Says ‘I Love AI’ but AI Artists Should Not Be on the Same Music Charts as Humans
summary: Kelly Clarkson has shared her admittedly “controversial” opinion on artificial intelligence, saying she thinks it can do “amazing things” but shouldn’t be able to create anything that competes with humans, particularly on music charts. The pop star shared her feelings about the technology during an appearance on the Las Culturistas podcast, saying she “loves AI” […]
content:
Kelly Clarkson has shared her admittedly “controversial” opinion on artificial intelligence, saying she thinks it can do “amazing things” but shouldn’t be able to create anything that competes with humans, particularly on music charts.

The pop star shared her feelings about the technology during an appearance on the Las Culturistas podcast, saying she “loves AI” but has issues with how it works in the music space.

“I love AI. Controversial, I don’t care,” she said. “Here’s the thing, I love AI. There are very amazing things with AI that I’m obsessed with. But also, and I’m very into it artistically too, I have fun with it just like everybody else does. But when you see AI artists competing on a chart with humans, I have an issue. I think there should be a separate chart.”

Popular on Variety

Clarkson continued by stating that AI is “welcome to the table,” and that it’s “really cool and creative what we’re going to create with AI musically.” “People who maybe can’t do certain things will be able to do it now and I think it’s a fun field to play in,” she said. “But I don’t think they should be competing with humans. It’s basically like having Olympics and then you’re having robots compete with humans, well who’s going to throw it further? Oh, I wonder. So I’m down with it and I think it’s a very interesting thing and what we’re going to do with it is going to be fun, but I do not think they should be competing.”

She went on to praise how AI is being used beyond music but that there should be limitations to the technology. “Here’s the thing. It’s not going anywhere,” she said. “I think it is interesting and there’s so many amazing scientific things that are happening. I don’t think it’s going anywhere but I think you have to be able to differentiate… We can’t lose human. We can’t lose what that is. But there could be an appetite for both, is what I’m saying.”

title: Chase Infiniti to Star in Dylan Clark’s ‘Portrait of God’ at Lionsgate With Sam Raimi and Jordan Peele Producing
summary: Golden Globe and Emmy nominee Chase Infiniti (“One Battle After Another,” “The Testaments”) will star in “Portrait of God,” from up-and-coming horror filmmaker Dylan Clark. Lionsgate has acquired the rights and has greenlit the feature for production, with Sam Raimi and Jordan Peele on board as producers. “We’re delighted to deepen our creative partnership with […]
content:
Golden Globe and Emmy nominee Chase Infiniti (“One Battle After Another,” “The Testaments”) will star in “Portrait of God,” from up-and-coming horror filmmaker Dylan Clark. Lionsgate has acquired the rights and has greenlit the feature for production, with Sam Raimi and Jordan Peele on board as producers.

“We’re delighted to deepen our creative partnership with Dylan Clark, whose remarkable talent and distinctive perspective make him one of the most exciting emerging voices in horror,” said Lionsgate Motion Picture Group chair Adam Fogelson, announcing the project. The studio tapped Clark to make his feature film directorial debut with the forthcoming untitled “Blair Witch” movie.

Fogelson continued: “With Sam and Jordan, two of the genre’s most influential producers, the extraordinary Chase Infiniti starring, and Dylan at the helm, this is an exceptional creative team. We believe they have all the ingredients for a film that is haunting, thought-provoking, and scary as hell.”

Popular on Variety

This project marks the first collaboration between Raimi and Peele, two of horror’s leading filmmakers. It also continues Raimi’s relationship with Lionsgate, which is backing “Magic,” the next movie he will direct.

Raimi and Rob Tapert will produce through their Ghost House shingle, as will Peele and Win Rosenfeld via their Monkeypaw Productions. Joe Russo, who co-wrote the screenplay with Clark, will also produce. Romel Adam and Jose Cañas will oversee the project for Ghost House. On behalf of Monkeypaw, Chris Rosati is executive producing through his first look deal at his shingle NAT20 Films. Scott O’Brien will oversee the project for the studio. Dan Freedman negotiated the deals on behalf of the studio.

The news comes as Clark readies his “Blair Witch” reboot for theatrical release next September.

“With ‘Blair Witch,’ I’m experiencing firsthand the trust Lionsgate places in its filmmakers, and I couldn’t be happier that ‘Portrait of God’ has found a home there as well,” Clark said. “I’m also thrilled to welcome Chase Infiniti to our team. She blew me away in ‘One Battle After Another’ and is one of the most exciting young actors working today.”

Clark is represented by UTA, 3 Arts, and Ginsburg Daniels Kallis, while Infiniti is represented by Gersh, Brillstein Entertainment Partners, and the Lede Company.

The Hollywood Reporter broke news about the developing project.

title: ‘Behemoth!,’ Starring Pedro Pascal, to Close Newport Beach Film Festival
summary: The 27th annual Newport Beach Film Festival will close with “Behemoth!” on Oct. 22, with writer and director Tony Gilroy set to attend. Pedro Pascal stars as gifted cellist Alex Serian, who returns home to Los Angeles and embarks on a life-changing adventure after spending the past 20 years performing on the road. The film […]
content:
The 27th annual Newport Beach Film Festival will close with “Behemoth!” on Oct. 22, with writer and director Tony Gilroy set to attend.

Pedro Pascal stars as gifted cellist Alex Serian, who returns home to Los Angeles and embarks on a life-changing adventure after spending the past 20 years performing on the road. The film features nine composers and is set to premiere Dec. 4. “Behemoth!” production designer Jade Healy will also attend closing night and will join Gilroy in conversation prior to the screening.

“We couldn’t have picked a better way to celebrate 27 years of Newport than closing with a filmmaker as exciting as Tony Gilroy,” said Gregg Schwenk, the CEO and executive director of NBFF. “This film has a deeply personal story about what music demands of the people who live inside it — and having Tony and Jade here in person for Q&A is exactly the kind of up-close experience that makes Newport unlike any other festival in the country.”

Popular on Variety

Taking place Oct. 15-22, the festival’s line-up also features “A Talent for Murder,” “Ink,” “Josephine,” “La Bola Negra,” “The Only Living Pickpocket in New York,” “Paper Tiger” and “Wild Horse Nine.” Aaron Burns’ Jimmy Stewart biopic, “Jimmy,” will also be featured, with the cast and crew set to be in attendance for a Q&A following the screening.

The Newport Beach Film Festival is the largest international cinema event in coastal Southern California, drawing in more than 50,000 attendees. Last year’s festival closed with Guillermo Del Toro’s “Frankenstein,” which stars Jacob Elordi, Mia Goth, Oscar Isaac and Christoph Waltz.

title: 10 Animators to Watch on AI, Animation’s Future and Why the Human Hand Still Matters: ‘Nobody Else Has Your Point of View’
summary: On the final day of the 10th annual SCAD AnimationFest in Atlanta, 10 animators and an Oscar-nominated director took the stage to talk about the future of their craft and why the human hand still matters. The 2026 class of 10 Animators to Watch, profiled in Variety’s New York issue, represents a broad cross-section of […]
content:
On the final day of the 10th annual SCAD AnimationFest in Atlanta, 10 animators and an Oscar-nominated director took the stage to talk about the future of their craft and why the human hand still matters.

The 2026 class of 10 Animators to Watch, profiled in Variety’s New York issue, represents a broad cross-section of the medium. The group includes artists from Ireland, France, Belgium, Bulgaria, Singapore, Hong Kong, Canada and the U.S., working across hand-drawn, stop-motion and CG animation at studios ranging from Hollywood’s biggest houses to independent productions. Each honoree also created a self-portrait for the issue. Variety moderated this conversation in partnership with SCAD Film Festival.

This year’s talented up-and-comers included Louise Bagnall, director of Cartoon Saloon’s “Julián”; Daniela Strijleva, production designer of Pixar’s “Gatto”; Tilly Fiddler, a stop-motion animator on Laika’s “Wildwood”; Amol Sathe, director of cinematography and lighting on Walt Disney Animation Studios’ “Hexed”; Clarisse Chua, storyboard artist on Brad Bird’s “Ray Gunn” and Nathan Greno’s “Swapped”; Chloë Aubert, animation director of “Iron Boy”; Maarten Lemmens, lead animator on DreamWorks Animation’s “Forgotten Island”; Eric Bofa Nfon, animation director of the hand-drawn feature “Tangles”; Ryan Gaffney, head of story on Warner Bros. Pictures Animation’s “The Cat in the Hat”; and Samm Lee, storyboard artist and animation director on Sony Pictures Animation’s “Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse.”

“Earlier this year, ‘KPop Demon Hunters’ won the Oscar for best animated feature, and behind every one of those wins is a small army of artists whose names often get overlooked,” Variety chief awards editor Clayton Davis told the SCAD audience. “Animation is film, and we must treat it that way.”

Several members of the class had good reason to be somewhere else. Lemmens’ “Forgotten Island” was the closing-night film of this year’s SCAD Animation Fest, the same day the movie opened in theaters across the country. Sathe, Strijleva and Lee are still working on and finishing their films.

Nonetheless, the conversation quickly became a reminder of just how much work goes into an animated film — and how many of those decisions never make it into the public conversation.

Bofa Nfon discussed the decision to move his “Tangles” animators away from the industry-standard twos and onto threes and fours, with one sequence even animated on eights. The choice wasn’t merely a budgetary calculation, though working at a slower frame rate meant fewer drawings for the independent production and created a different texture. “You don’t just take twos and push them into threes or fours,” Bofa Nfon said. “You have to think about the motion and where to select your drawings.”

Getty Images for SCAD

For Lemmens, the challenge on “Forgotten Island” was learning an entirely different visual language. When the directors began sending anime films to the crew, Lemmens realized he had some catching up to do. “I haven’t really watched anime,” he recalled thinking. He spent his Christmas break doing his homework and eventually became one of the film’s anime specialists because he was “one of the few people that actually did that homework.”

On the upcoming “The Cat in the Hat,” Gaffney helped crack the notoriously difficult and iconic characters Thing One and Thing Two by taking inspiration from the Baby Herman cookie sequence in “Who Framed Roger Rabbit,” the blockbuster 1988 live-action and animation hybrid. “The Things want to eat Waffles,” Gaffney told the crowd, about the character who is voiced by actor Matt Berry. “And I thought, ‘OK, I can take that somewhere.’”

For Chua, working with Bird on “Ray Gunn” meant learning how to interpret a director whose vision had been developing for decades. Bird sent the story team to study films including Roman Polanski’s “Chinatown” and Curtis Hanson’s “L.A. Confidential.” In contrast, Chua studied choreographer Busby Berkeley for a particular sequence. “It taught me how important it is to watch a lot of movies and understand your director,” Chua explained.

Bird’s process was also highly physical. When Chua pitched something that wasn’t working, Bird would sometimes acknowledge that his original instructions weren’t working either. “He would bring out his camera hands and start running around the meeting room, which was awesome,” she said.

Eventually, the conversation turned to the subject hanging over virtually every creative discussion in Hollywood: artificial intelligence. Each of the panelists does not treat AI as a single problem with one answer. Instead, they returned to the craft, specificity, collaboration and the value of work that bears the fingerprints of each of its creators.

Bagnall argued that the greatest defense against generic AI-generated imagery is to become more specific, not less. “AI tends toward homogeneity,” she said. “It tends toward the middle ground, the generic kind of solution to a problem. With that in mind, you can lean into specificity. You can lean into your own point of view. Nobody else has your point of view on the world.”

Aubert, whose “Iron Boy” premiered at Cannes, has heard variations of the same technological death sentence before. Fifteen years ago, she was told that 2D animation was disappearing in favor of 3D.

“I’ve never done 3D animation in my life,” she admits. “I secretly know how to do it, but don’t tell anybody.”

Her answer to technological change has been straightforward: keep making the work she wants to make. Aubert further explains: “I always laughed about it, because all I wanted was to draw, to animate, to share feelings with people. I just did what I wanted and showed what I wanted to do, and the more I showed that, the more people gave me work for it.”

Fiddler, a SCAD graduate in 2022 who went from an intern to a team member on the upcoming “Wildwood,” had a more personal reaction. “Before I was super aware of AI, I would see something that was AI and not clock it and then someone would tell me and I was immediately not interested in it anymore,” she said. “I watched behind-the-scenes footage of people making it, and it’s passed down through generations. I find that really emotional and exciting, and it’s what makes me want to keep making art.”

Getty Images for SCAD

Lee, who’s working on the top-secret and highly anticipated “Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse,” acknowledged that the uncertainty is real but argued that fear should not obscure the medium’s history of adaptation. “It’s a little scary, but I believe in us,” Lee asserts. “I don’t think we have to be afraid.”

Sathe agreed that technology should not obscure the industry’s most important asset, and that is its people. “A lot of the buzz nowadays is around technology, but at the end of the day, the best projects come from people collaborating, bouncing ideas off each other and relying on their teams, both emotionally and creatively,” he shared.

The panel also gave shout outs to the jobs on an animated project that deserve more credit. Those included production teams, technical directors, editors, IT workers, riggers and stop-motion’s so-called “puppet hospital.” Aubert had a particularly strong case for cleanup artists. “There’s a lot of ego in this industry, because animators can be stars and it gets to your head,” she shared. “So please don’t.”

Production teams received similarly strong praise. Gaffney, who began his career as a production assistant, said those teams are essential to keeping productions moving. Lee compared production workers to the “blood vessels” of a film.

Panelists like Lemmens warned students against viewing their classmates as competitors.

“Don’t treat your relationships with the people around you as competition,” he said. “What I’ve found is that being collaborative and being friends with the people around you, asking for feedback, ‘What do you think of this?’, encouraging each other to show stuff, actually gets you way further.”

Bofa Nfon offered a simpler lesson for those entering their first jobs. “At your first job, there’s a tendency to want to impress people and figure things out on your own,” he shared. “But don’t suffer in silence.”

The conversation ultimately returned to a question Variety posed on the first-ever “Pixels and Pencils” panel at SCAD in 2021, and has carried through every year since: Who will be a part of the first animated feature that will win the Oscar for best picture?

One student, Lily, a senior 3D animation major from Milledgeville, Ga., raised her hand and was brought onstage and dubbed her the group’s “11th animator to watch.”

The panel then offered Lily a collective crash course in surviving the animation business, unexpected opportunities and, as Lee put it, remaining curious about people outside the animation world. “Love everything you can love,” she shared. “Love other people, not just artists and people in the industry you want to go into, but people who aren’t in that industry.”

Getty Images for SCAD

And then finally, Joel Crawford, the director of DreamWorks Animation’s “Forgotten Island” and the recipient of the Variety Creative Impact Award, screened his new movie as the closing night film of the fest and sat down for an intimate discussion and signed posters and books for each of the over 400 attendees of the screening.

He co-wrote and co-directed the movie with his best friend, Filipino filmmaker Januel Mercado, and saw this as a love letter to a culture he loves so much. “With Januel being Filipino American and my wife being Filipino, and growing up in the Philippines, she would share stories that she was told and that kind of stuck with me and it felt like it’s time to celebrate the Philippines.”

Crawford, who received his first Oscar nomination for “Puss in Boots: The Last Wish and will be returning to the fifth edition of Variety’s “Pixels and Pencils,” spotlighting the directors behind the year’s standout animated features, at SCAD Savannah Film Festival on Oct. 26, had helpful advice to a room of aspiring artists. “[Do] not let other people’s success be failure because it’s so hard to not compare and it’s so hard to embrace the unknown. I think that’s the one that sticks with you of try and do your best to celebrate all the people around you and their successes. And don’t worry, it will come to you.”

title: TIFF Midnight Madness Hit ‘River’ Gets Winter 2027 Date From Blumhouse Atomic Monster
summary: River, the IFC title that Universal and Blumhouse Atomic Monster acquired out of TIFF’s Midnight Madness section for $10 million, is getting a January 15, 2027 theatrical release. Universal already had this MLK weekend date on hold for a Blumhouse title. Also opening on this date so far is Paramount’s Gina Prince-Bythewood’s Children of Blood […]
content:
River, the IFC title that Universal and Blumhouse Atomic Monster acquired out of TIFF’s Midnight Madness section for $10 million, is getting a January 15, 2027 theatrical release.

Universal already had this MLK weekend date on hold for a Blumhouse title. Also opening on this date so far is Paramount’s Gina Prince-Bythewood’s Children of Blood and Bone, Amazon MGM Studios/Miramax’s The Beekeeper 2 and Angel Studios’ Fing!

River stands at 94% on Rotten Tomatoes with critics. Pic stars Jane Levy (Evil Dead), Jessica Rothe (Happy Death Day) and Max Mattern (Devil in Disguise: John Wayne Gacy). Written and directed by Joshua Giuliano, it follows three estranged siblings who reunite in their hometown after the death of their father. As they set out to scatter his ashes at his favorite spot on a remote river, the trip devolves into a waking nightmare. Dane DiLiegro (Prey) also stars.

Watch on Deadline

Some circled River at TIFF, specifically Sony. Blumhouse Atomic Monster was passionate to get its hands on the project as their genre indie exec Sam Zimmerman worked with Giuiano on River during his time at Shudder. Also, Blumhouse Atomic Monster, Divide/Conquer and Spooky Pictures signed Giuliano’s next movie Occupant.

title: Veteran Writer-Producer & Propaganda Films Co-Founder Anne-Marie MacKay Signs With Established Artists
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Anne-Marie MacKay, veteran writer-producer and co-founder of Propaganda Films, has signed with Established Artists for management. Also a founding member of Palomar Pictures, Riddle Studios and Wondros, MacKay is credited with helping to launch the directing careers of David Fincher, Michael Bay, Antoine Fuqua, Gore Verbinski, Michel Gondry, Sofia Coppola, Mark Romanek, Dominic Senna […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Anne-Marie MacKay, veteran writer-producer and co-founder of Propaganda Films, has signed with Established Artists for management.

Also a founding member of Palomar Pictures, Riddle Studios and Wondros, MacKay is credited with helping to launch the directing careers of David Fincher, Michael Bay, Antoine Fuqua, Gore Verbinski, Michel Gondry, Sofia Coppola, Mark Romanek, Dominic Senna and Alex Proyas. She also has worked with David Lynch, Francis Ford Coppola, Sir Michael Apted, Ben Stiller, Forest Whitaker, Lee Daniels, and David O. Russell, providing both long and short-form opportunities for the filmmakers.

Emmy- and Grammy-nominated MacKay’s producing credits include Bleecker Street’s The Last Word, directed by Mark Pellington, Foster Boy, executive produced by Shaquille O’Neal and starring Matthew Modine and Louis Gossett Jr., Showtime’s Suge Knight feature documentary American Dream, American Knightmare, directed by Antoine Fuqua, Walter Mosley’s Always Outnumbered for HBO and the Cannes/Sundance selection The Girl from Nagasaki

Watch on Deadline

“Anne-Marie is a visionary builder and a true titan of our industry whose impact on modern

filmmaking and culture is undeniable,” said manager Corey Simon at Established Artists. “Her ability to discover and elevate singular artistic voices is legendary. I am deeply honored to partner with her as she continues to create groundbreaking, high-caliber stories for film and television.”

On the TV literary front, MacKay continues to be represented by Scott Kaufman at Buchwald.

title: ‘You Can See Everything’ Directors On Filming Complex Doc: “If We Can’t Agree On What’s Happening, There’s Something There” – NYFF
summary: “I guess we should just start at the beginning, and tell us how this happened,” New York Film Festival artistic director Dennis Lim asked filmmakers Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim at a Q&A after a screening of You Can See Everything on Wednesday night. It was the second public showing of the documentary, which was […]
content:
“I guess we should just start at the beginning, and tell us how this happened,” New York Film Festival artistic director Dennis Lim asked filmmakers Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim at a Q&A after a screening of You Can See Everything on Wednesday night.

It was the second public showing of the documentary, which was filmed in and over years and blew the roof off the Telluride Film Festival (see Deadline review). It’s a hard-to-describe flow of verité filmmaking unspooling in real time at the San Diego home of disgraced biotech entrepreneur Elizabeth Holmes in the days before she reported to Bryan federal prison in Texas. The Stanford dropout and Theranos founder is still serving a 10-year sentence for defrauding investors in the high-profile case.

Fielder and Oppenheim said the project, oddly, was launched during a magic show the two friends attended in L.A. in 2023, at the height of Holmes’ notoriety. “A magician there asked for a celebrity’s name, and someone called out ‘Elizabeth Holmes’,” Oppenhiem said. “I was like, so interesting. Elizabeth Holmes.” He said he “had just heard that she was looking for someone to document her life and that she had reached out to A24.”

Watch on Deadline

Fielder was also curious. “I knew that she hadn’t… spoken to anyone in, I think, seven years. Total silence.” He didn’t necessarily see a documentary brewing “because it felt like the story was very told. But I was really curious to meet her, just as a personal thing.”

RELATED: ‘You Can See Everything’ Directors On Filming Complex Doc

Holmes’ epic rise and fall was the subject of an HBO documentary and a Hulu miniseries starring Amanda Seyfried.

Fielder called A24, and went to meet Holmes. “I remember having this weird experience… where I’m like, “She seems so genuine at times. But then I’m like, no… I know she’s a liar… It was a weird mental thing.” Homes has always insisted she did nothing wrong.

She agreed to let the cameras into the home she shares with with her partner Billy Evans and their two young children.

Fielder made no promises to A24. “We don’t know what the story is. But we want to see what happens,” he said. The studio said, “‘OK, that’s fine. And if you want to pull the plug anytime, you can.’ Which was amazing.”

From left: ‘You Can See Everything’ filmmakers Lance Oppenheim and Nathan Fielder with the New York Film Festival’s Dennis Lim Jill Goldsmith/Deadline

They started filming. “And after, Lance and I would talk about what we thought happened there, and we’d completely disagree on… what we thought was happening. And we were like, ‘Oh, this is really interesting, if we can’t agree on what’s happening, there’s something here.’ And our curiosity sort of just like drove us from there.”

The filmmakers ultimately moved from one camera to three, shooting 16 hours a day with two small crews of which no more than four individuals were in the house at any one time. “We had a wide lens that would cover the whole house so if something happened, we wouldn’t miss it. And then the other two … lenses could be wide but then also zoom, so we could basically capture everything,” said Oppenheim.

“We were trying… essentially, to just take all the pressure away from any moment, so they wouldn’t really know what we were interested in necessarily.”

“Actually, we didn’t always either,” Fielder added.

“One thing we realized with the [initial] one camera that’s panning, which you see in some of the earlier scenes, is that the moment you say something to someone you want to see their face the moment they hear it. Especially in a movie like this, where you’re trying to evaluate if someone’s being honest or not. And when you have to swing, you’re missing a few seconds. And you realize this is maybe a problem in this kind of thing,” Fielder said.

He himself went from solely behind the camera to very much on, registering reactions to Holmes, including to her circular responses to questions like did she know her claims about Theranos’ blood-testing kit were false.

Fielder said he has no idea why she and Evans granted them the access they did.

“It’s so hard to understand… Maybe there was a sense that inviting someone who was a friend of theirs, no one would take that seriously. So I don’t know. It’s so hard to speculate as to why.”

You Can See Everything opens October 16 in theaters.

“I cannot tell you how weird it was that we were there,” Fielder said. “Why I’m excited for the movie to come out is I’m really curious to hear what everyone else thinks and what they make of certain things. I think it will actually help me understand… So I’ve been looking forward to this release for a while.”

title: Nithya Raman Reaches Out To David Ellison To Make Sure L.A Production & Jobs Return Now That ParaBros Deal Is Done
summary: Leading in polls in the Los Angeles mayor’s race, Nithya Raman went on a charm offensive Thursday with the film and TV industry, and Paramount’s CEO David Ellison in particular. “To David Ellison, to his co-CEO, I don’t just want those dollars that you’ve committed to productions to be spent in America — I want […]
content:
Leading in polls in the Los Angeles mayor’s race, Nithya Raman went on a charm offensive Thursday with the film and TV industry, and Paramount‘s CEO David Ellison in particular.

“To David Ellison, to his co-CEO, I don’t just want those dollars that you’ve committed to productions to be spent in America — I want them to be spent in Los Angeles,” the two-term councilmember said today at the Bloomberg Screentime conference, which is taking place in her Hollywood district. Raman said that though she was opposed to $111 billion merger of Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery, now that the deal has been approved she has no interest in “relitigating this into eternity.”

As has been the case many times in the past, the home of Hollywood has some unlikely bedfellows when it comes to the bottom line. It is unknown whether Raman has directly reached out to Paramount brass since U.S. District Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín signed off Tuesday on the antitrust settlement between the Ellison-run company and a dozen state attorneys general. Paramount reps did not respond to Deadline’s request for comment on any communication between the councilmember and the CEO.

Watch on Deadline

Paramount CEO David Ellison Getty

In full campaign mode, Raman emphasized during today’s panel interview that she will be a “relentless advocate” for uncapping the state’s current $750 million a year film and TV tax incentive program as a further move to get production back to California and L.A. With a room full of execs before her, Raman also reiterated she would “ensure that we had a film office in the mayor’s office that was liaising with other jurisdictions, that was making it as simple to shoot here as possible, as low cost to shoot here as possible, and that work would be established almost immediately.”

To that, with production significantly on the decline over the past six years and more than 50,000 jobs lost, Raman followed the headlines as Ellison and his newly minted co-CEO Ynon Kreiz prepare to meld the two iconic Hollywood companies.

“If I get to be mayor, I want to work with you and ensure and fight as hard as I possibly can to make sure that every single one of those shoots are happening here in Los Angeles,” the candidate said, addressing Ellison and Kreiz directly in absentia. “And I will do everything in my power to make sure that happens.”

Although Raman leads incumbent Mayor Karen Bass by double digits in many polls, the fact is one-third of voters in the City of Angels remain undecided just more than a month before the election. To that, the candidate has to win over a portion of those who voted for ex-The Hills regular Spencer Pratt in the three-way primary earlier this year — and she had a pitch.

“To every voter who voted for Spencer Pratt in the primary who is disappointed that he’s not in this general election, I want to speak directly to you,” Raman said of the Donald Trump ally. “I want to speak directly to them, and to say that I share your frustration with City Hall, and I will work with every molecule of my being to ensure that this city is working for you.”

Among his various post-primary endeavors, former Palisades resident Pratt has been instrumental, by all bipartisan accounts, in the crafting of federal film and TV tax incentive legislation — a bill Raman has said she also supports.

Leaning into her own outsider status, even with years on the L.A. City Council, Raman added, again addressing Pratt voters: “The frustrations that Angelinos have with the direction of our city is warranted. We have, under this mayor’s leadership, we have moved in the wrong direction and and away from actually delivering the kinds of services that we were able to deliver just a few years ago because of fiscal mismanagement under her leadership.”

“So, to those Pratt voters, I just want to say to you, I will do better for you,” she said.

title: SCAD Film Festival’s TV Sidebar To Feature ‘The Good Daughter,’ ‘Furious,’ ‘VisionQuest’ & ‘The Lowdown’
summary: The SCAD Savannah Film Festival’s third annual TV Sidebar is set, with four TV program screenings followed by award presentations and conversations with the stars of the series. The fest, which runs October 24-31 in Savannah, GA will spotlight episodes of The Good Daughter, VisionQuest, Furious and The Lowdown. Based on Karin Slaughter’s bestselling novel, […]
content:
The SCAD Savannah Film Festival’s third annual TV Sidebar is set, with four TV program screenings followed by award presentations and conversations with the stars of the series.

The fest, which runs October 24-31 in Savannah, GA will spotlight episodes of The Good Daughter, VisionQuest, Furious and The Lowdown.

Based on Karin Slaughter’s bestselling novel, The Good Daughter stars Meghann Fahy and Rose Byrne. Fahy will receive the Spotlight in Television Award on October 24 at a screening of one of the show’s episodes. In The Good Daughter, Fahy stars as Charlotte “Charlie” Quinn alongside Byrne as Samantha “Sam” Quinn. Written and executive produced by Slaughter and directed by Steph Green, the limited series premieres November 12 on Peacock.

Paul Bettany will receive the Virtuoso Award on October 26 at a screening of Marvel Television’s VisionQuest. The Disney+ series continues the story of Vision following the events of WandaVision, with Bettany returning to the role he has portrayed across the Marvel Cinematic Universe. The actor’s latest superhero installment will close out the trilogy that began with WandaVision, for which he received an Emmy nomination, and Agatha All Along.

Watch on Deadline

Emmy Rossum will receive the Outstanding Achievement in Television Award on October 28 at a screening of the Hulu Original drama series Furious. Created, written and executive produced by Elizabeth Meriwether, the thriller stars Rossum as FBI agent Alice Black, who is on the hunt for a mysterious and calculating female serial killer (Lola Petticrew). The series, on which Rossum serves as an EP, also stars Quincy Tyler Bernstine and Scoot McNairy.

RELATED: ‘The Lowdown’ Gets Season 2 Release Date At FX; First Photos Of Tommy Lee Jones & Betty Gilpin

Ethan Hawke and Sterlin Harjo will receive the Outstanding Collaboration in Television Award on October 30 at a screening of their FX and Hulu series The Lowdown. Created, executive produced, written and directed by Harjo, the Tulsa-set noir series stars Hawke as Lee Raybon, a self-proclaimed “truthstorian” and citizen journalist whose relentless pursuit of the truth continually lands him in trouble.

In addition, Deadline during the fest will present “Below the Line: Scoring for the Screen with the Alliance for Women Film Composers,” a behind-the-scenes look at how today’s most innovative voices are redefining the sound of cinema. The conversation will feature members of the Alliance for Women Film Composers discuss their creative process, the challenges and triumphs of the industry, and the role composers play in bringing depth and resonance to film and television.

title: Eddie Murphy to Star in Peacock Drama Series ‘The Chairman’ From ‘Mad Men’ Creator Matthew Weiner
summary: Eddie Murphy is attached to star in “The Chairman,” a drama series in development at Peacock created by Matthew Weiner. If greenlit, the project will mark his first-ever role in a live-action scripted series. Plot details for “The Chairman” are yet to be announced. The series will be produced by Universal Television and 101 Studios, […]
content:
Eddie Murphy is attached to star in “The Chairman,” a drama series in development at Peacock created by Matthew Weiner. If greenlit, the project will mark his first-ever role in a live-action scripted series.

Plot details for “The Chairman” are yet to be announced. The series will be produced by Universal Television and 101 Studios, which is run by “Yellowstone” executive producer David Glasser and is under a first-look film and television deal at NBCUniversal that began in January. “The Chairman” will also be the first project to come out of ex-Paramount boss Chris McCarthy’s deal at NBCUniversal, which was first reported in November 2025 and put him in a consulting role on the studio’s relationship with Glasser and 101. Murphy and Weiner serve as producers on “The Chairman.”

Murphy is among the world’s all-time greatest comedians, having launched his career as a cast member on “Saturday Night Live” for four seasons from 1980 to 1984. Since then, he has focused on comedy specials and movies; his only scripted TV role before “The Chairman” was voice acting on “The PJs,” an animated series he co-created. On the big screen, his credits include the “Beverly Hills Cop” franchise (1984-2024), “Coming to America” (1988), “Harlem Nights” (1989), “Dr. Dolittle” (1998), “Dreamgirls” (2006), “Dolemite Is My Name” (2019) and more.

Popular on Variety

Weiner is best known for creating and serving as showrunner on “Mad Men,” which ran for seven seasons on AMC from 2007 to 2015 and is widely regarded as one of the best TV series of all time. He was also a writer and executive producer on “The Sopranos.” Other credits include writing and producing on CBS’ “Becker” (1999-2002) and the 2018 Amazon Prime Video anthology series “The Romanoffs,” which he created.

title: Halle Berry Accused of Child Abuse by Ex Olivier Martinez, Who Is Seeking a Restraining Order
summary: Halle Berry is being accused of abusing her 12-year-old son by her ex-husband, actor Olivier Martinez, who has filed a petition for a temporary restraining order against the actress. Martinez alleges that on Sept. 26, the “Catwoman” actress “physically abused our son Maceo, by jumping on him, putting her hands around his neck, and choking […]
content:
Halle Berry is being accused of abusing her 12-year-old son by her ex-husband, actor Olivier Martinez, who has filed a petition for a temporary restraining order against the actress.

Martinez alleges that on Sept. 26, the “Catwoman” actress “physically abused our son Maceo, by jumping on him, putting her hands around his neck, and choking him.” Martinez is asking for sole custody, which would amend their current split arrangement.

The parents have been ordered to participate in confidential mediation to discuss custody, according to an update from TMZ.

Popular on Variety

In the request for a restraining order, Martinez contends that there have been “other instances of abuse over the course of the last few years. These other incidents involve additional physical attacks against our son, as well as verbal and emotional abuse from Petitioner to me.”

For example, Martinez alleges that Berry “told our son that I am ‘a white bitch trying to rob a Black woman’ due to child support issues. Ms. Berry then asked our son, ‘How do you feel about that as a Black man?’”

Martinez wrote in the filing that Berry had texted him to apologize after the incident. “I do not want to

permanently sever the relationship between our son and Petitioner, but I do not believe that they should be interacting with each other until Petitioner can take sufficient accountability for her actions,” he wrote.

Martinez also asked that Berry be ordered to not be under the influence of alcohol or other substances while conducting visitation with their son.

“I believe he may be traumatized by the incident” and does not want to spend time at her house, Martinez said in the filing.

Berry and Martinez filed for divorce in 2015 after being married for two years. Berry also has an 18-year-old daughter from a previous relationship.

Representatives for Berry did not respond to request for comment.

title: ‘Fast & Furious’ TV Adaptation Ordered to Series by Peacock, Eyed for 2028 Premiere
summary: The “Fast & Furious” TV series, first revealed to be in development earlier this year at the NBCUniversal upfronts, is closer to reality. Peacock announced Thursday that it has greenlit a new scripted television series based on the franchise. Vin Diesel, who revealed that a “Fast & Furious” scripted series was in development during the […]
content:
The “Fast & Furious” TV series, first revealed to be in development earlier this year at the NBCUniversal upfronts, is closer to reality. Peacock announced Thursday that it has greenlit a new scripted television series based on the franchise.

Vin Diesel, who revealed that a “Fast & Furious” scripted series was in development during the upfront presentation in May, is an executive producer along with One Race’s Sam Vincent (One Race), Original Film’s Neal H. Moritz and Pavun Shetty, and Jeff Kirschenbaum and Chris Morgan.

Mike Daniels (“Sons of Anarchy,” “Shades of Blue,” “The Rockford Files”) and Wolfe Coleman (“Shades of Blue,” “911: Lone Star”) will serve as co-showrunners, pilot writers and executive producers.

Popular on Variety

According to Peacock, the streamer is looking to premiere the “Fast & Furious” series by 2028.

Premiere would coincide with the next film installment, “Fast Forever,” which has been slated to hit theaters on March 17, 2028.

Universal Television, a division of Universal Studio Group, is the studio.

“For the last decade, we have realized that the fans have wanted more,” Diesel said at the upfront in May. “They wanted us to expand the legacy characters, their stories. And for the last decade, the desire has been for us to enter the TV space that Fallon has mastered. And I had to wait till it was right… It became right when Donna Langley started to oversee it all, because that’s when I knew that the integrity of the characters, the international appeal, what makes us all feel like family would be protected in the TV space… The news that I have here today is that Peacock is launching four shows from the ‘Fast and Furious’ universe.”

Previously in TV, Netflix aired the animated series “Fast & Furious Spy Racers” for six seasons between 2019 and 2021.

In case you’re one of the few out there who doesn’t know what the “Fast & Furious” franchise is about, here’s NBCU’s explainer: “This year marks the 25th anniversary of the launch of one of the most iconic film franchises in cinema history. On June 22, 2001, Universal Pictures released “The Fast and the Furious,” a high-octane thriller set amid the street-racing culture of Los Angeles. The film — starring Vin Diesel as Dominic Toretto, Paul Walker as Brian O’Conner, Jordana Brewster as Mia and Michelle Rodriguez as Letty — would ignite a cultural phenomenon.”

content:
Variety Awards Circuit section is the home for all awards news and related content throughout the year, featuring the following: the official predictions for the upcoming Oscars, Emmys, Grammys and Tony Awards ceremonies, curated by Variety chief awards editor Clayton Davis. The prediction pages reflect the current standings in the race and do not reflect personal preferences for any individual contender. As other formal (and informal) polls suggest, competitions are fluid and subject to change in response to buzz and events. Predictions are updated every Thursday.

Explore Awards Circuit Predictions Pages

Oscars | Emmys | Grammys | Tonys

Best International Feature Predictions Commentary (Updated: Oct. 1, 2026): The submission deadline for the best international feature Oscar has come and gone and now the industry waits to see how many countries are ultimately entering the race.

Popular on Variety

While we await the official tally, several contenders have already made their cases on the festival circuit. Spain’s “La Bola Negra” arrives with the TIFF People’s Choice Award, while Cannes has supplied two major players: Palme d’Or winner “Fjord,” representing Romania and the runner-up “Minotaur,” which will compete for France.

South Korea’s “Possible Love” also has significant momentum after Lee Chang-dong took the directing prize at Venice. And then there’s “Woman Unknown,” Denmark’s selection and the Golden Lion winner, which has perhaps the biggest question mark attached to its Oscar prospects as it still seeks U.S. distribution.

The list of predictions in all categories can be found here.

The Governors Awards, which will hand out honorary Oscars to Glenn Close and Ridley Scott, will take place Sunday, Nov. 15. Preliminary voting for the Oscars shortlist in 12 categories runs Dec. 7-11, with the shortlist announcement to follow Tuesday, Dec. 15. Following the close of the eligibility period on Dec. 31, 2026, nominations voting will run Jan. 11-15, 2027. The official Oscar nominations will be announced on Thursday, Jan. 21, 2027. The 99th Oscars will take place on Sunday, March 14, 2027 and will be hosted by Conan O’Brien. The ceremony airs live at 7 p.m. ET on ABC and in more than 200 territories worldwide from the Dolby Theatre at Ovation Hollywood.

title: There Is Precedent for Taylor Swift’s ‘Cleveland!’ Making the World Go Crazy: Paul McCartney’s ‘Silly Love Songs’ Era
summary: It is a controversy actually worthy of an exclamation point. When was the last time the internet lost its collective stuff over a single song the way it did this past week with Taylor Swift’s “Cleveland!”? And they say there’s no such thing as a monoculture anymore. It might have felt like everyone you knew […]
content:
It is a controversy actually worthy of an exclamation point. When was the last time the internet lost its collective stuff over a single song the way it did this past week with Taylor Swift‘s “Cleveland!”? And they say there’s no such thing as a monoculture anymore. It might have felt like everyone you knew had not only heard “Cleveland!” (unlike the millions of people coming onto X to proudly proclaim their unfamiliarity with “Choosin’ Texas” as ot busted chart records) but had a Very Hot Take on it. In the realm of her fandom, much of that discourse was defense of the track. But inherent in all that was the idea that the song needed defending. Because at the tip of this social tsunami was a strong supposition that swiftly powered a gazillion Instagram memes:

Love and marriage have made Taylor Swift lose her dang mind… maybe even turned her into the mayor of Simpleton.

Popular on Variety

But as the internet increasingly went into pile-on mode about the new song — almost ignoring that she’d simultaneously released three other new tracks, including the new single “Patient Zero,” all of them bringing the old, more morose Swift back to the phone — I began to feel a sense of deja vu. Where had I, and maybe the world, experienced a panic like this before, about an artist whose turn toward silly love longs had been seen as some sort of cultural betrayal, or basic job failure?

The answer, of course, was in the question. It was Paul McCartney, in the early and mid-’70s, who got besotted with the romantic sillies and asked, “What’s wrong with that?” And further demanded: “I’d like to know!” Because, you know, here he goes… again… giving John Lennon unending nightmares there on Central Park West. It wasn’t just “Silly Love Songs,” which came a few years later on; it was “The Lovely Linda,” the first song on his solo album, announcing that he had traded in the Beatles for matrimony and domestic bliss. His dream had come true, but in the eyes of those who had a different picture of what he ought to be doing, it was more like the dream was over, to quote his ex-partner.

Obviously the author of “Helter Skelter” came through that bout of disapproval over getting ditzy with love pretty unscathed, and so will the author of “Folklore” survive whatever blasts she takes for “Cleveland!” But the accelerant qualities of social media can make the scorn feel much more immediate and wide than the days when the worst McCartney had to face for a while was from Rolling Stone subscribers.

“Cleveland!,” for anyone not yet keeping score at home, was one of four new songs tagged onto an extended edition of 2025’s “The Life of a Showgirl” album, subtitled “The Encore.” The other three were what people have mostly come to expect from the singer, looking back on long-distant relationships with rue and regrets — that she might have treated one of her past loves poorly, in the subtly moving “Pink Clouding,” or that she ever got involved in the first place with guys who turned out to Not Be All That, in “Patient Zero” or “Babylon.”

The crime of “Cleveland!” wasn’t that she’d created another earworm — which the chorus hook almost undeniably is, if you’ve listened to it more than a couple of times — but that she’d she’d allegedly given up being a poet in the service of no longer being tortured. “Cleveland!” is one of the most prosaic entries in her nearly 300-song catalog, with lyrics that start by recounting recent nasty things that’ve been said against her — that she can’t dance, that she has no ass (that word is blotted out, by the woman who usually has no trouble dropping F-bombs), that she’s gotten old. The other theme is the one where her asslessness doesn’t matter, because Travis loves her anyway. It kind of recalls the songs on “Reputation” where Taylor exulted that her new guy adored her in spite of Kim and Kanye dragging her name through the mud, but this is undoubtedly the bubblegum version of that, between the hyper-cheery arrangement and no real recent scandal to react to; it pivots on the admittedly questional idea that her new husband is noble for cherishing her even though she’s only a better dancer than 99.9999% of the planet.

Throw in a spoken-word section — which gave some people PTSD, bringing up the repressed memory of the spoken bit from “Me!” that she actually eventually excised from that recording — and it was a recipe for much of the public to start piling on. Now, I was on record within a couple hours of the tune coming out last Thursday night as not minding the song, saying anyone who’s truly and madly in love deserves an outlier goofball moment in the course of their honeymoon phase. But some of the reactions were funny, the ones that were just amused instead of morally stricken. I LOL-ed at one meme I saw on Instagram, captioned “What happens when Taylor writes about Travis,” which pictured a young woman repeating phrases like “He’s my man… my man… MY man” while looking up Cleveland Heights on Wikipedia.

Swift had set her fandom up for this dichotomy when she filmed a conversation with Harvey Mason Jr. at the Grammy Museum a few weeks ago, before the amended album release was announced. She said then, “I think that the way that I’ve chosen to express myself as a lyricist has changed over the years, and there are times when like those contradictions will come up where fans will be like, ‘I can’t believe the same person who wrote this wrote this.’ Because one will be very simplistic and silly, and one will be very detailed and deep and we’re doing tons of allegory, and we’re just in a whole other world of atmospheric speech. But I think that that human contradiction is fun. I think that it’s fun to make playful songs. I think it’s fun to make songs that are desolate and lonely and just bedraggled lyrically as well.” Swifties assumed she meant to explain the difference between “Ruin the Friendship” and “Wood,” when really she was warning everyone that a song as exquisite as “Pink Clouding” would soon be juxtaposed with the unrepentant bluntness of “Cleveland!”

This all came to fore, for me, the other night when I went to an L.A. FYC screening of the Paul McCartney & Wings documentary “Man on the Run.” The middle of the movie goes deep into some of the resistance that critics and fans — an estranged Lennon at the top of the list — put up when songs about Linda became the focus of his attention, with an initial folky musical single-mindedness to match. Granted, McCartney already had a reputation as the Beatle who counterbalanced Lennon’s darkness with the extreme fizziness of a “Honey Pie” or “Your Mother Should Knows,” but he also had a quality of depth on his permanent record as the author of “Yesterday,” “Eleanor Rigby” or even, then very recently, “You Never Give Me Your Money.” Now he, Linda and the sheep were on seemingly the world’s most extended honeymoon, with moony music to reflect it. And for some dismayed fans, it only got worse from there, from McCartney tap-dancing on a TV special to putting out “My Love” as the embodiment of what would come to be known as adult contemporary.

Lennon dragged his ex-collaborator in interviews that bordered on the vicious, leading Paul to respond in song with “Too Many People,” before Lennon dug in further and better with the ultimate diss track, “How Do You Sleep,” taking the position that McCartney should rightfully be kept awake at night by the haunting thought of having become such a lightweight.

Lennon’s rejoinders hurt McCartney’s feelings so terribly badly that he went on to write and record “Silly Love Songs,” a sweet-faced F-you to Lennon and anyone else who’d objected to the previous few years of objectifying Linda as his true lady madonna.

So… Taylor Swift in 2026 as Paul McCartney in 1971? The analogy gets more complicated when we consider that, at times, Swift has been more of a John than a Paul, actually. (Then again, there were moments when Paul was more of a John, too, but that’s a digression for another day.) Swift’s brutal, bitter takedowns of not just some of her former loves but former business partners or industry enemies in some of the darker passages of “Folklore” could legitimately be characterized as Lennon-esque. And that was not so many years after the decidedly Paul-like “Shake It Off”… and not so many years before she began writing about her future husband with “So High School,” the pep-rally outlier on the otherwise fantastically depressing “Tortured Poets Department.”

As a lifelong McCartney fan, when rifling through his catalog, I’ve often skipped over “The Lovely Linda,” “My Love” (unless it got to the brilliant guitar solo, and then I was inexorably hooked) and “Silly Love Songs.” Yet I never shunned them entirely, and I was happy they existed. Similarly, in the week that the extended “The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore” has been out, I’ve played three of the four new tracks a good deal, while I have saved “Cleveland!” for, uh, special occasions. It’s never going to be a favorite, but it’s never going to feel like a moral affront, either. It’s always been my position that people ought to get at least a partial pass for the things they say and do in the immediate throes of a new love, or in the first aftermath of a breakup — it’s those extreme reactions that make the world go round. You can love that she’s in love without having to love the latest song that came out of that altered state… or without having to demonize it, either. (Especially when it’s, you know, a bonus track?)

In the bigger picture, perhaps we could listen to what the man said: Love doesn’t come in a minute. Sometimes, it doesn’t come at all. Those lines have always struck me as deep and resonant, weirdly, in a song that’s otherwise anything but.

In the meantime, back in inflammatory meme-land… To quote the sage poet who wrote the previously most famous song about Cleveland, Randy Newman: Burn on, big river, burn on!

title: Fox News Tops September And Q3 Ratings; MS NOW Sees Gains, CNN Shows Uptick In Some Categories
summary: Fox News again handily topped the September and third quarter ratings, although as its viewership was down versus the same periods in 2025. MS NOW saw gains in the most recent figures, and CNN also showed uptick in September and in certain dayparts for the quarter. In primetime in September, Fox News averaged 1.72 million […]
content:
Fox News again handily topped the September and third quarter ratings, although as its viewership was down versus the same periods in 2025.

MS NOW saw gains in the most recent figures, and CNN also showed uptick in September and in certain dayparts for the quarter.

In primetime in September, Fox News averaged 1.72 million viewers, down 32% from the same month in 2025. MS NOW averaged 839,000, up 3.6% from a year earlier. CNN posted 539,000, down 0.7% from 2025. In the 25-54 demo, Fox News averaged 156,000 viewers, down 44.3% from a year earlier, compared to 90,000 for CNN, up 3.4%, and 79,000 for MS NOW, up 16.2%.

In total day in September, Fox News averaged 1.11 million, down 31.1% from 2025. MS NOW averaged 544,000, up 6.7%, and CNN posted 373,000, down 7%. In the 25-54 demo, Fox News averaged 106,000, down 40.8%, compared to CNN with 53,000, down 14.5%, and MS NOW with 52,000, up 15.6%.

Watch on Deadline

In the third quarter primetime, Fox News averaged 2.06 million viewers, down 17% from a year earlier, compared to 930,000 for MS NOW, up 16%, and 607,000 for CNN, up 12.8%. In the 25-54 demo, Fox News averaged 183,000 viewers, down 24.7%, compared to CNN with 101,000, up 16.1%, and MS NOW with 84,000, up 27.3%.

In third quarter total day, Fox News averaged 1.32 million, down 15.8% versus 2025, compared to MS NOW with 592,000, up 20.3%, and CNN with 426,000, up 7.6%. In the 25-54 demo, Fox News averaged 120,000, down 24.5%, compared to CNN with 61,000, flat, and MS NOW with 56,000, up 36.6%.

Fox News’ The Five was the top cable news show in September, averaging 2.79 million viewers, followed by Jesse Watters Primetime with 2.4 million, Gutfeld! with 2.12 million, Hannity with 2.06 million and Special Report with Bret Baier with 2.04 million.

In the 25-54 demo, The Five was tops with 273,000, followed by Gutfeld! with 214,000, Jesse Watters Primetime with 212,000, Hannity with 204,000 and MS NOW’s The Rachel Maddow Show with 186,000.

Each network touted certain aspects of the figures. Fox News said that they were on track to have its highest rated midterm year ever. MS NOW promoted double digit viewership increases.

Among other networks, NewsNation said that its primetime viewership was up 12% in primetime in the third quarter and 8% in adults 25-54. NewsNation averaged 120,000 viewers in primetime during the third quarter, and 13,000 in the demo.

Newsmax averaged 185,000 in primetime for the quarter and 9,000 in the demo.

MS NOW’s top rated show in September was The Rachel Maddow Show, averaging 1.79 million viewers. CNN’s top show was NewsNight, averaging 610,000, and NewsNation’s was Cuomo, averaging 167,000. Newsmax’s top show was Rob Schmitt Tonight, averaging 305,000.

title: David Ellison’s “Coziness” With Donald Trump Is “Way Overstated”, Per Paramount Backer Gerry Cardinale
summary: Gerry Cardinale, Paramount board member, investor and key architect of its pending merger with Warner Bros. Discovery, says the notion that CEO David Ellison is tight with Donald Trump has been “way overstated.” “Forget about where you are on the political spectrum,” Cardinale said at the Bloomberg Screentime conference in L.A. on Thursday. “You have […]
content:
Gerry Cardinale, Paramount board member, investor and key architect of its pending merger with Warner Bros. Discovery, says the notion that CEO David Ellison is tight with Donald Trump has been “way overstated.”

“Forget about where you are on the political spectrum,” Cardinale said at the Bloomberg Screentime conference in L.A. on Thursday. “You have an administration that’s pro-business. Anybody in corporate America should have a relationship with that administration. And that’s not because it’s Trump. Trump is pro-business, he’s very interested in the technology community. So having that relationship does not mean in any way that there’s this coziness.”

Skydance’s pursuit of Paramount got complicated by a lawsuit Trump filed against Paramount-owned CBS News, but regulators approved it promptly approved it after the suit was settled for $16 million despite the dubious merits of the case. Then, during the chase for Warner Bros. Discovery, which Paramount expected to formally acquire next week after a year-long quest, Ellison and Paramount had numerous points of intersection with the Trump administration.

Watch on Deadline

Ellison and others visited Trump’s compound in Mar-a-Lago, courted him in Washington and hosted events for him, including around the White House Correspondents Association ceremony. In operating Paramount, Ellison acquired The Free Press and installed its founder and editorial leader, Bari Weiss, as editor-in-chief of CBS News. The news division and shows like 60 Minutes have made a number of changes to its programming that are widely perceived to be overtures to the administration.

And then there is the UFC, which has a multi-billion-dollar rights deal with Paramount. Trump has attended UFC events, including one spectacle last summer held at the White House. Bloomberg editor Lucas Shaw, who was interviewing Cardinale, nodded to the spectacle, which streamed live on Paramount+. “There’s a difference between having a relationship and staging a fight on the White House lawn,” he said.

Cardinale replied by naming senior leaders of TKO Group, parent company of the UFC, including Nick Khan and Ari Emanuel. “They were in the front row next to Trump, Is Trump too cozy with them? Is Ari too cozy with Trump?” Shaw mentioned that Emanuel used to have Trump as a WME client.

“The inference on ‘cozy’ here is just not appropriate,” Cardinale said. “There’s nothing to it. I’m telling you. I’ve been with David, by his side every step of the way. There’s nothing to it. It makes for great headlines and clickbait. There’s nothing to it. Absolutely not.”

title: Eddie Murphy Moves Into Scripted TV With ‘The Chairman’ For Peacock From Matthew Weiner
summary: Eddie Murphy is heading back to the small screen for his first scripted series. The Beverly Hills Cop and Coming To America star, who got his start on Saturday Night Live, is to star in The Chairman, a drama series from Mad Men creator Matthew Weiner that is in the works at Peacock. Murphy has […]
content:
Eddie Murphy is heading back to the small screen for his first scripted series.

The Beverly Hills Cop and Coming To America star, who got his start on Saturday Night Live, is to star in The Chairman, a drama series from Mad Men creator Matthew Weiner that is in the works at Peacock.

Murphy has starred in around 40 movies since 48 Hours and has never headlined a scripted series, although he has created two shows back in the day: animated comedy The PJs for Fox and The Royal Family for CBS, both in the 1990s.

Details of the series have not been disclosed, but it being written and exec produced by Weiner, who has not had a series picked up since The Romanoffs for Amazon in 2018.

Watch on Deadline

The Chairman comes from Yellowstone producer 101 Studios and Universal Television.

It marks the first project for the company, which is also behind series such as Landman and MobLand, since it struck a deal with NBCUniversal last year that coincided with Taylor Sheridan also moving his deal. The deal for the David Glasser-run company started in January of this year.

Murphy and Weiner, who also previously wrote and exec produced HBO’s The Sopranos, will also exec produce.

Murphy is coming off the back of Netflix documentary Being Eddie, which was directed by Angus Wall and came out last year. His last two movies were The Pickup, which came out last year via Amazon, and Beverly Hills Cop: Axel F. His next film is Shrek 5, which is set to be released next year.

title: ‘Fast & Furious’ TV Series Greenlit At Peacock
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Start those engines because the Fast & Furious franchise is coming to television. Deadline understands that Peacock has greenlit its first television series based on the hit movie franchise, which has made more than $7 billion at the global box office over the past 25 years. The series comes from Mike Daniels and Wolfe […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Start those engines because the Fast & Furious franchise is coming to television.

Deadline understands that Peacock has greenlit its first television series based on the hit movie franchise, which has made more than $7 billion at the global box office over the past 25 years.

The series comes from Mike Daniels and Wolfe Coleman, who will write and serve as co-showrunners.

The project was one of a number announced during NBCUniversal’s Upfront event in May in New York by franchise star Vin Diesel, who will executive produce the series.

“As you all know, we are very precious about these movies but over the last decade, we’ve realized that the fans have wanted more, they wanted us to expand the legacy characters, their stories,” he said at the Upfront. “And for the last decade, the desire has been for us to enter the TV space.”

Watch on Deadline

Diesel said he came around on the idea after Universal Studios chief Donna Langley also took oversight of NBCUniversal’s TV operation last year.

“That’s when I knew that the integrity of the characters, the international appeal, what makes us all feel like family will be protected in the TV space,” he said.

The series, from Universal Television, is set to premiere in 2028. Daniels and Coleman will exec produce alongside Diesel and One Race’s Sam Vincent, Original Film’s Neal H. Moritz and Pavun Shetty and Jeff Kirschenbaum and Chris Morgan.

Fast Forever, the 11th and final film in the franchise, is set for release on March 17, 2028.

Daniels recently served as showrunner for Peacock’s PONIES, and has worked on series including Shades of Blue, Sons of Anarchy and NBC’s upcoming The Rockford Files reboot. Coleman has exec produced series including 9-1-1: Lone Star and also worked on Shades of Blue.

At the Upfronts, Diesel announced that that there were three other Fast & Furious series projects in the works; one comes from The Endgame’s Nick Wooton and House of the Dragon’s Charmaine DeGraté, and the others come from Griselda showrunner Ingrid Escajeda and Lucifer showrunner Joe Henderson.

All of this comes as NBCUniversal is celebrating the 25th anniversary of the franchise, which started with The Fast and the Furious in 2001 and starred Diesel as Dominic Toretto, Paul Walker as Brian O’Conner, Jordana Brewster as Mia and Michelle Rodriguez as Letty.

title: ‘Boston Strong’ Author Casey Sherman Lines Up Book & Film ‘Vegas Strong’ About 2017 Killings
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Author Casey Sherman, whose book Boston Strong was adapted into the 2016 feature film Patriots Day starring Mark Wahlberg and Kevin Bacon, has partnered with Midnight Lute Productions on a new book and feature film project, Vegas Strong. The project will chronicle the worst mass shooting in American history at the Route 91 Harvest […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Author Casey Sherman, whose book Boston Strong was adapted into the 2016 feature film Patriots Day starring Mark Wahlberg and Kevin Bacon, has partnered with Midnight Lute Productions on a new book and feature film project, Vegas Strong.

The project will chronicle the worst mass shooting in American history at the Route 91 Harvest Festival in Las Vegas on October 1, 2017, and the “courage, compassion, and resilience that emerged in its aftermath.”

Much as Sherman did with Boston Strong, which he co-authored with Dave Wedge, Vegas Strong will focus on “the survivors, first responders, families, and community members whose lives were forever changed, and on those who came together to help one another heal.”



“I see so many similarities between the aftermath of the Boston Marathon bombings and the unspeakable tragedy that unfolded in Las Vegas,” said Sherman, speaking to Deadline on the anniversary of the killings. “I want to give a voice to all those who rushed into the fray to save lives, those who comforted and supported the families of the victims, and the survivors who refused to allow the actions of a madman to destroy their lives.”



In 2018, Sherman hosted more than 40 Las Vegas shooting survivors and family members of victims on a healing cruise in Germany. The experience gave Sherman a first-hand look at how the tragedy altered so many lives giving him a passion for their stories. The book will also devote several chapters to the Vegas Golden Knights and the role the NHL expansion team played in bringing the Las Vegas community together and giving residents something to cheer about during one of the city’s darkest times.



“The way the players played for something bigger than themselves during their inaugural season, ultimately reaching the Stanley Cup Final, reminds me of We Are Marshall,” Sherman said. “The organization went above and beyond to help the community heal.”



Sherman and Midnight Lute Productions plan to develop Vegas Strong as a feature film, weaving together the personal stories of October 1 survivors and first responders with the inaugural season of the Golden Knights.



“We feel Vegas Strong will be one of the most inspiring sports stories ever told,” said Midnight Lute producer Trent Othick. “The way the Golden Knights uplifted a broken community and did the unthinkable in their first season, opening the door for professional sports in Las Vegas, is exactly the kind of story we want to tell. Casey and I have been discussing it for years, and we feel now is the time as the Golden Knights enter their 10th season.”



Othick, a Las Vegas-based producer, has a personal connection to the October 1 tragedy, with family and friends directly affected by the shooting. He also helped Sherman organize the 2018 healing cruise. The company is led by Othick, ESPN and Fox Sports analyst Matt Muehlebach, former Fox Sports Productions president John Entz, and several former professional athletes. The company is backed by Las Vegas-based investment group LJM Associates, comprised of John Gaughan, Layne Marsh and Blaine Tripp, as well as Arizona businessmen Jim Berwick, Josh Snider, Timothy Snider and Jeff Brack.



Othick previously served as president of Go Productions, where he produced the Broadway run and national tour of A Bronx Tale, as well as feature films from Neil LaBute, Marcus Nispel and others, while developing various TV projects. Before Go Productions, Othick was president of Insomnia Entertainment, where he partnered with former UFC owners Lorenzo and Frank Fertitta.



Sherman is the author of 20 books including The Finest Hours, which was adapted into a 2016 Disney feature film starring Chris Pine and Casey Affleck; James Patterson’s The Last Days of John Lennon; The Ice Bucket Challenge; 12: The Inside Story of Tom Brady’s Fight for Redemption; Helltown; and, most recently, The Killer and Frank Lloyd Wright. Sherman is currently an executive producer of the Hulu docuseries Hunting Whitey, based on his book and narrated by Ben Affleck, and he also stars in the NBC Peacock true crime documentary Boston Strangler: Unheard Confession.

Sherman is represented by UTA. Midnight Lute Productions is represented by Matt Luber of Luber Roklin Entertainment and Ron Levin of Levin Law Corporation.

title: Ben Affleck’s ‘Animals’ Cast Wants Him to Run for Office: ‘Maybe They Hate Me’
summary: Ben Affleck plays a Brentwood businessman running for Los Angeles mayor in the new thriller “Animals.” The Oscar winner, who directed and co-wrote the film, is also a longtime political activist who has supported the presidential campaigns of Barack Obama, Hillary Clinton, Joe Biden and Kamala Harris. Now, his “Animals” cast would like him to […]
content:
Ben Affleck plays a Brentwood businessman running for Los Angeles mayor in the new thriller “Animals.”

The Oscar winner, who directed and co-wrote the film, is also a longtime political activist who has supported the presidential campaigns of Barack Obama, Hillary Clinton, Joe Biden and Kamala Harris.

Now, his “Animals” cast would like him to run for elected office.

Ben Affleck says there’s a “collective disappointment” with American politics and dismisses the idea that he’d ever run for office: “There’s nobody alive who thinks we’re doing it right.” pic.twitter.com/KMrIjelx0q — Variety (@Variety) October 2, 2026

“Maybe they hate me,” Affleck cracked at the “Animals” premiere on Wednesday night in Los Angeles.

Popular on Variety
