content:
EXCLUSIVE: Essential Film Group has boarded world sales on indie feature Hollow Moon, starring Jena Malone, Dermot Mulroney, Mekhi Phifer and Vannessa Vasquez as astronauts in a trip to outer space.

We first told you about the project this month when it was known as Moon People. It’s now known as Hollow Moon.

Stanley Yung directs the film written by Niko Foster. Pic follows a team of astronauts who travel to the Moon to confirm the discovery of water, but they soon encounter unexpected danger and struggle to survive. The pic was shot in Lexington, Kentucky and is now in post.

Malone plays Dr. Jennifer Foster while Mulroney will portray Sam Foster. Phifer is Cape Josh Briley and Vasquez is Dr. Diana Alvarez.

Watch on Deadline

Hollow Moon is a production of Al Bravo Films with producers Al Bravo, Michael Pizzimenti and Tim Sabo. EPs are Renata Stiglich and Pejman Partiyeli. Co-producers are Hemdee Kiwanuka, Jacov Bresler and Michelle Wang.

title: ‘Twilight Of The Dead’: Filming Wraps On “Final Chapter” Of George A. Romero’s Zombie Saga, Kate Beckinsale & Betty Gabriel Star
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Filming has wrapped on Twilight of the Dead, the long gestating “final chapter” of George A. Romero’s classic zombie saga. Underworld star Kate Beckinsale stars alongside genre regular Betty Gabriel (Get Out), newcomer Abigail London and John D. Hickman (Becky). Filming took place in Kentucky and wrapped last month. Greg Nicotero, the legendary Walking […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Filming has wrapped on Twilight of the Dead, the long gestating “final chapter” of George A. Romero’s classic zombie saga.

Underworld star Kate Beckinsale stars alongside genre regular Betty Gabriel (Get Out), newcomer Abigail London and John D. Hickman (Becky).

Filming took place in Kentucky and wrapped last month. Greg Nicotero, the legendary Walking Dead make-up effects supervisor and director who also worked with Romero on Day Of The Dead, handled all the special effects.

The horror project, which has buy-in from the Romero estate, is “set on a decimated earth where the last vestiges of humanity are trapped between warring factions and an evolving undead threat”.

Watch on Deadline

The Paz Brothers, Doron and Yoav Paz, whose movies include The Golem and Plan A, directed. Stunts vet Ho Sung Pak (Bullet Train) directed stunt and action sequences.



As we revelead, Bob Yari’s Magenta Light Studios has North American rights and is due to distribute the film in theaters across the U.S. and Canada. The Syndicate handles international sales.

Horror icon Romero had written a treatment for the movie before he passed in 2017 and regarded Twilight Of The Dead as the conclusion to his epic saga, which comprised six movies and various spinoffs and remakes. The last movie in the franchise came out in 2009. Twilight Of The Dead was first revealed in 2021. The producers previously told us they haven’t closed the door on the possibility of additional movies in a new franchise should this new one go well.

The film, whose cast and creative makeup has evolved in recent years, is driven by the Roundtable Entertainment team, led by producers John Baldecchi and Sarah Donnelly with executive producer and Roundtable President, Dominic Ianno, and in partnership with Suzanne Romero. Paolo Zelati is producer, screenwriter and author of the treatment together with Romero. Producers also include Bob Yari, Shaun Sanghani of SSS Entertainment and Aanaxion’s Kenneth Kim, Ho Sung Pak and George Furla.

title: ‘Celebrity Traitors’ Returns With Biggest Ever Launch Ep Of Nearly 9 Million Viewers
summary: The BBC’s Celebrity Traitors launch has become one of the most highly-anticipated of the year and a colossal 8.9 million viewers tuned in last night. They watched an opener of high high drama, and a little bit of eccentric comedy. No spoilers in this article – check out our recap here – but per the […]
content:
The BBC’s Celebrity Traitors launch has become one of the most highly-anticipated of the year and a colossal 8.9 million viewers tuned in last night. They watched an opener of high high drama, and a little bit of eccentric comedy.

No spoilers in this article – check out our recap here – but per the just-released overnight figures, last night’s 75-minute opener was watched by 8.9 million, peaking just over 9 million.

This is comfortably a record for the opening episode of The Traitors in the UK across both celebrity and civilian versions. The number will inevitably grow once people who missed last night’s ep catch up.

Last year’s Celebrity Traitors Season 1 kicked off with 3 million fewer viewers and the opener of the civilian Traitors from earlier this year was similarly far behind.

Watch on Deadline

Last night’s ep was watched by more than half of the overall number of people tuning in to TV at the time, an enormous share of nearly 55%. It became the second most-watched episode of TV this year, excluding sport, behind only the final episode of the civillian Traitors from January. It was followed by companion show Celebrity Traitors: Uncloaked, which drew in 3 million viewers.

Celebrity Traitors is into its second season and will air every Thursday and Friday night at 8 p.m. GMT (12 p.m. PT) for the coming month.

Cast this season includes Jerry Hall, Richard E. Grant, Myha’la, Bella Ramsey and Maya Jama.

There is also Joe Lycett, Miranda Hart, Romesh Ranganathan, Amol Rajan, Professor Hannah Fry, James Blunt, Julie Hesmondhalgh, Leigh-Anne Pinnock, Michael Sheen, Ross Kemp, Sharon Rooney, Joanne McNally, King Kenny, Rob Beckett, and Sebastian Croft.

The show is now arguably the BBC’s biggest entertainment juggernaut and anticipation was huge for last night’s opener. Trails have been shown during all BBC primetime shows for a while now. The fifth season of the civilian Traitors will kick off early next year. In the U.S., Peacock continues to air a successful version hosted by Scottish presenter Alan Cumming.

Celebrity Traitors is produced by Studio Lambert.

title: ‘The Good Girls’ Lead Ilse Salas to Star in Quijote Films’ ‘To Die on Your Feet’ (‘Morir de Pie’) a Project Pitched at Iberseries & Platino Industria (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Mexican actress Ilse Salas, winner of Mexico’s Best Actress Ariel Award for “The Good Girls” (“Las niñas bien”), will lead the cast of the Quijote Films wry dramedy “To Die on Your Feet” (“Morir de Pie”), which has been pitched this week at the Iberseries & Platino Industria in Madrid. This is the second fiction […]
content:
Mexican actress Ilse Salas, winner of Mexico’s Best Actress Ariel Award for “The Good Girls” (“Las niñas bien”), will lead the cast of the Quijote Films wry dramedy “To Die on Your Feet” (“Morir de Pie”), which has been pitched this week at the Iberseries & Platino Industria in Madrid.

This is the second fiction feature of Chilean director María Paz González who first broke out with her fiction debut, “Lina de Lima,” which world premiered at the Toronto Film Festival and won at FIC Valdivia. A journalist as well as filmmaker, she is also known for her 2011 feature documentary, “Hija.”

Described as a social-critique dramedy about a profession threatened by AI, “To Die on Your Feet” follows Cruz, an actress who works as a simulated patient for medical students. One night, she sees a body fall from her building and instead of helping, simply carries on with her life. Security cameras capture her actions. Unable to explain herself, she realizes that her profession has made her insensitive.

Popular on Variety

Salas is among the most acclaimed Mexican actresses of her generation. Aside from bringing home Mexico’s prestigious Ariel Award for “The Good Girls” in 2019, she was nominated for the Ariel for her performances in Alonso Ruizpalacios’ “Güeros” and Abner Benaim’s “Plaza Catedral,” Panama’s shortlisted entry to the 94th Academy Awards.

“Latin American cinema is the cinema I watch, seek out, make and dream about. Our voice needs to reach farther and we are making it heard,” said Salas.

The dramedy’s trajectory has taken it across the world through a variety of development and co-production programs in such festivals as Marseille, Toulouse, San Sebastián, the Berlinale and Discovery TIFF 2029. It has already been snapped up by Hulu, HBO and Mubi for various territories.

“To Die on Your Feet” also received backing from the Pfeffer del Sur fund of the José Ignacio International Film Festival.

Like many Chilean projects, it has enlisted a team of co-producers from various countries. The six-country co-production includes lead producer Quijote Films (Chile) alongside Amore Cine (Spain), Sutor Kolonko (Germany), Tarantula (Luxembourg), Bocacha (Uruguay) and MartFilms (Mexico).

Said Quijote Film’s Giancarlo Nasi: “We have spent years developing ‘Morir de pie’ as an international co-production and having Ilse Salas join as the lead is a decisive step forward. She is an actress we have admired for a long time, from films by filmmakers we love, such as ‘Güeros’ (Berlinale, Tribeca), to outstanding productions for major streaming platforms. Her career demonstrates extraordinary range, an exceptional level of acting and at the same time, a very special connection with audiences. It is precisely that combination of humor, discomfort and emotion that María Paz Gonzalez is looking for in this story.”

Meanwhile, Quijote, the Chilean production company with the largest number of completed international co-productions — 35 to date, including Chile’s first co-production agreements with Ukraine and South Africa — is now preparing a new milestone: the first Chile–Morocco co-production, the feature documentary “Don’t Let the Sun Go Up on Me,” co-produced with French company Haut et Court.

It will be directed by Moroccan filmmaker Asmae El Moudir, winner of the Best Director Award in Un Certain Regard at Cannes 2023 for “The Mother of All Lies.” The project is currently in development and participated in the Venice Production Bridge 2026.

However, the news comes amid a separate controversy: Chile’s Ministry of Cultures revoked the Audiovisual Minority Co-Production fund awarded to “The Smell of Apples,” the first Chilean co-production with the African continent, following an administrative observation.

The case is currently under review by the Quijote Films’ legal team, who are determining the next steps, just as the film, directed by John Trengove (“The Wound,” “Manodrome”), has had its world premiere in the Platform competition at TIFF 2026. Platform is the festival’s only competitive section and this year, the winning film also receives a direct spot in the Academy Awards race for Best International Feature Film. Pic was a strong contender to represent South Africa in that race, which has however gone to “Variations on a Theme” by Devon Delmar and Jason Jacobs.

title: ‘A Few Good Men’ on Broadway: Aaron Sorkin, Bradley Whitford and Team Behind Revival on Why It’s ’So Fucking Relevant’ in Trump Era
summary: Aaron Sorkin never truly feels his scripts are finished. “They’re just confiscated,” he says. “There comes a time when someone says, ‘Pencils down.’” So when director Michael Arden proposed the first Broadway revival of “A Few Good Men,” Sorkin saw an opportunity. “The play needed another draft or two,” Sorkin says. It had been a […]
content:
Aaron Sorkin never truly feels his scripts are finished. “They’re just confiscated,” he says. “There comes a time when someone says, ‘Pencils down.’”

So when director Michael Arden proposed the first Broadway revival of “A Few Good Men,” Sorkin saw an opportunity.

“The play needed another draft or two,” Sorkin says. It had been a hit when it ran on Broadway in 1989, and Sorkin himself adapted it into a 1992 film led by Tom Cruise and directed by Rob Reiner, but there was still more to be done. “Michael allowed me to do another draft and to hang a subtle lantern on this new, very relevant theme: A search for decency. What is it to be decent?”

The revival opens on Oct. 29 at Lincoln Center’s Vivian Beaumont Theater. And while the emphasis may have shifted, the plot remains the same: Amidst the court-martial investigation of two U.S. Marines accused of killing a Private, Joanne Galloway (played here by Krysta Rodriguez) must convince Daniel Kaffee (Tom Blyth) to pursue a lead implicating the imposing Colonel Nathan Jessep as complicit. That role — the personification of U.S. military might and of its corruption — was played on film by Jack Nicholson, and is now inhabited by Bradley Whitford, who’d been a replacement Kaffee in the first stage production.

Popular on Variety

The play’s depiction of extrajudicial killing and out-of-control military leadership resonate with Whitford. “I wish I lived in a world where this play wasn’t so terribly relevant again,” he says. “It should be a little courtroom chestnut about a time that has passed. But the fundamental argument on the planet today is: Do we survive through law and civil structures, or do we give into the dangers of thinking you can kill your way into security?” The question the plot of “A Few Good Men” asks is whether Jessep oversaw the murder of an inconvenient soldier in order to preserve unity among his corps. And the question hanging above it is whether Kaffee can push himself to do the right, but inconvenient, thing in fighting back.

Aaron Sorkin and Michael Arden during rehearsals for “A Few Good Men”

The concept of a lawless military felt familiar for the cast. “Every time you look at the news,” says Blyth, “you see something about Pete Hegseth’s military — and how it’s going back to this exact time.” Indeed, the only reason Sorkin didn’t set his new draft in the present day is that Guantanamo Bay, the U.S. military base where the play is set, has become a detention facility for migrants, complicating the story.

“I’ve admired this country,” says Blyth, an Englishman who came to the U.S. to study at Juilliard and has led films including “The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes” and “People We Meet on Vacation.” “To be doing this play, as a person who has chosen to come here, at a time when America is having a reckoning about war and masculinity — I’m loving sorting through Pandora’s box.” This marks Blyth’s Broadway debut, and he rapturizes about the theater in his adopted homeland. “I got the bug when I was really young, and American playwrights — it’s the epitome of great work.”

The play’s politics extend to gender: Rodriguez, a Broadway veteran, notes that her character, played on film by Demi Moore, outranks Blyth’s in the military, but she’s second on the legal team. “She’s insulted constantly,” Rodriguez says. “She’s diminished. She’s told no — and she finds a way every single time.” (And, she notes, Galloway must do all that Kaffee does “in a pencil skirt and heels.”)

The current Secretary of Defense comes up again, as Sorkin remarks to Rodriguez that “one of the things [Hegseth] is doing is kicking out women. Hyper-qualified women are gone.”

The misogyny “is not anachronistic,” Whitford says. “There are these moments when I go after her, but we have a president who says, ‘Quiet, piggy!’ to women. Why is this play so fucking relevant?”

But it isn’t just politics that make “A Few Good Men” both intriguing and thorny for its cast. Whitford, who after his first run in this play appeared on Sorkin’s TV shows “The West Wing” and “Studio 60 on the Sunset Strip,” has by now experienced the writer’s famously rhythm-driven dialogue — although there was a learning curve. (He recalls throwing up backstage the first night he played Kaffee, wondering, as he puts it, “Why did I let my life bring me to this?”)

Arden, who has won Tonys for musicals “Parade” and “Maybe Happy Ending,” notes that the two straight plays he’d wanted his whole career to direct were “this and a Shakespeare. Both are musicals in their own way.” As he puts it, “it moves from scene to scene with a dexterity that is technically impossible — and that’s what musicals are.”

The pace of the Sorkinian banter is meaningful beyond its showiness. It reflects the characters’ intelligence — though they’re at odds, none is the dumb one. “You see our competence in the way we can volley back and forth,” Rodriguez says. “It puts people at ease that we know what we’re talking about, that we can keep that ball in the air.”

But it is simply fun on its own terms, too. “It’s buoyant,” says Blyth. “And a lot of that is the pacing. We’re having fun with it — which you would think would be antithetical to the message of the play, but I’m a big fan of serving your medicine with something sweet.” He looks forward to hearing audience laughter: “The audience is much more receptive when they’re able to have a chuckle, right before they get slapped in the face with reality.”

Conjuring that reality has taken hard work. Much like Whitford back in the late 1980s, Blyth is realizing that Kaffee basically never gets to leave the stage. “I keep wandering off into the wings when a scene is done — when I should be starting the next scene,” he says. “It’s not that I want to leave!”

But then he’s filling the shoes of Tom Cruise — no small feat, even for a Juilliard grad. Making the politics seem urgent to a New York audience, may be relatively easy compared to this production’s more pressing task Blyth, Rodriguez, and Whitford are stepping into roles played by legendary movie stars in a film that, as many expressed in the wake of Reiner’s death, is now seen as a modern classic.

Arden says that many people he’s met think he’s making a new adaptation of the film’s script, not a revival of a play. “I have to correct them and remind them of theater history. We’re approaching it not as the film on stage but as if we were approaching a classic text. Even if they’ve seen the film, it will feel new and like we’re a pace ahead of the audience’s memory.”

“There’s a solemnity to the movie that the play does not have,” Whitford says. “Usually, if you’re doing a comedy, you have this artificial obligation to be funny all the time, and if you’re doing a drama, you have this artificial obligation to be irony-deficient.” This production, solemn about our obligations to one another but committed to providing a good night out at the theater, is neither. Says Whitford, “Aaron weaves those things together in a really organic way.”

Lead illustration: Columbia Pictures/Courtesy Everett Collection. From left: Pierre Mouton/Getty Images for Dom Perignon; Scott Kirkland/FXX via Getty Images; Taylor Hill/Getty Image

title: Madison Avenue Makeover: Marketers Face Big Challenges in Bid to Reach Elusive Consumers
summary: Capturing attention — the first job of advertising — has never been so difficult. With consumers distracted by alerts, texts, posts, emails and likes — not to mention the constant churn of daily life — it’s little wonder that more advertisers are breaking tradition and experimenting at a dizzying pace. In just the past few […]
content:
Capturing attention — the first job of advertising — has never been so difficult.

With consumers distracted by alerts, texts, posts, emails and likes — not to mention the constant churn of daily life — it’s little wonder that more advertisers are breaking tradition and experimenting at a dizzying pace. In just the past few months, Netflix granted a marketing partner permission to put its well-known ad character into one of its series in a cameo, and Zoom tapped a prominent news influencer to help examine what the company calls “solopreneurs” in a sponsored video series.

No one is giving up on good ol’ TV ads. But never before have advertisers seemed so willing to embrace something else.

Popular on Variety

Recent financials tell the tale. In the industry’s most recent upfront market, when U.S. media companies tried to sell the bulk of their commercial inventory, ad spending on broadcast TV dropped by approximately 5.3% compared to 2025, according to an analysis by Media Dynamics, a consulting firm that tracks such outlays. Spending on cable TV fell even more, with marketers cutting outlays by 7.7%. Meanwhile, the volume of ad commitments put toward streaming rose a whopping 30%.

With new types of advertising come new challenges. Those issues and the wealth of new opportunities will be on display Oct. 7 as Variety assembles marketing and advertising leaders in New York for the Variety Experience and Culture Summit: The IRL Advantage Presented by OUTFRONT. In preparation for a day of conversations, insights and analysis, we’ve studied five major areas of expertise that modern Madison Avenue leaders need to master:

Influencers and Creators: Digital-native personalities born of YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, Twitch, et al. are the most au courant vehicle in the business of ballyhoo. The data is clear: more young consumers recognize authenticity in creators and influencers than they do in many celebrities and journalists attached to traditional TV vehicles and movies. And yet, influencers aren’t immune to boneheaded moves. Good Good Golf, a popular golf content channel on YouTube, generated an unwelcome controversy in August after a 15-second clip from a commercial Good Good made went viral for all the wrong reasons,

showing one of Good Good’s founders shoving a woman. It was meant as a spoof on golfers’ obsession with their beloved golf clubs, but it backfired — to say the least. The uproar from consumers cost

Good Good its advertising partnership with Callaway Golf, and it led to the exits of Good Good’s CEO and president.

Measurement: Advertisers have, for decades, struggled to determine exactly how many people were exposed to a commercial, but that task has become exponentially more difficult in the digital age. Nielsen and a bevy of rival upstarts are all working to find new ways to capture all types of viewing. Still, the market is splintered around various techniques and proprietary audience-tracking systems devised

by media giants and the ad community. The absence of a common yardstick to measure success — a la Nielsen ratings and box office receipts — makes it harder to tell if marketers are getting any bang

for their bucks.

Programmatic buys: The rise of streaming has spurred the embrace of ad purchasing done on a programmatic basis that relies on specific algorithms designed to ensure that the spots are put in front of a specific target audience, like first-time car buyers or expectant mothers. But doing so also means in many cases that consumers see the same ads repeatedly — a condition that leads to what is known as “wear out,” or resistance to engaging with the spot.

Sports: Advertisers still want to put their spots in an arena — programming that reaches millions of people all watching at once. As streaming makes scripted fare and reality shows available at the click of a button, sports are seen as one of the last places to capture the biggest crowds. That has spurred dozens of advertisers who normally didn’t spend a lot of money on sports to start doing so, driving up prices and crowding the marketing field.

AI production: Ad agencies can cut costs by relying on AI and other types of technologies to

create all kinds of visuals. But should they? Sharp-eyed viewers may already have noticed fine print running in some TV ads that discloses how AI was used in the creation of a commercial. Some of the efforts are obvious and the graphics look off-kilter. As time goes by and such sights become more common, will there be any pushback?

title: CBS Sports, Tony Romo Break Up Following Pre-Season Intoxication Incident
summary: CBS Sports kicked off a massive industry spending spree when it lured former Dallas Cowboys quarterback Tony Romo to its NFL booth in 2017. Now the sports outlet is likely to tamp down on costs by parting ways with the celebrated color commentator. “CBS Sports and Tony Romo have mutually agreed to part ways. We […]
content:
CBS Sports kicked off a massive industry spending spree when it lured former Dallas Cowboys quarterback Tony Romo to its NFL booth in 2017. Now the sports outlet is likely to tamp down on costs by parting ways with the celebrated color commentator.

“CBS Sports and Tony Romo have mutually agreed to part ways. We thank Tony for his contributions over the past nine years and wish him the best moving forward,” the company said in a statement Friday. JJ Watt, who has filled in for Romo so far this season, will continue to do so alongside regulars Jim Nantz and Tracy Wolfson.

Romo in September pleaded no contest to a charge of operating while intoxicated stemming from an incident that took place in Milwaukee in July, and expressed hope that he’d be able to resume his NFL duties for the Paramount Skydance broadcast network. CBS Sports placed the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback on leave after he was arrested following a traffic stop made on Interstate 43 in Wisconsin.



On Friday, the announcer said he would “use this time to take a break, something I’ve never done before, and focus on my health and my family before moving on to my next opportunity.” He expressed pride in “what I accomplished at CBS Sports over the last nine years. I approached my role as a game analyst the way I’ve approached everything in my life–with a desire to win and be the best that I can be.”

Popular on Variety

Romo’s departure from CBS Sports may raise more questions than it answers. His exit opens a prime position during the network’s NFL season at a time when that sports has become even more critical to the fortunes of the company soon to be known as Skydance — the parent company formed from the merger of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery. The merged company will carry billions in debt, which could crimp its ability to spend heavily on new talent.

TV-sports outlets have been pouring out money to lure top NFL announcers, with Fox and Disney shelling out top dollar to lure, respectively, Tom Brady and Troy Aikman and Joe Buck. Many top announcers’ contracts are expected to lapse after the end of this season, including not only Aikman’s, but Greg Olsen at Fox, and Al Michaels at Amazon. The Athletic has reported that ESPN has secured Buck to a new deal and that Amazon has signed Kirk Herbstreit, who also calls college game at ESPN, to provisional terms. ESPN and Amazon declined to comment on the status of those announcers’ deals.

TV networks rushed to line up top talent to call games after the NFL struck a pivotal 11-year rights deal in 2021. At the time, the thought from many TV sports chiefs was that they had to spend money to make money. Tony Romo carved out new terrain at CBS Sports after revealing a knack for predicting game play — all but forcing CBS to re-sign the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback to a multi-season pact in 2020 valued at around $17 million a year.

Since that time, most of CBS’ contemporaries have followed suit. When ESPN signed former Fox Sports mainstays Buck and Aikman to deals in 2022 to call “Monday Night Football,” it was seen as a critical move that would help the Disney-backed sports-media giant soothe what had become a troubled relationship with the NFL. Amazon lured NBC Sports’ Al Michaels and ESPN’s Herbstreit to serve as the voices for “Thursday Night Football.” And Fox secured the services of none other than Brady, a move that crowded out sportscaster Olsen.

People familiar with the market estimate top football-booth personnel can earn between $15 million and $20 million per season.

CBS Sports may have other talent issues to juggle in weeks to come. Ian Eagle, an up and comer who calls secondary NFL games for CBS Sports, is also believed to have a contract that is set to lapse. He also calls NBA games for Amazon’s Prime Video.

Romo previously cited multiple back surgeries that spurred his retirement from the NFL as a factor in the recent incident, noting they “left me with constant, debilitating pain” which “led to a dependence on pain medication, and my efforts to get off those medications led to an over-reliance on alcohol.”

“None of this is an excuse,” Romo said. “These are my failures and I take responsibility for them.”





More to come….

title: Dan Houser on Leaving ‘GTA 6’ Studio Rockstar Games, Starting an Absurd New Company and Why He Doesn’t Play Open-World Games Anymore
summary: “Red Dead Redemption” and “Grand Theft Auto” mastermind Dan Houser is ready to spill the first significant details about his next video game projects. The co-founder and former head writer of Rockstar Games is currently developing two titles at his new media company, Absurd Ventures, which he formally launched in 2023 following his 2020 exit […]
content:
“Red Dead Redemption” and “Grand Theft Auto” mastermind Dan Houser is ready to spill the first significant details about his next video game projects.

The co-founder and former head writer of Rockstar Games is currently developing two titles at his new media company, Absurd Ventures, which he formally launched in 2023 following his 2020 exit from Rockstar.

“One is an open-world comedy which is trying to really lean into comedy and character memory, and that we’ll have more information on in the next few months,” Houser says on this week’s episode of Variety‘s “Strictly Business” podcast. “And the other is a dystopian sci-fi about a video game development gone very wrong, and about a rogue AI that discovered sentience. But unfortunately, it was made by two people that didn’t like each other, so it doesn’t like itself.”

Popular on Variety

The untitled games are just two of the many projects Houser and his longtime writing partner Jeffrey “Lazlow” Jones (a fellow Rockstar alum) have in the works at Absurd Ventures, which is building out its own original IPs beginning with three worlds: “A Better Paradise,” “American Caper” and the “Absurdaverse.” Currently, Absurd is rolling out graphic novels and comics, fiction podcasts, books and animated series, along with the planned games, to give consumers a full transmedia experience in each of these new Houser-created properties.

LISTEN to the full conversation on Variety’s “Strictly Business” podcast:

“It’s a privilege to be tied to stuff that was really successful and to have worked in great teams with great people and do innovative new things,” Houser says. “All we’re trying to do now is do a version of that for this period, and try and do it in a new way and see if there’s anything interesting we can say with new IP.”

In order to do that properly, Houser has been tuning out the noise surrounding the upcoming release of “Grand Theft Auto VI,” including the 27-minute extended look presented by Netflix in August.

“I haven’t seen it yet. I will try and avoid it because I always try and avoid stuff that’s going to distract or disrupt me creatively,” Houser says. “And given that I spend a large amount of time trying to make open-world games, and the rest of my conscious time trying to figure out innovative ways to market them, I don’t need to see what other people are [doing]. I’m always trying to think about new ways of doing it, not sit there in some kind of comparison of what I would have done differently.”

Absurd Ventures Absurd Ventures

This is not exclusive to “GTA” though, as Houser says he doesn’t “play a lot of open-world games” at all anymore: “I find when I play them, I can almost deconstruct the strengths and weaknesses of the team in real time and it’s distracting. I’m always thinking, ‘Well, their animation team is weak, but I think this game design is fantastic.’ And, ‘Oh, I can imagine that meeting when they discuss this feature.’ I’m not a game designer, I’m a sort of creative director. So I’m trying to always find new things that haven’t been done before, or that I can steal from older media, quite frankly or just inspired me or things I always thought about.”

Houser says he manages this by having a team full of people who are keeping up with the latest games and trends.

“It’s not my job within any company that I’ve ever worked at, thankfully, to be the person that understands what everyone else is doing,” Houser says. “I’m trying to think about new ways of doing it. So when we worked on ‘Red Dead Redemption,’ as soon as we started working, I never watched another Western. I never watched ‘The Sopranos’ until after I left Rockstar. I saw one episode, because my girlfriend-now-wife and I did watch the finale in real time. I’d not seen any of it before that moment. And then I watched it all during COVID. And I’m grateful. It’s so good that it would have disrupted everything I did on ‘GTA,’ had I watched at the time. So I really try and avoid things that I think are going to overly influence me.”

Until Houser is able to fully reveal what his next games look like, there will be speculation about how they will stack up to his previous work, especially after “Grand Theft Auto VI” launches Nov. 19 and the world sees the first “GTA” game made without him.

“In terms of will I always be compared to it? I don’t know,” Houser says. “I mean, hopefully, on some level there could be no greater compliment. On another level, I hope some of the stuff we make is going to be successful in its own right. It’s no problem to have made good things, but of course, if you make good things, if the new stuff’s not as impactful, that’s going to be disappointing in some ways. But it’s still a privilege to make anything, otherwise you’re just always drowning in your own previous creative work.”

Houser says he thinks his job “isn’t to be successful in media,” but “to make things I’m proud of.”

“Certainly, there was a lot of pressure making any ‘GTA’ game when I was on them,” Houser says. “And the way I would control that pressure for me was to say, am I making something with as much integrity as I can muster and am I making something I’m proud of? And does it feel fresh, new? And if that’s the case, let the results fall where they may. And certainly, even with games at Rockstar that were not successful, I was proud of them if we’d done what I thought was a good job. And so that’s going to be the same here. We can’t sit there going, if it’s not the biggest thing ever, I’m a failure. Because then you’ve got to process either, I’m a failure, I’m a success — but it feels just the same. So the work is the creative work, not what the market thinks of it.”

“Strictly Business” is Variety’s weekly podcast featuring conversations with industry leaders about the business of media and entertainment. (Please click here to subscribe to our free newsletter.) New episodes debut every Friday and can be downloaded at Apple Podcasts, Amazon Music, Spotify, Google Play, SoundCloud and more.

title: Tony Romo And CBS Sports Part Ways After His Drunk-Driving Arrest
summary: CBS Sports said Friday that it has mutually agreed with its lead NFL analyst Tony Romo to part ways, after he was put on leave in July following his arrest on suspicion of driving under the influence. “CBS Sports and Tony Romo have mutually agreed to part ways,” CBS Sports said today. “We thank Tony […]
content:
CBS Sports said Friday that it has mutually agreed with its lead NFL analyst Tony Romo to part ways, after he was put on leave in July following his arrest on suspicion of driving under the influence.

“CBS Sports and Tony Romo have mutually agreed to part ways,” CBS Sports said today. “We thank Tony for his contributions over the past nine years and wish him the best moving forward.”

The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback pleaded no contest after he was arrested July 23 on a Wisconsin highway. An open bottle of alcoholic beverage was found in the passenger side of the vehicle, according to the AP. He was taken into custody after field sobriety tests.

CBS put Romo on leave soon after, about a month before the start of the NFL season. JJ Watt moved into the booth with Jim Nance to replace Romo on the sports networks’ lead NFL announcer paring. The network said today Watt will continue to partner with Nantz and Tracy Wolfson “on our lead NFL announce team for the rest of the season. All other teams remain the same, including Ian Eagle, Ross Tucker and Evan Washburn.”

Watch on Deadline

Romo also released a statement today.

“I’m proud of what I accomplished at CBS Sports over the last nine years,” Romo said today. “I approached my role as a game analyst the way I’ve approached everything in my life – with a desire to win and be the best that I can be. I’m going to use this time to take a break, something I’ve never done before, and focus on my health and my family before moving on to my next opportunity. I am grateful for my time with CBS Sports and for the continued support of my family and friends, as well as the NFL community and fans.”

title: ‘The Great British Bake Off’ Host Alison Hammond Has Heart Check After Health Scare Live On TV
summary: Alison Hammond has revealed that she went to hospital to have tests done on her heart after suffering a health scare midway through presenting This Morning on ITV. The Great British Bake Off co-host posted an Instagram Story from her hospital bed on Friday, in which she told fans that she was “fine” but was […]
content:
Alison Hammond has revealed that she went to hospital to have tests done on her heart after suffering a health scare midway through presenting This Morning on ITV.

The Great British Bake Off co-host posted an Instagram Story from her hospital bed on Friday, in which she told fans that she was “fine” but was having “my old ticker checked out.”

Hammond said she may have suffered a palpitation or panic attack while she was live on television, meaning she had to leave the This Morning studio.

“I know you’re all worried about me,” she said. “Honestly, I am fine, first of all. I’m getting my old ticker checked out. I had a little bit of a palpitation, and now I’m getting it all checked out. But I think I’m okay. I’m hoping it was just a little panic attack or something like that. I love you all.

“I’m so sorry I left you. I would never normally do that. I would never leave a TV show, but so you know, I wasn’t very well. But hopefully I’m going to be all right. The doctors are so lovely, and they’re checking me out, and hopefully everything’s going to be fine.”

Watch on Deadline

Hammond and This Morning co-host Dermot O’Leary were presenting a segment about pets when the incident happened. Hammond left the studio, with O’Leary telling viewers after an ad break: “Welcome back to This Morning, Alison is feeling a little unwell, so she’s just had to duck out. Hopefully she’ll be back.”

Alison Hammond joined the This Morning team in 2003 after originally rising to fame on Big Brother in 2002. She has gone on to become one of the UK’s most beloved TV stars, hosting Bake Off with Noel Fielding since 2023. Hammond is also known for her viral interviews, including her 2017 sit-down with Ryan Gosling and Harrison Ford for Blade Runner 2049.

Signing off her Instagram message to fans on Friday, she said: “Look, I’m rocking it. Look how good I look. Still got my makeup on from This Morning. Lush. Love you, babs.”

title: ‘Spring Awakening’ Revival’s Off-Broadway Run Extended Into Spring
summary: The Spring Awakening off Broadway will continue into the spring. Citing “unprecedented demand,” the musical revival’s producers said Friday that the show from Steven Sater and the late Duncan Sheik is extending its run at Studio Seaview through Sunday, April 4. It had been set to wrap on Valentine’s Day at the venue. Previews start […]
content:
The Spring Awakening off Broadway will continue into the spring.

Citing “unprecedented demand,” the musical revival’s producers said Friday that the show from Steven Sater and the late Duncan Sheik is extending its run at Studio Seaview through Sunday, April 4. It had been set to wrap on Valentine’s Day at the venue.

Previews start November 27 ahead of opening night on December 17.

“The response to Danya Taymor’s production of Spring Awakening has been incredible.” Seaview CEO said. “It is a testament to the enduring power of Duncan Sheik and Steven Sater’s seminal work and the way this musical continues to resonate with audiences. We are thrilled by the unprecedented demand for this production and could not be more pleased to extend its life with this incredible cast and company.”

Adapted from Frank Wedekind’s 1891 play, Spring Awakening follows a group of German adolescents in the late 19th century as they explore their own sexuality against the backdrop of a deeply repressive world. Michael Mayer’s original Broadway production with stars-in-waiting Jonathan Groff, Lea Michele and John Gallagher Jr, ran from 2006-09 at the Eugene O’Neill Theatre and won a leading eight Tony Awards including Best Musical.

Songwriter Sheik, who died September 17 at 56, scored a pair of Tonys — Best Original Score and Best Orchestrations — for his contemporary rock score. He also was known for the hit single “Barely Breathing,” which spent a remarkable 55 weeks on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1996-97.

Spring Awakening was revived in 2015 in a Deaf West Theatre production directed by Michael Arden.

title: Chloe Veitch Signs With Independent Artist Group
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Independent Artist Group has signed Chloe Veitch, the British TV personality, host, and digital creator, for representation. Veitch was just announced to be one of the stars of Netflix’s celebrity edition of Million Dollar Secret, where she joins an ensemble cast that includes David Arquette, Christine Quinn, Bridget Everett and Adam Rippon. She is also […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Independent Artist Group has signed Chloe Veitch, the British TV personality, host, and digital creator, for representation.

Veitch was just announced to be one of the stars of Netflix’s celebrity edition of Million Dollar Secret, where she joins an ensemble cast that includes David Arquette, Christine Quinn, Bridget Everett and Adam Rippon. She is also set to appear in Netflix’s competition series Outside, which premiered this month from British creator group the Sidemen.

IAG will work with Veitch to broaden her creative range into scripted entertainment, developing opportunities for her across film, television and emerging vertical and micro-series formats.

The Essex-born Veitch first rose to prominence on the inaugural season of Netflix’s Too Hot to Handle in 2020, building a global audience and a social media following in the millions. She went on to star in Netflix’s The Circle, where she finished as runner-up and was voted Fan Favorite, followed by Perfect Match, where she participated as a cast member in Season 1.

Watch on Deadline

Veitch has since made the transition from reality star to host, most recently leading Netflix’s Sneaky Links: Dating After Dark. She previously hosted Too Hot to Handle: Extra Hot, a digital companion series for Too Hot to Handle, and continues to expand her career across hosting, TV, digital content and entertainment. Her additional credits include Foul Play with Anthony Davis, Celebrity Hunted, Celebrity Ghost Trip and The Netflix Afterparty.

Now based in Los Angeles, Veitch is continuing to build her U.S. career while maintaining the international audience she developed through her Netflix projects. She has amassed more than 3 million followers across social platforms, including approximately 1.7 million followers on Instagram, 1.4 million on TikTok, and more than 40,000 YouTube subscribers.

title: Dolly Parton Broadway Musical Sets Its Lead Cast With Katie Rose Clarke As Dolly
summary: Dolly: A True Original Musical, the upcoming Broadway production that turned out to be the late superstar’s final passion project, has set its lead cast, all handpicked by Dolly Parton herself. Katie Rose Clarke will star as Dolly Parton, reprising her role from her critically acclaimed performance in the show’s Nashville production. Carrie St. Louis, […]
content:
Dolly: A True Original Musical, the upcoming Broadway production that turned out to be the late superstar’s final passion project, has set its lead cast, all handpicked by Dolly Parton herself.

Katie Rose Clarke will star as Dolly Parton, reprising her role from her critically acclaimed performance in the show’s Nashville production.

Carrie St. Louis, who was involved in some of the earliest readings of the musical and just wrapped up an acclaimed run on Broadway in Just In Time, will be featured as Dolly, the ambitious and talented singer/songwriter trying to make her break in the Nashville music scene. 11-year-old Norah Nunes, who was one of the finalists of the “Search for Dolly” online open casting call, will play Little Dolly.

The cast will also include Grammy nominee John Behlmann as Carl Dean, Dolly’s devoted husband of almost 60 years, and Tony Award winner Gabriel Ebert as Porter Wagoner, the larger-than-life country music star who first introduced Parton to a national television audience.

Watch on Deadline

The musical, featuring new music from Parton as well as her classic hits like “I Will Always Love You,” “Jolene,” “Coat of Many Colors” and “9 to 5,” will begin previews at Broadway’s St. James on Monday, December 7, with an official opening on January 19, 2027, what would have been Parton’s 81st birthday.

Dolly: A True Original Musical had its world premiere last year in Parton’s hometown of Nashville, and tells Parton’s story in her own words and songs. She was a producer along with Danny Nozell, Adam Speers for ATG Productions and Gavin Kalin Productions.

Bartlett Sher (To Kill a Mockingbird, South Pacific), directs.

In addition to the music, Parton has written the musical’s book along with two-time Emmy Award winner Maria S. Schlatter, who previously partnered with Parton on the Emmy-winning Netflix film Christmas on the Square.

The music team for the production includes two-time Tony Award winner and two-time Grammy winner Stephen Oremus (music supervisor), Charity Wicks (music director), John Clancy (orchestrations), and Kent Wells (musical consultant). The music team is completed by Richard Dennison (vocal arrangements and music arrangements) and Gregg Perry (music arrangements and vocal arrangements) who are longtime collaborators with Parton.

The creative team includes Mandy Moore (choreography), Derek McLane (scenic design), Jennifer Moeller (costume design), Donald Holder (lighting design), Peter Hylenski (sound design), Nathan Amzi and Joe Ransom (video design), Robert Pickens (hair design) and Studio Pickens (makeup design).

Additional casting and other details for the Broadway production will be announced in the coming weeks.

title: ‘Verity’ Had a Much More Twisted Ending. Then Came the Focus Group Screenings
summary: SPOILER ALERT: This article contains spoilers for “Verity,” now playing in theaters. To say that “Verity,” a new erotic thriller featuring the ubiquitous Anne Hathaway and Dakota Johnson — who gets to call the former “a selfish, Machiavellian cunt” — has sharply divided critics would be an understatement. This thing has taken a bigger beating […]
content:
SPOILER ALERT: This article contains spoilers for “Verity,” now playing in theaters.

To say that “Verity,” a new erotic thriller featuring the ubiquitous Anne Hathaway and Dakota Johnson — who gets to call the former “a selfish, Machiavellian cunt” — has sharply divided critics would be an understatement. This thing has taken a bigger beating than a piece of beef hanging in Rocky Balboa’s meat locker (our own critic called it a “a flat-footed dud”). And the majority of the film’s detractors took issue with its ending. (It is still predicted to win the box office weekend, becoming Hathaway’s third No. 1 movie this year.)

Directed by Michael Showalter (“Search Party”) and adapted from Colleen Hoover’s bestselling novel, the film tells the tale of Lowen Ashleigh (Johnson), a struggling young author who’s recruited by Jeremy (Josh Hartnett), the hot husband of novelist Verity Crawford (Hathaway), to ghostwrite the final book in her popular series from their secluded (and palatial) house in the woods. You see, Verity suffered a recent accident that’s not only left her wheelchair-bound, but also unable to talk or move a muscle. Once Lowen finds a manuscript stashed away by Verity, however, she realizes her idol may be far more sinister than she seems.

Popular on Variety

While Showalter took a number of liberties with Hoover’s source material, including eliminating one of the dead children — a move Hoover, who consulted on the film, called “the best change we could have made” — he’s kept the book’s ending largely intact, though he almost didn’t.

Verity’s manuscript reveals that she was resentful of her two children — and how they’d pulled Jeremy’s attention away from her — from the moment they’d entered the world. One day, she took their son and daughter out on the lake in a kayak and, knowing the children couldn’t swim, capsized it on purpose, killing their daughter (the son miraculously survived). Lowen grows to hate Verity and feel deep sympathy for Jeremy after consuming their memoir, eventually fucking and falling for him. Only Verity is alive! She’s been faking being paralyzed and mute the whole time! Once Lowen and Jeremy discover this, he chokes her to death at Lowen’s behest and they dump her body in the lake.

The action jumps six months into the future. As Lowen (now pregnant) and Jeremy are packing up the Crawford home, she finds a letter tucked under the floorboards claiming that the manuscript was merely a writing exercise where Verity was envisioning the darkest version of herself, and that after finding the manuscript, Jeremy attempted to kill her. Consumed by guilt, Verity acted paralyzed as penance, and to remain close to Jeremy and their remaining child.

“We tried a hundred million different ways to end this movie,” Showalter tells Variety. “Figuring out how to end the movie was the biggest challenge and the last thing that we did.”

“Verity” ends with pregnant Lowen and Jeremy driving off together into their new life as she looks out the window and ponders what the truth was regarding Verity, ultimately determining that it will always remain a mystery. But that wasn’t the ending that Showalter and his team originally intended.

“There’s two very significant other ways that the movie ended,” he explains. “In one version, Lowen, in that car scene, has that moment where she says, ‘I don’t know who to believe. One thing’s for sure: Verity was a master manipulator.’ And then she puts on a pair of sunglasses, leans back, and has this very cat-with-a-mouse-in-its-mouth look, puts her hand out the window, and as they’re driving away and a song is playing, she’s making [waves through the air] with her hand. So, the idea is that Lowen is the master villain. And then, you cut back to Verity sinking into the lake and her eyes open.” Yes, Verity was still alive!

Dakota Johnson and Anne Hathaway in “Verity.” ©Amazon/Courtesy Everett Collection

It’s an ending that seems more in line with the film’s campiness on its face, but Showalter says he couldn’t seem to get it to land the way he’d wanted.

“We tried a hundred different versions of that — of Verity still being alive, and of Lowen being the dark phoenix, because we liked it and it was really, really cool,” he says. “It was this amazing moment of, Holy crap! Has Lowen been the mastermind the whole time? It was the ending we always thought we were gonna do and it was what we had planned on. So, not showing her put the glasses on was such a massive revelation to realize.”

Showalter and the studio held a series of focus group screenings with audiences — a mix of those who’d read the book and those who hadn’t — and they kept getting the same specific feedback regarding the “dark phoenix” ending.

“A lot of times, when you’re screening a movie [for focus groups] and you’re getting feedback, the feedback is generic. It’s like, ‘I didn’t like the ending,’ but they may not be able to really tell you why. And what we figured out was, it’s because they want Lowen to be in a place of uncertainty when the movie’s over,” he shares.

Showalter continues: “It took us a really long time to realize the audience isn’t ready to make the kind of decision at the end of the movie that we had been giving Lowen. Lowen had this moment where she put on the sunglasses and was like, I don’t give a shit, and the audience wasn’t ready to go there with her. The audience wanted her to be like, What the fuck have I done? We realized the audience is Lowen and the audience wasn’t ready to put those glasses on.”

Hoover was “open to changes” between the book and the movie but stresses she’s satisfied with the ending they went with. “I couldn’t be happier,” she tells Variety. “I feel like you walk away from the movie with the same feelings you walk away from the book with and that was what I was hoping we would ultimately end up with. Those screenings really helped.”

title: Skydance’s Track Record: 20 Years of Tom Cruise, Mark Wahlberg, Action and More Action
summary: Next week, Paramount and Warner Bros. will officially combine into one mega-studio with a familiar name: Skydance. The deal is expected to close on Tuesday. “By combining them, we aren’t rewriting history — we’re equipping these iconic studios with a more powerful engine. Together, we are Skydance: a creative-first home for bold, quality storytelling,” CEO […]
content:
Next week, Paramount and Warner Bros. will officially combine into one mega-studio with a familiar name: Skydance. The deal is expected to close on Tuesday.

“By combining them, we aren’t rewriting history — we’re equipping these iconic studios with a more powerful engine. Together, we are Skydance: a creative-first home for bold, quality storytelling,” CEO David Elllison wrote on X Friday when announcing the new name.

But Ellison’s Skydance Media has been active since 2006, and has a track record of producing primarily franchise titles, action films and streaming fare, though its television slate is somewhat more diverse.

Of course franchises like “G.I. Joe” and “Star Trek” will remain a priority for the new studio, but does Skydance’s track record indicate anything about where the new combined studio’s priority will lie?

It seems unlikely that the Warner Bros. label will give up making awards contenders, or that Paramount will abandon rom-coms. But one thing seems to be a given: Ellison is big on crowd-pleasers, action films and familiar franchises, some that are decades-old.

Skydance have earned more than $8.7 billion at the global box office, a healthy haul for a relatively small player. But how will the name translate from a production shingle making a handful of films and shows a year to a massive combined operation that Ellison promises will release at least 30 movies per year? If nothing else, Mark Wahlberg probably doesn’t need to worry about his career prospects for a while.

Here are five takeaways from Skydance Media’s earlier films and TV series:

title: Sony in Talks to Land ‘Battlefield’ Video Game Movie From Christopher McQuarrie and Michael B. Jordan
summary: Sony is in talks to acquire Christopher McQuarrie and Michael B. Jordan’s big-screen adaptation of the popular “Battlefield” video game after a multi-studio bidding war. Sony declined to comment on the negotiations. McQuarrie is attached to write, direct and produce the feature adaptation of Electronic Arts’ military first-person shooter game, with Jordan attached to produce. […]
content:
Sony is in talks to acquire Christopher McQuarrie and Michael B. Jordan‘s big-screen adaptation of the popular “Battlefield” video game after a multi-studio bidding war.

Sony declined to comment on the negotiations.

McQuarrie is attached to write, direct and produce the feature adaptation of Electronic Arts‘ military first-person shooter game, with Jordan attached to produce. The newly minted best actor Oscar winner could star in the film, but that’s dependent on several factors.

Additional producers include Electronic Arts’ Jesse Stern, Emerald Neon’s Carter Swan, Vertigo’s Roy Lee and Miri Yoon of Vertigo and Outlier Society president Elizabeth Raposo.

Popular on Variety

Electronic Arts’ “Battlefield” franchise launched in 2002 with the World War II-set “Battlefield 1942.” The games focus on large-scale, online multiplayer battles between opposing military forces. Over the next twenty years, the games and their expansion packs focused on historical events, alternate history and future conflicts. “Battlefield 6,” the 18th installment of the series, was released last year and is set between 2027 and 2028, with a storyline that centers on a conflict between a fractured NATO and a private military company. The game went on to become the bestselling first-person shooter of the year (and in the franchise’s history), eclipsing Activision’s “Call of Duty.”

To note: “Call of Duty” is also getting the big-screen treatment at Paramount, with Peter Berg set to direct from a script by “Yellowstone” scion Taylor Sheridan. The studio previewed the long-awaited film adaptation of the hit video game franchise as part of its CinemaCon presentation earlier this month; the “Call of Duty” movie is dated for theatrical release on June 30, 2028.

McQuarrie takes on “Battlefield” as his next mission after (seemingly) wrapping up Tom Cruise’s tenure as secret agent Ethan Hunt in the long-running “Mission: Impossible” movie franchise with last year’s “The Final Reckoning.” McQuarrie is set to direct Arnold Schwarzenegger in a third Conan the Barbarian movie, titled “King Conan.” He’s also working with Cruise on his upcoming outer-space shot movie, directed by Doug Liman.

Jordan is no stranger to the world of video game IP. The actor starred as Navy SEAL John Clark in Tom Clancy’s “Without Remorse” for Amazon and has been developing an adaptation of “Rainbow Six” as a follow-up film. Before that, though, Jordan stars in, directs and produces a reimagining of “The Thomas Crown Affair” for Amazon MGM Studios, which hits theaters on March 5, 2027. He will also star as suave South Florida detective Ricardo “Rico” Tubbs opposite Austin Butler’s James “Sonny” Crockett in Universal’s “Miami Vice ’85.”

McQuarrie is represented by CAA; Jordan is represented by 1v1 Entertainment, WME, Johnson Shapiro Slewett & Kole and 2PM Sharp.

TheWrap first reported the news that Sony is the current frontrunner in negotiations for the “Battlefield” movie.

title: Mary Louise Weller, Who Played Sorority Girl in ‘Animal House,’ Dies at 79
summary: Mary Louise Weller, the actress known for her role as Mandy Pepperidge in “Animal House,” died Thursday after a long illness. She was 79. Her longtime partner Michael Roy Curtis and multiple reports confirmed her death. Weller was born in New York City on Oct. 2, 1946, and raised in Westwood, Calif. Actor-singer Danny Kaye […]
content:
Mary Louise Weller, the actress known for her role as Mandy Pepperidge in “Animal House,” died Thursday after a long illness. She was 79.

Her longtime partner Michael Roy Curtis and multiple reports confirmed her death.

Weller was born in New York City on Oct. 2, 1946, and raised in Westwood, Calif. Actor-singer Danny Kaye was her godfather and friend of her father. As a teenager, she trained with the U.S. Equestrian Team.

The actress made her film debut in the 1972 American political comedy “Hail!” In 1978, she starred in the TV film “Hunters of the Reef” and “The Evil” and landed her role as Mandy Pepperidge in the John Landis comedy hit “Animal House.”

Popular on Variety

When asked in 2012 if she knew “Animal House” would be a hit, Weller said, “I’m pretty sure all of us knew that the movie would be a huge hit… The script was simply brilliant…” She recalled showing then-head of ABC Brandon Stoddard the script: “He also knew it would be an enormous hit… but he warned me that it would be the movie I would always be known for…”

Following her role as the Pi House sorority sister and love interest, Weller appeared in Larry Peerce’s adaptation of Sylvia Plath’s “The Bell Jar,” “Once Upon a Spy,” “Forced Vengeance,” “Blood Tide” and “Q.”

The actress’s television credits include “Baretta,” “Kojak,” “CHiPS” and “Starsky & Hutch.” Her final on-screen appearance was in 1983 on “Quincy, M.E.”

Weller acted in several plays in New York and wrote “Four Alone,” a play that was performed at the Greenhouse Theater in Pasadena, Calif.

Weller is survived by her cousin Sheila Weller, an author whose books include the 2003 memoir “Dancing at Ciro’s: A Family’s Love, Loss, and Scandal on the Sunset Strip” about her family’s life in 1950s Hollywood.

title: Shane Paul McGhie & Dasan Frazier To Headline Issa Rae’s Male Friendship Comedy Pilot At HBO
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Shane Paul McGhie (Poker Face, The Last Shift) and Dasan Frazier (A Different World, Delphi) are set as the leads in Untitled Male Friendship Show, Issa Rae’s new half-hour comedy pilot at HBO. Written and exec produced by Rae, the pilot centers on Menzel (McGhie), a 28-year-old barber, aspiring sports manager and professional best […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Shane Paul McGhie (Poker Face, The Last Shift) and Dasan Frazier (A Different World, Delphi) are set as the leads in Untitled Male Friendship Show, Issa Rae‘s new half-hour comedy pilot at HBO.

Written and exec produced by Rae, the pilot centers on Menzel (McGhie), a 28-year-old barber, aspiring sports manager and professional best friend to JB (Frazier), a 27-year-old up-and-coming boxer, as they navigate ambition, insecurity, loneliness and the double-edged sword of success within the high-stakes world of professional boxing in Las Vegas.

Prentice Penny, a key collaborator of Rae’s on Insecure, will serve as showrunner, executive producer and pilot director. Jax Clark will exec produce for Hoorae alongside A Penny For Your Thoughts and Jonathan Berry and Dave Becky for 3 Arts Entertainment.

Watch on Deadline

McGhie’s credits include guest roles in Poker Face, Abbott Elementary and Grey’s Anatomy and as Jevon in Andrew Cohn’s feature The Last Shift. He’s repped by Innovative Artists Entertainment and Josiah Akinyele at ColorCreative.

Frazier most recently appeared in A Different World, which was just renewed by Netflix for a second season. Upcoming, he’ll be seen in a recurring role in Delphi, Prime Video’s new series out of the Creed universe, from Michael B. Jordan’s Outlier Society. Frazier is repped by Paradigm, Tassell Talent Group and Fox Rothschild.

content:
Sony Pictures is in talks to land rights for a feature adaptation of the popular Electronic Arts video game Battlefield that has Michael B. Jordan attached to produce and potentially star and Christopher McQuarrie on board to direct. McQuarrie would also pen the script and produce.

Plot details are being kept under wraps. Sony had no comment.

Additional producers include Electronic Arts’ Jesse Stern, Emerald Neon’s Carter Swan, Vertigo’s Roy Lee and Miri Yoon and Outlier Society president Elizabeth Raposo.

A long-running first-person shooter franchise, Battlefield launched in 2022 with Battlefield 1942. The games center on multiplayer warfare across land, air and sea, taking place in settings ranging from both world wars to Vietnam and the near future. Over the course of its lifetime, the franchise has sold tens of millions of copies worldwide.

Watch on Deadline

TheWrap first reported the news of Sony’s involvement.

title: American Cinematheque Award Skipping 2026 After Sked Conflict With Honoree Ryan Gosling
summary: The American Cinematheque said Friday that its 40th annual American Cinematheque Awards Gala, which was set to honor Ryan Gosling, will not take place this year. Organizers said Gosling was no longer available to accept the award due to scheduling conflicts. Today, the AC only said the new date for the gala would be in […]
content:
The American Cinematheque said Friday that its 40th annual American Cinematheque Awards Gala, which was set to honor Ryan Gosling, will not take place this year.

Organizers said Gosling was no longer available to accept the award due to scheduling conflicts. Today, the AC only said the new date for the gala would be in 2027, and that there will be a new honoree.

The AC announced in June that Gosling was its pick for the honor, coming off the outsized success of his latest movie Project Hail Mary. The 2026 tribute ceremony was set for November 2 at the Beverly Hilton.

The event, a mainstay on the Hollywood awards circuit that attracts serious star power, is an annual fundraiser for the nonprofit American Cinematheque that offers year-round programming at its Aero Theatre in Santa Monica, Los Feliz 3 Theatre in Los Feliz and Egyptian Theatre in Hollywood.

Watch on Deadline

Gosling, meanwhile, is plenty busy. After Amazon MGM Studios’ Project Hail Mary dominated the box office after its March release to gross $684.6 million globally, he’s got Star Wars: Starfighter coming in May 2027, followed by a re-team with Starfighter director Shawn Levy and writer Jonathan Tropper on a Ghost Rider movie for Marvel that will hit theaters in 2028.

Most recently, the American Cinematheque Award bestowed its award on Michael B. Jordan last year and Jessica Chastain in 2024. Past honorees also include Eddie Murphy, Steven Spielberg, Martin Scorsese, Tom Cruise, Jodie Foster, Al Pacino, George Clooney, Julia Roberts, Robert Downey Jr., Amy Adams, Spike Lee, Scarlett Johansson, Ryan Reynolds and Helen Mirren among others.

title: Kennedy Center Honors To Move To Capital One Arena Amid Closure Of Arts Complex
summary: The Kennedy Center Honors will move to a new location for the first time in its history, as it will be held at Capital One Arena in Washington, D.C. The ceremony will take place at the new venue on December 7, a center spokesperson said. The honorees have not been announced, and a broadcast partner […]
content:
The Kennedy Center Honors will move to a new location for the first time in its history, as it will be held at Capital One Arena in Washington, D.C.

The ceremony will take place at the new venue on December 7, a center spokesperson said. The honorees have not been announced, and a broadcast partner will be announced at a later date. The event’s contract with CBS, which broadcast the event since its origin in 1978, expired last year.

The Kennedy Center’s main building, where the honors have been held, is currently closed amid an assessment for safety risks, officials with the complex have told a federal judge.

Rep. Joyce Beatty (D-OH), an ex officio member of the board, sued the center earlier this year over its plans to close the complex for two years for a large-scale renovation. She also challenged the board’s decision to add Donald Trump‘s name to the center.

Watch on Deadline

A federal judge issued a preliminary injunction ruling that only Congress could add another name to the center, and ordering that the president’s name be taken down from its façade and other materials. He later rejected the board’s plans to add Trump’s name to the façade in other ways. The judge also prohibited the center from closing for two years unless the board more fully weighed its impact. The center has said that the recent closure is temporary, with safety risks being assessed on a week-to-week basis following the recent collapse of part of the ceiling.

The December 7 date is the traditional weekend for the ceremonies. Trump hosted the event last year, with honorees including Sylvester Stallone and George Strait. At the time, its then-president, Ric Grenell, said the ceremony had raised $23 million.

But the finances of the center have deteriorated. Its attorneys from the Justice Department warned last month that it was facing “certain financial collapse within weeks” and that adding Trump’s name to the complex may be the only way to get him to “lead the financial rescue of the center.” The attorneys later told an appeals court that Trump had raised $17 million “to keep it afloat.”

The attorneys wrote that “the funds are fast being expended, and without the Trump Administration, the accounts will dry up and Center will continue its deterioration into an unsafe structure that will eventually collapse, with a determination to follow on how to proceed and what to do with the site.”

Since Trump took over the center and ousted board members appointed by his predecessors, the center has seen a drop in ticket sales, while artists have canceled performances. The Washington Post and CNN have recently done deep dives on the dire state of Kennedy Center finances. Major shows ended in July, which had been the original time frame for when Trump and the center planned for the long-term closure for renovations.

title: Jack Reynor, John Magaro & Natalia Dyer Latest To Join HBO’s ‘The Trial Of Louise Woodward’
summary: EXCLUSIVE: The Trial of Louise Woodward, HBO’s true-crime limited series from creator Matthew Barry, has added three more to its starry cast: Jack Reynor (Lee Cronin’s The Mummy), John Magaro (The Agency), and Natalia Dyer (Stranger Things). Reynor plays Gerry Leone, the lead prosecutor in the show’s central trial. Magaro plays lead defense counsel Barry […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: The Trial of Louise Woodward, HBO‘s true-crime limited series from creator Matthew Barry, has added three more to its starry cast: Jack Reynor (Lee Cronin’s The Mummy), John Magaro (The Agency), and Natalia Dyer (Stranger Things).

Reynor plays Gerry Leone, the lead prosecutor in the show’s central trial. Magaro plays lead defense counsel Barry Scheck, with Dyer as Middlesex County assistant district attorney Ada Lynn Rooney.

The trio joins a cast led by Catriona Chandler in the title role. Joanne Froggatt, Meghann Fahy, Sagar Radia, Chloë Sevigny, and Hugh Laurie also star.

The Trial of Louise Woodward tells the shocking true story of how, in 1997, an 18-year-old British au pair (Chandler) was accused of shaking to death a baby left in her care by her American host family, setting off an international media firestorm as the trial unfolds in full view of both the British and American public.

Watch on Deadline

As previously announced, Froggatt plays Louise’s mother, Susan, with Fahy and Radia as Deborah and Sunil Eappen — parents of the victim, Matthew Eappen. Sevigny plays defense attorney Elaine Whitfield Sharp, with Laurie as Judge Hiller B. Zobel, who presided over the murder trial.

Barry wrote the series, serves as showrunner and is exec producing alongside Susanne Bier, who directs all episodes, as well as Frank Spotnitz, Emily Feller, Tobi de Graaff, and Antoine Douaihy. Big Light Productions and Anton TV are the production companies.

An Irish-American actor known for roles in the likes of Midsommar and Flora and Son, Reynor has recently been seen in John Carney’s Power Ballad, Lee Cronin’s The Mummy, and the second season of Prime Video’s Citadel. Upcoming, he’ll be seen starring in the second season of Apple’s Presumed Innocent, Amazon MGM’s Seasons, and the remake of Japanese film A Colt Is My Passport from Amazon MGM’s Orion Pictures. He is repped by WME, Range, and Sloane, Offer, Weber & Dern.

Known for projects like Past Lives and First Cow, Magaro also stars in Presumed Innocent Season 2, as well as Paramount+’s The Agency. Upcoming, he’ll be seen starring alongside Jeremy Allen White, Mandy Patinkin and Isabella Rossellini in Jeremiah Zagar’s The Painted Bride. He is repped by UTA, Authentic Talent & Literary Management, and Felker McGinnis & Ryan.

Best known for playing Nancy Wheeler in Netflix’s Stranger Things, Dyer will next be seen starring alongside Kiernan Shipka and Cole Sprouse in Amazon MGM’s rom-com Goodbye Girl. She is repped by Circle Management + Production, CAA, and Jackoway Austen Tyerman.

title: ‘Behemoth!’ Review: Pedro Pascal Is a Classical Cellist Skating Through a Midlife Crisis in Tony Gilroy’s Elevated Bauble of a Music Drama
summary: "Behemoth!" is a classical-musician movie. It’s a midlife-crisis movie. It’s a romantic mystery. It’s Tony Gilroy fiddling around with pure movie form.
content:
I was a classical musician growing up, so I’m probably more disposed than most to like a movie set in the classical-music world. Then again, that could mean that I set a higher bar for authenticity when it comes to depicting it. There’s no doubt that the cinema’s reigning masterpiece of classical-music drama is “Tár” — a great movie in so many other ways that that remains only one dimension of it. But Todd Field inhabited that world, and allowed the audience to do so, in a way that no previous director had. Two other films leap to mind that have the ring of deep-dish classical-music reality: “Mr. Holland’s Opus,” which beautifully caught the experience of studying music in high school, and “Maestro,” a movie I may have enjoyed more than others, even though it left out a ton of stuff about Leonard Bernstein (like, for instance, the heart of his conducting career in the ’50s and ’60s!), because I instinctively filled all of that in.

Viewed on that scale, “Behemoth!,” Tony Gilroy’s drama about a professional cellist, played with perky mystery by Pedro Pascal, scores on the level of authenticity. Pascal’s character, a renowned musician named Alex Serian, has been a member of various world-class symphony orchestras, notably in Chicago, but the film presents us with a more plugged-in contempo angle on this kind of career. In the new era, orchestras are foundering, the pay isn’t what it used to be, and even a virtuoso string musician might need a side gig or two. For Alex, that has meant playing in orchestras that are assembled to record movie scores — a major industry, and one that “Behemoth!” depicts as being nearly as high maintenance as the prestige symphony circuit.

Popular on Variety

The conductors who oversee the recording of the movie scores are portrayed as hyper-demanding corporate perfectionists. (One of them, a prima donna played by Thomas Kretschmann, makes it feel like you’re seeing Klaus Kinski going to work for Skydance.) And from the film’s opening scene, which immerses us in the lingo of rehearsal, which is a mixture of old-school classical Euro directives (“pianissimo”) and Hollywood jargon (“new ink”), we’re right there in the cavernous recording studio, feeling the heat and the nuance.

My all-time pet peeve in classical-music films is that characters who are supposed to be playing the violin or cello almost never look real — you can see from a mile away that they’re faking it, imitating the finger and bow movements like crude mimes. Tony Gilroy has solved this problem in the most committed way possible: He had Pedro Pascal learn to play the cello. That’s really Pascal doing it, which is why everything about his motions looks real, from the vibrato to the bowing to the way he moves his head. That devotion works for the film. It allows us to feel that Alex is as genuine in his talent as a professional athlete or a star chef. Virtuosity is the air he breathes. Not every orchestra player is a virtuoso, of course, but Alex, we learn, was a child prodigy who came from a high-powered musical family (we see a clip of him playing Bach as a 6-year-old on “The Tonight Show”). That’s his pedigree, and it’s also his problem, since the family craziness has messed him up.

In addition to presenting its musical demimonde with reverent accuracy, “Behemoth!” has another quality going for it: The film is playful. It’s not a symphony — it’s a scherzo. This is only the fourth feature Gilroy has directed (it’s his first since “The Bourne Legacy” in 2012), but coming off the “Star Wars” television series “Andor,” which he created and was the showrunner for, he makes his enthusiasm for the filmmaking process palpable. For most of the film, Alex is doing movie-score session work, and Gilroy introduces an impish device: We see and hear the orchestra recording a score (the music might be suspenseful, romantic, pensive), until seconds later it becomes the score of “Behemoth!” itself. I’m not honestly sure I can say what this slightly meta gambit accomplishes, but it’s clever and fun. Gilroy got no less than nine acclaimed film composers to contribute their talents to the movie (they include James Newton Howard and Alan Silvestri and are billed as the Behemoth! Collective). But he could easily have executed the exact same trick with just one composer.

Leaping around in time, Gilroy draws us into Alex’s world with an effervescent wink at the badness of his behavior. Alex is wriggling out of a fling with Carol, the wife of one of the Chicago orchestra’s wealthy patrons — she’s played by Olivia Wilde, who radiates such intense stalker energy here that we’re not quite sure how to react. Alex just keeps calm, and that’s what Pascal does, more or less, throughout the movie. Alex’s life is falling apart, yet somehow he’s the eye of the storm; everyone around him is screwier than he is. With an elegant mustache and perfect gelled hair that dips down onto his forehead, Pedro Pascal has never looked more dashing — he’s like a refined Burt Reynolds, or maybe a passive Brando. Between his classical chops and his glamorous looks, women drop for Alex, but he’s an artist who has drifted through life, drinking and having flings, always ready to move on to the next woman and the next city and the next gig. It’s a frictionless life he revels in. But something’s got to give.

Gilroy seems to have been influenced by the elliptical quality of “Tár,” though not always to good effect. I enjoyed, to a point, the cut-and-paste chronology of “Behemoth!,” but there’s a flaw in: The actors look identical in every scene, so some of it is confusing — like the episode in Dallas where Alex meets Nadia (Eva Victor), a star violinist who seems his match. They sleep together. But then, after a fraught phone conversation with the billionaire who wants to marry her, she lashes out at Alex (who has done nothing wrong), and we’re not sure where this is going or why. A few scenes later, tragedy has struck. But did all these events happen one after another or years apart? We figure it out, but Gilroy should have made it easier to read.

Alex, after the debacle of his break-up with Wilde’s clingy diva in Chicago, returns to Los Angeles, where he grew up. He can get session work there, and does. He still seems mellow, but he’s bestirred by a pet obsession: listening to the original avant-pop compositions posted online by Viviana (Alexa Swinton), a 15-year-old girl who has become a local celebrity. It turns out that he’s got a connection to her; she’s Nadia’s daughter. But why is he so interested? He’s just got…a feeling.

Alex’s brother, a talented but scruffy podcast host, is played by Will Arnett with a lived-in self-doubt more interesting than anything about his character in “Is This Thing On?” It’s through their conversations that we start to piece together Alex’s troubled family life — but here, once again, Pascal suffers in such a placid way that we keep wanting more. The movie finally comes to a head in an expertly staged suspense sequence where Alex, pretending to be a caterer’s assistant, sneaks into Nadia’s stone mansion, finds what he was looking for, and then has to sneak out. Naturally, the music playing under all this is “movie music.”

What, in the end, is “Behemoth!,” apart from a movie with a dismally bad title? (You can’t remember it. You can’t pronounce it. And it’s hard to say what, exactly, it means or why it carries an exclamation point — though it is, of course, the title of one of the films that Alex is helping to record the score for.) “Behemoth!” is a midlife-crisis movie.
