Buoyed by great reviews and positive word of mouth, “Coyote vs. Acme” launched in late August and started strong with $15.9 million domestically. Ticket sales have since climbed to $59.8 million domestically and $45 million overseas, underscoring the value of PG-rated films with brand familiarity. Theater owners frequently complain that they don’t have enough new movies aimed at families. And while original animation has struggled in post-COVID years, remakes, spinoffs and sequels in known franchises, such as “Sonic the Hedgehog” and “PAW Patrol,” have been reliable as modest box office draws.

The success of “Coyote vs. Acme” is especially glaring given Warner Bros.’ abysmal 2026 box-office performance. The studio has siphoned off a string of money losers, including Tom Cruise’s dark comedy “Digger,” Maggie Gyllenhaal’s punk rock “The Bride!” and DC’s “Supergirl.”

“There was legacy value in that IP, and the box office grosses of ‘Coyote vs. Acme’ reflect it,” says analyst David A. Gross of FranchiseRe. “All-audience films are extremely valuable and among the biggest earners at the box office. And there would have been upside with stronger marketing.”

Moreover, the wall-to-wall negative press Zaslav generated for shelving a finished movie (that was supposedly well received in test screenings) wasn’t worth the headache, according to studio sources. The decision did little to endear the former television executive to the film community after his predecessor Jason Kilar’s ill-fated decision to put the studio’s 2021 slate simultaneously in theaters and on HBO Max had isolated many creatives in Hollywood. Although other employees within Warner Bros. pushed back on the decision to bury the film, Zaslav relegated the final call to accountants, sources add.

At the time, “Coyote vs. Acme” was the third casualty of Zaslav’s post-pandemic cost-cutting efforts. In 2022, he shocked Hollywood by shelving the $90 million DC-centric “Batgirl” and kid-friendly “Scoob! Holiday Haunt” for tax purposes. Those three films were greenlit by Kilar, the studio’s former chief who departed earlier that year. Zaslav, who succeeded Kilar, said at the time he was shifting the studio’s priorities back to theatrical and felt “Coyote vs. Acme” didn’t fit with the new creative direction of the company. Box office watchers wonder whether Zaslav understood the value of the Warner Bros. catalog. After all, “Coyote vs. Acme,” “Batgirl” and “Scoob” hail from well-known brands. And there’s a reason that studios invest so heavily in recognizable franchises – they’re designed to turn the kind of easy profits that help justify other original swings.

“We see so many remakes and sequels because they make money,” says Robbins. “The fact that ‘Coyote vs. Acme’ was based on IP plays into the curiosity behind Warner Bros. [getting rid of it].”

title: Peacock’s Free Trial Offer Returns – But You Won’t Find It On the Streaming Service
summary: Peacock subscribers were hit with another rate hike over the summer, with prices for the NBCUniversal streaming service rising for the fourth time in four years. The price hike came on the heels of Peacock dumping its free trial for new users, joining the ranks of rival streamers like Paramount+, Hulu and HBO Max, all […]
content:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

Peacock subscribers were hit with another rate hike over the summer, with prices for the NBCUniversal streaming service rising for the fourth time in four years. The price hike came on the heels of Peacock dumping its free trial for new users, joining the ranks of rival streamers like Paramount+, Hulu and HBO Max, all of whom also got rid of their free trial offers.

But there’s now a way to score a discount on Peacock, as well as take advantage of a free trial, though you’ll have to look elsewhere to claim the latter. Amazon is currently offering a 7-day free trial to Peacock through its Prime Channels hub.

The deal gets you access to Peacock Premium Plus for free for one week if you sign up through Amazon. Premium Plus is the ad-free streaming tier of Peacock, and now costs $19.99/month (up from $16.99/month earlier this year).

You won’t be able to find the free trial deal on the Peacock website. With the Prime Channels deal though, you can test drive the service for a week for free, with unlimited access to the entire on-demand library of TV shows and movies, as well as hundreds of hours of live sports streaming.

Though there isn’t a catch per se, the Peacock free trial offer is only open to Amazon Prime members (not a Prime member? Get a 30-day free trial here to claim the Peacock deal and get access to exclusive member discounts just in time for Prime Big Deal Days).

Sign in with your Prime member details and then head to the Prime Video Channels homepage to claim the Peacock free trial offer. Your subscription to Peacock renews at the regular $19.99/month rate after your free trial is up. Or you can cancel at anytime to avoid being charged.

What Are the Best Peacock Streaming Deals 2026?

In addition to the Premium Plus plan, Peacock’s latest rate increase brought the price of its Peacock Premium tier (which includes ads) to $12.99/month, up from $10.99/month previously. Its Peacock Select tier, meantime (which includes current and past seasons of select TV shows, but excludes movies, live sports and Peacock originals) jumped from $7.99 to $8.99/month.

Still, there’s a way to score a discount on a Peacock subscription. The streamer is offering an annual plan discount right now that gets you 12 months of access for the price of ten.

The total price is $129 and locks in access for an entire year. That saves you 17% versus paying for Peacock month to month. The limited-time offer is available to all new and eligible returning subscribers and there is no promo code needed.

Peacock has priced its annual subscription down to as low as $79.99 a year in the past, but with the streamer being home to the recent Olympics and Super Bowl this year, it was able to raise its prices to bring in audiences for the sporting events and it’s unlikely we’ll see a further discount from the current promotion live online.

How to Get Peacock for Free

In addition to the Prime Channels free trial offer mentioned above, you can get Peacock for free with a Walmart+ membership. Walmart+ costs $98/year and as part of your membership, members can choose between Peacock Premium or Paramount+ Essential at no added cost.

That’s in addition to perks like free shipping, free grocery delivery, special discounts, gas savings and more. Sign up for Walmart+ here (you can also test-drive the service for 30 day for just $1 here).

You can also stream Peacock online for free with Instacart+. The grocery delivery service offers an upgraded tier that gets members free grocery delivery, free restaurant delivery and an annual membership to Peacock for free. Instacart+ costs just $9.99/month or $99/year. Try it out with a 14-day free trial here.

Peacock is also home to hundreds of new movies such as “Obsession,” “F1” and “The Super Mario Galaxy Movie” plus fan-favorite shows like “Pluribus,” “New Girl,” “The Traitors” “The Office” and the Bravo universe franchises.

Peacock is also a top-choice streamer for sports fans, who can live stream live sports like the NFL, Premier League, Big Ten Football, and WWE.

title: James Van Der Beek Remembered In Tearful ‘Dawson’s Creek’ Reunion At Greg Berlanti’s Heroes Gala That Also Honored Katherine LaNasa
summary: In it its third edition, the Barbara Berlanti “Heroes Gala,” launched eight years ago by top TV producer Greg Berlanti in honor of his mom, who had died of cancer, hit close to home as the disease recently claimed one of the shows Berlanti has worked on, Dawson’s Creek. Series creator Kevin Williamson received the […]
content:
In it its third edition, the Barbara Berlanti “Heroes Gala,” launched eight years ago by top TV producer Greg Berlanti in honor of his mom, who had died of cancer, hit close to home as the disease recently claimed one of the shows Berlanti has worked on, Dawson’s Creek.

Series creator Kevin Williamson received the Barbara Berlanti Hero Award at the event held Saturday Night at the Barker Hanger in Santa Monica to raise money for F Cancer’s early detection, prevention, and psychosocial initiatives.

He was presented with the award by Dawson’s Creek star Joshua Jackson and TV writer-producer Julie Plec, who worked with frequent collaborator Williamson, Jackson and Berlanti on Dawson’s Creek, in recognition of his efforts around the one-time Dawson’s Creek table read to support Van Der Beek following his cholesterol cancer diagnosis and benefit F Cancer.

“In the days before we went on stage to do this reading to support James, his health took a turn, and Kevin opened up not only his heart for making sure that everybody was okay, but also his wallet to make sure that we were able to honor James and honor his family at this event in truly the most amazing way possible, to allow his children to be in a room filled with people there to celebrate their dad as they had seen him go through what he was going through with humility and grace and to see the love for him that existed outside of their family,” Jackson said as he and Plec, a 2022 Heroes Gala honoree, both choked up while talking about Van Der Beek.

Watch on Deadline

(L-R) Greg Berlanti, Joshua Jackson, Julie Plec and Kevin Williamson attend the Barbara Berlanti Heroes Gala Benefiting F Cancer at Barker Hangar on October 03, 2026 Chris Frawley/Getty Images

Williamson, who, like Berlanti, lost his mom to lung cancer, also fought back tears while remembering Van Der Beek’s journey on Dawson’t Creek, a series inspired by Williamson’s own coming-of-age.

“James Van Beek gave voice to my childhood, he was the soul of the show, and anyway, he was the ultimate upgrade,” Williamson said about the actor playing a character he had based on himself. “I had the great pleasure of knowing James over many years, I saw him go from a young kid to an extraordinary man — a husband, a father, and a friend.”

Williamson took a lighter note while recalling his and Van Der Beek’s dynamic early in the show’s run.

“James had a full character arc. He started out as a brat. He would get a script and he would call me, and he would be like, ‘Why do I have to say this word? Nobody knows what this word means.’ And I would say, ‘Well, don’t worry about it, the way you mumble, nobody is going to hear it anyway.’ That was our relationship — Dawson talking to Dawson.”

Van Der Beek’s death in February at the age of 48, “really knocked me over,” Williamson said. He called the September 2025 table read benefit “probably one of the most special nights of my life.”

“The only thing missing was James. He was meant to be there. We were holding down hope till the last second, the doctors just wouldn’t let him get on the plane, but he still showed up that night with his unshakable courage and his spirit,” Williamson said. “I think he’s here with us tonight. He’s going to be with us for always. He’s awesome, and so I can’t pretend I’m worthy of any award but I will accept it. I’ll accept it in memory of my mother. I will accept it in the memory of James Van Der Beek, and I will accept it for the entire Dawson’s Creek family.”

The Dawson’t Creek reunion also included Mary-Margaret Humes, who played Dawson’s (Van De Beek) mom on the show. She walked the red carpet with Jackson.

(L-R) Mary-Margaret Humes and Joshua Jackson attend the Barbara Berlanti Heroes Gala Benefiting F Cancer at Barker Hangar on October 03, 2026 Chris Frawley/Getty Images

The Emmy-winning The Pitt star Katherine LaNasa, who spoke about getting diagnosed with breast cancer in early 2023 while struggling to find work during the post-pandemic industry contraction, received the Inspirational Hero Award. It was presented to her by The Pitt creator/executive producer R. Scott Gemmill.

“Katherine is more than a survivor. She is a warrior,” Gemmill said. “I think her spirit — I’m pretty sure — was shaped from coming from a long line of tough, ballsy, smart, funny Southern women. I see that every day. Sometimes it’s a lot to deal with.”

Gemmill spoke of how LaNasa’s strength during her cancer battle has influenced her Emmy Award-winning portrayal of charge nurse David Dana Evans on The Pitt.

“That, along with her empathy and her grace, has shone new light on an entire profession, helping healthcare workers to be seen and heard from in a way that’s never happened to them,” Gemmill said.

(L-R) R. Scott Gemmill and Katherine LaNasa attend the Barbara Berlanti Heroes Gala Benefiting F Cancer at Barker Hangar on October 03, 2026 Chris Frawley/Getty Images

He referenced one of LaNasa’s most memorable storylines on the HBO Max medical drama.

She portrayed a sexual assault nurse examiner last year with such honesty and rawness for Tina Ivlev, who is also here, that it affected so many people’s lives,” Gemmill said. “But also affected policy to the point where Allegheny General Hospital is now getting $20,000 more to train additional sexual assault nurse examiners, and those men and women will go on to change people’s lives in such a positive way. That’s just because she was willing to use what she went through and tap into it and give it to others, and that is a hero. That is an inspiration. That is impact. That is change. That is overcoming adversity, using your gift to help others. And that is my friend and my muse, Katherine LaNasa.”

(L-R) Greg Berlanti, Octavia Spencer , Brunson Green and Robbie Rogers attend the Barbara Berlanti Heroes Gala Benefiting F Cancer at Barker Hangar on October 03, 2026 Photo by Chris Frawley/Getty Images

Actress-producer Octavia Spencer presented the Memorial Hero Award to trailblazing former NBA player Jason Collins, the first openly gay athlete to compete in one of America’s top professional sports leagues, who died of glioblastoma in May. The honor was accepted by Collins’ husband, Brunson Green.

Among those who attended the gala, co-chaired by Berlanti and Robbie Rogers, were LaNasa’s The Pitt co-stars Noah Wyle, Patrick Ball an Shawn Hatosy, and top executives at The Pitt studio Warner Bros. Television, where Berlanti is based under an overall deal, and platform HBO Max including Casey Bloys, Sarah Aubrey, Joey Chavez, Clancy Collins White, and Brett Paul. (Both companies sponsored the event.)

Other notable guests included Paramount TV Studios President Matt Thunell, former longtime head of Warner Bros. TV Peter Roth, Danielle Panabaker, LaNasa’s usband Grant Show, Jim Rash, who emceed the auction, Lisa Ann Walter, Matthew Lillard and Sarah Shah.

Most of them took to the dance floor when Seal closed out the night by performing some of his biggest hits.

title: Sheryl Lee Ralph Imagines ‘Abbott Elementary’ Running As Long As ‘Grey’s Anatomy’: “I Want To Take This Journey”
summary: Nobody knows where they might end up, but Sheryl Lee Ralph has some ambitious ideas about Abbott Elementary‘s run. As the ABC workplace sitcom enters its sixth season, premiering Wednesday, Oct. 7 at 8:30/7:30c, the Golden Globe nominee imagines it catching up to Grey’s Anatomy’s 23-season run. “I look at it like this: If Grey’s […]
content:
Nobody knows where they might end up, but Sheryl Lee Ralph has some ambitious ideas about Abbott Elementary‘s run.

As the ABC workplace sitcom enters its sixth season, premiering Wednesday, Oct. 7 at 8:30/7:30c, the Golden Globe nominee imagines it catching up to Grey’s Anatomy’s 23-season run.

“I look at it like this: If Grey’s Anatomy could be on for 20 years, why can’t we?” said Ralph to People.

After premiering back in 2005, Grey’s Anatomy returns to ABC with Season 23 on Oct. 15 at 10/9c, maintaining its position as the network’s longest-running scripted primetime show.

Watch on Deadline

With five seasons under her belt as the no-nonsense elementary teacher Mrs. Howard in Quinta Brunson’s sitcom, Ralph said, “I love Barbara Howard so much. I’m not going to tell you I’m tired of her because I’m not tired of her. I want to take this journey with her.”

“If this show lasts for five more seasons — that would be 11 seasons now — I would love to still be with her, and just as I continue to grow, I really hope Barbara Howard continues to grow, but it’s all in the hands of Quinta Brunson in the writers’ room,” she added.

Before Abbott Elementary received a Season 6 renewal in March, Brunson noted that she’s “looking forward to moving away” to other projects beyond the sitcom.

“We are so fortunate and blessed to be on a network TV show for five seasons, and for people to still be fans,” Brunson told Bustle last year. “That being said, I have cast members who would love to pursue other projects, and our show is very time-consuming. We shoot about seven months out of the year. That can stop people from being able to do a lot of other things.”

title: Tom Cruise’s ‘Digger’ To Lose Around $150M: Deconstructing The Disaster
summary: Tom Cruise will not be jumping on any couches this weekend. This as the Top Gun: Maverick and Mission: Impossible blockbuster star posts his lowest opening in 19 years, that being the reported $160M net priced Digger, which didn’t find an audience with an $8M domestic debut, a $20M global overall start and a C+ […]
content:
Tom Cruise will not be jumping on any couches this weekend.

This as the Top Gun: Maverick and Mission: Impossible blockbuster star posts his lowest opening in 19 years, that being the reported $160M net priced Digger, which didn’t find an audience with an $8M domestic debut, a $20M global overall start and a C+ CinemaScore.

Myriad sources tell us that the film stands to lose around $150M and that’s if it’s lucky to get to a global box office of $50M. Post pandemic pricey fall disasters such as last year’s Dwayne Johnson-starring The Smashing Machine and the 2022 Margot Robbie, Christian Bale and John David Washington absurdist period title Amsterdam, had similar single digit domestic openings, and finaled lower with respective global grosses of $21.1M and $31.2M, as]nd off of respective smaller budgets of $50M and $80M.

The timing of Digger‘s bombing is Shakespearan, coming at the most stinging moment when Skydance co-CEO (né Paramount CEO) David Ellison refused to honor Warner Bros Motion Picture Chiefs Michael De Luca and Pamela Abdy‘s contracts and bring them into the fold. This after Warner’s milestone 2025 global gross of $4.3B, the best since 2019, and 11 Oscar wins. The new ParaBros is inheriting several Burbank lot lucrative IP assets shepherded by De Luca and Abdy, such as Oceans Eleven, Gremlins, Gladys, Minecraft 2 and more going forward, 38 features overall, dated into 2029. In 2027, the Paramount-Warners Bros slate will overdeliver the state AG’s demands of 30 films annually with 36 titles.

Watch on Deadline

How did Warners pick up a shovel and break ground on a filibustery-dialogue driven satire about the MAGA era which follows an oil tycoon whose latest ice caps project literally misfires, causing a global environmental disaster? (Those who’ve seen Digger know there’s a meta twist).

Iñárritu first developed what would become Digger at Netflix (the project had a different title) where he made the 2 hour-39 minute stream of consciousness art movie Bardo. At the time, Leonardo DiCaprio was eyeing, however, after the streamer made the very similar $75M Adam McKay-directed environmental satire, Don’t Look Up, Iñárritu took the project to his Revenant producer Mary Parent at Legendary. There, Digger was developed with Tom Cruise in mind.

Emmanuel Lubezki, Pamela Abdy, Alejandro González Iñárritu, Tom Cruise, Mary Parent, Andy Sherman and Michael De Luca attend the ‘Digger’ premiere on Sept. 22, 2026 in London, England. Joe Maher/Getty Images

Cut to 2024. Warner Bros Discovery CEO David Zaslav is hot-for-teacher to land Cruise post-Top Gun Maverick, and dispatches De Luca and Abdy to make a non-exclusive originals and franchise deal with the global star. The first project under the pact? Digger. Pamela Abdy had worked with Iñárritu on his $17M priced Oscar-winning Birdman and $135M costing Leonardo DiCaprio western The Revenant while she was Production President at New Regency from 2013 to 2016. De Luca worked with Cruise when he was President and COO of New Line on the much thriftier priced Magnolia, also from Paul Thomas Anderson, which landed the star his third Oscar nomination (in Supporting Actor) at the time.

Cruise and Jason Robards Jr. in ‘Magnolia’

De Luca and Abdy, we hear, ran Digger through their analytical comps system. The combo of Cruise and Iñárritu justified a $125M production greenligiht. Legendary’s development costs were bought out by Warners, hence the reason why the production company isn’t co-financing ala other Warner projects like Dune and the Godzilla Kong movies. The cost with an extended schedule rose to around a net $160M shoot at Leavesden in the UK with tax credits. Many sources have argued that the cost was substantially higher before the pic’s near $100M global theatrical marketing spend.

At the LA Westwood premiere, Cruise exclaimed to De Luca and Abdy, “You didn’t even take a breath when we brought you this film. I don’t even think you turned the page on it. You’re just like — you’re in.”

Which raises the question, exactly which studio executive says “no” to Cruise?

With De Luca and Abdy painted by some as spendthrift in their loss of motion picture boss jobs at the new Skydance, let that executive who has said “no” to Cruise on his productions, cast the first stone.

Skydance was heavily involved in the co-financing of lengthy Cruise shoots Top Gun: Maverick (net $177M) and the last two Mission: Impossible movies, Dead Reckoning and Final Reckoning, which carried an exorbitant combined cost between $591M and $691M, again, those budgets driven up partly due to Covid stops, but also Cruise’s well known fastidiousness and drive for perfection.

“The problem is that there’s no one in Cruise’s camp to tell him ‘no’, and what might not work,” says one high level source who was involved with the Mission movies, “It used to be his producing partner Paula Wagner.”

“Everyone knows he likes to direct on the set,” adds another, “I don’t know how that worked out with Alejandro because he doesn’t take direction from anyone.”

De Luca and Abdy did tell Cruise “no,” and that’s when they passed on the actor’s project, Deeper, with Edge of Tomorrow director Doug Liman, a supernatural underwater thriller that carried a $270M budget ask and no script at the time. The project remains in deep development at Universal. De Luca and Abdy also passed on making Michael Mann’s Heat 2, the sequel to a lucrative title in the Warner library as the budget for that movie climbed to $160M, which was cheap enough for $2.7 trillion conglomerate Amazon to make.

The first weekend of October, a hot frame where Warners launched the first Joker to a final gross of $1.07B WW and A Star Is Born to $440M WW, was chosen. Marketing began to tease the movie as the role that we’ve never seen Cruise in: an old, crusty, balding Texan waving a shovel heroically in an apartment. Toe-dip screenings with illuminati critics showed great promise. We hear there were two test screenings. The first with a half hour longer edit didn’t go so well, however, a second test with a half hour shorter edit (approaching the pic’s current 2 hour, 9 minute running time) went much better. Insurance covered a reshoot involving Cruise’s makeup following the first test screening. Cruise began pre-production on the movie while doing press for Final Reckoning last year.

While Cruise worked it in regards to opening the movie including a stop at April’s CinemaCon, UK world premiere with the Royals, Q&As and even an appearance on Jennifer Hudson, his availability to the press wasn’t 100%. Read, trades were barred from red carpet appearances despite Cruise’s constant availably to them on the last two Mission: Impossibles and several red carpets for Top Gun: Maverick.

In July, LA-based press were invited to the Warners Burbank lot for the first trailer drop. Mobile phones were pulled, and questions not asked by the media as they watched Cruise onstage with a Gen Z podcaster who gushed over the star’s achievements and the promises of Digger. Later on, Cruise met and took a professional photo with each reporter in the room in addition to a massive group photo outside the Steve J. Ross theater on the Burbank lot.

Walking away, anecdotally, those in the room had their suspicions about Cruise in a Doctor Strangelove-like movie.

“When I see Tom Cruise, I want to see him as the Tom Cruise I know, not with all this makeup,” exclaimed one O.G. entertainment journalist.

Digger initially came on NRG tracking three weeks ago with an opening range of $17M-$23M. Those close to the movie say they were shocked by the polarizing reviews which stand at 51% Rotten. Bad word set in, not just here, but around the world, a 180 to the vibrant critical reaction and audience reception on One Battle After Another (94% certified fresh, and A CinemaScore).

Positive online buzz fell on Digger in RelishMix metrics from an 8.1 out of 10 on Sept. 15, to a 6.4 before opening. Said the social analytics corp in their weekly report: “Chatter has been mixed-negative for Digger. There’s skepticism with viewers who love the idea of Cruise, but side-eye the execution: ‘Impressive that after a nearly three-minute long trailer, I still don’t really know what this movie’s about.’ The sharpest criticism isn’t about hating the movie, it’s about distrust, suspicion that the ‘aging gracefully’ narrative is a PR construct. Comments needle at the film’s tonal identity, wondering if it’s satire or self-parody, ‘For me this looked funny at first viewing. Second time it just looks cynical and a bad Kubrick’s Dr. Strangelove rip-off. Hope my first take is right.’ Plus, ‘Why does this look like Tropic Thunder cosplay’ along with, ‘I understand even less about this movie after the full trailer than I did after the teaser.’ And, there are grumbles about the promo montage in the ‘Tom Cruise Retrospective’ trailer feeling like a premature Oscars reel.”

Iñárritu said he made the movie as a love letter to the younger generation, despite it starring a bunch of right wing-like crusty old dudes. Ironically, the 18-34 demo showed up at 60% majority, though clearly not enough of them.

Those close to Cruise have argued that even with Digger bombing, every time he has a new theatrical release it raises the whole value and churn of his library again; his box office worth standing at $14B+ across 53 titles. A similar excuse was given by Paramount insiders when Mission: Impossible-Final Reckoning didn’t hit an enormous box office number: The movie won’t profit in its first go-round, rather its nth cycle.

Breaking down the $148M estimated loss, this is realized per sources based on $127M in total revenues, meaning theatrical rentals, airline monies, domestic home streaming, PVOD, international TV and global costs of $275M, and that’s not just worldwide P&A near $100M, but also global home and TV costs. This is also figuring that Warners unleashes Digger on POVD soon and does a decent number relative to the box office cause people are curious.

Yes, at the end of the day, Digger is Birdman all over again, and should have been positioned as an awards arthouse play. Such originality comes at substantially less than $50M production costs. But again, Digger stars Cruise at full freight.

What would De Luca and Abdy’s fates had been at the new Skydance had the merger closed after Dune: Part Three?

Those in Ellison’s ears have whispered about the duo’s audacious bets, when the box office reality is that these titles (six-time Oscar winner and Paul Thomas Anderson’s highest-grossing movie One Battle After Another, and 4x Oscar winner and $372M grossing Sinners, and the bomb The Bride) were a small part of a very commercial run for the two that included the near billion dollar-grossing A Minecraft Movie, the highest grossing Final Destination, Conjuring and Beetlejuce movies of all-time, the launch of another auteur in Zach Cregger’s Weapons, half of Twisters, upcoming holiday family title The Cat in the Hat and the hopeful billion dollar grossing title Dune: Part Three and much more to come.

Exclaimed one rival distribution exec who has never worked with De Luca and Abdy, “When Mike and Pam hit it out of the park, they hit it out the park.”

Warner Bros didn’t return request for comment.

title: James Gunn Is Writing His Next Movie Following ‘Man of Tomorrow’: “Already In It”
summary: Amid Paramount’s industry-shaking acquisition of Warner Bros., James Gunn is remaining focused on his work. When asked if he’s ready to start writing his next film to follow Man of Tomorrow, the DC Studios co-CEO revealed he’s “already in it” while awaiting the edit for his upcoming sequel to 2025’s Superman. “I had to do […]
content:
Amid Paramount’s industry-shaking acquisition of Warner Bros., James Gunn is remaining focused on his work.

When asked if he’s ready to start writing his next film to follow Man of Tomorrow, the DC Studios co-CEO revealed he’s “already in it” while awaiting the edit for his upcoming sequel to 2025’s Superman.

“I had to do something while I was waiting for the assembly!!” wrote Gunn to a fan on Threads.

After wrapping production on Man of Tomorrow in August, the fourth film in Gunn’s new DCU franchise is set to premiere July 9, 2027 in theaters.

Meanwhile, Gunn and co-CEO Peter Safran are safe amid the Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery merger after David Ellison invited the DC Studios bosses to continue working at the company, which has been renamed to Skydance. All film units, Paramount and Warner Bros, are to report into Paramount Pictures co-chairs Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein.

Watch on Deadline

Since Gunn and Safran stepped into their position following the WBD merger in 2022, DC Studios has released Superman and Supergirl, with Clayface premiering Oct. 23 and The Batman: Part II currently in production, scheduled for a Feb. 18, 2028 premiere.

title: ‘Lanterns’ Finale: Hal Jordan’s Killer and Manhunter Revealed, Sinestro Creates [SPOILER], John Stewart Powers Up for ‘Superman’ Sequel
summary: SPOILER ALERT: This article contains spoilers for the “Lanterns” finale, now streaming on HBO Max. Have no fear, the “Lanterns” finale is here. The season finale — or possibly the series finale, since HBO hasn’t renewed the show yet — wrapped up the mystery posed by the show’s premiere of who killed Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler). The […]
content:
SPOILER ALERT: This article contains spoilers for the “Lanterns” finale, now streaming on HBO Max.

Have no fear, the “Lanterns” finale is here.

The season finale — or possibly the series finale, since HBO hasn’t renewed the show yet — wrapped up the mystery posed by the show’s premiere of who killed Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler). The episode, titled “Dirt and Stars,” also revealed the identity of the second Manhunter, and set up how John Stewart (Aaron Pierre) becomes Earth’s sole Green Lantern in DC Studios’ forthcoming “Superman” sequel, “Man of Tomorrow.”

Courtesy of John Johnson/HBO Max

The episode starts back in 2016 Rushville in the aftermath of the town’s destruction from the first Manhunter attack. Sheriff Kerry (Kelly Macdonald) finds Hal in the wreckage, and then it’s revealed that she picks him up from prison in 2026 after he’s released, waiting with beer and flowers. With their feelings for each other blossoming, the two go out for dinner, which is full of Rushville patrons with lingering hatred for Hal. Kerry defends him in front of everyone, the two later sleep together and Kerry invites Hal to her son Noah’s (Shea Pritchard) football game. However, Hal’s house is firebombed in the middle of the night, and he doesn’t manage to escape. Hal wakes up on the floor of a strange lab with Noah standing over him, explaining that he replaced Hal’s burnt skin using the same Manhunter technology that had healed John in 2016. After much speculation online, Noah is the secret second Manhunter!

Popular on Variety

In present day, back on the planet decimated by the Manhunters, John interrogates Sinestro (Ulrich Thomsen) and learns that Noah freed the villain from prison. Sinestro reveals that he harnessed the fear-inducing gas from the planet to create a new, yellow ring for Noah. As comics fans know, Sinestro is the creator of the Yellow Lanterns, an evil group opposed to the Green Lanterns who derive their power from fear. Sinestro offers John the chance to charge his depleted ring from the sinister, yellow lantern, but Hal’s hologram stops him, and they leave Sinestro marooned on the planet.

Courtesy of John Johnson/HBO Max

Noah ambushes John when he returns to Earth, the two drive back to Rushville together. Noah reveals that he didn’t burn down Hal’s house, but says he was the one who killed him. He claims he couldn’t let Hal reveal his identity as a Manhunter and the yellow lantern to Kerry. Noah says he’s trying to overcome his violent Manhunter programming, and asks that John kills him to protect everyone from what he might do. John doesn’t answer, but lets Noah go and play one last football game for Rushville.

Courtesy of John Johnson/HBO Max

John joins Kerry at Noah’s game and asks her about her son being a Manhunter, convinced that she knew all along. Then, in a flashback, we see the moments right before Hal’s murder and the truth is finally revealed. After Zoe Macon (Poorna Jagannathan) saved Kerry and replaced her severed finger years ago with Manhunter technology, Kerry somehow got pregnant with Noah, who turned out to be a Manhunter like Zoe. Knowing Noah’s identity and fearing what he was planning, Hal confronted Kerry, and said they could run away and protect themselves. Kerry refused to leave, and in her fear, shot and killed Hal as he tried to reason with her by saying, “Goddamnit, I love you.” In the present, John assures Kerry that he won’t kill Noah, and instead lets her continuing raising him (as he goes on to play football at the University of Nebraska).

Courtesy of John Johnson/HBO Max

In the episode’s final moments, John calls Guy Gardner (Nathan Fillion) to Rushville and shows off his “unsanctioned” ring and lantern he took from Hal. John names himself the Green Lantern of Earth, in a sort of “independent contractor” role, and tells Guy to look after the stars while he protects the planet. Hal’s hologram appears and gives some last words of wisdom to John, saying he’s ready to take on the Green Lantern mantle. John tells the hologram that his final words to Kerry before his death were “I love you,” and the Hal replica repeats them earnestly back to John.

With his ring powered up, John flies over and drops off a bag of money as restitution to the waitress Maggie (Hannah Christine Shetler) who lost her family in the Manhunter attack. He also has a touching reunion with his family back home, including his estranged mother Bernadette (Jasmine Cephas Jones). Finally, in a twist on the classic Green Lantern oath from the comics, John personalizes the phrase with an emphasis on his newfound accepting of his fear.

“In brightest day / in darkest night / I embrace my fear / I’ll do what’s right / I choose this ring / I choose this fight / in service to / this lantern’s light.

Courtesy of John Johnson/HBO Max

While there’s no word yet on “Lanterns” Season 2, despite the show’s strong ratings for HBO, we know that Pierre will reappear as John in next summer’s “Man of Tomorrow,” James Gunn’s “Superman” sequel. It may be an awkward reunion with Fillion’s Guy Gardner, but now we know how the two Green Lanterns from Earth have decided to split up their duties. How will things go when the two heroes come face to face? How will they team up with Superman, Supergirl and the fledgling Justice League when the alien Brainiac attacks? And could Chandler have a cameo as the hologram Hal within John’s ring? We’ll have to wait and find out when “Man of Tomorrow” continues the DC Universe’s story on July 9.

title: Korean Directors Rally Behind ‘The Assassin(s)’ as Political Firestorm Turns on Its Makers
summary: The Directors Guild of Korea (DGK) has come out in support of the team behind “The Assassin(s),” Hur Jin-ho’s thriller about the 1974 shooting of first lady Yuk Young-soo, as political anger over the Korean box office leader spills onto its cast and crew. Conservative politicians and online critics have accused the film of distorting […]
content:
The Directors Guild of Korea (DGK) has come out in support of the team behind “The Assassin(s),” Hur Jin-ho‘s thriller about the 1974 shooting of first lady Yuk Young-soo, as political anger over the Korean box office leader spills onto its cast and crew.

Conservative politicians and online critics have accused the film of distorting history, and it now faces a police complaint and a fight in the National Assembly.

“What we are facing now is not criticism or condemnation of a film, but attacks on individuals that have crossed the line,” the DGK said in a statement.

Popular on Variety

The guild said the hostility had moved past questioning the film’s content and its makers’ choices, and “is targeting the daily lives and livelihoods of those who took part, and has gone as far as demanding that such a film never be made again.”

The statement, which named neither Hur nor anyone else, accepted that every film attracts harsh reviews along with praise, and asked who could draw an exact line between fair and excessive criticism.

“Creators can be criticized for their work, but that criticism must not lead to the collapse of the creator’s personal life and livelihood,” the guild said.

The DGK added that its idea of a healthy creative environment includes standing beside filmmakers who want to begin again, because “the chance for that person to start their next story should not disappear simply because a film went through controversy and criticism.”

“The Assassin(s)” opened Sept. 23. Yoo Hae-jin stars as a police inspector who witnesses the Aug. 15, 1974 shooting at the National Theater, where Yuk, the wife of then-President Park Chung-hee, was killed during Liberation Day celebrations, and goes on to lead the investigation. Park Hae-il plays the head of a newspaper’s social affairs desk, and Lee Min-ho a rookie reporter. The official inquiry pinned the killing on Mun Se-gwang alone, saying he acted under instructions from Pyongyang and Chongryon, the pro-North Korean residents’ association in Japan. Hur’s film declines to name a culprit, and its detractors argue the open ending points the finger at Park Chung-hee or his government.

Controversy has not dented the box office. “The Assassin(s)” passed 1 million admissions in four days and led the Korean chart again over the Oct. 2–4 weekend, selling 412,012 tickets from 1,129 screens for a weekend gross of KRW4.07 billion ($3 million). Its running total stands at 2.23 million admissions and KRW21.9 billion ($16.3 million).

The backlash has spread well beyond the film. Rating sites filled up with one-star scores, and the social media accounts of cast members drew abusive comments. Kim Go-eun and Lee Young-ae, who had shared handwritten recommendations, and critic Lee Dong-jin, who had reviewed the film on video, were also targeted. One YouTube film reviewer with 4.17 million subscribers pulled a video about the title.

Lee Jong-bae, a former People Power Party (PPP) Seoul city councilor, has asked Seoul police to investigate Hur, Hive Media Corp. CEO Kim Won-kuk and writers Kwon Ki-jun and Lee Ji-min for defamation. His complaint argues that the plural title invites audiences to suspect a second culprit besides Mun. PPP lawmakers also tried to summon Hur to testify at the annual parliamentary audit, a move blocked by the Democratic Party on creative freedom grounds.

Park Chan-wook, appearing at a Sept. 26 audience Q&A, praised the film as smartly conceived.

In a Sept. 28 statement, the producers had said: “Nowhere in the film is any specific individual defined as being behind the incident, and the film’s hypotheses and dramatic settings are not presented as historical fact.”

The film will open the 37th Singapore International Film Festival on Oct. 21, with Hur due to attend alongside cast members Shim Eun-kyung and Park Sung-hoon. The festival runs through Nov. 1.

“Cinema must carry on as a place where different ideas and voices meet, even when it stirs up debate,” the DGK said. “If that freedom disappears, it becomes hard for new films and new stories to be born.”

title: Korea Box Office: ‘The Assassin(s)’ Holds Admissions Lead as ‘Chiikawa’ Generates Top Weekend Gross
summary: Director Hur Jin-ho’s political crime thriller “The Assassin(s)” held the top position at the South Korean box office in admissions over the weekend of Oct. 2–4, though Japanese animated feature “Chiikawa the Movie: The Secret of the Mermaid Island” captured the frame’s largest gross revenue. According to data from KOBIS, the tracking service operated by […]
content:
Director Hur Jin-ho’s political crime thriller “The Assassin(s)” held the top position at the South Korean box office in admissions over the weekend of Oct. 2–4, though Japanese animated feature “Chiikawa the Movie: The Secret of the Mermaid Island” captured the frame’s largest gross revenue.

According to data from KOBIS, the tracking service operated by the Korean Film Council, “The Assassin(s),” currently in the eye of a political storm, led all titles with 412,012 admissions across 1,129 screens, taking $3 million and representing 23.89% of the market. By contrast, “Chiikawa” generated a weekend-high $3.2 million from 405,978 admissions across 1,055 screens to take 25.31% of theatrical receipts, finishing second on the admissions chart.

“The Assassin(s)” dramatizes the August 15, 1974 assassination attempt on President Park Chung-hee and the resulting death of First Lady Yuk Young-soo. Starring Yu Hae-jin, Park Hae-il, and Lee Min-ho as investigators unpicking irregularities in the official inquiry, the production has amassed $16.3 million from 2,233,963 admissions since its launch on Sep. 23.

Popular on Variety

“Chiikawa the Movie: The Secret of the Mermaid Island” launched wide on Sep. 30 following limited festival previews. Directed by Kei Oikawa and adapted from the manga by Nagano, the animated fantasy adventure follows the titular character and friends traveling to an island haven before confronting a mysterious aquatic legend. Counting nationwide previews, the anime has grossed $4.7 million from 604,764 total admissions.

Gambling crime drama “Tazza: The Song of Beelzebub” placed third in its sophomore frame, taking in $2.2 million from 299,915 admissions across 1,093 screens for an 18% market share. Directed by Choi Kook-hee and starring Byun Yo-han, Noh Jae-won, and Ayaka Miyoshi, the fourth installment in the comic-adapted franchise has grossed $10.2 million from 1,365,648 viewers since its Sep. 23 rollout.

“The Odyssey” took fourth place in its ninth frame, drawing $1.2 million from 123,059 admissions across 678 screens. Its local gross reached $101.2 million from 11,998,236 ticket buyers, leaving the film just under 2,000 admissions shy of the 12-million-ticket threshold.

Action fantasy “Reawakened Man” opened in fifth place, earning $885,217 from 115,894 admissions across 830 screens. Directed by Baek Seung-ryong and adapted from the popular webtoon, the feature stars Koo Kyo-hwan as a job-seeker who discovers he resurrects three days after dying, using his ability to battle criminal syndicates. Since its mid-week premiere on Sep. 30, the film has taken $1.4 million from 189,802 viewers.

Auteur Lee Chang-dong’s Venice award winner “Possible Love” took sixth place, grossing $482,385 from 60,534 admissions across 202 screens. Starring Jeon Do-yeon, Sul Kyung-gu, Cho Yeo-jeong, and Zo In-sung, South Korea’s official international feature film submission has earned $1.7 million from 230,483 admissions since Sep. 23.

“Obsession” moved to seventh place with $283,437 from 33,886 admissions across 314 screens for a cumulative haul of $7.3 million from 916,738 viewers.

Warner Bros. Korea comedy remake “The Intern” placed eighth, generating $265,015 from 33,491 admissions across 502 screens. Directed by Kim Do-young and starring Choi Min-sik and Han So-hee, the comedy has accumulated $6.1 million from 834,866 admissions since Sep. 16.

“Digger” opened in ninth place with $222,627 from 27,580 admissions across 517 screens, lifting its cume to $234,385 from 28,551 viewers following its Oct. 3 bow.

Rounding out the top 10, “Avengers: Endgame Encore” took 10th place with $242,747 from 25,777 admissions across 116 screens, bringing its cumulative run to $1.3 million from 148,743 admissions.

The overall market collective gross for the weekend was $12.6 million, down from last week’s holiday high of $19.6 million.

title: J. Todd Anderson, ‘The Nice Guys’ Storyboard Artist and Longtime Coen Brothers Collaborator, Dies at 67
summary: J. Todd Anderson, the storyboard artist behind films like “The Nice Guys” and “Raising Arizona” and a longtime Coen Brothers collaborator, has died following a battle with cancer. He was 67. His death was confirmed in a Facebook post on Oct. 3 by his “Filmically Perfect” podcast co-host, George Willeman. “My erstwhile pod-partner, J. Todd […]
content:
J. Todd Anderson, the storyboard artist behind films like “The Nice Guys” and “Raising Arizona” and a longtime Coen Brothers collaborator, has died following a battle with cancer. He was 67.

His death was confirmed in a Facebook post on Oct. 3 by his “Filmically Perfect” podcast co-host, George Willeman. “My erstwhile pod-partner, J. Todd Anderson, passed away October 2nd in California,” Willeman wrote. “We had gotten together just a few months back, making plans to bring the show back as we still have/had lots of movies to talk about. While that cannot happen now, we hope to keep the website alive so that our old episodes can still be enjoyed.”

His sister, Kimberly Patterson, confirmed his death to the non-profit FilmDayton, which also shared a post to social media.

Popular on Variety

Anderson first began his work as a storyboard artist in the late 1980s with the Joel and Ethan Coen-written comedy “Raising Arizona.” From there on out, Anderson remained a frequent collaborator with the Coen Brothers, going on to storyboard each of their films. This included “Miller’s Crossing,” “Fargo,” “The Big Lebowski,” “The Ladykillers,” “True Grit,” “Hail, Caesar!” and “The Ballad of Buster Scruggs,” in addition to their solo projects like “Drive-Away Dolls” and “Honey Don’t” from Ethan and “The Tragedy of Macbeth” from Joel.

Beyond the Coen Brothers, he is credited with having worked on 1989’s “Twister,” 1991’s “The Addams Family,” 2009’s “Whip It,” 2018’s “The Predator,” and 2016’s “The Nice Guys.” Over his career, he was nominated for three Art Directors Guild awards for “The Tragedy of Macbeth,” “The Ballad of Buster Scruggs,” and “Hail, Caesar!” He also directed 1999’s “The Naked Man” and 2008’s “My Mummy.”

Born John Todd Anderson in Springfield, Ohio, he later attended Wright State University. The Tom Hanks Center for Motion Pictures at the university shared a tribute to Anderson on Facebook.

“A diverse storyteller, he directed two features, published a book of his storyboards for ‘The Big Lebowski,’ co-hosted Filmically Perfect (listen below), and wrote the words and music for the pop musical ‘Nativity.’ He also generously shared his stories and knowledge with emerging filmmakers whenever they asked,” they wrote. “Rest well, JT. We’ll raise a glass to you tonight.”

title: Sarah Jessica Parker Says She’s ‘Never’ Worn Her Archived ‘Sex and the City’ Wardrobe: ‘There’s a Huge Separation Between Myself and Carrie Bradshaw’
summary: Despite Carrie Bradshaw’s reputation for wearing trend-setting outfits, Sarah Jessica Parker never wears any of her “Sex and the City” character’s iconic wardrobe. But she does have it. “No, I don’t wear any of the wardrobe that I wore on the show ever. I have it. It’s an archive, but I never wear it. I […]
content:
Despite Carrie Bradshaw’s reputation for wearing trend-setting outfits, Sarah Jessica Parker never wears any of her “Sex and the City” character’s iconic wardrobe. But she does have it.

“No, I don’t wear any of the wardrobe that I wore on the show ever. I have it. It’s an archive, but I never wear it. I never have,” Parker told People in a recent interview.

For Parker, these one-of-a-kind outfits would feel too much like a costume, especially since they’ve already seen the screen. “There’s a huge separation between myself and Carrie Bradshaw. So it would be like walking around in Sarah Sanderson’s costume,” she continued, referencing her “Hocus Pocus” role. “It doesn’t seem applicable to my life.”

Popular on Variety

While Bradshaw has laid the character’s wardrobe to rest, she dressed as Bradshaw in the HBO series from 1998 to 2004. Parker revisited the role for two films and the spinoff series, “And Just Like That…,” from 2021 to 2025. Now, audiences have officially said goodbye to Bradshaw and all her iconic outfits. Parker bid her character an emotional farewell on social media when the spinoff ended.

“Carrie Bradshaw has dominated my professional heartbeat for 27 years. I think I have loved her most of all,” Parker wrote. “I know others have loved her just as I have. Been frustrated, condemned and rooted for her. The symphony of all those emotions has been the greatest soundtrack and most consequential companion. Therefore the most sentimental and profound gratitude and lifetime of debt. To you all.”

Parker added: “This chapter is complete” and called “And Just Like That” a “joy, adventure, the greatest kind of hard work alongside the most extraordinary talent of 380 that includes all the brilliant actors who joined us.”

title: ‘Lanterns’ Team Discusses How Theme Of Fear Played Part In Finale, Remixing The Oath And The Fate Of Earl
summary: SPOILER ALERT: This story contains details from Season 1 episode 8 of Lanterns on HBO. “Are You Afraid?” In Sunday nights season one finale of Lanterns, John Stewart (Aaron Pierre) finally foudn the answer and his destiny as he spoke the words audiences have been awaiting all season to hear. Not only did Stewart accept […]
content:
SPOILER ALERT: This story contains details from Season 1 episode 8 of Lanterns on HBO.

“Are You Afraid?”

In Sunday nights season one finale of Lanterns, John Stewart (Aaron Pierre) finally foudn the answer and his destiny as he spoke the words audiences have been awaiting all season to hear. Not only did Stewart accept his role as Earth’s protector by the end of the episode but also why Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler) was killed and for what reason.

The finale starts off with a flashback to Sheriff Kerry Kane (Kelly MacDonald) picking up Jordan from prison following a ten year sentence after admitting to fault for the deadly attack on Rushfield. This is also the start of their relationship with Jordan weary about how the town will accept his return.

Watch on Deadline

His instincts are correct as his house is firebombed with Jordan left for dead only to be saved by Kane’s son Noah (Shea Pritchard), who is not only able to regenerate Jordan’s burned skin but reveals his secret that he like his grandmother is a Man Hunter.

Flash forward to present day, where Stewart and Jordan’s hologram have captured Sinestro (Ulrich Thomsen) on a desolate planet and found out he has forged Noah a very powerful lantern that could be very deadly in the wrong hands.

Back on earth with the new Lantern in hand, Stewart is captured by Noah but ultimately released prior to Noah’s big football with the boy admitting he had killed the real Jordan after he had found out his plans for the new lantern. While watching the game, Stewart confronts Kerry about Jordan with her ultimately admitting she killed him after panicking when Jordan asks her to move away with Noah to protect from the Guardians.

Kerry asks to watch the end of the game before turning herself in and Stewart suggests that isn’t what Jordan would want before going on their separate ways. In the final moments, Stewart tells Guy Gardner he’s taking on the task of Guardian of earth and accepts role by speaking the oath that while rooted in the original has a new twist to it for this show before he sets flight.

Series creators and stars talked about the finale and the future of the show recently during a press conference.

When it came to Jordan’s Hologram, Chandler had an interesting outlook when it came to playing the real version of Jordan and the artificial one and felt that there was a paternal feeling to how he handled the material.

“I looked at the Hologram, as more of a younger Hal watching himself or the version of himself and the subconscious of how at the time he was put in that world,” Chandler said. “It’s almost like a father watching a son grow up in a way. He’s viewing himself, making these decisions and yet he gets to also converse with himself at the same time. So it is kind of rather complicated and I took the dialogue and did what I could with it to make it more complicated. So no one understood what I was doing and I thought maybe that might work out.”

The running theme of not just the episode but the season is the idea of fear and how characters handled and writer and co-creator Chris Mundy pointed how as a writing team they embraced that idea when writing this episode.

“If you’re gonna do this story, you’re gonna talk about fear and is it a good thing? Like Sinestro says it in the finale, fear is just emotional intelligence,” show co-creator Chris Mundy says. “Show me a species without fear, and I’ll show you something on the extinction list. We wanted this to be a really human story, we wanted to talk about these people with, that are very real, flawed or complicated who get to do these heroic things, and what would it actually mean? And so it was really important to us that to embrace that and treat that question really super seriously.”

The final moments between Stewart and Jordan clearly signaled this could be the last time the two may share a scene together going forward and Aaron Pierre talked about how after filming for so long the scene came together seamlessly when it came to how the characters felt about each other.

“We had filmed a lot by that point,” Pierre said. “Kyle and I on the day we’re thinking of all the months that we filmed prior to that, It’s all going into the moment. It’s all very loaded and it feels earned and it feels deserved. And hopefully the audience is open and receptive to that and allows it to resonate with different.”

Fans of the original comics are sure to notice a change in the famous Lantern slogan and Mundy said the idea of changing or “remixing it” had to do with the writers journey throughout the season and how it made sense to head in this direction by the end of it.

“I know Justin, one of the writers, was like, well, we’re not rewriting it, We’re remixing it.,” said Mundy. “I think the idea was, we sort of were taking a look back at what we’d done with the season and so John’s path was not the normal path. The ring didn’t choose him. He was interviewed. He was kind of raised for it. He was having to choose this thing. Then he decided not to do it, and then decided he needed to do it on his own terms. And so, it felt, we wanted to be true to the original, and respectful of the original, like his version is rooted in the OG version of it. We also wanted to tweak it to talk about the themes that we talked about, and fear, and make it, make it be a choice that he was choosing this thing, and not something he was like, Oh, I’m doing it because my parents wanted me to do it, or I’m doing it because of these things.”

As for everyone’s favorite pet plant Earl, not only is there signs we’ll see more of him next season, it seems when it comes toughness, he’s much more resilient then the man that feeds him.

“I think Earl is pretty Earl is pretty resilient,” co-creator and writer Damon Lindeloff said. “The botanical creatures of the galaxy can grow their own skin, I would imagine.”

title: Reggie McFadden Dies; ‘In Living Color’ Comedian Was 57
summary: Reggie McFadden, best known for his run on In Living Color, has died. He was 57. His sister, Bernice McFadden, confirmed his death to The Hollywood Reporter. She said the U.S. State Department notified the family that he died in Tanzania, where he had been living for several years. A cause of death is not […]
content:
Reggie McFadden, best known for his run on In Living Color, has died. He was 57.

His sister, Bernice McFadden, confirmed his death to The Hollywood Reporter. She said the U.S. State Department notified the family that he died in Tanzania, where he had been living for several years. A cause of death is not known.

“Rest in peace, fellow comedian, Reggie Mcfadden,” comic Tony Luewellyn wrote on Facebook. “Another fallen veteran comedy brother!”

The Brooklyn-born McFadden played various characters on In Living Color from 1993-1994. His other TV appearances included roles on Martin, Hangin’ with Mr. Cooper, Coach, Moesha, Getting Personal and Curb Your Enthusiasm. His film credits include Jacob’s Ladder and Little Nicky.

Watch on Deadline

McFadden had a comedy special on Comedy Central and was a regular performer in Las Vegas.

His Facebook page states he was the owner of a gold mining company and entertainment production company in Tanzania.

title: Philippines’ Regal Teams With Singapore’s Mocha Chai On ‘One For The Road’; Elijah Canlas, Gian Bernardino, Emilio Daez & JM Ibarra Head Cast
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Regal Entertainment producer Keith Monteverde is teaming with Singapore’s Mocha Chai Laboratories on coming-of-age drama One For The Road, directed by award-winning Filipino filmmaker Kip Oebanda (Bar Boys, Bar Boys: After School). The cast is headed by Elijah Canlas, Gian Bernardino, Emilio Daez and JM Ibarra playing four high school best friends who begin […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Regal Entertainment producer Keith Monteverde is teaming with Singapore’s Mocha Chai Laboratories on coming-of-age drama One For The Road, directed by award-winning Filipino filmmaker Kip Oebanda (Bar Boys, Bar Boys: After School).

The cast is headed by Elijah Canlas, Gian Bernardino, Emilio Daez and JM Ibarra playing four high school best friends who begin to grow apart as they enter adulthood. They are joined by Nour Hooshmand, Sofia Trazona and Mika Reins, among other cast.

The project has been selected for the Film Development Council of the Philippines (FDCP)’s International Co-Production Fund (ICOF), which supports international co-productions involving Filipino producers and filmmakers. The film is set to shoot entirely in the Philippines with a predominantly Filipino cast and crew.

Mocha Chai Laboratories will lead sound design for One For The Road. The company’s recent Singapore-Thailand co-production, Decalcomania, was nominated for Best Sound Design at the 2026 ContentAsia Awards.

Watch on Deadline

Written by Kip Oebanda and Victor Villanueva (Patay na si Hesus), One For The Road follows four high school best friends entering their mid 20s who are finding that careers, relationships and the pressures of adulthood are pulling them in different directions.

When tragedy brings them back together, they embark on a road trip that tests their friendship and forces them to confront the grief they have long avoided. The film blends road-trip comedy with coming-of-age drama.

Mocha Chai Laboratories co-founder Michelle Chang said: “I’m absolutely thrilled to be working with Regal Entertainment, a company I’ve long wanted to partner with because of its extraordinary legacy in Philippine cinema. One For The Road is a universally resonant film and what better way to start this journey than bring together Regal’s deep connection with Filipino audiences and MCL’s experience in international co-production and post-production.”

For Monteverde and Oebanda, the material has a personal connection: “I am too familiar with what it feels like to be young, trying to ‘grow up,’ while the world around you keeps narrowing your options and closing doors,” Monteverde said. “One For The Road puts a spotlight on struggles that many young Filipino men carry quietly today.”

Oebanda added: “There seems to be a pervasive sense of loneliness and isolation in modern cities and in capitalist societies, and it is by design. This feeling of burnout and isolation is rarely addressed in our films. In the Philippines, men in particular are taught to suck it up and be strong or to not cry when they are emotional.

“I want to make a film that will reach the masses with the message that we need to support and check on each other and normalize talking about grief and our mental health struggles. We can make a hilarious, fun movie without skirting away or downplaying the issue at hand. After all, many people mask their grief through humor and adventures.”

One For The Road is currently in principal photography in the Philippines and is slated for release in the second quarter of 2027.

title: Channing Dungey Poised For Expanded Post-Merger Role Overseeing Paramount & WBD Cable Networks – The Dish
summary: EXCLUSIVE: In addition to Casey Bloys and George Cheeks, the television/streaming structure of the combined Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery, recently named Skydance, would include expanded responsibilities for Channing Dungey who would be taking over the Paramount cable networks, I hear. As Deadline revealed on Friday, Paramount’s Chair of TV Media Cheeks, who currently oversees CBS Studios, […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: In addition to Casey Bloys and George Cheeks, the television/streaming structure of the combined Paramount–Warner Bros. Discovery, recently named Skydance, would include expanded responsibilities for Channing Dungey who would be taking over the Paramount cable networks, I hear.

As Deadline revealed on Friday, Paramount’s Chair of TV Media Cheeks, who currently oversees CBS Studios, is poised to add oversight of Warner Bros Television and Paramount Television Studios, with Dungey, Chairman and CEO, Warner Bros Television Group and US Networks, and PTVS President Matt Thunell both reporting to him alongside CBS Studios President David Stapf.

Continuing the streamlining trend of Skydance putting the combined Paramount and WBD TV studios under Cheeks, film studios under Josh Greenstein and Dana Goldberg and streamers (HBO Max and Paramount+) under Bloys, the company would be doing the same for the large array of cable networks it will own under Dungey, who also will continue to run the Warner Bros. TV Group, sources said.

Watch on Deadline

She would be adding oversight of the Paramount cable nets, which currently report to Cheeks, including the “core four,” MTV, Comedy Central, Nickelodeon and BET, as well as VH1, Paramount Network, TV Land, CMT, Pop TV, and Logo TV.

That would be in addition to her current cable portfolio as head of US Networks, which features WBD’s linear TV brands, including Discovery Channel, Food Network, HGTV, Investigation Discovery, TLC, Adult Swim, Animal Planet, Cartoon Network, HLN, OWN, TBS, TNT, Travel Channel, truTV, and Turner Classic Movies. Channing would be reporting to Cheeks on both the studio and cable network side.

Reps for Paramount and Warner Bros. TV declined comment.

With the move, Cheeks, whose domain is expanding to include two more TV studios and WBD’s cable portfolio as he takes charge of the combined company’s TV Studios and linear networks, including CBS and cable, is delegating day-to-day oversight of the cable brands, to Dungey, a highly respected veteran TV executive who had started executing her strategy for the WBD cable nets since adding the responsibility to her original job of running the Warner Bros. television studio almost two years ago.

The new studio structure reaffirms Paramount CEO David Ellison’s faith in former Skydance TV President Thunell who is put on the same level with two of the most decorated TV executives in the business who have decades of experience and oversee large portfolios in Channing and Stapf. Under the setup, Channing and Thunell, whose units both focus on development and production for streaming, are expected to work closely together.

Skydance is poised to unveil its official executive structure early next week, tied to Paramount’s acquisition of WBD closing Oct. 6.

Dungey added oversight of Warner Bros. Discovery’s basic cable networks at the end of 2024. She has led the unit through a period of uncertainty as WBD announced a plan to spin off its linear networks before Paramount emerged as a buyer for the entire portfolio. With her at the US Networks helm, Shark Week 2026 garnered its biggest ratings growth in over a decade, Puppy Bowl delivered its largest audience in eight years, Food Network achieved its first quarter of ratings growth in five years (in Q1 2026), and HGTV posted its strongest year-over-year gains this year in nearly two decades.

Among the programming synergies between the cable networks and WBTV under Dungey are a Bachelor Mansion crossover with HGTV and The Pitt season 1 getting a run on TNT.

title: Isaiah Washington Reveals His Wife’s 2025 Death In Social Media Post: “It Came As A Huge Shock to Me”
summary: Former Grey’s Anatomy star Isaiah Washington revealed via social media this weekend that Jenise Maria Garland, his wife of 29 years, died in June of 2025. Washington said his wife collapsed “suddenly” on May 31, 2025 and died on June 9. “It came as a huge shock to me and our entire family,” Washington wrote. […]
content:
Former Grey’s Anatomy star Isaiah Washington revealed via social media this weekend that Jenise Maria Garland, his wife of 29 years, died in June of 2025.

Washington said his wife collapsed “suddenly” on May 31, 2025 and died on June 9.

“It came as a huge shock to me and our entire family,” Washington wrote. “She succumbed to a massive hemorrhagic stroke and never recovered. Listen, y’all …some headaches are not just headaches or migraines, they can be much worse and a warning sign. Get a brain scan if you can and take those headaches seriously. She has been gone 16 months now, but she left 3 incredibly amazing children behind to continue her legacy. I don’t know if this is an appropriate post, because Jenisa Washington was extremely private, but I guess I just have to be reprimanded from her on the other side.”

Washington is best known for his role of Dr. Preston Burke on Grey’s Anatomy. He appeared in several episodes of P-Valley from 2020-2022.

title: John de Mol’s Formats Giant Talpa Studios Heads to Mipcom With New Shows ‘Sing With Me,’ ‘The Golden Elevators’ (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: John de Mol’s Talpa Studios, whose hit formats include quiz show “The Floor,” is heading to next week’s TV market Mipcom with a slate of new entertainment formats, led by “Sing With Me” and “The Golden Elevators.” “Sing With Me” is a feelgood music entertainment format developed in collaboration with Dutch producer IDTV, the creator […]
content:
John de Mol’s Talpa Studios, whose hit formats include quiz show “The Floor,” is heading to next week’s TV market Mipcom with a slate of new entertainment formats, led by “Sing With Me” and “The Golden Elevators.”

“Sing With Me” is a feelgood music entertainment format developed in collaboration with Dutch producer IDTV, the creator of “The Traitors.”

In the show, aspiring singers get the chance to share the stage with some of the country’s biggest artists. Every performance begins as a solo, but when one of the established artists hears something special, they can grab a microphone and join in, transforming the performance into a duet.

The format launches on SBS6 in the Netherlands on Nov. 7.

Popular on Variety

“The Golden Elevators,” a quiz show that combines general knowledge with social strategy, has been ordered by ITV in the U.K. and SBS6 in the Netherlands, where it is set to air early next year.

Ten contestants enter a skyscraper where they must choose between two elevators, each representing a possible answer to 10 questions. Choose correctly and you go up; choose the wrong one and you’re out.

Before the doors close, contestants may work together and share what they know – or deliberately send a rival into the wrong elevator – turning every question into a battle of knowledge, strategy and trust. Waiting at the top is a life-changing jackpot, to share with whoever makes it there.

Talpa Studios continues to expand its global footprint, with 26 formats active across 34 countries, and Sebastian van Barneveld, Talpa Studios’ director of global distribution, underscores the role that partnerships play in that growth, alongside the company’s investment in original IP.

Shows developed through partnerships now account for more than 40% of Talpa Studios’ catalog.

“In a rapidly changing market, strong ideas need more than creativity alone. Collaboration and flexibility are key to making them travel,” he said. “Our Mipcom slate reflects that approach: by combining original IP with creative partnerships and developing formats that can work across markets, platforms and audiences, we’re creating multiple routes for ideas to grow.”

The partnership model has delivered titles such as murder mystery format “A Party to Die For,” developed with ITV Studios, and “Let’s Play Ball,” originally co-developed by EndemolShine Nederland (part of Banijay Benelux), Talpa Studios and Signal.Stream. The format has since secured commissions in French Canada and Finland.

Signal.Stream, a strategic partner for Talpa Studios, focused on creating formats for the streaming generation, has developed several other titles that are gaining traction in the market. “Most Wanted” has new commissions in Slovakia, the Czech Republic and Romania, while “Catch Us” has added new commissions from TV4 in Sweden and ProSieben in Germany, alongside adaptations in the Netherlands and Hungary.

Talpa Studios’ established brands continue to build momentum around the world. “The Floor,” for example, has reached more than 30 territories. Meanwhile, “The Winner Takes It All” secured its first international sale to France Télévisions and a recommission in the Netherlands.

Daily reality competition “The Alliance,” nominated for the Netherlands’ most prestigious television audience award, launched on Prime Video in India with a celebrity adaptation, and the streaming giant has confirmed a second season.

“Caught in the Middle,” a high-energy studio game show in which a duo must outsmart 100 opponents closing in around them, is returning for a second season in the Netherlands and continues to travel internationally, with adaptations in Spain for Atresmedia and Australia for Seven Network.

De Mol is a reality TV legend, who previously led Endemol and Talpa Media, the creators of such iconic brands as “Big Brother,” “Deal or No Deal,” “Fear Factor” and “The Voice.” Talpa Studios, formed in September 2023, is led by CEO Maarten Meijs.

title: ITV Studios Travels to Mipcom With 10 New Titles on Its Formats Slate, Led by ‘The Chase Around the World’ (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: ITV Studios has unveiled 10 new titles on its Mipcom formats slate, led by “The Chase Around the World,” and also revealed the unscripted lineup, which includes “70 Up,” the final chapter of the groundbreaking documentary series “7 Up.” “The Chase Around the World,” a multi-country treasure hunt, is a spin-off of ITV’s game show […]
content:
ITV Studios has unveiled 10 new titles on its Mipcom formats slate, led by “The Chase Around the World,” and also revealed the unscripted lineup, which includes “70 Up,” the final chapter of the groundbreaking documentary series “7 Up.”

“The Chase Around the World,” a multi-country treasure hunt, is a spin-off of ITV’s game show “The Chase.” The series, comprising six hour-long episodes, is produced by Bright Entertainment for British broadcaster ITV.

The show sees six pairs of contestants attempt to track down some of the biggest brains in Britain – six individuals known as The Chasers – in undisclosed locations across Europe. Unravelling puzzles along the way, the winning pair will pit their knowledge against The Chasers in order to win a life-changing prize pot.

Popular on Variety

Also new to the slate is endurance experiment “Expedition Into the Wild.” The show had a very successful launch on Kanal 5 in Sweden, where it became the number 1 commercial title in its timeslot, outperforming the slot average by 60%, and has been commissioned for a second season. The show, which comprises 12 hour-long episodes, is produced by ITV Studios Sweden.

In the show, eight celebrity city dwellers with almost no survival skills are dropped into a remote natural environment for 18 days. Working in pairs, the contestants have only basic tools and limited food. They must build shelter, source supplies and tackle survival challenges.

“Celebrity Escape,” produced by Perpetual Entertainment for Three in New Zealand, sees seven comedians take on one of the most popular and fastest-growing activities in the world: the escape room.

Each hour-long episode of the show sees the comedians working as a team to navigate the puzzles, clues and scares of a new themed room, before voting out their competition.

All the while, another comedian, known as the Games Master, watches from the control room, chiming in to help or hinder as they see fit.

Over the six episodes, alliances shift, egos clash, and pressure builds as the group shrinks. In the finale, the last two contestants face a head-to-head escape where only one can win.

New food-entertainment series “Next on the Menu,” produced by South Shore for the U.K.’s Channel 4, sees four food superfans battle to create the next menu hit for a global brand, from Wagamama and KFC to Taco Bell and Krispy Kreme.

Each contestant must pitch, prototype and perfect their dream dish with their creations then stress-tested for taste, kitchen feasibility, and trialled with real customers, to win a place on the menu. The show is in four parts, with each episode an hour long.

Also new to the slate is “Apocalypse,” a new social experiment show from The Garden and ITV Studios Australia. It was the biggest unscripted original launch since 2024 for Binge, the Australian streaming service, and one of Channel 4’s biggest young-skewing entertainment launches of this year.

The series, which has eight hour-long episodes, sees 16 ordinary people enter an abandoned town that bears all the hallmarks of being ravaged by an apocalyptic event. With no running water, heating or electricity, they must survive for 28 days, scavenging for food and supplies and by reusing and repurposing anything they find.

“Secret Garden,” narrated by David Attenborough in the U.K., also joins the slate. The show, comprising five 60-minute episodes, is produced by Plimsoll Studios. It was the BBC’s biggest new factual series since 2025.

The series uncovers the wildlife stories hidden in the places we know best. Each episode follows one garden over an extended period, capturing animal behavior rarely witnessed by human eyes – from raising families and defending territories to hunting, courting and surviving the changing seasons.

Also on the slate is the reality format “How to Clean Up for Cash,” where loved ones secretly seek help for a family member or friend whose clutter has taken over their home.

While the unsuspecting homeowner is away for 48 hours, an expert team clears, sorts and values years of accumulated belongings, transforming the space that has become overwhelmed by clutter.

The six-parter, with each episode running for 30 minutes, is produced by MultiStory Media for ITV.

“Name That Tune,” which is based on the U.S. game show that debuted on NBC in 1953, is returning to the U.K. in 2027 after 29 years off air.

The show is a global staple of entertainment, with over 25 countries, including Australia, France, Germany and Italy, having produced localized versions across the last seven decades. Accompanied by the Name That Tune Live Band and led by a celebrity host, contestants race against the clock (and each other) to identify legendary tracks across various genres and eras.

The series, comprising nine 60-minute episodes, is produced by Bright Entertainment for ITV.

Also new to the slate is “The Ultimate Summer Star,” produced by Magga og Anders and ITV Studios Denmark for TV2 Echo. It is a sun-soaked spin-off of the smash-hit Norwegian format “The Ultimate Christmas Star,” which continues to deliver strong ratings with a 13% increase in total viewers from Season 2 to 3 in Norway, with a fourth season returning this December, a third season returning in Denmark, and a newly announced first season in Sweden.

Chaos unfolds as 24 celebrities head to a lakeside cabin to compete in a lineup of bonkers challenges. From laugh-out-loud antics to outdoor adventures, the tasks are silly, light-hearted and packed with warm-weather fun, as they compete to be crowned The Ultimate Summer Star.

The show has 24 30-minute episodes.

And finally, there is “The Joy of Pets,” which is produced by Bandicoot for ITV. The show, which has five 60-minute episodes, is a warm-hearted factual entertainment format celebrating the bond between people and their animals.

This format travels across the country uncovering uplifting, emotional and often surprising stories of pets, their owners and the veterinary professionals dedicated to their care.

Each episode combines behind-the-scenes access to a local veterinary practice, a community roadshow featuring expert advice and audience interaction, and inspiring local stories that showcase the life-changing impact animals have on the people around them.

“70 Up” Courtesy of ITV/Nick Wall

ITV Studios has also unveiled its full unscripted slate for Mipcom, led by “70 Up,” the final chapter of the groundbreaking series “7 Up,” the longest-running documentary series ever made.

“70 Up,” which comprises two 90-minute episodes, is produced by MultiStory Media for ITV.

The “7 Up” series, which follows the lives of 14 ordinary people, has been broadcast in 157 countries, including the U.S., Canada, Japan, China, Australia and France.

“70 Up” marks the culmination of this journey across seven decades. Building on the forensic questioning of the late director Michael Apted, Academy Award-winning filmmaker Asif Kapadia steps in to close the circle on a series that captures a lifetime from childhood through careers, marriage, parenting and beyond.

From Plimsoll Studios for ITV, comes the landmark natural history series “World’s Wildest Cities.” Across six hour-long episodes, the show follows a variety of urban animals to uncover the challenges of living alongside the human race. Each episode has a new cast of animals and focuses on one city: Rio de Janeiro, New York, Melbourne, Singapore and London, with the final episode revealing how the series was made, and the science behind the stories.

Another title looking at the changing world around us, “Ages of Ice,” which has three hour-long episodes, is produced by Northern Pictures for PBS and ABC Australia, and is narrated by actor David Tennant.
