It follows the brave scientists pushing the boundaries of exploration and human endeavor in Earth’s coldest corners to understand the changes of ice and what this means for our planet’s future. In the unforgiving grip of our planet’s polar regions, the series will follow these modern-day explorers as they try to understand how the fate of every place and every creature on our planet is tied to these frozen extremes.

New to the slate from Wonderhood Studios is a documentary series “Jesus Christ: The Man, The Mystery,” which has four hour-long episodes. Produced for the BBC, it draws on the latest historical research, archaeological discoveries, technological innovation and expert testimony to expand and sharpen our understanding of Jesus.

The story draws on the testimony recorded in the Gospel accounts, and elsewhere, to understand the world he inhabited and the foundations of the movement he inspired.

And finally, from Curious Films, there is “Spy Next Door: The Anna Chapman Story,” which is produced for Channel 4. It has all the ingredients of an espionage thriller, but is a true story, with access to people caught up in the Russian spy network as well as FBI operatives and former Russian insiders.

In 2010, 11 deep-cover Russian spies were arrested across the United States, sending shockwaves around the globe. At the center of it all was Anna Chapman (née Kushchenko) — the femme fatale turned media sensation. But before she became the face of the spy ring, she was recruited, trained and indoctrinated in the U.K. The series reveals how the actions of a few would trigger seismic, long-lasting and deadly consequences.

It comprises two hour-long episodes.

Variety spoke to Julie Meldal-Johnsen, executive VP global content and content strategy at ITV Studios, about the slate.

Referring to “70 Up,” she said, “I can’t think of another documentary project that is more ambitious, more far-reaching. There were so few filmmakers that could have done it justice [following the death of Michael Apted], but it’s incredible to be able to wrap up that endeavor, that vision, and bring back some people who haven’t been in it for a long time. Obviously, sadly, there have been a couple of deaths on the way. It is a feat of filmmaking that will be unparalleled. So that brings tears to my eyes every time, and we’re really, really, really proud of that.”

Turning her attention to “Jesus Christ: The Man, The Mystery,” she said, “It is very rare for us to have something in that space, but we were very keen. It’s a history documentary with archaeological discoveries thanks to new techniques, and some great expert testimony. We think this really will be a seminal documentary. And whether you’re Christian or not, I think it will be fascinating.”

She added, “ ‘World’s Wildest Cities’ features a different city every episode, and there are some really exotic animals, and this amazing drama that takes place in urban places. It’s quite a different approach to blue chip natural history.”

“Ages of Ice” has been three years in the making, she said. “We were excited to have it voiced by David Tennant, and the visuals on that are just stunning. It follows these polar-nauts to some of the most incredible and dangerous places on the planet, doing research to help us figure out how to manage water and changing climate.”

Talking about “The Chase Around the World,” a spin-off of ITV’s game show “The Chase,” she said, “What I love about ‘The Chase’ is taking the quizzes and the studio show and getting it out into the world. We say The Chasers are both beloved and feared, and to see them out of their environment – of a safe, comfortable studio – and out into the world is great. Some of the locations are just gorgeous. The photography in the series is really great too, and it’s fun, and it’s getting that scale – these wonderful locations – and I think it’s just a clever way of wrapping up a treasure hunt and bit of travel porn in a way.”

She also discussed “Spy Next Door: The Anna Chapman Story.” “I think there’s always a demand for stories about spies,” she said. “People are endlessly fascinated by spies, true or fictional, and it’s a remarkable story. And she was this glamorous woman, which just adds to the intrigue.”

title: La Oreja de Van Gogh Songs Set to Power an Ambitious Romantic Musical From Fernando González Molina (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: The songs of pop group phenomenon La Oreja de Van Gogh, which has just become the only Spanish band with a song in Spotify’s Billions Club, are heading for the big screen, set to be sung and power the emotional currents of an ambitious romantic musical, “Puedes Contar Conmigo.” Director of blockbuster “Palm Trees in […]
content:
The songs of pop group phenomenon La Oreja de Van Gogh, which has just become the only Spanish band with a song in Spotify’s Billions Club, are heading for the big screen, set to be sung and power the emotional currents of an ambitious romantic musical, “Puedes Contar Conmigo.”

Director of blockbuster “Palm Trees in the Snow,” Fernando González Molina is on board to helm the movie. Preeminent Spanish producers Beltrán Cortázar, Domingo Corral and Gonzalo Sálazar-Simpson are set to produce. La Oreja de Van Gogh will also serve as executive producer on the film, which bids fair to become one of the biggest upcoming titles from Spain.

“Seeing that our songs will gain a new life in cinema is a dream for us,” La Oreja de Van Gogh said in a statement. The movie project roles off its extensive 2026 comeback tour with Amaia Montero back as lead vocalist which staged over 100 concerts and sold more than 400,000 tickets to packed concerts across Spain, which confirmed the huge resilient across-generations fandom of the group. The group has over 50 Platinum and Gold Discs.

Popular on Variety

“We’re at a beautiful moment at our career, feeling the affection of many, many people and we believe ‘Puedes Contar Conmigo’ will be a marvellous celebration of what unites us with our audience,” the band added.

González Molina has had his biggest audience success with romantic dramas particularly 2010’s “Three Steps Above Heaven” (€9.9 million: $11.2 million), 2012’s I Want You” (€12.1 million: €13.6 million) and 2016’s “Palm Trees in the Snow,” a lush period piece which stood out for its scale, production values and spectacular visuals which grossed €17.1 million ($19.8 million) at the Spanish box office.

Little is known about the musical’s plot, currently being written by González Molina and screenwriter Miguel López Martínez, save that it is an original story, will use La Oreja’s lyrics and is in an advanced stage of development and writing.

The possibilities, however, are enormous given the longevity of La Oreja de Van Gogh – founded in 1996 – and its enormous repertoire. Also key is La Oreja d Van Gogh’s accessible style of broader audience pop-rock and surging choruses and above all the songs’ highly relatable emotions, whether nostalgia after break-up (“Los Rosas,” “La Playa”), fleeting fated love, (“Jueves”) and happiness at having lived a great romance (“El último vals”), to name just a few of the group’s greatest hits.

The Ambition of ‘Puedes Contar Conmigo’

Whatever the storyline line, the movie definitely looks set to be highly ambitious.

“We’ve always told stories through our music and knowing that these stories will inspire such a big visual and narrative universe fills us with illusion,” the band said.

“Translating the universe of the Oreja into an original story is a giant challenge for me,” González Molina added. “It’s also fulfilling a dream of updating big romantic musicals, which I have always loved, with the codes of contemporary cinema. With this film I’d love to make a cinema event that moves audiences like the songs of La Oreja de Van Gogh have done for decades.”

“Being part of such a genuine mix of talent such as La Oreja de Van Gogh and Fernando is authentic luck for us,” said the producers. “We feel we have the bases of what could be a great film: Our challenge is to support them to make this dream as large as possible,” they added.

A Pedigree Producer Package

That ambition knits with the C.V. of its producers. Cortázar, for instance, is the former CEO of Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo’s Suma Content where his credits include Los Javis’ seven-part 2023 series “La Mesías,” a first instance of their full-on creativity, each episode with different genre influences, knit by a pop sensibility and varying formats across multiple timelines, all of which anticipated “La Bola Negra.”

Founder of Lazona, Sálazar-Simpson is behind Goya Best Picture winner “No Rest for the Wicked,” and has produced two of the three highest-grossing Spanish films in Spain: 2014 comedy “Spanish Affair” (€56.2 million: $63.5 million) and Spanish Affair 2 (€36.1 million: $40.8 million).

“Puedes contar conmigo” also stands out as the first movie announced by Domingo Corral, the former Head of Fiction and Entertainment at Movistar Plus, behind “La Mesías,” “Querer” and “Riot Police” in series and “Sirât,” “La Bola Negra,” “The Beloved” and “Sundays” in films.

“As producers, we want to make a film that is different and unique and at the level of ambition which merit La Oreja de Van Gogh and their songs. Many are part of our emotional history across several generations and they have an enormous fan base in Latin America and the U.S. Hispanic,” said Corral, noting that one key reference is “La La Land.”

“We are fortunate to have Fernando in,” he added. “We are convinced that his vision and passion will deliver a great film full of unforgettable emotional moments.”

(L-R) Gonzalo Sálazar-Simpson, Fernando González Molina, Beltrán Gortázar, Domingo Corral @michaeloats

title: Talent Agency Cosmic Opens London Office, Led by Gabrielle de Cevins
summary: Cosmic Talents, which represents leading international heads of department, is opening a London office. It will be led by Gabrielle de Cevins, who joins Cosmic Talents as the agency’s U.K.-based agent. De Cevins brings eight years of in-house production experience to the role, including the last four at London-based feature film production company The Bureau […]
content:
Cosmic Talents, which represents leading international heads of department, is opening a London office. It will be led by Gabrielle de Cevins, who joins Cosmic Talents as the agency’s U.K.-based agent.

De Cevins brings eight years of in-house production experience to the role, including the last four at London-based feature film production company The Bureau (“Queen at Sea,” “Black Church Bay,” “A Long Winter”), and will oversee representation of the agency’s roster of directors of photography, production designers, costume designers and editors across the U.K. market for both features and commercials.

She will work hand in hand with Paris-based agents Marie Berg, Elodie Vongdara and Andréa Bernard.

Popular on Variety

In recent years, the agency’s talent have been responsible for the cinematography of films such as Edward Berger’s “Conclave” (Stéphane Fontaine), Magnus von Horn’s “The Girl With the Needle” (Michal Dymek) and Andrey Zvyagintsev’s “Minotaur” (Mikhail Krichman).

Berg, managing director and agent at Cosmic Talents, said, “The U.K. market is exceptionally creative. Its directors and the stories they tell are a constant source of inspiration. By opening this office, we want to strengthen our presence in the U.K. and establish a deeper connection with this vibrant creative community.

“Having a local representative brings greater spontaneity to our relationships and allows us to build meaningful connections with directors, clients and production partners.

“With a background in production, Gabrielle has a strong understanding of the realities and challenges of producing in the U.K. Her experience enables her to bridge creative ambitions with the practical demands of production, making her ideally positioned to support projects in this market.”

De Cevins said, “I’m delighted to be joining a team with such a strong commitment to artistic vision. Cosmic has built an exceptional roster over the years. I’m looking forward to helping production find the right creative partners for their projects, and to championing Cosmic talents within the U.K. market.”

title: Harvey Keitel Plays Acting Teacher in Gaurav Bhardwaj’s Debut Feature ‘The Method’ (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Harvey Keitel stars as a celebrated acting teacher in “The Method,” the first feature from director and co-writer Gaurav Bhardwaj, produced by “CTRL” banner Travelin Bone Entertainment alongside Imagination Infinite Motion Pictures. Mina Sundwall (“Murdaugh: Death in the Family,” “Lost in Space”) also features, as do Rakshit Bhuchar and Rohan Maletira, both of whom make […]
content:
Harvey Keitel stars as a celebrated acting teacher in “The Method,” the first feature from director and co-writer Gaurav Bhardwaj, produced by “CTRL” banner Travelin Bone Entertainment alongside Imagination Infinite Motion Pictures.

Mina Sundwall (“Murdaugh: Death in the Family,” “Lost in Space”) also features, as do Rakshit Bhuchar and Rohan Maletira, both of whom make their feature debuts with the film.

The story plays out in New York’s cutthroat acting scene, where a talented Indian actor chasing his craft falls under the sway of Keitel’s teacher. As ambition, friendship and artistic ideals pull against one another, the mentor challenges every one of them to consider what they would give up to succeed.

Popular on Variety

Production has wrapped in the New York and New Jersey area, and the film is expected to release in 2027.

“‘The Method’ is not simply a film about acting,” said Bhardwaj. “It explores the journeys of four artists: an Indian actor, a Canadian actor, an American playwright and director, and a revered acting teacher portrayed by the legendary actor, Harvey Keitel. At its core, it is a film about aspiration and relationships.”

Bhardwaj added that every character and arc carried personal weight for him, since at some point in his own creative career he had stood where each of them stands. “The film explores the universal struggle to preserve our identities when our ambitions begin demanding that we sacrifice parts of ourselves. I want audiences to experience the same conflict our characters face – the tension between the relationships we value and the ambitions we choose to pursue.”

Travelin Bone was set up by Marc Sternberg, Steve Garrow and Naresh Malik. Its Netflix original film “CTRL” preceded “The Method,” and the company is building out a film and TV slate aimed at both Indian and global viewers.

“With ‘The Method,’ we are bringing together exceptional talent and creative teams from both countries,” said Garrow, the company’s co-founder and CEO. “It has been a wonderful experience working with Gaurav and witnessing the clarity and confidence with which he has approached his first feature film, particularly alongside an iconic actor like Harvey Keitel.”

Garrow also credited Sundwall with real depth and presence on screen and said the two newcomers had delivered work beyond what he had expected.

“‘The Method’ reflects the philosophy of my company in many ways,” said Lalit Bhatnagar, founder of Imagination Infinite Motion Pictures. “We are at a moment when content is becoming increasingly global – and so is talent. The traditional boundaries between industries and markets are becoming less relevant, creating an extraordinary opportunity to bring together artists from different backgrounds to tell compelling stories.”

title: Former Prince Andrew Taking Legal Action Against Police Over Epstein Files Arrest
summary: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor is taking legal action against the police force that arrested him earlier this year. According to The Telegraph, which broke the news, the issue revolves around the search warrants used by Thames Valley Police and its chief constable in relation to his arrest. The legality of these warrants are being challenged by Mountbatten-Windsor’s […]
content:
Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor is taking legal action against the police force that arrested him earlier this year.

According to The Telegraph, which broke the news, the issue revolves around the search warrants used by Thames Valley Police and its chief constable in relation to his arrest. The legality of these warrants are being challenged by Mountbatten-Windsor’s lawyers via judicial review, The Telegraph reported.

The warrant was obtained a day before he was arrested and for days afterwards police were pictured searching Mountbatten-Windsor’s propeties in Sandringham and on the Windsor estate.

“Whilst our investigation into misconduct in public office continues, we are engaged in legal proceedings in relation to warrants previously obtained from the Central Criminal Court,” a Thames Valley Police spokesperson told Deadline. “As these legal proceedings are currently ongoing, it would be inappropriate for us to comment further.”

Watch on Deadline

Coming after his Prince title was stripped by his brother King Charles III, Mountbatten-Windsor’s arrest in connection to the Epstein Files sent shockwaves around the world. The landmark moment represented the first time a modern British Royal had been arrested. Images circulated globally of Mountbatten-Windsor hiding in a car on the way back from the police station.

He was reported at the time to have been arrested over the alleged sharing of confidential material with late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. The pair’s links had been the subject of intense press coverage and speculation for years. Mountbatten-Windsor has always denied wrongdoing.

Since his arrest, Mountbatten-Windsor has been lying low on the Sandringham Estate.

title: Execs Launch IP Studio & Unveil Viking Mythology Series
summary: EXCLUSIVE: A trio of executives have launched an IP studio focused on sci-fi, fantasy and horror. Antoine Disle, Orso Vesperini and Olivier Compere, who between them have made projects for Canal+, TF1 and Warner, are behind Forge Films Company, which has unveiled Viking mythlogy series Lost in Hel as first project from its slate. Forge […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: A trio of executives have launched an IP studio focused on sci-fi, fantasy and horror.

Antoine Disle, Orso Vesperini and Olivier Compere, who between them have made projects for Canal+, TF1 and Warner, are behind Forge Films Company, which has unveiled Viking mythlogy series Lost in Hel as first project from its slate.

Forge has brought in Head of Gaming & Interactive Experiences Léonidas Vesperini and former Lionsgate SVP Marc Lorber is advising the company, which launched over the summer.

Forge describes itself as a “next-generation genre studio and IP model,” which will focus on the sci-fi, fantasy and horror spaces and is keen on gaming. The exec team are based in the U.S., France and the UK, while individual projects like Lost in Hel will come out of the U.S.

Watch on Deadline

Forge has just unveiled a Breathe in Hel proof-of-concept on YouTube for its Lost in Hel series. Set after a Viking clan is shipwrecked on an unmapped island, the Lost in Hel universe follows Jarl Alvar and a Christian queen forced into an alliance as they attempt to unite sworn enemies against an ancient force. Directed by Nik Kacevski (Mad Max: Fury Road), Lost in Hel stars Jessica Ferguson (Cobra City, Sun Sparta), Troy Honeysett (Class of ’07, The Combination: Redemption), Masa Yamaguchi (The Condemned, Wolverine) and newcomer Grace Durrant.

The co-founders said: “Forge is built to identify distinctive creative talent and original IP early, test their potential with audiences, and give the strongest worlds the opportunity to grow across film, television, gaming and immersive experiences. Our model brings together creative ambition, audience engagement and industry expertise within a commercially viable and sustainable framework.”

title: Brian Cox Goes Digital: Top British TV Scientist Strikes Content Deal With New Sony Studio
summary: EXCLUSIVE: The first partnership for Sony Pictures Television’s (SPT) new digital studio was with Minecraft supremo Tom Simons AKA TommyInnit, but its second pact is in a different universe altogether. Renowned British scientist and broadcaster Brian Cox has struck a deal with SPT International Production’s Digital Studio that will see the pair create his formats […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: The first partnership for Sony Pictures Television’s (SPT) new digital studio was with Minecraft supremo Tom Simons AKA TommyInnit, but its second pact is in a different universe altogether.

Renowned British scientist and broadcaster Brian Cox has struck a deal with SPT International Production’s Digital Studio that will see the pair create his formats in the digital space for the first time.

Forged specifically for digital platforms, the content, which is part of a long-term partnership rather than specific series, will span science, astronomy and culture. “The collaboration aims to build a distinctive destination for science storytelling that combines world-class production values with the accessibility and immediacy of creator-led media,” SPT said.

Not to be confused with the Succession star, Cox, who has more than 5 million cross-platform followers and already has a YouTube channel with more than 16,000 subscribers, is one of the UK’s best-known scientists. The particle physicist has presented reams of science shows, mostly for the BBC, including Stargazing Live, The Planets and Brian Cox’s Adventures in Space and Time.

Watch on Deadline

Science has proved a hugely popular genre on YouTube and the BBC itself has been pushing further into the space. At the same time, traditional TV presenters like Holly Willoughby and Amol Rajan have started going direct to their audiences via YouTube.

Cox said: “It’s more important than ever to find new and engaging ways to deliver science and fact-based content to audiences, wherever they consume it. This collaboration with the Sony Pictures Television team is tremendously exciting for me, because we share a desire to make high quality, intellectually challenging, informative and entertaining content available to as many people as possible, across as many platforms as possible. We will have succeeded if our audience are entertained, challenged, terrified, excited and awestruck in equal measure by the dizzying picture of the universe painted by modern science.”

Sacha Khari and Matt Ford, the digital studio’s co-leads, said Cox is “better than anyone” at “taking the most complicated questions about existence and making them feel accessible and entertaining.” “On paper, Brian Cox and Tom Simons might look worlds apart, but there’s actually a lot in common. We work closely with distinctive talent, develop original ideas around them and grow audiences together to create scale and staying power,” they added.

Led by ex-BBC Studios and Channel 4 executives Ford and Khari, Sony’s digital studio launched last year to “engage with UK content creators, create digital originals and build creator partnerships.”

The TommyInnit deal, struck with the creator who runs the most popular Minecraft channel on Twitch, has seen him forge a 100 Questions YouTube series with guests including Cox and Stephen Fry.

title: Gillian Anderson Explains Confrontation With “Distracting” Superfans Who Sat In Front Row Of West End Show: “We Can All See You”
summary: Gillian Anderson has explained why she asked a group of superfans not to sit in the front row of her West End stage show, Who’s Afraid of Virginia Woolf?. Anderson is performing at Soho Place Theatre and was filmed confronting audience members following a performance. In the video, posted just after midnight on Sunday morning […]
content:
Gillian Anderson has explained why she asked a group of superfans not to sit in the front row of her West End stage show, Who’s Afraid of Virginia Woolf?.

Anderson is performing at Soho Place Theatre and was filmed confronting audience members following a performance. In the video, posted just after midnight on Sunday morning in the UK, Anderson tells fans: “You guys cannot sit in the front row.”

She continued: “I don’t care; you cannot sit in the front row. It’s so distracting.” The fans can be heard responding and apologizing. “You can’t come 20 times and sit in the front row, it’ll drive me mad,” Anderson adds, according to the video, originally posted on TikTok.

After the footage went viral (it has amassed more than 4 million views on TikTok alone), Anderson posted on X/Twitter, explaining the interaction she had following the show, which co-stars Billy Crudup.

Watch on Deadline

“The video doing the rounds is me talking with women I go back over 20 years with – so please don’t say anything negative to or about them,” she said. “We’re thrilled to be doing this show but for people in the front row, please be aware that in such an intimate venue we can all see you and sometimes, it can be a tad distracting!”

The 58-year-old Sex Education star added: “That’s all. All good. On with the show and love to everyone and thank you to all of those coming.”

It’s unclear whether her fans will respect her request. The TikTok user who posted the video of Anderson suggested that the women had booked to attend eight performances.

Anderson’s confrontation is part of a growing trend of actors voicing their concerns to theatergoers. Last month, Cate Blanchett, from the London stage of National Theatre’s Lyttelton Theatre after the curtain call of Electra/Persona, asked fans to put away their cellphones.

Blanchett said: “There are few places on this planet where we can simply be together and be present. I understand you like filming the curtain call – and it is kind of flattering in a way – but for anyone who is filming the show, please don’t, because it spoils it for the next group of people who come in and are present with us. So thank you very much.”

In April, Wicked star Cynthia Erivo halted her performance of Dracula at the Noël Coward Theatre after spotting an audience member recording the show. A month later, Rosamund Pike was critical of an audience member for texting during her Inter Alia show at the National Theatre.

title: MBC Studios Sets November 19 Release For Landmark Production ‘Traveller’s Hell’
summary: MBC Studios has announced a November 19 theatrical release date for long-awaited psychological thriller Traveller’s Hell about a young woman who picks up a stranger on a remote road. The feature is adapted from the best-selling novel of the same name by acclaimed best-selling Saudi author Osamah Almuslim, who wrote the screenplay. The release marks […]
content:
MBC Studios has announced a November 19 theatrical release date for long-awaited psychological thriller Traveller’s Hell about a young woman who picks up a stranger on a remote road.

The feature is adapted from the best-selling novel of the same name by acclaimed best-selling Saudi author Osamah Almuslim, who wrote the screenplay.

The release marks a significant milestone for the studio in a strategic partnership with Almuslim, first announced more than two years ago, aimed at adapting several of his popular literary works into film and television projects.

It also stands out for its female driven genre storyline and as the first feature for pioneering Saudi director Hana Alomair, who previously co-wrote and directed Whispers, one of Netflix’s first original series with Saudi Arabia in the wake of the country opening up in 2017.

Watch on Deadline

The Riyadh-based studio said the release would begin in Saudi cinemas, with rollouts to additional Arab cities to be announced in the coming weeks.

Shot on location across Saudi Arabia, the movie’s ensemble cast features Adwa Bader, Basil Alsole, Mohammed Ali, Shojaat Nashat, and Aziz Gharbawi.

The feature opens on an isolated road late at night as a young woman, driving alone, comes across a stranded male driver whose car has broken down on a mountain road notorious for disappearances and murders.

Choosing empathy over a creeping sense of foreboding, she offers him a ride to the nearest station. That single choice unleashes a harrowing chain of strange and terrifying events in the dead of night, turning a simple gesture of kindness into a real-life nightmare.

title: ‘I, Addict’ Creator Javier Giner Unpacks ‘This Solitude,’ a Film ‘About ‘Those Who Keep Functioning While Something Inside Them Is Falling Apart’
summary: Basque director Javier Giner’s “This Solitude” (“Esta Soledad”) recently premiered at the San Sebastián Film Festival’s New Directors section on Sept. 23. Giner is the creator and co-director of the Disney+ series “I, Addict,” based on his autobiographical book by the same name. It earned lead actor Oriol Pla the International Emmy for Best Actor. […]
content:
Basque director Javier Giner‘s “This Solitude” (“Esta Soledad”) recently premiered at the San Sebastián Film Festival’s New Directors section on Sept. 23. Giner is the creator and co-director of the Disney+ series “I, Addict,” based on his autobiographical book by the same name. It earned lead actor Oriol Pla the International Emmy for Best Actor.

Also starring Pla, “This Solitude” follows Leo and Lorea after their five-year relationship has ended. Each of them has to figure out how to continue living life on their own in Bilbao. Leo is a struggling actor who has to work as a grocery clerk to make ends meet while taking care of his disabled father. Lorea is a troubled writer who looks to a former prison inmate for companionship. Both must confront their loneliness and unresolved issues and look for meaning in a world that can sometimes feel cruel and scary.

Oriol Pla in ‘This Solitude’

“The film is about people who are losing control of their lives. Loneliness may be one of the few truly democratic things in life; what isn’t democratic are the resources we have to survive it,” Giner told Variety.

Popular on Variety

The film stars Pal, Marina Salas (“Join Me for Breakfast”), Gemma Martínez, Kai Etxaniz and Itziar Lazkano. Giner co-wrote the film with Luisa Matienzo, who is also one of the film’s producers along with Miguel Torrente. The production companies are Balance Media Entertainment, Fuga de Cuerpos, La Embajada TV and Basajaun Filmak. International sales are being handled by Filmax and they will release the film theatrically in Spain on Oct. 30.

Director Javier Giner, ‘This Solitude’ Photo Credit: David Herranza

Variety interviewed Javier Giner after the film’s premiere in San Sebastián.

There is a loneliness epidemic around the world and this film seems to address it.

Javier Giner: I didn’t set out to make a film about the loneliness epidemic. I’m a little wary of starting a film with a theme. This began with the desire to create, more than a film, an emotional state that would stay with the audience after they left the theater.

I looked around me and saw people with apparently full lives — jobs, friends, partners, phones that never stop, social media — and yet they were profoundly lonely and exhausted. I was fascinated by the contradiction: we’ve never had so many tools to avoid being alone and, paradoxically, so many ways of never truly connecting with anyone.

Is this story also autobiographical like your book “I, Addict”?

Giner: Everything I write is autobiographical in some way, but not in the sense that “I, Addict” was, where I was explicitly telling the story of a period in my own life. In “Esta Soledad,” the autobiography is in the gaze and in the emotions: Sadness, family relationships, certain ways of loving, the fear of losing someone, the feeling of not knowing what to do with your life. More and more, what interests me is whether what I write is emotionally true. To me, that is a deeper form of autobiography, and something I find endlessly fascinating.

The film is also about absent parents, both physically and emotionally. Do you think this is especially true for the new generation?

Giner: I think every generation inherits from the previous one not only its traumas, but also its emotional vocabulary, including the things it never had words for. The parents in “Esta Soledad” are not monsters. Even when they cause pain, they love their children and they do the best they can. But loving someone and knowing how to love someone are two very different things.

Children end up living with the emotional consequences of decisions they never made. I think we all spend part of our lives trying to understand what we received from our parents, and another part deciding what we’re going to do with it.

You chose to work with Oriol Pla again after “I, Addict.”

Giner: Oriol and I have something more valuable than simply understanding each other: we trust each other completely. And trust allows for things that are far more interesting and profound than comfort.

After “I, Addict,” we had already gone through some very emotionally demanding places together, so now we can arrive on set and barely need to talk. Sometimes a word or a look is enough. Or I can simply tell him, “I don’t know exactly what I’m looking for. Let’s find it together.”

Oriol can be explosive, physical, unpredictable, almost animalistic, and five seconds later he can do something tiny that breaks your heart. Very few actors can inhabit both of those extremes. As an actor, he’s a Stradivarius, and on top of that he’s an incredible human being. He’s my brother, my partner.

Bilbao seems to be a central character in the film, sometimes portrayed as lonely, dark and gritty. Would you agree?

Giner: Yes, although I never wanted to film Bilbao as a sad city, but rather as a state of mind. I wanted to film what almost never gets filmed anymore: not the postcard, but the humidity, the noise, the architecture, the industrial memory, that light that can change completely within a matter of minutes. There is something very physical about the city; at times, it almost seems to weigh on the bodies.

That connected with Leo and Lorea. Their external world remains exactly where it was while everything inside them has changed completely. The streets are the same, but they no longer mean the same thing. I believe strongly in that: Cities don’t change when we suffer; the way we look at them does. So Bilbao wasn’t there to illustrate their sadness. It had to remain indifferent to it. And paradoxically, that indifference is what ultimately makes the city so deeply emotional.

title: ‘Tulsa King’ Renewed for New York-Set Season 5 as Four Join Cast
summary: “Tulsa King” is heading to New York. The Sylvester Stallone series has been renewed for a fifth season at Paramount+ as the production migrates from Georgia to the Big Apple, coinciding with the Season 5 storyline. The renewal comes ahead of the Season 4 premiere on Oct. 16. Stallone’s daughter Scarlet Rose Stallone, who has […]
content:
“Tulsa King” is heading to New York.

The Sylvester Stallone series has been renewed for a fifth season at Paramount+ as the production migrates from Georgia to the Big Apple, coinciding with the Season 5 storyline. The renewal comes ahead of the Season 4 premiere on Oct. 16.

Stallone’s daughter Scarlet Rose Stallone, who has played Spencer on all four seasons of the show, has been promoted to series regular. Plus, four fresh faces are joining the cast in series regular roles: Erik Palladino (“I Play Rocky”), Glenn Fleshler (“Billions”), Anthony Skordi (“The Last Frontier”) and Nickola Shreli (“Power Book IV: Force”).

Variety reported in June that a writers’ room for a potential Season 5 had opened, with plans to relocate the production to New York. Stallone’s character, Dwight “The General” Manfredi, is originally from New York before he was exiled by his mob associates to Tulsa. Season 5 will see him returning to his mafia roots.

Popular on Variety

The move is also driven by budgetary considerations. Thanks to recent improvements to the state tax incentive, New York is now one of the most cost-friendly places to shoot in the world, with film and TV projects flocking to the state.

“We’re excited to welcome the cast and crew of ‘Tulsa King’ to New York State for its fifth season,” said Hope Knight, the CEO and commissioner of New York’s economic growth agency, Empire State Development. “Under Governor Hochul’s leadership, New York has built an unmatched home for film and television — world-class talent, iconic locations, and a Film Tax Credit Program that delivers real jobs and investment for New Yorkers. ‘Tulsa King’ represents the latest in a growing list of projects proudly filmed in New York.”

Drew Brown, EVP of physical production at Paramount TV added, “We are thrilled to bring fans even more of this incredible series, and to be shooting the next season of ‘Tulsa King’ in New York, where Dwight Manfredi’s story will continue to evolve. We’re proud of the work we’ve done in Georgia, and it remains an important venue for us.”

In addition to Stallone, “Tulsa King” Season 4 stars Martin Starr, Jay Will, Vincent Piazza, Annabella Sciorra, Chris Caldovino, McKenna Quigley Harrington, Frank Grillo, Mike “Cash Flo” Walden, James Russo, Kevin Pollak, Neal McDonough, Garrett Hedlund and Dana Delany. Gretchen Mol also joins the cast for Season 4 as a series regular.

Terence Winter is the head writer of “Tulsa King” and executive produces alongside Taylor Sheridan, Stallone, David C. Glasser, Ron Burkle, David Hutkin, Bob Yari, Thomas Kelly and Keith Cox. The series is produced by Paramount Television Studios and 101 Studios.

title: ‘Imperfect Women’ Renewed for Season 2 at Apple TV With Kerry Washington Returning
summary: “Imperfect Women” has been renewed for Season 2 at Apple TV, Variety has learned. Season 1 star Kerry Washington will return to lead the second season. The first season of the show is based on the book of the same name by Araminta Hall, while Season 2 will be based on an original idea built […]
content:
“Imperfect Women” has been renewed for Season 2 at Apple TV, Variety has learned. Season 1 star Kerry Washington will return to lead the second season.

The first season of the show is based on the book of the same name by Araminta Hall, while Season 2 will be based on an original idea built around Washington’s character. “Imperfect Women” debuted on Apple TV back in March. The first season also starred Elisabeth Moss and Kate Mara. Moss’ Love & Squalor Pictures had originally optioned the book for television.

Annie Weisman served as the writer and showrunner on Season 1. She will return for Season 2 as co-showrunner alongside Justin Hillian. The official logline for Season 2 states, “Eleanor (Washington) returns to her hometown roots in the affluent black enclave of Martha’s Vineyard, only to find that beneath it’s idyllic surface, lie secrets and scandals that threaten to upend everything she thought she knew about her past.”

Popular on Variety

“We were thrilled to see how deeply these women and their stories resonated with audiences around the world, and I’m so excited to step back into Eleanor’s shoes,” Washington said. “She’s intelligent and strong, but she also finds herself navigating complicated and sometimes messy situations. We at Simpson Street along with our incredible partners at Apple and Love & Squalor Pictures can’t wait to explore a fresh chapter for her and share where this story takes us next.”

Hillian was most recently the co-showrunner on the Showtime series “The Chi.” He has also worked on shows like “Snowfall” at FX and “I’m Dying Up Here,” also for Showtime. He is repped by WME, 3 Arts, and Yorn Levine.

“After a wildly entertaining first season, driven by the performances of Kerry, Lizzie and Kate, we jumped at the opportunity to expand the world of ‘Imperfect Women’ through Kerry’s fan favorite character of Eleanor,” said Matt Cherniss, Apple TV’s head of programming. “Annie and Justin’s thrilling new story felt like an exciting and natural next chapter. We can’t wait for fans to experience it.”

Weisman and Hillian are the creators, co-showrunners, and executive producers on Season 2. Washington executive produces via Simpson Street along with Pilar Savone. Moss and Lindsey McManus executive produce via Love & Squalor. 20th Television and Apple Studios produce.

title: Iberseries Takeaways: Woody Allen on His New Film, Los Javis Pact With HBO Max, the Tales of Cachou the Brown Bear and More
summary: When the going gets tough, the tough get going to places like Iberseries & Platino Industria. Its 6th edition, also a pre-Mipcom warm-up, ran over Sept.29-Oct. 2 at Madrid’s Matadero, its rehabilitated orange-red brick former slaughterhouse. That setting seems appropriate. There’s little evidence that Ampere Analysis’ maxim, coined a couple of years ago – a […]
content:
When the going gets tough, the tough get going to places like Iberseries & Platino Industria. Its 6th edition, also a pre-Mipcom warm-up, ran over Sept.29-Oct. 2 at Madrid’s Matadero, its rehabilitated orange-red brick former slaughterhouse.

That setting seems appropriate. There’s little evidence that Ampere Analysis’ maxim, coined a couple of years ago – a contracting sector chasing a 75% of peak TV business – has not changed.

Some parts of the TV business have hardly altered at all, such as its dependence on great writing, Steve Matthews, Banijay head of scripted, creative, said at an Iberseries company Spotlight.

Popular on Variety

Yet most companies, from Super Indies and network giants to small former auteur producers are pushing into AI, if only for backroom operations, and microdramas to push back against spiralling costs and diminishing revenues, sustaining cash-flow and not losing out on new growth opportunities.

That in turn is driving new mindsets. Making microdramas has made Argentinean producer Lorena Quevedo think of how long certain proceses take in cinema and series. “Suddenly a series we thought had an impossible budget we took up again saying: ‘If we made this microdrama, we cannot not make this series.’”

Needful of such insights, delegates broke attendance records up a massive 20% to 3,400 including day passes.

Iberseries & Platino Industria is organized by rights collection society EGEDA and Foundation Secuoya, in collaboration with producers’ assn. Fipca and sponsorship from Madrid Film Office and Film Madrid Region.

10 takeaways:

Woody Allen

The big star at Iberseries, or nearby at least in another part of Madrid, was the 90 year-old New Yorker. Starring an ensemble cast of Marton Csokas, Jemima Kirke Jakob Oftebro, Peter Vives and Alexi Wasser, the provisionally entitled Woody Allen Fall Project rolls Oct. 5 with WestEnd Films handling world sales. Small and debonair, Allen didn’t reveal so much about his upcoming film at an Oct. 1 press conference – he rarely does – though he teased it was a “comedy with romance, intrigue and infidelity.” He also said that Madrid – elegant and beautiful – was perfect for the “diplomatic atmosphere” he wanted for the film. The jury is out how the film will go. “It has to live up to my expectations. That doesn’t mean that it will, but I’ll do my best,” he said. Allen has however made pointed use of seeming postcard settings before, as in “Vicky Cristina Barcelona,” one of his most successful international shoots.

Los Javis, Mubi and an HBO Max Coup

In one of the biggest news announcements at Iberseries, Mubi acquired global on drama series “La Mesías,” created by Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi and sold by Movistar Plus International, which is to TV is what “La Bola Negra” is to cinema. In another, and a coup for HBO Max unveiled development on an enticing new crime series, to be exec produced by Los Javis at their Madrid manner Suma Content. The series is created by Fran Araújo, who co-penned Intl. Emmy-nominated “The Anatomy of the Moment,” and “Querer” co-scribe Eduard Sola, two of Spain’s most exciting writing talents. Most all talk about the Javis’ turns on “La Bola Negra.” They – and indeed HBO Max – are also rapidly creating ever more powerful creative hubs.

(L-R) Fran Araújo, Edu Sola (L-R) Fran Araujo, Eduard Sola Credit: Patricia J Garcinuno

Erik Barmack on What He Got Wrong About AI, and What He Might Have Got Right, to the Horror of Some

Iberseries debated genre.The real horror story for many was AI. Just take the macro stats. Barmack delivered some stats. Revenues for just two U.S. AI companies, Anthropic and OpenAI, are projected to grow to an annual $700 million in the next couple of years, worth 13-15 times the value of Europe and Latin America’s entire media industries. AI is “much more disruptive” than sound, cable TV or streaming. And if “AI companies don’t continue to grow, the entire stock market will crash.” Barmack is a highly respected former Netflix international head. He’s also a recognised AI expert. Could he be wrong? To the relief of much of his producer audience, he did say he’s been wrong on one count. When Sora started, I was sort of convinced that it was over and that we’d be stuck on these loops of of watching 15-second generated clips targeted to your algorithm. That turned out to be wrong because it was too expensive, basically, to make these videos. And there wasn’t a big enough audience for what’s called AI slop.”

The Holy Grail: Original Crime and Cachou

Presented at Iberseries, the big new Movistar Plus-Arte series “Killing a Bear” is a murder mystery, where the victim is Cachou. A giant Pyrenean brown bear, his death in real life and on screen sparks a criminal investigation, as the event is recounted episode by episode by different characters in six radically warring versions. This originality builds as it feeds into a broader portrait lending historical depth of an ancient Spain battling environmentalists and E.U. regulation to preserve its way of life. Crime still pays, accounting for 27% of scripted TV orders and 24% of first-run scripted TV ordered globally, making it the single most commissioned TV genre, Ampere Analysis’ Guy Bisson tells Variety. But what operators and big indies want is original crime to cut through the crowd, one of the sector’s Holy Grails.

Eduard Fernández in ‘Killing a Bear’ Bárbara Sánchez Palomero

Banijay’s Secret

Mipcom’s conference will kick off with a Jeff Zucker-Marco Bassetti keynote, moderated by Variety co-Editor in Chief Cynthia Littelton, post the Banijay-All3Media $8 billion merger. What’s Banijay’s secret? One obviously is scalable franchises. Another is its network of 170 companies worldwide.

“All of these are based on creativity, based on talent, based on writing,” Steve Matthews, Banijay head of scripted, creative, said at an Iberseries Banijay Spotlight. Connecting with great talent, and giving them the trust and resources to make the titles they envision is indeed the key to some of the greatest production operations and producers in the world.

Microdramas Open Up

Inevitably, Iberseries hosted a vertical drama panel. “I’m from Team Melodrama,” said Argentinean producer Lorena Quevedo, a panelist, arguing the key was “romantic tension.” Her first microdrama – and indeed Argentina’s, – “Dinero, Armas y Feliz Navidad,” released on ReelShort in September 2025, hit 273 million views. Most microdramas are classic melodramas,. The format, however, is opening up in the Spanish-speaking world. Though its slate is primarily made up of vertical dramas, Telemundo Studios has begun to develop 20-episode 10-minute horizontal series, said Telemundo’s Clo Fernandez. 3Pas Studios has recently made a vertical musical, is considering a comedic microdrama, added Javier Williams. Quevedo has produced a vertical actioner.

One Direction Amazon MGM is Heading In International: Genre at Scale

An Amazon MGM Studios Spotlight was led by Javiera Balmaceda, head of international originals, Latin America, Canada and Australia, and Nicole Morganti, Prime Video head of international originals, Italy & Southern Europe. Both pointed to big action swings – Mexico’s “Venganza,” produced by El Estudio’s Pablo Cruz, and espionage actioner Zeta,” starring Mario Casas as one way to go. Both topped Prime Video Global Top 10 charts. Latin America’s challenge, Balmaceda noted is not necessarily a lack of talent, but a shortage of experience and opportunities to work at scale.

Spanish Cinema: Size Matters

Scale threaded various panels. Another Example

Spain made 423 feature films in 2025, according to the European Audiovisual Observatory. In 2026, as Iberseries unspooled, only four movies can be described as box office hits: “Torrente for President” (€29.1 million: $32.8 million), “Tadeo and the Magic Lamp,” (€7.2 million) “Aida y vuelta” (€5.1 million), “La Bola Negra” (€14.9 million and counting fast) and The Beloved. All are high-end for Spain. Three are based on huge Spanish IP. Another stars Javier Bardem. “The future of Spanish cinema does not lie in making more films, but in getting more people to want to see them,” Atresmedia Cine MD Jaime de Ortiz de Artiñano said late August. That sentiment ran through multiple panels at Iberseries.

IPs: Their Power

Only 12-14% of new series premieres each year are based on existing IP but existing IP accounts for 40%-50% of the top 100 most in-demand series, Parrot Analytics Jaime Otero said at Iberseries. On average, titles based on IP has 2.3 times more demand than original titles. That rises to 2.9 times titles inspired by real events and 3 times for literary adaptations. Multiples companies are putting large faith in big IPs. At Iberseries, for example, Luis Fernandez, Telemundo president, drilled down at a keynote on its ways forward. One is live events. Another reaching out to YA auds. And another, a 2027 schedule which includes new seasons of “La Reina del Sur,” El Señor de los Cielos” and “Sin Senos No Hay Paraíso,” an awesome franchise trifecta.

Spanish-Language New Markets

Spanish-language series are successful because they have a captive audience of 600 million native Spanish speakers. Their growth, however, lies elsewhere, Parrot Analytics’ Jaime Otero suggested at Iberseries opening panel. The global demand for series from Spain, Portugal and Latin America series has increased 25% since late August 2024., driven by countries outside the region such as South Korea, up 245%, Japan and China, up 119% in two years, or in Scandinavia where it has doubled. Meanwhile demand in Latin America has edged up or down, according to the territory. Little wonder then that Spanish export and trade board ICEX held an event to boost Spanish talent in Shanghai this July.

And a Bake’s Dozen of Deals Announced by Variety at This Year’s Iberseries & Platino Industria:

*Movistar Plus International unveiled 33 new sales deals, led by Mubí taking the world on “La Mesias,” and to “Riot Police,” from “The Beloved” director Rodrigo Sorogoyen. International distribution deals were also led by ‘The Anatomy of a Moment,” “Querer,” “The New Years” and ‘The Nameless.’

*HBO Max announced that “La Bola Negra” writer-director-producers Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi are set to exec produce an ambitious new HBO Max drama series created by Fran Araújo and Eduard Sola.

*Beta Film has unveiled broad international sales for “Rex – Vienna Calling,” the latest incarnation of the hugely popular three-decade-old “Rex – A Cop’s Best Friend” franchise, as production gets underway on a second season.

*Globoplay has greenlit an adaptation of Raphael Montes’ “Uma Mulher no Escuro,” from Banijay Entertainment’s A Fábrica Brazilian banner. The order was announced at an Iberseries Banijay Spotlight panel.

*‘Elite’ star Ester Expósito is circling ‘Stink Eye,’ an Iberseries Co-Production & Financing Forum Title.

* “The Good Girls” lead Ilse Salas is set to to star in Quijote Films’ “To Die on Your Feet” (“Morir de Pie”) another project pitched at Iberseries & Platino Industria Forum.

*”Sin Filtro’ producer JK Media is producing its first original microdramas shot in the U.S. for TelevisaUnivision’s ViXMicrO.

*Belgian royalty series “King of Hearts” has secured key VRT backing. The coming-of-age drama series is from Giles Coulier, whose company, De Wereldvrede, is behind such hits as 2019 series “War of the Worlds” and Prix Europa winner, “Albatros.”

*‘Plaza Catedral’ director Abner Benaim, Chile’s Daniela Vega and Alfredo Castro have boarded fiction series “School of the Americas.”

*France’s Halley Production has boarded thriller ‘Carro Seco,’ about a killer who targets unscrupulous Barcelona real estate speculators. Javier Polo directs the buzz project at Iberseries & Platino Industria’s Co-Production and Financing Forum.

*Chile’s Sanfic is set to screen late documentarian Antonio Caro’s swan song “Monguen” among nine Chilean pics in Competition.

*”Strawberry and Chocolate” star Jorge Perugorría and Brazil’s Thiago Lacerda lead Havana-Set “Hotel Nacional,” another Iberseries Forum project.

title: ‘The Batman 2’ Pauses Production as Director Matt Reeves Steps Away for a ‘Family Matter’
summary: Warner Bros. and DC Studios have halted production on “The Batman Part II,” as director Matt Reeves takes a pause to deal with personal matters. “Production on ‘The Batman Part II’ has been temporarily paused while Matt Reeves focuses on a family matter,” a rep said in a statement. “Matt has the full support of […]
content:
Warner Bros. and DC Studios have halted production on “The Batman Part II,” as director Matt Reeves takes a pause to deal with personal matters.

“Production on ‘The Batman Part II’ has been temporarily paused while Matt Reeves focuses on a family matter,” a rep said in a statement. “Matt has the full support of DC Studios and we look forward to continuing the journey soon.”

Robert Pattinson returns as the Caped Crusader in the highly anticipated superhero sequel, which has already experienced several delays. “The Batman Part II” was originally set to open on Oct. 2, 2026, before Warner Bros. delayed it to Oct. 1, 2027. Then, in July, the studio pushed the film to February 2028. Reeves’ first “Batman” was released in March 2022.

Along with Pattinson, other cast members include Scarlett Johansson, Colin Farrell, Sebastian Stan, Andy Serkis and Jeffrey Wright.

Popular on Variety

After the first delay, DC Studios boss James Gunn took to Threads to justify the push, writing that it’s “fairly common” for major blockbusters to have yearslong gaps between sequels.

“To be fair, a 5-year gap or more is fairly common in sequels,” Gunn wrote on Threads at the time. “7 years between ‘Alien’ and ‘Aliens.’ 14 years between ‘Incredibles.’ 7 years between the first two ‘Terminators.’ 13 years between ‘Avatars.’ 36 years between ‘Top Guns.’ And, of course, six years between ‘Guardians Vol 2’ and ‘Vol 3.’”

In a recent interview with Collider, Pattinson said “The Batman Part II” is a completely “different take” from the first film.

“It’s so ambitious. I mean, I sort of said the other day on something that the first one was a different take on a Batman movie, and this one is another,” he told Collider in a recent interview. “It’s a real left turn from the first one, but somehow it keeps elements of the kind of feel of it. But it just feels really ambitious, and I’m excited to see how it turns out.”

title: ‘Imperfect Women’ Renewed For Season 2 By Apple Centered On Kerry Washington’s Character Eleanor
summary: Call it Imperfect Woman. The trend of streaming limited series becoming ongoing ones continues with Apple TV ordering a second season of thriller Imperfect Women. Taking a spinoff approach, it will follow one of the limited series’ three titular characters, Eleanor, played by Kerry Washington. Imperfect Women, based on Araminta Hall’s novel, revolved around best […]
content:
Call it Imperfect Woman. The trend of streaming limited series becoming ongoing ones continues with Apple TV ordering a second season of thriller Imperfect Women. Taking a spinoff approach, it will follow one of the limited series’ three titular characters, Eleanor, played by Kerry Washington.

Imperfect Women, based on Araminta Hall’s novel, revolved around best friends Eleanor and Mary (Elisabeth Moss) as they tried to solve the murder of the third member of their friends group, Nancy (Kate Mara), seen in flashbacks.

Washington and Moss executive produced the original installment in addition to starring and will also both executive produce Season 2.

There is no second Imperfect Women book so there is no source material for Season 2. Instead, it is based on an original story from series creator Annie Weisman and Justin Hillian. The two will serve as co-showrunners on the second season, which will change locations from Los Angeles, where Season 1 was set.

Watch on Deadline

In Season 2, Eleanor (Washington) returns to her hometown roots in the affluent black enclave of Martha’s Vineyard, only to find that beneath it’s idyllic surface, lie secrets and scandals that threaten to upend everything she thought she knew about her past.”

For now, there are no plans for Moss’ Mary and Nancy’s widower Robert (Joel Kinnaman) to be in the second installment which picks up on the Eleanor’s flash-forward scene in the finale, which resonated with fans. It showed her moving away from the toxic dynamic of her relationships and enjoying a new life on a yacht with a new love interest.

While cast deals are still being worked out, expected to return as part of the new Eleanor-centered installment are Leslie Odom Jr., who plays her brother, and Sheryl Lee Ralph, who plays their mother.

Justin Hillian, Annie Weisman Courtesy of WME, Joe Pugliese

As for the lingering question over Mary and Robert’s ambiguous glance at the end of the finale as the two were seen celebrating the birthday of Mary’s daughter together, that may be answered in Season 2 with a reference of the characters’ status.

“We were thrilled to see how deeply these women and their stories resonated with audiences around the world, and I’m so excited to step back into Eleanor’s shoes,” Washington said. “She’s intelligent and strong, but she also finds herself navigating complicated and sometimes messy situations. We at Simpson Street along with our incredible partners at Apple and Love & Squalor Pictures can’t wait to explore a fresh chapter for her and share where this story takes us next.”

The long list of limited series that have been picked up for additional installments include Apple TV’s Reasonable Doubt, Netflix’s Untamed, Squid Game, The Beast In Me and Beef, HBO’s Big Little Lies, The White Lotus, True Detective and Task, HBO’s Good American Family and FX’s Shōgun.

Imperfect Women is a co-production between 20th Television and Apple Studios. The second season is created, co-showrun and executive produced by Weisman and Hillian, and executive produced by Washington for her Simpson Street banner alongside Pilar Savone. Moss and Lindsey McManus, who initially optioned the book, via their production company Love & Squalor Pictures are executive producers alongside author Hall.

“After a wildly entertaining first season, driven by the performances of Kerry, Lizzie and Kate, we jumped at the opportunity to expand the world of Imperfect Women through Kerry’s fan favorite character of Eleanor,” said Matt Cherniss, Apple TV’s head of programming. “Annie and Justin’s thrilling new story felt like an exciting and natural next chapter. We can’t wait for fans to experience it.”

Hillian is repped by WME, 3 Arts and Priya Verma at Yorn Levine.

title: ‘Tulsa King’ Renewed For Season 5 With Move To NY; Scarlet Rose Stallone Promoted & Erik Palladino Among New Cast
summary: Paramount+ has renewed the Sylvester Stallone-led Tulsa King for a fifth season ahead of the show’s fourth season premiere on October 16. Production just kicked off in New York, a new location replacing Atlanta due to the storyline that will explore Dwight “The General” Manfredi’s (Stallone) mafia roots. Similar to his deal for seasons 3 […]
content:
Paramount+ has renewed the Sylvester Stallone-led Tulsa King for a fifth season ahead of the show’s fourth season premiere on October 16. Production just kicked off in New York, a new location replacing Atlanta due to the storyline that will explore Dwight “The General” Manfredi’s (Stallone) mafia roots.

Similar to his deal for seasons 3 and 4, Stallone recently signed a new deal that helped clinch the show’s Season 5 renewal.

Scarlet Rose Stallone will return as Spencer for Season 5 with a promotion to series regular. There will also be 5 new series regulars joining the fold: Erik Palladino (I Play Rocky), Glenn Fleshler (Billions), Anthony Skordi (The Last Frontier), and Nickola Shreli (Power Book IV: Force). New character descriptions are under wraps.

“We are thrilled to bring fans even more of this incredible series, and to be shooting the next season of Tulsa King in New York, where Dwight Manfredi’s story will continue to evolve. We’re proud of the work we’ve done in Georgia, and it remains an important venue for us,” shared Drew Brown, EVP, Physical Production, Paramount Television Studios.

Watch on Deadline

And New York is also welcoming the cast and crew to their new home.

“We’re excited to welcome the cast and crew of Tulsa King to New York State for its fifth season. Under Governor Hochul’s leadership, New York has built an unmatched home for film and television—world-class talent, iconic locations, and a Film Tax Credit Program that delivers real jobs and investment for New Yorkers. Tulsa King represents the latest in a growing list of projects proudly filmed in New York,” said Empire State Development President, CEO and Commissioner Hope Knight.

While Season 5 is in production, Season 4 will keep fans satiated as they follow Dwight as he fights to legitimize his empire and protect his crew as corrupt politicians, dangerous new enemies, and a crushing personal loss hit from every direction. However, every hard-won gain comes with even harder truths: about loyalty, leadership, and the cost of ambition. Each move drags Dwight deeper into the street instincts he left behind in New York – turning Tulsa into a battleground and Dwight into the one threat no one can afford to underestimate.

In addition to Stallone, Season 4 stars Martin Starr, Jay Will, Vincent Piazza, Annabella Sciorra, Chris Caldovino, McKenna Quigley Harrington, Frank Grillo, Mike “Cash Flo” Walden, James Russo, Kevin Pollak, Neal McDonough, with Garrett Hedlund and Dana Delany. Gretchen Mol also joins the cast as a series regular.

Terence Winter is head writer and executive producer. Tulsa King is also executive produced by Taylor Sheridan, Sylvester Stallone, David C. Glasser, Ron Burkle, David Hutkin, Bob Yari, Thomas Kelly, and Keith Cox. The series is produced by Paramount Television Studios and 101 Studios.

title: ‘Grey Gardens’ Helmer Michael Sucsy Sets Audible Adaptation ‘A Murder To Remember’ With Amazon MGM Studios
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Amazon MGM Studios is developing A Murder to Remember, a feature adaptation of Brynn Kelly’s Audible Original from Grey Gardens helmer Michael Sucsy. A Murder is described as a razor-sharp romantic thriller that follows a Jane Austen-obsessed American art expert and a broke but charming British lord who awaken after a blackout-drunk night at […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Amazon MGM Studios is developing A Murder to Remember, a feature adaptation of Brynn Kelly‘s Audible Original from Grey Gardens helmer Michael Sucsy.

A Murder is described as a razor-sharp romantic thriller that follows a Jane Austen-obsessed American art expert and a broke but charming British lord who awaken after a blackout-drunk night at a crumbling English abbey convinced they witnessed a murder. With no evidence of a crime and no one willing to believe them, the unlikely pair must uncover the truth before the killer silences them for good.

Kelly’s audiobook, described to Deadline as Knives Out meets Jane Austen, released in February 2024. Sucsy developed the project with Jackie Levine at Audible and Moritz Polter at Windlight Pictures before the package was set up at Amazon MGM. He’s directing from his own script and exec producing via his HungryDuck Productions, alongside Audible’s Rachel Ghiazza and Kelly. Audible’s Levine and Marshall Lewy are producing alongside Windlight Pictures’ Polter and Cosima Degler.

Watch on Deadline

Sucsy is best known for originating, co-writing, producing and directing Grey Gardens, an HBO drama starring Drew Barrymore and Jessica Lange that received 17 Emmy nominations and won six, including Outstanding Made for Television Movie. The TV movie also picked up a Golden Globe, with Lange winning an Emmy, and Barrymore winning both a Globe and a SAG Award for her performance.

Following Grey Gardens, Sucsy went on to direct Sony’s romantic drama The Vow, starring Rachel McAdams and Channing Tatum, which grossed $196 million worldwide against a $30 million budget, followed by MGM’s Every Day, based on David Levithan’s bestselling novel. He also directed on Netflix’s 13 Reasons Why and is repped by Paradigm, Anonymous Content, and Goodman, Genow, Schenkman.

title: Chris Wayland To Succeed Valari Staab As President Of NBCUniversal Local
summary: Chris Wayland will succeed Valari Staab as president of NBCUniversal Local, overseeing NBC and Telemundo local stations and other outlets. Staab disclosed her plans to retire earlier this year, and will work with Wayland in the coming weeks, with the transition before the end of the year, according to Cesar Conde, chairman of NBCU News […]
content:
Chris Wayland will succeed Valari Staab as president of NBCUniversal Local, overseeing NBC and Telemundo local stations and other outlets.

Staab disclosed her plans to retire earlier this year, and will work with Wayland in the coming weeks, with the transition before the end of the year, according to Cesar Conde, chairman of NBCU News Group.

In addition to 11 NBC stations and 31 Telemundo stations, NBCU Local also includes four regional sports networks, three national multicast networks and 17 streaming channels, along with LXTV Productions and Skycastle.

Wayland joined NBCU in 2019, and has led NBC10 Boston, Telemundo Boston and NBC Sports Boston. Conde wrote in a memo to staffers that Wayland “has been instrumental in the growth of NBC10 and was a key leader in the development and launch of the NBCUniversal Boston Media Center.”

Watch on Deadline

“Chris understands the power and importance of local media, and I know he will be an outstanding leader for NBCUniversal Local,” Conde wrote.

Staab has been with NBCU for more than 15 years and has spent 46 years in local TV and journalism.

“Under her leadership, what began as 10 NBC-owned stations grew into NBCUniversal Local’s nationwide, multiplatform portfolio of 50 media properties,” Conde wrote.

“Her impact can be seen not only in the organization she helped build, but in the generations of broadcasters and leaders she has supported and developed along the way,” he wrote.

In a statement, Staab said, “What gives me the greatest confidence is knowing that Chris leads with both vision and heart. He values our people, our culture, and the relationships that have been foundational to our success.”

Wayland previously was an executive at Tribune Media, Sinbeam Television and WHDH-TV.

title: Everything We Know About Prime Video’s ‘Things We Never Got Over’ Adaptation So Far
summary: Lucy Score’s Knockemout trilogy is on its way to becoming a TV series with the first book, Things We Never Got Over serving as the basis for the first season of Prime Video’s adaptation. The main cast has been assembled for the latest in the streamer’s ever-growing list of romance book adaptations and coming of […]
content:
Lucy Score’s Knockemout trilogy is on its way to becoming a TV series with the first book, Things We Never Got Over serving as the basis for the first season of Prime Video’s adaptation.

The main cast has been assembled for the latest in the streamer’s ever-growing list of romance book adaptations and coming of age stories. The creative team behind the show has shifted a bit since the adaptation was initially announced.

Read on to learn everything we know about the Things We Never Got Over TV show in the works at Prime Video:

When will Things We Never Got Over come out on Prime Video?

Watch on Deadline

The series hasn’t received a release date yet because it is still in early stages of production.

Is the Things We Never Got Over TV show in production?

Yes, the show is currently shooting in Vancouver, Canada.

Who is in the cast of Prime Video’s Things We Never Got Over TV show adaptation?

The Residence alum Molly Griggs will portray Witt twins Naomi and Tina, who center the first book in Lucy Score’s trilogy. Matthew Noszka (All’s Fair) and Tommy Martinez (Good Trouble, Laid) will portray brothers Knox and Nash Morgan.

Who else is behind Things We Never Got Over at Prime Video?

The Gift and Ringer’s Eric Charmelo and Nicole Snyder are adapting the series, serving as developers, showrunners and executive producers alongside Gina Girolamo for Strega Stories. Girolamo has an overall deal with Amazon MGM Studios. Author Score will also serve as co-executive producer.

Amy Rardin, who serves as an executive producer on Prime Video’s Every Year After, was first attached to showrun, executive produce and adapt the book.

What is Things We Never Got Over about?

Naomi Witt is on the run, not just from her fiancé and a church full of well-wishers, but from her entire life. She finds herself in rural Virginia coming to the aid of her hot mess of a twin, she falls for the small town and a sexy local, who helps her rediscover herself.

Knox Morgan is as gruff as they get when he first meets Naomi, mistaking her for her twin sister Tina, who has already wreaked havoc on Knockemout, Virginia. His brother is the Chief of Police, Nash Morgan. What starts out as an innocent move to help her twin sister Tina out becomes an entirely new situation in which Naomi is landed with a niece she didn’t know she had.

title: Trump Says He’ll Pay for ‘Patriotic Ads’ Himself Following Controversy Around Taxpayer-Funded TV Spots
summary: After controversy erupted over Donald Trump’s administration buying TV ad time (with taxpayer dollars) to air advertisements endorsing the president, Trump has now said he will fund what he calls “patriotic ads” himself. In a statement posted to Truth Social on Monday, Trump wrote: “The Radical Left is upset with the fact that I am […]
content:
After controversy erupted over Donald Trump‘s administration buying TV ad time (with taxpayer dollars) to air advertisements endorsing the president, Trump has now said he will fund what he calls “patriotic ads” himself.

In a statement posted to Truth Social on Monday, Trump wrote: “The Radical Left is upset with the fact that I am taking Ads, which I consider to be a positive promotion for our Great U.S.A., and paying for them with U.S.A. money. This is a rather standard thing to do but, rather than doing that, although nothing will make them happy, I have decided to do the Patriotic Ads, among others, and pay for them myself, and with money I raised for MAGA, Inc. MAKE AMERICA GREAT AGAIN! President DONALD J. TRUMP”

Variety previously reported Thursday that the administration had begun running the advertisements, which say that the president is fighting “communism, socialism and Marxism” as well as “the fake news media” among other claims, on Fox News, Newsmax, CBS, Fox, NBC, MS NOW, CNN and ABC.

Popular on Variety

In a statement to Variety, a White House spokesperson said, “These public service announcements are about reminding Americans to love their country and understand what makes it worth defending, at home, at our borders, and abroad. The ad is educational and unapologetically patriotic. We should be proud of our country.”

Last month, it was reported that the White House had spent more than $440,000 of U.S. taxpayer dollars on pro-Trump TV ads, which the White House again defended, noting that the “announcements are very clearly not campaign ads; President Trump is not on the ballot and there is no call to action,” they said, framing the advertisements as an act of patriotism. “Instead, the announcements are a reminder for Americans to love their country and know why it’s worth defending — at home, at the border, and abroad. That’s not partisanship — that’s a government that still believes in the country it serves.”

title: Neon Sets ‘Artificial’ Oscar Campaign With Andrew Garfield in Supporting Actor, Yura Borisov in Lead (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Sixteen years ago, Andrew Garfield played the Facebook co-founder who was pushed out of the company he helped create in “The Social Network” and came up short in the supporting actor race. Now, he’s playing the CEO pushed out of OpenAI — and who talked his way back in five days later. Different man, different […]
content:
Sixteen years ago, Andrew Garfield played the Facebook co-founder who was pushed out of the company he helped create in “The Social Network” and came up short in the supporting actor race. Now, he’s playing the CEO pushed out of OpenAI — and who talked his way back in five days later. Different man, different company. Same category, hoping for a different outcome.

As “Artificial” world premieres at the New York Film Festival, Variety has learned exclusively that the film’s awards campaign will include Garfield competing in the supporting actor category for Luca Guadagnino’s OpenAI drama, while Yura Borisov, who plays OpenAI co-founder and former chief scientist Ilya Sutskever, will campaign in lead actor. Oscar winner Mark Rylance, as AI pioneer Geoffrey Hinton, will join Garfield in the supporting race, while Monica Barbaro, as former OpenAI chief technology officer Mira Murati, will vie for supporting actress.

The campaign will extend across all the major categories, including best picture, director and acting, while Simon Rich’s screenplay will compete in original screenplay and every craft department will receive a full campaign.

Popular on Variety

For Guadagnino, “Artificial” marks his fifth appearance at NYFF, following “Call Me by Your Name,” “Bones and All,” “Queer” and “After the Hunt,” which opened the festival last year. After Lincoln Center audiences get the first official look at the film, it heads to the BFI London Film Festival.

Andrew Garfield in “Artificial” Neon

Garfield is a two-time best actor nominee for the war drama “Hacksaw Ridge” (2016) and the musical biopic “Tick, Tick … Boom!” (2021). While he has been the face of the marketing and plays the most famous name in the story, it’s not unprecedented for a film’s top-billed star to pursue a supporting nomination — as Meryl Streep did for “Into the Woods” and Oscar winner Catherine Zeta-Jones did for “Chicago.”

The film traces decades in the lives of Ilya and Sam Altman (Garfield), two men from completely different worlds who bond over a shared desire to change the world for the better amid the sunny glow of Obama-era tech optimism. They eventually find themselves at odds as the enormous — and increasingly dangerous — capabilities of their technology reveal themselves across the Trump and Biden years, before Altman is ousted. In other words, the audience rides with the man who pulled the trigger, not the one who took the bullet.

The best actor field is already crowded, with several contenders emerging from NYFF, including Pedro Pascal’s cellist in “Behemoth!”

Borisov is two years removed from his first Oscar nomination, for his breakthrough performance as the reluctant henchman Igor in Sean Baker’s best picture winner “Anora.”

The ensemble has Oscar pedigree throughout. Rylance won supporting actor for his turn in Steven Spielberg’s “Bridge of Spies,” while Barbaro is two years removed from her first nom for playing Joan Baez in the Bob Dylan biopic “A Complete Unknown.” The rest of the cast includes Cooper Hoffman as Greg Brockman, Ike Barinholtz as Elon Musk, Jason Schwartzman, Chris O’Dowd, Billie Lourd and Zosia Mamet.

Behind the camera, Guadagnino has assembled many of his regular collaborators. Marco Costa, an ACE Eddie Award nominee for “Challengers,” returns for his duties while Jessica Ronane, a two-time Artios nominee who has cast Guadagnino’s films since “Queer,” handled casting. Production designer Stefano Baisi, whose credits include “Queer” and “After the Hunt,” builds the world alongside ADG nominee Roberta Federico. J.W. Anderson, the Costume Designers Guild nominee who dressed “Challengers” and “Queer,” returns as well.

One of the new faces behind the lens is cinematographer Malik Hassan Sayeed, a Camerimage winner whose credits include Spike Lee’s “Clockers,” Hype Williams’ “Belly” and Beyoncé’s “Lemonade.” Damon Albarn, the Blur frontman and Grammy winner with Gorillaz, composed the original score and wrote the original songs heard in the film. Submission details for which original songs will vie for attention are forthcoming.

Guadagnino is hoping to make his triumphant return to an Oscar ceremony. “Call Me by Your Name” earned four nominations at the 90th Oscars and won adapted screenplay for James Ivory. Among the producers are Jeffrey Clifford, Jennifer Fox, Guadagnino, David Heyman and Rich. Fox is an Oscar nominee for best picture for “Michael Clayton,” while Guadagnino was nominated for “Call Me by Your Name.” Heyman is a four-time best picture nominee for “Gravity,” “Marriage Story,” “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood” and “Barbie.”

Now, Guadagnino, Garfield and company will see if “Artificial” can prompt their Oscar comebacks.

title: Blippi’s Meekah and Dove Release Music Video to Promote Children’s Body Confidence (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Meekah, best friend of children’s entertainment and education character Blippi, has teamed up with Dove on a new music video promoting body confidence. Moonbug Entertainment and the Dove Self-Esteem Project (DSEP) have partnered with Meekah for “My Body Is Amazing,” a music video celebrating movement, self-expression and the amazing things our bodies can do. Designed […]
content:
Meekah, best friend of children’s entertainment and education character Blippi, has teamed up with Dove on a new music video promoting body confidence.

Moonbug Entertainment and the Dove Self-Esteem Project (DSEP) have partnered with Meekah for “My Body Is Amazing,” a music video celebrating movement, self-expression and the amazing things our bodies can do. Designed to protect body confidence from an early age, the music video encourages children to focus on everything their bodies help them experience, explore and enjoy, rather than how they look.

Premiering ahead of International Day of the Girl, the video builds on Moonbug and Dove’s partnership in 2024, when the two brands joined forces on a collection of Blippi episodes and music videos focused on body confidence and self-esteem, including the Blippi “Wonderful Talent Show” special. This time, the partnership brings Meekah’s signature energy, creativity and love of movement to a song all about celebrating the incredible ways our bodies help us experience and explore the world.

Popular on Variety

“Meekah is all about encouraging kids to jump in, try something new and find their own way to experience the world,” said Liz Katz, associate general manager of Blippi who leads the Meekah franchise at Moonbug Entertainment. “Movement and self-expression are such a natural part of who she is, and this partnership with Dove gives us a wonderful opportunity to celebrate that.
