Hasbro is debuting its third Peppa Pig Play Cafe location in October this month, Variety has learned exclusively, adding one more fixed attraction to the company’s growing list of in-person experiences around the globe.

Opening in October in Suzhou, China, the third Peppa Pig Play Café in the region “brings the beloved preschool brand to life through immersive themed dining, interactive play experiences and character encounters,” per Hasbro. “Designed for young fans and their families, the destination features attractions, themed food offerings and opportunities to step into Peppa’s world through play and live experiences.”

“There’s always tweaks to make to everything, but as a whole, Peppa Pig Play Cafe has just been a great success for us,” Matt Proulx, Hasbro’s senior vice president of global experiences, partnerships and music, tells Variety. “What’s really important for us is that now we get into this rinse and repeat mode and you start to see after the first location, going into the second location, OK, what are your truths and what are the things that you need to be able to to rejigger? And I think what has been really interesting about this experience is that it provides that great play for that toddler, where kids can just run around, but then also that thematic type of eating situation where people are coming in, booking their tables, having good food.”

Popular on Variety

Proulx adds: “I think some of that’s the stuff that we’ve had to work on a little bit over the first couple locations. Just dialing in the menu to make sure that we’re providing really good food because otherwise, if you’re not the value proposition of what you’re offering just doesn’t hold any water. But from a play perspective, we’ve been really, really excited about how it’s actually come across.”

See below for some first-look images for the new Peppa Pig Play Cafe location:

Hasbro has been building up its in-person experiences and immersive attractions business with new and upcoming projects including Clue: Murder on the Menu, opening this week in Charlotte, North Carolina; Nerf Coaster at Galaxyland Powered by Hasbro in Alberta, Canada; Monopoly Experience: Treasures of Brazil in Sao Paulo, Brazil; the Play-Doh Imagination Center in Abha, Saudi Arabia; and Transformers: Battle of Cybertron in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

Today, Variety can exclusively confirm the title of one more upcoming attraction: Transformers Mission Energon Gramado.

Announced earlier this year, the attraction is set to open in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil before the end of 2026. The experience, which marks the country’s first fixed, immersive attraction, is made in collaboration between Hasbro and Dream Cars Automóveis e Eventos.

Amid the growing globalization of branded entertainment experiences, Proulx’s team has become increasingly focused on permanent installations, which of course take more time and money to build — and come with more risk.

“It’s really looking at the market where you’re going,” Proulx says. “Can the market sustain your experience? What’s the competition? Because fundamentally, we are all in the same battle for disposable income. Whether it’s my branded attraction or some mom-and-pop mini golf experience or go-kart, whatever it is, it is all disposable income. So what you have to make sure is, is the product you’re offering viable within that specific market?”

Proulx says the Gramado, where Hasbro’s Transformers Mission Energon will be based in Brazil, is “actually a very heavily touristed area and so they see a lot of turnover.”

“It has its own unique culture, and so that becomes a destination for people in Brazil,” Proulx says. “So we also took a lot of learnings from our local partner in terms of what their knowledge is. If you have the right operator in the right market, they’re going to help lead you and guide you into making the right decision. Because the one thing that I think gets missed sometimes as brands have now started to go into the location-based world is people are too brand forward and not enough experience forward. Our belief is that if you create a great experience with a great IP — and those things can be in unison, or one can trail the other a little bit — you’re going to actually be very successful. But if you’re so brand forward, and you’re not thinking about what that experience is in the background, you’re going to fail more times than you’re going to be successful.”

title: AI Film ‘Gods Don’t Give Gifts’ Sets First Trailer for December Theatrical Run, Plans Oscar Bid for Best Animated Feature
summary: It’ll take a bit longer for the first AI-generated film to make it to theaters — because it’s gunning for an Oscar. The AI studio Fable has shifted the U.S. release of “Gods Don’t Give Gifts,” the collection of four anthology shorts by the AI-focused YouTuber Gossip Goblin (né Zack London), from Oct. 30 to Dec. […]
content:
It’ll take a bit longer for the first AI-generated film to make it to theaters — because it’s gunning for an Oscar.

The AI studio Fable has shifted the U.S. release of “Gods Don’t Give Gifts,” the collection of four anthology shorts by the AI-focused YouTuber Gossip Goblin (né Zack London), from Oct. 30 to Dec. 4. While Fable has not yet disclosed a distributor for the film, the film’s trailer will make its debut in theaters on Friday, and its poster will spread across U.S. multiplexes.

Fable and London revealed their ambitious plans for a theatrical rollout in July, hoping to follow the path laid by YouTubers-turned-filmmakers Kane Parsons and Mark Fischbach, or Markiplier, who leveraged their respective YouTube followings to box office successes in “Backrooms” ($401 million) and “Iron Lung” ($51.2 million). Its story — which lies within the “second cycle of humanity” within the Gossip Goblin universe’s “13 cycles” and aims to satirize society’s relationship with AI — traces the fallout of humanity besting earthly limitations like death and memory through technology and how it grapples with humanity as a result.

Popular on Variety

But the roughly monthlong delay comes with an ulterior motive: a bid to get the project closer to the traditional Oscar campaign season. Fable plans to submit the film for consideration in the best animated feature category for the upcoming Oscars, testing both the Academy’s hesitation toward publicly AI-powered films and whether AI-generated projects can stand among films generally regarded as the year’s best in cinema.

The campaign will also include advanced screenings for Academy voters, pre-release screenings for critics and a billboard advertising campaign across Los Angeles next month, all to celebrate what Fable CEO Edward Saatchi claims is “a seminal, historic moment in animation.”

“For 5 years, the question has been when will an AI film win an Oscar? Gods Don’t Give Gifts is the first that has a shot at a nomination and then it’s all to play for,” Saatchi said in a statement. “We feel it could be this generation’s Toy Story – the fact that this generation’s Toy Story is a dark, satirical, bold statement on all 2026’s fears about AI and our species’ future is an appropriate commentary on the questions we are all confronting as a society.”

London describes the anthology in a statement as “part speculation, part critique” and hopes audiences can “take a premise seriously, follow its emotional consequences, and let the results be strange, funny, grotesque, and sad.”

“I made these films with AI, which some people find ironic,” he said. “But using a medium to interrogate that medium is one of the oldest moves in art; I may just be early to do it with AI. But what AI actually gave me is the ability to transmit stories onto a screen, with minimal filters, intervention, committees or constraints. Its enabled myself and a small talented team to envision an extravagant world, down to its smallest prop, and bring it to life with extraordinary fidelity – from jaw-dropping visuals of leviathans and space ships and talking apes, down to the scuffed up sneakers on a background extra.”

“Gods Don’t Give Gifts” will represent the biggest test of whether the Academy is willing to accept wholesale AI-generated films since its May ban on AI actors or AI-assisted scripts. But generally, according to its published eligibility rules, AI tools “neither help nor harm the chances of achieving a nomination” and the relevant Academy branches will “judge the achievement, taking into account the degree to which a human was at the heart of the creative authorship when choosing which movie to award.”

“If questions arise regarding the aforementioned use of Generative Artificial Intelligence, the Academy reserves the right to request more information about the nature of the use and human authorship,” the rules state.

The film’s violence, and “R” rating from the Motion Picture Association, may also serve as a barrier. The first R-rated film nominated for best animated feature was Charlie Kaufman’s 2015 stop-motion picture “Anomalisa.”

title: AI Studio Authors First, Backed by $10 Million, Pledges to Help Writers Faithfully Adapt Their Books
summary: A new startup pledges to give authors an easier way to bring their books to life for the screen. It, naturally, involves AI. Authors First, founded by private equity veteran Robert Hamwee, promises to let science-fiction and fantasy scribes adapt their titles as closely to their intended vision as possible. The company uses a combination […]
content:
A new startup pledges to give authors an easier way to bring their books to life for the screen. It, naturally, involves AI.

Authors First, founded by private equity veteran Robert Hamwee, promises to let science-fiction and fantasy scribes adapt their titles as closely to their intended vision as possible. The company uses a combination of AI generators like Seedance 2.5 and Nano Banana and “other technology,” including visual effects platforms such as Blender, to help craft the adaptations without the budget considerations traditionally associated with such work that could impede them at Hollywood studios.

The company launches after a more than $10 million seed funding round that includes Hamwee himself, the venture capital firm Brand Foundry and investors including The Family Office of David Blitzer, Andy Mills, Mike Duggal and John Kline. Hamwee leads the company as CEO, and his leadership team includes veterans of Hulu, Warner Bros. and Universal.

Popular on Variety

“As a lifelong fan of historical fiction, science fiction, and fantasy epics, I’ve always believed the definitive version of any story is in the author’s imagination,” Hamwee said in a statement. “We built Authors First to give them full creative control and modern tools so production budgets no longer dictate what’s possible on screen. For readers and fans, there’s nothing better than seeing a beloved world brought to life exactly as the author intended – without compromise.”

The studio‘s first project is “Genghis: Birth of an Empire,” an adaptation of British author Conn Iggulden’s 2007 book focused on Genghis Khan, “Wolf of the Plains.” The production team included a mixture of roughly 25 humans that the company says worked on the story, camera angles and character dialogue — though the project itself was mostly generated by AI.

According to Iggulden, the movie would never have been adapted without the use of AI, as the offers he received to adapt the book fizzled due to the budget needed for a historical epic.

“It would have taken significant capital and years of filming on location across thousands of miles of remote Mongolian landscape,” he said in a statement. “Readers finally get to experience history’s greatest rags-to-riches story exactly as I’d always envisioned it: uncompromised, epic, and true to the written word.”

The studio’s debut comes amid a boom in companies eager to capitalize on the AI boom with book adaptations. Utopai Studios is adapting “Not Another Teen Movie” screenwriter Mike Bender’s children’s book “The Most Serious Fart” and the Chinese literary classic “Journey to the West” with the help of AI, while the AI animation studio Intelligent Animation is adapting “The Dragon Prince’s Bride” for the microseries platform aTwist.

title: Lucy Hale To Headline ‘Scarlett Holmes’ Limited Series At Roku
summary: Roku has given a green light to Scarlett Holmes, a new Roku Original limited series, with Lucy Hale set to star and executive produce. Said to “put a fresh, romantic spin on the legendary world of Sherlock Holmes,” Scarlett Holmes, produced by Jaggi Entertainment, will debut exclusively on The Roku Channel in 2027. Written by […]
content:
Roku has given a green light to Scarlett Holmes, a new Roku Original limited series, with Lucy Hale set to star and executive produce. Said to “put a fresh, romantic spin on the legendary world of Sherlock Holmes,” Scarlett Holmes, produced by Jaggi Entertainment, will debut exclusively on The Roku Channel in 2027.

Written by Paris Herbert-Taylor and Katie Wilbert, Scarlett Holmes revolves around the titular character played by Hale, a modern descendant of Sherlock Holmes who has inherited his legendary powers of observation, but instead of solving crimes, she takes on mysteries of love, dating, and relationships.

Each episode’s storyline draws inspiration from a beloved romantic comedy. Joining Scarlett in each episode is her trusty sidekick, “Jane Watson,” (casting TBA) as they help clients navigate mixed signals, secret crushes, romantic dilemmas, and everything in between. But while Scarlett may be an expert at solving everyone else’s romantic problems, her own love life proves far more difficult to decipher. When she falls for “Ollie Moriarity” (casting TBA) — a charming podcast producer secretly planning an exposé on her methods —she’s faced with the toughest case of all: her own.

Watch on Deadline

“Lucy Hale has the wit, warmth and comedic instincts that make her the perfect creative partner to bring ‘Scarlett Holmes’ to life,” said Brian Tannenbaum, Head of Roku Originals. “This smart, sophisticated series celebrates two genres our streamers love—romance and mystery—through a fresh, playful take on one of the most recognizable legacies in storytelling.”

Scarlett Holmes is produced by Jaggi Entertainment with Sophie Tilson and Steve Jaggi serving as executive producers along with Hale. The series is overseen by Morgan Pichinson and Sabrina Lyall on behalf of Roku. Jaggi Entertainment handles international sales.

“I am a true diehard fan of romantic comedies, and Scarlett Holmes has that special something that made me fall in love with the genre in the first place,” said Hale. “And I love that it brings mystery into the rom-com world in a way that feels really fresh and fun. It’s charming, sexy, funny, and has a lot of heart. Scarlett is smart, curious, a little complicated, and like so many of us, looking for love. I feel completely thrilled to step into her shoes.”

Known for her work in Pretty Little Liars, Lionsgate’s F, Marry Kill, Hulu’s Which Brings Me To You and romantic comedy Puppy Love, Hale most recently wrapped production on thriller Legacy and romantic comedy Princess. She’s also executive producing the mystery drama Dead Letters, which is currently in development at Netflix, and will star in a dual role in the adaptation of the 2017 novel by Caite Dolan-Leach. She’s repped by CAA and Reel Talent Management.

“Scarlett Holmes is the kind of smart, feel-good storytelling audiences crave. Partnering with Roku on such a charming project has been an exciting journey, and we can’t wait for viewers to fall in love with Scarlett and her world,” said Steve Jaggi, CEO Jaggi Entertainment.

title: Amazon Strikes Six-Year Global Deal For Emmys Worth More Than $20M Per Year, Will Make Event Free To View
summary: The Emmys officially have a new rights holder. Amazon on Tuesday closed its deal with the Television Academy, as previewed last month, and it’s a significant pact. The partnership gives Prime Video the right to stream the annual TV awards ceremony for the next six years and is thought to be worth north of $120 […]
content:
The Emmys officially have a new rights holder.

Amazon on Tuesday closed its deal with the Television Academy, as previewed last month, and it’s a significant pact. The partnership gives Prime Video the right to stream the annual TV awards ceremony for the next six years and is thought to be worth north of $120 million in total.

The streamer has taken global rights to the event but will make it free to view on its Prime Video service each September.

Deadline understands that the deal is worth between $20M-$25M per year, with one source pegging the value at $24M per year.

Watch on Deadline

The deal succeeds the broadcast wheel, which has seen broadcast networks ABC, CBS, Fox and NBC rotate the rights to air the ceremony each year. That system has been in place for over 30 years, since 1995.

Mike Hopkins, head of Prime Video and Amazon MGM Studios, told Deadline that it wanted to create a “global event” on Prime Video.

“We thought we could increase the viewership, bring in a younger audience, work with the Academy to put a lot more energy, and maybe look at the production itself to try to innovate,” he said. “I feel that we can put the Emmys on a path to global growth and relevance that was probably harder to do when it was spinning from network to network and then distributed in various ways around the world.”

The global nature of the deal is interesting, particularly given the fee increase the TV Academy has secured. The broadcast networks have paid between $8M-$10M per year to air in the U.S., but it’s not clear how much revenue the Academy makes from international broadcasters. The event has aired live in a number of international markets including on CTV in Canada, Showcase in Australia, Canal+ in France, TNT across Latin America and Sky Italia, but in many territories it is aired and streamed on smaller services and networks.

Television Academy chair Cris Abrego added that he didn’t want to just renew the wheel deal. “I felt strongly from the outset that this was an opportunity to rethink the model,” he said. “Starting every year with a new partner, trying to find a production partner, a brand partner, trying to bring even the simpleness of learnings from the past event into the next year didn’t matter because of the different institutions… that was very challenging. As television and the industry is evolving, the telecast and much like the Academy needed to evolve, and so having a singular home was my goal from the outset.”

Former Banijay Americas boss Abrego said that making the show free to view, and not behind a paywall, was a “non-negotiable” for the Academy.

“I give Mike credit. From our early conversations, he understood that. It’s not simply just about distributing an award show, they really understood what the Emmys mean to the television community and what we could build around that and we’re really excited about it,” he added.

Amazon has put other events in front of the paywall including a number of Amazon Fire concerts and its Black Friday NFL game. Hopkins pointed to the fact that the company has a “very large ad business.”

“We have we have a variety of other economic levers we can pull to make it make financial sense for us. We also have nearly all of the streaming services as part of Prime Video in our subscription business, and many of this year’s winners are available to our Prime Video customers via driving to HBO Max or Apple TV. We see it as something that sits as part of our entertainment system with customers where we can celebrate these awards and nominees throughout the year. We can be the home of many of the best shows on television today, not just those that we make ourselves, but our partners are the ones that are always every year going to get the lion’s share of awards,” he said.

Amazon itself hasn’t performed particularly well at the Emmys over the last few years; this year, largely thanks to Spider-Noir, which also aired on MGM+, it scored 10 wins; last year, it won five awards at the Creative Arts Emmys and in 2024 it won four.

RELATED: ‘Widow’s Bay’ & ‘The Pitt’ Take Top Series Emmys As Matthew Rhys, Jean Smart & Others Make History: Full Winners List

Hopkins said, “We stand up and clap at the Emmys when our partners win.” This is helped by the fact that Amazon would like to become a one-stop shop for streaming subscribers, as evidenced by recent bundles.

One of the things that both Amazon and the TV Academy stressed was the need to appeal to younger viewers.

“We’ve been talking a lot about it. It’s a little premature to get into specifics, but I think it is about the format. I think it’s about the celebration of certain stories and artists that might appeal to younger audiences. I also think it’s finding ways to promote to those audiences so they’re aware that it’s on,” added Hopkins. “Ultimately, we know that that younger audiences are more inclined to stream than watch broadcast television.”

Amazon does have one star that clearly appeals to younger audiences: MrBeast. Conan O’Brien joked at this year’s Oscars that he was going to be replaced by Jimmy Donaldson, the host of Amazon’s Beast Games, but maybe MrBeast would be a better choice to host the Emmys.

“We hadn’t thought about yet, but if you know him, please give him a call,” laughed Hopkins.

Abrego said the Academy didn’t strike the deal to “just put on the exact same show.” “The amount of categories, the type of categories, the length of the show, the hope is that we have an awards show that’s as relevant and interesting and innovative as the shows that are winning the Emmys,” he said.

He wants to start having those conversations “in the next few days.” “We wouldn’t normally start having these conversations probably until May,” he said. “We could start those conversations tomorrow, and start to really think about that. That’s what’s exciting.”

title: Skydancing At Last: $110B Merger Of Paramount And Warner Bros. Discovery Officially Closes
summary: The long-gestating merger of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery officially closed Tuesday, yielding a new major player in media. Shares in the combined company, Skydance, will start trading later in the day on the New York Stock Exchange. Shares of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery have been discontinued on the Nasdaq. The closing brings to […]
content:
The long-gestating merger of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery officially closed Tuesday, yielding a new major player in media.

Shares in the combined company, Skydance, will start trading later in the day on the New York Stock Exchange. Shares of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery have been discontinued on the Nasdaq.

The closing brings to an end a year-long saga over who would control two century-old movie studios along with a pedigreed stable of TV studios, networks and streaming services including HBO and CNN. Now, attention will turn to the difficult economics faced by the new company, which starts off with some $80 billion in debt and an ambitious plan to convert a traditional media company into a full-on tech firm.

Larry Ellison, the billionaire co-founder of Oracle, is a key backer of Skydance. His son, David Ellison, an actor-turned-producer who has made a dramatic entrance to the Hollywood corporate scene at just 43 years old, is running the company as chairman and CEO.

Watch on Deadline

“Today is a historic day, not just for Skydance but for our entire industry,” David Ellison said in a statement. “From the start, our ambition was to bring these two storied studios together and create a stronger competitor, with the talent, resources, and reach to tell great stories in every genre, on every platform, for audiences everywhere. Now that ambition is a reality. We’re grateful to everyone who made this possible – the employees, creative talent, and production teams of both companies, who worked tirelessly to get us here and inspire audiences around the world every day, as well as the advisors and partners who guided this transaction to completion. Our focus now turns to the future: building a company that empowers creatives, entertains audiences and rewards shareholders. We couldn’t be more excited to get to work.”

Gerry Cardinale, a Skydance board member and key financier via his firm, RedBird Capital, called the merger close “a defining moment for the industry. By applying our owner-operator model to Paramount and WBD’s unmatched portfolio of iconic franchises, premium original programming, and live sports rights, we can protect that legacy while building for a media landscape that’s undergoing transformational change.”

The merger was set in motion about a year ago when Paramount, soon after combining with the previous incarnation of Skydance, made an unsolicited offer to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery. The overture was rebuffed initially, and it took more than a dozen tries for the board of WBD to finally warm up to the deal. Along the way, the board accepted a bid from Netflix to acquire just the streaming and studio side of the company. Ultimately, that proposal fell by the wayside when Paramount made its sweetened pitch to buy all of WBD.

The transaction sailed through regulatory approval, only to hit a major road block in July when the attorneys general of 12 states filed a lawsuit seeking to block the deal on antitrust grounds. The Writers Guild of America filed a similar suit. Thousands of actors, writers, producers and others in the creative community signed a petition opposing the deal. It will likely remain a talking point, especially for high-profile opponents like Mark Ruffalo, who stars in HBO series Task.

Initially, it seemed the legal and industry objections could have a chance to derail the combination, or at least result in a shrinking of its scale. In the end, though, the AGs agreed to settle with only so-called “behavioral remedies” being required in a 5-year consent decree. Skydance agreed to negotiate pay-TV deals for Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery as though they were still separate companies as well as supplying a minimum number of theatrical movie releases, among other concessions.

Ties between the Ellisons and President Donald Trump have long been scrutinized over the course of the year-long quest for WBD by Paramount, as well as Skydance’s $8.4 billion purchase of Paramount in 2025. While Skydance has steadfastly denied it has looked to appease Trump, critics have pointed to a series of moves by David Ellison and his senior leadership team. The company, which acquired rights to the UFC mixed-martial-arts circuit last year, broadcast a live match from the White House lawn over the summer. It also acquired the Free Press, a right-leaning digital news outlet, and installed its co-founder, Bari Weiss, as editor-in-chief of CBS News despite her lack of TV experience.

title: FilmNation Strikes Deal With High Road Over TV Slate
summary: EXCLUSIVE: FilmNation has partnered with nascent British indie High Road Entertainment. The two outfits will seek to co-produce projects and High Road will support them through financing and international market strategy, while also providing executive production expertise from development through production. The pair said Anora studio FilmNation’s “internationally focused approach to producing and financing ambitious […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: FilmNation has partnered with nascent British indie High Road Entertainment.

The two outfits will seek to co-produce projects and High Road will support them through financing and international market strategy, while also providing executive production expertise from development through production.

The pair said Anora studio FilmNation’s “internationally focused approach to producing and financing ambitious storytelling will be complemented by High Road’s experience in packaging, financing and bringing premium television projects to market.”

Recent FilmNation international TV projects include Prime Video’s adaptation of Isabel Allende’s The House of the Spirits and the upcoming adaptation of Graham Norton’s book Forever Home for Skydance UK network 5.

Watch on Deadline

High Road was launched earlier this year by former Buccaneer co-CEO Richard Tulk-Hart and former Cineflix Head of Scripted TV James Durie.

Further announcements regarding commissions already in place will follow, FilmNation and High Road said.

Kirstie Macdonald, FilmNation’s Head of Television, called High Road “an ideal partner for this slate.” “Their understanding of the international television landscape, combined with their financing, distribution and exec producing capabilities, makes them the perfect partner to build on the success achieved so far.,” she added. “We look forward to working together to bring these ambitious projects to life and to audiences globally.”

Tulk-Hart and Durie added: “FilmNation has built an exceptional reputation for identifying and supporting bold, distinctive stories and filmmakers,” said Richard and James of High Road Entertainment. “We’re thrilled to partner with the team and to help bring this slate to audiences around the world and build on the shows we have already got in production. Our focus is on supporting the great creative work Kirstie Macdonald and her team have built to date with the financing, production expertise and market strategy needed to realise these projects at the highest level.”

title: ESPN & HBO Vet Bomani Jones Teams With Playmaker For Long-Running Podcast ‘The Right Time’
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Bomani Jones, best known for his stints at ESPN and HBO, is teaming with podcast firm Playmaker for his long-running show The Right Time. The New York-based Playmaker, which is owned by Danish digital sports media company Better Collective, has built an estimable roster of podcasts with a eye toward the increasing cross-over to […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Bomani Jones, best known for his stints at ESPN and HBO, is teaming with podcast firm Playmaker for his long-running show The Right Time.

The New York-based Playmaker, which is owned by Danish digital sports media company Better Collective, has built an estimable roster of podcasts with a eye toward the increasing cross-over to video. The company’s roster includes The Roommates Show with New York Knicks teammates Jalen Brunson and Josh Hart, a bowling series hosted by L.A. Dodger Mookie Betts and various Shaquille O’Neal projects.

The Right Time launched in 2018 under ESPN’s auspices, and Jones acquired rights to it in 2021. He kept hosting it until leaving ESPN in 2023 and as he debuted as host of Game Theory, a late-night series that aired on HBO in 2022 and ’23.

Watch on Deadline

In a conversation with Deadline, Jones talked about the new era for his podcast, which a few days ago started daily production at a new, purpose-built studio in Harlem, NY. He also weighed in on the fast-changing sports media ecosystem, the rise of athletes as media creators, and how his early experience doing radio prepared him for the podcast age.

The conversation has been condensed and edited for clarity and length.

DEADLINE: How is the show changing, if at all, with the move to Playmaker?

BOMANI JONES: At this point, the audience is much more invested in the product itself than where it comes from. Like when I when I left ESPN, I think that I could respond to people with a certain sort of resentment because to me at that point, I was only doing the podcast for them anymore. I wasn’t doing television. So it didn’t matter if it was ESPN or not. ESPN at that point was not really prepared or knew what to do really with the podcast they had in terms of monetization, terms of promotion, and all of those things. Now, coming here, I didn’t really want to talk as much about Playmaker until we were ready to do everything at one time. We’re going to move into a new studio. We’re going to change the imaging around the show. So I wanted it to be that when people looked up, one day it was going to be like, ‘Oh, wow, this is different. This has been improved. This has been elevated.’

DEADLINE: YouTube is constantly updating its product with new features and AI tools. Having worked a lot in traditional media, does the amount of technical resources available to creators ever amaze you?

JONES: One thing you see across industries in different ways that has really become more stark and more pronounced post-pandemic is how readily and largely cheaply people can produce high-quality video content. That becomes important for people like me who, throughout the years, have had the advantage of being promoted by a large platform. Creators are just people, right? Just guys, just women who are able to put together something that looks very similar to the thing that you are putting together. Um, and that is where YouTube, in a lot of ways – I’m reluctant to use the term has democratized things, because I think that kind of misses the point – but I do think that it has created a situation where the competition that you have when you’re putting together a show is so many more people. You can’t be somebody like me or with the background that I have and be arrogant about the fact that you have this background and somebody else does not. There are a lot of people I’ve never heard of who are out here putting up really, really big numbers, and I’m the guy that has to figure out how to learn from them as much as vice versa.

DEADLINE: There’s also this new lane for athletes. So many of them are now media figures and podcast host. Their experience lends an authenticity to what they do, but not all of them are exactly entertainers. What do you make of it?

JONES: It’s a very wide range with athletes because the difference between the athletes and most celebrity digital products versus everybody else is, they’re not getting those jobs because they’re good at it. That doesn’t mean that many of them are not good at it. That’s just not the reason that they’re necessarily getting that opportunity. The people in charge of these places figure, ‘Hey, man, if we get a big name, and depending on what their audience is and who surrounds them, then we can build a product that people will listen to and that people will click on. We can get enough people to set it up and put it up window dressing around them that will support them.’ They can get guests and guests show up immediately with a different level of comfort. So, yeah, it’s a very interesting game to me now watching what it means for an athlete to have a show because it could be so many different things. Playmaker has the Roommates show with Jalen Brunson and Josh Hart. I went to the block party that they had. They can get 10,000 people there, and they can get Mariska Hargitay as a guest. They had Fabolous and Jim Jones. And a big part of that is, if you’re a Knicks fan, you want to hear from your favorite players. I think there are different roles, and different shows can play, but the competition with athletes is not really like my team against their team, as much as it’s all of us against the fact that there are only 24 hours in a day.

DEADLINE: In terms of revenue, like, obviously you have advertising. What about subscriptions or other sources?

JONES: We are working on subscriptions. Some of that I still need to talk with Playmaker about. I am a bit of an artiste in the sense that what I really want to do is come out here and make stuff. Uh, you know, and then by large, you know, by and large, we go and we work the other things out. But I know one thing that we talked about initially and part of why I was open to coming back into a studio. Um, was that the studio itself will make it easier for them to sell in different ways. Like, I think a great example, if you look at [YouTube and ESPN host] Pat McAfee’s show, it is just littered with all kinds of knickknacks, and if you look close, it’s like, ‘Ooh, it says UberEats right there. Oh, you know, it says this in those different places.’ And so I, one of the draws for a play of Playmaker for me was there appeared to be a creativity on their end about sales.

DEADLINE: It seems like you have found a happy medium betwee big media institutions and do-it-yourself, do you feel that way?

JONES: Yes, but I’ll be honest with you. I have been doing this since I was 19 years old, so 26 years and change. My goal is I always have my own goals that I am trying to achieve while also being cognizant of the agreements that I’ve made with people. And so I have to fulfill the obligations that I have made to them. Yeah. So now, I have been doing this long enough now. that I exist as a brand myself. Not as big as ESPN, obviously. But I exist there and I’m all, as I’ve been before, it’s just more pronounced because of the way it goes. I am working to do best for myself, and I am always looking to have partners who see my interest and their interests as being complimentary. And I have been fortunate enough now again to find another company that sees it this way, and that’s always an exciting thing.

DEADLINE: Are you encouraged by the state of sports media? There are increasing signs of influence by leagues over what appears on ESPN or other places. But then again, there are a wide range of digital outlets out there. Is there a significant diversity of voices in your opinion?

JONES: My my only concern about the industry at this point, and it’s everywhere. This isn’t just in sports, is, like, if somebody knew was to come come into the game, I don’t know how to tell them to, like, what they need to do to get their voice to cut through. Yeah. Like, it’s it’s so much that’s going on. Like, it gets you into, like, the Neil Postman idea – and he was just talking about television – that as it becomes a bit unregulated in terms of who can be heard and who can put things out. It is winding up with so much noise all over the place that how do people decide what there is to listen to? How does anybody truly matter? Like, we don’t really make big music stars anymore. For example, because there’s just so much all over the place. How do you cut through to become big? That is one question I have now about the industry. I do think that there’s a certain measure of ideological capture, one could argue, but I think a lot of that has to do with the attitudes of whoever is running the given company right now. Like the attitudes of the people in charge of ESPN 10 years ago are not the same as the attitudes of the people now. So it’s going to kind of land different. It’s gonna kind of sound different.

title: Jessica Biel to Play Hugh Hefner’s Wife in ‘Playmates’ Movie for Searchlight
summary: Jessica Biel has joined the cast of the upcoming film “Playmates,” Variety has learned. Biel will now star opposite previously announced cast members Lily-Rose Depp, Bill Pullman, and Indiana Elle. The film will mark the feature writing and directorial debut of Lorraine Nicholson. The official logline for “Playmates” states, “Elle (Elle), a thirteen-year-old know-it-all who […]
content:
Jessica Biel has joined the cast of the upcoming film “Playmates,” Variety has learned.

Biel will now star opposite previously announced cast members Lily-Rose Depp, Bill Pullman, and Indiana Elle. The film will mark the feature writing and directorial debut of Lorraine Nicholson.

The official logline for “Playmates” states, “Elle (Elle), a thirteen-year-old know-it-all who considers the Playboy Mansion her second home, meets Anna (Depp), one of seven hopefuls vying to be Playmate of the Month. The two form an unlikely friendship and try to help each other get what the other wants most, a magazine cover and a boy.”

Biel will play the wife of Hugh Hefner (Pullman) in the film, who is herself a former Playmate. While Hefner was married multiple times in real life, the character Biel will play is fictional.

Popular on Variety

As an actress, Biel has starred in films like “The Illusionist,” “New Year’s Eve,” “Valentine’s Day,” and “The A-Team,” as well as series like “7th Heaven,” “Candy,” “The Sinner,” and “The Better Sister.” Her work in “The Sinner” earned her both an Emmy and Golden Globe nomination. Biel has also been highly active and successful as a producer in recent years. Via her Iron Ocean production banner, she has executive produced shows like “Cruel Summer” and “Limetown,” as well as her own starring vehicles like “Candy” and “The Sinner.”

She is repped by UTA, LBI Entertainment, The Lede Company, and Yorn Levine Barnes.

Searchlight Pictures is the studio behind “Playmates.” As mentioned above, Nicholson will write and direct. Alex Orlovsky and Duncan Montgomery will produce via High Frequency Entertainment, with Depp producing in addition to starring. Searchlight vice president of production Richard Ruiz and creative executive Cornelia Burleigh will oversee the project for the studio.

title: ‘East of Eden’ Hits 6.5 Million Views in Four Days on Netflix
summary: “East of Eden” amassed 6.5 million views in its first four days of streaming on Netflix. That total took the John Steinbeck adaptation to the No. 1 spot on the streamer’s weekly TV rankings. Created by Zoe Kazan and starring Florence Pugh, the project has given the 1953 Steinbeck novel renewed popularity, with Penguin Classics […]
content:
“East of Eden” amassed 6.5 million views in its first four days of streaming on Netflix.

That total took the John Steinbeck adaptation to the No. 1 spot on the streamer’s weekly TV rankings. Created by Zoe Kazan and starring Florence Pugh, the project has given the 1953 Steinbeck novel renewed popularity, with Penguin Classics seeing a 200% increase in sales since Netflix announced the greenlight.

But the most-watched Netflix title overall during the week of Sept. 28-Oct. 4 was on the movies chart: “Unabomber,” starring Jacob Tremblay, hit 24.9 million views in its second week of streaming. “The Widower: ’Til Death Do Us Part” and “Tyler Perry’s Doing Life” also outranked the week’s top TV titles, taking the second and third spots on the movies chart with 11.6 million and 9.3 million views, respectively.

Popular on Variety

Back on the TV chart, “East of Eden” was followed by “Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story,” which achieved 5.7 million views in its third week of streaming.

More to come…

title: Inaugural Fantastic: Brasil at Rio Film Festival Creates International Bridge for Latin American Genre Cinema, Announces Winners
summary: RIO DE JANEIRO, Brazil – Fantastic:Brasil debuted at this year’s Rio Film Festival as a new industry platform for genre cinema in the largest country in South America. The initiative is a partnership between the Fantastic Pavilion Cannes, Rio Market, Festival do Rio, FICCI Industria, #LINK Documentary Industry Meeting, Mórbido Film Fest, and Sitges, and […]
content:
RIO DE JANEIRO, Brazil – Fantastic:Brasil debuted at this year’s Rio Film Festival as a new industry platform for genre cinema in the largest country in South America. The initiative is a partnership between the Fantastic Pavilion Cannes, Rio Market, Festival do Rio, FICCI Industria, #LINK Documentary Industry Meeting, Mórbido Film Fest, and Sitges, and launched three calls for emerging voices in Latin American genre cinema.

The initiative’s first edition is being held over Oct. 2-7 at Armazém da Utopia, the home of the festival’s industry arm, RioMarket. The initiative was conceived as a platform for the development, training, pitching, and international circulation of fantastic film projects. It brings together a collaborative network comprising the Fantastic Pavilion Cannes; Fantastic Embassy EFM Berlinale; Sitges – International Fantastic Film Festival of Catalonia; Festival do Rio; FICCI Industria, the industry program of the Cartagena de Indias International Film Festival; #LINK, a documentary industry meeting held in Buenos Aires and Rio de Janeiro; Mexico’s Mórbido Film Fest, and Sanfic Industry in Chile.

Founder of Mórbido Film Fest and executive director of the Fantastic Pavilion at the Marché du Film, Pablo Guisa Koestinger was in Rio for the first time to walk an industry aidinece through the initiative’s activities, which culminated in a pitching session and roundtable on Monday evening. Speaking with Variety at the event, the veteran said the Pavilion’s role in Fantastic:Brasil is “to connect the territory to the pipeline.”

Popular on Variety

“The fantastic is being made everywhere in the world, in every language and on every budget,” he adds. “Talent has never been the problem. The problem is circulation. A project developed in Rio should be able to find its partners in Colombia, Santiago, Mexico, Los Angeles, Berlin, Cannes, Abu Dhabi, and travel the world the way these stories deserve. We are making that possible. We are building the Fantastic Nation.”

At the end of the project presentations, Guisa told the audience at RioMarket he was “very happy with this first edition of Fantastic: Brasil, and I am confident we will watch films presented here coming out over the next few years, and you’ll all be able to tell everyone you heard about them first here at the Rio Film Festival.”

For its inaugural edition, Fantastic:Brasil featured three independent calls, each focused on a specific area of Latin American fantastic cinema. WomanInFan Brasil, the Brazilian edition of the program created by the Sitges Film Festival, dedicated to fantastic genre projects directed by Brazilian women; Monstra – Fantastic Queer Lab, a call for queer fantastic genre projects from across Latin America, presented in partnership with Mórbido Film Fest and its #LGBTerror section; and #LINK Vertical, a program dedicated to the creation, production and international circulation of audiovisual works conceived natively for the vertical 9:16 format.

Under the concept True Dystopic, the #LINK Vertical program brings together auteur documentary and genre cinema, using real locations in Rio de Janeiro as settings for imagining speculative futures. Each call included between four and six projects, with the chosen teams participating in a development lab and pitch sessions with industry professionals.

Through the resulting network, selected projects may have access to presentation and circulation opportunities at partner events and platforms, including the Fantastic Pavilion at the Marché du Film in Cannes, the Fantastic Embassy at Berlin’s European Film Market, FICCI in Cartagena de Indias, and Mórbido Film Fest in Mexico City. In this sense, Fantastic:Brasil creates an international circulation pathway connecting Rio de Janeiro, Cartagena de Indias, Mexico City, Berlin, and Cannes.

See the Fantastic:Brasil award winners below:



Fantastic Round Robin Award, Fantastic Pavilion, Marché du Film, Cannes

“Entranhas” (MONSTRA, Fantastic Queer Lab), dir. Lucas Procópio Caetano, Fourfé Filmes (Limeira, SP)

While getting ready for a show, drag queen Anorma tells three stories to her audience: a single person, bound, gagged, and blindfolded. With each story, clues emerge about who the victim is, how they connect to the tales, and why Anorma plans to kill them. Procópio Caetano co-wrote “Brazilian Horror Cinema in the 21st Century.” His short project “O Berço” won ECM+LAB/Panvision 2025 and was presented at the Marché du Film 2026.

“Fotograma” (WomanInFan Brasil), dir. Fernanda Pessoa de Barros, Muritiba Filmes (São Paulo/Curitiba)

A researcher studying São Paulo’s film history finds a mysterious 16mm film from the 1970s that depicts an apparent human sacrifice. As she investigates where it came from, she begins to see her own image inside it. The project went through EFM Fiction Toolbox and PAS Nantes. Barros is a former Berlinale Talent and has directed the documentaries “Histórias Que Nosso Cinema (Não) Contava,” “Zona Árida” and “Vai e Vem.” Her films have screened at IDFA, Sheffield DocFest and DOK Leipzig. This is her first fiction feature.

Mórbido Lab, SANFIC (Santiago, Chile)

“Chupacu” (MONSTRA, Fantastic Queer Lab), dir. Antonia Baudouin Andrade, Carneiro Verde Filmes (Goiânia/SP)

Isolated in a rural mansion during a testosterone-fueled barbecue, a group of “agro-machos” must rethink their relationships and everything they know about masculinity when the Chupacu, a terrifying alien monster, starts attacking… one ass at a time. Andrade worked on the script for Gustavo Vinagre’s Rotterdam-selected “Privadas de Suas Vidas” and worked in writers’ rooms for Amazon, Netflix, Star+ and Warner. “Chupacu” is her first feature as director. Her producer, Rodrigo Carneiro, is behind Teddy Award winner “Três Tigres Tristes.”

WomanInFan – Next phase in Cartagena

“O Que Acontece Quando a Coisa Acaba,” dir. Gabriela Amaral Almeida, Capivara Movies (Rio de Janeiro)

Summoned by her mother’s death, Alma returns to the family home. Trapped by her sister in a sinister psychological game, she must face the guilt of the past and the dangers of madness in the present. Almeida is the renowned director behind “Friendly Beast,” “Panic Room,” and “A Sombra do Pai.”

“Unclaimed Copper” (Working Title), dir. Guenia Reichmann Lemos, Moro Filmes (Curitiba)

In a world as overpopulated as it is lonely, where human ashes have become raw material for illegal drugs, Iori finds a semblance of family in an orphan girl and her building’s octogenarian doorman. Lemos has been an actress for over 35 years. Her short film “Tente Sua Sorte” won 29 awards.

Post-production awards (teaser)

“Entranhas,” Dir. Lucas Procópio Caetano · Teaser post-production by Mística. See above.

“Phantasmas Anonymas,” dir. Giovanna Patané Giovanini, Clubsoda Filmes (Rio de Janeiro), Teaser post-production by Acau

Through a silent, terrifying presence, the ghost of a woman searches the archives of Latin America’s first asylum. She links the historical erasure of women forcibly committed in the late 19th century to the real terror that still violates and imprisons us. The project is selected for BGDM MafiaMind 2026. Giovanini was part of Berlinale Talents Buenos Aires. Her documentary feature “Um Dia Para Susana” had Tribeca Film Institute support and screened at Mostra de São Paulo and Havana. This would be her first fiction feature.

title: Cynthia Erivo Called Sunny Hostin to Explain Why ‘The View’ Host’s Comments on Cornell 7 Case Sparked Backlash: ‘Lead With Empathy’ and Not the Law
summary: “The View” co-host Sunny Hostin revealed on the show’s “Behind the Table” podcast (via Entertainment Weekly) that Cynthia Erivo called her with concerns over Hostin’s viral segment discussing the Cornell 7 sexual assault case. The “Wicked” Oscar nominee explained to Hostin why she was getting backlash for her remarks. Hostin was accused of defending the […]
content:
“The View” co-host Sunny Hostin revealed on the show’s “Behind the Table” podcast (via Entertainment Weekly) that Cynthia Erivo called her with concerns over Hostin’s viral segment discussing the Cornell 7 sexual assault case. The “Wicked” Oscar nominee explained to Hostin why she was getting backlash for her remarks.

Hostin was accused of defending the seven accused men at the center of the case when she told viewers last week that “it’s important to understand why the DA did not bring a case” against them in 2024. She proceeded to explain the law without acknowledging at first that she disagreed with it, thus leading to outrage online.

Popular on Variety

“She allowed other boys and consented to other boys snorting ketamine off of her body, and under New York law, voluntary intoxication or drug use that merely impairs judgment does not legally constitute an inability to consent to sexual activity,” Hostin said last week, in her legal opinion, about the accuser, a woman who is going by Jane Doe. “That means if you voluntarily ingest drugs, voluntarily take alcohol, you can agree to have threesomes — which, in her statement, she agreed to have two separate threesomes.”

Hostin admitted on the “Behind the Table” podcast that she “led with the law” while discussing the Cornell 7 case on “The View” because “everyone else had spoken emotionally about it,” adding: “I needed, I felt, to bring us back to this New York law, which is really terrible and needs to be changed.”

The host soon got a call from Cynthia Erivo, who was in Paris working on a new project. “She called me and said, ‘Sis, I know you and I know your heart and your life’s work has been about protecting women and children. But, the clip that I saw doesn’t reflect who you are,’” Hostin said of Erivo’s message. “She then said, ‘I’m a blunt person and you are a blunt person.’ That’s why we get along so well, because we get the BS out when we talk to each other. She said she’s had to learn to give people her opinion in a way that they can receive it rather than just be blunt.”

Hostin said Erivo shared the following advice: “Instead of leading with the law, I need to lead with empathy so that people can receive the message about the law. That’s why the next time we talked about it, I led with that so that people would be able to receive the facts that, in New York, if you’re voluntarily intoxicated you’d have to be completely passed out, affirmatively say no, or you would have to be drugged involuntarily to prove sexual assault.”

“I was accused of defending these young men, and victim-shaming, which is something I would never do since I spent the majority of my career prosecuting sex crimes,” Hostin added. “So, I was kind of fascinated by the way people received the information that I gave, which was ultimately the law in New York must be changed because the bar is so very high. In New York, once someone is voluntarily intoxicated, to prove sexual assault. It’s already beyond a reasonable doubt, and then you add that on to it, the burden becomes so high. It’s almost impossible to prove sexual assault.”

The Cornell 7 is the name given online to the seven male students accused of drugging and gang raping their female classmate (Jane Doe) at Cornell University in October 2024. The woman is now suing her alleged assaulters as well as their fraternity, Cornell University, her former sorority and more. According to the woman’s attorney, Cornell’s original investigation into the alleged crime resulted in only two of the accused men being expelled. The other students received lesser sanctions, such as temporary suspensions, workshops or essay-writing assignments.

The case has earned widespread attention in Hollywood. Florence Pugh went viral on Instagram for urging men to speak out and to be “leading conversations about how we change the allowance and complicity of this behavior… This is really the moment where we need our men to be as horrified and as sickened as us.”

After Pugh’s post, several other celebrities such as Mariska Hargitay, Josh Gad, Hudson Williams and more used social media to also condemn the Cornell 7. “Arrest them,” wrote “Heated Rivalry” star Williams on his Instagram story while sharing a photo of the seven accused men. “Fuck them and fuck Cornell, too!”

title: RedBird Ponied Up $4 Billion to Fund Paramount’s Warner Bros. Discovery Takeover
summary: RedBird Capital Partners, led by Gerry Cardinale, invested $4 billion into Paramount’s deal to merge with Warner Bros. Discovery, the biggest Hollywood M&A deal in history, a source familiar with the deal confirmed to Variety. RedBird had already invested $2 billion in David Ellison’s Skydance Media for its takeover of Paramount Global, a deal that […]
content:
RedBird Capital Partners, led by Gerry Cardinale, invested $4 billion into Paramount’s deal to merge with Warner Bros. Discovery, the biggest Hollywood M&A deal in history, a source familiar with the deal confirmed to Variety.

RedBird had already invested $2 billion in David Ellison’s Skydance Media for its takeover of Paramount Global, a deal that closed in August 2025. The additional funding brings RedBird’s investment into the Ellisons’ media holdings to a total of $6 billion. RedBird had committed to backing Paramount’s bid for Warner Bros. Discovery but the amount had not been disclosed.

The Ellison family, through the equity investment from Larry Ellison (David’s multibillionaire father), holds the largest equity stake in Skydance. The Ellisons and investment firm RedBird together are the sole holders of Paramount Class A common stock, which gives them 100% control of the combined company’s voting shares. Cardinale, founder and managing partner of RedBird, serves as a director on Skydance’s board.

Popular on Variety

Cardinale, in a statement Tuesday with the Paramount-WBD merger closing, said: “This is a defining moment for the industry. By applying our owner-operator model to Paramount and WBD’s unmatched portfolio of iconic franchises, premium original programming, and live sports rights, we can protect that legacy while building for a media landscape that’s undergoing transformational change.”

According to Cardinale, David Ellison, Skydance co-CEO Ynon Kreiz “and the rest of our world-class Skydance team have the vision and track record to lead through this change. We’re proud to back them as we build a stronger Hollywood, expand opportunities for talent and create long-term value for our shareholders.”

Skydance claims that it has “the most diverse film and television library of any studio,” as well as the largest theatrical output in the industry, pledging to release at least 30 films in theaters annually. Its entertainment franchises include Top Gun, Harry Potter, White Lotus, SpongeBob SquarePants and more.

New York-based RedBird says it has investments in 50-plus companies, representing over $82 billion in enterprise value. In addition to its stake in Paramount Skydance, the firm has invested in Ben Affleck and Matt Damon’s Artists Equity, Ari Emanuel’s Mari global events and experiences company and the Fenway Sports Group, which owns the Boston Red Sox and other sports teams and businesses. RedBird also recently inked a deal acquiring control of Puck, valuing the media start-up at $250 million.

RedBird’s additional $4 billion investment in the combined Paramount-Warner Bros. was first reported by Bloomberg.

title: ‘East Of Eden’ Tops Netflix Charts With Soft Opening
summary: East of Eden, Zoe Kazan’s period miniseries adaptation of John Steinbeck’s classic novel, managed to score top spot on Netflix’s weekly ratings charts, but it did it with only 6.5M views. The series, which stars Florence Pugh as Cathy Ames, launched on October 1, and managed to hold off Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story and […]
content:
East of Eden, Zoe Kazan’s period miniseries adaptation of John Steinbeck’s classic novel, managed to score top spot on Netflix’s weekly ratings charts, but it did it with only 6.5M views.

The series, which stars Florence Pugh as Cathy Ames, launched on October 1, and managed to hold off Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story and Wonka’s Golden Ticket to lead the charts.

But its 6.5M opening was the lowest since the end of March, when the second season of One Piece topped the charts in its third week on the streamer with 5.9M views.

The series, which also stars Christopher Abbott and Mike Faist, which chronicles the dark side of the California dream, couldn’t compete with other, similar period fare.

Watch on Deadline

American Primeval, Mark L. Smith’s Taylor Kitsch and Betty Gilpin series set in 1857, opened with 10.4M at the start of 2025, and WWII miniseries All The Light We Cannot See, from Shawn Levy and Steven Knight, drew 9.8M in its first week.

Netflix was keen to point out that the series also hit the top ten in 80 countries and was number one in 22 countries and the adaptation helped Penguin Classic sell 200% more books since it was announced.

Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story drew 5.7M in its third week, taking its total to 32.3M.

The reboot of A Different World was third with 5.1M views, while Wonka’s The Golden Ticket was fourth with 4.3M views in its second week on the charts. The reality competition series opened with 4.6M and its ratings were helped by the season’s two-part finale, which dropped on September 30.

The rest of the list was made up on Lego One Piece, the second season of The Gentlemen, Crew Girl, WWE’s Raw, the first season of The Gentlemen and season 14 of Gabby’s Dollhouse.

title: Apple TV’s ‘Beat The Reaper’ Expands Cast With Damon Herrimon, Stephanie Nur, Artoun Nazareth & Molly Price
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Damon Herriman (Once Upon a Time in Hollywood, The Bikeriders), Stephanie Nur (Lioness, 1883), Artoun Nazareth (The Promised Land, Muppets Now) and Molly Price (Elsbeth, The Spot) have signed on as series regulars, joining Will Poulter and J.K. Simmons in Beat The Reaper, Apple TV’s upcoming dramedy. Details of their roles are under wraps. […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Damon Herriman (Once Upon a Time in Hollywood, The Bikeriders), Stephanie Nur (Lioness, 1883), Artoun Nazareth (The Promised Land, Muppets Now) and Molly Price (Elsbeth, The Spot) have signed on as series regulars, joining Will Poulter and J.K. Simmons in Beat The Reaper, Apple TV‘s upcoming dramedy. Details of their roles are under wraps.

Based on Josh Bazell’s novel of the same name, Beat the Reaper stars Poulter as Dr. Peter Brown, an intern at Boston’s worst hospital, with a talent for medicine, a shift from hell, and a past he’d prefer to keep hidden. But when a patient recognizes him from his dangerous past, Brown has eight hours to elude the government, mob hitmen, quack surgeons, and a trail of dead gangsters to somehow beat the reaper.

Beat The Reaper, Bazell’s debut novel, was released in 2009. The dark comedy tells the story of medical resident Peter Brown, who is also in the Federal Witness Protection Program due to his past as a mafia hitman. When a dying mobster ends up at the hospital where he works, he recognizes Peter as Pietro Brnwa, the hitman. Peter finds himself at a crossroads: he needs to save the mobster’s life or his past will be exposed.

Watch on Deadline

Sam Catlin (Sugar, Breaking Bad) adapted the novel for TV and serves as showrunner and executive produces for his Short Drive banner under his deal with Apple TV. Apple Studios and New Regency are serving as co-studios. Arnon Milchan, Yariv Milchan Natalie Lehmann, and Laura Delahaye executive produce. Tim Van Patten directs the first episode and serves as executive producer. Rachel Toffler co-executive produces for New Regency and Tiffany Prasifka co-executive produces for Short Drive.

Herriman can most recently be seen as Lawrence Cole in Reacher spinoff Neagley, and upcoming in Amazon MGM’s submarine actioner Subversion. He is repped by Art/Work Entertainment, Paradigm and Lisa Mann Creative Management.

Nur is known for her work in Taylor Sheridan’s Lionness and Yellowstone prequel 1883. On the film side she appeared opposite Anthony Hopkins in DJ Caruso’s Biblical period piece Mary on Netflix. Nur is repped by Innovative Artists and Trademark Talent.

Nazareth’s credits include The Odyssey, Ghostbusters: Afterlife, Dumb Money, The Promised Land, Muppets Now, The Conners, SEAL Team, and United States of Al, among others. He is repped by Venture Entertainment Partners and Artistic Talent.

Price is maybe best known for her work on John Wells’ NBC series, Third Watch. She’ll next be seen recurring on the new A24 suspense thriller, The Spot, with Claire Danes and Ewan McGregor. Price is repped by Innovative Artists and Abrams Entertainment.

title: Jessica Biel Joins Searchlight Pictures’ ‘Playmates’
summary: Jessica Biel has found her next feature project in Playmates, the Searchlight flick inspired by filmmaker Lorraine Nicholson’s experiences growing up at the Playboy Mansion. Biel is playing a wife to Hugh Hefner and former Playboy Playmate — a fictional character we’re told isn’t modeled off any of Hefner’s three wives, specifically. Bill Pullman is […]
content:
Jessica Biel has found her next feature project in Playmates, the Searchlight flick inspired by filmmaker Lorraine Nicholson’s experiences growing up at the Playboy Mansion.

Biel is playing a wife to Hugh Hefner and former Playboy Playmate — a fictional character we’re told isn’t modeled off any of Hefner’s three wives, specifically.

Bill Pullman is playing Hefner as previously announced, starring alongside child actress Indiana Elle and Lily-Rose Depp. Searchlight announced its acquisition of the Playboy-themed feature package late last month.

Nicholson’s feature directorial debut Playmates adapts her own original script — an L.A.-set coming-of-age story following 13-year-old know-it-all Elle (played by Indiana Elle), who considers the Playboy Mansion her second home. During her time at the Mansion, Elle meets Anna (Depp), one of seven hopefuls vying to be Playmate of the Month. The two form an unlikely friendship and try to help each other get what the other wants most, a magazine cover and a boy.

Watch on Deadline

Producers on Playmates include Alex Orlovsky and Duncan Montgomery of High Frequency Entertainment, as well as Depp. VP Production Richard Ruiz and CE Cornelia Burleigh are overseeing the project for the studio, reporting to Heads of Production and Development DanTram Nguyen and Katie Goodson-Thomas.

An Emmy and two-time Golden Globe nominee for her work as star and exec producer of USA Network’s The Sinner, Biel most recently exec produced and starred opposite Elizabeth Banks in The Better Sister, Prime Video’s limited series based on the novel by Alafair Burke. She came to the thriller following several years away from the screen.

Next up, Biel will be seen starring opposite John Cena in Matchbox: The Movie, a collaboration between Apple, Skydance and Mattel that begins streaming on Apple TV this Friday. She is repped by UTA, LBI Entertainment, and Yorn, Levine, Barnes.

title: Warner Bros. Water Tower Repainted To Add “A Skydance Corporation” Following Merger Close
summary: Just hours after the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger officially closed Tuesday morning, workers repainted the Warner Bros. water tower in Burbank to include “A Skydance Corporation” on the famed structure. CEO David Ellison revealed the merged company’s new name, Skydance, on Friday. Ellison had previously updated the Paramount water tower with “A Skydance Corporation” after Skydance […]
content:
Just hours after the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger officially closed Tuesday morning, workers repainted the Warner Bros. water tower in Burbank to include “A Skydance Corporation” on the famed structure.

CEO David Ellison revealed the merged company’s new name, Skydance, on Friday. Ellison had previously updated the Paramount water tower with “A Skydance Corporation” after Skydance Media’s takeover of Paramount Global in 2025. Skydance is the original name of the film production company Ellison founded in 2006.

You can see a photo of workers updating the tower below.

Workers change the sign on the Warner Bros. water tower to say “A Skydance Corporation” on Tuesday Getty Images

The year-long pursuit by Ellison to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery overcame numerous hurdles, fierce opposition and a two-month delay caused by antitrust lawsuits by 12 states and the Writers Guild of America.

Watch on Deadline

Ellison and co-CEO Ynon Kreiz laid out the new company’s priorities in a lengthy memo to staff this morning following the $110B merger close. Likely layoffs, required in order to pay down some $80 billion in debt and deliver $6 billion in projected cost savings, were among the many topics covered in the memo.

“What once was the peak, is now just the beginning,” Ellison wrote on Friday when he revealed the new name. “Paramount and Warner Bros. shaped over a century of culture. By combining them, we aren’t rewriting history – we’re equipping these iconic studios with a more powerful engine. Together, we are Skydance: a creative-first home for bold, quality storytelling.”

You can see a couple other photos below.

The Warner Bros. water tower with Skydance’s logo added to it Tuesday Getty Images

title: Dermot Mulroney Joins ESX & Warner Bros Crew HQ ‘Streets’ From Emelia Hartford
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Scream VI and The Hunting Wives actor Dermot Mulroney is jumping into the car of Ali Afshar’s ESX Entertainment and Warner Bros’ Crew HQ auto action pic, Streets. Mulroney will be playing the role of Gordon alongside pic’s star, producer and co-scribe Emelia Hartford. The ensemble cast includes Cody Christian, RJ Kyler, Jearnest Corchado, […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Scream VI and The Hunting Wives actor Dermot Mulroney is jumping into the car of Ali Afshar’s ESX Entertainment and Warner Bros’ Crew HQ auto action pic, Streets.

Mulroney will be playing the role of Gordon alongside pic’s star, producer and co-scribe Emelia Hartford. The ensemble cast includes Cody Christian, RJ Kyler, Jearnest Corchado, Ryder Franco, John Marshall Jones, Harry Jarvis, Spencer Belko and Struggle Jennings.

Hartford created the world and co-wrote Streets with filmmaker Shaun Paul Piccinino. The project is inspired by one of the auto world’s real-life mysteries—the 1939 disappearance of Jean Bugatti’s personal Type 57S Atlantic, considered the $100+ million “Holy Grail” of classic cars. Streets follows an East LA street racing crew thrust into a dangerous, high-stakes hunt across Southern California, where every turn presents a new clue and a potential disaster. Streets is directed by Piccinino (Lady Driver).

Hartford produces under her new production banner, Running Lean Productions.

Watch on Deadline

Streets was granted a California Film & Television Tax Credit with shooting occurring on the Warner Bros. lot in Burbank. Streets reps the premier launchpad for local workforce development in partnership with Warner Bros. Studios’ CrewHQ, a workforce initiative designed to train, mentor, and cultivate the next generation of film and television crew talent in California.

Mulroney will next be seen in Season 2 of Netflix’s The Hunting Wives, opposite Malin Akerman and Brittany Snow, returning as Jed Banks. He will also star alongside John Travolta and Mandy Patinkin in Roland Joffé’s historical crime thriller November 1963, and currently stars in Art Camacho’s action thriller Ruthless. It was recently announced that he will return as ‘Everett Stone’ for Searchlight’s The Families Stone. His acclaimed film and television credits include Anyone But You, Marvel’s Secret Invasion, New Girl, American Horror Story, August: Osage County, The Family Stone, Friends, and My Best Friend’s Wedding. The actor is repped by Paradigm.

title: George Cheeks Addresses Staffers in First Memo as Skydance TV Co-Chair: ‘CBS Remains a Cornerstone’
summary: George Cheeks, newly appointed to the role of Skydance TV co-chair and chief content officer, laid out his vision to staffers Tuesday, as the $111 billion merger between Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery officially closed. Hours after Skydance chairman and CEO David Ellison and co-CEO Ynon Kreiz sent a memo to employees at the combined […]
content:
George Cheeks, newly appointed to the role of Skydance TV co-chair and chief content officer, laid out his vision to staffers Tuesday, as the $111 billion merger between Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery officially closed.

Hours after Skydance chairman and CEO David Ellison and co-CEO Ynon Kreiz sent a memo to employees at the combined company outlining their operating philosophy and goals for the new company, Cheeks sent his own email to TV staffers across studios and networks.

That note started didn’t spell out a structure just yet, but it’s understood that divisional bosses who will report to him include Warner Bros. TV Group and U.S. networks chairman/CEO Channing Dungey, CBS Studios president David Stapf and Paramount TV Studios topper Matt Thunell. Alongside Cheeks, JB Perrette (previously WBD’s CEO/president of global streaming and games) serves as co-chair of Skydance TV, as well as chief business officer. Perrette additional holds those roles for the Skydance DTC streaming division.

Popular on Variety

“The work ahead is significant, and so is the opportunity,” he said in the note. “I am energized by the possibilities. Together, we’ll build on our collective strengths to create an even stronger future.”

Cheeks’ ascension at Skydance was a huge vote of confidence from Ellison, who had previously tapped the exec to serve as Paramount TV media chair last year when Skydance first took control of Paramount. Prior to that, Cheeks was one of the three co-CEOs of Paramount Global (previously known as ViacomCBS) — and was the only one of that triumvirate to make the transition to the new company.

Here’s his note:

Team,

Today is the start of a new chapter. By bringing together Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery, we’ve assembled a remarkable collection of television brands, networks and studios, backed by some of the most talented teams in the industry.

I want to acknowledge the hard work, creativity and dedication you each bring to this historic moment. Thank you for playing through the noise this past year. I am excited to move forward together and shape our future as one team.

Our Skydance Television group

This newly formed Skydance Television group is an unmatched mix of networks, studios, platforms and programming genres.

Our three television studios — Warner Bros. Television Studios, CBS Studios and Paramount Television Studios — will continue to create franchises, premium originals and unscripted hits that entertain viewers of all ages and interests and power our platforms and partners around the globe. CBS remains a cornerstone, underpinning our multiplatform strategy to deliver entertainment, news and sports to audiences at scale. CBS Sports, TNT Sports and Warner Bros. Discovery Sports together form an enviable and expansive global sports portfolio. CBS News is one of the most important brands in journalism, delivering national and worldwide news across broadcast, streaming and digital. At the local level, our 27 CBS stations serve 17 markets with best-in-class community journalism. Our cable portfolio features more than 50 channels globally, connecting viewers with culture-defining entertainment, kids and family programming and leading lifestyle brands.

There are too many standout shows to name individually, but one thing is clear: the breadth and quality of programming across this group is unrivaled, spanning some of the most watched, most acclaimed and most award-winning in the industry.

title: Unions and Democrats Stump for Federal Film Incentive: ‘We Are So Close to Getting This Done’
summary: A delegation of California Democrats campaigned with union leaders on Tuesday for a federal film incentive as they seek to build momentum to pass the measure by the end of the year. Sen. Adam Schiff and eight Democratic representatives from Southern California argued that the U.S. must counter incentives from 65 other countries that have […]
content:
A delegation of California Democrats campaigned with union leaders on Tuesday for a federal film incentive as they seek to build momentum to pass the measure by the end of the year.

Sen. Adam Schiff and eight Democratic representatives from Southern California argued that the U.S. must counter incentives from 65 other countries that have lured American production jobs overseas.

“We are so close to getting this done,” Schiff said in 100-degree heat outside the Alex Theatre in Glendale. “Whatever we can do to get this done, that is job No. 1. It just can’t wait. It’s too important. The losses so far have been too extraordinary.”

Lawmakers introduced a bill last month that would create a 20%-30% transferable tax credit for U.S. labor costs on films and TV shows. Schiff said that 12 senators are on board — six Democrats and six Republicans. The latest to join as cosponsors are Sens. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., and Chris Coons, D-Del., according to Schiff’s office.

Popular on Variety

They will have about five weeks during the lame-duck session of Congress after the election to try to pass the bill. Rep. Laura Friedman, whose office organized Tuesday’s press conference, said she is “cautiously, guardedly optimistic.”

“We need to have this on the president’s desk by mid-December, as far as I’m concerned,” she said in an interview, adding that she hopes the bill will pass in essentially its current form as part of a larger tax package. “This has been almost two years of constant work. It hasn’t just come together in the last few weeks. It’s been a snowball effect. It started out as this idea, and then we just kept building and building and building. So I feel like we have a great momentum.”

The proposal includes a 5% bonus for filming in a disaster area, which would apply to the entirety of Los Angeles County until January 2030, due to last year’s fires. There are also bonuses for independent films and for filming in rural opportunity zones. The total tax credit could rise to 50% or more when combined with state incentives in places like California and New York — easily surpassing the incentives offered by other countries.

“It is fair to say that these other countries they recognize the quality of these jobs — that’s why they put these measures in place,” said Duncan Crabtree-Ireland, the executive director of SAG-AFTRA. “That’s why they are eating not only our lunch, but our breakfast and our dinner as well. And we have to change that. This is our opportunity to do it.”

A coalition of industry unions published a report on Monday documenting the erosion of U.S. production as a share of global spending over the past 25 years. According to the report, the U.S. share fell from 74% to 42% in film and from 94% to 64% in television, though both industries have also grown considerably over that time period.

In August, President Donald Trump called on Congress to “immediately” pass an incentive and pronouncing that “Hollywood is a Complete and Total Disaster!”

The Motion Picture Association, representing the studios, has sought to emphasize that the bill would benefit not only California and New York, but all 50 states. The MPA has also been more cautious about the timing, saying that while it’s important to move quickly, it’s also important to “get this right.”

But union leaders said Tuesday that their members can’t afford to wait.

“When this passes in this lame-duck session, it will immediately impact production in 2027,” said Mike Miller, vice president of IATSE. “And there are hundreds of thousands of entertainment industry workers that are counting on it.”

title: ‘The Table: Day and Night’ Review: Café-Based Korean Romance With Kim Min-ha and Han Sun-hwa Is All Froth, No Kick
summary: An artisanal café in a quiet yet fashionable Seoul neighborhood provides the setting for a quartet of seasonal vignettes in Kim Jong-kwan’s romantic anthology “The Table: Day and Night.” Opening this year’s Busan Film Festival, the film — with its star-studded ensemble including Kim Min-ha, Shim Eun-kyung and Han Sun-hwa — will ensure a glitzy […]
content:
An artisanal café in a quiet yet fashionable Seoul neighborhood provides the setting for a quartet of seasonal vignettes in Kim Jong-kwan’s romantic anthology “The Table: Day and Night.” Opening this year’s Busan Film Festival, the film — with its star-studded ensemble including Kim Min-ha, Shim Eun-kyung and Han Sun-hwa — will ensure a glitzy curtain-raiser for South Korea’s premier cinematic event, but beyond this high-profile debut, Kim’s frothy, fitfully engaging effort will likely be met with a muted response further afield, limited only to specialist Asian showcases.
