An expansion of the director’s 2016 effort, “The Table,” which saw four different couples meet for coffee at the same table, in the same café, over the course of a single day, “The Table: Day and Night” is similarly constructed around four chance encounters that take place at a single, stylish coffeehouse. This time the meetups are spread across a number of weeks, as the summer heat cools gently into autumn, while the interludes themselves attempt to broach something more complex than simple relationship woes.

Popular on Variety

The first chapter, titled “A Midsummer Night’s Dream,” details the fairytale meeting between two customers, Hyeon-oh (Joo Jong-hyuk), a young man with a passion for rebuilding old watches, and Yoo-jin (Kim Min-ha), a forlorn dreamer, whose inherited antique timepiece has not worked in years. “Still Ourselves,” the second vignette, treads a precarious line between comic and tragic, when Young-min (Chang Ryul) is accosted by the beautiful yet increasingly unstable Sang-mi (Han Sun-hwa), a former middle-school friend who accuses him of not remembering her, before begging that he protect her from an encroaching unseen enemy.

In the third story, “T.P.A.,” successful web novelist Hye-jin (Shim Eun-kyung) is wooed by Dong-nam (Lee Hee-jun), a passionate filmmaker who pleads for her permission to adapt one of her most popular works for the big screen, while in the final tale, an aspiring pop idol, Nakyung (Jeon So-young) and her childhood boyfriend Jong-su (Kim Dong-hwi) discuss the fate of their adolescent relationship.

Kim has grown steadily in stature within the industry, since his acclaimed 2004 short “How to Operate a Polaroid Camera.” He has contributed to a number of anthologies and omnibuses, including the Netflix project “Persona” (2019) and the Hemingway-inspired crime collection “The Killers” (2024), while many of his feature films, such as “Worst Woman” (2016) and “Frosted Window” (2025), are likewise structured around a series of loosely connected vignettes.

He is clearly drawn to telling stories in snapshots, and exploring characters through fleeting moments and passing interactions. The perpetually populated tables of a busy urban eatery provide the perfect setting for these micro-dramas to play out, while lending a narrative consistency to the piece as a whole, even as the tone of each tale is allowed to flail wildly from the implausible to the pragmatic, the fantastical to the flirtatious.

Never allowing the action to bleed beyond the boundaries of the establishment, Kim invites the suggestion that the café itself plays cupid to those that chance to cross its threshold — a notion made all the more plausible when novelist Hye-jin begins casually concocting a workplace romance from her own imagination, between the café’s ever-present baristas. As is true throughout Kim’s work, the women prove infinitely more interesting protagonists than their male counterparts.

Kim Min-ha, a familiar face to many from her work on Apple TV’s “Pachinko,” is given little opportunity to shine in a segment that promises much, but leaves its potential unexplored. Shim (last seen in Sho Miyake’s Locarno winner “Two Seasons, Two Strangers”) portrays Hye-jin as a formidable artist, confident in her vision and stature within a male-dominated industry, even when she allows Dong-nam’s charm offensive to gain ground. Han’s Sang-mi is a similarly captivating presence onscreen, a bundle of nervous energy on the brink of exploding, captured brilliantly by one of Korea’s most consistently versatile emerging talents.

Master DP Kim Ji-yong, the man responsible for such ravishing visual delights as Park Chan-wook’s “Decision to Leave” and Lee Chang-dong’s current awards player “Possible Love,” shoots this hipster hideaway together with Lee Ju-yeon, in warm, inviting hues that come close to conjuring the scent of freshly roasted beans. The walls are decorated in eye-catching oil paintings of enigmatic, forlorn individuals who compose themselves in much the same manner as the café’s real clientele.

Whether these portraits represent past patrons, whose stories once unspooled over these same steaming cups, Kim declines to comment. One can’t help but feel, as the film closes with a montage of empty, inviting tables, that he is a storyteller more interested in the potential of this space to host endless fascinating characters, dramas and romances from one moment to the next, than in actually doing justice to the ones he has brought to life.

title: ’60 Minutes’ Beats Last Season’s Viewership Bar for First Time, But Football Brings Only Small Boost
summary: CBS News’ “60 Minutes” beat a crucial metric for the first time under new and heavily scrutinized managers but only managed to eke out a small boost to its ratings despite a robust football lead-in. The CBS newsmagazine lured an average of 10.2 million viewers on Sunday, when it offered an in-depth interview with Republican […]
content:
CBS News‘ “60 Minutes” beat a crucial metric for the first time under new and heavily scrutinized managers but only managed to eke out a small boost to its ratings despite a robust football lead-in.

The CBS newsmagazine lured an average of 10.2 million viewers on Sunday, when it offered an in-depth interview with Republican Senator Thom Tillis; a probe of how the U.S. workforce may be affected by A.I.;’ and a look at how the friars at an Italy’s Basilica of Saint Francis using lasers, high-tech cameras and advanced technology to repair the 13th-century edifice.

Those figures surpassed last season’s average audience for the series, which came in at about 9.1 million — the first time this season the show has been able to do so. At the same time, the show was only able to win 50,000 more viewers than it did in its year-earlier broadcast, when it snared approximately 10.15 million, according to Nielsen figures.

Popular on Variety

The Sunday broadcast lured approximately 2 million viewers between the ages of 25 and 54 — the demographic most coveted by advertisers in news programming. The figure also surpassed last season’s average, which stands at about 1.45 million.

CBS may have had higher hopes for Sunday’s telecast. CBS Sports’ telecast of the Kanas City Chiefs taking on the Las Vegas Raiders delivered an audience of 28.4 million, a number that CBS said represented the most-watched NFL game of the season and the best fourth-week telecast of an NFL game on any network.

CBS News remains under intense pressure to demonstrate stability at the program, which was overhauled in chaotic fashion at the end of last season, despite mustering a notable 9% uptick in overall viewership. Bari Weiss, CBS News’ editor in chief, ousted Tanya Simon, an executive producer with years of history working at the show, in favor of Nick Bilton, a journalist and screenwriter with less formal TV experience. Also pushed out were correspondents Scott Pelley, Cecilia Vega and Sharyn Alfonsi. Anderson Cooper left of his own volition following the end of his contract. Their replacements, which include Ross Douthat and contributors like Ariel Levy and Sebastian Junger, have top-shelf backgrounds, but also little experience working on a weekly TV program that emphsizes long-form enterprise journalism.

While executives are working furiously to put their stamp on the venerable program, and to keep generating high-quality stories despite a disruption in the off-season production process, they are also grappling with the vicissitudes of live TV. CBS’ NFL telecast on Sunday went late, meaning that “60 Minutes” spent more of its time directly opposite NBC’s “Sunday Night Football,” one of TV’s biggest audience generators.

Executive at Skydance, the company formed from the merger of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery, will want to see “60 Minutes” do more with its football audience. The show is supposed to act as a bridge between CBS’ football games and its Sunday-night primetime lineup, which this season includes “Marshals,” “Tracker” and “Cupertino.”

Meanwhile, “CBS Evening News” saw its overall viewership for last week surge, with overall viewership for the program up 18% compared with the year-earlier period, to 4.2 million. The program has in the past year had trouble keeping an audience over 4 million. Viewership in the 25-to-54 demo was up 46% to 585,000.

“CBS Evening News” has long run in third place behind ABC’s “World News Tonight” and NBC’s “NBC Nightly News.” CBS News President Tom Cibrowski has been working closely with the evening broadcast in recent weeks, even as he is also focusing on “CBS Mornings.” Cibrowski last week hired Steven Baker, a former executive producer of “Nightline,” as a consultant to help on both the evening and morning programs.

title: André Holland Joins Universal’s ‘Miami Vice ’85’
summary: EXCLUSIVE: André Holland (Moonlight, The Knick) is the latest to join the all-star cast of Universal’s Miami Vice ’85, led by Michael B. Jordan and Austin Butler. A character description for Holland is under wraps. From screenwriter Dan Gilroy and director Joseph Kosinski, Miami Vice ’85 explores the glamour and corruption of mid-1980s Miami in […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: André Holland (Moonlight, The Knick) is the latest to join the all-star cast of Universal’s Miami Vice ’85, led by Michael B. Jordan and Austin Butler. A character description for Holland is under wraps.

From screenwriter Dan Gilroy and director Joseph Kosinski, Miami Vice ’85 explores the glamour and corruption of mid-1980s Miami in an all-new version of the hit series Miami Vice. The film is inspired by the pilot episode of the landmark 1984-90 NBC series titled “Brother’s Keeper,” which aired September 16, 1984.

The previously announced cast includes Alden Ehrenreich, Whitney Peak, Camila Morrone, John Leguizamo, Danny Ramirez and Walton Goggins.

Watch on Deadline

Written by series creator Anthony Yerkovich, the two-hour premiere of Miami Vice introduced the world to Vice cop Sonny Crockett (Don Johnson) and New York detective Ricardo Tubbs (Phillip Michael Thomas), who are brought together by destiny, though they did not really vibe at first. They eventually become partners, but first they investigate Colombian drug lord Calderone (Miguel Piñero), the show’s main antagonist across Season 1.

In the episode, it’s revealed that Tubbs’ beef with Calderone runs deep and is the reason why the former is in Miami. He wants revenge for his slain brother, who was taken down after the cartel leader put out a hit on his life. Despite first appearances, Crockett and Tubbs decide they want to work together, taking down bad guys in the Magic City and having some fun in between.

Aside from the Crockett and Tubbs intro, the episode is famously known for a driving scene where the duo is in Crockett’s black Ferrari Daytona Spyder while listening to Phil Collins’ song In the Air Tonight.

Also notable, though not from this episode, John Leguizamo portrayed Calderone’s son Orlando twice in the series. Leguizamo will also star in Miami Vice ’85, though it is as yet unknown if he will reprise the role of Orlando.

The movie will be filmed for IMAX and is set for release on May 19, 2028. Production will begin this year.

The film is produced by Dylan Clark/Dylan Clark Productions (The Batman, The Penguin) and Kosinski (F1). Dan Gilroy is writing the script, based on characters created by Yerkovich from the series executive-produced by Yerkovich and Michael Mann. Eric Warren Singer wrote an earlier draft of the screenplay.

Holland is represented by WME and Anonymous Content.

title: ‘Saved By The Bell’ Star Dennis Haskins’ Cause Of Death Revealed
summary: We now have an official cause of death for Dennis Haskins. The actor, best known for playing Mr. Belding in Saved by the Bell, died from Parkinson’s disease, according to his death certficate obtained by TMZ. Haskins died September 27 in Burbank. It had been reported that Haskins was diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease in 2018, […]
content:
We now have an official cause of death for Dennis Haskins. The actor, best known for playing Mr. Belding in Saved by the Bell, died from Parkinson’s disease, according to his death certficate obtained by TMZ.

Haskins died September 27 in Burbank. It had been reported that Haskins was diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease in 2018, but had kept the diagnosis largely private.

Haskins initially played Principal Richard Belding in the Disney Channel series Good Morning, Miss Bliss, opposite Hayley Mills in 1989. After one season, the show was retooled as Saved by the Bell on NBC, where he reprised his role through its four-season run. Haskins returned as Mr. Belding for Saved by the Bell: The New Class in 1993 and played the role for seven more seasons, until the show’s finale in 2000.

Haskins had dozens of additional acting credits, including Hangin’ with Mr. Cooper, Malibu, CA, The Practice, The West Wing, The Rerun Show, The Stoneman, 7th Heaven, Going Down, Red Water, Tangy Guacamole, An Ordinary Killer, JAG, Dead End Road, It’s Always Sunny in Philadelphia, Men of a Certain Age, The Bold and the Beautiful, Victorious, Mad Men, Emerald Acres, How I Met Your Mother, Destroy the Alpha Gammas, New Girl, Hot in Cleveland, This Isn’t Working, Bill Nye Saves the World, Abstruse, Enigma, and A Bennett Song Holiday, among others.

Watch on Deadline

Haskins’ agent Jay Schachter confirmed the actor’s death to Deadline, saying in a statement, “It’s a tragic loss. Everyone loved Mr. Belding and those of us who got to know Dennis, loved him even more. He was a great person, and he loved, I mean absolutely LOVED his fans.



“He always had time for them, no matter what,” he continued. He was my client and dear friend for over 20 years, and I will miss him terribly. I’m heartbroken.”

Haskins was 75.

title: Doc Talk Podcast: Producer James Costa On Deadline’s For The Love Of Docs Series, Oscar Season And ‘NAZA’ Controversy
summary: Oscar winner All the Empty Rooms, Closure, Free Leonard Peltier, Welcome to Chechnya, Queendom, The Dating Game, Sara Bareilles: Good Grief – James Costa has played an important role bringing those films and many more to the screen as a producer or executive producer. Each year, he also takes on an important mission for Deadline: […]
content:
Oscar winner All the Empty Rooms, Closure, Free Leonard Peltier, Welcome to Chechnya, Queendom, The Dating Game, Sara Bareilles: Good Grief – James Costa has played an important role bringing those films and many more to the screen as a producer or executive producer.

Each year, he also takes on an important mission for Deadline: selecting the films that screen as part of our fall For the Love of Docs virtual series, which allows awards-worthy films to screen free to the public and guild members, and free to the filmmakers. It’s our gesture of support for the documentary community, presented in partnership with National Geographic Documentary Films.

On the latest episode of Deadline’s Doc Talk podcast, Costa joins us to discuss how he chooses the For the Love of Docs lineup – a slate this year that includes Seized, directed by Sharon Liese; Everybody to Kenmure Street, from director Felipe Bustos Sierra; Ask E. Jean, directed by Ivy Meeropol; J.J. Gerber’s The Life We Leave; and To Hold a Mountain, directed by Biljana Tutorov and Peter Glomazić (winner of the Grand Jury Prize for World Cinema Documentary at Sundance).

Watch on Deadline

We also talk Oscar season with Costa. It’s an unusual year with few obvious frontrunners at this stage, and with many “late-breaking” documentaries (meaning films that premiered late in the year, at Venice, Telluride and Toronto) emerging as strong contenders. This stands in contrast to 2025 when all the eventual Best Documentary Feature nominees premiered at Sundance at the start of the year.

RELATED: The Talk Of Telluride: Secret Screening Of Elizabeth Holmes Documentary ‘You Can See Everything’

One of the late-in-the-year films that has immediately risen to the top of Oscar conversations is NAZA, directed by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor (two of the four directors of Academy Award winner No Other Land). NAZA, featuring whistleblowers critical of Israel’s mass killing of civilians in its war in Gaza, has been denounced by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu – he’s pushing legislation that could potentially strip Abraham and Szor of their Israeli citizenship. The threats against the filmmakers have drawn a rebuke from the International Documentary Association, for which Costa used to serve as co-president of the board. We get Costa’s thoughts on the campaign against the directors and on the IDA’s defense of the Abraham and Szor.

That’s on the new episode of Doc Talk hosted by Oscar winner John Ridley (12 Years a Slave, Shirley) and Matt Carey, Deadline’s senior documentary editor. The pod is a production of Deadline and Ridley’s Nō Studios.

title: Skydance Sets Board With Laurene Powell Jobs, Bobby Kotick New Directors, Tony Blair As Advisor
summary: The new Skydance has unveiled its board of directors, effective immediately, led by chairman and CEO David Ellison and including newcomers Laurene Powell Jobs, founder and president of Emerson Collective, and Bobby Kotick, founder and former CEO of Activision. They will service as independent directors. Co-CEO Ynon Kreiz, who joined Skydance last week, also has […]
content:
The new Skydance has unveiled its board of directors, effective immediately, led by chairman and CEO David Ellison and including newcomers Laurene Powell Jobs, founder and president of Emerson Collective, and Bobby Kotick, founder and former CEO of Activision.

They will service as independent directors.

Co-CEO Ynon Kreiz, who joined Skydance last week, also has a seat.

Powell Jobs is highly influential leader in business and philanthropy and committed investor in journalism and media. Her nonprofit Emerson Collective investments include majority stakes in The Atlantic and Anonymous Content.

Kotick served as CEO of Activision for 32 years, building it into one of the world’s most successful video game companies before selling Activision Blizzard to Microsoft for $68.7 billion.

Watch on Deadline

RELATED: Skydance Putting All 3 TV Studios Under George Cheeks: Warner Bros. TV, CBS Studios, PTVS – The Dish

Former UK Prime Minister Tony Blair will join as a Board Advisor. Blair, who will be acting in a personal capacity, is Executive Chairman of the Tony Blair Institute for Global Change, a not-for-profit that helps leaders govern in the age of AI. Paramount said his global leadership experience and commitment to innovation position him as an invaluable advisor in shaping Skydance’s strategic priorities.

The other directors are continuing on from the board of Paramount, which was renamed Skydance this morning after closing its merger with Warner Bros Discovery.

“I am delighted to welcome Laurene and Bobby to our Board and honored to have Tony join us as an Advisor,” Ellison said. “Together with our other directors, they bring the experience and fresh perspectives we need to build Skydance into an extraordinary company, one that honors the legacies of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery while setting a bold course for the future.”

RELATED: RELATED: Skydance Putting All 3 TV Studios Under George Cheeks: Warner Bros. TV, CBS Studios, PTVS – The Dish

The full Skydance board:

David Ellison, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Skydance

Barbara Byrne, Former Vice Chairman of Barclays PLC (Independent Director)

Andy Campion, Chairman and CEO of Unrivaled Sports (Independent Director)

Gerry Cardinale, Founder, Managing Partner, and Chief Investment Officer, RedBird Capital Partners

Safra A. Catz, Executive Vice Chair and Former CEO, Oracle Corporation

Andy Gordon, President of Skydance

Justin G. Hamill, Managing Director and Chief Legal Officer, Silver Lake (Independent Director)

Lauren Powell Jobs, Founder and President, Emerson Collective (Independent Director)

Bobby Kotick, Founder and former CEO of Activision (Independent Director)

Ynon Kreiz, Co-Chief Executive Officer of Skydance

Sherry Lansing, Former Chairman and CEO of Paramount Pictures (Independent Director)

Paul Marinelli, President, Lawrence Investments, LLC

John L. Thornton, Chairman of RedBird Capital Partners

title: Donald Trump Weighs In On New Skydance: “They’re Terrific People, And It’s Going To Be A Great Company”
summary: President Donald Trump commented on Skydance’s acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, completed on Tuesday, by apparently showering praised on its CEO David Ellison and his father Larry. “It’s going to be a great company,” Trump told reporters when asked about the deal. “They’re terrific people, and it’s going to be a great company.” Trump’s ties […]
content:
President Donald Trump commented on Skydance‘s acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, completed on Tuesday, by apparently showering praised on its CEO David Ellison and his father Larry.

“It’s going to be a great company,” Trump told reporters when asked about the deal. “They’re terrific people, and it’s going to be a great company.”

Trump’s ties to the Ellisons was an ongoing point of interest in the saga of the $110 billion merger.

Some Democrats contended that the Justice Department greenlit the deal for political reasons, while warning that the Ellisons would steer CNN news coverage in a direction friendlier for the president. When Netflix and Paramount were vying for Warner Bros., Trump had said that he would be involved in the regulatory approval process, before later indicating that he would not.

Watch on Deadline

RELATED: A List Of Major Warner Bros. & Paramount Franchises, Film & TV Titles Coming Together At New Skydance

Trump and the elder Ellison are longtime allies; in March, Trump put him on the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology with other tech-forward execs including Meta founder and CEO Mark Zuckerberg, venture capitalist Marc Andreessen and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.

David Ellison, meanwhile, attended the president’s State of the Union address as a guest of Sen. Lindsey Graham (R-SC). Ellison held a dinner in honor of the Trump White House and the network’s correspondents in advance of last spring’s White House Correspondents’ Dinner, and the Skydance CEO was a guest of the recent White House State Dinner for China’s President Xi Jinping.

RELATED: Skydance CEOs Pressed On Layoffs & Donald Trump Interference As They Outline Future At Town Hall

On Tuesday, the first day of the new company, Ellison told a town hall that CNN would have “complete editorial independence,” and, in a conversation with Anderson Cooper, said that he would shield the network from Trump’s interference and criticism. Ellison also said that he supported CNN’s challenge of Trump’s ban on the outlet from the White House grounds.

Skydance’s settlement of a lawsuit brought by state attorneys general requires that it establish an independent review board to oversee CNN and CBS News, including establishing a set of standards and principles.

RELATED: Skydance Bumps Pay, Extends Contracts For Top Execs; New Bonuses For WBD Brass

RELATED: Skydance Shares Fall In New York Stock Exchange Debut Amid Debt Debate

RELATED: Skydance Credit Rating Cut By Fitch Citing Heavy Debt Load, Integration, Execution Risk

title: Megyn Kelly Tells Olivia Rodrigo to ‘Stick to Singing’ After Speaking Out About Cornell 7 Case: ‘You Don’t Know What the F— You’re Talking About’
summary: Following Olivia Rodrigo’s statement in support of the Jane Doe at the center of the Cornell 7 lawsuit on Sunday, Megyn Kelly is firing off at the singer, calling her a “know-nothing moron” who should “sit down and be quiet.” “Olivia, in sum, you don’t know what the fuck you’re talking about. Shut up and […]
content:
Following Olivia Rodrigo’s statement in support of the Jane Doe at the center of the Cornell 7 lawsuit on Sunday, Megyn Kelly is firing off at the singer, calling her a “know-nothing moron” who should “sit down and be quiet.”

“Olivia, in sum, you don’t know what the fuck you’re talking about. Shut up and stick to singing,” Kelly said on a Monday episode of her YouTube show. “I liked you better when you were in front of a microphone singing your weird little depressing songs.” She continued: “It’s better to keep your mouth shut and let people suspect you’re an idiot than to open it and prove them right. Ever hear that saying? It applies to you, sweetheart… We don’t need the participation of know-nothing morons who have been auto-tuned into fame and suddenly think they have something profound to say on the culture wars.”

The previous day, Rodrigo had shared a post to her Instagram story writing: “Shame on Cornell and on every institution who protects rapists and abusers over women. I stand with Jane Doe. Her bravery reverberates across the country and the crimes against her will not go unpunished. What she lived through matters, and so does the failure of those who could have intervened but chose not to. She deserves answers, consequences, and lasting change.”

Popular on Variety

The Cornell 7 lawsuit refers to the legal document filed by an unnamed Cornell University student who accused seven men of raping and drugging her at a frat house party in October 2024 — and faced no legal consequences. Her lawsuit filed against the university claimed that the school failed to protect her and prevent the alleged assault.

Following an investigation by the university at the time, two of the men were expelled, while the other five received lesser punishment. The lawsuit claims that some of them wrote essays to the school to reduce their disciplinary action, according to her attorney.

Florence Pugh, Mariska Hargitay, Hudson Williams, Josh Gad and more celebrities have used their platforms to condemn the case in recent weeks.

title: Skydance Sets Leadership Across Games, Experiences, Consumer Products and HR
summary: Skydance president Andy Gordon has solidified leadership positions across key areas outside the newly merged company’s TV and film divisions, including games and experiences, products and publishing, HR and global operations. Additionally, Skydance has revealed that Paramount and WBD’s games and experiences divisions will be merged into one team which will oversee projects based on […]
content:
Skydance president Andy Gordon has solidified leadership positions across key areas outside the newly merged company’s TV and film divisions, including games and experiences, products and publishing, HR and global operations.

Additionally, Skydance has revealed that Paramount and WBD’s games and experiences divisions will be merged into one team which will oversee projects based on IP ranging from Paramount’s “Star Trek,” “Mission: Impossible,” “SpongeBob SquarePants,” “South Park,” “Avatar: The Last Airbender” and “The Godfather” to Warner Bros.’ “Harry Potter,” DC Universe, “Mortal Kombat,” “The Matrix,” “Rick and Morty” and “Game of Thrones.”

Notably, this means combining the newly formed Paramount Games Studio with Warner Bros. Games’ internal video game developers, including Avalanche Software (the makers of “Hogwarts Legacy”), NetherRealm Studios, Rocksteady Studios, TT Games and the WB Games teams in Montreal and Boston.

Popular on Variety

In an email sent to staff Tuesday evening, which was obtained by Variety, Gordon announced the following:

Tony Driscoll will be president of games and experiences, in addition to leading corporate strategy and development

Josh Silverman will be president of global products and publishing

Jim Sterner will remain chief people officer and continue to lead HR operations

Jose Turkienicz will continue as president of global operations, including real estate, procurement, and studio operations, with a “focus on simplifying processes and improving service to our businesses so teams can bring ideas to market faster”

Jeff Silberman will be Gordon’s chief of staff in addition to continuing as executive vice president of corporate strategy

“We’re investing in our future growth engines alongside our core ambitions in TV, Film and direct-to-consumer: Games, Experiences, Consumer Products, and Publishing,” Gordon wrote. “These are core pillars of our strategy to build engagement and fandom in both the physical and digital worlds. We want to meet consumers where they watch, play, and engage. At the same time, we see opportunities to build on DC Comics’ storytelling and expand our e-commerce offerings to connect fans with the brands they love.”

Games and experiences chief Driscoll (who was named head of Paramount’s newly launched video game studio in June, a combo of Paramount and Skydance’s gaming assets) laid out early plans for his team in his own memo.

“We immerse our guests in theme parks, resorts, restaurants, retail, studio tours and more. We immerse our players in action, adventure, combat, competition and creativity, from ‘Batman’ to ‘SpongeBob,'” Driscoll wrote. “And no matter your role on this team, you are a creator, builder, operator, and steward of those worlds. We have the opportunity to create amazing spaces where friendships are formed and communities grow. That is only possible because of your hard work and talent. Whether it’s on Zoom or in person, my first priority in the coming weeks is meeting as many of you as I can from LA to London, Montreal to Tokyo, and beyond.”

title: Eddie Redmayne’s Kore-eda Hirokazu Film Is Still Being Scripted, Director Says at Busan
summary: Eddie Redmayne’s upcoming collaboration with Kore-eda Hirokazu is still at the screenplay stage, the Japanese filmmaker said Wednesday at a Busan International Film Festival press conference for his manga adaptation “Look Back.” “Right now, I am writing the script,” Kore-eda said about the Searchlight Pictures film. “I cannot share specific plot details at this stage, […]
content:
Eddie Redmayne‘s upcoming collaboration with Kore-eda Hirokazu is still at the screenplay stage, the Japanese filmmaker said Wednesday at a Busan International Film Festival press conference for his manga adaptation “Look Back.”

“Right now, I am writing the script,” Kore-eda said about the Searchlight Pictures film. “I cannot share specific plot details at this stage, but preparations are progressing smoothly. Please look forward to it.”

The director did not disclose a title. He expects to go public formally next year at the earliest and hopes to bring that film to Busan as well.

Popular on Variety

The festival has kept inviting Kore-eda back since his debut, and the opening ceremony even featured a piece of music named after him. “It is a city and a film festival for which I have exceptionally strong feelings,” he said.

He was joined by “Look Back” cast members Deguchi Natsuki, Makita Aju, Mori Nana and Ishikawa Ruka.

Kore-eda stumbled on the manga in a bookshop rather than through its serial run. “When I read it, I felt a shock like an impact,” he said. “It explored why people write stories, or in my case, why one makes films – that sort of creative impulse, or the heavy burden or karma that artists carry.”

On set, he avoided detailed scene-by-scene instruction and concentrated instead on the hours the four actors spent together and on how the town looked as the light and seasons shifted. “The cast understood that very well, and they appeared in front of the camera as individuals truly living inside that town,” he said.

As soon as the adaptation was confirmed, Kore-eda pushed for 35mm across all four seasons, in line with his longstanding conviction that anything that can be shot on celluloid ought to be. “Because there is no mindset of ‘we can fix it later,’ it creates a healthy tension for the cast and crew,” he said. “When that collective tension gathers, I believe it generates a magnetic field in that shooting location.”

The rotoscoped animation sequence late in the film stems from a single line. After a competition win, Fujino remarks that her dream was to see her manga animated, a comment that temporarily splits the two central characters. Kore-eda said the animation Fujino later makes stands in for a future the pair never got to share.

“Rather than conventional cel animation, rotoscoping sits halfway between live-action and drawn animation,” he said. “Having the characters move within the background art drawn by Kyoko felt like the most suitable form of expression.”

The film opens and closes on shots of Deguchi seen from behind. For the last of these, she said, Kore-eda instructed her, “Show Kyoko through your back.” After a long stretch shooting in Akita with her co-star, Deguchi found herself filming alone. “It felt like she was there, but not there… so with my heart feeling completely empty, I did that shot,” she said.

Makita, who plays Kyoko, is at Busan for the first time. Mori said she had done the Venice red carpet too, though the mood in Korea struck her as different. “There was a huge crowd, so I was nervous, but seeing everyone wave their hands made it so much fun,” she said.

title: Skeet Ulrich Says His ‘Scream’ Arc Couldn’t Be Completed After Melissa Barrera’s Firing: ‘There’s No Billy Loomis’ Without Her
summary: Skeet Ulrich, who starred in 1996’s “Scream” as Billy Loomis and later reprised the role in both 2022’s “Scream” and 2023’s “Scream VI,” has opened up about not being able to complete what he calls his “three-film arc” after his co-star, Melissa Barrera, was fired from the franchise. Speaking with US Weekly, Ulrich explained that […]
content:
Skeet Ulrich, who starred in 1996’s “Scream” as Billy Loomis and later reprised the role in both 2022’s “Scream” and 2023’s “Scream VI,” has opened up about not being able to complete what he calls his “three-film arc” after his co-star, Melissa Barrera, was fired from the franchise.

Speaking with US Weekly, Ulrich explained that he doesn’t see himself returning to the franchise because “without Melissa Barrera and Sam Loomis, there’s no Billy Loomis.” (Barrera played Sam Carpenter, who was revealed to be Loomis’ daughter.) “He was in her head. They had their chance at it and didn’t quite get to complete the three-film arc that they talked to me about.”

After starring in “Scream” and “Scream VI,” Barrera was ousted from the films by “Scream” franchise producer Spyglass due to social media posts criticizing Israel amid the war in Gaza in 2023. At the time, the company said it had “zero tolerance for antisemitism or the incitement of hate in any form, including false references to genocide, ethnic cleansing, Holocaust distortion or anything that flagrantly crosses the line into hate speech.”

Popular on Variety

After the firing, Barrera’s on-screen sister, Jenna Ortega, announced she wouldn’t return for 2026’s “Scream 7.” Neither Barrera nor Ulrich appeared in the recent film, which starred Matthew Lillard, Neve Campbell, Courteney Cox, Isabel May, Jasmin Savoy Brown, Mason Gooding and others.

Last month, Lillard, who starred alongside Ulrich in the original film, admitted he felt “ashamed” for acting in “Scream 7” after Barrera was ousted.

“I went back to do ‘Scream,’ and I got called out. And I’m like, ‘Oh, fuck. That’s brutal,’” he said during a 30th anniversary screening of the original “Scream.” “I feel bad about that. I feel ashamed about that. Because in that moment I was so excited to go back, I didn’t really think about Melissa and that journey. I didn’t say no. I’m embarrassed; that’s the truth… I blew that. I’m on the wrong side of history for that. I still like being in the movie [but] it may not have been the best idea.”

title: Co-Founder Nate Bolotin to Exit XYZ Films After Almost Two Decades With Studio (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Co-founder Nate Bolotin is leaving XYZ Films after almost two decades with the studio, Variety can reveal exclusively. Bolotin started the label in 2008 with partners Nick Spicer and Aram Tertzakian. Since its founding, XYZ has grown into a global film studio, encompassing production, financing, international sales and distribution. “Nate has been a trusted partner […]
content:
Co-founder Nate Bolotin is leaving XYZ Films after almost two decades with the studio, Variety can reveal exclusively.

Bolotin started the label in 2008 with partners Nick Spicer and Aram Tertzakian. Since its founding, XYZ has grown into a global film studio, encompassing production, financing, international sales and distribution.

“Nate has been a trusted partner and friend since the company’s inception,” XYZ Films said in a statement. “Our entire team recognizes and appreciates his contributions over the past eighteen years as we’ve grown from a scrappy start-up into the company that we are today. We’re excited to see what he does next.”

XYZ Films continues to be overseen by Spicer, CEO, Maxime Cottray, COO, and Tertzakian, Head of Creative. Key execs include Guy Danella, Head of Film, Pip Ngo, EVP of Sales & Acquisitions, and Marie Garrett, SVP of Sales & Acquisitions.

Popular on Variety

Upcoming titles from XYZ include “Flesh of the Gods,” with A24, starring Kristen Stewart and Wagner Moura and directed by Panos Cosmatos; “Egg Baby,” with Amazon MGM Studios, starring Ariana Greenblatt and directed by Natalia Anderson; “Banquet,” starring Meghann Fahy and directed by Galder Gaztelu-Urrutia; and “The Girlfriend,” starring Glenn Howerton, Meghann Fahy and Rosario Dawson and directed by Natalie Morales.

Previous XYZ works include Gareth Evans’ “The Raid” (2012) and “The Raid 2” (2014); Karyn Kusama’s “The Invitation” (2016); Babak Anvari’s “Under the Shadow” (2016); Macon Blair’s “I Don’t Feel at Home in This World Anymore” (2017); Panos Cosmatos’ “Mandy” (2018); Joe “Arctic” (2019); and Matt Johnson’s “BlackBerry” (2023).

title: Paramount Pictures Co-Chairs Josh Greenstein & Dana Goldberg Say In Day 1 Memo That Film Divisions Will Operate Independently
summary: Paramount Pictures Co-Chairs Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein sent out a Day 1 memo to the troops at the Paramount and Warner Bros. Motion Picture units. Among the priorities, we understand, is keeping legacies of both studios alive. In the memo, Goldberg and Greenstein say they see themselves as “stewards of two of the most […]
content:
Paramount Pictures Co-Chairs Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein sent out a Day 1 memo to the troops at the Paramount and Warner Bros. Motion Picture units.

Among the priorities, we understand, is keeping legacies of both studios alive. In the memo, Goldberg and Greenstein say they see themselves as “stewards of two of the most storied studios in Hollywood history.”

They also explained that the companies’ respective film divisions will operate independently.

RELATED: James Gunn & Peter Safran To Stay At DC Studios After Paramount-Warner Bros Merger

“We have organized our film divisions around the movies themselves. Paramount Pictures and Warner Bros. Pictures will continue to build and release their slate of films separately, under those brands. This means that each Warner Bros. Pictures or Paramount Pictures film you see will carry its respective logo. They are the cornerstone labels and will remain the homes for our largest commercial and filmmaker-driven projects. DC Studios, New Line Cinema and Paramount Primal will continue as distinct labels with specific mandates. Our animation and specialty labels, including Republic Pictures and Warner Bros. Clockwork, will also operate independently.”

Watch on Deadline

A more immediate priority for the duo — who have been working on getting the Paramount motion picture unit into financially reasonable shape — is getting under the hood of Warner Bros.

RELATED: New Line Boss Richard Brener Poised To Jump To Merged Paramount-Warner Bros – The Dish

Here is the full text of their memo:

Dear teammates,



Today marks Day One of a new chapter, and we are proud to share it with all of you. It’s an immense privilege to make movies, and an even greater honor to do so as the stewards of two of the most storied studios in Hollywood history. We take that responsibility seriously and have enormous respect for the people, work and relationships that have made these studios what they are today.



At the heart of that legacy is a simple belief that movies are best seen together, on a big screen. A century later, that human connection is still alive. Going to the movies is a communal tradition, where a story becomes a moment we carry together. That tradition is thriving, and David Ellison is making one of the biggest investments in its future. We believe in it, and we are all in.



Our mission is to build on these studios’ legacies as homes for the greatest filmmakers and storytellers. We will embrace their vision, back it with the best marketing and distribution in the business, and keep creating cultural moments that shape generations. That means taking bold swings, alongside crowd-pleasers, with a steady willingness to push boundaries.



We have organized our film divisions around the movies themselves. Paramount Pictures and Warner Bros. Pictures will continue to build and release their slate of films separately, under those brands. This means that each Warner Bros. Pictures or Paramount Pictures film you see will carry its respective logo. They are the cornerstone labels and will remain the homes for our largest commercial and filmmaker-driven projects. DC Studios, New Line Cinema and Paramount Primal will continue as distinct labels with specific mandates. Our animation and specialty labels, including Republic Pictures and Warner Bros. Clockwork, will also operate independently.



We won’t pretend a combination of this size comes without change. We know you will have questions, and we will respond to as many as we can, though we won’t be able to answer everything today. In the months ahead, we will spend time with the teams across both studios, listening, learning and sharing updates along the way. Your experience and perspective will be essential in shaping what comes next. What we can say with confidence is that our purpose is simple, and it starts with the work in front of us.



Our collective job is to give teams and filmmakers the support they need to do their best work, and to make movies that entertain and endure. The opportunity ahead of us is extraordinary, and we look forward to building on everything you have accomplished.



Together, we are going to build something special.



Long live the movies,



Dana & Josh

The missive comes just hours after Skydance co-CEO David Ellison sent his own memo.

title: ‘Dancing With The Stars’ Recap: Lots Of Breakthroughs On Mariah Carey Night Stiffen Competition
summary: SPOILER ALERT! This post contains details from Tuesday night’s episode of Dancing with the Stars. We’re officially a month into Season 35 of Dancing with the Stars, and the contestants are starting to feel the pressure of the competition. After Taylor Hanson and Britt Stewart were eliminated last week (which shook the remaining couples awake […]
content:
SPOILER ALERT! This post contains details from Tuesday night’s episode of Dancing with the Stars.

We’re officially a month into Season 35 of Dancing with the Stars, and the contestants are starting to feel the pressure of the competition.

After Taylor Hanson and Britt Stewart were eliminated last week (which shook the remaining couples awake as they were definitely not the worst ones by a mile), the competitors are all taking on Mariah Carey in Week 4.

Reality star Ciara Miller with Brandon Armstrong. The reality star really wanted to earn some 7s for her jazz routine to “Emotions” and prove she’s meant to last in this competition. Carrie Ann Inaba called it her “best dance so far, my dear.” Get those 7s, girl! SCORE: 21 out of 30

Watch on Deadline

Paralympian Ezra Frech with Daniella Karagach. These two came out swinging with another fiery performance, this time dancing a rumba to “Anytime You Need a Friend.” Derek Hough was thoroughly impressed: “It was seriously sophisticated. It was.” SCORE: 24 out of 30

Actor Harry Shum Jr. with Jenna Johnson. They’re looking for another set of solid scores from the judges for their tango to “It’s Like That.” This week, Jenna goes on the Grey’s Anatomy set with her celeb partner to practice in between takes. Fun fact: Harry danced in the original music video for this song, too. “A red hot tango from a man on a mission! Sharp as a knife. So intense. I mean, it gave me whiplash!” Bruno Tonioli says. Bonus points for the Glee reunion with former DWTS champ Amber Riley back in the ballroom to sing for this one. SCORE: 24 out of 30

Actress Jenna Dewan with Val Chmerkovskiy. Jenna is frustrated by her feedback from the judges, but she wants to take their critiques seriously. This week, she wants to focus on showing a softer and slower side to her dancing with a rumba to “My All.” Watch out Season 35, Jenna Dewan found her groove! All Derek Hough could do was stand up and clap. “All I have to say is: There she is.” SCORE: 24 out of 30

Reality star Tyler Cameron with Sharna Burgess. Tyler managed to skate by last week thanks to Taylor’s elimination, but he seems to know he needs to kick things into high gear if he wants to make it any further in the competition. This week, he and Sharna danced a foxtrot to “#Beautiful.” Color, well, nearly everyone surprised! The man can move! “The improvement is incredible. You should be proud of yourself,” Bruno tells him. SCORE: 21 out of 30

Reality star Maura Higgins with Mark Ballas. The Traitors duo is finding their groove, and Maura is settling into her clear natural affinity for dance. This week, they are taking on a waltz to “If It’s Over.” She’s already danced in frame, but now she wants to improve and go for higher scores. “I feel like right now the world needs that kind of beauty!” Carrie Ann exclaimed. SCORE: 25 out of 30 (a 9 from Carrie Ann! Maura falling to the ground in disbelief says it all.)

Late-night sidekick Guillermo Rodriguez with Whitney Carson. These two took a trip to New York City for rehearsals this week, since Guillermo is there for his day job. They are dancing a samba to “Obsessed.” As Witney says, “nothing can really prepare you for the samba.” He’s really trying, though. And hey, the steps he did (few as there were) were in time! “Listen, that wasn’t quite a samba, but it was 100% Guillermo,” Derek says. SCORE: 15 out of 30

Savannah Bananas midfielder Jackson Olson with Emma Slater. Jackson took a little break from rehearsals this week to celebrate his birthday, but he’s still putting his all into coming back strong after some lukewarm feedback from the judges in Week 3. He’s performing a waltz to “Without You.” There must be something in the air this week, because he looked like a completely different dancer. “I can see you almost for the first time,” Bruno tells him. SCORE: 21 out of 30

Actress Tatyana Ali with Jan Ravnik. The Fresh Prince star is living ut a childhood dream dancing to Mariah Carey. And she’s got the in-the-know pro this week, because Jan has toured with the pop star. They’re doing a jazz dance to “Fantasy.” After last week, can anyone be surprised that she kills it? Carrie Ann wanted her to have more energy for a jazz routine. Derek and Bruno agree. “But overall, I just love seeing what you’re doing,” Derek says. SCORE: 20 out of 30

Comedian and podcaster Connor Wood with Rylee Arnold. Rylee, Connor isn’t sure if you’ve noticed, but you tend to include grinding choreography in all of your routines. Well, the tradition continues this week, because they’re dancing a rumba to “Touch My Body.” I mean, what’s a girl to do? Unfortunately, the hips were not moving, but he did do a nice worm. “There’s a lot of moments where you’re playing it safe,” Derek says. Bruno loved it. “Frisky!” SCORE: 19 out of 30

Actress Julia Stiles with Ezra Sosa. Julia is riding high after receiving her highest scores last week. She’s really got to impress this week with a Viennese waltz to “Vision of Love” if she wants to keep the positive momentum going. “For me, that was a breakthrough,” Carrie Ann said. Well, ok then! SCORE: 21 out of 30

Olympian Amber Glenn with Pasha Pashkov. It’s a lot of pressure to close out the night, especially as the couple who walked away with the first 8s of the season and tied at the top of the leaderboard last week. This time, they’re dancing a rumba to “Hero.” Pasha calls the dance “the ultimate test” of their synchronicity as a couple. Turns out, they didn’t need to worry at all. “You never lost the ability to fill the room,” Bruno says. SCORE: 23 out of 30

Who goes home?

The competition is getting tough, so there’s not very many weeks that Guillermo can keep getting away with this, but somehow Ciara Miller and Brandon Armstrong go home on Tuesday night.

Next week is Super Bowl Night. Stay tuned to see what that means.

title: HBO Max And Paramount+ Will Eventually Combine After “Short-Term” Bundling Phase, David Ellison Says
summary: Skydance chairman and CEO David Ellison sees HBO Max and Paramount+ combining into a single streaming service over time after a “short-term” phase as separate-but-bundled services. “Long-term, the plan is basically to bring them together,” Ellison said at a press event held Tuesday on the Paramount lot to mark the closing of the merger of […]
content:
Skydance chairman and CEO David Ellison sees HBO Max and Paramount+ combining into a single streaming service over time after a “short-term” phase as separate-but-bundled services.

“Long-term, the plan is basically to bring them together,” Ellison said at a press event held Tuesday on the Paramount lot to mark the closing of the merger of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery. “It’ll take a period of time to do that. So, I think in the immediate [term], you will see them operated separately, with things like bundling or things that you’ll be able to see accelerated in the relatively short term. I can’t be specific about that yet today.”

Already, the company has managed to bring together the tech stacks of Paramount+, BET+ and Pluto TV, a shift that subscribers and viewers do not notice. Ellison credited “the way AI technology and other things have progressed” for providing a boost to that process. He stopped short of saying outright that those advancements could simplify the cumbersome process of uniting streaming services into a single product. And he also did not address the pricing or strategy for consumer adoption and retention of a single service with multiple branded tiers, a puzzle that general-entertainment services have to solve as they gain scale.

Watch on Deadline

Ellison said the centralization of tech stacks after the merger close will happen “as quickly as possible,” noting that the project was completed “in record time” after Skydance took over Paramount in August 2025.

Ellison’s projection, which came a few hours after the close of the Skydance merger, seemed to point in a different strategic direction than recent comments by Casey Bloys, the head of HBO and HBO Max Content who is now Co-Chair and Chief Content Officer, Skydance DT. Bloys hinted that bundling would be the focus given the distinct subscriber bases of the two services, which combined have more than 200 million global subscribers. A slide deck released by Skydance earlier this week included images of both streamers, indicating at least they would each continue independently, at least for now.

RELATED: Post-Merger Skydance Keeping Both HBO Max & Paramount+ Streaming Brands

Across the streaming landscape, a number of players have found it complex and expensive to meld two services into one. Disney has been chipping away at a long-term positioning of Disney+ as its mothership and Hulu programming migrating there behind a home-screen tile. Sometimes, viewer feedback can cause a rethink, as was the case when WarnerMedia merged with Discovery Communications in 2022. Initially, executives pursued a plan to merge unscripted and lifestyle service Discovery+ with HBO Max under the new umbrella brand Max. Warner Bros. Discovery stepped back from that plan and also reversed the Max rebrand amid viewer and partner confusion and resistance.

title: Skydance Co-Boss Ynon Kreiz On When ‘Barbie 2’ Will Be A Go: “Too Early To Talk About That.” However, There’s Hope
summary: At this afternoon’s presser for the newly-merged Skydance, we asked when Barbie 2 would be a go project. “Too early to talk about that,” was the official response from former Mattel CEO Ynon Kriez, newly-named Skydance co-CEO. Kriez was involved in the movie based on Mattel’s famed blonde doll. That Warner Bros. pic is the […]
content:
At this afternoon’s presser for the newly-merged Skydance, we asked when Barbie 2 would be a go project.

“Too early to talk about that,” was the official response from former Mattel CEO Ynon Kriez, newly-named Skydance co-CEO. Kriez was involved in the movie based on Mattel’s famed blonde doll. That Warner Bros. pic is the highest grossing in the studio’s history, with $1.44B at the global box office.

There was high drama before Paramount married Warner Bros as to whether the sequel was bound for a green light. Word was that former WBD CEO David Zaslav balked at paying increased wads of money for the CAA-repped Barbie team of stars Margot Robbie, Ryan Gosling, director Greta Gerwig, and her spouse and co-writer Noah Baumbach. In the meantime, a first-look deal was made with Baumbach but at Warners specialty label, Clockwork (which were told at the time didn’t encompass Barbie 2). There was a ticking clock as the film rights would revert back to Mattel at the end of the year and the toymaker would have to start from scratch with a frosh project — and frosh talent.

Cooler heads are now prevailing, and it is day one at the new Skydance. Kriez is now on the other side of the equation, and one of several priorities for Skydance Motion Picture Group chairs Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein is getting into the weeds on Barbie 2. That, and the 36 Warner Bros dated theatrical releases they’re inheriting and more. The duo need to figure out what state of development myriad projects are in, read: the Baz Luhrmann untitled film is not shooting yet and reportedly in pre-production. That was another audacious big auteur swing from the previous Warners motion picture administration. A new draft is in the wings for Weapons prequel, Gladys, but it’s in need of a director if it’s going to make a September 2028 release date.

Watch on Deadline

As far as Barbie 2 goes, stay tuned. Those heels aren’t necessarily made for walking. If there’s a takeaway from the new Ellison merger it’s to honor the legacies of each studios. Not erase them.

title: Chris Colfer On Returning For ‘Glee’ Revival: “I Know Nothing & Have Heard Absolutely Nothing”
summary: Chris Colfer is opening up about whether he would return to the Glee revival Ryan Murphy recently teased. The actor who played Kurt Hummel throughout the show’s six-season run was asked about the revival but said he didn’t know anything about it yet. “I know nothing and have heard absolutely nothing,” Colfer said in an […]
content:
Chris Colfer is opening up about whether he would return to the Glee revival Ryan Murphy recently teased.

The actor who played Kurt Hummel throughout the show’s six-season run was asked about the revival but said he didn’t know anything about it yet.

“I know nothing and have heard absolutely nothing,” Colfer said in an interview with Bustle. “I wish I did. It was a really tough show to do, and it would be really hard to do it now that Naya [Rivera] is gone. But I do know that Glee fans would probably come after me with pitchforks and jazz hands if I said no.”

Glee has lost several co-stars over the years, including Cory Monteith, Mark Salling, and Naya Rivera. Murphy recently revealed that he had “just finished” a script for a reboot and noted that the cast was “very enthusiastic” about the potential revival.

Watch on Deadline

“Well, funny you ask, cause I just finished the script an hour ago,” he told Entertainment Tonight. “So, we have a script. Brad [Falchuk], Ian [Brennan] and I, who wrote all the first two seasons, have written something. I’ve been in touch with around 10 of the original cast members. It’s very sweet, and they all had a lot of questions, but they all were very enthusiastic about the idea.”

Murphy added, “Nobody’s read it, so I don’t know, we’ll see. I vowed to myself that I wanted to write a couple of them to see what people think, particularly the cast, cause we were very close when we were making it.”

The Glee reboot doesn’t have a series order and is only an idea the creative team is developing for now.

title: Singapore Film Festival Stands by ‘The Assassin(s)’ After Korean Conservatives Demand It Be Dropped
summary: The Singapore International Film Festival (SGIFF) is keeping Hur Jin-ho’s “The Assassin(s)” as its opening film, a day after all 109 lawmakers of South Korea’s conservative People Power Party (PPP) asked the festival to pull it. The festival made no mention of the PPP in a statement issued Wednesday, saying only that it was aware […]
content:
The Singapore International Film Festival (SGIFF) is keeping Hur Jin-ho‘s “The Assassin(s)” as its opening film, a day after all 109 lawmakers of South Korea’s conservative People Power Party (PPP) asked the festival to pull it.

The festival made no mention of the PPP in a statement issued Wednesday, saying only that it was aware of the debate surrounding the film.

“The film was selected through SGIFF’s independent curatorial process for its artistic merit and contribution to contemporary Asian cinema,” the festival said.

SGIFF noted that the filmmakers have called the film an imagined story that mixes real events with invented characters, and that they have denied any intention to settle history, misrepresent facts or push a political agenda. The festival said it would screen the title on those terms. It also cited Korean Film Council data showing the film has passed roughly 2.5 million admissions at home and posted seat occupancy of around 47% over the Chuseok holiday.

Popular on Variety

“The Assassin(s),” which world premiered at the Toronto Film Festival and was second runner-up for the festival’s international People’s Choice award, will open SGIFF on Oct. 21. Hur is due to attend with cast members Shim Eun-kyung and Park Sung-hoon.

The PPP letter, sent Tuesday under the name of floor leader Jeong Jeom-sik and addressed to SGIFF executive director Jeremy Chua, expressed deep regret over the selection and urged the festival to reverse it immediately. It argued that by leaving room to read then-President Park Chung-hee as linked to the killing of his wife, the film distorts history “in a manner that runs deeply counter to public sentiment in the Republic of Korea.”

The letter cited a survey of 1,017 adults in which 58.2% called the film a distortion of history and 27.6% considered it a matter of creative freedom. It also pointed to objections from Park Ji-man, chairman of EG Group and the son of Park and Yuk, and to demands from foundations tied to the couple for an apology and an end to screenings. Jeong wrote that the party respects artistic freedom and festival independence, but argued that presenting the film with the weight of an opening gala to overseas audiences unfamiliar with modern Korean history could carry the damage seen in Korea to the rest of the world.

The row has already reshaped the film’s festival run at home. On Oct. 1, the Busan International Film Festival (BIFF) called off “Actors House: Lee Min-ho,” a career conversation with the film’s star, citing unavoidable circumstances. A day later, distributor Hive Media Corp. withdrew the cast and crew from all BIFF appearances, including the opening ceremony and an outdoor stage greeting, on safety grounds. That day, a conservative group also said it would picket actor Yoo Hae-jin’s home every day until the end of the month.

The Producers Guild of Korea (PGK) and the Cinematographers Guild of Korea (CGK) issued separate statements that evening. The PGK said the dispute had gone past criticism of the film and now amounted to threats against everyone who worked on it, from the producers and director to the cast and crew.

“Exposing the personal details and family relationships of individuals who participated in a project, or exerting pressure on their normal activities, goes far beyond legitimate criticism and can never be justified,” the PGK said.

“The Assassin(s)” opened in Korea on Sept. 23. Yoo stars as a police inspector who witnesses the Aug. 15, 1974 shooting at the National Theater, where Yuk Young-soo, the wife of Park Chung-hee, was killed during Liberation Day celebrations, and goes on to lead the investigation. Park Hae-il plays the head of a newspaper’s social affairs desk, and Lee Min-ho a rookie reporter. The official inquiry blamed Mun Se-gwang alone, saying he acted on instructions from Pyongyang and Chongryon, the pro-North Korean residents’ association in Japan. Hur’s film declines to name a culprit, and its detractors argue the open ending points to Park or his government.

Lee Jong-bae, a former PPP Seoul city councilor, has asked Seoul police to investigate Hur, Hive Media Corp. CEO Kim Won-kuk and writers Kwon Ki-jun and Lee Ji-min for defamation. PPP lawmakers also tried to summon Hur to testify at the annual parliamentary audit, a move the Democratic Party blocked on creative freedom grounds.

In a Sept. 28 statement, the producers said: “Nowhere in the film is any specific individual defined as being behind the incident, and the film’s hypotheses and dramatic settings are not presented as historical fact.”

The Directors Guild of Korea (DGK) has also come to the defense of the filmmakers, arguing that the backlash has spilled over from the film to the lives and livelihoods of the people who made it.

“Cinema must carry on as a place where different ideas and voices meet, even when it stirs up debate,” the DGK said. “If that freedom disappears, it becomes hard for new films and new stories to be born.”

title: Brazilian Cinema at Risk: A Report From Watching the Presidential Elections From the Rio Film Festival
summary: RIO DE JANEIRO, Brazil – Inside one of the refrigerated rooms of the Armazém da Utopia, the beautiful portside warehouse where the Rio Film Festival’s RioMarket takes place, renowned director Marcelo Gomes lifts his hand and makes an “L” sign. The room bursts into applause. Gomes had been sitting for over an hour alongside “The […]
content:
RIO DE JANEIRO, Brazil – Inside one of the refrigerated rooms of the Armazém da Utopia, the beautiful portside warehouse where the Rio Film Festival’s RioMarket takes place, renowned director Marcelo Gomes lifts his hand and makes an “L” sign. The room bursts into applause. Gomes had been sitting for over an hour alongside “The Blue Trail” actor Rodrigo Santoro and Rio Film Festival director Ilda Santiago by the time the upcoming presidential elections came up.

It was Friday morning, two days before the polls were due to open, and the room had flooded with people sporting Lula stickers attached to their T-shirts, the bright shades of red popping against the dark grey of the walls. That is because Lula, Brazil’s current president and campaigning candidate, had been parading the centre of Rio just a few hundred meters away from the port. As the hundreds of thousands of people made their way down the narrow roads following the politician, a few rerouted into the industry event, still carrying big flags and with faces lit up with hope.

Popular on Variety

“To me, the greatest diplomatic tool – the greatest instrument for countries and governments to understand one another and come to the table with a different perspective – is cinema,” says Santiago on stage while alerting the audience to the importance of strong public policies as the foundation of a healthy film industry. “I view cinema as a powerful diplomatic weapon.”

Having one of the most important presidential elections in the history of Brazil take place during the country’s largest film festival makes for a very particular encounter. Brazil, one of the greatest cinema nations in the world, has reaffirmed its international reach and success in grand fashion in the last two years: Walter Salles’ “I’m Still Here” won the country its first Oscar in 2025, with Kleber Mendonça Filho’s “The Secret Agent” bringing Brazil back to the glitzy awards earlier this year after picking up two prizes at the 2025 Cannes Film Festival. The sentiment has been palpable in festivals and markets around the world: Brazil is on the up and up. It is the country to bet on.

But this success, of course, has not happened in a miraculous silo. Brazil’s renewed industry is the product of Lula’s public policies. The president is perhaps the most culture-and arts-focused in the history of the country, having hosted regular screenings of Brazilian films at the presidential residency in Brasília and investing heavily in the country’s film sector following four years of a Jair Bolsonaro government that almost immediately did nothing to counteract a court judgement’s stripping away of near all public support for cinema.

“Bacurau” Photo Cinemascópio

Bolsonaro’s presidency was confirmed mere months before Mendonça Filho’s “Bacurau” and Karim Aïnouz’s “The Invisible Life of Eurídice Gusmão” both picked up awards at the Cannes Film Festival, a moment that could have pushed the country’s cinema to a rise similar to the one we have seen in the last two years. The government that came soon after brought it all to a screeching, heavily consequential halt. Soon after taking over the presidency, Bolsonaro cut the budgets for the National Cinema Agency (ANCINE) and the Audiovisual Sector Fund (FSA) by nearly 43%. Before the COVID-19 pandemic that further accentuated the sectorial crisis, the Bolsonaro government was behind an 18-month freeze of public funds for the national agency.

Conversely, once Lula was reelected in 2022, he pledged an investment of R$1.6 billion ($298 million) to support the national production of film and television, with federal funding targeting local audiovisual production to boost both the domestic and international markets. Lula’s government focused on tax incentives and subsidies, and installed cinema screen quotas to support the exhibition of Brazilian films in national cinemas. The results are staggering: last year, an Oxford Economics study commissioned by the Motion Picture Association revealed that the Brazilian audiovisual industry generated over 58% more jobs than the automotive industry, generating over 600,000 direct and indirect jobs.

Now, having experienced a reality where public policies contribute to a thriving industry, local producers, filmmakers, and film workers are faced with a devastating scenario. Last night, in the tightest presidential race in the history of Brazil, Lula took second place to Jair Bolsonaro’s son, Flávio, the former gathering 45.16% of valid votes against the latter’s 47.03%.

The future for national cinema is bleak under a potential Flávio Bolsonaro presidency, with the candidate vowing to mimic virtually all of his father’s policies—and tighten some even further. The Senator is also currently under investigation by the Federal Police for alleged money laundering, tax evasion, and corruption related to the financing of Cyrus Nowrasteh’s “Dark Horse,” an English-language biopic about former president Bolsonaro starring “The Passion of the Christ” actor Jim Caviezel as the far-right politician.

Authorities are currently looking at around R$61 million ($12 million) in funds provided by Daniel Vorcaro, the owner of Brazil’s Banco Master, to finance the film. Leaked messages show Flávio Bolsonaro himself directly negotiating payments with Vorcaro to fund the inflated project. Vorcaro is currently in prison, accused of multi-million financial fraud. He was detained in early March after a judge cited “strong indication” that he attempted to bribe a former central bank director.

Films playing at this year’s edition of the Rio Film Festival have tried to grasp the dire effects of the first Bolsonaro administration. Miguel Antunes Ramos “Dragons” is a portrayal of the images that have shaped Jair Bolsonaro’s political myth, from his early days on YouTube to the end of his term. João Paulo Cuenca’s “144 – Apocalypse Not” sees the director go on a vast road trip across the country in the aftermath posting a satiric tweet about the former president that resulted in 144 lawsuits and hundreds of thousands of death threats from the extreme right-wing movement within the Evangelical church. Dandara Ferreira’s “Anatomy of Chaos” offers unparalleled access to the Brazilian Senate to chronicle the high-profile congressional investigation on the federal government’s handling of and omissions during the COVID-19 pandemic.

When they were scheduled to play in Rio, they were seen as an encapsulation of a nefarious past the country was ready to move away from. Now, as they first meet audiences, they feel a stark premonition.

Karim Aïnouz and Carol Duarte at the Rio Film Festival, courtesy of Cristina Granato

The day before the elections, Aïnouz declared his vote for Lula while on stage at the Rio Film Festival to present “Rosebush Pruning.” The Brazilian director began a pro-Lula chant at the end of his speech, which mentioned the key role of public policies in fomenting his lauded career. As one walked the corridors of Armazém da Utopia ahead of polls opening, the feeling was still one of hope. On Monday morning, however, a visible veil of grief and gloom took over the previous sheen.

“The possible return to power by the same group that governed the country between 2019 and 2022 is a catastrophe,” veteran producer Paula Cosenza, head of label Trema, tells Variety. “The far-right candidate questions the legitimacy of artistic creation, academic knowledge, science, and the free exercise of the press, becoming a concrete threat to democracy. The previous experience left as a legacy the complete paralysis of the audiovisual sector, cuts in funding for public universities, in research, and a toll of more than 700,000 deaths due to COVID-19 in the pandemic. Cultural public policies should be state policies, but in Brazil, they seem to be government policies.”

Gomes echoes that thought, adding that the national audiovisual industry is of “great economic importance for Brazil.” “It is an industry recognized internationally, and that has reaped several major awards in recent years. An eventual change into a government that does not value culture can put all of that at risk.”

Ricardo Alves Jr., whose “The French Teacher” just premiered to acclaim in San Sebastián and is now playing in Rio, says he is “saddened” to realize how the semi-dystopian, conservative reality of his thriller is edging closer to real life in his home country. “Last night can only be seen as a horror film, watching the advancement of the far-right in the Congress, Senate and state governments,” he says.

“To elect Lula in the second round is essential to create a barrier against the total destruction of conquered rights, whether in education, human rights, or culture,” he adds. “The project that the extreme right presents is total destruction. Something even worse than 2018 is coming, when artistic production was severely attacked.”

It is poignant to be writing this report from the Armazém da Utopia, literally translated as the Warehouse of Utopia. It is here, with eyes turned towards the still possible, the still beating dream of a thriving industry, that the market is nurturing itself with hope as Brazil heads for a tense, future-defining second round in the polls.

title: The New Kindle Is Down to $100 for Amazon Prime Big Deals Day
summary: There are plenty of flashy tablets to shop during Prime Big Deals Day, but for anyone whose summer goals include finally finishing the stack of books on their nightstand, the newest Kindle release might be the smarter buy. The 2024 Amazon Kindle, available in black and the popular Matcha green, is down to an unbeatable […]
content:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

There are plenty of flashy tablets to shop during Prime Big Deals Day, but for anyone whose summer goals include finally finishing the stack of books on their nightstand, the newest Kindle release might be the smarter buy.

The 2024 Amazon Kindle, available in black and the popular Matcha green, is down to an unbeatable $103 today — the cheapest we’ve ever seen it. The device is Amazon’s lightest and most compact Kindle, but still packs in the core features most readers actually need: a crisp 6-inch glare-free display, 16 GB of storage, USB-C charging, dark mode and a front light that Amazon says is 25% brighter at its maximum setting than the previous model.

ALL-TIME LOW PRICE Amazon Kindle 16 GB (newest model) $103.99 $149.99 31% off Buy Now On Amazon

The biggest selling point is portability. The Kindle measures 6.2 x 4.3 x 0.32 inches and weighs just 5.56 ounces, making it small enough to slip into a purse, carry-on, beach tote or jacket pocket. Unlike an iPad or Fire tablet, the Kindle is built specifically for reading, with a matte, glare-free display that more closely resembles paper than a traditional screen. That means it is easier to use outdoors, in bed or on a plane, without the distractions of texts, email alerts and social media apps.

Popular on Variety

The screen is also sharper than casual readers might expect from Amazon’s cheapest Kindle. The 6-inch display has a 300 ppi resolution, the same pixel density found on pricier Kindle models, so text looks clean and book-like rather than fuzzy or tablet-y. The adjustable front light makes it usable at night, while dark mode flips the page to a black background with white text for lower-light reading.

This version comes with 16 GB of storage, which Amazon says can hold thousands of books. For most readers, that is more than enough — especially since Amazon content also comes with free cloud storage. Battery life is another major advantage over a traditional tablet: Amazon says a single charge lasts up to six weeks, based on 30 minutes of reading per day with wireless off and the light set to 13. It charges over USB-C, reaching a full charge in about four hours from a computer or about two hours with a 9W USB power adapter.

Shop Amazon’s Prime Big Deals Day 2026 Kindle deal here.

title: ITV Studios Unveils Mipcom Drama Slate Led by Lunar Thriller ‘First Woman,’ and a Further Four New Titles, Including Steven Moffat’s ‘Number 10’ (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: ITV Studios has unveiled its drama slate for Mipcom, led by lunar thriller “First Woman,” and a further four new titles, including Steven Moffat’s workplace drama “Number 10.” Among the talent heading for the distributor’s Cannes showcase are Luke Evans, Richard Armitage, Adrian Dunbar, Lauren Lyle and Emmy-winning “Sherlock” writer Moffat. Evans, whose credits include […]
content:
ITV Studios has unveiled its drama slate for Mipcom, led by lunar thriller “First Woman,” and a further four new titles, including Steven Moffat’s workplace drama “Number 10.” Among the talent heading for the distributor’s Cannes showcase are Luke Evans, Richard Armitage, Adrian Dunbar, Lauren Lyle and Emmy-winning “Sherlock” writer Moffat.

Evans, whose credits include “Nine Perfect Strangers,” “Murder Mystery” and “The Pembrokeshire Murders,” stars in World Productions’ psychological thriller “The Party”; Armitage, known for “Missing You,” “Red Eye” and “Fool Me Once,” leads in Eagle Eye Drama’s series “Winter”; Dunbar, who appeared in “Ridley” and “Inside No. 9,” is in the smash-hit police procedural “Line of Duty”; Lyle, from “Outlander” and “Vigil,” is the star of “Karen Pirie”; and Moffat, a BAFTA winner for “Doctor Who,” is coming with Hartswood Films’ “Number 10.”

The New Launches

The latest additions to the scripted slate feature the thriller “First Woman,” a co-production of Mammoth Screen and Alcon Entertainment in co-production with ZDF, starring Andrea Riseborough, Ashley Walters, Alex Hassell and Jennifer Ehle, following a female astronaut who mysteriously goes missing on the Moon, alongside the witty drama “Number 10,” set inside one of the most famous addresses in the world, featuring an all-star ensemble cast including Rafe Spall, Jenna Coleman and Katherine Kelly.

Popular on Variety

“Winter” Courtesy of ITV Studios

They are joined by gripping procedural “Winter,” based on the hit French drama “Balthazar,” starring a gifted yet unconventional pathologist in Bristol, played by Armitage, and World Productions’ suspenseful adaptation of Elizabeth Day’s bestselling novel “The Party,” launching on ITV on Oct. 11, and starring Tom Cullen alongside Evans, as well as co-star Sarah Solemani, who also pens the scripts.

Blockbuster Returners

Returning fan favorites on the slate include a trio of World Productions hits: police procedural “Line of Duty,” which is the most-watched U.K. TV drama of the 21st century, returning for its highly anticipated seventh season with Martin Compston, Vicky McClure and Adrian Dunbar reuniting, and Robert Carlyle joining the all-star cast; propulsive thriller “Vigil,” starring Suranne Jones and Rose Leslie, which is set in the Arctic Circle for its third instalment; and the cold-case detective drama “Karen Pirie,” adapted from celebrated crime writer Val McDermid’s bestselling series of novels. Completing the lineup is the third season of BBC’s biggest scripted launch of 2026 to date, with episode one from Season 2 attracting 9.1 million viewers, “Ludwig.” From Big Talk Studios, the International Emmy Award-winning detective drama, starring David Mitchell and Anna Maxwell Martin, follows a genius puzzle setter navigating life as a police consultant.

Iconic Franchises

ITV Studios has revealed that all four original seasons of Hartswood Films’ globally loved iconic award-winning “Sherlock” (2010-2017) have now joined the ITV Studios sales catalog. This fast-paced reimagining of the Arthur Conan Doyle classic stars BAFTA winners Benedict Cumberbatch, Martin Freeman and Andrew Scott, from creators Moffatt and Mark Gatiss.

Tom Clark, exec VP, global sales and commercial strategy at ITV Studios, said: “Our slate presents the very best in world-class storytelling, anchored by our ambitious new lunar thriller ‘First Woman,’ with a story that couldn’t be more timely and production qualities that are truly out of this world, in every sense. When it comes to crime and thrillers, I believe we have one of, if not the best lineup of any studio, with new and gripping titles like ‘The Party’ and ‘Winter,’ alongside blockbuster returners such as ‘Line of Duty’ and ‘Vigil.’”

Variety spoke to Julie Meldal-Johnsen, executive VP global content and content strategy at ITV Studios, about the drama slate.

Speaking about “Number 10” she said, “It’s absolutely fantastic. I think U.K. and global audiences are in for a real treat, and that’s not just sales spin. It’s an absolute delight. Steven’s scripts are utterly brilliant, sharp, witty, pacey. The cast is just fantastic.”

Regarding “Winter,” she said, “They’ve done an incredible job. It looks gorgeous. It’s stylish. It’s pacey. Richard Armitage plays this very brilliant forensic pathologist. It’s a case of the week. He uses his skills. He teams up with the local police force to solve a case.
