content:
“Anna Pigeon” has been renewed for Season 2 at USA Network, Variety has learned.

The drama series originally debuted on the basic cabler on Aug. 7, with the Season 1 finale set to air on Oct. 9. The show is based on Nevada Barr’s Anna Pigeon book series.

“It’s been really thrilling to see audiences fall in love with Anna and come to the park every week,” said series showrunner Morwyn Brebner. “We’re so grateful to our cast and crew who brought Nevada Barr’s iconic world to life with such heart and passion; we cannot wait to get back outside for season two.”

The series stars Tracy Spiridakos as Anna Pigeon, along with Paulina Alexis, Ronnie Rowe, Tricia Helfer, Kim Coates, Crystle Lightning, Cooper Levy, Manuel Rodriguez-Saenz, Ryan Northcott, Nikki Rae Hallow, Jordan Sledz, and Melanie Scrofano.

Popular on Variety

The Season 1 logline states that the show follows Pigeon, “a former city slicker who became a park ranger after a devastating loss changed the trajectory of her life forever. While Anna tries to outrun her demons, her focus turns to solving crimes that have taken place within national park grounds, no matter who or what gets in her way. Season two promises continued mystery and adventure, as Anna’s story continues to unfold.”

Brebner serves as showrunner, with Lea Thompson directing. Both are also executive producers alongside Brett Burlock, Sonia Hosko, Todd Berger, Julie Di Cresce, Tom Cox, Jordy Randall, Peter Emerson and Gordon Gilbertson. Leslie Cowan serves as producer. The series is produced by Cineflix and SEVEN24 Films for USA Network in association with Bell Media. Cineflix Rights is the exclusive international worldwide distribution partner, excluding the US.

“’Anna Pigeon’ has connected with audiences in a meaningful way, bringing a compelling new heroine and a fresh perspective to USA Network,” said Michael Sluchan, SVP of Scripted Content, Entertainment, at Versant. “We’re thrilled to continue Anna’s journey with Tracy, Morwyn, Lea and our incredible partners at Cineflix.”

“Anna Pigeon” is one of two scripted series currently airing on USA Network. The network also has Season 2 of the legal drama “The Rainmaker,” which is based on the John Grisham novel of the same name, set to debut on Oct. 16. USA Network has also greenlit the medical drama “Diplomatic Immunity” from Matt Corman and Chris Ord.

USA Network was one of the cable channels spun off into the standalone company Versant by Comcast in early 2026. Other channels now under Versant include MS Now (formerly MSNBC), E!, Syfy, and Oxygen.

title: ‘Baby Reindeer’ Battle Reignites: Netflix Suffers Blow In Bid To Get Fiona Harvey Lawsuit Spiked
summary: EXCLUSIVE: The battle over Baby Reindeer is back on. After legal proceedings were dormant for more than a year, Netflix has suffered a blow in its efforts to get Fiona Harvey’s lawsuit thrown out of court. Harvey, a former lawyer from Scotland, hit Netflix with a $170 million defamation lawsuit in 2024 after Baby Reindeer […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: The battle over Baby Reindeer is back on.

After legal proceedings were dormant for more than a year, Netflix has suffered a blow in its efforts to get Fiona Harvey‘s lawsuit thrown out of court.

Harvey, a former lawyer from Scotland, hit Netflix with a $170 million defamation lawsuit in 2024 after Baby Reindeer became a global sensation and she was identified as the show’s alleged stalker, Martha, played by Jessica Gunning.

Harvey claimed that the darkly comic series, which was billed as a “true story,” portrayed her as “a twice-convicted stalker who was sentenced to five years in prison.” Harvey has never been convicted of stalking Gadd, and she argued the series was “the biggest lie in television history.”

Watch on Deadline

The case was widely expected to go to trial in May 2025, but an appeal by Netflix put a halt to proceedings at the Central District of California Court. Now, the U.S. Court of Appeals, Ninth Circuit, has ruled that it lacks jurisdiction over the appeal. The ruling was made on technical grounds rather than on the merits of Netflix’s argument.

In its order, the appeals court said Netflix must either “file a motion to voluntarily dismiss this appeal or file a statement explaining why it should not be dismissed.” Netflix declined to comment.

Richard Roth, the attorney representing Harvey, told Deadline: “Netflix is doing everything to avoid a trial of this action. First, it made a motion before the federal district court which it lost. Then it appealed that decision, which was dismissed. Notwithstanding its efforts, there will be a trial in this action where its wrongdoing will be front nd center before a jury.”

U.S. District Judge R. Gary Klausner ruled in September 2024 that Harvey’s case should proceed because Baby Reindeer was wrongly billed as a “true story” after Netflix “made no effort” to fact-check creator Richard Gadd’s experiences and failed to “hide” Harvey’s identity.

Netflix has argued that Harvey’s claim fails because she “does not allege a provably false statement of fact was made about her.” Netflix has said that her reputation has already been tarnished by “past news stories detailing her previous harassment and stalking of public figures.”

Baby Reindeer was a massive and somewhat unexpected hit when it premiered in April 2024. The limited series has amassed 103 million views since its debut, as well as clinching Emmy, BAFTA, and Golden Globe awards.

title: ‘Scream’ At 30: Composer Marco Beltrami On Working With Wes Craven, Creating The Film’s Iconic Score & Why ‘Scream 4’ Missed The Mark
summary: As Gale Weathers would say, it all began with a scream over 911 and ended in a bloodbath that has rocked audiences worldwide since Wes Craven’s iconic slasher flick first hit theaters in December 1996. But just as memorable as Drew Barrymore’s gut-wrenching opening scene was Marco Beltrami’s chilling score, one that heightened the suspense […]
content:
As Gale Weathers would say, it all began with a scream over 911 and ended in a bloodbath that has rocked audiences worldwide since Wes Craven’s iconic slasher flick first hit theaters in December 1996. But just as memorable as Drew Barrymore’s gut-wrenching opening scene was Marco Beltrami’s chilling score, one that heightened the suspense and terror at every turn.

“I had never done a horror movie,” he says. “I had never even seen a horror movie.”

“[Wes Craven] really guided me through the process,” he continues. “I mean, he believed in what I was doing.”

I sat down with Beltrami to discuss Scream’s lasting impact three decades later, his memories of working with the late horror maestro and why he really didn’t want to return for Scream 4. Read our full conversation below.

This interview has been edited for length and clarity.

DEADLINE: We’re here to celebrate the 30th anniversary of the Scream soundtrack, which you scored. Take me back in time a little bit. How did Scream come into your life, and then what did getting that job mean for you at that point in your career?

MARCO BELTRAMI: It was the first movie, first feature film I had done, and so it meant a lot to me. I got the film because I had done a student film, and Wes Craven was working on this really low budget horror movie. And I guess he wasn’t happy with the music he was hearing. He really wanted to find something different. His assistant heard about me through this short film I had done, a student film, and she asked if I had a tape, and I actually sent in a piece of music I had recorded with this singer back when I was in college. I did this kind of voice, manipulated voice, and electronic tape, and it really resonated with Wes. He liked it, and so he asked me to come in and meet him, and I did. He showed me the beginning of the movie and asked me to score the opening scene, which was that scene where Drew Barrymore gets killed. It’s a kind of a long sequence. He gave me like two days to do it, and I sent it in, and I got the job. And I think the thing that was really cool about it was that he really found that the piece of music that I sent him with that voice really resonated with the emotional content of bringing Sidney’s character to life, and that was, I think, what got me the job.

DEADLINE: Talking about Wes Craven, you spoke a little bit about it, but what was he like when you you first met him, when you came on to the job, and if you could elaborate a little bit more of what he was looking from you musically?

MARCO BELTRAMI: He was the sweetest guy, like really soft spoken and sort of the antithesis of working for the newly formed Dimension Films, which was the Weinsteins. I had very little experience. I had never done a horror movie. I’d never even seen a horror movie, just because I’ve always been sort of like a scaredy cat, I guess. I don’t know. So I really had no experience with it, and he really guided me through the process. I mean, he believed in what I was doing, and like I said, a lot of horror movies up to that point, I think they really focused on, you know, having something suspenseful for the killer or all that kind of stuff. You know, if you think about Halloween scores and The Nightmare on Elm Street and all that. What he wanted to do was have the audience identify with Sidney and have the music be able to bring about her emotional vulnerability and inner strength, and I think that’s what that vocal idea, how it resonated with them, and that’s what I developed when I worked on Sidney’s theme, which was the first thing I worked on, and I actually used that same singer, Rose Thompson, so yeah.

DEADLINE: Going back a little bit. You mentioned that the Casey Becker opening was essentially what got you the job. Let’s call it your audition score. Was that the score that ended up being in the film?

MARCO BELTRAMI: No, no, it wasn’t. I think the thing that got me the job is probably because of my naiveness with horror scores. It really struck me as being like this horrific, over-the-top emotional thing, and I think I probably scored it almost a little bit operatically. Like when Drew Barrymore is running out of the house and she sees her parents there, and she’s getting stabbed. To me, it’s like this horrible tragedy, and so I wanted to have the music reflect that emotional intensity, and I think that’s what got me the job.

DEADLINE: Touching on Sidney a little bit more, you really did capture this emotional component with her. If you could just expand a little bit more on how you approached creating her theme.

MARCO BELTRAMI: I had basically a simple melody. It’s funny because the place where you really get to identify with her theme is when the sun is going down over Woodsboro and she’s at home all alone. So the music there is a combination of you know identifying with her, but also it has this sort of creepy surrounding to it. One of the things that I did, and this was strictly out of necessity, I didn’t have the money to have all the string players that I wanted at the time at the session. There’s this opening texture. I wanted it to be string harmonics, but I couldn’t. So I asked if anybody in the crew knew how to whistle, and Wes knew how to whistle, and his editor Patrick [Lussier], and I think maybe two of the producers. So I put them actually out of the string section, and I had them whistle in the beginning of that, and that gave it like this really kind of creepy overtone that became later on something that you know. It became in its own sound.

DEADLINE: Do you have a favorite score? Because, I’ll just tell you, I love Dewey’s Theme so much.

MARCO BELTRAMI: I view Dewey as almost like this Western, and I played it like that, just sort of having fun. I think my favorite scene is the sequence when Sidney is upstairs in her bedroom with Billy, and this whole musical stretch for me was fun, too, because she’s there and then it turns out that she gets chased by the killer. This whole sequence seems very dynamic to me and really, it’s just a great sequence of the movie.

DEADLINE: Now I want to ask about the other Screams. How would you say that the scores evolved over the first four films? Because, personally, as a fan, I always felt like each score kind of built off the last one. But then with Scream 4, and I might be saying something controversial. I mean no offense, but by 4, it felt a little less dangerous than the others. Was that a choice?

MARCO BELTRAMI: I have to be honest. It was not a project I wanted to do. In fact, I’m not even sure Wes really wanted to do it. Like it was something that Dimension was really forcing, and I wasn’t really writing music for Wes then. It was like I was writing these cues, and they would be approved by some clown in an office in New York. And even though the franchise had done really well, they had no budget for orchestral instruments. We had to do some little quick session in Eastern Europe. The whole thing was, I have to say, uninspired. I think the movie, of all the first four, is the weakest, and musically too, it’s the most uninspired. It’s a shame, but it’s the reality.

DEADLINE: You did all of the Wes Craven Scream films, but were noticeably absent from Scream 5 and 6, which were directed by Radio Silence. Was there ever any conversation of you doing those ones?

MARCO BELTRAMI: Very brief, but I never read any scripts. I had a little bit of contact with the directors on it. They did some sort of shout out to Wes at the end of the movie, but it seemed to be his own thing.

DEADLINE: So, then what convinced you to sign on for Scream 7?

MARCO BELTRAMI: You know what brought me back into it was Kevin [Williamson] calling me and telling me that he was doing it. I knew it’d be back to the world that Wes created, and I think that’s why I was eager to get back in. He wanted to really lean into Neve’s character and just make it almost like this family story.

DEADLINE: How did you approach the score this time around?

MARCO BELTRAMI: It’s really interesting. I realized when I was working on Scream 7 that through all these movies, I had never established a theme for the killer. Like it was always, you know, I played it creepy or I played, you know, different things, but there was no like signature sound. And I thought that’s something that I should really do. I guess it was really nerdy, but I based the killer’s theme on the musical interval of a seventh, and so I have these two descending sevenths, and that became a new addition to this, and I think it it makes it fun and holds together and brings a new level to it.

DEADLINE: When you go back and you hear the original score from Scream, do you hear it differently? And is there anything you would change about it?

MARCO BELTRAMI: No, I wouldn’t change it now. There’s things that I would do a little differently, but I wouldn’t change what I did there. It was my first film and I appreciate it for that. In fact, going back when I was working on Scream 7 to go back and listen to Scream again and all that, it was sort of a weird throwback, and it put me into a mental state I was in 30 years ago, which was really an odd thing because music has that ability to just transport you to another time. It was really kind of cool.

DEADLINE: I love that. And then my last question is: Scream 8 has been announced. We don’t know a ton about it, but I’m curious, have you been approached?

MARCO BELTRAMI: I was at the premiere for Scream 7. I was asked if I’d be interested to do it, and I said yes. But since then, I haven’t heard anything, so I really don’t know.

Three decades and six sequels later, Scream remains one of horror’s most enduring (and most profitable) franchises. Plenty of killers have been unmasked over the years, and the bodies have piled up in increasingly inventive ways. But without Beltrami’s score, the film that started it all may never have struck the same chord.

title: Theo Rossi, Ron Perlman & Rachelle Goulding Wrap Under-The-Radar Horror Film ‘Renew’, First Look Revealed
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Theo Rossi has added an under-the-radar horror film to his genre era in the shape of Renew, which will reunite him on screen with his Sons Of Anarchy, Come With Me and The Saviors co-star Ron Perlman. Filming recently wrapped on Renew, “a suspense-driven horror film that begins as an intimate love story before […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Theo Rossi has added an under-the-radar horror film to his genre era in the shape of Renew, which will reunite him on screen with his Sons Of Anarchy, Come With Me and The Saviors co-star Ron Perlman.

Filming recently wrapped on Renew, “a suspense-driven horror film that begins as an intimate love story before descending into visceral horror”.

Directed by Tommy DeNucci from a screenplay he co-wrote with Rossi, the film, which also stars Rachelle Goulding (Suits LA), “follows a husband and wife who return to the secluded Montana guest ranch where they were married to renew their vows, hoping to leave the past behind and begin again. But when she mysteriously disappears, he is forced to confront the life he fought to escape as he uncovers a hidden evil lurking beneath the ranch’s idyllic façade.” Below is a first-look image.

The ensemble cast also includes Ronnie Gene Blevins, Allison Dunbar, Sam Daly, Danny Rivera, Rebecca Creskoff, Darko Ostojic, Bonnie Gayle Sparks, Barron Boedecker and Chris Wilks. Diana Hull and Rossi produced the film.

Watch on Deadline

Production wrapped in Red Lodge and Roberts, Montana. Rossi was joined on the project by longtime producing partner Nicholas Carmona. DeNucci has previously directed Rossi in movies Vault and Play Dirty.

Rossi, also known for HBO’s The Penguin, Netflix’s Carry-On, and Emily the Criminal, commented: “What excited Tommy and me most was building the film around two people with a shared history who are trying to find their way back to each other. There’s hope, humor and heart in that, but also the weight of everything they’ve been through. When that hope comes under threat, you find out how far someone will go for the person they love. We wanted audiences invested in Randy and Liz from the very beginning, so they feel the danger right alongside them.”

Producer Diana Hull said: “Watching this cast and crew bring Renew to life in Montana was incredibly rewarding. The film asks a great deal of its performers, both emotionally and physically, and their commitment carried through every stage of production. We can’t wait for audiences to experience what we’ve created together.”

DeNucci added: “From the very first draft, we wanted audiences to settle into this beautiful Montana escape and genuinely fall in love with Randy and Liz. The more authentic their relationship feels, the more terrifying it becomes when everything begins to unravel. This remarkable cast brought that emotional journey to life in ways that exceeded every expectation.”

Rossie and Perlman will also join forces on the upcoming Sons of Anarchy reboot Legends.

title: ‘SNL’ Alum Punkie Johnson Sets Debut Stand-Up Special ‘Long Tiddie Short Story’ With Hartbeat
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Former Saturday Night Live cast member Punkie Johnson has announced that her debut stand-up special, Long Tiddie Short Story, will premiere on Hartbeat’s LOL Stand-Up YouTube Channel October 21st. In the special, Johnson steps into the ring to reflect on her time at SNL, her complicated relationship with queerness, and her own questionable life […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Former Saturday Night Live cast member Punkie Johnson has announced that her debut stand-up special, Long Tiddie Short Story, will premiere on Hartbeat’s LOL Stand-Up YouTube Channel October 21st.

In the special, Johnson steps into the ring to reflect on her time at SNL, her complicated relationship with queerness, and her own questionable life choices. It’s billed as a brutally honest and unfiltered hour about marriage, sex, drugs, and what can transpire when you pretend to be “normal.”

Johnson taped the hour at The Comedy Store in Los Angeles. Directed by Steven Feinartz, it’ll be available as a comedy album across audio streaming services on November 13, available for pre-order on October 21. The special is produced by Feinartz and Danielle Lee and exec produced by Johnson, Ethan Stern and Dominic Del Bene.

Hartbeat reunites with Johnson after producing her 2023 SiriusXM show, Love Thang, for Kevin Hart’s LOL Radio. Recently, she’s also filmed a role in their upcoming Barbershop TV series for Prime Video. The special joins a growing stand-up slate from Hartbeat, including the second installment of LOL Live at Hulu, with new half-hour specials currently rolling out monthly, as well as Funny AF, the stand-up competition series that was picked up for a second season after drumming up major viewership at Netflix.

Watch on Deadline

The deal to distribute Johnson’s special was spearheaded by Hartbeat President & Chief Distribution Officer Jeff Clanagan and VP, Comedy Eric Weil.

Clanagan told us, “Punkie is exactly the kind of singular comedic voice we want to champion at Hartbeat. We’ve had the opportunity to work with her across radio, television and now stand-up, and bringing her debut special directly to audiences on YouTube reflects our larger strategy of creating more ways for great comedians to reach fans wherever they are. We’re excited to continue building with Punkie and supporting her work across platforms.”

Weil added, “Punkie has the rare ability to be completely fearless and deeply personal at the same time. Long Tiddie Short Story is unmistakably her — honest, unpredictable and incredibly funny. We’re proud to be part of her first stand-up special and to continue a creative relationship with Punkie that has grown across radio, television and stand-up.”

A comedian, actress and writer from New Orleans, Louisiana, Johnson was with SNL for four seasons beginning in 2020. Touring nationally these days while developing original television and film projects, she’s previously been seen starring in two seasons of Lena Waithe’s The Chi, with additional roles in HBO Max’s Love Life, Netflix’s Space Force, HBO’s A Black Lady Sketch Show and CBS’s Ghosts.

Johnson also served as a writer/consultant on Peacock’s reboot of Queer as Folk and appeared in the cult hit comedy film Bottoms opposite Ayo Edebiri and Rachel Sennott. She is repped by Ethan Stern at Underscore, WME and Ziffren Brittenham.

title: London Film Festival Hails the ‘Great Andrew Scott’ as ‘Elsinore’ Opens 70th Edition With Tears, Cheers and ‘The Ethel Merman Disco Album’
summary: The 70th BFI London Film Festival kicked off on Wednesday with the European premiere of “Elsinore,” a movie that, as the credits rolled, left large swathes of the audience at the Royal Festival Hall wiping away tears. But just moments later, as the name of lead star Andrew Scott appeared on stage, the loud snuffles […]
content:
The 70th BFI London Film Festival kicked off on Wednesday with the European premiere of “Elsinore,” a movie that, as the credits rolled, left large swathes of the audience at the Royal Festival Hall wiping away tears. But just moments later, as the name of lead star Andrew Scott appeared on stage, the loud snuffles were replaced with whoops and, in rather uncharacteristically British style, a standing ovation for the actor.

Directed by Simon Stone from a script by Simon Beresford, “Elsinore” — already expected to be among the awards season hopefuls — sees Scott portray famed Scottish actor and “Chariots of Fire” star Ian Charleson. In 1989, while already succumbing to complications from AIDS, Charleson replaced Daniel Day-Lewis in “Hamlet” at London’s National Theatre after the actor had walked off stage mid-performance, never to return to the production. Charleson received rave reviews, but died just seven weeks after bowing out.

Speaking on stage ahead of the premiere, Stone introduced his cast, including “the great Andrew Scott.” While Scott said little before “Elsinore” began, afterwards he made a special presentation in which he called up the real-life individuals from the film and the actors portraying then, including the National Theatre’s stage doorkeeper for 46 years, Linda Tolhurst (played by Monica Dolan), itss long-serving dresser Ralph Mills (Paul Chahidi), and director and Charleson’s close friend Sean Mathias (Matthew Beard). But the biggest round of applause — and other standing ovation — was reserved for pioneering HIV/AIDS consultant Dr. Margaret Johnson (Olivia Colman).

Popular on Variety

“It’s difficult to underestimate the impact this person had on the development of treatment for people suffering with HIV and AIDS,” said Scott. “To our mind, she is a true life hero.”

Scott then signed off by introducing a song from camp classic “The Ethel Merman Disco Album,” performed in the film, as a tribute to Charleson. “We want you to be able to remember not just Ian’s death, but how extraordinarily he lived with such flair and zest and warmth and charm and passion and talent,” he said, adding that the song “encapsulates this man who loved this industry so much.”

Encouraging the audience to dance as they left the auditorium, Scott concluded: “He went out performing, so this one’s for you, Ian. We love you.”

Speaking to Variety before the premiere, LFF head Kristy Matheson said she’d first seen “Elsinore” — which has amassed widespread critical acclaim since premiering in Telluride — with colleagues during the summer. “It was one of those films where we walked out and we just had to really take a beat,” she said. “We were really so sure of the film from the second it finished.”

Bringing “Elsinore” to London as the curtain raiser not only felt like a perfect choice for the festival, but offered some considerable poignancy given the location of the opening night premiere — merely meters from where Charleson gave his final performance.

“I think it’s going to be such an incredible moment to screen that film literally a stone’s throw away from the National Theatre,” said Matheson. “So it feels like we’re going to bring this film home, and I’m just really excited and honored to do that.”

The London Film Festival runs Oct 7-18, with other major screenings including the likes of “Wild Horse Nine,” “La Bola Negra,” “Club Kid,” “Ink,” “Artificial,” “Primetime” and “The Debut” and a lineup of Screen Talks involving the likes of Danny Boyle, Cynthia Erivo, Sofia Coppola, Javier Bardem and John Malkovich.

title: Dewayne Perkins to Launch ‘I Swear We’re Friends,’ New Digital ‘Skitcom’ on YouTube (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: “The Blackening” and “The Studio” star Dewayne Perkins is launching a new digital series, “I Swear We’re Friends,” exclusively on YouTube this fall.Perkins is independently releasing the six-episode “skitcom,” which is described as a “love letter to television,” with each episode inspired by a beloved show: “Girlfriends,” “Succession,” “24,” “My Wife & Kids,” “Charmed” and […]
content:
“The Blackening” and “The Studio” star Dewayne Perkins is launching a new digital series, “I Swear We’re Friends,” exclusively on YouTube this fall.

Perkins is independently releasing the six-episode “skitcom,” which is described as a “love letter to television,” with each episode inspired by a beloved show: “Girlfriends,” “Succession,” “24,” “My Wife & Kids,” “Charmed” and “Touched By An Angel.”

With the series, Perkins — who got his start performing in his Chicago improv group 3Peat before the success of “The Blackening” put him on Hollywood’s radar — mixes the nostalgia of the past with the novelty of the present to create a “uniquely absurd comedic experience.”

“Twenty years after ‘Noah’s Arc,’ why are Black gay male friendships still so rarely at the center of comedy?” a release describing the series explains. “With ‘I Swear We’re Friends,’ Dewayne is helping fill a void that remains on-screen two decades later. The series isn’t about explaining Black queerness to an outside audience; it gives Black queer men the space to simply be funny, messy, complicated friends.”

Popular on Variety

Perkins leads the main cast alongside Devere Rogers (“Abbott Elementary,” “Honk for Jesus. Save Your Soul”), Brian Jordan Jr. (“Sistas”), Philemon Chambers (“Beauty in Black”) and Cameron J. Ross (“The Summer I Turned Pretty,” “Boomerang”).

Guest stars include Daryl Stephens (“Noah’s Arc”), Steven G. Norfleet (“Beauty in Black,” “Interview with the Vampire”), Courtney Taylor (“Abbott Elementary,” “Shrinking,” “Insecure”), Tracie Thoms (“Rent,” “The Devil Wears Prada”), Justen Ross (“Is God Is,” “Fight Night: The Million Dollar Heist”) and Jermelle Simon (“The Upshaws”). Grammy winner Durand Bernarr performs the show’s theme song.

The first two episodes debut on Oct. 14, with episodes three and four following on Oct. 21, and Season 1 concluding with episodes five and six on Oct. 28.

Perkins directed all six episodes with Sade Ndya (ASC Rising Star, Nike x Megan Thee Stallion) as the director of photography. He also wrote the series with James Rogers III (“The Chi”), Rogers and Higher Ground’s Mark Wright.

“I Swear We’re Friends” is produced by Nance Messineo & Cole Santiago of Ex-Girlfriend Co. Production Company (Doechii, Selena Gomez, Renee Rapp) and Natasha Forouzannia (Marvel’s “Ironheart”). Post-production on the series is by Skapa Films (Beyoncé’s “Renaissance” film, Victoria Monét, Megan Thee Stallion).

News of the digital series comes as Perkins is set to return in the ensemble cast of Apple TV’s Emmy-winning series “The Studio.” He’s also currently working on “The Blackening 2” for Lionsgate. (The 2023 horror-comedy, co-written by Perkins and Tracy Oliver, grossed more than $18 million on a $5 million budget.)

Up next, Perkins recently joined the cast of Scott “Kid Cudi” Mescudi’s latest directorial feature, the horror-thriller “Wrong Number.” Variety also exclusively revealed that he is developing a new comedy series at Hulu, which he is attached to write, executive produce and star in should it receive a green light. Stephen Curry, Erick Peyton and Sharla Sumpter Bridgett are also executive producing via Unanimous Media.

Finally, on Nov. 9, Perkins brings his one-man show, “How Being Black & Gay Made Me Better Than You!,” to Brooklyn’s Bell House as part of the New York Comedy Festival, following a sold-out show at the Netflix Is a Joke Fest earlier this year.

Perkins is represented by CAA, Artists First and attorneys Amber Payne and Isaac Dunham.

title: PlayStation to Launch New Crunchyroll Anime Hub for PS5
summary: Sony’s PlayStation will launch a new Crunchyroll anime hub within its PlayStation 5 gaming console’s home screen next year to more closely align the company’s anime projects and anime-inspired games. Launching in spring 2027, the new PS5 anime destination is “designed to make it easier for the PlayStation community to discover and explore the anime […]
content:
Sony’s PlayStation will launch a new Crunchyroll anime hub within its PlayStation 5 gaming console’s home screen next year to more closely align the company’s anime projects and anime-inspired games.

Launching in spring 2027, the new PS5 anime destination is “designed to make it easier for the PlayStation community to discover and explore the anime content they enjoy,” per Sony Interactive Entertainment.

While Crunchyroll has been accessible on the PS5 via an app since the gaming console was released in 2020, the goal here is to make Crunchyroll an integral part of a PlayStation user’s home-screen experience.

Popular on Variety

“Anime and gaming have deeply engaged and overlapping fan communities, and the new experience will bring those worlds closer together on PS5,” the Crunchyroll announcement reads. “Whether longtime anime fans or discovering a series through a game, character or world they already love, players will have a dedicated place to discover anime and anime-inspired games and easily access the full Crunchyroll app.

The PS5-Crunchyroll news was announced Wednesday by PlayStation president and CEO Hideaki Nishino at the inaugural Crunchyroll Anime Future Forum, where Sony also unveiled its new Crunchyroll Storyworks division.

“From Crunchyroll membership on PlayStation, to the upcoming Ghost of Tsushima: Legends anime series,” Crunchyroll president Rahul Purini said. “Today, we take that partnership with Sony Interactive Entertainment one step further with an anime hub on PlayStation. Serving fans means meeting them where they already are.”

The Crunchyroll-PlayStation integration comes on the heels of Sony launching “Live TV on PS5,” an offering of more than 100 free ad-supported video channels available via the PlayStation 5 video game console. The PlayStation 5 FAST channel offering debuted in August and Sony Pictures Television has plans to expand it globally in the coming months.

title: Movie Theaters Add New York Times Games to Pre-Show Experience (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Attention “Wordle” and “Spelling Bee” fans: interactive offerings from The New York Times Games are coming to a movie theater near you this fall. Through a new partnership between NYT Games and in-theater ad company Screenvision, the pre-show experience will begin rolling out nationwide by Thanksgiving. The deal (which has initially been set as a […]
content:
Attention “Wordle” and “Spelling Bee” fans: interactive offerings from The New York Times Games are coming to a movie theater near you this fall.

Through a new partnership between NYT Games and in-theater ad company Screenvision, the pre-show experience will begin rolling out nationwide by Thanksgiving.

The deal (which has initially been set as a one-year pact) marks the first time NYT Games is bringing an interactive play-along experience into movie theaters. NYT Games and Screenvision plan to “refresh” the pre-show Games content regularly and see potential to “experiment with additional formats” over the course of the collaboration.

The maker of “Connections” sees the partnership as “a new way to introduce audiences to new products and features, like Bonus Puzzles, through the experience of actually playing them.”

Popular on Variety

The NYT Games-Screenvision deal was announced Wednesday evening at a Screenvision event at the Angelika in New York City, which included a screening of “Ferris Bueller’s Day Off” and a Q&A with Matthew Broderick.

“Cinema has become one of the most powerful places for premium content to reach audiences because it combines scale, unparalleled attention and shared experience in a way no other platform can,” Screenvision Media CEO Geoff Schiller said. “We’re proud to partner exclusively with The New York Times to bring NYT Games to moviegoers nationwide, creating a first-of-its-kind experience that transforms the theater into a place not just to watch, but to participate.”

The New York Times chief marketing officer Amy Weisenbach added: “New York Times Games has become a shared daily ritual for millions of people, sparking conversation, connection and a little friendly competition. Working with Screenvision gives us an exciting and unexpected way to bring that experience to the big screen, inviting moviegoers across the country to play together and discover more of what NYT Games has to offer.”

title: ‘Ashes’ and ‘Mexican American’ to Open and Close Los Angeles’ GuadaLAjara Film Festival
summary: The GuadaLAjara Film Festival announced its full lineup for the annual event running from Nov. 5-7 at venues across Los Angeles. The festival will open with Watermelon Pictures’ “Ashes” directed by Diego Luna at the United Theater. The film follows Lucila who moves to Spain with her brother to reunite with the mother who left […]
content:
The GuadaLAjara Film Festival announced its full lineup for the annual event running from Nov. 5-7 at venues across Los Angeles.

The festival will open with Watermelon Pictures’ “Ashes” directed by Diego Luna at the United Theater. The film follows Lucila who moves to Spain with her brother to reunite with the mother who left eight years earlier. Confronted with discrimination and family obligations, she struggles to claim her independence while facing the wounds of her past.

To close the festival, there will be a 35mm screening of “Mexicanamerican” directed by Eddie Sánchez at the Linwood Dunn Theater. “Mexicanamerican” tells the story of Lalo and Beby, a Mexican couple who achieved the American Dream and slowly lost the culture, language and traditions they once shared with their children.

Popular on Variety

The Centerpiece Gala will present Netflix’s “14th” from Ava DuVernay. The film looks closely at the constitutional crises dominating headlines today and the pattern that emerges, which is hard-wired into history. “14th” exposes an unfinished battle to define America, now taking on drastic new dimensions. The film will screen at Vidiots.

“We are proud to bring these films to Los Angeles,” Ximena Urrutia, GLAFF executive director, said. “They tell our stories, honor our cultures and present some of the finest work of the year from Mexico, Latin America, the United States and beyond.”

The festival lineup includes U.S., West Coast, and international premieres, showcasing work from emerging and established filmmakers who are reshaping the cinematic landscape:

“Adam’s Apple,” directed by Amy Jenkins. A transgender teen and his mother chronicle their lives in an intimate portrait of a family in transition. Two decades of footage follow a boy’s path to manhood and his parents’ reckoning with change.

“Chicas Tristes (Sad Girlz),” directed by Fernanda Tovar. A striking coming-of-age drama seen through the eyes of two best friends whose bond is put to the test when they have drastically differing reactions to a traumatic experience at a party.

“City of the Dead (Ciudad de Muertos),” directed by J.M. Cravioto. When a body is found inside a suitcase, forensic photographer Enrique is drawn into a secret agent’s hunt for a serial killer.

“Dear Fátima (Querida Fátima),” directed by Lorena Gutiérrez, Jesús “Don Chucho” Quintana, Rodrigo Reyes, Dawn Valadez and Su Kim. A decade after the feminicide of her 12-year-old daughter Fátima, Lorena Gutiérrez camps outside Mexico’s National Palace and demands an audience with the country’s first female president.

“Shooting Stars,” directed by director Daniel Poler, follows Adrián Solano, a 22-year-old Venezuelan in search of meaning who inadvertently enters the 2017 Nordic World Ski Championships despite having never seen snow in his life. The film is executive produced by John Leguizamo, produced by ESPN, ESPN Deportes and TriBeCa Studios.

Short Films Spotlight Emerging Talent

“Para Los Contrincantes,” directed by Federico Luis

“He’s Out There,” directed by Kurt Andrew Schneider and Sam Davis

“Busy Bodies” by Kate Renshaw-Lewis

“The Long Con” by Aitch Alberto, starring Nava Mau

“La Mar” by Jean Chapiro Uziel

“Lucretia y Las Brujas” by Eduardo Lecuona

“Marga en el DF” by Gabriela Ortega

“Miriam” by Karla Condado

“Stalin Boys” by Ora DeKornfeld and Bianca Giaever

“Still Standing” by Victor Tadashi Suarez and Livia Albeck-Ripka

“The Motive” by Jorge Molina

“Vyann/Carne” by Adolfo Margulis

The festival will also include red-carpet premieres, panel conversations, master classes, industry and community events and special screenings throughout Los Angeles. Additional events and participating talent will be announced later.

title: ‘Carrie’s Matthew Lillard & Amber Midthunder On How The “Catastrophic” Finale Deviates From The Book: “It’s Part Of The Tragedy”
summary: SPOILERS: This post contains details about the Season 1 finale of Prime Video’s Carrie As Mike Flanagan leaves another mark on the Stephen King onscreen universe with Prime Video’s Carrie, Matthew Lillard and Amber Midthunder have joined his talented troupe of horror actors. While speaking to Deadline, the actors who play Principal Grayle and Miss […]
content:
SPOILERS: This post contains details about the Season 1 finale of Prime Video‘s Carrie

As Mike Flanagan leaves another mark on the Stephen King onscreen universe with Prime Video’s Carrie, Matthew Lillard and Amber Midthunder have joined his talented troupe of horror actors.

While speaking to Deadline, the actors who play Principal Grayle and Miss Desjardin in the series, all episodes now streaming, explained how Flanagan provides the “freedom” for his actors to “thrive” on screen.

“I think that we understand his capacity to tell stories. He’s a beautiful filmmaker, but he’s also an incredible man, and I think that combination—I will follow him into whatever he’s doing next because the way he leads, the way he directs, the way he tells stories, how human he is, it’s all you want to be a part of in this business,” said Lillard.

Midthunder explained, “I think especially with this, there’s no reason for any sort of hesitation or doubt or fear or concern about exactly what this is. I think that Mike has executed incredibly well, the things that people love about Carrie and also created a really beautiful show.”

Watch on Deadline

With the latest adaptation of King’s 1974 debut horror novel getting an eight-episode run to get to know these characters, it makes their fate all the more “tragic” in the fiery prom conclusion of the finale episode “AP Physics”.

Amber Midthunder as Miss Desjardin in ‘Carrie’

Lillard noted, “You’d have to ask Mike why he made this ultimate choice, but to me it really signifies how catastrophic the demise of Carrie is in that last moment, that if she was in control, she would have probably saved these two characters. She probably wouldn’t have destroyed the entire town, but I think it’s symbolic of when a kid is pushed too far, the things that could tragically happen.”

For Midthunder, their fate is “part of the tragedy,” even if it deviates from the book. “There’s a lot of questionable morality, in especially our iteration of this, and nobody is perfect, but I think that we have two characters who are quite consistent in sort of what they’re motivated by, consistent in their drive and their moral compasses, and so to see those people … who are consistently good, and yet they also fall, I think it just adds to the tragedy and then Carrie’s guilt.”

Read on about Matthew Lillard and Amber Midthunder’s experience on Prime Video’s Carrie, now available to stream.

DEADLINE: You’ve both been in such iconic horror franchises. I’m curious what was it about Carrie and Mike Flanagan that made you wanna be a part of this adaptation.

MATTHEW LILLARD: Honestly, if we’re being candid, it was Flanagan that brings you in, right? I think that we understand his capacity to tell stories. He’s a beautiful filmmaker, but he’s also an incredible man, and I think that combination—I will follow him into whatever he’s doing next because the way he leads, the way he directs, the way he tells stories, how human he is, it’s all you want to be a part of in this business.

AMBER MIDTHUNDER: Yeah, I think that he’s already proved that anything is safe in his hands, right? Any story you love, any adaptation, any original idea, but I think especially with this, there’s no reason for any sort of hesitation or doubt or fear or concern about exactly what this is. I think that Mike has executed incredibly well, the things that people love about Carrie and also created a really beautiful show.

LILLARD: Yeah, and I just want to jump on top. I think that one of the interesting things that … going into the project, he had all eight scripts written that you could sit down and talk about the first day. We had a month of rehearsal, and the first day of rehearsal, he could tell you every scene, how he was gonna shoot it, what angle he was gonna be at in the cut. He told you at what time he was gonna shoot it on what day. So, that sort of capacity to have a full understanding of where you are and where you’re going as an actor gives you a sense of, there’s freedom within form, and he is so built and ready to tell the story that there’s a freedom within that you know you’ll thrive.

Rahul Kohli as Mr. Peist and Matthew Lillard as Principal Grayle in ‘Carrie’

DEADLINE: I think this is the first time we’ve seen Principal Grayle in an adaptation on screen because it’s always been Mr. Morton. What was that like for you getting to originate that role, and since it’s so many episodes, actually flesh him out?

LILLARD: Yeah, it’s great. Every time you step into something, you make it your own. I mean, even if there were three iterations of him beforehand, I wouldn’t have watched it. I would have tried to just hold on to what’s in front of me. And it’s great, you’re trying to create something that resonates, you’re trying to make something that you’re proud of, and I think that he’s sort of the moral compass, he’s the grounding element. He’s the one trying to move everyone through this horrific experience. … I do think that for me, the interesting about Grayle is that he’s the calm in the storm, and I’m an actor that likes to make big choices and use my energy and sort of sometimes chew scenery, and with Mike, he was like, “I really want him grounded and strong and resolute, but simple,” simpler than I usually am. And so for me, it allowed me to sort of turn in a performance that’s different than a lot of things I’ve done before, and I’m at the end of the day, really proud of it.

DEADLINE: And for you, Amber, Miss Desjardin has been played by Betty Buckley and Judy Greer, some pretty amazing actresses. What was it like for you taking over that torch, but also getting to show more of her personal life the twist with Mr. Peist [Rahul Kohli] plays in all of it?

MIDTHUNDER: Getting to show this character as a fully rounded person is what I really liked about this. I think, all the adaptations of Carrie as a whole, it’s been done in the past beautifully, and so I think that’s why I think this lives in its own lane. It is a departure and sort of an independent thing that Mike has gone in depth to create. You spend so much time with so many of these characters, and you know them in a much more complicated and human sort of way, and I really liked getting to know this character and seeing her in a three-dimensional [way]. You see what she’s like outside of work, you see what she’s like at home, and how much she really earnestly cares for these students. And she’s new to this town, she’s new to this job, and I think she really is lonely, and she ends up in a relationship that she probably wouldn’t have been in otherwise. It’s often just comfort and sort of ease of circumstance. She wants to really protect these kids and be a resource for them and doesn’t know how. And I think this is a story of many tragedies, and one of them is her story with Peist and the fact that she so deeply and dearly wants to protect these kids. And ultimately, one of the biggest threats to them is right in front of her. And I think that really is a huge part of her story of kind of questioning herself and her worth and her credibility, and the journey of sort of re-finding that as well. That was something that I think is intimidating, but what I felt very comfortable sort of tackling with Mike.

Amber Midthunder as Miss Desjardin in ‘Carrie’

DEADLINE: Yeah, I enjoyed that plot line, seeing her really fleshed out as well. I’m curious, was there a discussion about whether or not to kill your characters in the end? I think they survive in the book.

MIDTHUNDER: I like that people think that we were like, “Yes, do it.”

LILLARD: I mean, the reality is that you’re reading all eight scripts, you find out you die in the end, and you’re like, “Wow.” You would hope that these characters who are at the center of trying to save Carrie, they’re really concerned about trying to protect her at all costs. But you’d have to ask Mike why he made this ultimate choice, but to me it really signifies how catastrophic the demise of Carrie is in that last moment, that if she was in control, she would have probably saved these two characters. She probably wouldn’t have destroyed the entire town, but I think it’s symbolic of when a kid is pushed too far, the things that could tragically happen.

MIDTHUNDER: And it’s part of the tragedy of it, right? There’s a lot of questionable morality, in especially our iteration of this, and nobody is perfect, but I think that we have two characters who are quite consistent in sort of what they’re motivated by, consistent in their drive and their moral compasses, and so to see those people, or Tommy [Joel Oulette] is included in that as well, people who are consistently good, and yet they also fall, I think it just adds to the tragedy and then Carrie’s guilt.

DEADLINE: Well, I’m curious to see how that maybe impacts her if there’s a season two, fingers crossed. But I also saw that both of you are reuniting with Mike Flanagan on Rot. Can you tell me anything about that? Have you guys started working on that at all?

MIDTHUNDER: I’m so surprised this is the first time we’ve been asked about this.

LILLARD: Yeah, so am I. I thought we’d get it all day. We’re really excited. Mike is executive producer. It’s being directed by Alex [Magistro], who’s Mike’s right-hand woman.

MIDTHUNDER: Yeah, I don’t think that there’s much that we can say. What I can say for my character is that it’s very different for me and it’s a little scary and definitely challenging, but I think in all the right ways. And I’m really excited for Alex. I think that she deserves this moment. I think that she knows the genre well. She’s an intelligent filmmaker and obviously has an incredible support behind her in Mike and in QWGmire, who also did Carrie.

LILLARD: We’re both very excited.

title: ‘You Can See Everything’: Elizabeth Holmes Docu Presales At Alamo Drafthouse A Record For A24 Film & No. 2 Behind ‘Avengers: Doomsday’

content:
EXCLUSIVE: The highly anticipated A24 Lance Oppenheim and Nathan Fielder directed documentary You Can See Everything about fallen Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes and her days before going to federal prison, is a hot ticket at Alamo Drafthouse.

So hot, that presales for You Can See Everything is the highest of any A24 title and any documentary that has played the Sony owned dine-in exhibition chain.

In addition, the documentary is currently the No. 2 presales title at Alamo behind only Disney/Marvel Studio’s Avengers: Doomsday and that doesn’t open until Dec. 18. You Can See Everything debuts limited on Oct. 16.

The 3-hour documentary, which Deadline first told you about, made a surprise world premiere at Telluride. The production was shot in early 2023 in secrecy. You Can See Everything follows Holmes in deep conversations with the wisenheimer deadpan Fielder as her and partner Billy Evans plot the second coming of blood testing corp Theranos. Fielder also has a heyday grilling Evans, the father of Holmes’ children, who as Pete Hammond exclaims in his platinum film review of the pic, “We go along for the ride wondering if maybe she is the sane one and Billy is the batsh*t crazy one.”

Watch on Deadline

Last night at the Academy museum, there was a special LA screening for You Can See Everything with Obsession director Curry Barker, Lanterns co-creator Damon Lindelof, Waiting for Godot‘s Alex Winter, composer Nathan Johnson, Being Heumann and The Invite producer David Permut, Argo actress Clea DuVall and more in attendance. The post Q&A with Fielder and Oppenheimer was moderated by Bill Hader.

You Can See Everything is 100% fresh currently on Rotten Tomatoes off 20 reviews. Docu filmmaker Oppenheim has his first feature narrative directed film currently in theaters, A24’s Primetime starring Robert Pattinson as To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen which has grossed over $35M stateside to date.

title: Get Your Wings, Again: Aerosmith Sets Pair Of Comeback Concerts At Hollywood Bowl
summary: Just as so many big-name rock acts are on farewell tours, at least one is making a live comeback. Ending what was billed as a permanent vacation from the concert stage, Aerosmith on Wednesday announced a pair of shows set for October 29 and November 1 at the Hollywood Bowl — with a little help […]
content:
Just as so many big-name rock acts are on farewell tours, at least one is making a live comeback. Ending what was billed as a permanent vacation from the concert stage, Aerosmith on Wednesday announced a pair of shows set for October 29 and November 1 at the Hollywood Bowl — with a little help from a lot of friends.

Along for the return ride will be a slew of other acts ranging from Heart, the Black Crowes, Run-D.M.C., Billy Idol and his longtime guitarist Steve Stevens to Sammy Hagar, Guns N’ Roses veterans Slash and Duff McKagan and members of Rage Against the Machine, Red Hot Chili Peppers, Alice in Chains, Godsmack, among others. See the full lineup below.

But there’s one oddity in the announcement: It doesn’t name any of Aerosmith’s members.

That is key because frontman Steven Tyler has battled voice problems in recent years, and drummer Joey Kramer was absent from the Boston group’s most previous tour — which was billed as a farewell. But the photo above was included with the announcement, and it features all five members of Aerosmith’s classic lineup: Tyler, Kramer, guitarists Joe Perry and Brad Whitford and bassist Tom Hamilton.

And here’s a teaser that was posted to Aerosmith’s socials on Tuesday:

&…. all will be revealed tomorrow. 7 am pt. pic.twitter.com/JSr0Tj3t2W — Aerosmith (@Aerosmith) October 5, 2026

It’s been more than two years since Aerosmith retired from touring. The group announced the “Peace Out” farewell tour in May 2023, but it was halted abruptly that September due to Tyler’s vocal cord and larynx problems. The postponed dates were rescheduled, but the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame band said “no more, no more” in August 2024.

That appears to have changed.

Aerosmith has amassed 17 platinum albums since 1970 while flooding airwaves with such classic songs as “Dream On,” “Walk This Way,” “Sweet Emotion,” “Back in the Saddle,” “Last Child,” “Janie’s Got a Gun,” and a slew of rock ballads including its lone No.1 pop single “I Don’t Want to Miss a Thing,” penned by Diane Warren for the 1998 movie Armageddon. After a mid-career lull in the 1980s, the band rocketed back with three consecutive albums from 1987-93 that sold at least 5 million copies each: Permanent Vacation, Pump and Get a Grip

Along with those mentioned above, here are the other acts scheduled to play with Aerosmith on at least one of the two dates: Andrew Watt, Chad Smith, Eric Church, Jerry Cantrell, Marcus King, Mike Inez, Nuno Bettencourt, Pat Monahan, Sully Erna, Tom Morello, Adam Wakeman, Audley Freed, Kenny Aronoff. Producer and Was Not Was frontman Don Was will serve as music director.

Ticket presales begin tomorrow, October 8, followed by a regular sale on October 10.

title: In New Book, Joe Biden’s National Security Aide Brett McGurk Describes Jeffrey Katzenberg & Steven Spielberg Advising POTUS On Major Gaza Speech
summary: Brett McGurk’s new book Brink: Inside the Race to Free the October 7th Hostages offers an insider account of the diplomatic rollercoaster to secure a ceasefire and hostage release in the war in Gaza. The book, published this week, also offers a glimpse at White House messaging about the conflict, including two figures the president […]
content:
Brett McGurk‘s new book Brink: Inside the Race to Free the October 7th Hostages offers an insider account of the diplomatic rollercoaster to secure a ceasefire and hostage release in the war in Gaza.

The book, published this week, also offers a glimpse at White House messaging about the conflict, including two figures the president turned to in delivering a key speech: Jeffrey Katzenberg and Steven Spielberg.

McGurk, who served as deputy assistant for national security affairs to Biden, wrote of the scene as they prepared the president for his address on May 31, 2024. While Katzenberg and Spielberg’s role have been reported before, McGurk gave a first-hand account in the room, for a speech focused on a proposal to end the fighting and to secure a release of the hostages.

By that point, the Gaza conflict had created divisions within the Democratic coalition, protests at college campuses and presidential appearances and concerns over its impact on the November elections. There was pressure from the campaign for the president to make an address on the crisis, per McGurk.

Watch on Deadline

McGurk wrote of the rehearsal, “In the Map Room, Biden peered at two screens behind me. ‘Jeffrey, Steven, welcome,’ he said. I turned around to see Jeffery Katzenberg and Steven Spielberg on Zoom. They greeted Biden warmly, Spielberg saying this was the speech they wanted to hear.

“It was a reminder that while I saw this speech as a policy address with a functional aim, it had a political purpose, too,” McGurk wrote.

He added, “The speech was timed for Friday night in Israel, when much of the country shuts down, allowing time for us to shape its reception there and around the world. Notably, we did not inform Netanyahu that we were making the speech until shortly before Biden delivered it, as we knew the address would lock Netanyahu into the terms of the deal now on the table.

“Biden said he was ready.

“Katzenberg advised, ‘Remember, slow Joe, let the audience hear every word.’

“Biden smiled, ‘Slow Joe? Don’t let Jill hear that.’

“He read through the draft, pausing at times to ask questions about the text, which we addressed with rewrites.”

McGurk wrote that he found Biden “fully engaged, leaning forward on the podium.”

He wrote, “The moguls told him he looked strong, and he did. There was no sign of the Biden we’d all see on a debate stage with Trump only four weeks later.”

The latter was a reference to Biden’s disastrous debate performance against Trump. What followed were weeks of calls on Biden to drop out, coming from some elected Democrats and prominent donors, until he exited the race on July 19. Katzenberg had played a prominent role as a top adviser to Biden’s re-election campaign.

While the Biden speech focused on a peace proposal, as it turned out, it would take until the next year, a week before Trump returned to office, for a ceasefire agreement to be reached.

title: Hulu Legal Drama ‘Conviction’ Casts Michael Gaston, F. Murray Abraham & Peter Friedman
