content:
EXCLUSIVE: Michael Gaston (The Leftovers, The Waterfront), F. Murray Abraham (The White Lotus, Homeland) and Peter Friedman (Succession, The Affair) have joined the recurring cast of Conviction, the Hulu drama series from David Shore.

She joins the previously announced Elisabeth Moss, who leads the series and executive produces, as well as Jimmi Simpson, William Jackson Harper, Kevin McKidd, Sebastian De Souza, Adam Godley, Linda Emond Ella Anderson, and Liza Colon-Zayas.

Based on the 2023 book of the same name by Jack Jordan, Conviction follows criminal defense attorney Neve Harper (Moss), a confident lawyer who finally has her shot at a career-making case: a high-profile murder where the husband is accused of killing his wife by setting their home on fire. But when a mysterious stranger begins blackmailing Neve, she is forced to compromise every legal, moral, and ethical obligation to gain an acquittal — or else risk her dark secrets being exposed.

Watch on Deadline

Gaston will play Detective Joe Sapricone. Abraham will play Dimitri Pasternak. Friedman will play Arthur Mill.

Executive producers include Shore (Shore Z Productions), Moss (Love & Squalor Pictures), Jordan, Warren Littlefield, Ann Johnson and Lisa Harrison (The Littlefield Co.), Bert Salke (Co-Lab21), Lindsey McManus (Love & Squalor Pictures) and Erin Gunn (Shore Z Productions).

Gaston is repped by Paradigm Talent Agency and Principal Entertainment LA. Abraham is repped by Innovative Artists Entertainment and Franklin, Weinrib, Rudell and Vasallo. Friedman is repped by Cornerstone Talent Agency and Lasher Group.

title: Questlove Reflects on the Power of Vulnerability and Being a Trailblazer: ‘I Gotta Be the Change I Want to Be’
summary: More than 30 years into his career, Questlove is still open to change. The Roots frontman and multi-hyphenate has performed in Jimmy Fallon’s in-house band for over a decade, was a producer on the “Hamilton” cast album, is an adjunct professor at NYU, hosts a podcast and has written eight books. Since 2020, Questlove has […]
content:
More than 30 years into his career, Questlove is still open to change.

The Roots frontman and multi-hyphenate has performed in Jimmy Fallon’s in-house band for over a decade, was a producer on the “Hamilton” cast album, is an adjunct professor at NYU, hosts a podcast and has written eight books.

Since 2020, Questlove has also directed four documentaries. It was that endeavor that he was initially most opposed to: “I had to do a lot of work to realize that — I know it’s cliché — I gotta be the change I want to be.”

Questlove sat down with Variety‘s Jem Aswad to discuss embracing vulnerability and being a changemaker at the Variety Experience and Culture Summit: The IRL Advantage presented by OUTFRONT.

Questlove said he would have called Prince his North Star when he first entered the industry. Now, with the “residue” of his Earth, Wind & Fire documentary still lingering, he said he feels like a new artist. “I’m still learning what the Questlove brand is,” he said. “I joke that this is Questlove 3.0 happening right now.”

“Earth, Wind & Fire (To Be Celestial vs That’s the Weight of the World)” was released in June. Directed and produced by Questlove, the documentary explores the band’s career and that of its founder, Maurice White. While creating the documentary, he read many of the books White read during the band’s genesis, which inspired his current approach to creativity.

Questlove recalled the “too cool for school” attitude he saw in artists like Miles Davis and his own mindset on his records as protecting vulnerability. “We see it in our politics. We see it in our creativity,” he said. “We’re going to implode as a world if we don’t learn what emotions are and how we can use our vulnerability.”

Questlove’s first documentary project, “Summer of Soul (…or, When the Revolution Could Not Be Televised),” about the 1969 Harlem Cultural Festival, came out in 2021. “You can’t discount the timing of everything,” he said of the film’s arrival after the initial lockdown and protests following the murder of George Floyd. He said people saw the film because they were curious, but “they didn’t realize how important it was to celebrate joy.”

His next project, “Sly Lives! (aka The Burden of Black Genius),” focused more on the tendency he noticed in Black creatives to self-sabotage after becoming successful. Then came the Earth, Wind & Fire documentary, which he made because he “wanted to make a film that lets us focus on our dreams.”

Still, Questlove didn’t think he was the right person for the job of documentarian prior to “Summer of Soul.” “I didn’t know I was a storyteller,” he said. “I’m out there like, ‘Well, search for a real storyteller,’ and they’re like, ‘Dude, you’re that storyteller.’ Once I realized it, it became a passion.” He described himself as someone who will use history to attract audiences, but will put things in his films to make the audience reckon with their present.

While he has ventured into filmmaking, Questlove has not left music behind. The Roots Picnic held its 18th iteration this May, headlined by Jay-Z. The festival has grown, but “we’re not just rubber-stamping,” he said. “We are curating the festival. We’re playing with some of the acts, and people really feel like a community.”

On “The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon,” The Roots serve as — among other things — the live walk-up music for guests. Some celebrities send requests for their entrance song, but Questlove said, “the magic of the show is what I choose your walk-on song.”

The best thing about “The Tonight Show,” Questlove said, is that it allows the band members to be present with their families. “The Beatles broke up after seven years, and we’re going on year 35 and we’re still like the best of friends,” he said. “We’re still as silly as we were in high school, and still fun. If you’re not friends with your partners, then all this is for naught.”

title: Disney Cruise Ship Believe to Debut ‘Encanto’ Musical, ‘Frozen’ Family Feast and More
summary: Disney has unveiled its latest cruise ship, Believe. The ship will embark on its maiden voyage on Dec. 18, 2027 from its homeport of Port Everglades in Fort Lauderdale, Fla. Among the brand-new experiences is the first stage adaptation of “Disney Encanto,” which will premiere on board and is being developed exclusively for the Disney […]
content:
Disney has unveiled its latest cruise ship, Believe. The ship will embark on its maiden voyage on Dec. 18, 2027 from its homeport of Port Everglades in Fort Lauderdale, Fla.

Among the brand-new experiences is the first stage adaptation of “Disney Encanto,” which will premiere on board and is being developed exclusively for the Disney Believe.

“Oaken’s Table: A Frozen Family Feast,” a brand-new, untold chapter in the “Frozen” story featuring Oaken, Anna and Kristoff, will also be unveiled. Set in a courtyard deep within the forest, Oaken and his family will invite guests to dine together while enjoying the musical stylings of his cousins.

Guests can also experience The Grand Hall, a living theater where characters from across the Disney universe take center stage, designed to evoke the vibrant world where the sky meets the sea from Disney Animation’s “Moana” films.

Popular on Variety

Among the other entertainment experiences based on Disney IP, the Wishing Well is a gathering space themed to the iconic settings and locales featured in the Disney animated classic “Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs.” Gazelle will be a “Zootopia”-inspired entertainment hub offering a variety of live shows designed for families to laugh, sing and compete together (plus adult-exclusive options at night). Inside Out: Joyful Sweets offers confectionery inspired by the Pixar series’ expanded cast of emotions from “Inside Out 2.” And there will be new cafes themed to “Big Hero 6″ and “Moana.”

Disney Believe joins its sister ships Disney Wish, Disney Treasure and Disney Destiny. It is part of the growth plan for Disney Cruise Line which will see the fleet expand to 13 ships in late 2030.

title: Payal Kapadia, Anurag Kashyap Joined by Kavita Gupta’s Cineroost as Producer on Prateek Vats’ ‘Chronicles of a Confession’ (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Kavita Gupta’s U.S.-based Cineroost has boarded Prateek Vats’ second feature, “Chronicles of a Confession,” as producer, joining Payal Kapadia and Anurag Kashyap on the project, which starts shooting in early November. Cineroost stepped in to handle global representation and U.S. markets, and to help get the film into production. It is the company’s next feature […]
content:
Kavita Gupta’s U.S.-based Cineroost has boarded Prateek Vats’ second feature, “Chronicles of a Confession,” as producer, joining Payal Kapadia and Anurag Kashyap on the project, which starts shooting in early November.

Cineroost stepped in to handle global representation and U.S. markets, and to help get the film into production. It is the company’s next feature after Vir Das’ “Baara Number.”

Penned by Vidur Nauriyal, Vats and Shubham, the drama centers on a Kashmiri shawl seller who admits to a crime he didn’t commit, kicking off a series of events nobody saw coming. The script was chosen for the Busan International Film Festival‘s Asian Cinema Fund, under its script development strand.

Vats broke through with “Eeb Allay Ooo!,” which world premiered at the Pingyao Film Festival in 2019 and took the Golden Gateway award at the Mumbai Film Festival that year. The film went on to screen at the Berlinale in 2020 and at Tribeca’s first online edition.

Popular on Variety

Ranjan Singh of Flip Films (“Songs of Forgotten Trees,” “Vagachipaani”) produces alongside Dubai’s Action Filmz, India’s Etched Films and Khan & Kumar Productions (“Lovers in the Blue Night”). The project’s producing and creative base stretches across India, the U.S. and the U.A.E. Kashyap and Kapadia serve as executive producers.

Kashyap, who was involved in Vats’ first film, said the director had spent a long time on a script he envies. “I almost want to steal it. And since I can’t, I have jumped on board as an executive producer,” Kashyap said. “It is an honor to associate with someone as great as Payal Kapadia who I have seen sticking to her voice and her ground as a filmmaker and then there is my own producer Ranjan Singh. What was there in this to not want to be part of it.”

Anand Bansal (“Dhuin,” “Gamak Ghar,” “The Elephant Whisperers”) is behind the camera, with Rajesh Thanickan (“Santosh,” “Homebound”) as supervising producer. Devika Dave (“Boong,” “Sherni”) handles production design, Himani Dehalvi (“Trial by Fire”) costumes and Bigyna Dahal (“The Fable,” “Khauff”) sound design.

“Prateek’s films mix humor and political commentary in a unique way which I have always admired. And this new project takes this to an even higher level,” Kapadia said.

“‘Chronicles of a Confession’ has been brewing for some years and I am thrilled that it is going on floor now,” Vats said. “The film solidifies my collaboration with producer Ranjan Singh, who has been with me since my debut feature, ‘Eeb Allay Ooo!'”

Gupta’s earliest film projects, 13 years ago, were with Kashyap, and the two have remained close. “Strong writing, the best creators and a stellar global creative team, everything about this film aligned with my vision for Cineroost – rare, global and rooted,” Gupta said.

The film marks the second major step in building out Cineroost’s slate.

“Business from films is not for my sustenance but really for my soul and passion,” Gupta said. “I find that to be a strength in the work I do in the creative world. I have the privilege of flirting with risk more than others.”

“A lot of my work for South Asian talent and projects has been under the radar,” she added. “I felt time has come for me to take bigger steps and come out from being in the shadows to do what I love, nurturing creative voices, enabling stories that matter and building bridges between divergent worlds.”

title: ‘Marshals’ Star Luke Grimes Says He Hasn’t Spoken to ‘Yellowstone’ Co-Star Kevin Costner ‘Since We Stopped Working Together’
summary: Kevin Costner and Luke Grimes may have played a father-son duo on-screen in “Yellowstone,” but off-screen, the two actors haven’t spoken since Taylor Sheridan’s Western drama concluded. “I’ve never spoken to Kevin since we stopped working together,” Grimes, who now stars in the “Yellowstone” spin-off “Marshals,” said in a recent interview with USA Today. “Not […]
content:
Kevin Costner and Luke Grimes may have played a father-son duo on-screen in “Yellowstone,” but off-screen, the two actors haven’t spoken since Taylor Sheridan’s Western drama concluded.

“I’ve never spoken to Kevin since we stopped working together,” Grimes, who now stars in the “Yellowstone” spin-off “Marshals,” said in a recent interview with USA Today. “Not for any other reason other than just, you know, we’re both busy guys and life moves on.”

“Yellowstone” ran for five seasons and came to an end in December, 2024. Costner appeared as the family patriarch, John Dutton, while Grimes played John’s youngest son, Kayce. Grimes appeared on the show throughout the duration of its run, while Costner’s character was killed off and subsequently did not return for the final six episodes of the show that made up Season 5B.

Popular on Variety

When asked if Costner would make a future appearance in “Marshals,” the actor said it “would be cool,” though he noted, “I doubt that will happen at this point.” He continued: “I just don’t know… I think, if there was a flashback, I’d probably rather it be with Monica than John. I think that’d be more poignant to the character, but we’ll see.” (Grimes was referring to Monica Long Dutton, Kayce’s wife, played by Kelsey Asbille. Her character has died of cancer by the time “Marshals” premieres.)

“I think that’d be more poignant to the character,” he said. “There’s been no conversation, but I sure would love it. I love working with her.”

Per the official “Marshals” logline, the spin-off follows Kayce as he ventures beyond Yellowstone Ranch and joins an “elite unit of U.S. Marshals, combining his skills as a cowboy and Navy SEAL to bring range justice to Montana, where he and his teammates must balance family, duty and the high psychological cost that comes with serving as the last line of defense in the region’s war on violence.”

Season 1 of the show premiered earlier this year in March, while Season 2 premiered Sunday.

title: ‘Star Wars: Galactic Racer’ Debuts on Amazon Luna Day and Date With Wide Release (Gaming News Roundup)
summary: “Star Wars: Galactic Racer” launched on Amazon’s gaming service Luna day and date alongside the game’s worldwide release across platforms including PlayStation 5, Xbox Series S and X and PC. Developed by Fuse Games, the studio behind the “Burnout” and “Need for Speed” franchises, “Star Wars: Galactic Racer” puts players behind the controls of a […]
content:
“Star Wars: Galactic Racer” launched on Amazon’s gaming service Luna day and date alongside the game’s worldwide release across platforms including PlayStation 5, Xbox Series S and X and PC.

Developed by Fuse Games, the studio behind the “Burnout” and “Need for Speed” franchises, “Star Wars: Galactic Racer” puts players behind the controls of a range of repulsorcraft in a racing circuit in a galaxy far, far away.

Set early during the New Republic era, the game introduces the Galactic League, an unsanctioned racing circuit assembled by Darius Pax. Players step into the role of Shade, a lone racer dreaming of glory and revenge. The high-stakes racing takes place across “Star Wars” planets like Jakku, the Graveyard of Giants, Ando Prime or Sentinel I.

Popular on Variety

“We’ve always believed Luna players deserve to be in the action from day one, and Star Wars: Galactic Racer makes that a reality for the first time,” said Jeff Gattis, head of gaming at Amazon. “Luna players can jump into the single-player campaign today without needing to own a console or wait for a lengthy download. And the best part: if they’re a Prime member, they already have it at no additional cost. It’s exactly the kind of experience we want to deliver on Luna, and we think players are going to love it.”

Prime members can start their engines on Amazon Luna on the same day as other platforms and play the single-player campaign.

See more gaming news from the week in the roundup below.

PARTNERSHIPS/COLLABS

Zara Larsson is collaborating with Winx Club for a limited-edition card from trading card brand Kayou.

Dressed in her outfit from the “Midnight Sun” music video, the card features Larsson posing alongside the Winx Club fairies. The collaboration will debut at New York Comic Con, which begins Thursday and goes until Sunday.

Kayou will also offer cards featuring “KPop Demon Hunters,” “My Little Pony” and “Monster Jam” at this year’s comic con.

*

Discord is teaming up with The Living Tombstone on an original Halloween track and a Halloween remix of the Discord ringtone.

The Living Tombstone’s new original track, “Don’t Hang Up the Call” and accompanying video are inspired by the quirks of how people actually spend time together on “Discord.” The Living Tombstone is putting its own spin on Discord’s iconic ringtone for the season.

The Living Tombstone’s have turned gaming and internet fandom into music inspired by the games and culture their fans love. Over 30 million users take part in personal, gaming and interest-based servers each month, including 7.2 million in music communities.

NEWLY ANNOUNCED GAMES

During RuneFest 2026 over the weekend, developer Jagex announced new content coming to “RuneScape,” “Old School RuneScape” and “RuneScape: Dragonwilds,” as well as an upcoming fourth “RuneScape” MMO game.

Still early in development, the as-yet-unnamed title will “bring the world of Gielinor to life in Unreal Engine, combining the depth, freedom and community-led spirit that have defined RuneScape for 25 years with the technology and game design possibilities of today,” per the team.

“RuneScape Reignited” launches Dec. 2, inviting players old and new to return together and rediscover “RuneScape” with the ultimate RuneScape experience.

Players can get full Reignited Access without a membership from Dec. 2 to Dec. 12. The Plugin API is launching in October, with players getting an early hands-on ahead of official release.

“Hoard of Dragons” kicks off in January, offering a sequel to the popular “Dragon Slayer” quest, “City of Gnomes” continues the gnome storyline, first stated in 2002 and “Secrets of Karamja” introduces a new end game raid. These arcs weave together “RuneScape”’s 2027 content into three distinct story narratives and also include an agility skill rework, new skilling and solo bosses, new area expansions and a new “Grandmaster Quest.”

“Luminance,” a brand-new update serving as a prelude to 2027’s “Blood Crystal Saga,” launches in December this year, and features the introduction of the Elves into “RuneScape: Dragonwilds,” new elven-themed customisation options for player characters and buildings alike and the Prayer skill. “The Blood Crystal Saga” kicks off in 2027 starting with the Song of Rebellion in early 2027. Official modding arrives on “Dragonwilds” in 2027 through a new partnership with CurseForge.

*

Step into the castle! “The Traitors” fans can now test their scheming skills with “The Traitors: Interactive Game” on iOS and Android platforms, Fusebox Games announced on Monday.

Players begin by choosing a defining trait: the outspoken leader, the adaptable chameleon or the chaotic wildcard, which will form the foundation of your character.

Set across 12 days, 22 players emulate the TV show at the castle by building trust with other players during missions as well as building believable theories during The Round Table.

“When it comes to adapting iconic entertainment IP, Fusebox Games is as faithful a partner as they come,” Fusebox Games CEO Terry Lee said. “Our history is built on story-based, choice-driven games that put players in control, making the deceit and strategy of The Traitors a natural fit. We’re giving fans the chance to step out of the audience and take a seat at the table and tell their own story at the castle.”

TECH

Google is introducing “Playground,” an experimental gaming platform that lets users create, play and share fully custom games with no coding experience required.

With “Playground”’s conversational interface, users can create custom games by typing what they want, remixing starter prompts or getting guided support to help them share their creativity with the world. Users can refine the rules with prompts, customize characters and tweak the environment until it’s what they envision. “Playground” is browser-based, games are playable across phones and laptops.

Once a game is ready, users have the option to keep their game private, generate a shareable link to send to friends and family or publish it to share with the broader “Playground” community. Since “Playground” supports multiplayer gameplay, gamers can also see in-game leaderboards and follow other creators to see their latest creations.

The upcoming “Unity Spark Integration: Playground” will soon offer integration with UnitySpark so creators who want to expand their concepts can take advantage of Unity Spark’s robust, professional-level mechanics, 3-D capabilities and the flexibility of the Unity runtime.

title: ‘Beyond The Spider-Verse’ Director Bob Persichetti On “Limitless” Fan Expectations And “Never Saying No”
summary: Bob Persichetti, a director of Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse, concedes that the audience bar is rising ahead of the third outing in the Oscar-decorated blockbuster franchise. “Expectations are kind of limitless and we have to try to meet them,” he told Sony Pictures Animation President Kristine Belson with a grin during a panel discussion at […]
content:
Bob Persichetti, a director of Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse, concedes that the audience bar is rising ahead of the third outing in the Oscar-decorated blockbuster franchise.

“Expectations are kind of limitless and we have to try to meet them,” he told Sony Pictures Animation President Kristine Belson with a grin during a panel discussion at the Crunchyroll Anime Future Forum.

Even though the chat took place at the Javits Center, where New York Comic Con will be held over the next few days, the point of the session was not plot teases or fan service. (Persichetti did show attendees the same work-in-progress footage from the film that screened at Cinema Con in April but Sony is holding back for now on an official teaser for the June 2027 release.)

The discussion instead focused on process and also, in keeping with the theme across other Crunchyroll sessions, about creating an animated work that draws on a multitude of influences but retains its originality.

Watch on Deadline

Belson asked Persichetti, who directs the films with Justin K. Thompson, about how things have changed since the first installment in 2018.

“There were all these questions of, like, ‘Wait, who is it really for?!'” he recalled. “Because it’s not an outright comedy. There’s going to be action in it and Spider-Man guys – what are you doing?! And I think it was at that moment when we were in the room together and we screened it. It was made very clear to us that, ‘Oh, we have been underestimating the general audience for a long time in terms of what the sophistication of an animated film can be.'”

The first film wound up winning the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature en route to a global box office haul of $395 million. The follow-up, Across the Spider-Verse, took in $690.5 million in 2023 and was nominated for Best Animated Feature, losing out to The Boy and the Heron.

Since the franchise left its unique mark, Persichetti said, “The animation industry is going, ‘Oh, you can make choices that seem unorthodox and still make money and still succeed.'”

In the sequel, he said, “we piled on like five different looks and wondered if it was working and people said, ‘not only is it working, but we want more,’” the director said. “What we learned is that the audience is fine with the image changing every shot. … That’s ultimately how we were able to do so many things in one movie. The narrative throughline was creating this incredible visual extravagance.”

Technology has evolved dramatically since a decade ago when the franchise began. The filmmakers and crew are “seeing more creative choices” at a preliminary stage of the process, Persichetti said. “We’re able to think about a movie, holistically, creatively, much earlier.”

The collaborative way of making the film revolves around keeping an open mind, with writer/producers Phil Lord and Christopher Miller in the mix and material taken from real-life experiences. For all of its visual energy, Persichetti said, the original film “was really a movie, in my eyes, that was about Miles and his family. It was also sort of a love letter to New York. It’s also a love letter to hip-hop music and, ultimately, a love letter to Spider-Man.”

The filmmakers have “never said no to an idea,” the director continued. “If it’s an idea we’re doing in the movie, it will be stress-tested repeatedly, and then maybe the real idea ends up being not that thing but pieces of the stuff, pieces of that idea might fall into place on something else.”

The breakthrough of the first film earned the directors considerable leeway, Perischetti said. “We are very fortunate because we’re now on our third movie. The first two movies were successful, and the studio trusts us to make these movies. So we get to explore, probably way more than others do. But I will say, even on that first movie, we were exploring things that nobody believed in, and at first we weren’t even sure worked.”

title: SiriusXM Reaffirms Commitment To Comics “At Every Stage Of Their Careers,” Says Raw Comedy Decision Predated Maniscalco’s Arrival
summary: EXCLUSIVE: SiriusXM has reframed its statement on the viral Raw Dog Comedy debacle amid ongoing fallout with comics online. A spokesperson tells Deadline in an exclusive statement, “SiriusXM has proudly supported the comedy community, and we have been listening to comedians speak out this week. Our decision to end Raw Comedy was due to the […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: SiriusXM has reframed its statement on the viral Raw Dog Comedy debacle amid ongoing fallout with comics online.

A spokesperson tells Deadline in an exclusive statement, “SiriusXM has proudly supported the comedy community, and we have been listening to comedians speak out this week. Our decision to end Raw Comedy was due to the channel’s underperformance and came prior to Sebastian joining the SiriusXM lineup. While the challenges facing working comedians are bigger than any one person or decision, we remain committed, as we have for more than two decades, to making SiriusXM and Sebastian Maniscalco‘s Comedy Radio a place where comedians at every stage of their careers can be heard.”

What steps SiriusXM will take to address the issue called to their attention by legions of working- and middle-class comics is not yet clear.

Watch on Deadline

Interestingly, while discourse surrounding SiriusXM caught fire across social platforms earlier this week, it concerns a decision announced by the satellite radio provider all the way back in April.

We had the scoop, which was that SiriusXM would be replacing Raw Dog Comedy — a long-running channel on its subscription service — with the 24/7 branded channel Sebastian Maniscalco’s Comedy Radio.

As subsequently argued by many, including nonprofit Stand Up for Stand Up, this evolution of SiriusXM’s comedy programming had quietly taken away a reliable source of revenue for many of the comics who need it most. Whereas Raw Dog had given airtime, culminating in residuals, to a broad base of stand-ups, what’s happened at the new channel is a concentration of airplay among the industry’s upper echelon of comics — living and dead — which has boxed out many others.

Calling SiriusXM’s move “devastating,” comedian Liz Miele said, “Because of this action, hundreds of comedians will no longer be able to have these royalties. Working class comedians, people that only make money on the road, that have no safety net, that depend on this money to just survive, are going from having that money to nothing.”

Perhaps, she argued, Maniscalco had previously been unaware of the impact of the rebrand on the broader comedy community. “But now you know, and you can help us. You can fix this. We would love to be reincorporated into the channel and start getting the streams and plays that we were getting before you took it over.”

SiriusXM’s statement reflects their perspective that Maniscalco is catching shrapnel in this situation that was not of his own making, and which he does not deserve. Read our original story on the Raw Dog Comedy debacle here; for SiriusXM’s next moves, stay tuned.

title: Warner Bros. TV Boss Channing Dungey Says It Is Time To “Begin A New Chapter” As She Adds Paramount Cable Networks To Portfolio
summary: Channing Dungey has officially added new responsibilities and reports to her dance card. Deadline revealed over the weekend that Dungey, formerly Chairman and CEO, Warner Bros. Television Group and US Networks, now also will oversee the Paramount cable networks such as MTV, Comedy Central, Nickelodeon and BET. Dungey, who took on oversight of the WBD […]
content:
Channing Dungey has officially added new responsibilities and reports to her dance card.

Deadline revealed over the weekend that Dungey, formerly Chairman and CEO, Warner Bros. Television Group and US Networks, now also will oversee the Paramount cable networks such as MTV, Comedy Central, Nickelodeon and BET.

Dungey, who took on oversight of the WBD networks such as Discovery Channel, TLC, HGTV and Food Network at the start of 2025, said it was time to “turn the page and begin a new chapter.”

RELATED: A List Of Major Warner Bros. & Paramount Franchises, Film & TV Titles Coming Together At New Skydance

Watch on Deadline

She now reports to George Cheeks, Co-Chair and Chief Content Officer, Skydance TV and JB Perrette, Co-Chair and Chief Business Officer, Skydance TV.

In a memo to staff Tuesday, Dungey highlighted the studio’s current run that has seen it secure 13 new series orders and 13 renewals since the start of the year, meaning that its slate now includes more than 80 titles for more than 20 platforms. This includes Apple’s Ted Lasso, HBO Max’s The Pitt and Netflix’s Running Point as well as HBO Max’s Lanterns, which she said ranks among the top five series launches in the streamer’s history.

RELATED: ‘Lanterns’ Stars Kyle Chandler & Aaron Pierre On Going Deeper Into Hal’s Psyche And The Jordan Boys Legacy

Dungey also said she was looking forward to working with “talented studio heads” Matt Thunell, who is President of Paramount Television Studios, and David Stapf, President of CBS Studios.

But she admitted there was uncertainty across the company, given the savings that Co-CEOs David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz have discussed.

“I imagine many of you are arriving at this milestone with mixed emotions: pride in what your teams have accomplished, genuine excitement about the possibilities ahead, and understandably, some uncertainty about what comes next,” she wrote. “I don’t have all the answers today — some things will come into focus quickly, while others will take more time to figure out — but I am committed to keeping you as informed as I can as we move forward,” she said. “I’m sure you are wondering what all these changes mean for each of you individually. I don’t have further details at the moment, other than to assure you that our new leadership respects and appreciates how special our amazing, industry-leading team is, and I will be working closely with them on the strategy for our future success.”

RELATED: David Ellison, Ynon Kreiz Praise Staff, Lay Out Priorities For New Skydance: “Getting Here Has Been Quite A Journey”

She concluded: “As we embark on this next chapter in the company’s storied history, my hope is we can work together to make this transition as smooth and positive as possible for all involved, and to build a future for the studios that’s bigger and better than ever.”

RELATED: Skydance Stock Struggles In First Days Of Trading

RELATED: Skydance Bumps Pay, Extends Contracts For Top Execs; New Bonuses For WBD Brass

title: Bryan Fuller & Don Mancini Make Surprise Cameo In ‘Carrie’ Prom Scene
summary: With chaperones like these, it’s a wonder the prom in Prime Video’s Carrie didn’t end in a higher body count. Now available to stream, the penultimate episode “Romantic Literature” of Mike Flanagan’s series adaptation of the Stephen King book ends with the iconic pig’s blood splattering of Carrie White (Summer H. Howell). As the camera […]
content:
With chaperones like these, it’s a wonder the prom in Prime Video‘s Carrie didn’t end in a higher body count.

Now available to stream, the penultimate episode “Romantic Literature” of Mike Flanagan‘s series adaptation of the Stephen King book ends with the iconic pig’s blood splattering of Carrie White (Summer H. Howell).

As the camera cuts to the crowd, we see a gymnasium full of stunned faces, including those of Flanagan’s fellow horror maestros Bryan Fuller (Hannibal, Dust Bunny) and Don Mancini (Chucky, Child’s Play).

Last week, Mancini congratulated Flanagan on his series adaptation of King’s 1974 debut novel. “CONGRATULATIONS TO @flanaganfilm AND TO CHUCKY’S OLD PAL @summerhhowell ON YOUR BRILLIANT, HEARTRENDING NEW VERSION OF #carrie,” he wrote on Instagram. “Fans of De Palma’s film (it’s my official Favorite Horror Movie) will love it; the TV series is rewardingly, and thrillingly, different. Summer, Chucky is very proud of you!”

Watch on Deadline

Howell, who takes over the title role in Flanagan’s Carrie, previously made her onscreen debut as Alice Pierce in 2013’s Curse of Chucky, reprising the role in Cult of Chucky (2017), both from writer/director Mancini.

Bryan Fuller and Don Mancini in ‘Carrie’ Prime Video

Flanagan previously shared praise for Fuller’s “terrific” version of the Friday the 13th prequel series Crystal Lake, which has since been taken over by showrunner and EP Brad Caleb Kane, premiering Oct. 15 on Peacock.

content:
SPOILER ALERT: The story includes details about the Season 4 finale of Apple TV‘s Ted Lasso, titled “Being Alive.”

If you thought the penultimate episode of Ted Lasso was packed with Mae’s shocking death, Keeley’s (Juno Temple) surprise pregnancy and Zelda’s (Tracey Ullman) unexpected (for some) deceit, you’d better buckled up for the finale.

The 56-minute episode featured a touching memorial for Mae, including a moving song by Niamh (Aisling Sharkey) and Siobhan (Rex Hayes); not one but two AFC Richmond manager shakeups with Roy Kent (Brett Goldstein) quitting the men’s team to take the helm of his old team Chelsea, signaling a possible exit for the fan favorite character; and Alice Chilton (Tanya Reynolds) promoted to head coach of the women’s team upon Ted’s (Jason Sudeikis) recommendation, with him and Coach Beard (Brendan Hunt) as her assistants.

And that was not all. The shareholder showdown offered a twist too, with Zelda’s henchman Hugo switching sides and securing the Milk sisters’ shares for Rebecca (Hannah Waddingham), which, along with Mae’s 2% left to her in her will, gave the accidental football club owner an unassailable majority 51% ownership.

Watch on Deadline

Additionally, Ted told his son Henry about his father’s suicide. Oh, and the finale also managed to squeeze in a marriage proposal as Rebecca spontaneously popped the question to long-term boyfriend Matthijs in her office.

Hunt, who co-created the series and co-wrote the finale with Sudeikis, spoke with Deadline about the episode’s twists and how they set up a potential fifth season, addressing speculation that a renewal is imminent. He explained whether the finale marked the exit of Goldstein as a series regular (and Temple by association as Roy and Keeley are a couple again). Goldstein is the creator, exec producer and star of a new Amazon comedy series, Escorted, in addition to his duties on Apple TV’s Shrinking and his movie career.

Bad news for fans of Ted Lasso‘s original Richmond men’s team who have been holding out hope for a larger presence of the players in the show’s new incarnation. The cameos by most of them in the Season 4 finale may have been the last we saw the team in a planned “passing of the torch” moment from the men to the women, Hunt said, explaining why Phil Dunster’s Jamie Tartt didn’t make the scene.

Hunt detailed how Ted’s conversation with Rebecca led to Alice’s promotion and how the new dynamic may impact Ted. He also cleared confusion over the title of the finale, originally listed as “The Departing Lass” but changed to “Being Alive” when the episode aired.

Additionally, Hunt addressed the divisive character Zelda and whether Ullman would come back next season and shared the surprising inspiration for Beard’s new look in Season 4.

In separate parts of the interview published earlier, Hunt revealed that there was an idea for the late actor Anthony Head to be in the Season 4 finale and explained why the finale employed a cover of the theme song performed by Brandi Carlile.

DEADLINE: I hear that Season 5 renewal is imminent. What do you say?

BRENDAN HUNT: Where did you hear that?

DEADLINE: I have my sources.

HUNT: Well, then that’s news to me. I certainly hope it happens, and I’m optimistic, but yeah, haven’t heard anything official yet. It would be nice though.

DEADLINE: And you don’t have a Season 5 writers room going, correct? My understanding is that the writers room will start after the green light.

HUNT: Yeah. As happened for Season 2, they can greenlight a room before they greenlight a season if they want, but neither has happened.

DEADLINE: There were two big manager changes at AFC Richmond in the finale, the most important for longtime fans being Roy Kent’s departure. We know how busy Brett is off-screen — he has a new show on Amazon, obviously Shrinking on Apple TV, movies. So, should we assume that he is leaving as a series regular?

HUNT: No, not necessarily. It is acknowledging that he’s a busy man and giving us some wiggle room I would say. But no, there’s no expectation of losing Roy and Keeley. But they are two very busy people, so wiggle room is a smart thing.

DEADLINE: So it’s possible that both Brett and Juno may not be series regulars in Season 5 and the Roy and Keeley storyline may not be as prominent?

HUNT: We have no idea. We don’t know if we’re coming back, and when we come back, we don’t know what’s going to be going on in their lives. But yeah, they’re both really busy. So yeah, the wiggle room.

DEADLINE: Ted’s line to Rebecca about wanting “to talk to her about the newly open manager position” came just after Roy had resigned, so I assumed that was for the vacated men’s team job, and Ted was pitching himself or Nate who had just resurfaced. Instead, we got Coach Chilton promoted. Are the two things connected?

HUNT: He doesn’t say the men’s manager position.

DEADLINE: But why did he say “newly open”?

HUNT: Because he’s coming in to let her know that he is no longer the manager of the women’s team.

DEADLINE: OK. Let’s talk about the decision to change that dynamic. It does make sense, Alice has proven herself, and it’s a women’s team, but Ted for the first time being a backup singer, how will that be? And will the show be called Alice Chilton next season?

HUNT: Yeah, I think Apple’s really excited about that (laughs). We just have to wait and see what is going to be the full impact of that dynamic. I’m certainly interested in finding out like, is this a bit pie in the sky for Ted to think he can just shift down to backseat and have someone telling him what to do and where to be and making demands of him? We’ll see how how he adjusted that. It might not be as easy as he thinks.

DEADLINE: What prompted him to do that? We didn’t get to hear his arguments to Rebecca.

HUNT: Well, he clearly is not spending enough time with his son, and he says to Henry in that previous scene, “I’m going to make some changes to make sure that I’m not missing as many of your games.”

DEADLINE: And the men’s team, is it now completely in the rearview mirror? Roy Kent was the only character that kept it in the picture even though we didn’t see any of their games or any of the players until the finale. Do we care about who the manager will be? Is there any chance for Nick Mohammed’s Nate to come back?

HUNT: I’m not sure that we do care. We do love Nick, though. The men showing up in that last episode was really meant to be a passing-of-the-torch moment, and I think that worked well. We’ve been very judicious with how much we see of the players this first season, and whether or not we’re coming back, we’ve taken the long view from the beginning.

Back in Season 1, we actually met the players just a very little bit, and a little more in Season 2 and Season 3. So if we’re able to come back, then yeah, we’ll certainly be able to start giving more time to these players now that we’ve gotten done a little bit.

DEADLINE: Speaking of the players, the two Irish twin sisters emerged as standouts at the end of the season with their hilarious telepathy pig bit in episode 9 and their touching performance at Mae’s memorial in the finale. Will we see more of that next season and more of Alice’s personal life? There was only one scene with her partner this season.

HUNT: We’ll have a lot to see but we like all these characters, and we’re gonna try to get into all of them, a little bit more now that we set the table with them. But in terms of the twins, Rex and Ash were just fantastic together. There were a few good nominees for the twins when we were casting, but in the end it was like, these are them, and the degree to which they are different and similar is fantastic. They’re so game for everything, and then to finally unlock that twin-telepathy thing towards the end was just really really cool.

DEADLINE: Did they sing that song themselves and how did that come about?

HUNT: That is a traditional Celtic song that gets sung at funerals a lot. It was actually first pitched by Declan Lowney, one of our directors, who is an Irishman himself. And yeah, they crushed it.

DEADLINE: Phil Dunster was not in the finale with the rest of the team. Was it just for logistical reasons because he has the HBO series Rooster?

HUNT: It was a logic thing. Jamie lives in Spain [He plays for Barcelona]. We’ve already seen him at that point, so we didn’t need to bring him back just to stand and applaud with the rest.

DEADLINE: Speaking of Jamie, your character Coach Beard underwent quite a transformation this season, and there was online chatter that Beard may have tried to copy Jamie Tartt’s look.

HUNT: I didn’t see that.

DEADLINE: Talk about Beard’s physical transformation. Is it simply a midlife crisis, or was there more to it?

HUNT: Yeah, he is going through a bit of a midlife crisis. First the Jane stuff, then trying to come back from the Jane stuff, and then getting the gut-punch of miscommunication on New Year’s. We were not specifically going for Jamie Tartt but what a compliment. I’ll take it.

DEADLINE: Was there inspiration for the look, though?

HUNT: Not specific to Jamie, no, the hair was more Hugh Grant in his Four Weddings and a Funeral days, and then went to the costume department and our designer Jackie Levy, and it was awesome. Like what trying-too-hard-to-look-like-a-young-person stuff do we have? Now maybe she had Jamie in mind. I can’t speak for her, but that was never discussed specifically.

DEADLINE: And the new look introduced at the end of the finale, was it Walter White-inspired?

HUNT: It’s just a bald head and goatee, Walter White didn’t invent that.

DEADLINE: Tracey Ullman’s character Zelda, I’m sure you’ve seen the discourse, she was very polarizing. Talk about her arc, and since Zelda technically is still a pretty significant Richmond owner, would you want her to come back?

HUNT: We love Tracey, and we love that character. Zelda has a stake but not a majority one. Again, the same with with Roy and Keeley, there’s wiggle room there. Hopefully we get the chance to have her come over for some more. But we’re not plot-obligated to have her around in every episode, and Tracey can go on with her life.

DEADLINE: The title of the finale changed last-minute to “Being Alive”? Why? Was “The Departing Lass” too British?

HUNT: Well, the change had been made a few weeks ago — it just apparently didn’t make it to whoever puts those titles up, so it was not as late a change as it seems. It had been “Being Alive” for the last like month at least. That was Jason’s call entirely. He didn’t walk me through his thought process entirely, what it did. I watched it last night, and when Hannah has her line about being alive, it was a nice little echo, frankly. So it is a little more than what the episode is about than just about the lass who has departed and a a cute little pun.

DEADLINE: I don’t think we ever find found out how the women’s team ended the football season, did they win the final game?

HUNT: They got promoted in the second to last episode, and then the win in the last episode is that they sold out. So the results of the game itself better than that.

title: Josh Hartnett Leads Netflix’s Exhilarating Sea Monster Thriller ‘Below’: TV Review
summary: The oceans’ vastness can feel ominous, and though scientists have studied what lurks beneath, so much remains unknown. In Netflix’s new limited series “Below,” creator Jesse McKeown introduces viewers to a tiny town in the Canadian province of Newfoundland, a man still haunted by his past and a family desperate to look ahead toward the […]
content:
The oceans’ vastness can feel ominous, and though scientists have studied what lurks beneath, so much remains unknown. In Netflix’s new limited series “Below,” creator Jesse McKeown introduces viewers to a tiny town in the Canadian province of Newfoundland, a man still haunted by his past and a family desperate to look ahead toward the future. Deeply intriguing and at times terrifying, “Below” is a perfectly paced thriller. The series masterfully blends genres, looking beyond the mythos of sea creatures to take a hard look at human nature, especially as we continue down the harrowing road of an irreparable climate crisis.



“Below” opens in 1986 in Newfoundland. Nine-year-old Calvin Penney (Azriel Dalman) and his family are relocating from Little Pot Rock to a slightly larger island, Snook’s Arm. Sitting in a boat, tugging their house behind them, the journey initially appears to be going smoothly. But, after a mysterious incident, Calvin is forced to cut the tow between the boat and the house, leaving his father to drown. Forty years later, adult Calvin (Josh Hartnett) is still haunted by the event.



Though his father’s death torments him, Calvin is an affable, hardworking widower. Fishing has long dried up in Snook’s Arm, so Calvin and his son Wade (Charlie Heaton) make a living by collecting ice for a local vodka brewery and running an Airbnb out of their home. Calvin is especially pleased to celebrate Come Home Year because his other children, Mary (Ruby Stokes) and Jay (Rohan Campbell), are back to the island for a week-long stay. Unfortunately, the visit doesn’t go as smoothly as Calvin expects. The brewery rejects his latest ice haul due to its stench, which leads him to Dr. Fonda Howander (Mackenzie Davis), who runs the local science center. Soon, after Wade, who loves to self-medicate his ADHD with alcohol and mushrooms, is involved in a horrific accident, and Snook’s Cove residents begin acting oddly, Calvin and Fonda realize something is amiss in the water.



Save for Hartnett’s hilarious attempt at a Newfoundland accent, “Below” is a gripping watch. McKeown offers audiences a beautiful snapshot of an eroding but close-knit community and a man determined to save it. Though Calvin’s children and sister Ruth (Willow Kean), who works as Snook’s Arms Harbor Master, realize there are very few resources left to hold on to, Calvin digs in his heels, determined to find a way forward. As the town and its residents descend into chaos after a massive iceberg emerges from the water, Calvin realizes it might all be connected to his father’s accident.



At just six episodes, each running 45 minutes or less, “Below” is engrossing because it’s more than it appears. Although a horrifying sea creature sits at the center of the show, this story is about a man desperate to cling to a decaying past, a grieving family and how greed can create monsters. Episode 4, “The Ocean Will Have Us All,” is particularly riveting. The episode centers around the creature, but it also showcases how far people are willing to go and who they will sacrifice — no matter the cost — for their own selfish gains. The final minutes of the episode show some gutting displays of inhumanity, which only begin to make sense in the penultimate episode, titled “Little Pot Rock.”



In the end, “Below” is a captivating ride blending horror and suspense while centering our very real climate crisis. As a result, McKeown delivers a truly unique story in a well-worn genre. By examining the Penney family and the place they call home, the show addresses the fragility of life, the impermanence of place and how small we are in the universe. Moreover, the series reminds audiences that change is inevitable, and the only way to deal with it is to shift and adjust when it comes.

“Below” is now streaming on Netflix.

title: Vancouver Film Festival Prizes: Big Wins for Immigrant Tale ‘Nina Roza,’ the ‘Polished Cinematic’ ‘In the Heart of the South’ and Separated Sisters Story ‘How We Stand’
summary: Geneviève Dulude-De Celles’ “Nina Roza,” Nyla Innuksuk’s “In the Heart of the South” and Marie Clements’ “How We Stand” are among the films taking top honors at the 45th Vancouver International Film Festival (VIFF). The festival announced its 2026 juried awards winners on Wednesday night, recognizing films across its Summit, Horizon, Tides, Arbutus, Vanguard and […]
content:
Geneviève Dulude-De Celles’ “Nina Roza,” Nyla Innuksuk’s “In the Heart of the South” and Marie Clements’ “How We Stand” are among the films taking top honors at the 45th Vancouver International Film Festival (VIFF).

The festival announced its 2026 juried awards winners on Wednesday night, recognizing films across its Summit, Horizon, Tides, Arbutus, Vanguard and Short Forum competitions.

The Summit Award went to “Nina Roza,” directed by Dulude-De Celles, which the jury praised for its compassionate exploration of the immigrant experience, identity and belonging. The film follows a protagonist returning to his hometown for the first time in 28 years, drawn back by the mystery surrounding a young artistic prodigy. “We all know what it’s like to long for home,” said the jury, “We were all enamored by this film’s direction, authentic performances, stunning cinematography, and evocative music.”

Popular on Variety

Ian Bawa’s “Strong Son” snagged a special mention.

For the Horizon Award, the jury selected Nyla Innuksuk’s “In the Heart of the South,” describing the film as a “strong example of Canadian cinema.” The jury praised its performances by Anna Lambe and Zorga Qaunaq and “polished cinematic approach.”

Nathan Donovan’s “Clubfoot” received the Horizon jury’s special mention.

Banchi Hanuse’s “Ceremony” scooped the The Tides Award for a feature about the disappearance of ooligan fish from Bella Coola and the Nuxalk Nation’s efforts to protect and preserve its lands and waters. “Through beautiful cinematography and inventive storytelling, the film documents the strengths of community members consistently challenging the boundaries of imposed systems while drawing upon the resilience and generosity of their ancestors,” the jury said.

A special mention went to Carol Nguyen’s “Still Night, Burning House.”

The Arbutus Award, which recognizes British Columbia filmmaking, went to Marie Clements’ “How We Stand,” a story of sisters separated by tragedy. The film confronts “difficult and traumatic history by bringing it into vivid, real, human focus. Its surrealist style, deft storytelling, heart, and powerful heroines at once entertain, educate and demand self-reflection—as individuals, and as a society,” the jury noted.

Hayley Gray and Kaayla Whachell’s “Send the Rain” won a special mention.

“Hear the Yellow,” directed by Banu Sıvacı, took the Vanguard Award kudos, praised for its “remarkable depth,” “originality,” “singular cinematic language” and “emotional precision,” said the jury, stating that through “bold character work and intelligent use of metaphor, it transports us into a vividly specific landscape while creating a powerful dialogue between rural and urban, and a family separated by time.”

Samuel Urbina’s “That Shadow Fading” received the Vanguard special mention.

The Short Forum Award was adjudicated to “Pre-Parenting,” an animated film by Taiwan-based filmmaker Yu Yu, with a special mention scored by Kamal Aljafari’s “Going Home.”

The juried awards come as VIFF wraps its 45th edition on Oct. 11.

The Vancouver International Film Festival (VIFF) 2026 Juries

Summit Award: Rhia Aden, Nach Dudsdeemaytha, Caitlyn Sponheimer

Horizon Award: Arjun Ayillath, Madeleine Davis, Michael Mann

Tides Award: Selwyn Jacob, Lyana Patrick, Jeff Lee Petry

Arbitus Award Jury: Josephine Anderson, Brenda Lieberman, David Taylor

Vanguard Award Jury: Joaquin Cardoner, Caroline Monnet, Sarah Shamash

Short Film Award Jury: Tanvi Bhatia, Ariel Bond, Thanh Lieu

title: James Gunn Responds to ‘Clayface’ Criticism: ‘The Public Voting on What IP They Want to See’ Isn’t ‘the Only Way to Make a Movie’
summary: James Gunn has an answer to the question of “who tf asked for a Clayface movie,” posed by a user on the DC Studios head’s Threads account earlier this week. “Who tf asked for Back to the Future? Casablanca? There’s Something About Mary? Pan’s Labyrinth? Fury Road? Weapons? The Matrix?” Gunn fired back on the […]
content:
James Gunn has an answer to the question of “who tf asked for a Clayface movie,” posed by a user on the DC Studios head’s Threads account earlier this week.

“Who tf asked for Back to the Future? Casablanca? There’s Something About Mary? Pan’s Labyrinth? Fury Road? Weapons? The Matrix?” Gunn fired back on the platform. (The user’s original comment has since been deleted.) “Although it may seem like it, Hollywood isn’t a place where the only way to make a movie is the public voting on what IP they want to see that they’ve seen countless times before.”

He posted again: “Sometimes someone — in this case initially Mike Flanagan and then James Watkins and Hossein Amini — were inspired by a relatively little-known fictional character and crafted what I believe is a very special story around that character. I’d take that inspiration a thousand times over some writer trying to make a buck by writing a listless screenplay about a majorly popular character he or she has no passion or feel for.”

Popular on Variety

Despite the fact that Clayface is a considerably nicher choice for a feature film compared to past DC movies like “Supergirl” and “Superman,” most fans have been eagerly awaiting the premiere of “Clayface” since the gory trailer premiered months ago. And while versions of the character have appeared on screen in the years since the comic’s 1940 debut, the film, directed by James Watkins (“Speak No Evil”), marks the first time audiences will see the shape-shifting villain in a film all of his own.

Tom Rhys Harries plays the titular character, also known as Matt Hagen. “Matt Hagen’s meteoric rise from Gotham street kid to Hollywood leading man is tragically cut short when a local crime boss’s actions leave him horribly disfigured,” reads the film’s official description. “Abandoned by his team and with nothing left, Matt seeks out a cutting-edge treatment that miraculously returns him to his former self… but also unexpectedly affects his grip on reality, spiraling him down a destructive path of all-consuming revenge.” Naomi Ackie, David Dencik, Max Minghella and Eddie Marsan also star.

“Clayface” hits theaters on Oct. 23.

title: Doha Film Festival Unveils Competition Lineup With Accent on Female Filmmakers and Middle East Fare
summary: The upcoming Doha Film Festival has unveiled its 15-title competition lineup made up mostly of Middle East premieres of movies from the region, seven of which directed by women. As previously announced, Yemeni-Scottish filmmaker Sara Ishaq’s timely drama “The Station,” which looks at the impact of Yemen’s civil war on the country, is set as […]
content:
The upcoming Doha Film Festival has unveiled its 15-title competition lineup made up mostly of Middle East premieres of movies from the region, seven of which directed by women.

As previously announced, Yemeni-Scottish filmmaker Sara Ishaq’s timely drama “The Station,” which looks at the impact of Yemen’s civil war on the country, is set as opener of the revamped event’s second edition, which will run Nov. 19-27 in the Qatari capital.

Similarly to last year’s inaugural event, the Palestinian plight features prominently in the selection with four Palestinian films in competition. They include: Hosam Abu Dan’s debut feature “Thirteen in Gaza,” shot entirely in the Gaza strip, that won a prize in Toronto; the doc “Sama,” by Rabab Khamis, about a 10-year-old girl from Gaza who collects plastic and cardboard to sell as fuel, which is world-premiering in Doha; and absurdist drama “Conversations with the Sea,” directed by Muayad Alayan, that launched in Venice.

Popular on Variety

Other standout titles in the Doha competition strand include Moroccan filmmaker and photographer Tala Hadid’s “Bardi” (film still, above) in which “farmers and workers in central Morocco become warriors and princes through Tbourida, a centuries-old equestrian tradition,” as the synopsis puts it. The film recently had its world premiere at the New York Film Festival.

Sub-Saharan Africa is repped by two entries: “House of the Wind” by Cameroon’s Auguste Bernard Kouemo Yanghu that won both the Lion of the Future for a first film and the Special Orizzonti Jury Prize at Venice; and gritty, rap-infused “My Semba,” a portrait of Angola’s underground scene that follows three orphaned siblings in Luanda and blends documentary and fiction filmmaking.

Three entries from Asia include “9 Temples to Heaven,” directed by Sompot Chidgasornpongse, which follows a family visiting nine temples in a single day in the hope of keeping their grandmother alive. The film is Thailand’s international Oscar submission.

Eleven of the 15 titles that will screen in Doha are supported by the Doha Film Institute.

“Cinema has the power to carry voices across borders and create connections where distance and difference might otherwise divide us,” said Doha Film Institute CEO Fatma Hassan Alremaihi in a statement. “Doha Film Festival was created to give those voices a home, particularly filmmakers who challenge conventions to bring unheard stories to the screen and demonstrate the possibilities of independent cinema,” she added.

The revamped Doha Film Festival has transformed the DFI’s existing Ajyal Film Festival, dedicated to youth and family-friendly cinema, into a more ambitious international event for a broader audience.

The top prizes to be dished out will be: best narrative, worth $75,000; documentary, worth $50,000; artistic achievement, worth $45,000; and the gender-neutral performance acting award, worth $15,000.

Key partners of the Doha Film Festival include Katara, Media City Qatar – Film Committee, and Visit Qatar.

See the full Doha Film Festival competition lineup below.
