Tommy Ng is also working on the webtoon as a project supervisor. Yeung and Eden Bernal are co-writing the script.

It will focus on the fan-favorite character of Dark Sky in Another World – a headless swordsman who serves as an assassin and a guardian – as Point Five Creations prepares future film and series entries in the franchise.

CSI, which is supporting the transmedia expansion, is an initiative under Hong Kong’s Cultural and Creative Industries Development Agency.

Led by CEO Cho Hea-seung, Creative SUMM is a leading Korean content studio known internationally for producing mega-hit webtoon The Red Sleeve, which accumulated more than 100 million views and inspired the hit MBC television drama, as well as acclaimed webtoons including Leafie, A Hen into the Wild, Beauty Water and Underdog.

title: Vietnam’s Mockingbird Launches Horror Duo & Comedy Drama ‘The Happiest Cell’ At Busan’s ACFM
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Mockingbird Pictures is launching three new titles at Busan’s Asian Contents & Film Market, heading a slate of horror, supernatural mystery, comedy and family drama as the range of genre films emerging from Vietnam and Southeast Asia continues to expand. Horror, the bedrock of Southeast Asian genre cinema, features prominently on the slate through […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Mockingbird Pictures is launching three new titles at Busan’s Asian Contents & Film Market, heading a slate of horror, supernatural mystery, comedy and family drama as the range of genre films emerging from Vietnam and Southeast Asia continues to expand.

Horror, the bedrock of Southeast Asian genre cinema, features prominently on the slate through two new titles: Indonesia’s The Doll Ghawiah and Vietnam’s The River Demon (Út Lan 2). However, another new title, Bluebells Studios’ The Happiest Cell, is a prison-set comedy drama revealing that Vietnamese studios are moving beyond horror to experiment with different genres.

Directed by Guntur Soeharjanto, The Doll Ghawiah is the latest chapter in Hitmaker Studios’ long-running The Doll universe, a franchise that has drawn around 5 million admissions in Indonesia. Set in 1988, this new installment follows a family who leaves Jakarta for Bandung in search of a fresh start, only to be terrorized by the restless spirit of a young girl and her doll, Ghawiah.

Watch on Deadline

RELATED: Zhang Yimou Teases ‘Three-Body Problem’ At BIFF Opening; Jury Talks ‘The Assassin(s)’ Controversy & Competition Impact

The River Demon, directed by Tran Trong Dan, pushes Mockingbird’s slate into darker territory with an intense supernatural horror story rooted in Vietnamese folk beliefs. Following the success of The Guardian Demon, the film expands the filmmaker’s exploration of curses, rural legends and buried secrets through the story of a haunted riverside village, where the emergence of a two-headed serpent marks the beginning of a series of terrifying events.

Directed by Nguyen Nhat Trung, The Happiest Cell features a star-studded cast headed by Tuan Tran (Leaving Mom), Ma Ran Do (Hijacked) and Luong The Thanh (Betting With Ghost). Scheduled for release in Vietnam on November 20, the film is described as a “story that finds humor, friendship and humanity inside one of society’s harshest environments.”

RELATED: Maggie Gyllenhaal On Telling Women’s Stories; Casting Ellen Burstyn & Dakota Johnson In ‘Flesh Impact’ – Busan

Meanwhile, some of Mockingbird’s older titles are finding success at the box office and through international sales. Zero Meets Hero (Nghỉ Hè Sợ Nghỉ Hưu), directed by Huynh Lap, recently closed its domestic run with nearly $8 million (VND207.7BN), making it the third highest-grossing Vietnamese film of 2026. Blending comedy, family drama and supernatural elements, the film revolves around the relationship between a Gen Z grandson and his war-veteran grandfather.

Luck For Sale (Lên Hương), directed by Khuong Ngoc, is set for U.S. theatrical release October 9 across AMC, Regal and Cinemark theaters, accompanied by special screenings and a promotional tour with the film’s director and cast. The film is built around themes of family, mortality and generational wounds.

“We are not looking for one single formula for Southeast Asian cinema,” said Phong Duong, Business Director of Mockingbird Pictures. “What excites us is the range – established franchises, box office performers, culturally rooted genre films, emotionally driven dramas and major star-led productions. Southeast Asia is producing increasingly diverse commercial cinema, and our role is to help each film find the international audience and market where it can connect most strongly.”

In addition to international sales, Mockingbird is also a distributor of local and international films in Vietnam, handling around 60 theatrical releases and more than 100 post-theatrical titles annually.

title: How ‘Dying to Survive’ Director Wen Muye Turned a Cook’s War Into $342 Million China Smash ‘Once Upon a Time in the Middle East’: ‘I Never Think About Social Issues in Advance’
summary: Xu Fu went to the Middle East for the money. The Shenyang cook, played by Shen Teng in “Once Upon a Time in the Middle East,” takes the head-chef job at the Dragon Restaurant because the pay could help clear his family’s debts. When war breaks out, he is shaken from his sleep and runs […]
content:
Xu Fu went to the Middle East for the money. The Shenyang cook, played by Shen Teng in “Once Upon a Time in the Middle East,” takes the head-chef job at the Dragon Restaurant because the pay could help clear his family’s debts. When war breaks out, he is shaken from his sleep and runs for an air-raid shelter.

Director Wen Muye says he never stopped to think about how grand the film’s backdrop was.

“Although the backdrop may seem very large, for a specific little person – an ordinary person – this is a very concrete predicament that he has to face,” Wen tells Variety. “We try not to consider how grand it is; we only consider how great an impact it has on the character.”

Popular on Variety

Chinese audiences have followed that cook a long way. Since opening on Aug. 11, the film has grossed RMB2.29 billion ($342 million) in China, making it the third-highest-grossing Chinese film of 2026. It is Wen’s follow-up to “Dying to Survive” and “Nice View.”

The idea came from a news report and from the experiences of real Chinese cooks who run restaurants in the region.

“For me, Xu Fu is still an ordinary person, an ordinary chef,” Wen says. “What he goes through is in fact connected to the work he does as a chef, the food he makes, and his relationship with war. There is room there to express the relationship between war and peace.”

Shen is one of China’s biggest stars and is closely tied to comedy. Wen says that reputation was part of his thinking when he cast him in a war drama.

“But the fundamental premise was first and foremost that Shen Teng was very suitable for the role of Xu Fu. In my mind, Xu Fu is a middle-aged Northeastern chef with a sense of humor, and Shen Teng is comparatively very well suited to the role,” he says. “At the same time, he has the ability and talent for comedic performance, which naturally brings a certain sense of ease to some of the heavier themes.”

With restaurant manager Ma Junsheng (Jiang Qiming), Xu Fu turns the failing restaurant into a going concern. Once the fighting reaches the city, it becomes a shelter for people trapped by the war. Wen wanted to follow an ordinary cook through a conflict, and the restaurant came with the job.

“At first, it exists and prospers; later, it disappears from the protagonist’s view; and in the end, after the protagonist has grown old and returns to the Chinese restaurant, he sees that it is still standing there,” Wen says. “This is in fact a symbol of a certain kind of peace.”

For much of the story, Xu Fu looks out for himself and treats the war as someone else’s problem. That changes when Ma is killed rescuing children whom terrorists are forcing to become suicide bombers. Wen says he didn’t set out to ask what ordinary people owe one another.

“I think it is driven by human nature – whether Xu Fu or Ma Junsheng, these characters are driven by instinct,” he says.

To prepare, the team interviewed many people working in the region. They spoke to cooks, to workers from a wide range of trades and to locals who had lived through the war. Wen then tried to put himself in each character’s place at each moment.

“I never think about social issues in advance. What I actually want to tell is the story of specific people,” Wen says. “War and peace are certainly one theme of this film, but if you always write characters with that idea in mind, there will actually be problems.”

Omar Sherif plays Seif, a Kurdish Iraqi orphan who becomes Xu Fu’s apprentice. Aarif Lee makes a special appearance as Tony, a Chinese American private in the U.S. Army, and Sherif Sobhy plays Zaid, a civil servant and restaurant shareholder whom the war drives to seek revenge.

Wen wrote the screenplay with Lang Qunli and Zhong Wei, his co-writer on “Dying to Survive” and “Nice View.” Ning Hao is executive producer; Wen joined Ning’s Dirty Monkeys’ 72 Transformations Film Project in 2016. Wen studied under Tian Zhuangzhuang at the Beijing Film Academy, and “Dying to Survive” won him best new director at the 2018 Golden Horse Awards.

Well Go USA Entertainment releases the film in North America on Oct. 9.

title: ‘Avatar: Seven Havens’ Takes the Franchise in an Intriguing, Postapocalyptic New Direction: TV Review
summary: This summer, the Avatar franchise reintroduced itself by revisiting its most iconic character: Aang, the namesake of “Avatar: The Last Airbender” and the original protagonist of a story now in its third decade. For its next act, the Avatar Studios imprint — overseen by original series creators Michael Dante DiMartino and Bryan Konietzko and tasked […]
content:
This summer, the Avatar franchise reintroduced itself by revisiting its most iconic character: Aang, the namesake of “Avatar: The Last Airbender” and the original protagonist of a story now in its third decade. For its next act, the Avatar Studios imprint — overseen by original series creators Michael Dante DiMartino and Bryan Konietzko and tasked with expanding the Nickelodeon children’s show into a multimedia enterprise — faces the tougher task of introducing new protagonists and ideas while preserving Avatar’s core appeal.

The Paramount+ series “Avatar: Seven Havens” quite literally brings the saga into the future. Specifically, it’s been more than two centuries since the conclusion of “Avatar: The Legend of Korra,” the sequel series that wrapped its run in 2014. “Seven Havens,” also created by DiMartino and Konietzko, uses the leap forward to fundamentally alter the composition of this fictional world. (Longtime animation hand Ethan Spaulding, who executive produces, and co-executive producer Sehaj Sethi also form the creative team.) Gone are the four nations, corresponding to the elements, who coexisted in harmony that was disrupted and then, episode by episode, restored. In their place is a world reduced to a wasteland by an environmental cataclysm, supposedly caused by Korra herself. The namesake havens are city-states that offer refuge from sandstorms, bandits and other threats — and the Avatar, a quasi-messianic figure able to “bend” all four elements, is a stigmatized bogeyman who hasn’t appeared for generations.

Popular on Variety

Enter Pavi (Saheli Khan), an orphan from the haven of Ellora who spends her days scrounging for food, trying to keep her multi-element bending abilities under wraps and talking to the inanimate objects she keeps around in lieu of friends. Pavi’s name is an indication of another way “Seven Havens” expands the Avatar mythos: by incorporating South Asian culture to the universe’s pre-existing blend of Chinese, Japanese, Inuit and other influences. Pavi’s favorite snack are the kachoris knowingly left out by a local shopkeeper, herself voiced by veteran actor Sakina Jaffrey. Food, in general, is an object of concern for “Seven Havens”: Mochi, kimchi jjigae and bitter melon are all cited by name in the first few episodes alone.

But an equally significant update “Seven Havens” makes to the cosmology is in how the show depicts the natural world — always a preoccupation for a story grounded in air, earth, fire and water. The “Harshlands” that surround Ellora are filled with rocks, sand and a strange, haunted beauty. The color palette of “Seven Havens” is warmer than prior Avatar series, favoring the oranges and pinks of an almost Saharan expanse. (The music, from franchise stalwart Jeremy Zuckerman, also sets “Seven Havens” apart aurally with a more electronic sound.) There are cats with monkey tails, and camels that roll up in a ball like armadillos! With a postapocalyptic landscape indifferent and even hostile to human needs, “Seven Havens” reminded me of “Scavengers Reign,” the magnificent yet short-lived series on HBO Max. Hopefully, having the IP tie-in will give “Seven Havens” more time to explore its environment.

And “Seven Havens” could use some time to grow. Pavi is a younger hero than even 12-year-old Aang, perhaps an attempt to introduce Avatar to a new generation of kids where the movie was more of a service to pre-existing fans. Shy, nerdy and a pacifist by nature, Pavi has a personality, if one that’s still in formation. She’s mentored by Jae (Major Curda), a member of Ellora’s municipal Bending Brigade, and his captain Karthik (Akshay Khanna), who has a more optimistic view of the Avatar’s potential than those that blame her for ending the world. In the six episodes provided to critics, this crew hasn’t quite coalesced into a unified team, but “Seven Havens” successfully cultivates enough curiosity about how its world works to buy some time.

“Seven Havens” introduces another quirk to the Avatar legend I’m forbidden from disclosing, though it takes some pressure off Pavi as Karthik explores his theory that the Avatar can help revive the dying art of bending. (There are fewer benders born to each successive generation, we’re told, even as manipulating the elements is a vital defense against an onslaught of lightning and wind.) Combined with the imagery and an expanded pool of references, “Seven Havens” successfully makes clear that it’s a new and different kind of Avatar series, while maintaining the transportive world-building that’s helped the franchise endure.

The first three episodes of “Avatar: Seven Havens” are now streaming on Paramount+, with remaining episodes airing weekly in batches of three on Fridays.

title: Italy’s RAI Inks Major Deal for High-Profile, Female-Led Titles With Beta Film Ahead of Mipcom (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Italian public broadcaster RAI has acquired a slate of international, female-led drama series from Beta Film ahead of Mipcom. The package comprises “Barton Vet,” in which a veterinarian and her family-run team save animals in the countryside; the French thriller “A Guilty Affair,” about a high school principal desperately searching for her missing daughter; and […]
content:
Italian public broadcaster RAI has acquired a slate of international, female-led drama series from Beta Film ahead of Mipcom.

The package comprises “Barton Vet,” in which a veterinarian and her family-run team save animals in the countryside; the French thriller “A Guilty Affair,” about a high school principal desperately searching for her missing daughter; and the hot-selling German period drama “Mozart Mozart,” which centers on the musical genius’ overlooked – and equally gifted – sister.

The deals see the biggest government-backed broadcaster in Italy buying two shows which are backed in their finance by two of the other largest public broadcast networks in Europe. France Télévisions and Germany’s ARD, which outscales the BBC. In this, RAI’s purchases are a reminder of how, despite ever tighter budgets, such public broadcastres still drive a lion’s share or orders and buys in Europe.

Popular on Variety

Barton Vet Credit: Joanna Bell/Shaftesbury/Beta Film

A U.S.-Canadian procedural drama, the 12-episode “Barton Vet” stars Georgina Reilly (“Quantum Leap,” “City on a Hill”) as Dr. Kate Barton, who takes over the family’s rural veterinary clinic following the death of her father. Saving the lives of animals while juggling love and hardship, Kate must learn to heal herself along the way. Katia Edith Wood (“The Borderline”), Nadeem Umar-Khitab (“The Handmaid’s Tail”) and Sonja Smits also star.

Directed by Felipe Rodriguez (“Virgin River,” “The Good Doctor”), the series is produced by Shaftesbury in association with BYUtv and Beta Film, which is also selling it internationally.

The four-part French drama “A Guilty Affair” follows Morgane, a high school principal desperately searching for her daughter, who has disappeared. Was the girl murdered by the new physical education teacher with whom she’s been having an affair?

Directed by Sandra Perrin (“High Season”), the show stars Helene De Fougerolles (“Balthazar”), Florent Peyre (“Commandant Saint-Barth”) and Vittoria Di Savoia (“You+Me – Against the World”).

“A Guilty Affair” is produced by France Télévisions, Episode Productions, Be-Films and RTBF. Beta Film is handling international sales.

Mozart Mozart Credit: WDR/Story House Pictures

Described as “a fresh and bold reimagining of the Mozart legacy,” the opulent, six-episode period drama “Mozart Mozart” is a tale of ambition set in 1780’s Vienna and follows Maria Anna Mozart, the talented but overlooked sister of Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart. When her brother’s behavior threatens the family’s future, Maria Anna secretly takes his place and performs under his name to the same stunning effect.

Directed by Clara Zoë My-Linh von Arnim (“Marzahn, Mon Amour”) with a modern pop-sensibility, the series stars Havana Joy Josephine Braun (“Love Sucks”) and Eren M. Güvercin, who toplines Fatih Akin’s latest film, “Ghost Song.”

The German series is produced by Story House Pictures, a driving force behind Beta mega-hit “Sisi,” and in co-production with ARD (WDR/SWR/ARD Degeto Film), ORF and Dreaming Sheep Company. Beta Film and Bavaria Media are handling world sales.

John Hopewell contributed to this article.

title: Indian Crime Drama ‘Chaar Yaar’ Sets Global Premiere on Prime Video (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: “Chaar Yaar,” an eight-episode Hindi-language crime drama about four Mumbai friends who stumble into the city’s underworld, is headed for a worldwide launch on Prime Video. Purav Jha, Naman Jain, Saqib Ayub and Prayrak Mehta play the leads. The supporting ensemble includes Sai Tamhankar, Sikandar Kher, Dibyendu Bhattacharya, Rajesh Tailang, Chunky Panday and Bhagavathi Perumal. […]
content:
“Chaar Yaar,” an eight-episode Hindi-language crime drama about four Mumbai friends who stumble into the city’s underworld, is headed for a worldwide launch on Prime Video.

Purav Jha, Naman Jain, Saqib Ayub and Prayrak Mehta play the leads. The supporting ensemble includes Sai Tamhankar, Sikandar Kher, Dibyendu Bhattacharya, Rajesh Tailang, Chunky Panday and Bhagavathi Perumal.

Vinay Waikul directs from scripts by Sambit Mishra and Saurabh Sawant. The three share creator credit with S. Hussain Zaidi. BBC Studios India developed the series, which was produced by Pranati Nagarsheth, Niraj Nagarsheth and P.S. Shyam for Pink Window Production Pvt. Ltd.

The story is set in Mumbai in the early 2000s. Jay, Tony, Saahil and Sameer come from middle-class homes, and each is weighed down by family duties while hoping for something better. Hard times bring them closer. Then a single choice, made because they feel they have no other option, puts them in the path of gangsters and draws the attention of the police. Their bid to change their lives turns into a dangerous chase, and the friendship becomes the one thing protecting them.

Popular on Variety

“‘Chaar Yaar’ combines friendship, ambition, humor, and unexpected twists that makes for a thoroughly entertaining ride,” said Nikhil Madhok, director and head of originals (SVOD) at Prime Video and Amazon MGM Studios India. “We have always been at the forefront of backing new talent, and the stellar performances from our young lead cast are an absolute treat to watch. Vinay Waikul’s direction and craft bring a unique new flavor to this world.”

The show will stream exclusively in Hindi on Prime Video in India and more than 240 countries and territories from Oct. 23.

Prime Video’s local slate includes “Mirzapur,” “The Family Man,” “Panchayat,” “Paatal Lok” and “Farzi.”

title: Annecy Sci-Fi Animation ‘Pilgrims,’ From ‘Japan Sinks: 2020’ Director Heo Pyoungkang, Lands at EST N8 (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: “Pilgrims,” a Korean sci-fi animated feature that played Annecy and took a prize at Bucheon, has been picked up for worldwide sales by EST N8. It is the first animated title for the film financing, sales and distribution company. EST N8 will launch international sales on the film at the Busan International Film Festival’s Asian […]
content:
“Pilgrims,” a Korean sci-fi animated feature that played Annecy and took a prize at Bucheon, has been picked up for worldwide sales by EST N8.

It is the first animated title for the film financing, sales and distribution company.

EST N8 will launch international sales on the film at the Busan International Film Festival‘s Asian Contents & Film Market. Sophie Changhui Shi, head of studios at EST N8, negotiated the deal with Hugh Cha, co-CEO of Desert Bloom Pictures, who represented producer 21 Studios.

The film is the first feature adapted from Kim’s bestselling collection “If We Cannot Go at the Speed of Light,” which has sold 400,000 copies, and is based on one of its short stories. The story is set in an idyllic community where emotional suffering has been eliminated and where every resident, on turning 18, must spend a year on Earth. When Sophie starts to remember Daisy, a friend who went missing on Earth, she discovers troubling truths about the village and begins to wonder whether a painless existence is worth having if it comes without love.

Popular on Variety

Kim Hyang-gi (“Along with the Gods,” “Innocent Witness”), Park Ji-hu (“All of Us Are Dead,” “Concrete Utopia”) and Lee Joo-young (“Itaewon Class,” “Broker”) lead the voice cast. Hwang Soyoon, lead singer of the band Se So Neon, wrote the music. Hwang’s solo output includes “Smoke Sprite,” a collaboration with BTS member RM.

“‘Pilgrims’ asks a universal question through a distinctly Korean science-fiction story: Is a life without pain worth living if it also means a life without love?” Shi said. “The film brings together Kim Choyeop’s bestselling source material, Heo Pyoungkang’s nearly two decades in Japanese animation, and a voice cast with internationally recognized credits. It represents exactly what EST N8 stands for: bringing bold, elevated Asian storytelling to global audiences, and we are thrilled to introduce it as our first animated feature.”

Heo makes a feature directing debut after close to 20 years in the Japanese animation industry. Heo’s résumé includes the Netflix series “Japan Sinks: 2020,” on which Heo was series director, and Yuasa Masaaki’s “The Night Is Short, Walk on Girl,” on which Heo directed a unit. We Hyun-song heads up character design. We’s credits include “Inside Out 2,” and We worked as a concept artist on “KPop Demon Hunters.”

“This film portrays the journey of those who willingly embrace pain to choose love,” Heo said. “I would describe it as a work that asks how we can accept this imperfect world we live in and learn to love one another.”

21 Studios is based in Seoul and develops and produces IP, with a focus on stories that move between film and television. The company is run by CEO Huh Kyubum, a former venture capitalist with Union Investment Partners who focused on investing in Korean content.

“Pilgrims” picked up the Technical Award at the 2025 Bucheon International Animation Festival. It then played in the Animated Thrills & Chills strand at this year’s Annecy Animation Festival before Special Movie City released it in Korean cinemas.

Huh said the team set out to keep the emotional intimacy of Kim’s story while building a world that feels cinematic. “The film’s recognition at BIAF and selection at Annecy have shown that Sophie’s choice can speak across cultures,” Huh said. “We are pleased to partner with EST N8 to bring the film to international audiences.”

Three EST N8 executives will run the sales campaign and global release strategy: Jan Paul Villanueva, EVP of acquisitions and global distribution; Cathy Ni, head of sales and U.S. distribution; and Shams Pasha, global sales and marketing executive.

EST N8’s Busan market lineup also includes “Tame,” the Thai horror debut from B-EST Pictures; “Master,” the Rotterdam prizewinner from Rezwan Shahriar Sumit; Dean Colin Marcial’s Manila-set crime thriller “Jaguar”; the Taiwanese action film “Dead End” from Chan Chun-hao; and Mariko Tetsuya’s “Dear Stranger.”

The company was formed when EST Studios and N8 combined. It finances, sells and distributes Asian films worldwide, and also releases international titles across Asia. Its production and sales credits include the Oscar-shortlisted, Emmy-nominated “Hidden Letters,” the Toronto selection “K-Pops!” and “The Monk and the Gun,” Bhutan’s Oscar submission.

title: Daughter Of Dead BBC & ‘Paddington’ Star Accuses Royal Mail Of Resurrecting Her Father’s Voice Using AI: “It’s Outrageous”
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Lucy Wynne can’t just watch TV. She’s usually scribbling, talking, or scrolling with half an eye on the big screen. On the day she heard her dead Dad’s voice reverberate around her living room, Wynne froze. It was November 2025, 11 years after her father had passed. She had been reminded of his anniversary […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Lucy Wynne can’t just watch TV. She’s usually scribbling, talking, or scrolling with half an eye on the big screen. On the day she heard her dead Dad’s voice reverberate around her living room, Wynne froze. It was November 2025, 11 years after her father had passed. She had been reminded of his anniversary just days earlier in a Facebook Memory, but the sound of his voice was a visceral jolt.

“F***ing hell, that was Dad. Did you hear that?” she turned to her husband. “No, don’t be stupid,” Darren replied. “It f***ing was,” Wynne exclaimed. She was certain because her father’s voice was his work. When he spoke, his words were heard, not just in Wynne’s childhood home, but in homes across the UK. Paul Vaughan was the voice of the BBC’s heavyweight science series Horizon, and Radio 4’s esteemed arts show Kaleidoscope. He narrated Threads, the atomic bomb drama burned into the brains of a generation of Brits. Vaughan was even the voice of Paddington audiobooks.

And now, on an unremarkable autumnal evening in Buckinghamshire, Wynne was convinced that Vaughan had returned to her in a Royal Mail Christmas ad on ITV. It was not a welcome apparition. Instead of fond memories of her father, Wynne was filled with dread. She thought it was unlikely Vaughan had ever worked for Royal Mail. He certainly hadn’t provided a voiceover from the afterlife. Wynne feared that Vaughan’s voice was somehow recreated without permission. “Bloody bollocks,” she told her husband. “Somebody’s done something.”

Watch on Deadline

A still from Royal Mail’s Christmas ad

The Royal Mail’s 2025 festive campaign (scroll to the end of this story to hear the audio) celebrated how Christmas cards can bring loved ones together. The ads tell mini-stories of people posting heartfelt messages and end with the same slogan, spoken by a mellifluous male narrator: “Royal Mail, it’s so much more than just a card.” The campaign celebrates tangible human interaction, but in doing so, misled its audience.

Responding to questions from Deadline, Royal Mail, Britain’s 500-year-old postal service, admitted that it used artificial intelligence to deliver its festive message to the nation. Instead of paying an actor or voiceover artist to deliver the ad’s slogan, Royal Mail commissioned the ad’s producers to cut the human from the loop. A Royal Mail spokesperson said this is “increasingly common,” but not so common that the company was prepared to be transparent about its editorial choice at the time the ad aired. We only know about the use of AI because Wynne just so happened to recognize what she thought was her father’s voice. But was it Paul Vaughan?

The “so much more than just a card” campaign was overseen by an ad agency called Darwin & the Machines. The agency worked with independent producer Untold Studios to film the human stories at the heart of the campaign, using real actors in the UK. Darwin & the Machines subcontracted the voiceover to a company called Fameplay, an AI specialist based in Czechia. Fameplay is backed by Czech Media Invest, which is chaired by Daniel Křetínský, whose EP Group also happens to own the Royal Mail.

A UK source who worked on the advert told Deadline that Fameplay’s Juraj Felix, a close associate of Křetínský, was present during filming and was evangelical about using AI. “He was obsessed with AI voiceover,” the source said. “The production team told him that it was not a great idea to use AI in connection with such a venerable British brand, but they saw a business opportunity.”

Royal Mail was aware of the plan, but a spokesperson insisted that the voiceover was “not designed to replicate any specific individual.” But what if the Christmas card campaign unintentionally replicated a specific individual? Vaughan’s voice was warm, authoritative, and unmistakably English. “When God speaks, he uses Paul Vaughan’s voice,” observed a Daily Telegraph obituary. His broadcasting, advertising, and audiobook work means there is a wealth of professional material in the public domain featuring his words. In short, Vaughan is exactly the kind of voice that is ripe for training an AI model.

ElevenLabs Summit in London in 2026

Deadline asked Fameplay a series of questions about how it generated the Royal Mail voice, and the company insisted no reference to Vaughan was used in its generative prompts. We can reveal that Fameplay licensed its AI technology from ElevenLabs, the $22 billion AI audio giant that counts Matthew McConaughey among its investors and has a partnership with Michael Caine. Deadline posed similar questions to ElevenLabs, but the company would only confirm that the Royal Mail narration was not a direct voice clone of Vaughan. Asked whether its AI model might have been trained on material voiced by Vaughan, meaning that generic prompts could generate something that sounded like him, ElevenLabs declined to comment.

Royal Mail told Deadline that the advert’s producers “carried out checks and advised that these did not identify any resemblance concerns.” The trouble is that Wynne did identify resemblance concerns. As Vaughan’s daughter put it, there is an “inflection in his voice that no one else has.”

Wynne’s instinctive response is supported by academic study. Dr Nadine Lavan, a voice psychology expert at Queen Mary University of London, said her research shows that family members are very good at recognizing the voice of a loved one. “With Wynne recognizing the voice from the advert as being Paul, we can conclude the voice is very similar,” Lavan said.

Audio analysis supports this conclusion. Vincent Hughes, a professor of forensic speech science at the University of York, said there was “considerable phonetic similarity” between the voice in the Royal Mail ads and that of Vaughan. His analysis was limited by the brevity of the Royal Mail audio, but it was enough for him to conclude that there was material overlap in “segmental patterns,” meaning the pronunciation of consonants and vowels, and “overall voice quality,” sometimes referred to as the “timbre” of a person’s voice.

Deadline also compared the Royal Mail ad with other Vaughan audio using three different open-source AI analysis tools. All three said there were enough similarities to conclude that there was a good chance the AI-generated voice was the “same speaker” as Vaughan.

“It’s outrageous,” said Wynne. “He could have died two weeks ago, for all they knew. He could have been in the care home for the past 10 years, slowly losing his capacity for speech, and then all of a sudden, he’s on the bloody telly. They have not bothered to do their background searches to figure out who this voice is.”

Wynne added that Vaughan would have hated the idea of AI taking away work from voiceover artists. “Pay the money and get somebody in to do the job,” she argued. Wynne has not received an apology from the Royal Mail after complaining. The company told Deadline: “We understand the concerns raised and have taken them seriously.” ElevenLabs has added Vaughan to its No Go Voices, meaning his voice cannot be directly cloned on its platform in the future.

Paul Vaughan

Peter Caulfield, an actor who founded the Nicola Coughlan-backed Save Our Voices Now campaign, said Vaughan’s expertise and unique delivery would have made him a perfect pick for the Royal Mail ad, so it was little wonder the company was drawn to a very similar voice. “Using AI in this way, whether inadvertently or not, without thorough checks, can result in a company stealing a voice from the grave and causing great upset to the family involved,” Caulfield added.

Ultimately, for critics of the Royal Mail ad, it serves as a cautionary tale about artificial intelligence. It is a reminder of the murky ways in which AI models are trained and the lack of accountability when they spit out synthetic results with real-world consequences. Wynne’s story also shows that AI is now infiltrating our daily media diets, without us even realizing. It reveals that even when national institutions like the Royal Mail sell us idealistic visions of authentic human connection, they are prepared to turn to a machine to tell their story.

Below is a video comparing the Royal Mail ad’s AI voice with authentic audio of Paul Vaughan from the BBC and a Paddington audiobook.

title: Hugh Hefner’s Widow Asks Jessica Biel “Please Reconsider” Starring In ‘Playmates’
summary: Nearly a decade after his death, Hugh Hefner’s widow is expressing her disapproval of a coming-of-age story inspired by her late husband. Crystal Hefner, who was married to the Playboy founder from 2012 until his death at age 91 in 2017, shared a screenshot of an Instagram DM she sent to Jessica Biel asking her […]
content:
Nearly a decade after his death, Hugh Hefner‘s widow is expressing her disapproval of a coming-of-age story inspired by her late husband.

Crystal Hefner, who was married to the Playboy founder from 2012 until his death at age 91 in 2017, shared a screenshot of an Instagram DM she sent to Jessica Biel asking her to “please reconsider” starring as Hugh’s fictional wife in Lorraine Nicholson’s Searchlight pic Playmates.

“Please reconsider playing Hugh Hefner’s ‘wife’ if this film intends to romanticize him or the Playboy world,” wrote Crystal in the message. “I was actually his wife, and I experienced sexual, emotional, financial and physical abuse in that relationship. Many other women have come forward with allegations of rape, coercion, drugging and exploitation as well. There are also deeply troubling concerns involving minors. I hope everyone involved in this film takes the time to listen to the women who lived it before helping Hollywood turn it back into nostalgia.”

Written and directed by Nicholson, and inspired by her childhood friendship with Hugh Hefner’s kids, Playmates is described as an LA-set coming-of-age story following 13-year-old know-it-all Elle (played by Indiana Elle), who considers the Playboy Mansion her second home. During her time at the Mansion, Elle meets Anna (Lily-Rose Depp), one of seven hopefuls vying to be Playmate of the Month. The two form an unlikely friendship and try to help each other get what the other wants most, a magazine cover and a boy.

Watch on Deadline

Crystal added in a post, “Regarding the film, I hope it’s not something that will glorify Hugh Hefner. With women in the leading roles, my hope is that the film ultimately delivers a message of empowerment: that women can find fulfillment, independence, and a sense of self beyond Playboy.”

With Bill Pullman playing Hugh Hefner, we’re told Biel’s character is a fictional role not inspired by any of his three wives.

Since Hugh Hefner’s death in 2017, Crystal has opened up about the toxic environment of the Playboy Mansion and the abuse she said she endured during her time there, with other Playboy models sharing similar experiences in recent years.

title: ‘Freddy vs. Jason’s Monica Keena Recalls Killing Freddy Krueger Was “Really Cathartic” After ‘Nightmare on Elm Street’ “Traumatized Me”
summary: After 23 years, Monica Keena is reliving her “final girl” moment in the ultimate horror crossover. The Freddy vs. Jason actress recalled why it was “really cathartic” killing off Robert Englund’s Freddy Krueger in the 2003 Ronny Yu-helmed slasher after his performance in A Nightmare On Elm Street (1984) did a number on her as […]
content:
After 23 years, Monica Keena is reliving her “final girl” moment in the ultimate horror crossover.

The Freddy vs. Jason actress recalled why it was “really cathartic” killing off Robert Englund‘s Freddy Krueger in the 2003 Ronny Yu-helmed slasher after his performance in A Nightmare On Elm Street (1984) did a number on her as a kid.

“The first horror movie that I ever saw as a kid was Nightmare on Elm Street, and it really did traumatize me,” she told Nerd Reactor. “I mean, it ruined my childhood. This was in second grade. It was horrible. I had to go to the pediatrician, my mom didn’t know what was wrong with me. I was losing all this weight. Teachers at school thought I was being abused at home.”

Keena continued, “Finally, she takes me to the pediatrician, and he’s like, ‘What’s going on?’ I said, ‘You’re not gonna understand. You’re not gonna believe me because he doesn’t show himself to grown-ups.’ Then he was really concerned. I said, ‘There’s this guy, and his name is Freddy Krueger.’ He explains stuff to me. My mom went to the Brooklyn Public Library, she got a clipping of Robert Englund from a newspaper article … and she showed me, ‘He’s a real guy in real life, he’s not Freddy Krueger. That’s just a character.’ And I had it taped up by my little childhood bed. I had it on my wall for years.”

Watch on Deadline

In Freddy vs. Jason, Keena starred as Springwood teen Lori Campbell, who ultimately decapitates Freddy Krueger after learning he murdered her mother, sending him to a watery grave with Jason Voorhees at Camp Crystal Lake.

“And I always said, ‘When I grow up, I’m gonna become an actress and I’m never gonna make movies that scare little kids.’ And then, here I am,” quipped Keena. “But the whole point is, then it was really cathartic because I got to kill him. I finally got to kill him.”

In her latest horror outing Last Chance Motel, Keena stars alongside Heather Langenkamp, who played Krueger’s original “final girl” Nancy Thompson in the first Nightmare on Elm Street film and multiple sequels.

title: Charlie Cox Shouts Out “Save ‘Daredevil'” Campaign At NYCC After Disney+ Cancels ‘Born Again’
summary: Following last month’s cancellation of Daredevil: Born Again, Charlie Cox is fueling hope that some blind justice will prevail. While teasing the third and final season of the Disney+ series with his co-stars at New York Comic Con, the actor shouted out fans behind the “Save Daredevil” campaign as the panel’s moderator mentioned the show’s […]
content:
Following last month’s cancellation of Daredevil: Born Again, Charlie Cox is fueling hope that some blind justice will prevail.

While teasing the third and final season of the Disney+ series with his co-stars at New York Comic Con, the actor shouted out fans behind the “Save Daredevil” campaign as the panel’s moderator mentioned the show’s pending conclusion.

“Wait, what?” asked the Matt Murdock actor jokingly, sparking “boo”s from disappointed fans.

Cox added, “All I’ll the say is, I imagine the ‘Save Daredevil‘ campaign will be gearing up for round two. Listen, we don’t want to invite the wrath of the ‘Save Daredevil‘ people.”

Watch on Deadline

The “Save Daredevil” fan campaign began in 2018 in response to Netflix’s cancellation of Daredevil after three seasons. The show was revived last year as Daredevil: Born Again on Disney+ with Cox reprising his role as the title vigilante.

Fans boo at New York Comic Con at the mention of 'Daredevil: Born Again' ending with its upcoming third season, but star Charlie Cox reveals that he thinks the “Save 'Daredevil' campaign will be gearing up for round two" after its release.#NYCC #Daredevil #DaredevilBornAgain… pic.twitter.com/6yJxd4aAXv — Entertainment Weekly (@EW) October 8, 2026

Last month, Deadline confirmed that Daredevil: Born Again will end after its third season, which has wrapped and is set for a 2027 premiere.

The cast includes Vincent D’Onofrio as Wilson Fisk, Deborah Ann Woll as Karen Page, Elden Henson as Foggy Nelson and Wilson Bethel as Bullseye, with confirmed Season 3 Defenders reunion with cameos from Krysten Ritter as Jessica Jones, Mike Colter as Luke Cage and Finn Jones as Danny Rand/Iron Fist.

title: Sarah Snook & ‘Game Of Thrones’ Stars Shows Adapted As Microdramas For Snips
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Succession star Sarah Snook and Game of Thrones actors Maisie Williams, Liam Cunningham, Iain Glen and Kit Harington are making their microdrama debuts. Vertical video platform Snips is adapting series that each actor or actress has starred in for the new medium, as the platform continues to seek films and TV shows to repurpose […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Succession star Sarah Snook and Game of Thrones actors Maisie Williams, Liam Cunningham, Iain Glen and Kit Harington are making their microdrama debuts.

Vertical video platform Snips is adapting series that each actor or actress has starred in for the new medium, as the platform continues to seek films and TV shows to repurpose in 9:16 ratio.

The show are Australian drama The Beautiful Lie, an ABC series starring Snook; Sky dark comedy Two Weeks to Live, starring Williams and Sian Clifford (Ludwig); Rome drama Domina, starring Cunningham; BBC drama Prisoners’ Wives, starring Glen, and BBC and HBO co-production Gunpowder, starring Harrington.

Each show will be transformed from its full-length format into 45-second to two-minute episodes.

Watch on Deadline

The Beautiful Lie debuted on ABC in Australia in 2017 as a modern reimagining of Tolstoy’s Anna Karenina, with Snook (known best as Succession‘s Shiv Roy) playing a retired tennis champion married to another tennis legend, who flies home to help her brother’s crumbling marriage, only to meet and feel an instant attraction to a charismatic music producer – who happens to be the brother of her sister-in-law.

Two Weeks to Live debuted on Sky in the UK in 2020, and follows Williams as a young woman on a secret mission to avenge her father’s mysterious death when she was a child, who along with her mother joins a pair of socially awkward brothers and goes on the run from murderous gangsters and the police. It was Williams’ first lead role after her run as Arya Stark in GOT.

Domina, another Sky show, debuted in 2021, when Cunningham playing the father of young Livia Drusilla (Kasia Smutniak), whose lose of her family sets her on a path to seizing power in Rome. Isabella Rossellini and Claire Forlani joined Cunningham, who played Ser Davos Seaworth in GOT.

Glen stars in Prisoners’ Wives, a two-season BBC drama from the early 2010s. The show follows the wives, girlfriends and partners of prisoners, with Glen playing a career criminal whose lavish lifestyle is running out, along with his money. Polly Walker (Rome); another GOT star, David Bradley; and a yyoung Phoebe Dyvenor (Bridgerton) also had roles in an ensemble cast.

Gunpowder, a miniseries from 2017, was set in 1603 with Harington playing Robert Catesby, a charismatic Catholic nobleman, who decides to blow up the Houses of Parliament with the King inside. Harington who starred as Jon Snow in GOT, is a real-life descendant of Catesby, and lead a cast also including Liv Tyler (The Lord of the Rings), Mark Gatiss (Sherlock) and Peter Mullan (My Name is Joe).

Snips model

Snips has sought to set itself apart from other microdrama apps by focusing on repurposing existing shows and films for the vertical space, rather than making its own originals.

“Viewing habits are changing, and people’s preferences are changing with them,” said Or Ben Shimon, co-founder and CEO of Snips. “That shift is exactly why the micro-drama industry has exploded the way it has. Now we’re seeing big-name actors get into the space, and that tells you everything about where this format is headed. We believe good shows are like music — they just need to be on the most modern format.”

Snips has been offering rights owners a revenue-share model that allows earnings to grow based on performance over the more traditional flat license fee agreement. Shimon believes this gives actors a direct stake in their titles’ performance, incentivizing them to promote the work to fans and followers.

Shimon is set to hit MIPCOM Cannes next week, meeting with sellers and content owners to acquire more titles for adaptation.

title: Dawn Porter to Director Documentary on Pioneering TV News Anchor Max Robinson
summary: Dawn Porter is set to direct a feature documentary on pioneering Black TV news anchor Max Robinson for Wise Child Studios. CNN anchor Victor Blackwell is among the producers. “Color Bars: The Story of the Black Journalist Who Broke the TV News Color Barrier” will recount the rise and fall of Robinson’s career in broadcast […]
content:
Dawn Porter is set to direct a feature documentary on pioneering Black TV news anchor Max Robinson for Wise Child Studios. CNN anchor Victor Blackwell is among the producers.

“Color Bars: The Story of the Black Journalist Who Broke the TV News Color Barrier” will recount the rise and fall of Robinson’s career in broadcast news for Wise Child Studios. Porter, known for her much-praised docus including 2020’s “John Lews: Good Trouble” and 2018’s “Bobby Kennedy for President,’ will produce through her Trilogy Films banner. Blackwell, who anchors “CNN This Morning Weekend” and hosts the weekly series “First of All with Victor Blackwell,” will produce through is Fresh Fruit Films.

“Max Robinson was an exceptional journalist by any standard, and he deserves to have a firm place in the history of American journalism,” said Jason Beekman, founder and CEO of Wise Child Studios. “He courageously broke barriers in front of a national TV audience while facing the incredible pressure of simply doing his job. We’re proud to bring his life and legacy to a wider audience, and thrilled to have Dawn Porter’s vision guiding the film.”

Popular on Variety

Robinson came on to the national scene in the late 1970s as an anchor for ABC News. He gained prominence as an anchor for the NBC and CBS affiliate stations in Washington, D.C. In 1978, Robinson made history by joining ABC News’ national anchor team. He was a founder of the National Association of Black Journalists in 1975. But Robinson’s tenure at ABC News was short-lived as he struggled with alcohol abuse. He died of complications from AIDS in December 1988 at age 49.

Robinson is an inspiring figure to a generation of journalists and media business insiders.

“I remember watching Max Robinson on television — he was one of the very few Black people on the evening news,” Porter said. “Later I joined ABC News and people still spoke about his impact on the newsroom. At a time when truth and courage in journalism are under assault, everyone should know the Max Robinson story.”

Blackwell equated Robinson’s impact to that of Sidney Poitier, Thurgood Marshall and Jackie Robinson.

“Max Robinson is my Sidney Poitier. He’s my Thurgood Marshall, my Jackie Robinson,” Blackwell said. “In our current media landscape and social climate, Max’s life and career are more relevant than ever. I’m excited and honored that Dawn has joined the team to tell his remarkable story.”

Wise Child Studios was formed in 2023 to develop and package a range of original content. Beekman is a former head of business and legal affairs for RadicalMedia. Wise Child’s investigative docuseries “Reality Check: Inside America’s Next Top Model” debuted on Netflix earlier this year. Other projects include the 2025 feature documentary “Asco: Without Permission”alongside Diego Luna and Gael Garcia Bernal.”
