title: Nicolas Cage Didn’t Sign AI Waiver For ‘Spider-Noir’ & “Probably” Won’t Work Again With “AI-Friendly” Amazon; Teases ‘True Detective’ Role
summary: Nicolas Cage told a New York Comic-Con audience today that, yes, he’s likely to do a season of HBO’s True Detective, as rumored, and no, he’s not likely to work again with Spider-Noir streamer Prime Video because Amazon is “very AI-friendly.” Currently at work on the film Perish, Cage took part in a Spotlight panel […]
content:
Nicolas Cage told a New York Comic-Con audience today that, yes, he’s likely to do a season of HBO’s True Detective, as rumored, and no, he’s not likely to work again with Spider-Noir streamer Prime Video because Amazon is “very AI-friendly.”

Currently at work on the film Perish, Cage took part in a Spotlight panel at Comic-Con this morning, during which he seemed to confirm the Season 5 True Detective scuttlebutt.

According to multiple media outlets, Cage addressed the True Detective plans while discussing the logistics of balancing feature films and television roles.

“Necessity is the mother of invention,” he said, adding, “What do I mean by necessity? Feed the family, and don’t do too many movies back to back to back. So I think I’m probably going to do another season of television. I think I might do a season of True Detective. That’s OK that I’m the first to announce that, right?”

Watch on Deadline

Cage has apparently been in talks for a True Detective role since last year.

As for AI, Cage is no fan. In fact, he wouldn’t sign an AI waiver when he signed up for the sole season of Prime Video’s Spider-Noir.

“How do you survive AI?,” Cage said today. “Amazon is a very AI-friendly company to the tune of 50 billion dollars invested in OpenAI. I am not an AI-friendly actor….I’m not a member of their club. I didn’t sign the waiver to let them use AI on Spider-Noir. I’m probably not going to be working with that studio again, but that’s okay.”

Cage added that he’d prefer to work with young Gen Z directors who are “going at it their own way, whether it’s through the YouTube culture or whatever it is.”

“They’re doing it from scratch and by hand,” he said. “I want to get with that.”

title: Andy Allo To Guest Star On ‘The Rookie: North’
summary: Andy Allo (Upload, Pitch Perfect) will guest star in ABC’s The Rookie: North as Brooke, a warm, smart, attractive, and effortlessly charming first-year ER resident who is still adjusting to the pressures of the job. Brooke handles it all with humor, empathy, and confidence, and she quickly forms a connection with a rookie police officer […]
content:
Andy Allo (Upload, Pitch Perfect) will guest star in ABC‘s The Rookie: North as Brooke, a warm, smart, attractive, and effortlessly charming first-year ER resident who is still adjusting to the pressures of the job. Brooke handles it all with humor, empathy, and confidence, and she quickly forms a connection with a rookie police officer (Jay Ellis).

Expanding the universe of the hit ABC series The Rookie, The Rookie: North introduces Alex Holland, who believed his midlife wasn’t worthy of a crisis. But after a violent home invasion ignites a dormant purpose, Alex battles a lifetime of failed commitments by joining the Pierce County Police Department as a rookie. Policing from the urban coast to the rural forest where backup isn’t just five minutes away, Alex must prove to his skeptical training officer, his fellow rookies, and himself that he’s finally found something worthy of the fight.

The series also stars Chris Sullivan, Karen Fukuhara, Froy Gutierrez, Janet Montgomery, Mya Lowe, and Malik Watson, and is set to premiere in 2027.

Watch on Deadline

Alexi Hawley will serve as executive producer and writer of The Rookie: North, with Fillion, Mark Gordon, Bill Norcross, and Michelle Chapman also executive producing. Ellis is a producer.

Allo most recently starred in the hit sci-fi comedy series Upload on Amazon, opposite Robbie Amell from creator Greg Daniels. She previously recurred on NBC’s Chicago Fire as Lieutenant Wendy Seager. Her film credits include the Netflix feature Absolute Dominion for director Lexi Alexander, the third installment of the Universal franchise Pitch Perfect for producer Elizabeth Banks. Allo is repped by Verve and Zero Gravity.

title: ‘Other Mommy’ Cooks At No. 1, ‘Social Reckoning’ Ghosted; ‘Verity’, ‘Resident Evil’ Nice Holds & ‘The Odyssey’ Back In Top 10 – Box Office Update
summary: SATURDAY UPDATE: Horror Other Mommy from Universal is now eyeing a $28 million weekend with 3,365 playdates, barreling ahead atop the box office. The film is so far playing well across the board but best in the West, South and South Central U.S, with LA’s AMC Burbank the top grossing cinema. Tracking was strong on […]
content:
SATURDAY UPDATE: Horror Other Mommy from Universal is now eyeing a $28 million weekend with 3,365 playdates, barreling ahead atop the box office. The film is so far playing well across the board but best in the West, South and South Central U.S, with LA’s AMC Burbank the top grossing cinema.

Tracking was strong on this out of the gate with an effective campaign. Early numbers are shrugging off a soft D+ CinemaScore and PostTrak at 47% in the top two boxes and a not great 33% definite recommend. It’s sitting at 18% with RT critics, 46% with audiences — all of which could impact the longevity of its run. But maybe not. Is mommy horror especially, creepily alluring? (Will be back with stats on that.) Demos are 51% male to 49% female. The largest cohort is 18 to 24-year-olds at 38%.

In week two, Amazon MGM’s R-rated psychological thriller Verity takes the no. 2 spot with a decent hold, grossing $4 million Friday from 3,572 theaters for an early 3-day weekend estimate of $14.2 million (-56%). The cume now stands at $56.6 million. Directed by Michael Showalter with a screenplay by Nick Antosca based on the Colleen Hoover bestselling book, it stars Anne Hathaway, Dakota Johnson and Josh Hartnett.

Watch on Deadline

Similar week two drop as another Hoover adaptation, Reminders Of Him, from Universal back in March.

Columbia Pictures’ Resident Evil continues to hold well grossing $2.3 million on Friday at 3,085 locations for an estimated $8.2 million in week 4 (-35%), bringing its latest domestic total to $138.4 million through Sunday. Zach Cregger (Weapons, Barbarian) reinvents the popular franchise in an all-new story starring Zach Cherry, Kali Reis and Paul Walter Hauser.

Paramount’s survival thriller Heart Of The Beast is looking at a $6.9M weekend (down 37%) at 3,365 theaters in its third weekend out for acume of $49.5M. It made $1.96M Friday. The David Ayer film has an A- CinemaScore, a 94% RT audience score, great staying power. A retired Special Forces veteran (Brad Pitt) and his combat dog must survive the harsh Alaskan wilderness after a plane crash.

Columbia Pictures and Alcon Entertainment’s The Social Network made $2.15 million on Friday from 2,606 locations. The film is projected to open to $6 million for the weekend.

Inspired by true events and the whistleblower who started the social media reckoning we’re seeing play out today, this Aaron Sorkin original screenplay is a companion piece to the hit film The Social Network anda true David and Goliath story. Frances Haugen (Mikey Madison), a young Facebook engineer, enlists the help of Jeff Horwitz (Jeremy Allen White), a Wall Street Journal reporter, to go on a dangerous journey that ends up blowing the whistle on the social network. Written and directed by Aaron Sorkin.

Cinemascore is B-. Audiences like it more than critics at 70% vs 54% Rotten Tomatoes scores. PostTrak: At 75% in the top two boxes and a 59% definite recommend. Demos are 75% male/43% female and 25 to 34-year-olds with 28% of the audience 25-34. Played very well on the coasts with the West and the East representing 54% of the overall gross. AMC Lincoln Square in NY is the leading location.

That said, The Social Network opened to $22M and legged out to $97M back in 2010 as the hugely entertaining origin story of Facebook and its bizarre founder Mark Zuckerberg grabbed the zeitgeist. The massive power wielded by Zuckerberg and other tech titans has only grown since and is certainly worth exploring, but the WSJ stories and Haugen’s explosive testimony before Congress were back in 2021, well covered and much has happened since, except any dramatic fallout for Facebook. It may be that general public is less intrigued at this point by the ills of social media as by AI which is now leading the national conversation.

Universal’s PG-rated Forgotten Island is forging on in week 3 with no real competition in the kids’ market (until Cat In The Hat in November). CinemaScore is a solid A and the DreamWorks Amination film by Joel Crawford and Januel P. Mercado sits at 95% and 96% with RT critics/auds. The projected 3-day weekend is $5.2 million (-27%) after $1.1M Friday for a projected new cume of about $30 million.

A24’s Primetime ($1.26M weekend, 2,269 screens, est. week 3 cume $38.7M); Digger ($3M weekend, 3,321 screens, est. week 2 cume $14M); Angel And The Bad Man ($935K opening, 2,263 screens); and, notably, The Odyssey look to round out the top ten. After a week hiatus, The Odyssey reclaimed lucrative 70MM Imax prints for a nearly 60% jump in box office this weekend. The Christopher Nolan film — in week 18 –has a projected 3-day gross of $2 million at 560 locations for a cume of $622 million.

FRIDAY PM: Mom is bringing home the bacon. Other Mommy is on track for a $27.5 million opening weekend on 3,365 screens to top the domestic box office. This despite some scathing reviews for the Universal Pictures release by Rob Savage from producer James Wan and Blumhouse Atomic Monster. Jessica Chastain stars in dual roles as real mom and mom creature.

Horror films are a good bet Halloween month and this one topped expectations for Thursday previews of $3.6 million leading into a solid weekend. Friday is at $12.3 million. The number is solid especially given a $19 million budget.

Good comps are Universal’s The Black Phone 1 and 2 with, respectively, $23.6M and $27.3M opening weekends after $3 million and $2.6 million in Thursday previews. U’s The Exorcist: Believer debuted to $26.5M after $2.85 in previews.

The Social Reckoning from Sony Pictures is indeed struggling at no. 5 after soft previews ($650k) with Friday at $2.3M and the three-day weekend $6M at 2,606 locations. That’s on the lower end of initial projections of about $7M.

The comp was Digger last week, the costly Warner Bros. debacle that opened to $8 million, after $1.2 million in previews. The Aaron Sorkin film (after incentives) cost $30M, significantly less than the Tom Cruise-starring climate change romp, and was 50% financed by Alcon. Reviews were not good here either but matter more as the Facebook-Mark Zuckerberg takedown aims for a more picky crowd than the one turning out for a stretchy mommy.

Backing up, no. 2 for the weekend is Amazon MGM’s Verity in week 2 on 3,572 screens with $3.7 million Friday, a $13.3M weekend and a cume of $55.6 million total for the romantic thriller from the Colleen Hoover novel.

Sony’s Resident Evil is third in week 4 on 3,085 screens with a Friday around $7M for an estimated cume of $137M.

Paramount’s survival thriller Heart Of The Beast is in fourth place in week 3 at 3,365 theaters with an anticipated Friday take of $6.2M for a $49M cume.

A24’s Primetime, Digger and Angel And The Bad Man from Angel Studios round out the top ten.

FRIDAY AM: Universal Pictures release Other Mommy saw a strong $3.6M from previews beginning at 2 p.m. Thursday from 2,850 theaters and opens today on 3,365 screens. The Social Reckoning is reckoning with $650k.

Other Mommy, the Jessica Chastain-toplined horror by Rob Savage from producer James Wan and Blumhouse Atomic Monster sees a young girl (Arabella Olivia Clark) form a relationship with a sinister entity in her home who looks uncannily like her own mother. Oscar winner Chastain and It: Chapter Two star plays dual roles as the real and the other mother.

RELATED: The 65 Movies That Have Made More Than $1 Billion At The Global Box Office

The previews were strong for a Blumhouse movie of this size, though early reviews are very far from kind. Horror has been a safe bet in the run-up to Halloween, and while the market is crowded, there are no new tentpoles. The R-rated Other Mommy was eyeing an opening in the mid-$20 million range. We’ll see how the reviews and audience reaction impact the weekend.

Jessica Chastain in ‘Other Mommy’ Universal Pictures/Everett Collection

Sony’s The Social Reckoning from Columbia Pictures and Alcon Entertainment took in a soft $650K for Thursday previews starting at 4 p.m. at 2,368 locations. Aaron Sorkin’s follow-up to 2010’s The Social Network is at 59% fresh with critics on Rotten Tomatoes. Inspired by true events, Facebook whistleblower Frances Haugen (Mikey Madison) enlists the help of Wall Street Journal reporter Jeff Horwitz (Jeremy Allen White) to expose the nefarious doings of the social media giant. Jeremy Strong stepped in as Mark Zuckerberg, who was played by Jesse Eisenberg in Social Network.

RELATED: ‘The Social Reckoning’ New York Red Carpet Premiere Photos: Jeremy Strong, Mikey Madison, Jeremy Allen White & More

The comp for this was Digger, which posted previews of $1.2M last week. The Social Network production cost (after incentives) came in at $30M is significantly cheaper than the Warner. Bros pic, and it is 50% financed by Alcon. Projections are for an opening weekend in the mid-single digit millions.

How the week’s top 5 went:

1. Verity (Amazon MGM) 3,510 theaters, Wk $42.4M

2. Resident Evil (Sony) 3,256 theaters, Wk $17.8M, Total $130.2M/Wk3

3. Heart of the Beast (Paramount) 3,481, Wk $15.1M, Total $42.5M, Wk 2

4. Primetime (A24) 2,894, Wk $10.8M, Total $38.8M, Wk 2

5. Digger (Warner Bros.) 3,321, Wk $11.2M

title: Ailing Barry Manilow Cancels Tonight’s Vegas Performance
summary: An ailing Barry Manilow has canceled tonight’s performance at the International Theater at the Westgate Las Vegas Resort & Casino after cutting short last night’s show. Tonight’s cancellation comes just two days after the singer’s much-anticipated return to the Vegas residency on Thursday after a six-week hiatus. Manilow has been treated for the lung cancer […]
content:
An ailing Barry Manilow has canceled tonight’s performance at the International Theater at the Westgate Las Vegas Resort & Casino after cutting short last night’s show.

Tonight’s cancellation comes just two days after the singer’s much-anticipated return to the Vegas residency on Thursday after a six-week hiatus. Manilow has been treated for the lung cancer he initially disclosed last December.

“After a triumphant welcome-back concert on Thursday, Barry got hit with bronchitis and had to cancel his Friday and Saturday shows,” a representative for the musician told Deadline’s sister publication Variety.

Manilow took to the Westgate stage on Friday but reportedly ended the show after just a few songs, joking with the audience, “Talk amongst yourselves” before exiting. The night before, he said from the stage, “I’m back!”

Watch on Deadline

The Vegas residency was originally scheduled to begin last February but was repeatedly postponed as the singer battled the cancer and previous bouts of bronchitis.

In May, he wrote on social media, “Good news! I went to the doctor yesterday and he said I’m making great progress and look great! Well of course I do! Thank you very much! All the training and exercising I’ve put in is paying off. He did say, however, that I’m not quite ready for Vegas. That means I won’t be able to return for our May shows at @WestgateVegas.”

As of mid-day today, Manilow had not yet made any social media comments on the latest cancellations.

title: Busan-Winning ‘Shape of Momo’ Director Tribeny Rai Turns a Girl’s Death Into a Village Boundary Dispute in Asian Project Market Drama ‘A Chronicle of Minor Things’
summary: Two villages squabble over which of them holds jurisdiction over the spot where a 15-year-old girl died in “A Chronicle of Minor Things,” the new project from “Shape of Momo” director Tribeny Rai. The working-titled project is part of the Asian Project Market, which runs within the Busan International Film Festival’s Asian Contents & Film […]
content:
Two villages squabble over which of them holds jurisdiction over the spot where a 15-year-old girl died in “A Chronicle of Minor Things,” the new project from “Shape of Momo” director Tribeny Rai.

The working-titled project is part of the Asian Project Market, which runs within the Busan International Film Festival’s Asian Contents & Film Market (ACFM).

The girl is discovered at daybreak, hanging from a tree. Her body has not yet been cut down when the quarrel begins, because the tree is rooted in one village while the branch she hangs from stretches over the other. In death, she turns into a border dispute.

Rai’s debut, “Shape of Momo,” explored the close-knit relationships within a household of women. It premiered at Busan in 2025, where it won the Songwon Vision Award and the Taipei Film Commission Award, and later took the Golden Royal Bengal Tiger Award at the Kolkata International Film Festival and the Grand Jury Prize at the Indian Film Festival of Los Angeles. This time, Rai is turning her attention to her own village. “The village becomes a microcosm where power, money, and politics enter ordinary life in intimate ways, until we stop seeing them as systems at all,” she says.

Popular on Variety

Rai says she gravitates toward stories that feel pressing to her right now, and given the state of the world, this one feels timely. She aims to build a world rooted firmly in the village that viewers will slowly come to see as their own. “I want the film to leave behind a quiet, unsettling realization – this is not a world apart from ours; it is the world we already live in,” she says.

The script is in development.

Producer Kislay, who worked with Rai on “Shape of Momo,” says Rai has a gift for capturing characters with all their complications and contradictions, and that the new film widens her lens from a single family to a whole hilltop community whose calm surface hides a shifting world. What especially struck Kislay is how she treats its picturesque setting. “In most films, such a setting might become a space of leisure or escape. Here, it becomes a metaphor for the larger forces at play, forces that are shaping both Bishnu, the protagonist, and the world around him,” Kislay says.

At the APM, the team hopes to find co-producers and financiers to move the project forward. Though grounded in a particular culture, the film deals with ambition, desire and social change, themes the producer believes will speak to audiences internationally.

title: ‘Memories of a Dead End’ Director Choi Hyunyoung Confronts the Lies That Follow Tragedy in Subway Disaster Drama ‘All’s Well That Ends Well’ at Busan Asian Project Market
summary: A teenage ballerina hailed for sacrificing herself to rescue others in a subway disaster becomes the center of a spiraling web of lies in “All’s Well That Ends Well,” the new project from “Memories of a Dead End” director Choi Hyunyoung. The project is part of the Asian Project Market, which runs within the Busan […]
content:
A teenage ballerina hailed for sacrificing herself to rescue others in a subway disaster becomes the center of a spiraling web of lies in “All’s Well That Ends Well,” the new project from “Memories of a Dead End” director Choi Hyunyoung.

The project is part of the Asian Project Market, which runs within the Busan International Film Festival’s Asian Contents & Film Market (ACFM).

Jung-hyun, a gifted high school dancer, has had to abandon ballet because her family is poor. She is quietly falling for classmate Min-ho and still dreams of dancing again when the subway catastrophe tears her life apart. Accounts of her bravery move the country, money and compensation flood in, and her family is suddenly in the spotlight. But the tragedy conceals something nobody knows, and the falsehoods about Jung-hyun keep growing. Her relatives, the press and others pulled into the case each shape their own account to suit what they want and believe, and the mystery of the missing girl steers them all toward an end none of them sees coming.

After “Memories of a Dead End,” Choi went through a number of personal changes, including a life-threatening reaction to medication. The experience left her asking which story she would choose if she had just one film left in her. Her answer took her back to herself at 14, standing at the site of the tragedy, a story she had shut away for over 20 years.

Popular on Variety

“For me, making this film feels less like simply choosing my next project and more like finally finding a way to tell a story I have carried with me for a very long time,” Choi says.

She has long been drawn to what lingers once a major event has passed, and how it keeps shaping lives, relationships and decisions. “So this is not really a film about the disaster itself. It is about what comes afterward: how people survive, how they live with what has happened, and how society chooses to see them,” she says.

Choi wants to avoid handing viewers neat conclusions. Instead, she hopes they will picture themselves as a survivor, a relative, a reporter or a bystander and ask, “What would I have done?” and “How do we look at people after tragedy?”

The screenplay is in its fourth draft, and the project already has development support from the Korean Film Council (KOFIC). Choi says conversations about financing, co-production and casting are beginning, and she wants the film’s creative and financial frameworks to grow in tandem.

Producers Jeon Jiseong and Kwon Mizy go back years with Choi: Jeon since university and Kwon as producer of her first feature. The script exceeded their expectations, they say. “What struck us was not only the premise itself, but the way the story unfolds and the questions she is trying to explore through it.”

In Busan, the pair hope to line up co-producers, financiers and sales partners to take the film beyond Korea and move it toward a firm production and financing plan, with pre-production to follow once those pieces fall into place. “We are particularly interested in partners who respond to the project creatively as well as financially, and who see its potential to travel internationally while preserving the cultural and historical specificity of the story,” they say.

Choi, who has lived in the U.K. for the past few years, has also been writing several scripts that could be set up as Korea-U.K.-Japan co-productions.

title: ‘Other Mommy’ Star Arabella Olivia Clark on Working With Jessica Chastain and Being Mentored by Mckenna Grace
summary: Arabella Olivia Clark is proud to scare you. The 10-year-old actress joined Variety over Zoom from her Los Angeles hotel room the morning after the premiere of “Other Mommy, wearing a jacket with her character’s name, Bela, printed on the front. Clark plays the daughter of Ursula (Jessica Chastain) and Russ (Jay Duplass), a young […]
content:
Arabella Olivia Clark is proud to scare you.

The 10-year-old actress joined Variety over Zoom from her Los Angeles hotel room the morning after the premiere of “Other Mommy, wearing a jacket with her character’s name, Bela, printed on the front. Clark plays the daughter of Ursula (Jessica Chastain) and Russ (Jay Duplass), a young girl terrorized by a sinister figure who looks just like her mother, known as the titular Other Mommy.

Released on Friday, the Rob Savage-directed film debuted at No. 1, earning $12.6 million domestically on its opening day. This is Clark’s first leading role, and she’s just getting started.

Popular on Variety

For Clark, who previously played a younger version of Amanda Seyfried’s character in the 2025 film “The Housemaid,” “Other Mommy” marks her first time leading a feature film. Clark might specialize in frightening audiences, but she’s not easily frightened herself.

“I love spiders. I love snakes. I like all the creepy stuff,” she replies when asked what scares her the most. “I love the dark, so I don’t really know what I would be afraid of.”

Her mom, Rachel Clark, joins her off-camera in their L.A. hotel room, adding that nothing overtly frightening has ever held her back. “She’s always willing to try everything,” she says. “Even if she can’t do something, she’s like, ‘Yeah, I’ll try that.’”

Clark’s open mind and adventurous spirit extend well beyond the screen. When she’s not acting, Clark takes sailing and swimming lessons — the latter of which came in handy for “Other Mommy” — and spends much of her free time reading. Before even landing the role of Bela, she read the film’s source material, Josh Malerman’s 2024 novel “Incidents Around the House,” in just three days. By her second audition, she was well prepared, though the story still managed to get under her skin. “I got chills!” she shares.

But a few chills have never held her back. In fact, she’s a certified thrill-seeker at just 10 years old, even when it comes to her love for reading. Her favorite book is “Bunnicula,” a vampire rabbit set on a series of paranormal adventures, and she’s currently reading one of Jeff Kinney’s “Awesome Friendly Spooky Stories” books, which she proudly holds up to the camera. Combine that with her work on “Other Mommy” and “The Housemaid,” and she’s officially earned her status as a horror aficionado.

Though she excels in the genre, she’s not quite ready to limit herself to it just yet. She aspires to venture into science fiction, particularly a potential sequel to “E.T.,” which would give her the chance to fulfill her dream of working with Steven Spielberg. Perhaps the film will also feature an appearance from yet another dream collaborator: Rocky, the beloved alien from “Project Hail Mary.”

“Maybe Rocky and E.T. could be friends, because they’re both aliens, right?” Clark ponders.

Whether she’s facing a terrifying doppelgänger, diving into a massive water tank or imagining supernova adventures, Clark is eager to try just about anything. Below, she discusses filming “Other Mommy,” learning from Chastain and her mentor-like relationship with former child actress Mckenna Grace.

OTHER MOMMY, Arabella Olivia Clark, 2026. ph: Bernard Walsh /© Universal Pictures /Courtesy Everett Collection ©Universal/Courtesy Everett Collection

“Other Mommy” scared me so bad! Were you scared while making it?

Well, Rob Savage was always making sure I felt safe on set, and Jessica and Jay were always showing me different things and telling me different stories and making funny faces.

What was it like getting to work with Jessica Chastain? I know you mentioned you had a lot of fun together behind the scenes.

Working with Jessica Chastain was a great experience. I spent time with her and her kids, and she’s a great mom. We were always going to the park and hiking and all that stuff. One time — well, a bunch of times — I was in her trailer, and she was also studying for Harvard. And I can’t believe it! She’s a mom, and also studying for Harvard and also filming a movie at the same time. I learned a lot from her.

What was one of your favorite memories that you have from being on set for “Other Mommy”?

One of my favorite memories is when Jessica did her witch cackle. She’s like, “OK everybody, it’s going to be loud.” And she did it, and I was so surprised. She could be a witch in a movie.

That part scared me! How did it not freak you out?

Well, once the camera’s rolling, it’s one thing. But when it’s not rolling, they’re all telling funny jokes or telling funny stories or showing me different pictures. Or taking pictures with me.

You were also in “The Housemaid,” which had me scared too. Do you love doing scary stuff?

I really do. Paul Feig was amazing. I played a young role of Amanda Seyfried, and I’m always gonna look up to her.

What is your favorite movie that Amanda’s done? I think my favorite is probably “Mamma Mia.”

That’s my favorite! And “Mean Girls.”

There’s a part in the movie where you play Other Bela, an evil version of your character. Which version was more fun to play?

Other Bela!

You should play a bad guy in your next horror movie.

Okay! I also want to do sci-fi. Like sharks and stuff. I like experiencing the stuff that’s not actually real. I want to go to space and then have aliens and octopuses and sharks in the movie. Like a whole sci-fi movie combined!

What’s your favorite sci-fi movie?

I love “The Meg.” And “Project Hail Mary,” the new one that just came out. I love Rocky! I want my own Rocky. I love science and doing all different projects and space. I would love to be in space. And I love reading spooky stories in the dark with a flashlight at night.

You’re only 10, and I still get scared at 23. You’re braver than I am!

Thank you! I love doing all the stunts. I got to do different flips and spins, and I love doing acrobatics. And I love the water scenes too, because I got to swim a lot, and that’s one of my hobbies. Swimming and sailing.

How did you film that scene in the water?

Arabella: It was a big, big pool. It was massive. It was a big tank that was, like, 20 feet down?

Rachel: It was 20 feet down. Watching her film in the water was one of the scariest moments as a mom, because the tank was pitch black. There were balls. She had that Sherpa hoodie on, pulling her down, and they had the pyrotechnic people where there was an explosion in the water. And they had to yank her underwater. The timing and everything was so well orchestrated. But of course, as a mom, it was very anxiety-producing.

Arabella: It was fun. I love swimming, and I love being in deep pools. I can dive down all the way to 10 feet!

Do you know who Mckenna Grace is?

Yes!

Well, you remind me so much of her. I was just talking about how I think you’re going to have the same career as her!

Rachel: Do you want to know something? Mckenna Grace is so sweet. She reached out to Arabella and offered to mentor her and be there for her to talk about things like growing up in the industry.

Arabella: We only talked online. But I’m hoping to meet her in person!

title: New ‘Naruto’ Anime Series and ‘Shadow Rising’ Manga Revealed
summary: Big news for “Naruto” fans: the franchise is getting a new anime TV series and author Masashi Kishimoto is releasing another “Naruto” manga titled “Shadow Rising.” The new anime series will be a crossover with the popular manga “NINKŪ” and will be supervised by both Kishimoto and “NINKŪ” creator Koji Kiriyama. Per the description for […]
content:
Big news for “Naruto” fans: the franchise is getting a new anime TV series and author Masashi Kishimoto is releasing another “Naruto” manga titled “Shadow Rising.”

The new anime series will be a crossover with the popular manga “NINKŪ” and will be supervised by both Kishimoto and “NINKŪ” creator Koji Kiriyama.

Per the description for the upcoming “NARUTOxNINKŪ” anime, “Team 7 members Naruto, Sasuke, and Sakura are given a mission by Kakashi. Since Kakashi cannot participate himself, Naruto is appointed acting leader. As a result of this decision, Naruto is fully motivated to make the mission a success. However, on the way, Team 7 finds themselves lost in another world. What appears before the bewildered trio is a boy with a face resembling a frog’s, named Fūsuke. What awaits them in this strange new world?”

The news was announced Saturday during a “Naruto” panel at New York Comic Con, which concluded with the unveiling of new “Naruto” manga, “Shadow Rising.” That reveal came at the very end of the panel in a teaser video that noted more details will be shared during Jump Festa 2027 in December.

Popular on Variety

Also during the panel, a message from “Naruto” live-action movie director Destin Daniel Cretton was shared that teases more about the upcoming film.

“When we kicked off our worldwide search for Team 7 this summer, I talked about what an honor it is to bring Kishimoto-sensei’s incredible world and characters to life,” Cretton wrote. “The further we get into making this film, the more excited I am about what we’re creating. What I’ve always loved about Naruto is that he’s the character who might normally get sidelined as a sidekick. He’s excitable, he tries too hard, and people underestimate him. But he has an incredible heart. No matter how many times he fails or gets knocked down, he never stops believing in himself or fighting for the people he loves. That spirit is at the heart of the story we’re telling. These characters mean so much to so many people, myself included, and I carry that with me as we make this film. We’re approaching the world, relationships, and journeys Kishimoto-sensei created with a lot of care, and we want to capture what makes ‘Naruto’ so special. We’re hard at work and will have more to share soon. Until then, thank you for your passion, your patience, and for being along for the ride. I can’t wait for you to see what’s ahead!”

Watch the teaser for the upcoming “NARUTOxNINKŪ” anime and new manga “Shadow Rising” in the videos below.

title: Catherine Zeta-Jones Comments On Actors “Giving Themselves Over” To AI, Prefers “Real People”
summary: Catherine Zeta-Jones wants to see less AI “actors” onscreen and more undiscovered human talents. The Oscar winner recently commented on actors that have “given themselves over” to artificial intelligence companies, explaining that she prefers “not knowing anything” about the actors she watches in movies and television. “There’s so many actors already, who have given themselves […]
content:
Catherine Zeta-Jones wants to see less AI “actors” onscreen and more undiscovered human talents.

The Oscar winner recently commented on actors that have “given themselves over” to artificial intelligence companies, explaining that she prefers “not knowing anything” about the actors she watches in movies and television.

“There’s so many actors already, who have given themselves over to an AI company, and that’s everyone’s choice,” she told the Associated Press. “But I like going to the theater and seeing real people talk.”

Zeta-Jones continued, “I like going to movies and not knowing anything about the actors. I don’t wanna know who they’re sleeping with, what they wore, what they drink in the morning, how they keep their figure. I wanna be taken away and see a character, and that has happened for years.”

Watch on Deadline

The Kill Jackie star’s comments come amid ongoing concerns around AI’s plagiarism of copyrighted materials and the threat it poses to jobs in Hollywood and beyond, as well as recent warnings from those working in AI that continued progress could “cause a billion deaths.”

In response to the idea of AI actors, Catherine Zeta-Jones says she prefers "real people" in her art.#CatherineZetaJones #KillJackie pic.twitter.com/6zCvFqyBzl — The Associated Press (@AP) October 9, 2026

California Gov. Gavin Newsom signed an executive order last month to fast-track stringent oversight and control of AI. Convening “a group of world-leading experts” within the next 60 days, the order lays out a discussion of “safety plans” and “an emergency shutoff, or ‘kill switch,’ for frontier models.”

On a federal level, Trump has brushed off concerns about AI as “a hoax,” insisting the U.S. government “already have tremendous CRIMINAL and REGULATORY power” over AI companies.

title: Jimmy Kimmel Mourns Talk Show’s Costume Designer Rodney Muñoz’s Death At 60: “A Huge And Generous Heart”
summary: The Jimmy Kimmel Live family is mourning the death of costume designer Rodney Muñoz at age 60. On Friday, the talk show host paid tribute to the late Emmy winner who designed costume for Kimmel’s ABC talk show since 2002, after a friend of Muñoz announced that he died on Oct. 2. “Our dear friend […]
content:
The Jimmy Kimmel Live family is mourning the death of costume designer Rodney Muñoz at age 60.

On Friday, the talk show host paid tribute to the late Emmy winner who designed costume for Kimmel’s ABC talk show since 2002, after a friend of Muñoz announced that he died on Oct. 2.

“Our dear friend and Costume Designer for almost 30 years, Rodney Muñoz, has sadly passed away,” wrote Kimmel on Instagram, sharing behind-the-scenes photos of Muñoz’s work on the show.

“Rodney was one of the most talented people I’ve had the pleasure of knowing. He was a funny, surly, hard-working man whose tough exterior hid a huge and generous heart. Rodney helped many of us through difficult times. He was a devoted son, brother, and Uncle; a great baker, and a caring friend. No man saw me in my underpants more,” added Kimmel. “We will miss Rodney as he joins his beloved parents in whatever comes next.”

Watch on Deadline

Kimmel’s post comes after Muñoz’s friend Joe Dietl announced his death last weekend, noting that he suffered “many health issues” in recent years after he was diagnosed with COVID, which required him to be put into a coma and on a ventilator.

Born Sept. 4, 1966 in Los Angeles, Muñoz received his BFA and MFA in costume design at NYU, where he graduated in 1993, before going on to work as costume designer on The Late Show with David Letterman from 1995 to 2000.

Following his work with Kimmel on Comedy Central’s The Man Show, Muñoz became the costume designer for Jimmy Kimmel Live! when it launched in 2003.

His work on the ABC talk show earned him a Primetime Emmy in 2010 for Outstanding Costumes for a Variety/Music Program or a Special.

In addition to working in wardrobe on NBC’s Fear Factor in 2002 and the indie gay series Where the Bears Are from 2012 to 2018, Muñoz also designed costumes for the stage in the off-Broadway shows I Sent a Letter to My Love (1995), The Preservation Society (1996) and Ancient History/English Made Simple (1996).

title: ‘SNL UK’ Cold Open Features Face-Off Between Prince William & Harry: “Oh Look, It’s The Woman From ‘Suits'”
summary: The warring Windsors took center stage in the SNL UK cold open. It was Prince William (Freddie Meredith) and Kate Middleton (Annabel Marlow) vs Prince Harry (Jack Shep) and Meghan Markle (Ayoade Bamgboye) at Sandringham, as the family members were fooled into reuniting by the dastardly Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor (George Fouracres). “Look, this is where your […]
content:
The warring Windsors took center stage in the SNL UK cold open.

It was Prince William (Freddie Meredith) and Kate Middleton (Annabel Marlow) vs Prince Harry (Jack Shep) and Meghan Markle (Ayoade Bamgboye) at Sandringham, as the family members were fooled into reuniting by the dastardly Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor (George Fouracres).

“Look, this is where your grandpa asked if I was related to Beyoncé,” Markle quipped as she reacquainted herself with her surroundings. Harry replied: “Classic. And over here, this is where he asked if I was related to him.”

Enter William and Kate. “If it isn’t Prince Ginger Pubes,” Prince William said. “I told you not to call me that because you know I don’t have a comeback,” responded Harry. “Oh look, William, it’s the woman from Suits,” Middleton chimed in. Harry’s retort: “She’s not on Suits anymore. She doesn’t do anything anymore.”

Watch on Deadline

The reunion was interrupted by King Charles, Camilla, and later a snivelling Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, as Fouracres declared: “Did somebody say Pizza Express Woking?!”

When the King dropped the Prince from Andrew’s name, Mountbatten-Windsor growled: “That’s Prince Andrew to you.” Larry Dean’s King Charles clapped back: “Andrew, enough is enough. You’re arrogant. You’re entitled. You represent an outdated institution that has had centuries of war, tax evasion, and slavery, and that’s all great, but you have also been accused of terrible things, and that’s where I draw the line.”

A grovelling Andrew replied to his brother: “I swear, I never believed for one moment that my actions would have consequences.”

Danny Dyer hosted SNL UK Season 2’s fourth episode, with music from Sasha Keable.

SNL UK is produced by Universal Television Alternative Studio’s UK production team and Broadway Video. Lorne Michaels serves as executive producer. James Longman is lead producer.

title: How Candle House’s Immersive Theater Show ‘The Pineapple’ Became a Spooky L.A. Hit, Playing 76 Shows With Just One Ticket for Each Performance
summary: Part of the thrill of theater is that you’re taking part in a one-time experience, never to be recorded or repeated, in which anyone who wasn’t part of that live audience with you will simply have to take your word for how it was. Still, you may seek out clues about whether your experience of […]
content:
“The reactions have really impressive depth and breadth,” Neiden told me, “but all the reactions I’ve heard have been intense in one way or another. Ultimately, what I’ve taken pride in is hearing that regardless of how people felt about it, that they’ve never experienced anything quite like it. Even if they had seen a lot of experimental theater, maybe the themes in this were different, for instance… Most people that I’ve spoken to have found it in equal measure scary and silly, and maybe cathartic, and that’s the best-case scenario for me.

“Not everyone is going to like it,” Neiden continued. “And sometimes I don’t think there’s any way to fully know if something’s for you before going in. I’ve seen shows that I thought would be 100% up my alley, and then I saw them and it was maybe not so much, versus seeing something that seemed totally out of left field but like, ‘Oh, give it a shot,’ because I heard something good, from someone I trust. This is a place to take a risk, to surrender, and at the very least, to experience something that can only happen for you in that moment — something altogether fleeting that is just yours. You know, the most tangible souvenirs people walk away with from ‘The Pineapple’ are a lei and a memory.”

Rett Keeter, Cece Kelly, Ian Michaels and Evan Neiden star in “The Pineapple,” produced by Candle House in North Hollywood, California Sona Earnest

His reference to the actual lei that attendees leave with does require some setup, so now’s as good a time as any to attempt a plot summary. (I was about to say “fruitless” attempt, but well, you’ve seen the title.) Everyone exiting the show had a Hawaiian-style plastic flower chain placed around their neck to send the off into the NoHo night, which might seem like an unexpectedly comic touch at the end of a show that is focused on … aliens. Even though the narrative is sci-fi/horror-oriented, and participants are promised an actual alien encounter. It appears the aliens in question have become convinced that one thing all human beings love is beach culture, and that our national or global anthem is the Jimmy Buffett song “Margaritaville.” When an alien baby is finally produced, it takes the form of… a pineapple. So there’s an extent to which you might call the final subgenre the show lands in as, for lack of a better term, tiki horror.

But that’s getting ahead of the initial setup. When you sign up for the show (and sign waivers), you are ostensibly answered a classified ad for someone who needs a fellow believers in UFOs to help participate in a ritual that will bring the aliens out into the open. On the day of your encounter, you start getting texts from the young man who placed the ad, berating you if you don’t seem enthusiastic enough. He also sends coordinates about which back street parking lot to show up in, and which unmarked door to knock on (“underneath the State Farm sign”) at exactly the appointed time. Once admitted, after being sure I’d shown up at the wrong place, he shined a flashlight in my eyes, made certain I knew the safe word, recorded me giving consent, and relieved me of shoes, phone, and ost everything else. I was led into a dingy room that served as his bedroom, with a sleeping bag, walls full of conspiracy theory cutouts connected by thumbtacks and string, and kitchen tools to squeeze pineapple pulp into juice.

Without recounting every amusing or harrowing detail, a good deal of interactive psychological grilling ensued. I was asked questions about living and deceased family members, failed relationships, religious affiliations, etc…. all of which I knew could and would be used against me later. The young man spilled some details of his own, like how he was abandoned in a superstore parking lot when he was 8, and had lived a sad and itinerant life since then before eventually coming to realize that his real family was from space, and now it was time to meet up. My hands were taped together and I was made to crawl on all fours to a bathroom, where another man was soaking in a bloody tube, handcuffed, revealing that he’d been the previous respondent, chosen to be impregnated with an alien baby, but failed the attempt when it turned out he had lied about not having an allergy to pineapple juice. Then he, too, asked me personal details, asked me to hold his hands in prayer, and…

Rett Keeter, Cece Kelly, Ian Michaels and Evan Neiden star in “The Pineapple,” produced by Candle House in North Hollywood, California Sona Earnest

Perhaps it’s OK to stop there, as things got considerably weirder from there, including the introduction of the cast’s one woman, who is some kind of operative for the aliens… and whose otherworldliness is apparent, apart from the maniacal grin on her face, by the fact that she is wearing a sticker identifying her as “WOMAN.” I had learned ahead of time, from reading the L.A. Times’ review, that my encounter would likely involve some kissing on the lips, massaging and (no lie) spooning. I had a sneaking suspicion all of this would happen with the gnarlier male cast members and not the beautiful woman, which did turn out to be the case. (Names of the very improv-capable cast members were released only after the show concluded its run: Rett Keeter, Cece Kelly, Ian Michaels and Neiden.)

Cece Kelly in “The Pineapple,” produced by Candle House in North Hollywood, California Sona Earnest

I had expected the show to be frightening, but apart from one moment where a flashlight came on to reveal a figure in the dark inches away, there were no jump scares, or anything that even induced very much anxiety. (The only truly scary moment was when someone pulled some opaque goggles off my face and my brand new $400 glasses went flying off with them. “We want you to have your spectacles,” a voice said quietly when I expressed panic about having them stepped on, and eventually I was able to rejoin the land of the sighted.) I think you can only experience so much fear in a show in which, toward the end, you will be dancing to “Margaritaville.” I laughed out loud a few times… maybe most when, not long after I was played back the recording of myself saying “I consent,” the tables were turned on my tormentor and someone played back his consent recording.

title: ‘The First Taste of Loneliness’ Review: A Sentimental but Affecting Study of Family Life After Bereavement
summary: The most moving scene in “The First Taste of Loneliness” is not, in fact, its most tear-streaked. Gu You’s heartfelt family portrait opens on an extended, anguished scene of three women — a mother, her daughter and her granddaughter — keeping vigil at the bedside of their beloved husband, father and grandfather as his longtime […]
content:
The most moving scene in “The First Taste of Loneliness” is not, in fact, its most tear-streaked. Gu You‘s heartfelt family portrait opens on an extended, anguished scene of three women — a mother, her daughter and her granddaughter — keeping vigil at the bedside of their beloved husband, father and grandfather as his longtime battle with pancreatic cancer comes to a close. Emotions run high and loud; the camera peers closely into their grief. But it’s a quieter, more composed moment a little later that really jabs at the heart. A short time after her father’s death, Yue (Zhou Xun) opens the final jar of his famous homemade pickles, tastes them, and with the bittersweet knowledge that she’ll never get to do so again, declares it a good batch.

“The First Taste of Loneliness” is best when focused on such small but important everyday details. Its portrayal of the immediate, intense pain of mourning can be overwrought, but the bulk of this admittedly overlong film is given over to a more patient, restrained and gracefully observed study of how life reshapes itself around an absence — as Yue, her mother Luna (Xi Meijuan) and her teenage daughter Moon (Wang Shengdi) deal with the sadness, the relief and the faint sense of betrayal that comes from carrying on, while keeping space for the dead man’s spirit in their respective lives.

Popular on Variety

Shot and structured with grand-scale elegance to counter the intimacy of the storytelling, this is a stirring final entry in Gu’s “Landscape” trilogy, which began with his Cannes-premiered 2019 debut “Dwelling in the Fuchun Mountains” and continued with 2023’s “Dwelling by the West Lake” — the three films connected not directly by characters or narratives but a shared style of melancholic family portraiture. Premiering in the main competition at the Busan Film Festival, “Loneliness” again demonstrates the filmmaker’s formal prowess, with its preponderance of ambitiously floating pans and heavily populated setpieces. It has a broader, more populist streak than its predecessors, which could net it greater global distribution, but has its artistic downsides: An overreliance on stickily emotive ballads to unnecessarily articulate the characters’ feelings is a particular debit.

Somewhat heavily expository dialogue informs us that Yue, formerly a fashion director in Beijing, has recently returned with Moon to the family apartment in the city of Hangzhou in southeast China. Home to Luna and her late husband for decades, it’s a roomy, rambling space with spectacular views of the Qiantang River and, in Zhou Xingyu’s excellent production design, a storied buildup of clutter. Mikiya Takimoto’s camera lingers affectionately on stacked bookshelves — not even old cassette tapes have been thrown away — and desktops heavy with ornaments, notes and photographs that reveal in shorthand a life rich in love. Even in death, the man maintains a palpable presence in the home.

But it may be time for at least some remnants of the past to make way for the present. Luna implores Yue, recently divorced, not to get stuck in a holding pattern, either in her career or her relationships — but Luna, too, needs to make some changes. She tentatively accepts the romantic advances of another man, Xu (Xu Chaoying), opening herself to a kind of happiness she’d largely forgotten how to feel. Moon, meanwhile, is struggling at school but on the precipice of adulthood; as the young woman begins to make her own decisions in life, Yue must relinquish a degree of maternal responsibility.

Written by Gu with Yang Yikun, the screenplay, delicately braids these three arcs in such a way that each woman’s new freedoms complement the others’, while Takimoto’s bravura camerawork — painting in watercolor shades of misty gray and mossy green — often physically connects their stories in languid, widely swooping movements. And while the three leads’ performances are sensitively synched, Xi Meijuan is especially poignant as a widow trying to maintain a level of grieving decorum while embracing fresh experiences and sources of joy: A lovely scene of her and Xu dancing with other couples in a public square hits just the right note of romantic sentimentality tempered with elegiac sorrow. If “The First Taste of Loneliness” hits overly maudlin notes elsewhere — literally so, in the case of Sylvian Wang’s plaintive, piano-heavy score — it never feels cynical or manufactured in its emotions. Its moments of overstatement are entirely human, en route to a lighter, softer state of serenity.

title: Philippines Revamps International Co-Production Fund With Minority and Majority Tracks, Unveiled at Busan Market
summary: The Philippines has revamped its International Co-Production Fund (ICOF) around two tracks, with the amount of cash on offer tied to the size of the Filipino stake in a project. The Film Philippines Office (FPO) unveiled the new framework at the Busan International Film Festival’s Asian Contents & Film Market. The Majority Track covers projects […]
content:
The Philippines has revamped its International Co-Production Fund (ICOF) around two tracks, with the amount of cash on offer tied to the size of the Filipino stake in a project.

The Film Philippines Office (FPO) unveiled the new framework at the Busan International Film Festival‘s Asian Contents & Film Market.

The Majority Track covers projects led by Filipino producers working with foreign partners. Features and series on this track can receive up to PHP13 million ($210,000), and documentaries and shorts up to PHP5 million ($80,000).

To qualify, the Filipino side must own at least 20% of the project and hold the largest share among the co-producers. Two Filipinos must fill above-the-line roles – director, writer or actor – and five more must work in key creative or technical crew positions. Applicants need a release strategy for both the home market and abroad. Foreign partners must take a minority stake and make a matching creative or technical contribution.

Popular on Variety

The Minority Track is for international productions in which a Filipino producer is the junior partner. Features and series can draw up to PHP7 million ($113,000), with documentaries and shorts capped at PHP3 million ($48,000).

The bar is lower here. Filipino producers need a stake of 10% or more, and the production must hire either two Filipino above-the-line talents or three Filipino crew members in key creative or technical roles. Applicants must also show how the film will reach audiences outside the Philippines.

Both tracks offer the same top-ups. Qualifying ASEAN co-productions earn an extra PHP1 million ($16,000), and projects that clear a cultural test can collect up to PHP2 million ($32,000) more. The FPO noted that the dollar figures may vary with exchange rates.

The FPO sits within the Film Development Council of the Philippines (FDCP), the national film agency that reports to the Office of the President. It runs the country’s incentives for international co-productions and for line and post-production work. It also provides endorsements for government permits and makes location referrals.

Several ICOF-backed films have won festival prizes. Tommy Ng Ka Chung’s “Another World” was co-produced by Filipino company Overmind Corp with partners in Hong Kong and Singapore, and won best animated feature at the 62nd Golden Horse Awards in November 2025. Janus Victoria’s “Diamonds in the Sand,” which has Japanese and Malaysian co-producers, took the Mulberry Award for best debut film at Udine’s Far East Film Festival.

Marianne Métivier’s “Elsewhere at Night” won best screenplay at the Torino Film Festival. James J. Robinson picked up best Australian director at the Melbourne International Film Festival for “First Light.” Mouly Surya’s “This City Is a Battlefield” won best cinematography at the Bandung Film Festival.

The FPO’s separate Film Location Incentive Program has backed two prizewinners. Rafael Manuel’s “Filipiñana” won a special jury award for creative vision in Sundance’s World Cinema Dramatic competition, and Morgan Knibbe’s “The Garden of Earthly Delights” won best film at Torino.

title: Lego Is Bringing Marvel and ‘Star Wars’ Together for First-Ever Fan-Designed Crossover Set
summary: Ever wondered what would happen if Darth Vader joined the Avengers? Or if the Millennium Falcon got a Tony Stark-approved upgrade? Lego is giving fans the chance to find out. The toy company announced a first-of-its-kind Lego Ideas challenge at New York Comic Con on Saturday, inviting builders to combine the worlds of Marvel and […]
content:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

Ever wondered what would happen if Darth Vader joined the Avengers? Or if the Millennium Falcon got a Tony Stark-approved upgrade? Lego is giving fans the chance to find out.

The toy company announced a first-of-its-kind Lego Ideas challenge at New York Comic Con on Saturday, inviting builders to combine the worlds of Marvel and “Star Wars” for a chance to have their creations turned into an official Lego set. The competition marks the first time the two Disney-owned franchises have been brought together in a Lego Ideas challenge, allowing fans to dream up their own cross-universe creations.

The announcement was made by filmmaker, actor and Marvel Comics writer Kevin Smith, who is also working on the upcoming “Star Wars/Marvel: Hope Assembles” comic series. Set to launch in January, the series will mark the first official crossover between the two comic book universes, arriving as “Star Wars” prepares to celebrate its 50th anniversary in 2027.

Popular on Variety

“Working on the upcoming Star Wars/Marvel: Hope Assembles comic series has been incredibly exciting, and this Lego Ideas challenge reflects the same spirit of creativity inspired by these two iconic universes,” Smith said in a statement. “This challenge gives fans a chance to be part of something never done before and I can’t wait to see all of the creative Marvel and Star Wars mash ups it inspires!”

The competition invites fans to submit original builds across three categories: vehicles, characters and scenes. That could mean reimagining familiar spacecraft with superhero technology, bringing characters from the two franchises face-to-face or creating entirely new settings that unite their respective worlds.

Submissions are now open through the Lego Ideas platform, with fan voting set to begin Dec. 8. Grand prize selections will be announced in 2027, with winning designs eligible to be developed into official Lego products.

The challenge builds on Lego’s longstanding relationships with both franchises, which have produced some of the company’s most elaborate and collectible sets. Lego’s “Star Wars” partnership dates back to 1999, while its Marvel lineup has brought characters including Spider-Man, Iron Man and the Avengers into brick form through everything from smaller character sets to large-scale collector’s builds.

“This challenge is a milestone for Lego Ideas and our fan community,” said Fede Begher, senior vice president and head of product group at the Lego Group. “For the first time ever, fans can build with both Marvel and Star Wars in a single LEGO Ideas challenge, unlocking entirely new possibilities for creativity and storytelling.”

Fans can enter the “Star Wars” and Marvel crossover challenge and review the official submission guidelines at ideas.lego.com/campaigns/hope-assembles

title: Bill Maher Slams Cornell and the ‘Depravity’ of Fraternities Amid Sexual Assault Lawsuit: ‘I’m Glad to See Them Eating a S— Sandwich’
summary: During Friday night’s episode of “Real Time,” Bill Maher slammed his alma mater, Cornell University, and the “depravity” of fraternities while speaking about the ongoing Cornell 7 lawsuit. Maher, who graduated from the university in 1978, began by noting that the “alleged gang rape at the Cornell frat house is deeply disturbing. But since it’s […]
content:
During Friday night’s episode of “Real Time,” Bill Maher slammed his alma mater, Cornell University, and the “depravity” of fraternities while speaking about the ongoing Cornell 7 lawsuit.

Maher, who graduated from the university in 1978, began by noting that the “alleged gang rape at the Cornell frat house is deeply disturbing. But since it’s my alma mater, where I walked those hallowed halls for four years with so many memories, I don’t want to let my personal feelings get in the way… because they’re all bad.”

He proceeded to say that “Cornell sucks and I fucking hated it.” “I’m glad to see them eating a shit sandwich. It’s true,” he said. “Also, this shit could have happened anywhere there are fraternities, because it happens everywhere there are fraternities. Any place that’s all male, no girls allowed, just doesn’t function without depravity. Ask the Catholic Church, ask the Taliban. Human nature is bad, and the best we can do is create institutions that don’t make it so easy to be worse.”

Popular on Variety

Maher then called for the abolition of Greek life, explaining that everything that is “inherently bad about men gets worse if you put them in a fraternity.” He continued: “The drinking gets worse, the cruelty, the treatment of women, the tribalism, the peer pressure, one-upmanship, conformity, segregation, nepotism, bullying, elitism and just general assholery.”

“A gentleman, gentlemen, is someone who, in that situation, doesn’t exploit the woman; he saves her,” he added. Maher also went on to throw a few jabs at sororities, calling them “bitch factories producing the Karens of tomorrow.”

The Cornell 7 lawsuit refers to the legal document filed by an unnamed Cornell University student who accused seven men of raping and drugging her at a frat house party in October 2024 — and faced no legal consequences. Her lawsuit filed against the university claimed that the school failed to protect her and prevent the alleged assault.

Following an investigation by the university at the time, two of the men were expelled, while the other five received lesser punishment. The lawsuit claims that some of them wrote essays to the school to reduce their disciplinary action, according to her attorney.

With his remarks, Maher joins a list of celebrities including Florence Pugh, Mariska Hargitay, Hudson Williams, Josh Gad and more who have used their platforms to condemn the case in recent weeks.
