Li Wei, who is making animated feature Born Of The Tide with Kling AI tools, said one useful aspect of AI filmmaking is that results can be seen right away, so it’s easier to get feedback from multiple people on the crew. “There’s going to be a lot of trial and error in AI filmmaking, but effective communication can be used between the various production members, so everyone has a chance to feed back into the production,” Li said.

Lee presented a teaser of upcoming series Rendering Love, produced by MBC C&I and Barunson E&A, which combines live-action scenes filmed the traditional way with AI generated characters to tell the story of a virtual K-pop group. He observed that different roles and ways of working are emerging in AI production crews.

“All staff members working on a project must fully understand the technology. That’s the only way to have high quality content. If you’re updating to a new model, the team leaders need to analyse the new features and share that understanding so all staff members are on the same page. The technology is changing constantly and if anyone is lagging behind, overall quality can decrease.”

The speakers also discussed whether there was a need to introduce industry standards in AI filmmaking, but Kim suggested it was still too early, at least in South Korea. “Creators in Korea have their own ideas and imagination and want to unleash that using AI tools. We need to see where all this is heading before we start talking about regulations and standards.

“But one thing I’m very aware of as a filmmaker is thinking about whether you’re infringing somebody’s rights. That’s something we need to be conscious of from the early stages.”

The panel, entitled New Cinematic Possibilities: Reimagining Filmmaking with Kling AI, took place as part of the InnoAsia track at Asian Contents & Market (ACFM), which is running until October 13.

title: Globo Bets on ‘To Love Is to Care’ at Mipcom as It Ushers ‘Super Drama’ Concept: ‘Titles That Represent the Best of the Brazilian Telenovela Tradition’
summary: Brazilian media powerhouse Globo arrives at Mipcom with “To Love is to Care,” its latest primetime telenovela by lauded author Walcyr Carrasco. The melodrama stars a roster of some of Brazil’s biggest screen stars, including Chay Suede, Letícia Colin, Tony Ramos and Antônio Fagundes. The market marks Globo’s introduction of the telenovela to the international […]
content:
Brazilian media powerhouse Globo arrives at Mipcom with “To Love is to Care,” its latest primetime telenovela by lauded author Walcyr Carrasco. The melodrama stars a roster of some of Brazil’s biggest screen stars, including Chay Suede, Letícia Colin, Tony Ramos and Antônio Fagundes. The market marks Globo’s introduction of the telenovela to the international market following a successful run in its home country.

“To Love Is to Care” is created and written by veteran Carrasco, an Emmy winner for his hit series “Hidden Truths.” Carrasco created the novela with Claudia Souto, with renowned director Amora Mautner taking over the artistic direction.

The story follows the transformation of Adriana (Colin), a woman shattered by a terrible murder and who discovers the strength to start over, driven by an unquenchable thirst for justice. The story gathers all the classic elements of a successful telenovela: passion, revenge, and a major whodunnit arc. The novela also joins two of Brazil’s most popular actors as a majorly successful romantic pairing, with Colin’s Adriana falling in love with Chay Suede’s idealist lawyer Pedro.

Popular on Variety

In a statement, Carrasco said the original idea for the story came from a personal experience. Two years ago, he broke a leg and faced a long recovery process that allowed him to realize the importance of “care, empathy, and human connection.” “I realized how the act of caring transforms both the caregiver and the person being cared for,” he noted. “That experience left a deep impression on me and sparked a desire to tell a story set in that world, one that speaks of solidarity, resilience, and affection.”

Angela Colla, head of international business at Globo, says “To Love is to Care” is one of its “Super Dramas” at Mipcom. These are titles that represent “the best of the Brazilian telenovela tradition combined with Globo’s production excellence.”

“They are stories that stir emotions, spark conversations across generations, and forge deep connections with audiences that extend far beyond the individual episodes,” adds Colla, who says “To Love Is to Care” brings together all these essential elements: “A strong female lead, a sweeping love story, a compelling mystery that hooks the audience, and universal themes that transcend borders.”

Courtesy of Globo

“It is a project of immense technical and artistic scale, impressing right from the premiere with striking sequences, such as the flood scene, which mobilized a production team of 270 professionals,” she goes on. “It is the kind of story with high potential to engage viewers anywhere in the world.”

The strength of “To Love Is to Care” can already be observed in its performance in Brazil. In its first 12 weeks, the telenovela reached over 119 million Brazilians. Digital engagement mirrored this success: the hashtag #QuemAmaCuida (“To Love is to Care” in its original title) spent over 13 hours among Worldwide Trending Topics and 97 hours in Brazil’s Trending Topics, while interest in the storyline generated more than 139,000 Google searches since its premiere.

Colla says the reception from Brazilian audiences confirms “that people continue to look for strong, well-told stories.” “‘To Love Is to Care’ delivered an impactful first chapter that won over the audience from the beginning and has maintained a high level of engagement throughout the plot,” she emphasizes. “The narrative structure brings universal elements that work in different markets: a determined girl who goes after what she wants, a great love story, and the classic mystery of ‘who killed?’”

“This combination of technical excellence and emotional engagement leaves us very excited and confident that the reception in the international market will also be very positive,” she adds, referring to its upcoming experience Super Dramas at Mipcom, where “To Love Is to Care,” “Anything Goes” and Three Graces” proved early highlights at a Globo Showcase held Sunday evening in Cannes .

title: Sally Field Was Like a ‘Mother Figure’ While Filming ‘Mrs. Doubtfire,’ Says Star Matthew Lawrence: ‘We Really Became a Family Unit’
summary: Matthew Lawrence is reflecting on his experience filming “Mrs. Doubtfire,” where he played Sally Field and Robin Williams’ son. The 1993 film followed Williams as Daniel, a father who disguises himself as the titular Scottish nanny for his three children — played by Lawrence, Lisa Jakub and Mara Wilson — to prove to his estranged […]
content:
Matthew Lawrence is reflecting on his experience filming “Mrs. Doubtfire,” where he played Sally Field and Robin Williams’ son.

The 1993 film followed Williams as Daniel, a father who disguises himself as the titular Scottish nanny for his three children — played by Lawrence, Lisa Jakub and Mara Wilson — to prove to his estranged wife, Miranda (Field), that he has matured.

“We really became a family unit on that set,” Lawrence told Entertainment Weekly about working with his on-screen parents and Pierce Brosnan, who played the boyfriend of Field’s character.

Lawrence shared that, even before rehearsals began, the cast dedicated time to getting to know each other, “so [Field] kind of really became another mother figure.”

Popular on Variety

The actor was just 12 when filming the movie and recalled that Field was “so sweet” during the experience, and “she was so caring, so kind. I don’t know how anybody could have anything bad to say about the lady… She was great.”

As a child actor, Lawrence revealed Field, Williams and Brosnan “neither treated me and talked down to me as a child, nor did they overexpose me to the adult world.”

The trio of adult actors “walked a line” that was “absolutely wonderful,” making it “one of those incredible, once-in-a-lifetime experiences,” Lawrence recalled, adding that “Sally in particular… she was amazing.”

Lawrence has continued to occasionally run into Field over the past three decades since “Mrs. Doubtfire” premiered. “She’s always great,” he said. Earlier this year, the actor published a graphic novel, “The Lawrence Brothers Detective Agency,” with his real-life brothers, which included a tribute to Field and Williams.

title: ‘Artemis Fowl’ Animated TV Show Set at Disney
summary: Artemis Fowl is coming to TV. An animated series adaptation of the bestselling book franchise has been greenlit for Disney Channel and Disney+. Author Eoin Colfer announced the news during the “25 Years of Artemis Fowl” panel at New York Comic Con. Colfer will serve as an executive producer of the series, which follows the […]
content:
Artemis Fowl is coming to TV.

An animated series adaptation of the bestselling book franchise has been greenlit for Disney Channel and Disney+. Author Eoin Colfer announced the news during the “25 Years of Artemis Fowl” panel at New York Comic Con.

Colfer will serve as an executive producer of the series, which follows the 13-year-old genius Artemis Fowl, who “uncovers an underground world of armed and dangerous — and surprisingly high-tech — fairies as he launches a plan to capture one and steal its magic to heal his dying mom and save his family,” per the logline.

The first “Artemis Fowl” book was published in 2001, and Colfer followed it up with 10 additional novels, the latest of which came out in 2021. The series has sold more than 35 million copies worldwide and has been translated in 48 languages.

Popular on Variety

This isn’t the first time the child prodigy has graced the screen. A live-action film adaptation based on the first book debuted on Disney+ in 2020 to negative reviews. The movie was removed from the streaming service in 2023.

“For more than two decades, Eoin Colfer’s ‘Artemis Fowl’ books have captivated readers around the world with unforgettable characters, imaginative world-building, and gripping adventures,” said Ayo Davis, president of Disney Kids & Family. “Bringing this beloved franchise to life as an animated series gives us the opportunity to introduce a new generation to Artemis’ world while honoring the longtime fans who have cherished these stories for years.”

Colfer said, “I am proud and delighted to be part of the formidable team that is putting the ‘Artemis Fowl’ animation on screen. Everyone is so talented and so positive that I feel certain the fairy world is in excellent hands.”

The “Artemis Fowl” series is also executive produced by Ben Juwono and Colleen Evanson.

title: Tom Cruise’s ‘Digger’ Now Stands to Lose $245 Million After Dropping 60% in Second Weekend
summary: “Digger” will go down in box office history for all the wrong reasons. Tom Cruise and director Alejandro González Iñárritu’s R-rated environmental satire is tracking to lose $245 million in its theatrical run, according to knowledgeable sources. It will wind up as one of the biggest flops, not just of the year but potentially of […]
content:
“Digger” will go down in box office history for all the wrong reasons.

Tom Cruise and director Alejandro González Iñárritu’s R-rated environmental satire is tracking to lose $245 million in its theatrical run, according to knowledgeable sources. It will wind up as one of the biggest flops, not just of the year but potentially of all time.

After “Digger” opened last weekend to $8 million domestically and $20 million globally, Warner Bros. was primed to lose between $150 million to $200 million theatrically. The studio is now bracing for a larger write-down after ticket sales for the movie declined by 60% in its second weekend, bringing its tally to $14.4 million domestically and $35.3 million globally. That’s despite the best efforts of Hollywood stars, including Anne Hathaway, Jane Fonda, Guillermo del Toro and Mandy Patinkin, who came to the defense of “Digger” and have been encouraging audiences to go to theaters.

“Digger” is expected to end its box office run with roughly $50 million globally. For reference, the movie needs $350 million globally to break even because theater owners get to keep about half of ticket sales. A Warner Bros. spokesperson had pushed back, saying the film’s break-even point is $300 million.

Popular on Variety

“Digger,” an offbeat dark comedy starring Cruise as a wealthy oil tycoon whose company causes a potential catastrophe, was always a risky proposition as a rare big-budget, starry original tentpole in today’s unforgiving box office landscape. Warner Bros. greenlit the film for $125 million, but the budget soared to $160 million to $180 million after production went over schedule. The studio spent another $100 million on global marketing efforts. Sources say those figures don’t include the studio’s award spend. A movie like “Digger,” which boasts a major star and acclaimed director, would have commanded an Oscar campaign around $15 million, but those efforts could be scaled back given the film’s frosty reception. (Reviews for “Digger” were so bad that Warner Bros. ran social media spots that encouraged moviegoers to “decide for yourself.”)

Most movies don’t earn a profit purely from their theatrical release, although box office dollars are important because they dictate downstream deals for TV, Pay 1 and streaming. Profitability for the studio will take even longer because Cruise has a deal that allows him to earn a percentage of revenues before the studio recoups any costs.

“Digger,” the studio’s last standalone release before merging with Paramount, extends a dismal year for Warner Bros. Theatrical losses have been piling from commercial disasters such as “The Bride” and “Supergirl.” Warner co-chiefs Mike De Luca and Pam Abdy, who departed the company last Friday as “Digger” landed on the big screen, enjoyed a historic box office run in 2025 with hits including “Sinners,” “A Minecraft Movie” and “Weapons.” But after the duo pushed several big swings into this calendar year, not a single film has managed to cross $100 million domestically. Warner Bros.’ theatrical fortunes should rebound in December when Denis Villeneuve’s “Dune: Part III,” starring Timothée Chalamet, Zendaya and Robert Pattinson, lands on the big screen.

title: ‘Musk’ Director Alex Gibney Confirms Universal Wavered in Planning Overseas Release, Says He Tried to Interview Elon Musk: ‘His Response Was Writing “Gibney Is a Douche”’
summary: Alex Gibney, director of the 3-hour-and-45-minute Elon Musk-centered documentary “Musk,” discussed the lengths he went to to interview the tech billionaire for the film and why he believes Universal Pictures hesitated to plan an international release in a new interview with The New York Times. Although Musk does not appear in the film (though Gibney […]
content:
Alex Gibney, director of the 3-hour-and-45-minute Elon Musk-centered documentary “Musk,” discussed the lengths he went to to interview the tech billionaire for the film and why he believes Universal Pictures hesitated to plan an international release in a new interview with The New York Times.

Although Musk does not appear in the film (though Gibney did create an avatar of him to simulate interviews in the doc), the director said it wasn’t for lack of trying, explaining that he and producer Jessie Deeter “reached out.” “Deeter knew him from two previous films. She had his cellphone number. She had an email address,” said Gibney. “She wrote sometimes folksy, sometimes detailed notes about how much we wanted his perspective. His response was writing ‘Gibney is a douche’ on Twitter.”

Ahead of the film’s release, Musk called it a “hit piece” and said “dogshit is worth more respect.” He added that Gibney “has ZERO integrity” and is a “horrible human.”

Popular on Variety

Gibney also noted that he “approached a lot of friends of his and business colleagues, and a lot of them said, ‘I can’t talk to you because Elon won’t give you permission.’” He cited Ashley St. Clair, Musk’s former girlfriend and the mother of his 14th child, and Justine Musk, his first wife, as major gets for the documentary.

And while it was reported last month that “Musk” would indeed get an international release despite legal threats from the SpaceX founder, Gibney confirmed with a “Yes” that the studio wavered on those release plans when the interviewer asked if that was the case. When questioned about what happened, Gibney responded: “Were they concerned that in this political environment, a film about the world’s richest man was problematic? Maybe, but you have to ask them.”

The paper noted that Universal declined to comment beyond what the company said in a previous statement: “We’ve always been committed to releasing this film, and our plans haven’t changed.”

“Musk” seeks to make sense of the world’s richest man and the outsized influence he has on the world, diving deep into his shift to MAGA supporter, controversies surrounding his Occupy Mars mission and Tesla’s self-driving cars and his contentious relationships with several of the mothers of his 14 children.

The documentary opened in theaters on Friday from Bleecker Street and generated $68,900 from four locations (an average of $17,225 per screen)

title: ‘Artemis Fowl’ Animated Series Greenlit At Disney Channel, Disney+ With Author Eoin Colfer As EP — NYCC
summary: More than 25 years after introducing the world to Artemis Fowl, author Eoin Colfer is teaming up with Disney for an animated series adaptation. On Sunday at New York Comic-Con, Colfer announced during the “25 Years of Artemis Fowl” panel that the series has been greenlit for Disney Channel and Disney+, and he will serve […]
content:
More than 25 years after introducing the world to Artemis Fowl, author Eoin Colfer is teaming up with Disney for an animated series adaptation.

On Sunday at New York Comic-Con, Colfer announced during the “25 Years of Artemis Fowl” panel that the series has been greenlit for Disney Channel and Disney+, and he will serve as executive producer.

Based on the book series that launched in 2001, Artemis Fowl follows the titular 13-year-old genius as he uncovers an underground world of armed and dangerous — and surprisingly high-tech — fairies, which gives him the idea to capture one and steal its magic to heal his dying mom and save his family.

“I am proud and delighted to be part of the formidable team that is putting the Artemis Fowl animation on screen,” said Colfer. “Everyone is so talented and so positive that I feel certain the fairy world is in excellent hands.”

Watch on Deadline

Ayo Davis, president of Disney Kids & Family, said, “For more than two decades, Eoin Colfer’s Artemis Fowl books have captivated readers around the world with unforgettable characters, imaginative world-building, and gripping adventures. Bringing this beloved franchise to life as an animated series gives us the opportunity to introduce a new generation to Artemis’ world while honoring the longtime fans who have cherished these stories for years.”

In addition to Colfer, EPs include Ben Juwono and Colleen Evanson.

title: Bend Film Festival Prizes Go To ‘Hot Water,’ ‘Edward Said: Between Worlds,’ ‘Kikuyu Land,’ ‘The Lake’ & More
summary: The Bend Film Festival wraps on Sunday after presenting awards for the 23rd edition of the cinematic spectacle in central Oregon. Ramzi Bashour’s debut feature Hot Water, starring Lubna Azabal (Coriolanus), Daniel Zolghadri (Funny Pages), and Dale Dickey (Widow’s Bay), won Best Narrative Feature. The filmmaker, born in Lebanon and based in New York City, […]
content:
The Bend Film Festival wraps on Sunday after presenting awards for the 23rd edition of the cinematic spectacle in central Oregon.

Ramzi Bashour’s debut feature Hot Water, starring Lubna Azabal (Coriolanus), Daniel Zolghadri (Funny Pages), and Dale Dickey (Widow’s Bay), won Best Narrative Feature. The filmmaker, born in Lebanon and based in New York City, crafts an offbeat road trip movie involving a mother and son “stopping at diners, motels, and hot springs” in the American West.

The jury, comprised of Whitaker Lader, Charlie Sextro, and Sebastián Hernández, wrote Hot Water “charmed our socks off. The film took us on a memorable journey across the U.S. where we were privileged to witness the prickly detours of a mother/son relationship. Although this marks the director’s feature debut, it was clear to us that this is only the beginning of a long, storied filmmaking career considering how much life and love they packed into a low-budget movie.”

Palestinian-American academic, literary critic, and political activist Edward Said, Mantova, September 19, 2001. Photo by Leonardo Cendamo/Getty Images

In Documentary Feature Competition, the top prize went to Edward Said: Between Worlds, director Maiken Baird’s portrait of the late Palestinian scholar and activist. The film traces Said’s journey from Mandatory Palestine (then under British control) to exile with his family in Egypt after the 1948 Nakba and establishment of the state of Israel, and his eventual relocation to the U.S. where he became a professor of comparative literature at Columbia University in New York. After the 1967 Arab Israeli war and Israel’s occupation of Gaza and the West Bank, Said became a leading voice for the Palestinian cause.

Watch on Deadline

The documentary jury, comprised of Oscar winner Diane Becker (Navalny), Mia Bruno, and myself, wrote, “In his own words more than two decades after his death, through the archive recordings of his own voice, Edward Said: Between Worlds is a nuanced, timely, and reflective film of the complicated Palestinian identity after the war in 1948 as well as a portrait of the Palestinian academic who advocated for coexistence in a time where such voices were few and far between.”

‘I Got Bombed at Harvey’s’ FunMeter

Documentary jurors presented a Special Jury Award for Craft to I Got Bombed at Harvey’s, directed by Bryan Storkel and Amy Bandlien Storkel, a rollicking story of a man with a grudge and a thousand pounds of dynamite with which to exact vengeance on his perceived enemy at a Nevada casino.

“These filmmakers elevate the true crime genre through a riveting story of toxic masculinity and a patriarch’s malign control over his sons who become unwilling accomplices in a bizarre bombing plot,” we wrote. “This entertaining film is highlighted by superb editing, an electric pace, well-lit interviews with relevant participants, seamless integration of archive and recreations that evoke Lake Tahoe in 1980 and the locus of action – Harvey’s Wagon Wheel Resort and Casino.”

The Lake‘ Courtesy of Abby Ellis

The doc jury also selected a winner in the 2026 Environmental/Outdoor Features Competition, choosing from among nonfiction films “centered on the relationships between humans and nature — by turns adversarial, exploitative, mutually beneficial and endlessly evolving.” The top prize there was awarded to The Lake, directed by Abby Ellis, a film exploring the environmental catastrophe posed by the rapidly shrinking Great Salt Lake in Utah.

“What is at stake when we remain locked in a stalemate over how to address the dire state of our natural world?” the jury wrote. “What would it take for a community, a government, an industry, to recognize and act on how truly desperate the situation has become? Through the riveting exploration of those frantically navigating what is at once both so imperative and so intractable, The Lake illuminates the powerful truth that we do not have time to waste.”

Mr. Mungai in ‘ Kikuyu Land Courtesy of Trifilm Studios/Photo by Andrew H. Brown

In the competition for Best Indigenous Feature, the prize went to Kikuyu Land, directed by Bea Wangondu and Andrew H. Brown. That film, set in Kenya’s contested tea fields, examines “the enduring legacy of colonial exploitation.”

“The issues at the center of this film reach far beyond its borders,” wrote the Indigenous Feature jury, comprised of LaRonn Katchia, Dawn Jones Redstone, and Johnnie Jae. “Colonialism has shaped communities around the world, and its effects continue to influence the lives people lead and the futures they are trying to create. This film offers a powerful example of that kind of reckoning, showing that accountability can begin when we’re willing to turn the same scrutiny we apply to the world back toward ourselves.”

In a statement, BendFilm Programming Director Selin Sevinç noted, “These award winners represent the kind of bold, urgent independent cinema we’re committed to championing. Each of these films meets the moment with artistry, authenticity, and vision. I can’t wait to see what’s next for both these stories and their talented tellers.”

The Tower Theatre, one of the venues for the Bend Film Festival. Matthew Carey

The festival, which opened Wednesday, October 7 and closes Sunday, presented its Indie Filmmaker of the Year Award to Oscar-nominated director Rory Kennedy. She brought two of her films to Bend – The Trial of Alec Baldwin and Freefall: A Reckoning for Boeing.

Actress Tantoo Cardinal was named BendFilm’s Indigenous Honoree. The star of Killers of the Flower Moon, Dances With Wolves, Black Robe and many other films was born in Alberta, Canada and is of Cree and Métis heritage.

The 2027 Bend Film Festival is set to unfold from October 6-10.

These are additional prizes award at the 2026 Bend Film Festival:

SHORT FILM COMPETITION

The 2026 Narrative, Animated and Documentary Shorts jury comprised Daniel Crooke, Max Geschwind and Laura Henneman. The inaugural Youth Jurors were Poppy Post, Mac Schlaadt, and Cora Martin.

Best Animated Short Film: Living with a Visionary by Stephen P. Neary

“For its inventive animation and the way it uses the form to tell a story that feels both deeply personal and completely original, this film shows us what it means to love and live alongside someone whose creative drive and purpose can consume everything around them— and how the person beside the visionary has a story and perspective of their own.”

Best Comedy Short Film: The Oracle by JJ Adler

“This film had us laughing from the beginning and kept finding ways to surprise us as it went along. The premise is so simple and clever, but the ensemble — led by an all-too-recognizable character actor — had us in the palm of their hand the entire time. The sharp, confident, neurotic, and genuinely funny filmmaking demonstrates a firm grasp on telling this deeply chaotic but also resonant story about our desire for certainty and how ridiculous we can become when we’re desperate for someone, or something, to tell us what to do.”

Best Dramatic Short Film: Skin on Skin by Simon Schneckenburger

“This film announces the arrival of a major new voice in international cinema, one whose commanding control over craft and tone anchors this story’s volatile milieu with rich soulful resonance. While it’s a story of two strangers, and their emotional and physical proximity to one another, it’s also a study of the walls erected to divide neighboring nations, labor and capital, and the majority from the other. That you can practically feel the sweat on the brows of these characters speaks to the overwhelming audiovisual power that director Simon Schneckenburger imbues in every frame of this raw cry for liberation and connection.”

Best Documentary Short Film: Still Standing by Victor Suarez and Livia Albeck-Ripka

“This haunting documentary details a devastating environmental reality through an urgent and unexpected lens, not simply in its atypical focus selecting whose story to tell, and when, but through its arresting formal approach which evokes displacement, dread, and the near-invisible danger of lingering contamination. The chilling contradiction found in the filmmakers’ blend of immediacy and detachment mirrors the transformation of 9,000 homes in Altadena, California from domestic bliss to toxic abyss after quote-unquote surviving the Eaton fires of early 2025.”

Best Indigenous Short Film [selected by jurors LaRonn Katchia, Dawn Jones Redstone, and Johnnie Jae]: First Descent: Kayaking the Klamath by Jessie Sears

“This film weaves together the generations of work following the historic removal of multiple dams on the Klamath River with the hopeful journey of the next generation of Indigenous river stewards as they navigate, and learn their relationship to this precious resource.”

Special Jury Award for Creative Vision: Dropping Off by Will Mayo and Ian Scott

“This film surprised us with its blend of comedy and drama and its unusual cinematic approach to a recognizable setting. The strong visual and editing style, combined with a wonderfully natural central performance brought both perspective and emotional weight to a fictional story that still feels like it could be unfolding, right now, in a Los Angeles neighborhood.”

Youth Jury Award for a Short Film: The Boy with the Dinosaur Head by Imran J. Khan “This film explores the complexities of identity in a society that deems differences to be undesirable, and the impact this has on younger generations.”

title: Palme d’Or Prestige: ‘Fjord’ Tops Indie Openers, ‘Naza’ Eyes $500k Surge – Specialty Box Office
summary: Neon’s Cannes Palme d’Or-winning drama Fjord starring Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve had a terrific $124k opening on four screens in New York and Los Angeles, as documentary Naza marks a strong week two expansion. Cristian Mungiu’s Fjord is the director’s second Palme d’Or for Mungiu and the seventh consecutive win for Neon. The film […]
content:
Neon’s Cannes Palme d’Or-winning drama Fjord starring Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve had a terrific $124k opening on four screens in New York and Los Angeles, as documentary Naza marks a strong week two expansion.

Cristian Mungiu’s Fjord is the director’s second Palme d’Or for Mungiu and the seventh consecutive win for Neon. The film also took the FIPRESCI Award at Cannes and is Romania’s Oscar entry for Best International Feature. It follows a devout Romanian Norwegian couple named Gheorghius who resettle in a village in a distant fjord where they become close to their neighbors, the Halbergs. Their children bond. But when adolescent Elia Gheorghiu shows up at school with bruises, the community questions the traditional education the Gheorghiu yougsters are getting from their parents. Rotten Tomatoes Certified Fresh at 90%.

Naza by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, two of the Oscar winning directors of No Other Land, will top $500k Monday after a week two expansion.

Watch on Deadline

Some exhibitors are including four-day weekend estimates to note Monday, the Columbus Day holiday in the U.S.

After grossing $125k over its first eight days at the IFC Center in New York, the doc broadened to 85 engagements in 30+ markets for an estimated $298k for the 3-day weekend and an estimated $378.2k over the four days, bringing its cume to $504,074.

The film, released independently with the backing of The Guardian and MK2, sees the directors interviewing Israeli soldiers and intelligence officers, whose identities are hidden, on the civilian death toll in Gaza. It will continue to roll out through October.

At 100% certified fresh with critics on Rotten Tomatoes.

Chris Rock’s Misty Green from A24 launched in limited release on six screens in NY and LA to $85.7k for the three-day weekend and $98.7k for the four days. Star Rosalind Eleazar’s portrait of a talented actress fighting for her second act in Hollywood has earned praise since the film’s TIFF premiere alongside a cast including Daniel Kaluuya, Adam Driver, Anna Kendrick and Rock himself. Expand selectively into top markets this weekend.

Bleecker Street is eyeing a circa $70k three-day gross for Alex Gibney’s documentary Musk on four screens for a per theater average of $17.2k. The buzzy Venice-premiering doc has a near four-hour runtime that limits showtimes.

California Schemin’ from Magenta Light Studios directed by James McAvoy opened to an estimated $18.7k at five locations in NY and LA. McAvoy stars with Seamus McLean Ross, Samuel Bottomley, Lucy Halliday and Rebekah Murrell in the story of two Scottish lads from Dundee who conned the music industry by pretending to be an established Californian rap duo.

Julia Loktev’s sweeping documentary My Undesirable Friends Part II – Exile opened exclusively at New York’s Film Forum this weekend. A follow up to Part I released last year, which was short-listed for the Oscar for Best Documentary Feature and won both the NYFCC and LAFCC awards for Best Non-Fictions film, is estimated to gross $7.5k limited by the 6-hour running time and seating capacity (100 seats).

Independently released with the support of Cinetic and mTuckman media, the Venice and Telluride selection next opens Los Angeles on Oct. 16 before rolling out to markets across the country throughout the fall

Holdover If I Go Will They Miss Me is estimated to gross $29.6k on 42 screens for a rising new cume of $980.7k in week 5. The Rich Spirit release stars Danielle Brooks and J Alphonse Nicholson and is directed by Walter Thompson-Hernandez. RT certified fresh at 95%, it will continue to play exclusively in theaters in coming weeks.

Notable: Fathom Entertainment’s release ofGuillermo del Toro’s Pan’s Labyrinth 20th Anniversary, ranked no. 11 at the domestic box office with an estimated $1.66 million from 1,168 locations.In postwar Spain, a young girl discovers a mysterious labyrinth and a magical world while living under the rule of her brutal stepfather. The 2006 film stars Ivana Baquero, Sergi López, Maribel Verdú and Doug Jones.

Trafalgar Releasing’s concert film Queen Budapest pulled in at no. 16 with an estimated $681k from 312 locations.The concert film captures Queen’s 1986 stadium performance in Budapest during the Magic Tour. Featuring Freddie Mercury, Brian May, Roger Taylor and John Deacon, the restored film is directed by János Zsombolyai.

title: Dhar Mann Says Creator City In L.A. Will Bring Brands, Creators & Culture Under One Roof
summary: Dhar Mann took center stage at MIPCOM on Sunday for the market’s first-ever pre-opening headline session. He broke down the vision for his soon-to-open studio site, Creator City. Mann founded Dhar Mann Studios and recently announced Creator City, a four-acre campus in L.A. with multiple sound stages and, he said, 175 sets able to house […]
content:
Dhar Mann took center stage at MIPCOM on Sunday for the market’s first-ever pre-opening headline session. He broke down the vision for his soon-to-open studio site, Creator City.

Mann founded Dhar Mann Studios and recently announced Creator City, a four-acre campus in L.A. with multiple sound stages and, he said, 175 sets able to house 15 productions concurrently.

“It’s basically where creators, brands, and culture [will] all come together in one place,” Mann said. “All of the sets that we have in our current studio, they’re unbranded, because five years ago nobody was taking me seriously, nobody was taking YouTubers very seriously.

“But now all the sets [at Creator City] are actual brands. When you see content being created, it’s not just a random coffee shop, it could be a Starbucks, it’s not just a random retail store, it could be a Target.”

Watch on Deadline

DMS is working with a handful of brands that will be launch partners. “This is going to be the place that the top creators in the world come to make content [and] when they’re shooting content, it’s [with] actual real brands that live in the real world.”

The DMS founder, who talked about starting out shooting on a phone while struggling to pay his rent, added: “You’re going to start to see all kinds of storytelling around real brands coming out of that studio. We’re having our grand opening Super Bowl week.”

Talking of brands, Mann said DMS is expanding a relationship with consumer electronics giant Samsung that has already yielded one scripted series, Unlikely Romances, about seemingly improbable couples. There will be a new show called Unlikely Families.

“When it comes to family, it’s not always about blood, it’s often about love,” Mann said. “There’s so many people that became like brothers to me or father figures. This whole series is about families that come together due to unlikely circumstances, and they seem like they would never work out as a family. But against all odds, love is more important than blood. It’s coming out in the next couple months.”

DMS has struck deals with media giants Disney and Fox and the DMS founder said the future of entertainment is about bridging the traditional business and the creator economy. “There is such a magic that happens when folks from the traditional world and the creator world can come together,” he said.

DMS, meanwhile, is ramping up production. It will have a new original every month from later this year. “The future is definitely building IP,” Mann said. “Starting in December, every single month we are launching one new series on our YouTube.”

Mann was joined by former MTV and Disney exec Sean Atkins, CEO of DMS, and said the duo hashed out the content strategy for the studio based on a digital-first rather than traditional, business model.

“The thinking is just different for us, because of the low-cost model, because of the speed,” Mann said. “We’re able to just continue to throw as many darts on the wall and see which one sticks. We had the realization, as we’re working on pitching all these different platforms. One day I had a conversation with Sean, and it was like, ‘Why don’t we just do that ourselves, on our own YouTube?’”

A Pep Talk For Trad Media

Speaking to a room of TV folk, Mann was asked about the anxiety many staffers and execs in the traditional business are feeling amid waves of consolidation, fragmentation and change.

In a characteristically upbeat manner, he gave the Cannes crowd a pep talk. “Don’t get married to your job title, get more married to the skills that you have, and develop those,” he said.

“There’s so many people out there, such as myself, that really value those skills and are looking to work with folks like you. So, while I understand there’s a lot of doom and gloom, there are also so many exciting opportunities that are happening if you’re open to it.”

title: Theatrical Is Alive: YTD Domestic B.O. Surges Past $8 Billion, Two Months Sooner Than 2025
summary: The motion picture studios can easily sing that 42nd Street song “We’re in the Money” as the U.S. and Canada box office clicked past the $8 billion mark on Friday. Why is this a big deal? Because in post-Covid times distributors and exhibitors were thankful enough to even hit $8 billion in North America. Rentrak […]
content:
The motion picture studios can easily sing that 42nd Street song “We’re in the Money” as the U.S. and Canada box office clicked past the $8 billion mark on Friday.

Why is this a big deal? Because in post-Covid times distributors and exhibitors were thankful enough to even hit $8 billion in North America.

Rentrak points out that 2026 hit the $8 billion mark in 282 days, matching the exact pace of 2011 and reaching that milestone a full 59 days earlier than in 2025. Last year the domestic box office for Jan. 1-Dec. 31 finaled at $8.87B. Currently for the Jan. 1-Oct. 11 period, the U.S./Canada box office stands at $8.07B, +20% ahead of the same period in 2025 ($6.75B).

This is the fourth time that the domestic box office has clicked past $8B post-pandemic, the other two years being 2024 ($8.7B) and 2023 ($9B, the best domestic take post-Covid).

Watch on Deadline

Many box office sources have forecasted that this year will final at $10 billion (Disney/Marvel Studio’s Avengers: Doomsday and Warner Bros/Legendary’s Dune Part III are expected to do the trick). Exhibitors and studios continue to yearn for the good old days: Between 2015-2019, the North American box office grossed $11B+ annually. The highest domestic B.O. year ever per Rentrak was 2018 with $11.9B.

Top ten movies at the domestic box office so far in 2026:

Spider-Man: Brand New Day (Sony) $956.8M The Odyssey (Uni) $622.9M Toy Story 5 (Dis) $480.2M The Super Mario Galaxy Movie (Uni) $429.8M Michael (LG) $372.3M Project Hail Mary (AMZ) $344M Obsession (Focus) $263.4M The Devil Wears Prada 2 (20th) $220.5M Backrooms (A24) $197.5M Minions & Monsters (Uni) $183.1M

title: Hugh Hefner’s Ex-Wife Calls Him a ‘True Gentleman’ After His Widow Crystal Harris Urges Jessica Biel to ‘Reconsider’ Playing His Wife
summary: Kimberly Hefner, who was married to Hugh Hefner from 1989 until their divorce was finalized in 2010, has taken to social media to share a statement in support of her late husband after his former wife, Crystal Harris, alleged she experienced sexual, emotional, financial and physical abuse while married to the Playboy magazine founder. Harris […]
content:
Kimberly Hefner, who was married to Hugh Hefner from 1989 until their divorce was finalized in 2010, has taken to social media to share a statement in support of her late husband after his former wife, Crystal Harris, alleged she experienced sexual, emotional, financial and physical abuse while married to the Playboy magazine founder. Harris shared her story following the news that Jessica Biel would play a fictional version of Hefner’s wife in the upcoming film “Playmates.”

“I was married to Hef for over 21 years. We shared a lifetime of beautiful memories, raised 2 wonderful sons together, and had a deeply loving bond that remained strong until his passing on September 27th, 2017 and continues with me to this day,” wrote Kimberly. “I often told him if you look up the word gentleman in the dictionary you would find his name and photograph. Hef was in every sense of the word, a true gentleman, kind, loving, generous, philanthropic, and a man of extraordinary character.”

Popular on Variety

She continued: “Losing Hef was devastating, and his absence is still deeply felt. I had the privilege of knowing and loving the man behind the public image, and I will always treasure the life and memories we shared. I will always believe the world was a better place because he was in it. I am forever grateful and blessed.”

Before they tied the knot, Kimberly and Hugh met when she was modeling for Playboy’s Playmate of the Month centerfold. Hugh met Harris at a Halloween party at the Playboy Mansion when she was a 21-year-old college student. She moved into the mansion shortly thereafter and married Hugh in 2012. The two remained together until his death in Sept. 2017, after which Harris published her 2024 memoir “Only Say Good Things: Surviving Playboy and Finding Myself,” in which she revealed her experiences at the mansion.

“Playmates” will revolve around “Elle (Indiana Elle), a 13-year-old know-it-all who considers the Playboy Mansion her second home, and meets Anna (Lily-Rose Depp), one of seven hopefuls vying to be Playmate of the Month,” per the film’s synopsis. “The two form an unlikely friendship and try to help each other get what the other wants most, a magazine cover and a boy.”

Lorraine Nicholson, the daughter of Jack Nicholson, is writing and directing the Searchlight film. Bill Pullman will star as Hugh.

See Kimberly’s post below.

title: Quentin Tarantino Play ‘The Popinjay Cavalier,’ Starring Sacha Baron Cohen, to Open on West End in March
summary: Quentin Tarantino’s first-ever stage play, “The Popinjay Cavalier” starring Sacha Baron Cohen, will open at London’s Phoenix Theatre in March. Written and directed by Tarantino, the play — described as a “swashbuckling comedy” — will hold previews from Feb. 23, with opening night set for March 18. It’s set to run for three months, closing […]
content:
Quentin Tarantino‘s first-ever stage play, “The Popinjay Cavalier” starring Sacha Baron Cohen, will open at London’s Phoenix Theatre in March.

Written and directed by Tarantino, the play — described as a “swashbuckling comedy” — will hold previews from Feb. 23, with opening night set for March 18. It’s set to run for three months, closing on June 13. Tickets will go on sale via the play’s website at 9 a.m. BST on Monday, starting at just £25.

“I’m keen with anticipation to give the West End a great night out,” Tarantino said in a statement.

Popular on Variety

Set in 1830s Europe, “The Popinjay Cavalier” is a “rambunctious comedy of deception and disguise inspired by the grand swashbuckling epics of stage and screen,” as the play’s synopsis reads. “A sweeping celebration of theatre and its heightened romance, told with Tarantino’s signature style and unmistakable wit, ‘The Popinjay Cavalier’ is inspired by the classic swashbuckler genre of old Hollywood, including the writings of George Bruce, Ernst Vajda and Jesse Lasky Jr.”

Added Baron Cohen, whose casting was first revealed last month: “Quentin called, I said yes before he even got to say his first ‘motherf—er’. When the best director in the world calls, you don’t ask questions. I am beyond delighted that we will be losing our West End virginity together, I have made him promise not to be gentle.”

Producers Tom Rothman, chairman and CEO of Sony Pictures Entertainment’s Motion Picture group, and Sonia Friedman said it is a “joy and an honor to be developing this play with Quentin — and absolutely quite an adventure.”

They continued, “How lucky we are that one of the great storytellers of our time has chosen to make his theatrical debut. To see Quentin in action in a rehearsal room is extraordinary. His delight in working with actors, fencers, acrobats, musicians and our creative team is infectious, and there is such pleasure in hearing his delicious language come alive and discovering what his world can become on stage.”

The duo went on to say that Baron Cohen is a “fearless, brilliantly inventive actor with the wit, mischief and daring this role demands. We feel immensely fortunate to be producing this show. Audiences are in for a tremendous treat.”

The creative team joining Tarantino includes scenic and costume designer Tom Pye, lighting designer Natasha Chivers, sound designer Ian Dickinson, fight director Philip d’Orleans and action coordinator Sam Lyon-Behan, with music by Tim Phillips and casting by Jim Carnahan, CSA.

Further casting will be announced at a later date.

title: After Kelly Clarkson Slams Brooklyn Novelty Store, Shop Says the ‘One-of-a-Kind’ Singing Bird She Wanted Wasn’t Actually For Sale
summary: After Kelly Clarkson took to X on Saturday to share her experience “being treated like Julia Roberts” in “Pretty Woman” during a visit to Art of Play, a novelty shop in Brooklyn, the local business is responding to her claims, saying it has received “widespread outrage” since and explaining that the item she wanted to […]
content:
After Kelly Clarkson took to X on Saturday to share her experience “being treated like Julia Roberts” in “Pretty Woman” during a visit to Art of Play, a novelty shop in Brooklyn, the local business is responding to her claims, saying it has received “widespread outrage” since and explaining that the item she wanted to buy — a bird permanently fixed to the store’s wall– was not actually for sale.

In her initial tweet, which has garnered nearly 260,000 likes and 32.2 million views, the singer wrote that she had driven to the store, which she thought “looked really rad and had a few things in mind to buy.” She continued, writing that she “literally was looked at as if I couldn’t afford it and was told he could find something comparable for me. Wow, dude. You’re an idiot and just lost a huge sale.” She then named the store and told her fans to visit if they “enjoy being treated like Julia Roberts character in Pretty Woman,” accompanied by a thumbs-down emoji.

Popular on Variety

On Sunday, the business posted a multi-slide carousel to the store’s Instagram account sharing their side of the story. They began by clarifying that the item Clarkson inquired about purchasing was “a one-of-a-kind singing and dancing bird automaton who plays an important role in the magic shows we host here.” “Molly is permanently attached to the wall and isn’t for sale. However, the negative experience Kelly described on Twitter would resonate with anyone who has ever felt judged in a shop,” the caption read.

The business continued to note that “whether someone comes in to make a purchase or simply look around for a while, they are equally welcome. We greet everyone who walks in the door with the invitation to ‘pick things up and play.’ And they do, many stay for hours enjoying our puzzles, games and toys.”

Art of Play also acknowledged the significant backlash they’ve been receiving since Clarkson’s statement, before quoting the singer and concluding the message.

“Imagine our surprise when our small local business was suddenly attacked by 8 million people who have never visited our store. It’s been a surreal experience to be the focus of such widespread outrage after just one mention by a celebrity. Thanks to all our friends for their support and welcome to all the curious folks who have discovered us amidst the drama. We’re going to keep our heads down and hopefully, we can clear things up with Kelly someday. As a talented popular singer once said ‘what doesn’t kill you makes you stronger.'”

In a Feb. 2025 Instagram post’s caption, the business wrote that Molly is the store’s “beloved shop bird” and “mascot,” and she is one of the few items in Art of Play that has a “Do Not Touch” sign.

See the full posts below.

title: John Stamos Addresses Mike Love’s Health as Beach Boys Concert Footage Raises Concerns: ‘We Don’t Know What the Future Holds — We Have Tonight’
summary: Following many Beach Boys fans and followers expressing concern for Mike Love after seeing footage from the group’s Saturday night show in Cincinnati, John Stamos has stepped in with a statement acknowledging that Love is in poor health as they are doing these shows and suggesting that his longtime friend’s time on stage may be […]
content:
Following many Beach Boys fans and followers expressing concern for Mike Love after seeing footage from the group’s Saturday night show in Cincinnati, John Stamos has stepped in with a statement acknowledging that Love is in poor health as they are doing these shows and suggesting that his longtime friend’s time on stage may be nearing an end.

“I’ve played with Mike for 41 years. I never imagined how deeply it would affect me to see someone larger than life face something so human and fragile,” Stamos said in his Instagram post, managing expectations on his way to performing with the Beach Boys at a show scheduled for Sunday at Nashville’s Ryman Auditorium.

“We hope he’ll be doing what he loves for years to come, but we don’t know what the future holds. We have tonight,” Stamos said. The actor-musician added, “The Mike Love we see tonight may not be exactly the Mike we’ve always known. But he’s still every bit the Mike we love.” (Scroll down to read Stamos’ complete statement.)

Popular on Variety

The Beach Boys had been off the road since July, canceling several months of dates as Love addressed health concerns, with a pledge to take up where they left off. More gigs kept being canceled, one by one, until the group finally resumed action, first with a private performance and then a return to public touring with Saturday’s Cincinnati show. But many were alarmed by what they saw in fan-posted video, with Love appearing much weaker and less engaged than he was even in July’s shows.

The frontman for the group for the last six and a half decades remained seated and largely motionless for the entire show in Ohio, not taking any of the many lead vocals he was still doing when the Beach Boys performed for three nights at the Hollywood Bowl in July. One short clip that quickly circulated on social media showed Stamos urging Love to do some hand gestures from his seat, and the Beach Boys’ mainstay gamely complying, but without much apparent energy, before going back to sitting in place.

The Nashville show is the last one on the Beach Boys’ itinerary until mid-November, when they are scheduled to play in Orlando Nov. 11 and Bristol Nov. 13. After that, they just have one gig publicly announced for 2027, in contrast to the usual robust touring schedule they would usually have announced by this time, leading fans to wonder if they really may be prepared to be winding up Love’s time fronting the group.

Coincidentally, across the country, another Beach Boys mainstay from the beginning, Al Jardine, is doing a concert Sunday night in which guest appearances have been promised by two other historical Beach Boys members, Bruce Johnston (who until a few months ago was still part of Love’s touring unit) and David Marks.



John Stamos’ complete statement from Sunday afternoon:

I’m boarding a plane to Nashville to play with the Beach Boys at the Ryman Auditorium, struggling to put my feelings into words.



My beloved friend, father figure, musical hero and mentor, Mike Love, is facing serious health challenges. We hope he’ll be doing what he loves for years to come, but we don’t know what the future holds. We have tonight.



Mike is a fighter. Despite doctors, family and friends urging him to focus on his health, he insists on being on stage. He says he needs his band, the audience, his friends and drummer surrounding him to lift him up.



I’ve played with Mike for 41 years. I never imagined how deeply it would affect me to see someone larger than life face something so human and fragile.



The Mike Love we see tonight may not be exactly the Mike we’ve always known. But he’s still every bit the Mike we love.



His lyrics, optimism, unforgettable hooks and more than 7,000 concerts have brought joy to generations. What he’s given me personally is immeasurable.



Forty-one years of stages, airplanes, hotel rooms, laughter and moments nobody else saw. He married Caitlin and me. He’s shared experiences with my family, and now my son.



Mike didn’t just give me a place in his band. He gave me a place in his life.



He taught me how to entertain, hold a stage, connect with an audience and make people feel something. I carry those lessons everywhere. He’s made me a better musician, entertainer and man.



This life with Mike and the Beach Boys has become part of my identity. I’ve felt entrusted with being a steward of this extraordinary music, carrying it to new generations.



Tonight, at the Ryman, sharing the stage with Mike, I want to be completely present. Hear every harmony, familiar joke and cheer. Feel that first chord hit and watch age, illness and time disappear. Just a bunch of guys making music together.



Maybe the hardest part of loving someone is becoming so accustomed to the miracle of having them there that you forget it’s a miracle at all.



Tonight, I won’t forget.



I want to cherish every second without feeling those seconds slipping away.



That’s what I’m giving him.



We don’t know what tomorrow brings. But we have tonight.

title: ‘Animals’ Star Luis Gerardo Méndez on Working With Ben Affleck and Speaking Out About Immigration: ‘You Could Be Next’
summary: When Luis Gerardo Méndez got a call from his agents that Ben Affleck wanted to cast him in “Animals,” he was surprised the Oscar winner even knew who he was. “They sent me the script, and it had a very beautiful note at the end from Ben, just saying like, ‘Hey, Luis, I really want […]
content:
When Luis Gerardo Méndez got a call from his agents that Ben Affleck wanted to cast him in “Animals,” he was surprised the Oscar winner even knew who he was.

“They sent me the script, and it had a very beautiful note at the end from Ben, just saying like, ‘Hey, Luis, I really want you to be in the movie. This script is not ready. I’m gonna do a rewrite specifically about your character, so I’m gonna call you around Christmas because I would love to hear your thoughts,’” Méndez tells me.

They didn’t meet in person until the first day of rehearsals.

Popular on Variety

“Ben saw me and he came to me with his massive Batman back and hugged me, and he started screaming to everyone like, ‘This guy is the best actor in Mexico. He’s incredible!’” says Méndez, who first gained fame in his native Mexico with his starring role in the 2013 comedy “The Noble Family.” “He brought me to his office and he started speaking like nonstop for an hour about me and how excited he was to work with me. At the end I was like, ‘Ben, can I ask you something? Why are you so excited to work with me?’ And he was like, ‘“Narcos: Mexico.” Your character is incredible. I was watching “Narcos,” and I called Matt [Damon, who was originally supposed to star in the film] and said, ‘Hey, dude, are you watching “Narcos?” The cop. We need to get the cop.’”

Méndez starred in the third season of the Netflix series “Narcos: Mexico” in 2021 as corrupt cop Victor Tapia.

Affleck stars in “Animals” — he also directed the film and co-wrote the script — as a businessman running for Los Angeles mayor when he and his wife (Kerry Washington) receive a phone call saying that their son Denny (Christopher Woodley) has been kidnapped.

Méndez plays Ramon, the undocumented Mexican boyfriend of the couple’s housekeeper (Adriana Paz), who finds himself unexpectedly thrust into trying to resolve the kidnapping when things take a drastic turn.

As for Affleck’s script changes for Ramon, Méndez says, “It was so magical because it was like if Ben had read my mind, like all the things that I thought about the character that were missing, about the proper representation, about the proper way of speaking of the characters … everything was there.”

While the film is meant to entertain, Méndez hopes it also fosters conversations around immigration.

“What I want the audiences to think about for a second is: no one leaves their homes because they want to,” he says. “They leave it because they’re running away from violence, from political persecution. We need to understand that. The vast majority of the immigrants, not just in the U.S. but in the whole world, they just want to work and they’re very hard workers. They just want to do the right thing like our characters in the movie. They’re taking the biggest risks with the least protection. They’re doing the right stuff in a system that won’t allow them to shine or to be heroes.”

Méndez splits his time between Los Angeles and Mexico City. He also travels the globe as a goodwill ambassador for UNHCR (Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees).

Méndez chokes up when asked about ICE. “To hear about these families getting separated, it’s really hard for me to speak about it, especially with what happened yesterday here in New York,” he says in reference to the recent ICE shooting of 28-year-old Oscar Belgal. “I feel like no matter what your immigration status is, no one should lose their dignity. It’s as simple as that.”

He also warns about global warming’s effect on immigration. “We’re going to see massive amounts of people moving, leaving. We’re seeing it already in California,” Méndez explains. “We don’t know if tomorrow we’re going to be the ones migrating. No one has any certainty about that. We must understand that. We must be welcoming because we don’t know what’s going to happen in the next 20 or 30 years. It’s about empathy and also about you could be next, we could be next.”

title: ‘Artificial’s Ike Barinholtz Teases What Makes His “Menacing” Elon Musk Performance “A Little Ridiculous”
summary: As Luca Guadagnino explored the rise of AI in Artificial, Ike Barinholtz explored the psyche of Elon Musk with his portrayal of the OpenAI co-founder. While discussing how he got into character as Musk, the actor explained what made his performance “menacing” but also “a little ridiculous” in the Neon film, which premieres Christmas Day […]
content:
As Luca Guadagnino explored the rise of AI in Artificial, Ike Barinholtz explored the psyche of Elon Musk with his portrayal of the OpenAI co-founder.

While discussing how he got into character as Musk, the actor explained what made his performance “menacing” but also “a little ridiculous” in the Neon film, which premieres Christmas Day in US theaters, starring Andrew Garfield as OpenAI CEO Sam Altman.

“Well, the good news is, I got to play him in an era where he was really kind of looked at as the next Tony Stark,” he told Discussing Film. “But I had to do these scenes that are him kind of behind the curtain a little bit, so there’s not like tape on it and stuff.”

Barinholtz added, “So, we tried to make something that felt menacing to the people in the room, but as you pull out 37,000 feet down, looking down, it does seem a little ridiculous.”

Watch on Deadline

Penned by Simon Rich, Artificial centers around the controversial firing and subsequent rehiring of Altman by OpenAI’s board of directors within a span of five days in November 2023.

Ike Barinholtz says his portrayal of Elon Musk in Luca Guadagnino's ‘ARTIFICIAL’ is just before he became “menacing” publicly.



“I got to play him in an era where he was looked at as the next Tony Stark but I also did these scenes that are him [menacing] behind the curtain.” pic.twitter.com/DkvlTZjyeU — DiscussingFilm (@DiscussingFilm) October 11, 2026

The cast also includes Yura Borisov, Monica Barbaro, Cooper Hoffman, Jason Schwartzman, Chris O’Dowd, Mark Rylance, Zosia Mamet, Cooper Koch and Billie Lourd.

title: Robert Pattinson Approached Chris Hansen Portrayal In ‘Primetime’ As “A Fan”: “I Was Trying To Make Him Cool”
summary: Although Chris Hansen has made clear that the feeling is not mutual, Primetime‘s Robert Pattinson has confessed he’s a fan of the To Catch a Predator host. Following Hansen’s ongoing criticism of the Lance Oppenheim-helmed film, which is now playing in theaters, Pattinson explained that he “was trying to make [Hansen] look cool” in the […]
content:
Although Chris Hansen has made clear that the feeling is not mutual, Primetime‘s Robert Pattinson has confessed he’s a fan of the To Catch a Predator host.

Following Hansen’s ongoing criticism of the Lance Oppenheim-helmed film, which is now playing in theaters, Pattinson explained that he “was trying to make [Hansen] look cool” in the Ajon Singh-penned A24 movie, which was based on a 2007 Esquire article by Luke Dittrich.

“I mean, it’s weird. I was trying to make him cool. He is cool. I’m a fan,” Pattinson told ET. “I think in some ways, it’s an aesthetic thing; what I think is cool might not be cool to other people.”

While Hansen has accused the film of capitalizing on his name, Pattinson noted that he’s seen the film introducing the Dateline alum to a whole new generation of fans.

Watch on Deadline

“From the screeners we’ve gone to, I think it’s amazing when you see really, really young audiences and people turning up dressed as Chris Hansen,” he said. “Everybody’s doing Chris Hansen impressions, and they’re gonna be putting Chris Hansen posters on their walls.”

Robert Pattinson insists he's a fan of Chris Hansen and thinks it's awesome more people will get to discover him thanks to 'Primetime.' pic.twitter.com/NpWQKZuAnz — Entertainment Tonight (@etnow) October 11, 2026

Pattinson continued, “I think it’s kind of awesome, and it’s at the same age that I discovered him. And then [they] go back, and look at his work, and rediscover or discover all the important work he’s doing as well.”

Before giving his official review of Primetime, Hansen has gone on a public rollercoaster of reactions to the project, including contemplating legal action and purchasing ad space before upcoming screenings of the movie to promote his true-crime streaming network TruBlu, where he continues his sting investigations.

Now in theaters, Primetime follows Chris Hansen (Pattinson) as he attempts to make television history with NBCs To Catch a Predator (2004-’07), a hidden camera show that set up stings for adult men seeking sex from minors online.

title: Noah Centineo Credits ‘Street Fighter’ Stunt Coordinator With Bringing Game’s “Specific Fighting Style” To Screen: “Insane Fights”
summary: To outlast the best and bring Street Fighter to the big screen, stunt coordinator John Valera paid close attention to the combat styles in the video game. Noah Centineo, who plays Ken Masters in the Paramount adaptation of the Capcom video game, which premieres Oct. 16 in Imax, credited Valera with capturing the “different fighting […]
content:
To outlast the best and bring Street Fighter to the big screen, stunt coordinator John Valera paid close attention to the combat styles in the video game.

Noah Centineo, who plays Ken Masters in the Paramount adaptation of the Capcom video game, which premieres Oct. 16 in Imax, credited Valera with capturing the “different fighting styles” of the game’s many characters.

“Every character comes from a different background, pretty much, right?” he explained to GamesRadar+. “So there’s like over almost 150 characters, all the different backgrounds, different fighting styles, and John Valera, our stunt coordinator, had to research for every character and every fight that they were in their specific fighting style.”

Centineo added, “Yes, the signature moves in the game [are in the movie], so that he could make them fight against each other in their signature styles, in their specific fighting styles. Meticulous attention was paid to detail, and I think it’s really a triumph. The movie has insane fights, and every character is brutal.”

Watch on Deadline

Co-written and directed by Kitao Sakurai, Street Fighter also stars Callina Liang as Chun-Li, Joe “Roman Reigns” Anoa’i as Akuma, David Dastmalchian as M. Bison, Cody Rhodes as Guile, Andrew Schulz as Dan Hibiki, Eric André as Don Sauvage, Vidyut Jammwal as Dhalsim, Curtis “50 Cent” Jackson as Balrog, Jason Momoa as Blanka, Don Lee as Gouken, Orville Peck as Vega and more.

Based on the video game series that launched in 1987, the latest Street Fighter adaptation comes after Jean-Claude Van Damme led the 1994 live-action movie, followed by 2009’s Street Fighter: The Legend of Chun-Li, starring Kristin Kreuk.

title: ‘The Rookie’ Season 9 & Spinoff ‘North’ Get Premiere Dates, Teaser & Guest Stars As ABC Sets ‘Rookie’ Block On Wednesday
summary: The Rookie is on the move… again. ABC’s hit crime procedural starring Nathan Fillion will premiere its ninth season on Jan. 6 in a new time period on a new night, Wednesday at 9 PM. It will serve as a lead-in to new spinoff The Rookie: North, headlined by Jay Ellis, which will debut on […]
content:
The Rookie is on the move… again. ABC‘s hit crime procedural starring Nathan Fillion will premiere its ninth season on Jan. 6 in a new time period on a new night, Wednesday at 9 PM. It will serve as a lead-in to new spinoff The Rookie: North, headlined by Jay Ellis, which will debut on the same date and air Wednesdays at 10 PM.

The news was revealed in a sizzle reel played at New York Comic-Con Sunday which provided a first glimpse at the shows’ new seasons, including John Nolan (Fillion) & Co.’s mission to rescue LAPD squad members Tim (Eric Winter) an Lucy (Melissa O’Neil) who were kidnapped in the Season 8 finale cliffhanger.

During the Rookie universe NYCC panel, Alexi Hawley, creator, executive producer and showrunner of both series, announced that Troian Bellisario, Dulé Hill and Molly Kunz will guest star in The Rookie Season 9 as a new rookie, Watch Commander and EMT, respectively, and confirmed that Andy Allo will guest star in the premiere season of The Rookie: North.

Watch on Deadline

This marks the eighth time period change for stalwart The Rookie which started its eight season in the Tuesday 10 PM slot before being relocated to Mondays at 10 PM to make room for ABC’s latest light character-based procedural R.J. Decker. (As revealed at Comic-Con, the Season 9 premiere will be a two-parter. )

The Rookie and The Rookie: North will now run in a block on Wednesday, presumably following ABC’s comedy block of Abbott Elementary and Shifting Gears. ABC is yet to announce its midseason schedule but Wednesday 8-9 PM has been traditionally its comedy block, with Abbott Elementary as the anchor with a 22-episode full-length season while Scrubs and Shifting Gears both have limited-run orders, one for the fall, one for midseason.

ABC was expected to pair The Rookie and The Rookie: North together, a practice regularly employed by networks in expanding franchises that helps to launch new offshoots and allows for seamless crossovers. That is in the cards here. We already knew that Fillion is making an appearance in The Rookie: North pilot, and Hawley told Deadline in May that he was envisioning 2-3 crossover episodes a season. He revealed on the NYCC panel that Winter and O’Neil also will be in the spinoff, which is set in the Pacific Northwest.

Patrick J. Adams/The Riker Brothers/Storm Santos

Bellisario will recur on The Rookie as Stephanie Monroe, a thirty-something, single-mother looking to reinvent her life by becoming a police officer. She will be on the opposite side than her character on Amazon’s On Call, who was a training officer with her own rookie. Bellisario, who directed an episode of The Rookie last season, will be partnered with Nolan, and Fillion called her his most favorite rookie to train so far.

Psych alum Hill will guest star as Lt. Hughes, a distracted, thirty-year veteran of the job trying to navigate his new job as Watch Commander while his personal life is in growing turmoil. Hughes will likely be filling in while Watch Commander Tim Bradford is abducted.

Kunzwill guest star as Quinn, a small town girl determined to become an EMT in Los Angeles.

As Deadline reported, Allo will recur on The Rookie: North as Brooke, a warm, smart, attractive, and effortlessly charming first-year ER resident who quickly forms a connection with a rookie police officer (Ellis).

The teaser, which you can watch below, shows Tim and Lucy in captivity, with Tim being tortured, and the dangerous rescue operation.

“We’re risking everything we love to save them,” Nolan says.

The teaser also introduces Ellis’ Alex Holland, who is encountering some of the same problems Nolan did while embarking on a new career as a cop midlife but in a leafier, more rural environment — and the same conviction.

“It’s what I’ve been missing all these years, doing something that matters,” Alex says at the end.

Both The Rookie, which is set and films in Los Angeles, an The Rookie: North, set in the Pacific Northwest and shooting in Vancouver, air on ABC and stream next day on Hulu. They are produced by Lionsgate Television in partnership with 20th Television.

title: ‘The Riverbank,’ ‘Elza’ Top Rio Film Festival Awards as ‘On Behalf of My Son,’ ‘The French Teacher’ and ‘London’ Scoop Key Prizes
summary: Enock Carvalho and Matheus Farias’ Locarno-winning “The Riverbank” has taken Best Fiction Feature Film at this year’s Rio Film Festival, with Eryk Rocha’s “Elza” scoring Best Documentary Feature Film. The awards were handed out tonight at an imposing ceremony at Rio de Janeiro’s legendary Odeon cinema. “The Riverbank” is set in Recife and follows young […]
content:
Enock Carvalho and Matheus Farias’ Locarno-winning “The Riverbank” has taken Best Fiction Feature Film at this year’s Rio Film Festival, with Eryk Rocha’s “Elza” scoring Best Documentary Feature Film. The awards were handed out tonight at an imposing ceremony at Rio de Janeiro’s legendary Odeon cinema.

“The Riverbank” is set in Recife and follows young cleaner Izaquiel (Caique Copque), whose nightly search for intimacy leads him to magnetic fisherman Jeremias (Ítalo Martins). As violence closes in, both embark on a journey into the depths of the mangroves, where reality and myth intertwine, exposing the invisible structures of power that govern their world. This is the duo’s directorial feature debut, and it comes a few months after Farias won a Platino Award for his editing of Kleber Mendonça Filho’s Oscar-nominated “The Secret Agent.”

“Elza” marks the follow-up to Rocha’s “The Falling Sky,” which premiered to great acclaim at Directors’ Fortnight. The film is a comprehensive documentary about one of Brazil’s most renowned singers and public figures, Elza Soares. Drawing on rare archival materials and intimate conversations between Soares and the director during the final years of her life, “Elza” traces the icon’s seven-decade career while revealing the many facets of the woman behind the legend. The project comes with the backing of high-calibre partners, including Aruac Filmes (“Cinema Novo”), Maria Farinha Filmes (“The Beginning of Life”), Globo Filmes (“I’m Still Here”), RAI Cinema and Gullane+.

Popular on Variety

Other major Brazilian films of the year have also taken top awards, including Gabriel Martins’s Toronto-selected “On Behalf of My Son,” Venice-selected “London” by Victor di Marco and Márcio Picoli, and Ricardo Alves Jr.’s “The French Teacher,” which just bowed at San Sebastián.

This year’s Premiére Brasil jury was presided over by veteran “La Bola Negra” producer Esther García and also included co-director of programming at the Berlinale, Jacqueline Lyanga; French producer Sophie Erbs; composer Flavia Tygel; and casting director Marcela Altberg.

The New Trends jury was presided over by director and editor Karen Harley; screenwriter Maira Oliveira; producer Dora Amorim; director and screenwriter Guto Parente. The Felix Jury, dedicated to films broaching LGBTQIA+ issues, was presided over by lawyer Ericka Gavinho; director and screenwriter Clara Anastacia; cultural critic Guilherme Terri, also known as Rita Von Hunty; filmmaker Vita; and cultural programmer Rodrigo Gerace.
