content:
14th is coming out of the gate strong.

Ava DuVernay’s documentary examining threats to the 14th Amendment, which held its world premiere Friday at the New York Film Festival, earned a leading six nominations Tuesday as the 11th annual Critics Choice Documentary Awards announced its nominees.

Close behind with five nominations each: You Can See Everything, the documentary about Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim; Once Upon a Time in Harlem, directed by David Greaves and produced by Liani Greaves; and Nuisance Bear, directed by Gabriela Osio Vanden and Jack Weisman.

‘Everybody to Kenmure Street’ Icarus Films

Several films landed four nominations each including Everybody to Kenmure Street, directed by Felipe Bustos Sierra; Rehearsals for a Revolution, directed by Pegah Ahangarani; Remake, directed by Ross McElwee; The History of Concrete, directed by John Wilson; and Everest: The Other Side, directed by Oscar winners E. Chai Vasarhelyi and Jimmy Chin.

Watch on Deadline

Scroll for the full list of nominees.

L-R: Ava DuVernay with Dr. Carla Hayden, the librarian of Congress ousted by President Trump Netflix

14th’s nominations come in the categories of Best Documentary Feature, Best Political Documentary and Best Historical Documentary, as well as DuVernay for Best Director, Spencer Averick for Best Editing, and Jason Moran for Best Music Score.

Winners will be revealed at a gala event November 8 at The Edison Ballroom in Manhattan, with Ross Mathews serving as emcee.

“This year’s nominees reflect the range of voices, perspectives, and stories that make documentary filmmaking so compelling,” said Christopher Campbell, Critics Choice Association’s VP, Documentary. “These films challenge us to see the world in new ways and reinforce the vital role documentaries play in informing, engaging, and inspiring audiences. We are proud to recognize the exceptional talent and creativity behind this year’s nominated films.”

Critics Choice Documentary Awards

As previously announced, Ron Howard will receive the Critics Choice Impact Award, an honor recognizing “filmmakers whose work, influence, and commitment to nonfiction storytelling have made a significant and lasting impact on the documentary form, broadening its reach and championing its continued evolution.” Howard’s documentaries include Avedon (2026), Jim Henson Idea Man (2024), We Feed People (2022), Rebuilding Paradise (2020) and Pavarotti (2019).

Oscar-nominated filmmaker Jehane Noujaim, as previously announced, will receive the CCA’s Pennebaker Award, an honor that will be presented by DA Pennebaker’s widow and collaborator Chris Hegedus. “Named in tribute to trailblazing documentarian DA Pennebaker, the award (formerly the Critics Choice Lifetime Achievement Award) celebrates filmmakers whose careers have made a profound and lasting contribution to the art of documentary storytelling.”

Feature-length documentaries, two-part documentaries and short-form documentaries are eligible for nomination if first released commercially in the U.S. between January 1-December 31, 2026. Documentaries may be delivered to audiences theatrically or by broadcast, cable, or streaming. Documentary series of three episodes or more are eligible for nomination if a majority of the episodes of the series’ eligible season have been released between January 1-December 31, 2026.

title: Ryan Coogler’s ‘The X-Files’ Reboot Picked Up To Series At Hulu
summary: Ryan Coogler’s long-gestating The X-Files reboot, starring Emmy nominee Himesh Patel (The Odyssey, Station Eleven) and Danielle Deadwyler (The Bell Jar, The Chaperones), has been ordered to series at Hulu. From Onyx Collective and 20th Television, the reimagining of Chris Carter’s classic series follows two highly decorated but vastly different FBI agents, played by Deadwyler […]
content:
Ryan Coogler‘s long-gestating The X-Files reboot, starring Emmy nominee Himesh Patel (The Odyssey, Station Eleven) and Danielle Deadwyler (The Bell Jar, The Chaperones), has been ordered to series at Hulu.

From Onyx Collective and 20th Television, the reimagining of Chris Carter‘s classic series follows two highly decorated but vastly different FBI agents, played by Deadwyler and Patel, who form an unlikely bond when they are assigned to a long-shuttered division devoted to cases involving unexplained phenomena.

Sinners filmmaker Coogler wrote, directed and executive produced the pilot via his Proximity Media. He executive produces with showrunner Jennifer Yale. Executive producers also include Zinzi Coogler and Sev Ohanian for Proximity Media and The X-Files creator Carter. Co-executive producers are Simone Harris for Proximity Media, along with Deadwyler and Patel.

“I’ve loved The X-Files for a long time, so getting the chance to write and direct the pilot has meant a great deal to me,” said Coogler. “What Chris Carter created is special, and we wanted to honor everything that made the original series connect with so many people while also finding our own way into that world. Danielle and Himesh, along with the rest of our cast, have brought such original perspectives and performances to these characters, and watching that come together has been one of the most rewarding parts of the experience. I couldn’t have asked for better collaborators than my crew, colleagues at Proximity Media and our partners at Onyx Collective and 20th Television. I’m grateful for the trust and support they’ve given us as we take on this new chapter.”

Watch on Deadline

The series order caps a more than three-year journey for the project, which falls under Coogler’s five-year exclusive television deal with Disney, the parent company of Hulu, 20th TV and Onyx.

Carter first revealed during a 2023 podcast interview that he had spoken with Coogler who was “going to remount The X Files with a diverse cast,” adding, “He’s got his work cut out for him because we covered so much territory.”

“We’re looking forward to continuing this journey as executive producers and especially excited to work closely with Jennifer Yale, Simone Harris, and the entire cast and crew as we bring this new chapter of The X-Files to life,” said Zinzi Coogler, Sev Ohanian and Ryan Coogler, founders of Proximity Media. “It was also incredibly special to have our fellow Proximity co-founder Ludwig Göransson contribute the score for the pilot, making this a true collaboration across the Proximity family.”

Carter’s original X-Files starred Gillian Anderson and David Duchovny as FBI Special Agents Dana Scully and Fox Mulder, who investigate cases involving paranormal phenomena. The series premiered on Fox in 1993 and ran for nine seasons. It spawned two feature films, The X-Files (1998) and The X-Files: I Want to Believe (2008), as well as a 2016 revival, which aired on Fox for two seasons.

title: Stephen Amell Says Putting on the ‘Baywatch’ Red Trunks Felt ‘So Familiar’ Because ‘It’s a Superhero Show’
summary: Stephen Amell, star of the upcoming “Baywatch” reboot, first came to public attention as Oliver Queen in DC superhero series “Arrow.” But the actor says his new role isn’t so different. “Once I got on it and I put on the red trunks, I realized, like, why does this feel so familiar?” Amell said of […]
content:
Stephen Amell, star of the upcoming “Baywatch” reboot, first came to public attention as Oliver Queen in DC superhero series “Arrow.” But the actor says his new role isn’t so different.

“Once I got on it and I put on the red trunks, I realized, like, why does this feel so familiar?” Amell said of working on “Baywatch.” “It’s because it’s a superhero show. That’s what it feels like to me, and that makes my job easy.”

While spending the working day on the beach might seem like a dream job, Amell went on to explain the reality was somewhat different. “I thought that when I was doing ‘Arrow,’ that shooting from 7 o’clock at night until 7 o’clock in the morning on a rooftop or in a damp building somewhere in Vancouver was going to be the toughest thing that I ever did,” the actor revealed during a panel at Mipcom in Cannes, France. “But man, sunrise to sunset on the beach in Venice, you go through all of the emotions. At some point you’re hot. At some point you’re cold. At some point you’re probably itchy. It was a lot.”

Popular on Variety

Stephen Amell and Brooks Nader attend the “Baywatch” photocall during MIPCOM 2026 at the Palais des Festivals (courtesy of Mipcom) Frederic DIDES/360 medias

He added: “But man, getting to shoot, especially on Venice Beach — my family and I rented a house there – like, this is the California dream and adventure. It was so special.”

“Baywatch” first launched in 1989. The show, which is owned by Fremantle, ran for 11 seasons and at its peak was one of the world’s most-watched show with over a billion viewers every week across 200 countries, turning its cast – including David Hasselhoff and Pamela Anderson – into superstars.

The 12-episode reboot, which is produced by Fremantle and Fox Entertainment, sees a new cast of lifeguards don the red bathing suits including Amell, Brooks Nader and Shay Mitchell. Some original cast members are also set to make an appearance, with David Chokachi reprising the role of Cody Madison while Erika Eleniak, Michael Bergin and Kelly Packard return as guest stars.

Fox president Michael Thorne, who joined Amell on the Mipcom panel alongside Nader and Fremantle CEO Jens Richter, said it was important to the team to “embrace what made the show so special: heroism, escapism, a beautiful, intelligent, heroic, flawed cast of characters” while at the same time updating the series for a modern audience.

“The original rescues are so funny,” he acknowledged. “Pamela Anderson would walk up to the edge of the beach, she wouldn’t even put her feet in the water — her hair was perfect, her makeup was on — and she’d reach out very gently and be like, ‘Okay, I saved you!’ And that just doesn’t do it [for viewers today].”

“So we tried to capture the heart and the humanity, the juicy soap, and I think where we really elevated it is in the rescues and what it means to be a lifeguard today.”

“Baywatch” bows in Jan. 2027 on Fox. Fox Entertainment Global holds domestic distribution rights while Fremantle is repping global sales.

title: Drake Bell Blasts SAG-AFTRA After Losing Health Insurance: ‘Do Not Become an Actor. Do Not Join SAG’
summary: “Drake & Josh” actor Drake Bell is putting SAG-AFTRA on blast after he revealed he does not qualify for health insurance. On his Instagram Story on Tuesday, Bell posted a screenshot of the SAG-AFTRA health plan website that says “you do not qualify for Health Plan coverage at this time. Your reported covered earnings from […]
content:
“Drake & Josh” actor Drake Bell is putting SAG-AFTRA on blast after he revealed he does not qualify for health insurance.

On his Instagram Story on Tuesday, Bell posted a screenshot of the SAG-AFTRA health plan website that says “you do not qualify for Health Plan coverage at this time. Your reported covered earnings from July 2025-June 2026 did not meet minimum eligibility requirements, or you did not qualify other eligibility rules.”

The webpage says that Bell has earned $17,480.53 and that he needs $11,452.47 more to qualify by reaching the $28,933 required for the SAG-AFTRA Health Plan.

Popular on Variety

“Do not become an actor. Do not join SAG. You can work for 35 years and they still say [middle finger emoji],” Bell wrote on the screenshot. He then tagged SAG-AFTRA and its president, “Lord of the Rings” and “The Goonies” actor Sean Astin, in his scathing message.

“@SAGAFTRA really though @SeanAstin you’re doing a bang up job. How about stop using actors to run things maybe? They literally just know how to say words in front of a camera.”

Bell has recently turned to music and voice work after his acting career slowed down following Nickelodeon’s “Drake & Josh” series in the 2000s. In 2024, he came forward on the docuseries “Quiet on Set: The Dark Side of Kids TV” and revealed that he’d been sexually abused as a teen by dialogue coach Brian Peck.

Bell is the latest celebrity to speak out about troubles obtaining SAG-AFTRA health insurance. “Atypical” actor Jack Haven and “Princess Diaries” star Heather Matarazzo both revealed last month that they wouldn’t qualify for health insurance if they didn’t get more work soon.

“I’m in a bit of an emergency situation,” Haven said in a YouTube video at the time. “I need to make $4,000 by the end of the month in order to qualify for SAG health insurance starting in January.” Haven later obtained enough work after reaching out publicly, and Matarazzo shared that she faced a similar situation.

“I am literally in the same boat right now. Lots of my fellow actors are,” she wrote. “I remember a time when we didn’t have to earn a minimum to qualify for insurance. Glad to see that Jack has gotten an offer that will let them to qualify for 2027.”

Variety has reached out to representatives for SAG-AFTRA and Bell for further comment.

title: Black Bear Acquires Love Triangle Comedy Spec From Writing Duo Cassidy Alla and Read Masino (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Black Bear has acquired the rights to a comedy spec script from up-and-coming writing duo Cassiy Alla and Read Masino, Variety can reveal exclusively According to an official logline, the untitled film “tells the story of when a mother and daughter inadvertently start dating the same man; the whole family – each at their own […]
content:
Black Bear has acquired the rights to a comedy spec script from up-and-coming writing duo Cassiy Alla and Read Masino, Variety can reveal exclusively

According to an official logline, the untitled film “tells the story of when a mother and daughter inadvertently start dating the same man; the whole family – each at their own crossroad in life and love – must deal with the chaotic fallout.”

Alla and Masino, both working toward their feature breakouts, have a movie in development at Netflix with Berlanti/Schechter producing and Nahnatchka Khan (“Totally Killer”) directing. The duo met while working as assistants at Apatow Productions. Masino worked as a writers’ assistant on Amazon’s “Spider-Noir” and Apple’s “Brothers” and “The Muppet Show,” while Alla worked for showrunner Justin Noble, co-creator of “The Sex Lives of College Girls.”

Popular on Variety

“This script is one of the funniest and most poignant scripts we have seen in years about romance, family and the dysfunction so often associated with both,” said Michael Heimler, Partner, President of Production & Operations at Black Bear. “Cassidy and Read are two of the most exciting voices we’ve read in some time, and we can’t wait to bring this story to life.”

Alla and Masino added in a joint statement, “We had so much fun writing this chaotic comedy about a family (not to be confused with a family comedy) and couldn’t ask for a better partner on this project than Black Bear.”

Black Bear, which launched its distribution arm in 2025, is the studio behind recent films like “Train Dreams,” “Sing Sing” and “The Imitation Game.” The upcoming Black Bear slate includes “Honeymoon / Funeral,” starring Rebecca Ferguson, Greta Lee and Carrie Coon; “Wicker,” starring Olivia Colman, Alexander Skarsgård and Peter Dinklage; and Guy Ritchie’s “Wife and Dog” with Benedict Cumberbatch and Rosamund Pike.

Alla is represented by UTA and Mosaic. Masino is represented by UTA and Artists First.

title: Druski Hosting ‘SNL’ Is the Show’s Most Interesting Move in Years
summary: As “Saturday Night Live” trudges on this season with a little-known cast, uneven sketches and yet another horrendous appearance by obvious misogynist Shane Gillis, news that comedian and internet personality Druski, aka Drew Desbordes, will host the Nov. 7 episode suddenly gives me hope. I think it’s the most interesting thing “SNL” has done in […]
content:
As “Saturday Night Live” trudges on this season with a little-known cast, uneven sketches and yet another horrendous appearance by obvious misogynist Shane Gillis, news that comedian and internet personality Druski, aka Drew Desbordes, will host the Nov. 7 episode suddenly gives me hope. I think it’s the most interesting thing “SNL” has done in years.

Admittedly, I’m not the biggest “Saturday Night Live” fan. I’ve tuned in rarely over the years, usually only when an actor or artist I find fascinating hosts. In the last decade, it’s been rare: Eddie Murphy hosting in 2019, Megan Thee Stallion appearing in the iconic “Girl Talk” sketch with Ego Nwodim and Dave Chappelle’s 2025 appearance, where he paid homage to his beloved sketch comedy series “Chapelle’s Show.” But I’ve mostly had very little interest in tuning in over the years.

The idea of bringing Druski to Studio 8H at least feels like a cutting-edge thing that the “SNL” of old might have done. The 32-year-old comedian is the first content creator to ever host the show, which has sparked a lot of kerfuffle (some rightfully so) about influencers stepping into spaces previously reserved for “true celebrities.” But I would argue that Druski has never been an influencer. He has always been a comedian first, an artist who honed his craft by posting short skits on his Instagram page and eventually building an organic audience of 35+ million followers and billions of views across Instagram, TikTok and YouTube.

Popular on Variety

Until more recently, mainstream studios and streamers have ignored Druski in favor of blondes who’ve never read a book. However, Druski has been a name in the Black community for nearly a decade. Just a few years into posting, the Maryland-born comedian appeared in music videos for major hip-hop artists like Drake and Lil Yachty. Instead of using a musician as the opening act for their 2021 tour, rappers J. Cole and 21 Savage had Druski open for them. In addition to his comedy work, Druski created “Coulda Been Records,” which allowed artists to join his Instagram Live posts and collaborate. He had a starring role in Peacock’s 2023 film “Praise This” opposite Chloe Bailey, and in 2025 launched the 10-city arena tour Coulda Fest, which sold out immediately.

However, it’s Druski’s ability to put his finger on the pulse of societal touchstones with elaborate, hilarious and self-funded skits that makes him almost a singular entity in the comedy space today. While older comedians regurgitate tired material or appear in the prequels and sequels of the latest recycled IP, Druski calls out the hypocrisy of megachurches and takes Erika Kirk to task while indicting white supremacy and American conservatism. On a more granular level, his work has commented on the horrors of 21st-century dating, “hat fishing” (when men hide their balding hairlines under fitted caps), and the terror that we all feel at airports when encountering aggressive and impatient TSA agents. Druski’s comedy embodies what it means to be a young American at this particular moment.

Though his perspective is often from a Black lens, American culture overall is typically siphoned from Black culture before moving into the mainstream. Because Black people have been so subjugated in this country via slavery, Jim Crow, racism and now the Trump administration, knowing how to weave in and out of white spaces is essential to Black survival. However, that revolving door does not work the other way. As a result, the mainstream often has blind spots or is years late in “discovering” Black talent.

It’s the same reason why so many people publicly admonished Will Smith’s actions at the 2024 Oscars while Black people collectively still feel that Chris Rock deserved that slap. There’s a reason comparing Taylor Swift to Beyoncé never made sense, or why, when DEI is erased from boardrooms, marketing campaigns like Sydney Sweeney’s “Good Genes” are greenlit. Or, that somebody has the idea that Kendall Jenner is suddenly the person to solve racism with a Pepsi. It’s the same reason why movies, commercials and television have felt stale and uninspired for years. Innovation can only happen when new ideas and perspectives are taken into account.

For Black talent like Druski — and even Issa Rae before him — rejection means taking things into their own hands and building an audience organically. It’s only later that the mainstream wakes up and comes knocking after something has already been built. In fact, “SNL” is rather late in bringing Druski to its stage: In June, he hosted the 2026 BET Awards, becoming the youngest host in the show’s 25-year history. He’s also slated to star opposite Chris Pine and Emma Stone in the upcoming film “The Catch.”

Druski has worked for years to build his own platform and digital leverage, which extends well beyond the confining term of “influencer.” He has been a shining star in the Black community for years; everyone else — including “SNL” — is just now catching up.

title: Music Industry Moves: Jesse Jo Stark Signs With WME, Rebecca Allen Steps Down at Universal Music U.K.
summary: Singer-songwriter-actress and Chrome Hearts co-creative director Jesse Jo Stark has signed with WME for worldwide representation in all areas. Stark’s new album “Muse” is out Nov. 6, which follows dates opening for or performing with Post Malone, Guns N’ Roses and Jane’s Addiction, as well as multiple festival appearances. In addition to her work at […]
content:
Singer-songwriter-actress and Chrome Hearts co-creative director Jesse Jo Stark has signed with WME for worldwide representation in all areas.

Stark’s new album “Muse” is out Nov. 6, which follows dates opening for or performing with Post Malone, Guns N’ Roses and Jane’s Addiction, as well as multiple festival appearances. In addition to her work at Chrome Hearts, Stark also helms the clothing line Deadly Doll.

+ Veteran music executive Rebecca Allen is leaving Universal Music Group U.K. after 27 years, according to Music Week. She will continue in an advisory role at UMG.

Popular on Variety

Following the merger of EMI and Island in July 2024, Allen was appointed as president of the new Audience & Media division, and subsequently promoted to the newly-formed, “first-of-its-kind” leadership role of chief artist and strategy officer in December 2025. Previously, she was president and later co-president of the relaunched EMI (alongside Jo Charrington), following her role as president of Decca from 2017 to 2020 – becoming the first female president at a Universal Music U.K. label.

“I leave enormously proud of what we’ve created together, grateful for the friendships, the adventures, the lessons and the laughter, and for 27 years that have shaped me in more ways than I probably even realise yet,” Allen wrote in a farewell letter to staff, per MW. “It’s been quite a ride. I can’t thank you all enough for being on this journey with me. Love to you all.”

+ Sony Music Publishing Colombia has entered into a global catalog administration agreement with the Estate of acclaimed Colombian singer, songwriter and accordionist Omar Geles, one of the most influential artists to work in vallenato music. The agreement encompasses more than three-hundred celebrated works penned by the Latin-Grammy nominated songwriter including the vallenato anthem “Cuatro Rosas,” as well as classics such as “A Blanco y Negro,” “Tu Hombre Soy Yo” and “Tarde lo Conocí.”

“In the name of my family and the Omar Geles state, we want to extend our most sincere gratitude for opening your doors and allow us to be part of the Sony Music Publishing family,” said Maren García. “We hope to build a relationship based in trust, respect, and the commitment of continuing to take Omar Geles’ legacy to new generations. Thanks for making us feel at home since the first moment and for continuing to write the history of the legacy of my eternal love, a legacy that will continue to live in each one of his songs.”

Jorge Mejía, President and CEO, Latin America and U.S. Latin, Sony Music Publishing said, “Omar Geles was not only a defining voice in vallenato music, but one of the great songwriters of his generation. It is a true honor to partner with his family to preserve, promote and expand his legacy, ensuring that his songs continue to inspire audiences around the world for generations to come.”

+ The Music Publishers Association, the U.K. trade body representing music publishers, has named Faber Music CEO Richard King as its new Board Chair for a three-year term, following a vote by its Board of Directors. He succeeds Paulette Long OBE, who remains an MPA Board Director following the conclusion of her term as Chair.

Having served as CEO of leading independent music publisher Faber Music since 1999, King brings more than 25 years of publishing leadership to the role, with experience spanning classical, film and TV, pop and printed music. He previously served as an MPA Director from 2002 to 2019 before rejoining the Board in 2022. He was a PRS director for 18 years to 2022, a Director of PRS Foundation for 9 years to 2024 and has been a Director of PML since its inception in 2012. King will work alongside Peter Jackson, who joined the MPA as Managing Director in July.

“I’m looking forward to building on the great work of Paulette and the MPA executive team, particularly by using my experience as a music publisher to further amplify our sector’s voice on the issues that matter most to members,” King said. “There is plenty to build on. The Government’s recently announced Plan for Music and new National Plan for Music Education are welcome steps, but we need to ensure these initiatives lead to meaningful, sustained long-term change. At a time of enormous change, it is more important than ever that music publishers have a strong and unified voice.”

Paul Clements, CEO of the MPA Group, added, “Richard has been an important voice within the MPA for many years and I know he will bring fresh thinking, challenge and real ambition to the role of Chair. Peter has already made a huge impact since joining us, bringing new energy and ideas to the team and a clear vision for how we can do even more for our members.

“I’d also like to thank Paulette for her outstanding leadership and contribution as Chair. With Richard leading the Board and Peter driving the MPA forward day-to-day, we have a brilliant team in place for this next chapter.”

title: ‘A Few Good Men’, ‘Other Desert Cities’ Sell Out; ‘Hamilton’ Grosses Huge $3M – Broadway Box Office
summary: A Few Good Men and Other Desert Cities, starry new revivals on the Broadway stage, sold out their performances last week, with the latter production (starring Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Ed Harris, Allison Janney, Joe Keery and Lily Rabe) hitting the upper reaches of the box office chart with a gross in excess of $2 million. content:
A Few Good Men and Other Desert Cities, starry new revivals on the Broadway stage, sold out their performances last week, with the latter production (starring Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Ed Harris, Allison Janney, Joe Keery and Lily Rabe) hitting the upper reaches of the box office chart with a gross in excess of $2 million.

As impressive as that number is, it still falls well short of the week’s top earner: The ever-popular Hamilton, newly recharged with the return of original cast member Christopher Jackson to the cast, grossed an amazing $3,090,634.

All three shows, along with Billy Crystal’s new 860, Oh, Mary! (now starring Bowen Yang) and Chicago (with Reece Weaver), helped push the total receipts for the 29 Broadway productions for the week ending October 11 to $35,292,434, a whopping increase of 27% over the previous week.

Watch on Deadline

Total attendance for the week was 248,496, about 10% more than the previous week.

A new infusion of star power contributed to the strong figures. A Few Good Men, the non-prof Lincoln Center Theater revival of Aaron Sorkin’s classic military courtroom drama, stars Sorkin’s old West Wing buddy Bradley Whitford (along with Tom Blyth and Krysta Rodriguez) and sold out its first three previews for a gross of $555,367. Official opening night is set for Thursday, October 29.

Other Desert Cities, the Jon Robin Baitz play directed by John Benjamin Hickey, grossed $2,157,355, selling out eight previews at the Hudson. Opening night is October 18.

Crystal’s solo show 860 – the title refers to the address of the comedian’s longtime home that burned down in the Pacific Palisades fires – filled 92% of its seats at the Imperial, a noticeable improvement over the previous week’s 83%. The gross for the seven previews was $1,173,760. Opening night is October 21.

Another recent arrival doing well is non-prof Roundabout’s The Imaginary Invalid starring Bill Irwin, filling 90% of seats at the Haimes and grossing $429,863. Opening night is October 22.

Some other notable numbers:

Cole Escola’s Oh, Mary! broke yet another house record at the Lyceum, with Bowen Yang in the title role drawing big crowds. For the week ending October 11, the comedy grossed $1,592,306 , a record both for the Lyceum and for the production. (Oh, Mary! opened on July 11, 2024, and became the first show in Lyceum history to gross more than $1 million in a single week; the comedy has broken its own record 15 times);
