Asian Project Market 2026 winners:

APM Busan Award: A Chronicle Of Minor Things (India), dir. Tribeny Rai

CJ ENM Award: Casparina (Indonesia), dir: Reza Rahadian

VIPO Award: Goldfish (Indonesia), dir: Aditya Ahmad

ArteKino International Award: Once Upon A Time In The Philippines (Philippines, France Norway), dir: E Del Mundo

Songwon Award: Satellite Of Love (South Korea, Germany), dir: Park Syeyoung

CathayPlay Award: Uncle (Taiwan), dir: Yen Hao-hsuan

Kantana Award (Virtual Production): Fatimah (Thailand), dir: Panu Aree

Kantana Award (Picture): Red Hunger (South Korea), dir: Kim Jinyeong

Kongchak Studio Award: Goldfish (Indonesia), dir: Aditya Ahmad

Sorfond Award: A Chronicle Of Minor Things (India), dir: Tribeny Rai

QCinema Special Award: Goldfish (Indonesia), dir: Aditya Ahmad

title: Judge Rules Trump Administration Can’t Resume Ban On CNN, MS NOW & Politico From White House Grounds
summary: UPDATED, with additional comment: A federal judge prohibited the Trump administration from banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House grounds, granting the three outlets a preliminary injunction that ensures access for the foreseeable future. U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly, a Trump appointee, wrote in his opinion that the news outlets “are likely […]
content:
UPDATED, with additional comment: A federal judge prohibited the Trump administration from banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House grounds, granting the three outlets a preliminary injunction that ensures access for the foreseeable future.

U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly, a Trump appointee, wrote in his opinion that the news outlets “are likely to succeed not only on their due process claim, but also on their two First Amendment claims.”

Kelly did caution that “no one should interpret the court’s decision to suggest that President Trump’s concerns about accuracy and fairness in the media’s reporting are unfounded, or that the government is powerless when its true aim is to protect national security when classified information is unlawfully disclosed.” But when it came to the blanket ban on the three outlets, the judge was unpersuaded by the government’s justifications.

Trump announced on Sept. 18 that he was barring CNN, MS NOW and Politico from access to White House grounds, complaining that they were “‘reporting’ fake news.”. A day later, their reporters who tried to enter the security checkpoint found their hard passes deactivated.

Watch on Deadline

The news outlets sued, and Kelly issued a temporary restraining order halting Trump’s restriction on the outlets, something that forced the White House to restore the hard passes to dozens of reporters and other staffers. That TRO expired on Tuesday; the preliminary injunction means that the White House cannot enforce Trump’s ban in the long term, either until a trial or an appeal. The news outlets warned that the White House was likely to reimpose the ban absent further court intervention.

In defending the ban, the government cited national security reasons, although DOJ attorneys also argued that the news organizations did not meet “minimum requirements of professionalism.” While the DOJ pointed to stories published or aired that had to do with national security, they also cited as an example an MS NOW report that Trump aides considered an option of adding the president’s name to Ford’s Theatre. Trump later denied it.

In his 26-page opinion, Kelly cited D.C. Circuit precedents in that reporters had a right to due process before their hard pass is revoked.

“To put it mildly, [the news outlets] likely did not receive notice either of the conduct that would subject them to revocation of their hard passes, or of the magnitude of the revocation sanction itself,” the judge wrote.

The judge noted that some of the stories flagged by the White House were published earlier this year and written by reporters who later had their hard passes renewed. Then came Trump’s ban, and they were revoked. They included a CNN report from January 2026 on the top secret bunker being built beneath the East Wing, and an MS NOW story that quoted an anonymous White House official who said the president underestimated Iran’s willingness to resume the war.

The White House press office sent letters to the news organizations on September 22, informing them of the reasons and their ability to contest the action, but that was four days after the ban was implemented.

The judge also sided with the news outlets’ in their claims that Trump was engaging in retaliation and viewpoint discrimination in violation of the First Amendment.

“President Trump’s own comments suggest that he intended the revocation of Plaintiffs’ hard passes to alter their reporting on him, bolstering the case that his action here is sufficient to deter a reporter of ordinary firmness from reporting in the same way she had before. After explaining that he excluded Plaintiffs from the White House because they ‘purposely write negative news . . . to try and diminish the Republicans and a Republican administration,’ President Trump remarked that he is prepared to take ‘the ban . . . as far as you can,’ but that he would “love it” if they “could straighten themselves out.”

The judge added, “The record is clear that President Trump made the decision at issue. And his announcement of the ban and later remarks explaining the reason for it make this a straightforward conclusion: President Trump likely banned Plaintiffs from the White House because he believes that their reporting is generally inaccurate and biased against him.”

He also dismissed the government’s national security argument. He noted that there was “no evidence in the record” that he made the decision to revoke the passes for those reasons “from the get go, nor at any time has he directly stated that national security was the reason for his decision.”

The judge explained that because the D.C. Circuit has held that the White House press area is a “non public forum,” the government cannot limit access based on someone’s viewpoint.

The judge wrote that “it is likely that Plaintiffs were selected by President Trump for revocation of their access to the White House press area because he believes their coverage of him and his administration is generally inaccurate and biased—in other words, it was ‘an effort to suppress the speaker’s activity due to disagreement with the speaker’s view.'”

The judge also ruled that the news outlets should put up a nominal bond of $1.00 as the case moves forward.

Theodore Boutrous Jr., the lead attorney representing the news outlets, said in a statement, “When the president issued his ‘ban on the free press,’ he blatantly and explicitly violated due process and the First Amendment. Since then, the President has repeatedly, candidly, and consistently admitted in public that he banned our clients from the White House to punish reporting he doesn’t like and to try to force journalists to cover him in ways he prefers.”

Boutrous added, “The harm this ban did to our clients, the First Amendment, and the public as a whole is profound. The court was right to enjoin the White House from enforcing this ‘unconstitutional ban on the free press’ for the foreseeable future.”

The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

title: James McAvoy Recalls Being Bullied On The Set Of HBO’s ‘Band Of Brothers’
summary: James McAvoy recalls his first day on the set of Band of Brothers and says a co-star bullied him. During a visit to Bravo’s Watch What Happens Live while playing “Spill the IMDb-tea,” McAvoy made the revelation while keeping mum about the names. After being shown a photo of the HBO series, McAvoy took a closer look […]
content:
James McAvoy recalls his first day on the set of Band of Brothers and says a co-star bullied him.

During a visit to Bravo‘s Watch What Happens Live while playing “Spill the IMDb-tea,” McAvoy made the revelation while keeping mum about the names.

After being shown a photo of the HBO series, McAvoy took a closer look at the image and said, “Hold on, let me just see, is he in there? No, I don’t think he is in there. Ah, yeah, he is.”

“All right, so, I’m not going to tell you who it was,” he added. “[But] … one of the guys in that picture decided to bully me, on my first day as a professional actor out of acting school! So he got him and his buddies to just stand and point at me and laugh at me, for like three minutes.”

McAvoy explained that the scene he was shooting involved “a ton of actors,” adding, “It was one of those scenes with everybody in it, and we’re in a bar. And I had a scene, and all these guys were, like, in it for nine, 10 months, and you get one line in one episode and one line 10 episodes later. They were all pissed. And I come in for one episode, and I’ve got an arc and scenes. I’ve got tons of lines.”

Watch on Deadline

The actor noted that his co-stars Dexter Fletcher and Robin Laing reached out to him and told him, “Come hang with us, man.”

McAvoy rated his experience on the Band of Brothers set saying that “a part from that day it was a nine, but that day it felt like a two [out of 10].”

Bravo host Andy Cohen said he would get the tea from McAvoy during the commercial break but the actor said that he would not confirm who it was. However, McAvoy noted it wasn’t David Schwimmer, since he wasn’t in the photo they put on screen.

The photo in question featured Donnie Wahlberg as Carwood Lipton, Kirk Acevedo as Joe Toye, Scott Grimes as Donald Malarkey, Philip Barantini as Wayne A. “Skinny” Sisk, Neal McDonough as Lynn “Buck” Compton, Adam James as Cleveland O. Petty, Frank John Hughes as William “Wild Bill” Guarnere, and Ross McCall as Joseph Liebgott.

Band of Brothers was a 2001 drama series created by Tom Hanks and Steven Spielberg and based on the Stephen E. Ambrose’s non-fiction book of the same name.

Watch McAvoy’s interview in the video below.

title: ‘Dancing With The Stars’ Recap: Super Bowl Night Sends Home A Fan Favorite
summary: SPOILER ALERT! This post contains details from Tuesday’s episode of Dancing with the Stars. Another week, another night of Dancing with the Stars. It’s the first-ever Super Bowl night in the ballroom, so the remaining couples are dancing to songs from former Super Bowl halftime performers, including Shakira, Lady Gaga, Jennifer Lopez, Bad Bunny, and […]
content:
SPOILER ALERT! This post contains details from Tuesday’s episode of Dancing with the Stars.

Another week, another night of Dancing with the Stars.

It’s the first-ever Super Bowl night in the ballroom, so the remaining couples are dancing to songs from former Super Bowl halftime performers, including Shakira, Lady Gaga, Jennifer Lopez, Bad Bunny, and more. As we know, Disney loves synergy, and this is no exception since ABC and ESPN are hosting the big game this season.

The judges are joined tonight by Joe Buck, the lead play-by-play announcer for ESPN’s Monday Night Football. Don’t expect any sophisticated remarks from him, considering he tells the audience early on he has no idea about the technical aspects of any of the dances, but he’s excited to weigh in.

Let’s dive into Super Bowl Night.

Watch on Deadline

Reality star Maura Higgins with Mark Ballas. These two are still on cloud 9, literally, after getting the first 9 of the season last week from Carrie Ann. This week, they’re dancing a tango to “Only Girl (In the World)” by Rihanna. In her intro package before the performance, she seems to be struggling with pain in her neck, so staying in frame might be tough. She definitely comes across a little stiff, but otherwise powers through. “Maura, once again a beautiful performance,” Carrie Ann tells her but reminds her that her movement needs to be more “punctuated” on the Latin dances. SCORE: 33 out of 40

Savannah Bananas midfielder Jackson Olson with Emma Slater. The pair have been in the bottom two the past two weeks, and Olson also has to prepare for the Banana Bowl (which went down over the weekend), so who’s to say how he’ll do with a salsa to “Uptown Funk” by Mark Ronson ft. Bruno Mars. Not sure how much salsa there was in the final product, but they certainly brought the energy. “I think this was your best dance,” Derek says. “It just felt like you really commitTed and owned that floor.” SCORE: 31 out of 40

Olympian Amber Glenn with Pasha Pashkov. They got great feedback on their rumba last week, but they weren’t too thrilled to go down on the leaderboard. Their upside down split is also making the rounds on social media, so they’re excited to get back out on the ballroom floor and raise the bar. This week, they’re taking on a samba to “Mi Gente” by J Balvin & Willy William. “She knows how to get the party started!” Bruno says, pointing out she’s also finally playing more within the style of dance, as they judges have been asking her to do for a few weeks. SCORE: 34 out of 40

Reality star Tyler Cameron with Sharna Burgess. These two gave the judges their “breakthrough dance” of the season last week, and now is Cameron’s time to shine as a former football player. He’s performing a jazz to “The Time (Dirty Bit)” by Black Eyed Peas, and Burgess is really focusing on his balance (which is kind of nonexistent). The song was perfect for him, since the judges previously compared him to Patrick Swayze, and yes, they did hit a lift…obviously. “Tyler, I love when you go dirty dancing!” Bruno says, also complimenting his improvement on his timing and his form. SCORE: 30 out of 40

Comedian and podcaster Connor Wood with Rylee Arnold. Their scores dropped slightly last week, so this is another chance for Wood to prove that he’s got some hip action in him with a samba to “Hips Don’t Lie” by Shakira ft. Wyclef Jean. And you know what? Those hips were doing something! “You really didn’t have the correct hip-foot action for the samba,” Bruno told him. It’s hard to say how his sins were worse than the other men before him, whose footwork could also use some finesse, but hey! SCORE: 25 out of 30

Actress Julia Stiles with Ezra Sosa. This movie star also had a breakthrough last week, and she seems to really be enjoying the experience now that she’s let go a little. Nowhere to go but up from here! Stiles says she’s channeling the queen herself with a jazz to “Jenny From the Block” [Track Masters Remix] by Jennifer Lopez ft. Jadakiss & Styles P, which also featured an homage to her film Save the Last Dance right in front of her co-star Sean Patrick Thomas. “I know this is the wrong movie, but I think we just got served!” Carrie Ann screams. SCORE: 33 out of 40

Actress Tatyana Ali with Jan Ravnik. The Fresh Prince star was a little hurt by Carrie Ann’s 6 last week, so she really wants to improve this week. She and Ravnik are dancing a salsa to “Squabble Up” by Kendrick Lamar, which is an interesting combination, and the judges sort of unfairly hold that against them in the scoring. Both Derek and Carrie Ann say it might’ve been too laid back for a salsa (maybe they should’ve been given a song above 100 bpm), but Joe Buck says it was his favorite of the night! “You’ve got it,” Bruno assures her, but wants her to go even further. SCORE: 29 out of 40

Late-night sidekick Guillermo Rodriguez with Whitney Carson. After once again getting the lowest scores of the week, Jimmy Kimmel’s right-hand man thinks maybe the judges were just having a bad day. Witney doesn’t think so, and she’s really honing in on his technique. She’s got her work cut out for her teaching him a salsa to “Tití Me Preguntó” by Bad Bunny, but Guillermo is going for a 6, especially from Carrie Ann. “You took the note, and you made it work!” she tells him. SCORE: 22 out of 40

Actress Jenna Dewan with Val Chmerkovskiy. This week’s performance will be all about passion, because these two are dancing a paso doble to “Bad Romance” by Lady Gaga. Dewan is also filming The Rookie, so things are getting challenging as Val drills her on the technique — even on set between takes. “Incandescent! Thrilling from start to finish!” Bruno yells. SCORE: 36 out of 40 (straight 9s!)

Actor Harry Shum Jr. with Jenna Johnson. The Grey’s Anatomy actor is finally starting to feel like a leading man, and as they reach their flow, they’re performing a samba to “Yeah!” by Usher ft. Lil Jon & Ludacris. Shum Jr. got to see Usher’s halftime performance live, so hopefully he’ll be able to bring some of that same energy to the ballroom, but he’s going to have to remember this is a Latin dance and not a hip-hop routine. “If that was a halftime show, amazing. I loved every minute of it. But, it’s a samba,” Carrie Ann said. “You need to put more content in your dances.” SCORE: 33 out of 40

Paralympian Ezra Frech with Daniella Karagach. Bringing up the rear this week, these two are coming off heaping praise from the judges for their rumba on Week 4. For Super Bowl night, they’re performing a salsa to “Hot in Herre” by Nelly. Frech wants to bring a decade of missed parties to the ballroom floor tonight. (he was training to make it to the Paralympics, to be fair). “I genuinely get lost in your performances,” Derek says, “Fantastic way to close the show.” SCORE: 36 out of 40 (another straight set of 9s!)

Who goes home?

In a move that had the audience distraught but should’ve been expected at some point, Guillermo and Witney are sent home Tuesday night. Next week is Dedication Night, where the remaining stars will be honoring someone or something special in their life.

title: Candle In The Wind: 5-Year-Old Media Firm Faces New Questions After Hello Sunshine Exit
summary: Now that Candle Media’s glow has dimmed further with the sale of its Hello Sunshine majority stake, fresh questions are being raised about the firm’s future. The financials around the deal for Reese Witherspoon’s company, which she is buying back from Candle in partnership with France-based Mediawan, have not been disclosed. But one veteran financier […]
content:
Now that Candle Media‘s glow has dimmed further with the sale of its Hello Sunshine majority stake, fresh questions are being raised about the firm’s future.

The financials around the deal for Reese Witherspoon’s company, which she is buying back from Candle in partnership with France-based Mediawan, have not been disclosed. But one veteran financier familiar with the transaction told Deadline it likely represents a loss of several hundreds of millions of dollars for Candle. The main culprits: a $900 million valuation when the firm took a majority stake in Hello Sunshine in 2021 – a sky-high level given its output and lack of profitability – and dramatic changes in the media landscape of late.

Five years ago, Candle lit up with $2 billion in backing from private equity mainstay Blackstone. At the time, the industry was on a major streaming binge, and the company had two titans at the helm in co-founders Kevin Mayer and Tom Staggs. The two had spent years together in high posts at Disney, helping to pull off major M&A deals like the Pixar, Marvel and Lucasfilm acquisitions and the thunderbolt merger with Capital Cities-ABC that brought ESPN into the fold.

Watch on Deadline

Today, industry observers wonder if the next logical move for Candle would be to swing a deal for the company’s main remaining asset, kids entertainment powerhouse Moonbug. Private equity firms, after all, view their funding and portfolios in terms of returns within years, not decades.

Moonbug, which produces CoComelon, is in better financial shape than many of its peers. But the nearly $3 billion Candle paid to acquire it has set a high bar. One source familiar with the strategic thinking of Mayer and Staggs says a deal to unload the company is not imminent but has been actively explored. As it has regrouped, Candle has cut staff and restructured from its origins as a buyer of assets to primarily an operator of them.

‘CoComelon’ Netflix

RELATED: Candle Media Restructures, Folding Animation Into Moonbug As Hello Sunshine Chief Sarah Harden Takes Over Rebranded Studio

A Candle rep declined comment when contacted by Deadline. Blackstone did not respond to a request for comment.

Difficulties for private equity-backed players extend far beyond the entertainment sector, and stem largely from higher interest rates. In an article about the increasingly tenuous state of small- and mid-sized private players, published Tuesday in parallel with the Hello Sunshine news, the Wall Street Journal quoted a banker as saying the situation is approaching a “period of reckoning.” As money returns to the sidelines, private equity fundraising is on track for its worst year since 2020.

The rate-driven increase in the cost of borrowing money is squeezing a lot of firms like Candle, given that they have to try to sell assets at even higher levels to account for the difference in rates. For those in the media business, however, demand for streaming programming is also receding as Netflix and other players tighten their belt and the industry braces for the impact of the Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery merger. Skydance, their new parent company, is promising at least $6 billion in cost savings related to the deal. Podcast platforms, which once splashed cash around, have also cut their spending.

One of Candle’s early investments, along with Hello Sunshine, was a minority stake in Will Smith’s production company Westbrook. Less than three months after that deal was announced in January 2022, Smith became an industry pariah after slapping Chris Rock onstage at the Oscars, earning a 10-year ban from the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences. While Smith has returned to starring roles, the episode added another wrinkle to the already difficult task of profiting from film and TV production.

Along with Westbrook, the company invested in Spain-based Exile Content Studio and social media storytelling firm ATTN:.

No one who has done business with Mayer and Staggs or who is familiar with the company’s operations blames them personally for the firm’s struggles. It simply seems to be a case of unfortunate timing.

Given their largely charmed run at Disney, where each served a tour of duty at the company’s strategic planning division before rising to higher positions, both are sought-after and respected executives. Even after Candle’s founding, the pair were retained by former Disney CEO Bob Iger as consultants. David Zaslav brought Mayer in as he was about to close the Warner Bros. Discovery merger in 2021. Drawing on the expertise he developed at Disney overseeing the launch of Disney+ and leading a number of sports initiatives, Mayer also served as chairman of sports streamer DAZN just prior to Candle’s launch.

“We did move aggressively,” Mayer said of Candle during an appearance on a Deadline-moderated panel at last month’s Zurich Summit. “When I thought about what I wanted Candle to be, I wanted it to be a modernly configured media company that had a flywheel around great storytelling told by great storytellers.”

Candle spent some $4 billion on acquisitions, Mayer recalled, musing about how different that outlay is from the massive level of Disney and other giants. “There is a certain minimum scale you probably need to make an impact,” he said.

Moonbug, while it accounts for three-quarters of Candle’s spending, is a property with heft in the YouTube-driven creator economy. At the Zurich conference, Mayer noted that CoComelon‘s Netflix incarnation was the streamer’s most popular title from 2021-2024. (It has fallen off since then, and shifted to Disney+.) The company’s YouTube channel gets 13 billion views a month, he said, more than all of Disney including ESPN and four times the viewing of MrBeast.

“There’s no doubt they’d look to do a deal if they get an offer in the right ballpark,” one investor says. “But in today’s climate, is anybody going to step forward to make that kind of offer? That’s really the question.”

For Mayer and Staggs, despite their sterling reputations, “this is going to take some time for people to get over,” the investor added. “Though this business can have a short memory if the money is right.”

title: Aaron Sorkin Thinks About Reviving ‘The West Wing’ for a ‘Couple of Seconds Every Day’: ‘I Miss It’
summary: “The West Wing” stays on Aaron Sorkin’s mind. Created by Sorkin, the beloved NBC series ran from 1999 to 2006 and is widely regarded as one of the best TV shows of all time. Asked by Entertainment Weekly about potentially reviving it, Sorkin said: “There’s probably a couple of seconds every day when I think […]
content:
“The West Wing” stays on Aaron Sorkin‘s mind.

Created by Sorkin, the beloved NBC series ran from 1999 to 2006 and is widely regarded as one of the best TV shows of all time. Asked by Entertainment Weekly about potentially reviving it, Sorkin said: “There’s probably a couple of seconds every day when I think about it.”

Though he noted that “it would be very, very tricky to do in the current environment,” he added that it “would be fun” and “I miss it.”

Popular on Variety

“The West Wing” starred Martin Sheen as President Josiah “Jed” Bartlet, Allison Janney as press secretary C.J. Cregg, Richard Schiff as communication director Toby Ziegler, Rob Lowe as deputy communications director Sam Seaborn, John Spencer as chief of staff Leo McGarry, Bradley Whitford as deputy chief of staff Josh Lyman, Dulé Hill as presidential aide Charlie Young, Stockard Channing as First Lady Abbey Bartlet and more.

Of what President Bartlet would think about the current state of U.S. politics, Sorkin told EW: “I’d like to take a little time before I put words in Jed Bartlet’s mouth. I’ll just say that I don’t think his reaction would be dissimilar to most of our reactions to what’s going on right now.”

Sorkin isn’t the only one who is open to a “West Wing” revival — Whitford and Hill told Variety last month that they’d both be on board if Sorkin decided to bring it back.

“I’ll work him,” Whitford said of Sorkin. “I think there could be a limited series of some kind.”

Added Hill, “I think if he writes it, then we all will be there … It would be a lovely thing to hopefully steer the collective consciousness of our society back toward humanity and connectivity and understanding.”

Sorkin is currently doing the press rounds for his latest movie, “The Social Reckoning,” a follow-up to 2010’s “The Social Network” with Jeremy Strong playing Mark Zuckerberg.

title: Joanna Hogg to Preside Over El Gouna Film Festival Jury
summary: British director Joanna Hogg (“The Souvenir,” “The Eternal Daughter”) will preside over the jury of Egypt’s El Gouna Film Festival, which runs Oct. 15-23. Hogg, who is one of the U.K.’s leading auteurs, will also be giving a masterclass titled “Life Into Film” during the festival. Joining Hogg on the El Gouna jury panel will […]
content:
British director Joanna Hogg (“The Souvenir,” “The Eternal Daughter”) will preside over the jury of Egypt’s El Gouna Film Festival, which runs Oct. 15-23.

Hogg, who is one of the U.K.’s leading auteurs, will also be giving a masterclass titled “Life Into Film” during the festival. Joining Hogg on the El Gouna jury panel will be Egyptian actress Nahed El Sebaie (“19 B”); Egyptian composer Khaled Hammad, whose career spans three decades and comprises “The Yacoubian Building” and “The Inevitable Journey to Find a Wedding Dress”; Iraqi-Kurdish filmmaker Shawkat Amin Korki (“Memories on Stone,” “The Exam”); and Turkish auteur Yeşim Ustaoğlu, whose drama film “What Remains” recently premiered positively at San Sebastian.

The fest, held in the Red Sea resort roughly 250 miles south of Cairo, also announced the composition of the other jury rosters for its ninth edition.

Popular on Variety

The Swiss-Iraqi filmmaker, producer, and multidisciplinary artist known as Samir will preside over El Gouna’s feature documentary competition and “Green Star” jury, which will judge films competing for the documentary prizes and also the fest’s award recognizing the best film addressing environmental issues. Joining him on this jury panel are Afghanistan-born, Netherlands-based filmmaker Aboozar Amini (“Kabul, Between Prayers”); Belgian producer Julie Frères (“From Abdul to Leila,” “The Other Side of the Sun”); Zurich Film Festival director and co-owner Reta Guetg; and Lebanese film editor Gladys Joujou (“Talking About Trees,” “Bye Bye Tiberias”).

Finally, El Gouna’s short films competition jury is made up of groundbreaking Saudi director Meshal AlJaser (“Naga”); Tunisian director Amel Guellaty (“Where the Wind Comes From”); and Greek actor and director Christos Passalis, who starred in “Dogtooth” and Sundance Audience Award winner “Hold Onto Me.”

title: Russell Brand Was ‘Ruthless and Calculated’ With a ‘Voracious’ Desire for ‘Sexual Contact,’ Prosecution Alleges in Rape Trial Opening Statement
summary: Russell Brand was “ruthless and calculated” with an “indiscriminate and voracious” desire for sexual contact, the prosecution alleged in its opening statement at the actor and comedian’s rape trial in London. Brand has been charged with three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one count of indecent assault. He has pleaded not […]
content:
Russell Brand was “ruthless and calculated” with an “indiscriminate and voracious” desire for sexual contact, the prosecution alleged in its opening statement at the actor and comedian’s rape trial in London.

Brand has been charged with three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one count of indecent assault. He has pleaded not guilty and denied all charges.

The jury was selected on Tuesday, consisting of eight men and four women. The case involves six female plaintiffs, all of whom are given automatic lifelong anonymity according to U.K. law, and relates to alleged offenses that occurred between 1999 and 2009.

Arriving to Southwark Crown Court on Wednesday morning, Brand sported a black suit, pinstriped shirt, loose white tie and sunglasses. He was accompanied by his wife, Laura Gallacher, whose hand he clasped. According to BBC News, Brand told reporters on his way inside: “I feel blessed. I feel of course concerned, but hopeful that this process will lead to good outcomes for everybody — that is my prayer,” he said. Inside the courtroom, Brand appeared to be rubbing what looked like a rock or pebble in his hand.

Popular on Variety

Riel Karmy-Jones KC is leading the prosecution and set out the case against Brand. As the BBC reports, the six alleged victims “did not know each other, have never met each other” and “came forward independently of each other,” Karmy-Jones noted.

Brand was “ruthless and calculated” and “sometimes might tell women what they wanted to hear” to satisfy his sexual appetite, Karmy-Jones alleged. “The circumstances of the offending were as wide and as varied as the defendant’s career,” she said. “His strong desire for some form of sexual contact was indiscriminate and voracious.”

Karmy-Jones called Brand “a flirt with a huge sexual appetite — childlike in his expectation that his every desire should be met.” He would “appear indifferent” after an alleged assault, she claimed. “Sometimes he would leave promptly after the incident, sometimes making an excuse to get away or sometimes simply continuing as though nothing wrong had happened,” she said, according to BBC News.

The prosecution brought in testimony from a former friend of Brand’s, who claimed that the comedian bragged to him that he wanted to sleep with “5,000 women” in his lifetime and had laid out “rules” to achieve this, including telling them “what they want to hear.”

Turning to the first alleged victim, who was in her 20s at the time of the incident in 1999, the prosecution said when she first met Brand she assumed he was gay. Later at her home, she invited him to make himself a cup of tea while she used the bathroom. When she emerged, she was shocked to find him “partially undressed.”

“Perhaps some of her confusion can be explained by how the defendant was behaving, because as she came out of the bathroom he was prancing around the room — a bit like an ostrich, doing silly walks like Basil Fawlty,” Karmy-Jones said, as reported by BBC News. “She was taken aback, she was shocked and didn’t really know what to do — and in her words she froze a bit.”

The prosecution then alleged that Brand raped her. She “described drifting out of her head, knowing there was nothing she could do, as he pulled her trousers and underwear down, penetrated her vagina with his penis — raping her,” Karmy-Jones said.

The complainant claims she didn’t report the alleged incident at the time because of Brand’s “celebrity status,” which she “now greatly regrets.” When she did eventually file a police report and Brand was questioned about the incident, the prosecution claimed he did not remember her name or the incident, but insisted that he “had never engaged in non-consensual activity.”

The second incident occurred in 2001, the prosecution claimed, and involved a woman in her 30s at the time who was working at MTV. The prosecution alleged that Brand “lurched forward and grabbed her breasts,” and then “squeezed them with both his hands,” as BBC News reports. He then asked her where the toilets were, and when she showed him to them he asked her to “come in” and allegedly grabbed her forearm. She resisted and managed to pull herself away. The woman said she told one other person at the time, but did not formally report it until 2023 as she thought it could be relevant information after the Metropolitan Police began their investigation into Brand.

The third alleged victim claims she met Brand at a party in Soho in 2004, where he grabbed her breasts in the middle of a conversation, the prosecution claimed. The woman remembers Brand having a “big, weird grin” on his face during the alleged incident, and then pulled her to the toilets where he allegedly orally raped her.

The fourth allegation occurred at Capital Radio in 2004/2005. Brand allegedly pushed the woman against a wall and “aggressively” kissed her while grabbing “her body, at her breasts, sides and buttocks,” the prosecution said, according to BBC News. The alleged victim tried to push him off but “he was too strong and he continued to kiss her on her face, and down her neck and onto her chest area, grabbing her bum and moving his mouth towards her cleavage, and grabbing her breast so hard that it was painful,” Karmy-Jones said. When she did finally push him away, he “sniggered like it was a joke,” she added.

In the mid-2000s, Brand was best known as a comedian and actor, presenting shows such as “Big Brother’s Big Mouth” and starring in films such as “Get Him to the Greek” and “Forgetting Sarah Marshall.” He has since pivoted to podcasting and influencing online.

The trial is expected to run for six weeks.

title: Banijay Kids & Family Sells ’Little Princess’ to Sky U.K. (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: “Little Princess,” the British pre-school animation classic, is heading to Sky UK, in a deal struck with Banijay Kids & Family which sees the pay TV buying its complete catalog. Further new distribution deals on “Little Princess,” a four-time BAFTA nominee, have been struck with Nordisk Film, RTV Slovenia and Italy’s TIM. Based on the […]
content:
“Little Princess,” the British pre-school animation classic, is heading to Sky UK, in a deal struck with Banijay Kids & Family which sees the pay TV buying its complete catalog.

Further new distribution deals on “Little Princess,” a four-time BAFTA nominee, have been struck with Nordisk Film, RTV Slovenia and Italy’s TIM.

Based on the best-selling children’s books by award-winning author and illustrator Tony Ross, “Little Princess” launched on the U.K.’s Channel 4 “Milkshake” children’s TV block in 2006 and ran through four seasons of a total 135 episodes, the last ending in 2020.

First time round, when on linear TV, “Little Princess” was released in 140 territories. The deal announced by Banijay Kids & Family on Wednesday at Mipcom o underscore that what the market is looking for is evergreen brands, not necessarily brand new linear TV shows.

Popular on Variety

“Little Princess” has, however, cultivated from 2008 to a fandom base on YouTube and other platforms, underscoring its resilient appeal.

Sky U.K. has acquired all series and specials. Nordisk Film has acquired Seasons 1-3 and the series’ specials for SVOD across the Nordics; RTV Slovenia has Seasons 1-2, and Telecom Italia’s TIM for its Italian streaming platform aggregator, TIMVision.

“Little Princess” is produced by The Illuminated Film Company, also behind Eric Carle’s “The Very Hungry Caterpillar and Other Stories” and the RTS Award winning “The Rubbish World of Dave Spud.”

Set in a comfy world of gentle blocked colors, an ever blue sky, lovely grass low hills stretching to the horizon, and a purple-bricked castle, “Little Princess” turns on the antics of the bubbly, ever inquisitive and endearing titular character.

Sporting a permanent yellow crown teeth and craggy mild teeth who confronts every day problems – such as getting a scratch after a very minor accident on “I Need a Plaster. Coddled by her parents and the cast service, she learns, however, that she might be a princess but won’t always get her own way. Each episode, as Banijay Friends & Family notes, is told with a warm blend of humor and surprise.

“Across the industry, we’re seeing continued demand for trusted, established IP that can cut through in an increasingly crowded landscape. With a new U.K. home on Sky and partners across Europe, ‘Little Princess’ demonstrates the enduring value of distinctive characters and storytelling that audiences know and love,” said Julia Rowlands, SVP Sales, Co-Productions and Acquisitions, Banijay Kids & Family.Led by CEO Benoît Di Sabatino, Banijay Kids & Family brings together leading production companies – Monello Productions, Movimenti Production, Procidis, Tiger Aspect Kids & Family, Zodiak Kids & Family France, and Zodiak Productions UK – spanning France, Italy, and the U.K.

It is behind preeminent kids’ brands including “Totally Spies!,” “Mr Bean,” “Once Upon a Time…, LoliRock,” “Super Happy Magic Forest,” “Street Football” and “MiniHeroes of the Forest.”

title: Russell T Davies Calls BBC Boss’ AI ‘Doctor Who’ Comment ‘Clumsy’ and Teases Show’s Future: ‘You’ll Start to See Production’ in ‘Summer Next Year’
summary: Outgoing “Doctor Who” showrunner Russell T. Davies has criticized BBC director general Matt Brittin over recent comments he made regarding an AI-generated episode of the cult show. Speaking at the Royal Television Society conference last month, Brittin said he’d been sent a fully AI-generated episode of “Doctor Who,” which he described as “pretty good.” Although […]
content:
Outgoing “Doctor Who” showrunner Russell T. Davies has criticized BBC director general Matt Brittin over recent comments he made regarding an AI-generated episode of the cult show.

Speaking at the Royal Television Society conference last month, Brittin said he’d been sent a fully AI-generated episode of “Doctor Who,” which he described as “pretty good.” Although he was quick to add it was “not going to replace humans,” his wording sparked instant criticism, and Brittin later admitted he had “got into trouble” over what he’d said. Now one of the biggest names in “Doctor Who” has spoken up.

“That’s a clumsy thing to say in an industry where he’s got writers and artists and it specifically affects people, they’re the first to take the blow,” said Davies, speaking to BBC Radio 4’s The Media Show. “My inbox went ping ping ping ping ping, so God knows what his was like.”

Popular on Variety

Davies — who revived “Doctor Who” in 2005 and then returned again in 2023 — also said that Brittin, who only recently joined the BBC following a career at Google, “hasn’t worked in television for that long and might not be so fruity with an opinion in future.”

The future of “Doctor Who” — a BBC icon for more than 60 years — is currently up in the air following the departure of Disney+ as a co-financier. This summer, Davies announced he would be stepping back and the BBC cancelled the planned Christmas special. Last month, the BBC launched a competitive tender inviting pitches from producers to reboot the series. “Line of Duty” creator Jed Mercurio is among those to have submitted their interest.

But while fans wait to see what happens, Davies, despite no longer being involved in the show, assured that a new series was definitely happening and there wouldn’t be too long to wait.

“You’ll start to see production with a brand-new Doctor, a brand-new companion, summer next year,” he said.

title: Human Imagination, Directable AI: How Asian Directors Wrap Kling AI Into Their Workflows
summary: On a packed morning commute, a dozing man, frayed by overwork and crushing pressure, turns into a giant worm. Apart from a few passengers who recoil in fear or surprise, the majority remain drowsy and indifferent. The worm, however impossible to miss, is shoved, bumped, and pushed around with everyone else in the stifling subway […]
content:
On a packed morning commute, a dozing man, frayed by overwork and crushing pressure, turns into a giant worm. Apart from a few passengers who recoil in fear or surprise, the majority remain drowsy and indifferent. The worm, however impossible to miss, is shoved, bumped, and pushed around with everyone else in the stifling subway car.

This is a scene from the short film Worm Train screened at the Asian Contents & Film Market (ACFM) during the 31st Busan International Film Festival (BIFF). The latest endeavor from prominent South Korean director and writer Sung-Soo Kim, the film was inspired by Franz Kafka’s “The Metamorphosis”. Unlike Gregor Samsa who is confined to his room after transforming into a huge insect, the protagonist still has to go to work, a dark and bleak absurdity that lays bare the alienation, isolation, and hypocrisy of modern life.

Kim started the project in February but halted in March because of that very cramped subway scene. “At the time, AI could generate a giant insect but couldn’t precisely capture its physical collisions with passengers and the chain of reactions that followed,” he said at a panel dedicated to AI and filmmaking at ACFM. He didn’t resume production until late September, when the latest Kling 4.0 model allowed him to generate continuous motion between frames and better control character movement, scene transitions, and the progression of shots.

A veteran in South Korean commercial cinema whose hits include Musa and 12.12: The Day, Worm Train was the first film where Kim applied this technology that had been in the film industry for a decade. By folding AI into his conventional production workflow, one centered on the director’s creative vision and collaboration with specialists across disciplines, he found AI was directable and viable. “Technology can present everything we imagine, but it is we who give meaning and value to those cinematic images,” he said.

“What makes cinema more cinematic in the age of AI?” Kim posed at the two-hour panel titled “New Cinematic Possibilities: Reimagining Filmmaking with Kling AI,” held on Sunday. Across the four filmmakers present, the answer seemed broadly consistent: human vision, and technology brought under its direction.

For Sang Wook Lee, now leading MBC C&I’s AI section, it was more about finding how far AI-generated content can go while remaining engaging and acceptable to audiences. He brought Rendering Love, a microdrama series powered by Kling AI and co-developed with Barunson E&A, the production company behind Oscar-winning film Parasite.

The K-pop romantic comedy follows the virtual idol group LEVRIT with their real identities hidden and a female fan who sees through them. “The work itself is about the boundary between virtual and real, so our production followed the same boundary: We use live action for the real world and AI to generate LEVRIT’s stage performances,” he said, adding that Kling’s Motion Control was instrumental in transferring the movements filmed with real performers to the virtual characters before blending them into the live-action story.

Harry Hyun, director of Netflix Korean hit Crypton Man, agreed that the “boundary” was key to the hybrid pipeline. The director and founder of creative content startup MooAm introduced a new IP, Natasha, a 100-minute period romance thriller inspired by Baek Seok’s poem “Me and Natasha and a White Donkey.” In this film, live-action shooting was used for character-driven scenes where nuanced performances are essential while costly setting such as the snowstorm in 1944 and large crowd scenes were generated with Kling.

Kling tools including All-in-One Reference, V2V, 10-bit HDR output, and support for up to 10 keyframes as control points in the 4.0 model were all integral to the production. “By setting up to 10 keyframes as control points, we can guide changes in a character’s state and key story beats according to the director’s intent,” she cited an example.

The discussion also extended into the cinematic presentation of long-form feature animation with Chinese director Wei Li’s Born of the Tides. Having more than 20 years of experience in animation, Li’s credits include Lotus Lantern, Jiang Ziya: Legend of Deification, and Big Fish & Begonia. For Born of the Tides, he, for the first time, infused AI tools into traditional animation methods he has worked with for decades. “For animation, AI lowers the cost of trial and error, giving niche stories that were once difficult to present a chance to be realized at a high quality,” he said.

The 105-minute film spans more than 2,350 shots and 200 characters. “At this scale, wide shots were almost impossible in the past because faces rendered too small could lose definition on the big screen,” he explained. “Kling’s native 4K video generation helps render large-scale sequences such as the dragon-boat race and the fish market explosion for the big screen.”

Across the panel, both established filmmakers once wary of AI and creators building hybrid pipelines seemed to land on a similar view: AI is increasingly becoming something directors can direct, serving their imagination, folding into their workflow, and expanding their cinematic expression. That is, perhaps, what makes cinema more cinematic.

“One day, the term ‘AI film’ itself may fade,” Kim said. “Just as we no longer make a point of calling films ‘talkies’ or ‘color movies,’ what remains ultimately is cinema. And the ones creating it will still be us.”

title: Russell Brand Rape Trial: ‘Forgetting Sarah Marshall’ Star Had “Indiscriminate & Voracious” Sexual Appetite
summary: Russell Brand had an “indiscriminate and voracious” appetite for sexual contact that led to a decade of criminal offending, a court has heard. Brand took his place in the dock on Wednesday at London’s Southwark Crown Court, as the prosecution began making its case against the Forgetting Sarah Marshall star in a trial that will […]
content:
Russell Brand had an “indiscriminate and voracious” appetite for sexual contact that led to a decade of criminal offending, a court has heard.

Brand took his place in the dock on Wednesday at London’s Southwark Crown Court, as the prosecution began making its case against the Forgetting Sarah Marshall star in a trial that will stretch into December.

Brand faces seven charges, encompassing three counts of rape, three charges of sexual assault, and one of indecent assault. The charges pertain to allegations made by six women, spanning a decade from 1999 to 2009. Brand has pleaded not guilty to all charges and has consistently denied wrongdoing.

Riel Karmy-Jones KC, the barrister leading the argument for the prosecution, accused Brand of being “charming,” “ruthless,” and “calculating” in his efforts to satisfy his hunger for sexual activity. She said Brand “cared not” who the women were or how he left them feeling.

Watch on Deadline

“He would be nice when he wanted to be funny — undoubtedly charming, likeable even — when he wanted something in return. But then demanding, entitled, a flirt with a huge sexual appetite, childlike in his expectation that his every desire should be met,” Karmy-Jones said.

Karmy-Jones said the six women who had made the allegations against Brand did not know each other and had never met. She said they came forward after watching the 2023 Channel 4 documentary, Russell Brand: In Plain Sight.

Brand walked into Southwark Crown Court in a black pinstripe suit, buttoned-down shirt, and white tie, knowing today would be the first full day of evidence after a jury was sworn in on Tuesday. He was again accompanied by his wife, Laura. Brand’s defense barrister is Ian Winter KC.

The jury members, comprising eight men and four women, took their place in Courtroom 3 of Southwark Crown Court for the first time. Judge Mr Justice Bennathan whittled down a list of 50 individuals to swear in the 12-strong jury.

The judge dismissed people who had watched Channel 4’s Russell Brand: In Plain Sight, or read the investigation in The Times of London or The Sunday Times. He also asked prospective jury members to leave if they had worked for MTV, Channel 4, or Capital Radio.

During a hearing on Monday, he said those individuals selected to serve on the jury “absolutely cannot carry out any research about Russell Brand,” including Googling the comedian or searching for him on social media. He warned that this could prejudice the trial and was a criminal offense.

Brand acted in Despicable Me and Get Him to the Greek. Before his work in Hollywood, he was a regular fixture on British television and radio, hosting Big Brother’s Big Mouth and a Radio 2 show.

The actor and comedian, who was married to Katy Perry, has reinvented himself as a Christian convert who evangelizes about free speech and free thinking in MAGA America.

Brand has continued posting on streaming and posting on his social media channels during the legal proceedings. He spoke of feeling God’s presence as he entered the court building. “Today, I feel blessed. I feel, of course, concerned but hopeful that this process will lead to good outcomes for everybody involved,” he told Sky News on Wednesday. “That’s my prayer.”

title: ‘La Bola Negra’, ‘Woman Unknown’, ‘NAZA’ & ‘Fjord’ Among 68 Films On Shortlist For 39th European Film Awards
summary: The European Film Academy has unveiled the shortlist of films in the running for prizes at its 39th European Film Awards ceremony scheduled to take place on January 16, 2027 in Athens. A total of 68 feature films have been shortlisted for a possible nomination for the European Film Awards, with the winners voted for […]
content:
The European Film Academy has unveiled the shortlist of films in the running for prizes at its 39th European Film Awards ceremony scheduled to take place on January 16, 2027 in Athens.

A total of 68 feature films have been shortlisted for a possible nomination for the European Film Awards, with the winners voted for by members of the European Film Academy.

Forty-five films are selected for the fiction shortlist including Cannes 2026 Palme d’Or winner Fjord, Venice Golden Lion winner Woman Unknown and awards season frontrunners such as La Bola Negra and Coward.

The 15 titles in the documentary shortlist include bombshell documentary NAZA and French box office break out Whispers in the Woods. The animation shortlist includes festival breakouts In Waves, Iron Boy and Jim Queen.

Watch on Deadline

Representing 40 European countries, the films bring together established and emerging filmmakers, including directors working across borders. Twenty-five films are directed or co-directed by women.

Voted on by more than 5,700 cinema professionals based in some 50 countries across Europe, the European Film Awards have placed themselves at the heart of the wider awards season following a move to a January slot from the 2026 ceremony onwards, having taken place in December for many years.

The January 16, 2027 slot once again falls the day after the end of nomination voting in the Academy Awards on January 15, and before the January 21 nominations announcement. The Golden Globes will also be done and dusted with its 2027 ceremony set for January 10.

With campaigning largely on hold ahead of the Academy Awards nominations announcement, the January 16 slot allows European teams in the running to return to Europe from L.A. for the ceremony in Athens, before hitting the campaign trail again if they have made it on to the final Oscar shortlists.

The 38th ceremony in Berlin earlier this year saw Norwegian director Joachim Trier’s Sentimental Value sweep the board to win best film, director, screenwriter for Eskil Vogt and Trier, as well as best actor and actress for Stellan Skarsgård and Renate Reinsve respectively, and best score for Hania Rani. It then went on to win Best International Feature Film at the Oscars.

Nominations in the European Film Award categories of best film, documentary, animation, director, actress, actor, screenwriter, casting director, cinematographer, composer, costume designer, editor, make-up and hair artist, production designer and sound as well as for the Discovery – Prix Fipresci award will be announced on 14 November 2026 during the Thessaloniki International Film Festival.
