title: Rohit Jain Launches Tiger TV
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Rohit Jain is launching Tiger TV, a streaming platform dedicated to Hindi and Punjabi content. The platform will launch on October 15, 2026. It will be available on the Lionsgate Play app across Asia, and as a standalone app in the US, UK, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand. The platform will also be on […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Rohit Jain is launching Tiger TV, a streaming platform dedicated to Hindi and Punjabi content.

The platform will launch on October 15, 2026. It will be available on the Lionsgate Play app across Asia, and as a standalone app in the US, UK, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand. The platform will also be on Amazon Prime Video Channels and YouTube Primetime Channels.

Jain previously had an eight-year stint as President of Lionsgate Play Asia. He bought the streamer in South Asia and Southeast Asia last year.

In their announcement, Tiger TV organizers said they plan to build a “₹500 crore+ portfolio of Punjabi and Hindi content IP over the next three years” with a slate of over 50 premiere titles in its first year of operation.

Watch on Deadline

The streamer’s Punjabi titles include Laal Salaam, Rubb Rakha, Jahankilla, Hanji Kaun, Janaur, Ikk Tu Hoven Mutiyare, and Tu Te Punjab, with performers such as Diljit Dosanjh, Ammy Virk, Gippy Grewal, Neeru Bajwa, Sonam Bajwa and Arminder Gill set to feature.

On the Hindi side, the slate includes Jeevan Ya Bheema Con, Mantu Bhaiya Ki Dili Dezire, The Taj Story and Aakhri Sawal. At the launch, organizers also unveiled the first look at Daanav, a Hindi crime thriller original starring Angad Bedi and Pooja Gor.

Jain also unveiled Eklavya, the first in a slate of AI projects. The project features Yug R.Ai, an AI actor.

Tiger TV will be available for ₹349 per quarter or ₹799 per year in India, and from 5.99 per month in the US (USD), Canada (CAD), the UK (GBP), Australia (AUD), and New Zealand (NZD).

title: Electrify Enlists Ex-Vice Exec Al Brown & Former YouTube EMEA Boss Patrick Walker For Creator Push
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Al Brown and Patrick Walker, two of the best-known digital execs working in Europe, have joined creator house Electrify. Former Vice programming chief Brown has been named EVP Creative and Editorial, while ex-YouTube EMEA boss Walker will become Chief Strategy Officer at the London-based Electify, which is known for investing in digital creators and […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Al Brown and Patrick Walker, two of the best-known digital execs working in Europe, have joined creator house Electrify.

Former Vice programming chief Brown has been named EVP Creative and Editorial, while ex-YouTube EMEA boss Walker will become Chief Strategy Officer at the London-based Electify, which is known for investing in digital creators and building their online brands.

Electrify’s media brands include Veritasium, fern, Mentour Pilot, Astrum, Fireship and The Rundown AI, with the overall roster collectively reaching more than 65 million subscribers across platforms.

The hires of Brown and Walker come as YouTube audiences increasingly turn to the TV set to consume the Google-owner video service. Electrify pointed to recent data showing that of the approximately 2.6 billion views and 371 million hours watched, more than 130 million hours – around 36% of total watch time – was through TV screens screens.

Watch on Deadline

Walker has a reputation for straddling the entertainment and tech worlds, and was previously Managing Director, EMEA, at YouTube and Director of Media Partnerships, EMEA, at Facebook, putting him at the center of online video and creator-led media as it was growing. He also ran multi-channel network Rightster (later known as Brave Bison), and was a founding investor and Chief Content Officer at early YouTube network Base79.

Brown spent more than a decade at Vice, where he became VP of Programming for Vice Studios UK and executive-produced series including State of Undress and Gaycation, before going on to senior roles at Future Studios and Independent Studio.

At Electrify, he will work closely with creators and teams across its media brands on existing channels and formats while developing original formats and exploring where established audience relationships can open up new entertainment and original IP.

“A big audience isn’t a brief to make more of the same. It gives you permission to take creative risks, find new talent and build formats that can take those ideas somewhere audiences haven’t seen before,” said Brown.

Walker will focus on finding and bringing in the new creator-founded media brands, developing new platform, distribution and licensing opportunities beyond YouTube; and working directly with creators to build longer-lasting businesses around their audiences and IP. He will also lead Electrify’s relationships with platforms and distribution partners, as the company looks at opportunities across streaming, connected television and other forms of distribution.

“YouTube is already a living-room medium for hundreds of millions,” said Walker. “The opportunity now is to build creator-founded brands that can travel across every screen without losing what made audiences choose them in the first place.”

title: Nia Long Joins Teyana Taylor’s Directorial Debut ‘Get Lite’ at Paramount (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: After starring in the blockbuster biopic “Michael,” Nia Long has joined the cast of Teyana Taylor’s directorial debut “Get Lite.” The Paramount movie stars Emmy winner Storm Reid and NFL rookie-turned-actor Ceyair Wright. Wright (“Space Jam: A New Legacy”) plays a talented, but sheltered, dance student who finds inspiration, love and family in the last […]
content:
After starring in the blockbuster biopic “Michael,” Nia Long has joined the cast of Teyana Taylor‘s directorial debut “Get Lite.”

The Paramount movie stars Emmy winner Storm Reid and NFL rookie-turned-actor Ceyair Wright. Wright (“Space Jam: A New Legacy”) plays a talented, but sheltered, dance student who finds inspiration, love and family in the last place he expected: the subways of New York City. Reid (“The Last of Us,” “Euphoria”) is the girl who opens his life to new possibilities.

The role reunites Long and Reid after they co-starred in the hit 2023 thriller “Missing”; Long has also appeared in multiple projects for producer Kenya Barris, including his 2023 Netflix comedy “You People” and his 2020 series “#BlackAF.” She joins an acclaimed ensemble cast that features Leslie Odom, Jr., Aunjanue Ellis-Taylor, Jodie Turner-Smith, Asante Blackk, Woody McClain, Tylil James and Khayr Bullock.

Popular on Variety

Production on “Get Lite” is underway in New York City, with Taylor directing from a screenplay by Maurice Williams, based on a spec script by Eric Gross that appeared on the Black List in 2020. Paramount has slated the film for a wide theatrical release on Aug. 20, 2027.

In addition to starring in the film, Reid will produce alongside Barris and Anni Weisband for Khalabo Ink Society; Robyn Simpson for A Seed & Wings Productions, Reid’s banner; and Bill Karesh for Offbrnd. Taylor is also producing the film with Courtney “Coco” Gilbert, under their production banner, The Aunties.

Last month, Long, a four-time NAACP Image Award winner, received a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame, literally cementing her status as a film and TV icon. She most recently starred in “Michael,” the blockbuster biopic about late pop star Michael Jackson, directed by Antoine Fuqua and produced by Oscar winner Graham King. The Lionsgate film grossed more than $1 billion worldwide, surpassing “Oppenheimer” as the highest-grossing biopic of all time. In the film, Long portrays Katherine Jackson, matriarch of the Jackson family, alongside Oscar nominee Colman Domingo as Joe Jackson and Jaafar Jackson, Michael Jackson’s nephew, as the king of pop.

Up next, Long executive produces and stars in the Netflix film “Don’t Ever Wonder,” reuniting with her “Love Jones” co-star Lorenz Tate. She is also set to star with Ice Cube in “Are We Done Yet?“, the third film in their “Are We There Yet?” family comedy franchise, and reprise her role in the next “Friday movie.”

Long’s memoir — which chronicles her life and career, including iconic roles in “Boyz n the Hood,” “The Best Man” franchise, “Soul Food,” “The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air,” “Third Watch,” “Tyler Perry’s The Single Mom’s Club,” “Dear White People,” “Fatal Affair,” The Banker,” “Roxanne, Roxanne” and more — will be published in 2027.

title: ESPN Launches ESPN JV YouTube Channel for Kids
summary: ESPN JV isn’t for second-stringers. The new YouTube channel aims to cultivate younger sports fans who will keep the Disney sports-media giant in mind as they grow up. The new channel, to be found at youtube.com/@ESPNJV will feature interactive challenges and appearances by both familiar Disney characters and top sports figures as well as videos […]
content:
ESPN JV isn’t for second-stringers.

The new YouTube channel aims to cultivate younger sports fans who will keep the Disney sports-media giant in mind as they grow up. The new channel, to be found at youtube.com/@ESPNJV will feature interactive challenges and appearances by both familiar Disney characters and top sports figures as well as videos that test viewers’ sports knowledge and explore memorable sports moments.

“ESPN JV is about creating an exciting entry point into sports for the next generation of fans,” said Celia Bouza, ESPN’s vice president of multi-platform video, in a statement. ” By combining ESPN’s connection to the biggest moments and personalities in sports with creative, interactive storytelling, we’re building a destination where kids can explore their interests, discover new sports and develop a lifelong love of the game.”

Popular on Variety

The launch of the new outlet marks ESPN’s latest attempt to bring young kids and their families to its screen. Over the past several years, the Disney sports division has tapped Marvel super heroes, “Toy Story” and “Inside Out” figures and characters from the popular cartoon “Big City Greens” for sundry alternative telecasts of basketball and hockey games, among other events.

The channel will feature an original animated series, “The Sports Explorers,” which stars an “ESPN Squad.” Ez, Shay, PJ and Nora each bring unique perspectives to the world of sports, helping young fans discover new games. The series was developed through a creative collaboration between ESPN and WSC Studios, the creative production arm of WSC Sports.

ESPN says new videos will be added regularly.

.

title: RadicalMedia’s New CEO Wants to Test Business Models That Give Production Powerhouse Stakes in Work It Does for Others
summary: At production powerhouse RadicalMedia, the only thing constant is change. Originally conceived as a way for founders Jon Kamen and Frank Scherma to explore new content formats after many years in the advertising business, the firm now has a reputation as a go-to place for music documentaries, branded entertainment and long-form content. Radical Media has […]
content:
At production powerhouse RadicalMedia, the only thing constant is change.

Originally conceived as a way for founders Jon Kamen and Frank Scherma to explore new content formats after many years in the advertising business, the firm now has a reputation as a go-to place for music documentaries, branded entertainment and long-form content. Radical Media has touched everything from the Questlove musical documentary “Summer of Soul” to the streaming version of “Hamilton” that made its way to Disney+ to “This Is a Gardening Show,” the offbeat Zach Galifinakis series on Netflix that is built from episodes just 15 minutes long.

The founders intend to keep testing new frontiers, with one tweak to the company’s leadership ranks. Justin Barocas, a founder of the Anomaly agency, is taking up the reins as CEO, while Kamen will move to an executive-chairman role and Scherma will maintain his position as president. With that move, Barocas would like to see the company increase the number of theatrical properties it takes from Broadway to screens, and move into taking a greater amount of ownership in the content it creates.

Popular on Variety

“It’s not very different from what we see in the marketplace now where the work-for-hire and the services business is changing,” says Barocas, during a recent interview at Radical’s offices in downtown Manhattan. “Being able to commercialize it in very different ways is one of the key areas.” RadicalMedia could look at models that include co-financing, maintaining backend rights, developing proprietary formats, and retaining underlying rights in stage adaptations and branded projects.

Across the advertising ecosystem, owning some of the work created for ads and other promotions has long been a sort of Holy Grail. Many ad concepts become pieces of popular culture, spurring everything from memes to merchandise. Agencies, which once relied on a steady commission, never really got to benefit from any ancillary uses of the intellectual properties they had a hand in creating.

Many have tried. In 2006, for example, the agency once known as Crispin Porter + Bogusky, took a minority stake in the Haggar clothing company as part of its arrangement with the manufacturer. But similar work continues today. Many media agencies are developing practices in what is called “principal media,” a term meant to describe the process of buying up commercial inventory from media companies and re-selling it to advertisers, rather than simply negotiating prices and placements.

RadicalMedia is testing these waters as more advertisers demonstrate a yen to create their own content. Geico is working on a holiday-themed special that is expected to utilize the many ad characters it has created over the years. Athletic-clothing brand Under Armour has set up its own internal studio to better handle its content needs as more advertisers work to capture consumer attention across a wider array of media outlets.

“The idea of being able to use entertainment to solve brand challenges and really commercialize our strengths is where I think what we’re working on in terms of the future. This is the destination for music storytelling, whether it’s theater adapting to streaming or television, whether it’s artists who want to tell their story in a different way,” says Barocas who says that “being able to take that strength and commercialize it” will give Radical Media an incentive “to be true partners” with advertisers, artists and media and entertainment companies.

Kamen sees the new moves as part of the original maneuvers that originally gave rise to Radical. The “constant disruption” of the media and marketing industries “has been going on forever,”: he says. When he and Scherma founded the company, “we always looked and wanted for Radical to have an attitude of embracing whatever those changes will be. HE adds: “We’ve sometimes been ahead of the curve.”

In an earlier era, Radical Media was involved with an MTV dating series, “Gamekillers,” that was produced along with the advertising agency BBH and was backed by a sponsorship from Unilever’s Axe deodorant. Some of the personality types used in the show were also featured in Axe commercials. And Radical enjoyed a long working relationship with the iconoclastic ad agency Wieden + Kennedy, which devised work for Nike that took the company well beyond the typical 30 second commercial.

New concepts with similar themes have surfaced in the broadband era. Some advertisers can back documentaries or series that end up alongside more traditional content selections on Amazon’s Prime Video or NBCUniversal’s Peacock. “There’s no question that brand dollars are going to continue to play a role, even in this streaming universe,” says Kamen. Marketers will need to determine how to make advertising part of the on-demand experience, but “How do you do that effectively? How do you do that tastefully? How do you do that while embracing an audience and making sure that you’re appreciated for having brought something?”

The executives say Radical’s current team will remain in place. Chris Kim, Dave Sirulnick and Jim Bouvet, who head up the company’s studio, entertainment and commercials divisions, respectively are expected to continue in their roles.

Barocas is in many ways making a return to RadicalMedia, rather than an arrival. He worked alongside Radical’s team when he held a job at Wieden, and Kamen gave Barocas and others time to develop Anomaly in Radical’s offices. He intends to keep burnishing the company’s hard won skills in bringing advertisers “something incredibly different” than others, Barocas says. In an industry that is shifting to accommodate new technology, even RadicalMedia wants one thing to remain the same — its reputation.

title: From Bob Hope to Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade to ‘Wicked: One Wonderful Night’: How NBC Became America’s Home for TV Specials
summary: It didn’t get great reviews. The host was awkward on camera as he navigated the emerging medium. The musical numbers and sketches didn’t translate well to the home screen. But none of it mattered. Bob Hope’s first-ever television special for NBC — “The Frigidaire Star Spangled Revue” — was a big hit with viewers when […]
content:
It didn’t get great reviews. The host was awkward on camera as he navigated the emerging medium. The musical numbers and sketches didn’t translate well to the home screen.

But none of it mattered. Bob Hope’s first-ever television special for NBC — “The Frigidaire Star Spangled Revue” — was a big hit with viewers when it aired in the late afternoon in Eastern time zones on Easter Sunday, April 9, 1950.

Hope was already a big box office draw and a major radio star for NBC. He was the first of the big radio comedy titans to try out a TV program. He earned a whopping $40,000 (from Frigidaire) for the first special. A few months later, Variety reported that Hope had signed with Frigidaire for six more NBC specials, also for $40,000 apiece (or about $555,000 today).

Popular on Variety

Hope would go on to host another 283 variety and comedy specials for NBC over the ensuing 46 years. The run, which included specials broadcast from behind the lines during the Vietnam War, remains a hallmark of longevity between a star and a network. It helped cement NBC’s reputation as a home for big entertainment specials and live events.

Bob Hope (1903-2003) honed his comedy chops in the waning years of vaudeville, grinding his way through short sets and long bills in the late 1920s and ‘30s. That experience set him up for a nearly 60-year run of hosting TV variety specials for NBC. #NBC100@nbc @UniversalTV pic.twitter.com/EmStRt0xh6 — Variety (@Variety) October 12, 2026

In radio and TV, NBC has consistently invested in special events to offset its regularly scheduled series. Some were designed to draw huge crowds to one-night-only performances, such as the famed 1983 concert special “Motown 25: Yesterday, Today, Forever.” Some were designed to become annual traditions, such as the Tournament of Roses parade, the Rockefeller Center Christmas Tree Lighting and the reigning champion of NBC’s holiday specials, the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade.

“Today’s special is money in the bank for both the sponsor and the network,” Variety reported in 1957, when we also noted that ABC and CBS had gone “spec-happy,” following NBC’s lead.

For NBC, the company born as a radio network that is marking its 100th anniversary this year, the specials tradition endures. NBC delivered a surprise smash 13 years ago with an ambitious live musical staging of “The Sound of Music” starring Carrie Underwood. More recently, NBC brought Cynthia Erivo and Ariana Grande together for the musical special late last year, “Wicked: One Wonderful Night” that doubled as promotion for Universal Pictures’ theatrical release of “Wicked: For Good.”

Cynthia Erivo and Ariana Grande perform on 2025’s “Wicked: One Wonderful Night” special Griffin Nagel/NBC

NBC has a proud history of airing landmark concert specials, from “Motown 25” in 1983 to Elvis Presley’s legendary 1968 comeback vehicle to last year’s “Wicked: One Wonderful Night.” #NBC100@nbc @UniversalTV pic.twitter.com/hJU25QIWLO — Variety (@Variety) October 13, 2026

Many of NBC’s top franchises are decades-old traditions that have become part of the annual calendar for viewers, a way to mark time between seasons. That’s a gift from NBC’s stewards of the past to the current generation of executives. Jen Neal, executive VP of live events and specials for NBC and Peacock, never takes it for granted.

“The audience’s desire for these communal experiences are as vital as ever — even more so today than in past years because there’s so much going on in the world,” Neal tells Variety. “At a time when media is very fragmented and there are so many options and so many places that you can consume content, live TV still remains one of the most powerful ways to bring people together.”

For advertisers as well as viewers, there’s something extra special about reaching viewers at a time when they’re likely to be reflective and nostalgic, especially around the holiday season.

“Live TV events does this differently than anything else,” Neal says. “NBCUniversal does that extraordinarily across sports and Olympics and news. But with the big live specials, it’s truly the place that you can bring people together for those habitual patterns during certain times of year.”

Here’s a look at some of the event-izing of its airwaves in roughly its first 50 years.

1938

Bob Hope is tapped to host NBC’s “The Pepsodent Show,” which vaults him to radio stardom and begins Hope’s 60-year partnership with NBC.

Bob Hope Getty Images

1951

NBC televises the annual Christmas tree lighting in Rockefeller Center for the first time as part of “The Kate Smith Show.”

1953

The Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade airs on NBC as an hourlong special. In 1969, the parade telecast expanded to three hours. Today, the broadcast draws more than 20 million viewers. This year marks the 100th anniversary of the parade.

The Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade in 1999 Craig Blankenhorn/NBCU Photo Ban

1954

NBC owner RCA introduces its cutting-edge color television system with the New Year’s Day broadcast of the Tournament of Roses parade.

1964

NBC first airs the Golden Globes. By the 2000s, the show was enshrined as an important precursor to the Oscars. Ricky Gervais as well as Tina Fey and Amy Poehler are among the NBC-affiliated stars who made multiple appearances as hosts of the kudocast during the NBCUniversal era.

Tina Fey and Amy Poehler host the Golden Globe Awards in 2013 Paul Drinkwater/NBC

1968

“Elvis, the ’68 Comeback Special” marks Elvis Presley’s return to live performances. It is renowned as one of the most-watched concert specials of all time.

Elvis Presley from his 1968 comeback special NBCU Photo Bank

1974

“The Dean Martin Celebrity Roast” series of specials begins a 10-year stretch of bawdy ribbing and playful skewering. Guests included everyone from then-California Gov. Ronald Reagan to Truman Capote to Joe Namath.

Dean Martin, Don Rickles and Orson Welles on an early installment of “The Dean Martin Celebrity Roast.” Paul W. Baley/NBC

1976

NBC airs the 4½-hour special “NBC: The First 50 Years.”

(Pictured top: Bob Hope and George Burns)

title: Jamie Foxx Boards Indie Crime Thriller ‘East of the River’ as Producer (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Jamie Foxx has joined the indie crime thriller “East of the River” as a producer. He boards through his Foxxhole Productions alongside Alex Marks. The film, directed by Dennis Latos, follows two estranged brothers reuniting to face the underground poker ring that destroyed their family. The film stars Ben Barnes (“The Chronicles of Narnia” franchise, […]
content:
Jamie Foxx has joined the indie crime thriller “East of the River” as a producer. He boards through his Foxxhole Productions alongside Alex Marks.

The film, directed by Dennis Latos, follows two estranged brothers reuniting to face the underground poker ring that destroyed their family. The film stars Ben Barnes (“The Chronicles of Narnia” franchise, “The Punisher”), Ben Ahlers (“The Gilded Age,” “Little Brother”), Callie Hernandez (“The Flight Attendant,” “Alien: Covenant”) and Maria Sten in here first film role since starring in television’s “Neagley.”

The cast also includes David Zayas (“Dexter,” “Dexter: Resurrection”), John Bedford Lloyd (“Ozark”, “The Bourne Supremacy”), Catherine Curtin (“Stranger Things,” “Orange Is the New Black”), Nathan Wallace (“Daredevil: Born Again,” “NCIS: Origins”), and Steven Gregory (“Gravesend”). The film also features former WWE wrestler James Storm and former NFL running back Dalvin Cook.

Popular on Variety

Post-production of the film recently wrapped. Global distribution rights are available through CAA Media Finance.

“East of the River” was and written by Elise Finnerty with story by Jim Tamburino. Ben Grant served as director of photography on the film.

In addition to Foxx and Marks, the film is produced by Nicolas Alvo at Ruta 5 Films, and Benjamin Wiessner at Vanishing Angle, alongside Latos and Finnerty. Executive producers include David Schuster of Gloves Up Entertainment Steven Gregory, John Harms, Gerry Ambrose and Foxx’s daughter Corinne Foxx. The film is presented by Gloves Up Entertainment in association with Echo Bend Productions.

“We’ve been fans of Dennis since first discovering his short film, ‘Leylak’, where his command of character and storytelling immediately stood out. This film is a powerful continuation of that voice, and we’re proud to support this exceptional project,” Jamie and Corrine Foxx and Marks said in a joint statement.

Latos said, “I wanted to capture the kinetic, dangerous energy of a world most people never see. This isn’t just a story about poker, it’s a high-octane look at what happens when you’re backed into a corner and forced to gamble with your life. We’ve fused a gritty family drama with the pulse-pounding stakes of the criminal underworld to give the audience a cinematic experience that is both deeply felt and truly thrilling.”

Schuster added, “When Dennis Latos and I set out to make our first independent feature film, I never imagined that we’d have such a talented cast and amazing crew. With Dennis and I originally being from Queens, this project is close to our hearts. I am grateful to our amazing producing partners, Jamie, Alex, Nicolas, Benjamin, and Elise.”

Barnes is represented by Gersh, Luber Roklin Entertainment and ID Public Relations. Ahlers is represented by Gersh, Artists First and Felker Toczek Suddleson McGinnis Ryan LLP. Hernandez is represented by Independent Artist Group, Entertainment 360 and Paul Hastings. Sten is represented by CAA, Brillstein Entertainment Partners, The Initiative Group and Granderson Des Rochers. Zayas is represented by Buchwald, ATA Management, Jill Fritzo Public Relations and Schreck Rose Dapello Adams Berlin & Dunham. Bedford Lloyd is represented by CESD Talent Agency. Curtin is represented by Artists & Representatives, Fusion Entertainment and Sullivan Talent Group. Wallace is represented by UIA Talent & Brian Twohig of Roger Paul Talent. Gregory is represented by Bright Artists Management.

title: Doug Belgrad Leaving As Netflix VP Of Film Amid Layoffs
summary: Doug Belgrad is departing Netflix where he has been Vice President of Film for more than two years. His exit, which was confirmed by the streamer, is part of the major layoffs at Netflix today. Ironically, Belgrad was Head of Film Dan Lin‘s first hire after a round of layoffs when Lin replaced Scott Stuber […]
content:
Doug Belgrad is departing Netflix where he has been Vice President of Film for more than two years. His exit, which was confirmed by the streamer, is part of the major layoffs at Netflix today.

Ironically, Belgrad was Head of Film Dan Lin‘s first hire after a round of layoffs when Lin replaced Scott Stuber and restructured Netflix’s film department.

There have been rumblings of late that there would be a shake-up in the motion picture department at Netflix. This due to the decline in viewership for their movies, i.e. during the first half of 2026, features clocked 23 billion hours of viewership, -3.1% vs previous cycles. In an effort to stunt their movies more, Netflix for the first time is committing to longer windows (on some titles) in theaters and will be reporting grosses on such movies as Cannes winner La Bola Negra, David Fincher’s The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, Peter Berg’s Mosquito Bowl, Danny Boyle’s Ink, Greta Gerwig’s Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew and animated title Charlie and the Chocolate Factory. This all occurring after losing their bid to buy Warner Bros. Studios. There’s been heavy gossip that former Warner Bros Studio heads Michael De Luca and Pam Abdy would be going over to the streamer, however, sources say their recent lunches with CEO Ted Sarandos were merely on a peer basis. Netflix would need to make a fire breathing commitment to theatrical for De Luca and Abdy to make the segue to the streamer; the duo recently passed over by Skydance co-CEO David Ellison for top posts at the Paramount-Warner Bros merger.

When Belgrad arrived at Netflix, there were four challenges: There wasn’t enough product in the pipeline, the streamer was known for overspending, post-production would drag out and filmmakers weren’t always supported with editorial feedback. Lin and Belgrad addressed these issues and there’s now a full slate of titles through 2028. Belgrad focused much of his time on shepherding filmmakers through the post-production.

Watch on Deadline

While at Netflix, Belgrad supervised a team of 35 production executives. Belgrad also tended to Sony’s output deal at Netflix. In addition to being a billion dollar pay one deal, the pact also calls for Sony to funnel a number of direct-to-streaming movies to Netflix (the Culver City lot was responsible for the streamer’s most watched movie ever Kpop Demon Hunters, which also doubled as Netflix’s first movie to open at No. 1 at the weekend box office in late August 2025). Belgrad worked with Sony leadership’s of Tom Rothman, Sanford Panitch and Elizabeth Gabler, to identify which pictures would fill direct-to-Netflix slots. These movies included People We Meet on Vacation, Voicemals from Isabelle (51M views in 11 days), and 72 Hours starring Kevin Hart. Other direct Sony-to-Netflix movies in the pipeline are Grown Ups 3 (Belgrad was the exec on the first two movies at Sony), Matter of Time with Ben Stiller, and Yeti starring Chris Pine.

Before joining Netflix in May 2024, Belgrad spent 25 years at Sony Pictures, and was ultimately co-president under Amy Pascal. He joined the Culver City lot in 1989 and was promoted to become co-president of production at Columbia in 2003 and president in 2008. He shepherded the Men in Black franchise, the Adam Sandler canon at Sony, and Oscar-nominated American Hustle and Captain Phillips, to name a few.

Upon stepping down from Sony as President of the Motion Picture Group in 2016, he formed 2.0 Entertainment, which was key in producing and co-financing such Sony movies as Gran Turismo and the last two Bad Boys, 2024’s Bad Boys: Ride Or Die and Bad Boys for Life, the latter a massive pre-Covid hit grossing $426.5M and the highest in the franchise.

Belgrad is still the Chairman of 2.0. He’s not planning immediately to reunite with his former colleagues there, but a producing future isn’t out of the question. 2.0 is an active producer with not just Sony, but Paramount as well, co-financing such titles as the latter’s The Heart of the Beast, Primate, and the upcoming Children of Blood and Bone.

More to come.

title: Jami McGuigan Joins Select Management Group’s Canadian Team As Talent Manager
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Select Management Group, the next-generation talent management firm, today announced that veteran talent booker, producer, and strategic partnerships leader Jami McGuigan has joined the Select Canada team as a talent manager. McGuigan will help grow the company’s Canadian presence and scale its efforts to cultivate the next generation of Canadian talent. Her work will […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Select Management Group, the next-generation talent management firm, today announced that veteran talent booker, producer, and strategic partnerships leader Jami McGuigan has joined the Select Canada team as a talent manager.

McGuigan will help grow the company’s Canadian presence and scale its efforts to cultivate the next generation of Canadian talent. Her work will focus in particular on digital talk show and format creators, helping clients develop original programming and build partnerships with brands and media companies.

McGuigan joins as Select continues to expand its Canadian footprint following the January launch of its Toronto office, the company’s first international location. She brings over clients including Michael Mendieta and Roxie Nafousi.

Before joining Select, McGuigan worked with top media and entertainment properties including Comic Relief, Equality Now, and Bell Media across talent booking, strategic partnerships, and show development. Prior to that, she spent nearly a decade at The Late Show with Stephen Colbert, booking and producing musical performances, and worked on Broadway Video productions at 30 Rockefeller Plaza, including The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon.

Watch on Deadline

Earlier in her career, McGuigan helped book and produce events across the Dick Clark portfolio, including the Golden Globe Awards, American Music Awards, Academy of Country Music Awards, and Dick Clark’s New Year’s Rockin’ Eve. As a producer, her work has contributed to Emmy-, Peabody-, and Webby Award-winning productions.

“Jami has spent her career at the intersection of talent and entertainment, and she brings an incredible network and understanding of the industry to Select Canada,” said Select Management Group Partner and Head of East Coast Caroline Nardilla. “We’re excited to have her helping us discover and expand opportunities for the next generation of Canadian talent as we continue to grow our presence in the market.”

Since launching in January, Select Canada has gone from 20 to more than 40 creators on its talent roster. The Toronto office provides on-the-ground representation and support across 360-talent management and brand partnerships, while connecting next-generation Canadian talent to Select’s broader network across North America.

Whereas traditional agencies have gotten increasingly into the creator economy as time has gone on, with film & TV as foundational pillars, Select’s early expertise came in the creator space. They’re best known for representing stars of the Secret Lives of Mormon Wives franchise, and producing both the original Hulu show and its upcoming Orange County spin-off, out November 12.

Select Management is part of the Propagate Content family of companies, which also includes Artists First, Authentic Talent & Literary Management, Parker Management, and Sway Social, among others. In July, they announced the promotion of talent manager Paul Luckenbaugh to the newly created role of Head of Theatrical Talent, signaling their growing investment in filmed entertainment, amid the growing industrywide convergence of traditional and creator-led talent.

title: Mongolian-German Feature ‘Zogsool’ Wins Big At Busan Film Festival’s Vision Awards
summary: Mongolian-German feature Zogsool was the big winner in the Vision Awards at this year’s Busan International Film Festival, taking four prizes including the Vision of Jiseok Award. Directed by former cinematographer Sakhya Byamba, the film also took the NETPAC Award, FIPRESCI Award and one of two Hylife Vision Awards. Filmed on the Mongolian grasslands, the […]
content:
Mongolian-German feature Zogsool was the big winner in the Vision Awards at this year’s Busan International Film Festival, taking four prizes including the Vision of Jiseok Award.

Directed by former cinematographer Sakhya Byamba, the film also took the NETPAC Award, FIPRESCI Award and one of two Hylife Vision Awards. Filmed on the Mongolian grasslands, the film portrays the chaos of the early days of the Covid pandemic.

Other multiple award winners included Full Moon from Korea’s Jeong Jihye, which took the CGV Award, K-Movie Award and Songwon Vision Audience Award for a Korean film.

Selvi, a Tamil-language drama from India’s Sailesh Rathnakumar, won the other Hylife Vision Award as well as the Taipei Film Commission Award. Other Indian winners included Birds In The Dark, directed by Shashank Walia, which won the Songwon Vision Audience Award for an Asian film.

Watch on Deadline

BIFF Mecenat Awards went to Yang Bo’s China-France co-production Agaar and Can I Talk To You? from Korea’s Yi Seungjun, while A Woman Dancing On The Waves, from Choi Se-Dam, was given a Special Mention.

The Heart Of Eurasia Award was presented to Ria, directed by the Philippines’ Arvin Belarmino. (See full list of award winners below). Busan International Film Festival’s awards ceremony for the main competition section will be held on October 15.

title: Avatar Entertainment Adapting Vicente Vallés Novel ‘La Caza Del Ejecutor’ As TV Series
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Avatar Entertainment has acquired rights to Spanish journalist Vicente Vallés’ novel Hunting the Executioner (La Caza del Ejecutor). The London- and L.A.-based production and management company and content financier has attached screenwriters Borja Moreno and Pablo Riquelme Cuartero to adapt the book into an eight-part TV shows. Avatar founder Larry Robinson is executive producing […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Avatar Entertainment has acquired rights to Spanish journalist Vicente Vallés’ novel Hunting the Executioner (La Caza del Ejecutor).

The London- and L.A.-based production and management company and content financier has attached screenwriters Borja Moreno and Pablo Riquelme Cuartero to adapt the book into an eight-part TV shows. Avatar founder Larry Robinson is executive producing the project. No streamer or network attached at this stage.

Hunting the Executioner follows a handsome American CIA agent who partners with a beautiful Spanish secret agent as they travel the world trying to identify and neutralize a mysterious assassin killing western spies throughout the world.

This is the second novel written by journalist Vallés, a veteran newscaster who anchors the evening news on Spanish broadcaster Antena 3. His previous novel Operation Kazan was once set up at Universal Television, though the story involving a Russian-backed U.S. Presidential candidate ultimately was put into turnaround. Moreno and Cuartero had been hired by Universal to it.

Watch on Deadline

Robinson, who spoke with Deadline in Cannes at MIPCOM, said: “I am excited to work with the legendary Vicente Vallés, Pablo Riquelme Cuartero and Borja Moreno to develop this exciting book into a super premium action thriller series that could air around the world.”

The news comes Avatar signed an agreement for the rights to the Katy Hogan novel Out of the Darkness, Robert Enright’s bestselling Sam Pope action book series, and Mary Dearborn’s biography of Ernest Hemingway for a TV adaptation.

Moreno and Riquelme Cuartero are managed by Avatar, while Vallés’ novel is published by Editorial Espasa part of Grupo Planeta. Robinson and Avatar are repped by CAA.

title: Netflix Layoffs Underway, Streamer Cutting 1,000 Jobs, 6% Of Workforce
summary: Netflix has initiated a major round of layoffs Wednesday, eliminating about 6% of its global staff or some 1,000 jobs for its biggest round of job cuts in four years. The product, tech, legal and HR teams are among the most impacted by the cuts, which have been expected as the company faces slower growth […]
content:
Netflix has initiated a major round of layoffs Wednesday, eliminating about 6% of its global staff or some 1,000 jobs for its biggest round of job cuts in four years.

The product, tech, legal and HR teams are among the most impacted by the cuts, which have been expected as the company faces slower growth and increased competition.

Co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters unveiled the move in a memo to employees this morning, a copy of which was obtained by Deadline (read it below). A rep for Netflix had no comment.

“Decisions like these are never easy, and we don’t take them lightly,” the CEOs wrote. “Our mission — to entertain the world — is ambitious, and delivering on it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritize our people and resources. Our business is strong and growing, and we remain on track to deliver our full-year forecast. We’ll continue to invest aggressively in high-impact areas to improve our service and further drive growth and innovation. Doing that means making focused choices across the business so we can keep delivering for our members, partners, employees, and investors.”

Sarandos and Peters acknowledged the challenging media environment, calling it “one of the most dynamic times in the history of entertainment” that is “perfectly suited to a company like ours that’s built at the intersection of technology and entertainment,” adding, “Now it’s on us to step up and meet the moment.”

Watch on Deadline

Other tech and media companies that have been undergoing layoffs include Amazon and Disney, with newly merged Skydance expected to soon join them.

Netflix had not had major layoffs since the big staff reduction of 2022, with the February product division cuts of several dozen employees among the most notable ones.

The share price of the giant streamer has dropped more than 40% over the past year (off 25% year to date) as Wall Street has increasingly scrutinized its viewer engagement, which increased only 2% over the first half of the year to 97 billion hours viewed. The stock is trending down about 1% in late-morning trade today at just under $70, a big comedown from a 52-week high of $125.

Sarandos addressed the topic of engagement earlier this month at a Bloomberg conference. “Overall, we’re not growing as fast as I want us to, and we’re working on making that move faster,” he said.

The company’s unsuccessful bid for the Warner Bros studio and streaming assets also spooked Wall Street as investors took it as a sign the company felt it needed a major deal to continue to grow, a notion Netflix’s top executives have dismissed.

Additionally, the streamer has gone through one of its longest droughts without a breakout new series that has captured the zeitgeist the way shows like Stranger Things, Squid Game, Bridgerton, Queen’s Gambit, Wednesday, Baby Reindeer and, most recently, Adolescence, did. (It recently found success with its latest Harlan Coben adaptation I Will Find You, which landed on the Most Popular English series list.) Netflix also is coming off a rare third-place finish at the Emmys behind rivals Apple TV and HBO.

Interest in Netflix’s existing series is showing signs of waning too, with many returning series posting season-to-season viewership declines.

The streamer has been shifting strategy by leaning into live events including sports — with upcoming NFL Thanksgiving Eve and Christmas Day games and the Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua boxing match — as well as video podcasts and creator-driven content. It launched an advertising tier in 2022 and started cracking down on password sharing in 2023. Last March, it raised the prices of its U.S. plans, the second hike in a little over a year, and also has tried bundling.

The company has been raising its profile in theatrical distribution with its upcoming features The Mis-adventures of Cliff Booth, La Bola Negra and Possible Love all set for theatrical release before hitting the platform along with Greta Gerwig’s Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew, which hits Imax screens in February of 2027 ahead of a wide release.

RELATED: First Trailer For Greta Gerwig’s ‘Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew’ Teases Punk Rock Multiverse & Cosmic Creation Of Aslan

Coming up on the series front are The Hunting Wives S2, The Diplomat S4, the final season of Emily in Paris, Pride and Prejudice, and Lupin: Part 4.

In the most recent second quarter, Netflix reported revenue growth of 13% year over year to $12.6 billion, and operating margin was 33%. The company reports Q3 earnings October 20.

Here is Sarandos and Peters’ memo in full:

Team – We wanted to share that we are making a number of organizational changes and, as a result, we’ll be letting go of roughly 6% of our colleagues, with the greatest impact to our product, tech, legal, and HR teams.



Decisions like these are never easy, and we don’t take them lightly. Our top priority today is to support those who are leaving Netflix. The process will vary somewhat by country, but leaders will be connecting with impacted employees soon. If you are leaving, please know that we will support you throughout this transition and make sure you have as much clarity and context as possible. We also want to say thank you. What you’ve built, and the care you brought to Netflix, have made a lasting difference and we will always be grateful.



For the rest of the team, we know you have questions, too. Our mission – to entertain the world – is ambitious, and delivering on it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritize our people and resources. Our business is strong and growing, and we remain on track to deliver our full-year forecast. We’ll continue to invest aggressively in high-impact areas to improve our service and further drive growth and innovation. Doing that means making focused choices across the business so we can keep delivering for our members, partners, employees, and investors.



We know changes like this are tough, but let’s stay focused. This is one of the most dynamic times in the history of entertainment – and it’s a moment perfectly suited to a company like ours that’s built at the intersection of technology and entertainment. Now it’s on us to step up and meet the moment, together, like we always do.



Ted and Greg



Jill Goldsmith contributed to this report

title: Variety’s 2026 Artisans to Watch: ‘Obsession’ Makeup Head, ‘Project Hail Mary’ Animation Supervisor, ‘La Bola Negra’ Composer and More
summary: In 2026, moviegoers came back to cinemas, packing theaters to see blockbusters like “The Odyssey,” “Project Hail Mary,” “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” “Toy Story 5,” “Michael” and “The Super Mario Galaxy Movie” and low-budget films like “Backrooms” and “Obsession.” But all those movies needed skilled artisans to complete the directors’ visions, including those on Variety’s […]
content:
Cinematographer, “The Invite”, “Club Kid”

Newport-Berra’s range is on display in two films this awards season: “The Invite,” directed by and starring Olivia Wilde, and “Club Kid,” directed by and starring Jordan Firstman.

“I tend to enjoy working with actor-directors because we get this dynamic experience on set where they get to direct the film both from outside and from within during the scene, which I think is a special opportunity for a director to be inside the moment,” Newport-Berra says.

“The Invite” takes place over one night and follows two dynamic couples inside one apartment. The premise provided Wilde and Newport-Berra with a creative challenge. “We loved the script, but we thought, ‘How do we make this really sing on screen?’ It can’t just feel like a play. It can’t just be about presenting the material. It needs to be dynamic.”

Newport-Berra sought ways to liberate his camera within the confines of the space.

With no big cranes available, lensing and composition had to tell the story. “Olivia and I looked through a lot of references, took a lot of photos and talked about why certain images make us feel awkward, seduced, anxious or in love,” he explains.

“We really used composition and the focal lengths of our lenses to either compress people and make things feel flat and claustrophobic, or we would use a wider lens to make it feel very intimate, gentle, sexy and seductive.”

“Club Kid” emphasizes the character dynamics. Firstman’s Peter finds his life turned upside down after years of partying in New York clubs when he learns he has a 10-year-old son, Arlo (Reggie Absolom). Newport-Berra wanted to handle the relationship between Reggie and Jordan’s characters with care. “It was through rehearsals, and every morning, Jordan and I would check in, read through the script together, and feel whatever we were feeling that day,” Newport-Berra says. — J.T.

title: ‘Maximum Pleasure Guaranteed’ Renewed for Season 2 at Apple TV
summary: “Maximum Pleasure Guaranteed” has been renewed for a second season at Apple TV. Per the official logline, the series stars “follows newly divorced mom Paula (Tatiana Maslany) as she falls down a dangerous rabbit hole of blackmail, murder and youth soccer. Convinced she witnessed a crime — while simultaneously struggling through a custody battle and […]
content:
“Maximum Pleasure Guaranteed” has been renewed for a second season at Apple TV.

Per the official logline, the series stars “follows newly divorced mom Paula (Tatiana Maslany) as she falls down a dangerous rabbit hole of blackmail, murder and youth soccer. Convinced she witnessed a crime — while simultaneously struggling through a custody battle and an identity crisis — Paula begins her own investigation, one that could unravel a greater conspiracy while also holding the keys to rebuilding her family and sense of self.”

The cast also includes Jake Johnson as Paula’s ex-husband Karl alongside Murray Bartlett, Dolly De Leon, Brandon Flynn, Jessy Hodges, Jon Michael Hill, Charlie Hall, Kiarra Hamagami Goldberg and Nola Wallace.

Popular on Variety

David J. Rosen created “Maximum Pleasure Guaranteed” and serves as showrunner. Executive producers include Rosen and director David Gordon Green as well as Simon Kinberg Audrey Chon and Anonymous Content’s Bard Dorros, who developed the project. Apple Studios and Counterpart Studios produce.

“We are delighted to continue the story of ‘MPG’ and deeply grateful to Apple and our incredible cast and crew. This is all pretty amazing for a show whose title came from a spam email,” Rosen said in a statement.

Speaking to Variety about the twist in the Season 1 finale, Rosen said, “I always intended it to be a reframing. We’ve felt Paula is a reliable narrator, but we feel moments of unreliability. As Karl says over and over, she’s eccentric, acting in a way that’s not consistent. The audience is like, ‘Screw you, Karl! She’s going through a lot right now!’ But what we come to realize in the end is that something more was afoot. Paula is more complicated than we thought.”

title: Bob Daly to Step Down as Chair of AFI Board of Directors (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: After 17 years of leadership, Bob Daly will step down as chair of the American Film Institute Board of Directors at the next trustee meeting on Wednesday, Oct. 21, Variety can reveal exclusively. Daly, former Warner Bros. chair and co-CEO, joined the AFI Board in April 1981 and was named chair on Oct. 8, 2009, […]
content:
After 17 years of leadership, Bob Daly will step down as chair of the American Film Institute Board of Directors at the next trustee meeting on Wednesday, Oct. 21, Variety can reveal exclusively.

Daly, former Warner Bros. chair and co-CEO, joined the AFI Board in April 1981 and was named chair on Oct. 8, 2009, succeeding co-chairs Jon Avnet and John Cooke.

“In a career that brought me from running CBS to Warner Bros. to the Los Angeles Dodgers, I can honestly say that serving as Chairman of the AFI Board of Directors has been one of the greatest honors of my life,” said Daly. “This is a board that represents all aspects of the film and television communities, and to see they come together with a shared passion for the art form has been a wonder to behold. Long live the AFI!”

Daly’s expansive history in Hollywood touched some of the most powerful institutions in the entertainment business, including CBS Entertainment, Warner Music Group, the Los Angeles Dodgers and, of course, Warner Bros. He began his career at CBS as a gofer in 1955. He spent 25 years at the network and eventually served as its president, overseeing all television operations. After his time at CBS, Daly joined Warner Bros. as chairman and co-CEO in 1980. During his 19 years at the studio, he and his co-CEO, Terry Semel, were credited with 16 consecutive years of record earnings. They also supervised the release of 13 Best Picture Oscar nominees, and snagged three wins with “Chariots of Fire,” “Driving Miss Daisy” and “Unforgiven.”

Popular on Variety

Following his time at WB, Daly joined the Los Angeles Dodgers as chair and CEO for four years before selling the team in 2004. Daly also served as chair of the charity Save the Children.

“Leadership is an art in itself — and in that regard, Mr. Daly is a master,” said Bob Gazzale, AFI president & CEO. “Over the past forty years, no single person has had a greater impact on AFI’s work in preservation, celebration and education than Bob Daly — and we have promised to march forward each day with a promise to prove him proud.”

The AFI, founded in 1967, is a nonprofit organization created to preserve the heritage of the motion picture, to honor the artists and their work and to educate the next generation of storytellers. Former Lucasfilm president Kathleen Kennedy serves as chair of the AFI Board of Trustees, which includes Avnet, Pam Abdy, Sean Astin, Alan Bergman, Halle Berry, Jim Breyer, James L. Brooks, Ava DuVernay, Jamie Erlicht, Rich Frank, Mike Hopkins, Alan Horn, Patty Jenkins, Michael B. Jordan, Donna Langley, Eva Longoria, Bryan Lourd, Christopher Nolan, Edward James Olmos, Shonda Rhimes, Charles Rivkin, Jay Roach, Ted Sarandos, Chris Silbermann, Octavia Spencer, Steven Spielberg, Todd Wagner and Edward Zwick.

title: Box Office: ‘Street Fighter’ Aims for $30 Million Opening, ‘You Can See Everything’ Could Score $8 Million Start
summary: Strength in numbers? Movie theater operators are hoping the adage proves true as four new movies aim to bolster the October box office. Paramount’s video game adaptation “Street Fighter” will lead over fellow newcomers, with opening weekend estimates of $25 million to $35 million from 3,500 North American theaters. Disney’s survival thriller “Whalefall” should secure […]
content:
Strength in numbers? Movie theater operators are hoping the adage proves true as four new movies aim to bolster the October box office.

Paramount’s video game adaptation “Street Fighter” will lead over fellow newcomers, with opening weekend estimates of $25 million to $35 million from 3,500 North American theaters. Disney’s survival thriller “Whalefall” should secure second place with $10 million to $12 million from 3,065 venues. Meanwhile A24’s much-hyped Elizabeth Holmes documentary “You Can See Everything” is aiming for a strong $7 million to $8 million from just 800 locations, and the Focus Features remake of Jane Austen’s “Sense and Sensibility” is targeting $5 million to $8 million from 2,436 screens.

Although “Street Fighter” is projected to claim the No. 1 spot, the PG-13 action-adventure carries the biggest budget among the quartet and will need to stick around in theaters to justify its price tag. Legendary and video game developer Capcom co-financed the film for $82 million, with Paramount only on the hook for distribution. The long-gestating “Street Fighter” was originally set at Sony as part of Legendary’s pact with the studio and moved to Paramount once the initial deal expired. Overseas, “Street Fighter” is projected to earn roughly $35 million from 65 markets.

Popular on Variety

“Street Fighter” is the third movie based on the Capcom video game series. The first live-action film, released in 1994 and starred Jean-Claude Van Damme, was box office hit with $100 million, not adjusted for inflation. The second, 2009’s “Street Fighter: The Legend of Chun-Li,” was a major misfire for 20th Century, earning just $12.8 million against a $50 million budget. This reboot, directed by Kitao Sakurai and starring Noah Centineo and Andrew Koji, takes place in 1993 as two estranged fighters are recruited to enter a tournament that forces them to face off against each other.

“Whalefall” cost $60 million and also requires substantial staying power, since theater owners keep about half of ticket sales. Directed by Brian Duffield, “Whalefall” follows a scuba diver (Austin Abrams) who is swallowed by a sperm whale and has only one hour of oxygen left in his tank as he figures out how to escape. Reviews have been mostly positive, with one critic calling the film “amusing genre pulp.”

“You Can See Everything” cost around $7 million to produce, and exhibitors believe the movie could become the rare breakout documentary. Earlier this year, Amazon MGM’s “Melania,” a $40-million-budgeted glimpse at first lady Melania Trump, landed the biggest opening for a non-music or concert doc in over a decade with $7.1 million from 1,778 theaters. Most non-fiction films, however, would be lucky these days to earn that much by the end of their box office runs.

Hype for “You Can See Everything” has been high since A24 unveiled the top-secret project at Telluride Film Festival in early September. Comedian Nathan Fielder and “Primetime” filmmaker Lance Oppenheim quietly worked for more than three years on the movie, which offers an unhinged look at the Theranos founder a month before she began an 11-year prison sentence for defrauding investors. The doc will benefit from stellar reviews and positive word-of-mouth; it holds a 100% on Rotten Tomatoes, with Variety’s Owen Gleiberman describing the unconventional story as a “one-of-a-kind [ …] circus.”

“Sense and Sensibility,” which carries a $25 million budget, hopes to serve as counterprogramming against the male-skewing “Street Fighter” and “Whalefall.” Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles star in the latest adaptation of the Jane Austen classic as sisters Elinor and Marianne Dashwood, who navigate love, loss and financial uncertainty as they are forced to leave their family estate in Sussex.

“Sense and Sensibility” has been reworked for the screen a number of times, most notably with director Ang Lee’s 1995 film starring Emma Thompson and Kate Winslet as Elinor and Marianne Dashwood. That film was a critical and commercial smash, earning seven Oscar nominations and generating $135 million at the box office, not adjusted for inflation. Focus Features over the years has backed two prior remakes of Austen’s work, including the 2005 version of “Pride and Prejudice” with Keira Knightley and Matthew Macfadyen as well as 2020’s “Emma,” which starred Anya-Taylor Joy. The well-reviewed “Emma” was released digitally while theaters were closed due to the pandemic.

So far, the October box office has been uneven. Tom Cruise’s dark comedy “Digger” and Aaron Sorkin’s Facebook drama “The Social Reckoning” flopped, while Colleen Hoover adaptation “Verity” and “Other Mommy” with Jessica Chastain are shaping up to be modest wins. Luckily, it won’t take much to improve upon last October, which hit a three-decade low amid a pileup of disasters including Dwayne Johnson’s MMA drama “The Smashing Machine” and Disney’s sci-fi sequel “Tron: Ares.”

title: Warner Records Names Jim Roppo Vice Chairman
summary: Just hours after his departure from Republic Records was announced, Jim Roppo has been officially named vice chairman of Warner Records Group. He will be based in Los Angeles and report to Chairman & CEO Aaron Bay-Schuck; his start date will be confirmed in the coming weeks. Roppo joins the company following nearly three decades […]
content:
Just hours after his departure from Republic Records was announced, Jim Roppo has been officially named vice chairman of Warner Records Group. He will be based in Los Angeles and report to Chairman & CEO Aaron Bay-Schuck; his start date will be confirmed in the coming weeks.

Roppo joins the company following nearly three decades at Universal Music Group, where he most recently served as Chairman and CEO of Republic Records, overseeing global strategy, operations, and artist development. Prior to that, he was President and COO of Republic Collective, an umbrella group housing flagship imprints including Republic, Island, Def Jam, and Mercury.

Bay-Schuck said, “Everything we do is rooted in artist development, and Jim has spent his career ensuring that creatives have the tools, resources, and support to reach their full potential. Few have excelled across so many parts of our business – from digital to commerce to marketing – and that range, paired with a track record of breaking stars, will be invaluable as we accelerate the next phase of growth for Warner Records Group.”

Popular on Variety

Roppo added, “I’m excited to join Warner Records at such an important moment, with undeniable momentum across the roster. My focus has always been on backing great music and helping teams win, and I look forward to bringing that to Warner. My biggest thanks to Aaron for this opportunity.”

Roppo joins a company that has seen recent success with releases from Madonna, Zach Bryan, Sombr, Benson Boone, Teddy Swims, Linkin Park and more.

title: ‘Street Fighter’ With $70M WW Global Start & ‘The Devils’ Are First Paramount & Warner Bros Pics Opening Post-Merger – Preview
summary: Here we go. The first two movies under the newly combined Paramount Warner Bros merger, Legendary’s Street Fighter via the Melrose lot and Clockwork’s limited 4K re-release of Ken Russell’s 1971 The Devils, hit theaters this weekend in what is a future of titles dated on top of each other, appealing to myriad demos. Skydance […]
content:
Here we go.

The first two movies under the newly combined Paramount Warner Bros merger, Legendary’s Street Fighter via the Melrose lot and Clockwork’s limited 4K re-release of Ken Russell’s 1971 The Devils, hit theaters this weekend in what is a future of titles dated on top of each other, appealing to myriad demos.

Skydance co-CEO David Ellison yearned to merge the two historic studios in order to scale up and compete in a hyper-changing entertainment business. And scale up, Ellison is achieving.

For the period of Jan. 1-Oct. 11, the combined domestic box office for Paramount and Warner Bros stands at $941.6M, ranking fourth behind Universal ($1.86B), Disney ($1.6B) and Sony ($1.37B). The billion threshold stateside is feasibly within reach for the new Skydance with six Paramount/Warner Bros movies left to release this year including next weekend’s R-rated DC genre title Clayface, family animated WB title The Cat in the Hat (Nov. 6), Paramount’s Johnny Deep edgy Ebenezer (Nov. 13), Legendary’s sci-fi tentpole Dune: Part 3 (Dec. 18), family title The Angry Birds 3 (Dec. 23) and Mr. Irrelevant (Dec. 25).

A No. 1 global and domestic rank is expected this weekend in the feature take of legacy Capcom fisticuffs videogame Street Fighter with a high $30Ms domestic and mid $30M international start resulting in a near $70M global opening or more. There’s often comps between the 1987 born arcade game to its rival 1992 conceived Midway martial arts videogame Mortal Kombat. However, when it comes to box office comps, there’s a desire to steer clear of coming Street Fighter to the recent New Line Mortal Kombat movies which respectively opened at $23.3M in 2021 (which was a Covid day-and-date release on HBO Max) and this past summer’s sequel which debuted to $38.5M in North America. Reason being is that Mortal Kombat was R, and Street Fighter is PG-13, hence there’s an opportunity around the world to bring in families and younger men under 18. Also, Street Fighter is less violent. Mortal Kombat II undelivered overseas next to domestic, $49.8M to $79.8M. The hope and the plan is for Street Fighter to play to a much broader age group.

Watch on Deadline

First choice is best with men over and under 25 on the Legendary co-financed movie which was made for a net $82M with Capcom. Street Fighter is the first theatrical release under Legendary’s new global distribution deal with Paramount. No Rotten Tomatoes critical scores yet on the Kitao Sakurai directed movie which is booked at 3,500 theaters, and has a heavy Imax and PLF footprint. Previews start Thursday in U.S./Canada at 2PM with a 7PM fan event that has bonus footage and giveaways.

Street Fighter steps out everywhere overseas sans China where Paramount doesn’t have rights. In like-for-likes comps, Predator Badlands looks to be the right comparison which debuted to $31.2M overseas. Street Fighter should rally in Latin America, particularly Mexico and Brazil, the UK, Australia as well as Asia where the game is popular. No headwinds expected from local fare in Korea or Japan.

‘Ken Russell’s The Devils’ Warner Bros. Clockwork

Meanwhile, we’re hearing that Warner Bros Clockwork’s unearthed naughty Catholic movie, The Devils, is going in 350 playdates this weekend in key U.S./Canada cities. The Devils is the first theatrical release for the frosh genre auteur label led by Christian Parkes.

L-R: Austin Abrams and Josh Brolin in ‘ Whalefall 20th Century Studios

Also bowing is 20th Century Studios’ feature take of Daniel Kraus survival thriller novel, Whalefall, with $11M-$12m domestic in 3,000 theaters, and about the same overseas for a $24M WW start on the high end. Whalefall stars Austin Abrams, who is coming off hot with Resident Evil, as well as Josh Brolin and Elizabeth Shue. The net $60M production was shot here in the Golden State. Like-for-like overseas comps are the 20th Century movies The Amateur ($14.8M offshore start) and Send Help ($19M). The domestic launch counts 500 PLF screens including Dolby, 4D and D-Box. The Brian Duffield directed movie is going everywhere overseas except Denmark which will open on Oct. 22. Previews start Thursday at 2PM. The PG-13 movie is best with women under 25 and men over 25 in first choice.

L-R: Esmé Creed-Miles as Marianne Dashwood and Daisy Edgar-Jones as Elinor Dashwood in ‘ Sense And Sensibility Focus Features

In more diversified bookings, Focus Features has the remake of Jane Austen’s Sense and Sensibility starring Daisy Edgar-Jones and Caitríona Balfe which is hitting 2,436 theaters with an eye of $8M domestic for the mid-$20M Universal Working Title financed feature. This is a wider opening for Sense Sensibility versus Working Title and Focus’ pre-Covid Austen movie Emma which was platformed and at its widest point of 1,565 theaters posted a $4.8M weekend in the first weekend of March 2020, just before all cinemas shut down. First choice best with women over 25, followed by women under 25. The PG rated movie starts previews in U.S./Canada tomorrow at 2PM. Sense and Sensibility has already swooned UK, Norway and France with a combined running overseas cume of $8M. The Georgia Oakley directed movie is courting Germany and Australia tomorrow. Reviews stand at 76% fresh. The previous Oscar winning 1995 version starring Emma Thompson and Kate Winslet and directed by Ang Lee was 97% certified fresh on RT.

You Can See Everything‘ A24

With a very good shot to over perform is the A24 Lance Oppenheim and Nathan Fielder directed doc You Can See Everything which follows the latter’s interaction with fallen Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes before her federal prison stint. High single digits is what it’s looking like now for North America, but if the Gen Z crowd shows up, this could crack $10M+ at 800 theaters, which would be amazing. The most recent doc comp, Melania, opened to $7M on 1,700 theaters, which repped the best start for a documentary in a decade. You Can See Everything is on almost half of that theater count with hundreds of sellouts already. Shot over four years in secret, You Can See Everything cost under $10M and had a marketing campaign spend under $10M. Forty four reviews on RT are at 100%.

Also wide this weekend at 1,200 is the Roadside Attractions’ Ángel Gómez Hernández directed Crawlers. The second weekend of Universal and Blumhouse Atomic Monster’s D+ CinemaScore horror movie, Other Mommy, is expected to decline -60% to -70% in North America in its second frame after a No. 1. opening of $27.8M. Other Mommy through yesterday counts $33.5M at the domestic box office.

title: CAA Signs ‘Off Campus’ Star Ella Bright
summary: EXCLUSIVE: CAA has signed Ella Bright, the female lead of the hit romantic drama series Off Campus and upcoming comedy Narcs. Bright’s profile has risen quickly with the success of Off Campus, a romantic drama series from Prime Video based on the bestselling book series from Elle Kennedy, where she stars opposite Belmont Cameli. The […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: CAA has signed Ella Bright, the female lead of the hit romantic drama series Off Campus and upcoming comedy Narcs.

Bright’s profile has risen quickly with the success of Off Campus, a romantic drama series from Prime Video based on the bestselling book series from Elle Kennedy, where she stars opposite Belmont Cameli. The show has her playing Hannah Wells, an aspiring songwriter navigating college life and a complicated romance with its star hockey player.

Off Campus attracted 36 million viewers worldwide in its first 12 days, thereby bringing Amazon its third most-watched series debut of all time, behind only The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power and Fallout. In addition to starring in the series, Bright has performed and recorded several songs for its soundtrack, including “Baby Now That I Found You,” featuring Niall Horan, and “Girl That I Am,” written by Amy Allen. She recently wrapped filming the show’s second season, along with Gable, an indie true-life wrestling drama where she stars alongside Finn Cole and Ben Foster.

Off of the heat on Off Campus, Bright just inked to star opposite Mason Thames in the coming-of-age comedy Narcs, which will mark her first studio lead.

Watch on Deadline

Previously, the actor has been seen playing a young Kate Middleton on Netflix’s The Crown and starring in seven seasons of the British television series Malory Towers, for which she earned nominations at both the BAFTA Children’s Awards and the Children’s & Family Emmy Awards. She appears opposite Will Ferrell and John C. Reilly in the comedy Holmes & Watson and made her West End debut in Harry Potter and the Cursed Child in 2017.

Bright continues to be represented by Prime Talent Media, Accelerate in the UK, Derek Kroeger at Myman Greenspan, and Viewpoint.

A writers room is underway, we hear, with Season 2 production slated for the first half of 2027. Starring Emmy winner Tatiana Maslany and Jake Johnson, Maximum Pleasure Guaranteed follows […]
content:
Maximum Pleasure Guaranteed will be back for another go-round. Apple TV announced Wednesday that it has renewed the dark comedy thriller for a second season.

A writers room is underway, we hear, with Season 2 production slated for the first half of 2027.

Starring Emmy winner Tatiana Maslany and Jake Johnson, Maximum Pleasure Guaranteed follows newly divorced mom Paula (Maslany) as she falls down a dangerous rabbit hole of blackmail, murder and youth soccer. Convinced that she witnessed a crime — while simultaneously struggling through a custody battle and an identity crisis — Paula begins her own investigation, one that could unravel a greater conspiracy while also holding the keys to rebuilding her family and sense of self.

RELATED: 2026 TV Cancellations Photo Gallery: Series Ending This Year & Beyond

Watch on Deadline

The series hails from Apple Studios and Counterpart Studios and is written and executive produced by creator and showrunner David J. Rosen. David Gordon Green served as director and executive producer. The series is also developed by and executive produced by Simon Kinberg and Audrey Chon for Genre Films under their first-look deal with Apple TV, and Bard Dorros for Anonymous Content.

In addition to Maslany and Johnson, the ensemble cast is led by Murray Bartlett, Dolly De Leon, Brandon Flynn, Jessy Hodges, Jon Michael Hill, Charlie Hall, Kiarra Hamagami Goldberg and Nola Wallace.
