That codependent, dangerous relationship she has with him in some ways starts off very vulnerable and true and relatable. A lot of times I’m trying to figure out, ‘How do I relate to this person? How do I justify the things that they do?’”

A key win Kane had in developing the show was that “Crystal Lake” avoided the previous rights-holder complexities that have challenged films in the past. For example, the ninth and tenth installments — “Jason Goes to Hell: The Final Friday” and “Jason X” — couldn’t use the “Friday the 13th” moniker in the titles. Luckily, the previous friction had dissipated.

“There were really no issues rights-wise with the show,” Kane says. “We weren’t given any particular parameters about what we could and couldn’t do. There were discussions about the hockey mask, because that’s such an iconic look for Jason and that’s what everybody thinks about. But we’re doing a show that predates Pamela’s murder in the first movie, and the hockey mask … obviously, we all know that didn’t come until the third movie. This is the ‘Star Wars’ of slashers … It’s episode three.”

One critical component of getting the time and place to feel right was recreating the ’70s, rather than leaning on a corny pastiche or tired visual clichés. The quest for verisimilitude was essential for Kane.

“When I think of that texture to ’70s movies, I think of the paranoid ’70s thrillers that commented on the decade more accurately than anything else,” he says. “I think about ‘The Parallax View’ and ‘Klute’ and ‘All the President’s Men.’ There was a look and a feel to them. Movies like William Friedkin’s ‘Sorcerer’ … I didn’t want it to feel homage-y. I wanted it to feel steeped in the 70s. You could really go with the crazy things that are happening in the story and not feel like, ‘Oh, this is pageantry. This doesn’t feel real.’”

Ultimately, Kane believes “Crystal Lake” is buoyed by Cardellini, the not-so-secret weapon at the heart of the show.

“She’s in one great thing after another. It’s because she’s in them that they are elevated to the level that they are,” he says. “I really believe we’re doing a ‘Friday the 13th’ show here. There’s a question of whether it should be elevated to being peak TV, but she brings that to it. She brings gravitas, passion and authenticity to everything she does. Thankfully, she brought it to our show as well.”

Watch the trailer for “Crystal Lake” below. All eight episodes are now streaming on Peacock.

title: UK’s Bectu Union Unveils New Chief
summary: The UK’s broadcasting union has a new chief. Noel McClean has been appointed Head of Bectu and will take over from the retiring Philippa Childs early next year. McClean previously spent 13 years at Bectu, rising up to National Secretary, before he became a Deputy General Secretary at Bectu parent union Prospect. McClean described the […]
content:
The UK’s broadcasting union has a new chief.

Noel McClean has been appointed Head of Bectu and will take over from the retiring Philippa Childs early next year.

McClean previously spent 13 years at Bectu, rising up to National Secretary, before he became a Deputy General Secretary at Bectu parent union Prospect.

McClean described the move as “the honour of my life.” “Philippa has guided Bectu through eight tricky years which included Covid and the US film and TV slowdown, delivering for members at every turn,” he added. “The work is never done though, and in the face of continuing problems like BBC cuts, competition from streamers, consolidation, AI and global economic headwinds our members need the support of their union more than ever.”

Childs added: “I have had the pleasure of working with Noel throughout my time as Head of Bectu and have seen his hard work, tenacity, and thoughtfulness at first hand. He understands the challenges workers are facing across the creative industries and will work tirelessly on their behalf. I couldn’t be leaving Bectu in safer hands and I feel confident that under his leadership the union will continue to grow, both in membership terms but also in influence.”

Watch on Deadline

title: Comcast Gave $7.5 Million To Help Fund Donald Trump’s White House Ballroom, New Report Reveals
summary: Comcast gave $7.5 million to help Donald Trump fund a new White House ballroom, but the donation was well below that of an array of other contributions from major tech companies like Apple and Amazon, according to a new report. The Washington Post obtained a list of all major donors to the project. The White […]
content:
Comcast gave $7.5 million to help Donald Trump fund a new White House ballroom, but the donation was well below that of an array of other contributions from major tech companies like Apple and Amazon, according to a new report.

The Washington Post obtained a list of all major donors to the project. The White House had previously disclosed a list of donors, including Comcast, but did not include the amounts.

The top contributors included Nvidia and Apple, which each gave $25 million, as did the Adelson Family Foundation and the Charlie Ergen household and donor advised fund, per the Post. Another $22 million came from Google’s settlement of Trump’s lawsuit after YouTube suspended his account in the wake of the January 6th attack on the Capitol. The Laura and Isaac Perlmutter Foundation gave $20.27 million. Ike Perlmutter, the former CEO of Marvel Entertainment, is a longtime supporter of the president. Amazon gave $5 million, per the report.

Outside of Comcast, no other major media companies were listed as contributors of $100,000 or more.

Watch on Deadline

A Comcast spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The total donations reached almost $330 million. It’s unclear how expensive the ballroom will end up costing, as previous reports have put the figure up to $500 million.

A federal judge ruled earlier this year that ballroom construction had to stop because Congress first had to approve it. U.S. District Judge Richard Leon did allow for building of an underground bunker to continue.

The Supreme Court, however, has allowed the ballroom to proceed as the case moves through lower courts. That may make the situation moot, as construction of the ballroom, replacing the East Wing of the White House, is well underway, with the framing of the structure visibly rising on the White House grounds.

title: Hudson Williams, Zach Galifianakis & Jay Baruchel Set For ‘The Assembly’ Season 2 At Canada’s CBC
summary: EXCLUSIVE: CBC celebrities, assemble! The names in the hot seat for Season 2 of the Canadian version of The Assembly are in, and they’ve got some collective star power. Heated Rivalry star Hudson Williams, The Hangover‘s Zach Galifianakis and This is the End actor Jay Baruchel have signed up to be grilled by a cast […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: CBC celebrities, assemble! The names in the hot seat for Season 2 of the Canadian version of The Assembly are in, and they’ve got some collective star power.

Heated Rivalry star Hudson Williams, The Hangover‘s Zach Galifianakis and This is the End actor Jay Baruchel have signed up to be grilled by a cast of autistic and neurodivergent interviewers for the six-part series.

Also on the cast list are three-time Olympic gold medalist Marie-Philip Poulin, Miss Universe Canada Ashley Callingbull, who has appeared in Netflix, CBC and APTN comedy North of North, and singer-songwriter Lights.

The second season of CBC’s show premieres on CBC Gem and CBC TV on Sunday, November 1 at 9 p.m. ET (9:30 NT). Special extended ‘Producer’s Cuts’ will be released on CBC Gem the same day from 9 a.m. ET. Here’s the trailer.

Watch on Deadline

The Assembly began life in France on France Télévisions as Les Rencontres du Papotin, and has since spawned returning versions in countries such as the UK, Spain and Australia. Guests across versions have included Camille Cottin, President Emmanuel Macron, Antonio Banderas, Michael Sheen, David Tennant, Stephen Fry and Sam Neil.

Each version features the cast of autistic and neurodivergent interviewers audiences, who collectively quiz celebrities in an ask-anything interview format. In Canada, interviewers from the first season will return alongside additional new ones.

“The response to The Assembly’s first season was incredible,” said Jennifer Dettman, Executive Director, Unscripted Content, CBC. “Our interviewers bring such a fresh, honest energy to the traditional talk show, and we’re excited to showcase more engaging conversations with some of the most well-known national and international celebrities.”

In Canada, Small Army Entertainment makes the series for CBC. Season 1 won a Canadian Screen Award for Best Direction, a Golden Sheaf Award at Yorkton Film Festival, three Telly Awards and was nominated for the Banff Rockie Award.

“This season of The Assembly is full of surprises and promises to deliver even more of the heart, humour and authentic conversations that can only happen on a show like this,” added executive producer Stephen Sawchuk. “Being back for a second season shows that the series is resonating with audiences,” added Sean De Vries, the other exec producer. “It’s heartening to have a hit show that thrives on authentic human connection.”

For CBC, Sally Catto is General Manager, Entertainment; Dettman is Executive Director, Unscripted Content; and Susan Taylor is Executive in Charge of Production.

title: Al Pacino To Receive SAG-AFTRA Life Achievement Award
summary: Al Pacino, the nine-time Oscar-nominated star of such iconic films as The Godfather and it sequels, Dog Day Afternoon, Scarface and his Best Actor Academy Award-winning role in Scent of a Woman, will receive the 62nd SAG-AFTRA Life Achievement Award. The honor, bestowed annually by the actors’ guild for career and humanitarian accomplishments, will be […]
content:
Al Pacino, the nine-time Oscar-nominated star of such iconic films as The Godfather and it sequels, Dog Day Afternoon, Scarface and his Best Actor Academy Award-winning role in Scent of a Woman, will receive the 62nd SAG-AFTRA Life Achievement Award.

The honor, bestowed annually by the actors’ guild for career and humanitarian accomplishments, will be handed out during SAG-AFTRA’s 2027 Actor Awards ceremony February 28 at the Shrine Auditorium & Expo Hall in Los Angeles. The union made the announcement Thursday.

Pacino’s career spans seven decades, with his major film debut coming with 1971’s The Panic in Needle Park. His breakthrough came when Francis Coppola cast him as Michael Corleone in The Godfather, earning him his first Oscar nom (for Supporting Actor) for a character he would reprise in two sequels. That first role led to films like Serpico, Dog Day Afternoon and 1983’s Scarface, playing the Cuban mobster Tony Montana.

His other film credits in that stretch included Sea of Love and Dick Tracy, and then in 1992 he became the first male actor to score two acting Oscar noms for two films in the same year, for Glengarry Glen Ross and Scent of a Woman. The latter, in which he played the blind, ornery Lt. Col. Frank Slade on the brink, earned him his Oscar.

Watch on Deadline

Other 1990s movie hits for Pacino included Frankie and Johnny, Carlito’s Way, Heat, Looking for Richard, The Devil’s Advocate, Donnie Brasco, The Insider and Any Given Sunday.

His TV credits include playing Roy Cohn in HBO’s 2003 adaptation of Tony Kushner’s Pulitzer-winning play Angels in America, winning him an Emmy, Golden Globe and a SAG Award. He won another Emmy for playing Dr. Jack Kevorkian in HBO’s TV movie You Don’t Know Jack. Also for HBO, he portrayed Penn State football coach Joe Paterno in Paterno and Phil Spector in Phil Spector.

More recently, films included Quentin Tarantino’s Once Upon a Time in Hollywood, Martin Scorsese’s The Irishman and Ridley Scott’s House of Gucci, and he played Nazi hunter Meyer Offerman for two seasons on Prime Video’s Hunters.

His humanitarian efforts and social causes have included participating in 2001 America: A Tribute to Heroes telethon supporting September 11 families; the ONE Campaign’s 2005 Make Poverty History initiative addressing extreme poverty, hunger and AIDS; and a 2012 campaign supporting Hurricane Sandy relief. He supports the Shakespeare Center of Los Angeles, and in 2009 he received the Southern California Chapter of the Arthritis Foundation’s Jane Wyman Humanitarian Award.

“Like so many actors, I have spent my life in awe and appreciation of the force of nature that is Al Pacino,” SAG-AFTRA president Sean Astin said in a release Thursday announcing the award, which most recently went to Harrison Ford last year, preceded by Jane Fonda (2024), Barbra Streisand (2023), Sally Field (2022), Helen Mirren (2021) and Pacino Godfather II co-star Robert De Niro (2020). “When you watch him perform, you are witnessing a student and a master. Al Pacino is an artist of extraordinary courage, intensity and heart whose work has always set an exceptional standard of skill and talent. All of that and he’s just plain fun to watch. SAG-AFTRA is proud to celebrate Al Pacino with our union’s highest honor.”

Pacino will add SAG-AFRTA’s highest honor to a list of accolades that includes two Tony Awards (Best Featured Actor for 1969’s Does a Tiger Wear a Necktie? in his Broadway debut and Best Actor for 1977’s The Basic Training of Pavlo Hummel), the AFI Life Achievement Award, the Golden Globes’ Cecil B. DeMille Award and a Kennedy Center Honor.

“I wondered and wandered most of my life but have always felt at home with a script and my fellow actors,” Pacino said. “It’s the work and the actors along the way that have been among the greatest joys of my life. It’s an honor to be recognized by SAG-AFTRA in celebrating the journey.”

title: ‘The Baby-Sitters Club’ Stage Musical Sets Los Angeles World Premiere Opening Date, Venue
summary: EXCLUSIVE: The Baby-sitters Club: A New Musical based on Ann M. Martin’s book series that inspired the 1995 film and two TV series, will make its world premiere this spring with Center Theatre Group at the Kirk Douglas Theatre in Los Angeles. Previews for the four-week run will begin on May 6, 2027, ahead of […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: The Baby-sitters Club: A New Musical based on Ann M. Martin’s book series that inspired the 1995 film and two TV series, will make its world premiere this spring with Center Theatre Group at the Kirk Douglas Theatre in Los Angeles.

Previews for the four-week run will begin on May 6, 2027, ahead of its May 16 opening. The dates and venue were announced today by the producing team, which includes Mountain A, the production company co-founded by Oscar-winning actor Natalie Portman.

“The Baby-sitters Club was a formative part of my childhood, as was musical theater, and I feel so lucky to get to be part of bringing these two worlds together,” Portman said. “I can’t wait to share the joy these characters brought me as a kid with audiences this spring.”

Deadline previously announced the development of the project with a book by Kate Wetherhead (The Devil Wears Prada), music and lyrics by Mark Sonnenblick (KPop Demon Hunters), and direction and choreography by Annie Tippe (Octet).

Watch on Deadline

Casting for the project will begin soon, with The Telsey Office handling in New York and Henry Russell Bergstein Casting in Los Angeles.

In addition to Mountain A – which was co-founded by Portman and Sophie Mas – producers will include TWTheatricals; Riva Marker for Linden Productions (Stereophonic); Naia Cucukov Richards & Lucy Kitada (Netflix’s The Baby-sitters Club series); Peter Richards for Working Barn Productions; and Center Theatre Group. Co-producers are Gregg Arst and Laura Kaufmann of Tanna Entertainment, and Mickey Liddell and Pete Shilaimon of LD Entertainment.

The musical reimagines Martin’s book series and features characters Kristy, Mary Anne, Claudia and Stacey who, at 25 years old, return to Stoneybrook for an overdue reunion.

The synopsis: “As old friendships are rekindled and long-buried tensions resurface, the women find themselves confronting the grown-up questions that define this chapter of their lives: who they are, what they want, and whether the lives they’ve built are the ones they truly imagined for themselves. At the heart of their journey is a reminder that, even as we grow and change, friendship can be a powerful source of strength and support—and that we don’t have to navigate life’s challenges alone.”

“We’re creating something that is big hearted and timeless, while honoring what people love about The Baby-sitters Club,” said Linden Productions and TWTheatricals in a joint statement.

Martin’s book series is one of the most successful children’s book line in publishing history with more than 200 million books in print worldwide. Launched by Scholastic in 1986, the series was originally conceived as just four books – Kristy’s Great Idea, Claudia and the Phantom Phone Calls, The Truth About Stacey, and Mary Anne Saves the Day – but ultimately expanded to more than 250 titles and four spin-off series.

Adaptations included the 1990 HBO television series, the ’95 feature film from Sony Pictures, and, most recently, the critically acclaimed 2020-21 Netflix series.

title: Daniel Henney Joins Apple TV’s ‘Disavowed’ (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Daniel Henney has joined the cast of Apple TV’s upcoming action thriller “Disavowed.” Per the longline, “Disavowed” follows “legendary CIA case officer Brad Griffin, who is abruptly fired in the middle of a global hunt for an elusive assassin responsible for killing his colleague. Disgraced and outcast from the world of intelligence, all bets are […]
content:
Daniel Henney has joined the cast of Apple TV’s upcoming action thriller “Disavowed.”

Per the longline, “Disavowed” follows “legendary CIA case officer Brad Griffin, who is abruptly fired in the middle of a global hunt for an elusive assassin responsible for killing his colleague. Disgraced and outcast from the world of intelligence, all bets are off when Brad decides to go after the 15 million dollar federal bounty on the assassin’s head.”

Henney joins James Marsden who stars as Brad Griffin, Norman Reedus (“The Walking Dead”) and Bokeem Woodbine (FX’s “Fargo”). Henney will play Jae Chun, a successful attorney to high-profile figures.

Popular on Variety

Henney’s previous works include starring as Lan Mandragoran opposite Rosamund Pike in Prime Video’s “The Wheel of Time.” The 28-year-old American actor got his start in Korea with the 2005 romantic comedy-drama “My Lovely Sam-Soon.” He later starred in “Criminal Minds: Beyond Borders” and “Criminal Minds.” His film credits include “Missing, X-Men Origins: Wolverine” and “Big Hero 6,” in which he voiced Tadashi Hamada. He also voices Jinn in the English version of the Netflix series “Genie, Make a Wish.”

The “Disavowed” series was originally announced back in May with Marsden in the lead role. The release date is yet to be announced. It is created and executive produced by Art Marcum and Matt Holloway. Tom Spezialy and Marsden will also executive produce. Blue Marble Pictures produces, with Theresa Kang and Caroline Garity serving as executive producers. Apple Studios will also produce.

Henney is represented by Buchwald, More Medavoy Management and Toczek Suddleson Law Group.

title: IShowSpeed Partners With Breakwater Studios, Obamas’ Higher Ground to Bring ‘The Eyes of Ghana’ Doc to Theaters (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Streaming superstar IShowSpeed has partnered with Breakwater Studios and Barack and Michelle Obama’s Higher Ground to bring Ben Proudfoot’s upcoming documentary “The Eyes of Ghana” to theaters for a one-night-only screening on Oct. 28, Variety can reveal exclusively. Participating exhibitors include Regal, AMC, Cinemark, select theater chains and independent cinemas. “The Eyes of Ghana,” which […]
content:
Streaming superstar IShowSpeed has partnered with Breakwater Studios and Barack and Michelle Obama’s Higher Ground to bring Ben Proudfoot’s upcoming documentary “The Eyes of Ghana” to theaters for a one-night-only screening on Oct. 28, Variety can reveal exclusively. Participating exhibitors include Regal, AMC, Cinemark, select theater chains and independent cinemas.

“The Eyes of Ghana,” which premiered at the 2025 Toronto International Film Festival, follows Ghanaian cinematographer Chris Hesse, who, as his eyesight declines, attempts to rescue more than 1,000 films capturing Africa’s fight for independence in the 1950s and ’60s. The tapes were hidden for decades after the 1996 overthrow of Kwame Nkrumah, Ghana’s first president and a leader of the African liberation movement.

“It is a great honor to be part of ‘The Eyes of Ghana’ and help bring this extraordinary piece of history to

the big screen. I felt a profound connection to Ghana when I visited this year, and learning about Chris

Hesse’s work deepened my understanding of the country and its people,” said IShowSpeed. “His camera

captured the birth of African independence, and his determination to preserve those images has ensured

that future generations can witness it for themselves. I’m humbled by his legacy and proud to help bring

his story to my community.”

Popular on Variety

IShowSpeed, who’s real name is Darren Watkins Jr., is a Cincinnati native with more than 200 million followers and subscribers across streaming and social media platforms. Known for his high-energy demeanor, his livestream content covers gaming, sports, stunts and travel. He was named to the inaugural TIME100 Creators list and ranked No. 1 on Rolling Stone’s 2025 Most Influential Creators list.

IShowSpeed’s involvement in “The Eyes of Ghana” is just the latest example of digital creators mobilizing their audiences to movie theaters. Back in January, YouTuber Mark Fischbach, aka Markiplier, directed, starred in and self-distributed his sci-fi horror film “Iron Lung.” Not only did his fans call theater chains to encourage them to screen the movie, but they also showed out in droves on release day. The film opened to $17 million and ended its run with $50 million worldwide against a budget of just $3 million.

“Chris Hesse spent more than six decades documenting and safeguarding an extraordinary chapter of

Ghanaian and African history,” stated Ethan Lewis, head of non-fiction at Higher Ground. “Higher Ground is proud to partner with IShowSpeed, Ben Proudfoot and Breakwater Studios and this accomplished team of artists to bring this remarkable story to theaters on Oct. 28th. ‘The Eyes of Ghana’ speaks to the power of film to preserve our collective memory, and to the responsibility we share in making sure these stories reach the next generation.”

In addition to IShowSpeed, the film is produced by Proudfoot, Nana Adwoa Frimpong, Moses Bwayo, Anita Afonu, Brandon Somerhalder, Lewis and Vinnie Malhotra. Executive producers include Barack and Michelle Obama, Sir John Akomfrah, Kofi Amoo-Gottfried, Paula Madison, Dan and Lian Gill, Max Johnson, Jonathan E. Lim, Michael Risley, Josh Rosenberg, David Treatman and Esther Wojcicki.

Tickets and local showtimes are available at TheEyesOfGhana.com. Check out the trailer below.

title: Mike Leigh Gets Standing Ovation at London Homecoming Premiere of ‘Tender Loving Care,’ Likely His Final Film
summary: U.K. audiences aren’t usually ones to give standing ovations, but when one of their most cherished filmmakers makes a final bow, unwritten rules are allowed to be broken. This was certainly the case for Mike Leigh, who on Thursday received a hero’s welcome at the London Film Festival premiere of “Tender Loving Care,” a film […]
content:
U.K. audiences aren’t usually ones to give standing ovations, but when one of their most cherished filmmakers makes a final bow, unwritten rules are allowed to be broken.

This was certainly the case for Mike Leigh, who on Thursday received a hero’s welcome at the London Film Festival premiere of “Tender Loving Care,” a film he’s said will likely be his last.

The director — an icon of British cinema with a celebrated body of work that includes “Secrets & Lies,” “Naked,” “Vera Drake” (which opened the 2004 London Film Festival), “Happy-Go-Lucky” and “Topsy-Turvey” — was welcomed to the stage ahead of the screening with applause, cheers and, after a few seconds, with almost the entire room at London’s Royal Festival Hall rising to their feet in appreciation.

When the clapping died down, the director responded, in typical Leigh style, with: “You haven’t even seen it yet.”

Popular on Variety

Starring Kate O’Flynn, Marion Bailey and Paul Jesson, “Tender Loving Care” — set and shot in London — explores themes of aging, grief and relationships, while casting a harsh light on the underfunded British health and welfare system. The film premiered at Telluride and won both the top prize at the San Sebastian Film Festival and best leading actor award for O’Flynn.

Speaking via video in San Sebastian and echoing comments he’d made earlier, Leigh said the film was “more than likely” his final film due to his own health issues. “It’s quite straightforward, I have a medical condition [myositis], which affects my muscular movement, and it’s quite difficult to move around,” he said. “[It’s] certainly more difficult than it should be for a filmmaker, and therefore it’s more than probable that this film will have to be my last film. That’s all.”

He added: “It’s a practical matter to do with my medical condition — a physical condition.”

Leigh has a long history with the London Film Festival, with many of his films have screened there. Alongside titles such as “Another Year,” “Peterloo,” “Naked,” “Vera Drake,” “Life Is Sweet” (which had its world premiere at LFF in 1990), “Mr. Turner” and last year’s “Hard Truths,” Leigh brought his very first feature, “Bleak Moments,” to the festival in 1971.

title: ‘The Conners’ Boss Bruce Helford Hired to Run ‘Newlyweds’ at NBC After Gail Lerner’s Firing
summary: After Gail Lerner’s recent announcement that she’d been fired as the showrunner of “Newlyweds,” the upcoming NBC sitcom she co-created with Jamie Lee Curtis, the network has hired Bruce Helford to take over. Helford is a veteran writer-producer who has created and overseen several comedian-driven series over the course of decades. As a creator or […]
content:
After Gail Lerner’s recent announcement that she’d been fired as the showrunner of “Newlyweds,” the upcoming NBC sitcom she co-created with Jamie Lee Curtis, the network has hired Bruce Helford to take over.

Helford is a veteran writer-producer who has created and overseen several comedian-driven series over the course of decades. As a creator or co-creator, his credits include “The Drew Carey Show,” “The Norm Show” starring Norm Macdonald, “George Lopez” and more. He also wrote and executive produced on the original run of “Roseanne,” its 2018 revival, and its 2018-2025 sequel series “The Conners.” Helford is repped by UTA and Ziffren Brittenham.

“Newlyweds” premieres on Oct. 23. Lerner announced that she had been fired on Oct. 9, writing in an Instagram caption, “The reason I’ve been given is ‘creative differences.’ The cloudy part: I’m so sad to be separated from the most joyous TV experience of my life. The cast, crew, and writers are unparalleled. The silver lining: the first six episodes were made under my leadership, and I wouldn’t change a thing.”

Popular on Variety

Per the official description, “Newlyweds” is “a later-in-life love story about Jeanie (Téa Leoni), a free-spirited woman, and James (Tim Daly), a buttoned-up professor, who marry impetuously after a whirlwind courtship. James only has eyes for Jeanie, but quickly learns that loving her means learning to love her sprawling, eccentric world of friends and family and vice versa.” Along with Leoni and Daly, the cast includes Curtis, Emma Meisel, Ignacio Diaz-Silverio and Bill O’Neill.

Lerner retains her credit as executive proucer alongside Helford; Curtis; Eric and Kim Tannenbaum and Jason Wang for the Tannenbaum Company; Scott Schwartz; and Lionsgate Television. Pam Fryman directed and executive produced the pilot. Universal Television is the studio.

title: Tracy Morgan, Jane Krakowski, Daniel Radcliffe and More Join NBC Comedy Panels at New York Comedy Festival
summary: Some of the funniest names associated with NBC will appear on panels at the New York Comedy Festival. On Saturday, Nov. 14, “The Fall and Rise of Reggie Dinkins” will hit the festival with an advanced screening of Season 2, Episode 3, followed by a conversation with the cast and creative team. Tracy Morgan, Daniel […]
content:
Some of the funniest names associated with NBC will appear on panels at the New York Comedy Festival.

On Saturday, Nov. 14, “The Fall and Rise of Reggie Dinkins” will hit the festival with an advanced screening of Season 2, Episode 3, followed by a conversation with the cast and creative team. Tracy Morgan, Daniel Radcliffe, Erika Alexander, Bobby Moynihan, Precious Way and Jalyn Hall will appear on the panel alongside series co-creators and executive producers Robert Carlock and Sam Means. Josh Horowitz of the “Happy Sad Confused” podcast will moderate.

Plus, on Sunday, Nov. 15, “Brooklyn Nine-Nine” duo Dan Goor and Luke Del Tredici will speak on a panel about the evolution of NBC comedy alongside series star Chelsea Peretti, “30 Rock” actors Jane Krakowski and Judah Friedlander, and Jane Levy, who stars on Goor and Del Tredici’s upcoming project, “Sunset P.I.”

Popular on Variety

The group of actors and showrunners will celebrate the series Goor and Del Tredici have influenced as producers and writers, including “Parks and Recreation,” “30 Rock” and “Brooklyn Nine-Nine.”

Both panels are free (with tickets required) and are taking place at the Hard Rock Hotel in Times Square. Both events are also extensions of the NBC100 programming. The network behind “Saturday Night Live” and “The Office” is celebrating 100 years of storytelling, culminating in a three-hour primetime special on Dec. 10.

Goor and Del Tredici are gearing up to debut their next NBC sitcom, a single-camera workplace comedy starring Jake Johnson as a cynical detective working at a past-its-prime private investigator agency in Hollywood. Johnson is joined by cast members Levy, Langston Kerman, Mary Shalaby and Keith David. Rounding out the ensemble are Spencer Moss, Nelson Franklin, Patrick Gallagher, David Paymer and Wrenn Schmidt. NBC announced it was picking up “Sunset P.I.” to series in May.

The New York Comedy Festival runs from Nov. 6 to 15.

title: Bernie Orenstein Dies: Writer-Producer On ‘Sanford & Son,’ ‘That Girl,’ ‘Kate & Allie’ & More Was 95
summary: Bernie Orenstein, whose TV career spanned writing for Candid Camera to writing and producing That Girl, The New Dick Van Dyke Show, Sanford & Son, What’s Happening!!, Kate & Allie and others, has died. He was 95. His family said Orenstein died September 14 but did not provide details. Orenstein had been a writer on […]
content:
Bernie Orenstein, whose TV career spanned writing for Candid Camera to writing and producing That Girl, The New Dick Van Dyke Show, Sanford & Son, What’s Happening!!, Kate & Allie and others, has died. He was 95.

His family said Orenstein died September 14 but did not provide details.

Orenstein had been a writer on Alan Funt’s hidden-camera show Candid Camera in the 1960s when he began penning episodes of sitcoms and variety shows including The Monkees, The Roger Miller Show, Accidental Family, Away We Go — which featured a young George Carlin — and Hey, Landlord. His breakout gig was as a scribe for ABC’s big-budget variety show The Hollywood Palace from 1965-68. That would be Orenstein’s first project with his eventual longtime writing and producing partner Saul Turteltaub.

Together, they wrote and produced such TV fare as That Girl — led by Marlo Thomas — The New Dick Van Dyke Show and The Beautiful Phyllis Diller Show. Orenstein and Turteltaub also worked on episodes of the campy anthology comedy Love, American Style before becoming writer-producers on the classic Redd Foxx sitcom Sanford & Son in 1974. That season, the NBC comedy finished second behind All in the Family in the year-end primetime ratings, and ranking No. 7 in 1975-76.

They remained with the show until its 1977 wrap, also working on its short-lived spinoff Grady and shorter-lived continuation series The Sanford Arms, which aired a handful of episodes with much of the Sanford & Son cast sans its stars. Foxx had moved on to his own NBC variety series, and Demond Wilson left amid a salary dispute.

Orenstein and Turteltaub’s next big show was ABC’s What’s Happening!!, an urban comedy that debuted in 1976. Taking a cue from Norman Lear’s wildly popular shows of the era, first season was popular, ranking No. 25 in primetime year-end ratings in the three-network universe. But subsequent seasons were less successful, and the show ended in 1979.

The duo would continue to write and produce TV series and specials well into the 1990s, creating the single-season 1982 Mickey Rooney-Dana Carvey sitcom One of the Boys and working on such ’80s shows as One in a Million, Double Trouble, E/R, Foley Square and You Again? Their biggest series that decade was Kate & Allie, the CBS comedy starring Susan Saint James and SNL original Jane Curtin as divorced best friends sharing a Greenwich Village apartment. Orenstein and Turteltaub served as EPs and writers for its final season in 1988-89.

Partners for more than three decades, they would go on to write and produce for the 1990s comedies Baby Talk and Cosby, the latter being Orenstein’s final screen credit.

Born on February 5, 1931, in Toronto, Orenstein got his start in TV in the 1950s as an actor on the Canadian shows Encounter and On Camera. He later would have bit roles on Sanford & Son, That Girl and The New Dick Van Dyke Show.

“As a writer there’s a great advantage,” Orenstein said in a 2016 interview with the TV Academy Foundation. “You’re never out of work. You can always sit down at the typewriter or computer.”
