title: Tatiana Maslany, Tony Shalhoub & John Turturro Set For ‘Rhinoceros’ Broadway Revival This Spring
summary: Emmy winners Tatiana Maslany and John Turturro and Tony winner Tony Shalhoub will take to the Broadway stage this spring in a Roundabout Theatre Company revival of Eugène Ionesco’s absurdist classic Rhinoceros, last seen on Broadway in 1961. To be directed by Diane Paulus, Rhinoceros will begin previews at Roundabout’s Todd Haimes Theatre on Wednesday, […]
content:
Emmy winners Tatiana Maslany and John Turturro and Tony winner Tony Shalhoub will take to the Broadway stage this spring in a Roundabout Theatre Company revival of Eugène Ionesco’s absurdist classic Rhinoceros, last seen on Broadway in 1961.

To be directed by Diane Paulus, Rhinoceros will begin previews at Roundabout’s Todd Haimes Theatre on Wednesday, April 7, 2027, with an official opening on Sunday, April 25, 2027. The limited run will play through Sunday, June 13, 2027.

Roundabout’s previously announced spring entry, a revival of The Full Monty, has been postponed due to cast availability and will be rescheduled at a later date (the company had not announced the cast).

The Paulus-directed Rhinoceros had its critically acclaimed world premiere this past summer at the American Repertory Theater at Harvard University, and marks the first Ionesco play to be staged by the Roundabout.

Watch on Deadline

Maslani will play Daisy, Shalhoub will play Jean and Turturro has been cast as Bérenger. In the landmark 1961 Broadway production, those roles were portrayed by, respectively, Anne Jackson, Zero Mostel and Eli Wallach. Mostel won a Tony Award for his performance, and reprised the role for Tom O’Horgan’s 1973 film adaptation co-starring Gene Wilder and Karen Black.

Complete casting for the Roundabout production will be announced later.

The creative team includes scenic design by Riccardo Hernández, costume design by Anita Yavich, lighting design by Jen Schriever, sound design by Fitz Patton, special effects design by Markus Maurette, hair & wig design by Tom Watson, make-up design by Kyle Krueger, fight direction by Thomas Schall and movement by Jill Johnson.

The synopsis: “Can you hear it? The stampede of hooves…the trumpeting of beasts… our friends and neighbors changing before our very eyes. Do we maintain our humanity, or join the herd?” The three primary cast members play “small-town friends and colleagues who find themselves facing a world-shaking new movement.”

Maslany, a 2016 Emmy winner for Orphan Black and more recently starring in Apple TV+’s drama series Maximum Pleasure Guaranteed, last appeared on Broadway in 2023’s Grey House and, before that, 2018’s Network.

Shalhoub, a multiple Emmy winner for Monk and The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel, won a 2018 Tony for The Band’s Visit. Other Broadway credits include Arthur Miller’s The Price, Lend Me a Tenor, Conversations with My Father, The Heidi Chronicles and others. He’ll next be seen on TV in CBS upcoming series Einstein.

Turturro won an Emmy for his guest performance in Shalhoub’s Monk, and has been nominated for The Night Of, Severance and Mr. and Mrs. Smith. His many films include Do the Right Thing, The Color of Money and the upcoming A Statement. His Broadway credits include Life (x) 3 in 2003 and Relatively Speaking in 2011.

title: Strand Releasing Takes North American For Hanaël El Yousfi’s TIFF-Selected ‘The Daughters Of Abraham’
summary: Strand Releasing has acquired North American distribution rights to Hanaël El Yousfi’s The Daughters of Abraham following its international premiere in the Discovery section at the 2026 Toronto International Film Festival. The debut feature of French director Hanaël El Yousfi, The Daughters of Abraham follows Myriam and Eva, friends in their early twenties as they […]
content:
Strand Releasing has acquired North American distribution rights to Hanaël El Yousfi’s The Daughters of Abraham following its international premiere in the Discovery section at the 2026 Toronto International Film Festival.

The debut feature of French director Hanaël El Yousfi, The Daughters of Abraham follows Myriam and Eva, friends in their early twenties as they enjoy one of the last carefree summers of their youth in Marseille.

Between nights out with friends, and family and community obligations, the two young women are trying to figure out where their lives will go from here.

Their respective close-knit Muslim and Jewish families struggle between supporting their daughters as modern, liberated young women, and wanting them to live within the traditional expectations of their communities.

Watch on Deadline

A slip in judgement and a betrayal of trust creates tensions between friends and within families, building to a crisis that disrupts the balance of their social circle, and leads them to take hold of their own destinies.

The North American deal was brokered by Alice Lesort, Head of International Sales at Paris-based Losange Films, with Marcus Hu and Jon Gerrans of Strand Releasing.

The Daughters of Abraham is written by El Yousfi, with Raphaël Chevènement and Mia Grace Brown, and produced by Charles Gillibert for CG Cinéma. It stars Mélissa Guers, Ava Baya and Gabriella Cohen.

“Toronto was an especially moving experience, because it was there that I realized my film didn’t belong to any one community, but to everyone who has ever had to negotiate the space between their heritage and their freedom,” said El Yousfi.

“Perhaps that is the most beautiful thing that can happen to a film: discovering that what you thought was deeply personal is, in fact, profoundly universal…I’m delighted that this story will now have the opportunity to connect with North American audiences thanks to Strand Releasing.”

Prior to its TIFF international premiere, The Daughters of Abraham won the Audience Award and a Special Prize for the cast at France’s Angoulême Francophone Film Festival. It will open in France on December 30.

The film continues to travel the festival circuit, with an upcoming Latin American premiere at the Sao Paulo Film Festival. Strand will release the film in 2027.

Producer Charles Gillibert said ”As a producer, it is always very important that our young, talented filmmakers access the international market and that their films travel as much as possible around the world. Hanaël El Youfsi is a strong and talented voice with an incredibly powerful gaze on how young women, wherever they come from, need to fight and emancipate themselves. I am very happy that Strand Releasing will bring the film to North American audiences.

Lesort added: “The critical response and audience reception in Toronto confirmed that its themes resonate far beyond France, where the story is set.”

“We’re thrilled to be able to have this debut feature film that carefully balances the politics of the world between the intimacy of two friends and makes it so universal,” said Strand’s Gerrans.

title: Brad Caleb Kane On Making ‘Crystal Lake’ A “Small-Town Show” In Same N.J. Locations Where ‘Friday The 13th’ Filmed, “Faithfully” Re-Creating An Iconic Scene & “Twin Peaks-y” Ideas For Season 2
summary: As Crystal Lake brings Jason Voorhees fans to his roots, the Peacock prequel series takes the Friday the 13th franchise back to where it all began. Series creator Brad Caleb Kane told Deadline “the amazing thing” about filming the eight-episode show — all episodes now available to stream — where the original 1980 slasher also […]
content:
As Crystal Lake brings Jason Voorhees fans to his roots, the Peacock prequel series takes the Friday the 13th franchise back to where it all began.

Series creator Brad Caleb Kane told Deadline “the amazing thing” about filming the eight-episode show — all episodes now available to stream — where the original 1980 slasher also filmed in Blairstown, NJ, is that the township “hasn’t changed in 45 years.”

“It’s still exactly the same,” explained Kane. “The structures are the same, maybe some paint jobs are different, and we had to do a little bit of that. But basically, it’s exactly the same town intact as it was 45 years ago, which is amazing.”

Fans of the original Sean S. Cunningham-helmed horror film might remember one of the opening scenes, in which camp counselor Annie Phillips (Robbi Morgan) hitchhikes through Crystal Lake, crossing a small bridge and cutting a corner in downtown Blairstown with a noticeable round red payphone on the sidewalk and visiting Trudy’s diner before meeting her demise.

Watch on Deadline

In episode 4, “A New Beginning,” writers Evan Endicott and Josh Stoddard re-created the scene with a hitchhiking hippy named Willow (Oona Roche), even rebuilding the interior of Trudy’s diner on a soundstage.

Blairstown, New Jersey served as the filming location for Crystal Lake in ‘Friday the 13th’ (1980) and ‘Crystal Lake’ (2026)

‘Crystal Lake’ re-creates a ‘Friday the 13th’ scene at Trudy’s diner, the interior of which was rebuilt on a soundstage.

Kane also emphasized the importance of filming in New Jersey, “because honestly, like trees look different in Jersey. You can’t recreate that feel anywhere else, so we wanted to re-create that feel and the only way to do it is in the same state.”

Although the nearby Camp No-Be-Bo-Sco, which is still an active camp and horror fan destination, was not available to stand in for Camp Crystal Lake as it once did in 1980, Kane and directors Celine Held and Logan George were able to rebuild the camp’s boathouse on a soundstage in order to “faithfully” recreate movie’s opening kill with his own twist in episode 5, “The New Blood”.

“It’s still there and it’s still intact, and we walked through it, because we couldn’t shoot there,” explained Kane. “And obviously now that you’ve seen the show, you know that we recreate a scene in that boathouse, shot-for-shot from the movie. Our great production designer Lester Cohen rebuilt it from scratch to the exact specifications at Camp Ocawasin in New Jersey, which was our campground that we created for the show.”

‘Crystal Lake’s Claudette (Danielle Kotch) and Barry (Pheonix Parnevik) re-create the opening kill from ‘Friday the 13th’

In addition to recreating some memorable scenes and locations in the series about Jason Voorhees’ grieving mother Pam (Linda Cardellini), Crystal Lake also revisits some fan-favorite locals in its cast of characters, including diner owner Trudy (played by Dorothy Kobs in the first movie, Bernadette Quigley in the prequel series), police officer Dorf (Ron Millke, Cameron Scoggins) and hermit Crazy Ralph (Walt Gorney, Nick Cordileone), as well as new faces, including Pam’s romantic interest, Officer Levon Brooks (William Catlett), his reporter sister Brianna (Devin Kessler) and Pam’s single friend Rita (Joy Suprano).

Kane found it “exciting” revisiting Crystal Lake and its residents through the series, which he envisions through a “Twin Peaks-y vibe.”

“I mean, this is a world that I return to over and over and over again,” he said. “I return to these movies, we all do, somehow. They became iconic for a reason. But there’s a lot we don’t know about the town. We meet these really colorful characters in the first movie, we meet Trudy and Officer Dorff and so-called Crazy Ralph, even though he turns out to have a point. But we don’t see that much of them ultimately. Some are dispatched, some are just there for momentary common comic relief.”

Kane continued, “And, you know, with a show like this, we have the opportunity to open it up and spend a little more time with them. Everybody loves a small-town show, and within the world of Friday the 13th, that just becomes more amplified and interesting.”

Walt Gorney as Crazy Ralph in ‘Friday the 13th’; Nick Cordileone as Ralph in ‘Crystal Lake’

With a wealth of characters to explore (and eventually slaughter), Kane hopes to revisit Crystal Lake for another season. “I do have ideas for Season 2 in mind,” he confirmed.

“Obviously, it’s not just Pam’s story, it’s Crystal Lake, so you have all of the peripheral characters who are interesting to me,” explained Kane. “You have the opportunity for this to be more of a Twin Peaks-y kind of vibe, with Ralph and with Dwarf and Trudy and all of those characters. There’s a lot more to get into with them. But obviously, the nexus is always gonna be Pam and Jason and their story.”

After giving fans “a little dopamine hit” with his nods to the original movie, Kane noted that the show “could run into the events” of Friday the 13th (1980) if Peacock gives them enough time.

“It wouldn’t happen in a second season,” Kane clarified. “There’s more story to tell, for the residents of Crystal Lake and to the extent that Linda wants to continue the journey with us, with Pam. So, we’ll see.”

As for Cardellini, she joked that she’s game to continue the show until Pam “kills every resident.”

title: New AFM Summit To Explore Federal Production Tax Incentive
summary: The American Film Market set an inaugural New Global Screen Economy Summit on opening day that will examine a proposed federal production tax incentive, and unveiled an expanded lineup of speakers across 45+ sessions. AFM runs Nov. 10–15 at the Fairmont Century Plaza in Los Angeles.. The new summit will also delve into the creator […]
content:
The American Film Market set an inaugural New Global Screen Economy Summit on opening day that will examine a proposed federal production tax incentive, and unveiled an expanded lineup of speakers across 45+ sessions.

AFM runs Nov. 10–15 at the Fairmont Century Plaza in Los Angeles..

The new summit will also delve into the creator economy, new IP sources and the evolving studio system.

Panelists over the five days are from UTA, CAA, the MPA, Artists Equity, Alamo Drafthouse, Trafalgar Releasing, Ashland Hill, Cineverse, Crunchroll, Gersh, Lionsgate, Range Select, Rentrak, Spooky Pictures, Project X, Wrapbook and more. Speakers include AGC’s Stuart Ford, Evan Shapiro, Amy Baer, Wesley Wang, and Tyler Chou.

AFM’s 47th edition spans the Fairmont Century Plaza, AMC Century City 15 and The Pavilion.

Watch on Deadline

“Our industry is undergoing a fundamental transformation, and while the pace of change can feel overwhelming, the opportunities are incredibly exciting,” said Jackie Brenneman, president and CEO of the Independent Film & Television Alliance, which produces AFM.

“From how stories are discovered and what gets made to how content reaches audiences and the renewed excitement around the theatrical experience, nearly every part of our business is being reimagined. We’re expanding AFM to bring new voices and perspectives into the conversation alongside the industry leaders and innovators driving this change. This complements the tremendous business and dealmaking activity at the heart of the Market while creating more opportunities to connect, exchange ideas and discover new opportunities together.”

The kickoff session Nov. 10 is called The New Federal Production Incentive: A Turning Point for U.S. Production with Steven Paul, chairman-CEO of SP Media Group; SP Media Group president Scott Karol; and Josh Rogin, SVP of Federal Affairs for the MPA.

Another new addition this year is AFM House, which will feature four days of conversations, presentations and live demos of emerging technologies. Home to the expanded AFM Innovation Hub, presented in partnership with Marché du Film’s Cannes Next, AFM House will host the North American debut of the Cinemas Club, bringing together industry leaders to explore the future of theatrical exhibition and moviegoing.

title: Steven Soderbergh to Help Finish ‘The Batman 2’ Filming After Matt Reeves Stepped Away for Family Matter
summary: Steven Soderbergh is stepping in to help complete “The Batman Part II” while director Matt Reeves is on hiatus dealing with a personal matter, Variety has confirmed. “As Matt Reeves continues to attend to an ongoing family matter, Steven Soderbergh, as an admirer of Matt’s work, approached Matt and will step in, with the full […]
content:
Steven Soderbergh is stepping in to help complete “The Batman Part II” while director Matt Reeves is on hiatus dealing with a personal matter, Variety has confirmed.

“As Matt Reeves continues to attend to an ongoing family matter, Steven Soderbergh, as an admirer of Matt’s work, approached Matt and will step in, with the full support of DC Studios, to help the writer-director complete the final weeks of principal photography on The Batman Part 2,” a studio rep said in a statement. “Matt and Steven will work closely together with the actors and crew to fulfill Matt’s vision of the film.”

Soderbergh said in his own statement, “I thought Matt Reeves’ work on ‘The Batman’ was stunning; it was intentional, specific and rigorously coherent. The goal here is to work with Matt and his team to generate footage that will integrate seamlessly with what’s already been shot so Matt can properly finish his film.”

Popular on Variety

More to come…

title: Netflix Shocker: Bela Bajaria Leaving After 10 Years Amid Layoffs, Peter Rice to Replace as Chief Content Officer
summary: In a major executive shake-up, Bela Bajaria is out at Netflix after 10 years at the streamer, most recently serving as its chief content officer. She will be replaced by former Disney and Fox executive Peter Rice, as first reported by Puck. As chief content officer, Rice will lead Netflix’s global content organization, overseeing scripted […]
content:
In a major executive shake-up, Bela Bajaria is out at Netflix after 10 years at the streamer, most recently serving as its chief content officer.

She will be replaced by former Disney and Fox executive Peter Rice, as first reported by Puck. As chief content officer, Rice will lead Netflix’s global content organization, overseeing scripted and unscripted series, film, live events and more across all regions.

Bajaria’s exit comes amid a significant workforce reduction at Netflix. Around 1,000 employees (6% of the company) were laid off this week in what marks the streamer’s largest axing to date. Netflix’s film VP Doug Belgrad and film director Sheroum Kim were also pink slipped as part of the restructuring.

Popular on Variety

“I want to thank Bela for a decade of dedication, innovation, creativity and leadership,” Sarandos, Netflix’s co-CEO, said in a statement. “She led enormous changes at Netflix. She helped broaden our content offering to include the large-scale expansion of unscripted programming and the launches of live events and sports, in addition to crafting and running a world class, global slate of films and series. I’m incredibly grateful for everything she’s done to help Netflix entertain the world.”

Bajaria joined Netflix in 2016 after she was let go from NBCUniversal, where she had served as president of Universal Television. In that role, she had produced shows that aired on Netflix, including “Unbreakable Kimmy Schmidt” and “Master of None.” Sarandos first brought in Bajaria to help Netflix launch an unscripted division, as well as licensing and studio co-productions. Bajaria was later elevated to head of global in 2020 as Cindy Holland exited the company, and was named chief content officer in January 2023.

Under her watch, Bajaria oversaw popular TV series including “Bridgerton,” “Squid Game,” “Adolescence,” “Beef,” “Stranger Things” and “Wednesday,” and films such as “KPop Demon Hunters” and “Frankenstein.” She also pushed Netflix into more live sports and events like “The Roast of Tom Brady” and deals with the NFL and WWE.

But in recent months, as Netflix growth has slowed, so too has the aura around its original programming. The streamer won just 16 Primetime Emmy Awards this year — down from 30 in 2025 and quite a distance from 2021, when it tied the record for most Emmys won by an outlet in a single year, with 44. All told, 2026 was Netflix’s lowest Primetime Emmy haul since 2016.

“I know this is a big change in a year that has already had its share,” Sarandos wrote in a memo to staff. “But I also see an opportunity to take our slate to the next level, especially in UCAN [United States and Canada] where we have an outsize impact in creating big, buzzy hits that our members love and drive conversation around the world.

Rice’s own ousting at Disney in 2022, by then-CEO Bob Chapek, was a huge shock to the industry given his stature at the company. A well-regarded executive with strong talent relations, Rice was most recently chairman of Walt Disney Television and chairman of general entertainment for the Walt Disney Company. There he oversaw ABC, FOX Broadcasting, Fox Sports, ABC News, ABC Studios, Disney Channel, Freeform, FX Networks, Hulu, National Geographic, Onyx Collective, Disney Television and Twentieth Century Fox Television, with more than 300 shows and 4,000 hours of television a year. Programs during his tenure included “The Simpsons,” “American Idol,” “Modern Family,” “This Is Us,” “The Bear,” “Abbott Elementary,” “Shogun” and “Only Murders in the Building,” along with ABC News programming and sporting events such as the Super Bowl, NBA Finals and FIFA World Cup Finals.

Since he was let go from Disney, Rice worked as a producer on movies such as Jason Reitman’s “Saturday Night,” “28 Years Later” and “28 Years Later: The Bone Temple” at Sony, as well as “Warfare” and Chris Rock’s “Misty Green” at A24. He is currently producing Alex Garland’s “Elden Ring” and Sonoya Mizuno’s “Stages,” as well as well as the opening and closing ceremonies for the LA28 Olympic and Paralympic Games.

Earlier in his career, Rice was president of 21st Century Fox and CEO of Fox Networks Group, and Fox’s lead executive on the Hulu board. He also headed Fox Searchlight Pictures where he shepherded indie favorites like “Slumdog Millionaire,” “Juno,” “Little Miss Sunshine” and “Sideways.”

“Peter is one of the most effective at-scale operators in the entertainment industry. His business acumen is sharp, his talent relationships are exceptionally strong, and his experience across TV and film is deep and broad,” Sarandos said. “He understands what makes stories resonate, and he’s spent his career helping talent do the best work of their lives. I’m excited to welcome him to Netflix as chief content officer as we continue to scale and deliver members more of the stories they love.”

Added Rice, “Netflix has fundamentally changed the way stories are made, shared and experienced around the world. They’ve shown again and again that they’re willing to take chances on distinctive voices and fresh ideas, and I’m excited to work with the team to help bring even more great stories to members everywhere.”

Mike Schneider contributed to this report.

title: Taylor Sheridan’s ‘Frisco King’ Starring Samuel L. Jackson Sets Release Date (TV News Roundup)
summary: Samuel L. Jackson is the new returning king in town in Taylor Sheridan’s “Frisco King,” where he reprises his role of Russell Lee Washington Jr.. The New Orleans gangster establishes a new kingdom in Frisco, Texas, where he discovers a hustler running his business amid the suburban town. Per the series logline, “Recruiting an ambitious […]
content:
Samuel L. Jackson is the new returning king in town in Taylor Sheridan’s “Frisco King,” where he reprises his role of Russell Lee Washington Jr..

The New Orleans gangster establishes a new kingdom in Frisco, Texas, where he discovers a hustler running his business amid the suburban town. Per the series logline, “Recruiting an ambitious protégé, a loyal driver and a growing network of eccentric partners, Lee transforms small hustles into big business. But, every new score raises the stakes, and as his influence grows, so do the risks, forcing Lee to stay one grift ahead. Frisco may not know it yet, but its new king has arrived.”

The series will premiere on Paramount+ Dec. 18 with two episodes, followed by new episodes weekly. Starring alongside Jackson are Asa Germann, Kai Caster, Lilah Pate and Savanna Gann, with a special appearance by Sylvester Stallone.

Popular on Variety

Written by Sheridan, “Frisco King” is executive produced by Stallone, Jackson, Sheridan, David C. Glasser, Ron Burkle, David Hutkin, Bob Yari, LaTanya Richardson Jackson and Keith Cox. Christina Alexandra Voros and Michael Friedman executive produce in addition to both directing four episodes, with Voros directing the pilot. The series is produced by Paramount Television Studios and 101 Studios,

Watch the teaser for “Frisco King” below.

In other TV roundup news:

Specials

CBS set “The Price is Right at Night: Live Holiday Special” and “The Price is Right: 20 Seasons of Drew Carey” to air in December.

“The Price is Right at Night: Live Holiday Special” will premiere on Dec. 13 at 8 p.m. ET on CBS. The broadcast marks the first time television’s longest-running game show will air in real time. Viewers will also get behind-the-scenes access with host Drew Carey, announcer George Gray, the models and the production team as they race to keep the show on track.

On Dec. 15, CBS will air “The Price is Right: 20 Seasons of Drew Carey.” The special will celebrate two decades of Carey as host, featuring celebrity appearances from previous episodes including Mila Kunis, Jack Black and Snoop Dogg.

The live holiday special is produced by Fremantle, with John Quinn as showrunner and executive producer. The Drew Carey special is produced by Fremantle, with James Davis and Quinn as executive producers. Both specials will be available to stream on Paramount+.

Initiatives

FilAm Creative announced its inaugural TV Creator Lab cohort of 25 writers.

The tuition-free, five-month program is designed to help emerging television creators develop their original scripted series. The selected writers will learn from working television executives, producers, showrunners and industry professionals.

The Lab launched Oct. 8 at Patriot Pictures in Los Angeles. The cohort gathered for a conversation with Lionsgate SVP of Television Richard Rothschild, Greg Coolidge (“The Continental: From the World of John Wick”) and Oren Segal, moderated by television director Francis dela Torre (“Almost Paradise”).

The writers selected are Angel Cielo, Candice Sarangay, Celena Cipriaso, Eileen Cabiling, Ella Espiritu, Eric J. De La Rosa, Eugene Ramos, Faith Christy Soliven, Frances Rubio, Geri Carillo, Hermie Castillo, Jaime Estepa, Jalen Giovanni Jones, Joshua Labata, Joy Regullano, Kim Marcelino, Nicole Wolf, Noël Wiggins, Rebecca Williams Spindler, Roann Enriquez, Rommel Rojas, Stacie Gancayco-Adlao, Teodorico Sajor, Walter Boholst and Yasmine Gomez.

*

The American Film Institute announced the mentors for its 2026 Writers’ Room Ready program.

This year’s mentors are Brad Ingelsby (“Task,” “Mare of Easttown”), Peter Gould (“Better Call Saul,” “Breaking Bad”) Patrik-Ian Polk (“Noah’s Arc,” “P-Valley”), Sev Ohanian (“Sinners,” “Searching”) and Sarah-Violet Bliss (“Scorn,” “Search Party”).

The creatives will be paired with AFI Class of 2025 graduates:

Brad Ingelsby with Nathan Bouton — “Black Tide,” one-hour drama

Peter Gould with Kirby Saxton — “Holy Water,” half-hour comedy

Patrik-Ian Polk with Chri’shawn Julius — “Pop Puss,” half-hour comedy

Sev Ohanian with Edward Nenedzhyan — “The Optic,” one-hour drama

Sarah-Violet Bliss with Annabel Newland — “Glitter,” half-hour comedy

“Great writing is taught in community, not isolation,” said Susan Ruskin, AFI Conservatory dean and executive vice president of the American Film Institute. “We are deeply grateful to our accomplished mentors, whose wisdom, expertise and generosity empower our Writers’ Room Ready participants to transform their potential into professional practice in the industry.”

The Writers’ Room Ready program recognizes outstanding original television pilot scripts written by AFI Conservatory Screenwriting Fellows.

Partnerships

Elmo and his “Sesame Street” friends are taking on an African safari adventure in a special PBS ‘Nature’ primetime crossover. “Sesame Street and the Great Elephant Adventure” premieres on Wednesday, Oct. 14 at 8 p.m. ET on PBS and PBS Kids and will stream on pbs.org/nature, YouTube,pbskids.org, the PBS KIDS Video app and the PBS app.

Per the release, “The adventure begins at the group’s safari lodge, where they meet the lodge manager and her young daughter, who introduce Elmo and Abby to Kenya’s culture, nature and wildlife. Along the way, Elmo struggles with the idea of leaving his adopted elephant behind but comes to learn that the greatest way to care for his new friend is to let her thrive where she belongs: in the wild.”

“Bringing Elmo and the ‘Sesame Street’ friends into the world of ‘Nature’ allows us to tell a unique story filled with adventure, discovery, and heart,” Sal Perez, executive producer for Sesame Workshop, said. “We hope this special event sparks curiosity in children and encourages them to see themselves as explorers and problem solvers, while reminding viewers of every age that some of life’s greatest lessons come from experiencing nature.”

Programming

Moonbug Entertainment announced that actress and performer Lauren Vaz will join Cashaé Monya in playing Meekah in the global “Blippi” franchise.

“Lauren brings such a natural warmth, confidence and sense of fun to Meekah,” Liz Katz, Associate General Manager of “Blippi” and lead of the Meekah franchise, said. “She really captures the curiosity and big-sister energy that families know and love about Meekah. We’re so excited to welcome her to our ensemble cast alongside Cashaé Monya as we enter an exciting new chapter for Meekah, with more to share in the weeks ahead.”

“Blippi” is a live-action kids’ franchise built around curiosity, exploration and real-world adventures. Meekah is an established character who can be brought to life by different performers. Vaz now joins Monya in sharing the role across the Blippi franchise, as Meekah prepares to enter an exciting new chapter.

“Getting to step into Meekah’s shoes is incredibly special to me,” Vaz said. “I love how she encourages kids to be curious, express themselves and have the confidence to jump in and try something new. Having already been part of the Blippi world on tour, I’m so excited to continue this journey with Meekah and bring my personality, creativity and sense of fun to all the adventures ahead.”

Executive News

Hearst Media Production Group named Amy DeGregorio as executive vice president of sales and revenue.

In the newly created role, DeGregorio will act as a key member of HMPG’s executive team and strategic advisor to the company’s president on revenue growth, commercialization and new business opportunities. She will be responsible for driving revenue strategy and overseeing sales and sponsorship activity.

Prior to her new role, DeGregorio served as senior vice president, managing director of sales for educational/informational programming for HMPG since 2022.

“Amy has done an exceptional job building meaningful brand partnerships and seamlessly integrating sponsors into our E/I programming,” said Bryan Curb, HMPG president. “As HMPG continues to expand, we want to bring that same expertise and strategic approach to our entire portfolio, creating new opportunities for brands to engage with our award-winning content and loyal audiences.”

In 2016, DeGregorio joined Litton Entertainment, which was rebranded to HMPG in 2022, as senior director, integrated marketing. She was promoted to vice president, integrated marketing and, in 2020, senior vice president, client solutions. Before joining Litton, she worked at CBS Television Stations, and has held roles at NBCUniversal, truTV, ABC Television and MTV Networks.

title: ‘Fourth Wing’ TV Series Casts Emilio Sakraya as Xaden Riorson
summary: Attention, “Fourth Wing” cadets: Amazon Prime Video’s TV adaptation of Rebecca Yarros’ bestselling romantasy series has found your wing leader. Emilio Sakraya has been cast in the role of Xaden Riorson, Variety has learned. He will star opposite Esther McGregor (“We Were Liars”) as Violet Sorrengail on the Prime Video TV series. Amazon declined comment. […]
content:
Attention, “Fourth Wing” cadets: Amazon Prime Video’s TV adaptation of Rebecca Yarros’ bestselling romantasy series has found your wing leader.

Emilio Sakraya has been cast in the role of Xaden Riorson, Variety has learned. He will star opposite Esther McGregor (“We Were Liars”) as Violet Sorrengail on the Prime Video TV series. Amazon declined comment.

Sakraya has a hefty list of credits in both TV and film from his native Germany as well as in the U.S.; his credits include “Rhinegold,” “Tribes of Europa” and “Warrior Nun.” His other recent projects include “Those About to Die,” and he’s set to appear in Season 3 of “One Piece.”

“Fourth Wing” is set inside the brutal world of Basgiath War College, where there is only one rule: graduate or die. Twenty-year-old Violet Sorrengail was always expected to live a quiet life — but she’s sent on an entirely different path when her mother, a general in the military, orders her to join the hundreds of candidates striving to become dragon riders, the elite of Navarre.

Popular on Variety

Starting with the release of New York Times bestseller “Fourth Wing” in May 2023, Yarros’ “The Empyrean” book series currently includes sequels “Iron Flame” (November 2023) and “Onyx Storm” (January 2025.) This September, Yarros released the novella “Threshing Day,” which tells 13 stories set in the “The Empyrean” universe. The titles and release dates for the planned fourth and fifth books have yet to be announced.

Ordered to series at Amazon in May, Meredith Averill (“Anne With an E”) is showrunner and executive producer of “Fourth Wing.” The show is also executive produced by Kilter Films (Lisa Joy — who also directs the pilot, Jonathan Nolan and Athena Wickham), Outlier Society (Michael B. Jordan and Elizabeth Raposo) and Premeditated Productions (Liz Pelletier and Sherryl Clark).

title: Denis Villeneuve Chose to Direct New James Bond Movie After ‘Dune 3’ Because ‘I Need a Powerful Rocket to Pull Me Away From Arrakis’
summary: Denis Villeneuve recently told Empire that he returned to “Dune” for a third and final chapter so he can be “severe with the material,” and that his upcoming James Bond movie will be the “very powerful rocket” he needs to “pull me away from Arrakis.” “I said, ‘Maybe it’s a good idea to go back […]
content:
Denis Villeneuve recently told Empire that he returned to “Dune” for a third and final chapter so he can be “severe with the material,” and that his upcoming James Bond movie will be the “very powerful rocket” he needs to “pull me away from Arrakis.”

“I said, ‘Maybe it’s a good idea to go back to this project, not out of nostalgia, not because I miss it, but the opposite — I’m tired of it.’ I want to make sure that I will be severe with the material. That I will not be complacent,” he explained. “I thought, ‘When it’s done, I need a very powerful rocket to pull me away from Arrakis.’ When I was asked to do the next Bond, I said: ‘OK, this is what I need.’”

Villeneuve, director of “Prisoners,” “Sicario” and “Arrival,” has not helmed a film outside the “Dune” franchise since “Part One” was released in 2021. “Dune: Part Two” hit theaters in 2024, and “Dune: Part Three” will debut on Dec. 18, 2026.

Popular on Variety

In June 2025, it was revealed that Villeneuve, a self-described “die-hard Bond fan,” will direct the next 007 movie. There’s been much speculation about who will take up the mantle after Daniel Craig’s 15-year run. Gary Oldman recently claimed that the next James Bond has already been picked, but no official casting announcement has been made.

Based on Frank Herbert’s “Dune Messiah,” “Dune: Part Three” chronicles Paul Atreides’ fall from prophetic liberator to tyrannical emperor. Timothée Chalamet stars as Paul alongside Zendaya, Jason Momoa, Florence Pugh, Robert Pattinson, Anya Taylor-Joy, Rebecca Ferguson, Josh Brolin and Javier Bardem.

In her own sit-down with Empire, Zendaya discussed the arc of her character, Chani, in “Dune: Part 3.” She revealed that in the new film, Chani feels “a deep pain” and “a deep betrayal” as Paul becomes unrecognizable from the man she fell in love with.

“In the previous film, she opened herself up to the idea of letting someone in, allowing a space for love or gentleness,” she said. “Well, we see how that goes. That part of her life is not as present anymore.”

title: Steven Soderbergh To Work With Matt Reeves To Complete Final Weeks Of Principal Photography On ‘The Batman Part II’
summary: EXCLUSIVE: As director Matt Reeves continues to attend to an ongoing family matter, Steven Soderbergh is coming on to help finish principal photography for the final weeks of DC Studios’ The Batman Part II. The news comes after production was paused on the film so that Reeves could focus on the personal matter. Soderbergh has […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: As director Matt Reeves continues to attend to an ongoing family matter, Steven Soderbergh is coming on to help finish principal photography for the final weeks of DC Studios’ The Batman Part II. The news comes after production was paused on the film so that Reeves could focus on the personal matter.

Soderbergh has been longtime admirer of Reeves work, and with Reeves unable to be on set, the Oscar-winning director offered to help with finishing principal photography on the film. Although Reeves is unable to be on set, the two will work together and remain in communication until filming has ended, with Reeves taking over post-production duties when he is ready to return.

The studio released a statement in regards to Soderbergh coming on to the production:

Watch on Deadline

“As Matt Reeves continues to attend to an ongoing family matter, Steven Soderbergh, as an admirer of Matt’s work, approached Matt and will step in, with the full support of DC Studios, to help the writer-director complete the final weeks of principal photography on The Batman Part 2. Matt and Steven will work closely together with the actors and crew to fulfill Matt’s vision of the film.”

Soderbergh also released a statement:

“I thought Matt Reeves’ work on The Batman was stunning; it was intentional, specific, and rigorously coherent. The goal here is to work with Matt and his team to generate footage that will integrate seamlessly with what’s already been shot so Matt can properly finish his film.”

Deadline first broke the news earlier this month that production would be paused while Reeves attended to a family matter. Prior to the pause, filming had been underway in London. The film is set to bow on February 18, 2028. Sources say it is too early to say whether the stoppage will have an effect on the release date.

The cast has Robert Pattinson, Andy Serkis and Colin Farrell returning respectively as Batman, Alfred and Penguin, with new additions Scarlett Johansson, Sebastian Stan, Brian Tyree Henry, Jayme Lawson, Charles Dance, Gil Perez-Abraham and Sebastian Koch.

title: Netflix Names Peter Rice As Chief Content Officer
summary: Moments after it emerged that Netflix had gotten rid of Bela Bajaria, it named Peter Rice as her replacement. Former Disney exec Rice takes the job starting October 26. Rice will oversee all content at Netflix including scripted and unscripted series, film and live events. Rice’s last full-time job was as Chairman of Walt Disney […]
content:
Moments after it emerged that Netflix had gotten rid of Bela Bajaria, it named Peter Rice as her replacement.

Former Disney exec Rice takes the job starting October 26.

Rice will oversee all content at Netflix including scripted and unscripted series, film and live events.

Rice’s last full-time job was as Chairman of Walt Disney Television and Chairman of General Entertainment for The Walt Disney Company. He was fired in June 2022 and replaced by Dana Walden.

He was named Head of Ceremonies and Content for the LA28 Olympic and Paralympic Games in July 2025.

Watch on Deadline

RELATED: List Of Hollywood & Media Layoffs From Paramount To Warner Bros Discovery To CNN & More

“Peter is one of the most effective at-scale operators in the entertainment industry. His business acumen is sharp, his talent relationships are exceptionally strong, and his experience across TV and film is deep and broad,” said Ted Sarandos, Co-CEO, Netflix. “He understands what makes stories resonate, and he’s spent his career helping talent do the best work of their lives. I’m excited to welcome him to Netflix as Chief Content Officer as we continue to scale and deliver members more of the stories they love.”

“Netflix has fundamentally changed the way stories are made, shared and experienced around the world,” said Rice. “They’ve shown again and again that they’re willing to take chances on distinctive voices and fresh ideas, and I’m excited to work with the team to help bring even more great stories to members everywhere.”

Internal Email from Ted Sarandos

title: Netflix’s Chief Content Officer Bela Bajaria Exiting
summary: Bela Bajaria is out at Netflix. The news comes only 24 hours after the streamer underwent a massive cull, laying off around 1,000 employees. Bajaria joined the company in 2016, initially running its unscripted TV slate, and was named Chief Content Officer in January 2023. There have been rumors about her being axed by the […]
content:
Bela Bajaria is out at Netflix.

The news comes only 24 hours after the streamer underwent a massive cull, laying off around 1,000 employees.

Bajaria joined the company in 2016, initially running its unscripted TV slate, and was named Chief Content Officer in January 2023.

There have been rumors about her being axed by the company for the past couple of weeks, all denied by Netflix. Former Disney exec Peter Rice has replaced her.

Watch on Deadline

RELATED: Netflix’s Bela Bajaria Has No Regrets Over Failed Warners Buy: “It Was Always A Nice To Have At A Certain Price”

It comes amid slowing growth for the streamer. Co-CEO Ted Sarandos said recently at the Bloomberg Screentime event, “At the time we said that, I think we were pretty unsophisticated about how we talked about engagement. Meaning, in that world, all the revenue is equal, a profit is equal, all engagement is equal, and all engagement is not equal. We are growing engagement, on 200 billion hours of watching, we grew 2% in our last announcement.”

RELATED: List Of Hollywood & Media Layoffs From Paramount To Warner Bros Discovery To CNN & More

Netflix has been struggling with ratings for second seasons for many of its shows including Beef and The Four Seasons. On its last earnings video, Sarandos claimed that it actually has improved this problem this year and said it was “very common” in the industry. Such issues, however, can’t have helped Bajaria’s cause.

“I want to thank Bela for a decade of dedication, innovation, creativity and leadership,” said Ted Sarandos, co-CEO of Netflix. “She led enormous changes at Netflix. She helped broaden our content offering to include the large-scale expansion of unscripted programming and the launches of live events and sports, in addition to crafting and running a world class, global slate of films and series. I’m incredibly grateful for everything she’s done to help Netflix entertain the world.”

RELATED: Netflix Layoffs Affect Unscripted Casting & Development Execs Impacted

Here is Sarandos’ internal email in full:

Hi everyone,



I have an important update to share about our Content leadership.



After a phenomenal decade at Netflix, Bela is leaving the company. It’s hard to overstate the impact Bela has had during her time here. From expanding our content offering to include the large-scale expansion of unscripted programming and the launches of live events and sports to helping shape the broadening of our content offering around the world. So much of what you see on Netflix today can be traced back to a Bela initiative: Insatiable, Queer Eye, Lupin, You, The Diplomat, WWE, YuYu Hakusho, The Night Agent, Heeramandi: The Diamond Bazaar, Squid Game, Tyson vs Paul, Cien años de soledad, the NFL. She also helped reshape our strategy to focus on fewer, bigger, better movies, championing films like KPop Demon Hunters, The Adventures of Cliff Booth, and Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew, as well as bringing award winning films like La Bola Negra and Possible Love to Netflix.



A tremendous and diverse range of content (and that’s just a snapshot), bringing joy to our members across so many genres.



Bela has built and shaped a truly global Content organization, hiring brilliant people and empowering them to make good decisions. I am incredibly grateful to her for everything she’s done.



I know this is a big change in a year that has already had its share. But I also see an opportunity to take our slate to the next level, especially in UCAN where we have an outsize impact in creating big, buzzy hits that our members love and drive conversation around the world.



To help us seize on this moment, I’m excited to share that we’ve hired a new leader. Peter Rice is joining Netflix as our new Chief Content Officer beginning next week. Peter is one of the most effective at-scale operators in the entertainment industry. His business acumen is sharp, his talent relationships are exceptionally strong, and his experience across both TV and film is deep and broad. On the film side, running Fox Searchlight, he helped bring beloved fan favorite films like Slumdog Millionaire, Little Miss Sunshine, Sideways and Juno to screens. And more recently, as Chairman of Walt Disney Television, he led one of the most successful television divisions in the world, where he was responsible for a massive breadth and scale of shows ranging from The Simpsons, American Idol ,and Modern Family, to The Bear, and Abbott Elementary, along with ABC News programming and major sporting events such as the Super Bowl, NBA Finals and FIFA World Cup Finals. He’s one of the few people in our industry who has ever operated at the quality and scale that we do at Netflix every day. In the last few years, he has turned his attention to creating and has produced films with Alex Garland, Danny Boyle, Chris Rock, Jason Reitman and Aaron Sorkin at Sony and A24.



I’ve gotten to know Peter personally over the years, and I’ve always been impressed by his straightforward approach, the depth of his relationships and his exceptional creative and business instincts. Talent should have the best experiences of their life here, and Peter and I both believe that Netflix can and should be the home of the best storytellers in the world.



It’s been an eventful series of days here, and I realize we’ve asked you to absorb a lot of news and a lot of information. But we all know change is what we do at Netflix. Greg and I will host a companywide town hall on Wednesday, October 21. I want everyone to hear how we’re thinking about the strategy and our execution amid this week’s changes, and to have a chance to ask questions. It will be informal and mostly Q&A, so please bring your questions about this week’s changes and anything else on your mind.

Please join me in thanking Bela, and welcoming Peter to the team.



Ted

title: White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia Defends Calling Herself A Lawyer Even Though She Did Not Pass Bar Exam
summary: White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia defended calling herself a lawyer even though she is not licensed to be an attorney at law. The Wall Street Journal reported that after graduating from Pepperdine Law School in 2011, Zacharia took the California bar exam but did not pass. In an appearance on Jack Posobiec’s show on […]
content:
White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia defended calling herself a lawyer even though she is not licensed to be an attorney at law.

The Wall Street Journal reported that after graduating from Pepperdine Law School in 2011, Zacharia took the California bar exam but did not pass.

In an appearance on Jack Posobiec’s show on Real America’s Voice, Zacharia said that “a lot of the misinformation, miscommunication” is “around the fact that I labeled myself a lawyer, and I consulted for a very long time many people in the field. ‘Is it okay and acceptable if I label myself lawyer, not attorney at law, not Katie Zacharia esquire, but lawyer, and provide legal analysis, not legal advice. And they said absolutely, across the board. You can call yourself a lawyer.'”

Since Zacharia took the post, there have been questions raised of her legal credentials, as she has talked of being a lawyer in numerous media appearances. Trump referred to her as an “attorney” in a Truth Social post announcing her selection. She also was general counsel of the advocacy group Fix California, founded by Ric Grenell.

Watch on Deadline

On Tuesday, shortly after giving her first press briefing, Zacharia appeared with Donald Trump as he embarked on a three-day campaign swing. When a reporter asked Trump where she passed the bar exam, he turned to her and she said, “When I moved to China.” She told The New York Times that she misunderstood the question and thought it was asking for information of where she was after law school.

In the interview with Posobiec, Zacharia said that she got a job in the international practice division of a Chinese law firm. “There’s no Chinese bar,” she said. “I had enough credentials, which was my law degree, to be able to do this practice. And these were multi-million dollar agreements and transactions that were cross border, and there I had all the necessary requirements to do that.”

The Campaign for Accountability filed a complaint with the State Bar of California on Wednesday, challenging her description of herself as a lawyer and as a general counsel.

In her Real America’s Voice interview, Zacharia also described the scramble to prepare for Tuesday’s briefing. After calling on three reporters, she called an end of the briefing, which lasted just 14 minutes. Zacharia said that she received the briefing materials only the night before and woke up at 3 a.m. to prepare. It wasn’t until about 8 a.m., she said, that the materials were finalized. “I never had a full briefing beforehand,” she said.

She also was asked about the inevitability of a Saturday Night Live skit, and said that she would like a “Scarlett Johansson type character.” But she said that she is not watching “anything right now except what he’s doing and focusing on what the president is up to and trying to amplify that.” “I do not want to see any of the other X or Instagram or TV right now.” She will get a short reprieve, as new episodes of SNL are not scheduled for the next two weeks.

title: ‘Crystal Lake’s Linda Cardellini Used Pam Voorhees’ Grief As “Fuel For Her Rage,” Reveals Her Favorite Kill Scenes: “Feels A Little Too Good”
summary: SPOILERS: This post contains details about the Peacock series Friday the 13th With the Friday the 13th prequel series Crystal Lake, longtime fans are treated to a backstory for the mother of all slashers. Linda Cardellini, who plays Jason Voorhees’ grieving mother Pam in the Peacock series from Brad Caleb Kane, which is now available […]
content:
SPOILERS: This post contains details about the Peacock series Friday the 13th

With the Friday the 13th prequel series Crystal Lake, longtime fans are treated to a backstory for the mother of all slashers.

Linda Cardellini, who plays Jason Voorhees’ grieving mother Pam in the Peacock series from Brad Caleb Kane, which is now available to stream, explained to Deadline that she used the maternal character’s grief as “fuel for her rage,” which ultimately pushes her to take murderous action months after her son Jason (Callum Vinson) drowns in the titular lake.

“It’s an interesting line that I walk as Pam because there’s part of her that doesn’t believe he’s totally gone, so there’s a real grief and a real longing that happens, but also hidden in there is a real hope that he might still be out there somewhere,” she explained. “So, that’s a really fun thing to play, because sometimes it can be total grief, and sometimes it can be in pain, and sometimes it can be grief hidden with a little bit of hope for who might be around the corner. And I think as that starts to pick up with her, that grief turns.”

Watch on Deadline

Cardellini continued, “But I think the real grief is how people have treated him, because he’s such a sweet vulnerable kid when we first meet him, and she loves him so much. Watching the world treat him poorly is terrible for her, and the idea of that continues to just spiral out of control and it goes to the place that she fears the most, fuel for her rage. And I think that that rage is relatable. I think that it overtakes her though. I think finally releasing that rage overtakes her, and it feels a little too good to her, so there’s a switch that comes on after that.”

Set several years before the events of Friday the 13th (1980), the prequel series gives Pam her first taste for blood as a pair of mysterious men come poking around about her past. She uses a familiar weapon to get rid of them.

Linda Cardellini as Pam Voorhees in ‘Crystal Lake’

“The first one with the machete, I enjoy. That was big,” said Cardellini. “We shot that for a week, that whole sequence, so we really took time with it, which was nice.”

As she grieves the loss of her son, Pam takes a maternal interest in Jason’s friend Grace (Gwendolyn Sundstrom), whom she notices has a neglectful mother. While confronting Grace’s mom at the fast-food restaurant where she works, Pam takes the squabble a little too far.

“There is some anger that comes out when I have a mallet in the fast food restaurant,” recalled Cardellini. “And that seething anger, before that kill really happens, was I think somewhere, that something needed to come out of her. So, that was a fun one for me.”

Linda Cardellini as Pam Voorhees in ‘Crystal Lake’

Now streaming on Peacock, Crystal Lake stars Cardellini as Pam Voorhees, who struggles to grieve after her son Jason drowned the summer before. As two strangers begin digging into her mysterious past, Pam goes to murderous lengths to keep her secrets buried and find her son, whom she’s convinced is still alive after his body was never recovered.

title: Olivia Rodrigo and Chappell Roan Compete on Game Shows Hosted by David Byrne in the Retro Video for ‘Expectations’ Remix
summary: Olivia Rodrigo and Chappell Roan appear on vintage game shows in the retro music video for the “Expectations” remix, featuring appearances from musician David Byrne and producer Dan Nigro. The clip, directed by Bardia Zeinali, shows Rodrigo and Roan (in her first-ever feature) appearing on sets clearly inspired by “Family Feud” and “Hollywood Squares.” Byrne […]
content:
Olivia Rodrigo and Chappell Roan appear on vintage game shows in the retro music video for the “Expectations” remix, featuring appearances from musician David Byrne and producer Dan Nigro.

The clip, directed by Bardia Zeinali, shows Rodrigo and Roan (in her first-ever feature) appearing on sets clearly inspired by “Family Feud” and “Hollywood Squares.” Byrne appears as Johnny Johnson, host of the “Big Expectations” show, where he asks three Rodrigos in different outfits “a little bit how you got here.”

What follows is a trip to the different sets and a new “Expectations” verse from Roan, who shows up on the set of “Sister Squabble” to contend with Rodrigo in a “Family Feud” face-off. “I took her to a concert front row thought it’d be fun,” she sings. “Her hand moving up my skirt, no piercing on her tongue / She said she’d call me later, that was three weeks ago / Classic L.A. behavior, she could’ve just said no.”

Popular on Variety

Nigro, who produced “Expectations” along with Roan and Rodrigo’s albums, pops up at the end clutching a giant brick of a phone straight out of the 1990s. His appearance makes sense, as he produced the track and its parent album “You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love.”

Speaking to Apple Music’s Zane Lowe on Thursday afternoon, Roan and Rodrigo explained why they teamed for the remix. “This is obviously my first feature,” said Roan. “I’ve never done this before, so it feels perfect to me. I don’t know. I feel like it represents a generation of songwriters that are just really thinking about their lyrics. I felt like with this song, I was like, ‘Wow, it’s so cool that she is putting a pretty difficult concept within the pop song,’ which is my favorite pop songs ever.”

Rodrigo explained that she had asked Byrne to appear in the video but was a “bit sheepish” about making the request. “I always feel shy asking people for favors, but he was so down,” she said. “He showed up the entire day. He had a character that he had built out and he made this Johnny Johnson character. There’s so many outtakes we have of him just improvising and riffing and he was so into it. And I was like, ‘Gosh, David, maybe he should be an actor too one of these days.” He’s very multi-talented.”

Beyond sharing Nigro as a producer, Rodrigo and Roan go back some years, as the latter supported the former on both her “Sour” and “Guts” tours. Roan recently performed at Rodrigo’s Daisy Chain Fields Festival in late August as part of an all-female lineup that featured Doechii, Rachel Chinouriri, Garbage, the Breeders and more.

title: The 27 Best ‘American Horror Story’ Characters, Ranked
summary: “American Horror Story” has given audiences a lot to chew on over the years: wildly inventive themes, sadistic imagery, over-the-top performances and gleefully macabre mythology. But arguably its greatest contribution to television since its debut in 2011 is its characters, an ever-expanding company of ill-fated spooks and kooks who rarely find a happy ending, and […]
content:
“American Horror Story” has given audiences a lot to chew on over the years: wildly inventive themes, sadistic imagery, over-the-top performances and gleefully macabre mythology.

But arguably its greatest contribution to television since its debut in 2011 is its characters, an ever-expanding company of ill-fated spooks and kooks who rarely find a happy ending, and yet we relish in watching their descent into whatever brand of hell the series is conjuring that season. The citizens of this connected universe of horror storytelling, from creators Ryan Murphy and Brad Fulchuk, are ultimately what stitch it all together, and have proven to be the enduring draw for audiences left wanting more from their favorites.

For its 13th season, “AHS” has banked on the bedrock of those characters by dipping back into its stable of actors and their alter egos for a mashup season. The satanic-centric story has been a chaotic exercise in fan service, with varying degrees of success. When it works, there are undeniable pleasures in seeing characters thought to be done and dusted come back for one more shot at a good line reading or an uncanny interaction with someone who shares their face. Many of those characters are on this list, some elevated by the extra screen time and some demoted for disrupting a previously perfect storyline.

As “AHS” plays the hits for 13, let’s rank the best characters from the series. The following list isn’t necessarily a grading of performance, but rather character arc, impact and sheer entertainment value. It should also be noted that “AHS13” focuses almost exclusively on characters from the first eight seasons, with good reason. Even for their flaws, those characters are the series’ best work. More recent seasons were considered for this list, but frankly, “AHS” hasn’t aged all that well –– even though some of its characters have.

title: Jenna Ortega Says She Hopes ‘Klara and the Sun’ Encourages People to ‘Put Down the Computers and Phones’ as Dystopian Film World Premieres in London
summary: Jenna Ortega hopes that her new film, the dystopian sci-fi “Klara and the Sun,” can remind people to live in the moment in the age of AI and all-consuming technology. “I think we gotta put our focus on one another and put down the computers and phones,” the star told Variety on the red carpet […]
content:
Jenna Ortega hopes that her new film, the dystopian sci-fi “Klara and the Sun,” can remind people to live in the moment in the age of AI and all-consuming technology.

“I think we gotta put our focus on one another and put down the computers and phones,” the star told Variety on the red carpet at the movie’s world premiere at London Film Festival on Thursday night.

Ortega, wearing a stunning yellow lace dress and hair piece, added: “Remember to be present and to appreciate people while they’re standing right in front of you.”

Based on Nobel Prize winner Kazuo Ishiguro’s bestselling 2021 novel of the same name, “Klara and the Sun” is set in a future where advances in genetic engineering have divided humans into strict social classes. Ortega plays Klara, an artificial android companion who is purchased for an ailing girl named Josie (Mia Tharia). “Klara and the Sun” is directed by “Thor” helmer Taika Waititi and also stars Amy Adams as Josie’s mother, Aran Murphy (son of Cillian Murphy), Natasha Lyonne, Steve Buscemi and more.

Popular on Variety

Waititi, Adams, Murphy and Lyonne all walked the London Film Festival red carpet on Thursday night, alongside Waititi’s wife Rita Ora, author Ishiguro and a surprise appearance from Florence Pugh, who stunned in a blue floral gown with statement sleeves. Pugh enthusiastically greeted Ortega and Adams before they all posed for photos together alongside producer Rachel Forman.

Florence Pugh, Amy Adams, Jenna Ortega and Rachel Forman at the “Klara and the Sun” world premiere in London. Getty Images for BFI

Standing alongside Ortega, Adams added that everyone she’s spoken to has gotten “something different” out of the film. “That, to me, is a really successful film that communicates something different to each viewer. So I like hearing what people get out of it,” she said.

Ortega clarified that though Klara is an “artificial friend,” she doesn’t work like the AI that we know today.

“AI I guess pulls all this information from the internet and Klara gets all her information from the real world,” she said. “So that’s a little bit different. She’s kind of like a toddler in a sense. Playing her specifically in this film was really interesting because Taika wanted a more human approach, so he didn’t want to do movement that was too robotic, maybe more sort of clumsy and unknowing.”

Waititi echoed Ortega in saying that the film’s message is to “put the phone down.”

“I would just like people to remember what friendship is, connect with people and just be,” he said. “Just be in the moment.”

Ishiguro acknowledged that, since his novel came out in 2021, the world’s awareness and attitude about AI has changed greatly.

“This film doesn’t address a lot of the anxieties that you and I may have right now about where we’re going with the technology. I mean, I think quite rightly, it’s really come center stage,” he said. “I’m aware that this film is coming out into a very different world to the one that my novel came out in five years ago, and I don’t know how that will change people’s expectations or how people look at things. But I’ll say that this isn’t another film about how an AI machine seems to be nice and then becomes sinister and ends up killing all the nice people in the film. It’s not that sort of story.”

Ishiguro is wading more into film, confirming to Variety that he’s working on a new project with Tim Burton, for which he penned an original script. Though Burton and Ishiguro have a mutual friend in “Wednesday” star Ortega, he said she’s not the one who introduced them.

“I thought this was supposed to be a big secret!” Ishiguro said. “No, Jenna didn’t introduce us. Tim lives quite near where I live in North London, and I was dropping in on him in his very strange and wacky and beautiful house. I mean, it looks like a Tim Burton set. And we started to talk about a project and I wrote a script on spec. We decided to just do it privately between the two of us, and then take it to people.”

He added that it’s not a “war film,” saying: “Genre-wise, it’s very hard to pigeonhole. It’s a Tim Burton film!”

“Klara and the Sun” is set to hit theaters via Sony Pictures on Oct. 23.

content:
A wind-whipped brushfire ignited in western Malibu today and spread from one to five acres in a matter of about 15 minutes. Within 30 minutes, the incident was estimated at about 20 acres, including various spot fires that erupted as winds pushed the flames forward.

Dubbed the Bryson Fire, the blaze was first reported shortly before 5 p.m. near the intersection of Mullholland Highway and Encinal Canyon Road. The ignition point seems to be just north of Encinal in between the former Malibu Golf Club and Saddle Rock Ranch. More specifically, TV reports have the blaze starting right next to the Camp Kilpatrick juvenile detention center.

According to the Watch Duty app, evacuation warnings were issued from the L.A. County line in the north and south toward Point Dume. See map below.

Watch on Deadline

Santa Ana winds were fanning the fire in the area at about 26 mph out of the NNE, according to a National Weather Service reading for the Malibu Hills. At 4:56 p.m., the temperature was 84 degrees with a relative humidity of 13%.

The area is sparsely populated with private estates set atop hills or within canyons, making firefighting access difficult. Among the properties in the area are Saddle Rock Ranch, where

Water-dropping helicopters and fixed-wing aircraft were dispatched to the scene.

City News Service contributed to this report.

title: Anna Faris Was “Hurt” By Chuck Lorre’s Comments About Her ‘Mom’ Exit: “Yikes”
summary: Six years after announcing her departure from CBS’s Mom, Anna Faris has reacted to Chuck Lorre’s comments about her exit. On Thursday, the actress shared a statement explaining that she “never took a day of [the show] for granted” after series co-creator Lorre wrote in his new memoir Sitcom that he “was, in fact, correct” […]
content:
Six years after announcing her departure from CBS‘s Mom, Anna Faris has reacted to Chuck Lorre‘s comments about her exit.

On Thursday, the actress shared a statement explaining that she “never took a day of [the show] for granted” after series co-creator Lorre wrote in his new memoir Sitcom that he “was, in fact, correct” about his initial reluctance to cast her as Christy Plunkett in the sitcom.

“Yikes. Yes, I read a few things. I really didn’t see that coming. Of course it hurts,” she began in a statement on Instagram. “Chuck gave me a job I loved, and for seven years I never took a day of it for granted. I’m proud of what we made together, and nothing changes how grateful I am for those people and those years.”

Faris continued, “I’ve been sober for a year and a half. I was on a show about recovery and then I lived it. Now I’m healthy, I’m working, and I’m happier than I’ve been in a long time. If anyone reading this is where I was, I hope that’s useful. It gets better. I’m proof.”

Watch on Deadline

Premiering in 2013, Faris starred in the first seven seasons of Mom as recovering alcoholic Christy, who struggles to maintain a job, her family and her sobriety as her mom Bonnie (Allison Janney), who’s also in recovery, moves in with her.

Faris left the show in 2020 to “pursue new opportunities,” leaving Janney as the sole lead for the eighth and final season, which ended in 2021.

In an excerpt from Sitcom, Lorre wrote, “I wasn’t sure Anna would be appropriate for this kind of material. Then I thought about how badly I’d bungled my working relationship with Charlie Sheen.

After his experience with Charlie Sheen on Two and a Half Men, Lorre recalled conceding, “Someone’s personal life is none of my business. The mom in Mom would be, and should be, Anna Faris.”

Lorre added, “As the years went by, it became apparent that my initial reluctance to hire Anna was, in fact, correct. After six years, she left the show for mysterious reasons that were not mysterious to anyone on the show.”

title: Diddy’s Prison Head Injury Mystery Deepens; Feds Deny Fight With Drug Kingpin Sent Grammy Winner To Hospital
summary: A dust-up with a drug lord was not what sent Sean Combs to the hospital with a head injury last week, the Bureau of Prisons insists. However, the actual cause of the injury and Combs’ current status is under lock and key. “While, for privacy, safety, and security reasons, we do not comment on the […]
content:
A dust-up with a drug lord was not what sent Sean Combs to the hospital with a head injury last week, the Bureau of Prisons insists. However, the actual cause of the injury and Combs’ current status is under lock and key.

“While, for privacy, safety, and security reasons, we do not comment on the conditions of confinement for any individual in our custody, we can tell you that the story you are referring to is false and did not happen,” officials at FCI Fort Dix in New Jersey say of reports by TMZ and others that Diddy got in a fight on October 9 with fellow inmate Christopher “Dudus” Coke. The reports claim that the alleged brawl was over the spotlight and cell sweeps a recent NBC News exposé on Combs’ contraband and high living had brought down on the minimum-security facility and its more than 4,200 residents.

Coke may not have been involved, but clearly something went down, because Combs was taken to a local hospital early on October 10 with something wrong with his noggin. He retuned to Fort Dix about 12 hours later, without stitches or any noticeable treatment, I’m told. Since then, the whole situation has gone on lockdown, literally and figuratively.

RELATED: Trump Celebrity Supporters: Famous Folks In Favor Of The 47th President

Convicted by a NYC jury of two counts of transportation to engage in prostitution in July 2025 at the end of lurid and violence-detailing trial, Combs was sentenced in September 2025 to a 50-month stint with time served.

With a release date that has gone back and forth since, Diddy currently is scheduled to be released on March 2, 2028.

It is extremely rare for the BoP to reveal anything about a prisoner, not matter how high-profile they are. Yet, in the Combs case and leaks about what went down last week, it seems some information or misinformation allegedly was coming from inside Fort Dix, and officials felt compelled to address the matter. The BoP added today: “Sean Combs is in the custody of the Federal Bureau of Prisons and is incarcerated at the Federal Correctional Institution Fort Dix. Beyond this, we have no additional information to provide.”

In fact, even those close to Combs have little information, I’ve learned.

“We appreciate the BOP’s clarification, which confirms our concerns about the accuracy of the initial reports,” Combs spokesperson Juda Engelmayer told Deadline on Thursday. “We have not independently verified the circumstances surrounding the alleged incident, and I don’t want to speculate about what may or may not have happened. At this point, we have no verified information indicating that Sean was attacked by Christopher Coke or anyone else, or that he sustained injuries.”

Combs has been in solitary confinement since images of him with a smuggled-in smartphone and other luxuries were made public. Stuck in the SHU (Special Housing Unit), as its termed, Combs has very limited communication with the outside world.

That communication is limited by design, and by choice, it seems.

Over the past week, Diddy has not used the daily call he is permitted to touch base with his attorneys. Nor has he contacted other reps from solitary. Because 56-year-old Combs is over 18, the Bureau of Prisons is not required to pass along any info to anyone about him. To put it simply, if Combs wants someone, anyone, to know what’s going on, it’s his call to make.

The Bad Boy Records founder has not been making that call.

The mitigating factor might be when he is released from the SHU. Unless there is another incident, Combs will be in solitary confinement for at least one more week, sources say.

In the free world, and having failed to secure a pardon from old party pal Donald Trump, Combs is pursuing a fast-track appeal of his case. At the same time, the much-accused three-time Grammy winner is battling multiple civil suits and a possible sexual battery indictment by the L.A. District Attorney.

After a trial in summer 2025, the Southern District of New York’s U.S. Attorney’s Office fell far short in its efforts to convince a Manhattan jury that Combs was guilty of racketeering conspiracy and sex trafficking charges. If Combs had been found guilty in the trial full of filmed sex parties and freak-offs, Cassie Ventura beatings, drug binges, threats, exploding cars and allegedly hanging people off balconies, the one-time mini-mogul could have received a life sentence.

title: Greta Gerwig On Securing Led Zeppelin’s “Stairway to Heaven” For ‘Narnia’ Trailer: “They Too Love C.S. Lewis”
summary: As Netflix debuted the first trailer this week for Greta Gerwig’s Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew, fans were treated to an iconic needle drop. Gerwig recently explained how she was able to convince Led Zeppelin to let her license “Stairway to Heaven” for the feature adaptation of C.S. Lewis’ prequel book, after the band has notoriously […]
content:
As Netflix debuted the first trailer this week for Greta Gerwig‘s Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew, fans were treated to an iconic needle drop.

Gerwig recently explained how she was able to convince Led Zeppelin to let her license “Stairway to Heaven” for the feature adaptation of C.S. Lewis’ prequel book, after the band has notoriously shot down all previous requests to feature the 1971 song on screen.

“I showed them and I talked to them, Robert Plant and Jimmy Page, and I was so moved that they allowed me to use the song,” Gerwig told Stephen Colbert at a Q&A. “They did it because they saw the heart of the story in the film and they too love C.S. Lewis, and they have a reverence for his work. The whole thing was very fortuitous. But I’m so happy that it got to be this song.”

Gerwig explained that the song was “exactly the story” of the movie. “It’s an epic song. It’s an amazing song. It’s a narrative. It’s about a spiritual journey,” she said.

Watch on Deadline

“It’s about the true path of enlightenment and spirituality, and then this path of false idols and the wrong roads you can go down,” added Gerwig. “And I was like, ‘This is exactly the story of this movie.’ It really is a spiritual quest and a spiritual journey, so to me, this was the song that made sense to introduce this into the world. But this song, they had not let it be used in anything.”

Previous failed attempts to license “Stairway to Heaven” include a 1995 episode of The Simpsons, Almost Famous (2000) and last year’s Stranger Things finale, while Mike Myers poked fun at the band’s protectiveness of the track in a scene from Wayne’s World (1992).

Premiering Feb. 12, 2027 in Imax before its April 2 Netflix debut, Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew follows two children Digory (David McKenna) and Polly (Beatrice Campbell) as they explore the office of Digory’s Uncle Andrew (Daniel Craig) and end up in a magical wood filled with pools that lead to other worlds. One pool takes them to a dead city, where they awaken its queen (Emma Mackey) who exterminated its population, accidentally setting her loose on London.

title: Nawazuddin Siddiqui to Star as Delhi Street Detective in ‘Kabootar’ (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Indian thespian Nawazuddin Siddiqui is attached to lead “Kabootar,” the debut feature from writer-director Ishan Sharma, produced by Nikhil Chaudhary of MDC Filmworks. The film is structured as a co-production between MDC Filmworks in India, Haiku Films in France, and Rein Film in Norway, with Rohit Saxena serving as co-producer on the Indian side. Principal […]
content:
Indian thespian Nawazuddin Siddiqui is attached to lead “Kabootar,” the debut feature from writer-director Ishan Sharma, produced by Nikhil Chaudhary of MDC Filmworks.

The film is structured as a co-production between MDC Filmworks in India, Haiku Films in France, and Rein Film in Norway, with Rohit Saxena serving as co-producer on the Indian side. Principal photography is scheduled to begin in Delhi in early 2027.

Set against the crumbling architecture of Old Delhi, “Kabootar” centers on Mehboob, a street detective who secretly reads letters written to a Djinn in search of prospective clients. His path crosses with Naoko, a Japanese tourist carrying the weight of a painful past, and Ruby, a young child searching for his parents.

Popular on Variety

Siddiqui is among the most decorated actors of his generation in Indian cinema. He has appeared in Anurag Kashyap’s “Gangs of Wasseypur,” Ritesh Batra’s “The Lunchbox,” and Nandita Das’s “Manto” – all of which debuted in Cannes – and starred in Netflix’s hit thriller series “Sacred Games.” He received an International Emmy nomination for his lead role in Netflix film “Serious Men.”

Chaudhary said: “Nawaz is an actor of extraordinary range. He can be dangerous in ‘Gangs of Wasseypur’ and heartbreakingly gentle in ‘The Lunchbox.’ He’s also one of the few Indian actors with a real international presence. His films have gone to Cannes multiple times, and he has been nominated for an International Emmy. For an India-France-Norway co-production, that matters enormously in taking ‘Kabootar’ to audiences around the world. Just as important, he knows Delhi intimately. For Ishan and I, this film is a love letter to the city, and we needed an actor who could understand it, feel it and embody it. He does all three.”

Sharma, who developed the script through the production and storytelling Workshop at the Festival des 3 Continents in Nantes – formerly known as the Produire au Sud Workshop – added: “Nawaz has been an invisible collaborator to a generation of young writers and directors, myself included. We write with his performances in our minds. From ‘Anwar Ka Ajab Kissa’ to ‘The Lunchbox,’ I’ve always admired the intensity and love he brings to a character, and his rare ability to move between hope and despair, light and dark, without losing either. ‘Kabootar’ asks something of him that audiences haven’t seen before. To have him take that leap with us is a gift. I can’t wait to build this world with him.”

The project has been selected for a series of international market showcases, including the Tasveer Film Market in Seattle, Film Bazaar in Goa – organized by India’s National Film Development Corporation (NFDC) – and the NFDC lineup at this year’s European Film Market in Berlin. Later this month, Chaudhary will pitch the film in the APN+ Track of the Asian Producers Network in Singapore.

Casting director Dilip Shankar, whose credits include “Life of Pi” and “Monsoon Wedding,” said: “Nawazuddin will bring Mehboob’s eccentric humor, emotional depth and quiet vulnerability to life with rare authenticity. The character demands mischief, rage, tenderness and grace. With his rooted presence and remarkable nuance, Nawazuddin embodies Mehboob’s essential contradictions. His performance anchors ‘Kabootar’ in the lived-in, poignant texture of Old Delhi.”

Sharma is a graduate of the Satyajit Ray Film & Television Institute. His short films “The God of Panic Street” (2019) and “A Season of Mangoes” (2022) have played international festivals and collected several awards, including the Cinema Experimenta Award.
