title: Aran Murphy on Playing an Angry Young Man in ‘Youth’ and ‘War’ — and His Father Cillian’s Influence
summary: Aran Murphy is having quite a month, as he co-stars on not one, but two HBO shows — “Youth” and “War” — and plays one of the leads of Taika Waititi’s dystopian film “Klara and the Sun,” set to be released on Oct. 23. But if you think you’ve seen the 19-year-old actor before, it […]
content:
Aran Murphy is having quite a month, as he co-stars on not one, but two HBO shows — “Youth” and “War” — and plays one of the leads of Taika Waititi’s dystopian film “Klara and the Sun,” set to be released on Oct. 23. But if you think you’ve seen the 19-year-old actor before, it could be because of his strong resemblance to his Oscar-winning father, Cillian Murphy. “I don’t even think we look that much alike, but people seem to think otherwise,” the younger Murphy tells Variety.

In both “War” and “Youth,” Murphy plays a troubled teenager negotiating complex relationships with his parents as they navigate divorce. “Youth” follows Sharon Horgan as a rambunctious 50-year-old divorcée dipping back into the dating pool. As her son Rauri, Murphy plays a creepy, brooding university dropout whom audiences also can’t help sympathize with. After only a few days at school, he returns home because a rumor has been spread about him and a drunken hookup that suggests he may be a predator. Did Murphy decide for himself whether Rauri is to be believed about his innocence during the incident? “Yeah!” he says. “I mean, I’d like to think so. It’s up to the audience; I don’t decide that. But I want to back my character.”

Popular on Variety

Murphy’s and Rauri’s life trajectories are very different, but their timelines aren’t, which helped him get into character. “Contextually, we both just left school and were 18 — it was really about making decisions and whether college is the right thing, that kind of entrance into adult life, so that was a nice thing to draw on to relate to him,” he says.

He adds that Hogan’s strong scripts and professionalism helped Murphy find his footing on set.

“She was so awesome and charismatic and open to ideas that it was easy to just work and create that bond over shooting,” Murphy says. “The words were already so good, we were able to springboard off that and find the chemistry on the day.”

In “War,” Murphy has a raucous introduction in the Oct. 15 episode as Gabriel, who’s torn between his mother (Sienna Miller as Carla) and stepfather (Dominic West as Morgan) during their ugly, high-profile divorce. Caught between Carla, a past-her-prime actress, and Morgan, a billionaire social media entrepreneur, Gabriel finds himself in the crossfire, used as an asset to negotiate between them. Like Rauri in “Youth,” Murphy similarly credits his character’s duality and relatability to creator George Kay.

“It was all in the script — his frustration with what’s going on and nowhere to put it,” Murphy says. “I’m sure it’s a pretty universal kind of thing: People just want to take their anger out in some way.”

One manifestation of Gabriel’s anger is physical, meaning that Murphy needed to throw a punch while the character is drunk at a party after his friend makes a rude remark about his parents’ divorce.

“I’d never had to do something like that — that was new,” Murphy says. “That was a bit nerve-racking, because you don’t want to accidentally punch someone in the face.”

Acting professionally is all pretty new to Murphy. Despite growing up with artistic parents (his mother, Yvonne McGuinness, is an Irish visual artist), Murphy originally saw himself on the football field.

“That faded pretty quickly,” Murphy says. “I did a play when I was 11, and that was a really big deal for me. That was kind of the thing that showed me I wanted to [perform] for real when I became of age.”

Murphy, of course, grew up watching his father act. “Seeing my dad onscreen in dramatic situations as an 8-year-old was pretty full-on,” he says, mentioning Ken Loach war drama “The Wind That Shakes the Barley,” which won the Palme D’Or at the 2006 Cannes Film Festival. “I think I need to revisit it as a 19-year-old.”

He’s seen most, but “definitely not all,” of his father’s filmography, and is “forever grateful” for informing his film education at a young age, and having insightful conversations with him about acting. But Cillian’s biggest role for Murphy has been as a supportive father, rather than a public figure or acting influence. “I think living with someone who’s in the public eye, the novelty of that wears off pretty quick,” Murphy says.

Murphy was more starstruck by working with Waititi on “Klara and the Sun” starring Jenna Ortega and Amy Adams. Based on the novel by Kazuo Ishiguro, the film follows Ortega as a robot girl experiencing the grandeur of human life for the first time. Though the movie is coming out this month, it was shot in early 2024 when Murphy was 16.

“It was incredibly surreal. One minute I was in school, and then the next I was flying out to New Zealand and shooting a Taika Waititi film at 16, so it was just absolutely nuts,” Murphy says. “[Ortega and Adams] are so great, just being in their presence and being able to learn so much. They’re also so kind and accommodating. It’s just a massive learning experience, and I’m really grateful for it.”

Despite his pride in the project, he says he’s “not a fan” of AI, adding “I don’t think it’s a net positive for the industry.” For Murphy, this film is important for “opening those discussions” about AI and “talking about the importance of human life and especially friendship and love and human qualities.”

With this momentum behind him, Murphy says he’s eager to keep learning: “I’m just auditioning and crossing my fingers. Basically, I’m just open to anything.”

title: Woodstock Film Festival Names Jessica Edwards as Executive Director
summary: Jessica Edwards has been named the new executive director of the Woodstock Film Festival, the organization announced Sunday as the 27th annual festival came to a close. Edwards will take over the role from Meira Blaustein, the festival’s co-founder. “I have had the pleasure of working with Jessica at the Woodstock Film Festival over the […]
content:
Jessica Edwards has been named the new executive director of the Woodstock Film Festival, the organization announced Sunday as the 27th annual festival came to a close. Edwards will take over the role from Meira Blaustein, the festival’s co-founder.

“I have had the pleasure of working with Jessica at the Woodstock Film Festival over the past few years, and I have nothing but the greatest respect for her,” said Blaustein. “As a filmmaker, a distribution consultant, and a former publicist, Jessica brings with her deep understanding, creative vision, and vast and strong contacts in the film industry. As a resident of the Hudson Valley, she knows and loves the region and its community. I am confident that she will not only retain the vision of the Woodstock Film Festival, which I have worked so long and hard to build and nurture, but will lead it towards an exciting new growth. I can’t wait to see what the next few years will bring. Welcome, Jessica!”

Claude Dal Farra, who serves as president of the festival’s board, also welcomed Edwards appointment.

Popular on Variety

“From our very first meeting with Jessica, it was clear to us that she was the natural person to succeed Meira and carry forward the extraordinary work Meira has done over more than 25 years,” she said. “Jessica understands what makes the Woodstock Film Festival special — its commitment to filmmakers, its independent spirit, and its deep connection to the Hudson Valley — while also bringing the experience, energy, and vision to lead it into its next chapter. On behalf of the Board, we are tremendously excited to welcome Jessica as our new Executive Director, and to work with her on the future of the Festival.”

Edwards shared that this role is one she considers a “dream job.” “I’m honored to build on the founders’ legacy and help shape the festival’s future,” she said. “Woodstock’s history is shaped by its creativity, innovation, and independent spirit. I want to carry that spirit forward by bringing filmmakers and industry partners from around the world together with audiences here in the Hudson Valley. My vision for the festival is to create opportunities for people to meet, share ideas, and discover films together — connections that I hope will support filmmakers and inspire the next generation of cinema lovers.”

The festival ran from Wednesday to Sunday, during which an Honorary Maverick Award was presented to Blaustein to recognize her leadership, more than 26 years of dedication to independent cinema and the legacy she has built.

Festival winners included “Mouse” by Kelly O’Sullivan and Alex Thompson, “Rehearsals for a Revolution” by Pegah Ahangarani, “Washed Up” by Isabel Moncloa Daly and “They’re Here” by Laura Poitras & Rachel Lauren Mueller.

title: Cindy Crawford & Family Pay Tribute To Late Son Presley Gerber: “‘Til We Meet Again, Our Sweet Boy”
summary: Following Presley Gerber’s death at age 27 last month, his family has shared a statement paying tribute and thanking fans for their support. On Sunday, Cindy Crawford mourned the loss of her first-born she described as a “sweet, beautiful soul” in a statement signed by herself, husband Rande Gerber and their daughter Kaia Gerber, after […]
content:
Following Presley Gerber‘s death at age 27 last month, his family has shared a statement paying tribute and thanking fans for their support.

On Sunday, Cindy Crawford mourned the loss of her first-born she described as a “sweet, beautiful soul” in a statement signed by herself, husband Rande Gerber and their daughter Kaia Gerber, after Presley died on Sept. 20 in a rehab facility.

“We are beyond heartbroken to lose our beloved son and brother. We feel so blessed to have had Presley in our lives for 27 years,” read the statement shared on Instagram. “He is a sweet, beautiful soul who loved and is loved, now and forever. We are so proud of how he showed up in the world, with kindness and vulnerability.

“We are grateful for the outpouring of love and support from so many who know and love our family and even strangers who feel our pain. Til we meet again our sweet boy. We love you forever, Mom, Dad and Kaia,” the statement concluded.

Watch on Deadline

After Presley died in a Santa Monica rehab facility last month, Los Angeles County Medical Examiner’s Office performed an autopsy and deferred a cause and manner of death, pending SMPD’s investigation of the death as a “possible overdose.”

Presley, who was arrested and charged with a DUI in 2019, had previously been open about his struggles with mental health and substance abuse, chronicling his journey on Instagram.

title: How A24 Spurred A Meme Craze & Got The Many To Watch ‘You Can See Everything’: Documentary  Opens To $15M Milestone
summary: Less than two months ago, the public didn’t even know that a Nathan Fielder co-directed and starring documentary which followed controversial Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes even existed. And here we are with A24 having cracked the code on Gen Z again with an awesome $15M opening; 2,000-plus sellouts, and lines around the block for the […]
content:
Less than two months ago, the public didn’t even know that a Nathan Fielder co-directed and starring documentary which followed controversial Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes even existed.

And here we are with A24 having cracked the code on Gen Z again with an awesome $15M opening; 2,000-plus sellouts, and lines around the block for the 3-hour You Can See Everything, this after their all-time grossing hit Backrooms ($400.6M WW).

In addition to being the second best opening for a documentary at the domestic box office behind 2004’s Fahrenheit 9/11 ($23.9M), the whole box office resonance of You Can See Everything brings to mind when niche HBO-born Sacha Baron Cohen spread his wings with Borat which opened to $26.4M. In fact, the debut here for You Can See Everything is the best for a movie in under 1,000 locations since 2006’s Borat.

Yes, theatrical is becoming the alpha and streaming the basic cable in today’s world. But still, the needle to thread for theatrical success remains nuanced. There’s plenty of adult sophisticated fare at the fall box office that’s struggling. How to trapped lasers in a bootle and make originality king? A documentary which follows a deadpan wisenheimer who eloquently and hysterically grills an arguably vain, tech baron who swindled hundreds of millions of dollars, before her federal prison stint, is the way to go. But more so, the documentary is dressed up as a noir with a thrilling score, grey overcast tones and a third act that’s bananas fun, especially if you’ve been obsessed with Holmes and the fictional portrayals of her in the Hulu Emmy winning limited series The Dropout.

Watch on Deadline

And that runtime of 3 hours proved to be no deterrent. The documentary has plenty of twists and turns in The Odyssey and Spider-Man: Brand New Day sense of the word. There’s even advice out there as to when to take a bathroom break in the movie:

essential information if you’re seeing Nathan this weekend pic.twitter.com/Gi4IvUB0GP — 🍓✨carlye wisel (@carlyewisel) October 17, 2026

A24 has long been hailed for their guerrilla marketing and ability to speak to the Gen Z crowd. That wasn’t lost this weekend with 70% under 25 showing up this weekend. The pic at 56% guys to 44% women was a date film with 44% watching You Can See Everything with a partner, spouse, girlfriend or boyfriend.

How do you do it, A24? Keep it cool, keep it simple, and never act like you’re overselling the demo. They can sniff if they’re being pressured. Then pray, pray they take ownership of it after the pure placement of materials on social. And that’s what we saw going on here with the You Can See Everything fans posting a plethora of memes reminiscence of Barbie‘s run-up when moviegoers spurred the Barbenheimer online fandom.

Secrecy was the special sauce with You Can See Everything directed by Lance Oppenheim and Fielder sub rosa over the last four years. They had the freedom to pursue the project without a deadline or any obligation to deliver a finished film. A24 even made clear that if nothing came of it, the project could simply be scrapped. In the end what Fielder and Oppenheim delivered was an Empire Strikes Back-like sequel to Alex Gibney’s 2019 HBO doc The Inventor: Out for Blood in Silicon Valley. Critical reviews are at 99% on Rotten Tomatoes with audiences at 98%. Screen Engine/Rentrak Postmark exits are an awesome 91% definite recommend which are scores that massive Marvel movies like Black Panther and Star Wars Force Awakens land. At 4.8, it’s the biggest Letterboxed score ever.

Who the hell drops a movie at Telluride in secrecy? A24, that’s who. The small town awards season kick-off fest typically has secret screenings that are playing at other festivals (i.e. last year’s Frankenstein which bowed at Venice and went on to play TIFF), however, to needle drop a world premiere sans any intel was a gong that rang around the world. A24 dropped the teaser just as the movie was hitting the screen in Colorado on Sept. 6. A trailer followed on Sept. 23 with Fielder opening it up by asking Holmes “You really feel you did nothing wrong?” to which she responds earnestly, “I did not.” A24 says it’s their second most viewed trailer ever dropped after Backrooms.

Holmes’ unhinged partner Billy Evans, who is a big part of the documentary and mans her social media, insisted that her Twitter handle be tagged by A24 in the trailer drop. LOL.

Might as well tag me. 🫠 — Elizabeth Holmes (@ElizabethHolmes) September 7, 2026

And then came the memes, so myriad, we can’t run them all; Kermit and Miss Piggy as Fielder and Holmes stealing the show:

Outdoor intrigued with Holmes’ buzzing eyes.

Can't miss it. You Can See Everything opens nationwide tomorrow. pic.twitter.com/waq2gKYdSX — A24 (@A24) October 15, 2026

Even more jaw dropping, A24 didn’t do any sports buys on You Can See Everything. That maneuver, no matter the movie, is always the power pill for many major studio tentpole campaigns. That said A24 did break their own marketing rules and took out sports spots on Backrooms which mushroomed to an $81.4M record opening for the NY based studio (the movie was originally forecasted at $30M+ in its pre-weekend forecast) back in late May.

We understand that You Can See Everything wasn’t a coastal play and exceeded in its big markets from Nashville, TN at the Belcourt which had lines around the block to the Scotiabank in Toronto. Top five cities were NYC, LA, San Francisco, Chicago, Boston and Seattle. The Kabuki theater in San Francisco was the documentary’s top gross, which stands to reason as tech heads flocked to the film.

A24 was keen to keep this release tight and limited this weekend, to get in the cultural ether and make tickets a prized fetch. For when You Can See Everything goes wider next weekend, look out DC’s Clayface because Holmes is coming for blood.

It’s clear with the success of You Can See Everything: Bust out the Holmes and Fielder Halloween costumes, stat.

content:
The 27th Woodstock Film Festival has concluded with the announcement of its Maverick Award winners and a new executive director.

On Sunday, the festival named Jessica Edwards as its new executive director, taking over for co-founder Meira Blaustein, as Kelly O’Sullivan and Alex Thompson’s Mouse won Best Narrative Feature during Sunday’s awards brunch.

“To call this a dream job would be an understatement,” said Edwards in a statement. “I’m honored to build on the founders’ legacy and help shape the festival’s future. Woodstock’s history is shaped by its creativity, innovation, and independent spirit. I want to carry that spirit forward by bringing filmmakers and industry partners from around the world together with audiences here in the Hudson Valley.

“My vision for the festival is to create opportunities for people to meet, share ideas, and discover films together — connections that I hope will support filmmakers and inspire the next generation of cinema lovers,” she added.

Watch on Deadline

Blaustein, who has served as executive director since co-founding the film festival in 2000, received a special Honorary Maverick Award recognizing her visionary leadership and enduring legacy.

“I have had the pleasure of working with Jessica at the Woodstock Film Festival over the past few years, and I have nothing but the greatest respect for her,” said Blaustein.

“As a filmmaker, a distribution consultant, and a former publicist, Jessica brings with her deep understanding, creative vision, and vast and strong contacts in the film industry,” she continued. “As a resident of the Hudson Valley, she knows and loves the region and its community. I am confident that she will not only retain the vision of the Woodstock Film Festival, which I have worked so long and hard to build and nurture, but will lead it towards an exciting new growth. I can’t wait to see what the next few years will bring. Welcome, Jessica!”

Meanwhile, this year’s competition winners include Best Documentary Feature recipient Rehearsals for a Revolution, Best Ultra Indie winner Washed Up and Best Short Documentary winner They’re Here for Best Short Documentary, decided by jury members like Aya Cash, Corbin Bernsen, Debra Granik, Ellen Kuras, Bill Horberg, Michèle Stephenson, Marshall Curry, Lori Singer, Robert Stone, Amy Gossels, Shelby Stone and more.

title: Tom Arnold Denies Chuck Lorre’s Claim That He Made Writers Put His Name On ‘Roseanne’ Scripts: “Never”
summary: As Chuck Lorre’s memoir continues to make the rounds, Tom Arnold is the latest sitcom actor to respond to criticisms of himself in the book. Following Lorre’s claim in Sitcom that writers on Roseanne (1988-’97) were told to “put Tom’s name on the front page [of scripts]—­as if Tom had written them,” Arnold emphasized that […]
content:
As Chuck Lorre‘s memoir continues to make the rounds, Tom Arnold is the latest sitcom actor to respond to criticisms of himself in the book.

Following Lorre’s claim in Sitcom that writers on Roseanne (1988-’97) were told to “put Tom’s name on the front page [of scripts]—­as if Tom had written them,” Arnold emphasized that he “never would put my name on a script” that he didn’t write, recounting from his perspective “how it went on the show.”

“Roseanne and I sat around talking about what we wanted to do in the next season, or maybe some ideas we had that’d be fun episodes, or groundbreaking, or whatever our bullsh*t was, and I’d write them down,” explained Arnold to Entertainment Weekly. “We kind of doodled around. And then, you know, in probably June, the head writer and the writers would come back and the show starts shooting in August.”

Arnold noted that after breaking the story with the writers’ room, no matter whose name was on the script, it had “every writer’s fingerprints on it.”

Watch on Deadline

“They all work on everything,” he explained. “Even the guys that are brought in to be the punch-up guys, the joke guys, everybody in the room at some point is pitching different things.”

Roseanne and Tom Arnold on ‘Roseanne’

Serving as a producer on Seasons 3-6, during which he had a recurring guest spot as Arnie Thomas, Arnold recalled he “didn’t realize Chuck was having such a hard time, because it seemed to go pretty well. There’s nothing outstanding.”

“I know one thing I said to Chuck early on… I said, ‘You’re in charge of the writers, but they have to have their name on a script every year. Each one of these guys,'” he noted. “Because you get more money, you just get more. I want everybody to have their name on a script. We’ll write extra scripts, whatever we gotta do.”

Arnold continued, “One friend that I really made a point, a guy named Joel Madison, who I just talked to, I don’t think Chuck liked him because he did not give him a script. It was two weeks before we were done, and I found out. I go, ‘Hey, Chuck, you’ve gotta give Joel a script. I told you you had to do that.’ He said, ‘Oh, shoot. Yeah, well, all I’ve got is this one with my name on it.’ I go, ‘Put Joel’s name on it. You’re the head writer, you make a lot of money, put his name.'”

Lorre, who was a writer and producer on Roseanne in Seasons 3 and 4, claimed in his memoir that writer Danny Jacobson once “showed me a sloppy, hand-­scribbled couple of pages and explained this was a ‘script’ by the show’s new executive producer, Tom Arnold. It had been part of Danny’s job to write real scripts and put Tom’s name on the front page—­as if Tom had written them.”

The 10x Emmy nominee alleged that “several other staff writers would be ordered to do this on many occasions,” which Jacobson confirmed to EW, claiming that Arnold’s then wife Roseanne “bullied me into letting him write a script, which as Chuck described, was exactly right. So it was really — it was a bad energy on the show.”

title: Julianne Moore Says ‘The Debut’ Is ‘One of the Best Scripts I’ve Ever Read’ as Jesse Eisenberg’s Musical Comedy Closes London Film Festival on a High Note
summary: “The Debut” ended London Film Festival on a high note Sunday night as director Jesse Eisenberg and star Julianne Moore gushed over each other to a packed audience at the Royal Festival Hall. “I mean, this movie stars my favorite person, Julianne Moore,” Eisenberg began as the duo came onstage to introduce the musical comedy. […]
content:
“The Debut” ended London Film Festival on a high note Sunday night as director Jesse Eisenberg and star Julianne Moore gushed over each other to a packed audience at the Royal Festival Hall.

“I mean, this movie stars my favorite person, Julianne Moore,” Eisenberg began as the duo came onstage to introduce the musical comedy. “But ironically, strangely, it’s the story of my life.”

Written and directed by Eisenberg, “The Debut” stars Moore as Mona Friedman, a shy New Jersey housewife who auditions for a part in her local theater’s production of a fictional musical called “Nosy Neighbors.” After she’s cast in the supporting role of Miss Danielle, Friedman’s life begins to unravel as she becomes more consumed with playing the part and falls under the spell of director Jerry Blankenbuehler (Paul Giamatti).

Eisenberg said he started doing community theater when he was “7 years old and miserable,” and it changed his life forever. “I wanted to write about that experience in my life, but I could only picture Julianne, to the point where I was writing it and she was inspiring me,” he added. “It’s the most thrilling experience to watch her and edit her for two years.”

Popular on Variety

Moore, wearing a chic black gown, returned the praise. She called “The Debut” an “incredible gift” and said it’s “one of the best scripts I’ve ever read in my entire life.”

“It was such an honor to receive it and such a thrill to go to work every day and to get to do this incredible part with these tremendous actors,” she said, adding of Eisenberg: “He’s a beautiful writer, exemplary director and just a great talent.”

In response, Eisenberg quipped: “I just want to note that the only time I’m called beautiful, it’s about writing.”

“The Debut” team fully leaned in for the U.K. premiere, with each guest finding a fake Playbill for “Nosy Neighbors” at their seat. During the screening, there was plenty of audible laughter and several rounds of applause for high points in Moore’s campy performance.

Ahead of “The Debut” U.K. premiere, #LondonFilmFestival attendees are given Playbills for the movie’s fictional musical “Nosy Neighbors.” pic.twitter.com/4LpSKJcaQD — Variety (@Variety) October 18, 2026

Sadly, Eisenberg said that Giamatti could not attend as he has COVID-19. “I wish he could be here. He is the greatest guy and you would love to hear him talk,” he said. “Paul’s been my favorite actor since I’m young, Julianne’s been my favorite actress since I’m young.”

Alongside Moore and Giamatti, “The Debut” also stars Eisenberg, Halle Bailey, Colton Ryan and Bonnie Milligan as actors in the musical. Bernadette Peters, Lilli Cooper, Maulik Pancholy and Havana Rose Liu round out the cast.

Of acting with his childhood heroes, Eisenberg said it was “the thrill of a lifetime” but also “very strange.”

“I was spending so much time enthralled with them, and then it was like Michael Jordan said, ‘Here, you take the ball!’ And I’m like, ‘What is this thing?’ So it was so distracting to me. I hope to never act alongside them again,” he joked. “I was my worst self.”

“The Debut” premiered at Telluride Film Festival last month, where it earned rave reviews and Oscar buzz for leading lady Moore. In Variety‘s review, chief film critic Owen Gleiberman wrote: “‘The Debut,’ a small-town-theater comedy rooted in big ideas, is a funny and dizzying mind-bender. It’s like ‘Waiting for Guffman’ made by the Coen brothers at their most rivetingly unhinged.”

“The Debut” is set to hit theaters on Dec. 11 via A24.

title: Joe Manganiello Says Ben Affleck’s Scrapped Batman Film Would Have Seen Deathstroke ‘Dismantle Batman’s Entire Life’ and Kill Commissioner Gordon
summary: Joe Manganiello, who was set to reprise the role of Deathstroke in Ben Affleck’s scrapped Batman film, is telling all about what would have happened had the superhero film made it to theaters. In his new memoir “Bloodlines,” published on Tuesday, the actor wrote that Affleck, who was attached as the writer, director, producer and […]
content:
Joe Manganiello, who was set to reprise the role of Deathstroke in Ben Affleck’s scrapped Batman film, is telling all about what would have happened had the superhero film made it to theaters.

In his new memoir “Bloodlines,” published on Tuesday, the actor wrote that Affleck, who was attached as the writer, director, producer and star, planned to make the film “a superhero version of David Fincher’s ‘The Game’” in which Deathstroke would “dismantle Batman’s entire life” after being made to think the Caped Crusader killed his son (via EW).

Manganiello, who first played Deathstroke, a DC supervillain, briefly in 2017’s “Justice League,” wrote that murdering Commissioner Gordon, holding Alfred Pennyworth hostage and breaking into the Batcave would all be a part of Deathstroke’s revenge plan, and that the film would have included a fight in which “Deathstroke would nearly kill both Batman and Batgirl before they would both escape via an aboveground train.”

Popular on Variety

According to the “Magic Mike” actor, the film would have concluded with a “climactic one-on-one showdown through the streets of Gotham.” “It sounded good to me,” Manganiello wrote. “I told Ben how great I thought his films were, especially ‘The Town,’ and how I was really looking forward to seeing his Best Picture version of a Batman movie.” He went on to explain that Affleck’s roles on set sounded like “a lot” for a single person, to which the “Argo” director responded: “Yeah, I know…But don’t worry, you’re in good hands. You’re in good hands, man.”

Ultimately, the film never came out. Recently, Ben Affleck appeared on the “Happy Sad Confused” podcast and called the “Justice League” reshoots the “low point of my career.”

“The experience of ‘Justice League’ was so negative for lots of different reasons, some of which have to do with where I was at personally and some of which had to do with the tragedy that happened at that time,” Affleck said. “I saw how not to make a movie like that, which is where the studio is at odds with the filmmaker. You are really making a mistake. I was really glad and gratified that Zack got to release [his version via the Snyder Cut]. That was fucking great. I was really happy for him. That was shitty, him being taken off that movie and the reshoots that we did. If you want the low point of my career, it was that.”

title: Taylor Swift’s ‘The Life of a Showgirl’ Spends 15th Week at No. 1 on Albums Chart
summary: Taylor Swift holds steady at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 as “The Life of a Showgirl” spends a 15th non-consecutive week atop the chart. This week, “Showgirl” earned an additional 87,000 equivalent album units thanks to its “Encore” edition, which touted four new tracks including the Hot 100-topping “Patient Zero.” “Showgirl” was initially released […]
content:
Taylor Swift holds steady at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 as “The Life of a Showgirl” spends a 15th non-consecutive week atop the chart.

This week, “Showgirl” earned an additional 87,000 equivalent album units thanks to its “Encore” edition, which touted four new tracks including the Hot 100-topping “Patient Zero.”

“Showgirl” was initially released in October 2025, moving a whopping 2.7 million copies in its opening frame. Swift released the “Encore” edition on September 24, collecting 173,000 equivalent units in its first week. Last Monday, “Patient Zero” held steady at No. 1 on the Hot 100 for a second week, marking Swift’s 51st career week at the top and giving her the fifth-highest total in chart history for weeks at No. 1 behind Mariah Carey (101), Rihanna (60), the Beatles (59) and Drake (58).

Popular on Variety

The singer, meanwhile, has been performing at private events over the past few months, including an appearance at the Grammy Museum and a Ross House FYC showcase. Just last night, she gave her first full-band performance since the Eras Tour at the Academy Museum 6th Annual Gala. Swift ran through songs including “I Knew It, I Knew You” and “The Fate of Ophelia,” as well as “Blank Space” and “Love Story.”

Elsewhere on the Billboard 200, rock group Greta Van Fleet earned its fourth top 10 with their latest, “Palace for the People,” which bows at No. 9. Olivia Rodrigo’s “You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love” lands at No. 2, followed by Morgan Wallen’s “I’m the Problem” at No. 3, Ella Langley’s “Dandelion” at No. 4 and Noah Kahan’s “The Great Divide” at No. 5. Drake’s “Habibti” lands at No. 6; Olivia Dean’s “The Art of Loving” bumps to No. 7; Kahan’s “Stick Season” rises to No. 8; and Drake’s “Iceman” rounds out the top 10.

title: Betty McGuire, ‘Growing Pains’ Actress, Dies at 100
summary: Betty McGuire, the actress best known for her role as grandmother Kate Malone on the ABC sitcom “Growing Pains, died Oct. 8 at the Motion Picture & Television Fund’s Wasserman Campus in Woodland Hills, Calif., of natural causes. She was 100. Keith Gerchak, McGuire’s POA, confirmed her death. McGuire had a seven-year run on “Growing […]
content:
Betty McGuire, the actress best known for her role as grandmother Kate Malone on the ABC sitcom “Growing Pains, died Oct. 8 at the Motion Picture & Television Fund’s Wasserman Campus in Woodland Hills, Calif., of natural causes. She was 100.

Keith Gerchak, McGuire’s POA, confirmed her death.

McGuire had a seven-year run on “Growing Pains” as Kate Malone, mother to Joanna Kerns’ Maggie. She was a recurring character in Seasons 1-2 and again in Seasons 4-7.

Aside from “Growing Pains,” McGuire’s career in television includes appearances in shows including “Falcon Crest,” “The Doris Day Show,” “Columbo,” “Star Trek: Deep Space Nine,” “Hill Street Blues,” “ER,” “CSI: Miami,” “MacGyver,” Moonlighting” and “Charlie’s Angels.”

Popular on Variety

On the silver screen, McGuire appeared in feature films such as “Cheech & Chong’s Up in Smoke” and Michael Crichton’s “Coma.”

The actress also performed with notable Broadway names including Ethel Merman, Barbara Cook, Bea Arthur and Tony Randall in original productions of “Plain and Fancy,” “Happy Hunting” and “Oh, Captain!” She headlined as “Mame” at Caesars Palace in Las Vegas and toured in productions of “Gypsy,” “Auntie Mame,” “Mame,” “Oliver!” “How to Succeed in Business…” and “The Ziegfeld Follies of 1956.”

Later in life, McGuire volunteered as a receptionist and advocate at the Coalition for Economic Survival legal clinic in Los Angeles to offer support for low-income tenants facing eviction. She was an active resident of The Motion Picture & Television Fund Home. On Channel 22, the on-campus TV station at the retirement community, she hosted her own talk show, “GabFest.”

McGuire has no survivors.

title: ‘SNL UK’ Takes Aim At Shane Gillis On ‘Weekend Update’: “You Stupid F*cking C*nt”
summary: While Saturday Night Live was off this weekend, its British counterpart pulled no punches in criticizing last week’s episode of the U.S. sketch comedy show. On Satuday, SNL UK‘s “Weekend Update” co-host Ania Magliano ended the segment with a joke about Shane Gillis, following his complaint during last weekend’s SNL opening monologue that “women just […]
content:
While Saturday Night Live was off this weekend, its British counterpart pulled no punches in criticizing last week’s episode of the U.S. sketch comedy show.

On Satuday, SNL UK‘s “ ” co-host Ania Magliano ended the segment with a joke about Shane Gillis, following his complaint during last weekend’s SNL opening monologue that “women just dress like whores now” at the gym.

“A ride operator at Munich Oktoberfest was praised for giving out free cycling shorts to female riders. Wearing the gym shorts will protect women from being up-skirted, but it does make them vulnerable to something much worse,” said Magliano as a still of Gillis’ monologue appeared next to her.

With the audience already erupting in laughter, Magliano dug in her heels, poking fun at the United States’ strict broadcasting rules after Gillis accidentally dropped the F-bomb during a sketch.

Watch on Deadline

Magliano continued, “Last week on SNL, comedian Shane Gillis also caused controversy by dropping the F-bomb. Oh Shane, you’re not allowed to say that, you stupid fucking cunt.”

Although Gillis quickly apologized for the expletive, he’s yet to respond to the ongoing backlash from fellow comedians and fans alike over his monologue, especially in the wake of an alleged gang rape by fraternity members known as the Cornell 7.

Gillis’ latest hosting gig on SNL comes after he hosted in 2024 and 2025, following his removal from the NBC sketch comedy‘s featured cast days after he was announced in 2019. The decision came in response to resurfaced videos of Gillis mocking Asian accents, in addition to using ethnic and gay slurs.

title: Betty McGuire Dies: Broadway Actress & ‘Growing Pains’ Guest Star Was 100
summary: Betty McGuire, the Broadway actress who also appeared on the ABC sitcom Growing Pains, has died. She was 100. On Sunday, McGuire’s rep confirmed that the actress died of natural causes on Thursday, Oct. 8 at the Motion Picture & Television Country House and Hospital in Woodland Hills. Born 1933 in Bridgeport, Connecticut, McGuire made […]
content:
Betty McGuire, the Broadway actress who also appeared on the ABC sitcom Growing Pains, has died. She was 100.

On Sunday, McGuire’s rep confirmed that the actress died of natural causes on Thursday, Oct. 8 at the Motion Picture & Television Country House and Hospital in Woodland Hills.

Born 1933 in Bridgeport, Connecticut, McGuire made her Broadway debut as Rebecca in the 1955 musical Plain and Fancy, also appearing on the Great White Way in Happy Hunting (1956) and Oh Captain! (1958), working with such talents as Ethel Merman, Barbara Cook, Bea Arthur and Tony Randall. She also starred in touring productions of Auntie Mame, Gypsy and Oliver!.

McGuire’s onscreen debut came in a 1973 episode of The Doris Day Show, before she went on to appear in shows like Columbo, Phyllis, Charlie’s Angels, Hart to Hart, Little House on the Prairie, Moonlighting, Matlock, MacGyver, Star Trek: Deep Space Nine, Murphy Brown, CSI: Miami, ER, 7th Heaven and more.

Watch on Deadline

The actress was best known for her recurring guest role as grandmother Kate Malone on Growing Pains.

McGuire also starred in movies like Cheech & Chong’s Up in Smoke (1978), Hometown USA (1980), The Incredible Shrinking Woman (1981) and Wishmaster (1997).

Outside of acting, McGuire spent years volunteering for the Coalition for Economic Survival legal clinic in Los Angeles, offering support to low-income tenants fighting eviction. She also hosted GabFest, a segment of NBC Nightly News with Lester Holt that spotlit her fellow residents at The Motion Picture & Television Fund Home.

title: Jesse Eisenberg TV Series Produced By Peter Rice To Be Taken Out By A24
summary: Jesse Eisenberg is shifting his attention to television. Coming off his latest movie as a writer-director, A24’s The Debut, starring Julianne Moore, Eisenberg is prepping a TV series, also for A24. Written, executive produced and to be directed by Eisenberg, the show, which is expected to be taken out in the coming weeks, is executive […]
content:
Jesse Eisenberg is shifting his attention to television. Coming off his latest movie as a writer-director, A24‘s The Debut, starring Julianne Moore, Eisenberg is prepping a TV series, also for A24. Written, executive produced and to be directed by Eisenberg, the show, which is expected to be taken out in the coming weeks, is executive produced by former Disney and Fox executive Peter Rice, who was just named Chief Content Officer for Netflix, under his A24 deal.

The yet-untitled series is based on a short story by Eisenberg about a young woman where new ideas and relationships challenge her beliefs, sources said. In a interview with THR on the red carpet for the London Film Festival premiere of The Debut, Eisenberg noted that It is about the beginning of the culture wars and follows an 18-year-old girl in the fall of 2002.

It is unclear whether the short story in question is the tale of Harper Jablonski, a freshman struggling with her college experience, from Eisenberg’s 2016 collection of short stories, Bream Gives Me Hiccups.

Watch on Deadline

Netflix — now with Rice at the content helm — will likely be in the mix for the series; the streamer is home to such high-profile A24 shows as Beef and the upcoming untitled Millie Bobby Brown & David Harbour spy drama and Trigger Point, headlined by Joel Edgerton.

Given Rice’s new job, he is not expected to have hands-on involvement going forward but will likely retain his executive producer credit having developed the series. Netflix’s top film executive Dan Lin and Ori Marmur remain EPs on Netflix’s Avatar: The Last Airbender series and Prime Video’s The Boys franchise, respectively.

After an early stage career as a child actor, Eisenberg made his screen debut on TV as part of the main cast of Fox’s 1999 comedy-drama series Get Real. He then transitioned to movies where his main focus has been for the past two and a half decades, including his Oscar-nominated performance as Mark Zuckerberg in The Social Network and his Oscar win for writing his 2024 feature A Real Pain.

The Debut marks Eisenberg’s third feature as a writer-director, following the 2022 When You Finish Saving the World and A Real Pain. In TV, he most recently starred in the 2022 FX limited series Fleishman Is In Trouble. He previously developed a TV series adaptation of his short story collection Bream Gives Me Hiccups for Amazon and A24 a decade ago and single-camera comedy The Market for J.J. Abrams’ Bad Robot and Warner Bros. TV.

title: TikTok Restores ‘Musk’ Doc Account “After An Error” Resulted In Suspension
summary: As Alex Gibney takes on Elon Musk with his latest documentary, the Bleecker/Universal project is continuing to push back against censorship on social platforms. Following the reported “permanent suspension” of the doc Musk‘s promotional TikTok account, the platform has claimed the decision was the result of “an error” and has since restored the profile. “I […]
content:
As Alex Gibney takes on Elon Musk with his latest documentary, the Bleecker/Universal project is continuing to push back against censorship on social platforms.

Following the reported “permanent suspension” of the doc Musk‘s promotional TikTok account, the platform has claimed the decision was the result of “an error” and has since restored the profile.

“I can confirm that the advertising account has been restored after an error,” a TikTok spokesperson told The Verge on Sunday. A source close to production confirmed to Deadline that the account has been restored.

The reversal comes after Bleecker Street was informed of the account’s “permanent suspension” on Friday, according to The Hollywood Reporter. A spokesperson for the distributor expressed their “disappointment” in the timing, given the doc’s premiere this weekend.

Watch on Deadline

While Musk does not have an investment in TikTok, his longtime friend Larry Ellison, who also invested in Musk’s Tesla and X, is a part-owner of the short-form video platform.

Last month, YouTube, Instagram, Meta, TikTok and Musk-owned X rejected the trailer over depiction of “political” or “election” content, with Meta calling the decision “an error” and reversing it shortly after.

Producer Nick Shumaker commented on the social platforms’ blocking of the trailer, empashizing, “We’ve got to be as loud as possible about this right now.”

“It feels like the folks who own these companies have an interesting perspective on what the First Amendment is,” he explained. “I was joking about it with Gibney the other day where it’s almost like the half amendment now… That’s all I can really ascertain because it was a big surprise because the trailer is not a political ad.”

Now playing in theaters, Musk producers have described the project as “a definitive and unvarnished examination” of the tech trillionaire and his less than savory business practices.

title: Katseye Says They’re ‘So Proud’ of Sophia Ahead of Her Return to the Group: ‘She’s Our Sister’
summary: Katseye is excited to welcome Sophia Laforteza back to the group after a brief hiatus. Members Lara Raj, Daniela Avanzini, Megan Skiendiel and Yoonchae Jeung shared their support for their “sister” on the carpet at the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show on Sunday. “We are so happy that she’s coming back,” Raj told E! News, speaking […]
content:
Katseye is excited to welcome Sophia Laforteza back to the group after a brief hiatus. Members Lara Raj, Daniela Avanzini, Megan Skiendiel and Yoonchae Jeung shared their support for their “sister” on the carpet at the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show on Sunday.

“We are so happy that she’s coming back,” Raj told E! News, speaking for the group. “We are so proud of her. I think she’s really been so brave, and we respect her so much for taking the space and taking time for her health. She’s our sister, so we can’t wait for her to come back.”

Laforteza announced in August that she would be taking a step back from upcoming promotional activities to prioritize her “mental health and wellness.” HYBE x Geffen confirmed earlier this month that Laforteza is scheduled to return to group activities beginning in January 2027.

Popular on Variety

The girl group kicked off its “Wildworld” tour in Dublin on Sept. 1, with the first U.S. stop in Miami on Oct. 13. The tour continues across North America through the end of November, with shows in Boston, Montreal, Chicago, Los Angeles and Mexico City.

Laforteza’s step back from the group comes after member Manon Bannerman announced her own temporary hiatus in February. There has been no announcement made about her return to the group.

Katseye formed and gained popularity as K-pop trainees on the 2023 reality competition series “Dream Academy.” Their new documentary, “Katseye: Wild Hearts,” hit Disney+ and Hulu on Oct. 16. The film picks up where Netflix docuseries “Pop Star Academy: Katseye” left off, following the group on their journey to pop stardom after leaving the competition series.

title: Taika Waititi Confirms His ‘Star Wars’ Movie Has Been Put ‘on Ice’ Indefinitely
summary: Taika Waititi’s “Star Wars” movie, which has been in development since 2020, is officially on hold, the director confirmed while promoting his latest film “Klara and the Sun.” “I hate to break this to you, but we’re going to actually put it on ice and we’re working on a different thing together,” Waititi told Inverse […]
content:
Taika Waititi’s “Star Wars” movie, which has been in development since 2020, is officially on hold, the director confirmed while promoting his latest film “Klara and the Sun.”

“I hate to break this to you, but we’re going to actually put it on ice and we’re working on a different thing together,” Waititi told Inverse while discussing “Star Wars.” His publicist reportedly told him not to say more about it during the conversaiton. “Well, there’s your answer,” Waititi said. “I don’t even know how to dress it up or make it even vague.” “It’s very iced. I’ve got about four other movies I’m trying to do,” he continued. “Ice ages do come to an end… Who knows?”

Back in Jan., the director had said he was “trying to go back and harness a little bit more of the fun from the original films, which is what I remember [from] them.”

Popular on Variety

“The stakes are very high, and there’s serious things going on, but there’s also a lot of fun to be had in those films. That’s what I was trying to bring back,” Waititi continued. “I was trying to work in a world that was a little bit separate to that because they’ve got so many things going on within that space. For me to do something there, it would need to be a little different and a little bit more its own thing.”

Previously, exiting Lucasfilm boss Kathleen Kennedy said Waititi’s “Star Wars” was “still somewhat alive.”

Thus far, Waititi’s latest directorial effort, “Klara and the Sun,” has met a mixed response from critics and fans. Variety’s Guy Lodge wrote in his review that “Jenna Ortega tries hard to illuminate this misbegotten Kazuo Ishiguro adaptation, but Waititi’s decision to play it for strained, whimsical comedy is ruinous.”

title: Jason Sudeikis Hopes to Continue ‘Ted Lasso’ for Season 5, Says Coverage of Split From Olivia Wilde Missed a ‘Million Little Things’: ‘It’s Always More Complicated’
summary: Jason Sudeikis opened up on a recent episode of “Talk Easy with Sam Fragoso,” discussing his hopes for “Ted Lasso” Season 5, how the show “saved” him from “self-harm” and what the public got wrong about his closely followed 2020 split from ex Olivia Wilde. Sudeikis and Fragoso talked “Ted Lasso” up top, as the […]
content:
Jason Sudeikis opened up on a recent episode of “Talk Easy with Sam Fragoso,” discussing his hopes for “Ted Lasso” Season 5, how the show “saved” him from “self-harm” and what the public got wrong about his closely followed 2020 split from ex Olivia Wilde.

Sudeikis and Fragoso talked “Ted Lasso” up top, as the host asked whether the actor wanted to continue the show for Seasons 5 and 6. (The Season 4 finale aired earlier this month.) Sudeikis said he “would like to,” but the status of future seasons remains unknown: “Yeah, I just don’t know,” he said, assuring Fragoso he wasn’t being coy “intentionally.” “We haven’t started a writers’ room or anything like that,” he noted. He added that he would “assume” Apple would continue the show if the main cast wanted to return.

The former “Saturday Night Live” star also got candid about what “Ted Lasso” saved him from, as he’s mentioned on multiple occasions. “Some form of self-harm. Flat out,” Sudeikis answered, describing a feeling that he hadn’t felt since “the confusing teenage years.” “ That’s probably the rawest, most, maybe embarrassing, but I don’t think it’s embarrassing… It does bubble up shame in me to think like, ‘How dare you? How dare you have those kinds of thoughts,’ you know?” The actor continued to describe wanting to be a drummer or a dancer as a teen to get out his emotions. “So how did [‘Ted Lasso’] save me? To a certain degree, it helped [and] it carried me as sometimes the work has done in the past.”

Popular on Variety

Sudeikis’s ex-fiancé, Olivia Wilde, also came up, as the host asked about what the “Ted Lasso” star feels the public coverage of their separation missed. (Sudeikis specifically made headlines in 2022 when Wilde was served with child custody documents during her appearance at CinemaCon.)

“Oh, gosh. I mean, a million little things,” he responded. “But, but what’s interesting is that it allows you capacity for empathy for when others go through those. And you need not be as lucky as we are to get to do something that we love.”

He continued: “I don’t wish it on anyone because I don’t think it really moves the needle. And to be clear, this isn’t like, all evil is just misunderstood or something like that. I just mean these, interpersonal situations that then get portrayed as being these binary situations of right and wrong… It’s always more complicated, more human than that.”

Sudeikis praised Wilde’s work: “Olivia loves what she does and is very, very good at and always has been. I’m thrilled for her.” (The actress and director is in the middle of the Oscars conversation for her work on “The Invite.”)

title: ‘Glee’ Reunion: Chris Colfer Joins Darren Criss Onstage to Perform ‘Baby It’s Cold Outside’ During London Concert
summary: Darren Criss’ one-night-only concert at the Royal Albert Hall in London became a “Glee” reunion when the singer surprised audiences by bringing out Chris Colfer and performing “Baby It’s Cold Outside” as an homage to their characters on the hit show, Kurt Hummel and Blaine Anderson. Criss began the song solo, telling the audience he’d […]
content:
Darren Criss‘ one-night-only concert at the Royal Albert Hall in London became a “Glee” reunion when the singer surprised audiences by bringing out Chris Colfer and performing “Baby It’s Cold Outside” as an homage to their characters on the hit show, Kurt Hummel and Blaine Anderson.

Criss began the song solo, telling the audience he’d be singing both parts, even though “it’s not supposed to be like that, but I’ve managed to pull off so many things,” he said, before Colfer joined him a few verses later. “The only thing inappropriate about doing this song is doing it without me,” joked Colfer before he began singing.

Criss and Colfer first performed the song during the Season 2 Episode 10 titled “A Very Glee Christmas,” which aired in 2010. Their characters were fan favorites who began dating in Season 2 before getting engaged and married in the final season.

Popular on Variety

Last month, following long-swirling rumors of a potential “Glee” reboot, creator Ryan Murphy officially weighed in and revealed there’s a script. “Well, funny you ask, ’cause I just finished the script an hour ago,” Murphy told Entertainment Tonight. “So, we have a script. Brad [Falchuk], Ian [Brennan] and I, who wrote all the first two seasons, have written something. I’ve been in touch with around 10 of the original cast members. It’s very sweet, and they all had a lot of questions, but they all were very enthusiastic about the idea.”

Murphy noted that although there is a script, “nobody’s read it.” “So I don’t know, we’ll see,” he continued. “I vowed to myself that I wanted to write a couple of them to see what people think, particularly the cast, ’cause we were very close when we were making it.”

“Glee” first premiered in Sept. 2009, and in addition to Michele, Colfer and Criss, it starred Corey Monteith, Naya Rivera, Dianna Agron, Matthew Morrison, Jane Lynch, Heather Morris and more.

title: Ju Ji-hoon & Choo Young-woo Return To ‘The Trauma Code: Heroes On Call’ With Seasons 2 & 3 In Production At Netflix
summary: The Trauma Code: Heroes on Call will be back in the emergency room for Seasons 2 and 3.
