title: Christina Applegate Reveals MS Misdiagnosis: “I Am Back At Square One”
summary: Christina Applegate, diagnosed with multiple sclerosis back in 2021 and has become a leading advocate for people coping with the disease, revealed shocking news today: She was misdiagnosed and does not in fact have MS. In an emotional episode of MeSsy, the podcast she hosts with Jamie Lynn Sigler as, in Applegate’s description, the poster […]
content:
Christina Applegate, diagnosed with multiple sclerosis back in 2021 and has become a leading advocate for people coping with the disease, revealed shocking news today: She was misdiagnosed and does not in fact have MS.

In an emotional episode of MeSsy, the podcast she hosts with Jamie Lynn Sigler as, in Applegate’s description, the poster children of MS, the former Married With Children star says recent tests turned up with some very surprising results.

In the first part of a two-part podcast episode, Applegate describes the moment her doctor told her the latest news: “She came into my room and said, ‘Congratulations, you don’t have MS.’ I was, like, not happy at all. Everybody else was so happy.”

“You don’t get misdiagnosed and then all of the sudden I’m better,” a tearful Applegate says. “I haven’t gotten better, Jamie! If anything, I’ve gotten worse. So I’m back at square one where I don’t know what’s going on with me. And that’s going to be an online investigation that my doctors are going to be getting into just to find out what has been going on since 2021, why did this happen?”

Watch on Deadline

Summing up the latest development, Applegate says, “It’s a mindf*ck for sure.”

In the second episode of the two-parter, Applegate and Sigler welcome Dr. Marwa Kaisey, associate professor with the Cedars-Sinai Medical Center department of neurology, to the show. The doctor explains that MS misdiagnoses are “fairly common.”

“We don’t have one single test for MS,” Kaisey says. “It’s not like we have something like a pregnancy test that says, ‘Yes. You have it.’ ‘No. You don’t.’ It’s a list of criteria.” According to Kaisey, nearly one in five people diagnosed with MS don’t actually have it, “and a majority of them were on medication to treat their MS.”

Applegate describes the psychic toll taken by her illness. “I’ve gone through a great depression because of it,” she says during the second episode. “But I lost everything. I lost my job. I lost — I’m sorry. What do you say to someone who’s been living with this for six years — God, I’m so sorry — because it stopped my life. I still have to use wheelchairs when I go to the doctor’s office. I can’t walk from the car to the room. I’m still in this. Nothing magical happened when she said, ‘You don’t have MS.’ Nothing magical happened.”

Applegate also shares her new feelings about her longtime MS advocacy. “It’s weird because I feel like I let everybody down,” she says. “It’s this weird feeling because I became this — you and I, the poster children for MS. And everything I was doing, I had a reason. I had a f*cking reason as to why my day sucked every day, and now I don’t have a reason and it’s very unnerving and it’s very confusing for me.”

According to the Mayo Clinic, MS is a chronic, immune-mediated disorder of the central nervous system (the brain and spinal cord) that causes muscle weakness, vision changes, numbness, memory loss and gastrointestinal issues.

Applegate, who has written about her illness in the memoir You With the Sad Eyes, announced last March that she had been hospitalized for treatement and testing. “I’m taking a moment to focus on my health,” she wrote on Instagram at the time, “but I’ll be back with more to say soon enough.” The podcast resumed on April 21 with Sigler hosting along with various special guests.

Applegate was while filming the Netflix series Dead to Me when she first experienced symptoms, and has appeared in public only infrequently since the diagnosis. In an emotional 2024 appearance at the Emmy Awards, Applegate was greeted with a standing ovation to present the nominees in the Supporting Actress in a Comedy Series category.

With her usual wry sense of humor, she joked, “You’re totally shaming me with disability by standing up, but it’s OK.”

On the new podcast episodes, Applegate assures Sigler and her audience that the podcast will continue. Her health journey, she notes, “is the same game with a different name.”

title: ‘Unsolved Mysteries’ Returns As Video Podcast
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Unsolved Mysteries is back and it has a new form. The iconic true-crime series is returning as a video podcast. This comes more than three years after its previous audio-only podcast ended and a couple of years since Netflix released new episodes of its reboot. Jordan Murphy, who previously hosted NBC’s Tool Academy and […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Unsolved Mysteries is back and it has a new form.

The iconic true-crime series is returning as a video podcast. This comes more than three years after its previous audio-only podcast ended and a couple of years since Netflix released new episodes of its reboot.

Jordan Murphy, who previously hosted NBC’s Tool Academy and has featured in episodes of General Hospital and Grey’s Anatomy, will host the podcast, which comes from Unsolved Media and Audacy.

It will launch on YouTube on October 29 with new episodes released weekly on Thursdays. There will also be updates to cases previously profiled on the Unsolved Mysteries series and podcast released on select Tuesdays.

The show, which explores cases spanning mysterious murders, strange disappearances, wanted fugitives, and unexplained deaths, will focus on mysteries including the disappearance of Amelia Earhart, the vanishing of Malaysia Airlines Flight 370, and the still-unsolved heist at Boston’s Stewart Gardner Museum this season as well as lesser-known cases.

Unsolved Mysteries, which was originally hosted by Robert Stack and ran for over 500 episodes between 1987 and 2010, previously aired on NBC between 1987 and 1997 and CBS picked it up for two years after it was cancelled. Lifetime aired a number of new episodes in 2001/2002 and Spike also picked it up between 2008 and 2010 with Dennis Farina replacing Stack following The Untouchables actor’s death in 2003.

There were around 80 episodes of the audio podcast and Netflix rebooted the show in 2020 and has made 30 episodes across five volumes.

“We’re thrilled to be expanding the Unsolved Mysteries brand in this pivot to the video podcast world,” said Terry Meurer, Unsolved Mysteries co-creator and President and CEO of Unsolved Media. “There are still so many mysteries that need to be solved and we know we can reach a wide audience on YouTube and through Audacy’s distribution. And we hope our audience can help solve these mysteries, as they have for decades.”

“Unsolved Mysteries has an incredibly passionate audience and a legacy that continues to resonate across generations, and we’re excited to bring the podcast into a new era with video,” added Leah Reis-Dennis, Head of Podcasts, Audacy. “With Jordan Murphy at the helm and all-new cases to explore, this next chapter brings a fresh dimension to a beloved franchise and offers advertisers new opportunities to engage with a devoted fanbase across both audio and video.”

title: Snap Taps Robert Downey Jr. To Boost New SPECS AR Glasses
summary: Robert Downey Jr. is launching a collection of original episodes touting SPECS, as the actor partners with Snap as Honorary Chief Customer Experience Officer for its new augmented reality glasses. The short videos, which demonstrate applications showing how wearers can elevate workspaces, master golf, relax with an entertaining show, or develop artistic skills, are available […]
content:
Robert Downey Jr. is launching a collection of original episodes touting SPECS, as the actor partners with Snap as Honorary Chief Customer Experience Officer for its new augmented reality glasses.

The short videos, which demonstrate applications showing how wearers can elevate workspaces, master golf, relax with an entertaining show, or develop artistic skills, are available to watch on the SPECS website or YouTube, which will update as new episodes drop, Snap said. The goal with the series is to make SPECS technology “feel useful, approachable, and entertaining.”

SPECS and Downey Jr.’s partnership will make its broadcast debut tonight during the New York Knicks vs. Philadelphia 76ers Tip-Off game. An original episode will broadcast during Game 1 of the World Series on Friday, October 23.

In his role, Downey “will guide customers to understand and imagine what’s possible” using the tiny with the hand and voice-directed computer built into the glasses. He’ll work across the SPECS organization to explore new capabilities, shape new Lens experiences, develop original content and collaborate on hardware and in-person experiences.

Watch on Deadline

“Trying is believing. Having tested practically every wearable tech that’s come to market in the last 20 years, and been largely unimpressed, I was absolutely sold on SPECS within 40 seconds,” said Downey Jr. “The applications are endless. Families can share experiences instead of hunching over devices, skills can be honed, big business can streamline development. In short, it delivers on the promise of AR glasses made by a certain techno optimist superhero I portrayed” — aka MCU’s Tony Stark/Iron Man.

“Life imitates art – imitates life! I’ve never experienced the confident, warm and creatively inviting atmosphere that Evan has cultivated at SPECS anywhere else in the tech sector. Wait’ll you see what we create for you to enjoy,” he said.

Snap CEO Evan Spiegel welcomed Downey Jr. to SPECS, saying “Robert has been imagining what this technology could become for nearly twenty years, and it’s an honor to work with him to bring that vision to life.”

title: Netflix’s Jinny Howe Restructures UCAN Scripted Operation By Genre, Ups Cole Galvin To VP
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Jinny Howe, Netflix’s Head of UCAN (U.S.-Canada) Scripted Series, is introducing a new structure to the division she has overseen for almost 14 months. The changes include breaking the teams into genre-specific pods, Cole Galvin being elevated from Director to VP and Neil Thomas to Director. The reorg had been in the works for […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Jinny Howe, Netflix‘s Head of UCAN (U.S.-Canada) Scripted Series, is introducing a new structure to the division she has overseen for almost 14 months. The changes include breaking the teams into genre-specific pods, Cole Galvin being elevated from Director to VP and Neil Thomas to Director.

The reorg had been in the works for awhile, way before the layoffs last Wednesday that impacted 1,000 across Netflix, including several director and manager-level executives in the scripted series operation, and the major Netflix executive shakeup the following day, which saw Chief Content Officer Bela Bajaria exiting, replaced by Peter Rice.

Management changes of that caliber often have a ripple effect, with the attention quickly focusing on two of Bajaria’s direct reports, Howe and Netflix Head of Film Dan Lin. As Deadline reported on the day of the Bajaria-Rice switch, a Lin exit was likely, one by Howe was not.

Watch on Deadline

Lin was ousted over the weekend, while Howe’s move to restructure her division is further confirmation that she is staying on, along with her stepping up over the weekend to nab The Apology, a hot series project starring Gwyneth Paltrow, with a two-season order. Rice is said to have spoken with Howe about working together.

A rising executive at Netflix where she has had four promotions since joining the company in 2018 as VP, Drama Series, Howe has shepherded seven series that have landed on Netflix’s Most Popular English series list. She manages the largest market in Netflix’s global business, driving roughly 35% of overall revenue with about 50 greenlights this year.

Howe had not reorganized the UCAN Scripted Series operations since she took over at the end of August 2025 following the departure of Peter Friedlander. The goal for the new structure is to provide more depth and curation in specific lanes instead of spreading attention across every lane at once, better match of material to executives with expertise in a space and strong relationships with those creators, and better specialization.

Drama Development

The team overseeing all drama (except prestige fare), which has been overseen by VP, Drama Development Michael Azzolino since January 2025, will be split into two areas led by Azzolino and Cole Galvin, who both will report to Howe.

Drama, Thriller, & YA, run by Galvin, is targeting co-viewing adult audience with a female skew. It will focus on sophisticated relationship dramas (family, friendship, workplace), propulsive mystery/thrillers (The Apology, God of the Woods, His & Hers), YA/early adult and romance (Lovesick, Calabasas, Poser). Part of the team and reporting to Galvin is former Media Res President of Scripted Lindsey Springer, who joined Netflix in August.

Genre, Action, & Crime, run by Azzolino, is targeting co-viewing adult audience with a male skew. It will focus on action, adventure, sci-fi, world-building, horror, Westerns, spy dramas, and crime. Continuing to report to Azzolino and part of his pod are the tentpole/IP team led by Teddy Biaselli, who was promoted to VP last November, and Carrie Gillogly (Director, Drama Development) who will be shepherding muscular programming that does not fall into Biaselli’s purview.

Comedy Development

The lanes under Netflix’s VP, Comedy Tracey Pakosta, who continues as head of the department reporting to Howe, will be led by her existing team members:

Brooke Kessler (Director, Comedy) is in charge of the Commercial Comedy strategy, creating big, entertainment-forward, broadly appealing content for large audiences (Nobody Wants This, Running Point, Tires).

Andrea Alvarado (Director, Comedy) is overseeing the Auteur-Driven strategy, curating comedy IP and creating more risk-forward, unique, award-focused content.

Continuing in their existing roles on Pakosta’s team are Robbie Praw (VP, Stand-up Comedy), who leads Stand-up Comedy and the newly formed Netflix Is a Joke Studio, a mini studio/incubator working across formats with comedian talent in-house, and Billy Wee (Director, Comedy), who continues to lead Adult Animation.

Studio

The team led by Nne Ebong (VP, Studio Scripted Series), which manages talent deals and titles, reporting to Howe, will continue to focus on self-generating, ground-up, early stage development on shows that are not actively coming in through the open marketplace (The Decorator, The Understudy). Neil Thomas, who joined Netflix in 2023, has been promoted to Director, Studio Scripted Series.

Current Programming & Specialty

Renate Radford (VP, Current Scripted Series) will continue to lead current programming, and Nora Skinner (VP, Specialty Scripted Series) will continue to be in charge of Specialty, which is elevated, prestige series.

The seven series Howe has steered onto Netflix’s Most Popular list are I Will Find You, His & Hers, The Night Agent, Bridgerton S1, Inventing Anna, Maid, and Queen Charlotte: A Bridgerton Story. Out of Netflix’s 111 Emmy nominations this year, 83 of them came from the scripted series and variety specials on her slate.

Howe also has been aggressive in securing competitive packages, winning the bidding wars for such projects as The Corrections starring Meryl Streep and Hancock Park with Regé-Jean Page.

2026 has been challenging for Netflix, with global viewership rising 2% for the first half of the year, raising Wall Street concerns over slowing engagement growth. The bright spots out of the UCAN division include I Will Find You, the year’s biggest original series debut and #5 Most Popular English TV series, surprise breakout His & Hers, which made an appearance on the Most Popular List; Bridgerton Season 4 with 100M views in six months; and The Diplomat, which just returned for a very well-received fourth season.

Coming up are Scooby-Doo: Origins; Kennedy, starring Michael Fassbender; Rabbit, Rabbit, headlined by Adam Driver; The Roman, executive produced by Martin Scorsese and starring Oscar Isaac; The Age of Innocence; The God of the Woods; Langdon; Assassin’s Creed; The Watcher, and Untamed Season 2.

Galvin has been at Netflix since late 2017 when he joined as Manager. He was promoted to Director of Original Series in June 2019.

During his tenure, Galvin developed one of Netflix’s biggest YA series Ginny & Georgia. He also has been involved in the English-language adaptations of Harlan Coben’s novels, from the 2020 The Stranger to this year’s I Will Find You. Other recent series he worked on include East of Eden and The Beast In Me.

title: Russell Brand Accuser Says She Reported Comedian To Channel 4 In 2009 After He Allegedly Lay His Head On Her Lap & Demanded Massage
summary: Editor’s note: This story contains details of alleged sexual offenses that some readers may find distressing. A woman has revealed that she complained to Channel 4 about Russell Brand’s behavior in 2009 after he allegedly put his head in her lap and demanded a massage, a court has heard. The woman, whom we are calling […]
content:
Editor’s note: This story contains details of alleged sexual offenses that some readers may find distressing.

A woman has revealed that she complained to Channel 4 about Russell Brand’s behavior in 2009 after he allegedly put his head in her lap and demanded a massage, a court has heard.

The woman, whom we are calling Complainant 6 (C6) as she has a lifelong right to anonymity, was working for Channel 4 at the time of the alleged attack. Giving evidence as part of Brand’s rape trial, C6 claimed she reported her experience to her line manager and was assured the matter had been escalated.

Brand faces three charges of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one of indecent assault based on allegations made by six women. He will set out his defense later in the trial, denies all charges and has pleaded not guilty. Deadline has been reporting from a live video feed of the courtroom since the trial began, but a tech outage meant remote access was down this morning.

Watch on Deadline

In evidence to London’s Southwark Crown Court, C6 alleged that the comedian and actor had forced her to give him a massage. Speaking from behind a screen, she said she was working for Channel 4 at the time and had “briefly” met Brand once before. According to Sky News, C6 alleged Brand briefly left the room they were both in, returned and lay his head on her lap, before saying, “Come on then.”

C6 alleged she could feel his breath on her vagina. “I just thought I need to get him off me, so my hands went down at a diagonal [during the massage]. I was so repulsed by the situation I just thought, ‘Oh, you’re so bony. Ugh,” she was quoted by Sky News as telling the courtroom.

The court has been told repeatedly that Brand declined to answer questions when interviewed by police. He instead relied on a prepared statement, in which he claimed that he did not recall meeting the women and did not remember their names. He said any sexual contact was consensual.

Yesterday at the trial, a former MTV employee said she didn’t initially report her allegation of rape against Brand because she feared being “seen as trouble.”

The trial continues.

title: Dwayne Johnson Transforms Into a 70-Year-Old Man in Shocking ‘Lizard Music’ Set Photos
summary: Move over, Mark Kerr, and make way for the Chicken Man. Dwayne Johnson was spotted in Brooklyn on Tuesday shooting his new movie “Lizard Music” from director Benny Safdie. Like with his previous collaboration with the “Uncut Gems” director, 2025’s “The Smashing Machine,” Johnson has gone through a serious prosthetic transformation. This time around, instead […]
content:
Move over, Mark Kerr, and make way for the Chicken Man.

Dwayne Johnson was spotted in Brooklyn on Tuesday shooting his new movie “Lizard Music” from director Benny Safdie. Like with his previous collaboration with the “Uncut Gems” director, 2025’s “The Smashing Machine,” Johnson has gone through a serious prosthetic transformation. This time around, instead of a hulking MMA behemoth, Johnson has turned into a 70-year-old known as the Chicken Man.

In the set photos, Johnson, sporting a tan bucket hat and coat and holding a slice of pizza, walks alongside his young co-star Theo Clark Leber, who carries an oversized lizard plush. The artist behind Johnson’s look is Kazu Hiro, who just turned Tom Cruise into a geriatric oil baron for “Digger.”

Popular on Variety

NEW YORK, NY – OCTOBER 20: Theo Leber and Dwayne Johnson are seen filming “Lizard Music” in Coney Island, Brooklyn on Oct. 20, 2026, in New York City. (Photo by Jose Perez/Bauer-Griffin/GC Images) GC Images

“Lizard Music,” based on Daniel Pinkwater’s children’s book of the same name, follows a young boy who “stumbles upon strange lizard musicians on late-night TV, leading him to befriend a peculiar man with an elderly chicken,” according to an official logline. Other cast members include Rachel McAdams, Colman Domingo, David Krumholtz, Jeff Goldblum, Alicia Silverstone and Regina Hall.

From Amazon MGM Studios, “Lizard Music” is set for release on Christmas Day 2027.

During a career retrospective talk at the 2025 Toronto Film Festival, Johnson said it was an easy yes to sign on for “Lizard Music,” sharing that it only took “about 45 minutes” of convincing from Safdie. He also revealed that he shed 30 pounds of muscle to play the Chicken Man.

“I’m so excited to get a chance to hopefully transform again like I was able to do in ‘Smashing Machine,’” Johnson said. “[It means] eating less chicken.”

title: ‘Lioness’ Season 3 Closes With 9.7 Million Viewers in Seven Days, a Series High and the No. 5 Paramount+ Finale Ever
summary: “Lioness” showed strong audience growth throughout its third season and ended on a high note: The finale reached 9.7 million viewers in its first seven days of availability. That total marks not only the most-watched episode in the series’ history, but the No. 5 most-watched finale of all time compared to other Paramount+ originals. Additionally, […]
content:
“Lioness” showed strong audience growth throughout its third season and ended on a high note: The finale reached 9.7 million viewers in its first seven days of availability.

That total marks not only the most-watched episode in the series’ history, but the No. 5 most-watched finale of all time compared to other Paramount+ originals. Additionally, the series saw an average of 8.5 million viewers per week throughout Season 3, which ran from Aug. 2 to Sept. 20, showing a 62% increase from Season 2’s weekly average in 2024. Each week of Season 3 brought in more viewers than the week before it.

“Lioness” also performed well compared to streaming programming on other networks, making it onto Nielsen and Luminate’s top 10 charts eight weeks in a row. Per Nielsen, the series achieved its first-ever billion-minute total during finale week, and Season 3 reached a cumulative 3.9 billion minutes watched during its eight-week run, up 62% from Season 2. Catch-up viewing was also strong, with Seasons 1 and 2 reaching a combined 2.5 million minutes watched in the same window.

Popular on Variety

“Lioness” was created by Taylor Sheridan and is produced by Paramount Television Studios and 101 Studios. Zoe Saldaña and Nicole Kidman star alongside Laysla De Oliveira, Genesis Rodriguez, Dave Annable, Jill Wagner, LaMonica Garrett, James Jordan, Austin Hébert, Jonah Wharton, Hannah Love Lanier, Thad Luckinbill, Ian Bohen, Michael Kelly, Morgan Freeman and Nicole Kidman. Sheridan executive produces with David C. Glasser, Saldaña, Kidman, Ron Burkle, David Hutkin, Bob Yari, Michael Friedman, Jill Wagner, David Lemanowicz, Geyer Kosinski and Keith Cox.

title: Elizabeth Holmes Mania: ‘You Can See Everything’ Drives 186% Viewership Spike for Amanda Seyfried’s ‘The Dropout’ (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: “The Dropout,” Hulu’s 2022 limited series in which Amanda Seyfried plays Elizabeth Holmes, has seen a massive audience spike due to the buzz surrounding A24’s new Holmes documentary “You Can See Everything.” Viewership of “The Dropout” jumped by 186% in September compared to the month before, driven by the Sept. 6 announcement that “You Can […]
content:
“The Dropout,” Hulu’s 2022 limited series in which Amanda Seyfried plays Elizabeth Holmes, has seen a massive audience spike due to the buzz surrounding A24’s new Holmes documentary “You Can See Everything.”

Viewership of “The Dropout” jumped by 186% in September compared to the month before, driven by the Sept. 6 announcement that “You Can See Everything” had been produced in secret. That interest continued growing as the film’s Oct. 16 wide release approached, with viewership during the week of Oct. 12 increasing 92% compared to the week before.

The data remains impressive when looking at specific totals: In August, before the buzz around “You Can See Everything” began, “The Dropout” was watched for 420,000 hours (or roughly 62,000 views when divided by the series’ nearly seven-hour runtime) — already decent for a four-year-old series. In September, viewership skyrocketed to 1.2 million hours, or 176,000 estimated views. The week of Oct. 12 alone brought in another 422,000 hours watched or 62,000 views; in other words, “The Dropout” brought in as many eyes during that seven-day period as it did in the entire month of August.

Popular on Variety

Interest remains high now that the film is in theaters: “The Dropout” has reached 997,000 hours watched (148,000 views) to date this month, bringing the total since September to 2.2 million hours, or 296,000 estimated views.

JustWatch, a service that centralizes information about where various streaming programs are available, also reported increased interest in “The Dropout.” The series jumped 200% in search points week-over-week after the release of “You Can See Everything,” and is in the No. 10 position on the site’s current streaming search rankings.

“The Dropout” isn’t the only piece of Holmes media enjoying a bump thanks to the success of “You Can See Everything”: John Carreyrou, the journalist who brought down Holmes’ fraudulent empire, returned to the New York Times bestseller list with his 2018 book “Bad Blood: Secrets and Lies in a Silicon Valley Startup.”

Directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, “You Can See Everything” premiered as a surprise screening during the Telluride Film Festival, before which its existence had not been made public.

“The Dropout” was created by Elizabeth Meriwether and was widely loved upon its 2022 release, with Seyfried winning the Emmy for lead actress in a limited series. That year, Meriwether and Seyfried both indicated to Variety that they would be interested in making another project about Holmes — “I’m not kidding, a two hour special!” Seyfried said — though Seyfried was more reticent in a recent interview.

title: Robert Downey Jr. Signs On as Pitchman for Snap’s $2,200 Specs AR Glasses
summary: Robert Downey Jr., whose famous portrayal of Marvel’s Iron Man had him decked out with a variety of high-tech gadgetry, is donning Snap’s Specs augmented-reality glasses in a new role as lead spokesman for the devices. Downey Jr.’s partnership with Specs kicked off with a collection of original episodes featuring him showing off the tech […]
content:
Robert Downey Jr., whose famous portrayal of Marvel’s Iron Man had him decked out with a variety of high-tech gadgetry, is donning Snap‘s Specs augmented-reality glasses in a new role as lead spokesman for the devices.

Downey Jr.’s partnership with Specs kicked off with a collection of original episodes featuring him showing off the tech in everyday situations — at work, golfing, watching TV and “developing artistic skills.” (Watch them on the Specs site or on YouTube.) The actor-producer-entrepreneur’s pact with the company will make its broadcast debut Tuesday night during the New York Knicks vs. Philadelphia 76ers NBA tip-off game, while an original episode of RDJ’s content series will also make its broadcast debut during Game 1 of the World Series on Friday, Oct. 23.

Snap has said Specs will begin shipping “later this fall.” The glasses are available for pre-order starting at $2,195 for the WiFi-only version and $2,395 for a model with Verizon 5G connectivity. The device, which Snap CEO Evan Spiegel unveiled last month, responds to voice commands and hand gestures to interact with apps and the world around you.

Popular on Variety

Downey Jr. has been bestowed the “honorary Chief Customer Experience Officer (CCEO)” title for Specs. He will “work across different parts of the Specs organization to explore new capabilities, shape new Lens experiences and develop original content,” and will collaborate on hardware and in-person experiences, according to Snap.

“Trying is believing. Having tested practically every wearable tech that’s come to market in the last 20 years, and been largely unimpressed, I was absolutely sold on Specs within 40 seconds,” RDJ said in a statement. “The applications are endless.”

Spiegel added: “Robert has been imagining what this technology could become for nearly 20 years, and it’s an honor to work with him to bring that vision to life.”

title: Starz Gets Back on Verizon Fios After New Carriage Pact
summary: The cable network Starz and its ancillary properties are available once again on Verizon’s Fios service following an interruption in service due to a battle over the terms of a new contract. Starz said on Tuesday that all of its networks and on-demand services were back on Verizon. The Starz services went dark in late […]
content:
The cable network Starz and its ancillary properties are available once again on Verizon’s Fios service following an interruption in service due to a battle over the terms of a new contract.

Starz said on Tuesday that all of its networks and on-demand services were back on Verizon. The Starz services went dark in late September.

“We are pleased to have reached a mutually beneficial agreement that brings Starz’s premium programming to Verizon Fios customers,” said Alison Hoffman, president, Starz Networks, in a prepared statement. “We remain committed to delivering bold storytelling for women and underrepresented audiences and to serving viewers who value our distinctive programming.”

Popular on Variety

In addition to programs such as “Outlander” and “Fightland,” Starz is home to the “Power” franchise, and also shows films including “Michael,” “Shelter,” “In The Grey” and “Power Ballad.”

The premium service has shifted its business toward streaming in recent years; the company closed the October-December quarter with 12.7 million U.S. streaming subscribers, up 370,000 customers from the previous period, with a total of 17.6 million across all platforms.

In its most recent fiscal quarter, Starz posted revenue of $307.9 million, down from $317.9 million. The company is expected to report third quarter results on Thursday, October 29.

In trading earlier Tuesday, shares of Starz rose 13 cents, or .57%, to $22.93

title: Bob Iger Looks Back At Challenges Of His Disney CEO Comeback In New Memoir ‘One Last Time’
summary: Penguin Random House has unveiled Bob Iger’s upcoming book ‘One Last Time: Managing Crisis and Building Resilience at Disney’, out March 1, calling it “an inspiring candid memoir of leadership in times of adversity.” The book by the former two-time CEO of Disney and author of ‘The Ride of a Lifetime’ (2019), written with Dan […]
content:
Penguin Random House has unveiled Bob Iger’s upcoming book ‘One Last Time: Managing Crisis and Building Resilience at Disney‘, out March 1, calling it “an inspiring candid memoir of leadership in times of adversity.”

The book by the former two-time CEO of Disney and author of ‘The Ride of a Lifetime’ (2019), written with Dan Schwerin, is available for preorder.

The blurb on the publisher’s website tees up with a call by then chairman of Disney’s board to the former chief executive less than a year into retirement to ask if he’d be willing to return to his old job. “Finances were shaky, leadership was flagging, morale was dangerously low, and the brand was tarnished. They needed him back.”

Iger had unexpectedly departed as Disney CEO in early 2020, succeeded by his handpicked successor and head of the company’s giant Parks & Experiences division Bob Chapek, but remained to oversee creative endeavors. The Chapek reign was short and rocky. The ousted exec, in his own tome published last month, largely blamed Iger for his demise. In Behind the Castle Walls: My Thirty Years at the Happiest Place on Earth, he says he was set up to fail.

Watch on Deadline

One Last Time is a business book as Iger returned to an entertainment industry beset by existential threats. “To survive, the company—and Iger himself—would have to become more resilient, innovative, and, above all, creative. Iger would also have to learn to be a new kind of leader, and he would be challenged in ways he never imagined,” the blurb said.

“How do you lead through periods of adversity? How do you regain the trust of employees, customers, and shareholders? Iger would have to develop a new playbook, for a new era, and he would make his share of mistakes along the way,” reads the blub.

More to come

Starz and Verizon have inked a deal that restores all Starz channels, Starz On Demand and the Starz app to Verizon Fios.

Starz programming includes the full Power Universe and upcoming Power: Origins, drama Fightland, every episode of Outlander and the series’ prequel Outlander: Blood of my Blood as well as the upcoming season of the award-winning P-Valley, the current season of the crime drama S.W.A.T. Exiles and thriller Tip Toe.

“We are pleased to have reached a mutually beneficial agreement that brings Starz’s premium programming to Verizon Fios customers,” said Alison Hoffman, President, Starz Networks. “We remain committed to delivering bold storytelling for women and underrepresented audiences and to serving viewers who value our distinctive programming.”

Starz went dark on Verizon Fios early this month as the two weren’t able to reach agreement on a new distribution deal.

Watch on Deadline

As per usual, details of the agreement weren’t released. Verizon complained at the start of the dispute that Starz was “selling its service direct to consumers for as low as $2.50 a month [but] demanding Verizon customers pay double that amount for access to the same content..” Starz insisted that Verizon “mischaracterized our position.”

Starz film offerings include Michael (Jaafar Jackson), Shelter (Jason Statham), In the Grey (Jake Gyllenhaal, Henry Cavill and Eiza González), and the musical comedy Power Ballad (Paul Rudd and Nick Jonas).
