Leica is the latest high-end brand to get in on the sport’s growing cultural cachet, teaming up with Formula 1 on a new licensing deal that will see the German camera maker release a $9,950 special-edition camera inspired by the racetrack. The Leica Q3 43 […]
content:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

Formula 1‘s luxury ambitions are extending to the camera business.

Leica is the latest high-end brand to get in on the sport’s growing cultural cachet, teaming up with Formula 1 on a new licensing deal that will see the German camera maker release a $9,950 special-edition camera inspired by the racetrack.

Leica Q3 F3 Formula 1 Edition Buy Now $9,950

The Leica Q3 43 Formula 1 Edition, available beginning Oct. 20, arrives as the racing league continues to build a business beyond the paddock, capitalizing on a surge in mainstream interest that has made Formula 1 an attractive partner for luxury brands.

The camera itself takes its design cues from the cockpit, with carbon-fiber detailing on its wireless charging handgrip, thumb rest and shutter button. Its black Microvelour covering is modeled after the textured surface of Formula 1 steering wheels, while red accents on the controls mimic the color-coded buttons used by drivers during races.

There’s also an F1 logo stamped on the top plate and lens cap, a co-branded carrying strap and custom packaging with a red interior. The carbon-fiber components, which are manufactured and tested in Germany, mark a departure from materials traditionally used in Leica cameras.

Leica has also developed an exclusive “Formula 1” photography setting that boosts contrast and color saturation to better capture the atmosphere of the racetrack. The effect can be previewed directly in the camera’s viewfinder and applied while shooting through the Leica FOTOS app, rather than added in post-production.

Otherwise, the limited-edition model shares its technical foundation with the existing Leica Q3 43, including a fixed 43mm APO-Summicron f/2 lens, a full-frame sensor capable of shooting at 60, 36 or 18 megapixels, hybrid autofocus and video capabilities.

Leica will introduce the camera at its Los Angeles store and gallery on Oct. 20, with Formula 1 presenter Ariana Bravo and former world champion Jenson Button on hand for the unveiling. The event will also include an exhibition of 26 racing photographs by Italian motorsport photographer Callo Albanese.

The Leica Q3 43 Formula 1 Edition will be available beginning Oct. 20 at Leica stores, the company’s online shop and specialist retailers for $9,950. It is compatible with existing Leica Q3 and Q3 43 accessories.

title: ‘Billions’ and ‘John Wick 3’ Star Asia Kate Dillon Says Acting Jobs Have ‘Diminished’ and They’re in Need of Customer Service Work
summary: Asia Kate Dillon, who starred in shows like “Orange Is the New Black” and “Billions,” took to social media on Tuesday to share that they are looking for service work after their acting work “has all but diminished” after eleven years in the industry. Dillon began their statement by going through previous service jobs they’ve […]
content:
Asia Kate Dillon, who starred in shows like “Orange Is the New Black” and “Billions,” took to social media on Tuesday to share that they are looking for service work after their acting work “has all but diminished” after eleven years in the industry.

Dillon began their statement by going through previous service jobs they’ve held, from dishwasher to floor manager to food runner. “When I was fifteen, I got my first job in food service,” they wrote, and stayed in the industry until they were able to support themselves full-time as an actor.

“I continued working in food and general customer service, alongside any acting gigs I could rustle up, until the fall of 2015 when I was finally able to make the transition to a full time income stemming from just my acting work. I have worked exclusively in theater, film and TV for the last eleven years,” Dillon continued. “Now, like for many, many performer colleagues of mine — particularly those of us who are trans/nonbinary/gender nonconforming — acting work has all but diminished, and I’m in need of service work once more.”

Popular on Variety

Dillon first appeared in single episodes of shows like “Younger,” “Opus for All” and “Master of None” before booking “Orange Is the New Black,” which they went on to star in for 19 episodes as Brandy Epps. In 2017, they landed the role of Taylor Mason on “Billions,” which they played across six seasons and 71 episodes. Dillon also had roles in “John Wick: Chapter 3 – Parabellum,” “The Outside Story” and “Gen: Lock,” and starred in the film “Outerlands” in 2025.

In late 2026, Dillon publicly came out as non-binary. They were the first gender nonbinary performer to play a nonbinary character on a major TV show. In 2020, the actor called for the SAG Awards (now known as the Actor Awards) to abolish gender-specific categories, writing that “separating people based on their assigned sex, and/or their gender identity, is not only irrelevant when it comes to how an acting performance should be judged, it is also a form of discrimination.”

Read Dillon’s full statement here.

Hello!

In the year 2000, when I was fifteen, I got my first job in food service. It was a weekend gig at the (locally) famous, always bustling Ithaca Bakery. I worked mornings; first up was sorting the freshly baked piping hot bagels in their respective bins, and then I would move into rotating and stocking the drink fridges. Throughout my shift my duties included maintaining the coffee station in the center of the retail floor – lids, sugars, straws, stirrers, sleeves, I kept everything very tidy – cleaning and restocking the restroom, mopping up inevitable customer spills, ferrying dirty and then clean dish bins to and from the dining areas, and greeting customers. I loved it.

Ranging from dishwasher to food runner to floor manager, I continued working in food and general customer service, alongside any acting gigs I could rustle up, until the fall of 2015 when I was finally able to make the transition to a full time income stemming from just my acting work. I have worked exclusively in theater, film and TV for the last eleven years.

Now, like for many, many performer colleagues of mine – particularly those of us who are trans/nonbinary/gender nonconforming – acting work has all but diminished, and I’m in need of service work once more.

I love customer service. I love creating welcoming environments for people to relax in and connect with each other. I love food and drink. I am passionate and curious, and a great teammate. I imagine the hurdle to reentry will be learning the new POS systems, but I’m a quick study. I’m available for part time, night and weekend work.

Thanks in advance for your consideration.

All best,

Asia Kate Dillon

(they/them)

title: Park Min-young, Yook Sung-jae, Go Soo Lead Prime Video Korean Office Romance ‘Nine to Six’
summary: Park Min-young, the star of “Marry My Husband,” will lead “Nine to Six,” a Korean office romance. Yook Sung-jae of K-pop group BtoB and Go Soo co-star in the 12-episode series. Park plays Kang Yi-ji, a senior manager on the legal team at a company called Chronic Motors. Logical and driven, Yi-ji has carved out […]
content:
Park Min-young, the star of “Marry My Husband,” will lead “Nine to Six,” a Korean office romance. Yook Sung-jae of K-pop group BtoB and Go Soo co-star in the 12-episode series.

Park plays Kang Yi-ji, a senior manager on the legal team at a company called Chronic Motors. Logical and driven, Yi-ji has carved out her place in a workplace dominated by men and regards love and marriage as little more than a passing chemical impulse. She once wanted to study astronomy but went into law because her mother pushed her toward it.

Two men upend her orderly routine.

Popular on Variety

Yook plays Han Sun-woo, a legal intern who would rather be designing jewelry and who trusts his instincts over logic. When Yi-ji is put in danger, he shields her without a second thought, and she may start to view him differently.

Go plays Park Hyun-tae, an executive director in Chronic Motors’ Seoul office who has come back from the company’s European headquarters after climbing the corporate ladder at a young age. Hyun-tae has long been convinced that romance only complicates life. Yi-ji, whose competence wins his respect, puts that view to the test.

The series sets the younger colleague’s openness against the executive’s grasp of her ambitions, leaving Yi-ji to work out whether she can let someone in without sacrificing the career she has spent years building.

Choi Ji-oh wrote the series. Lee Hyung-min, whose credits include “Strong Girl Bong-soon,” “Miss Night and Day” and “I’m Sorry, I Love You,” directs alongside Oh Song-hee (“The Escape of the Seven”).

The series debuts on Prime Video on Nov. 25 across 240-plus countries and territories.

Park’s other credits include “Siren’s Kiss” and “Confidence Queen.” Yook has appeared in “The Haunted Palace,” “The Golden Spoon” and “Guardian: The Lonely and Great God,” while Go’s work includes “Missing: The Other Side,” “Colony” and “Parole Examiner Lee.”

“Nine to Six” joins a Prime Video lineup that already carries “Love in Disguise,” “A Love Other Than Yours,” “See You at Work Tomorrow!,” “Spring Fever,” “Surely Tomorrow,” “Head Over Heels” and “Good Boy.”

title: Charli Xcx Cancels Tour Date In Arizona: “It Breaks Me That I Can’t Be With You”
summary: Charli Xcx is canceling her penultimate Music, Fashion, Film Tour date in the U.S. as she battles sickness. The singer took to social media to confirm she won’t perform at the Desert Diamond Arena in Glendale, Arizona, because she’s not feeling well. “I have been fighting sickness throughout this run of shows and have now […]
content:
Charli Xcx is canceling her penultimate Music, Fashion, Film Tour date in the U.S. as she battles sickness.

The singer took to social media to confirm she won’t perform at the Desert Diamond Arena in Glendale, Arizona, because she’s not feeling well.

“I have been fighting sickness throughout this run of shows and have now completely lost my voice,” the singer shared on her Instagram Stories. “I put absolutely everything I have into my performances, both physically and emotionally, and it breaks me that I can’t be with you tomorrow.”

Charli Xcx noted that her “team worked hard to fund a new date but ultimately were unable to,” adding, “I’m so disappointed, but promise to return to AZ in the future.”

Watch on Deadline

“Again, I’m sorry to the angels who had made plans to be there tomorrow,” she continued. “I know how much time, planning, and care it takes to come to concerts and appreciate everyone’s support immensely.”

Charli said she was “now resting ahead of the final show in Vegas,” adding, “I want to be back onstage and finish this tour together with you.”

Charli kicked off her Music, Fashion, Film Tour in Philadelphia on September 11.

The singer had recently performed on October 17 and 18 at the Kia Forum in Los Angeles and on October 14 at the Viejas Arena in San Diego. Other U.S. cities she visited included New York City, Boston, D.C. and Atlanta.

Her last U.S. date is Friday, October 23, at the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas. The tour is planned to end in Paris on February 24, 2027.

title: ’10 Things I Hate About You’ Cast Reunites To Honor Heath Ledger With Julia Stiles On ‘Dancing With The Stars’
summary: In a dance dedicated to the late Heath Ledger, Julia Stiles reunited with much of the cast of the 1999 film 10 Things I Hate About You during Tuesday night’s episode of Dancing with the Stars. Stiles told her partner Ezra Sosa that she had always admired his “lust for life” and wanted to replicate […]
content:
In a dance dedicated to the late Heath Ledger, Julia Stiles reunited with much of the cast of the 1999 film 10 Things I Hate About You during Tuesday night’s episode of Dancing with the Stars.

Stiles told her partner Ezra Sosa that she had always admired his “lust for life” and wanted to replicate that in her contemporary routine, which the pair aptly performed to “Can’t Take My Eyes Off You” by Frankie Valli.

Ledger’s Patrick Verona memorably serenades Stiles’ Kat Stratford with the song at the end of the film.

The end of the Dancing with the Stars performance on Tuesday night featured Stiles linking arms with several of her other former cast members including Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Gabrielle Union, Larisa Oleynik, Susan May Pratt, and Andrew Keegan.

Watch on Deadline

In the last few moments of the routine, Sosa leaves Stiles on the dance floor as her monologue from the film played in lieu of music and a still from the film took over the screen at the back of the room. Stiles placed a rose underneath the photo before joining her co-stars.

She scored four 9s on the routine, among the highest of the night. “Watching you, it just makes me want to open my heart,” judge Carrie Ann Inaba told her after the performance.

Ledger died in 2008 from an accidental overdose. Later that year, he received a posthumous Oscar for his performance as the Joker in Christopher Nolan’s The Dark Knight. He and Stiles met on the set of 10 Things I Hate About You, which is a modern retelling of Shakespeare’s Taming of the Shrew. It was Stiles’ first major feature film.

title: ‘Dancing With The Stars’ Recap: Dedication Night Features A Lot Of Tears & ’10 Things I Hate About You’ Cast Reunion
summary: SPOILER ALERT! This post contains details from this week’s episode of Dancing with the Stars. It’s Dedication Night in the ballroom, so grab your tissues. Tuesday night’s episode of Dancing with the Stars featured the remaining 10 celebrity contestants and their pro partners perform routines dedicated to someone important in the former’s life. There are […]
content:
SPOILER ALERT! This post contains details from this week’s episode of Dancing with the Stars.

It’s Dedication Night in the ballroom, so grab your tissues.

Tuesday night’s episode of Dancing with the Stars featured the remaining 10 celebrity contestants and their pro partners perform routines dedicated to someone important in the former’s life. There are a lot of parents and siblings among the mix, as is typical, as well as a few curveballs. Maura Higgins is dedicating her dance to the entire nation of Ireland. Tatyana Ali and Julia Stiles have both chosen to honor former co-stars who have died.

All of the night’s performances also featured special appearances, either by the person being honored or someone else close to them.

Watch on Deadline

Also, can anyone believe it’s already Week 6? We are officially at the halfway mark of the season, and it appears the competition is just kicking up. No one has scored above a 9 yet, and last week marked the first instance of straight 9s.

Not to mention, there’s some internal tension this week after pro Val Chmerkovskiy was suspended for a week because of remarks he made online in response to judge Carrie Ann Inaba’s criticism of his wife, Jenna Johnson, during Super Bowl Night. Alan Bersten is filling in for Val this week with Jenna Dewan.

Also, former pro Kym Johnson is a guest judge this week. Anyway, let’s get into the dances.

Paralympian Ezra Frech with Daniella Karagach. The athlete is dedicating a contemporary to “Bloodline” by Mon Rovia to his mom. He gets emotional telling Daniella about his mom’s support throughout his life as he navigated growing up with a disability. His mom opens the dance with him before turning the reins over to his pro partner for a tribute that left the judges both touched and impressed. “The dancing, by the way, that was brilliant!” Bruno said. SCORE: 37 out of 40 (and the first 10 of the season courtesy of Kym)

Actress Tatyana Ali with Jan Ravnik. After “popping [her] booty” last week, the Fresh Prince of Bel-Air star is slowing things down with a viennese waltz to “(You Don’t Know) How Glad I Am” by Nancy Wilson dedicated to her late Fresh Prince costar James Avery, featuring her other former costar and DWTS host Alfonso Ribeiro. She also chose to record the track to sing for the performance. Naturally, the performance was overflowing with emotion. “It was like watching an old Hollywood film come to life,” Carrie Ann Inaba said through tears. SCORE: 32 out of 40

Reality star Maura Higgins with Mark Ballas. Even though her home nation can’t vote for her, the TV personality wants to dedicate her paso doble to “I’m Shipping Up to Boston” by Dropkick Murphys in honor of Ireland. They also get a little help from Irish step dancer Lochlan “Lucky” Howard to help them nail the ode to the country. “Oh my days, Maura! Could you be anymore Irish?! That was fantastic!” Derek Hough told her. SCORE: 35 out of 40

Savannah Bananas midfielder Jackson Olson with Emma Slater. The Banana baller has finally found his confidence, just in time to take on a Quickstep to “L-O-V-E” by Nat King Cole, which he has dedicated to his mom. He says his mom has a knack for finding the extraordinary in every kid, including him, and he wants to exemplify that in his dance. Seems like it resonated. “I see where you get this confidence from and your joy,” Carrie Ann tells him. SCORE: 32 out of 40

Olympian Amber Glenn with Pasha Pashkov. Although she says they weren’t the closest growing up, Amber wants to dedicate a contemporary to “Breathe Me” by Sia to her sister Brooke. She remembers growing closer to her sister as she got older, during a mental health crisis, and that’s the story she wants to tell with the performance. “The raw emotion in that, the athleticism, the vulnerability…sometimes in life you just need someone to lift you up, and what a beautiful way to say thank you to your sister,” Kym tells her. SCORE: 38 out of 40

Actress Jenna Dewan with Alan Bersten. She’s not letting the pro shakeup break her stride this week as she honors her mom with a viennese waltz to “Unchained Melody” by The Righteous Brothers. Alan is determined to make the dance special for both of them and exemplifies the grace that Jenna says her mom instilled in her. Mission accomplished! “Oh my god, I love it when you get lyrical!” Bruno exclaims. “That was fantastic!” SCORE: 37 out of 40

Actor Harry Shum Jr. with Jenna Johnson. After earning his first 9 last week, he’s dedicating a foxtrot to “Stop This Train” by John Mayer to his wife this week. The Grey’s Anatomy actor says that no one has uplifted him more, so who better to honor in a dance? It was a family affair, also featuring his parents and his daughter. “And they can all dance!” Alfonso says. The judges agree. “What a beautiful way to tell your story to the world,” Carrie Ann tells him. She also compliments Jenna’s choreography. SCORE: 36 out of 40

Comedian and podcaster Connor Wood with Rylee Arnold. This funny guy is getting serious on Dedication Night with a viennese waltz to “Piano Man” by Billy Joel for his dad. He was at the bottom of the leaderboard last week, so he wants to improve, and he also wants to do justice to his dad’s legacy. “You have come a very long way. You should be proud,” Derek tells him. Carrie Ann gives him the most improved award! SCORE: 32 out of 40

Reality star Tyler Cameron with Sharna Burgess. Carrie Ann told him last week he was “actually becoming a dancer,” so now it’s time to get out from the bottom of the leaderboard. This week, he’s dedicating a contemporary to “Supermarket Flowers” by Ed Sheeran to his late mother and mothers everywhere, featuring a special appearance from his fiancée. And guest what?! He’s gonna be a girl dad! SCORE: 32 out of 40

Actress Julia Stiles with Ezra Sosa. These close out the night with a contemporary to “Can’t Take My Eyes Off You” by Frankie Valli dedicated to her late 10 Things I Hate About You co-star Heath Ledger. This is the second week in a row where Julia will be referencing one of her old films in a dance, but this one is much more emotionally charged. She cries in practice talking about working with him and says she wants to recreate his “lust” for life. The end of the performance also featured the cast of 10 Things I Hate About You reuniting on the ballroom floor, including Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Gabrielle Union, Susan May Pratt, and Andrew Keegan. “Watching you, it just makes me want to open my heart,” Carrie Ann says. SCORE: 36 out of 40

Who goes home?

It’s a little sad someone has to go home on Dedication Night…so they sent home no one! Next week, in honor of Halloween, is Horror Movie Night.

title: Italian Content Investment Dropped 7.4% in 2025 Largely Due to Uncertainty Over Domestic Tax Credits, Rome MIA Market Report Says
summary: Investment in content production destined for Italy’s film TV and streaming industries dropped 7.4% to €2 billion ($2.24 billion) in 2025, compared with the previous year, with the scripted sphere suffering most amid uncertainty over government support of the country’s tax credits and the ongoing transition in viewership from linear to streaming. That is the […]
content:
Investment in content production destined for Italy’s film TV and streaming industries dropped 7.4% to €2 billion ($2.24 billion) in 2025, compared with the previous year, with the scripted sphere suffering most amid uncertainty over government support of the country’s tax credits and the ongoing transition in viewership from linear to streaming.

That is the main takeaway from a report issued on Wednesday by Italian TV producers’ association APA during Rome’s MIA market, which is dedicated to international TV series, animation, feature films and documentaries.

After reaping the rewards of a protracted growth spurt, Italian producers in 2025 faced a forced slowdown as the country’s right-wing government dithered with ongoing regulatory modifications to tax incentives for domestic film and TV production. The domestic tax credit modifications impasse did not impact Italy’s international production rebates, which remained firmly in place.

Popular on Variety

“This situation hinders producers’ ability to plan, increases financial burdens, and shrinks profit margins,” the report pointed out. “It negatively impacts all companies — especially smaller ones — by straining liquidity and limiting their capacity for future investment,” it added. Hopefully, there is some relief in sight with the new tax credit now in place. The so-called application “window” to apply has been reopened.

The report underlined that unscripted content remains the backbone of Italian broadcasting programming, with an output of over 17,000 hours of original, first-run content, being churned out by Italian producers last year. Independent production accounts for 59% of these titles. Unscripted offerings from streaming platforms in Italy have also expanded, with a 51% increase in the number of titles and a 30% rise in total hours.

Within Italy’s unscripted sphere, the factual genre has seen the most significant growth, up 36% in terms of number of hours, with the number of domestic factual titles adapted from international formats doubling. Game shows are also gaining ground on linear networks, both in early evening and primetime slots.

As for scripted originals, the number of titles in 2025 grew 9% to a total 101 shows produced for the current season. But this growth is driven primarily by 74 smaller domestic series for linear networks, that don’t tend to travel, while the number of Italian originals served up by streamers last year stands the same as 2024 with 27 titles, most of which are, similarly, “local for local” product.

The report underlined that Italian scripted content continues to reach broad and demographically diverse audiences. In the linear broadcasting sphere, Lux Vide’s “Sandokan,” a modern take on the classic pirate tale adapted from Italian author Emilio Salgari’s iconic book series, and BiBiFilm’s “La Preside,” about a feisty female principal of a school in a crime-ridden Naples neighbourhood, both drew a hefty average of over 4.6 million viewers per episode. In the streaming space, Picomedia’s Naples-set prison drama “The Sea Beyond” is still a big hit on state broadcaster RAI’s streaming and linear outlets, as is Aurora TV’s period drama “Il Paradiso delle Signore.”

The standout Italian original on Netflix is serial killer series “The Monster of Florence,” pictured above, directed by genre specialist Stefano Sollima that launched from the 2025 Venice Film Festival and garnered 9.7 million global views in its first week in October 2025.

Meanwhile, as in the rest of the world, the market share for linear television (both free-to-air and pay-TV) is steadily shrinking in Italy while global platforms continue to grow. The streaming segment, which accounted for 21% of the market in 2020, has now reached 43% in the Italian market and “is set to surpass linear television in value in the short-to-medium term,” the report said.

Also in line with global TV trends, microdramas are starting to gain traction in Italy with ReelShort, DramaBox, NetShort and DramaWave already among the country’s top 15 entertainment apps in terms of user spend, the report said. And the first original Italian microdrama production has been released, titled “Tutto in una notte,” produced by Fascino PGT, with its 54 episodes distributed on Italian platform WittyTV and on social media.

title: ‘When I Existed,’ a Cannes Market Standout, Swooped On for World Sales by M-Appeal and Now Bound for Tallinn Black Nights (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Berlin-based M-Appeal has boarded “When I Existed,” a buzzy, feel-good second-chance drama comedy and Kafkian social satire which proved a standout at the Cannes Market’s Ventana Sur Goes to Cannes showcase, marking an auspicious debut for Uruguay’s Alejandro Damiani and Martin Avdolov. A select but discerning sales agent of Latin American movies, M-Appeal has picked […]
content:
Berlin-based M-Appeal has boarded “When I Existed,” a buzzy, feel-good second-chance drama comedy and Kafkian social satire which proved a standout at the Cannes Market’s Ventana Sur Goes to Cannes showcase, marking an auspicious debut for Uruguay’s Alejandro Damiani and Martin Avdolov.

A select but discerning sales agent of Latin American movies, M-Appeal has picked up international sales on “When I Existed” (“Cuando Existia”) just weeks before the feature’s world premiere in the Critics’ Picks Competition at the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival.

The feature debut of writer-directors by Damiani and Martin Avdolov, “When I Existed” unfolds its humane modern parable when Silvio Bertolini retires after spending 40 years building Uruguay’s foremost gates construction company.

Popular on Variety

Attempting to draw his pension, and with his credit cards frozen, he discovers that the National Pension and Retirement Fund, also his bank, register him as deceased.

Sent from pillar to post – to the bank’s Accounts, Payments and Claims treading dark puddled basement corridors and joining seemingly interminable lines. He meanwhile reconnects with old friends from his sculling boat club of youth, and re-awakes – but is it too late? –to what it really means to be alive: Spending time with his wife who hopes retirement will open a new chapter in their life together.

Driving “When I Existed” is a notably modulated performance from César Troncoso, star of “The Pope’s Toilet” and “The Eternaut,” as Silvio, ranging from smiling containment of a reasonable man to outraged anger, paralysis from anxiety, wistful regret and lovelorn solitude. Silvia Kutica (“Avellaneda’s Moon,” “Argentina, Land of Love and Revenge”) plays Silvio’s now increasingly estranged wife of 40 years.

“When I Existed” is lead produced by Federico Cetta for Uruguay’s El Cielo Cine who describes as “a story of reinvention built around the things that truly matter.”

Structured as near any film of ambition these days an as international co-production, “When I Existed” is co-produced by David Matamoros at Barcelona’s Doce Entertainment and Andrés Rosenblatt at Montevideo’s Metropolis Films as co-producers. Matías Burgos at Moon Ideas, also based out of Montevideo, serves as associate producer.

“This story speaks to us in a world where we have the constant feeling that time is slipping away between obligations we don’t always choose,” said Avdolov. “What do we do with the time we have? Today we need small acts of resistance against a logic that tends to make everything increasingly automatic and artificial. For me, making this film has something of that.”

“What won us over about ‘When I Existed’ was its rare mix of humor and humanity,” said M-Appeal co-founder Maren Kroymann.

She added: “Silvio is a charming man who struggles to accept retirement, while his wife has been waiting for this moment, hoping they can finally enjoy life together. Their story is both touching and deeply relatable, reminding us how easily we can get caught up in our habits and lose sight of what matters most. It’s a film that makes you laugh, moves you, and reminds us that it’s never too late to reconnect with the people we love.”

‘When I Existed,’ Broken Down by Damiani and Avdolov

“When I Existed” is shot with unusual elegance but sense of humor by Manuel Branaa, a camera operator on J.A. Bayona’s Netflix smash-hit “Society of the Snow.” This is caught in the the lateral tracking shot with which it opens, crossing a dark granite stone tomb taking in the red and yellows of flowers left on it. Asethetically, it’s a highly pleasing composition, but the flowers are wilting.

Drawing a counterpoint between the open expanses of marshlands, where Silvio catches up with his boat club best friends of youth, the charcoal grey and black corridors and barred doors and windows of the National Pension and Retirement Fund’s labyrinthine office conveys a sense of claustrophobia – that of a man caught not only in a bureaucratic system but his own self-absorption.

“When I Existed” delves into “the nature of the system, the ego, bureaucracy, technological trends, the dangers of alienation, and the erosion of humanity,” said Damiani and Avdolov. “We poured our souls into even the smallest details – things that might go unnoticed by others, but which, to us, made the work feel complete and purposeful,” they added.

Damiani has worked for years in advertising, as a copywriter and designer, wining Uruguay’s fist Golden Lion, then in VFX rising to Creative Director at top Uruguayan VFX house Aparato.

Avdolov has transitioned to filmmaking from a career as a novelist (“Violeta Corazón,” “Camba”), short-story writer and author of the non-fiction “El Corazón Creativo” (“The Creative Heart”).

“When I Existed” is born from the deepest fear any human being can have: how are we supposed to live? No one teaches you that,” Damiani told Variety.

It is also semi-autobiographical. “Working on ‘When I Existed’ made us realize how much of ourselves we poured into the film’s protagonist,” they added. “For many years, we had channeled our energy and creativity into other people’s projects. Following the pandemic – and having passed the age of 40– we decided to commit ourselves to our own meaningful projects. We see this film as a reminder that we are not here to live someone else’s life;

Damiani’s 2016 short, “M.A.M.O.N. (Monitor Against Mexicans Over Nationwide),” went viral, hitting over 13 million views on YouTube.

El Cielo Cine

Of features, “El Cielo Cine” has produced with Argentina 2025’s well-received adopted son drama “Emi,” directed by Ezequiel Erríquez, and Santiago Giralt’s 2023 “Norma,” a later-life self-discovery tale starring and co-written by Mercedes Morán (“Neruda,” “My Sad Dead”) which scored a best comedy Platino Award nomination.

title: Noel Clarke Pleads Not Guilty to Sexual Offense Charges
summary: Noel Clarke has pleaded not guilty to six sexual offense charges. Appearing at Westminster Magistrates Court in London on Wednesday morning, the actor, writer and director entered not guilty pleas in relation to all the charges, which include two charges of sexual assault, three charges of voyeurism and one charge of exposure. The charges relate […]
content:
Noel Clarke has pleaded not guilty to six sexual offense charges.

Appearing at Westminster Magistrates Court in London on Wednesday morning, the actor, writer and director entered not guilty pleas in relation to all the charges, which include two charges of sexual assault, three charges of voyeurism and one charge of exposure.

The charges relate to alleged offenses that took place between 2007 and 2016 involving five women.

As well as a long-running role on “Doctor Who” as dimension-hopping hero Mickey Smith, Clarke won critical acclaim for his teen dramas “Kidulthood,” “Adulthood” and “Brotherhood.”

Popular on Variety

He also co-wrote Sky drama “Bulletproof” with Ashley Walters, which ran for three seasons. It was cancelled in spring 2021 after The Guardian published an article containing multiple sexual misconduct allegations, which Clarke denied at the time.

Clarke eventually brought a libel claim against the newspaper, which he lost last year after the judge, finding in favor of The Guardian, held that the paper’s reporting was “substantially true.” Justice Steyn also found Clarke to lack credibility as a witness.

The actor was ordered to pay £3 million ($4 million) of the paper’s legal costs.

Last month, Clarke was charged by London’s Metropolitan Police after the U.K.’s Crown Prosecution Service (similar to a D.A.) gave authorization having reviewed a file of evidence.

He will next appear in court on Nov. 18.

title: Ozzy Osbourne Was ‘Flying High’ Until the ‘Day He Passed’ After Final Concert, Sharon Osbourne Says: ‘We Hadn’t Seen Him That Way in Years’
summary: Ozzy Osbourne’s final “Back to the Beginning” concert kept him “flying high” until the day he died, his wife Sharon Osbourne said. Speaking at a London screening of the film “Ozzy & Black Sabbath: Back to the Beginning” — which chronicles the July 5, 2025 Birmingham show that took place just weeks before the heavy […]
content:
Ozzy Osbourne‘s final “Back to the Beginning” concert kept him “flying high” until the day he died, his wife Sharon Osbourne said.

Speaking at a London screening of the film “Ozzy & Black Sabbath: Back to the Beginning” — which chronicles the July 5, 2025 Birmingham show that took place just weeks before the heavy metal legend’s death at 76 — on Tuesday night, Sharon recalled the importance of the event to Ozzy. Besides featuring the final performances from Ozzy and Black Sabbath, “Back to the Beginning” brought together other genre heavyweights including Metallica, Guns N’ Roses, Slayer, Pantera, Tool and more.

“He was like, flying high again. He was so happy. Until the day he passed, he was still on that high,” Sharon told moderator Phil Alexander. “He was so excited, so thankful to everyone. It was just joyous for us to see him that way, because we hadn’t seen him that way in years. He was laughing, telling jokes again. It was brilliant.”

Popular on Variety

Sharon said the idea for the concert came about because Ozzy “wanted to perform one more time to say thank you and goodbye to everyone.” Although his health was touch and go — with emphysema making his vocal performance unpredictable — he was “so determined mentally to do this,” Sharon said.

“He was just praying that his longs would work and that he could sing,” Sharon remembered. “He could have been great at soundcheck, and then the gig would happen and he wouldn’t even be able to speak. But it’s mind over matter.”

She added that Ozzy’s fellow Black Sabbath members weren’t even aware of how bad his condition had become. “The guys didn’t know how sick Ozzy was. I mean, even my kids — we never told my kids,” she said. “So nobody knew how sick he was.”

Having the support of his community made all the difference, Sharon said, pointing out Black Sabbath co-founder Tony Iommi and keyboardist Adam Wakeman in the audience. “Ozzy’s closest friends were up there with him. You asked them to do something, and they delivered.”

“You know, it’s only this community that would do that,” she continued. “Can you imagine going to ask all these little girls that sing in a fucking leotard, saying, ‘We really need you. Do you think you could turn up in three months’ time?’ They’d say, ‘Fuck off, I’m too big for that.'”

On the day of the concert, Sharon remembered being “petrified, because I didn’t know whether he could literally get through it.” But Ozzy was having a grand old time, watching every act and “applauding in the dressing room.”

“He was overcome with it all. He was so, so happy,” Sharon said. “He was just genuinely moved by the whole thing. He just couldn’t believe it.”

The concert film includes behind-the-scenes footage, including of “Aquaman” star Jason Momoa, who was the event’s emcee. Sharon revealed that he didn’t exactly know that would be his job on the day.

“I thought, why tell him? It ruins the surprise!” she said with a laugh. “I said, you know, just go out there and talk to the crowd and introduce the different bands. And he’s like, ‘I can’t do that.’ Fuck off, you’re an actor!”

Asked about what made Ozzy so special as a performer, Sharon concluded that “nobody sounded like” him.

“Nobody had the soul that Ozzy had in his voice … It wasn’t just blabbing words, it was heartfelt in everything,” she said. “There’s a lot of singers that think, ‘Oh, don’t you think I’m sexy? I’m gonna take my shirt off, sweat a bit and rub me old tits.’ And it’s like, you need more than that.”

However, she cheekily added: “He would like to show his bum — that was his swan song.”

“Ozzy & Black Sabbath: Back to the Beginning” hits cinemas worldwide on Oct. 28 via Trafalgar Releasing.

title: Oscar Entries From Thailand, Nepal Head to Tokyo Filmex Competition; Lee Kang-sheng Joins Jury
summary: Thailand’s and Nepal’s Oscar submissions, “9 Temples to Heaven” and “Elephants in the Fog,” are among 10 titles competing at the 27th edition of Tokyo Filmex, which will run Nov. 20–29 in the Japanese capital’s Yurakucho district. Taiwanese actor Lee Kang-sheng, who has appeared in every feature by auteur Tsai Ming-liang since “Rebels of the […]
content:
Thailand’s and Nepal’s Oscar submissions, “9 Temples to Heaven” and “Elephants in the Fog,” are among 10 titles competing at the 27th edition of Tokyo Filmex, which will run Nov. 20–29 in the Japanese capital’s Yurakucho district.

Taiwanese actor Lee Kang-sheng, who has appeared in every feature by auteur Tsai Ming-liang since “Rebels of the Neon God” in 1992, will sit on the three-member international jury. Additional jurors will be named later. The panel will pick a Grand Prize winner, whose director will receive JPY700,000 ($4,500), and a Special Jury Prize winner, whose director will receive JPY300,000 ($1,900). Both awards will be handed out at a ceremony on Nov. 29.

The competition is open to emerging Asian directors with films finished in 2025 or 2026. Four of this year’s selections are first features.

Popular on Variety

Sompot Chidgasornpongse, who has worked as assistant director to Thai filmmaker Apichatpong Weerasethakul, makes his narrative debut with “9 Temples to Heaven.” The deadpan family comedy follows a 63-year-old man who drags nine relatives on a one-day tour of nine temples after a fortune teller warns that his mother will soon die. The mother won’t get out of the car. The film launched in Cannes’ Directors’ Fortnight and picked up best director and best actor at the Shanghai International Film Festival.

Abinash Bikram Shah’s “Elephants in the Fog” won the Jury Prize in Cannes’ Un Certain Regard strand, the first Nepali film to make the festival’s official selection. The debut feature centers on Pilati, head of a kinnar, or third-gender, community in a village hemmed in by elephant forest, who takes over the hunt for a missing girl when police won’t help.

Venice supplies four competition titles. Phuttiphong Aroonpheng’s Horizons entry “The Burning Giants” follows a young policeman who begins to doubt a government operation that closes off a forest and moves out its Indigenous Karen residents after a strange white smoke starts burning people. Michelle Zhou drew on her own life for her debut “Big Little Things,” also from Horizons, in which a woman takes a hired fake boyfriend back to Harbin for the Lunar New Year holiday to keep her girlfriend secret from her mother. It won Venice’s Premio Autrici Under 40 prize for young female directors and has four Golden Horse nominations.

Iranian filmmaker Ali Asgari’s “A Bit of Light,” from Venice’s main competition, tracks a Tehran doctor who loses his license for treating injured protesters and plans to kill himself. Amie Song’s debut “Gu Shi,” made through Venice’s Biennale College Cinema program with Anocha Suwichakornpong as executive producer, wraps its politics in a fairy tale about a family hiding out in an isolated house wedged between forest and sea.

Two films come from Toronto. Korean director Yoon Dan-bi’s “The World Before,” from the Platform competition, centers on a 17-year-old girl on a southern island who is drawn to a childhood friend back home for his grandmother’s funeral. It earned a special mention in San Sebastian’s New Directors section. Filipino filmmaker John Torres’ first narrative feature “The Remotes,” which also played the New York Film Festival, is a neo-noir in which a widowed detective close to retirement connects a run of fatal road crashes to a voice app designed to retrain reckless drivers.

Singaporean director Priscilla Ang’s debut “Ah Girl,” set in 1994 and framed in 4:3, won the Youth Jury Award in Rotterdam’s Bright Future section and has three Golden Horse nominations. Rounding out the selection is “A Song From Beyond,” the fifth feature from Japan’s Sugita Kyoshi, whose “Haruhara-san’s Recorder” won the FIDMarseille Grand Prix. A photographer agrees to act in a student’s graduation film, only to find that her estranged father has been cast as the father.

Novelist Maha Harada’s directing debut “In My Father’s Room,” revealed as the opener earlier this month, will kick off the festival. Harada adapted it from one of her own short stories, and it stars Yu Aoi as a museum guard who receives an unfamiliar key from her estranged father, played by Issey Ogata, a month after his death. The film premiered in competition at San Sebastian, where it won the Fipresci Prize and the Ateneo Guipuzcoano Award.

Anthony Chen’s “We Are All Strangers” will close the event. The film completes the Singaporean director’s “Growing Up” trilogy, after “Ilo Ilo” and “Wet Season,” and centers on a hawker-stall owner and his son, 21, who both marry and end up sharing a small public housing flat. It was the first Singaporean film picked for the Berlinale’s main competition and is Singapore’s Oscar submission.

Both titles sit in the 12-film Special Screenings section. Korean auteur Hong Sang-soo’s 34th feature, the black-and-white “The Day She Returns,” arrives from Berlin’s Panorama, while Kogonada’s Hong Kong-set “Zi,” dedicated to the late composer Sakamoto Ryuichi, comes from Sundance’s NEXT section. Ann Hui’s 1981 Hong Kong New Wave thriller “The Story of Woo Viet,” starring a 25-year-old Chow Yun-fat, screens in the M+ 4K restoration that premiered in Venice Classics.

Poh Si Teng’s documentary “American Doctor,” about three U.S. volunteer physicians who treated the wounded in Gaza before lobbying the media and Congress, took the Hot Docs Audience Award after premiering in Sundance’s U.S. Documentary Competition. Japanese filmmaker Irie Yu’s documentary feature debut “The Day He Retires” will world premiere at the festival. It follows Takeishi Kenji, who left his job at 50 to open Fukaya Cinema in Saitama, as he hands the theater to a new generation at 76.

Lee will also be on screen in a double bill of Tsai’s two newest “Walker” films, the series running since 2012 in which he plays a present-day version of Tang dynasty monk Xuanzang, moving through cities around the world at a glacial crawl. “Dust,” the 11th chapter, was shot in San Sebastian and premiered at Venice. The 12th, “Night Journey,” takes place in the Czech town of Jihlava and is a Golden Horse nominee for best documentary short.

Jia Zhangke’s “Torino Shadow,” made at the invitation of Turin’s National Cinema Museum and first shown as a Cannes special screening, headlines a shorts program alongside work by younger directors. These include Carlo Francisco Manatad’s “And If Thuy Didn’t Exist,” a special mention recipient in Locarno’s shorts competition, and “The Bovine Comedy” from “A Useful Ghost” director Ratchapoom Boonbunchachoke, which won Locarno’s Pardino d’Oro for best auteur short.

The Made in Japan sidebar has three titles. Yamanishi Tatsuya’s “Goodbye, Absence” and Sasaki Omoi’s “22nd Century Cat” will both world premiere in Tokyo. Xavier Tera’s debut “The Color of the Sun,” set in Okinawa in 2012 and lensed on 35mm by Sayombhu Mukdeeprom, won the Fipresci Prize in Venice’s Horizons section.

Screenings will take place at Yurakucho Asahi Hall, Marunouchi Piccadilly and Human Trust Cinema Yurakucho. Talents Tokyo 2026, held in cooperation with Berlinale Talents, will run in parallel at Vision Center Yurakucho and Yurakucho Asahi Square. The 25 films unveiled so far span three sections.

title: Watermelon Pictures Acquires North American Distribution Rights To Sara Ishaq’s ‘The Station’
summary: EXCLUSIVE: The Station, the debut narrative feature from Yemeni-Scottish filmmaker Sara Ishaq, has been picked up for North America by Watermelon Pictures. Watermelon will release the film theatrically later this year. The Station debuted in the Critics’ Week competition at the 2026 Cannes Film Festival. The official synopsis reads: Set against the backdrop of war-torn […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: The Station, the debut narrative feature from Yemeni-Scottish filmmaker Sara Ishaq, has been picked up for North America by Watermelon Pictures.

Watermelon will release the film theatrically later this year.

The Station debuted in the Critics’ Week competition at the 2026 Cannes Film Festival. The official synopsis reads: Set against the backdrop of war-torn Yemen, The Station follows Layal, who runs a women-only petrol station where the rules are simple: no men, no weapons, no politics. A rare sanctuary of safety and solidarity, the station becomes a vibrant gathering place where women from every walk of life come together with humor, resilience, and hope. When Layal’s younger brother faces forced enlistment, she reunites with her estranged sister to save the one life they still can, embarking on an emotional journey that balances warmth, wit, and quiet defiance in the face of extraordinary circumstances.

Manal Al-Mulaiki, Abeer Mohammed, Rashad Khaled, and Saleh Al-Marshahi star in the film. The film was produced by Screen Project and Georges Films, and co-produced by One Two Films, KeplerFilm, Barentsfilm, Setara Films, The Imaginarium Films, and ZDF Das kleine Fernsehspiel – ARTE. Jon Kilik (Babel) serves as executive producer.

Watch on Deadline

“I couldn’t think of better hands to entrust our film to in the US than Watermelon Pictures,” Ishaq said in a statement.

“Yemen so often makes US headlines in the most negative light, while the spirit and humanity of its people remain largely unknown to the American public. Watermelon Pictures understands what it means to humanize our narratives and bring them to audiences who rarely get to see us on our own terms.”

title: ‘Doctor Who’ Actor Noel Clarke Pleads Not Guilty To Sexual Assault, Voyeurism & Exposure
summary: Noel Clarke, the British actor who starred in Doctor Who and Kidulthood, has pleaded not guilty to a series of sexual offenses. London’s Metropolitan Police said in September that Clarke had been charged with two counts of sexual assault, three charges of voyeurism, and one count of exposure. The alleged offenses took place between 2007 […]
content:
Noel Clarke, the British actor who starred in Doctor Who and Kidulthood, has pleaded not guilty to a series of sexual offenses.

London’s Metropolitan Police said in September that Clarke had been charged with two counts of sexual assault, three charges of voyeurism, and one count of exposure. The alleged offenses took place between 2007 and 2016, involving five women.

Clarke appeared at Westminster Magistrates’ Court on Wednesday. He pleaded not guilty to all the charges and will next appear at Southwark Crown Court on November 18, according to BBC News.

Watch on Deadline

Detectives had been investigating Clarke for a year, arresting the actor on September 25, 2025.

He has not worked in the entertainment industry in any substantial on-screen capacity for years. He played Mickey Smith in Doctor Who, while his last series on UK television was ITV’s Viewpoint in 2021.

Clarke created hit indie movie Kidulthood and had roles in other productions, including Star Trek Into Darkness and Bulletproof.

title: BBC Scraps TikTok Generation TV News Bulletin ‘The Catch Up’
summary: EXCLUSIVE: The BBC has canceled The Catch Up, a nightly news bulletin that was aimed at the TikTok generation. The BBC has canned The Catch Up as part of the planned closure of BBC Three, the youth network that will be switched off for a second time in spring 2027. BBC Three’s brand will be retained on […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: The BBC has canceled The Catch Up, a nightly news bulletin that was aimed at the TikTok generation.

The BBC has canned The Catch Up as part of the planned closure of BBC Three, the youth network that will be switched off for a second time in spring 2027. BBC Three‘s brand will be retained on iPlayer.

The Catch Up was launched in 2022 and was pitched as an attempt to “bring back” 16- to 24-year-old viewers to traditional news bulletins. Its debut coincided with BBC Three being restored to linear TV, a decision that was reversed on Tuesday.

The two- to four-minute news bulletin was designed to provide young viewers with a roundup of the day’s headlines in an accessible format, complete with graphics and a conversational tone.

Watch on Deadline

Tuesday’s bulletin was hosted by BBC journalist Ben Henley-Washford and featured a report on BBC Three’s demise as a linear television network.

“The BBC has announced it is closing BBC Three,” Henley-Washford said. “Not just yet, though. They said the TV channel, along with BBC Scotland’s channel, will close in the spring as the corporation continues to make £500 million pounds worth of savings by 2028.”

He did not mention that The Catch Up would be discontinued.

When The Catch Up launched, then editor Amanda Goodman told Press Gazette: “We want to create relatable news for young people that doesn’t necessarily sound like the BBC, or the BBC they think exists at present.”

BBC News was not on TikTok in 2022, but this has changed. The BBC News account now has 16.5 million followers and more than 1 billion likes.

A BBC News spokesperson said: “The BBC is the UK’s leading news publisher for 16-34 year olds in the UK – reaching around half of 16–34-year-olds each week across its BBC News platforms, including youth-focused offerings such as Newsbeat, as well as Newsround for a younger audience.

“Further to this, there are significant and growing numbers of young people accessing BBC News across our social channels – including TikTok, Instagram and YouTube. We have been clear in our commitment to providing news to young people and developing our news offering to reach audiences where they are.”

title: Amelia Dimoldenberg’s Manager Spearheading Entertainment & New Media Biz At Three Six Zero
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Amelia Dimoldenberg and Munya Chawawa’s manager is spearheading an Entertainment and New Media division at her international management outfit Three Six Zero. Rebecca Dowell is leading the division focused on multi-hyphenate talent, digital creators and IP-led projects, and will continue working with these high-profile creators, along with new clients like feminist arts and culture […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Amelia Dimoldenberg and Munya Chawawa‘s manager is spearheading an Entertainment and New Media division at her international management outfit Three Six Zero.

Rebecca Dowell is leading the division focused on multi-hyphenate talent, digital creators and IP-led projects, and will continue working with these high-profile creators, along with new clients like feminist arts and culture title Polyester Zine.

Dowell joined Three Six Zero from YMU two years ago as manager and reps the likes of Dimoldenberg, Chawawa and Victor Kunda. She leads a core management team, which is expected to expand as the division’s roster grows.

The new division will rep talent across the “entertainment and digital media landscape, driving the company’s expansion into next-generation cultural influence,” Three Six Zero said.

Watch on Deadline

Dowell is now repping Polyster Zine, expanding its Polyester Podcast from an audio-only show into a vodcast, while she will also represent founder Ione Gamble and Senior Editor Gina Tonic individually across publishing, film and television

Before YMU, Dowell worked for boutique management company MOXIE, at Studio71UK. Her YMU exit came at the same time as a number of others in the bustling UK agency industry.

Three Six Zero reps high-profile stars like Will Smith and Calvin Harris.

title: How TIFFCOM Is Building On Cannes Recognition To Strengthen Global Networks, Co-production & Japanese IP
summary: At this year’s Marché du Film at the Cannes film festival, it would be no exaggeration to say that Japanese content and creators were everywhere you turned. Designated ‘Country of Honour’ at the market, Japan was involved in a slew of panels, workshops and labs; played a prominent role in Cannes flagship programs, including Cannes […]
content:
At this year’s Marché du Film at the Cannes film festival, it would be no exaggeration to say that Japanese content and creators were everywhere you turned.

Designated ‘Country of Honour’ at the market, Japan was involved in a slew of panels, workshops and labs; played a prominent role in Cannes flagship programs, including Cannes Animation, Co-Production Day, and Producers Network; and also launched the Japan IP Market, a three-day initiative co-hosted by the Marché and Japan’s leading contents market TIFFCOM.

The Marché decided to shine a spotlight on Japan in recognition of the strength of its content and intellectual property (IP), as well as recent efforts – by the Japanese government, local studios, and independent filmmakers and producers – to engage with the rest of the world. As Deadline noted at TIFFCOM two years ago, Japan was once reliant on its huge domestic market, but is now actively seeking co-production, collaboration and exports, focusing its efforts on North and South America, Europe, and the rest of Asia.

All these efforts are being supported by the Japanese government, which last year launched the ‘Content Industry Growth Investment Support Program’, branded as IP360, which aims to expand overseas sales of Japanese content (across film, anime, games and music) to $126BN (JPY20 trillion) by 2033.

Watch on Deadline

“Historically, sectors including Japanese anime and live-action content have been optimized for the domestic market, lacking an industrial structure designed to expand into global markets,” explains TIFFCOM CEO Yasushi Shiina.

“At Cannes this year, as the Country of Honour, the public and private sectors joined forces to showcase Japan’s key strengths, including anime and manga. In doing so, we built networks with international producers, distributors, and other industry professionals, driving strong momentum toward transforming the sector into an IP-driven industry that generates global revenue.

“Following this, TIFFCOM will leverage the home-ground advantage of being hosted in Japan to promote Japanese IP alongside a diverse array of participants. For international attendees as well, we aim to make TIFFCOM a platform where they can connect directly with Japanese partners and unlock new business opportunities.”

Yasushi Shiina [L] & Kaori Ikeda [R]

A key program within TIFFCOM is the Tokyo IP Market: Adaptation & Remake (TIPM), an initiative that the Cannes IP event was also based on, which brings together publishers and production companies holding rights to Japanese manga, audiovisual works, novels and games. This year, the number of participating IP holders has expanded from six to ten companies, including content giants such as Amuse Creative Studio, Kadokawa, Nippon Animation, Shochiku and Toei.

TIPM organizes a series of one-on-one meetings between the rights holders and international producers, mostly from North America, Europe and the rest of Asia. In addition, eight of these companies will hold an open pitch event, with audiovisual support from Imagica Group, to present their flagship IP.

“We co-organized the Japan IP Market in Cannes – the Cannes edition of TIPM – with the Marché du Film, and the event generated an exceptionally strong response,” explains TIFFCOM managing director Kaori Ikeda. “Thanks to this success, the Tokyo edition is seeing an increasing number of leading producers attending from Europe and Hollywood. We’re excited to offer everyone in Tokyo this premier opportunity to connect with high-quality Japanese IP.”

Another key TIFFCOM track is the Tokyo Gap Financing Market (TGFM), which presents projects with Asian elements and at least 60% of their funding in place, that are seeking to complete their budgets through co-production, sales, distribution and other forms of investment.

This year, the event has selected 24 projects including Vincci Cheuk’s Hong Kong-Japan co-production 38.83; Boo Junfeng’s multi-territory co-production Trinity; François-Marc Baillet’s animated feature Back To Tomioka; five projects selected through a partnership with Canada’s Frontières genre market, and three in partnership with Italy’s Cinecitta (see here for the full list of selected projects).

In addition, TGFM talk sessions will introduce Japan’s various support schemes – including grants for international co-productions from Japan’s Agency for Cultural Affairs (Bunka-cho) – alongside funding from Canada and Brazil.

Japanese producers have been co-producing with their East Asian neighbors in Taiwan and South Korea for quite some time but have recently been venturing further afield into Southeast Asia and Europe. “Two factors are driving this,” says Ikeda. “First, production volume is increasing across Asia as a whole, including Southeast Asia, and production capabilities are also rising.

“Second, opportunities to build networks with one another at film festivals and markets across Asia are expanding. Platforms such as TGFM are facilitating mutual introductions, leading to an increasing number of co-production projects with Southeast Asia. Japan also recently joined the new Asian Producers Alliance with the Agency for Cultural Affairs as the representative member.”

In Europe, co-productions between Japan and France have been the most common, but Ikeda observes that projects with Italy have also increased following the signing of an official Japan-Italy co-production treaty in 2024.

Recent co-productions involving Japan include Sleep No More, from Indonesian filmmaker Edwin, which premiered at this year’s Berlinale; Ria, from the Philippines’ Arvin Belarmino, which won the Heart of Eurasia Award at Busan film festival, and Boo’s upcoming Trinity, which has around ten co-producers across Europe and Asia. Trinity, Ria and Janus Victoria’s Japan-Philippines co-production Diamonds In The Sand were all selected for various editions of TGFM.

‘Ria’

Meanwhile, TIFFCOM’s conference program will present around 20 sessions organized along thematic lines: intellectual property (IP), artificial intelligence (AI), Japanese TV, Asian Series & Films, market trends and co-production. Key sessions include an ‘Unlocking the Global Potential of Japanese IP’, with speakers from Credeus (Kokuho), Amazon MGM Studios and Netflix’s One Piece; an AI-themed keynote with AGBO’s Chris Brearton and Dominic Hughes; and the annual session by the Association of Japanese Animations, presenting data on the anime industry.

Leading Japanese broadcasters Nippon TV and TBS will host sessions on their international activities; an Anime Co-Production Conference will feature speakers including Ervin Han (The Violinist), and a “Beyond Country of Honour” session has speakers from Toho and K2 Pictures, along with TIFFCOM’s Shiina and Cannes Marché Head of Industry Programs Alexandra Zakharchenko.

Last year’s TIFFCOM had more than 4,600 attendees from 46 countries and regions, an increase of 13% from the previous year, while international participation rose by 10%. As of two weeks before this year’s edition, Ikeda says that visitor registrations – mostly buyers and producers – were up about 10% on the same point last year.

“East Asia continues to drive strong participation, led by Taiwan and South Korea, as well as a dedicated pavilion from Thailand,” Ikeda says. “Some companies from China, including streaming platforms, will also take part. And in a notable new trend, we are also seeing increasing participation from companies offering AI and data analytics solutions.”

TIFFCOM is taking place October 28 to 30 at the Tokyo Metropolitan Industrial Trade Center in Hamamatsucho district, which is just a few train stops away from Tokyo International Film Festival’s main venues in Hibiya-Ginza. The festival is running from October 26 to November 4.

title: Jon Gosselin Filming Netflix Tell-All Documentary About ‘Jon & Kate Plus 8’ With Kids Collin and Hannah
summary: “Jon & Kate Plus 8″ is getting the behind-the-scenes treatment per Netflix. Patriarch Jon Gosselin and two of his kids, Collin and Hannah, are filming a Netflix documentary about their time filming the show, the streamer announced. Per the official logline, “For nearly a decade, a family’s chaos and love played out on TV as […]
content:
“Jon & Kate Plus 8″ is getting the behind-the-scenes treatment per Netflix.

Patriarch Jon Gosselin and two of his kids, Collin and Hannah, are filming a Netflix documentary about their time filming the show, the streamer announced.

Per the official logline, “For nearly a decade, a family’s chaos and love played out on TV as comfort viewing. Years later, conflicting accounts have emerged from within the family itself — competing memories of the same childhood, the same home, the same spotlight. The new documentary takes a closer look, piecing together the story from every angle: the children who grew up on camera, the adults who built a brand around them, and the audience that couldn’t look away. It’s an intimate look at how real life became a phenomenon the world thought it knew.”

Producing the project are Mike Gasparro and Julia Willoughby-Nason for The Cinemart (“American Murder: Gabby Petito,” “Death of the Pastor’s Wife”).

title: Vivian Wilson, Model and Elon Musk’s Estranged Daughter, Signs With Echo Lake Entertainment (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Vivian Jenna Wilson, the model and estranged daughter of Elon Musk, has signed with Echo Lake Entertainment for representation in all areas. The 22-year-old has made a name for herself in fashion and as a digital media personality. She had major appearances at New York, Milan and Paris Fashion Weeks, and she is currently the […]
content:
Vivian Jenna Wilson, the model and estranged daughter of Elon Musk, has signed with Echo Lake Entertainment for representation in all areas.

The 22-year-old has made a name for herself in fashion and as a digital media personality. She had major appearances at New York, Milan and Paris Fashion Weeks, and she is currently the face of Desigual. She was recently revealed as the face of Awe Inspired’s upcoming campaign, and she starred in a campaign for Mugler.

As the face of Off-White, she hosted the fashion house’s Los Angeles launch event for its L/Ab c/o Off-White line. Wilson has also worked with brands such as Gucci, Alexander McQueen, Acne Studios, Savage x Fenty and more.

Popular on Variety

Wilson is transgender and has become a vocal advocate for LGBTQ causes such as the Trevor Project.

She and her twin brother, Griffin Musk, are the eldest children of the world’s wealthiest man. Wilson publicly came out as transgender in 2020, and two years later, when she was 18 years old, she legally changed her name. She wrote in her petition to a Los Angeles court that she no longer wished to be related to Elon Musk “in any way, shape, or form.” The two have talked about each other in the media but have been estranged for years.

“We’re excited about representing an extraordinary and charismatic artist like Vivian,” said Tanayri Novoa of Echo Lake Entertainment in a statement. “In a very short time, she’s made her mark on fashions biggest stages while using her voice for something that matters. This is just the beginning for her, and I’m thrilled to help build what’s next across fashion, entertainment and beyond.”

Wilson’s signing comes as Echo Lake continues to expand its digital talent management business, pursuing digital creators and emerging talent across the industry.

Wilson will continue to be represented by Savannah Britt and John Panichella of The Brittprint x JPPR.

title: ‘Rings of Power’ Season 3 Trailer: Dragons, Balrogs and Ringwraiths Go to War in Middle-Earth
summary: “The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power” dropped its epic Season 3 trailer on Wednesday ahead of its premiere on Prime Video on Nov. 11. The new trailer shows Sauron’s evil army full of orcs, dragons and ringwraiths wreak havoc on Middle-Earth as the heroes fight back against the onslaught. The first four […]
content:
“The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power” dropped its epic Season 3 trailer on Wednesday ahead of its premiere on Prime Video on Nov. 11.

The new trailer shows Sauron’s evil army full of orcs, dragons and ringwraiths wreak havoc on Middle-Earth as the heroes fight back against the onslaught. The first four episodes of Season 3 will premiere on Nov. 11, followed by two more on Nov. 18 and the final two on Nov. 25.

“All the peoples of Middle-Earth are engaged in the heroic struggle against Sauron and his army of Orcs,” the logline reads. “His terrifying Ring-servants, the Nazgnagôl, roam Middle-Earth clad in black armor as tensions rise among the Elves trying desperately to hold the front lines; familial ties are strained among the Dwarves in Khazad-dûm; political factions push the island kingdom of Númenor to the brink of civil war; and in the eastern lands of Rhûn, Gandalf enlists his full powers of magic and persuasion as he fights to turn the tide of impending darkness.”

Popular on Variety

The “Rings of Power” cast members include Charlie Vickers, Morfydd Clark, Robert Aramayo, Ismael Cruz Córdova, Charles Edwards, Robert Strange, and Markella Kavenagh. “Stranger Things” star Jamie Campbell Bower, Eddie Marsan, Andrew Richardson, Zubin Varla and Adam Young also joined the cast for Season 3. At this year’s San Diego Comic Con, it was revealed that Simon Pegg would voice the Balrog this season.

“The Rings of Power” Season 3 is produced by showrunners J.D. Payne and Patrick McKay. The pair will also executive produce along with Lindsey Weber, Justin Doble, Kate Hazell, and director Charlotte Brändström. Brändström is joined by directors Sanaa Hamri and Stefan Schwartz, each director overseeing multiple episodes in the upcoming season. Matthew Penry-Davey is producer with Ally O’Leary, Tim Keene, and Andrew Lee as co-producers.

Watch the trailer below.

title: Netflix Touts International Success Amid Content Leadership Shake-Up, Eyes More Broadcaster Deals After TF1 and Globo Pacts
summary: As Netflix undergoes its biggest content leadership shake-up in years, co-CEO Ted Sarandos has a clear message: The streamer’s international strategy is working, it’s the U.S. slate that needs fixing. Speaking during Netflix’s third-quarter earnings call Tuesday, Sarandos defended the company’s content strategy as the appointment of former Disney executive Peter Rice to replace Bela […]
content:
As Netflix undergoes its biggest content leadership shake-up in years, co-CEO Ted Sarandos has a clear message: The streamer’s international strategy is working, it’s the U.S. slate that needs fixing.

Speaking during Netflix’s third-quarter earnings call Tuesday, Sarandos defended the company’s content strategy as the appointment of former Disney executive Peter Rice to replace Bela Bajaria as chief content officer raises questions about the streamer’s future commissioning priorities.

“Our strategy is unchanged,” Sarandos said, emphasizing that Netflix originals remain at the heart of its business. “The anchor of that strategy are the Netflix originals. Differentiated, exclusive, ambitious, professionally produced series and films and live events.”

Popular on Variety

He said the streamer pairs that “exclusive programming with kind of a broad offering of third-party programming, including second run titles.” He then said Netflix also looks “to new ways to bring third-party content onto the service as well to complement those originals. Like we just did with TF1 in France, where you’re ingesting a full network of programming.”

While the leadership shake-up has cast uncertainty over the company’s commissioning priorities, Netflix executives pointed to strong performance across Europe, Latin America and Asia, where local productions continue to drive engagement, subscriber growth and revenue.

“We had great results in APAC, LATAM and EMEA. Our local titles from those regions are driving engagement and they’re driving business growth. And you can see how our business model works here,” said co-CEO Greg Peters on the call.

Sarandos acknowledged that the U.S. slate needs to deliver stronger results, particularly as American hits remain an important driver of engagement around the world. But he indicated that the company’s international content operation would not undergo a fundamental change under Rice.

In the U.K., one of Netflix’s most established international production hubs, the shake-up has generated some anxiety, although local producers believe the British scripted operation, led by Anne Mensah, enjoys a great deal of autonomy, having delivered delivered a string of global hits including “Baby Reindeer” and “Adolescence.”

“I have a sense they have real autonomy in the U.K.,” said one scripted producer who has worked with the local originals team. “Much more so than some of the other streamers who are much more dependent on what the American scripted commissioners or heads think about stuff.”

The recent layoffs have nevertheless unsettled Britain’s independent production community, which has already endured several difficult years of shrinking budgets and fewer commissions. With Netflix among the remaining major buyers of high-end unscripted programming, any slowdown in spending could have significant consequences for local producers.

Still, producers expect any changes introduced by Rice to take time to filter through, particularly in scripted television, where projects are commissioned years in advance. Much of the next two to three years of programming is already planned, with productions such as “The Gentlemen” Season 3 unlikely to reach screens before 2028.

Beyond the uncertainty surrounding Netflix’s commissioning priorities, the earnings call highlighted another part of the streamer’s international strategy: its growing interest in partnerships with traditional broadcasters to expand its local programming offering.

France, where Netflix is believed to have roughly 14 million subscribers, was mentioned during the call not as a showcase for its local originals (with the exception of Omar Sy’s hit heist show “Lupin”), but as an example of a distribution strategy that could be replicated elsewhere. Earlier this year, Netflix kicked off its distribution deal with leading commercial broadcaster TF1, giving subscribers access to the network’s linear and on-demand programming directly through the streaming platform.

Speaking about the company’s broader approach to licensing and partnerships, Peters said Netflix was looking for new ways to bring more programming to subscribers.

“We are always seeking new ways to expand our offering, new ways to provide more professionally produced film, TV, live events, more core entertainment value. And that means we do things like licensing. It also means we look for new creative partnerships like we did with TF1,” Peters said.

The deal has been delivering encouraging results, according to Peters. “We are very pleased with the early performance that we’ve seen in that integration. We have been able to enhance an already very compelling service for our French members with even more local popular French programming.”

Peters said TF1 viewing on Netflix was growing every month and early testing suggested the additional programming was generating incremental viewing rather than simply drawing audiences away from Netflix’s existing offering.

The executive said Netflix will look to “replicate similar positive results with other partners.”

These type of alliances with broadcasters are allowing Netflix to expand its offering with local programming without having to bear the full cost of producing it. For broadcasters, such partnerships offer a way to reach Netflix’s large subscriber base while bringing additional revenue from existing programming. Producers, meanwhile, are more wary of these types of deals because it impacts the value of shows that suddenly become simultaneously available on multiple platforms, therefore losing their exclusivity.

The push for more licensing deals comes as Netflix is seeking to loosen some of the investment obligations imposed on streamers in Europe.

In France, Netflix became the country’s largest private contributor to local creation in 2025, investing €308 million ($345 million) across film and television, according to French broadcasting regulator Arcom. Yet the streamer has also been seeking to limit some of its investment obligations. Alongside Amazon Prime Video and Disney+, Netflix has lodged an appeal with France’s highest administrative court, the Conseil d’État, challenging new sub-quotas for investment in documentaries and animation.

At the European level, Netflix is also lobbying for more flexible local content requirements as the European Commission reviews the Audiovisual Media Services Directive, which kicked off in 2022.

In Italy, Netflix already has licensing arrangements with public broadcaster RAI that give the streamer second-window access to some of its biggest shows, including “Sandokan,” a modern adaptation of Emilio Salgari’s classic pirate adventures, and Naples-set prison drama “The Sea Beyond.”

Whether that relationship could evolve into a broader aggregation deal along the lines of TF1 remains unclear. But Netflix’s Italian content chief, Eleonora Andreatta, previously served as RAI’s head of drama, giving her deep ties to the broadcaster and the local production community.

In Spain, licensing programming from established broadcasters is already a significant part of Netflix’s business. The volume of licensed content on Netflix in Spain rose from 2,420 hours in 2024 to 2,829 hours in 2025, according to estimates from Ampere Analysis. That included approximately 700 hours sourced from public broadcaster RTVE and commercial broadcaster Atresmedia, up from 543 hours the previous year.

While broadcaster partnerships are giving Netflix more ways to expand its international offering, Rice’s arrival has also raised questions about how much the company will continue to spend on original productions, particularly films.

“It’s very interesting Netflix hasn’t gone for someone who’s not a TV person but has a very high film profile,” said one leading Spanish producer, who questioned whether Netflix’s previous emphasis on producing a large volume of original films had delivered sufficient results.

“Netflix was producing around 80 original films [in the U.S.] out of which I don’t know how many were remotely relevant, just pouring tons of money in originals that nobody was seeing,” the producer said.

“Rice has been the head of a studio and head of a studio internationally and someone who knows the world market. It’s going to be key to see who is named to substitute Dan Lin and how that could play a role also in films and originals.”

Brazil offers another example of Netflix’s growing appetite for broadcaster partnerships, and it was the international market Sarandos spent the most time discussing during the call. Netflix recently struck its largest-ever licensing agreement with Globo, Latin America’s biggest media company, securing 18 titles from a broadcaster that had long resisted licensing its programming to Netflix within Brazil.

“This is the most meaningful licensing deal we’ve ever done in Brazil,” Sarandos said. “They are the leading series and film producer and distributor in that country. And they have also been a long holdout licensing content to us locally.”

Although Netflix previously carried Globo programming elsewhere in Latin America and internationally, the broadcaster had kept much of its content off the platform in its home market, where it operates its own premium streaming service, Globoplay.

The new agreement, which starts December and runs through mid-2027, includes Brazilian rights to Walter Salles’ Oscar-winning drama “I’m Still Here” and “India — A Love Story,” the internationally successful telenovela created by Glória Perez that won an International Emmy in 2009.

Fourteen of the 18 titles are films, offering a potentially valuable second window for Brazilian productions that often struggle to find audiences beyond their domestic theatrical release. While “I’m Still Here” grossed $19.6 million in Brazil, many local films attract only a fraction of that audience.

“A lot of other Brazilian films make 10,000 admissions in theaters. And that kills the film,” producer Rodrigo Teixeira said at the San Sebastián Film Festival’s Creative Investors Conference.

If broadcaster partnerships are helping Netflix expand its offering in Europe and Latin America, India shows why the streamer is unlikely to retreat from investing in local originals. It was the standout performer in the third quarter, with viewing hours jumping 24% year-over-year and revenue rising nearly 20%, according to Peters.

Sarandos also singled out Korea, Japan and the Nordic countries as examples of markets where local programming has been delivering strong results.

Vivek Couto, co-founder and CEO of Media Partners Asia, said Asia-Pacific remains Netflix’s fastest-growing region when currency fluctuations are excluded, although its contribution to revenue still trails its share of the subscriber base.

“Asia is about a fifth of Netflix’s subscribers but only around 12% of its revenue,” Couto said. “We see APAC reaching $8 billion by 2030, with upside, and the real question is what it takes to get to $10 billion.”

Couto said India and Japan would be central to that expansion, alongside continued growth in Southeast Asia, where Netflix has been investing in programming that resembles traditional free-to-air television.
