In an internal memo earlier this week, BBC content chief Kate Phillips told colleagues that her department will make “tough” choices to support the corporation’s belt-tightening. Phillips announced that […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: The BBC will merge TV and audio commissioning teams across comedy and other genres amid plans to close around 100 roles in its content unit.

In an internal memo earlier this week, BBC content chief Kate Phillips told colleagues that her department will make “tough” choices to support the corporation’s belt-tightening.

Phillips announced that she will combine TV and audio commissioning teams across comedy, arts, and classical music from January 2027.

“This is about creating more opportunities for commissioners to collaborate, share ideas and develop the strongest possible content for audiences wherever they are,” she said.

Practically, this will mean that comedy chief Chris Sussman will oversee the genre across TV and radio, with Julia McKenzie, Radio 4’s commissioning editor for comedy and entertainment, joining his team.

Watch on Deadline

Suzy Klein, head of arts and classical music TV, will oversee audio and video commissioning for arts, with Matthew Dodd, commissioning editor for arts on Radio 4, joining her team. Sam Jackson, controller of BBC Radio 3 and BBC Proms, will oversee audio and video commissioning for classical music.

Phillips announced the change in an email detailing how the content unit will contribute to the BBC’s plans to save £500 million ($669M).

The BBC will close around 100 roles across the content unit by the end of its current financial year, despite the division’s headcount being relatively low compared with other areas of the broadcaster.

“Although staff costs are a relatively small proportion of our overall budgets, some headcount reduction will be required,” content teams were told. “We’ll prioritise voluntary redundancy and closing vacancies wherever possible, with the aim of keeping compulsory redundancies to a minimum.”

The BBC’s content unit has previously announced that it will contribute £100M of savings to the corporation’s overall goal of £500M. This will include slashing commissioning spend by £80M, cutting 100-150 hours of original TV shows and 350-400 hours of audio by March 2028.

“These changes will mean decommissioning some shows, fewer commissions across our genres, as well as a reduction in our development spend by around 15%, focusing on fewer ideas with the strongest chance of success,” the BBC has said.

The broadcaster has already announced that series including RuPaul’s Drag Race UK, Blankety Blank, Celebrity Mastermind, and Live At The Apollo are all casualties of the cuts.

Earlier this week, the BBC confirmed that BBC Three, BBC Scotland and Radio 4 Extra would close as television services by spring next year.

Phillips told colleagues: “I’d like to say a heartfelt thank you to everyone in BBC Content who is working incredibly hard to ensure we’re set up for future success. I know things aren’t easy at the moment; and there will be more change to come. But I’m so proud of all that we do.”

title: David Krumholtz Explains Why He Missed ’10 Things I Hate About You’ Reunion On ‘DWTS’: “Love Them All”
summary: As Julia Stiles paid tribute to Heath Ledger on Dancing with the Stars, one 10 Things I Hate About You star was unable to attend the televised reunion. Following Tuesday’s “Dedication Night” on Season 35 of the ABC dance competition show, David Krumholtz explained why he was not able to join his co-stars in supporting […]
content:
As Julia Stiles paid tribute to Heath Ledger on Dancing with the Stars, one 10 Things I Hate About You star was unable to attend the televised reunion.

Following Tuesday’s “Dedication Night” on Season 35 of the ABC dance competition show, David Krumholtz explained why he was not able to join his co-stars in supporting Stiles at the live taping.

“Good morning, here I am in the Catskill Mountains, upstate New York. Fall foliage in full effect,” he began in a video on Instagram. “I am here shooting a film. I could not be in LA for Dancing with the Stars last night.”

Krumholtz continued, “I would have loved, loved, loved to have been there. Everyone looked so amazing. Julia’s tribute to my dear friend who I miss every single day was amazing and stunning, and I’m so proud of her. And I thought the cast looked amazing.

Watch on Deadline

“They all look so young still, and it would have been weird,” said Krumholtz, taking off his beanie to reveal a bald spot. “Because I shaved what’s left of my hair, and then it becomes a whole internet fodder. ‘Oh, look what happened to him.’ I didn’t want that. But that’s not why I wasn’t there. I would have dealt with it. Anyway, love them all, love you all.”

Stiles commented on Krumholtz’s post, “We love you Krumholtz!”

After Stiles performed a dance with pro Ezra Sosa to Frankie Valli’s “Can’t Take My Eyes Off You”, she was joined onstage by her 10 Things co-stars Larisa Oleynik, Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Gabrielle Union, Andrew Keegan and Susan May Pratt.

Krumholtz’s post comes after her explained in August that he recently “decided to put my career on hold” to focus on his mental health, following a previous announcement that some believed was him retiring.

title: EA Cuts Around 400 Jobs, Shuts Down BioWare
summary: After going private in August, Electronic Arts (EA) is cutting about 3% of its staff and shutting down video game developer BioWare. On Wednesday, EA reportedly notified employees in an email that the company would be laying off around 400 people, including about 50 at BioWare, as the company focuses on more lucrative projects, according […]
content:
After going private in August, Electronic Arts (EA) is cutting about 3% of its staff and shutting down video game developer BioWare.

On Wednesday, EA reportedly notified employees in an email that the company would be laying off around 400 people, including about 50 at BioWare, as the company focuses on more lucrative projects, according to Bloomberg.

Closing down BioWare’s Edmonton, Canada studio, the announcement also included the cancellation of a Mass Effect game in early development.

“For more than 30 years, BioWare has been more than a studio. It has been a home for storytellers, developers, and the players who brought our worlds to life,” said a spokesperson for the developer in a statement. “Baldur’s Gate. Neverwinter Nights. Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic. Dragon Age. Mass Effect. Anthem.”

Watch on Deadline

The statement continued, “Now, after more than three decades of shared adventures, BioWare is closing and early development on the next Mass Effect project is ending. There is nothing easy about writing those words. Our focus right now is on our incredibly talented team who put their hearts into these games, and supporting one another through this transition.

“What generations of BioWare built together is something to celebrate and remember. These games became so much more because you played them, debated your choices, fell in love with the characters, and made these worlds your own. From all of us at BioWare, thank you for being the most meaningful part of our story,” they added.

In EA’s email, the company said it would attempt to help impacted employees find another role internally.

Last year, EA went private in a $55B deal led by Silver Lake, Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund and Jared Kushner’s investment firm Affinity Partners.

title: Sara Bareilles Is “Still Holding Out” For A ‘Girls5eva’ Movie: “We’d Do It In A Heartbeat”
summary: Although Girls5eva was cut short after three seasons, Sara Bareilles still has some “Big P*ssy Energy” to work out with her inner Fledge Mulholland. The 2x Grammy winner recently admitted she’s “still holding out” for a movie adaptation of the Peacock/Netflix series, which ran for three seasons from 2021 to 2024, noting that she and […]
content:
Although Girls5eva was cut short after three seasons, Sara Bareilles still has some “Big P*ssy Energy” to work out with her inner Fledge Mulholland.

The 2x Grammy winner recently admitted she’s “still holding out” for a movie adaptation of the Peacock/Netflix series, which ran for three seasons from 2021 to 2024, noting that she and her co-stars would “do it in a heartbeat.”

“I would do that show until I was dead in the ground. I loved it so much,” she said on The Zach Sang Show. “They just stopped paying us to do it. I would do it for free—I maybe wouldn’t do it for free, but I would do it for very little.”

Bareilles continued, “We wanted to tour. We wanted to do all kinds of things. I’m still holding out for a Sex and the City style movie, like a Girls5eva film. That feels finite, we could do it.”

Watch on Deadline

When asked if the rest of the cast would sign on, she said “100 percent,” adding, “They loved it. We loved it. We loved each other, and we loved doing that. I think we’d do it in a heartbeat.”

Created by Meredith Scardino, Girls5eva followed the four surviving members of the titular late ’90s/early aughts girl group as the reunite to make their comeback amid the stresses of being a woman of a certain age. Bareilles starred alongside Busy Philipps, Paula Pell, Renée Elise Goldsberry and Ashley Park.

title: ‘860’ Broadway Review: Billy Crystal Remembers The Stuff Of Life And Loss
summary: Billy Crystal’s career, from his catch-a-rising-star stand-up days of the 1970s, his groundbreaking role as TV’s first regular-cast gay character on the sitcom Soap and through his years as both a top Hollywood director and what many consider the greatest host in Oscar history, gets a fine, funny and emotional telling in 860, Crystal’s new […]
content:
Billy Crystal‘s career, from his catch-a-rising-star stand-up days of the 1970s, his groundbreaking role as TV’s first regular-cast gay character on the sitcom Soap and through his years as both a top Hollywood director and what many consider the greatest host in Oscar history, gets a fine, funny and emotional telling in 860, Crystal’s new solo show opening tonight on Broadway.

And if the fact that it’s Crystal himself performing the career retrospective that most stars don’t live to see, the show quickly dissipates any notion of self-congratulations or back-patting: Crystal is the sort of comic who can infuse his material with just the right amount of self-deprecation to seem like something of an underdog in life’s kennel, a pretty impressive feat given the man’s charmed life.

Well, charmed from the outside. Taking its title from the street address of Crystal’s longtime Pacific Palisades home, where the comedian raised his two daughters with wife Janice and where, in his home office, he kept a lifetime of treasured keepsakes, 860, smoothly directed by Scott Ellis, begins in tragedy: The home was destroyed in the apocalyptic 2025 Palisades wildfires, incinerating decades-worth of career mementos, cherished childhood touchstones and the relics of a past that marked the many friendships and family moments that are a source of emotional grounding for a sentimental pack-rat like Crystal.

Watch on Deadline

In fact, it’s that sentimentality that goes a long way in heading off potential audience resistance. Crystal is, after all, a wealthy, heavily insured man, and a focus on the loss of stuff – none of his family or friends were injured in the blaze – could, in less skilled hands, be more than a little off-putting.

But Crystal uses these lost objects the way Proust pondered a madeleine, as a vibe-inducing cue that can transport him – and, with him as our guide, us – back to the highlights of a life filled with many. And since we’ve all borne witness to so many this star’s transformational moments both public and private, we can’t help being moved by the poignance of the nostalgia offered up from stage of the Imperial Theatre.

Avery Brunkus

With a set design by Tony winner Scott Pask that recreates Crystal’s now-lost sanctum sanctorum down to the framed photos of dear friends and co-stars past, and baseball memorabilia from his own childhood mitt to equipment autographed by Babe Ruth and Lou Gehrig and Ted Williams and Joe DiMaggio. Jen Schriever’s lighting design makes sure we’re looking at the right spot at the right time, and video work – old home movies, classic performance clips – by Hana S. Kim and Kylee Loera is emotionally transporting and plot-moving in equal measure.

Those videos (along with the sound design by Dan Moses Schreier) take us right back to a past that can be terrifying (news and personal footage of the fires), hilarious (a clip from Soap reminds us of just what a jewel we had in Katherine Helmond) and heart-tugging (the moment when Crystal was briefly caught off guard by the surprise appearance of his friend Muhammad Ali onto the stage of an early HBO comedy special. Pure gold).

As helpful as all the film evidence is, Crystal, if need would ever be, could do without it: This is a performer whose early skills for mimicry and delivering a punch line have, if it’s even possible, sharpened over the decades. His recreation of the career-making ’70s routine in which he plays both parts of a ringside conversation between Ali and sportscaster-nemesis Howard Cosell is as uncanny as ever, and his recollection of an early-career spot as the opening act for Blood, Sweat and Tears works even if you’ve never heard of David Clayton-Thomas or “Spinning Wheel.”

The show business highlights are here, of course. There’s the “You look marvelous” era of Saturday Night Live, his Hannibal Lecter Oscar-host entrance, late-night guest appearances, City Slickers, When Harry Met Sally, and even, as if to demonstrate the play’s expanse, a quick mention of his film debut in Joan Rivers’ dismal Rabbit Test, “the worst movie ever made,” as its star recalls.

Lots of these career milestones are, in hindsight, bittersweet, as such memories tend to be. The 1986 Comic Relief fundraiser stirs recollections of his great friend Robin Williams and the toll of that death, and his love of baseball is inextricably tied to the father he lost as a teenager.

But no other moments in the show cut as close to the bone as the recollections of Crystal’s longtime best friend, Rob Reiner. He first broaches the subject in a roundabout fashion, paying tribute to Norman Lear, the groundbreaking TV producer who saw a young Crystal perform at the Comedy Store and hired him to play the best friend of Reiner’s Michael Stivic in an episode of All in the Family. Addressing Lear directly, Crystal says, “You told me, ‘I think you two will be great together,'” then adds, after a recap of This is Spinal Tap, The Princess Bride and When Harry Met Sally, “So that’s why I wanted to thank Norman Lear. Unknowingly, he made it possible to have the friend of a lifetime.”

Crystal, inevitably, circles back to Reiner, saying about the Palisades fire, as if warning the audience of rough times ahead, “2025 was the worst year of our lives. We couldn’t imagine anything worse than our house burning down. But then on December 14th, there was a phone call.” In a flash, “the unimaginable became reality.”

While 860 doesn’t ignore its creator’s lows, Crystal is too much the entertainer to leave the stage without some light and hope. There’s a sweet moment when he, grieving the loss of his friend, recalls some inspirational words from Ali, something getting back up when you’re knocked down, and the comic takes it to heart. And there are a few objects that, against all odds, survive the blaze, though by the end of 860 we know Crystal could do just fine without stuff.

Title: 860

Venue: Broadway’s Imperial Theatre

Written And Performed By: Billy Crystal

Directed By: Scott Ellis

Running Time: 1 hr 35 min (no intermission)

title: ‘Heated Rivalry’ to Release in Movie Theaters, Two Episodes at a Time
summary: Forget about going to the cottage. “Heated Rivalry” fans will be going to movie theaters in November. Almost a year after the queer hockey romance series premiered in the U.S., Regal will release all six episodes in more than 650 theaters nationwide for a limited run Nov. 6-30. “When a series connects with audiences the […]
content:
Forget about going to the cottage. “Heated Rivalry” fans will be going to movie theaters in November.

Almost a year after the queer hockey romance series premiered in the U.S., Regal will release all six episodes in more than 650 theaters nationwide for a limited run Nov. 6-30.

“When a series connects with audiences the way ‘Heated Rivalry’ has, we look for ways to bring it to the big screen and give fans a reason to experience it together,” Brooks LeBoeuf, senior vice president of U.S. content at Regal, said in a statement Thursday. “Nearly a year after its premiere, we’re proud to work with our partners to turn a season fans have watched again and again into a true theatrical event. It’s a chance to celebrate the story, its creators and its performances before Season 2 arrives in 2027.”

Based on Rachel Reid’s bestselling novels, “Heated Rivalry” follows rival hockey players Shane Hollander (Hudson Williams) and Ilya Rozanov (Connor Storrie) as they secretly fall in love. The series quickly became a global hit, with Williams and Storrie becoming two of Hollywood’s most sought-after actors. Written and directed by Jacob Tierney, “Heated Rivalry,” currently in production of its second season, also features François Arnaud, Robbie G.K., Christina Chang, Ksenia Daniela Kharlamova, Sophie Nélisse and Dylan Walsh.

Popular on Variety

During the theatrical run, which Regal is leading in partnership with Sphere Abacus, moviegoers can revisit the series in order across three paired screenings: Episodes 1 and 2 (“Rookies” and “Olympians”), Episodes 3 and 4 (“Hunter” and “Rose”), and Episodes 5 and 6 (“I’ll Believe in Anything” and “The Cottage”). Tickets for each pairing cost $9.99.

“‘Heated Rivalry’ is a global phenomenon creating a rush of social media and press activity wherever it lands,” said Hana Palmer, executive director, global distribution and partnerships at Sphere Abacus. “We’re very excited to give audiences the opportunity to watch the drama unfold on big screens in North America, the U.K., Australia and New Zealand.”

Regal screenings will also feature welcome content from the series’ cast and director, while participating locations will offer limited-time themed cocktails: Summer in Montreal and Russians Don’t Blush. In-theater marketing support is provided by PaperAirplane.

Advance tickets for “Heated Rivalry” are available now at theater box offices, on mobile apps and through REGmovies.com.

title: JJ Watt Named CBS Sports’ New Lead NFL Analyst in Multi-Year Deal
summary: JJ Watt, the former defensive end, will take on one of the biggest on-air roles in sports after officially being named the new lead NFL analyst for CBS Sports, being handed the post following the exit of his predecessor, Tony Romo. Watt will continue to call CBS’ top games alongside Jim Nantz and Tracy Wolfson […]
content:
JJ Watt, the former defensive end, will take on one of the biggest on-air roles in sports after officially being named the new lead NFL analyst for CBS Sports, being handed the post following the exit of his predecessor, Tony Romo.

Watt will continue to call CBS’ top games alongside Jim Nantz and Tracy Wolfson — including next season when the network telecasts Super Bowl LXII from Atlanta.

“I’ve had a front-row seat to JJ’s growth as a top-tier broadcaster, watching him tackle this role just like he did his hall-of-fame playing career,” said David Berson, chairman of the global sports group at Skydance, CBS’ corporate parent, in a statement. “He’s insightful, entertaining, passionate, meticulous in his preparation, and the ultimate teammate. He has a unique ability to see things and communicate to fans of all levels. We are thrilled to have him leading our NFL coverage.”

Watt joined CBS Sports in 2023 as a studio analyst on “The NFL Today.” Last season, Watt moved to the booth to call games with Ian Eagle and Evan Washburn. At the start of the 2026 season, he began calling games with the Network’s lead team, working with Nantz and Wolfson. He has been filling in for Romo, whoin September pleaded no contest to a charge of operating while intoxicated stemming from an incident that took place in Milwaukee in July.

Popular on Variety

He did not. CBS Sports and the former quarterback said earlier this month that they would split, a move sports-media aficionados attributed to some disillusionment with Romo’s recent on-air performance.

Watt also has critical on-the-field experience., having played for the Houston Texans and Arizona Cardinals. He is the only player in NFL history to record multiple seasons with at least 20 sacks.

TV-sports outlets have been pouring out money to lure top NFL announcers, with Fox and Disney shelling out top dollar to lure, respectively, Tom Brady and Troy Aikman and Joe Buck. Many top announcers’ contracts are expected to lapse after the end of this season, including not only Aikman’s, but Greg Olsen’s at Fox, and Al Michaels’ at Amazon. ESPN has secured Buck to a new deal — but so far, not Aikman — and Amazon has signed Kirk Herbstreit, who also calls college game at ESPN, to provisional terms. ESPN and Amazon have so far declined to comment on the status of those announcers’ deals.

TV networks rushed to line up top talent to call games after the NFL struck a pivotal 11-year rights deal in 2021. At the time, the thought from many TV sports chiefs was that they had to spend money to make money. Romo carved out new terrain at CBS Sports after revealing a knack for predicting game play — all but forcing CBS to re-sign the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback to a multi-season pact in 2020 valued at around $17 million a year.

Since that time, most of CBS’ contemporaries have followed suit. When ESPN signed former Fox Sports mainstays Buck and Aikman to deals in 2022 to call “Monday Night Football,” it was seen as a critical move that would help the Disney-backed sports-media giant soothe what had become a troubled relationship with the NFL. Amazon lured NBC Sports’ Al Michaels and ESPN’s Herbstreit to serve as the voices for “Thursday Night Football.” And Fox secured the services of none other than Brady, a move that crowded out sportscaster Olsen.

People familiar with the market estimate top football-booth personnel can earn between $15 million and $20 million per season.

CBS Sports may have other talent issues to juggle in weeks to come. Ian Eagle, a veteran who calls secondary NFL games for CBS Sports, is also believed to have a contract that is set to lapse. He also calls NBA games for Amazon’s Prime Video.

title: TV Festival Manchester Sets Dates, Venues and Advisory Chair
summary: The TV Festival, previously known as Edinburgh TV Festival, has unveiled the first details of its inaugural event in Manchester. Set to be held for the first time in the northern city next year, the festival will keep its four-day schedule but will take place later in the month than usual. Previously the festival, which […]
content:
The TV Festival, previously known as Edinburgh TV Festival, has unveiled the first details of its inaugural event in Manchester.

Set to be held for the first time in the northern city next year, the festival will keep its four-day schedule but will take place later in the month than usual.

Previously the festival, which has been held in the Scottish city of Edinburgh for fifty years, would traditionally take place in the last week of August.

Next year’s edition will take place after the U.K.’s August public holiday, running from Aug. 31 to Sept. 3.

Popular on Variety

The change of location has had a mixed response, with many citing Edinburgh’s charm and proximity to annual comedy festival the Edinburgh Fringe as reason’s for the festival success. The decision was made by The TV Foundation, a charity that organizes the festival, who believe the move will make the event more accessible to the television community.

It will take place at Versa Studios Manchester – formerly the site of the iconic Granada Studios — and Aviva Studios, which is the home of the Manchester International Festival and Factory International.

The area has been home to some of Britain’s best-known television shows including “Coronation Street,” “University Challenge” and “The Royle Family.”

“With Greater Manchester as our new home, we’re ready to grow and realise the Festival’s full potential over the coming years; whether that’s extending the programme into evening sessions, new creative partnerships or opening the doors to public-facing events or screenings,” said the festival’s CEO, Campbell Glennie. “We have the potential to create a city-wide celebration of the TV and broader creative industries for the next generation.”

The advisory chair for next year’s addition will be Sony Pictures Television’s president of international production, Wayne Garvie.

Garvie said: “I feel privileged to be bringing the Television Festival to a city I love, a city renowned for innovation, culture, and having a damn good time. We’ll make this an unforgettable event, with emerging voices and global names, argument and laughter, so come and join us to plot the future of our industry.”

title: Julia Stiles Asked Michelle Williams for Permission to Do Heath Ledger ‘DWTS’ Tribute; David Krumholtz Explains Why He Missed Reunion
summary: Ahead of her emotional “Dancing With the Stars” tribute, Julia Stiles reached out to Heath Ledger’s former partner Michelle Williams. Speaking to Extra after the performance — which saw Stiles dance to Frankie Valli’s “I Can’t Take My Eyes Off of You” in a sweet homage to her and Ledger’s 1999 classic “10 Things I […]
content:
Ahead of her emotional “Dancing With the Stars” tribute, Julia Stiles reached out to Heath Ledger‘s former partner Michelle Williams.

Speaking to Extra after the performance — which saw Stiles dance to Frankie Valli’s “I Can’t Take My Eyes Off of You” in a sweet homage to her and Ledger’s 1999 classic “10 Things I Hate About You” — Stiles said, “I did ask Michelle if this was OK, and she said yes.”

Stiles declined to elaborate further, saying “I don’t really want to speak for them” when asked what Ledger’s family might think of the tribute. Williams and Ledger dated from 2004 to 2007 and share a daughter, Matilda.

Popular on Variety

Stiles reunited most of the “10 Things I Hate About You” cast on the “DWTS” stage on Tuesday, including Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Larisa Oleynik, Gabrielle Union, Susan May Pratt and Andrew Keegan. However, fans noticed one key cast member was missing: David Krumholtz, who played Michael, the nerdy friend of Gordon-Levitt’s character Cameron.

Krumholtz addressed why he was not in attendance via a video posted to Instagram on Wednesday, saying that he’s in upstate New York shooting a movie. “I could not be in L.A. for ‘Dancing With the Stars’ last night. I would have loved loved loved to have been there,” he said. “Everyone looked so amazing.”

Speaking of Ledger, he added: “Julia’s tribute to my dear friend, who I miss every single day, was amazing and stunning, and I’m so proud of her.”

Stiles commented on his post, “We love you Krumholtz!”

After the performance, Stiles told Variety that it was important to have as much of the cast on stage as possible. “I begged them, each and every one of them, and they all rallied. They really did,” she said, adding: “At 17 years old, I never would have thought that I’d be here at 45, celebrating my body, dancing on the show that I absolutely love and that fans are still interested in this movie and still moved and touched by this movie.”

title: ‘Blippi’ Spinoff ‘Meekah’ Set at Moonbug Entertainment, the Studio Behind ‘Cocomelon’ (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Moonbug Entertainment, the studio that produces popular preschool series “Cocomelon” and “Blippi,” has set its newest series. “Meekah” will premiere on Nov. 7 on its own YouTube channel as a spinoff. A spinoff of “Blippi,” the series stars Lauren Vaz as Blippi’s best friend. Per the official description, “While Blippi loves discovering how things work, […]
content:
Moonbug Entertainment, the studio that produces popular preschool series “Cocomelon” and “Blippi,” has set its newest series.

“Meekah” will premiere on Nov. 7 on its own YouTube channel as a spinoff. A spinoff of “Blippi,” the series stars Lauren Vaz as Blippi’s best friend. Per the official description, “While Blippi loves discovering how things work, Meekah loves jumping in and seeing what she can do, turning everyday play into adventures where kids can bounce like an astronaut, kick like a soccer player, invent new dance moves and more. She is joined on select adventures by her Mini Movers, a group of young kids who move, dance, imagine and play alongside her. Together, they help bring each adventure to life while giving kids at home an easy way to follow along and join in.”

On Nov. 2, Moonbug will debut a Meekah-led music video titled “Happy Place.” Then will come the official series premiere on Nov. 7, titled “Superhero Meekah Saves the City.” The episode will see Meekah and the Mini Movers defeat a giant cardboard robot. Moonbug also has plans to release a music video called “Bubble Pop” and a mermaid-themed episode that will help children practice different swim strokes and learn about ocean creatures and sustainability. New episodes will premiere every other Saturday and run for roughly 15 minutes. According to Moonbug, the series focuses on “imaginative storytelling, energetic physical play, games and original music, with adventures spanning fantasy role play, dance, creative challenges and more. Movements are designed to be big, clear and safe for preschoolers to try at home, with Meekah modeling checking for space and getting help from grown-ups.”

Popular on Variety

Aimed at ages 3-6, “Meekah” utilizes Moonbug’s core learning principles, a UCLA-backed initiative first reported on by Variety in April. In a June interview, the chief creative officer Rich Hickey expanded on the company’s four areas of focus: “navigating real-life moments, modeling positive relationships, promoting learning through play and telling authentically inclusive stories.”

“Meekah has an incredible ability to ignite curiosity and make kids feel like they can jump right in with her,” said Lizzy Easterday, Senior Director of Creative at Moonbug Entertainment. “We wanted to build a series around that spirit, where kids aren’t just watching the adventure unfold – they’re part of it. Movement is at the heart of every episode, giving children opportunities to jump, dance, imagine and express themselves in their own way. It’s about inspiring curiosity, celebrating creativity, building confidence and reminding kids that there’s no one right way to play.”

See a teaser for “Meekah” below.

title: Puck Yeah! ‘Heated Rivalry’ Gets Limited Theatrical Run With Regal For Season 1
summary: The boy aquarium has some competition next month as Heated Rivalry fans are treated to a jumbotron-sized event that should hold them over until Season 2. From Nov. 6-30, fans can experience all six episodes of Season 1 on a screen befitting of Shane (Hudson Williams) and Ilya’s (Connor Storrie) cinematic love story with a […]
content:
The boy aquarium has some competition next month as Heated Rivalry fans are treated to a jumbotron-sized event that should hold them over until Season 2.

From Nov. 6-30, fans can experience all six episodes of Season 1 on a screen befitting of Shane (Hudson Williams) and Ilya’s (Connor Storrie) cinematic love story with a limited theatrical release at more than 275 Regal Cinema locations nationwide, in partnership with Sphere Abacus and Crave.

With distribution led by Regal, the show will also be available on the big screen at AMC, Cinemark and other participating theaters, for more than 650 locations total. At $9.99 for the paired-episode screenings, advanced tickets are now available at Regal.

Screenings will feature exclusive welcome content from the show’s cast and directors, and participating locations will also have themed cocktails for purchase, including the “Summer in Montreal” and “Russians Don’t Blush.”

Watch on Deadline

“When a series connects with audiences the way Heated Rivalry has, we look for ways to bring it to the big screen and give fans a reason to experience it together,” said Brooks LeBoeuf, SVP of U.S. content at Regal. “Nearly a year after its premiere, we’re proud to work with our partners to turn a season fans have watched again and again into a true theatrical event. It’s a chance to celebrate the story, its creators, and its performances before Season 2 arrives in 2027.”

Hana Palmer, Sphere’s executive director of global distribution and partnerships, said, “Heated Rivalry is a global phenomenon creating a rush of social media and press activity wherever it lands. We’re very excited to give audiences the opportunity to watch the drama unfold on big screens in North America, the UK, Australia and New Zealand.”

With Rachel Reid’s Game Changer novel The Long Game serving as the basis for Season 2 of Jacob Tierney’s Crave Original series adaptation, production began on the sophomore season in Canada in August.

Deadline recently reported that Justice Smith, Charlie Gillespie, Daniel Diemer, Shaheen Jafargholi, Emily Hampshire, Edvin Ryding, Robert Naylor, Sabrina Jalees, Priyanka, Brendan Morgan, David Tomlinson, Gerry Dee, Michelle Mylett, Lauren Chan and Nick Stahl have been cast in Season 2, which is set to premiere in spring 2027.

title: Investigation Discovery Buys SXSW True-Crime Doc ‘My Brother’s Killer’
summary: EXCLUSIVE: My Brother’s Killer, the true-crime documentary directed by Circus of Books’ Rachel Mason, has landed at Investigation Discovery. The film, which is exec produced by The Decline of Western Civilization director Penelope Spheeris, will debut on the Skydance-owned cable network on December 3. It comes after the doc premiered at SXSW earlier this year. […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: My Brother’s Killer, the true-crime documentary directed by Circus of Books’ Rachel Mason, has landed at Investigation Discovery.

The film, which is exec produced by The Decline of Western Civilization director Penelope Spheeris, will debut on the Skydance-owned cable network on December 3.

It comes after the doc premiered at SXSW earlier this year. It followed that up with a festival run that saw it win the Best Documentary Jury Award at the Outshine LGBTQ+ Film Festival and ahead of its launch at the AFI Fest on October 24.

After Billy Newton was found murdered on October 29, 1990, his case was forgotten by most but haunted many: from the LAPD detectives first at the scene to his family in Wisconsin, fellow adult performers and LGBQT+ community members in West Hollywood – who were left wondering: who would want to harm someone as beloved as Billy? My Brother’s Killer follows Mason as she investigates his case, partnering with the LAPD, London’s family and friends, as well as authors and podcasters Christopher Rice and Eric Shaw Quinn. The film shows how original assumptions, overlooked evidence, and new theories help find the missing puzzle pieces in order to get to the truth.

Watch on Deadline

The doc, which features personal archival footage of Newton and interviews with his friends, ultimately leads to the shocking revelation of Newton’s actual killer.

Produced by FutureClown Productions, Josh Braun, Ben Braun and James Cude also serve as exec producers, while Dion Labriola serves as producer.

“From the moment we saw Rachel Mason’s powerful film and finished processing the stunning revelations of its final moments, we knew we wanted to use our platform to bring this story to the widest possible audience. My Brother’s Killer chronicles how one man’s tragic passing inspired a decades long pursuit of the truth and in doing so delivers a deeply moving portrait of Billy Newton and the underserved community that refused to let him be forgotten,” said Jason Sarlanis, President of ID.

title: Space 11 & SK Films Bringing Artemis II To The Big Screen With ‘Return To The Moon: The Story Of Artemis II’
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Space 11 Corp. and SK Films are behind Return to the Moon: The Story of Artemis II, a new space film with Duncan Copp and Christopher Riley directing. The producers are targeting a PLF rollout for the film, which they say will combine NASA’s real Artemis II mission imagery with the voices of the […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Space 11 Corp. and SK Films are behind Return to the Moon: The Story of Artemis II, a new space film with Duncan Copp and Christopher Riley directing.

The producers are targeting a PLF rollout for the film, which they say will combine NASA’s real Artemis II mission imagery with the voices of the four astronauts who lived it. Worldwide theatrical release is targeted for summer 2027.

The synopsis reads: “Between April 1 and 11, 2026, the crew of the spacecraft Integrity traveled 695,081 miles and reached 252,756 miles from Earth, setting a new record for human spaceflight. The film follows the mission from the launch pad to splashdown in the Pacific.”

Space 11 says it is collaborating with NASA under a Space Act Agreement to shoot giant-screen interviews with the Artemis II crew: Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, Mission Specialist Christina Koch and Mission Specialist Jeremy Hansen of the Canadian Space Agency.

Watch on Deadline

The narrative will be interwoven by the four astronauts in their own words and NASA’s high-resolution photography and footage, reformatted for giant screens. A 45 minute version and a shorter format are being planned to go out via SK’s network of giant-screen and specialty theaters, including IMAX theaters, museums, science-centers, and other institutional venues. The film will also be offered to school groups.

Duncan Copp and Christopher Riley have both worked with NASA’s astronauts, engineers and scientists, past and present. Copp and Riley produced Ron Howard-presented In the Shadow of the Moon, winner of the World Cinema Documentary Audience Award at Sundance. Riley, a two-time BAFTA nominee, has worked with the Artemis II crew before, on hit immersive experience The Moonwalkers: A Journey with Tom Hanks, which he co-wrote with Hanks.

The film is produced by Andrea Iervolino (Ferrari), founder of Space 11. Producer Nicola Allieta will also participate in this production.

SK, the natural history and science content specialist, most recently released Ocean Dreams, narrated by Shailene Woodley.

Andrea Iervolino, Founder of Space 11, stated: “Artemis II belongs to everyone who looked up at the Moon in April. We are honored to tell this story in collaboration with NASA and alongside the four astronauts who took us there. Our responsibility is to make a film that everyone behind this mission, from the teams at NASA and the Canadian Space Agency to the families who waited at home, will watch with pride. With Duncan Copp and Christopher Riley, who know this crew and this history as few filmmakers do, and with SK Films, we will share that journey with audiences around the world.”

Bert Ulrich, Executive Vice President of Production at Space 11 and former NASA Film and Television Liaison, added: “In more than two decades at NASA, I learned that nothing moves people like real imagery and the voices of those who were actually there. This film is built on both: NASA’s own photography and footage, and the Artemis II crew recounting the flight themselves. On a giant screen, it is as close as most of us will ever come to flying aboard Integrity. If it inspires young people to reach for a seat on a future mission, it will have done what the best space documentaries have always done.”

“NASA’s Artemis II Mission is the perfect subject for giant screen cinema: it invites audiences to experience a historic accomplishment, with the extraordinarily personal perspective of its astronauts, on a scale unparalleled by any other cinematic experience” said Wendy MacKeigan, CEO of SK Films. “We are excited to be working with Space 11 and the brilliant creative team to bring this film to audiences around the world.”

title: The Lede Company Acquires Lauren Winslade’s London-Based Agency Aisle 8
summary: The Lede Company has acquired London-based fashion and lifestyle agency Aisle 8, Aisle 8 founder Lauren Winslade will join as President of Brand for The Lede Company London, bringing her full team of 21 into the firm. Matthew Avento will continue to oversee the Talent and Strategic Communications divisions at the firm’s London office. Founded […]
content:
The Lede Company has acquired London-based fashion and lifestyle agency Aisle 8,

Aisle 8 founder Lauren Winslade will join as President of Brand for The Lede Company London, bringing her full team of 21 into the firm. Matthew Avento will continue to oversee the Talent and Strategic Communications divisions at the firm’s London office.

Founded in 2014 and based in Farringdon, London, Aisle 8’s current roster includes MERIT, Ferrari, Astrid & Miyu, Our Place, Jigsaw, Dr Dennis Gross, Wonderskin, Bicester Village, Jo Loves, and Ruggable, and UK launch work for Away, Vuori, Kulfi, and Le Monde Gourmand.

The agency’s services include brand development, media relations, influencer and talent partnerships, social strategy, and strategic counsel across fashion, beauty, and consumer lifestyle sectors. All of these services will be absorbed into Lede’s operations.

Watch on Deadline

Winslade’s career spans two decades across agency, in-house, and global corporate roles. She began at luxury agency Aurelia PR working on Versace, Salvatore Ferragamo, and Cîroc Vodka, before moving to Ketchum and later Hill & Knowlton, where she led fashion and beauty strategy for clients including Intel and P&G. In 2007, she joined fashion e-tailer my-wardrobe.com, building the company’s global PR function across the UK, US, Australia, Scandinavia, and the Middle East. She was recruited by Harrods in 2012 to head PR & Communications, where she led a 20-person team shaping the store’s omni-channel presence. She launched Aisle 8 in 2014.

“We are so excited to add Lauren, a brilliant brand builder, and her incredible Aisle 8 team to The Lede Company London,” Christine Su, Co-CEO of The Lede Company, said in a statement. “With a rare instinct for turning brands into cultural movements, Lauren has built one of London’s most respected communications agencies. The team’s deep relationships across UK media and their expertise in everyday luxury will both help us better serve our clients and further expand our presence internationally.”

Winslade added: “When I launched Aisle 8 in 2014, I saw a gap in the market for an agency built on relationships, commercial focus and a digital-first approach to communications. A decade on, joining Lede brings the scale, talent, expertise, and ambition to take that vision even further. More than an acquisition, this is an opportunity to build something bigger for our clients and our people, and I’m thrilled to be starting this next chapter together.”

title: Skydance Nordics & Germany Boss Says “We’re Doing Our Best To Manage The Change” After Mega-Merger
summary: “We’re doing our best to manage the change but I’m not naïve.” That was the verdict of Christina Sulebakk, who runs the newly-minted Skydance’s operation in the Nordics, Germany and Benelux, over how she is approacing the $110B merger in her territories. Sulebakk, who has been with various iterations of the newly-merged group for 15 […]
content:
“We’re doing our best to manage the change but I’m not naïve.”

That was the verdict of Christina Sulebakk, who runs the newly-minted Skydance‘s operation in the Nordics, Germany and Benelux, over how she is approacing the $110B merger in her territories.

Sulebakk, who has been with various iterations of the newly-merged group for 15 years, beginning at HBO Europe, added that “the transformation feels more substantial because the entire media ecosystem is evolving simultaneously.”

Speaking at the Munich Media Days conference, Sulebakk was asked about the “elephant in the room” and considered how “some are energized by change and see it as a constant source of opportunity,” while “others naturally worry about what it means for their role, their team, their leaders, their relationships, and the future.”

Sulebakk is one of the first senior international Skydance executives to speak publicly since the merger closed earlier this month. The majority of Skydance international is being led out of L.A. by JB Perrette, although questions remain over the final shape of the non-U.S. part of David Ellison’s behemoth, including how territories may eventually get divided up.

Watch on Deadline

“We’re doing our best to manage the change, but I’m not naïve,” said Sulebakk. “I understand that change will have an impact. What may feel even more significant is that the entire industry is changing at the same time. RTL is going through change, ProSieben is going through change, and Netflix is going through change.”

She said her approach is about “being present” and communicating. “From a leadership perspective, communication is essential,” she added. “Everything starts with communication: being present, honest, and as transparent as possible. That means sharing as much as you’re allowed to share.”

“I’m not here to hold a pen and have a title”

Once bedded in, Sulebakk, who took on the German-speaking markets and Benelux territories at the old Warner Bros. Discovery at the start of 2026, stressed that she wants to be an active leader.

She pointed to the potential for partnerships with platforms like YouTube and talked up windowing possibilities on the likes of Netflix, Prime Video and Hulu.

“I’m not here to hold a pen and have a title,” she added. “I want things to change. I want to look for opportunities in the market.”

title: Fox Nation Plans to Place Promos for Chris Harrison’s ‘The Vow’ on ABC Stations
summary: Disney’s ABC might be on the lookout for an incursion Fox Nation. Promos for the new “The Vow,” an original dating series led by Chris Harrison, former host of the ABC mainstay “The Bachelor,” are slated to air in local ad inventory on several ABC stations in roughly a dozen markets, according to a person […]
content:
Disney’s ABC might be on the lookout for an incursion Fox Nation.

Promos for the new “The Vow,” an original dating series led by Chris Harrison, former host of the ABC mainstay “The Bachelor,” are slated to air in local ad inventory on several ABC stations in roughly a dozen markets, according to a person familiar with the matter. The promos would surface even though Warner Bros. Television, producer of “The Bachelor,” recently sent a cease-and-desist letter to the Fox News Media streaming service calling for it to stop making visual and creative references to “The Bachelor.”

Fox Nation will stay on the march. The new promo is expected to run in local ad inventory on ABC stations in New York City, New York City, Los Angeles, Chicago, and Dallas, this person says. Fox News declined to make executives available for comment.

Popular on Variety

“The Bachelor” has been a mainstay part of the ABC schedule for about three decades, and Harrison served as host for 25 seasons. The promos could air during primetime programs such as “Grey’s Anatomy” one of ABC’s most-watched series.

“I believe in true love,” Harrison says in the promo. “Always have.” At the end of the vignette, graphics inform viewers that the new show debuts November 11 on Fox Nation — as rose petals, a key element of “The Bachelor,” are seen on screen.

WBTV on September 18 claimed recent promos for “The Vow” represented “a plain attempt to capitalize on and ‘ride on the coattails’ of WB’s instantly recognizable intellectual property and the Franchise’s goodwill in violation of, inter alia, state and federal trademark, copyright, and unfair competition laws,” according to a copy of the cease and desist letter reviewed by Variety. “Without having seen the Series itself, we cannot comment on it and reserve all rights in connection therewith. To be clear, though, we have no objection to Fox and Lionsgate releasing a dating show hosted by Chris Harrison in and of itself. But thus far, Fox and Lionsgate have promoted the Series entirely on the back of the Franchise, not on its own merits.”

Fox Nation seemed undaunted by the effort. Your letter appears designed not to vindicate legitimate copyright and trademark interests, but to restrict FOX Nation and Chris Harrison from promoting a competing dating show. It is unfortunate that Warner Bros. is targeting Mr. Harrison in this malicious and vindictive manner,” the company said in a September 24 response.

Buying local inventory on stations is a tried-and-true method for companies to get commercials on air that might otherwise be blocked. In the world of TV promotion, it’s almost impossible to get a rival network to pick up an ad that disparages or emulates its programs. The alternative, a select few have discovered, is to purchase ad slots on local stations or cable and satellite systems and deliver the equivalent of a hard elbow to the ribs: Stop watching this and start watching us.

In 2014, the CW ran ads on the cable network once known as ABC Family telling TV viewers to stop watching “Pretty Little Liars” and turn instead to its own “The Originals.”

The technique was also used to great effect by Time Warner’s TNT in 2004. When the cable outlet was running “Without A Trace” on Mondays, it bought up ads during NBC’s “E.R.,” which just happened to air opposite the current season of “Trace” on CBS on Thursday nights. “”If you’ve been watching ‘E.R.’ on Thursday nights,” the narrator told viewers, “you’ve missed the drama critics say is…Gripping. Stylish. Addictive.” And of course, available at that exact moment on CBS as the promo blared.

Top NBC executives were barely aware the spots were running on the network’s affiliates and even some of local stations the Peacock owned. The plan that had been orchestrated in part by Steve Koonin, who at the time was exec veep and chief operating officer of TNT and its sister outlet, TBS. Once The Wall Street Journal called to ask about the presence of the spots on NBC, the network disclosed the promos were being pulled from all of its owned stations – even though they had been on the air for about four weeks.

Others have tested the method. In 2009, ABC snatched up ad inventory on various cable distributors – who usually get about two minutes per hour to sell to their own clients – on a range of cable-news outlets, including CNN and MSNBC. Between the hours of 6 a.m. and 9 a.m. – the exact time when ABC’s “Good Morning America” was on, the promos suggested viewers tune in to the “GMA” team of the time: Diane Sawyer, Robin Roberts, Chris Cuomo and Sam Champion. Alan Ives, executive creative director and executive producer at ABC News, put the plan into place.

Advertisers have also tapped the technique. The Super Bowl was once off-limits to any brewer other than Anheuser Busch InBev, which paid handsomely to ensure it would be the only malt-liquor sponsor of the event. Rrivals such as Diageo and MillerCoors hawked their wares during the broadcast of the game: In 2009, MillerCoors touted Miller High Life in one-second ads that ran on local stations across the U.S., and in 2003, Diageo ran local ads for its Smirnoff Ice during the pigskin classic.













.

title: Judge Orders Donald Trump to Testify Under Oath in $10 Billion BBC Defamation Case
summary: President Donald Trump must sit for a deposition in his defamation lawsuit filed against the BBC, the judge overseeing the case ruled. “Engaging in discovery is burdensome, but is a burden we undertake, especially if we file a lawsuit,” Magistrate Judge Enjoliqué Aytch Lett, , said at a hearing in the case Thursday, as reported […]
content:
President Donald Trump must sit for a deposition in his defamation lawsuit filed against the BBC, the judge overseeing the case ruled.

“Engaging in discovery is burdensome, but is a burden we undertake, especially if we file a lawsuit,” Magistrate Judge Enjoliqué Aytch Lett, , said at a hearing in the case Thursday, as reported by CNN.

Trump filed the lawsuit in Florida in December 2025, alleging defamation and trade practices violations after BBC program “Panorama” condensed his Jan. 6, 2021, speech to make it seem like he said: “We’re going to walk down to the Capitol… and I’ll be there with you. And we fight. We fight like hell.” He is seeking $10 billion in damages.

Popular on Variety

The BBC subsequently apologized for the error, saying the broadcast gave “the mistaken impression that President Trump made a direct call for violent action.”

A spokesman for Trump’s legal team said in a statement: “The formerly respected and now disgraced BBC defamed President Trump by intentionally, maliciously, and deceptively doctoring his speech in a brazen attempt to interfere in the 2024 Presidential Election. The BBC has a long pattern of deceiving its audience in coverage of President Trump, all in service of its own leftist political agenda. President Trump’s powerhouse lawsuit is holding the BBC accountable for its defamation and reckless election interference just as he has held other fake news mainstream media responsible for their wrongdoing.”

In a filing on Wednesday, Trump’s lawyers said that the president could appear for the interview between Jan. 11 and 22, 2027, and claimed that the BBC was “wrong to claim that President Trump is avoiding his deposition in this action.”

title: Tom Hanks Returning to Broadway After 14 Years for New Play ‘This World of Tomorrow’
summary: Tom Hanks will star in the play “This World of Tomorrow,” marking his return to Broadway for the first time in 14 years. Hanks was last on Broadway in Nora Ephron’s 2013 play “Lucky Guy,” which earned him a Tony nomination. This time, the celebrated actor will be joined by theater veteran Kelli O’Hara, who […]
content:
Tom Hanks will star in the play “This World of Tomorrow,” marking his return to Broadway for the first time in 14 years.

Hanks was last on Broadway in Nora Ephron’s 2013 play “Lucky Guy,” which earned him a Tony nomination. This time, the celebrated actor will be joined by theater veteran Kelli O’Hara, who appeared alongside him in the show’s Off Broadway run last year at the Shed.

“This World of Tomorrow” is based on a series of short stories written by Hanks. He’s co-writing the adaptation with James Glossman. Described as a “time-travel romance,” the play takes place at the end of the 21st century and follows Bert Allenberry, who is determined to change his future by returning to the past. “When Bert journeys back — again, and again, and again — to one remarkable day at the 1939 New York World’s Fair in Queens, he discovers that the future is shaped not by technology, but by the choices we make for love,” per the official logline.

Directed by Kenny Leon, whose recent Broadway credits include “The Balusters,” “Othello” with Denzel Washington and Jake Gyllenhaal, and “Our Town” with Jim Parsons and Katie Holmes, is directing the show. It will play at a Shubert theater to be announced. Complete cast and creative team details will be confirmed soon.

Popular on Variety

“I’m so excited to continue this work on this amazing new American play,” said Leon. “There’s no time like the present to further explore this story of love and time travel from Glossman and Hanks. More than anything, I look forward to even more audiences who will have the chance to witness the onstage chemistry of Kelli O’Hara and Tom Hanks.”

Adds The Shed’s artistic director Alex Poots, “A beloved actor of our times, Tom Hanks co-created and starred in ‘This World of Tomorrow’ with the illuminating Kelli O’Hara for their sold out run at The Shed. Reminding us that while the world changes, the deepest of human connections endures and the power of love can transcend any era. Now this story of second chances gets to reach an even wider audience on Broadway.”

Producer Brian Anthony Moreland described Hanks as “one of the great storytellers of our time” and called it an “incredible privilege” to bring this play to Broadway.

“There is something extraordinary about bringing a story that explores the power of love across time to a place where the magic of live theater happens every night,” Moreland said. “At its heart, ‘This World of Tomorrow’ reminds us that no matter how much the world changes, the one thing that remains timeless is our capacity to love.”

title: Sylvester Stallone Defends AI After His Pitch for a ‘Half Human, Half AI’ Movie Ignited Outrage: ‘You Get Blasted’ by Hollywood but ‘I Would Take That Risk’
summary: Sylvester Stallone is ready to embrace AI. During an interview on “The Overlap” podcast, the Oscar winner said that he received backlash for trying to get a “half human, half AI” movie off the ground but he didn’t care because “AI is here to stay.” Stallone did not mention the project, but he’s spoken previously […]
content:
Sylvester Stallone is ready to embrace AI. During an interview on “The Overlap” podcast, the Oscar winner said that he received backlash for trying to get a “half human, half AI” movie off the ground but he didn’t care because “AI is here to stay.” Stallone did not mention the project, but he’s spoken previously about a failed pitch to use AI so he could play a young Rambo on the big screen.

“I get in trouble for this [but] AI is here to stay,” Stallone said on the podcast. “I wanted to do half-human, half-AI and put it together, and of course everyone’s going nuts. I go, ‘That’s happening, guys. People are selling their images. There’s going to be 20 Elvis avatars … This is happening.’”

Popular on Variety

Stallone continued, “I would take that risk, even though you get blasted bombastically from the creative community. And their [complaints are] right! They’re right. But we can’t stop this. It’s an avalanche. It’s just out of our control. If you don’t go with it, you will be trampled by it.”

A “John Rambo” origin story movie is currently in the works with “Street Fighter” and “To All the Boys I Loved Before” actor Noah Centineo taking over the title role. Stallone is not involved in the movie but did previously try to make a young Rambo movie with himself back in the role via AI and de-aging VFX.

“Everyone thought I was crazy,” Stallone said on the “Bingeworthy” podcast last year. “AI is sophisticated enough to go through Saigon to see him at 18 years old and basically use the same image. So it isn’t as big a stretch.”

During his interview on “The Overlap,” Stallone acknowledged that AI will make it increasingly difficult for new actors to break into the industry, explaining to young performers: “You’ve just chosen the most difficult profession in the world. And it’s going to get more difficult because of AI. I know my daughter [Scarlet Rose Stallone] is an actress. I said, ‘Please get into gaming. Do something [else].’”

Watch Stallone’s full interview on The Overlap in the video below.

title: Former Eminem Employee Pleads Guilty to Stealing and Selling Unreleased Music
summary: A man who was charged with stealing and selling unreleased Eminem music that leaked to the web last year has pleaded guilty to criminal infringement of copyright. In March 2025, former Eminem employee Joseph Strange was charged with copyright infringement and interstate transportation of stolen goods after he sold the rapper’s music to individuals who […]
content:
A man who was charged with stealing and selling unreleased Eminem music that leaked to the web last year has pleaded guilty to criminal infringement of copyright.

In March 2025, former Eminem employee Joseph Strange was charged with copyright infringement and interstate transportation of stolen goods after he sold the rapper’s music to individuals who put more than 25 songs online in January. Today, the United States Department of Justice announced that the 48-year-old entered a guilty plea and will be facing a maximum of five years in prison.

“Joseph Strange abused a position of trust to unlawfully copy and sell unreleased music belonging to Eminem, profiting from works that were not yet authorized for public distribution,” said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division in a statement. “His conduct undermined both legal and artistic rights. The Criminal Division remains committed to protecting intellectual property, holding accountable those who seek to profit from theft of creative content, and working with our law enforcement partners to deter and disrupt these crimes.”

Popular on Variety

A representative for Eminem did not immediately return Variety‘s request for comment.

According to the original criminal complaint, Strange was a former sound engineer for Eminem from 2007 until 2021 who worked at a recording studio in Ferndale, Michigan, and had access to the music that leaked. Several studio employees contacted the FBI after discovering that unreleased music had hit the web in January 2025.

The FBI identified numerous individuals who purchased the music, including one named Doja Rat, who said he paid Strange $50,000 for songs. According to Doja Rat, Strange said he had over 300 songs and handwritten lyric sheets. FBI agents then searched Strange’s residence and seized hard drives that had copies of Eminem’s unreleased music.

Data provided by streaming providers showed that by November 2025, the infringing songs had been accessed more than eight million times and the amount of the files is estimated to be at least $750,000.

“Our republic is built on the right to property,” said U.S. Attorney Jerome F. Gorgon Jr. for the Eastern District of Michigan. “We will protect that right by punishing criminals who steal the physical or intellectual property of Americans.”

“Detroit has always been a city where creativity thrives, and no one has the right to steal or profit from another artist’s work without their permission,” said Special Agent in Charge Jennifer Runyan of the FBI Detroit Field Office. “Today’s guilty plea reinforces a simple principle: accountability follows those who compromise the integrity of another person’s creative labor. I want to commend the outstanding work of our FBI Oakland County Resident Agency and the entire investigative team, whose persistence and professionalism drove this case forward. We also appreciate the cooperation of Mathers Music Studio throughout the investigation. Protecting intellectual property means protecting the time, talent, and livelihoods behind it, and we will continue to treat these violations with the seriousness they deserve.”

Strange will be sentenced on January 27, 2027.

title: Neil DeGrasse Tyson, Bill Nye & Dr. Mae Jemison Join Broadway’s ‘Galileo’ Musical As Co-Producers
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Prominent members of the scientific community Neil deGrasse Tyson, Bill Nye and Dr. Mae Jemison have joined Broadway’s upcoming Galileo musical as co-producers, the show’s lead producers announced today. “Galileo’s story reminds us that scientific discovery begins with the courage to question what we think we already know,” said producers Amanda Lipitz, Henry Tisch, […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Prominent members of the scientific community Neil deGrasse Tyson, Bill Nye and Dr. Mae Jemison have joined Broadway‘s upcoming Galileo musical as co-producers, the show’s lead producers announced today.

“Galileo’s story reminds us that scientific discovery begins with the courage to question what we think we already know,” said producers Amanda Lipitz, Henry Tisch, and Jordan Roth. “What unites Dr. Mae Jemison, Bill Nye, and Neil deGrasse Tyson is not only their extraordinary passion for science, but their lifelong commitment to sharing that passion with others.

“Each,” the statement continues, “has devoted their career to making science more accessible, sparking curiosity, and inspiring millions of people to look at the world with a deeper sense of wonder. Bringing them together as co-producers creates a powerful connection between science and the arts, and we’re thrilled to have them join us in bringing this event to Broadway.”

Watch on Deadline

Tyson is the Frederick P. Rose Director of the Hayden Planetarium; Nye is the scientist, educator, and television host; and Jemison is a former NASA astronaut and the first woman of color in space.

Neil deGrasse Tyson, Bill Nye and Dr. Mae Jemison Dr. Neil deGraStarTalk/C. Picadas/Production

Galileo, starring Raúl Esparza in the title role, begins preview performances on Tuesday, November 10, at the Shubert Theatre, with an opening night set for Sunday, December 6. The musical features a book by Danny Strong and an original score by Zoe Sarnak and Michael Weiner, with direction by Michael Mayer and choreography by David Neumann.

“Galileo remains a seminal figure,” Tyson said, “not only in the history of science but in the history of civilization. A stark reminder that what is discovered to be objectively true in the universe is not always welcomed by cultural, political, or religious dogma. I am proud to be a part of this effort to bring Galileo’s story to life. Society needs it now more than ever.”

Said Jemison, “At eight years old, I talked my mother into enrolling me in dance classes while I insidiously learned everything I could about the Gemini and Apollo missions. At Stanford, I danced, choreographed, performed, made silk screen prints, all while earning a degree in chemical engineering. Taking dance classes at Alvin Ailey while earning my MD at Cornell Medical School, I realized that both science and dance were outlets for impacting the world around me…Galileo’s story is both universal and personal. This new musical showcases the science and history, while also revealing the humanity behind it.”

Nye commented, “I am excited indeed to join the Galileo musical as a co-producer. We’re bringing the passion, beauty, and joy of science to the Broadway stage. Galileo changed our understanding of our place in space as well as our fundamental grasp of our understanding of the way things move in nature. This show celebrates his spirit of inquiry, discovery, and critical thinking.”

According to the synopsis: “When luminary Galileo peers into the heavens, what he sees challenges humanity’s understanding of the world. Unwilling to deny the truth, Galileo finds himself in a fight with the most powerful institution on Earth. As his trusted confidant Maffeo Barberini ascends to power, friendship leads to betrayal, and the dreams Galileo has envisioned for himself and for his brilliant daughter Virginia Galilei begin to slip away. Belief, ambition, and love pull the trio out of orbit, each confronting what they’re willing to sacrifice for what matters most.”

In addition to Esparza, the principal cast includes Jeremy Kushnier, Joy Woods, Bradley Dean, Jordon Lee Garcia, and Javier Muñoz. Michael Park will alternate as Galileo at certain performances.

title: Tom Hanks & Kelli O’Hara Heading To Broadway Next Fall In ‘This World Of Tomorrow’
summary: Tom Hanks and Kelli O’Hara are Broadway-bound in a Fall 2027 production of This World of Tomorrow, a new play written by Hanks and James Glossman. The strictly limited engagement will be directed by Tony Award winner Kenny Leon at a Shubert theater to be announced. The announcement was made today by producer Brian Anthony […]
content:
Tom Hanks and Kelli O’Hara are Broadway-bound in a Fall 2027 production of This World of Tomorrow, a new play written by Hanks and James Glossman.

The strictly limited engagement will be directed by Tony Award winner Kenny Leon at a Shubert theater to be announced.

The announcement was made today by producer Brian Anthony Moreland in association with The Shed (Alex Poots, Artistic Director and Meredith “Max” Hodges, Chief Executive Officer). The play debuted at The Shed Off Broadway for a a sold-out eight week engagement last year.

This World of Tomorrow is based on a series of short stories written by Hanks. The upcoming engagement will mark Hanks’ return to the Broadway stage after more than 14 years, when he gave a Tony-nominated performance in Nora Ephron’s play Lucky Guy.

Watch on Deadline

The synopsis: “It’s the end of the 21st century and Bert Allenberry is determined to change his future by returning to the past. When Bert journeys back—again, and again, and again—to one remarkable day at the 1939 New York World’s Fair in Queens, he discovers that the future is shaped not by technology, but by the choices we make for love.”

In a statement, director Leon said, “I’m so excited to continue this work on this amazing new American play. There’s no time like the present to further explore this story of love and time travel from Glossman and Hanks. More than anything, I look forward to even more audiences who will have the chance to witness the onstage chemistry of Kelli O’Hara and Tom Hanks.”

Added Alex Poots, The Shed’s Artistic Director, “A beloved actor of our times, Tom Hanks co-created and starred in This World of Tomorrow with the illuminating Kelli O’Hara for their sold out run at The Shed. Reminding us that while the world changes, the deepest of human connections endures and the power of love can transcend any era. Now this story of second chances gets to reach an even wider audience on Broadway.”

“There is something extraordinary about bringing a story that explores the power of love across time to a place where the magic of live theater happens every night,” said producer Moreland. “Tom Hanks is one of the great storytellers of our time, and for me to bring his remarkable new play to Broadway, and to reunite with Kenny Leon (Othello) is an incredible privilege. At its heart, This World of Tomorrow reminds us that no matter how much the world changes, the one thing that remains timeless is our capacity to love.”

Complete cast and creative team details will be announced shortly.

title: Mayor Zohran Mamdani & Neon Partner On Free ‘Once Upon A Time In Harlem’ Screenings Across NYC
summary: Neon has partnered with Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s office to host four free screenings of Once Upon a Time in Harlem across New York City this October. The screenings will happen on Saturday, October 24, and Sunday, October 25, at AMC Magic Johnson Harlem, Film Forum, and Film at Lincoln Center. See the full screening schedule […]
content:
Neon has partnered with Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s office to host four free screenings of Once Upon a Time in Harlem across New York City this October.

The screenings will happen on Saturday, October 24, and Sunday, October 25, at AMC Magic Johnson Harlem, Film Forum, and Film at Lincoln Center. See the full screening schedule below. You can RSVP for the screenings here.

SCREENING SCHEDULE:

Saturday, October 24

Watch on Deadline

— 1:00 PM at AMC Magic Johnson Harlem, 2309 Frederick Douglass Blvd, New York, NY 10027

— 4:45 PM at Film Forum, 209 W Houston St, New York, NY 10014

Sunday, October 25

— 1:00 PM at AMC Magic Johnson Harlem, 2309 Frederick Douglass Blvd, New York, NY 10027

— 3:45 PM at Howard Gilman Theater, Film at Lincoln Center, 144 W 65th St, New York, NY 10023

“Once Upon a Time in Harlem brings the personalities, ideas, and debates behind the Harlem Renaissance to life for a new generation of New Yorkers,” Mayor Mamdani said of the film in a statement.

“We are proud to partner with the filmmaking team to offer free screenings to New Yorkers this weekend, ensuring that as many New Yorkers as possible get the chance to experience this film. Our city owes a debt of gratitude to the artists of the Harlem Renaissance whose enduring legacy is still felt in every jazz club, in every gallery, and in the movement for social justice that still continues to this day.”

The only film this year to screen at the Sundance, Cannes, Telluride, Toronto, and New York Film Festivals, Once Upon a Time in Harlem is nominated for five Critics Choice Documentary Awards, including Best Documentary. The film won the 2026 Library of Congress Lavine / Ken Burns Film Prize and the Maysles Film Center Albie Award.

Inventive in form, the film was conceived and filmed in 1972 by the late William Greaves. The film is shaped around a cocktail party Greaves hosted at Duke Ellington’s home in Harlem. Greaves invited every surviving creator of the Harlem Renaissance he could locate – many of whom had not seen one another in more than 50 years. For four hours, the group of artists laughed, drank, and debated their position in the rapidly shifting cultural landscape. Greaves filmed it all.

The footage was originally shot for a film about the Harlem Renaissance called From These Roots, which Greaves completed in 1974 using only archival materials. The interviews and discussions from the party were put to the side. However, Greaves, who went on to become a major figure of American independent cinema, completing over 70 films, including the now-seminal Symbiopsychotaxiplasm films, believed Once Upon a Time in Harlem was his greatest work. He spent much of the rest of his life wrestling with how to finish the film. He died in 2014, with the film incomplete. His widow, Louise Greaves, continued working on the project until she died in 2023, at which point his son, David Greaves, and David’s daughter, Liani Greaves, picked up the mantle. Film producer Anne de Mare oversaw the restoration and digitization of the footage used in the doc. We spoke with the team behind the film ahead of their world premiere at Sundance.

Neon picked up the film following the screening at Sundance, beating out Netflix and Mubi. The film was released earlier this month, in time for William Greaves’ centenary.

title: Trump Ordered By Judge To Sit For Deposition In $10B Lawsuit Against The BBC
summary: Donald Trump has been ordered by a judge to sit for a deposition by December as part of his $10 billion lawsuit against the BBC. Trump sued the BBC for defamation in December over a Panorama documentary that misleadingly edited his speech before the January 6 attack on the Capitol. The BBC has been attempting […]
content:
Donald Trump has been ordered by a judge to sit for a deposition by December as part of his $10 billion lawsuit against the BBC.

Trump sued the BBC for defamation in December over a Panorama documentary that misleadingly edited his speech before the January 6 attack on the Capitol.

The BBC has been attempting to depose the U.S. president and has wanted to set a new date after Trump postponed his October 16 testimony, citing “matters of national importance” while he was campaigning in Georgia.

U.S. Magistrate Judge Enjoliqué Lett has now said Trump must sit for the deposition by December 11 unless the discovery period is extended, per reports. The judge reportedly threatened sanctions, including dismissing the case, if Trump’s team does not comply.

Watch on Deadline

Trump claims that the Panorama documentary — which was produced by October Films and spliced together two parts of Trump’s Capitol riots speech — was streamed on iPlayer by “hundreds of individuals” using a VPN in the U.S., despite it being geoblocked in America. His lawyers have accused the BBC of a “brazen” attempt to interfere in the 2024 U.S. election, which the corporation denies.

In the fallout from edited speech, BBC director general Tim Davie and Deborah Turness, who led the news division, stepped down. The BBC apologized, calling it an “error of judgment,” but they did not offer to pay any damages.

title: Stage 32 Launches Marketplace To Combat AI Slop
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Script platform Stage 32 has launched an official marketplace to partly help combat an influx of AI-written projects. The Stage 32 Marketplace, which launched yesterday, allows executives to discover film and TV projects that have been fully vetted via an “evaluation process” conducted by humans. Only scripts submitted across Stage 32’s 15-year existence with […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Script platform Stage 32 has launched an official marketplace to partly help combat an influx of AI-written projects.

The Stage 32 Marketplace, which launched yesterday, allows executives to discover film and TV projects that have been fully vetted via an “evaluation process” conducted by humans. Only scripts submitted across Stage 32’s 15-year existence with “exceptional valuations” will appear on the markteplace and execs can then review each project’s credentials and download scripts and materials, while requesting meetings with the creators.

Since 2011 launch, Stage 32 has evaluated 235,000 projects, it said. The marketplace kickstarts with more than 4,000 and access for 3,000 industry execs.

Recent projects to have started life on Stage 32 include Jeffrey Dean Morgan and Jack Quaid thriller Neighborhood Watch and No Address starrring William Baldwin.

Watch on Deadline

Richard Botto, who runs Stage 32, said the platform has a strict no AI policy and is using the marketplace as one way to combat AI slop.

“There’s no shortage of great material being written, but producers and executives simply don’t have the time or resources to evaluate everything that’s out there,” said Botto, a WGA screenwriter, producer of the Sundance award-winning Another Happy Day.

“As a writer and producer myself, I saw this challenge from both sides. I built Stage 32 to bring the industry closer together, and the Marketplace is the culmination of that vision.”

title: John Mayer Sets Up His Own Label, Sob Rock Records, in Partnership With Mercury to Release First New Solo Music in Five Years
summary: John Mayer has had his hands full with what felt like a hundred projects over the past few years — with putting out new music not among them. It takes a stretch of the memory to even recall that he announced a parting of ways with Sony Music back in 2022, with no followup revelation […]
content:
John Mayer has had his hands full with what felt like a hundred projects over the past few years — with putting out new music not among them. It takes a stretch of the memory to even recall that he announced a parting of ways with Sony Music back in 2022, with no followup revelation about where, if anywhere, he planned to go next . Now, after hinting at the beginning of this year that new studio recordings were afoot, he’s finally publicly kicking the recording artist part of his career back into gear.

Mayer and associates announced Thursday that he has started up his own label, Sob Rock Records — which shares the name of the last album he put out for Sony, 2021’s “Sob Rock” — to be operated in partnership with Universal Music’s Mercury Records. No album has yet been announced, but his first single in five years, “Tom and Jerry,” is arriving under his new shingle Friday.

Popular on Variety

“Working with Tyler Arnold and the talented team at Mercury Records has already proven to be a great partnership,” Mayer said in a statement. “The path from creative vision to execution has never been easier or more rewarding. I feel very inspired, and I’m excited for what’s to come.”

“John Mayer is one of the greatest artists of all time,” said Arnold, Mercury’s chairman-CEO,

and I couldn’t be prouder to welcome him to Mercury Records. We’re excited to be part of his next chapter and to partner with his label, Sob Rock Records, to help bring his creative vision to life.”
