He said he was probably the first, if not the only, Hong Kong filmmaker to make a non-action film inside the U.S. studio system.

“Had I gone to America or Hollywood with the knowledge that I have of film and marketing and dealing with corporate, I probably would have fared better,” Chan said. “I was too young then, too naive.”

Asked later by an audience member how he navigates censorship in mainland China, Chan said: “Dealing with a corporate is very, very difficult. And if I can survive that, I can survive anything.” He added that limitations of budget, stars, studios or censorship tend to push filmmakers to be more creative.

After Hollywood, Chan set up Applause Pictures, a pan-Asian venture that made 10 films in two and a half years, most of them horror. Its output included “The Eye” franchise and the “Three” horror omnibus films, which brought together directors including Park Chan-wook, Miike Takashi, Kim Jee-woon and Fruit Chan. He also executive produced “One Fine Spring Day” for Korean director Hur Jin-ho – director of SGIFF opener “The Assassin(s)” – whose debut “Christmas in August” he loved. But a planned three-part love story with Hur and Japan’s Iwai Shunji found no investors.

“If we continue this pan-Asian effort, I’m going to be stuck with making horror films my whole life,” Chan said of the decision to move on to mainland China, where his first film was the 2005 musical “Perhaps Love.”

An aspiring screenwriter in the audience asked how he handles a scene that isn’t landing. “I don’t usually fix it for them. I make them fix it over and over and over and over again,” Chan said, adding that after saying “great” to everything at home, he doesn’t do the same with his writers.

He credited nine writers on “The Warlords,” and said screenwriters joke that his films’ writers would not fit in a minibus. “I milk the writer to death, and then I milk another writer,” he said. “So the writers’ community really don’t like me very much. But making movies is not about being well-liked.”

Though he is often seen as a genre-hopper, Chan said the same concerns run through his work, citing the love triangles in his debut “Alan & Eric: Between Hello and Goodbye,” “Comrades,” “Perhaps Love” and even “The Warlords,” which he called a love triangle between three brothers.

“Making every movie is answering some sort of life questions that I have at that stage, in point of my life,” he said. “So in a way, I’ve been making the same movie in my mind in the last 36 years.”

title: ‘Ebenezer’ Creates a Real Venmo Profile for Scrooge, Which Hands Out Money and Accepts It, Too
summary: The surly miser Ebenezer Scrooge is no longer just a fictional character haunting the holidays — he’s on Venmo. To promote Ti West’s upcoming adaptation of the notorious character in the film “Ebenezer,” starring Johnny Depp in the titular role, the Paramount promotional team created a Venmo account for Ebenezer Scrooge. The official account for […]
content:
The surly miser Ebenezer Scrooge is no longer just a fictional character haunting the holidays — he’s on Venmo.

To promote Ti West’s upcoming adaptation of the notorious character in the film “Ebenezer,” starring Johnny Depp in the titular role, the Paramount promotional team created a Venmo account for Ebenezer Scrooge. The official account for the film announced the news on X, writing, “Ebenezer Scrooge is now on @venmo. Think he’s feeling generous? 💰 Send a request: https://venmo.com/u/EBENEZERmovie” accompanied by a video of people making requests for various amounts of money and Scrooge’s stingy payouts. Despite the request, Ebenezer’s response is always the same, giving just a penny in return.

An error message reading, “We’re sorry the transaction could not be completed. Please contact the person you’re trying to pay” appeared when two Variety staffers tried to request some money. A source close to promotion confirmed that the Venmo has been working — it just grew so popular with requests that it temporarily caused a jam in the system and is being fixed.

Popular on Variety

Although Scrooge’s Venmo is dishing out money, he also appears to be accepting it. The public feed of his account is filled with payments made out to him. “For cheers and joy! (And maybe a little luck please)” one benefactor wrote. Another wrote, “$ Retainer Fee — for the Ghost of Christmas Past to haunt my exes with a little bah humbug spirit.” Several others paid Scrooge to boost his Christmas spirit.

It is unclear where this sent money will actually end up.

Paramount Pictures’ “Ebenezer” will hit theaters on Nov. 13. The official logline reads: “The name you know, the story you don’t.” Judging from the trailer, West — known for directing the horror trilogy “X” — is zooming in on the darker aspects of Charles Dickens’ beloved story, showing Depp’s character being haunted by some seriously scary ghosts and getting buried alive.

Depp stars alongside Rupert Grint, Andrea Riseborough, Sam Claflin, Daisy Ridley, Arthur Conti, Ellie Bamber, Henry Lloyd-Hughes, Charlie Murphy, Tramell Tillman and Ian McKellen. Based on “A Christmas Carol” by Charles Dickens, Nathaniel Halpern adapted the screenplay.

“Ebenezer” marks Depp’s return home to Hollywood for the holidays as his first major movie since his highly publicized 2022 trial against ex-wife Amber Heard. Both Depp and Heard accused the other of domestic abuse and defamation during their relationship, with Depp ultimately awarded $10 million in compensatory damages and $5 million in punitive damages from Heard, while Heard was awarded $2 million in compensatory damages. His last major Hollywood studio film was “Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald” in 2018.

title: ‘Clayface’ Cashing In $3.5M+ Thursday Previews – Box Office
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Peter Safran and James Gunn’s DC entree into lower budget genre movies, Clayface, is off to a solid start in previews tonight with an estimated $3.5M, if not more. Domestic weekend forecasts are between $20M-$25M, which if that occurs, would deliver the newly combined Paramount-Warner Bros its second back-to-back No. 1 opener at the […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Peter Safran and James Gunn’s DC entree into lower budget genre movies, Clayface, is off to a solid start in previews tonight with an estimated $3.5M, if not more.

Domestic weekend forecasts are between $20M-$25M, which if that occurs, would deliver the newly combined Paramount-Warner Bros its second back-to-back No. 1 opener at the box office after last weekend’s Street Fighter ($31M).

Previews started at 2PM today for the James Watkins directed Clayface which though based on the Batman villain, is a standalone story about baby face Hollywood actor Matt Hagen, who in reaching for the stars, falls short, kisses the wrong girl at the party, and –oops– there goes his face. The screenplay by Mike Flanagan in December 2024 got Gunn and Safran excited, and it was off to the races to make this movie which is coming in at a net production cost of $44M before P&A, shot in the UK.

In regards to preview comps, Clayface‘s money is higher than the R-rated Sony/Marvel movie Kraven the Hunter ($2M previews, $11M dismal opening), and not far from the pre-Covid PG-13 DC spinoff Birds of Prey ($4M previews, $33M opening). Next to horror films, Clayface‘s cash is similar to Blumhouse Atomic Monster’s Other Mommy ($3.6M previews, $27.8M opening) and ahead of 2022’s Smile ($2M previews, $22.6M opening). How about this? Clayface‘s previews are higher than Digger‘s $1.2M ($8M opening). Mic drop.

Watch on Deadline

The hope is that the DC movie isn’t front loaded tonight, as all eyes are on the potential hold of A24 documentary You Can See Everything following its great midweek business and fantastic $15.6M opening last weekend. That Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim co-directed documentary about Theranos architect Elizabeth Holmes expands to 2,600 locations tomorrow after bowing in 855 sites.

Clayface glides into the weekend with a 76% certified fresh Rotten Tomatoes critics score which is higher than The Flash (63%), Supergirl (52% Rotten), Joker Folie a Deux (31%), Shazam Fury of the Gods (49%), James Wan’s Aquaman and the Lost Kingdom (33%), and almost as good as Birds of Prey (79% certified fresh).

‘V for Vendetta’ Warner Bros. Pictures

Note this isn’t the first time in DC movie history that they’ve ventured into low-to-mid-sized budget fare. In the early aughts, there was DC/Vertigo’s The Losers in 2010 which cost $25M before P&A and opened to $9.4M and finaled at $23.5M domestic. There was also the Josh Brolin-Megan Fox starring 2010 fantasy western Jonah Hex which bombed with a $5.3M opening, $10.5M stateside final next to its $47M production cost. And there was the R-rated Wachowski sisters adapted and produced 2005 feature take of the DC Vertigo title, V for Vendetta, which yielded a No. 1 $25.6M North American opening off a $50M production cost, and a finaled domestic take of $70.5M, and $134.7M global.

We’re hearing that previews for the Fathom release of Laika’s stop-motion animated title Wildwood is around $1M. The hope is that the Travis Knight directed movie can break double digits in its opening. The 100% certified fresh critical score and 98% with audiences on RT will certainly help.

We’ll have more preview grosses in the AM.

Tonight’s numbers are per distribution sources.

title: ‘The Imaginary Invalid’ Broadway Review: Molière Gets Clowned By A Winning Bill Irwin
summary: The La-Z-Boy-style brown leather recliner that’s a focal point of Bill Irwin’s The Imaginary Invalid opening tonight on Broadway doesn’t really mesh with the eye-popping 17th Century French frills and finery that suggest a stage invasion of brilliantly plumed vainglorious peacocks, but no matter. Irwin knows how to clown an audience, and in this enjoyable, […]
content:
The La-Z-Boy-style brown leather recliner that’s a focal point of Bill Irwin‘s The Imaginary Invalid opening tonight on Broadway doesn’t really mesh with the eye-popping 17th Century French frills and finery that suggest a stage invasion of brilliantly plumed vainglorious peacocks, but no matter. Irwin knows how to clown an audience, and in this enjoyable, broadly comic interpretation, the buffoonery is at least as much the point as some pointed critiques of modern-day American health care.

Styles that might butt heads in most contexts fall loonily into place in Irwin’s puckish universe, a place wherein characters can seem possessed by the slapstick-happy ghosts of dead vaudevillians one moment and recite the pointed social commentary of truth-telling jesters the next. Does it always work? More than you’d have a right to expect.



Bill Irwin, Bill Irwin, Dylan Baker , Rachel Bloom, Ava Lalezarzadeh, Daniel Croix Henderson Joan Marcus

In adapting Molière’s 1673 three-act comédie-ballet for Broadway’s Roundabout Theatre Company, Irwin, forever carrying the banner of the clowning style on which he is an expert – think Pierrot crossed with Harold Lloyd – cuts the ballet dance-and-musical parts (more or less, but no spoilers here) in favor of a pared down, fast-moving, 90-minute sketch filled with gorgeous, color-coded costumes from Karen Perry and an acting approach from all concerned that’s every bit as loud as those Louis XIV get-ups.

Watch on Deadline

At its frequent best (and as directed by Brandon J. Dirden), this take is lots of fun. The plot, though streamlined, is accented with some verbal modernisms in keeping with that reclining easy chair, as if slipped in to keep things askew.

Irwin plays Argan, a wealthy hypochondriacal aristocrat (attired like some Frenchified, night-capped Ebenezer Scrooge) who spends his days worried about his latest imagined illness and summoning his servants, doctors, wife, daughter and brother to his side mostly to help him indulge in his health obsession.

Those folks, of course, have lives and concerns of their own. Wife Béline (Crystal A. Dickinson) mostly wants hubby to really get sick and die already so she can inherit the fortune. Brother Béralde (Dylan Baker) just wants Argan to face reality and schemes to get it done. Daughter Angélique (Ava Lalezarzadeh) only has eyes and attention for her handsome new beloved Cleante (Daniel Croix Henderson) and needs to figure out a way to convince her stubborn dad that the beau is her perfect match and so what if he’s not a doctor.

Servant Toinette (Rachel Bloom) is more than happy to assist Angélique in any way possible, in part because she knows true love when she sees it but more likely because she enjoys getting one over on the demanding old fool who employs her. There are accommodating doctors (the wonderful Brooks Ashmanskas), forever ready with the cure-all enemas upon which Argan insists, and a goofy doctor’s son (Hiram Delgado) who Argan wants for a son-in-law.

Farce, as you might expect, ensues, with various plots and plans and motivations slamming into one another as the brilliantly attired cast comes and goes and swirls around the sedentary Argan. Beowulf Boritt’s 17th Century great room is as lovely as it is efficient, with panels and doors providing easy access in and out of the action for the ever-busy characters. (Their comings and goings are easy to keep track of, thanks to the color-coded costumes – each character is assigned a dominant color scheme, so much so that brother Béralde is once referred to as “the green man.”)

No need to point out that complications get ever more complicated, that it’ll all work out in the end and that this fine cast knows just how to maneuver the farce and deliver the bons mots. Bloom, as the jester-like truth-teller, is a stand-out, pointedly delivering her lines with a modern-sounding ease rather than the amusing Mid-Atlantic upper crusty thespianism the posher characters utilize.



Crystal A. Dickinson, Bill Irwin, Rachel Bloom

But Irwin, of course, is the draw here. Even the most clown-phobic among us – and, yes, a little panto can indeed go a long way – might be won over anytime this rubber-limbed, clay-faced sui generis performer enters a room. This, after all, is a man who can upstage even while all-but-permanently seated on an otherwise motion-filled stage. When he was last on Broadway in the brilliant Eureka Day, Irwin proved that he could convincingly inhabit a normal human absent as any trace of the harlequin, but no such restrictions are required for The Imaginary Invalid.

Indeed, the man who once held his own against both Robin Williams and Steve Martin in an Off Broadway production of Waiting For Godot gets free reign to clown around here, especially in a lovely moment that closes the show. That La-Z-Boy doesn’t stand a chance.

Title: The Imaginary Invalid

Venue: Broadway’s Todd Haines Theatre

Written By: Molière, adapted by Bill Irwin from a translation by Doug Skinner

Directed By: Brandon J. Dirden

Cast: Bill Irwin, Brooks Ashmanskas, Dylan Baker, Rachel Bloom, Hiram Delgado, Crystal A. Dickinson, Daniel Croix Henderson, Ava Lalezarzadeh

Running Time: 1 hr 30 min (no intermission)

title: ‘Nobody Wants This’ Creator Erin Foster Responds To Adam Brody’s “Free Palestine” Comments: “It’s Complicated”
summary: As Nobody Wants This returns to Netflix for Season 3, Erin Foster has addressed Adam Brody’s recent comments on the Israel-Hamas conflict. The series creator recently explained that although she does “disagree” with the star of her 6x Golden Globe-nominated romantic-comedy, Brody is “entitled to a different opinion” from hers, following his “Free Palestine” comments. […]
content:
As Nobody Wants This returns to Netflix for Season 3, Erin Foster has addressed Adam Brody‘s recent comments on the Israel-Hamas conflict.

The series creator recently explained that although she does “disagree” with the star of her 6x Golden Globe-nominated romantic-comedy, Brody is “entitled to a different opinion” from hers, following his “Free Palestine” comments.

“You know, it’s complicated. I think our work environment, our set is very similar to dinner tables around the world where people are having debate and discussion and disagreeing,” she explained on an upcoming episode of the Not Skinny But Not Fat podcast. “While I love Adam, I also disagree with him. And that’s okay.”

Foster added, “I think that as the creator of the show, all I can say is that I want our Jewish fans to know that I see you and I hear you and I understand how you feel. And the show has always been and always will be a love letter to Judaism. That is why I made this show. It’s because of how beautiful of an experience I’ve had becoming Jewish and being a Jewish person, and sitting here right now at this time in the world where there is almost zero positive representation of Jewish people, I think it’s so important to have that.”

Watch on Deadline

“That being said, everyone is entitled to a different opinion than me. I can just tell you what I created this show for, what the intention of the show is,” said Foster, who also makes a guest appearance in Season 3, now available to stream.

In Nobody Wants This, inspired by Foster’s relationship with her music exec husband Simon Tikhman, agnostic podcaster Joanne Williams (Kristen Bell) begins an unexpected romance with Rabbi Noah Roklov (Brody), which shakes both their families as Joanne immerses herself in Noah’s culture and decides to convert to Judaism.

Last month, Brody told GQ, “Put me down as thinking it’s a genocide. Put me down as wanting a free Palestine. It’s awful that it’s taken so much death and misery, but it does feel like it’s reaching a breaking point that it should have a while ago. I’m hopeful that another administration can really do some good and correct some of these policies that are helping that situation be as awful as it is.”

The show’s Season 1 rabbi consultant subsequently called Brody an “ignorant Jew” for referring to the situation in Gaza as a genocide, calling his words “truly shocking.”

Since Israel’s ongoing strikes on Gaza in the wake of Hamas’ Oct. 7, 2023 attack, multiple organizations have classified Israel’s actions as a genocide against Palestinians, including the United Nations, Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch.

title: Joe Perry Bows Out Of Tonight’s Hollywood Vampires’ Flick West Coast Debut As Aerosmith Ramps Up For Hollywood Bowl Gigs
summary: If you were planning on catching the West Coast debut of the Hollywood Vampires’ documentary tonight at the Newport Beach Film Festival, be warned Joe Perry will not be in the sold out Lido Theater. While info for the 8 pm PT showing of the Daniel E. Catullo III helmed Unleashed Spirits: The Rise of […]
content:
If you were planning on catching the West Coast debut of the Hollywood Vampires‘ documentary tonight at the Newport Beach Film Festival, be warned Joe Perry will not be in the sold out Lido Theater.

While info for the 8 pm PT showing of the Daniel E. Catullo III helmed Unleashed Spirits: The Rise of the Hollywood Vampires promises a “Live Q&A following the screening with Director Daniel E. Catullo III and members of the Hollywood Vampires!” the Aerosmith guitarist and Vampires co-founder announced Thursday afternoon he can’t make it after all.

“For anyone that may be planning to attend the West Coast premiere of the Hollywood Vampires docufilm Unleashed Spirits: The Rise of the Hollywood Vampires at the Newport Film Festival, I’m sorry to say that with Aerosmith performing together for the first time in three years, and rehearsing diligently for our two upcoming shows at the Hollywood Bowl, it’s become clear that I won’t be able to break away to attend personally,” Perry posted on his social feeds.

Disappoint for fans who hoped WME repped Perry would be there like he was for the flick’s Boston world premiere on September 18, but you can’t deny the 76-year old Rock’n’Roll Hall of Famer has been busy. Perry and HV bandmates Alice Cooper, Johnny Depp and Tommy Henriksen are just off a two-month European tour, and have a new-ish live album of rock classics.

Watch on Deadline

Add to that Perry plus self-styled fellow “Toxic Twin” Stephen Tyler and the rest of Aerosmith unveiled earlier this month they were truly back in the saddle for a two-night stint at the iconic Hollywood Bowl.

Book ending Halloween, the October 29 and November 1 Live Nation promoted shows will see the band joined by likes of Guns’n’Roses Slash and Duff McKagan (the latter a former HV touring member), the living members of Run DMC, Billy Idol, the Black Crowes, Alice in Chains’ Jerry Cantrell, Heart, Eric Church and more diving into the Boston Bad Boys’ five decade deep catalog.

No word if Aerosmith are planning to go on a tour of their own afterwards, or take up another Vegas residency as they did in 2019- 2022.

The Hollywood Vampires were originally formed in the 1970s as a drinking gang for Cooper, The Monkees Micky Dolenz John Lennon, The Who’s Keith Moon, and Harry Nilsson. With Cooper off the booze years ago and Lennon, Moon and Nilsson no longer with us, the latest version of the Vampires came together in 2012 by the OG shock rocker, Perry and Depp. Since their 2015 live debut on the Sunset Strip, the band has toured regularly with guitarists Depp and Perry relieving Cooper on lead vocals for a couple of Bowie and Johnny Thunders’ tunes every show.

title: Sacha Baron Cohen Says Marvel’s ‘Ironheart’ Producers Wanted To Ensure He Was “Not Insulted” Playing Devil As Jewish Actor
summary: With his recent addition to the MCU, Sacha Baron Cohen is praising the Ironheart production team for taking his Jewish identity into account. The 3x Oscar nominee recently recalled that the producers and directors on the Disney+ series wanted to ensure that he was “not insulted” as a Jewish actor being asked to portray Mephisto, […]
content:
With his recent addition to the MCU, Sacha Baron Cohen is praising the Ironheart production team for taking his Jewish identity into account.

The 3x Oscar nominee recently recalled that the producers and directors on the Disney+ series wanted to ensure that he was “not insulted” as a Jewish actor being asked to portray Mephisto, a demon character often likened to the devil.

“It was a wonderful meeting when I was offered it,” he explained during a Happy Sad Confused live podcast taping. “It was primarily, I think, an almost entirely Black producing and directing team. And they said, ‘We want to offer you Mephisto, but we are aware of the negative association of Jews historically with the devil, and we want to make sure that you’re not insulted by us offering this.’ It was such an amazingly considerate, empathetic thing to say. And I was like, ‘Yeah, I’m good.'”

Cohen added, “I think for the Jews out there, sometimes we don’t feel seen. We don’t feel like people can empathize with us, that we are suffering too. And so to have this entirely Black producing and directing team be so empathetic, was a moment of being seen. It was an amazing experience.”

Watch on Deadline

Last year, Cohen’s Mephisto was revealed in the Season 1 finale of Ironheart, having offered Parker (Anthony Ramos) his hooded cloak to help him achieve his desires

title: Prince William Declares His Love for Christopher Nolan Movies and ‘The Traitors’ in Surprise Appearance on ‘The Graham Norton Show’
summary: Prince William has made a surprise appearance on Graham Norton’s sofa, where he admits he’s a “big fan” of director Christopher Nolan and gameshow “The Traitors.” The episode, which was recorded on Thursday and will air in the U.K. on Friday, sees His Royal Highness the Prince of Wales (to give him his full title) […]
content:
Prince William has made a surprise appearance on Graham Norton’s sofa, where he admits he’s a “big fan” of director Christopher Nolan and gameshow “The Traitors.”

The episode, which was recorded on Thursday and will air in the U.K. on Friday, sees His Royal Highness the Prince of Wales (to give him his full title) grace the famous red sofa alongside Cate Blanchett, Hannah Waddingham and conservationist Robert Irwin.

All Norton’s guests this week are involved in the Earthshot Prize, which William spearheads.

Popular on Variety

Jorja Smith also appeared on the show, performing live before joining the other guests on the sofa.

During his appearance, the British royal told Norton he switches off with “music and film.”

“I love getting immersed in deep-thinking films,” William told the talk-show host. “I like action films too, but I like something a bit different. I’m a big fan of everything Christopher Nolan does. His films are fantastic – ‘The Dark Knight’ series is psychologically dark and deep and I absolutely love that. He takes concepts that are completely out there and makes them incredibly entertaining.”

William also revealed he watches “The Traitors” with his two youngest children, Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis. “I love it, the family love it. Charlotte and Louis are obsessed with it. It’s really good telly,” he said. “I saw [‘Celebrity Traitors’ contestant] Ross Kemp the day after the first episode and I couldn’t help but try – in the most appropriate way – to touch him to see what reaction I got from him. Turns out he was really jumpy!”

Asked if he ever fantasised about having any other job William said: “I did want to be a policeman when I was younger, I thought I could make a good one. And then I went through a phase of wanting to be a DJ – I wasn’t very good.”

As well as sharing some insight into the Earthshot Prize and his family life, William helped act as a judge for audience members who came up to the stage to tell their funniest stories.

title: Kore-eda Hirokazu Ditched AI Notes on His ‘Sheep in the Box’ Script: ‘I’d Like to Stand on the Human Side’
summary: Kore-eda Hirokazu ran the screenplay for his AI-themed Cannes title “Sheep in the Box” past a generative AI chatbot, then cut it loose after concluding that notes from something with no personal history with cinema were of no use to him. Kore-eda, who is receiving the Cinema Honorary Award at the Singapore International Film Festival, […]
content:
Kore-eda Hirokazu ran the screenplay for his AI-themed Cannes title “Sheep in the Box” past a generative AI chatbot, then cut it loose after concluding that notes from something with no personal history with cinema were of no use to him.

Kore-eda, who is receiving the Cinema Honorary Award at the Singapore International Film Festival, says he shared the script with the chatbot because of the film’s subject matter and went back and forth with it several times. He nicknamed it “Chat-kun.”

Set in the near future, “Sheep in the Box,” which debuted at Cannes, follows a couple whose 7-year-old son died two years earlier and take in a humanoid robot built from his data. Ayase Haruka plays Otone, an architect who throws herself into caring for the robot, while comedian Yamamoto Daigo, in his first lead role, plays her husband Kensuke, who insists it is only a machine.

Popular on Variety

“It praised me a lot. Lots of praise, and then something like, ‘However, if you fleshed out the protagonist’s mother a little more, it would be a better film.’ What it said was correct,” Kore-eda tells Variety. “But it only ever says correct things. And I wondered what it was that made this so boring.”

Plenty of films are already being made by following that kind of advice, he says, pointing to action movies where a fight on the roof of a train arrives exactly when you expect it. “Situations all start to look alike: ‘They’ll go into a tunnel here,’” he says. “There are lots of films now that make you think there’s some computer serving as the model.”

His conclusion was that the chatbot has probably never lived a life that needed cinema. It may hold more film data than any ordinary viewer, he says, but it has no film that changed its life and no personal film history — not even the experience of getting hooked on something trashy before slowly learning what makes a movie good.

“However few films a person has seen, however skewed their taste, the opinion of someone who has a film that changed their life will lead to more interesting work in the end,” Kore-eda says. “After a few rounds I became convinced of that, so I ended our relationship there.”

He did not use AI on the film. The question of what humans “should” do in filmmaking is the wrong one, he says. Robots may one day outrun people, yet the Olympic 100 meter races will still be held and audiences will still be moved.

“That’s not because we should. It’s because it’s fun,” he says. “In the same way, the act of making things is fun. I’d like to stand on the human side. So I intend to keep AI out of the process as much as possible.”

The festival is also screening “Look Back,” Kore-eda’s live-action adaptation of Fujimoto Tatsuki’s 2021 one-shot manga, which competed in Venice. Deguchi Natsuki plays Fujino, an outgoing student who draws manga for her school newspaper, and Makita Aju plays Kyomoto, a reclusive classmate who idolizes her work. Their friendship, built on a shared love of making manga, carries into adulthood and ends in grief.

Kore-eda first read the manga during the COVID-19 pandemic, in a year when all of his filmmaking had come to a halt, and it pushed him back toward making films.

“In the end, I suppose it came down to: ‘I can’t quit now,’” he says.

About half of the producers and actors who helped him keep working over the years have since died, Kore-eda says, and he feels them watching him in the same way that Fujino feels watched by Kyomoto. “Realizing that was probably the big discovery for me. It’s never pressure. It’s encouragement, and it makes me want to do things properly, to make something properly.”

Of the two films he premiered this year in Cannes and Venice, he says: “If there’s a common point, I’d say it’s how we face the dead.”

Japanese cinema may be drawing international attention, but Kore-eda says challenges remain. Young Japanese directors are being noticed around the world, he says, yet filmmakers such as Hamaguchi Ryusuke and Fukada Koji often find it easier to raise money in France than at home.

“That’s the Japanese market. It’s really difficult. It’s a challenge for me too,” he says.

By his estimate, anime accounts for roughly 70% of Japan’s total box office, even though far more live-action films are made. Meanwhile, long-running independent arthouse cinemas, known in Japan as mini-theaters, have been closing one after another, and the culture now survives mainly in Tokyo and other big cities.

“Filmmakers up to the generation of Hamaguchi and Fukada grew up watching films in mini-theaters,” Kore-eda says. “When those disappear, how will the next filmmakers develop?”

Despite Japan’s shifting cinematic landscape, Kore-eda’s career has been going from strength to strength. Asked what the biggest change has been in the over three decades since his debut feature, “Maborosi,” he says: “Well, I suppose it’s realizing that it’s okay to be free.”

title: ‘Bridgerton’ Breakout Hannah Dodd to Lead Lucas Jones’ Romantic Drama ‘Miss You Forever, Zara Drake’ (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Hannah Dodd, best known for her portrayal of Francesca in Netflix’s hit Regency-era period drama “Bridgerton,” has landed her first lead film role. The British actress, also seen in “Enola Holmes 2” and “Anatomy of a Scandal,” has joined upcoming “Miss You Forever, Zara Drake,” a romantic drama exploring love and trauma written, directed and […]
content:
Hannah Dodd, best known for her portrayal of Francesca in Netflix’s hit Regency-era period drama “Bridgerton,” has landed her first lead film role.

The British actress, also seen in “Enola Holmes 2” and “Anatomy of a Scandal,” has joined upcoming “Miss You Forever, Zara Drake,” a romantic drama exploring love and trauma written, directed and produced by actor and poet Lucas Jones (“Break Clause”) in his feature directorial debut. Jones will also lead the film, alongside Dodd.

Set to shoot in the U.K. and U.S. in spring 2027, the film centers on Zara Drake, a woman at the peak of her ascent to adoration and notoriety. But one year after falling in love with Isaac Owens, frontman of a soon-to-be washed-up band, she seems to have disappeared from the face of the planet.

Popular on Variety

As per the synopsis: “Set in a timeless age between New York City and the tree-lined streets of England, ‘Miss You Forever, Zara Drake,’ explores the dichotomy of a love fuelled by resounding generational trauma and empty success. Built on the iconography and heritage of the 90s fashion scene, two lost souls fight to outrun their trauma.”

Jones is producing the film alongside Eli Banfield for Maryland Films. Executive producer is Richard Holmes. Key creatives working alongside Jones include cinematographer Brendan Harvey and composers Sindri Már Sigfússon and Kjartan Holm, with original music by Ava Lily, casting by Des Hamilton and additional casting by Lauren Bayly.

Dodd made her TV debut in the Hulu series “Find Me in Paris,” followed by “Harlots,” and later played Sandra, the illusionary adult form of Sprite in Chloe Zhao’s MCU feature “Eternals.” In 2022, she starred as the younger version of Sienna Miller’s character in Netflix miniseries “Anatomy of a Scandal” alongside roles in Netflix feature “Enola Holmes 2” and Lifetime miniseries “Flowers in the Attic: The Origin.” That same year it was announced she’d be replacing Ruby Stokes in the third season of the Shondaland-produced “Bridgerton” as Francesca, the quietest and most introverted of the Bridgerton family.

Alongside roles in recent TV rom-com “Break Clause,” Jones has also appeared in the series “Get Millie Black” and the feature “We Work for the Dead.” Aside from his work on screen, the Londoner is an accomplished poet whose work explores themes of masculinity, love, grief and connection. His book “I Still Believe in Miracles: Poems to Find Meaning in Difficult Times” was released earlier this year. Jones also once fronted the band The Rose Affair.

title: Netflix, ‘Elite’ Star Ester Expósito and Locarno Winner Mar Coll Adapt ‘La Regenta,’ a ‘Fresh Female Perspective’ on a Big Spanish Classic (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Netflix, ‘Elite’ star Ester Expósito and Locarno Winner Mar Coll are adapting Clarín’s classic novel into a feature film which went into production Oct. 23, produced by María Zamora at Elastica Films (“Alcarràs” “Romería”). Bombshell news – nothing was known of the movie until Friday’s announcement – “La Regenta” now weighs in as one of […]
content:
Netflix, ‘Elite’ star Ester Expósito and Locarno Winner Mar Coll are adapting Clarín’s classic novel into a feature film which went into production Oct. 23, produced by María Zamora at Elastica Films (“Alcarràs” “Romería”).

Bombshell news – nothing was known of the movie until Friday’s announcement – “La Regenta” now weighs in as one of Spain’s biggest movies of 2027.

Lambasted in its day, Clarín’s “La Regenta” is now acclaimed as a masterpiece, second only to “The Quixote” in Spain, “one of the great novels of the 19th century, alongside ‘Madame Bovary’ and ‘Anna Karenina,’” English writer Julian Barnes said this week.

Popular on Variety

The current adaptation will be a new contemporary version that reinterprets the classic from a “fresh female perspective,” Netflix announced Friday.

“La Regenta” marks Netflix’s latest venture into revered big literary IP in the Spanish-speaking world after adaptations of Gabriel García Márquez’s “One Hundred Years of Solitude” on Colombia and “The Eternaut” in Argentina. Both were Netflix Global Top 10 non-English hits and signature shows for the U.S. streaming giant.

Published over 1884-85, “La Regenta” turns on Ana Ozores, young, beautiful and married off to Victor Quintanar, a man twice her age and ex magistrate of Vetusta, a sleepy stifling provincial city where, says Netflix “everything is known and everything is judged.”

Seeking sense to her loveless existence, at least in the novel Ana attracts the predatorial lust of Magistral Fermín de Pas, her sensual confessor at La Vetusta cathedral, as well as the attentions of local Don Juan Álvaro Mejías.

“What begins as a private crisis becomes a silent struggle between desire, faith and social power, where Ana’s every move is watched, judged and used by those around her,” the synopsis ends.

Besides Expósito “La Regenta” is fronted by International Emmy Award winner Oriol Pla (“I, Addict,” “The Day After Tomorrow”) as Magistral Fermín de Pas, Vito Sanz (“Billionaires’ Bunker”) as Victor Quintanar and Borja Luna (“Breathless,” “No Traces”) as Álvaro Mesía,

The film big cast also features Clara Ingold (“Iron Reign”) as Petra, Carlos González (“La Bola Negra”) as Frígilis, Ana Torrent (“Thesis”) as Doña Paula, Itsaso Arana (“The Other Way Around,”) as Visitación, and Gonzalo de Castro (“The Inmortal”) as Ripamilán,

Clarín’s monumental, nearly 700-page novel mixes a searing portrait of a backward, hypocritical and vulgar provincial Spain; a vision of toxic masculine egotism; with a deep dive into the psychology and contradictions of its two central characters, Ana and Fermín de Pas.

“La Regenta” the film is written by Coll, Anna R. Costa, co-scribe of series standout “Madrid Arde” and the Barcelona-based Diego Vega, one of Peru’s top auteurs (“October,” “My Lucky Day”).

Coll on ‘La Regenta’

“Clarín’s novel is so rich that dozens of different adaptations can be made from it, like those that came before ours or those that will follow it,” said Coll.

“I have tried to approach the material, humbly, from a radically personal perspective, as I always do,” she added. “I have made my own what has moved me most in the novel, and what explores the loneliness and heartbreak of this regent’s wife, who tirelessly longs to give meaning to her life. A luminous character inhabiting a universe poised to prey on her. A woman whose sensitivity and stubborn search constitute, in themselves, a form of resistance.”

As an adaptation, “La Regenta” fits Coll like a glove. A founding mother of the Newest Catalan Cinema and cultured dissident as Clarion before her, Mar Coll, throughout a now 20-year career, has consistently questioned established thought. That has been Catalan upper middle-class hypocrisy and emotional paralysis (Goya winner “Three Days With the Family”), the comic patriarchy of paternal narcissism (series “Matar al Padre”) and the superiority of Scandinavian social models (“This Is Not Sweden”), Variety has written.

Her latest film, “Salve María,” which won a Locarno Special Mention in 2024, took a beg-to-differ view on maternity, questioning what still remains a taboo: whether all women are cut out for motherhood.

María Zamora and Elastica Films

Zamora, whose productions also include 2023 San Sebastián Golden Shell winner “The Rye Horn” and Cannes Directors’ Fortnight winner “Creatura,” won Spain’s National Cinematography Award for championing a new generation of Spanish auteurs, often women, driving their impact on the international film scene and helping them make on occasions a remarkable impact in domestic Spanish distribution.

title: Asif Kapadia on Bringing the ‘Profound’ ‘7 Up’ Documentary Series to a Close After More Than 60 Years: ‘It’s a Dream Job’
summary: From a charismatic Formula 1 racing legend to a brilliant but flawed soccer god to a troubled, tragic singer, Academy Award-winning docmaker Asif Kapadia has made a career out of telling the stories of larger-than-life figures. But when it comes to his “dream job,” it was a group of “ordinary people” in their seventies who […]
content:
From a charismatic Formula 1 racing legend to a brilliant but flawed soccer god to a troubled, tragic singer, Academy Award-winning docmaker Asif Kapadia has made a career out of telling the stories of larger-than-life figures. But when it comes to his “dream job,” it was a group of “ordinary people” in their seventies who stole his heart.

Speaking at Rome’s MIA Market on Thursday, Kapadia opened up about what it was like to be handed the reins of the ground-breaking “Up” documentary series, which followed the lives of 14 everyday Brits over the course of more than six decades. The final, two-part installment aired last month in the U.K. on ITV.

“In the U.K., this is one of the most important television shows made. There’s nothing [like it],” Kapadia said. “It deals with humanity and life. Real people. Ordinary people.”

Popular on Variety

The “Up” series of films launched in 1964 with “7 Up,” capturing the lives of 10 boys and four girls in England all aged seven at the time. Cameras then revisited the group every seven years to chart their journey from childhood to teenagers, to adulthood, through careers, marriage, divorce, parenting, bereavement and more.

The longest-running documentary series ever made, it’s been broadcast in 157 countries, including the U.S., Canada, Japan, China, Australia and France.

All but the first in the series were directed by Michael Apted, who passed away in 2021. Kapadia was handed the baton to direct the final installment, saying he “felt very honored and privileged to have a chance to be a part of it.”

“It was like finishing off something someone had started — just closing the circle,” he said. “It’s a dream job.”

The acclaimed director of “Senna,” “Diego Maradona” and “Amy” — an intimate portrait of the late singer Amy Winehouse that won the Oscar for best documentary feature in 2016 — Kapadia was appearing in conversation with MIA’s head of doc content Marco Spagnoli, who said that when Apted attended the Rome market in 2018, he described the “Up” series as “his life-defining project.”

Sharing the story of how he found himself at the helm of the final chapter, Kapadia described how he grew up watching the iconic series in his North London home, huddled around the TV set with his parents and siblings. Fast forward more than four decades and “someone knocks on the door of my office and says, ‘Are you Asif?’ ‘Yeah.’ ‘Did you make “Senna”?’ ‘Yeah.’ ‘Would you be interested in making the “7 Up” film?’”

The director grinned. “I was very busy working on other things, but there was no way I could say no,” he said. “It’s like a dream.”

Best known for his ambitious documentary features, Kapadia described the process of adapting to the rigors of television production. “It was essentially a TV budget, which was not a lot of time, not a lot of money. It was very small,” he said. “We had to do it fast. But what I decided to do — because I can’t help myself — is to go back to the dailies, and to see things that have never been seen that had been filmed previously.”

In the end, the director wound up incorporating footage of “14 characters who have been filmed for 63 years,” along with Apted himself, whose work on the “Up” series began with the second installment. “I made him a character as well, because I’m kind of looking at the nature of filmmaking and documentary, which the series in a way created that,” Kapadia said.

“I’ve got 15 characters over 60 years. It’s a lot of material, so that was the real challenge. But I’m really quite proud of it,” he said. “It’s quite amazing and profound and beautiful, because of how it somehow covers life. It’s all there somewhere.”

The 12th edition of Rome’s MIA Market runs Oct. 19 – 23.

title: Fremantle Global Entertainment Exec Chris O’Dell Retires After 19 Years At ‘Got Talent’ Maker
summary: Chris O’Dell, one of Fremantle’s longest-serving entertainment execs, is retiring from the Got Talent and X Factor company. He has been at RTL-owned Fremantle since 2007 and left just shy of 20 years of service on October 9. During that time he has worked on shows such as Got Talent, Idol, X Factor and The […]
content:
Chris O’Dell, one of Fremantle‘s longest-serving entertainment execs, is retiring from the Got Talent and X Factor company.

He has been at RTL-owned Fremantle since 2007 and left just shy of 20 years of service on October 9. During that time he has worked on shows such as Got Talent, Idol, X Factor and The Price Is Right, and worked closely with major UK talent such as Ant & Dec and Simon Cowell.

O’Dell, who was as most recently Head of Global Entertainment Production, announced his retirement on LinkedIn and this was subsequently confirmed by a Fremantle rep.

Jennifer Mullin CEO at Fremantle said: “Chris joined Fremantle as a flying producer, supporting the seamless execution of our productions across different territories, and went on to become an executive producer before taking on the leadership of our global entertainment production team in 2014.

Watch on Deadline

“Over those 19 years, he has played a hugely important role in bringing some of Fremantle’s biggest and most successful entertainment formats to audiences around the world – from X Factor, Got Talent and Idol to Family Feud, Price is Right, Password and Farmer Wants a Wife. I want to thank Chris for his commitment, expertise and contribution over the last 19 years, and wish him happiness and success for the future and his retirement.”

O’Dell’s exit comes seven months after Ben Crompton replaced Andrew Llinares as Global Head of Entertainment at Fremantle. He’s also the second long-serving Fremantle exec to depart this year following the exit of International and Commercial COO Bob McCourt in July.

“It’s been amazing working with Chris, who is loved by all at Fremantle and beyond,” said Crompton. “The legacy of all the fantastic shows Chris has worked on is a testament to his breadth of knowledge, experience and leadership. We wish him all the best in his retirement, and he will be greatly missed.”

O’Dell began his career in regional TV in the UK and then moved to become a series producer at London Weekend Television, where he worked on the original Blind Date. He went on to become Head of Entertainment Series at ITV Studios predecessor Granada, and then had spells at Objective Television and IMG Media before joining Fremantle in 2007.

“I have also been very fortunate to work with some fabulous on-screen talents, including Cilla Black, Bruce Forsyth, Simon Cowell, Ant & Dec, Bradley Walsh, Matthew Kelly, Tess Daly and countless other stars, both in the UK and around the world,” wrote O’Dell on LinkedIn.

“Just as importantly, I have been a part of some wonderfully talented teams. All with the same goal: to create television that make audiences smile. It’s both a privilege and an emotional wrench to decide to step away from the day-to-day of everything this job demands. I’m sure I’ll miss it, but I’m also sure it’s time for me to start a new chapter.

“I want to thank anyone who has ever helped me over the years. I know TV can sometimes feel like a challenging place, but I also believe the world will never lose its appetite to be entertained by the ideas that you all continue to create. Cherish it.”

title: Prince William Says He’s A Christopher Nolan & ‘The Celebrity Traitors’ Super Fan
summary: Prince William has declared his love for Christopher Nolan films and The Celebrity Traitors in an unexpected appearance on The Graham Norton Show. Sitting on the BBC late-night show’s famous red sofa, the Prince of Wales told Norton that he relaxes by watching movies and listening to music. “I love getting immersed in deep-thinking films. […]
content:
Prince William has declared his love for Christopher Nolan films and The Celebrity Traitors in an unexpected appearance on The Graham Norton Show.

Sitting on the BBC late-night show’s famous red sofa, the Prince of Wales told Norton that he relaxes by watching movies and listening to music.

“I love getting immersed in deep-thinking films. I like action films too, but I like something a bit different,” he told Norton during the show’s recording on Thursday.

“I’m a big fan of everything Christopher Nolan does. His films are fantastic – The Dark Knight series is psychologically dark and deep and I absolutely love that. He takes concepts that are completely out there and makes them incredibly entertaining.”

On The Celebrity Traitors, he added: “I love it, the family love it. Charlotte and Louis are obsessed with it. It’s really good telly.”

Watch on Deadline

He continued: “I saw Ross Kemp the day after the first episode and I couldn’t help but try – in the most appropriate way – to touch him to see what reaction I got from him. Turns out he was really jumpy.”

William appeared on Norton to discuss The Earthshot Prize, his environmental initiative. He said: “For many years I was hearing stories about environment issues and one thing that struck me was the negativity and doom, which got me down. I thought we could do something more powerful and more optimistic and the idea of an awards’ ceremony came about and we could talk about urgency and optimism together.”

Other guests include Cate Blanchett, Hannah Waddingham, and conservationist Robert Irwin. Singer-songwriter Jorja Smith completes the lineup.

The Graham Norton Show will air tonight on the BBC and screens on BBC America in the U.S.

title: Ryu Murakami Dies: Japanese Author & Filmmaker, Best Known For ‘Almost Transparent Blue’, Was 74
summary: The Japanese writer and filmmaker Ryu Murakami has died. He was 74. Murakami’s publisher, Gentosha, announced his death today in a lengthy statement on their website. “Author Ryu Murakami passed away at his home on October 17, 2026, at the age of 74. We hereby express our deepest condolences and share this news,” the statement […]
content:
The Japanese writer and filmmaker Ryu Murakami has died. He was 74.

Murakami’s publisher, Gentosha, announced his death today in a lengthy statement on their website.

“Author Ryu Murakami passed away at his home on October 17, 2026, at the age of 74. We hereby express our deepest condolences and share this news,” the statement read.

“The funeral was held as a private family service. In accordance with the family’s wishes, they are declining all condolence visits, monetary offerings, floral tributes, telegrams, and other gifts.”

Born in Nagasaki Prefecture in 1952, Murakami made his writing debut in 1976, while still a university student, with Almost Transparent Blue, which won both the 19th Gunzo New Writers’ Award and the 75th Akutagawa Prize.

Watch on Deadline

The book became a hit, selling more than 3.5 million copies across its hardcover and paperback editions. In 1980, he received the 3rd Noma Literary Newcomer’s Award for Coin Locker Babies.

Murakami also wrote and directed several film adaptations of his own works, including Tokyo Decadence, which explores the lives of women in Tokyo during the bubble economy, and Kyoko, the story of a young Japanese woman’s relationship with a Cuban-American serviceman stationed in the country. In 1994, he published A World Five Minutes Later, set in an alternate reality where Japan did not surrender in World War II. In 1997, he won the 49th Yomiuri Literary Prize for In the Miso Soup.

Away from writing, he also served as the primary interviewer on the long-running economic and business talk show Cambrian Palace on TV Tokyo.

title: Donald Trump Wanted Google Maps To Change Name Of Atlantic Ocean
summary: President Donald Trump’s continuing desire to name parts of the world after himself or the U.S. almost made it to the oceans. During a rally in South Carolina, Trump told supporters he had called Google CEO Sundar Pichai to ask about changing the name of the Atlantic Ocean on Google Maps. “I only like two […]
content:
President Donald Trump‘s continuing desire to name parts of the world after himself or the U.S. almost made it to the oceans.

During a rally in South Carolina, Trump told supporters he had called Google CEO Sundar Pichai to ask about changing the name of the Atlantic Ocean on Google Maps.

“I only like two oceans: The Atlantic Ocean and the Pacific Ocean. I’m not going to put either Trump or America on any other ocean but these two, so we seriously looked at the Atlantic Ocean, and I called Google Maps, who were really great with the lake,” said Trump. “I said: ‘Sundar, I’m thinking of the Atlantic Ocean.'”

Trump claimed the Google boss responded, “No, no, no. This time I’m not doing it. Oceans are different, sir. They cover a lot of countries. Please don’t ask us to do that.”

Watch on Deadline

Trump’s “proposal” now appears to be on the back burner. “So I’ll probably pass. Should I pass it?” the President asked his supporters. “I think let’s keep it the Atlantic Ocean.”

The “lake” Trump referenced was Lake Ontario, which Trump has renamed Lake America amid the trade war between his administration and Canada.

Google Maps currently displays the water as ‘Lake Ontario (Lake America)’ and also uses the same phrasing for the Gulf of Mexico.

Trump has also pondered renaming the Strait of Hormuz, writing on social media last month: “Should we change the name Hormuz Strait to TRUMP STRAIT??? Like America itself, it would be ‘hotter’ than ever before!”

South Park recently lampooned Trump’s ongoing name-change drive by renaming the show South America for its 29th season.

title: U-KNOCK 2026 Brings Korean Content Companies To Hollywood For Investment & Global Partnerships
summary: U-KNOCK 2026 will connect Korean content and technology companies with U.S. investors and entertainment partners on November 4–6, 2026, at The Biltmore Los Angeles. The program is hosted by South Korea’s Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism and organized by the Korea Creative Content Agency (KOCCA). Now in its third year, U-KNOCK builds on relationships […]
content:
U-KNOCK 2026 will connect Korean content and technology companies with U.S. investors and entertainment partners on November 4–6, 2026, at The Biltmore Los Angeles. The program is hosted by South Korea’s Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism and organized by the Korea Creative Content Agency (KOCCA).

Now in its third year, U-KNOCK builds on relationships with international investors and Hollywood studios, emphasizing deal-making and long-term partnerships. Key programs include the International Content Investment Forum on November 5 and one-on-one investment and business meetings on November 6.

The November 5 forum, themed “What Makes Content Last,” will bring together Korean and U.S. leaders in media, finance and technology to examine how cultural success becomes enduring commercial value. Discussions will explore IP monetization, global franchise expansion and emerging business models driven by AI, digital platforms and evolving investment strategies.

U.S. participants include The Raine Group; Shamrock Capital; Atwater Capital; J.P. Morgan Global Corporate Bank; Amblin Entertainment; and Anonymous Content, who all bring perspectives across entertainment finance, investment and production.

From Korea, speakers will include global transmedia company CJ ENM; YLAB, which develops webtoon universes and screen adaptations; character-IP company IPX (formerly LINE FRIENDS); creator-focused comedy label MetaComedy; Moneygraphy, the original-content media outlet from financial platform Toss; and bemyfriends, a provider of direct-to-consumer fandom business solutions. Together, they will examine how stories travel across formats, how content models evolve and how global fan communities can support sustainable businesses.

Five Korean companies will then present at the Korean Company Showcase. Modhaus, the company behind K-pop group tripleS and Web3 fan-participation platform COSMO, will appear alongside YN Culture & Space (YN C&S), known for its LED-wall virtual production and advanced production infrastructure; Klleon, which develops real-time multilingual interactive digital humans; Contents First, operator of Tappytoon and its global audience of more than 14 million readers; and Studio Eon, which uses an Unreal Engine-based pipeline to produce science-fiction animation. The companies will present their business models and plans for North American expansion.

On November 6, the five showcase participants will be joined by seven more companies for one-on-one business meetings. The full 12-company delegation spans original story IP in drama, film, animation and web novels, as well as generative AI, interactive entertainment and fan platforms. Meetings are intended to connect the companies with North American investors, buyers, studios and other potential business partners.

The additional participants include Big Ocean ENM, with crime procedurals Flex X Cop and Another Heaven, the latter in development; EO Content Group, developing action-espionage series TEAM-K; and Mstoryhub, whose webtoon IP includes The Remarried Empress. LOCUS is developing Kkokdu, a 3D family fantasy feature inspired by Korean funeral traditions. RECOV combines K-pop touring, merchandise and VIP services, while JIRO brings AI content-production platform Dropshot AI and AI-generated K-pop idol IP SEORIA. Draftify’s PlaySquad rounds out the lineup with playable livestreaming that lets viewers influence gameplay.

U.S. and international investors, buyers and production executives interested in attending the International Content Investment Forum or requesting one-on-one meetings with the 12 participating Korean companies can register and submit meeting requests at www.uknockglobal.com.

title: Megyn Kelly Slammed for Attacking Christina Applegate Over MS Misdiagnosis; ‘The View’ Hosts Call Her a ‘Bully’ and a ‘Fungus That Thrives’ on Outrage
summary: Megyn Kelly was lambasted by “The View” hosts Whoopi Goldberg, Sara Haines and more for attacking Christina Applegate after the Emmy winner revealed she was misdiagnosed with MS. Kelly reacted to Applegate’s news on her eponymous talk show by alleging Applegate must be “crying now because I guess she no longer gets to be the […]
content:
Megyn Kelly was lambasted by “The View” hosts Whoopi Goldberg, Sara Haines and more for attacking Christina Applegate after the Emmy winner revealed she was misdiagnosed with MS. Kelly reacted to Applegate’s news on her eponymous talk show by alleging Applegate must be “crying now because I guess she no longer gets to be the face of this disease.”

“This is, like, the problem with celebrities like wanting to lean into their health problems,” Kelly said on her talk show, shading Applegate’s health journey a “wild goose chase.”

“So, let me ask you, m’am, you think Christina wanted to have MS so she could have a good time? Are you crazy?” Goldberg fired back on “The View,” with Haines also asking, “Who wants to be the face of MS?” (via Entertainment Weekly).

Popular on Variety

“Talk about kicking someone when they’re down,” Haines continued. “She got a diagnosis and wanted to help other people. [She’s] now feeling the pain of not knowing what her identity is and, more importantly, what her diagnosis is. Megyn Kelly sold her soul for politics. Which one did a better job here? She literally has sunk so low in my book.”

Ana Navarro said she didn’t “even want to get into the Megyn Kelly of it all because I think she’s like a fungus that thrives on oxygen that she gets by purposely creating outrage” on sensitive topics, with Haines then calling Kelly a “bully” and Sunny Hostin slamming Kelly as “an ugly person.”

Goldberg concluded: “The idea that you would come out and say something like this, Megyn, is unbelievable, that you don’t have the wherewithal to recognize that someone is saying, ‘This is what’s happening to me. That’s how we get through our lives. We connect to each other. That’s what this is about, and I’m going to connect to you and say rethink your position on this, because you’re wrong.”

Applegate originally revealed that she had been diagnosed with MS in 2021, and retired from acting after the finale of her hit series “Dead to Me” the next year. She then become a fierce advocate for people with the disease — which causes damage to the central nervous system — and started the “MeSsy” podcast alongside “The Sopranos” star Jamie-Lynn Sigler as a way to share her experience and spread awareness.

After taking a seven-month break from the podcast, Applegate returned to the program on Oct. 21 and broke down in tears while telling listeners that new technology led to the discovery that she was diagnosed with MS.

“This may come as great news, but to me, I’m back at square one,” Applegate said. “It’s hard to say that [my doctor] came into my room and she said, ‘Congratulations, you don’t have MS.’ You don’t get misdiagnosed and then all of the sudden I’m better. I haven’t gotten better … If anything, I’ve gotten worse in some ways. So I’m back at square one, that I don’t know what’s going on with me.”

Applegate added that “it’s weird because I feel like I let everybody down” after becoming such a big advocate for the MS community. She said that she’s still in a “state of shock,” adding: “It’s a mindfuck, for sure.”
