Acclaim and box office success are raising the possibility that a documentary could finally break one of the Academy’s longest-standing barriers. If it earns a nomination, the achievement would be historic. But it would also raise an uncomfortable question: Why did it take this long?

To celebrate this potential historic nomination, Variety is ranking the 20 films that should have received a best picture nomination in the past 40 years.

The films mentioned here span genres, styles and subjects, from the pursuit of an NBA dream to a high-wire walk between the World Trade Center towers, from a confrontation with Indonesia’s history of mass killing to a real-time account of Edward Snowden’s revelations.

You can blame the Academy at large for some of these omissions; others tie directly to the Documentary Branch itself, which snubbed many of them in its own category.

If “You Can See Everything” finally breaks through, it will undoubtedly have earned its place in history. But it should not have been the first. Many others from this very year could also be deemed worthy, such as “Once Upon a Time in Harlem” and “Naza.”

Read the list below.

Honorable mentions: “An Inconvenient Truth” (2006); “Senna” (2010); “The Act of Killing” (2012); “Apollo 11″ (2019)

title: James Gunn Defends the DC Universe, Says He Dislikes the Idea That ‘Individual Stories Aren’t Meaningful Unless They Lead to Something’
summary: James Gunn took to Threads on Saturday to defend the DCU and his decision to expand the universe with “individual stories” amid criticism that his films aren’t building toward a major crossover event. Responding to a commenter who pointed out that Gunn doesn’t necessarily need to lay the foundation for one totally interconnected universe, the […]
content:
James Gunn took to Threads on Saturday to defend the DCU and his decision to expand the universe with “individual stories” amid criticism that his films aren’t building toward a major crossover event.

Responding to a commenter who pointed out that Gunn doesn’t necessarily need to lay the foundation for one totally interconnected universe, the DC Studios co-head wrote, “I couldn’t agree more.” “DCU is just an alternate universe; we can enter at any location or time and tell THAT story. I dislike the idea that individual stories aren’t meaningful unless they lead to something else. People not understanding this is strange to me, because ‘Star Wars’ has essentially been doing this for 50 years across movies, shows, games and books, admittedly without the tonal variety,” he wrote.

Gunn pointed out that this approach doesn’t mean there isn’t any connectivity, adding that the “Superman” saga begins with “Superman” and extends into “Man of Tomorrow,” “and contains many characters we’ve introduced in other stories.” “But that doesn’t mean those other stories only exist to set up what’s happening there. I would love people to be seeing ‘Clayface’ because it’s a great, fun horror movie unto itself, not because of where else Clayface will show up three movies from now,” he concluded.

Popular on Variety

In the post that Gunn responded to, the user had replied to an image that listed out his DC Universe foundation — “Superman,” “Peacemaker,” “Supergirl,” “Creature Commandos,” “Clayface” and “Lanters” — followed by the text: “What is this building towards???”

“Clayface,” which his theaters on Friday, is Gunn’s latest DCU installment, following 2025’s “Superman” and this year’s “Supergirl.” (Ahead of the film’s release, comic fans pointed out that the character, who has never been the subject of a standalone feature film, is a considerably nicher choice than previous DCU films.) It generated $24 million from 3,458 North American theaters in its debut, comfortably taking the No. 1 spot at the box office.

Directed by James Watkins, “Clayface” follows the titular Batman villain, a rising movie star also known as Matt Hagen (Tom Rhys Harries), who volunteers for a highly experimental medical procedure after his face is severely disfigured. Naomi Ackie, David Dencik, Max Minghella and Eddie Marsan also star.

Variety’s Guy Lodge called the film “its own ugly animal; perhaps the characters and conflicts introduced here would pall if given the franchise treatment, but in the context of a single, genre-melding romp, they’re fresh and ickily enjoyable.”

Gunn’s next film, “Superman: Man of Tomorrow,” hits theaters July 9, 2027.

title: John Oliver Issues Urgent Warning Ahead of Midterms About the Republican Party’s Nazi Ties
summary: John Oliver returned to the “Last Week Tonight” desk after a two-week absence and focused the entirety of Sunday night’s episode on a “worrying trend that’s been on the rise” amongst the Republican Party ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections — they’re apparent affinity for Nazis. There is Peter Oberacker, a Republican candidate for […]
content:
John Oliver returned to the “Last Week Tonight” desk after a two-week absence and focused the entirety of Sunday night’s episode on a “worrying trend that’s been on the rise” amongst the Republican Party ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections — they’re apparent affinity for Nazis.

There is Peter Oberacker, a Republican candidate for New York’s 19th congressional district. Back in 2015, Oberacker posted a photo to Facebook on Veterans Day memorializing his late grandfather — in full Wehrmacht uniform — who’d died fighting for Nazi Germany. Oberacker later claimed it was the only photo of his grandfather that he had.

“Yeah, not great!” exclaimed Oliver. “If that is the only picture that you have, maybe consider having no pictures of him! You can sit Veterans Day out. No one will think that’s weird.”

Popular on Variety

The HBO host then brought up how Elon Musk delivered what very much appeared to be a Nazi salute to Trump supporters at a rally following his election in 2025.

“Everything about that screams, ‘Nazi!’” said Oliver, adding, “Well, almost everything. To be fair to the Nazis, unlike Elon, they at least looked sharp in their suits.”

He continued, claiming, “It does feel that the Republican Party has been getting way too comfortable with some, at best, Nazi-adjacent shit,” including Paul Ingrassia, Trump’s nominee to the Office of Special Counsel, who withdrew his nomination after leaked group chat messages revealed him saying, “I do have a Nazi streak in me from time to time, I will admit it.” and Brandon Herrera, a Republican nominee for Texas’s 23rd congressional district, who posted a YouTube video in 2022 where he referred to the MP-40 as “Hitler’s street sweeper” followed by footage of him and a friend goose-stepping to a Nazi marching song.

Even Karl Rove, the architect of George W. Bush’s presidency, issued a warning last month at the Texas Tribune Festival that his party was being taken over by “bigots” like Bo French, a candidate for Texas Railroad Commissioner known for racist social media posts, adding, “Nick Fuentes goes to Dallas and meets with a bunch of Republican leaders. This guy is a Nazi.”

Oliver argued that Israel’s war in Gaza has led “some on the far-right to seize on this moment and elevate antisemitic conspiracy theories,” including Tucker Carlson’s warm podcast interview with the Hitler-worshipping neo-Nazi Nick Fuentes. The Heritage Foundation president Kevin Roberts defended Carlson’s chummy interview with Fuentes and said the podcaster was under attack from “globalist forces,” later walking back the defense by claiming that he, the leader of the top conservative think tank, doesn’t pay attention to the news.

Fuentes claimed on his podcast that “whites built everything” and “Jews are money-changers, bullshit artists, psychopaths, charlatans, grifters, manipulators… why do you think they’re so obnoxious? Why do you think they’re so fucking obnoxious? They have no manners because they’re from the third world. They come from the literal ghetto.”

Cue Oliver: “It makes it all the more laughable that Tucker made such a show of offering Fuentes, a man who’s literally spent thousands of hours on the internet saying whatever he wants, the chance to finally say what he thinks… And the worrying thing is, it’s not just Tucker. Fuentes has been inching closer and closer to mainstream Republicans over the years,” such as GOP Congressman Paul Gosar, who gave the keynote speech at Fuentes’s America First Political Action Conference in 2021 and Marjorie Taylor Greene, who did the same in 2022. Trump also infamously dined with Fuentes at Mar-a-Lago in November 2022, and none other than Kanye West brought him there — one month after West tweeted, “I’m going death con 3 On JEWISH PEOPLE.”

“Nazis getting power doesn’t historically bode well for anyone, including, for what it’s worth, Nazis, who didn’t exactly have the best 1945,” reasoned Oliver, who further highlighted the Republican Party’s “groyper problem” by pointing to a Manhattan Institute analysis of the GOP that determined, “Nearly four in ten in the current GOP (37%) believe the Holocaust was greatly exaggerated or did not happen as historians described,” including “54% of men under 50.” The comedian then pointed to the leaked group chats from leaders of Young Republican groups around the country praising Hitler and spouting racial epithets left and right.

“There are some who will say, ‘Calm down. This seems to be just a bunch of kids and shitty streamers. You can just ignore it,’” said Oliver, which is something JD Vance argued when he was asked about the group chat, saying, “Kids do stupid things.” They weren’t kids, though, but rather full-grown adults in their twenties and thirties.

“The far-right fringe currently rising up in this party is not remotely new, from the John Birch Society through Barry Goldwater and Pat Buchanan, the Republican Party has always left its door ajar for bigots, cranks and conspiracy theorists,” asserted Oliver. “Have you ever listened to the Nixon Tapes? They would do numbers on Rumble today.”

Other sketchy GOP candidates include Marshall Rawson, running for Florida House District 10, who marched with neo-Nazis in Charlottesville. Oliver brought up how, when 28 GOP officials were asked if they’d denounced Rawson given his neo-Nazi ties, only three responded, and two of them stood by Rawson.

“The point here is: Far-right views in the Republican Party are by no means irrelevant and they are way past the point of being ignorable —some of them are literally on the ballot in nine days, in an election, by the way, where the single biggest campaign spender is [Elon Musk], you know, of the Adolf-aloha wave.”

title: Korea Box Office: Anime Phenomenon ‘Chiikawa’ Remains Unstoppable as Yeon Sang-ho Thriller ‘Paradise Lost’ Debuts
summary: Japanese animated sensation “Chiikawa the Movie: The Secret of the Mermaid Island” maintained a commanding grip on the South Korean box office over the weekend of Oct. 23–25, capturing nearly 45% of nationwide ticket revenue in its fourth frame. According to data from KOBIS, the tracking service operated by the Korean Film Council, the Toho-distributed […]
content:
Japanese animated sensation “Chiikawa the Movie: The Secret of the Mermaid Island” maintained a commanding grip on the South Korean box office over the weekend of Oct. 23–25, capturing nearly 45% of nationwide ticket revenue in its fourth frame.

According to data from KOBIS, the tracking service operated by the Korean Film Council, the Toho-distributed fantasy release took in $2.5 million from 320,293 admissions across 1,115 screens, accounting for 44.7% of the weekend market.

Directed by Kei Oikawa and adapted from the popular manga by Nagano, the fantasy feature tracks the small protagonist and companions journeying to a scenic coastal island before uncovering a sinister local mystery. Driven by enduring youth and family turnout, the animated blockbuster pushed its cumulative South Korean haul to $17.5 million from 2,248,137 total admissions since launching on Sep. 30.

Popular on Variety

Director Hur Jin-ho’s political thriller “The Assassin(s)” held second place, earning $520,822 from 68,241 admissions across 730 screens to capture 9.2% of the frame. Distributed by Hive Media Corp, the period drama reconstructs the August 15, 1974 assassination attempt on President Park Chung-hee and stars Yu Hae-jin, Park Hae-il, and Lee Min-ho investigating irregularities surrounding the inquiry into the death of First Lady Yuk Young-soo.

The production’s theatrical run continues against persistent political blowback and legal challenges, with conservative civic groups and bereaved family members lodging defamation complaints alleging historical distortion over its depiction of state involvement. Despite protests that previously prompted 19 film guilds to issue a joint statement defending cinematic freedom, the release lifted its cume to $25 million from 3,374,517 admissions since its Sep. 23 rollout.

CJ Entertainment’s psychological thriller “Paradise Lost” opened in third place, generating $502,962 from 66,699 admissions across 803 screens for an 8.9% market share. Directed and co-written by Yeon Sang-ho and starring Kim Hyun-joo and Bae Hyun-sung, the mystery follows a desperate mother navigating a closed religious community while searching for her missing son. Following its world premiere at Toronto and an Oct. 21 mid-week rollout, the title has accumulated $769,865 from 104,877 total admissions.

Warner Bros. and DC Studios’ “Clayface” debuted in fourth place, collecting $388,947 from 48,245 admissions across 655 screens for 6.9% of the market. Since opening on Oct. 21, the film has grossed $595,460 from 77,153 viewers.

CJ ENM’s gambling drama “Tazza: The Song of Beelzebub” took fifth place in its fifth weekend, taking in $371,743 from 46,919 admissions across 618 screens to claim 6.6% of receipts. Directed by Choi Kook-hee and starring Byun Yo-han, Noh Jae-won, and Ayaka Miyoshi, the fourth installment in the franchise pushed its gross to $15.3 million and stands on the brink of two million tickets at 1,999,477 admissions.

Plus M Entertainment’s period drama “Still Shining” opened in sixth place, earning $148,298 from 21,564 admissions across 562 screens. Directed by Song Il-gon and starring veteran actor Kim Hye-ja alongside Cha Mi-kyung, the drama traces the lifelong bond between two women who promised to sing together in Seoul during the Japanese colonial era. Counting mid-week business since its Oct. 21 debut, the release has taken $278,527 from 41,037 viewers.

Universal’s tentpole “The Odyssey” placed seventh in its twelfth weekend, drawing $164,558 from 20,189 admissions across 341 screens. Its cumulative haul reached $106.2 million from 12,311,245 admissions since opening on Aug. 5.

Amazon MGM Studios and Warner Bros.’ psychological thriller “Verity” opened in eighth place, pulling in $120,876 from 16,416 admissions across 458 screens and has grossed $178,096 from 25,190 admissions since its Oct. 22 bow.

Director Kore-eda Hirokazu’s live-action manga drama “Look Back” took ninth place in its third weekend, earning $126,854 from 15,624 admissions across 190 screens, lifting its cumulative total to $1 million from 131,051 admissions.

Rounding out the top 10 was domestic action thriller “Killing Time” with $82,439 from 11,244 admissions across 274 screens. Directed by Jang Jun-yeob and starring Ryu Hye-young and Nam Yoon-su, the film centers on a popular YouTube crew that collapses overnight after an accident claims a member’s life during a live broadcast; when they stage an extreme comeback stunt to regain fame, mysterious figures force them into a real, deadly survival game. Since its Oct. 21 release, the thriller has grossed $135,388 from 19,121 viewers.

The overall market collective gross for the weekend was $5.6 million, down from last week’s $6.7 million.

title: Eric Bauza, Emmy Award-Winning Looney Tunes Voice Actor, Dies at 46
summary: Eric Bauza, the Emmy Award-winning voice actor behind Looney Tunes characters like Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, died Sunday at his home as a result of hypertensive cardiovascular disease, according to Los Angeles County Medical Examiner records. He was 46. Bauza’s death was announced by his family, who shared a statement to the actor’s Instagram […]
content:
Eric Bauza, the Emmy Award-winning voice actor behind Looney Tunes characters like Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, died Sunday at his home as a result of hypertensive cardiovascular disease, according to Los Angeles County Medical Examiner records. He was 46.

Bauza’s death was announced by his family, who shared a statement to the actor’s Instagram account on Sunday.

“Eric Bauza, Emmy Award-winning voice actor and the modern voice of iconic Looney Tunes characters Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, along with dozens of other beloved cartoon characters, has passed away suddenly,” they wrote. “More details to come.”

Popular on Variety

Over the course of his career, Bauza was one of the industry’s most in-demand voiceover actors, lending his voice to characters like the aforementioned Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, but also Tweety, Elmer Fudd, Foghorn Leghorn, Porky Pig, Road Runner, Charlie the Dog and others in this year’s Looney Tunes film “Coyote vs. Acme.” He also voiced characters in “Space Jam: A New Legacy,” “Looney Tunes Cartoons” and more.

Bauza had more than 400 acting credits to his name, with his first, “The Ripping Friends” in 2001. He went on to voice characters in “Avatar: The Last Airbender,” “Chowder,” “Alvin and the Chipmunks: The Squeakquel,” “Scooby-Doo! Mystery Incorporated,” “Fanboy & Chum Chum,” “Ben 10 Omniverse” and many more. In 2026 alone, Bauza had already lent his voice to projects including “Chibiverse,” “Minions & Monsters,” “Forgotten Island,” “Rick and Morty,” “Superkitties” and “Avatar: Seven Havens,” among others.

In Variety’s Peter Debruge’s review of the 2024 film “The Day the Earth Blew Up: A Looney Tunes Movie,” he called Bauza, who voiced both Porky and Daffy, a “vocal MVP” who “brings a manic energy to the pair.”

Bauza was nominated for five Daytime Emmy Awards for his work on “Looney Tunes Cartoons,” “Mupped Babies” and “The Adventures of Puss in Boots.” He won three Children’s & Family Emmy Awards for “Teen Titans Go!,” “Bugs Bunny Builders” and “Looney Tunes Cartoons,” and earned a nomination for “Daffy in Wackyland.”

At the time of his death, Bauza was in pre-production on two projects, “Bye Bye Bunny: A Looney Tunes Musical” as Daffy Duck and “The Dragon Masters” as The Shogun King.

Chris DeFaria, who produced “Coyote vs. Acme,” told Variety that he will remember Bauza as someone with an “absolutely tireless dedication” to the animation art form, and reflected on his “pure expression of dedication, talent, enthusiasm, love and fun.”

“He embodied everything we wanted from this film, including the major theme of the movie that a little guy can make a difference in this world,” said DeFaria. “He’s a voiceover artist for animated characters that have historic precedents and roles, and somehow out of that, he carved out a place in this business. And this past year, he had such an incredible impact, both on our movie, of course, but also on bringing attention to this amazing art form.”

“Eric Bauza was a unique voice talent who brought joy and laughter to millions around the world. During his 15 years at Warner Bros. Animation, he was the voice of Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck among countless other characters,” said Warner Bros. Television Group and US Networks Chairman Channing Dungey in a statement. “He followed in the footsteps of giants like Mel Blanc. Eric said that carrying on the legendary legacy of the Looney Tunes was among the greatest honors of his life. In addition to his incredible talent, Eric was a treasured part of our animation family. Our hearts go out to his loved ones.”

Bauza was born on Dec. 7, 1979, in Scarborough, Toronto. According to his SBV talent bio, he began his animation career as a character designer at a production studio in Hollywood. He worked in the animation department on films including “Good Vibe,” “Nimbrod and Stinky’s Antarctic Adventure,” “The Drawn Together Movie!,” “Slacker Cats,” “El Tigre: The Adventures of Manny Rivera” and more.

title: China Box Office: ‘Resident Evil’ Stays at No. 1 as Market Hits Fall Lull
summary: Constantin Film and Sony Pictures’ horror reboot “Resident Evil” secured the top spot at the mainland China box office for the third consecutive weekend, grossing RMB37.6 million ($5.6 million) over the Oct. 23–25 frame, according to data from Artisan Gateway. Since rolling out during the Golden Week holiday corridor on Oct. 5, the film has […]
content:
Constantin Film and Sony Pictures’ horror reboot “Resident Evil” secured the top spot at the mainland China box office for the third consecutive weekend, grossing RMB37.6 million ($5.6 million) over the Oct. 23–25 frame, according to data from Artisan Gateway.

Since rolling out during the Golden Week holiday corridor on Oct. 5, the film has generated a cumulative haul of $64.8 million.

New Classics Pictures’ crime procedural drama “Traces of Justice” held onto second position, taking in $4.7 million in its fourth weekend. Directed by Chen Sicheng (“Detective Chinatown”) and co-written with Zhang Ji and Yan Zijie, the period investigation epic has lifted its cumulative cume to $92.4 million since premiering on Oct. 1. Starring Zhang Yi, Ma Li, and Chen Minghao alongside guest appearances by Karry Wang, Fan Chengcheng, and Chen Feiyu, the multi-decade drama chronicles an elite public security detective unravelling major criminal mysteries based on real cases.

Beijing Joy Fun Pictures’ domestic body-swap comedy “Mr. & Mrs. Pardon” remained in third place, generating $2.6 million over the three-day weekend to lift its cumulative gross to $55.5 million. Directed by Shen Chunyang and written by Ma Duo, the satirical feature stars real-life comedic pair Shen Chunyang and Xiao Shenyang alongside Jia Bing and Yu Yang as an uninspired middle-aged couple forced to navigate marriage and domestic friction after swapping bodies.

Popular on Variety

Dirty Monkeys’ war comedy-drama “Once Upon a Time in the Middle East” took fourth position in its eleventh weekend of release, collecting $800,000. Directed by Wen Muye (“Dying to Survive”) and starring Shen Teng, Jiang Qiming, Aarif Rahman, and Omar Sherif, the enduring summer blockbuster has amassed a cumulative total of $355.5 million since launching on Aug. 11.

Pearl Studio’s computer-animated fantasy comedy “All Wishes Come True!” rounded out the top five, pulling in $600,000 over its two-day weekend frame. Directed by Mu Zhengyang, the long-running family hit has reached a cumulative total of $306.6 million across 15 weeks in release since opening on July 18.

Mainland China’s overall weekend box office dropped to a muted $18.6 million, reflecting a pronounced post-holiday slump across the theatrical landscape. The 2026 year-to-date box office reached $4.7 billion, trailing the same period in 2025 by 29.1%.

title: ‘Moon Knight’ Star May Calamawy Fronts ‘Night Feeds,’ Opener of New Tokyo Horror Festival Yami (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: “Night Feeds,” a psychological horror short from Rana Roy starring May Calamawy (“Moon Knight”), will open the first edition of the Yami International Film Festival, Tokyo’s new showcase for horror and darker genre fare. “Breeder,” from Alex Goyette, will close the festival, which runs Nov. 20–26 at Human Trust Cinema Shibuya. The event is run […]
content:
“Night Feeds,” a psychological horror short from Rana Roy starring May Calamawy (“Moon Knight”), will open the first edition of the Yami International Film Festival, Tokyo’s new showcase for horror and darker genre fare.

“Breeder,” from Alex Goyette, will close the festival, which runs Nov. 20–26 at Human Trust Cinema Shibuya.

The event is run by Yami Inc., a Japanese company known for horror exhibitions and other genre-themed attractions. Its goal is to introduce Japanese audiences to new horror filmmakers from home and abroad. An open call ran from late May to the end of August and brought in 182 entries from 40 countries and territories. Six features were picked for the feature competition and eight shorts for the short competition.

Yami chose to open with a short and close with a feature. The organizers believe both formats will shape where the genre goes next.

Popular on Variety

“Night Feeds” was made at the American Film Institute. It follows a new mother whose isolation and anxiety become tangled up with dread about a war in the world outside, until it’s hard to tell what’s real and what’s a nightmare. Calamawy’s credits also include Lee Cronin’s “The Mummy.”

“Breeder” is a horror thriller that mixes dark comedy with scares in a story built around breeding. Dot-Marie Jones, a multiple Emmy nominee for “Glee,” plays Patti, a character pushed close to madness.

Roy and Goyette will both travel to Tokyo to sit on the jury. Japanese actress Sukezane Kiki, whose international credits include “Heroes Reborn,” “Lost in Space” and “Westworld,” completes the three-person panel.

The feature competition includes two Asian premieres: Zoe Berriatúa’s Spanish title “Buffet Libre” and Abner Pastoll’s South Korea-U.K. co-production “Nervous.” The other four features will have their Japan premieres. On the shorts side, Rick Kawanaka’s Japanese entry “The Pot” will be the festival’s only world premiere. Katagiri Eriko’s “When You Open the Door” will screen as a special presentation.

Producer Wada Arihiro (“Silver Express,” “Fujiko”) is the festival director and also heads programming.

“Physical terror, psychological horror, the unease lurking beneath the everyday, and dark humor. The films presented at Yami each explore ‘fear’ in their own distinctive ways,” Wada said. “Rather than simply fitting within the boundaries of established genres, we sought out films that unsettle the senses, challenge expectations, and reveal new forms of fear. Come to Shibuya, Tokyo, and experience the cutting edge of horror from around the world.”

The lineup:

Feature Competition

“Species,” Marion Le Corroller (France, Belgium)

“Buffet Libre,” Zoe Berriatúa (Spain)

“Hold to Death: Hand in Hand,” Alex Wang (Taiwan)

“Gaua,” Paul Urkijo Alijo (Spain, U.S.)

“Nervous,” Abner Pastoll (South Korea, U.K.)

“No Rest for the Wicked,” Kasper Kalle (Denmark, Iceland)

Short Competition

“Idols,” Matt Halsall (South Korea, Japan, U.K.)

“The Pot,” Rick Kawanaka (Japan)

“Dormant,” Cris Gavrilova (Russia)

“Bestiary,” Anne Zinn-Justin (France)

“Amira,” Javier Yañez Sanz (Spain)

“Hollow Paths,” Francesco Madeo (Italy)

“Floor,” Jo Bareun (South Korea)

“Happy,” Victor Basallote (Spain)

Opening Film

“Night Feeds,” Rana Roy (U.S.)

Closing Film

“Breeder,” Alex Goyette (U.S., Canada)

Special Screening

“When You Open the Door,” Katagiri Eriko (Japan)

title: Eric Bauza Dies: Voice Of Bugs Bunny & Daffy Duck In ‘Coyote Vs. Acme’ & Much More Was 46
summary: “He followed in the footsteps of giants like Mel Blanc.” So said Channing Dungey, Chairman, Warner Bros. Television Group and US Networks tonight after the family of Eric Bauza announced the death of the most recent voice actor behind characters like Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, including in this year’s much-loved Coyote vs. Acme. Bauza […]
content:
“He followed in the footsteps of giants like Mel Blanc.”

So said Channing Dungey, Chairman, Warner Bros. Television Group and US Networks tonight after the family of Eric Bauza announced the death of the most recent voice actor behind characters like Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, including in this year’s much-loved Coyote vs. Acme. Bauza was 46.

Filling the shoes of the legendary Mel Blanc at Looney Tunes was no small task, but the Emmy-winning Bauza did so capably for years. Dungey called Bauza an “incredible talent.”

Besides the two biggies, other Looney Tunes characters he brought to life included Tweety, Foghorn Leghorn, Pepé Le Pew, Porky Pig, Road Runner, Elmer Fudd and Marvin the Martian. He voiced many of those characters in Looney Tunes Cartoons, for which Bauza last year won the first ever Children’s and Family Emmy Award for Outstanding Voice Performance in an Animated Program.

Watch on Deadline

That alone would have been a career, but Bauza also voiced Stimpy, the animated Luke Skywalker, Puss in Boots, Bam-Bam Rubble, Donatello, Leonardo, the animated Jason Bourne, Robert “Big Bob” Belcher, Woody Woodpecker, Two-Face, Jimmy Olsen and Aquaman.

Said Dungey in a statement: Eric Bauza was a unique voice talent who brought joy and laughter to millions around the world. During his 15 years at Warner Bros. Animation, he was the voice of Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck among countless other characters. He followed in the footsteps of giants like Mel Blanc. Eric said that carrying on the legendary legacy of the Looney Tunes was among the greatest honors of his life. In addition to his incredible talent, Eric was a treasured part of our animation family. Our hearts go out to his loved ones.

title: James Gunn Claps Back At Critics Of Continuity In His DCU
summary: With DC’s Clayface in theaters this weekend and Marvel’s Avengers: Doomsday barreling toward us, users online have been playing compare/contrast. One commenter apparently had questions about the connectivity between the projects in the DC Cinematic Universe being created by James Gunn and Peter Safran. Listing six recent projects — Superman, the Peacemaker series, Supergirl, the […]
content:
With DC’s Clayface in theaters this weekend and Marvel’s Avengers: Doomsday barreling toward us, users online have been playing compare/contrast.

One commenter apparently had questions about the connectivity between the projects in the DC Cinematic Universe being created by James Gunn and Peter Safran. Listing six recent projects — Superman, the Peacemaker series, Supergirl, the animated Creature Commandos, Clayface and the much-lauded series Lanterns — the person is question asks, “What’s this building towards??????”

Reposting that comment on Threads, an account called lostuslandcomics replied, “Gunn doesn’t have to build towards anything if the individual pieces work on their own…I think the MCU reprogrammed people’s expectations.”

Watch on Deadline

Gunn commented over the weekend, “I couldn’t agree more. DCU is just an alternate universe; we can enter at any location or time and tell THAT story. I dislike the idea that individual stories aren’t meaningful unless they lead to something else.”

The co-CEO of DC Studios went on to point out that “Star Wars has essentially been doing this for 50 years across movies, shows, games and books.” He added that his Superman Saga — which continues with next year’s Man of Tomorrow — “contains many characters we’ve introduced in other stories. But that doesn’t mean those other stories only exist to set up what’s happening there.” (Marvel might argue that that “only exist” bit is a little reductive.)

He ended with, “I would love people to be seeing ‘Clayface’ because it’s a great, fun horror movie unto itself, not because of where else Clayface will show up three movies from now.”

Here is Gunn’s reply in full:

I couldn’t agree more. DCU is just an alternate universe; we can enter at any location or time and tell THAT story. I dislike the idea that individual stories aren’t meaningful unless they lead to something else. People not understanding this is strange to me, because Star Wars has essentially been doing this for 50 years across movies, shows, games and books, admittedly without the tonal variety. Now, this doesn’t mean there isn’t connectivity.

The Superman Saga starts with Superman and travels into Man of Tomorrow and onward, and contains many characters we’ve introduced in other stories. But that doesn’t mean those other stories only exist to set up what’s happening there. I would love people to be seeing ‘Clayface’ because it’s a great, fun horror movie unto itself, not because of where else Clayface will show up three movies from now.

title: Donald Trump Posts 1,300+ Word Sunday Night Diatribe About “Complete And Total Loser” Bill Maher, Nine Days After Praising Their “Great Dinner”
summary: Donald Trump posted more than 1,300 words slamming Bill Maher, just nine days after praising the “great “dinner at the White House with the Real Time host. Trump was upset over some of the jokes and comments that Maher made on Friday’s show. Maher praised the Oct. 15 dinner too, at which they were joined […]
content:
Donald Trump posted more than 1,300 words slamming Bill Maher, just nine days after praising the “great “dinner at the White House with the Real Time host.

Trump was upset over some of the jokes and comments that Maher made on Friday’s show. Maher praised the Oct. 15 dinner too, at which they were joined by Stephen A. Smith and Kid Rock, but his Friday show apparently set Trump off, including Maher’s references to the president’s low approval numbers.

Trump wrote on Truth Social, “There were so many other falsehoods Bill spewed, but I won’t waste time in FACT CHECKING him. He isn’t worth it. Bill: Don’t call anymore. It’s useless, and tell Chuck LaBella not to call so much, and say how much you love ‘TRUMP,’ and want to get together, because you’re a hopeless guy, who is just trying to cater to your small group of ‘fans.'” LaBella is a longtime producer with Maher.

In his Truth Social post, Trump called Maher a “pothead” and said he “looked like hell this time.” The president also challenged Maher’s claim that the dinner lasted four hours.

Watch on Deadline

Trump wrote, “Overall, I thought it was a good meeting. It didn’t last four hours, it lasted two hours, maybe less, and everybody was happy. We have the timestamps. I learned nothing, and felt it was a waste of time.”

A spokesperson for Maher did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Trump’s post is a bit of deja vu. Maher dined at the White House last year and later was complimentary to Trump, but the president later attacked the host and deemed the experience a “total waste of time for me to have this jerk at the White House.” In June, the Kennedy Center Board (which is appointed by the president) honored Maher with the Mark Twain Prize. Then another dinner was arranged for earlier this month, and Trump initially deemed the evening “very informative.”

“Smart people. Stephen A. is great. Bill Maher — I will tell you what. He likes me a lot more than people understand, and I actually like him. It was a good dinner,” Trump told reporters last week.

On Friday, Maher’s guest was former White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt, who stayed loyal throughout. During the interview, Maher called Trump “half sane.”

At the White House dinner, Maher said, “We have a nice conversation and he goes, ‘You’re my enemy. Pass the peas.’ I mean, he will say that, ‘You’re my enemy,’ and then a minute later, we’re just talking normally, and we don’t act like enemies.”

In his monologue, Maher made a joke about Ohio Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy running an ad featuring Democrat Amy Acton’s mother, saying she doesn’t trust her daughter. Ramaswamy has defended the spot, even though Acton says her mother stayed with her step father. He was charged with sexually abusing the younger Acton when she was a child.

Maher joked, “Trump said this is fair game. A 12-year-old rape victim is fair game? I know that looks bad. It sounds better on a birthday card to Jeffrey Epstein.”

Trump wrote on Truth Social on Sunday, “After the first dinner, Bill Maher was friendly, I guess, everyone walked away pleased. He gave me a good first show, with lots of Laughing Machine laughter, which is a real term, but it is what it is, and then reverted back to his former self, and his old ways. I understand that. He’s doing his thing. I never took it very personally. I would always mock his Low Ratings, whenever I heard. He’s not a nice guy, and what he spouts isn’t what he believes. He has to cater to his base, which is mostly composed of Losers, and people who don’t like working.”

title: Holland Taylor Reveals Why She Didn’t Renew Her ‘Two And A Half Men’ Contract
summary: At the time of his very public meltdown and split from Two and a Half Men, Charlie Sheen was one of sitcom TV’s highest-ever paid stars at a reported $1.8 million an episode. One of his co-stars let her contract lapse after Season 6 for very different reasons. Holland Taylor, who played the overbearing mother […]
content:
At the time of his very public meltdown and split from Two and a Half Men, Charlie Sheen was one of sitcom TV’s highest-ever paid stars at a reported $1.8 million an episode. One of his co-stars let her contract lapse after Season 6 for very different reasons.

Holland Taylor, who played the overbearing mother of Sheen and Jon Cryer’s characters, says she no longer wanted to be tied to the show by contract.

“When the six years was up, I said, ‘I don’t want to be on a contract anymore but I will visit the show occasionally if you want,'” Taylor recalled recently on the Alchemy with Anthony Mason podcast.

“In fact, they were astonished because when your contract runs out is when people usually back up the [Brink’s] truck,” she said. “And they never paid me very well on that show. I was paid on that show what I had made on a series like eight years before or something.”

Watch on Deadline

Taylor also points out that she was a four-time Emmy nominee for the show.

“They said, ‘We can’t pay you any more money.’ First of all, I said, “You could actually pay me the cost of this building, but don’t bother because I don’t want to continue on under contract.”

The Emmy-winning actress says the powers that be on the CBS show kept arguing about money.

“They said, ‘But we can’t afford to give you more.’ I said, ‘I’m cool with it. I just will come back as a guest some from time to time.'”

Taylor did, however, point out that, along with Sheen massive salary, others on the show got pay bumps.

“John quadrupled his salary or something like that,” she said.

“I loved a lot about that show,” she continued, “but they were not full of courtesies.”

title: ‘Young Sheldon’s Emily Osment Reveals She Requested An Intimacy Coordinator For Teen Co-Star Montana Cooper: “He Was A Baby!”
summary: When it comes to intimacy coordinators, Emily Osment was an early adopter. The Young Sheldon actress didn’t want one for herself, but rather for her co-star, Montana Jordan. As they shot the show in the early part of the decade, the plot called for Jordan’s Georgie Cooper to become romantically involved with Osment’s Mandy McAllister. […]
content:
When it comes to intimacy coordinators, Emily Osment was an early adopter.

The Young Sheldon actress didn’t want one for herself, but rather for her co-star, Montana Jordan.

As they shot the show in the early part of the decade, the plot called for Jordan’s Georgie Cooper to become romantically involved with Osment’s Mandy McAllister. In real life, Jordan was 18 and Osment was 29.

Osment recently recalled her reaction in Jessica Radloff’s book, Young Sheldon: The (Juicier-Than-Meemaw’s Brisket) Inside Story of the Hit Comedy, via People.

“My concern wasn’t the discomfort of making out with someone after just meeting them; I’m an actor, so that’s something I’m used to. My discomfort was that he was eighteen,” said Osment. “And that made me uncomfortable. He was a baby! A baby with a mullet.”

Watch on Deadline

Osment began her career as a child actress, first in two of the Spy Kids films and then as Lilly Truscott on Hannah Montana. That may helped her feel protective over her young co-star. (Her brother is Sixth Sense star Haley Joel Osment.) She said Jordan was “such a sweet kid,” and even if he was uncomfortable with the scenes she feared that “he would just eat his discomfort.”

Osment continued: “I don’t know if Montana even knew if he could ask for that.”

At the very least, she wanted her co-star to know help was available. “Like, let’s give him the option, too. Make him comfortable.”

Alex Reid — who directed many of Mandy’s episodes — supported the decision.

“She was totally right. She was a thousand percent right,” he told Radloff. “We don’t have sex scenes on the show, so it wasn’t a muscle we were used to using, and they were just kissing. But we totally dropped the ball on that.”

He added, “Obviously they worked that out, and they have a great chemistry now, but that was kind of embarrassing.”

Young Sheldon co-creator Steve Molaro said Osment “had every right” to ask for an intimacy coordinator, before adding that she was “later comfortable without one.”

title: Tokyo Film Festival Opens With ‘Sukiyaki’ and a Plea for Peace as Japan’s Government Restates Global Content Ambitions
summary: The 39th Tokyo International Film Festival opened Monday with a rain-soaked red carpet and a ceremony at Hulic Hall, where Japan’s government used the occasion to restate its goal of selling JPY20 trillion ($133 billion) worth of Japanese content overseas by 2033. The festival received 1,892 film submissions from 112 countries and regions this year. […]
content:
The 39th Tokyo International Film Festival opened Monday with a rain-soaked red carpet and a ceremony at Hulic Hall, where Japan’s government used the occasion to restate its goal of selling JPY20 trillion ($133 billion) worth of Japanese content overseas by 2033.

The festival received 1,892 film submissions from 112 countries and regions this year. It opened with “Sukiyaki,” which tells how the title tune was written and went on to top the U.S. Billboard chart in 1963. Director Zeze Takahisa took the stage with Okada Junichi, who plays composer Nakamura Hachidai, Matsuzaka Tori, who plays lyricist Ei Rokusuke, and Seino Nana, who plays Nakamura Junko.

Zeze said the film is set in the years after the war, as Japan entered its period of rapid economic growth, and that its founding idea is the war itself and how the characters come to think about what peace means. “Through this film, I hope this festival, too, can become a festival of peace,” he said.

Popular on Variety

Matsuzaka said the shoot began in April last year and that the film had taken a little over a year to reach audiences. “It isn’t just about enjoying the music. It’s a film where you can feel the live energy, as if you were actually in the venue,” he said.

Seino said she had watched her co-stars’ stage performances from the audience seats during filming. “Seeing everyone’s souls colliding, going beyond their roles, really moved me,” she said.

In a video message played during the ceremony, Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae said her cabinet has designated content, including film, as a strategic priority under its Japan growth strategy, with public-private domestic investment set to accelerate. To reach the 2033 target, the government plans production support for Japanese films and efforts to attract foreign location shoots.

“Film has the power to connect people’s hearts across countries and regions, and to deepen understanding of diverse cultures and values,” Takaichi said.

Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry Akazawa Ryosei said overseas sales of Japanese content have already grown to around JPY6.1 trillion ($40.7 billion), and that the government has sought roughly JPY250 billion ($1.67 billion) across ministries in its fiscal 2027 budget request to support growth investment in the content industry.

Akazawa pointed to the fifth “Kingdom” film, which made the franchise the first series in film history to see five consecutive installments pass JPY5 billion ($33 million) at the box office, with a cumulative gross above JPY30 billion ($200 million). He also noted that the festival’s Centerpiece film, “Godzilla Minus Zero,” the follow-up to Oscar visual effects winner “Godzilla Minus One,” will open worldwide next month, including in Japan, Asia and North America.

Festival director Hisamatsu Takeo, who said he is approaching 50 years in the film business, thanked guests for turning out in bad weather before declaring the festival open. “There are so many kinds of film in the world, each with its own appeal and its own way of being enjoyed,” Hisamatsu said. “Nothing would make me happier than sharing the appeal of such diverse and varied cinema with all of you and enjoying it together.”

Filmmaker Rolf de Heer, president of the competition jury, which also includes actor Watanabe Makiko, DI colorist Yov Moor and producers Oh Jungwan and Alex Lo, recalled seeing an Ozu film more than 50 years ago. “I still remember one shot, so perfect. And Oshima, and of course Kurosawa. ‘Dersu Uzala’ is in my brain,” de Heer said. “So we as the jury are very privileged to be able to work in the country of those masters.”

Actor and singer Nakajima Kento, serving as TIFF Navigator, said walking the carpet carried a special sense of occasion. “It was raining today, but I felt it was a blessing of rain that would help the future of film flourish even more,” he said.

Among those on the carpet were director Milcho Manchevski and the cast of “Sister Brother Manhole Cover,” including Sara Klimoska, on her third visit to Tokyo. Director Qiu Jiongjiong led the cast of “Fuxi: Four Tales of Feasting,” and Indonesian auteur Garin Nugroho the “Red Before Dawn” team.

Judy Ongg represented “Sunshine Women’s Choir,” a gala selection title billed by TIFF as Taiwan’s No. 1 hit. Ongg won best actress at the seventh Taiwan Film Critics Society Awards, was nominated for best supporting actress at the 28th Taipei Film Awards and is nominated in the same category at the upcoming 63rd Golden Horse Awards.

The carpet also welcomed Academy CEO Bill Kramer, Academy president Lynette Howell Taylor and chief membership, impact and industry officer Meredith Shea, who are in Tokyo for TIFF’s Academy in Tokyo program.

“This is the first time the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences has participated in an international film festival. To be part of such a major platform as the Tokyo International Film Festival makes this especially meaningful, and we feel honored to be here,” Kramer said.

title: Lula’s Election Win: How Taylor’s Swift’s Advice to Fandom Helped Him to a Historic Victory and Defeat for Trump
summary: Don’t expect Brazilian filmmakers to return emails on Monday. Many will be sleeping off joyously celebrating. In a historic turnaround election victory, leftist incumbent Lula staged a dramatic run-off comeback victory Sunday, beating far-right Flávio Bolsonaro to secure a fourth term as Brazil’s President. This is the first time in the history of Brazil’s democratic […]
content:
Don’t expect Brazilian filmmakers to return emails on Monday. Many will be sleeping off joyously celebrating. In a historic turnaround election victory, leftist incumbent Lula staged a dramatic run-off comeback victory Sunday, beating far-right Flávio Bolsonaro to secure a fourth term as Brazil’s President. This is the first time in the history of Brazil’s democratic elections that a candidate who has come second in the first-round elections has won the second round.

The win is a defeat for U.S. President Donald Trump, a Bolsonaro ally, and a victory for Brazil’s film industry, which had feared a decimation of governmental movie funding in line with Javier Milei’s huge cuts in Argentina if Bolsonaro were to win.

Popular on Variety

Lula’s turnaround victory marks a huge win for Brazil’s environment, social politics and health services and stops Latin America’s slide to the right as Europe faces that possibility in France and Spain.

Confirmed by Brazil’s electoral authority, with Lula taking 51.79% of the vote, his triumph is also one for fandom as the election was fought on social media before polling booths. In an unprecedented online wave, the day after Lula came second in the first round, fan accounts for major artists such as Billie Eilish, Lady Gaga, Katseye, Demi Lovato, Harry Styles, Katy Perry, and Selena Gomez ignited a movement, offering their massive platforms to amplify the current president’s campaign and help boost their access to young audiences. More than 600 Brazilian fanbase groups came out in support of Lula in the run-up to the Oct. 25 election, according to the Guardian.

“I’m not sure whether to open this speech with ‘comrades’ or ‘fandoms from all over Brazil’,” Lula said earlier this month, starting a speech at a rally on São Paulo’s Avenida Paulista which attracted a crowd estimated by its organizers at over a million.

“We’re inspired by these artists, and Taylor is always talking about how young people should take the lead,” said Josiane, a Swiftie in São Paulo, quoted by the same source.

Social media was reckoned Lula’s Achilles’ Heel, with his own Workers’ Party accusing Meta’s platform Instagram of restricting the reach and sound of its posts, as well as Lula’s profile and visibility on search engines.

On Oct. 19, Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court (TSE) gave Meta 24 hours to show that it is not favouring one presidential candidate over the other in its content feeds. (Meta denied any bias but admitted some of Lula’s campaign ads were taken offline temporarily due to technical errors.)

In parallel, federal deputy André Janones, a Lula supporter, launched a WhatsApp broadcast channel called “Lula’s Army,” which featured a 90-minute interview with Lula and scaled to 10 million-plus members by runoff time.

Brazil’s predominantly left-leaning film industry and its international counterpart have not stood on the sidelines. Guillermo del Toro, Pedro Almodóvar, Mark Ruffalo, Tilda Swinton and Javier Bardem among many more joined Brazilian stars to urge a vote for Lula, holding up their forefinger and extending their thumb in an “L” sign repeated on stage by Jordan Firstman when he appeared at the Rio Film Festival early October to present “Club Kid.”

Variety reported on site in detail from the RioFest’s RioMarket, in an article which went viral in Brazil how, having talked for an hour on a panel with Rodrigo Santoro, renowned director Marcelo Gomes lifted his hand and makes an “L” sign. “The room bursts into applause.” That was before the first-round election.

Two days later on Oct. 4, where Flávio Bolsonaro won a leading 47.03% to Lula’s 45.16%, the festival was sunk in a “visible veil of grief and gloom,” Variety reported.

Over the last two years,Brazilian cinema has exploded on the world stage, Walter Salles’ “I’m Still Here” winning an International Feature Oscar and Kleber Mendonça Filho’s “The Secret Agent” a record four Academy Award nominations for a Brazilian film this year. Gabriel Mascaro’s “The Blue Trail” scooped the Berlin Festival’s Grand Prize in 2025. Now, Variety reported, Brazilian cinema was “at risk.”

That has not come to happen. In an acceptance speech on Oct. 25 Lula promised governmental moneys for healthcare, books and culture.

With Lula’s fourth mandate, Brazil looks set to remain a huge oasis of progressive pro-film governmental policies, aiding filmmakers throughout the region, seen in the latest films, for example, of Rodrigo Teixeira.

Much of Latin America’s film industry, looking to Brazil for co-production partnership and as a bastion of democracy, will share Lula’s supporters’ jubilation and a sense of relief.

title: Trump Calls Bill Maher a ‘Complete and Total Loser,’ Tells Him ‘Don’t Call Anymore’ in Lengthy Truth Social Post
summary: President Donald Trump lashed out at Bill Maher in a 1,300-word Truth Social post on Sunday after tuning into Maher’s late-night show on HBO. “Let’s talk about this COMPLETE AND TOTAL LOSER, Bill Maher,” Trump wrote at the top of the post, a few days after the pair’s second dinner together at the White House. […]
content:
President Donald Trump lashed out at Bill Maher in a 1,300-word Truth Social post on Sunday after tuning into Maher’s late-night show on HBO.

“Let’s talk about this COMPLETE AND TOTAL LOSER, Bill Maher,” Trump wrote at the top of the post, a few days after the pair’s second dinner together at the White House.

Trump went on to call “Real Time With Bill Maher” a “Low Rated Show” and said HBO, once a home for quality programming in his view, had lost its heat. He also claimed Maher had long wanted him as a guest on the program, and said that would never happen.

Much of the post dealt with the latest dinner, which Trump said Stephen A. Smith and Kid Rock also attended. Trump alleged that Maher was drunk and had a drink in hand while touring the White House. He also called Maher a “major POTHEAD” and said the comedian “looked like hell this time.”

Popular on Variety

“It didn’t last four hours, it lasted two hours, maybe less, and everybody was happy,” Trump wrote. “We have the timestamps. I learned nothing, and felt it was a waste of time.”

Trump placed responsibility for both meetings on Chuck LaBella, a business associate of Maher’s who he said had worked as a “gofer” on NBC’s “The Apprentice.” According to Trump, LaBella and Kid Rock repeatedly pushed for a sit-down, and LaBella phoned 10 times before the second dinner was arranged.

“My first response was, ‘Fellas, this guy’s a Goofball,’” Trump wrote.

The president also disputed points Maher had made on air since the visit. He rejected Maher’s comments on his approval numbers and support among Republicans, citing CNN polling that he said put him at 98% to 99% within the party, and defended his endorsement record. He also took issue with Maher’s views on Iran and accused him of lying about illegal voting in California.

Trump denied ever planning a pool for the press briefing room. “I am thinking about moving the Press, and putting them in a different location, but I will use that location for very badly needed space,” he wrote.

Trump praised former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt for her appearance as a guest on “Real Time,” though he described the person putting questions to her as a “biased, dumb SLEAZEBAG.” He told Maher to switch off what he called his “Laugh Machine” and said he would ask Republicans to stop covering the comedian.

“I never watched your show much, but I will never watch it again, because it is nothing more than FAKE NEWS that America, and the World, is unfortunately subjected to,” Trump wrote.

Maher first dined with Trump at the White House in late March 2025, at a meeting brokered by Kid Rock, and afterward described the president on “Real Time” as “gracious and measured.”

title: ‘VelociPastor 2’ Leaves FilmQuest Audience Roaring, Celebrating Human-Made Films in an AI Era
summary: Who knew that one of this year’s giddiest celebrations of filmmaking would be a movie where the stunt dummies are obvious, the dinosaur costumes are obviously homemade and you can literally see the strings on special effects shots? That’s the joy of “VelociPastor 2,” the long-awaited sequel to 2017’s “The VelociPastor.” The first film was […]
content:
Who knew that one of this year’s giddiest celebrations of filmmaking would be a movie where the stunt dummies are obvious, the dinosaur costumes are obviously homemade and you can literally see the strings on special effects shots?

That’s the joy of “VelociPastor 2,” the long-awaited sequel to 2017’s “The VelociPastor.” The first film was a modern cult comedy classic made on a $36,000 budget, which followed the adventures of Doug Jones (Gregory James Cohan), a man of God who turns into a bloodthirsty dinosaur while he’s cleaning up his neighborhood from pimps and drug dealers, and his girlfriend Carol (Alyssa Kempinski).

“VelociPastor 2” is even more ambitious, moving the action to “Italy” and spinning a yarn of a giallo-esque killer who is targeting area virgins. While the scope has widened, the low budget still keeps things charmingly ramshackle. Even after raising $118,297 on Kickstarter, all of the seams are still showing. But the effect is a tribute to low-budget filmmaking, poking fun at everything from wild inconsistencies that any script supervisor would have caught (the opening scene features Doug putting on a crucifix again and again) to wildly long pieces of exposition delivered via ADR.

Popular on Variety

The Sunday FilmQuest screening of “VelociPastor 2,” a festival known for attracting audiences filled with indie filmmakers, was primed to enjoy the movie and laughed boisterously throughout. Beyond the jabs at the joys and flaws of low-budget filmmaking, the movie is filled with plenty of other jokes in the spirit of “Airplane!” that kept spirits high.

There was also a sense of gratitude that so many of the jokes showed affection for the “let’s put on a show” enthusiasm that inspires both films. A frequent topic of discussion at the Provo, Utah-based festival has been the infiltration of AI in the industry, which is met with near-universal distrust and disinterest. In fact, one of the biggest applause points before every screening at the fest is a promise that the feature presentation doesn’t include AI.

But the joy of “VelociPastor 2” is the knowing silliness of low-budget filmmaking gone wrong, something that would be too complex to try to craft an AI prompt. Whether it’s miniatures that don’t show the true scope of Italian city life or two extras playing a ferocious game of Frisbee without actually tossing a disc, it feels like a uniquely human satire.

During a post-screening Q&A, director and cowriter Jesse Gouldsbury and some members of the creative team shared stories of how difficult it was to get “VelociPastor 2” made. But despite the challenges of filming a microbudget dinosaur movie, it was clear through their laughter that they wouldn’t have it any other way.

“VelociPastor 2” is currently seeking distribution. It’s also in the middle of a series of roadshow screenings. Future dates and locations are listed on the film’s official site.
