title: Animated Movie ‘Apple Cadabra – I Shrunk Myself’ Boarded by Epsilon Film (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Epsilon Film has acquired worldwide rights to “Apple Cadabra – I Shrunk Myself,” an animated family adventure movie based on “Petronella Applesauce,” one of Germany’s most successful children’s book series. Epsilon Film will launch international sales on “Apple Cadabra – I Shrunk Myself” at the American Film Market, which runs Nov. 10-15 in Los Angeles, […]
content:
Epsilon Film has acquired worldwide rights to “Apple Cadabra – I Shrunk Myself,” an animated family adventure movie based on “Petronella Applesauce,” one of Germany’s most successful children’s book series.

Epsilon Film will launch international sales on “Apple Cadabra – I Shrunk Myself” at the American Film Market, which runs Nov. 10-15 in Los Angeles, where buyers will get a first look at footage from the movie.

“Apple Cadabra – I Shrunk Myself,” which is produced by the team behind “The Elfkins” and “Rabbit Academy,” centers on two children who are magically shrunk into a miniature world.

Popular on Variety

“Blending fantasy, humor, suspense and adventure with an emotional story about empathy and overcoming prejudice, ‘Apple Cadabra – I Shrunk Myself’ brings the beloved literary franchise to the big screen in a magical family adventure with international appeal,” said Epsilon Film in a statement.

Alice von Einem, managing director of Epsilon Film, said, “What immediately captured our imagination was the idea of two children suddenly finding themselves shrunk into Petronella’s enchanted garden and experiencing an entirely new world from a tiny perspective. The film combines a highly commercial adventure premise with universal themes of friendship, courage and belonging, making it a wonderful family event for audiences around the world.”

The film is directed by Ute von Münchow-Pohl (“The Elfkins,” “Rabbit Academy”) and Felix Schichl. The screenplay is by Claudio Winter (“The Elfkins,” “Rabbit Academy”) and Seraina Nyikos.

Character design is by Oliver Kurth (“Monster Family 2,” “Grand Prix of Europe”). The producers are Dirk Beinhold and Valentin Greulich for Akkord Film, the animation studio behind “The Elfkins” and “Rabbit Academy.” Co-production partners include Seru Animation (“My Fairy Troublemaker”), PFX (“The Whalesinger”), VAST and JewelLabs Pictures. Tobis Film will distribute the film widely in German theaters.

At AFM, Epsilon Film will be based at Suite No. 334, the Fairmont Century Plaza Hotel, Los Angeles.

title: Discover Asia’s IPs & Co-Production Opportunities at Taiwan Creative Content Fest 2026
summary: Organized by the Taiwan Creative Content Agency (TAICCA), the 2026 Taiwan Creative Content Fest (TCCF) will take place from November 6 to 9, 2026, at Taipei Nangang Exhibition Center, Hall 2, 7F. The event continues to serve as a key platform connecting Taiwan with the global content industry, showcasing three flagship pillars: Pitching, Market, and […]
content:
Organized by the Taiwan Creative Content Agency (TAICCA), the 2026 Taiwan Creative Content Fest (TCCF) will take place from November 6 to 9, 2026, at Taipei Nangang Exhibition Center, Hall 2, 7F. The event continues to serve as a key platform connecting Taiwan with the global content industry, showcasing three flagship pillars: Pitching, Market, and Forum.

TCCF PITCHING: Bringing Stories to the Global Stage

2026 TCCF PITCHING announced its lineup of selected projects. This year’s selections demonstrate that international co-productions have become a defining trend across the global film and television industry, with international co-productions led by or involving Taiwan accounting for more than 60% of selected projects. New to TCCF PITCHING this year, each of the four Project Segment pitching sessions (Feature Films, Series, Animation, and Documentaries) will offer its own major prize of at least $30,000, bringing the total prize pool to more than $310,000 (TWD 10 million). Selected teams will also be eligible to apply for up to approximately $93,000 (TWD 3 million) in early-stage development support through TAICCA’s Creative Content Development Program.

TCCF FORUM: Reshaping the Future of Global Content

Under the theme “Reshape,” this year’s TCCF FORUM will present 12 keynote talks and panel discussions over four days, bringing together more than 20 leading experts from Taiwan and around the world to examine the normalization of international co-productions, consolidation among streaming platforms, the rise of IP as a core asset, and the ways short-form content and AI technologies are upending the content industry landscape. TAICCA Chairperson Sue Wang noted that FORUM brings together frontline expertise in IP development, international co-production, and resource integration from Japan, South Korea, France, Thailand, Indonesia, Canada, and Turkey, opening a golden gateway for Taiwan’s creative talent to reach international markets.

TCCF MARKET: Connecting Content with Global Opportunities

At the heart of industry transactions is TCCF MARKET, which this year will bring together 107 exhibitors from seven countries – Taiwan, South Korea, Thailand, Japan, Singapore, France and the Philippines. Focusing on rights transactions for international film and television content and promising IPs, the number of exhibitors in IP categories such as publishing, comics, and characters has increased by 13% year-on-year. The biggest new initiative at this year’s MARKET is TCCF’s first collaboration with Vieshow Cinemas at Mitsui Shopping Park LaLaport Nangang to host the Spotlight Screenings, which offer international buyers, overseas media, and other key industry professionals an exclusive preview of selected high-profile titles.

Registration & Event Information

Registration for FORUM is open now through 11:59 p.m. on November 2, 2026, and is available to TCCF badge holders only. To purchase a badge, please visit the TCCF official website at tccf.tw/en, where detailed session and speaker information is also available.

title: Japan’s Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi Pledges Support For Japanese Film At Tokyo Fest Opening
summary: It was pouring with rain at the opening of this year’s Tokyo International Film Festival, but as Japanese actor and festival navigator Kento Nakajima pointed out, rain symbolizes prosperity, and the local film industry can certainly expect plenty of that in the coming year. Addressing the opening ceremony in a video message, Japan’s Prime Minister […]
content:
It was pouring with rain at the opening of this year’s Tokyo International Film Festival, but as Japanese actor and festival navigator Kento Nakajima pointed out, rain symbolizes prosperity, and the local film industry can certainly expect plenty of that in the coming year.

Addressing the opening ceremony in a video message, Japan’s Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi reiterated the government’s pledge to boost exports of Japanese content to $127BN (JPY20TR) by 2033 as part of its IP360 initiative.

“Under the Takaichi Cabinet, the content sector – including film – has been designated as one of the 17 Strategic Sectors within our Japan Growth Strategy. Guided by our Public-Private Investment Roadmap, we are accelerating domestic investment through close collaboration between the public and private sectors,” Takaichi said.

“To achieve our goal of expanding overseas revenue from Japanese content to 20 trillion yen by 2033, we are committed to providing large-scale, long-term, and strategic support. This includes backing the production of Japanese films capable of moving audiences worldwide, as well as actively attracting international film productions to shoot on location in Japan.”

Watch on Deadline

Speaking on stage at the ceremony, cabinet minister Ryosei Akazawa, whose portfolio includes the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI), mentioned government spend of around $350M (JPY55BN) in the current fiscal year to support the industry.

He also namechecked the latest installment in the blockbuster live-action Kingdom franchise, Kingdom 5: The Clash Of Souls, which was released in Japan in July and has grossed more than JPY6BN ($38M) to date.

“This is the fifth film in the franchise to gross more than JPY5BN at the box office and in total the franchise has made more than JPY30BN ($200M),” Akazawa said. He also cited the upcoming Godzilla Minus Zero, which is playing at Tokyo film festival’s Centrepiece film, as an example of Japanese content that is helping to boost exports

“Japan’s content industry has grown to reach 6.1 trillion yen [$39BN] in overseas sales, establishing itself as a vital pillar of our economy.”

Following the politicians’ speeches, the opening ceremony introduced all the main sections and juries of this year’s Tokyo film festival line-up. Many stars had braved the torrential rain, caused by a typhoon lurking offshore in the Pacfic, to walk the red carpet, including Nakajima, Takumi Kitamura, Tadanobu Asano, Mei Nagano and the team behind the opening film Sukiyaki – director Zeze Takahisa and stars Okada Junichi, Tori Matsuzaka, Nana Seino,

Australian filmmaker Rolf de Heer is heading this year’s main competition jury, which also includes Korean producer Oh Jungwan, French colorist Yov Moor and Japanese actress Makiko Watanabe (New York-based producer Alex Lo was named as a jury member but couldn’t make it).

De Heer said: “Whether it’s as an actor, colorist, producer or director, we on this jury are all filmmakers – and as filmmakers we have directly or indirectly been influenced by the great Japanese masters. For me, I remember an Ozu film more than 50 years ago, and can still remember one shot that was so perfect. So we as jury are very priviledged to be able to work in the country of those masters.”

Takahisa Zeze said of his opening film: “This film is set during the time right after the war in Japan, a time of extraordinary economic growth, and we’ve tried to capture that period. The characters in the film are all thinking and acting on what they could do to achieve peace. We hope this festival also serves as festival for peace.”

title: BBC Pays $530,000 To ‘Mr. Nobody Against Putin’ Exec Over Antisemitism Claims
summary: The BBC has paid £400,000 ($534,000) to one of the exec producers behind Oscar-winner Mr. Nobody Against Putin, who told The Telegraph she was the victim of antisemitism at the broadcaster. Lucie Kon was commissioning editor at documentary strand Storyville before leaving last year after several years in post. She told The Telegraph she was […]
content:
The BBC has paid £400,000 ($534,000) to one of the exec producers behind Oscar-winner Mr. Nobody Against Putin, who told The Telegraph she was the victim of antisemitism at the broadcaster.

Lucie Kon was commissioning editor at documentary strand Storyville before leaving last year after several years in post. She told The Telegraph she was victimized after the October 7 attacks and was told Zionists like her were “evil,” amongst other claims.

Kon said she formally complained to BBC management via a grievance and appeals process. While we understand an internal BBC investigation did not uphold her complaint, she has now been awarded a £400,000 payout, the first of its kind from the BBC over antisemitism claims.

“I think I became a problem,” Kon told The Telegraph. “I think I made too much noise about being a Jew inside the BBC. I stood up for my community. I was open about being a Zionist.”

Watch on Deadline

As a Storyville commissioning editor, Kon was one of the EPs on Mr. Nobody Against Putin, which won the Oscar for Best Documentary feature earlier this year. Her other credits include We Will Dance Again and Sundance winner One in a Million.

In the wake of October 7, antisemitism has been an issue the BBC has struggled to get to grips with and documentary strand Storyville is in the eye of the storm. Just after October 7, then-Storyville lead commissioning editor Emma Hindley generated headlines after embracing a director on stage who was later accused of making antisemitic remarks. The BBC later said the hug was due to the director being “visibly distressed” and not an endorsement of his views.

A BBC spokeswoman said: “While we do not comment on individual staffing matters, antisemitism in any form is not tolerated at the BBC. If allegations or concerns are raised, they are taken seriously and investigated in accordance with our policies. We have robust procedures in place to deal with any behaviour that is contrary to our values.”

title: Disney+ Among Buyers For RTÉ & BBC Drama ‘The Walsh Sisters’
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Disney+ is among a raft of buyers for RTÉ and BBC comedy-drama The Walsh Sisters. Based on a book series from bestselling author Marian Keyes, Season 1 was Irish broadcaster RTÉ’s highest-rated drama of the past two years. The BBC and RTÉ have greenlit a Season 2 of the show, which is in production. […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Disney+ is among a raft of buyers for RTÉ and BBC comedy-drama The Walsh Sisters. Based on a book series from bestselling author Marian Keyes, Season 1 was Irish broadcaster RTÉ’s highest-rated drama of the past two years. The BBC and RTÉ have greenlit a Season 2 of the show, which is in production.

Disney+ has now snagged second window rights for the UK, meaning The Walsh Sisters will launch on the streamer after it has played on the BBC. The show is distributed by Cineflix Rights, which did the deal. It has also sold the show to TV2 in Norway, TV4 in Sweden and MTV Oy in Finland. Pickbox has snagged the show for the Balkans. Yes has taken it for Israel.

Stan was already on board for Australia and Roku’s Howdy streamer has just acquired it for the U.S.

Watch on Deadline

The Walsh Sisters is the story of the dysfunctional but lovable Walsh family of five sisters, their mother, and bemused father. Set and filmed in their Dublin hometown, it follows the sisters as they navigate life’s messiness, including secrets, family feuds, and moments of grace.

In Season 2, Caroline Menton (Oddity), Danielle Galligan (House of Guinness), Máiréad Tyers (Extraordinary), Stefanie Preissner (How to Adult) and Louisa Harland (Derry Girls) reprise their roles as the five sisters. As well as starring, Preissner adapts the Keyes’ books for TV. Aidan Quinn (Legends of the Fall) and Carrie Crowley (Hope Street) also return as the sisters’ parents.

“The comedy, drama and emotion woven through the lives of the closely-knit Walsh family and their loved ones has really been taken to heart by audiences,” said Sandra Piha, SVP, Sales, Pan-Regional, UK, Eire, and Nordics, Cineflix Rights, who brokered the Disney+ and Nordic deals. “We’re thrilled to be bringing the series to more viewers around the world through these latest deals, and we can’t wait to see where their stories go next in Season 2.”

The deals with TVNZ and BBC (Netherlands) were closed by Chris Bluett, SVP, Sales, Asia Pacific and Benelux; the Pickbox and Yes deals were closed by Lucy Rawson, VP, Sales, German-speaking Europe, CEEMEA, and Southern Mediterranean.

The series is produced by Cuba Pictures, part of Vice Studios, and Metropolitan Pictures for RTÉ, in association with the BBC, Screen Ireland, and Cineflix Rights.

title: Ted Sarandos Shrugs Off U.S. Troubles To Mark Netflix’s 10 Years In Korea
summary: He might be under fire in the U.S., but Ted Sarandos was all smiles in Korea this weekend. The Netflix co-CEO took to the stage at an event in Seoul marking the streamer’s tenth anniversary in Korea, from where the likes of Squid Game, Kpop Demon Hunters and Kingdom have come. Korea was one of […]
content:
He might be under fire in the U.S., but Ted Sarandos was all smiles in Korea this weekend.

The Netflix co-CEO took to the stage at an event in Seoul marking the streamer’s tenth anniversary in Korea, from where the likes of Squid Game, Kpop Demon Hunters and Kingdom have come. Korea was one of Netflix’s biggest bets financially, and has proven one of its most important markets.

“Ten years ago, we dreamed big, but none of us could have imagined that Korean stories would move hearts around the world, and land right at the center of global culture,” said Sarandos.

“For Netflix, Korea is more than a market. It is where we discovered new possibilities, and where we learned how far a story can travel, and it is one of our most treasured partners for the future we are building together. To every creator, every actor, every crew member, and every fan in Korea: thank you, from the bottom of my heart.”

Watch on Deadline

Sarandos was speaking after a difficult period for Netflix, during which its shares tumbled despite decent third quarter results. Wall Street remains spooked amid mass layoffs at the streamer and a share price that has fallen sharply throughout 2026.

Netflix countered criticism of its performance in the U.S. by pointing to international titles such as Plastic Beauty, The Secret Woman and The Perfect Lie, which are on track to become the most-watched titles ever in Japan, Denmark and the Netherlands, respectively.

The Korea event will have been a further tonic for Sarandos, with the likes of Lee Jung-lae, Lee Byung-hun and Park Hae-soo from Squid Game, Ahn Hyo-seop from Kpop Demon Hunters and stars from D.P., Physical 100, Hellbound, Mask Girl, Culinary Class Wars, The Devil’s Plan and Agent Kim Reactivated taking to stage at the Korea Fan Festival at the Sangnam Oil Tank Culture Park. The event ran October 24 and 25.

Stars from upcoming shows Possible Love, Tantara, Grand Galaxy Hotel, She, Wolf (fka Beauty in the Beast), All of Us Are Dead Season 2 and Solo Leveling also appeared at the event, where Netflix outlined a series of stas to highlights its local impact.

Top non-English content

Netflix said Korean content was the most-watched non-English language content on the app and that over 80% of subscribers watch it. The streamer launched in the country on January 6, 2016.

The streamer noted flagged that more than 200 Korean titles had hit its Global Top 10 chart in the past five years, with Squid Game Season 1 unsurprisingly staying there the longest (32 consecutive weeks). Teach You a Lesson was noted as the tenth most-watched non-English title in the streamer’ history, with all three seasons of Squid Game in the top ten.

Other stats thrown out include working with more than 80 Korean production companies, filming taking place in more than 100 towns and cities, and a third of its originals being led by first-time writers and/or directors.

title: Sharjah Film Festival Partners With UAE’s Media Authority in Push to Assist Emerging Filmmakers
summary: The Sharjah Intl. Film Festival for Children and Youth is adding a federal partner to its push to build a more substantial and sustainable pipeline for emerging filmmakers. The organization behind the festival signed an agreement with the UAE’s recently established National Media Authority covering areas from film screening procedures to training and technical support. […]
content:
The Sharjah Intl. Film Festival for Children and Youth is adding a federal partner to its push to build a more substantial and sustainable pipeline for emerging filmmakers. The organization behind the festival signed an agreement with the UAE’s recently established National Media Authority covering areas from film screening procedures to training and technical support.

The memorandum of understanding was signed Monday on the opening day of SIFF’s 13th edition by the National Media Authority and FANN – Media Discovery Platform, the Sharjah organization that runs the festival and whose name derives from the Arabic word for “art.” The agreement makes the authority an official supporting partner of SIFF while establishing broader cooperation between the two organizations.

Popular on Variety

The partnership comes as SIFF increasingly looks beyond screenings and workshops to the practical hurdles facing young filmmakers trying to enter the industry. Ahead of the festival, SIFF director Sheikha Jawaher bint Abdullah Al Qasimi told Variety that learning to make a film represents only one part of that journey.

“Our agreement with the National Media Authority reflects this commitment,” Al Qasimi said Monday. “It is an important step in bringing together national efforts to support the film industry and help emerging filmmakers turn their ideas and perspectives into creative work.”

The new agreement addresses another piece of that infrastructure. The National Media Authority will help facilitate permits required to screen participating films, coordinating, where necessary, with embassies, consulates, cultural organizations and government entities. Festival teams will also receive training on the authority’s electronic services and technical support intended to streamline regulatory procedures.

The agreement comes during a period of restructuring for the UAE’s media landscape. Established by federal decree in December 2025, the National Media Authority took over functions previously held by the UAE Media Council, National Media Office and Emirates News Agency, bringing media regulation and development under a single federal body. Its mandate includes media policy and legislation, licensing and content standards.

“Supporting content created for children and youth is an important part of our strategy to develop a competitive and sustainable national media sector,” National Media Authority secretary-general Mohammed Saeed Al Shehhi said Monday.

For FANN, the agreement adds a federal institution to an ecosystem Al Qasimi has argued must extend beyond the festival itself. SIFF’s expanding Industry Hub and pitching program are designed to connect filmmakers with producers, supporters and funders, with the aim of turning introductions into financing, production support and longer-term collaborations.

The agreement also allows National Media Authority representatives to participate in festival juries and film evaluations, while the two organizations will collaborate on SIFF’s media and communications activities.

SIFF runs through Nov. 1, with 71 films from 38 countries in its selection.

title: Instagram Is Testing Ability to Share Videos up to 90 Minutes Long and Launches on Apple TV — but Unlike YouTube, It’s Still Not Going to Pay Creators
summary: Meta’s Instagram is trying to make itself a place for longer-form entertainment content from digital creators, including testing out video lengths of up to 90 minutes and letting users watch Reels and more on Apple TV. The moves are meant to position Instagram as a bigger potential competitor to YouTube. But for now, Instagram is […]
content:
‘s Instagram is trying to make itself a place for longer-form entertainment content from digital creators, including testing out video lengths of up to 90 minutes and letting users watch Reels and more on Apple TV.

The moves are meant to position Instagram as a bigger potential competitor to YouTube. But for now, Instagram is still not planning a revenue-sharing program akin to YouTube’s that would compensate creators for sharing their work on the platform.

Instagram announced the test of the new features in (of course) a video shared Monday on the platform.

Popular on Variety

“I have been against doing long-form video on the platform for a long time,” Instagram head Adam Mosseri said in the video, alongside VP of product Tessa Lyons. Mosseri said that one of his concerns has been “how do we make sure that we keep Instagram not just about entertainment, but about connecting with friends.”

But now, Mosseri has been sold on the need for Instagram to “lean into” long-form videos.

The new Instagram Features (which it is testing in the U.S. with a small group of creators) allows longer horizontal videos to Instagram, in some cases up to 90 minutes long. Creators can also share clips as Reels to help people discover a long-form feature video. And soon, Instagram Lives will show up beyond just a creator’s followers, to be discovered by new audiences in the Reels tab. Instagram also is planning to introduce a new feature that will let you use your phone as a remote control for playback of videos on TVs.

“Creators can build a fuller body of work on Instagram, while fans have more ways to discover and keep up with what they love,” an Instagram rep said.

As for whether Instagram will introduce an ad-revenue share in the future, the Instagram spokesperson said “it’s too early to share a long-term monetization model, but we’re exploring ways for creators to earn from brands, fans and Instagram, including performance-based incentives. Over time, we think there will be compounding benefits for creators to tell new stories, reach new audiences, and find new partners, which should lead to many monetization opportunities.”

title: Walter Koenig, Chekov on Original ‘Star Trek,’ Dies at 90
summary: Walter Koenig, who memorably played Chekov in the original “Star Trek” series and seven “Star Trek” feature films, died Sunday in Los Angeles, Variety has confirmed. He was 90.  His reps said in a statement, “Today we mourn the passing of Walter Koenig, whose talent, warmth, and unforgettable performances left a lasting mark on generations […]
content:
Walter Koenig, who memorably played Chekov in the original “Star Trek” series and seven “Star Trek” feature films, died Sunday in Los Angeles, Variety has confirmed. He was 90.

His reps said in a statement, “Today we mourn the passing of Walter Koenig, whose talent, warmth, and unforgettable performances left a lasting mark on generations of fans around the world. He passed of old age at home in North Hollywood last night surrounded by his daughter and niece.

“Best known for his iconic role as Pavel Chekov in ‘Star Trek: The Original Series,’ Walter helped inspire audiences with his optimism, humor, and adventurous spirit. Beyond ‘Star Trek,’ his long and distinguished career showcased his versatility as an actor and his genuine love for his craft. His remarkable talent continued to shine in his later years, most recently with his performance in the short film ‘Mr. Fleischmann,’ for which he received the Platinum Award for Best Actor at the 2026 Independent Shorts Awards — a fitting recognition of a lifetime devoted to his craft.

“Walter’s legacy extends far beyond the screen. Through countless convention appearances and interactions with fans, he shared his kindness, wit, and appreciation with everyone fortunate enough to meet him. He understood what Star Trek meant to people and embraced the community that grew around it.

“On behalf of all of us, we extend our deepest condolences to Walter’s family, friends, colleagues, and the millions of fans whose lives he touched over the decades.

“Thank you, Walter, for the memories, the inspiration, and for boldly going where few have gone before.”

Koenig’s Chekov, an arrogant young navigation officer in the original series, was introduced to the series to appeal to teenage viewers — his hairstyle recalled that of the Monkees’ Davy Jones.

The Russian-born Chekov was also used to poke fun at the Soviet way of falsely taking credit for every important human invention.

Koenig played Chekov in the 2015 TV movie “Star Trek: Renegades,” set at a time in which the character has been elevated to admiral. The film, aimed as a backdoor pilot for a new “Star Trek” television series, was funded through crowdsourcing.

The Chekov character was not included in “Star Trek: The Animated Series” in the early ’70s because of the show’s limited budget, but Koenig penned an episode of the series entitled “The Infinite Vulcan.”

Koenig’s Chekov was central to the plot of 1982’s “Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan” and consequently the actor enjoyed considerable screen time in the film, generally considered the best of the “Star Trek” movies.

Koenig was also associated with another sci-fi franchise, J. Michael Straczynski’s “Babylon 5,” in which he played the evil Psi Cop Alfred Bester (named by the show’s creators after the science fiction writer). He appeared in 12 episodes of that show from 1994-98.

Walter Marvin Koenig was born in Chicago. The family of Russian Jewish heritage was originally named Koenigsberg, and he attended Fieldston High School in Fieldston, N.Y., where he did some stage work, before starting at Grinnell College in Iowa, where he was initially pre-med; he transferred to and graduated from UCLA with a degree in psychology. After a professor urged him to pursue a career in acting, he began studying at the Neighborhood Playhouse in New York; there his classmates included Christopher Lloyd, with whom he would be reunited on “Star Trek III: The Search for Spock,” in which Lloyd played the villainous Klingon Commander Kruge, as well as James Caan and Dabney Coleman.

Koenig made his small-screen debut with an uncredited role in an episode of “Combat!” in 1962, followed by guest-starring roles on “The Untouchables,” “General Hospital,” “The Alfred Hitchcock Hour,” “Ben Casey,” “Gidget” and “I Spy.” After the original “Star Trek” series went off the air in 1969, he worked occasionally in TV, guesting on “The Virginian,” “Ironside” and “Columbo” (in an episode that had William Shatner as the special guest star). He played a deputy sheriff in an unremarkable low-budget film called “Nightmare Honeymoon,” starring Dack Rambo.

During the 1980s, when he was busy with the “Star Trek” movies, he appeared as Pompey in a 1984 TV adaptation of “Antony & Cleopatra” that also featured Nichelle Nichols and future “Star Trek: Enterprise” actor James Avery.

The actor appeared in a string of low-budget science fiction movies over the years, including “Moontrap,” in which he starred, and “Deadly Weapon,” both in 1989; as well as Cynthia Rothrock martial arts vehicle “Sworn to Justice” in 1996 and independent horror film “Mad Cowgirl” in 2006.

A one-character film that Koenig wrote and performed, “You’re Never Alone When You’re a Schizophrenic,” was screened at the 1996 New York Film Festival.

He voiced Chekov in a variety of “Star Trek” video games, including 1998’s “Starfleet Academy: Chekov’s Lost Missions.”

The actor guested on an episode of the CBS sitcom “Almost Perfect” titled “Where No Woman Has Gone Before” in 1997 and voiced himself on a 2002 episode of “Futurama” titled “Where No Fan Has Gone Before,” which also featured the voices of William Shatner and Leonard Nimoy, among other “Star Trek” regulars. He also guested on “Diagnosis Murder” (in an episode that featured several other “Star Trek” actors) and “Son of the Beach.”

He penned the 2008 sci-fi legal thriller “InAlienable,” in which he also appeared (the tagline was “From the mind of Walter Koenig”).

Koenig also had a stage career that spanned three decades.

In the early 1990s he toured with Mark Lenard (who played Spock’s father Sarek on “Star Trek”) in “The Boys in Autumn,” in which Koenig played a middle-aged Tom Sawyer reunited after decades apart with Lenard’s Huckleberry Finn.

Koenig also directed theater, including “Hotel Parsadiso” for Company of Angels, “Becket” for Theatre 40, “America Hurrah!” at Oxford Theater, “Twelve Angry Men” at the Rita Hayworth Theatre, “Matrix” at the Gascon Theatre Institute and “Three by Ten” at Actors Alley in Los Angeles.

Koenig taught acting classes at UCLA, at Actors Alley and elsewhere.

His satiric fantasy novel “Buck Alice and the Actor-Robot” was re-released in 2006; he created the comic book “Raver” published by Malibu Comics. In 2013 Bluewater Comics published the graphic novel “Walter Koenig’s Things to Come.”

Koenig penned the memoirs “Chekov’s Enterprise: A Personal Journal of the Making of Star Trek — The Motion Picture,” published in 1980, and “Warped Factors — A Neurotic’s Guide to the Universe,” published in 1998.

Anton Yelchin portrayed a much younger Chekov in the rebooted “Star Trek” films.

Back in the days of the original “Star Trek” series there was a period of tension between Koenig and George Takei, who played Sulu, but the two came to be close friends, and in September 2008, Koenig served as best man at Takei’s wedding to Brad Altman.

Koenig a daughter, actress-writer Danielle Koenig. A son, actor and editor Andrew Koenig, died in 2010.

title: Harry Styles Waltzes His Way Through ‘Coming Up Roses’ Music Video
summary: Harry Styles puts his waltzing skills to the test in the video for “Coming Up Roses,” the latest single to get the music video treatment from his fourth album “Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally.” For the clip, Styles reunites with directing duo Bradley & Pablo, who helmed the videos for “Watermelon Sugar” and “Late […]
content:
Harry Styles puts his waltzing skills to the test in the video for “Coming Up Roses,” the latest single to get the music video treatment from his fourth album “Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally.”

For the clip, Styles reunites with directing duo Bradley & Pablo, who helmed the videos for “Watermelon Sugar” and “Late Night Talking.” Throughout the visuals, he waltzes with various partners before a woman does an interpretive dance to the song. In the end, they all come together for a photo finish, smiling for the camera.

Styles initially hinted at the release of the music video during the 27th of 30 shows at New York City’s Madison Square Garden on Saturday night. The singer is currently on his “Together, Together” tour, which will conclude its MSG residency on October 31. He’ll wrap up this leg of the trek in Melbourne and Sydney in November and December before picking back up in Glendale, Arizona in April.

Following his Arizona shows, Styles will perform a series of shows in respective cities including Arlington, Pasadena, Toronto, Chicago, Berlin, Nanterre, Madrid, Rome and Dublin. He’ll bring this live era to a close with three shows at London’s Wembley Stadium on August 24, 27 and 28.

Variety recently broke the news that famed documentary director John Wilson has been rolling cameras on Styles at MSG since August, capturing footage for a doc expected to blend live performances with a glimpse into Styles’ world. One source described it as featuring authentic human stories of everyone involved in the tour, from the singer and his fans to the countless others behind the scenes.

Styles most recently released his fourth album “Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally” this past March. The project, led by the single “Aperture,” debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 with 430,000 equivalent album units.

title: Music Industry Moves: Mary J. Blige Sells Music Catalogs to Primary Wave; Stella Lefty Signs With Make Wake for Management; Boyz II Men Ink With Warner Records Nashville
summary: Mary J. Blige has sold undisclosed shares of her publishing and recorded-music assets to Primary Wave Music, the company announced on Monday morning. Included in the deal are some of Blige’s greatest hits, including “Family Affair,’ “My Life,” “Mary Jane (All Night Long),” “You Bring Me Joy,” “Be Without You,” “I Can Love You,” and […]
content:
Mary J. Blige has sold undisclosed shares of her publishing and recorded-music assets to Primary Wave Music, the company announced on Monday morning. Included in the deal are some of Blige’s greatest hits, including “Family Affair,’ “My Life,” “Mary Jane (All Night Long),” “You Bring Me Joy,” “Be Without You,” “I Can Love You,” and others; further details were not announced.

Known universally as “the Queen of Hip-Hop Soul,” over the course of her three-decade-plus career Blige has sold an estimated 50 million records worldwide across 15 studio albums, two live albums and 83 singles, which have garnered her nine Grammy Awards amid 37 Grammy nominations, two Oscar and one Emmy nom. She was honored with a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 2018 and inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2024. She kicked off her first-ever Las Vegas residency, “Mary J. Blige: My Life, My Story.” The 20-date residency began this past May and will run through February 2027 at Dolby Live at Park MGM.

Natalia Nastaskin, Primary Wave’s Chief Content Officer, said “From the moment I heard ‘You Remind Me’ on NY’s KISS-FM, I became a Day 1 Mary J. Blige fan. For over 30 years, she has gifted the world with hit after undeniable hit and in the process has created the soundtrack of our lives. To partner with the Queen herself on her extraordinary catalog and her everlasting legacy is an honor for me and for our entire Primary Wave team.”

* Sandlot-Atlantic Outpost recording artist Stella Lefty, who is enjoying one of the biggest hits of the year with “Boston,” has signed with Nashville-based Make Wake Artists for management representation. At the company, which also manages Luke Combs, Lefty will be managed by founder and CNO (Chief Navigation Officer) Chris Kappy and managing partner Sophia Sansone.

Launched in 2015, the company’s roster includes Jon Bellion, Flatland Cavalry, and Dylan Marlowe, among others.

“Stella’s connection to her fans reminds me of Luke’s fan connection very early on… It is real!!!,” Kappy said in a statement. “Stella has the talent, authenticity and drive to build something truly special, and our team is committed to helping her realize that potential.”

+ Veteran vocal group Boyz II Men have signed with Warner Records Nashville and will launch an all-new country project, scheduled for release in 2027. Since emerging from Philadelphia with their 1991 debut, “Cooleyhighharmony,” the group has sold an estimated 60 million albums worldwide and wont four Grammy Awards and a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame.

“Boyz II Men’s global influence is decades in the making,” shared Warner Records Nashville Chair & President, Cris Lacy. “Every genre and culture has benefited from their original music, and their impact on artists in the current country landscape, while perhaps surprising to some, is quite profound. When I learned that growing up listening to artists like Randy Travis was seminal in their desire to collaborate with Nashville’s award-winning singers and songwriters, I knew we had to be a part of it.”

+ Pop vet JoJo has partnered with Seeker Music, which has acquired the singer-songwriter’s original and re-recorded versions of her first two albums – “JoJo” and “The High Road” – as well as future releases and projects. The celebration kicks off with Seeker’s release of a deluxe 20th anniversary edition of “The High Road,” featuring the original album and four bonus tracks from the original 2006 editions, as well as acoustic versions. Jojo has also collaborated in the past with Seeker CEO and founder Evan Bogart; Seeker already held interest in two of her hits via deals with other cowriters.

“Deciding who to trust with such a personal and important part of my catalog wasn’t something I took lightly,” Jojo said. “Over time it was heartening to learn more about Seeker’s ethos and see how involved and passionate Evan is — someone who truly understands artists because he is a creator himself. It feels full-circle to have both versions of these albums together with a team committed to finding new ways to amplify it.”

Bogart added, “I’ve personally been such a fan for so long, and it means the world to all of us at Seeker to be partnering with her. This is just the beginning!”

+ Believe has named Mel Curley as Global Head of Editorial & Marketing Partnerships. Based in New York, Mel will report to Darya Pourshasb, Believe’s Chief Marketing Officer. According to the announcement, Curley will lead Believe’s global EMP strategy, strengthening relationships with key digital platforms and unlocking new editorial and promotional opportunities to support artists and labels growth and international development across Believe’s Artist Services, Label & Artist Solutions and TuneCore.

She joins from Amazon Music, where she served as Global Head of Independent Label Relations, overseeing relationships with more than 350 independent distributors, labels and artists. Previously, she held senior positions at Arista Records and at Sony Music Entertainment.

Pourshasb said, “As competition for audience attention intensifies, our ability to connect artists and labels with fans across digital platforms has never been more important, which is why Editorial and Marketing Partnerships are a key pillar of our music marketing strategy. Mel brings an exceptional combination of DSP expertise, music industry experience and strategic vision.”

+ Hybe Americas has announced the launch of Tru Records, a new record label “created to discover and develop the next generation of Latin pop artists,” according to the announcement. Latin music veteran Alejandro Mejía will be the company’s first general manager, and its first artist is Santos Bravos, the first Latin pop group created by Hybe Americas.

“The launch of Tru Records represents a unique opportunity to champion Latin American talent and bring it to new audiences around the world,” Mejía said. “Starting this new chapter with Santos Bravos and with the support of Hybe Americas allows us to build careers with international reach while staying true to our Latin identity and the stories we tell.”

title: Reed Hastings On Netflix Shakeup, YouTube Rivalry And How Streamer Can Go Back To “Being Thrilling”
summary: Netflix co-founder Reed Hastings ended his three-decade association with the company he co-founded last June, but he has a lot to say about how the company can get back to “being thrilling.” The exec said he “read about” Netflix laying off 1,000 workers, about 6% of its staff, but did not know in advance about […]
content:
Netflix co-founder Reed Hastings ended his three-decade association with the company he co-founded last June, but he has a lot to say about how the company can get back to “being thrilling.”

The exec said he “read about” Netflix laying off 1,000 workers, about 6% of its staff, but did not know in advance about this month’s cutbacks.

“It’s hard because I’d like to be in the fray helping,” he said in an appearance on the podcast On with Kara Swisher. “Those are traumatic moments, saying goodbye to some people and getting other people to focus on, ‘OK, we really need to take up our creative excellence and just to be supportive.’ But they’re very competent people. They’ll figure it out. So I’m not worried about it.”

Along with the staff cuts, Netflix also overhauled its executive ranks, replacing content chief Bela Bajaria with Peter Rice and ousting film head Dan Lin. Amid the overhaul, Swisher asked if the company’s new leaders should significantly retool the company’s approach to programming given the recent slowdown in viewership growth.

Watch on Deadline

“I think the strategy is doing more and better television shows, more and better movies,” he replied with characteristic directness.

Hastings added that the company would do well to return to its roots, albeit with newer offerings like live sports now in the mix. “The core brand property is about being thrilling,” he said. “We realized, it took a long time, that we could be distrusted, we could be disliked, but we can never be boring, OK? That the essence of an entertainment brand is to be thrilling.”

The co-founder also weighed in on YouTube, whose share of viewing on TV screens continues to increase as Netflix remains in a holding pattern. He noted key differences between the companies’ business models. “They have 3 million paid creators who are fighting for attention,” he said. While that population occasionally introduces blockbuster cultural properties like Obsession and Backrooms, he said it still represents “an incredibly small amount of viewing on YouTube. And it took a while to develop it. It’s the stuff that’s very attention-grabby. So in hacking attention, YouTube’s platform is very good. … It’s a highly tuned machine for attention and it’s winning viewing hours.”

Asked whether Netflix should lean into short-form fare, Hastings zoomed out to the bigger picture of entertainment’s evolution. “If you look at the beginning of television in the 1950s and 1960s, movie viewing went way down because suddenly there’s this new hot object, television,” he said. “And then movies got a lot better in the 1970s. There was a whole creative revolution in the pacing and the realism. And then movies fought back and became, again, up until the internet or up until Covid, really a substantial art form. So I would say the parallel there is, you know, YouTube is the television and that example and where the movies is we have to take up the creative bar and push ourselves to be ever more gripping, real, connecting, and do what we do – I say we. Which they do incredibly well.”

Swisher pushed Hastings on Netflix’s ill-fated pursuit of an acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studios-and-streaming division, a move that continues to weigh on the company’s stock. The former Netflix chief noted that Paramount paid Netflix a $2.8 billion breakup fee as part of clinching its $110 billion purchase of all of WBD and forming Skydance.

“At the price that we had bid, we were really happy,” Hastings recalled of the jockeying with Paramount. “Then the price went up a bunch and it seemed a bridge too far. … We could have done it. It’s not a ‘can’t,’ but a ‘choose not to.'”

Netflix’s Co-CEO structure, a unique setup in corporate America, was implemented first with Hastings and Ted Sarandos and then with Sarandos and Greg Peters.

Asked why it has worked well at the company, Hastings offhandedly said he didn’t expect it to remain common “over the next 100 years of Netflix.”

Swisher paused on that line, asking Hastings why he believed the company would endure for another century.

“Because I think humans are going to be around, and you love entertainment,” he replied.

title: ‘Young Americans’ Hulu Pilot Sets Five For Lead Roles Opposite Scott Foley
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Hulu has cast its five young leads for D.C. drama pilot Young Americans: Billie Boullet (Man on Fire), Sam Rechner (Scream 7), Mia Isaac (Black Cake), newcomer Oscar Winter Iannone, and Lauren Mei (Avatar: The Last Airbender). The actors join Scott Foley, whose casting as U.S. President Judd Burchfield was first announced. Boullet will […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Hulu has cast its five young leads for D.C. drama pilot Young Americans: Billie Boullet (Man on Fire), Sam Rechner (Scream 7), Mia Isaac (Black Cake), newcomer Oscar Winter Iannone, and Lauren Mei (Avatar: The Last Airbender).

The actors join Scott Foley, whose casting as U.S. President Judd Burchfield was first announced.

Boullet will play Julia Burchfield, the independent, sharp-witted daughter of the President, who, after a year of isolation following her older sister’s mysterious death, is desperate to reclaim a normal teenage life by enrolling at the elite Capitol Crest, her sister’s alma mater.

Rechner plays Rome Washburn, the brooding and charismatic son of a controversial senator, who finds himself increasingly disillusioned with the political world he was born into and desperate to forge an identity of his own.

Watch on Deadline

Isaac plays Saskia Carmichael, the beautiful, calculating adopted daughter of a powerful Washington media dynasty and the queen bee of Capitol Crest, who wields her considerable social influence with ruthless precision.

Iannone plays Hogan Young, the charming, cocky and ambitious son of the Vice President, who has every intention of following his father into politics — and ultimately surpassing him.

Mei plays Harper Sinclair, a precocious, fiercely intelligent scholarship student at Capitol Crest who becomes Julia’s unlikely guide to the school’s treacherous social hierarchy, concealing a mischievous and mysterious streak beneath her buttoned-up exterior.

In Young Americans, from writer-EPs Chris Hutton & Eddie O’Keefe, as the children of the nation’s elite battle it out at Capitol Crest Academy in Washington D.C., their teenage dramas begin to mirror the larger political games of their parents. Amidst the secrets, scandals, and deadly ambitions, a forbidden romance between two students from opposing political families threatens to escalate tensions to a breaking point.

Bruce Miller, creator of Hulu series The Handmaid’s Tale and The Testaments, is also exec producing alongside Priscilla Porianda via White Oak. 20th Television is the studio.

Most recently seen as the female lead opposite Yahya Abdul-Mateen II in Netflix’s Man on Fire, Boullet previously played Anne Frank in Disney/Nat Geo’s A Small Light. Other credits for the French actress include Brad Anderson’s sci-fi action thriller World-Breaker, BBC’s The Worst Witch alongside Bella Ramsey and Prime Video’s The Power. She is repped by UTA and Curtis Brown.

Rechner broke out with roles in Steven Spielberg’s The Fabelmans and Netflix’s Heartbreak High, which debuted in the streamer’s Global Top 10. Most recently seen in Paramount’s Scream 7, he has Amazon’s untitled Navy SEAL drama starring Alan Ritchson and Taiwanese filmmaker Midi Z’s next feature, The Exiles, coming up. He is repped by CAA, Marquee Management, and Jackoway Austen.

Previously seen in Black Cake, The Perfect Couple and Life Is Strange, Isaac is repped by 3 Arts Entertainment, UTA, and Morris Yorn Barnes.

For Iannone, Young Americans marks a major career milestone — his first booking out of drama school. Originally from Litchfield, Connecticut, he studied at the American Academy of Dramatic Arts. He is repped by Canopy Media Partners and Skrzyniarz & Mallean.

Mei recently wrapped Will Ropp’s film Dedicated to Morris Burke and can be seen in the current season of Netflix’s Avatar: The Last Airbender. Currently studying psychology, cognitive science, and film at Harvard University, she is repped by Juniper Rose Management, CESD, and Goodman, Genow, Schenkman.

title: Abramorama Dances To North American Rights For ‘Make Work’ About New York City Ballet’s Choreographic Institute
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Abramorama has acquired North American distribution rights to Make Work, the documentary commissioned by the New York Choreographic Institute (the Institute) and directed by two-time Emmy-nominated filmmakers Linda Saffire and Adam Schlesinger (Restless Creature: Wendy Whelan) and produced by Saffire, Schlesinger and Adrian Danchig-Waring. The North American theatrical release is being lined up for […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Abramorama has acquired North American distribution rights to Make Work, the documentary commissioned by the New York Choreographic Institute (the Institute) and directed by two-time Emmy-nominated filmmakers Linda Saffire and Adam Schlesinger (Restless Creature: Wendy Whelan) and produced by Saffire, Schlesinger and Adrian Danchig-Waring.

The North American theatrical release is being lined up for March 5, 2027. The film will play at next month’s Doc NYC.

Set inside the studios and stages of The Institute and New York City Ballet, Make Work “offers rare, intimate access to the creative process behind contemporary ballet. The film follows four choreographers, Harrison Ball, Sarah Foster-Sproull, Caili Quan and Houston Thomas, as they develop new work with NYCB dancers, revealing the pressure, experimentation, collaboration and uncertainty that take place before a ballet reaches the stage. With only two weeks to create original work during the Institute’s residencies, the choreographers navigate the delicate balance between honoring ballet’s traditions and pushing against its boundaries.”

Interwoven are reflections from leading choreographers Kyle Abraham, Lar Lubovitch, Annabelle Lopez Ochoa, Justin Peck, Alexei Ratmansky, Pam Tanowitz and Christopher Wheeldon, who share perspectives on their creative practices and the enduring influence of George Balanchine on New York City Ballet and the evolution of ballet itself.

Watch on Deadline

The announcement comes as Danchig-Waring took his final bow with NYCB on Sunday, October 18, 2026, during a farewell performance marking the conclusion of his more than 24 years with the company. In the film, Danchig-Waring, who serves as a producer on Make Work and as Artistic Director of the New York Choreographic Institute, NYCB’s hub of creativity, gives his perspective on the institution and the artists working to shape its future.

Saffire and Schlesinger previously co-directed and produced Restless Creature: Wendy Whelan, which premiered at the New York Film Festival and was released by Netflix, and Sporting Dreams. They also co-produced Smash His Camera, which won Best Director at the Sundance Film Festival. Schlesinger’s producing credits include Ai Weiwei: Never Sorry, which received the Sundance Special Jury Prize and was shortlisted for an Academy Award, as well as Page One: Inside the New York Times and God Grew Tired of Us, winner of both the Audience Award and Grand Jury Prize at Sundance.

“We’ve always been drawn to the moments audiences never get to see,” said co-directors Linda Saffire and Adam Schlesinger. “With Make Work, we wanted to sit in the room while a ballet is being born, when ideas are fragile, when dancers and choreographers are taking real risks together, and when failure is part of the process. What we found was an art form deeply rooted in Balanchine’s legacy and fiercely committed to reinventing itself. These choreographers are asking what ballet can be, and who it can be for, and we hope the film lets audiences feel what it takes to answer that question.”

“For more than two decades, New York City Ballet has been my home, and the studio has been where I’ve learned the most about what it means to be an artist,” said Adrian Danchig-Waring. “The Institute exists to give choreographers the time, space and trust to experiment, and to fail, and that is where the future of ballet is being written. Make Work honors that process and the courageous artists who are shaping ballet’s next chapter.”

“Make Work gives audiences a rare and intimate window into the creative process at one of the world’s most influential ballet institutions,” said Karol Martesko-Fenster, CEO of AB2 Media Group / Abramorama, and Damon G. Smith, SVP of Business Growth and Creative Strategy. “The film captures something universal about making art — the uncertainty, the risk, the collaboration and ultimately the courage required to create something that has never existed before.”

title: Walter Koenig Dies: ‘Star Trek’s Original Ensign Chekov Was 90
summary: Walter Koenig, who originated the role of Ensign Pavel Chekov in the 1960s Star Trek TV series and several subsequent movies about the adventures of the USS Enterprise, has died, according to his rep. He was 90. Zachery McGinnis of Galactic Productions posted Monday on Facebook that Koenig died of natural causes in North Hollywood […]
content:
Walter Koenig, who originated the role of Ensign Pavel Chekov in the 1960s Star Trek TV series and several subsequent movies about the adventures of the USS Enterprise, has died, according to his rep. He was 90.

Zachery McGinnis of Galactic Productions posted Monday on Facebook that Koenig died of natural causes in North Hollywood but did not provide other details. George Takei, who played Sulu on the original Star Trek, also posted on Koenig’s death.

“Walter’s legacy extends far beyond the screen,” McGinnis wrote in part. “Through countless convention appearances and interactions with fans, he shared his kindness, wit, and appreciation with everyone fortunate enough to meet him. He understood what Star Trek meant to people and embraced the community that grew around it.” See the full post below.

Koenig played the Russian-American navigator Chekov for second and third seasons of CBS’ Star Trek series from 1967-69 and reprised the role in Star Trek films from 1979-91. The character’s introduction for Season 2 came at the height of the U.S.-USSR Cold War.

The news comes as the original hugely popular and influential Star Trek series created by Gene Roddenberry is marking its 60th anniversary.

Born on September 14, 1936, in Chicago, Koenig has a brief early career as a dancer before turning to acting. His earliest roles including guest spots on such 1960s TV series as Combat!, The Untouchables, Ben Casey, Gidget, I Spy, The Alfred Hitchcock Hour and Jericho. He also appeared in the 1963 pilot episode of what would become one of TV most popular soap operas, ABC’s General Hospital.

Walter Koenig Everett Collection/Getty Images

But his big break would come with Star Trek in 1967 — the start of a 25-year journey as the navigator of the starship USS Enterprise. The original series launched a universe that has kept tens of millions of Earthlings enthralled for six decades.

“That camaraderie among Star Trek fans became more extensive when they started having conventions,” Koenig said in a2013 interview for the TV Academy Foundation. “It wasn’t only what you’d traditionally call nerds. It was people who had a sense of humanity and a sense of justice. People who had imagination and people who loved monsters. It covered a much larger canvas than was initially thought.”

Star Trek was not widely popular during its initial 1960s run, never placing within the year-end Top 30 among primetime series during its three seasons in an era dominated by rural comedies, westerns and variety shows. Its peak audience was for the pre-Koenig first season in 1966-67, when it ranked No. 52 in the three-network universe. But it began a second life in syndication during the 1970s that made it among the most popular TV series — indeed, media properties — of all time.

Koenig’s TV and film castmate Takei paid tribute to him on Monday, writing:

“My heart is heavy. Walter Koenig, our Ensign Pavel Chekov, passed away early today.



“Walter and I met on the bridge of the Enterprise in the 1960s, and we stayed friends for nearly six decades. When Brad and I married in 2008, Walter stood beside us as our best man. Just last month, on Sept. 14, he turned 90, on the same day Brad and I celebrated our 18th wedding anniversary. I will always treasure that he and I shared that date.



“Walter was more than Chekov. He was a writer, a teacher, a thoughtful man, and a loyal friend. To the fans who loved him for so many years, thank you. He loved you too.



“Rest well, my dear friend. Keep navigating a steady course.

Here is McGinnis’ full post on Koenigs death:

Today we mourn the passing of Walter Koenig, whose talent, warmth, and unforgettable performances left a lasting mark on generations of fans around the world. He passed of old age at home in North Hollywood last night surrounded by his daughter and niece.



Best known for his iconic role as Pavel Chekov in Star Trek: The Original Series, Walter helped inspire audiences with his optimism, humor, and adventurous spirit. Beyond Star Trek, his long and distinguished career showcased his versatility as an actor and his genuine love for his craft.



His remarkable talent continued to shine in his later years, most recently with his performance in the short film Mr. Fleischmann, for which he received the Platinum Award for Best Actor at the 2026 Independent Shorts Awards—a fitting recognition of a lifetime devoted to his craft.



Walter’s legacy extends far beyond the screen. Through countless convention appearances and interactions with fans, he shared his kindness, wit, and appreciation with everyone fortunate enough to meet him. He understood what Star Trek meant to people and embraced the community that grew around it.



On behalf of all of us, we extend our deepest condolences to Walter’s family, friends, colleagues, and the millions of fans whose lives he touched over the decades.



Thank you, Walter, for the memories, the inspiration, and for boldly going where few have gone before.



Rest in peace.



MORE TO COME…

title: CAA Signs Bloodline Banter Comedy Duo
summary: EXCLUSIVE: CAA has signed Landon Mauk and Riley Mitchell, a pair of cousins better known as comedy duo Bloodline Banter. Mauk and Mitchell are a Nashville-based pair with zero filters, too many opinions, and absolutely no plans to mind their own business. They’ve gained an online following with their namesake podcast, where they’ve demonstrated a […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: CAA has signed Landon Mauk and Riley Mitchell, a pair of cousins better known as comedy duo Bloodline Banter.

Mauk and Mitchell are a Nashville-based pair with zero filters, too many opinions, and absolutely no plans to mind their own business. They’ve gained an online following with their namesake podcast, where they’ve demonstrated a knack for making audiences feel like they’re just hanging out with their two most chaotic relatives. On Bloodline Banter, they have the kinds of conversations that only family can produce — ones that usually happen around a kitchen table two hours after everybody should have gone home. Currently, the pod has over 102K followers on Instagram and over 32K on Instagram.

Recently, the duo has begun taking their act to the stage with Bloodline Banter Live!, a show that is part live podcast, part stand-up comedy, and completely unscripted. They sold out their first announced show, in Huntsville, AL, in less than 10 minutes, with 9-10,000 unique customers trying to buy tickets. They accommodated high demand by adding second and third shows at the same venue, which sold out in the same amount of time.

Watch on Deadline

Currently, Mauk and Mitchell are setting touring plans for 2027/2028. Beyond touring, they’re focused on continuing to expand their reach and building out their business around podcasting, DTC/merchandising, brand partnerships, TV conscripted and PPV content.

To get Deadline’s Comedy Means Business newsletter, covering all things comedy, in your inbox, sign up here.

title: ‘Call of Duty’ Movie Will Be About the ‘Cost of War and Having to Be a Warrior,’ Says Director: ‘These Are Not Comic Books or Cartoon Characters’
summary: Paramount Pictures’ upcoming “Call of Duty” movie, based on the massively popular video game franchise, is definitely not going to feel like a comic book tentpole or make soldiers out to be superheroes, director Peter Berg recently told ComicBook. The “Friday Night Lights” and “Lone Survivor” director is helming the video game adaptation from a […]
content:
Paramount Pictures’ upcoming “Call of Duty” movie, based on the massively popular video game franchise, is definitely not going to feel like a comic book tentpole or make soldiers out to be superheroes, director Peter Berg recently told ComicBook. The “Friday Night Lights” and “Lone Survivor” director is helming the video game adaptation from a script by Taylor Sheridan. The movie will draw inspiration from the “Call of Duty: Modern Warfare” games.

“If you really look at the missions and the storylines and the characters like Captain Price, Soap, Ghost and Alex, these are complicated humans. These are not, and no disrespect, cartoon characters or comic books. These are very nuanced storylines; there’s a real soul to the ‘Modern Warfare’ universe. Yes, there’s violence and hardware and equipment and killing. But underneath it, I think the game, and the creators of the game, are really looking at the cost of war, the cost of having to be a warrior who’s, for whatever reason, chosen to put himself between real danger and the rest of us, and the burden that these guys carry.”

Beginning with “Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare” in 2007, the “Modern Warfare” storyline marked the first “Call of Duty” video game to break from the franchise’s original World War II setting. Paramount has yet to reveal any plot details for its upcoming film adaptation, nor has any casting information been made available.

Berg noted at CinemaCon earlier this year that “Taylor and I are both deeply connected to the special ops community” before a sizzle reel highlighted the video game franchise’s continued successes, including 1 billion players and a lifetime revenue of $35 billion.

Paramount announced its “Call of Duty” movie in September 2025. Sources said at the time that while the pact is focused on making one “Call of Duty” movie, the deal included the potential for Paramount to expand the “Call of Duty” universe across film and TV. The movie is currently on Paramount’s release schedule for June 30, 2028.

title: Pasifika Entertainment Advancement Komiti Announces 2026 Writers Fellowship Class
summary: The Pasifika Entertainment Advancement Komiti has named the third cohort of its annual PEAK Writers Fellowship. This year’s cohort includes Kanani Koster, Erin Lau, Sean Oketani, Neil Tinkham and Pouariʻi Tanne. Supported by Netflix, the fellowship selects five up-and-coming writers whose work honors Pasifika (people of Pacific Islander descent) experiences, providing them with mentorship, professional […]
content:
The Pasifika Entertainment Advancement Komiti has named the third cohort of its annual PEAK Writers Fellowship.

This year’s cohort includes Kanani Koster, Erin Lau, Sean Oketani, Neil Tinkham and Pouariʻi Tanne. Supported by Netflix, the fellowship selects five up-and-coming writers whose work honors Pasifika (people of Pacific Islander descent) experiences, providing them with mentorship, professional development and networking opportunities as they continue to expand their professional television careers.

Founded by PEAK co-founder, director, screenwriter and showrunner Dana Ledoux Miller and co-managed by program manager and screenwriter Bryson Chun, the fellowship serves as the only Hollywood writing program created by a Pasifika storyteller.

“I’m so grateful that in this time of industry uncertainty, Netflix continues to invest in emerging writers,” Miller said. “Fellowships like this not only make it possible for our communities to steward our own stories from script to screen, they allow the five incredible writers in this year’s fellowship to challenge and upend expectations of who we are expected to be as artists.”

Each fellow is paired with an experienced industry mentor who helps refine their scripts to be professionally presented. Also included in the fellowship are weekly panels and conversations with writers, showrunners, executives, representatives, actors and other industry professionals, offering insight on the entertainment industry.

This year’s fellows will receive mentorship from Ryan Belezon and Jeffrey Gelber (“Boulevard”); Aminta Goyel (“Pivoting”); Lauren Thompson (“Ghostwriter”); and Michelle Giannusa (“Ripple”).

“We received a record number of applications this year, which shows how sorely this fellowship is needed,” said Averie Huffine, the interim executive director of PEAK. “But I think it’s also due to Netflix being synonymous with great programming, and the reputation of Dana and Bryson’s incredible mentorship.”

See the list of fellows below.

Kanani Koster — “Clinic Daze”

A half-hour dramedy following the ragtag yet passionate staff of an underfunded abortion clinic hustling to provide compassionate care to their patients, all while navigating their own chaotic personal lives.

Koster is a native Hawaiian writer and director. Her work uses raunchy blue comedy to hide a desire to make a difference in this world. Kanani is a 2024 American Film Institute directing alum, 2024 ‘Ohina Lab Fellow and ‘23 Punky Aloha Scholar for Kanaka ‘Ōiwi and Pasifika Creatives. Her work has been supported by the Tribeca Film Festival, Gotham’s Project Market, Visionary Justice Story Lab and the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation. Her shorts have played at AFI Fest, SeriesFest, Hawai’i International Film Festival, and the Smithsonian Museum.

Erin Lau — “The Hālau”

“The Hālau” is a one-hour family drama that follows 16-year-old Maile Johnson who, after her mother’s death, is forced to live with her estranged family on Oahu and enter the world of competitive hula dancing.

The Native Hawaiian filmmaker explores empathy, redemption and legacy through her work. She has been supported by the Sundance Institute, Tribeca Studios, Film Independent, Ryan Murphy’s Half Initiative and more. Her work spans narrative, documentary and episodic storytelling and has been featured on the Criterion Channel, Netflix and PBS.Lu’s most recent directing credit was for Fox’s action-packed procedural “Rescue: HI-Surf.” She is also currently a fellow in the 2026 ImagineNATIVE Screenwriting Series Lab and the Sundance Institute | The Asian American Foundation (TAAF) Accelerator.

Sean Oketani — “[Pair]adise”



Two queer, hapa Hawaiian best friends decide to ditch their jobs as hotel servers and spend the day playing tourists in Waikīkī.

Oketani is a Native Hawaiian writer, director and storyteller born and raised on the island of Oʻahu. He graduated from Chapman University’s Dodge College of Film and Media Arts with a BFA in television writing and production. He wrote and produced his undergraduate thesis, “Gay Church,” a short-form comedy pilot. He has worked across the programming, education, and outreach departments at the Hawaiʻi International Film Festival (HIFF). In 2025, he was selected as an ʻOhina Labs Writers Fellow and received the ʻOhina Judge’s Award for his short film script, currently in pre-production.

His work often draws from the intersection of his identities and perspectives, navigating both lived and inherited experiences. He is passionate about crafting compelling narratives that explore the contradictions and overlaps of identity, culture and belonging. He is inspired by Indigenous and Pasifika cinema; queer art and literature; and the influence of digital culture, both on and offline.

Neil Tinkham — “West Coast Chamorus”



A straight-laced Chamoru father must confront his past as a gangbanger when he returns to Los Angeles with his son for medical treatment.

Tinkham is a Chamoru filmmaker originally from Guam. His work reflects his island upbringing and the Chamoru diaspora community. His short movies have received funding from the Corporation for Public Broadcasting, the Pacific Islanders in Communications and the Guam Council for the Arts and Humanities Agency. His work has screened at film festivals and regional museums and received distribution. In 2018, Neil’s feature-length screenplay “Jungle” was optioned by New Zealand-based production company Popgun Filmmakers, and, in 2022, his screenplay “The Taotaomona” was selected for the Second Annual Indigenous List, compiled by the Sundance Institute, ImagineNative and The Black List. Other scripts Tinkham has written have placed in screenwriting labs and competitions, including the Ohina Filmmakers Lab and the Page International Screenwriting Awards.

Pouariʻi Tanner — “The Assistant”

When a Māori current affairs crew arrives in Hollywood to profile its Indigenous stars, they discover their promised access doesn’t exist and must navigate the assistants, gatekeepers and strange characters operating behind the scenes of the Indigenous entertainment industry.

Tanner is a Cook Islands writer and producer based in Rarotonga. Her work draws on her experience across Indigenous film, television and media, using comedy and character-driven storytelling to explore the strange intersections between island communities and larger cultural institutions. She previously worked with the Sundance Institute’s Indigenous Program and created and produced the documentary series “Turtle Town” in the Cook Islands. She is currently developing three short films through Pasifika TV’s film masterclass, to be completed and released in 2027. Through her production company, Pacific Standard Time, she is developing original film and television projects from the Pacific.

title: Eric Bauza’s ‘Looney Tunes’ Legacy: ‘Coyote vs. Acme’ Producer Says Voice Actor Behind Bugs Bunny and More Had a ‘Deep Love of the Craft’
summary: Chris DeFaria, the former president of animation and innovative technology at Warner Bros. and producer of “Coyote vs. Acme,” shared his thoughts on the sudden death of Eric Bauza, the voice of many “Looney Tunes” characters. I’m heartbroken to share that my friend and colleague Eric Bauza passed away last night. The world lost a […]
content:
Chris DeFaria, the former president of animation and innovative technology at Warner Bros. and producer of “Coyote vs. Acme,” shared his thoughts on the sudden death of Eric Bauza, the voice of many “Looney Tunes” characters.

I’m heartbroken to share that my friend and colleague Eric Bauza passed away last night. The world lost a great voice.

Eric carried the legacy of Looney Tunes with a devotion few bring to their work. He voiced Daffy Duck, Bugs Bunny, Porky Pig, Marvin the Martian, and so many more. And he never treated them as a job. To him, they were icons who deserved to be honored, protected, and kept alive for new generations. He championed these characters tirelessly in every room he walked into.

Eric never forgot whose shoulders he stood on either. He had enormous reverence for Mel Blanc, the master who gave these characters their original voices, and he used to say he was only borrowing Mel’s Cadillac, and that he promised to return the keys when he was done. That was Eric.

A man handed one of the great legacies in animation, who treated it as a trust rather than a trophy. He drove it with love and cared with a little bit of mischief, and he left it in better shape than when he found it.

After Mel’s passing in 1989, the voices he carried by himself were divided among many talented performers.

Then Eric came along.

He started by trying a few of the voices, and in what felt like no time at all, he was doing nearly all of them. It’s a feat that few, if any, had pulled off since Mel himself.

But what Eric achieved went far beyond impressions. Learning the sound of a character is hard enough. Eric did something deeper.

He learned to be them, to think like Bugs, to scheme like Daffy, to stutter and squirm like Porky. That’s why they never sounded like imitations when he performed them. They sounded alive.

What made it more remarkable was that his talent was largely his own. He was self-taught, and he built that astonishing range through curiosity, relentless practice, and a deep love of the craft. You could hear that love in every line. I was lucky enough to share time with Eric at Warner Brothers, and luckier still to have worked alongside him most recently on “Coyote vs Acme.”

Eric had a devilish wit, and was never more alive than when he stepped into those characters with a mischievous spark that made them feel new while honoring everyone who came before them.

And yes, Eric was always late. I like to think that somewhere right now, Bugs, in fact, is tapping his foot and checking his watch, and Eric is strolling in with a grin, a perfect excuse in a line so funny that all is forgiven within seconds.

He was worth the wait every single time.

Thank you, Eric, for the laughter, the artistry, the joy you gave us all. I know you promised to return Mel’s keys when you’re done. Take your time. You always did.

— As told to Jazz Tangcay

title: Jess Gabor and Arthur Langlie to Star in Christina Kallas’ Thriller ‘He Talks to Me’ (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Jess Gabor and Arthur Langlie will star in “He Talks to Me,” a psychological thriller from director Christina Kallas and screenwriter Alejandro Adams, Variety can reveal exclusively. Mike S. Ryan developed the project and will produce through his banner Greyshack Films. Derrick Tseng will also produce. According to an official logline, “He Talks to Me” […]
content:
Jess Gabor and Arthur Langlie will star in “He Talks to Me,” a psychological thriller from director Christina Kallas and screenwriter Alejandro Adams, Variety can reveal exclusively.

Mike S. Ryan developed the project and will produce through his banner Greyshack Films. Derrick Tseng will also produce.

According to an official logline, “He Talks to Me” follows “Melody (Gabor), a young single mother in rural Arkansas, who is followed home by local police officer Bryce Hagan (Langlie) for what begins as a casual interrogation and spirals into a harrowing test of survival, coercion and endurance.” Other cast members include Sayra Player, Adam David Thompson and Ryan Siegel.

Other projects from Kallas, a two-time Berlinale and Slamdance alumna, include “Paris is in Harlem” and “The Rainbow Experiment.” She is a former president of the Federation of Screenwriters in Europe and a member of the Actors Studio.

Gabor recently wrapped production on Tony Goldwyn‘s “Hello Darkness” and can next be seen in a recurring role in Season 3 of “Daredevil: Born Again.” Her other recent film credits include David Michod’s “Christy,” “The Friend” with Bill Murray and Greyson Horst’s “Throuple.” On the small screen, she starred in Season 2 of the Paramount+ series “School Spirits” and had a breakout performance on Season 9 and Season 10 of “Shameless.”

Arthur was last seen in Kent Jones’ 2025 drama “Late Fame,” which starred Willem Dafoe and Greta Lee. His upcoming credits include “Cut Your Teeth,” from director Samuel Goodwin and producer Aaron Moorhead, and” Trash Pandas,” from director Ana Brown and producer Peter Cambor.

Gabor is repped by Anonymous Content, Buchwald, and Jackoway Austen Tyerman; Langlie by UTA; Adams by Range Media Partners; Thompson by CGF Talent; Player by Exclusive Artists Agency; and Siegel by Avenue B Talent.

title: Walter Koenig, Chekov on ‘Star Trek,’ Remembered by George Takei: ‘Keep Navigating a Steady Course’
summary: Walter Koenig’s “Star Trek” colleagues are remembering the actor who played Chekov in the original “Star Trek” series, calling him “a loyal friend.” Koenig died Sunday in Los Angeles. His “Star Trek” co-star George Takei reminisced over Koenig serving as best man at his wedding. Takei, who played Lieutenant Hikaru Sulu, wrote on Instagram, “My […]
content:
Walter Koenig‘s “Star Trek” colleagues are remembering the actor who played Chekov in the original “Star Trek” series, calling him “a loyal friend.” Koenig died Sunday in Los Angeles. His “Star Trek” co-star George Takei reminisced over Koenig serving as best man at his wedding.

Takei, who played Lieutenant Hikaru Sulu, wrote on Instagram, “My heart is heavy. Walter Koenig, our Ensign Pavel Chekov, passed away early today.

“Walter and I met on the bridge of the Enterprise in the 1960s, and we stayed friends for nearly six decades,” the post continued. “When Brad and I married in 2008, Walter stood beside us as our best man. Just last month, on Sept. 14, he turned 90, on the same day Brad and I celebrated our 18th wedding anniversary. I will always treasure that he and I shared that date. Walter was more than Chekov. He was a writer, a teacher, a thoughtful man, and a loyal friend. To the fans who loved him for so many years, thank you. He loved you too. Rest well, my dear friend. Keep navigating a steady course.”

Adam Nimoy, Leonard Nimoy’s son, wrote, “So sad to hear about the loss of Walter Koenig. Such a nice guy and when we were on the convention circuit together a pleasure to hang out with. Here he is with Celeste Yarnall in ‘The Apple,’ one of my favorites of the oddball episodes. Farewell.”

So sad to hear about the loss of Walter Koenig. Such a nice guy and when we were on the convention circuit together a pleasure to hang out with. Here he is with Celeste Yarnall in “The Apple”, one of my favorites of the oddball episodes. Farewell. pic.twitter.com/NuUJvHgR3h — Adam Nimoy (@adam_nimoy) October 26, 2026

Michael Okuda, a scenic artist and technical consultant on several “Star Trek” installments, recalled his interview for the Roddenberry archive, writing, “Mourning the passing of Star Trek legend Walter Koenig.
