title: Parallax Films Boards Sales On ‘Fuxi: Four Tales Of Feasting’ Ahead of Tokyo World Premiere
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Parallax Films has boarded international sales for Fuxi: Four Tales Of Feasting, directed by Chinese artist-filmmaker Qiu Jiongjiong, which is receiving its world premiere in the main competition section of Tokyo International Film Festival. Qiu is known internationally for his debut narrative feature A New Old Play, which won the Special Jury Prize at […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Parallax Films has boarded international sales for Fuxi: Four Tales Of Feasting, directed by Chinese artist-filmmaker Qiu Jiongjiong, which is receiving its world premiere in the main competition section of Tokyo International Film Festival.

Qiu is known internationally for his debut narrative feature A New Old Play, which won the Special Jury Prize at the 2021 Locarno Film Festival.

Rooted in the folklore of China’s Sichuan province, Fuxi: Four Tales Of Feasting unfolds through four separate feasts spanning four millennia, that “bring the living and the dead, gods and ghosts, to the same table”. The word “fuxi” in its title is a Sichuan expression meaning “the joy of the belly”.

Parallax describes the film as a “handcrafted mythic fantasy” referencing Qiu’s unique style of filmmaking that combines painting, theatre and cinema. “Rather than reproducing reality, Qiu uses hand-painted scenic flats, handmade props and theatrical staging to give physical form to his imagination, creating a cinematic universe entirely his own,” Parallax explains.

Watch on Deadline

The cast includes Lee Kang-sheng, Taiwanese filmmaker Tsai Ming-liang’s longtime leading actor, playing two grandmothers in different chapters of the film, marking his first female roles on screen. He is joined by actor-filmmaker Lee Hong-chi, whose directorial debut Love Is A Gun won the Lion of the Future award at Venice, and Annie Chen, known for her role in Netflix series Born For The Spotlight.

Produced by David Tang, Ningyuan Ding and Zhao Jin, Fuxi is a co-production between Hong Kong, Taiwan and Japan. The project received support from international film funds and project markets including Hong Kong-Asia Film Financing Forum (HAF), MPA APSA Academy Film Fund, Red Sea Fund, Doha Film Institute and Network of Asian Fantastic Films (NAFF) at Korea’s Bucheon International Fantastic Film Festival.

The film’s visual world also extends beyond the screen in Fuxi: A Feast For The Universe, Qiu’s large-scale solo exhibition at A4 Art Museum in Chengdu. Bringing together paintings, sets, props and installations, the exhibition translates the film’s imagined universe into a new spatial narrative.

The deal for world sales on Fuxi extends Parallax’s relationship with Qiu, with the company also representing his seven previous films, which include A New Old Play, experimental documentary shorts and documentary features.

title: Donnie Iris, Pittsburgh’s Favorite Rocker, Who Scored Hits With the Jaggerz and as a Solo Artist, Dies at 83
summary: Donnie Iris, regarded as Pittsburgh’s biggest hometown rock hero for a six-decade career that included hit singles in the 1960s and ’80s, died Monday at 83. He had been fighting bladder cancer for three years. Iris’ biggest chart success came as a member of the Jaggerz, who reached No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100 […]
content:
Donnie Iris, regarded as Pittsburgh’s biggest hometown rock hero for a six-decade career that included hit singles in the 1960s and ’80s, died Monday at 83. He had been fighting bladder cancer for three years. Iris’ biggest chart success came as a member of the Jaggerz, who reached No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1970 with “The Rapper” — a song that dealt with “rapping” with girls, not the genre whose name had not yet been coined. That group petered out, but he went on to have continued success, especially regionally, as the frontman of Donnie Iris and the Cruisers in the age of power pop and Midwest rock. A decade after “The Rapper” broke through, Iris had a hit again with “Ah! Leah!,” which reached No. 29 on the Hot 100 in 1980. They had two more mid-level chart hits in 1981 with “Love Is Like a Rock” and “My Girl.” His modest success during that era on the Billboard charts was hardly indicative of just how beloved he was in his native Pennsylvania and the Midwest region, widely seen as being to Pittsburgh what Michael Stanley was to Cleveland. “For my money, he was the most beloved Pittsburgh musician of all time,” Joe Grushecky told the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette. Grushecky, as the leader of the Iron City Houserockers, would have been one of the few other viable candidates for that title. But, as he told the newspaper, “I don’t know anyone who was loved more than Donnie. He just had that warmth about him, and it came through in his performance.” Iris was a trouper to the end, performing his final show less than a month ago, on Sept. 28, at Citizens Live at the Wylie, seated in a chair shortly after having radiation treatment in the afternoon.

“He sang like a bird that night,” his longtime keyboard player and best friend, Mark Avsec, told the Post-Gazette. “It was the first time on a chair, and he didn’t like that. But the poor guy, the cancer was spreading, and he was in pain, and he really wanted to do that show and be with the people.”

Iris began singing in a doo-wop group in high school in the early ’60s, then moved on to rock ‘n’ roll and R&B cover bands before the Jaggerz were formed in 1964. They were eventually signed to Gamble Records, the brainchild of Philly soul greats Kenny Gamble and Leon Huff, and released their first album, “Introducing the Jaggerz,” in 1969.

In the late ’70s, he became a guitarist for Wild Cherry, after that group had already hit the big time with “Play That Funky Music.” It was in the Wild Cherry days that he met Avsec, who continued on with him in Donnie Iris and the Cruisers and continued to perform with him all the way to last month.

They recruited Marty Lee Hoenes, Albritton McClain and Kevin Valentine to complete Donnie and the Cruisers and released their first album, “Back on the Streets,” in 1980, followed by “King Cool” the following year, “The High and the Mighty” in 1982 and “Fortune 410” in 1983 before being dropped by MCA Records in 1984. Even set adrift from major labels, they continued to record into the 2010s.

Iris was championed in 2025 in a well-read blog post by industry pundit Bob Lefsetz, who wrote, “I didn’t buy the solo debut, ‘Back on the Streets,’ but I did buy the follow-up, ‘King Cool.’ The joke, of course, was that Donnie Iris was anything but cool. He was a man whose music was au courant, but whose look was passé, maybe because by time he made it he was in his late thirties, whereas his contemporaries had all made it in their twenties…”

Lefsetz continued, “Donnie specializes in straight-ahead rock, and all his records are very listenable. So I did, listen that is. I know ‘Stagedoor Johnny’ and ‘Never Did I’ by heart, not that you can hear them on streaming services, MCA has only deigned to release the greatest hits. And then Donnie Iris lost his deal with MCA and disappeared. ‘Ah! Leah!’ survived, some people remember seeing him on MTV, but there was no press, no airplay, it’s like he didn’t exist.”

Then, as Lefsetz noted, “Turns out he became a mortgage broker… Sure, Donnie continued to play music, but he needed to pay the rent, put food on the table. You’d be stunned so many of your heroes end up working straight jobs.”

Indeed, per the Post-Gazette, Iris went on to own SimCorp in Aliquippa. He admitted he got some business from customers who wanted to deal with the rock star they’d identified with or grown up with, or whose annual birthday shows they were still going to see. “It got me some business I normally wouldn’t have,” he acknowledged.

Lefsetz was compelled to write about iris by seeing a video of him performing “Love Is Like a Rock” and, like many fans, being impressed he still had his chops, “sans plastic surgery, sans much hair. It’s still him, the essence… What is truly stunning is when he starts picking that Fender. Like it’s a high school in New Castle, Pennsylvania and it’s another night in the sixties. And he’s not only picking, HE’S INTO IT!… Donnie isn’t showing off, he’s just doing what he does, AT 82! It put a smile on my face, made me feel good not only about Donnie Iris, but rock and roll.”

In one of dozens of responses to Lefsetz’s column, his partner Avsec wrote, “We’ve been together for almost 50 years… And one of the joys of my life is watching the crowd watch Donnie. I’ve never seen such JOY on people’s faces. It happens every time we play, and we’re fortunate enough to be playing decent size venues, especially in Western Pa and Northeastern Ohio. Donnie is going through his third course of chemotherapy. If the treatments drag him down, he does not show it. He still sings his butt off. Screams and everything. I don’t think he has ever had so much fun on stage. Donnie always tells me he’s having the time of his life. Same goes for me.”

In another response, former A&M promo executive Richard Pachter wrote, “‘Ah! Leah!’ may be the most rock and roll video ever made. That rug! Those teeth! That skinny guy with the hairy chest! But despite all that, it’s beyond great. It’s the personification of it all. I’m not kidding! THAT is rock and roll!”

title: ‘Mirzapur’ Tops a Decade of Indian Streaming as New Commissions Fall, IMDb Report Finds (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Viewer interest in Indian shows on IMDb rose about 17-fold over the past decade, even as the number of new shows and seasons commissioned in the country has dropped for two straight years, according to a new IMDb study that traces the growth of Indian streaming through its most popular titles. “10 Years of Streaming […]
content:
Viewer interest in Indian shows on IMDb rose about 17-fold over the past decade, even as the number of new shows and seasons commissioned in the country has dropped for two straight years, according to a new IMDb study that traces the growth of Indian streaming through its most popular titles.

“10 Years of Streaming in India – An IMDb Report 2026” draws on page views from the more than 250 million people who visit IMDb worldwide each month. It ranks each year’s 10 biggest Indian series from 2016 to 2026, a total of 110 slots filled by 64 different shows. It also looks past the top tier at how viewing habits and production patterns have shifted, including the rise of streaming franchises.

“Mirzapur” led the pack with nine appearances, having made the list every year since it launched. “Scam 1992” was the only show to chart five times off a single season.

Crime and thriller titles took 48 of the 110 positions. In the later years, horror, romance, comedy and drama all made gains.

Among streamers, Prime Video and Amazon MX Player combined for 34 positions across 17 series, more than any other service. Netflix logged 21 positions spread over 18 series, the broadest range of distinct titles of the platforms the report examined.

YouTube emerged as a launchpad. Thirteen of the 64 charting series started life there, and 11 of those were later picked up by subscription services. The report credited the platform with giving a wide base of creators room to build stories that can travel to bigger audiences.

The Viral Fever (TVF) stood out on the production side. The company was behind nine of the charting series and 17 of the Top 10 slots, close to one in every six entries, a run that opened with “TVF Pitchers” in 2016 and reaches “Sapne vs Everyone” this year.

On the talent front, the report named Pankaj Tripathi, Ali Fazal, Vikrant Massey, Jitendra Kumar, Kapil Sharma and Sunil Grover as “The MVPs of Streaming,” a group linked to recurring franchises and a string of hit series. Kay Kay Menon, Naveen Kasturia and Mona Singh ranked as the most versatile performers, each appearing in at least five series in a variety of roles rather than being anchored to one franchise. The study also pointed to multi-hyphenates such as Shahid Kapoor, Vijay Sethupathi, Samantha, Barun Sobti and Karan Tacker as examples of actors carrying an established screen persona into a new format.

Production volume told a more cautious story. Commissions of new series and seasons hit 202 in 2023, then slipped to 169 in 2024 and 145 in 2025. The report read this as a sign of a pickier market as the business consolidates. Hindi-language shows made up 66% of Indian streaming originals in 2025.

“Building on the success of last year’s report on Indian cinema, we turned our lens to series and used IMDb Data to understand how a decade of streaming has reshaped audience interests,” said Yaminie Patodia, head of IMDb India.

Patodia said IMDb also brought in industry leaders to weigh in on what comes next, among them Gaurav Gandhi of Prime Video, Gunjan Soni of YouTube, Monika Shergill of Netflix, former Applause CEO Sameer Nair and Vijay Koshy of TVF.

“Through this report, we continue to empower professionals in India with the authoritative data and insights they rely on IMDb and IMDbPro for, and to make the creative and business decisions that will shape the next decade,” Patodia said.

IMDb is owned by Amazon.

title: Tokyo Jury President Rolf de Heer on FIAPF’s New A-List: ‘It Matters a Great Deal to Some People, and Not at All to Others’
summary: FIAPF’s decision to make A-list status official, with Tokyo among the 17 festivals named, is unlikely to change much about the event, according to the filmmaker leading its competition jury. Australian filmmaker Rolf de Heer, the director of “Bad Boy Bubby” and “Ten Canoes,” was asked at the 39th Tokyo International Film Festival’s jury press […]
content:
FIAPF’s decision to make A-list status official, with Tokyo among the 17 festivals named, is unlikely to change much about the event, according to the filmmaker leading its competition jury.

Australian filmmaker Rolf de Heer, the director of “Bad Boy Bubby” and “Ten Canoes,” was asked at the 39th Tokyo International Film Festival’s jury press conference on Tuesday whether the classification mattered or was a redundant system.

“I think Tokyo has always been considered one of those festivals by most people who attend festivals. Tokyo was effectively an A festival. And so in that sense, I don’t think it makes a lot of difference,” de Heer said.

He allowed that the classification seems to be carrying more weight in determining the quality of films a festival can secure. “And so in that sense, it may help that it is officially now again A, but I don’t think it changes the festival so much,” de Heer said.

In March, FIAPF, the international federation of film producers’ associations, replaced its four-category accreditation system with a single list and designated 17 festivals as A-list, a term the industry had long used informally. They include Cannes, Berlin, Venice, Toronto, Busan, Shanghai, Cairo and Tokyo. Busan and Toronto made the list for the first time.

Korean producer Oh Jungwan, founder of Bom Film Productions (“The Foul King,” “A Tale of Two Sisters,” “A Bittersweet Life”), said de Heer’s answer covered it and that she was “not a film festival person.”

“So I don’t know what is A-list or not. So maybe probably A-list means good, so but as an audience, we’re not going to the festival because of their A-list or not. We just go to watch film and enjoy the feeling, the festival feeling,” Oh said.

Pressed by the journalist, who had hoped someone would call out a system that ranks some festivals above others, de Heer offered a final word: “It matters a great deal to some people, and not at all to others. And that is as it should be.”

The rest of the jury, Japanese actor Watanabe Makiko (“M/Other,” “Love Exposure,” “Tokyo Vice”), New York- and Tokyo-based producer Alex Lo of Cinema Inutile, whose credits include Jim Jarmusch’s Venice Golden Lion winner “Father Mother Sister Brother,” and Tokyo-based colorist Yov Moor (“The Taste of Things,” “Grand Tour”), did not weigh in on the question. The five-member panel will choose the Tokyo Grand Prix from 15 competition titles. The festival runs through Nov. 4.

De Heer was also asked about prospects for Australia-Japan co-productions. “It makes no sense for a Japanese film to shoot in Australia, it makes no sense for an Australian film to shoot in Japan. Europe is very good at doing co-productions only on a financial basis, really. Australia is not so good at that,” he said. Co-productions built on “a natural story where some things need to be shot in Japan, some things need to be shot in Australia” will always be possible, he added, “if the scripts come and if they are right.”

Lo, whose “Heads or Tails?” won best director at Tokyo last year, said producers in Europe, the U.S. and elsewhere “are increasingly seeking co-production opportunities,” largely because local government support is lacking.

On how a divided jury would settle on a winner, de Heer said the answer would depend on the situation. “I’m with four other very reasonable people, and I’m sure we can find a way through that we don’t end up with some sort of lesser compromised film, but a really interesting film that maybe some of us don’t like,” he said.

Oh, a Tokyo juror for the second time, recalled once arguing for seven hours on behalf of a film. “Every other jury [member] hated me,” Oh said, adding that she hoped she would not have to fight de Heer for seven hours this time.

title: Jon Stewart Trolls Trump’s Nicki Minaj Fixation After ‘Beautiful Ass’ Comment: ‘He’s Like Yogi Bear Floating Towards a Pie’
summary: On Monday night’s episode of “The Daily Show,” Jon Stewart trolled Donald Trump’s fixation on Nicki Minaj as the president’s odd remarks about the rapper’s “beautiful ass” have been making the rounds across the internet. Stewart began the evening’s show by focusing on the midterm elections, and the issues that voters are, “for some reason,” […]
content:
On Monday night’s episode of “The Daily Show,” Jon Stewart trolled Donald Trump’s fixation on Nicki Minaj as the president’s odd remarks about the rapper’s “beautiful ass” have been making the rounds across the internet.

Stewart began the evening’s show by focusing on the midterm elections, and the issues that voters are, “for some reason,” fixated on: the economy, cost of living and the war in Iran. “Donald Trump is actually back out there on the campaign trail to make his closing arguments. I imagine the president will be laser-focused on the issues that matter most,” said Stewart before cutting to a clip of Trump saying: “I looked at his ass, and I’ve never done that with a man before. A man’s ass, his ass, the ass. His ass was like a big piece of muscle.”

“And by the way, don’t feel left out, ladies. Trump’s got plenty of ammo left for you,” he continued, before cutting to a clip of the president during Saturday’s rally in Michigan showing him saying, “By the way, I looked at one hell of a beautiful ass before — Nicki Minaj. That’s hard to miss.”

Stewart, bewildered, said, “How the fuck is this real? ‘Stand up, Nikki. Twirl around. Give us a look at that.’ Talk about inflation, my God!” He continued: “Look at Trump’s face when Minaj is talking. Look at what he’s doing. He’s transfixed. He’s staring at her ass. He’s like Yogi Bear floating towards a pie on a windowsill.”

Stewart also took aim at an ad from Ohio Republican governor hopeful Vivek Ramaswamy that features Democratic candidate Amy Acton’s estranged mother.

“Well, that could be a compelling ad if it weren’t for just a couple of mitigating factors,” said Stewart. “For instance, Acton’s mother hasn’t spoken to her daughter in 50 years, and the reason is, oh, cartoonishly evil word generator, she lost custody of her kids because her husband at the time was indicted for raping her daughter.”

Stewart then cut to a clip of Trump defending the ad, and calling the reporter asking him if “the sexual abuse allegations mean nothing to” him a “horrible little reporter.” Stewart then asked: “When did Donald Trump become Miss Hannigan?”

Ahead of last week’s show, it was announced that Stewart would remain the host of “The Daily Show” through 2028. Stewart’s contract was set to end at the end of 2026 after signing a one-year renewal in November 2025. Stewart made his hosting debut on “The Daily Show” in 1999, left in 2015, and returned in February 2024. After his return, “The Daily Show” ratings went up.

title: ‘Ghosts: The Possession of Button House’ Scares Up U.K., Ireland Box Office Win
summary: Lionsgate U.K.’s horror-comedy “Ghosts: The Possession of Button House” debuted at the summit of the U.K. and Ireland box office, collecting £2.4 million ($3.2 million) across its opening weekend. Warner Bros.’ DC horror thriller “Clayface” opened in second position with $2.6 million. Amazon MGM Studios’ comedy feature “Ali G: Who Iz I?” claimed third place, […]
content:
Lionsgate U.K.’s horror-comedy “Ghosts: The Possession of Button House” debuted at the summit of the U.K. and Ireland box office, collecting £2.4 million ($3.2 million) across its opening weekend.

Warner Bros.’ DC horror thriller “Clayface” opened in second position with $2.6 million. Amazon MGM Studios’ comedy feature “Ali G: Who Iz I?” claimed third place, generating $1.7 million in its debut session.

Black Bear’s animated fantasy “Wildwood,” directed by Travis Knight, secured fourth spot with an opening haul of $1.36 million. Paramount’s “Street Fighter,” which led the chart in the previous session, rounded out the top five in its sophomore outing, adding $1.35 million to lift its cumulative total to $5.6 million.

Universal’s animated feature “Forgotten Island” placed sixth in its second weekend, collecting $1.2 million for a cume of $3.7 million. Sony’s psychological thriller “Verity” followed in seventh position in its fourth frame, adding $857,067. The Colleen Hoover adaptation’s running total is now $14.4 million.

Universal’s supernatural horror “Other Mommy” took eighth place in its third session with $576,822, bringing its gross to $6.2 million. Mubi’s “Fatherland” debuted at No. 9, generating $264,083 from 86 locations over the three-day frame with a sturdy $3,144 screen average – the fourth highest average per site among new releases. Including preview screenings, the drama’s total opening reached $415,017, surpassing “Cold War” to mark director Paweł Pawlikowski’s biggest-ever launch in the territory.

Studiocanal’s animated holdover “Shaun the Sheep: The Beast of Mossy Bottom” rounded out the top 10 in its sixth frame, collecting $408,089 to lift its cume to $6.1 million.

Meanwhile, Mubi’s documentary “Making Marie Antoinette” opened across six sites, taking $1,737 over the weekend for a $24,355 cume. The limited platform bow kicks off a staggered rollout that will expand to additional cinemas ahead of Park Circus’ re-release of Sofia Coppola’s 2006 feature “Marie Antoinette” on Nov. 13.

Looking ahead to the upcoming theatrical frame, mid-week event programming kicks off on Tuesday with Trafalgar Releasing’s broadcast of the Royal Ballet’s “Manon,” followed on Wednesday by music documentary “Ozzy & Black Sabbath: Back to the Beginning,” directed by Ben Wainwright-Pearce across 100+ locations.

Wide commercial rollouts arriving on Friday across 300+ locations are led by Disney’s mountain survival documentary “Everest: The Other Side,” directed by Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi and Jimmy Chin; A24’s dark comedy “Primetime,” directed by Lance Oppenheim and starring Robert Pattinson, Merritt Wever, Skyler Gisondo, and Phoebe Bridgers; Black Bear’s comedy “Wicker,” directed by Alex Huston Fischer and Eleanor Wilson, starring Olivia Colman, Alexander Skarsgård, Peter Dinklage, and Elizabeth Debicki; and Kaleidoscope Entertainment’s family comedy “Arnie & Barney,” directed by Sean Heuston.

Other releases on Friday include Universal’s comedy “I Love Boosters,” directed by Boots Riley and starring Keke Palmer, Naomi Ackie, Demi Moore, and LaKeith Stanfield; Action Xtreme’s “Bad Day at the Office” across 100+ screens; Munro Films’ documentary feature “Peter Asher: Everywhere Man,” directed by Dayna Goldfine and Daniel Geller across 100+ sites; and “Pan’s Labyrinth” (20th Anniversary 4K Restoration) across 100+ locations.

Specialized, festival, and international titles debuting Friday include BUFF Studios’ “City of Masks,” directed by Andrea M. Catinella; Picturehouse Entertainment’s “Nightborn”; Netflix’s “Gentle Monster,” directed by Marie Kreutzer and starring Léa Seydoux and Catherine Deneuve; Studiocanal’s “Animol”; and Metis Films’ “In the Shadows”. BFI Distribution is releasing a 4K restoration of Ken Russell’s classic “The Devils,” starring Vanessa Redgrave and Oliver Reed across 25+ screens, and Studiocanal is bowing the 25th anniversary 4K re-release of Richard Kelly’s “Donnie Darko,” starring Jake Gyllenhaal across 25+ locations.

The weekend wraps on Saturday with Trafalgar Releasing’s event cinema presentation of “BTS World Tour ‘Arirang’ in Sao Paulo: Live Viewing”.

title: Bill Kramer Says AMPAS Plans To Expand List Of Festivals That Can Serve As Qualifiers For The International Oscar Category
summary: The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences will expand the list of festivals that can serve as standalone qualifiers for the International Film Oscar category, AMPAS CEO Bill Kramer confirmed this morning during an interview with Deadline at the Tokyo Film Festival. Kramer, who has become a frequent fixture on the international festival circuit […]
content:
The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences will expand the list of festivals that can serve as standalone qualifiers for the International Film Oscar category, AMPAS CEO Bill Kramer confirmed this morning during an interview with Deadline at the Tokyo Film Festival.

Kramer, who has become a frequent fixture on the international festival circuit in recent years, is at Tokyo alongside AMPAS President Lynette Howell Taylor and Chief Membership, Impact and Industry Officer Meredith Shea to take part in a series of public talks titled Academy in Tokyo. The sessions are one of the headline events this year at the Tokyo Film Festival. Kramer will also receive an honorary leadership award. Ahead of the festivities, Kramer sat down with Deadline in Tokyo.

“Our plan is to expand the number of festivals,” Kramer told Deadline when asked about the list of festivals that can serve as feeders for the International Oscar category. Currently, under the rules introduced in May, films that win the top award at Berlin, Busan, Cannes, Sundance, Toronto, and Venice can be automatically submitted for the international category alongside films chosen by a country’s official submission committee.

Watch on Deadline

Kramer continued: “We started with six festivals because we wanted to make sure there were juried awards, which not every festival has.”

Kramer added that the new rule is part of the Academy’s plan to globalize its efforts and approach the international category in a “more holistic way.”

“A few years ago, the first thing we did was create a rule allowing refugee filmmakers who are no longer in their home country to have their films submitted by a host-country committee,” Kramer said.

“That was the first step in creating a broader aperture for who can participate in the category. The next step was to consider how we could select films beyond committee-selected submissions and ensure greater global representation.”

Kramer said AMPAS remains in constant conversation with film festivals across the globe.

“We want to make sure there is proper global representation in the number of festivals we’re working with for this category,” he said. “It’s all about inviting more films into the conversation.”

On the topic of international, Kramer said 25% of the Academy’s membership now resides outside the United States—a natural reflection, he believes, of global shifts in film production and consumption.

“I think the lines between U.S. and non-U.S. cinema, first-run and classic films, animation, and documentaries have become much less distinct,” he said. “A lot of this has to do with the pandemic, when people at home watched films they normally wouldn’t have watched—young people especially. It changed the nature of our industry.”

Kramer said the Academy’s increasing global makeup is one of the main factors that makes YouTube the most appropriate broadcast home for the Oscars moving forward. It was announced in December 2025 that YouTube won the rights to host the Academy Awards starting in 2029. The Google-owned service outbid other offers, including one from the Oscars’ longtime home ABC, which has been hosting the event since 1976. Disney’s deal runs through 2028. YouTube’s first show will be the 101st Oscars ceremony, and its deal will run through 2033.

“The beauty of the YouTube deal is that everyone will see the same show,” he said. “We’ll have control over fan engagement and reach 2.5 billion people around the world at the same time, on the same night, in more than 30 languages. It also gives us more quality control over what our fans see and experience. That’s really important.”

YouTube’s deal for the Oscars has been one of the biggest shifts as streaming platforms take on more live events. Netflix has the SAG Awards, now renamed The Actor Awards, and Prime Video will broadcast the Emmys from 2027. But the alliance between big tech and the film world hasn’t been without substantial friction; take Amazon’s mishandling of Luca Guadagnino’s Artificial.

When asked whether the Academy has planned for similar scenarios, Kramer concluded: “There’s no censorship allowed at the Academy, at the Oscars, or on our broadcast. We’ve been very clear about that, and Google and YouTube completely understand.”

The Tokyo Film Festival runs until November 4.

title: Rolf de Heer & Fellow Tokyo Jury Members Talk Festival ‘A-List’ Ratings, Co-Production & How To Judge Films
summary: Australian filmmaker Rolf de Heer, president of the competition jury at this year’s Tokyo International Film Festival, talked about the significance of ‘A-list’ ratings for film festivals at the jury press conference today. Tokyo has recently had its status as an A-list festival reaffirmed by the Fédération Internationale des Associations des Producteurs de Films (FIAPF), […]
content:
Australian filmmaker Rolf de Heer, president of the competition jury at this year’s Tokyo International Film Festival, talked about the significance of ‘A-list’ ratings for film festivals at the jury press conference today.

Tokyo has recently had its status as an A-list festival reaffirmed by the Fédération Internationale des Associations des Producteurs de Films (FIAPF), a Brussels-based global organization that rates film festivals. But the practice of rating festivals, and the process and criteria for rating them, has proved controversial over the years.

In March this year, FIAPF overhauled its festival accreditation system for the first time since 2007, with a new framework that classifies 17 festivals as “A-list” and expanding the overall number of accredited festivals around the world. Five of these festivals are based in the Asia Pacific region, including Tokyo, Busan, IFFI Goa, Cairo and Shanghai.

When asked about the ratings system, De Heer said: “Tokyo has always been considered an A-list festival by most people who attend festivals, so in that sense I don’t think it makes a lot of difference. This sort of categorization seems to be becoming more important in terms of the quality of films that are available to a festival, so in that sense it may help that Tokyo now officially has that rating again, but I don’t think it changes the festival so much.”

Watch on Deadline

FIAPF’s old system classified festivals in four groups: competitive, specialized, non-competitive and documentary and short film festivals. The 2026 reform collapsed the four categories into one group of 49 accredited festivals across 29 countries on five continents.

When pushed on the subject with another question, De Heer said: “It matters a great deal to some people and not at all to others, and that is at it should be.”

De Heer is heading the main competition jury at this year’s Tokyo film festival, along with Korean producer Oh Jungwan, New York and Tokyo-based producer Alex C. Lo, French colorist Yov Moor and Japanese actress Makiko Watanabe. The jury also talked about international co-productions, as several films in this year’s line-up of 15 competition titles have been structured this way.

Lo agreed with a question from the audience about the growing trend: “I didn’t notice there’s an increasing number of co-productions in the festival line-up, but it’s true that a lot of producers in Europe, US and the rest of the world are increasingly seeking co-production opportunities, mainly due to the link to their local government production support.”

When asked about the potential for co-productions between Japan and Australia, De Heer noted that the Australian film industry does not approach co-production in the same way as European producers: “It makes no sense for a Japanese film to shoot in Australia, and it makes no sense for an Australian film to shoot in Japan. Europe is very good at doing co-productions only on a financial basis. Australia is not so good at that.

“The sort of co-productions that work out of Australia have a natural story where some things need to be shot in Japan, some things in Australia. Those will always be possible if the scripts come and if they’re right.”

The jury also talked about their criteria for judging the 15 films in competition, which includes titles from across Europe and the Asia Pacific region. Oh Jungwan said: “For me as a jury member, I’m looking at whether I’m convinced by the story the director is telling and the way he’s telling it.” She later said she’s also prepared to fight for the films she loves and once had a seven-hour discussion about a film when serving on another jury.

Yov Moor said: “When watching each film, I’m looking at what is interesting and sincere in the film, but also really trying to imagine what the next film of this director could be.”

Makiko Watanabe added: “I try to see films without any preconceived notions and don’t try to look for answers while watching. As jury, there are other things we need to look at, but mostly I’ll look for what touches me and later digest what I took from the film.”

Tokyo International Film Festival opened last night and runs for ten days in the Hibiya-Ginza district of Tokyo. It closes on November 4 with the awards ceremony and a screening of Korean filmmaker Yeon Sang-ho’s Colony.

title: Ryan Gosling & Zach Shields Duo Dead Man’s Bones Returns With New Song Plus Music Video Starring Rain Spencer And Noah Jupe
summary: Spooky season is about to reach its peak, and Ryan Gosling’s band Dead Man’s Bones are contributing to the holiday spirit this year with a new song and music video. The rock duo comprising Project Hail Mary star Gosling and Godzilla: The New Empire producer Zach Shields released their first and only self-titled album in […]
content:
Spooky season is about to reach its peak, and Ryan Gosling’s band Dead Man’s Bones are contributing to the holiday spirit this year with a new song and music video.

The rock duo comprising Project Hail Mary star Gosling and Godzilla: The New Empire producer Zach Shields released their first and only self-titled album in collaboration with the Silverlake Conservatory Children’s Choir in 2009, so their new single “Lost in the Night” marks the first song they’ve released in 17 years.

Along with the song comes a music video starring Rain Spencer (The Summer I Turned Pretty) and Noah Jupe (Hamnet, Avengers: Secret Wars). The clip opens with Spencer in a graveyard, walking through it with a black and white filter. Then it cuts to Jupe, laying on a bench.

Gosling, who performed a rendition of his Barbie hit “I’m Just Ken” at the 2024 Oscars, has Star Wars: Starfighter coming out next year and Marvel’s new Ghost Rider movie also slated to arrive in 2028. The actor demonstrated his singing (and dancing) skills in La La Land (2016) as well.

Watch on Deadline

Shields is penning the script for the Gladys prequel film to Weapons (2025) with Zach Cregger. Prior to producing Godzilla vs. Kong: The New Empire, he co-wrote Godzilla vs. Kong, Godzilla: King of the Monsters and Krampus for Universal with Michael Dougherty.

He previously collaborated with Spencer on the play Dad’s Leg, which also starred Emily Althaus and Ted Monte and ran at Los Angeles’ Hudson Theatre from Feb. 20 to March 2. The dark comedy watches two estranged sisters (Spencer and Althaus) fight over their father’s soon-to-be-amputated leg while rehashing their past.

RELATED: Gabriel Basso Making Directorial Debut With Thriller ‘Iconoclast’; Will Star Opposite Courtney Eaton, Noah Centineo & Rain Spencer

Spencer has boarded The Maid of Orleans with filming underway in Paris on the project from Sarah Elizabeth Mintz, which marks a reunion between Spencer and the Good Girl Jane director. The actress also recently wrapped production on the Anne Hathaway-produced feature Little Five opposite Ariana Greenblatt. She currently can be seen starring in the Jane Campion-produced Big Girls Don’t Cry, which was directed by Paloma Schneideman and premiered at Sundance this year. She also has a return to the role of Taylor Jewel in the Summer I Turned Pretty movie for Amazon MGM on the horizon. Also with Amazon, Spencer is set to star in the adaptation of E. Lockhart’s Genuine Fraud.

Before that, Spencer and Jupe collaborated in a two-hander theatrical workshop for a play Shields wrote. Jupe has Avengers: Secret Wars coming out in 2027, in which he plays a key role.

The band’s Instagram first teased new music Oct. 22, and Gosling’s partner, actress Eva Mendes, collaborated on the Instagram post to boost the promo video.

RELATED: ‘We Were Liars’ Author E. Lockhart Praises Rain Spencer’s “Full Range” Ahead Of ‘Genuine Fraud’ Adaptation

title: ‘Gilded Age’ Creator Julian Fellowes Calls HBO’s Casey Bloys “Our Protector & Our Defender From Very Early Days” During Season 4 Premiere
summary: Julian Fellowes attended The Gilded Age’s Season 4 premiere at the Plaza Hotel in New York City, where he thanked Casey Bloys for believing in the series from the start. “I have a special place in my heart for Casey Bloys, our protector, our gladiator, our defender from very, very early days,” Fellowes said before […]
content:
Julian Fellowes attended The Gilded Age‘s Season 4 premiere at the Plaza Hotel in New York City, where he thanked Casey Bloys for believing in the series from the start.

“I have a special place in my heart for Casey Bloys, our protector, our gladiator, our defender from very, very early days,” Fellowes said before the screening. “Anyone who enjoys the show owes him a great deal. I certainly do, and I say that with both pride and happiness.”

Deadline reported in 2019 that, after NBC ordered the series, the creator’s vision for the period piece proved too ambitious for the constraints of broadcast TV. Universal TV shopped the series, and it landed at HBO in a competitive situation. The series finally premiered in 2022, with Season 4 debuting on Sunday, November 1.

During the presentation, Fellowes also gave a shout-out to NBCU’s Pearlena Igbokwe as “one of the first to recognize” the specialness of the series. He also mentioned Bob Greenblatt for not letting it rest and for making the series, and called HBO’s Francesca Orsi “wonderful” for bringing the series home.

Watch on Deadline

Fellowes said that he had always been interested in the Gilded Age, calling it “a very interesting period of American history,” adding, “I think it was the beginning of modern America, and it was the moment that America decided they didn’t want to copy Europe and have five generations before anyone could be invited for dinner and all that kind of thing.”

“Whatever one says about the so-called robber barons, the fact is, within a few years, the century would begin what we would know of as the American century,” he continued. “And in both world wars, the voice of America was the loudest at the peace table, because America had arrived, and it was the big, giant new power of the world.”

title: Jay Z & Apple Make It Official! Hova’s Headlining The Super Bowl Halftime Show
summary: Less than 48 hours after walking off stage at L.A.’s Sofi Stadium this weekend, Jay Z has made it official. The hip hop icon and Roc Nation founder has picked himself to headline the Super Bowl LXI halftime show in the City of Angels. “From Reasonable Doubt to standing on the Super Bowl Halftime stage, […]
content:
Less than 48 hours after walking off stage at L.A.’s Sofi Stadium this weekend, Jay Z has made it official. The hip hop icon and Roc Nation founder has picked himself to headline the Super Bowl LXI halftime show in the City of Angels.

“From Reasonable Doubt to standing on the Super Bowl Halftime stage, this has been a journey,” the Hard Knock Life rapper stated today, almost a week after Deadline confirmed his role in the February 14 big game at the aforementioned SoFi. Thirty years of music, work, and culture on the world’s biggest stage. This run continues to be a dream come true.”

Halftime show sponsor Apple Music posted a to the point video on social media casting the doubters aside.

Watch on Deadline

After dancing around the unveiling for several days, NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell came clean too tonight.

Following in the Roc Nation picked halftime footsteps of Dr. Dre, Eminem, May J Blige, Kendrick Lamar, Snoop Dogg in 2022, Rihanna in 2023, Usher in 2024, the great (and Drake beefing) Kendrick in 2025, and the show stopping Bad Bunny in 2026, the league boss had nothing but praise for the man born Shawn Carter: “For several years, we’ve had the privilege of working closely with Jay-Z and Roc Nation, and I’ve seen the extraordinary impact he has had on the Super Bowl Halftime Show,” Goodell declared Monday

“When we first reached an agreement with Roc Nation to produce the show, I had just one request: that Jay-Z take the stage himself one day, whenever the moment felt right to him,” the Commissioner went on to say, with no small amount of hyperbole. “I couldn’t be more excited for fans around the world to experience the artistry, creativity and cultural impact he will bring to the Super Bowl stage.”

Now with the marquee act all settled, the real question is who Jay Z’s guest stars will be.

If for nothing more than the inclusion of their mega #1 hit Crazy in Love, it seems obvious that Beyoncé will join her spouse for a tune or two.

Other possible collaborators that look hot are the Roots, who Jay Z was on stage with at the band’s Roots Picnic in Philadelphia this past summer. Nas and Pharrell Williams were part of Jay Z’s NYC shows earlier this year and Dre and Snoop were there at SoFi this past weekend. Add to that, Jay Z’s London gigs atTottenham Hotspur Stadium featured a mini-Fugees reunion with Lauryn Hill and Wyclef Jean.

Put bluntly, Jay Z may or may not have 99 Problems, but the ESPN and Disney+ shown Super Bowl LXI ain’t one.

title: ‘Friends’ Cast Entered Matthew Perry’s Funeral Holding Hands and Cried Around the Casket, Netflix Documentary Reveals
summary: “The One About Matthew Perry” is revealing new details about the life and death of the late “Friends” actor. In Mary Robertson’s three-part Netflix documentary, which debuted on Oct. 27, one of Perry’s best friends, Roger Costillo, says production paused on “Friends” in 2001 while Perry entered rehab. “They had to shut down production for a while until […]
content:
“The One About Matthew Perry” is revealing new details about the life and death of the late “Friends” actor. In Mary Robertson’s three-part Netflix documentary, which debuted on Oct. 27, one of Perry’s best friends, Roger Costillo, says production paused on ”Friends” in 2001 while Perry entered rehab.

“They had to shut down production for a while until Matt worked out what he had going on,” Costillo said.

As Perry’s sister Mia Perry Bowick put it, “There was an incredible amount of shame and guilt that came along with that, because he knew how many people were working on these shows, that their livelihood was dependent on it. He hated that he had to do that to people, but he also knew that he had to get well.”

The doc also includes a clip of Perry talking about the rehab experience during a 2002 interview with Larry King. “I needed to focus on nothing but sobriety,” he said. “‘Friends’ producers, I asked them for the most time that they could give me. Not even guaranteeing that I’d be back. They shot around me. The three executive producers are wonderful.”

As fans may remember, Season 6 ended with Chandler proposting to Monica (Courteney Cox), and when Season 7 premiered five months later, Perry was noticeably thinner. He later described in his memoir, “You can track the trajectory of my addiction if you gauge my weight from season to season — when I’m carrying weight, it’s alcohol; when I’m skinny, it’s pills. When I have a goatee, it’s lots of pills.”

©Warner Bros/Courtesy Everett Collection

His sister explained in the doc that during Season 7, he commuted back and forth from rehab in Malibu to the set of ”Friends,” so he could be there for Chandler and Monica’s wedding, which served as the finale.

“Both sides of the family came to the filming to watch them get married. It was a really big deal, because we’re all worried about him. We don’t know what’s going to happen in the future. To try to navigate relationships while also battling this crippling addiction is, I would say, near impossible,” Bowick said. “So I think the unspoken truth that we all were sitting with in some way or another was, ‘Is this his wedding?’ I was on set, and I remember watching Monica walk down the aisle, and when Matthew said his vows to her, the emotion in his eyes, everything was so real.”

She continued: “He and Courteney had such a lovely relationship, and years working through this thing that there was so clearly actual love there — platonic love, but love. It’s a happy memory, mixed with some sadness.”

In the final episode of “The One About Matthew Perry,” Bowick recalled seeing the “Friends” cast — Cox, Jennifer Aniston, Lisa Kudrow, David Schwimmer and Matt LeBlanc — at his funeral in 2023.

“At the funeral, we arranged for just the family to have it be open casket for a little while for all of us. The funeral was very small — close friends and family,” she said. “The rest of the ‘Friends’ cast all walked in together. I hadn’t seen them in easily 20 years. Jen Aniston was the first one of them to come up to me and give me a huge hug. But they all did.”

Bowick added, “And then, all five of them walked up to the casket holding hands and stood around him, crying.”

title: Meghan Markle to Co-Host ‘Junior MasterChef Australia’
summary: Meghan Markle, the Duchess of Sussex, is set to take on a new role as co-host of “Junior MasterChef Australia.” The news was announced in a press release from Australia’s Channel 10 on Tuesday, saying that Markle would feature as a “special guest” on a new series next year alongside chef and presenter Poh Ling […]
content:
Meghan Markle, the Duchess of Sussex, is set to take on a new role as co-host of “Junior MasterChef Australia.”

The news was announced in a press release from Australia’s Channel 10 on Tuesday, saying that Markle would feature as a “special guest” on a new series next year alongside chef and presenter Poh Ling Yeow. She previously appeared on “MasterChef Australia” as a guest judge earlier this year, drawing the show’s largest Sunday audience since 2023, and hosts her own lifestyle series “With Love, Meghan” on Netflix.

“I had an incredible time with the whole team at ‘MasterChef’ this past April, so when they approached me to come back and work with this young group of talent, it was an easy yes,” Markle said in a statement. “I love cooking with my own kids, so seeing what these young stars create in the kitchen is going to be a lot of fun. I can’t wait to see what they cook up!”

Added Yeow, “I had a lovely time filming with Meghan earlier this year, and being reunited will be a real treat. I can’t wait to meet our pint-sized culinary adventurers — I’m expecting plenty of delicious surprises and a little mischief, too.”

Markle and Prince Harry recently moved back to the U.K. after six years in California. Since returning, it was reported that the former “Suits” star wished to return to acting, with a rumored role in “The Gentlemen” Season 3 that remains unconfirmed.

She has been in the headlines in the past week after speaking out following allegations that her father, Thomas Markle, possessed child sex abuse images. Thomas Markle has denied the allegations.

“I am deeply distressed at the news that has come to light in the last 24 hours, and my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed,” Markle said in a statement, adding that in 2018, a letter about her father was sent to the Metropolitan Police and its Royalty and Specialist Protection unit and was “subsequently shared” with her. “It made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father and I was given assurances that these were being investigated,” she said.

“Junior MasterChef Australia” is produced by Endemol Shine Australia (ESA), part of media and entertainment group Banijay Entertainment, and distributed internationally by Banijay Rights.

title: ‘Harry Potter’ HBO Series Casts James Potter and Lily Potter, Plus Charlie Weasley in Character’s Screen Debut
summary: The “Harry Potter” HBO series has cast another casting spell. Harry Gilby, Jasper Talbot and Hannah Chinn have joined the cast as Charlie Weasley, James Potter and Lily Potter, respectively. The actors will appear in Season 1 of the series, which is dubbed “Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone.” James and Lily Potter, parents of […]
content:
The “Harry Potter” HBO series has cast another casting spell.

Harry Gilby, Jasper Talbot and Hannah Chinn have joined the cast as Charlie Weasley, James Potter and Lily Potter, respectively. The actors will appear in Season 1 of the series, which is dubbed “Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone.”

James and Lily Potter, parents of the titular orphaned wizard, appeared in the “Harry Potter” movies in flashbacks, photographs and magical manifestations. Charlie Weasley is a minor character in the books and does not appear in the films, so the HBO series is straying from the movies regarding Ron Weasley’s older brother.

The first season of the “Harry Potter” TV show premieres on HBO on Dec. 25. The second season, based on the second book in J.K. Rowling’s beloved fantasy series, “Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets,” is currently filming at Leavesden Studios outside London.

The logline for Season 1 reads, “There is nothing special about Harry Potter — or so his Aunt Petunia tells him. But when a mysterious letter of admission to Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry arrives, it opens the door to a hidden world of magic, friendship and adventure. Yet behind Hogwarts’ enchanted walls lie dark secrets. Harry must find the courage to prove himself against the darkest wizard of all.”

“Harry Potter” stars Dominic McLaughlin as Harry Potter, Arabella Stanton as Hermione Granger, Alastair Stout as Ron Weasley, John Lithgow as Albus Dumbledore, Janet McTeer as Minerva McGonagall, Paapa Essiedu as Severus Snape, Nick Frost as Rubeus Hagrid, Rory Wilmot as Neville Longbottom, Lox Pratt as Draco Malfoy, Leo Earley as Seamus Finnigan, Elijah Oshin as Dean Thomas, Tristan Harland as Fred Weasley, Gabriel Harland as George Weasley, Ruari Spooner as Percy Weasley, Alessia Leoni as Parvati Patil, Sienna Moosah as Lavender Brown, Finn Stephens as Vincent Crabbe, William Nash as Gregory Goyle, Warwick Davis as Filius Flitwick, Sirine Saba as Pomona Sprout, Daniel Rigby as Vernon Dursley, Bel Powley as Petunia Dursley, Paul Whitehouse as Argus Filch, Johnny Flynn as Lucius Malfoy, Bertie Carvel as Cornelius Fudge, Luke Thallon as Quirinus Quirrell, Katherine Parkinson as Molly Weasley, Amos Kitson as Dudley Dursley, Gracie Cochrane as Ginny Weasley, Richard Durden as Cuthbert Binns, Louise Brealey as Rolanda Hooch, Bríd Brennan as Poppy Pomfrey, Leigh Gill as Griphook and Anton Lesser as Garrick Ollivander.

“Game of Thrones” favorite Kit Harington will join Season 2 as Gilderoy Lockhart alongside Bonnie Hill as Ginny Weasley, Lenny Rush as Dobby, Billy Barratt as Tom Riddle, Rafe Spall as Arthur Weasley, Molly Hewitt-Richards as Moaning Myrtle and Jasper Ambrose as Colin Creevey.

The “Harry Potter” series is written and executive produced by Francesca Gardiner. Mark Mylod will executive produce and direct multiple episodes of the series for HBO in association with Brontë Film and TV and Warner Bros. Television. The series is executive produced by Rowling, Neil Blair and Ruth Kenley-Letts of Brontë Film and TV, David Heyman of Heyday Films, Laura Neal and Jon Brown.

Gilby is represented by Independent Talent Group and Untitled Entertainment. Talbot is represented by United Agents. Chinn is represented by 42.

title: ‘Barbara Forever’ Director Brydie O’Connor on Celebrating a Lesbian Icon Who Did It All – and Getting Support From Christine Vachon
summary: Lesbian artist Barbara Hammer felt invisible for most of her life. She started making films in the late 1960s, but emerging queer filmmakers often face the same challenges today. “I really felt her frustration at so many different points,” says Brydie O’Connor, director of “Barbara Forever.” “We had such wonderful partners, but we were all […]
content:
Lesbian artist Barbara Hammer felt invisible for most of her life. She started making films in the late 1960s, but emerging queer filmmakers often face the same challenges today.

“I really felt her frustration at so many different points,” says Brydie O’Connor, director of “Barbara Forever.”

“We had such wonderful partners, but we were all working overtime on this little movie that could. All the success that we’ve seen with this film hasn’t translated into funding for new projects or making money. I really hope that it will at some point.”

After screenings at Sundance and Berlinale, O’Connor is bringing the film to Ji.hlava Intl. Documentary Film Festival, where she presented it at the U.S. Docs showcase in 2023.

Produced by A Space Time Films and Killer Films production in co-production with Kartemquin Films, it gained powerful allies in Kristen Stewart and uber-producer Christine Vachon.

“Christine was like: ‘I love that it’s an unconventional approach to an unconventional artist.’ I’m such a fan of her filmography and some of her films are the most groundbreaking queer films I’ve ever seen. That’s what supporting a new generation of queer artists looks like,” notes O’Connor.

Making a film about someone who, despite her influence, isn’t exactly a household name, wasn’t easy.

“We kept hearing: ‘We love your enthusiasm for Barbara Hammer, you emerging lesbian filmmaker. But does that relate to the present day and broader audiences?’”

Hammer passed away in 2019.

“I was wondering: How did she do it all? How did she make over 85 films? How did she archive her entire life in 125 boxes that she eventually sold to Yale? How did she have such a successful relationship towards the end of her life? The complexity of just living, being ambitious and trying to make it happen feels very relatable to me,” she says.

“Now, so many people are being introduced to Barbara and feeling so moved by this film. I’m so grateful for that. It’s such a win to release it, but it was hard to convince people of its place in the market.”

Ironically enough, Hammer’s work often felt ahead of her time. Like today’s influencers, she wasn’t afraid to interview passers-by, film herself or share intimate moments with the camera.

“It feels very contemporary. Barbara started using social media at the end of her life, and she was certainly interested in it. She put herself in the frame as a way to process her feelings and certain situation in her life. She filmed everything.”

But there was a reason behind her methods.

“Barbara had this idea that it would offer insight into how one lesbian, and one woman, navigated the world. In the influencer era, that throughline isn’t necessarily as present. When she was first understanding her sexuality, she had never heard the word ‘lesbian’. This set her on this mission to document everything so that other people could see themselves in her work. I think that was part of her impetus to be so prolific.”

O’Connor started researching Hammer’s work as a student.

“She felt invisible when she was coming out, but she also felt invisible in the film and art world. She felt like she wasn’t getting recognized in the way she thought she should be,” she admits.

Hammer wanted the fame that was eluding her – and she wasn’t afraid to say it.

“When you talk to people who were in the scene or had encountered her, they say: ‘Barbara had a huge personality. She was really pushy, you know.’ I think that’s so human. She knew that she had to overemphasize the importance of her work and her presence. It was about becoming a lesbian icon at a time when the world didn’t really want a lesbian icon.”

Although Hammer made personal, experimental films, she still cared about her audience and wanted to engage with them. Up until her death from cancer.

“Connecting with others through art was really at the core of her practice. It’s also why she loved teaching. I definitely try to take at least a page out of Barbara’s book in that regard,” says O’Connor.

“After one screening, a woman came up to me. She said: ‘I’ve never heard of Barbara Hammer. I’m from Texas and I’m not queer. But I was so moved because my father is at the very end of his life, and he keeps telling our family that he’s at peace. After seeing this movie, I finally understand what he’s saying,’” she recalls.

“That’s been one of the greatest gifts. Just talking to audiences.”

title: David Bowie Immersive Concert Experience ‘Stage’ From Brett Morgen to World Premiere at Berlin Film Festival
summary: The world premiere of the David Bowie immersive concert experience, “Stage,” has been set for Feb. 14 at Berlin’s Uber Arena. It will play during the Berlin Film Festival, representing a rare foray into alternative programming at the European film event. The experience, which combines previously unseen Bowie concert footage and immersive sound and light, […]
content:
The world premiere of the David Bowie immersive concert experience, “Stage,” has been set for Feb. 14 at Berlin’s Uber Arena. It will play during the Berlin Film Festival, representing a rare foray into alternative programming at the European film event.

The experience, which combines previously unseen Bowie concert footage and immersive sound and light, is designed around recently discovered and restored footage from the 1978 Isolar II World Tour, during which Bowie performed material from his album “Heroes.”

Presented in association with the Berlinale, the production is a collaboration between Rob Hallett’s Wonderworld, the David Bowie Estate and documentary filmmaker Brett Morgen, who first discovered the original camera negatives while working on his Grammy Award-winning film “Moonage Daydream.

With a three-screen presentation, the immersive experience combines large-scale projections and transparent LED screens with an elaborate lighting design by renowned lighting designer Patrick Woodroffe, whose credits include collaborations with the Rolling Stones and Elton John.

The production is further enhanced by a specially created sound mix from Academy Award winner Paul Massey (“Bohemian Rhapsody,” “Michael,” “Moonage Daydream”).

Using state-of-the-art 7.1 surround technology and spatial audio design, the production places audiences at the center of a live David Bowie concert experience.

Tricia Tuttle, director of the Berlinale, said: “The Berlinale is a place where cinema, art and new forms of storytelling intersect. It’s like a dream come true: Bowie, Brett Morgen, a world-class sound and light team all coming together in the city’s premiere music arena. To have this world premiere in Berlin, a city so closely connected to David Bowie, makes the experience especially meaningful.”

Rob Hallett, founder of Wonderworld and former president of AEG International, said: “David Bowie has bestowed upon us an extraordinary treasure — an unprecedented concert experience that has yet to be witnessed. Working hand-in-hand with David Bowie’s Estate and Brett Morgen, we are ensuring this experience is 100% faithful to his legacy while making his genius accessible to global fans and a new generation.”

Morgen will also be a headline speaker as part of the talks program of Berlinale’s European Film Market. Further details will be revealed in the coming weeks.

title: Vantage Media Takes North American Rights To Pole-Dancing Drama ‘Exotic’ As Trailer Unveiled
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Vantage Media has acquired North American rights to Polish feature Exotic, about a woman’s journey toward self-discovery through pole dancing, ahead of its premiere at the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival. The picture follows a writer whose quest to master pole dancing evolves into something far more profound when the process and community of […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Vantage Media has acquired North American rights to Polish feature Exotic, about a woman’s journey toward self-discovery through pole dancing, ahead of its premiere at the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival.

The picture follows a writer whose quest to master pole dancing evolves into something far more profound when the process and community of dancers she encounters help her figure out her true self. It is the first feature of Sonja Orlewicz-Zakrzewska and grew out of her personal fascination with pole dancing.

The deal was negotiated by Jessica Russo, COO of Productions and Acquisitions at VMI Worldwide and Vantage Media, and Daniel Vadocky, Head of Sales at Berlin-based Pluto Film, which has also unveiled a first international trailer to coincide with the announcement. Gutek is handling the Polish release.

“At a time when women’s rights and freedoms are increasingly being challenged in America, Exotic delivers a timely and empowering message about the importance of embracing who we truly are,” said Russo at Vantage/VMI.

Watch on Deadline

“Through the art of dance, the film celebrates female strength, confidence and self-expression, reminding us that empowerment often begins with the courage to step outside our comfort zones. Exotic is more than a story about pole dancing; it’s a celebration of sisterhood, self-discovery, and the freedom to unapologetically be yourself.”

“We are very pleased to have secured a North American distribution deal ahead of the film’s world premiere,” added Vadocky at Pluto Film. “It is a strong sign to its international appeal and audience potential. We have full confidence that Vantage/VMI will successfully distribute the film across all platforms.”

Exotic was shot during a recent real-life edition of a pole-dancing Exo Stars Camp featuring real participants and instructors, maintaining the authenticity of this vivid bubble.

“As soon as I discovered exotic pole dance, I got so invested that I went straight to Exo Stars Camp,” explains the writer-director. “I was fascinated by the clash of the fragile, intimate universes we carried within us around the camp. It soon became clear that the camp itself was a perfect place to confront fears, leave one’s comfort zone and express oneself more than daily life ever allows. “

The film stars Jaśmina Polak, Magdalena Koleśnik and Monika Frajczyk. Director of Photography is Adam Suzin, with Tomasz Kajetan Naruszewicz as Editor and Tymek Papior as Composer.to here. It received support from the Polish Film Institute’s microbudget scheme aimed at first-time directors.

Director, scriptwriter, visual artist and photographer Orlewicz-Zakrzewska holds a master’s degree in photography from the Cinematography Department of the Łódź Film School.

Her first short, Cross’n’Carry (2019), screened at festivals including New Horizons, HollyShorts and BEAST Portugal. She also took part in the script training lab Atelier Scenariuszowe and the EAVE Producers Workshop (2021).

As a cinematographer, she worked on Enthusiasts, a documentary series for Canal+. Her video art and photography have been shown in numerous exhibitions including the Leica Gallery Warsaw.

Exotic will debut in the First Feature Competition of Estonia’s Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival running from November 6 to 22.

title: Meghan Markle To Co-Host ‘Junior MasterChef Australia’
summary: She might not be set to appear in The Gentlemen, but Meghan Markle is headed for the Junior MasterChef kitchen. The Duchess of Sussex will be a “special guest” on Junior MasterChef Australia, the Network Ten version of Banijay’s culinary cook-off series, and comes after an appearance on MasterChef Australia earlier this year. She will […]
content:
She might not be set to appear in The Gentlemen, but Meghan Markle is headed for the Junior MasterChef kitchen.

The Duchess of Sussex will be a “special guest” on Junior MasterChef Australia, the Network Ten version of Banijay’s culinary cook-off series, and comes after an appearance on MasterChef Australia earlier this year.

She will host alongside Poh Ling Yeow when the show, in which junior chefs compete to be crowned champion, returns to the Skydance-owned Ten next year after six years off air.

“I had an incredible time with the whole team at MasterChef this past April, so when they approached me to come back and work with this young group of talent, it was an easy yes,” said Markle. “I love cooking with my own kids, so seeing what these young stars create in the kitchen is going to be a lot of fun. I can’t wait to see what they cook up.”

Watch on Deadline

Markle hosted a lifestyle and cooking show for Netflix, With Love, Meghan, which premiered last year. Two seasons of the show debuted in 2025, but with Markle and Prince Harry’s Neflix coming to an end, the show has also finished.

Yeow said the news of MasterChef Australia‘s return would be “met with plenty of excitement,” and added: “I had a lovely time filming with Meghan earlier this year, and being reunited will be a real treat. I can’t wait to meet our pint-sized culinary adventurers – I’m expecting plenty of delicious surprises and a little mischief, too.”

Banijay Entertainment’s Endemol Shine Australia is making the show, with Banijay Rights distributing internationally.

Markle has been in the headlines recently due to the allegations he father, Thomas Markle, possessed child abuse images. The Duchess released a statement, saying: ”I am deeply distressed at the news that has come to light in the last 24 hours, and my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed.”

She has not had contact with her father since 2018, when she was made aware of allegations against him.

Last week, several cast members were added to the third season of Netflix crime caper The Gentlemen. Though Markle had been heavily linked to a role, she was not on the list and it now appears she is not joining the ensemble.

title: ‘Harry Potter’ Series Finds Its Lily & James Potter In Jasper Talbot & Hannah Chinn; Harry Gilby To Play Charlie Weasley
summary: HBO’s Harry Potter series has cast the roles of the titular wizard’s parents, James and Lily Potter, with Jasper Talbot and Hannah Chinn, respectively. Additionally, Harry Gilby joins as Charlie Weasley, the second eldest son of Molly and Arthur Weasley after Bill, whose siblings also include Percy, Fred, George, Ron, and Ginny.
