content:
HBO‘s Harry Potter series has cast the roles of the titular wizard’s parents, James and Lily Potter, with Jasper Talbot and Hannah Chinn, respectively. Additionally, Harry Gilby joins as Charlie Weasley, the second eldest son of Molly and Arthur Weasley after Bill, whose siblings also include Percy, Fred, George, Ron, and Ginny.

Harry’s parents did not appear much in the hit films based on the J.K. Rowling book series, and it is unknown how big a role they will play in the new HBO series. According to the first novel, James and Lily Potter were killed by the most evil dark wizard, Voldemort. Lily sacrificed her life on that day to protect wee Harry, just a baby at the time of her death, with a love shield. When Voldemort unleashed an evil curse on the Potters, it bounced off Harry and hit He-Who-Shall-Not-Be-Named, leaving his physical form nonexistent and his powers pretty useless. Harry was left with a lightning bolt scar on his forehead, a painful memento that marks the horrible night he lost his parents.

In the upcoming Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone, viewers will be introduced to Harry (Dominic McLaughlin), who has nothing special about him- or so his Aunt Petunia (Bel Powley) tells him. But when a mysterious letter of admission to Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry arrives, it opens the door to a hidden world of magic, friendship and adventure. Yet behind Hogwarts’ enchanted walls lie dark secrets. Harry must find the courage to prove himself against the darkest wizard of all.

Watch on Deadline

In addition to McLaughlin, the series also stars Arabella Stanton as Hermione Granger, Alastair Stout as Ron Weasley, John Lithgow as Albus Dumbledore, Janet McTeer as Minerva McGonagall, Paapa Essiedu as Severus Snape, Nick Frost as Rubeus Hagrid, Rory Wilmot as Neville Longbottom, Lox Pratt as Draco Malfoy, Leo Earley as Seamus Finnigan, Elijah Oshin as Dean Thomas, Tristan Harland as Fred Weasley, Gabriel Harland as George Weasley, Ruari Spooner as Percy Weasley, Alessia Leoni as Parvati Patil, Sienna Moosah as Lavender Brown, Finn Stephens as Vincent Crabbe, William Nash as Gregory Goyle, Warwick Davis as Filius Flitwick, Sirine Saba as Pomona Sprout, Daniel Rigby as Vernon Dursley, Paul Whitehouse as Argus Filch, Johnny Flynn as Lucius Malfoy, Bertie Carvel as Cornelius Fudge, Luke Thallon as Quirinus Quirrell, Katherine Parkinson as Molly Weasley, Amos Kitson as Dudley Dursley, Gracie Cochrane as Ginny Weasley, Richard Durden as Cuthbert Binns, Louise Brealey as Rolanda Hooch, Bríd Brennan as Poppy Pomfrey, Leigh Gill as Griphook, and Anton Lesser as Garrick Ollivander.

The series is written and executive produced by Francesca Gardiner. Mark Mylod will executive produce and direct multiple episodes of the series for HBO in association with Brontë Film and TV and Warner Bros. Television. The series is executive produced by Rowling, Neil Blair, and Ruth Kenley-Letts of Brontë Film and TV, David Heyman of Heyday Films, Laura Neal, and Jon Brown.

Talbot is represented by United Agents. Chinn is represented by 42. Gilby is represented by Independent Talent Group and Untitled Entertainment.

title: Brett Morgen’s David Bowie Immersive Concert Experience Set For Berlinale World Premiere
summary: The spirit of late pop and rock icon David Bowie is set to return to Berlin, the city he called home in the mid-1970s. The Berlin Film Festival has announced it will world premiere U.S. documentarian Brett Morgen’s immersive concert experience David Bowie “Stage” during its 77th edition in the city’s 17,000-capacity Uber Arena venue. […]
content:
The spirit of late pop and rock icon David Bowie is set to return to Berlin, the city he called home in the mid-1970s.

The Berlin Film Festival has announced it will world premiere U.S. documentarian Brett Morgen’s immersive concert experience David Bowie “Stage” during its 77th edition in the city’s 17,000-capacity Uber Arena venue.

Combining previously unseen Bowie concert footage and an immersive sound and light experience, the production is billed as “a new way of experiencing one of the most influential artists of the 20th century”.

The work is designed around recently discovered and restored footage from the 1978 Isolar II World Tour, during which Bowie performed material from his landmark album ‘Heroes’.

Watch on Deadline

Morgen first discovered the original camera negatives while working on his Grammy Award-winning, Oscar-nominated bio-doc Moonage Daydream, charting Bowie’s life and career. World premiering in Cannes in 2022, it was the first film to be officially authorized by Bowie’s estate.

The new three-screen immersive experience combines large-scale projections and transparent LED screens with an elaborate lighting design by lighting designer Patrick Woodroffe, whose credits include collaborations with The Rolling Stones and Elton John.

The production is further enhanced by a specially created sound mix from Academy Award winner Paul Massey (Bohemian Rhapsody, Michael, Moonage Daydream), and places audiences at the centre of a live concert experience using state-of-the-art 7.1 surround technology and spatial audio design.

The production is a collaboration between Rob Hallett’s Wonderworld, the David Bowie Estate and Morgen.

“David Bowie has bestowed upon us an extraordinary treasure, an unprecedented concert experience that has yet to be witnessed,” said live entertainment veteran and former AEG International President Hallet.

“Working hand-in-hand with David Bowie’s Estate and Brett Morgen, we are ensuring this experience is 100% faithful to his legacy while making his genius accessible to global fans and a new generation.”

Berlinale Director Tricia Tuttle added: “To have this world premiere in Berlin, a city so closely connected to David Bowie, makes the experience especially meaningful,” added Tricia Tuttle, Director of the Berlinale.

“The Berlinale is a place where cinema, art, and new forms of storytelling intersect. It’s like a dream come true: Bowie, Brett Morgen, a world-class sound and light team all coming together in the city’s premiere music arena.”

Morgen, whose credits also include Kurt Cobain bio-doc Cobain: Montage of Heck and Jane about Jane Goodall, will also be a headline speaker in the talks program of the Berlinale’s European Film Market (EFM).

The 77th Berlinale will run from February 10 to 21, 2027, with the David Bowie “Stage” world premiering on February 14.

title: Riley Voelkel & Shiva Negar To Voice Adult Animated Comedy Project ‘Above Average’
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Riley Voelkel and Shiva Negar will lend their voices to adult animated comedy series Above Average. The show, which is in late-stage development, comes from creators Andrew Deutsch and Cailin Walker-Bent at Canadian animation collective Red Pants Productions and Josh Harris at JVH Media in the UK. Above Average is billed as an irreverent […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Riley Voelkel and Shiva Negar will lend their voices to adult animated comedy series Above Average.

The show, which is in late-stage development, comes from creators Andrew Deutsch and Cailin Walker-Bent at Canadian animation collective Red Pants Productions and Josh Harris at JVH Media in the UK.

Above Average is billed as an irreverent look at celebrity culture, corporate power and society’s obsession with being exceptional. It is set in Metrocropolis, the superhero capital of the world, where crime-fighting is big business, saving lives requires a license and public image often matters more than public service.

The series follows Gadget Kid, an ordinary teenager with extraordinary ambitions, but absolutely no superpowers. Determined to make a difference, he turns to SALT, three washed-up, middle-aged superheroes operating out of a dilapidated laundromat, and their accountant.

Watch on Deadline

Riley Voelkel’s credits include The Originals and Hightown. “I’ve had the opportunity to watch this project grow over time and seeing it evolve and reach this stage has been such a great experience,” she said. “I’m excited to be stepping into the world of voiceover and it’s been a blast to watch everything come to life.”

Shiva Negar, whose credits include American Assassin, added: “There’s something incredibly refreshing about a superhero comedy where the heroes are anything but super. They’re flawed, imperfect, and often a complete mess, which ironically makes them all the more human and relatable.

“I’ve already had so much fun experimenting with different voices and personalities, and I’m excited to be part of this wonderfully imaginative and hilarious world that Andrew and Cailin have created, and to reunite with Josh Harris after our time together on American Assassin.”

Deutsch and Walker-Bent will write and direct the series and oversee voice direction and casting. Above Average is being developed as an eight-parter. Animatic and character designs already in place. Check out the first-look at the images from the show.

Red Pants Productions, JVH Media

title: ‘You Can See Everything’ Ruled Ineligible for DGA Feature Prize, Will Compete Only in Documentary Category
summary: SPOILER ALERT: This article contains major spoilers for “You Can See Everything,” now playing in theaters. Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s “You Can See Everything” will not be in the running for the Directors Guild of America Awards top prize this season. A representative for the DGA confirmed to Variety that the A24 documentary about […]
content:
SPOILER ALERT: This article contains major spoilers for “You Can See Everything,” now playing in theaters.

Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s “You Can See Everything” will not be in the running for the Directors Guild of America Awards top prize this season.

A representative for the DGA confirmed to Variety that the A24 documentary about Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes will compete solely in the outstanding directorial achievement in documentary category and will not be considered for outstanding directorial achievement in theatrical feature film, the award that has aligned with the best director Oscar in all but a handful of years since 1949.

The guild referenced in its own rule book, which explains the entry criteria for theatrical feature film award as “re-releases, animated films and documentaries are not eligible.” That line in the rule book seems to leave no room for a hybrid or an exception.

A24 and several awards strategists had hoped to get around the classification. The thinking inside the studio and among consultants was that the film’s unusual construction, which blurs the line between nonfiction and staged narrative, might have allowed the guild to treat it as a both a feature and a documentary. The argument gained momentum after Amanda Seyfried, who appears in the film and previously won an Emmy for playing Holmes in the Hulu limited series “The Dropout,” was positioned for acting consideration at the Oscars for supporting actress.

The DGA sees it differently. The guild classifies films based on how they are produced and submitted, and “You Can See Everything” is a documentary by that measure, regardless of how other awards bodies or voting blocs choose to interpret it.

The ruling matters because the DGA feature award is one of the most reliable bellwethers in the Oscars. Only eight times in the guild’s history has the DGA winner failed to go on to win the Oscar for best director. Without a shot at that prize, the film loses a key piece of precursor momentum, though a documentary win at the guild could still bolster its standing in the Academy’s documentary feature and best picture, a category that has never had a nonfiction film nominated.

The 174-minute film opened in theaters on Oct. 16 and has drawn some of the strongest reviews of the year and exceptional box office, with critics and audiences debating whether to categorize it as traditional documentary, a reality television-like concept or something new entirely.

A24 and its strategists remain in active conversations with other guilds and awards bodies, including BAFTA, SAG-AFTRA and the Golden Globes, about how a film like “You Can See Everything” should be classified.

There’s still hope for it to be embraced across the board at the Oscars.

In addition to being eligible for best documentary feature at the 99th Academy Awards, the film will also be submitted as seen on A24’s awards site: best picture (Nathan Fielder, Lance Oppenheim, Tatiana Bears, Maggie Ambrose and Jack Davis), director (Fielder and Oppenheim), supporting actress (Seyfried), supporting actor (Christopher Abbott), production design (Alex DiGerlando and Rebecca Meis), cinematography (David Bolen), costume design (Katina Danabassis), film editing (Adam Locke-Norton), makeup and hairstyling (Stephanie Pasicov and Kerrie Smith), sound (Paul Hsu and Richard Carlos) and original score (Ari Balouzian).

Nominations for the 79th annual DGA Awards will be announced in January.

A24 declined to comment.

title: Led by ‘Money Heist’ Star Itziar Ituño, Eco-Thriller ‘Patagonia’ Has Movistar Plus Betting on a Latin America-Spain Creative Bridge
summary: Spain’s Movistar Plus continues to double down on its strategies to further amplify Spanish series and storytelling internationally with the world premiere of the highly anticipated eco-thriller “Patagonia.” Bowing at the upcoming South International Series Festival in Cádiz, the series is the latest major co-production to be boosted by the Spanish streamer and the fruit […]
content:
Spain’s Movistar Plus continues to double down on its strategies to further amplify Spanish series and storytelling internationally with the world premiere of the highly anticipated eco-thriller “Patagonia.”

Bowing at the upcoming South International Series Festival in Cádiz, the series is the latest major co-production to be boosted by the Spanish streamer and the fruit of a pioneering collaboration with Chile’s Wood Producciones and Spain’s Atlantika Films. Germany’s ZDF Studios handles international distribution for the series, which is set for release on Movistar Plus in January 2027.

Led by “Money Heist” star Itziar Ituño, “Patagonia” is a six-episode series following Ituño’s Alicia, a desperate mother who travels from the Basque Country to Chile’s titular region to find her missing teenage son, Noah (Unai Arana).

As the search continues, Alicia must navigate her own family conflicts while dealing with the mysteries of the ancient forest and a dangerous illegal logging network. The series is created by Chilean writers María Elena Wood and Patricio Pereira. The former is behind Platino Prize best series winners “News of a Kidnapping” and “Dignity,” while the latter produced “Mary & Mike.”

“Patagonia” is directed by Rodrigo Susarte, who recently helmed the high-concept sci-fi “Hidden Island,” featured on this year’s Berlinale Series Market Selects. Speaking with Variety ahead of the film’s premiere, Susarte says he was drawn to the idea of an eco-thriller because it amplifies a suspense story’s core hook, which is “what we fail to see.”

“I didn’t want the series to explain the climate crisis,” he adds. “I’d rather it leaves the audience with a lingering sense of unease. Maybe the real question isn’t what we’re doing to the forest, but what part of ourselves disappears along with it.”

Courtesy of Movistar Plus

Wood adds that “Patagonia” was born from a desire “to tell a story in which a unique territory is not merely a backdrop, but a protagonist.” “We envisioned a contemporary Western set in the southern reaches of the globe—a place where extraordinary nature, isolated communities, economic interests, and deeply human conflicts coexist,” she notes.

Susarte mentions his work in the series was inspired by films by Werner Herzog and Jane Campion. The former is a particularly resonant influence given his infamous experience of shooting “Aguirre, the Wrath of God” in the depths of the Peruvian forest. When asked about the experience of shooting in Hornopirén, Susarte says it was a chance to physically experience how organisms can shape one another in nature.

“There, the forest isn’t a backdrop; it’s a presence, with its own rules, its own light, and its own sense of time,” he says. “The first thing you learn is that you’re not in charge. The weather rewrites your shooting schedule every morning, and there’s an almost philosophical lesson in learning to accept that without giving up. Filmmaking is, at its heart, an attempt to control things. Patagonia constantly reminds you where that control ends.”

The director also notes an interesting paradox that guided the shoot: “We were telling a story about the destruction of a forest while moving through it with an entire film crew.” “Shooting there demanded an awareness of the footprint we were leaving behind, of entering a space that doesn’t belong to us.”

“For me, bringing ‘Patagonia’ to life between Chile and Spain has been a truly unique experience, and undoubtedly one of the most rewarding projects of my career,” notes Atlantika Films producer Nano Arrieta. “Working alongside Pato and Mané at Wood Producciones has been a real privilege. From day one, we knew we were in excellent hands, with access to some of the finest crews in Chile. On the Spanish side, we made an equally strong commitment to bringing together top-tier talent in the Basque Country.”

The producer also mentions how “Patagonia” is feeding into an “incredibly exciting moment for Spanish cinema.” Arrieta brings up names like Oliver Laxe, Los Javis and Alauda Ruiz De Azúa as exponents of this new wave. “These are bold, distinctive filmmakers with powerful creative voices, and they’re helping push Spanish storytelling into exciting new territory.”

“Great moments in an industry usually come from something deeper than the market itself, [they come] from having confidence in your own voice,” adds Susarte. “I think that’s a big part of what’s happening in Spain right now. Stories that don’t feel the need to apologise for being local, and platforms like Movistar Plus have understood that. What I hope is that this moment doesn’t simply end with success, that it creates room for bolder creative voices, and that the dialogue between Spain and Latin America continues to grow.”

Courtesy of Movistar Plus

On top of launching “Patagonia,” Atlantika is currently developing “When Devils Rule,” a series based on an original idea by Arrieta and starring Oscar-nominated “Emilia Perez” actress Karla Sofia Gascón. “When Devils Rule” will also reunite Susarte and Ituño. The six-part series will be pitched at Tallinn’s TV Beats Co-Financing Market running Nov. 16-17.

“The concept is quite wild, actually. It’s a hyperrealistic story, deeply rooted in the political and social chaos of our times, but with one supernatural twist: demons,” says the producer of the series. “The central idea is pretty simple, and perhaps a little provocative. What if the political madness, moral corruption and sheer absurdity of the world we’re living in could only be explained by the fact that demons are actually behind it all?”

As for Susarte, he’ll soon start his festival journey with “Invunche,” a reinterpretation of a tale from Chilote mythology, originating in the Chiloé Archipelago in southern Chile and combining Indigenous beliefs with Spanish legends. “I’ve set it in a time when information reaches us in fragments, distorted and out of order. At the heart of it is the same idea I’ve always been drawn to: what does a place reveal about the people who inhabit it, and what does what we’re willing to lose reveal about us?”

Wood is currently developing two features, both international co-productions. “Arca” is directed by Matías Bize (“The Punishment”), written by Julio Rojas (“Case 63”), and co-produced with Spain’s Potenza, Brazil’s Trema, and Chile’s Céneca and Wood Productions. It is a psychological thriller that confronts its protagonists with an extreme moral dilemma in the face of a world spiraling out of control.

The second project, “Lucila,” is an animated feature film centered on the childhood of Gabriela Mistral in the Elqui Valley, exploring the emotional and creative world of the person who would go on to become one of the great voices of Latin American literature.

“Patagonia” is produced by María Elena Wood and Pereira and Atlantika’s Nano Arrieta and Claudia Ruiz. Production oversight is shared with ZDF Studios’ Sebastián Krekeler, Susanne Frank, and Peter Nadermann, plus Cristina Merino at Movistar Plus. “Patagonia” is an exclusive Movistar Plus series.

title: South International Series Festival: ‘American Hostage,’ Ronan Bennett, Great European Series and Andalusia’s TV Build
summary: Opening on Oct. 30 with “American Hostage,” honoring “Toy Boy” showrunner Ronan Bennett and “Money Heist” star Alvaro Morte, the fourth edition of South International Series Festival weighs in with a mouthwatering fiction competition, dominated by series from Europe, and an ever stronger Andalusian presence. “The aim of the festival is to keep growing,” says […]
content:
Opening on Oct. 30 with “American Hostage,” honoring “Toy Boy” showrunner Ronan Bennett and “Money Heist” star Alvaro Morte, the fourth edition of South International Series Festival weighs in with a mouthwatering fiction competition, dominated by series from Europe, and an ever stronger Andalusian presence.

“The aim of the festival is to keep growing,” says director Carles Montiel. One growth axis is “international scope,” the other one “connecting Andalusia’s industry with the rest of Spain and abroad.”

It has already come far on both counts, while backing from Spain looks assured. “We have already reached a certain level of recognition from Spanish producers, Spanish broadcasters, Spanish platforms and streaming services which consider us an attractive festival,” Montiel adds.

That tells in a Fiction Competition which sources four world premieres, three from two of Spain’s most bullish streaming services in Spain.

Movistar Plus, the biggest Spanish pay TV/SVOD operator – behind “La Bola Negra,” “The Beloved” and “Querer” and now “The Castle” and “Killing a Bear” – brings “Patagonia,” a high-stakes race against time missing son/eco thriller with “Money Heist” and “Intimacy” star Itziar Ituño, and “The Center,” Season 2 which lifts the lid on the hidden world of Spain’s National Intelligence Center (CNI) winning fans for an espionage thriller which is fully grounded in the daily lives of its operatives.

“Infamy,” a slow-burn cold case psychological thriller set and shot in a benighted town in the Basque Country’s Bizkaia, is a first window HBO Max acquisition for Spain.

A fourth world premiere, “Stepping Up,” created, written and starring Josh Pugh (“Sneakerhead,” “How Are You? It’s Alan (Partridge)”) weighs is as a half-hour series expansion of Pugh’s short-format “Stepping Up: Channel 4 Comedy Blap.”

The series is produced by the U.K’s Roughcut Television (“Big Boys,” “Things You Should Have Done”), founded by “The Office” producer Ash Attala.

South’s other five Fiction Competition titles are backed by movers and shakers on the European scene: “Still Breathing” is backed by Norwegian public broadcaster NRK, a consistent source of top-notch drama such as “A Better Man”; “Someone Should Ban Sunday Afternoons,” from Spain’s Isabel Coixet, is one of the latest series aired On Arte, behind Series Mania standout “Etty,” and produced by France’s Maui Entertainment, headed by “The Bureau” showrunner Eric Rochant.

German public network ARD Degeto, plus international distributor Beta Film, a driving force behind European sculpted shows, both back “Blindspot Berlin.”

“Snake Killer marks Amazon MGM Studios’ first Danish original. It will act as a flagship for a delegation of Danish producers and broadcaster execs that will hit Cadiz’s SISF. Bedeviled by rising costs, as the rest of the world, Denmark’s industry is eager to co-produce. “They’re looking for partners in Spain, not just because of the rebates, I guess, but its landscapes and light, especially in Andalusia, which can help evolve series beyond their borders,” says Montiel.

The Stars and Panels

SISF honors showrunner-writer Bennett (“Top Boy,” “The Day of the Jackal”), Alvaro Morte, “Money Heist’s” professor, and Ana Duato (“Remember When”); Isabel Coixet delivers a masterclass. Of multiple, Industry talks take in The Young Adult Phenomenon: Literary Adaptations Without Borders, analyzing Wattpad adaptations from “Mala influencia” to “Boulevard,” to the international impact of series like “My Life with the Walter Boys,” produced by Sony Pictures Television International for Netflix. Wattpad Webtoon Studios’ Mar Vila, Sony Pictures Television’s Celia Duffy and Spotlight Media’s Anxo Rodriguez are speakers. One Creative Talks highlight looks set to be a mano a mano on directing between Javier Ruiz Caldera, fresh off San Sebastián hit “5 More Minutes,” and Paco Cabezas, (“Wednesday,” “The Walking Dead: Daryl Dixon”), also director of the fearsome “La nena,” which screens at SISF.

Non-Fiction Buzz Titles

South International Series Festival will showcase at least one non-fiction gem: “The Oligarch and the Art Dealer,” an Arte series – again – co-created, written and directed by Andreas Dalsgaard charting the $1 billion dispute between Swiss art dealer Yves Bouvier and Russian billionaire Dmitry Rybolovlev and the currency of the ultra-rich: Investing in art. “Better than gold. Better than diamonds,” says Dalsgaard. Highly rated, the three-part docusueries has already proved a Sundance and CPH-DOX highlight.

There’s good word too on “The Dirty Years: Where is Nani?” from Mediaset España, using talking heads and archive footage to reconstruct the case of “El Nani,” a young small time criminal who disappeared in police custody in 1983. The subsequent court case involving the Francoist throwback police culprits became a show trial for Spain’s young democracy.

SISF: Maintains Its Hallmark Diversity

Sporting a high-voltage U.S. play in “American Hostage” and a clutch of premium agenda-driven series, South International Series Festival will close on Nov. 4 with “Física o Química. The New Generation” Season 2. Set to bow in December on free-to-air broadcast network Atresmedia’s SVOD feed Atresplayer, it reps a resurrection of an iconic 2008-11 high school series which launched the careers of “La Bola Negra’s” Javier Calvo and “Money Heist’s” Úrsula Corberó. “Diversity is one of the key elements for us right now,” says Montiel. “We want to reach a wide audience, sometimes screening series which otherwise won’t be seen in Spain, but also broadening industry connections.”

Andalusia Calling

Projects submitted to Boost, SISF’s Andalusia-focused co-production platform, have risen from around 15 the first year, 25-30 in 2025 and over 60 this year, says Montiel. That’s symptomatic of broader growth and the reputation of SISF of forging industry contacts. A new industry umbrella initiative, South Connect, targeting Andalusia’s industry, creates meeting and networking opportunities for producers, Andalusia-based directors and location managers, “We would like to help the Andalusian industry to connect more with the Spanish and international industry,” says Montiel. SISF section Sur profiles series either from Andalusian companies, led this year by the feel-good second chance drama “Olivia,” from Womack Producciones, or Andalusia-born directors, such as Paco Cabezas, creator of the envelope-pushing crime thriller “La Nena,” or shot in part in Spain’s broader south, such as Netflix hit “The Glass Cuckoo.”

A closer look at SISF’s Fiction Competition:

“American Hostage,” (Shawn Ryan, Eileen Myers, U.S)

MGM+ true-events-based crime thriller “American Hostage,” produced by Sony Pictures Television, set in 1977 and led by “Mad Men” star John Hamm playing a respected Indianapolis radio host phoned by a madman hostage taker (Giovani Ribisi) who demands to be interviewed. A Toronto Primetime world premiere, the series has been mostly well received by critics. Hamm’s performance is “chamber music,” says John Anderson in The Wall Street Journal. Ribisi’s, he adds, is “death metal.”

“Blindspot Berlin,” (David Nawrath, Germany)

On Dec. 19, 2016, a truck plowed into a crowd at a local Christmas market in Berlin, killing 13 and injuring dozens. Headed by “All Quiet on the Western Front’ star Albrecht Schuch, “Blindspot Berlin” tracks rookie Isra (Bayan Layla) and police investigator Frank (Schuch) as they battle to prevent the attack, chronicling “systemic failures and human errors,” says creator Nawrath (“Your Honor”). Produced by Neuesuper (“8 Days”) with among others, German broadcast giant ARD Degeto.

“The Center,” Season 2 (David Moreno, Spain)

Fast-paced, fulsomely budgeted and ranging from Strasbourg to El Salvador, Season 1 saw Spain’s National Intelligence Center (CNI) race to unmask a traitor and foil a Russia-led conspiracy.

In its second outing, a brutal double assassination unleashes a wave of hatred in Spain as CNI head Michelín (Juan Diego Botto) battles to save his wife, kidnapped by the Russian intelligence services. Rising Spanish scripted stars David Moreno and David Ulloa, behind Canneseries title “The Immortal,” return as creator and director for Season 2.

‘Infamy,’ (‘Infamia,’ Agustina Macri, Beatriz Sanchís, Spain)

Starring Susana Abaitua, who broke out in “Crazy About You” and “Patria,” then carried the weight of big Netflix ETA infiltrator movie “She Walks in Darkness.” Here she plays Emma Cruz, a lawyer investigating the disappearance of two girls 20 years ago in her hometown. A dark atmospheric thriller, says Variety, which “alternates between moments of stillness and slow-burn tension, where emotions, silences, and discomfort have time to emerge,” adds lead director Macri.

‘Patagonia,’ (Patricio Pereira, María Elena Wood, Spain, Chile)

Itziar Ituño plays a Basque teacher whose son Noah disappears without trace in the depths of Patagonia’s dazzling millennial-old larch tree forests. She flies to Chile to find him. Ending on a huge cliffhanger in Ep. 2, the series look set to lift to another level as a family drama gaining large social point when Alicia decides to stay in Hornopirén, the northern gateway to Patagonia, to battle illegal logging mafias.

‘Snake Killer,’ Anders Olholm, Amazon MGM. Studios, Denmark

Brutal – one early brawl with a potential informant goes on for minutes – a blunt crime thriller driven by a terrific turn from Pilou Asbæk (“Game of Thrones”) as Brian “Smiley” Petersen, head of Copenhagen’s notorious no-rule-book Uropatruljen narcotics squad. Mixing “the familiar mechanisms from the classic American cop cinema and Danish social realism,” director Anders Ølholm has told Variety, produced by Nordisk Film Production, and acquired for international by Reinvent Yellow.

“Somebody Should Ban Sunday Afternoons,” Isabel Coixet, Arte, France

Released on energetic pan-European public broadcaster Arte in March, after Isabel Coixet had hit a home run with movie “Three Goodbyes.” Tim Robbins makes guest appearances in a drama comedy miniseries where three twenty-something film buff flatmates spend Sunday afternoons watching the saddest films they can find, while navigating existential qualms. A tribute o French cinema – Agnès Varda,Chantal Akerman. “Melancholic, touching and sometimes chatty,” said Le Parisien in an upbeat review.

“Still Breathing,” (Karianne Lund, NRK, Norway)

Announced by Variety last May, it follows Petra, 26, an idealistic medical intern at an under-funded Norwegian hospital, joins three other young doctors facing impossible moral dilemmas of a health system stretched beyond the limit. Teaming “Occupied” writer Karianne Lund, “Safe House” director Erik Svensson and “Beforeigners” producer Rubicon TV, a Banijay company, a series which is agenda-driven but “raw and gripping,” international distributor DR Sales told Variety.

“Stepping Up,” (Josh Pugh, Channel 4, U.K.)

A chosen family comedy sitcom with Pugh playing Josh, a desperate to help stepdad and to come across as a “good bloke.” Problem is his family doesn’t have any problems. “The perfect mix of hyper silly and hyper real,” said Charlie Perkins, head of come, Channel 4, when announcing the six-part series order. If it’s anything as good as the supremely top-notch cringemaking short format on Channel 4 Comedy Blaps, Cadiz is in for a treat.

What South Says About International TV?

New Models

Described as a Movistar Plus “Exclusive” rather than Original, “Patagonia” marks the first major premium series from the biggest Spanish pay TV/SVOD operator whose creators are not Spanish but rather María Elena Wood (“News of a Kidnapping,” “Dignity”) and Patricio Pereira (“Mary & Mike”), pioneers of premium TV fiction in Chile as Movistar Plus in Spain. Directing is Chile’s Rodrigo Susarte, helmer on 2025 breakout “Hidden Island.” The Basque Country’s Atlantika Films, headed by Nano Arrieta and Claudia Ruiz, also produces. “Patagonia” is a “new way of producing international fiction,” says Arrieta.

’Hyper Distribution’

Partnering Movistar Plus, which has its own international TV distribution operation, “Patagonia” is sold, however, by Germany’s go-getting ZDF Studios. As global streaming services take first TV window in Spain, that leaves series open to negotiate other territory tights. Disney+, for instance, bowed Olivia on July 1 but Mediterráneo Mediaset España Group handles international distribution. Netflix’s third quarter results highlighted aggregation deals with TF1 and Globo. Such tie.ups are well established in Spain as its TV scene opens up. Mediaset España has a years-old co-releasing alliance with Prime Video. Disney+ streams 300 hours of Atresplayer and parent Atresmedia from a deal announced in September 2025.

Just How Good Is European Scripted?

“Still Breathing” is billed as Norway’s answer to “The Pitt.” Its debut this April gave NRK its biggest-ever opening for a drama outside of the pubcaster’s Christmas shows. Backing also comes from two institutions on Europe’s TV scene: a prized pick-up by New8, a network of Nordic public broadcasters and Germany’s ZDF, Netherlands NPO and Belgium’s VRT. Coin from the Banijay Scripted Fund allowed for a deep dive in early development research. It’s scored a great 8.5 audience review on IMDB. Its reception at Cadiz and possible plaudits will test its audience reach beyond its Northern European homeland,

France Looks to Spain

Few broadcasters are as bullish about building a European TV production network than Arte, which brings Isabel Coixet’s “Someone Should Ban Sunday Afternoons” to Cadiz. Coixet is just the latest major Spanish talent produced or co-produced by Arte which also takes in Rodrigo Sorogoyen (“The New Years”), Jorge and Alberto Sánchez-Cabezudo (“Killing a Bear”) and Alberto Rodríguez (“The Anatomy of a Moment”), now nominated for an Intl. Emmy, All three series are Movistar Plus Originals. Spain burst on the international TV scene in 2018 when “Money Heist” gave Netflix its first non-English global blockbuster. It has now seen second phase lift-off, primarily through France.
