“What made me nervous was how it could negatively affect my acting career and my personal life,” Lawrence said on the “Call Her Daddy” podcast about her biggest concern with joining the franchise when she was 20 years old. “The one thing I was always sure of when I was younger was that I wanted to be a mom, and this looked so different then doing some indies. ‘Twilight’ had just come out and everybody saw what that was. It was more like… how is this going to change my life and my acting career?”

Watch Lawrence’s full interview on the “Call Her Daddy” podcast in the video below.

title: Sundance 2027 In Boulder Unveils Legacy Lineup With ‘Better Luck Tomorrow’, ‘Memento’, ‘Y Tu Mamá También’ & More
summary: Sundance Film Festival 2027 has announced its first lineup for the inaugural Boulder, Colorado edition with the The Legacy Program, formerly known as From the Collection, which includes archival and restored screenings of indie classics that launched at the fest. Cinephile social platform, Letterboxd, is a co-presenter of the Legacy program, and there will be […]
content:
Sundance Film Festival 2027 has announced its first lineup for the inaugural Boulder, Colorado edition with the The Legacy Program, formerly known as From the Collection, which includes archival and restored screenings of indie classics that launched at the fest.

Cinephile social platform, Letterboxd, is a co-presenter of the Legacy program, and there will be forthcoming details for onsite activations at the Boulder cinema event which takes place Jan. 21-31. The Legacy portion of Sundance will occur during the fest’s second half from Tuesday, Jan. 27-Sunday, Jan. 31.

There will still be an online portion of the festival, which will run from Thursday, Jan. 28-Sunday, Jan. 31.

The Legacy lineup includes the 2002 Sundance Film Festival version of Better Luck Tomorrow (Justin Lin); a digital 4K restoration of Dogtown and Z-Boys (Stacy Peralta); a 35th anniversary screening of Fool’s Fire(Julie Taymor); Nitrate Kisses (Barbara Hammer), which premiered in the U.S. at the Festival 35 years ago and whose director is at the center of Brydie O’Connor’s 2026 Sundance Film Festival documentary Barbara Forever; a 25th anniversary screening of Real Women Have Curves (Patricia Cardoso); a 35th anniversary screening of Swoon (Tom Kalin); and a 25th anniversary screening of a 4K restoration of Y tu mamá también (Alfonso Cuarón).

Watch on Deadline

The Legacy program will also include a two-part session on the final weekend of the Festival called “Sundance Film Festival presents: Cinema Interruptus featuring Memento” (Christopher Nolan), featuring a 4K restoration and discussion. Legacy screenings will include director appearances and select cast members in attendance,



Next reps the 30th anniversary of Sundance Institute and the UCLA Film & Television Archive. Together they established a film preservation initiative, the Sundance Institute Collection at UCLA, to ensure the long-term preservation of independent film. The Collection currently holds material from over 1,000 titles and has participated in restorations of Hoop Dreams, River of Grass, Mysterious Skin, Doom Generation, Just Another Girl on the IRT, High Art, Go Fish, Three Seasons, Paris Is Burning, Superstar, Unzipped, The Hours and Times, SLAM, and, this year, Better Luck Tomorrow and Swoon.



“We’re excited to kick off the Festival season in earnest with this first 2027 Sundance Film Festival announcement, revealing some of our Legacy programming,” said Eugene Hernandez, Director, Sundance Film Festival and Public Programming. “Each year we honor the legacy of our founder Robert Redford and the history of the Sundance Film Festival by looking back at just a few of the films and filmmakers who have shaped our history. Our first festival in our new home in Boulder, Colorado will bring change, but as we evolve, we’ll keep at our core what we celebrate: our rich history. Sundance will always uplift independent voices, and our Legacy slate is a beautiful example of that. We are also pleased to announce Letterboxd’s co-partnership for the Legacy category — it’s great to collaborate with organizations that build momentum and excitement for a culture of cinematic discovery, and we look forward to having them at the Festival with us in January.”

“Revisiting and becoming newly acquainted with films from our previous lineups in a theatrical setting, in community, and with some of the talent behind the films is a rare treat — even more so when these projects have been restored,” said Kim Yutani, Director of Programming, Sundance Film Festival.

“We’re really looking forward to welcoming back these artists and know that audiences will enjoy the opportunity to complement the new films we will soon be announcing with these classics.”

“Our Legacy programming at the Sundance Film Festival grew out of a partnership with the UCLA Film & Television Archive and its continued growth is running in parallel to the incredible moment repertory cinema is having across the country right now,” said John Nein, Sundance Film Festival Senior Programmer and Director of Strategic Initiatives. “This program offers a space for brand-new restorations of classic independent films to be discovered or rediscovered by audiences as the creative teams behind these films reunite — it’s an exciting way of celebrating what these artists have brought to independent storytelling.”

Below are descriptions of the Legacy lineup:



25th Anniversary of Better Luck Tomorrow / U.S.A. (Director, Screenwriter, and Producer: Justin Lin, Screenwriters: Ernesto Foronda, Fabian Marquez, Producers: Julie Asato, Ernesto Foronda) — To escape the crushing pressure of academic perfection, a group of high-achieving teens lead a secret, thrill-seeking double life of petty crime that quickly spins out of control. Cast: Karin Anna Cheung, John Cho, Roger Fan, Sung Kang, Parry Shen, Jason Tobin. Fiction. Better Luck Tomorrow premiered at the 2002 Sundance Film Festival as part of the U.S. Dramatic Competition. It was subsequently released with small changes in the edit. The original 2002 Sundance Film Festival cut of Better Luck Tomorrow was restored by the UCLA Film & Television Archive in collaboration with Sundance Institute and Perfect Storm Entertainment, with funding provided by Chris Quintos Cathcart, co-CEO of Unapologetic Projects. The 4K restoration utilized the original 35 mm camera negatives, 35 mm Sundance Film Festival print, and DA-88 sound materials and was supervised by filmmaker Justin Lin at Resillion and Deluxe Audio Services. Additional lab services by Roundabout Entertainment, Inc. The release version has also been restored and archived. Special thanks to Paramount Pictures for permission to screen the film.

25th Anniversary of Dogtown and Z-Boys / U.S.A (Director and Screenwriter: Stacy Peralta, Screenwriter: Craig Stecyk, Producer: Agi Orsi) — The Z-Boys: outcast surf rats from the run-down Dogtown neighborhood in Venice, California, who revolutionized skateboarding with their innovative style and attitude. The documentary is an exploration of the birth of a cultural phenomenon, narrated by Sean Penn and featuring old-school skating footage, a blistering soundtrack, and interviews with Tony Alva, Jay Adams, and Tony Hawk. Dogtown and Z-Boys premiered at the 2001 Sundance Film Festival as part of the U.S. Documentary Competition and won the Audience Award: Documentary and Directing Award: Documentary. 2027 marks the 25th anniversary of its theatrical release. The 4K digital restoration was undertaken from the original 35 mm elements by Sony Pictures Classics. The restoration was approved by the filmmakers.



35th Anniversary of Fool’s Fire / U.S.A. (Director, Screenwriter, and Producer: Julie Taymor, Producer: Kerry Orent) — A captured dwarf, Hopfrog, is forced to become jester to a tyrannical king. But when the King is gifted with another little person, whom the king debases and shames, Hopfrog plots a terrible revenge. Based on the story “Hop-Frog” by Edgar Allan Poe. Cast: Michael J. Anderson, Tom Hewitt, Mireille Mossé. Fiction. Fool’s Fire premiered at the 1992 Sundance Film Festival as part of the U.S. Dramatic Competition. This new restoration was created by the nonprofit IndieCollect in collaboration with Julie Taymor and with support from the Golden Globe Foundation, using a 6.5K scan of the original 35 mm negative and a soundtrack restored by Endpoint Audio Labs from the optical track negative. Featuring an extended conversation with Julie Taymor and clips from The Making of Fool’s Fire, exploring the film’s artistry and cutting-edge use of high definition.

Nitrate Kisses / U.S.A. (Director: Barbara Hammer) — A portrait of queer sexuality that weaves striking images of four lesbian and gay couples with archival footage, interviews, sexual imagery, and queer cinema dating back to the 1930s to unearth forbidden and long-invisible histories. Documentary. Nitrate Kisses had its U.S. premiere at the 1993 Sundance Film Festival as part of the U.S. Documentary Competition. Nitrate Kisses was preserved by the Academy Film Archive. The original 16 mm A/B-rolls were scanned at 4K and restored by BB Optics. The mono mix was digitized from the original 16 mm mag track. The restoration was funded by Frameline and supervised by The Estate of Barbara Hammer and Brydie O’Connor.



The 25th Anniversary of Real Women Have Curves / U.S.A. (Director: Patricia Cardoso, Screenwriters: George LaVoo, Josefina López, Producers: George Lavoo, Effie Brown) — Ana, a first-generation Mexican American teenager, fights for her independence and her curves in a war of wills with her mother. Based on the play by Josefina López. Cast: America Ferrera, George Lopez, Ingrid Oliu, Lupe Ontiveros, Brian Sites. Real Women Have Curves premiered at the 2002 Sundance Film Festival as part of the U.S. Dramatic Competition and took home the Audience Award: Dramatic and the Special Jury Prize for Acting for America Ferrera and Lupe Ontiveros. Supervised by director Patricia Cardoso and director of photography Jim Denault, this new 4K restoration was undertaken by Criterion in collaboration with Warner Bros. Pictures, Sundance Institute, and the Academy Film Archive from the 35 mm original camera negative.



The 35th Anniversary of Swoon / U.S.A. (Director and Screenwriter: Tom Kalin, Producers: Christine Vachon) — The true story of Nathan Leopold and Richard Loeb, who kidnapped and brutally murdered 14-year-old Bobby Franks in Chicago in 1924. The revelation that these wealthy Jewish college students had a sexual relationship scandalized the nation. After their arrest and trial, they were sentenced to life plus 99 years. Cast: Craig Chester, Michael Kirby, John A. Mudd, Daniel Schlachet, Natalie Stanford, Michael Stumm, Ron Vawter. Swoon premiered at the 1992 Sundance Film Festival as part of the U.S. Dramatic Competition and took home the Excellence in Cinematography Award: Dramatic. Swoon was restored by the Academy Film Archive and UCLA Film & Television Archive in collaboration with Frameline, Strand Releasing, and Sundance Institute in 4K from the original 16 mm A/B camera negatives, 35 mm interpositive, 35 mm dupe negative, and 35 mm magnetic track. The restoration was supervised by Tom Kalin and Ellen Kuras at Roundabout Entertainment, Inc. and Deluxe Audio Services. Restoration funding was provided by the Academy Film Archive and UCLA Film & Television Archive with additional support from Frameline, Ellen Kuras, Strand Releasing, and Sundance Institute.



The 25th Anniversary of Y tu mamá también / Mexico (Director, Screenwriter and Producer: Alfonso Cuarón, Screenwriter: Carlos Cuarón, Producer: Jorge Vergara) — After their girlfriends jet off for the summer, a pair of Mexico City teenagers become bewitched by an older Spanish woman they meet at a wedding. When she agrees to accompany them on a road trip, the three form an increasingly intense and sensual bond. Cast: Gael García Bernal, Diego Luna, Maribel Verdú. Y tu mamá también screened at the 2002 Sundance Film Festival as part of the Special Events category. Newly restored by Esperanto Films in 4K under the supervision of filmmaker Alfonso Cuarón and cinematographer Emmanuel Lubezki. The feature is a Janus Films release.

MEMENTO, Guy Pearce, 2000



LEGACY SPECIAL EVENTS

Memento / U.S.A. (Director: Christopher Nolan) — A former insurance investigator who now suffers from anterograde amnesia uses notes and tattoos to hunt down his wife’s murderer. Fiction.

Memento had its U.S. festival premiere at the 2001 Sundance Film Festival in the U.S. Dramatic Competition and it took home the Waldo Salt Screenwriting Award. Restored in 4K from original interpositive materials by Umbrella with approval from director Christopher Nolan.

Cinema Interruptus is also part of our Offscreen program, to be announced in its entirety soon.

As part of the screening, there will be Sundance Film Festival presents: Cinema Interruptus featuring Memento. A tradition first established by the late Roger Ebert, Cinema Interruptus is communal film criticism in two sessions. As Memento screens, participants can yell “Stop!” at any point to make a comment or ask a question, after which the film will resume. Critic and author Josh Larsen — who hosted Interruptus at the University of Colorado Boulder’s Conference on World Affairs from 2017 to 2024 — will moderate the discussion, with the goal of finishing the entire movie by the end of the second session.

title: TBD Post Hires Industry Veteran Matt Wallis As Head Of Post & Operations
summary: EXCLUSIVE: The co-creator of Showtime’s Emmy-nominated Disgraced has joined Austin’s TBD Post. Matthew Wallis was named Head of Post & Operations at the Texas-based post-production studio, which works on feature films, series, commercials and branded content for clients including Apple TV, Netflix, Disney and next-gen filmmakers like hugely popular YouTuber Markiplier. Wallis is known as […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: The co-creator of Showtime’s Emmy-nominated Disgraced has joined Austin’s TBD Post.

Matthew Wallis was named Head of Post & Operations at the Texas-based post-production studio, which works on feature films, series, commercials and branded content for clients including Apple TV, Netflix, Disney and next-gen filmmakers like hugely popular YouTuber Markiplier.

Wallis is known as co-creator and co-exec producer on 2017 feature doc Disgraced, which followed the 2003 case of the death of Baylor University basketball star Patrick Dennehy at the hands of teammate Carlton Dotson. He was also head of post on CNN’s High Profits. The 20-year industry veteran has served as producer and post-production supervisor on more than 100 hours of film and TV.

At TBD Post, Wallis will oversee staff, technology, strategy, and workflow across editorial, color, VFX, sound, and finishing, and lead projects from bid through delivery. His hire is part of an expansion of headcount at TBD, which is set to take advantage of the new Texas film incentive scheme, which will total $1.5B over ten years.

Watch on Deadline

TBD’s founders – Ted Griffis and Brandon Thomas – were among the group that last month launched Goldenrod, a technology-focused production business that consults on opportunities available from the expanded Texas Moving Image Industry Incentive Program.

“I’ve worked with TBD since the company started, first as a client, then as a producer. I knew what this team could do long before I considered joining, and that’s most of why I did,” said Wallis. “After twenty years building the systems that let creative people do their best work, I’m bringing all of it here, starting the way I always do, by listening and asking a lot of questions. I’m excited for our future, and the future of post production in Texas.”

TBD’s recent credits include Markiplier’s feature Iron Lung, Netflix sports pic The Long Game and Apple TV documentary Fathom, as well as film, television and commercial projects for brands such as Range Rover, EA, Bacardi and Dodge.

“Matt has sat in our suites and theaters as a client for over a decade,” said Griffis. “He’s seen our work from the other side of the glass, and he knows exactly where we can go next. Handing him the reins on operations frees the rest of us to stay hands-on with the craft and keep raising the bar for our clients.”

title: Four ‘Star Trek’ Vets Reunite For Sci-Fi ‘Life 2.0’, OneTwoThree Media Launches AFM Sales; Brit Comedy With Stephen Fry, Jane Horrocks Also On Slate
summary: EXCLUSIVE: OneTwoThree Media is launching worldwide sales ahead of the AFM on the sci-fi feature Life 2.0, written and directed by Star Trek alum Michael Dorn (Star Trek: The Next Generation, Star Trek: Deep Space Nine), who also stars. Dorn is joined in the film by fellow Star Trek franchise vets Marina Sirtis (Star Trek: […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: OneTwoThree Media is launching worldwide sales ahead of the AFM on the sci-fi feature Life 2.0, written and directed by Star Trek alum Michael Dorn (Star Trek: The Next Generation, Star Trek: Deep Space Nine), who also stars.

Dorn is joined in the film by fellow Star Trek franchise vets Marina Sirtis (Star Trek: The Next Generation), Michelle Hurd (Star Trek: Picard), and Dominic Keating (Star Trek: Enterprise).

Dorn “plays an operative in deep-space isolation, with only an AI hologram for company, until an enigmatic new companion arrives. An accident uncovers the truth about their origins, forcing a fight for survival against motives engineered back on Earth.”

Produced by Emily Corcoran for Cork Films and Michael Dorn for Sabrejet, the film was shot entirely in the UK. The project marks Dorn’s feature directing debut and is the first science-fiction feature to reunite Dorn and Sirtis since 2002’s Star Trek: Nemesis.

Watch on Deadline

Alongside this title, the company has taken on international sales for two further features: the UK sci-fi comedy Time Travel Is Dangerous! and the US psychological thriller The Black Box.

Also new to OneTwoThree Media’s slate is Time Travel Is Dangerous!, directed by Chris Reading. The London-set comedy feature is narrated by Stephen Fry and stars Johnny Vegas, Jane Horrocks, Sophie Thompson, and Mark Heap, with Brian Blessed voicing an octopus monster. It premiered at the Austin Film Festival.

The third new addition is U.S. film The Black Box, described as a psychological thriller directed by Vitor Cardoso and Ricardo R. Marques. Set in the Hollywood Hills during a graduation farewell party, “a group of friends stumbles upon ‘The Black Box’ — an elusive internet sensation and twisted version of Truth or Dare said to choose its own players.”

Deals across the slate were negotiated for OneTwoThree Media by Joey Dawson with Emily Corcoran of Cork Films on Life 2.0, and Chris Reading of The Unreason Ltd on Time Travel Is Dangerous!, and Alan Green with Mark Silba on The Black Box.

title: Olivia Holt, Jaimie Alexander & Rohan Campbell Set For Scout Taylor-Compton’s Horror Movie ‘Survive: The Game’; Filming Underway In Spain
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Olivia Holt (Heart Eyes), Jaimie Alexander (Thor) and Rohan Campbell (Halloween Ends) have been set to lead Scout Taylor-Compton’s Survive: The Game, a horror movie currently filming entirely in Gipuzkoa, Spain, at Zinealdea Studios, and on location in Irún, Spain. The synopsis reads: “When a group of friends unearth an ancient board game inside […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Olivia Holt (Heart Eyes), Jaimie Alexander (Thor) and Rohan Campbell (Halloween Ends) have been set to lead Scout Taylor-Compton’s Survive: The Game, a horror movie currently filming entirely in Gipuzkoa, Spain, at Zinealdea Studios, and on location in Irún, Spain.

The synopsis reads: “When a group of friends unearth an ancient board game inside a secluded cabin with a violent past, each roll of the dice brings a deadly fate to life, and the only way to survive is to finish the game.”

Holt, who recently starred in horror Heart Eyes, will appear opposite Alexander, best known for her five-season run as Jane Doe on Blindspot and her recurring role as Lady Sif in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Campbell, who broke out opposite Jamie Lee Curtis in Halloween Ends and currently stars in Netflix’s Below, rounds out the lead cast.

Taylor-Compton is directing from a script she wrote with Michael Kennedy (Heart Eyes). An actress-turned-filmmaker known for the Halloween franchise, she previously wrote and directed Road to Recovery and co-directed Last Chance Motel.

Watch on Deadline

The film is being produced by Randy Wayne and Talia Bella under their Rebellium Films banner, Tom O’Connell and Scout Taylor-Compton of Building Blocks Productions, and Amy Covell of Red Phoenix Productions. Executive producers include Leire Apellaniz of Sr. y Sra., Mark Albela, Michael Kennedy, and Dauntless Productions. The production sees the film as having franchise potential.

“I’ve played the final girl. I spent years learning what it takes to survive a horror movie: the running, the screaming, the moment you finally turn around and fight,” said Taylor-Compton. “With Survive: The Game, I wanted to ask a different question. What if the thing chasing you isn’t outside the door? What if surviving means confronting the worst version of yourself first?”

“This is the fourth film we’ve worked on with Scout, and the second she’s directing for Rebellium,” said producer Randy Wayne. “She’s a powerhouse with an extreme attention to detail and an unmatched drive. Audiences are going to meet antagonists they’ve never seen before – creative, scary, and inventive. We’re honored to help bring Survive: The Game to life with her.”

Holt is repped by WME, Entertainment 360, and Yorn, Levine. Alexander is repped by Gersh, Berwick & Kovacik and Ginsburg Daniels Kallis. Campbell is repped by CAA, Sol22 and Webster Talent Management. Taylor-Compton is repped by Innovative Artists.

title: Independent Creative Management Signs Serhat Metin
summary: EXCLUSIVE: UK agency Independent Creative Management (ICM) has signed Havoc actor Serhat Metin. Metin is known for last year playing a detective, Cortez, in Netflix’s Havoc, the police action thriller starring Tom Hardy, Timothy Oliphant, Forest Whitaker and Jessie Mei Li. He has also appeared in Havoc director Gareth Evans’s Sky series Gangs of London, […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: UK agency Independent Creative Management (ICM) has signed Havoc actor Serhat Metin.

Metin is known for last year playing a detective, Cortez, in Netflix’s Havoc, the police action thriller starring Tom Hardy, Timothy Oliphant, Forest Whitaker and Jessie Mei Li.

He has also appeared in Havoc director Gareth Evans’s Sky series Gangs of London, and has credits for Michael Flatley’s Blackbird, Guy Ritchie’s The Gentlemen in 2019 and the likes of Aladin, The Mummy, American Assassin and Patient Zero.

The Turkish-Cypriot actor is based in London and began his acting career after transitioning from amateur boxing in 2011.

Watch on Deadline

He joins the likes of Tom Prior, Shane Afolabi, Nathaniel Jacobs, Eshe Asante and Erol Ismail on the books at ICM, which is part of Independent Creative Group and led by CEO Katerina Michael.

“I’m delighted to have joined ICM and have been incredibly pleased with the support and opportunities they’ve provided in such a short space of time,” said Metin.

“Katerina and the team at ICM understand my vision for my acting career and we are definitely on the same page regarding the next steps. I’m excited to be working with a team that understands my vision and shares my enthusiasm for what lies ahead.”

Michael said ICM would “look forward to supporting him as he takes the next exciting step in his career,” and added: “I’m extremely confident that Serhat has a very promising future ahead of him. He has a fantastic presence, genuine talent and all the qualities needed to build a successful career.”

title: Director Gregory Nava Remembers Dolores Huerta, the Civil Rights Icon Who Introduced Him to His Wife and Trusted Them With Her Life Story
summary: Director Gregory Nava is paying tribute to civil rights icon Dolores Huerta, who died Wednesday at 96. Huerta introduced Nava to his wife, Barbara Martinez Jitner, and served as a witness at their wedding. In the last years of her life, she sat with them for more than 70 hours and told them things she […]
content:
Director Gregory Nava is paying tribute to civil rights icon Dolores Huerta, who died Wednesday at 96.

Huerta introduced Nava to his wife, Barbara Martinez Jitner, and served as a witness at their wedding. In the last years of her life, she sat with them for more than 70 hours and told them things she had never told anyone.

On Tuesday night, the two filmmakers drove to Bakersfield to say goodbye.

Huerta, the co-founder of the United Farm Workers and the woman who gave the country the phrase “Sí, se puede,” died Wednesday morning at her home, surrounded by family. A family spokesperson said the cause was cancer.

“We were blessed to be by Dolores’ side last night in Bakersfield, to say goodbye and stand with her family in love,” Nava and Martinez Jitner wrote in a joint statement. “Dolores was a great light and a fearless warrior for justice. She set the world ablaze with her passion for equality and inspired generations to discover their own power.”

The pair have spent the better part of three years preparing the first dramatic feature about Huerta’s life, which Variety first reported in April 2024, with Nava writing and directing and Martinez Jitner co-writing and producing with him. Huerta, who had been approached by a long line of filmmakers for her life rights, chose the two people she had known for decades.

“In these last few years, Dolores and her beautiful family welcomed us even closer, entrusting us with the telling of her life — its extraordinary courage, its struggles and joys, its deepest pain,” they said. “It has been one of the greatest privileges of our professional lives, and a deeply personal trust. We will honor it with tenderness and care, carrying her voice and her story to generations yet to come.”

Nava helmed films like “El Norte,” his 1983 drama about two Guatemalan siblings crossing into the United States, which earned him an Oscar nomination for original screenplay and helped put a face on the immigration debate of the Reagan years. He followed up with the drama “Mi Familia” and the biopic “Selena,” the 1997 film that made Jennifer Lopez a movie star. All three sit in the Library of Congress’ National Film Registry. Martinez Jitner has been his collaborator since “Selena.” In 2002, she became the first Latina to executive produce a primetime network drama with PBS’ “American Family,” which Nava created.

When Variety broke the news of the biopic, Nava described his subject as “like an earthquake that shook this country.” Huerta, for her part, said she had spent a year sharing “intimate, never before disclosed details” of her journey and that Nava “has made classic movies that are the most authentic and impactful of our American Latino experience.”

In March, Huerta told The New York Times that Cesar Chavez, her partner in building the farmworkers movement, raped her in 1966 in a secluded grape field. She had carried the secret for 60 years, out of fear it would unravel everything the union had won. “My silence ends here,” she said at the time.

Dolores Clara Fernández was born April 10, 1930, in Dawson, New Mexico, the daughter of a coal miner and a mother who ran a hotel in Stockton, Calif., that catered to farmworkers. She taught elementary school for a year and quit after watching hungry children arrive in class barefoot, deciding she could do more for them by organizing their parents.

In 1962, she and Chavez founded the National Farm Workers Association, which became the UFW. She helped lead the 1965 Delano grape strike alongside Filipino labor leader Larry Itliong and negotiated the first contracts in the fields. In 1988, while protesting outside a George H.W. Bush fundraiser in San Francisco, a police officer beat her with a baton, breaking four ribs and rupturing her spleen. She recovered and spent the next decade recruiting Latinas to run for office.

President Barack Obama awarded her the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2012. California made April 10 “Dolores Huerta Day” in 2018. Huerta was a mother to 11 children.

The last time I saw Nava and Huerta in a room together was Oct. 24, 2025, at the Critics Choice Association’s Celebration of Latino Cinema and Television in Beverly Hills, a night I co-programmed and hosted. Huerta was the evening’s Icon Award recipient, and it was Nava who walked onstage to hand it to her. He talked about her as a force of history, while she spoke about the young people in the room and how they needed to get off the sidewalk and into the street to fight. She was 95 then, and nobody in the ballroom was sharper and more energizing.

“Today, we mourn,” Nava and Martinez Jitner wrote. “We send all our love and gratitude to her family. The baton is now in our hands. We will carry it forward, Dolores.”

They closed with the three words she spent six decades proving true: “Sí, se puede.”

title: YouTube Q3 Ad Revenue Rises 9% to $11.2 Billion as Alphabet Misses Earnings Estimates
summary: YouTube continued to vacuum up digital ad dollars in the third quarter of 2026, but the video platform grew at slower pace than in recent quarters. Its growth also was lower than Alphabet overall, given a sales boom in the internet giant’s Google Cloud division, which saw revenue double. Meanwhile, Alphabet came in below analyst […]
content:
YouTube continued to vacuum up digital ad dollars in the third quarter of 2026, but the video platform grew at slower pace than in recent quarters. Its growth also was lower than Alphabet overall, given a sales boom in the internet giant’s Google Cloud division, which saw revenue double. Meanwhile, Alphabet came in below analyst estimates for Q3 on the top and bottom lines.

For Q3, YouTube ad revenue was $11.2 billion, an increase of 9.2% from the year prior, below analyst projections. That’s compared with growth of 15% in the year-earlier period and 13% in Q2 and 11% in Q1 of this year. Note that in addition to advertising sales, YouTube also generates a massive amount of subscription revenue, which Alphabet said topped $60 billion in 2025.

In the quarter, YouTube surpassed 150 million YouTube Music and Premium subscribers globally (including trials), according to the company. It previously crossed the 125 million mark in March 2025.

Overall, Alphabet posted revenue of $127.6 billion (up 25%) and net income of $26.17 billion (down 25%), translating to earnings per share of $2.12. That fell short of Wall Street consensus estimates of $128.2 billion in revenue and EPS of $3.02, per LSEG data.

“We had a strong quarter and are now on a half-trillion dollar revenue run rate,” Sundar Pichai, CEO of Google and Alphabet said in announcing the earnings. “Our deep full stack approach is driving momentum across the business, with Alphabet revenues growing 25% year-over year. Our AI investments are driving overall Search query growth, including commercial queries. In fact, our year-over-year query growth rate is the highest it’s been in the last five years.”

In addition, according to Pichai, the Gemini AI app has reached 1 billion users, which he said makes it the fastest-growing product in Google’s history.

Like other AI “hyperscalers,” Alphabet is spending heavily on building out capacity for artificial intelligence applications. In Q2, the company had raised full-year 2026 capex guidance to $195 billion-$205 billion, up from its previous projection of $180 billion-$190 billion, driven by AI data center buildouts.

title: LaKeith Stanfield Exits ‘Molepeople’ Horror Movie, Director Ben Wheatley Replaces Rob Savage
summary: Ben Wheatley (“Normal”) is taking over directing duties for Paramount Primal and Blumhouse Atomic Monster’s upcoming movie, “Molepeople.” Rob Savage (“The Boogeyman, “Other Mommy”), who was set to helm the project, has departed due to scheduling conflicts, with previously announced star LaKeith Stanfield also exiting the film. “Molepeople” was announced earlier this month during Blumhouse […]
content:
Ben Wheatley (“Normal”) is taking over directing duties for Paramount Primal and Blumhouse Atomic Monster‘s upcoming movie, “Molepeople.”

Rob Savage (“The Boogeyman, “Other Mommy”), who was set to helm the project, has departed due to scheduling conflicts, with previously announced star LaKeith Stanfield also exiting the film.

“Molepeople” was announced earlier this month during Blumhouse Atomic Monster’s New York Comic-Con presentation. Nathan Elston wrote the script for the horror movie about a man who descends into the abandoned tunnels beneath New York City, where he discovers a “twisted society lurking beneath the streets.” The film — co-financed and co-produced by Blumhouse Atomic Monster and Paramount Primal, with Paramount handling worldwide distribution — is set for theatrical release on Aug. 27, 2027.

Producers include Blumhouse Atomic Monster chief Jason Blum; Paramount Primal heads J.D. Lifshitz and Raphael Margules; and James Harris. Savage will remain on board as an executive producer, alongside Ryan Turek, Tracy Rosenblum and Elston.

British filmmaker Wheatley has built a reputation for bold, original storytelling. His most recent film, the action thriller “Normal,” starred Bob Odenkirk and was written by “John Wick” creator Derek Kolstad. The movie premiered at TIFF’s Midnight Madness program ahead of an April 2026 theatrical release. Wheatley made his feature debut in 2009 with “Down Terrace,” followed by 2011’s “Kill List,” which earned six British Independent Film Award nominations, including best director and best screenplay.

Since then, Wheatley has built a resume that spans indie films (“High-Rise,” starring Tom Hiddleston; “Free Fire,” executive produced by Martin Scorsese; the experimental feature “Bulk”) and major studio productions (Warner Bros.’ “Meg 2: The Trench,” starring Jason Statham; Netflix’s “Rebecca”). He is represented by WME, Independent Talent Group, and Johnson Shapiro Slewett & Kole.

title: Selena Gomez and Demi Lovato Recreate ‘Princess Protection Program’ Moments in New Rare Beauty Campaign
summary: Selena Gomez and Demi Lovato are bringing back “Delena.” The former Disney Channel stars have reunited for a new campaign for Gomez’s beauty brand, Rare Beauty, recreating moments from their 2009 film “Princess Protection Program” and their early Youtube videos together. Titled “Still Making Each Other Blush,” the campaign introduces the limited-edition “Delena” Soft Pinch […]
content:
Selena Gomez and Demi Lovato are bringing back “Delena.”

The former Disney Channel stars have reunited for a new campaign for Gomez’s beauty brand, Rare Beauty, recreating moments from their 2009 film “Princess Protection Program” and their early Youtube videos together.

Titled “Still Making Each Other Blush,” the campaign introduces the limited-edition “Delena” Soft Pinch Liquid Blush Bundle, named after the fan-coined nickname for the childhood friends. The $50 set features two shades of Rare Beauty’s bestselling liquid blush: Hope, a nude mauve favored by Gomez, and Virtue, a beige peach selected by Lovato.

The bundle, which includes a Soft Pinch Blush Brush and is exclusively available on Rare Beauty’s website. But you can shop other products featured in the campaign separately on retailers such as Ulta and Sephora.

Delena Soft Pinch Liquid Blush Bundle Buy Now

The campaign references several moments from the pair’s Disney Channel years. In one image, Gomez and Lovato recreate the poster for “Princess Protection Program,” wearing updated versions of the blue and yellow gowns worn by their characters, Carter Mason and Princess Rosalinda. In a video posted to Gomez’s Youtube channel, the pair revisit their 2008 YouTube series, “The Demi and Selena Show,” with the two answering questions, discussing childhood crushes and lip-syncing to “One and the Same,” their duet from the film.

Gomez and Lovato first met as children on “Barney & Friends” before going on to star in separate Disney Channel franchises, “Wizards of Waverly Place” and “Camp Rock.” The two remained close throughout their early careers but have spoken publicly about periods of distance in their friendship.

The Rare Beauty campaign follows a recent public reunion in April, when Gomez attended the opening night of Lovato’s “It’s Not That Deep” tour in Orlando, Fla. Their appearance together marked one of their first public reunions in nearly a decade.

“Selena and I have shared a lot of memories over the years since childhood, so being able to connect in this way, in a campaign that feels so nostalgic to both of us, is such a full-circle moment,” Lovato said in a statement. “I’ve loved her liquid blush since she launched the brand so this was really fun to work on. Being on set together felt like we were back in our old bedrooms making YouTube videos and playing with makeup.”

Gomez added: “The experiences I’ve shared with Demi are truly unique. Coming together for this campaign was a beautiful reminder of that history and a chance to celebrate who we are today. One and the same… always.”

Gomez launched Rare Beauty in 2020, with the Soft Pinch Liquid Blush becoming one of the brand’s signature products. The new collaboration pairs two existing shades in a limited-edition set rather than introducing a new formula.

title: Cynthia Erivo Calls Out Public’s ‘Annoyance’ Over Ariana Grande Friendship: ‘Why Are They Showing Emotion? How Dare They Cry!’
summary: Cynthia Erivo is reflecting on the attention her friendship with “Wicked” co-star Ariana Grande received while on the press tour for the movie musical and its sequel. The theater star and singer has rocketed to greater heights of fame following Jon M. Chu’s adaptation of “Wicked,” which stars Erivo as the wicked witch Elphaba opposite […]
content:
Cynthia Erivo is reflecting on the attention her friendship with “Wicked” co-star Ariana Grande received while on the press tour for the movie musical and its sequel.

The theater star and singer has rocketed to greater heights of fame following Jon M. Chu’s adaptation of “Wicked,” which stars Erivo as the wicked witch Elphaba opposite Grande’s Glinda the Good. Many moments from the press tour for the 2024 film went viral online, and the close relationship between the stars was called into question.

“It was interesting that there were many people who had become psychologists from their couches,” Erivo told The Guardian during an interview for her upcoming courtroom drama “Prima Facie.” “There was this weird sort of, what’s the word I’m looking for … annoyance … at the fact that two women could actually be friends. Like, why are they friends? Why are they connected? There must be something wrong with them.”

Many viral moments included the co-stars hugging, crying and — perhaps most infamously — “holding space” by pinching each other’s pointer fingers. “Why are they showing emotion? How dare they cry? And how dare they laugh? And how dare they be emotive and alive?” Erivo asked.

“It’s a double-edged sword,” she added. “Because if we were dead behind the eyes and showing no emotion, there would have been something else to say about it. I wish there was someone who could have been like, ‘Right, this is the proper balance of emotion that you should show. Don’t show this. Don’t show that. Just this amount.’”

One of the most memorable moments happened when Erivo jumped into action after a man grabbed Grande on the red carpet in Singapore. Erivo described the moment as terrifying and said her reaction was just “‘Get this man away from us now.’”

The internet began positioning Erivo as Grande’s “bodyguard,” a description she feels uncomfortable with. She said that reaction was centered in misogyny and misogynoir. “I was like: ‘Oh, you think because I look like this that you could talk to me this way about something that was a human thing that I would have done for any friend, and hopefully a friend would have done for me,’” she said. “But I must be a bodyguard.”

title: CNN, MS NOW And Politico Amend Lawsuit To Challenge Trump Ban On Access To Air Force One And Certain White House Areas
summary: CNN, Politico and MS NOW have filed an amended lawsuit against Donald Trump, this time challenging the White House’s continued exclusion of the outlets from Air Force One and areas of the White House where other reporters have gained access. A judge ruled earlier this month that the White House cannot revoke the hard passes […]
content:
CNN, Politico and MS NOW have filed an amended lawsuit against Donald Trump, this time challenging the White House‘s continued exclusion of the outlets from Air Force One and areas of the White House where other reporters have gained access.

A judge ruled earlier this month that the White House cannot revoke the hard passes of dozens of reporters for the outlets, after Trump banned CNN, MS NOW and Politico from even entering the White House grounds.

But the outlets have continued to be restricted from pool duties, in which smaller groups of reporters are ushered into the Oval Office for press availabilities or are assigned to travel with the president on Air Force One.

The outlets’ legal team wrote in the amended complaint that “these exclusions reflect an unstated policy to carry out the President’s directive to take his viewpoint-discriminatory and retaliatory ban ‘as far as you can.’ Indeed, the President has been explicit that he intends to limit access to the Oval Office to news organizations that cover him favorably, declaring hours after this action was filed that ‘publications that only write negatively . . . shouldn’t be allowed access to the most important Office anywhere in the World.'”

Watch on Deadline

More to come.

title: Harry Shum Jr. On Reprising Roles In ‘Glee’ Revival & ‘Crazy Rich Asians’ Series: “Would Love To Try & Find A Way To Make It Work”
summary: Harry Shum Jr. is currently a contestant on Dancing with the Stars, and two franchises he’s been part of are getting continuations: Glee and Crazy Rich Asians. On October 7, Deadline reported that HBO ordered a series of Crazy Rich Asians, and on October 21, Disney+ and Hulu ordered a Glee reboot. “You know what? I love […]
content:
Harry Shum Jr. is currently a contestant on Dancing with the Stars, and two franchises he’s been part of are getting continuations: Glee and Crazy Rich Asians.

On October 7, Deadline reported that HBO ordered a series of Crazy Rich Asians, and on October 21, Disney+ and Hulu ordered a Glee reboot.

“You know what? I love those two franchises,” Shum Jr. told Entertainment Weekly after his participation on DWTS. “Obviously, the last of [Crazy Rich Asians] ended on the characters that Gemma [Chan] and I play, so I would love to try and find a way to make it work.”

Shum Jr. played Charlie Wu in the 2018 Jon M. Chu-directed romantic comedy. The actor appeared in a mid-credits scene teasing his love story with Chan’s Astrid. Although the character was supposed to be the main focus of a Crazy Rich Asians sequel, it’s unclear whether Shum Jr. will reprise his role in the TV series.

Watch on Deadline

The Glee announcement made no mention of actors who could reprise their roles, but Shum Jr. said that although he’s “currently really, really busy now,” he “would love to keep continuing because I love those franchises.”

Shum Jr. played Mike Chang on Glee, introduced in the fourth episode of the inaugural season. The actor recurred during the first two seasons before being promoted to regular for Seasons 3 and 4. He went on to continue appearing as Mike during the series’ final two seasons on Fox.

Deadline recently reported that OG Glee stars Heather Morris and Chord Overstreet were in talks to return to the Glee reboot, after previously reporting that Lea Michele was also in talks to reprise her role as Rachel Berry.

title: LaKeith Stanfield Exits Paramount’s ‘Molepeople’ As Ben Wheatley Replaces Rob Savage As Director
summary: Two key creatives have fallen out of Molepeople, Paramount’s new horror thriller co-financed and co-produced by Blumhouse Atomic Monster and Paramount Primal: star LaKeith Stanfield and director Rob Savage, who hands over the reins to English filmmaker Ben Wheatley. Reasons for Stanfield’s departure haven’t been disclosed; Savage’s are chalked up to scheduling conflicts. We’re told […]
content:
Two key creatives have fallen out of Molepeople, Paramount’s new horror thriller co-financed and co-produced by Blumhouse Atomic Monster and Paramount Primal: star LaKeith Stanfield and director Rob Savage, who hands over the reins to English filmmaker Ben Wheatley.

Reasons for Stanfield’s departure haven’t been disclosed; Savage’s are chalked up to scheduling conflicts. We’re told the situation is amicable across the board.

Savage is fresh off the release of Other Mommy, a Jessica Chastain-led horror film for Blumhouse Atomic Monster and Universal, based on a novel by Josh Malerman, which while underperforming with critics, topped the domestic box office the weekend of October 9 and has grossed nearly $100M worldwide at time of reporting.

In Molepeople, a man descends into the abandoned tunnels beneath New York City, where he discovers a twisted society lurking beneath the streets. Paramount is set to distribute the film worldwide on August 27, 2027; they announced the casting of Stanfield and Ben Mendelsohn, who remains on board, the same day Other Mommy opened. It’s unclear whether to expect a shift in schedule, as reports had the film entering production in the UK as soon as the end of November.

Watch on Deadline

Penned by Savage’s Other Mommy collaborator Nathan Elston, Molepeople was developed independently, with Savage first announced as director in October 2024. Raphael Margules and J. D. Lifshitz, who were set to produce via their BoulderLight Pictures banner, brought the project into Paramount after being tapped to lead the studio’s new genre-focused label, Paramount Primal.

Jason Blum is producing alongside Lifshitz, Margules and James Harris. Ryan Turek and Tracy Rosenblum will exec produce alongside Savage and Elston.

A respected genre filmmaker, Wheatley most recently directed the Bob Odenkirk-led action thriller Normal, which released through Magnolia Pictures after premiering in the Midnight section of TIFF. Perhaps best known for the films Free Fire, executive produced by Martin Scorsese, and an adaptation of J.G. Ballard’s High-Rise — both for StudioCanal — he made his debut with Down Terrace, followed by Kill List, which earned six British Independent Film Award nominations, including Best Director and Best Screenplay. His filmography also includes a take on Daphne du Maurier’s Rebecca for Netflix and Meg 2: The Trench for Warner Bros., among other projects. He is represented by WME, Independent Talent Group and Johnson Shapiro Slewett & Kole.

Savage broke out with Host, an ingenious screenlife flick emerging from the Covid pandemic period, which released with Shudder and Vertigo Releasing. Subsequently, he’s helmed the horror flicks Dashcam and The Boogeyman for Momentum and 20th/Hulu, respectively. He is repped by Independent Talent Group, WME, Exile Entertainment and Jackoway Austen Tyerman.

Stanfield is coming off turns in Boots Riley’s I Love Boosters and Neon’s stoner comedy The Wrong Girls. Upcoming, he has Warner Bros.’ Taylor Sheridan-penned F.A.S.T. and John Lee Hancock’s Monsanto film for Netflix, among other projects. He is repped by CAA, Stark Management and Ginsburg Daniels Kallis.

title: Fox News Tops October Ratings, But Viewership Drops Vs. 2025; MS NOW And CNN Show Gains As Midterms Approach
summary: Fox News again topped October ratings by a wide margin, but its viewership fell during the month when compared to the same period in 2025. MS NOW and CNN, meanwhile, showed gains, likely driven by the approaching midterms. In primetime, Fox News averaged 1.68 million viewers, down 28% from the same period in 2025. MS […]
content:
Fox News again topped October ratings by a wide margin, but its viewership fell during the month when compared to the same period in 2025.

MS NOW and CNN, meanwhile, showed gains, likely driven by the approaching midterms.

In primetime, Fox News averaged 1.68 million viewers, down 28% from the same period in 2025. MS NOW averaged 925,000, up 14%, and CNN posted 598,000, up 19%. In the 25-54 demographic, Fox News averaged 145,000, down 36%, compared to 107,000 for CNN, up 39%, and 95,000 for MS NOW, up 30%.

In total day, Fox News averaged 1.1 million viewers, down 27%, compared to 588,000 for MS NOW, up 16%, and 402,000 for CNN, up 3%. In the 25-54 demo, Fox News averaged 98,000, down 33%, compared to MS NOW with 62,000, up 38%, and CNN with 60,000, up 2%.

Fox News’ viewership also was down in the third quarter, by 17% in primetime and 16% total day.

Watch on Deadline

The network still had the top five shows in cable news, led by The Five, which averaged 2.7 million total viewers, followed by Jesse Watters Primetime with 2.34 million, Special Report with Bret Baier at 2.02 million, Gutfeld! with 1.98 million and The Ingraham Angle with 1.94 million. In the 25-54 demo, The Five averaged 238,000, followed by Gutfeld! with 191,000, Jesse Watters Primetime with 189,000, Hannity with 184,000 and The Rachel Maddow Show with 184,000.

MS NOW’s top show was The Rachel Maddow Show, averaging 1.72 million viewers. CNN’s top show was The Source with Kaitlan Collins, averaging 630,000.

The figures are from Nielsen via the networks. Status first reported on the October numbers.

In its ratings release, Fox News pointed to YouTube video views since the start of the year, at 3.8 billion through Oct. 27, compared to 2.96 billion for MS NOW and 2.36 billion for CNN. Those figures were ahead of the major broadcast networks. The figures are from Emplifi.

In October, 2022, the major news networks saw a slight total day audience boost preceding the midterms, although primetime viewership dropped.

title: Inaugural West Hollywood Human Rights Film Festival To Showcase Oscar-Contending Documentaries, 20th Anniversary Screening Of ‘Blood Diamond’
summary: EXCLUSIVE: The inaugural West Hollywood Human Rights Film Festival is set to unfold November 20 and 21, a cinematic showcase of “award-winning documentaries on global human rights, social justice and civil liberties.” In addition to Oscar-contending nonfiction features and shorts, the new festival will highlight one important narrative feature – a 20th anniversary screening of […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: The inaugural West Hollywood Human Rights Film Festival is set to unfold November 20 and 21, a cinematic showcase of “award-winning documentaries on global human rights, social justice and civil liberties.”

In addition to Oscar-contending nonfiction features and shorts, the new festival will highlight one important narrative feature – a 20th anniversary screening of Blood Diamond, the drama directed by Edward Zwick and starring Oscar winners Leonardo DiCaprio, Jennifer Connelly, and two-time Oscar nominee Djimon Hounsou.

“Twenty years after Blood Diamond brought the devastating human toll of conflict diamonds to a global audience, the evening offers a timely look at the film’s enduring legacy and at what has, and has not, changed in the two decades since the film’s release,” festival organizers note. “The film’s cultural impact is undeniable. The term ‘blood diamond’ has entered the global vocabulary, and the film continues to resonate with new generations of viewers.”

A Palestinian boy in Gaza undergoes surgery in ‘ American Doctor Watermelon Pictures

The West Hollywood Human Rights Film Festival’s documentary slate boasts 14th, the new documentary from Oscar-nominated filmmaker Ava DuVernay that explores the U.S. Constitution’s crucial 14th Amendment, and threats to it under President Trump (including, but not limited to, the administration’s attempt to circumvent the amendment’s guarantee of birthright citizenship). Also in the lineup: American Doctor, director Poh Si Teng’s examination of three U.S. physicians who volunteered their medical expertise to treat Palestinian children severely injured in Israel’s yearslong attack on Gaza. American Doctor and 14th recently made DOC NYC’s shortlist of the year’s best documentaries.

Watch on Deadline

Admission to the screenings is free. Scroll for the complete lineup. The festival is organized by West Hollywood Mayor John Heilman together with veteran impact producers Bonnie Abaunza and Kathleen Rodgers of GSD Group.

“In recent years, we’ve seen the rise of authoritarian regimes all around the world,” commented Mayor Heilman. “We’ve seen organized hostility to women, ethnic minorities, immigrants, LGBTQI+ people and people with disabilities. We are seeing incredible backsliding rather than progress on human rights. The West Hollywood Human Rights Film Festival provides a forum to highlight human rights violations and to honor those filmmakers who are highlighting the work of human rights defenders.”

Heilman added, “West Hollywood is the right place for this festival because of the City’s long-standing commitment to human rights for everyone, but also because so many writers, producers and film-making businesses call West Hollywood their home.”

In a statement, GSD Group co-founders Kathleen Rodgers and Bonnie Abaunza said, “Hollywood became a cultural force because it was willing to tell bold stories that meant something. That willingness is under real pressure right now, from corporate consolidation and threats of censorship at the highest levels of government. This festival is a place to remember what those stories can do, and to gather around the values that brought so many of us to this work in the first place.”

Leonardo DiCaprio and Jennifer Connelly in ‘Blood Diamond’ Warner Bros.

In November 2027, the festival intends to expand to an annual three-day event that adds narrative feature films to the program. This year’s inaugural edition will open Friday, Nov. 20 at Pacific Design Center with the Blood Diamond event. On Saturday, Nov. 21, the festival presents its “all-day Showcase of current documentaries and documentary shorts that spotlight critical human rights stories,” with the London Hotel in West Hollywood serving as the host venue.

A nine-member judging committee reviewed the submissions and selected winners across several human rights categories, the festival notes. The committee included three human rights activists, three documentary filmmakers and three West Hollywood representatives. The selected films will screen throughout the day, each followed by a panel discussion and awards presentation.

This is the lineup for the inaugural West Hollywood Human Rights Film Festival:

Friday, November 20:

Opening Night: Blood Diamond screening

Saturday, November 21:

Documentary Films Selected

American Doctor (director Poh Si Teng)

Birds of War (directors Janay Boulos and Abd Alkader Habak)

Everybody to Kenmure Street (director Felipe Bustos Sierra)

14th (director Ava DuVernay)

Rehearsals for a Revolution (director Pegah Ahangarani)

Documentary Shorts Selected

The Baddest Speechwriter of All (director Ben Proudfoot)

La Tierra del Valor (The Home of the Brave) (director Cristina Costantini)

Maybe Tomorrow (directors Waad Al-Kateab and Wafa Mustafa)

title: ‘Smile 3’ Sets David Bruckner to Direct While Franchise Creator Parker Finn Helms ‘Possession’ Remake (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Put on a happy face, because “Smile 3” is officially in the works. Paramount has hired David Bruckner to direct and Nick Antosca to write the screenplay. They’re taking over for Parker Finn, who created the series and will remain involved as a producer. (Finn pitched the framework for the third installment.) Bruckner’s credits include […]
content:
Put on a happy face, because “Smile 3” is officially in the works.

Paramount has hired David Bruckner to direct and Nick Antosca to write the screenplay. They’re taking over for Parker Finn, who created the series and will remain involved as a producer. (Finn pitched the framework for the third installment.)

Bruckner’s credits include the 2022 “Hellraiser” reboot, 2017’s psychological thriller “The Ritual” and 2020’s supernatural horror film “The Night House.” Bruckner is particularly in demand as of late: he’s currently writing and developing a reboot of the sci-fi horror classic, “The Blob,” for Warner Bros., as well as Universal’s adaptation of “The Caretaker,” starring Sydney Sweeney, plus he’s set to direct “Mice” for A24.

Antosca is best known for creating Apple’s miniseries “Cape Fear” and co-creating Hulu’s “The Act,” as well as writing 2021’s “Antlers” and the most recent Colleen Hoover adaptation “Verity.”

Plot details for the third “Smile” movie haven’t been revealed. The first film stars Sosie Bacon as a therapist who becomes haunted by hallucinations after witnessing a patient die. In the second, Naomi Scott plays a pop singer who begins to experience a series of disturbing events as she embarks on tour. Since each “Smile” movie has functioned as a standalone sequel, with a separate story and new stars, it’s unclear who will appear in the threequel.

Finn wrote and directed 2022’s “Smile” and the 2024 sequel “Smile 2.” The original film — commissioned for streaming before pivoting to a theatrical release — became a sleeper hit, with $105 million domestically and $217 million globally. The follow-up wasn’t quite as big at the box office but became a commercial win, with $69 million domestically and $139 million globally against a modest $28 million budget. In total, the franchise, produced by Temple Hill, has earned more than $350 million worldwide.

Although Finn isn’t spearheading “Smile 3,” he’s still working closely with Paramount, having signed a first-look deal with the studio after the first “Smile” became a theatrical success. Finn is directing a remake of the 1981 supernatural thriller “Possession,” starring Callum Turner and Margaret Qualley and set for June 11, 2027.

title: Vishal Bhardwaj, Shaunak Sen-Mentored Co-Production Fund Picks Ladakh-Set ‘Kakthet’ as Winner (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Stenzin Tankyong’s debut feature “Kakthet” (Idiot), set in the remote high-altitude region of Ladakh, has been selected as the winner of the inaugural INR40 lakh ($42,000) feature film co-production fund run by Humans of Cinema and Safarnaama Pictures. The Ladakhi-language project was selected from nearly 400 entries after an extensive screening and evaluation process. The […]
content:
Stenzin Tankyong’s debut feature “Kakthet” (Idiot), set in the remote high-altitude region of Ladakh, has been selected as the winner of the inaugural INR40 lakh ($42,000) feature film co-production fund run by Humans of Cinema and Safarnaama Pictures.

The Ladakhi-language project was selected from nearly 400 entries after an extensive screening and evaluation process.

The film follows the precarious future of a government school and the community around it – both dependent on one reluctant grade 10 student who has never passed an exam, and whose teachers must attempt the impossible: save the school by saving the one student determined not to be saved.

Tankyong has spent eight years making films that bring Ladakh’s stories, landscapes and culture to international audiences. His short films “Sekool” (2019) and “Last Days of Summer” (2023) have screened at festivals including the International Film Festival Rotterdam, the Clermont-Ferrand International Short Film Festival and the Dharamshala International Film Festival.

“Kakthet” is produced by Ritu Sarin and Rajesh Thanickan, alongside French co-producers La Belle Affaire Productions. A filmmaker and producer whose career spans more than 30 years, Sarin co-founded both White Crane Films and the Dharamshala International Film Festival. Thanickan’s credits include Neeraj Ghaywan’s “Homebound,” executive produced by Martin Scorsese and premiered at Cannes in 2025; “Santosh,” which premiered at Cannes in 2024; and “Our Share of Sand,” which premiered at the 2026 Venice International Film Festival’s International Critics’ Week, where it won the Audience Award.

The project had already attracted international industry attention before the fund selection, winning the Co-Production Features Grant at WAVES Film Bazaar in 2025 and being chosen as one of 30 projects for the 2026 Asian Project Market, held alongside the Busan International Film Festival.

The fund was launched by Humans of Cinema founder Harshit Bansal and Safarnaama Pictures founder Nazim Momin, a U.S.-based engineer and producer. Filmmakers Vishal Bhardwaj and Shaunak Sen are attached as mentors, with Sen also serving as executive producer of the winning project. The jury comprised actor Imran Khan, filmmaker Arati Kadav, “All That Breathes” producer Aman Mann and festival director Aseem Chhabra.

“The past few months working on this fund have been both unbelievably challenging and incredibly rewarding. We were pleasantly surprised by the sheer number of brilliant projects we received from across the country, and we’re even more convinced how desperately initiatives like these are needed in South Asia right now. It was definitely a testing process, but we couldn’t be happier with the result. Stenzin is an exciting new filmmaker with a distinct voice, and we’re excited to be an ally in his journey of making his debut feature,” Bansal said.

“Stories like ‘Kakthet’ remind us why it is important to create opportunities for voices that emerge from outside the mainstream. I’m glad to be associated with this initiative and look forward to seeing Stenzin Tankyong bring his vision to life,” Bhardwaj said.

“The ‘Kakthet’ script mobilizes lightness, absurdity and humor to tell the story of a slow lamentation underwriting several lives in Ladakh. The story of Singay and the motley group of students and teachers always stays curious and sensitive, while never lapsing into judgement. I look forward to supporting the team in realising this project,” Sen said.

“I want to congratulate the Humans of Cinema and Safarnaama team who have worked tirelessly to create this fund. I was amazed at the passion, rigour and love they’ve put in selecting the winner. I want to congratulate the winning film and above all, I want to applaud all the filmmakers who applied. So many stories represented fearlessness and fierceness, and I was really inspired by them,” Kadav said.

“I’m delighted that ‘Kakthet’ has been selected for the inaugural HoC x Safarnaama Pictures Co-Production Fund. For independent filmmakers in India, finding support for stories rooted in our own regions, languages and lived experiences can be challenging. The fact that this support comes from within our own country makes this recognition especially meaningful for us. For a film in Ladakhi, grounded in the culture and realities of Ladakh, this support offers real encouragement to tell a story that might otherwise struggle to reach the screen and a wider audience. Initiatives like this create valuable opportunities for newer voices in independent cinema, bringing the diverse cultures and experiences of our country to wider audiences. I’m glad Kakthet (Idiot) is part of this first edition, and I thank HoC, Safarnaama Pictures, the jury and mentors for helping us take the film forward,” Tankyong said.

The screenplay is in its fourth draft. In July 2026, the team completed a three-week recce across the Changthang region and Leh for location scouting, production planning and the capture of visual and sonic material for a proof-of-concept teaser. Principal cast, crew and shooting locations are now in place, with the team focused on securing additional financing and establishing co-production relationships across Asia, Australia and Europe.

title: Alexander Payne Hit With Copyright Suit Over ‘The Holdovers’ Script
summary: A screenwriter sued Alexander Payne on Wednesday, alleging that the script for “The Holdovers” was based on his unproduced screenplay set at a children’s hospital. The screenwriter, Simon Stephenson, took his allegations to the Writers Guild of America in 2024, but was advised that the union could not adjudicate the issue and was referred to […]
content:
A screenwriter sued Alexander Payne on Wednesday, alleging that the script for “The Holdovers” was based on his unproduced screenplay set at a children’s hospital.

The screenwriter, Simon Stephenson, took his allegations to the Writers Guild of America in 2024, but was advised that the union could not adjudicate the issue and was referred to a lawyer. Payne later denied the allegations at the Sarajevo Film Festival, saying the claim was “the stupidest thing in the world.”

In addition to Payne, the lawsuit names as defendants “Holdovers” screenwriter David Hemingson, producer Mark Johnson, Miramax, Focus Features, and other corporate entities.

The suit contends that there are 46 “matched incidents” in the plots of the two scripts. As described in the complaint, Stephenson’s script, “Frisco,” tells the story of a dispirited doctor at the hospital who is stuck looking after a precocious teenage patient. The two develop a friendship on a trip to San Francisco, culminating in the doctor’s decision to quit his job and set off on a cross-country trek.

The lawsuit argues that the similarities with “The Holdovers” are more than mere coincidence, and that the structure and incidents of “Frisco” “were meticulously transposed into ‘The Holdovers,’ with surface cosmetic details changed.”

“Screenplays are often called the blueprint for a film,” the lawsuit states. “The Defendants built their film using ‘Frisco’ as their blueprint.”

Stephenson is an experienced screenwriter, with credits on “Paddington 2,” “Luca” and “The Electrical Life of Louis Wain.” He wrote “Frisco” in 2012-13, drawing on his experiences as a pediatrician, and the script was ranked third on the Black List — the list of the best unproduced screenplays in Hollywood.

According to Stephenson, his agents sought to interest Payne in making the film, and got him to read it in 2013 and again in 2019. But he passed, the lawsuit states, with his producing partner telling Stephenson’s agent that “Payne did like it but was not interested in prod or directing it.”

The suit alleges that elements of the “Frisco” script made their way into drafts of “The Holdovers” via Payne’s input to Hemingson.

title: ‘Lord of the Rings,’ ‘Spider-Man’ Digital-Human Pioneer Remington Scott to Head Eros Imagination (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: The Hollywood technologist who led Gollum’s motion capture on “The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers” and built the first digital humans made with Light Stage technology for “Spider-Man 2” will run Eros Imagination, a new creative technology and experiences business set up by Eros Innovation. Eros Innovation, an AI company founded by the […]
content:
The Hollywood technologist who led Gollum’s motion capture on “The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers” and built the first digital humans made with Light Stage technology for “Spider-Man 2” will run Eros Imagination, a new creative technology and experiences business set up by Eros Innovation.

Eros Innovation, an AI company founded by the Lulla family that draws on the film, music and IP library of Eros Media World, announced Remington Scott’s appointment as head of the unit in London. Scott will oversee creative production, the development of specialist talent and international partnerships.

The new outfit will mix human artists with visual effects, AI, digital-human tools, real-time production and games. Beyond serving Eros’ own businesses, it will go after deals with outside studios, streamers, filmmakers, game developers, musicians, estates and rights holders. It will work next to Eros Brahmand, the group’s film and content studio, and supply technology and production support for films, series, franchises and live immersive shows. Planned services run from AI-assisted filmmaking and post-production to immersive concerts, virtual production and playable game characters.

One of its first projects centers on Mohammed Rafi, the celebrated Indian playback singer. Eros has a signed deal with Rafi’s family, and the plan is an immersive music experience that combines an authorized digital performance with cinematic storytelling, high-end visuals and audience interaction. The project depends on rights and creative approvals. Eros said it is meant to introduce Rafi’s music to younger audiences. It will also give the unit digital-human and production workflows that it could reuse with other authorized artists and properties.

The unit will use Eros Innovation’s in-house Large Cultural Model (LCM) family, multimodal AI that covers language, images, video, voice and music. Eros built the models on its rights-controlled catalog, using about 1.5 trillion rights-cleared cultural tokens. Eros Imagination will team with the company’s India-based AI researchers and engineers to link the models with performance capture and real-time rendering, with humans leading the creative work. A system called Nexus will help choose the AI models and tools for each job, weighing quality, creative control, rights and cost. Eros said filmmakers and artists keep creative control.

The unit will also draw on the AI-powered Creator Studio work Eros Innovation has done with U.K. government bodies and the British creative tech sector.

Eros wants characters, artists and properties made for a film or live show to move into games, interactive stories, social content and new commercial formats where the rights allow it. The unit is also set to build digital identity systems that let artists and estates store, authorize and license digital versions of their faces, voices and performances. The company named consent, authenticity, provenance and IP protection as core principles.

Ridhima Lulla, co-founder and co-president of Eros Innovation, said Eros Brahmand is where the company develops and produces stories, while the new unit “will help build the creative technologies and experiences that allow those stories, characters and artists to move beyond the traditional boundaries of film, music and entertainment. We are not simply bringing together a production team and third-party AI tools; we are building on Eros’s own Large Cultural Models, multimodal intelligence and extensive cultural IP. Remington brings an exceptional combination of filmmaking experience, technical expertise and creative vision, and our Mohammed Rafi partnership provides a meaningful starting point.”

Scott has worked for more than 30 years across film, games and immersive entertainment. He was motion capture director on “Final Fantasy: The Spirits Within” and oversaw digital humans for “Superman Returns,” “Beowulf” and “Watchmen.” “Spider-Man 2” won the Academy Award for visual effects. On the games side, he has worked on “Call of Duty,” “Assassin’s Creed,” “Spider-Man” and “Just Cause.”

He also worked on two Emmy-nominated immersive productions: the Notorious B.I.G. virtual concert “Sky’s the Limit” and a Fox Sports tribute to coach Jimmy Johnson for Super Bowl LIX. His other credits include a Madison Beer virtual concert that won awards and Netflix’s “Altered Carbon” AR experience, which won a Lumiere Award. TheWrap put him on its 2022 Innovators List.

“Artificial intelligence, digital humans, real-time production and immersive technologies are giving filmmakers and creators tools that can fundamentally expand what is possible,” Scott said. “What excites me about Eros Imagination is combining these capabilities with Eros’s filmmaking heritage, extensive intellectual property and cultural intelligence. The Mohammed Rafi experience offers an opportunity to demonstrate how technology can celebrate a legendary artist while preserving the authenticity and emotional connection that made his work timeless.”

Eros said more partnerships and projects for the unit will be unveiled later.

title: ‘Pixels and Pencils’ Panelists Talk the Dangers of AI, Demanding Animation Processes and the Importance of Human Creativity
summary: As artificial intelligence continues to advance, animators are increasingly facing questions about the future of their craft and the role of human creativity in filmmaking. But the majority are not interested in letting AI into their art of storytelling. At Variety‘s “Pixels and Pencils” panel in Savannah, Georgia on Monday, leading filmmakers discussed the process […]
content:
As artificial intelligence continues to advance, animators are increasingly facing questions about the future of their craft and the role of human creativity in filmmaking. But the majority are not interested in letting AI into their art of storytelling.

At Variety‘s “Pixels and Pencils” panel in Savannah, Georgia on Monday, leading filmmakers discussed the process of bringing animated stories to life and why technology can’t replace the work behind them. Six panelists joined Variety‘s Clayton Davis for the discussion, which was moderated in partnership with SCAD Savannah Film Festival. They included Brad Bird for Netflix’s “Ray Gunn”; Daniel Chong for Pixar’s “Hoppers”; Joel Crawford and Januel Mercado for DreamWorks Animation’s “Forgotten Island”; Travis Knight for Laika’s “Wildwood”; and Leah Nelson for Independent Film Company’s “Tangles.”

Meg Weichman, the artistic manager of SCAD’s Theatres and Festivals, introduced this year’s panel, which she described as a celebration of the “imagination, artistry and collaboration that brings extraordinary animated stories to life.”

But to make something “extraordinary” requires significant effort, which is part of what makes the process “magical,” Chong said.

“Every set, every character, every piece of cloth, every piece of hair, every moment of atmosphere, all of that is created and made from ground zero. There’s no camera you can point at,” Chong told the audience. “It’s just completely fabricated and made and created, and that’s a pretty amazing thing, because that’s one of the reasons why I think these movies take so long, is because they have to create their own world.”

Creating an animated film typically takes well over a year — and sometimes much, more more. From the first idea to its big-screen release, Bird’s “Ray Gunn” took roughly 30 years to finalize, though he wasn’t consistently working on the film throughout that period.

“Ray Gunn” is voiced by Sam Rockwell and Scarlett Johansson. ‘Ray Gunn’ ©2026 Skydance Animation

But Bird was willing to put in the work, saying that a good story “has to come from life. You can’t create the illusion of life without having one, and that’s what we are in charge of — making the illusion of life and bringing people to something new.”

“Wildwood” also required an extensive production process, especially considering it used stop-motion animation. The film used 2,800 shots, a process Knight described as a “pain.”

“Stop motion is progressive. You start on frame one and you work your way all the way through in slow motion until you have a performance,” he said. “There is something extraordinarily magical about being a part of that.”

Despite the time and effort needed, the filmmakers said the process is what makes work meaningful. Chong added, “When you see people taunting that, ‘Oh, I can make this with the click of a button,’ or, ‘I can do this with these shortcuts,’ I think we just have to have faith that these processes are the way they are, and they’re as hard as they are to make for a reason, because that’s what makes these movies great and that’s what makes them resonate with humans.”

The panelists agreed that the humanity behind these films allows stories to resonate with audiences — something AI can’t replicate. But the industry’s future remains uncertain as technology advances and animators continue to adapt. Bird advised artists in the audience to keep learning the ins and outs of animation as the field evolves .

The filmmakers also discussed how different animation styles can shape of story. Deciding whether to use 2D animation, 3D animation, stop motion or even Claymation depends on the film’s narrative, Mercado said.

“It really is the story that dictates the visual storytelling and drive of the characters,” he shared. “That’s how we were able to play with various styles of anime and manga that followed the character point of view in these sections of [‘Forgotten Island’].”

“Forgotten Island” DreamWorks Animation

Crawford added, “For ‘Forgotten Island,’ we’re like, ‘This is an exploration of memories and how we experience them’ and thinking we all reflect memories in different ways. To have the animation style switch up depending on who the teller of the memory is was just a really exciting opportunity.”

The panelists also challenged the common misconceptions of working as an animator, which for “Tangles” director Nelson, included actually needing to be an animator.

“What I had to do, because I’m not an animator, was do everything else to communicate the vision — anything I could think of to communicate to my team what I hoped for and what I wanted to fight for,” she said. “I used all the other tools I could think of. I did a lot of acting references. I filmed myself doing the actions if I couldn’t draw it.”

title: Paris Jackson Wants No More “Smoke & Mirrors” Over MJ Money After Estate Trashes Her Latest Claims As “Nonsensical”
summary: Despite a court order to the contrary, Paris Jackson claims John Branca, the executor of her father’s fortune and legacy, has once again failed “to meet his fundamental disclosure obligations” and yet, at the same time, wants to hand out tens of millions to himself and his law firm. Calling the assertions and the demands […]
content:
Despite a court order to the contrary, Paris Jackson claims John Branca, the executor of her father’s fortune and legacy, has once again failed “to meet his fundamental disclosure obligations” and yet, at the same time, wants to hand out tens of millions to himself and his law firm. Calling the assertions and the demands for financial consequences “nonsensical,” the flush Michael Jackson Estate once again wants the deceased superstar’s daughter to beat it, to put it politely.

With a December 4 hearing penciled in with retired Judge Mitchell Beckloff for this latest dust-up between the ‘Zombies in Love’ singer and the Michael EP, Paris Jackson’s team view things in very black and white terms.

“Enough of the smoke and mirrors — Paris is asking to reduce the management fee,” a spokesperson for the younger Jackson told Deadline. “Executor Branca has repeatedly failed to meet deadlines ordered by the judge that are in place to provide Paris and her siblings visibility about how the Estate is being run. Since money is what motivates Executor Branca, this is the only way to enforce the timeline he agreed to.”

Watch on Deadline

To be precise, in a filing in LA Superior Court late last week, Paris Jackson’s Stradling Yocca Carlson & Rauth attorneys accuse longtime foe Branca of playing loose with the rules that he himself insisted upon.
