EXCLUSIVE: Sarah Dillistone has made her first big hire at Channel 4’s in-house production biz.

Dillistone has snapped up The Cube creator Adam Adler as Creative Director and he will lead on the creation of new shows for the nascent unit.

Adler is a highly-regarded British formats executive who is best known as creator of ITV’s The Cube, which ran for 11 seasons and nearly 100 episodes beween 2009 and 2021. An American version aired for three seasons on TBS. Adler’s other creations include Bar Wars and The Games, while he has most recently been EPing Channel 4’s upcoming Derren Brown: Incognito. He is a former Channel 4 entertainment commissioner and also ran an indie, Gameface, before moving to ITV Studios-owned label Potato.

Channel 4’s in-house production biz emerged from the UK government’s botched attempt to sell off the broadcaster and is one way in which the Gogglebox network can forge IP, which can then be sold around the world. The unit, which Channel 4 says is separated from its commissioning team by a “clear operational firewall,” unveiled ex-Made in Chelsea showrunner Dillistone as its lead at the start of 2026. She relocated to London from L.A., where she spent six years making shows like Perfect Match and The Ultimatum.

Watch on Deadline

More updates on the creative and development side of Channel 4 in-house are expected soon.

Dillistone called Adler an “unrivalled creative force.” “He is one of the most prolific format creators around spanning gameshow, reality and entertainment,” she added. “Adam’s experience originating ambitious and unpredictable formats from The Cube to Channel 4’s brand new reality series Incognito, coupled with my own background originating and showrunning reality, social experiments and relationship shows, makes for an exciting mix.”

Adler added: “I’m really excited to be joining Dilly at the start of this new venture. Channel 4 has always had attitude and originality, and I’d love us to bottle some of that up and take it out into the world. The ambition is to create exciting ideas with that same spirit, for TV and beyond.”

In other Channel 4 news, highly-rated docs chief Alisa Pomeroy has taken on the top head of unscripted job amid the restructure that is seeing around half of commissioners laid off. Pomeroy’s fiefdom has expanded vastly and she is now looking after documentaries, factual entertainment, reality, entertainment and specialist factual.

A day before Pomeroy’s promotion, Broadcast reported that comedy boss Charlie Perkins and entertainment chief Steve Handley are leaving. A scripted supremo looking after both drama and comedy is expected to be appointed in the coming months. New content boss David Brindley begins his rein in January.

title: Mayur More & Ashlesha Thakur To Lead ‘Beta Builder’, Debut Hybrid AI Feature From Abundantia AiOn & InVideo
summary: EXCLUSIVE: Mayur More and Ashlesha Thakur will star in the first AI-driven feature film from the pact between India’s Abundantia Entertainment and video tech firm InVideo. Beta Builder has InVideo’s Global Creative Lead, Hridaye A. Nagpal, attached to direct, with principal photography beginning today in Mumbai. The Indian city will, per the producers, serve “as […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: Mayur More and Ashlesha Thakur will star in the first AI-driven feature film from the pact between India‘s Abundantia Entertainment and video tech firm InVideo.

Beta Builder has InVideo’s Global Creative Lead, Hridaye A. Nagpal, attached to direct, with principal photography beginning today in Mumbai. The Indian city will, per the producers, serve “as both its home and creative starting point.”

Abundantia is producing through its Abundantia AiOn division, which was formed last year as an AI production division framed as “human-first and AI-empowered.” Last year, it partnered with Sanket Shah’s San Francisco-headquartered InVideo on a slate of five AI-powered films launched over three years with a ₹100 crore ($10.5M) commitment behind it.

Beta Builder will tell the story of Jai, a self-taught, genius architect from Dharavi, a densely populated area of Mumbai, who “gets a chance to realize his dreams in the world of virtual reality), only to discover that winning means far more than proving himself. An underdog in every sense, Jai must fight the system that holds him back, win the love of his life, and give his community a voice in shaping its own future.”

Watch on Deadline

Producers say it is “rooted in one of India’s most iconic geographies and set against the limitless possibilities of a virtual world,” with the story exploring “ambition, belonging and what it truly means to build something that lasts.”

The film is being positioned as a hybrid production, “pairing full-blown, live-action filming with AI-driven production,” and More (Kotak Factory & Black, White & Gray: Love kills) is starring alongside Thakur (The Family Man).

“We are about to see a wave of fascinating films,” said director Nagpal. “With AI-assisted filmmaking, storytellers can dream much bigger, and backing a bold idea finally feels possible. The partnership between Abundantia and InVideo gives filmmakers the scale and creative support to take on ideas like this. Beta Builder is our bet on that future, with a live-action shoot and AI working side by side”

Last month, Abundantia founder and CEO Vikram Malhotra outlined his vision for using AI in production in an interview with Deadline, while revealing Abundantia AiOn was morphing into a fully native standalone AI studio. He has sought to find the balance between the opportunity of AI and the

“The capability needed to run AI at studio level will not be found solely within the conventional media and entertainment system,” he said at the time. “It is truly a confluence of technology and art.”

Today, he said in a statement: “In our partnership with InVideo and Sanket, our focus is to leverage AI and tell stories that are unique, impactful and entertaining. I am delighted that the first film in our slate is one that tells a story set in a relatable, young world and explores aspirational possibilities beyond.

“In Hridaye, we have a filmmaker who combines a strong creative vision with a deep command over technology, which makes him the ideal person to lead and bring Beta Builder to life. I am excited about how AiOn is enabling unique stories and storytellers to come to the fore and bring their best to fans all over the world.”

“At InVideo, our mission has always been to put powerful tools in the hands of storytellers,” added Shah, CEO of InVideo. “Beta Builder is where that mission takes the form of a full-length film, made with a partner of Abundantia’s calibre. It is a story about building something that lasts, which makes it the right film to begin this slate with.”

Abundantia is known for the likes of Prime Video series Breathe and Daldal, Netflix crime-comedy Maa Behen, Baby, Toiler – Ek Prem Katha, Chhorii and Subedaar, the action thriller starring Anil Kapoor.

InVideo, which is U.S.-based with offices in India, positions itself as a agnostic AI filmmaking platform with more than 50 million users. Its backers include Peak XV, Tiger Global, Greenoaks, RTP Global, Base Partners, and Hummingbird. The company’s original productions include Sony LIV’s Penumbra, Juicebox and Hachiko.

title: Young Storytellers Nonprofit Launches Jamie Tarses Fund in Tribute to the Influential TV Executive
summary: Young Storytellers, the nonprofit that supports writing development programs in Los Angeles public schools, has established the Jamie Tarses Fund to pay tribute to the late ABC and NBC executive and help support the organization’s work. Young Storytellers recruits volunteers from the entertainment industry and others with writing experience to work with students in elementary, […]
content:
Young Storytellers, the nonprofit that supports writing development programs in Los Angeles public schools, has established the Jamie Tarses Fund to pay tribute to the late ABC and NBC executive and help support the organization’s work.

Young Storytellers recruits volunteers from the entertainment industry and others with writing experience to work with students in elementary, middle school and high school. The program pairs mentors and students to develop short stories that will be performed on stage by actors at the culmination of each school’s program. In 2025, Young Storytellers facilitated the work of 786 volunteers who mentored more than 440 students weekly at 39 public schools and after-school sites across Los Angeles.

Tarses, who died in 2021 at the age of 56, was an influential creative executive who rose through the ranks at NBC and was recruited to ABC as the first woman to head entertainment at a Big Three network. Tarses was involved with Young Storytellers early on and joined its board in 2003. Matt Tarses, Jamie’s brother who is a prominent writer-producer, said the establishment of the fund was a fitting tribute to his sister.

“Jamie was never happier than when she was helping writers tell their stories,” said Tarses. “She had a gift for it and everyone who worked with her benefited tremendously from her guidance. In return, she bullied us into doing the same thing for the kids at Young Storytellers. Of course, it became one of the most joyful and rewarding things I’ve done, as she surely knew it would be. When we were trying to come up with ways to honor her memory, Young Storytellers was the obvious choice.”

Young Storytellers hosts an annual fundraiser dubbed “The Biggest Show” that features performances of selected stories generated through its various school programs. The Jamie Tarses Fund will be formally unveiled tonight as part of this year’s Biggest Show program held at the Wilshire Ebell Theatre.

“Jamie understood that the most powerful thing you can tell a young person is that their ideas deserve to be taken seriously,” said Jaylene Benggon Chung, managing director of Young Storytellers. “She built that belief into this organization, and it is still at the center of everything we do. Because of this fund, the kids who come through our doors will keep feeling her generosity, whether or not they ever learn her name.”

Young Storytellers launched in 1997 with a single program at Playa del Rey Elementary School. Contributions to the Jamie Tarses Fund, which will fund Young Storytellers’ activities, can be made via the Young Storytellers website.

Earlier this week, Young Storytellers tapped Kevin Bolling to serve as its new executive director. Bolling previously worked for the nonprofit Secular Student Alliance. Before that, he headed fundraising for the Gay Men’s Chorus of Los Angeles.

title: Batman Casting in DC Universe ‘Isn’t Far Away,’ Says James Gunn: A ‘Movie Star’ Isn’t Mandatory but He’ll Be ‘Around the Same Age’ as Superman
summary: Robert Pattinson may be the star of Matt Reeves’ “The Batman” series, but another Caped Crusader will soon take flight in the rebooted DC universe under James Gunn. The DC Studios chief has revealed a few details on who will don the cowl in his new universe, which launched with last year’s “Superman” starring David […]
content:
Robert Pattinson may be the star of Matt Reeves’ “The Batman” series, but another Caped Crusader will soon take flight in the rebooted DC universe under James Gunn.

The DC Studios chief has revealed a few details on who will don the cowl in his new universe, which launched with last year’s “Superman” starring David Corenswet. When Gunn and Peter Safran took the reigns of DC Studios in 2022, they announced several movies and shows in the first chapter of the world, such as “Superman,” “Supergirl,” “Lanterns” and “Clayface.” In addition to several other so-far unreleased projects, they revealed a Batman movie titled “The Brave and the Bold,” which would be separate from Pattinson’s hero in Reeves’ series.

In an advance video from “The Suicide Squad: Is It Canon? The Official Podcast,” set to release Friday, Gunn shut down rumors that Batman is cast yet, while also revealing the type of actor fans can expect.

“It won’t be too long before we’re casting Batman. We haven’t cast yet, by the way — all the people thinking he’ll show up in this or that, it’s all bullshit,” he said. “When we do cast the DCU Batman, which isn’t very far away, if I gave somebody a day role in ‘The Suicide Squad’ that is going to be the best Batman, I’m not going to rule him out from that. I want to get everybody into account. One of the things that excites me about casting Batman is being able to pick a Batman who’s actually the best actor for that role. Superman’s have always been chosen based on who the best actor for that role is. And for some reason, Batman’s are always chosen as movie stars.”

James Gunn confirms casting of the Batman "isn't very far" and he will be of similar age as SUPERMAN



"I'm gonna get everyone into account. One of the things that excites me is.. being able to pick a Batman who's actually the best actor"



(@SupesandSabers) pic.twitter.com/AN49imKEf6 — Everything_DCU (@EverythingDCU_) October 29, 2026

When asked by “The Suicide Squad” actor Steve Agee if he needed to think about a Batman actor’s age when casting, considering “they’re going to be doing this 10 years from now,” Gunn replied “definitely.”

“People are always looking for little hints about the casting of Batman,” Gunn said. “Roughly, Batman and Superman are around the same age. I don’t think they’re drastically different ages. They’re future best pals, contemporaries.”

To put a potential Batman actor’s age into perspective, “Superman” star Corenswet is 33. So a Batman in his mid-30s seems likely. Corenswet will headline the following chapter of the DCU with next summer’s “Man of Tomorrow,” out July 9.

title: ‘Monarch: Legacy of Monsters’ Eyes Season 3 Renewal at Apple TV With New Writers, Showrunner
summary: Apple TV and Legendary Television are currently in talks for a third season of “Monarch: Legacy of Monsters,” but with some major changes. According to an individual with knowledge of the situation, Season 3 of the show would be helmed by a new showrunner and new writers, and would feature new Titans from Legendary’s Monsterverse. […]
content:
Apple TV and Legendary Television are currently in talks for a third season of “Monarch: Legacy of Monsters,” but with some major changes.

According to an individual with knowledge of the situation, Season 3 of the show would be helmed by a new showrunner and new writers, and would feature new Titans from Legendary’s Monsterverse. No word yet on if that would mean characters from the first two seasons would not carry on into the third. Sources say that multiple individuals have been approached about potentially taking over showrunning the series.

The series originally debuted on Apple TV in 2023, with the second season launching in Feb. 2026.

Still in the works, though, is the spinoff series starring Wyatt Russell as Col. Lee Shaw. That show will follow Shaw on a mission in 1984 as he tries to prevent the Soviets from unleashing a devastating new Titan.

Chris Black and Matt Faction originally created “Monarch,” with Black serving as showrunner and executive producer on Season 2. Joby Harold and Tory Tunnell of Safehouse Pictures are also executive producers on the show, with Jen Roskind, Matt Shakman, Lawrence Trilling, and Andrew Colville executive producing Season 2. Hiro Matsuoka and Takemasa Arita executive produce on behalf of Toho Co., Ltd., the owner of the Godzilla character.

Harold will serve as showrunner on the spinoff series, with Harold also developing multiple series within the world of the Legendary Monsterverse. In addition to Russell, the cast includes Millie Brady, Pilou Asbaek, Corey Stoll, Ralph Ineson, Nyasha Hatendi, Connie Nielsen and Stana Katic.

title: ‘PUBG’ Live-Action Series From Donald Glover, Stephen Glover in Development at Netflix
summary: Netflix is developing a live-action series based on the battle royale video game “PlayerUnknown’s Battlegrounds” (“PUBG”) with Donald Glover attached to star. In addition to starring, Glover and his brother and frequent collaborator Stephen Glover will write and executive produce the “PUBG” show, with Donald also planning to direct. Michael Schaefer of Neon TV will […]
content:
Netflix is developing a live-action series based on the battle royale video game “PlayerUnknown’s Battlegrounds” (“PUBG“) with Donald Glover attached to star.

In addition to starring, Glover and his brother and frequent collaborator Stephen Glover will write and executive produce the “PUBG” show, with Donald also planning to direct. Michael Schaefer of Neon TV will also executive produce, as will Fam Udeorji for Gilga, and Taeseok Jang and Sujin Lee for LV3H, the entertainment division of “PUBG” publisher Krafton.

“PUBG” was originally published by Krafton in 2017. The game does not have a plot, but rather sees large numbers of players dropped into one of several maps featuring a wide array of weapons, vehicles, and other items in a last-man standing deathmatch. Exact plot details for the potential show are under wraps.

“PUBG” is one of the most popular video games in the world even nearly 10 years after it was released. It broke multiple Guiness world records upon its initial release and continues to pull in hundreds of thousands of active users daily.

Donald and Stephen most famously worked together on the hit FX series “Atlanta.” Donald created and starred in the show, with Stephen serving as a writer and executive producer throughout its four-season run. They then teamed on the Amazon series “Swarm” and the musical film “Guava Island,” with Stephen also writing for Donald’s Amazon series “Mr. and Mrs. Smith.”

Donald is also known for his work on shows like “Community” and “30 Rock,” as well as for starring in films like “The Martian,” “Spider-Man Homecoming,” “Solo: A Star Wars Story,” and “The Super Mario Galaxy Movie.”

Donald is repped by The Team and Johnson Shapiro Slewett & Kole. Stephen is repped by WME and Ginsburg Daniels Kallis.

Should the “PUBG” show go forward, it would be the latest video game adaptation to find a home at Netflix. The streamer is currently at work on an “Assassin’s Creed” TV series and a “Gears of War” live-action film. Animated series based on games like “Clash of Clans” and “Minecraft” are also in the works, while Netflix currently airs shows like “Splinter Cell: Deathwatch” and “Cyberpunk: Edgerunners.”

title: Cannes Chief Thierry Fremaux Hails French Film Model as CNC Head Gaëtan Bruel Vows to Fight for Its Future at 80th Anniversary
summary: France’s National Film Board, the CNC, marked its 80th anniversary with a three-day gathering of industry leaders in Paris, including Cannes Film Festival chief Thierry Frémaux who praised the country’s unique film funding system. CNC president Gaëtan Bruel, meanwhile, warned against attempts to dismantle a model that has helped make France a global cinema powerhouse. […]
content:
France’s National Film Board, the CNC, marked its 80th anniversary with a three-day gathering of industry leaders in Paris, including Cannes Film Festival chief Thierry Frémaux who praised the country’s unique film funding system. CNC president Gaëtan Bruel, meanwhile, warned against attempts to dismantle a model that has helped make France a global cinema powerhouse.

The anniversary celebrations, held from Oct. 26-28 at the Cinémathèque française, came at a particularly fraught moment for the institution which faces growing political scrutiny and budgetary pressures as France heads toward the 2027 presidential election.

Frémaux, who also heads the Institut Lumière in Lyon, highlighted the CNC’s key role on display across films showcased at Cannes and other major festivals.

“We don’t say it because the Americans accuse us of constantly favoring certain things, because they themselves cannot imagine that the selection process is conducted in complete independence. But you can see just how much French money, the CNC and French professionals are absolutely everywhere,” Frémaux said during an onstage conversation with film historian Antoine de Baecque at the French Cinémathèque on Wednesday.

Frémaux also pointed out the CNC’s support for film restoration, noting that countries around the world have begun developing similar initiatives.

“Every country in the world has its masterpieces. And not all masterpieces have been restored, so there is still plenty of work to be done. Many countries are now giving themselves the means to do this, following the French model,” he said.

Frémaux emphasized that France’s film funding system not only supports contemporary production but also helps preserve cinema’s history and nurture future generations of film lovers.

“People are finally beginning to understand that money from cinema goes back into cinema. It has taken a long time, but I’m starting to read things about it. Journalists are always a little slow,” he joked. “But the fact remains that this money from cinema also goes toward cinema’s history. And that brings us back to the fundamental role of building an educational and intellectual foundation for cinephilia as a driving force in protecting contemporary creation.”

The event wrapped with a forceful defense of the institution from Bruel, who took over as CNC president last year and is facing pressures from populist parties, including the far right party Rassemblement National. In its latest budget proposal, unveiled earlier this month, the party outlined plans to strip down the National Film Board, privatize public broadcasting and slash public broadcasting funding

“We are going through, on a global scale, one of the deepest crises this sector has experienced since the invention of cinema,” Bruel said. “These 80 years have not been a smooth ride. They have been marked by successive upheavals. But what we are experiencing today is as though we were facing the ocean head-on, as though the upheavals of eight decades were happening all at once.”

Bruel also pointed to the industry’s shifting power dynamics, as streaming platforms are now facing new competition from YouTube.

“A few years ago, streamers seemed to be triumphing over television and movie theaters. Today, faced with YouTube, they themselves are discovering their vulnerabilities, and they are seeking to converge with traditional broadcasters, a sign that yesterday’s world has not said its last word,” he said.

For Bruel, these changes make the CNC’s mission more important than ever, particularly as public support for the arts faces increasing criticism.

“According to some, the CNC is a dispensable appendage, and all we would need to do is cut it off to get better. You can always cut off an arm, but you’d better be sure of what you stand to gain and what you stand to lose,” he said.

Bruel argued that France’s film funding model also serves a civic role, in giving people access to culture, through an extensive network of movie theaters, as well as film education programs allowing an estimated two million schoolchildren to visit movie theater each year.

The CNC’s 80th anniversary brought together a broad cross-section of France’s film and television industries for three days of discussions exploring the institution’s history and its evolving role in the entertainment landscape.

Among the prominent filmmakers participating were Olivier Assayas, Arnaud Desplechin, Amélie Bonnin and Rachid Hami, alongside producers Anne-Dominique Toussaint, Alex Berger and Simone Harari Baulieu, and leading animation executives including Illumination Studios Paris co-founder Jacques Bled and Xilam Animation founder Marc du Pontavice.

The program explored the defense of theatrical exhibition, the rise of French animation, the expansion of the CNC’s remit into television, video games and immersive creation, and the challenges posed by Hollywood’s global dominance. A panel devoted to protecting movie theaters featured Desplechin alongside exhibitors Aurélie Delage and Camille Labé, and former UGC chief Alain Sussfeld. Another discussion examined the CNC’s expansion into television, bringing together Berger, Harari Baulieu, former CNC director general and Arte president Jérôme Clément, and screenwriter-director Clémence Madeleine-Perdrillat.

Looking ahead, Bruel signaled that the CNC would soon present a broader strategy for digital creators and social media platforms like YouTube, arguing that they should contribute more fairly to the financing of French audiovisual creation, on par with streaming services.

His words on investment alluded to the European Commission’s current review of the Audiovisual Media Service Directive which allows members states to require streaming platforms such as Netflix, Disney+ and Prime Video to invest in European film and television production. The review could also open the door to bringing YouTube under similar investment obligations to level the playing field between broadcasters, streamers and digital platforms.

“Will we remain one in the future? No battle is lost in advance, especially when we have so many strengths in our hands, and you can count on the CNC to play its full part. But the answer, by definition, remains open,” Bruel concluded.

title: NewFilmmakers Los Angeles Sets Partnership with Mar del Plata International Film Festival
summary: EXCLUSIVE: NewFilmmakers Los Angeles (NFMLA) has announced an inaugural partnership with the Mar del Plata International Film Festival in Argentina. Under the collaboration, NFMLA will bring a selection of eight short films by its alumni to the festival in November, and participate in an industry panel exploring the role that film festivals, markets and creative […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: NewFilmmakers Los Angeles (NFMLA) has announced an inaugural partnership with the Mar del Plata International Film Festival in Argentina.

Under the collaboration, NFMLA will bring a selection of eight short films by its alumni to the festival in November, and participate in an industry panel exploring the role that film festivals, markets and creative organizations play in building sustainable careers for emerging storytellers.

The showcase includes coming-of-age comedy The Almost Adults by Brazilian director Rafaella Buzzi, who is currently developing her first feature film Large Land Crisis, as well as Mexican writer, director and producer Alan Maldonado’s Lobo: Christmas Special, about a seven-year-old boy who receives a Polly Pocket toy and must defend both his treasured gift and his emerging sense of identity against his older brother’s bullying.

Further titles include Los Angeles-based Brazilian writer and director Rodrigo Carvalhedo’s Musings, following an uninspired poet whose encounter with her Muse sparks a journey into the nature of creativity and inspiration; Korean-American filmmaker, writer and cinematographer Yohahn Ko’s intimate and psychologically tense family drama Earboy, and writer, director and AFI Conservatory graduate Gianfranco Fernández-Ruiz’s When Big People Lie which premiered at Telluride and received Best Short Film Drama at NFMLA’s Annual Awards.

Watch on Deadline

The selection also features Venezuelan screenwriter and filmmaker Bettina López Mendoza’s Más Allá, following a young girl navigating the dangerous Darién Gap between Colombia and Panama; folk horror Haint by Jahmil Eady, who was raised between New York City and South Carolina’s Gullah Geechee community; and Is It Like, A Date?!? by Los Angeles-based writer, filmmaker and playwright Eliana Pipes.

The eight short films be showcased in a special out of competition event on November 8, combining screenings and filmmaker Q&As to providing audiences and attending industry members with an opportunity to engage directly with participating artists and explore the inspirations, creative decisions and experiences behind their work.

The new partnership builds on a relationship which strengthened last year when NFMLA Executive Director Larry Laboe attended the 2025 Mar del Plata International Film Festival as a jury member.

NFMLA said it represented an important milestone in its international programming and commitment to connecting independent filmmakers with audiences, industry professionals and cultural institutions around the world.

The creative and curatorial framework for the partnership was developed by Mar del Plata Co-Artistic Directors Gabriel Lerman and Jorge Stamariano, whose vision helped shape the collaboration’s emphasis on discovering distinctive cinematic voices and strengthening connections between filmmaking communities across borders.

The agreement was formally executed by NFMLA Executive Director Larry Laboe and Carlos Luis Pirovano, President of Argentina’s National Film Board, the Instituto Nacional de Cine y Artes Audiovisuales (INCAA), and supported its International Affairs and Film Commission Manager Diego Marambio Avaria.

NFMLA said its aim and that of the festival was to expand access to global exhibition opportunities while encouraging meaningful dialogue between established and emerging film communities.

title: ‘Bosch: Start Of Watch’: First Look At Cameron Monaghan, Omari Hardwick In MGM+ Prequel
summary: We’re getting the first look at Cameron Monaghan and Omari Hardwick in MGM+’s upcoming Bosch prequel series Start of Watch ahead of it January 10 premiere. The streamer has released some first-look images, which you can see above and below. Bosch: Start of Watch explores the origin story of Michael Connelly’s legendary detective Harry Bosch. […]
content:
We’re getting the first look at Cameron Monaghan and Omari Hardwick in MGM+‘s upcoming Bosch prequel series Start of Watch ahead of it January 10 premiere. The streamer has released some first-look images, which you can see above and below.

Bosch: Start of Watch explores the origin story of Michael Connelly’s legendary detective Harry Bosch. The series stars Cameron Monaghan as rookie cop Harry Bosch and Omari Hardwick as veteran officer Eli Bridges.

Based on Connelly’s bestselling book series, Bosch: Start of Watch takes viewers back to 1992 Los Angeles, following 26-year-old Harry Bosch during his earliest days as a rookie cop. The series will explore a city on the edge, teeming with racial tension, gang violence, and a fractured LAPD. Amid routine calls and growing unrest, Bosch finds himself drawn into a high-profile heist and a web of criminal corruption that will test his loyalty to the badge and shape his future as the detective who lives by the code, “Everybody counts or nobody counts.”

Series regulars also include Ariana Guerra as Rosa and JD Pardo as Cory. Kathleen Wilhoite, William Fichtner, Rafi Gavron, Raphael Sbarge, Azita Ghanizada, Kenneth Miller, Seamus Dever, Ryan McPartlin, Marco Rodriguez and Shelli Boone also appear in the eight-episode series.



Bosch: Start of Watch is produced by Fabel Entertainment. The series is co-created and executive produced by Tom Bernardo and Brian Anthony, with Bernardo serving as showrunner. Michael Connelly, Henrik Bastin, Jamie Boscardin Martin, Stephen Kay and Jasmine Russ also serve as executive producers. Mark Douglas is a co-executive producer and Theresa Snider serves as co-executive producer for Hieronymus Pictures.

Watch on Deadline

Bosch: Start of Watch premieres Sunday, January 10 with two episodes, followed by a weekly release through the finale on Sunday, February 21 on MGM+ in the United States, United Kingdom, Belgium, Ireland, Italy, Germany, Netherlands, Spain and Latin America.

title: ‘9-1-1’ Fuels Buzzy Return For ABC’s Thursday Night Procedural Slate With ‘9-1-1: Nashville’ & ‘Grey’s Anatomy’

All three series premiered ahead of previous season averages after seven days of viewing, led by the 8.14 million who tuned in for the Season 10 debut of 9-1-1 across ABC, Hulu, Hulu […]
content:
EXCLUSIVE: ABC‘s Thursday nights are back in action with the return of its popular procedural slate: 9-1-1, 9-1-1: Nashville and Grey’s Anatomy.

All three series premiered ahead of previous season averages after seven days of viewing, led by the 8.14 million who tuned in for the Season 10 debut of 9-1-1 across ABC, Hulu, Hulu on Disney+ and digital platforms. The episode was up 88% from its live + same-day audience of 4.33 million and 4% ahead of last season’s 7.82 million average.

In L+SD, 9-1-1 had already piqued plenty of interest for the fiery emergency that 118 faced as a volcano erupted in the middle of Los Angeles, up 49% over last season’s premiere among adults 18 to 49. 9-1-1 was the top drama of the night in competitive multi-platform measurement, per Nielsen.

9-1-1: Nashville earned 6.76 million total viewers after seven days for its Season 2 premiere, up 90% from the 3.55 million who watched live + same-day. The episode was up 9% from the Season 1 finale and 1% from last season’s average.

Watch on Deadline

The episode, in which Station 113 responds to a museum overrun by biblical-scale events, hit a series high among adults 18 to 49 with a 0.33 rating, up 16% over the series debut.

As for Grey’s Anatomy, the stalwart medical drama returned for Season 23 with 5.58 million total viewers, marking a 129% increase over the L+SD audience of 2.44 million.

On Thursday’s episodes, 9-1-1 is still dealing with the aftermath of that volcanic eruption, while on 9-1-1: Nashville, a blinding agent strikes Nashville during a pollen storm, leaving Blythe and others critically ill. There’s a lot going on for Grey’s Anatomy with Blue fighting to reclaim his place at Grey Sloan as Joe is pulled from motherhood back into the OR, and Jules and Winston navigate their strained relationship.

Monarch: Legacy of Monsters is going for a reboot. Apple TV and Legendary Television are in renewal talks for a third season that would take the show in a new direction, featuring new Titans from Legendary’s Monsterverse.

Search is underway for new writers and showrunner who will take over from the series’ Season 1 and Season 2 creative team, led by showrunner/executive producer Chris Black who co-created Monarch with Season 1 executive producer Matt Fraction.

The news comes six months after Season 2 wrapped its run on Apple TV May 1.

Monarch: Legacy of Monsters is executive produced by Joby Harold and Tory Tunnell from Safehouse Pictures. Hiro Matsuoka and Takemasa Arita executive produce on behalf of Toho Co., Ltd., the owner of the Godzilla character. Season 2 was also executive produced by Chris Black, Jen Roskind, Matt Shakman, Lawrence Trilling, and Andrew Colville.

Watch on Deadline

Legendary, which licensed Monsterverse rights from Toho, has a multi-series deal with Apple TV, which includes Monarch: Legacy of Monsters and its upcoming untitled spinoff centered on Young Lee Shaw, with Wyatt Russell reprising his role as Colonel Lee Shaw. The series is showrun by Harold, who is developing multiple other entries in the franchise alongside producing partner Tunnell via their Safehouse Pictures banner.

In addition to Russell, the offshoot stars Millie Brady, Pilou Asbaek, Corey Stoll, Ralph Ineson, Nyasha Hatendi, Connie Nielsen and Stana Katic. Harold, Tunnell and Russell executive produce alongside Andy Goddard, Kyle Bradstreet, Jim Skotchdopole, Max Borenstein, Chris Black, Alex Boden and Toho’s Matsuoka and Arita. JD Dillard serves as director and executive producer.

title: Skydance Sports Chief David Berson Sets Exec Roster, With New Roles For Jeff Gerttula, Craig Barry & More
summary: David Berson, the CBS Sports veteran who is now chairman of Skydance’s Global Sports Group, has set his leadership team and named veteran execs Jeff Gerttula and Craig Barry to key roles. The appointments are the latest to come down from senior leadership in an effort to organize and restructure Skydance, which was created by […]
content:
David Berson, the CBS Sports veteran who is now chairman of Skydance‘s Global Sports Group, has set his leadership team and named veteran execs Jeff Gerttula and Craig Barry to key roles.

The appointments are the latest to come down from senior leadership in an effort to organize and restructure Skydance, which was created by this month’s $110 billion merger of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery. The new entity has platforms across broadcast TV, streaming, cable and digital. Berson was elevated to the top role the week the merger closed, with TNT Sports chief Luis Silberwasser announcing his departure.

By and large, the new roster confirms to the usual practice with mergers, wherein executives from the company doing the acquiring (CBS parent Paramount, in this case) prevail over the other side. One notable exception is Barry, who worked at the TNT and Turner sports division for nearly four decades. As Skydance Global Sports Group‘s EVP and Chief Content Officer, Barry will lead all production across remote setups and live events, along with talent, features and editorial.

Watch on Deadline

Gerttula, a veteran CBS Sports digital exec, will oversee digital, international, strategy and business development for sports. “As we are still assessing the international structure and operating model, Jeff will be the point person with the international sports teams,” Berson noted.

Sports Business Journal had the first report on the appointments, which have now been confirmed by Deadline.

Notable exits as part of the reorg include those of TNT Sports communications and talent chief Nate Smeltz; CBS production EVP Harold Bryant; TNT Sports CFO Sophia Constantinides; TNT Sports Ventures president Patrick Crumb; TNT Sports HR SVP Donald Knight; and TNT SVP of strategic partnerships Raphael Poplock.

In the memo, Berson saluted the departing execs’ “leadership, partnership and immeasurable contributions, calling them “excellent executives whom I greatly admire and respect.”

title: Joseph Mazzello Leads Cecil Hotel Horror ‘A Grim Life,’ Cappu Films Boards Sales (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Joseph Mazzello, the “Bohemian Rhapsody” and “Jurassic Park” actor, heads the cast of “A Grim Life,” a supernatural thriller set inside Los Angeles’ Cecil Hotel. Hong Kong outfit Cappu Films has picked up international sales, it was unveiled at the Tokyo International Film Festival’s TIFFCOM market. Francesco Lucente writes and directs. Mazzello, whose credits also […]
content:
Joseph Mazzello, the “Bohemian Rhapsody” and “Jurassic Park” actor, heads the cast of “A Grim Life,” a supernatural thriller set inside Los Angeles’ Cecil Hotel.

Hong Kong outfit Cappu Films has picked up international sales, it was unveiled at the Tokyo International Film Festival‘s TIFFCOM market.

Francesco Lucente writes and directs. Mazzello, whose credits also take in “The Pacific,” plays Tom, a filmmaker down on his luck who pays the bills scrubbing toilets and can’t stop reworking the one script he has. A friend steers him toward “Böse,” a lost silent picture from 1931, and Tom’s hunt for an artistic breakthrough pulls him toward a dark secret.

Max Beesley (“Jack Ryan”) plays producer Joe, with Wes Studi (“Avatar: Fire and Ash”) as Nic, Carl Lumbly (“Captain America: Brave New World”) as Henry and Arnetia Walker (“Bookie”) as Chelsea. Studi is a 2019 recipient of an Academy Honorary Award.

The building itself does much of the work. The film draws its scares from the hotel’s hallways and concealed rooms, leaning on sound, shadow and Tom’s deepening isolation to tighten the dread.

Lucente also produces. The project will move into pre-production in December 2026 ahead of a January 2027 shoot, with delivery penciled for July 2027.

“‘A Grim Life’ is a deeply personal project for me, one that explores the darker side of ambition, obsession, and the sacrifices we make in pursuit of our dreams,” Lucente said. “The Cecil Hotel provides an extraordinary and haunting backdrop for a story where the boundaries between reality and the supernatural begin to disappear.”

Cappu first presented the film to buyers in Busan and is keeping those conversations going before cameras roll. Janice Woo of Cappu Films said the Cecil Hotel and the lost film give the project an immediately compelling premise, “while Tom’s desperation gives the story its emotional center.” She added: “Following our work with Francesco on ‘Starbright,’ we’re pleased to continue the relationship with a project that brings together a distinctive atmosphere and an experienced cast.”

Lucente previously directed the drama “Badland” and the fantasy “Starbright,” which stars Ted Levine, John Rhys-Davies and Diego Boneta.

Besides “Starbright,” the Cappu slate carries another Lucente fantasy, “Sinbad,” plus the action titles “Lion Fist” and “Red Bird.” The company’s catalog spans horror, fantasy, action and arthouse fare, and also includes TV series and library titles from Hong Kong cinema’s Golden Era.

title: Mathis Landwehr Martial Arts Films ‘Lion Fist,’ ‘The Last Kumite’ Land Korea, Latin America Deals at Tokyo Market (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Mathis Landwehr-led martial arts feature “Lion Fist” has been picked up for South Korea, Latin America and the CIS. Fellow Landwehr starrer “The Last Kumite” has also found a South Korean home, sales outfit Cappu Films revealed at the Tokyo International Film Festival’s TIFFCOM market. Studio DHL has taken South Korean rights to both films. […]
content:
Mathis Landwehr-led martial arts feature “Lion Fist” has been picked up for South Korea, Latin America and the CIS.

Fellow Landwehr starrer “The Last Kumite” has also found a South Korean home, sales outfit Cappu Films revealed at the Tokyo International Film Festival‘s TIFFCOM market.

Studio DHL has taken South Korean rights to both films. Great Movies picked up “Lion Fist” for Latin America, and Kinologistika LLC bought the title for the CIS.

Taim M. Adams directed “Lion Fist,” which casts Landwehr as Joe, a fighter who walks out of prison and learns his son needs surgery to survive. To pay for it, Joe signs up for a vicious martial arts competition carrying a $100,000 purse. Gary Daniels, Kurt McKinney, Keith Cooke and Brice Akuesson round out the cast.

Sean David Lowe and Keith W. Strandberg wrote the screenplay, and Mike Möller choreographed the fights. Lowe produced the film with Wayne Graves, and the pair hold the same credit on “The Last Kumite.”

“These deals give the films a wider international audience, and we look forward to meeting buyers for the remaining territories in Tokyo,” said Janice Woo of Cappu Films.

Ross W. Clarkson directed “The Last Kumite,” in which a fighter is forced into a lethal tournament to save his abducted daughter. Landwehr again tops the cast, joined by Cynthia Rothrock, Billy Blanks, Matthias Hues and McKinney.

“Both movies bring a nostalgic style of martial arts movies back to the screen. Already selling to many countries in the world, we trust in Cappu Films to find the right partners for new territories,” said Lowe.

Beyond the two fight films, Cappu Films is handling French action title “Red Bird,” Carter Ward’s “Step Back,” “Doors Closing” and Francesco Lucente’s fantasy “Starbright.” The company’s library spans action, horror, fantasy and arthouse fare, along with Hong Kong Golden Era titles and TV series.

title: Margot Robbie ‘May Be Over’ Playing Harley Quinn, but James Gunn Would ‘Bend Over Backwards’ to Include Her in the DCU
summary: As James Gunn’s fledgling DC Universe continues to grow, he’s revealed that one key character will “almost certainly” return: Harley Quinn. But Margot Robbie, who played the anti-hero in three DCEU movies, may not be back. On “The Suicide Squad: Is It Canon? The Official Podcast,” Gunn was joined by Jennifer Holland and Steve Agee, […]
content:
As James Gunn‘s fledgling DC Universe continues to grow, he’s revealed that one key character will “almost certainly” return: Harley Quinn. But Margot Robbie, who played the anti-hero in three DCEU movies, may not be back.

On “The Suicide Squad: Is It Canon? The Official Podcast,” Gunn was joined by Jennifer Holland and Steve Agee, who starred in his debut DC movie “The Suicide Squad,” to discuss which parts of the pre-reboot film will carry over into the new universe. The trio discussed several dead characters from the film and actors that have played multiple DC roles (such as Sean Gunn, Nathan Fillion and Michael Rooker), but ultimately decided that most of the movie is canon to the rebooted DC Universe.

“That settles it then. I think that ‘The Suicide Squad’ is within the canon of the DCU. It’s decided,” Gunn said. “I’d say, we have one small asterisk, which is what exactly is the future of Harley Quinn? I want to be given a little leeway with this by the fans because I’m not sure exactly how that’s going to manifest itself. But other than that, I think that we can pretty much say the entire movie is canon. I don’t think there’s a problem.”

Earlier in the podcast, Gunn explained that Robbie has become “kind of the biggest female star in the world” and that he isn’t sure if she’d return to play Harley Quinn. She debuted as the first live-action Harley Quinn in David Ayers’ “Suicide Squad” in 2016, then returned for “Birds of Prey” in 2020 before joining Gunn’s standalone sequel in 2021.

“She’s just so crazy. I love her as Harley. I don’t know if she wants to play Harley again. She may be over that,” Gunn said on the podcast. Since “The Suicide Squad,” Robbie has of course conquered the box office as “Barbie” in addition to starring in Emerald Fennell’s “Wuthering Heights.” She’s next set to star in Tim Burton’s “Attack of the Fifty Foot Woman,” so her schedule may be too packed to revist Harley Quinn — at least for now.

title: Patrick Stewart’s Final Movie Is ‘Avengers: Doomsday’; He Said Before His Death That ‘I Can’t Imagine Retiring. I’ll Forever Be an Actor’
summary: Patrick Stewart’s final movie role will be in the upcoming “Avengers: Doomsday,” which marks his ninth time playing the “X-Men” character Charles Xavier on the big screen. Marvel Studios confirmed the news in their tribute to the late actor, who died at 86 years old after a brief battle with Alzheimer’s and Lewy Body Dementia. […]
content:
Patrick Stewart‘s final movie role will be in the upcoming “Avengers: Doomsday,” which marks his ninth time playing the “X-Men” character Charles Xavier on the big screen. Marvel Studios confirmed the news in their tribute to the late actor, who died at 86 years old after a brief battle with Alzheimer’s and Lewy Body Dementia.

“Stewart made his debut as Professor X in 2000’s ‘X-Men,’ where he embodied the composure, class, and wisdom of the beloved telepathic mutant and mentor of the X-Men,” Marvel Studios wrote in a tribute. “For more than 25 years, he brought a gravitas and profundity to the [character]… He returned to the role once more with 2026’s ‘Avengers: Doomsday,’ his final on-screen appearance.”

In between “X-Men” and “Avengers: Doomsday,” Stewart popped up as Charles Xavier in various Marvel sequels, prequels and reboots such as 2003’s “X2: X-Men United,” 2006’s “X-Men: The Last Stand,” 2009’s “X-Men Origins: Wolverine,” 2013’s “The Wolverine,” 2014’s “X-Men: Days of Future Past,” and 2017’s acclaimed “Logan.” The role, along with Captain Picard in the “Star Trek” franchise, will go down as Stewart’s most iconic screen character.

“We lost one of the greats of stage and screen today,” Stewart’s longtime “X-Men” co-star Hugh Jackman wrote on Instagram in a tribute. “And, in my book, a tremendous friend and man. I learned so much from him. I will miss you, Patrick Stewart, all of my days.”

In one of Stewart’s now-final interviews published by TV Insider in July, the actor spoke about his decision to return as Charles Xavier in “Avengers: Doomsday” and told fans that he would never “retire” from acting.

“As any actor my age will tell you, there are fewer and fewer available roles as we get older. That being said, I still continue to receive interesting offers and I love being challenged by new work,” Stewart said at the time. “I can’t imagine ever officially retiring. I’ll always and forever be an actor.”

Marvel Studios put out its own statement mourning the loss of Stewart by saying the company is “deeply saddened” by his passing, adding: “Sir Patrick brought Professor Charles Xavier to life with extraordinary grace, intelligence, and humanity, defining the character for generations of fans, from ‘X- Men’ to ‘Logan’ to ‘Avengers: Doomsday.’ He was a singular talent, a generous collaborator, and a true gentleman.”

“We’ve been lucky enough to work with some of our childhood heroes. And Sir Patrick Stewart will always be one of them,” added “Avengers: Doomsday” directors Joe and Anthony Russo in their own statement. “A legendary actor with an unmistakeable presence, and an unmatched integrity. Thank you for entertaining all of us, sir. And for teaching us humanity, both on and off the screen.”

“Avengers: Doomsday” opens in theaters Dec. 18 from Disney and Marvel Studios.

title: Skydance’s JB Perrette Reveals His Full Leadership Team, Announces Departures of Several Execs Not Joining Following the Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger
summary: Skydance’s JB Perrette, who now serves as co-chair and chief business officer of Skydance TV and Skydance Direct-to-Consumer, has unveiled his new executive org structure — and announced several departures from the pre-merged Warner Bros. Discovery and Paramount Skydance entities he now oversees. Exiting the combined company are Dan Barnes, Michael Bishara, Jamie Cooke, Domenic […]
content:
Skydance’s JB Perrette, who now serves as co-chair and chief business officer of Skydance TV and Skydance Direct-to-Consumer, has unveiled his new executive org structure — and announced several departures from the pre-merged Warner Bros. Discovery and Paramount Skydance entities he now oversees.

Exiting the combined company are Dan Barnes, Michael Bishara, Jamie Cooke, Domenic DiMeglio, Marco Nobili, Pank Patel and Juan Sola.

From the WBD side, Barnes was previously head of global advertising revenue for HBO Max; Bishara was exec VP and general manager of global streaming and digital studios at Warner Bros. Discovery; Cooke was exec VP and GM of Central Eastern Europe, Middle East, Turkey and Africa at Warner Bros. Discovery; and Sola was head of streaming for Latin America at Warner Bros. Discovery.

On the Paramount side, Di Meglio was exec VP, chief marketing and chief data officer at Paramount Streaming; Nobili was exec VP and international general manager of Paramount+ and Patel was head of Paramount International Networks.

“Their work has been instrumental to the success of the DTC and/or TV businesses, and I am incredibly grateful for their efforts throughout their impressive tenures,” Perrette said in a memo to staffers. “Please join me in wishing them all the best on their next endeavors.”

Also, as part of his memo, Perrette noted that Ronald Goes, who had served as President of International TV Production at Warner Bros. Discovery, will now report to Warner Bros. TV Group chair Channing Dungey — adding Skydance’s international TV production to her oversight as well. Goes and the Warner Bros. International TV studio operation previously reported to Warner Bros. International president Gerhard Zeiler, who is not joining Skydance.

In his Thursday memo, Perrette — who was previously WBD’s CEO/president of global streaming and games — spelled out a detailed leadership structure that he noted will likely change over time as the merger implementation continues.

“We have been as thoughtful as possible, albeit in a very compressed time frame. Despite our best efforts, there will undoubtedly be further clarifications and refinements that need to be made, particularly within sub-teams that will need to be more specifically realigned to this new structure,” he wrote. “Thank you in advance for your patience and understanding, and most importantly, your help working it through with us in this next phase to make sure we get to the right answer.”

Perrette had previously announced that his direct reports would include Jay Askanasi (Advertising), Ray Hopkins (Distribution) and David Decker (Content Sales). In the new memo, he spelled out more direct reports, including, on his global team, Jeff Cusson, EVP and Head of Communications, Skydance DTC; Shauna Spenley, CMO, Global DTC and International TV; Trey Turner, COO, International; Josh Walker, COO, DTC; Liz Wright, CFO, Skydance TV Segment; and a new head of Pluto/AVOD to be announced later.

Perrette also revealed his regional and local teams, including Andrew Georgiou, the interim President & MD Europe & Africa, who will lead Europe & Africa; James Gibbons, President & MD APAC & MENA; Kasia Kieli, President & MD, Poland; and Fernando Medin, President and MD LATAM/U.S. Hispanic.

Here’s Perrette’s full memo, with additional appointments:

Team,

As you learned from David and Ynon earlier this month, my role in the company is one that purposefully bridges DTC and TV. The industry and consumer behavior continue to evolve at a fast pace, and these two businesses have more crossover and interconnections than ever. We need to aggressively drive each business forward while also being attentive to maximize the strategic and financial opportunities between the two, and at the same time be transparent and data-led when there are inevitable trade-offs that need to be decided…make them with speed, and stay clear that our north star is what’s in the best interest of the overall Skydance company (not individual units, countries or other agendas).

To do this, we will have some leaders more dedicated to TV and others to DTC, and many leaders wearing both hats (or more). Our structure will leverage strong local/regional expertise and relationships, and global scale and capabilities … and success will require everyone to make this local and global set-up a powerful network vs. a dreaded matrix. The focus needs to be on collaboration and putting points on the board to ensure we win, rather than who put them on the board. We have a one-of-a-kind portfolio of DTC and TV assets that I’m convinced can work better and more powerfully together, engaging and delighting billions of consumers around the world while also being the cash, profit and revenue growth engine for the company.

The painful part in these transitions is that we have to say goodbye to many talented leaders who have delivered significant value to the prior companies, and more importantly, have been great friends, colleagues, and mentors to so many. I want to thank Dan Barnes, Michael Bishara, Jamie Cooke, Domenic DiMeglio, Marco Nobili, Pank Patel and Juan Sola (gracias!) for all they’ve done getting the company to where it is today. Their work has been instrumental to the success of the DTC and/or TV businesses, and I am incredibly grateful for their efforts throughout their impressive tenures. Please join me in wishing them all the best on their next endeavors.

Below is our new leadership team as of today. We have been as thoughtful as possible, albeit in a very compressed time frame. Despite our best efforts, there will undoubtedly be further clarifications and refinements that need to be made, particularly within sub-teams that will need to be more specifically realigned to this new structure. Thank you in advance for your patience and understanding, and most importantly, your help working it through with us in this next phase to make sure we get to the right answer. So, joining the previously announced Jay Askanasi (Advertising), Ray Hopkins (Distribution), and David Decker (Content Sales) to help lead this charge will be (in alphabetical order):

GLOBAL

Jeff Cusson, EVP and Head of Communications, Skydance DTC: As previously announced by Casey, Jeff will lead the communications strategy for the streaming services with a shared reporting line to me, Casey and Mel Zukerman, Chief Communications Officer, Skydance. The international communications teams will hard-line into his organization but continue to have a dotted-line relationship into the country GM/MD and be part of their leadership team.

As previously announced by Casey, Jeff will lead the communications strategy for the streaming services with a shared reporting line to me, Casey and Mel Zukerman, Chief Communications Officer, Skydance. The international communications teams will hard-line into his organization but continue to have a dotted-line relationship into the country GM/MD and be part of their leadership team. Shauna Spenley, CMO, Global DTC and International TV : Shauna will expand her role to include oversight for marketing of International TV, partnering with me and George Cheeks, with all streaming and TV marketing teams internationally hard lining into her organization. This will help make the operations more effective and efficient … but local marketing teams, particularly in larger FTA markets will continue to have a dotted-line relationship into the country GM/MD and be part of their leadership team. She will also have a dotted line to Rebecca Mall, CMO, Skydance. Juan Sola’s team, Domenic’s DiMeglio’s team and marketing focused resources in other groups will move into Shauna’s team.

This will help make the operations more effective and efficient … but local marketing teams, particularly in larger FTA markets will continue to have a dotted-line relationship into the country GM/MD and be part of their leadership team. title: ‘Days Of Our Lives’ Actor Robert Kelker-Kelly’s Cause Of Death Revealed
summary: Days Of Our Lives and Another World actor Robert Kelker-Kelly died of arteriosclerotic heart disease, commonly known as coronary artery disease, according to the Office of the Regional Medical Examiner in St. Charles, Mo. as reported by People. The manner of death was ruled natural. Kelker-Kelly died October 3 at his home in St. Peters, […]
content:
Days Of Our Lives and Another World actor Robert Kelker-Kelly died of arteriosclerotic heart disease, commonly known as coronary artery disease, according to the Office of the Regional Medical Examiner in St. Charles, Mo. as reported by People. The manner of death was ruled natural.

Kelker-Kelly died October 3 at his home in St. Peters, Missouri. He was 62.

St. Peters police officers had responded to his home for a report of an unconscious man who was not breathing, according to police at the time. Kelker-Kelly reportedly had complained of chest pain shortly before becoming unresponsive. Paramedics “attempted life-saving measures,” but Kelker-Kelly was pronounced dead at 9:09 pm, according to police.

Kelker-Kelly’s acting career began in 1987 when he was cast as Sam Fowler on NBC’s Another World, appearing in the daytime drama for three years until 1990. His big break came two years later when he landed the established role of Bo Brady on Days of Our Lives, taking over for Peter Reckell, who had exited. He portrayed Bo Brady opposite Kristian Alfonso’s Hope Brady and Lisa Rinna’s Billie Reed before Reckell returned to the role in 1995.

Watch on Deadline

In 1996, he returned to Another World playing the role of professional race car driver Bobby Reno, who later was discovered to be Dr. Shane Roberts. He played the role until 1998.

He also portrayed Stavros Cassadine on General Hospital in 2001, appearing in guest spots from 2002-14.

Kelker-Kelly later became a professional pilot, working in the field from 2003 to 2015.

title: Channing Dungey To Oversee Warner Bros. International TV Production As Division Moves Under Skydance TV Studios
summary: Warner Bros. International TV Production, the division that operates around 20 production companies around the world that make international versions of formats such as The Bachelor, has a new home within Skydance. The unit, which is run by President Ronald Goes, will sit under Skydance TV Studios and will be overseen by Warner Bros. Television […]
content:
Warner Bros. International TV Production, the division that operates around 20 production companies around the world that make international versions of formats such as The Bachelor, has a new home within Skydance.

The unit, which is run by President Ronald Goes, will sit under Skydance TV Studios and will be overseen by Warner Bros. Television Group chief Channing Dungey.

The news emerged from a note from JB Perette, Co-Chair & Chief Business Officer, Skydance TV and Skydance Direct-To-Consumer (DTC), sent to colleagues this afternoon, seen by Deadline.

Interestingly, Warner Bros. International TV Production (WBITVP) never sat under Dungey’s leadership as Goes reported to Gerhard Zeiler, who was President, International, Warner Bros. Discovery.

Watch on Deadline

It caps an interesting couple of years for the division; before Skydance’s acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, WBITVP was set to join the Discovery side of the business when former WBD chief David Zaslav planned to create Discovery Global, lead by Gunnar Wiedenfels, as part of its split with studios and streaming, before the entire studio became a major acquisition target.

WBITVP is a collection of production companies including Twenty Twenty, which is behind HGTV’s Castle Impossible and Netflix’s Love Con Revenge, Wall to Wall, which produces Magnolia’s Back to the Frontier, Ricochet, which makes BBC’s The Repair Shop, Belgium’s Eyeworks, Holland’s BlazHoffski as well as divisions in France, Germany, Switzerland, Spain, Italy, Finland, Sweden, Denmark, New Zealand and Australia.

These companies also produce international versions of Warner Bros.’ hit formats including The Bachelor franchise, First Dates and FBoy Island as well as newer titles including Unacceptable, 100 Cooks and Harry Potter: Wizards of Baking.

Goes leads the senior management team alongside colleagues including Andy Zein, EVP, Creative Format Development & Sales, and Alex Ogilvie, Group SVP, Finance & Operations.

The move should help WBITVP work closer with Warner Bros. Television Group, which is led by Dungey, who has a number of new units reporting to her including the Paramount cable networks.

content:
EXCLUSIVE: Director Jason Perlman’s Bad Influence has rounded out the cast of the YA horror film, which has recently wrapped filming.

From screenwriter Brandon Cohen, Bad Influence is described as a modern-day Thelma & Louise fueled by female rage, following Isabelle (McGraw) and Kira (Gomez) on a road trip home for spring break, when they pick up mysterious hitchhiker (Liam), who is not what he seems.

Watch on Deadline

Bad Influence producers are Debbie Liebling, Joel David Moore and Zachary Burgess. Moore and Liebling previously collaborated on Dodgeball: A True Underdog Story (2004) and Grandma’s Boy (2006). Executive producers include Steven Silverstein, Cathy Raduns, Raymond Merrill, Carmelo Chimera, Syed Ali Saeed, Denis Schoenhofer, Natalie Kline, Jarod Einsohn and Michelle and Melissa Macedo.

title: Skydance TV & DTC Co-Chair JB Perrette Unveils Leadership Team, Executive Departures
summary: JB Perrette, Co-Chair & Chief Business Officer of Skydance’s TV and direct-to-consumer divisions, has revealed key members of his executive team, several departures, and a pending opening for the leader of Pluto TV. It is the latest in a series of of organizational appointments for Skydance, which was officially formed this month by the merger […]
content:
JB Perrette, Co-Chair & Chief Business Officer of Skydance‘s TV and direct-to-consumer divisions, has revealed key members of his executive team, several departures, and a pending opening for the leader of Pluto TV.

It is the latest in a series of of organizational appointments for Skydance, which was officially formed this month by the merger of Warner Bros. Discovery and Paramount. Perrette, who spearheaded the global expansion of HBO Max and was on the executive team that launched Hulu, is one of the few WBD execs to remain in a top Skydance role after the close of the $110 billion combination.

Among those exiting as part of the new structure, Perrette revealed in an internal memo, are Dan Barnes, head of global ad revenue for HBO Max; Michael Bishara, EVP and GM of global streaming and digital networks at WBD; Jamie Cooke, EVP of Central Europe, Middle East, Turkey and Africa for WBD; Domenic DiMeglio, chief marketing and data officer for Paramount Streaming; Marco Nobili, international GM of Paramount+; Pank Patel, head of Paramount’s international media networks; and Juan Sola, head of Latin American streaming for WBD.

Another high-ranking exec, Efrain Miron, EVP and head of content strategy and licensing for Paramount DTC, is stepping away from his current post to “explore other opportunities within the company,” Perrette wrote. (Read his full memo below.)

The memo also left a blank for the future head of Pluto, the free streamer seeking a new leader who will help it harmonize with subscription siblings Paramount+ and HBO Max.

Pluto is a key asset in the new streaming organization but the onetime FAST channel pioneer, which launched in 2014, has been surpassed by rivals like Tubi and the Roku Channel. Top Pluto execs Tom Ryan, who co-founded the service, and Jeff Schultz both departed former parent Paramount over the past two years. As Paramount navigated back-to-back mergers with the former iteration of Skydance and WBD, they were not replaced.

Perrette, a longtime former NBCUniversal, Discovery and WBD exec, has a diverse portfolio in his new Skydance role. Along with aspects of streaming he has shepherded at other companies, he now oversees advertising, distribution and international across both streaming and linear. He works closely with George Cheeks, Co-Chair of TV, but Cheeks looks after other programming areas as chief content officer.

“As you learned from David and Ynon earlier this month, my role in the company is one that purposefully bridges DTC and TV,” Perrette wrote in an internal memo, alluding to CEO David Ellison and Co-CEO Ynon Kreiz. “The industry and consumer behavior continue to evolve at a fast pace, and these two businesses have more cross-over and interconnections than ever. We need to aggressively drive each business forward, while also being attentive to maximize the strategic and financial opportunities between the two.”

Here is Perrette’s full memo:

Team,



As you learned from David and Ynon earlier this month, my role in the company is one that purposefully bridges DTC and TV. The industry and consumer behavior continue to evolve at a fast pace, and these two businesses have more cross-over and interconnections than ever. We need to aggressively drive each business forward, while also being attentive to maximize the strategic and financial opportunities between the two, and at the same time be transparent and data-led when there are inevitable trade-offs that need to be decided…make them with speed, and stay clear that our north star is what’s in the best interest of the overall Skydance company (not individual units, countries or other agendas).



To do this, we will have some leaders more dedicated to TV and others to DTC, and many leaders wearing both hats (or more). Our structure will leverage strong local/regional expertise and relationships, and global scale and capabilities…and success will require everyone to make this local and global set-up a powerful network vs. a dreaded matrix. The focus needs to be on collaboration and putting points on the board to ensure we win, rather than who put them on the board. We have a one-of-a-kind portfolio of DTC and TV assets that I’m convinced can work better and more powerfully together, engaging and delighting billions of consumers around the world while also being the cash, profit and revenue growth engine for the company.



The painful part in these transitions is that we have to say goodbye to many talented leaders who have delivered significant value to the prior companies, and more importantly have been great friends, colleagues, and mentors to so many. I want to thank Dan Barnes, Michael Bishara, Jamie Cooke, Domenic DiMeglio, Marco Nobili, Pank Patel and Juan Sola (gracias!) for all they’ve done getting the company to where it is today. Their work has been instrumental to the success of the DTC and/or TV businesses, and I am incredibly grateful for their efforts throughout their impressive tenures. Please join me in wishing them all the best on their next endeavors.



Below is our new leadership team as of today. We have been as thoughtful as possible albeit in a very compressed timeframe. Despite our best efforts, there will undoubtedly be further clarifications and refinements that need to be made particularly within sub-teams that will need to be more specifically re-aligned to this new structure. Thank you in advance for your patience and understanding, and most importantly your help working it through with us in this next phase to make sure we get to the right answer. So, joining the previously announced Jay Askanasi (Advertising), Ray Hopkins (Distribution), and David Decker (Content Sales) to help lead this charge will be (in alphabetical order):



GLOBAL



Jeff Cusson, EVP and Head of Communications, Skydance DTC: As previously announced by Casey, Jeff will lead the communications strategy for the streaming services with a shared reporting line to me, Casey and Mel Zukerman, Chief Communications Officer, Skydance. The international communications teams will hard line into his organization but continue to have a dotted line relationship into the country GM/MD and be part of their leadership team.



Shauna Spenley, CMO, Global DTC and International TV: Shauna will expand her role to include oversight for marketing of International TV, partnering with me and George Cheeks, with all streaming and TV marketing teams internationally hard lining into her organization. This will help make the operations more effective and efficient…but local marketing teams, particularly in larger FTA markets will continue to have a dotted line relationship into the country GM/MD and be part of their leadership team. She will also have a dotted line to Rebecca Mall, CMO, Skydance. Juan Sola’s team, Domenic’s DiMeglio’s team and marketing focused resources in other groups will move into Shauna’s team.



Trey Turner, COO, International: In addition to his responsibilities in Finance, Trey will take on the new role of COO of International reporting to me to help steer and continue to transform the large international portfolio. Moving to Trey’s team will be Pank Patel’s strategy team, Louis Goldstein, Vanessa Brookman, Lee Hobbs and Myriam Lopez-Otazu.



Josh Walker, COO, DTC: Josh will have a dual role of COO, DTC, reporting to me and supporting Casey, and of CFO, DTC, reporting into Dennis Cinelli, CFO, Skydance. As COO, he is responsible for business strategy and planning, content strategy, planning, analysis and acquisitions, pricing, podcasting and project/program management. Moving to Josh’s team will be Rodrigo Mazon and most of Michael Bishara’s team.



Liz Wright, CFO, Skydance TV Segment: Liz will be the chief financial officer for the Skydance TV segment, leading finance for CBS and our global television networks business. In her new role, Liz will partner with George and me for Skydance TV and report into Dennis Cinelli.



Head of Pluto/AVOD: This is a big and important business for us and deserves dedicated leadership to help drive it day in and day out. We will conduct a search for a strong leader of Pluto/AVOD with internal and external candidates, and I will share more as we get through that process. Reporting into this new role will be Olivier Jollet, Will Gurman, and Kevin Kroll, and on an interim basis this team will report to Josh and me.



REGIONAL/LOCAL



Internationally, we will have four regional leaders who will help drive the combined TV and Streaming businesses and will report to me.



These regional leaders and their teams will have direct oversight for distribution, ad sales, business and commercial development across both networks and streaming as well as TV programming in their markets, and will work in partnership with global functional teams above as well as with Jay Askinasi in Advertising, Ray Hopkins in Distribution, and David Berson in Sports (rest assured the common objective is to be pragmatic about what makes sense or where there is value-add…we will work together to clarify further in the coming weeks). These leaders are (in alphabetical order, and to be clear only changes in reporting are listed below the regional leaders not their full teams):



Andrew Georgiou, interim President & MD Europe & Africa will lead Europe & Africa: Andrew will be taking on a new role outside the company next year, but he has offered to help me manage this transition before his departure and as we search for his replacement. Moving to Andrew’s team will be: Alessandro Araimo, MD Southern Europe: responsible for Italy, Spain, France, and will now add Turkey and Africa



Qaisar Rafique, EVP Commercial Development: will be responsible for all distribution and business development in Europe, and oversight for Central and Eastern Europe (excluding Poland)



Reemah Sakaan, President 5 and MD UK & I: will take on leadership for the company’s UK and Ireland entertainment business, including her existing role leading Channel 5



Christina Sulebakk, MD Nordics, Benelux, GSA: will continue to lead the Nordics, Germany, Austria, Switzerland (GSA), and Benelux



James Gibbons, President & MD APAC & MENA will lead Asia Pacific & Middle East and North Africa (APAC & MENA): Moving under James will be Beverley McGarvey, Jason Monteiro, and Shonali Bedi.



Kasia Kieli, President & MD, will lead Poland: Given the unique scale, profile, and breadth (i.e.: entertainment, news, sports, digital, studios) of our leading TV and digital business in this market, Kasia will continue to operate Poland as a more integrated media team.

A few other personnel items to share: Leah Hooper, Regional Streaming Lead for Europe, reporting to me is finishing her maternity leave and I’m looking forward to having her back in January; Ronald Goes is moving over to the Skydance TV Studios side of the business under Channing; and Efrain Miron is stepping away from the DTC organization to explore other opportunities within the company. The foundation that’s been set by Efrain’s leadership will continue to benefit the business moving forward.

I know you will likely have questions, and I fully appreciate the continued and unfortunate anxiety and distraction that this process causes. We will continue to work through it as quickly and respectfully as possible. In the meantime, please join me in congratulating this new leadership team…I’m incredibly excited to get going. The leaders announced above will now start working through their respective structures asap.
