title: ‘Beef’ Actor Justin H. Min’s ‘Journey There,’ Hong Sangsoo’s Locarno Winner ‘Nowhere to Lay My Eyes’ Rack Up International Sales for Finecut
summary: Hong Sangsoo’s “Nowhere to Lay My Eyes,” a triple prizewinner at the 79th Locarno Film Festival, and Kim Jin-yu’s “Journey There,” the first Korean production to star “Beef” actor Justin H. Min, have picked up a new batch of territory deals through Seoul-based sales outfit Finecut. For “Nowhere to Lay My Eyes,” Carlotta Films has […]
content:
Hong Sangsoo’s “Nowhere to Lay My Eyes,” a triple prizewinner at the 79th Locarno Film Festival, and Kim Jin-yu’s “Journey There,” the first Korean production to star “Beef” actor Justin H. Min, have picked up a new batch of territory deals through Seoul-based sales outfit Finecut.

For “Nowhere to Lay My Eyes,” Carlotta Films has taken France, Mimosa Films has Japan, Kligger has Argentina and The Stone and the Plot has Portugal. The new pacts add to earlier sales to The Cinema Guild for North America, Filmgarten for Austria, Hugoeast for China, Atalante for Spain, Cola Films for Taiwan and the Institute of Contemporary Arts for the U.K.

The film is Hong’s 35th feature. At Locarno it won best direction, best performance and the Ecumenical Jury Prize. It sees the director team up again with regulars Kim Minhee (“By the Stream”) and Kwon Haehyo (“What Does That Nature Say to You”), and marks his first outing with Choi Myeonggil, whose credits include TV series “Durian’s Affair.” Jeonwonsa Film Co. produced.

“Journey There” has sold to Andrews Film for Taiwan, KDDI Corporation for Japan, Lev Cinema for Israel and Izagur Media for Mongolia, while Kairos Distribution acquired inflight rights. The drama centers on a middle-aged widow who begins getting ready for her own journey and gets drawn into relationships she never saw coming in the apartment she has just moved into.

Min’s credits include Kogonada’s “After Yang” and the Netflix series “Beef” and “The Umbrella Academy.” The film is the second feature from Kim, whose first, “Bori,” took two prizes at the 24th Schlingel International Film Festival. Kim’s own company, Pado, produced.

“Journey There” was released in Korea on Oct. 28. It has been invited to the Moscow International Film Festival, the New York Asian Film Festival and, more recently, the Paris and London Korean film festivals.

Fresh from Busan’s Asian Contents & Film Market, Finecut heads to AFM with a slate that includes the animated “Long Long Night.” The film will screen there for buyers for the first time in its English-dubbed version. It also has invitations from Toronto, Busan and Sitges under its belt.

Also on offer are “Dora,” selected for Cannes’ Directors’ Fortnight and Busan’s Gala Presentation section, and “Wi-Fi Love in the Palace,” a period fantasy romance toplined by Kim Young-hoon of K-pop group The Boyz.

title: Ian McKellen Pays Tribute to Close Friend Patrick Stewart: ‘He Wore His Heart on His Sleeve’
summary: Ian McKellen wrote a moving tribute to Patrick Stewart, his close friend of many years, following his death Thursday at age 86 after suffering from Alzheimer’s and Lewy Body Dementia. “Before everything else, Patrick was defined by being born and bred in Yorkshire, the proud county in the north of England which he loved to […]
content:
Ian McKellen wrote a moving tribute to Patrick Stewart, his close friend of many years, following his death Thursday at age 86 after suffering from Alzheimer’s and Lewy Body Dementia.

“Before everything else, Patrick was defined by being born and bred in Yorkshire, the proud county in the north of England which he loved to the end. You could hear it in his accented voice and in the stern honesty with which he told you what he thought and felt. Yorkshiremen have no truck with half-truths or avoidance of big issues. He wore his heart on his sleeve, which made him a man to rely on, to admire and in my case, love,” McKellen wrote on Instagram.

“We first met as ambitious young actors with the Royal Shakespeare Company half a century ago but we weren’t in the same productions. My first strong memory was a few years later, meeting him in the street in central London when he told me about an offer to take over a leading part in ‘Star Trek’. “But Patrick think of your stage career in the UK. Do you really want to risk — getting lost in Hollywood for years and years?” Well, he took the risk and thank goodness for us all that he did for not just his devoted Trekkies but film and theater audiences, who marveled at his using international celebrity to star in a string of cinema successes (‘X-Men‘ of course) and in great classical plays by Shakespeare, Ibsen, Arthur Miller, Peter Shaffer, Pinter and Beckett at Stratford-upon-Avon, in London’s West End and on Broadway.

“America was his adopted home, where he met his adored Sunny who has cared for him through sickness and health, through thick and thin. But he never forsook his origins: and the proudest achievement of the most respected and beloved actor of his generation on either side of the Atlantic, was his appointment as Chancellor of Huddersfield University in Yorkshire.”

“His farewell performance in ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ is yet to be seen,” McKellen concluded.

Stewart and McKellen’s friendship was one of the most beloved in the entertainment industry. The two became friends while playing Professor X and Magneto, respectively, in 2000’s “X-Men.” Looking back in a 2020 interview with Wired, Stewart said, “We had adjoining trailers. On those kind of movies, you spend more time sitting in your trailer than you do in front of the camera. So Ian and I hung out together, drinking tea — and maybe, in the afternoon, something a little stronger — and we got to know one another, and the charm of it was that we found we had so much in common.”

McKellen was the officiant when Stewart married his wife, Sunny Ozell, in 2013. “I’ll be frank with you — I’m in love with [him],” Stewart joked in the same interview. “But then, so is my wife in love with him, too, so that’s all right.” The friends made headlines several times over the years for so openly showing affection to each other, frequently kissing on the lips at red carpet events.

Ian McKellen, left and Patrick Stewart kiss at the U.K. premiere of McKellen’s film “Mr Holmes” in 2015. Stuart C. Wilson/Getty Images

In addition to the original “X-Men” in 2000, Stewart and McKellen starred in in the sequels “X2” (2003) and “X-Men: The Last Stand” (2006), then made a cameo in “The Wolverine” (2013) before fully reprising their roles in 2014’s “X-Men: Days of Future Past.” Stewart also starred in 2017’s “Logan,” and both appear in “Avengers: Doomsday,” which will be released this December.

The pair has also worked together onstage, performing in a 2013 Broadway production of both Samuel Beckett’s “Waiting for Godot” and Harold Pinter’s “No Man’s Land” before doing “No Man’s Land” again in 2016 on London’s West End.

title: California Begins Discussion on Unlimited Film Incentives: ‘That Is a Heavy Lift’
summary: California lawmakers began a discussion Thursday about removing the cap on the state’s $750 million incentive for film and TV production, while acknowledging that such a move would face budget hurdles. At an Assembly committee hearing in North Hollywood, a handful of state lawmakers heard testimony from union leaders and industry advocates who argued that […]
content:
California lawmakers began a discussion Thursday about removing the cap on the state’s $750 million incentive for film and TV production, while acknowledging that such a move would face budget hurdles.

At an Assembly committee hearing in North Hollywood, a handful of state lawmakers heard testimony from union leaders and industry advocates who argued that the program — which was doubled last year — is not enough to stop the outflow of production jobs.

Betsy Beers, the creative partner of Shonda Rhimes, told the committee that she had hoped to shoot a new “Grey’s Anatomy” spinoff in Santa Clarita. But the show, which is set in West Texas, did not get a California tax credit.

“We lost a lot of time, and a lot of money, and now we are filming in Albuquerque,” Beers said. “We want to be here.”

Because the state incentive is capped, projects must apply during periodic windows and then compete with other shows on a “jobs ratio” score. Beers said the show lost out initially because it didn’t get score highly enough. When ABC tried again in the fall, the program was already oversubscribed and was no longer taking applications.

“The program is still not competitive or predicable enough to address the loss of production to other regions,” said Arlen Valdivia, vice president of state government affairs at the Motion Picture Association. “There needs to be more done to make California competitive.”

FilmLA, the permitting agency, reported last week that production volume continues to fall in the Los Angeles area, even as the share of scripted TV shows receiving a state subsidy has nearly doubled. Several speakers at Thursday’s hearing called for eliminating the $750 million cap entirely — saying the limit leaves producers uncertain about whether they will get the credit.

Georgia’s credit has no limit and New York’s allows the state to pull from allocations for future years — amounting to an uncapped credit. Rick Chavez Zbur, who chairs the Assembly Select Committee on Growing and Retaining the Creative Economy in California, said he expects to make improvements in the next legislative session.

“I want to try to do our best to make whatever changes we can, and I think either increasing the cap or eliminating it,” Zbur said after the hearing. “But you know that is a heavy lift. But we’re going to try this year to make as much progress as we can.”

Lawmakers are also dealing with a structural deficit and deep cuts to Medicaid — which has intensified competition for tax dollars.

During the hearing, Zbur floated the idea of “dynamic scoring” — suggesting that the state should account for the benefit from the film credit instead just looking at the headline cost. That idea, he said, would be key to persuading lawmakers that an unlimited credit is a worthwhile investment.

“The way we’re looking at the return needs to be what we’re focused on,” said John Harabedian, another member of the committee. “It becomes a regional fight. It becomes a best-use-of-a-dollar fight… The numbers are going to convince our colleagues that don’t necessarily live in L.A.”

Rowan Isaaks, an economist with the state Legislative Analyst’s Office, cited research showing that film credits return 20-50 cents for every dollar invested by the state. He also expressed skepticism about dynamic scoring. “It’s subject to a lot of uncertainty,” he said.

Stephen Cheung, the president of the Los Angeles Economic Development Committee, cited his own group’s research, which found a return of $1.07 to state and local coffers. That report was funded by the MPA.

Assemblyman Nick Schultz floated the idea of extending the expiration date of the state program, which is currently set to sunset in 2030, as a way of offering greater certainty to productions. He and other also suggested providing a subsidy for above-the-line costs — salaries for actors, directors, etc. — and opening up eligibility for the program to commercials and game shows.

“Why should we be picking and choosing?” he asked. “Why should we be picking winners and losers? Let’s incentivize all of it to stay.”

The state raised the base credit from 20% to 35% last year, while increasing the overall cap from $330 million to $750 million.

“The higher credit might mean fewer projects overall,” Isaaks noted. “There’s a possibility that the more generous our credit is, the fewer productions we can fund in total.”

Since Gov. Gavin Newsom expanded the state incentive last year, lawmakers have added additional measures to bolster it. The Legislature created a $10 million incentive for post-production and passed a bill to expedite studio rebates and exempt credits for independent films from a $5 million credit cap.

While Congress is considering a 20% nationwide incentive, several speakers argued that even if that passes, California will still face stiff competition from other states.

“We should not assume the work will return because federal policy changes,” said Lindsay Dougherty, leader of the Hollywood Teamsters.

title: Matthew Weiner Exits Peacock, 101 Studios Series ‘The Chairman’ Starring Eddie Murphy (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Matthew Weiner is no longer involved with the drama series “The Chairman” that is currently in development at Peacock, Variety has learned exclusively from sources. The project was first reported to be in the works at the streamer less than a month ago, with Eddie Murphy attached to star. According to sources, creative differences between […]
content:
Matthew Weiner is no longer involved with the drama series “The Chairman” that is currently in development at Peacock, Variety has learned exclusively from sources.

The project was first reported to be in the works at the streamer less than a month ago, with Eddie Murphy attached to star. According to sources, creative differences between Weiner and the show’s producers caused them to part ways.

A new showrunning team is already said to be in place and will be announced in the coming days. The show’s writers’ room has been placed on a two-week hiatus as the new creative leads come onboard.

Exact plot details for “The Chairman” remain under wraps. Should it get picked up to series, it would be the first live-action series in which Murphy has starred since his days as a cast member on “Saturday Night Live.”

The series will be produced by Universal Television and 101 Studios, which is run by “Yellowstone” executive producer David Glasser. 101 is currently under a first-look film and television deal at NBCUniversal that began in January. “The Chairman” will also be the first project to come out of ex-Paramount boss Chris McCarthy’s deal at NBCUniversal, which was first reported in November 2025 and put him in a consulting role on the studio’s relationship with Glasser and 101. Murphy serves as a producer “The Chairman” in addition to starring.

Weiner is best known for creating the seminal TV drama “Mad Men,” which aired for seven seasons on AMC and won 16 Emmy Awards. “The Chairman,” assuming it is to be greenlit, would have marked Weiner’s first TV writing credit since 2018, when he created the Amazon Prime Video series “The Romanoffs.”

title: ‘Ghosts’: Rebecca Wisocky Talks Hetty’s Good, Long Look In The Mirror In Two-Part Halloween Special
summary: SPOILER ALERT! This post contains details from the two-part Halloween special for CBS’ Ghosts. More ghosts from Hetty Woodstone’s (Rebecca Wisocky) past come back to haunt her in Thursday’s Ghosts Halloween special, which finally introduces audiences to her mustachioed and estranged sister Margaret (Maria Thayer). She arrives at Woodstone when Jay (Utkarsh Ambudkar) replaces a […]
content:
SPOILER ALERT! This post contains details from the two-part Halloween special for CBS‘ Ghosts.

More ghosts from Hetty Woodstone’s (Rebecca Wisocky) past come back to haunt her in Thursday’s Ghosts Halloween special, which finally introduces audiences to her mustachioed and estranged sister Margaret (Maria Thayer).

She arrives at Woodstone when Jay (Utkarsh Ambudkar) replaces a broken mirror inside the mansion with a similarly old-looking one from a nearby flea in the hopes that Sam (Rose McIver) won’t notice. Turns out, Margaret’s ghost is inside that “new” mirror. Well, good thing Sam is on that book tour for a while and Kyle (Ben Feldman) can also see the ghosts, so he’s able to alert Jay to the new problem at hand.

“I’ve been begging to meet my mustachioed sister Margaret ever since I mentioned her in a like almost throwaway quip in Season 1, and I’m so glad that they did it,” Wisocky tells Deadline.

Watch on Deadline

To Hetty’s surprise, Margaret’s mustache has disappeared, because her spirit has been trapped inside a mirror since her untimely death and exists as a reflection of herself. Apparently, if a spirit catches a glimpse of itself in a mirror as it passes from its human body, it’ll be trapped. That mirror used to belong to the Woodstone family. It was in Margaret’s room as she died from disease, and Hetty distracted herself from the horrors of losing her sister with lines of cocaine on said piece of furniture.

“We make such delicious light of Hetty’s adoration for cocaine, and it, in fact, would have been prescribed medicinally in health at that time. But nonetheless, she was escaping. She was escaping pain, escaping the truth,” Wisocky said. “She was, I think, disarmed and confused and made very, very uncomfortable by the fact that her sister was dying, and her sister was also the person that she loathed the most in the world. That’s an interesting landscape. I’m not at all surprised that in that moment she chose — not to do something selfish. She didn’t know that her sister was going to be sucked into the mirror, but she chose to do something to numb the pain of it.

“So I think that that’s that that’s interesting, and might be an interesting thing for her to take a look at at a certain point,” she adds.

Margaret, understandably, does not give Hetty the grace that Wisocky does. She does blame Hetty for ending up in the mirror, just as Hetty has blamed Margaret throughout her entire mortal life and afterlife for stealing her one true love.

“I think Hetty has clung to this idea that the tragic turning point in her life was her inability to be allowed true love and to marry this painter, Julian, and that her sister was the villain that prevented that all from happening,” Wisocky explains.

One might imagine Hetty’s surprise then, when, she comes to discover all these years later that isn’t the truth. In fact, her sister had expressed interest in Julian first, and Hetty simply couldn’t be bothered to listen.

“When she realizes that this fundamental pivot point in her life, she was not seeing clearly, I think that opens her up to being, I think, a little more malleable to her interpretation of love, to her expectation in relationships, and to her capacity to trust her own version of history,” Wisocky said. “So that sounds like there’s room for a whole lot of growth that could come out of that.”

She adds: “I also love learning more about young Hetty and about all the turning points in which she might have become a different, happier person. I love the historical accuracy that at this period of time, both of these young women lived in a world in which their only potential hope for happiness was to marry well, and that they were forced into competition with one another rather than being one another’s allies. All that feels very accurate and very tragic, and I love that Hetty is proven to be wrong about the opinions that she has about the history of her own life. I love it when my character is proved to be wrong.”

Hetty and Margaret make amends, and Hetty actually helped her younger sister finally fulfill her dream of seeing Paris by sending the mirror to live with Trevor’s daughter Abby. At its core, Wisocky says, forcing Hetty to take a literal and figurative look in the mirror is what the CBS comedy series is all about.

“It’s a comedy about death and regrets. It’s about all the ways in which people were incapable of living their own truths in their own lives, and you can’t help but touch on some really intense, deep themes, and ask these characters to take a hard look at what really happened and whether or not they’re actually reliable narrators of their own lives,” she said. “Hetty is an especially great character through which to do that because she so brazenly believes in her own status and her own rightness of her opinions.”

After Thursday’s two-part special, Ghosts goes on hiatus again until the upcoming Christmas episode. Season 6 premieres in the spring. Luckily, as promised, the Halloween episodes also address what happened to Pete (Richie Moriarty), but the outlook there is concerning — even if its ripe with storytelling possibility. At the end of the second episode, Pete reappears on Woodstone property at the exact anniversary of his death, but he seem to remember nothing. It’s as if he just died.

“It was terrifying for us to start the episode in a post-Pete world, because when Flower disappeared, we were really sad, but we thought at the very least she was likely sucked up. But when a ghost disappears, we’ve never experienced that before. We have no idea what happened to him,” Wisocky said. “Getting to experience being a new baby ghost all over again, and to see how the other ghosts maybe use that to their advantage, or how people will interpret or misinterpret Pete’s reality back to Pete, I think there’s a lot of fun to be had with that.”

The actress knows that audiences are likely chomping at the bit to find out what happens next.

“We’ve put them through the ringer with this oddball introduction to Season 6, and they’ve waited so long to see us…we feel badly they’re going to have to wait so long to see the Christmas episode too,” she acknowledged.

In the meantime, she left viewers with a taste of what’s to come in Season 6.

“We have our 100th episode. We are so so grateful for our fans for supporting us in a way that has allowed us to get it to 100 episodes. It’s honestly an incredibly strong season to be six seasons in. There’s so many of these episodes are just incredibly exciting and have such a really wonderful motor. You’re going to see more of Elias. You’re going to see much more of Bela. You’re going to see a lot of Nancy. There’s a really particularly beautiful and moving storyline with Sheila Carrasco’s character Flower that I think is really going to surprise people,” she said. “I’m so sorry the fans had to wait so long to see us for Halloween. I’m so sorry they’re going to have to wait more than a month to see the Christmas special. But boy, is it worth it! It’s so good. Utkarsh is full on comedy action hero mode, and there are a lot of zany things that happens. It’s the episode that has the highest stakes that we’ve ever done. I’ll leave it at that.”

The two-part Ghosts Christmas special will air December 10 at 9 p.m. ET/PT on CBS.

title: Poorna Jagannathan Joins Hulu’s ‘Young Americans’ Pilot, Natalia Leite To Direct
summary: Poorna Jagannathan (Deli Boys, Lanterns) has been cast as a series regular in Hulu’s Young Americans pilot. She joins the previously announced Scott Foley, Billie Boullet, Sam Rechner, Mia Isaac, Oscar Winter, and Lauren Mei. The Handmaid‘s Tale helmer Natalia Leite has been tapped to direct the pilot, reuniting with the Emmy-winning Hulu drama’s creator […]
content:
Poorna Jagannathan (Deli Boys, Lanterns) has been cast as a series regular in Hulu‘s Young Americans pilot. She joins the previously announced Scott Foley, Billie Boullet, Sam Rechner, Mia Isaac, Oscar Winter, and Lauren Mei. The Handmaid‘s Tale helmer Natalia Leite has been tapped to direct the pilot, reuniting with the Emmy-winning Hulu drama’s creator Bruce Miller who executive produces Young Americans.

From writers and executive producers Chris Hutton and Eddie O’Keefe, the show’s logline reads as follows: As the children of the nation’s elite battle it out at Capitol Crest Academy in Washington, D.C., their teenage dramas begin to mirror the larger political games of their parents. Amidst the secrets, scandals, and deadly ambitions, a forbidden romance between two students from opposing political families threatens to escalate tensions to a breaking point.

Jagannathan will play Maya Washburn. Once a close friend and political ally of the President (Foley), Maya is now a controversial senator galvanizing a disillusioned electorate just as her son (Rechner) is falling in love with the President’s daughter (Boullet).

Watch on Deadline

In addition to Hutton and O’Keefe, Young Americans is also executive produced by Miller and Priscilla Poriand, both on behalf of White Oak. 20th Television is the studio.

Jagannathan most recently starred in HBO’s Lanterns, starring opposite Aaron Pierre and Kyle Chandler, in the role of Zoe. Notable credits include the Netflix comedy series Never Have I Ever and a leading role in the Apple movie Wolfs, and playing the beloved character Auntie in Hulu’s Deli Boys. She will next be seen in the Apple TV crime drama Nocturne, premiering October 30. Jagannathan is repped by Gersh, Untitled, and Hansen Jacobson Teller.

Leite co-executive produced and directed the first three episodes of Hulu’s Black Cake. She most recently directed a block of Netflix’s Age of Innocence and Hulu’s The Twisted Tale Of Amanda Knox. Leite is repped by WME, Curate and Srda.

Nellie Andreeva contributed to this report.

title: Ian McKellen Pays Tribute To Patrick Stewart: “He Wore His Heart On His Sleeve”
summary: As the world mourns Sir Patrick Stewart’s death at age 86, a longtime friend and collaborator is paying tribute to his legacy. Sir Ian McKellen, who starred as Magneto opposite Stewart’s Professor X in the X-Men films, explained what made the late actor “a man to rely on, to admire and in my case, love” […]
content:
As the world mourns Sir Patrick Stewart‘s death at age 86, a longtime friend and collaborator is paying tribute to his legacy.

Sir Ian McKellen, who starred as Magneto opposite Stewart’s Professor X in the X-Men films, explained what made the late actor “a man to rely on, to admire and in my case, love” after he Stewart’s rep revealed he died following a diagnosis of Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia.

“Before everything else, Patrick was defined by being born and bred in Yorkshire, the proud county in the north of England which he loved to the end,” he began on Instagram. “You could hear it in his accented voice and in the stern honesty with which he told you what he thought and felt. Yorkshiremen have no truck with half-truths or avoidance of big issues. He wore his heart on his sleeve, which made him a man to rely on, to admire and in my case, love.

“We first met as ambitious young actors with the Royal Shakespeare Company half a century ago but we weren’t in the same productions. My first strong memory was a few years later, meeting him in the street in central London when he told me about an offer to take over a leading part in Star Trek. ‘But Patrick think of your stage career in the UK. Do you really want to risk—getting lost in Hollywood for years and years?’ Well, he took the risk and thank goodness for us all that he did for not just his devoted Trekkies but film and theatre audiences, who marveled at his using international celebrity to star in a string of cinema successes (X-Men of course) and in great classical plays by Shakespeare, Ibsen, Arthur Miller, Peter Shaffer, Pinter and Beckett at Stratford-upon-Avon, in London’s West End and on Broadway.”

Watch on Deadline

McKellen continued, “America was his adopted home, where he met his adored Sunny who has cared for him through sickness and health, through thick and thin. But he never forsook his origins: and the proudest achievement of the most respected and beloved actor of his generation on either side of the Atlantic, was his appointment as Chancellor of Huddersfield University in Yorkshire.

“His farewell performance in Avengers: Doomsday is yet to be seen,” added McKellen after he and Stewart recently reprised their roles from the X-Men franchise in the upcoming MCU movie, which premieres Dec. 18 in theaters.

Stewart’s rep announced that the 3x Golden Globe-nominated actor died on Wednesday at his Los Angeles home, with wife Sunny Ozell by his side.

title: Matthew Weiner Exits Eddie Murphy Peacock Series ‘The Chairman’ As Showrunner
summary: The Chairman is getting a new showrunner. Mad Men creator Matthew Weiner, who had been tapped as writer, executive producer and showrunner on the high-profile drama starring Eddie Murphy, has departed the series in the works at Peacock, Deadline has confirmed. The project, from David Glasser’s 101 Studios and Universal Television, is closing in on […]
content:
The Chairman is getting a new showrunner. Mad Men creator Matthew Weiner, who had been tapped as writer, executive producer and showrunner on the high-profile drama starring Eddie Murphy, has departed the series in the works at Peacock, Deadline has confirmed.

The project, from David Glasser’s 101 Studios and Universal Television, is closing in on a new showrunner and will be moving forward, I hear. The writers room, the majority of which is expected to stay, has gone on a two-week hiatus to accomodate the showrunner transition.

According to sources, the decision to part ways with Weiner was creative and was made by Peacock, Universal TV and 101 Studios executives based on the pilot script by the Emmy winner. I hear Weiner had been brought in to develop and write an idea that had already been conceived and pitched to Murphy, and the take he delivered was a departure from that.

Watch on Deadline

Plot details of the new series have not been disclosed.



The Chairman marks Murphy’s first scripted series and 101 Studios’ first announced project under the company’s NBCUniversal deal, which started in January.

Weiner’s exit was first reported by Variety.

title: Justin H. Min Starrer ‘Journey There’ & Hong Sangsoo’s ‘Nowhere To Lay My Eyes’ Sell To Multiple Territories
summary: Korean sales company Finecut has sold Journey There, starring The Umbrella Academy‘s Justin H. Min, to multiple territories. The Seoul-based company has also closed further deals on Hong Sangsoo’s Locarno film festival awards winner Nowhere To Lay My Eyes. Journey There has gone to Japan (KDDI Corporation), Taiwan (Andrews Film), Mongolia (Izagur Media) and Israel […]
content:
Korean sales company Finecut has sold Journey There, starring The Umbrella Academy‘s Justin H. Min, to multiple territories. The Seoul-based company has also closed further deals on Hong Sangsoo’s Locarno film festival awards winner Nowhere To Lay My Eyes.

Journey There has gone to Japan (KDDI Corporation), Taiwan (Andrews Film), Mongolia (Izagur Media) and Israel (Lev Cinema), while Kairos Distribution has picked up inflight rights.

The film marks the first Korean production for Min who is known for roles in Netflix series Beef and The Umbrella Academy, as well as Kogonada’s After Yang.

Directed by Kim Jin-yu, Journey There follows a middle-aged woman who, after losing her husband, begins preparing for a journey of her own, only to encounter unexpected connections in her new apartment.

Watch on Deadline

The film is Kim’s second following debut feature Bori, which won two awards at the Schlingel International Film Festival. Produced by Kim’s Pado production outfit, it has played at festivals including Moscow International Film Festival and the New York Asian Film Festival. Korean release is scheduled for October 28.

Nowhere To Lay My Eyes, which won Best Direction, Best Performance and the Ecumenical Jury Prize in Locarno, has gone to France (Carlotta Films), Japan (Mimosa Films), Portugal (The Stone And The Plot) and Argentina (Kligger). It was previously sold to Austria (Filmgarten), China (Hugoeast), North America (The Cinema Guild), Spain (Atalante), Taiwan (Cola Films), and the UK (ICA).

Finecut negotiated the additional deals at the recently concluded Asian Contents & Film Market in Busan. The company is now moving on to the AFM in Los Angeles where it will also be selling animated feature Long Long Night, which screened in Toronto, Busan and Sitges film festivals; Cannes Directors Fortnight title Dora; and fantasy romance Wi-Fi Love In The Palace, starring Kim Young-hoon.
